issues.title: [FEATURE]: Restore the legacy UI with the persistent left sidebar as an option
issues.body:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

The recent sidebar redesign (#20242) replaced the classic two-panel layout
(persistent left sidebar + session panel) with a Codex-style unified view.
For me this is not a visual refresh — it removed the single most important
part of my daily workflow, and there is currently no way to go back.

**What I want changed / added:**

1. Keep the **legacy UI with the persistent left sidebar** available as an
   option (a `legacy` / `classic` UI toggle or config flag is enough — it
   doesn't have to be the default).
2. If the legacy layout can't be maintained, at minimum restore an
   **always-visible left sidebar** — not hover-only menus or a collapsed rail
   that requires extra clicks.

**Why this matters (the benefit):**

I live inside opencode for hours every day. The left sidebar gives me an
at-a-glance, persistent view of my projects, workspaces, and sessions:

- I can see and switch between projects/contexts without breaking flow.
- Sessions are one click away, not buried behind hover or search.
- Context switching stays fast and predictable.

The new interface hides all of this behind a single unified list with
hover/focus interactions. Every session feels slower and more disoriented.
This is not an aesthetic preference — removing the sidebar with no escape
hatch is a functional regression for anyone who relies on it.

**Related:**

- #4583 asked for a way to go back to the old UI.
- #20242 introduced the sidebar redesign.

Happy to provide screenshots, my opencode version, and platform details if
that helps. Please don't leave those of us who depend on the left sidebar
behind.

issues.title: [2.0.22 / 2.0.27] Turns are aborted with nothing asking for it: the v2 report your tracker asked for twice

labels.name: type/feature
labels.description: New behaviour or an improvement

labels.name: area/core
labels.description: Agent loop, tools and config

labels.name: version/v2
labels.description: OpenCode 2.x

labels.name: platform/windows
labels.description: Windows

labels.name: platform/linux
labels.description: Linux

issues.body:
**What this is.** A turn dies with nothing asking it to, and the engine no longer says who asked. The store keeps one truth and the stream another, and the fields that could settle it were lost between versions. This is the report your tracker's own closings asked for twice, from someone who did the work.

**Summary.** A store holding **5,524 assistant turns** holds **27** marked `error.type = "aborted"` — the store's field for how a turn ended. Nothing I did coincides with any of them. They die early, they cluster into a few sessions, the log says nothing at the death, and **25 of the 27 sit in sessions the engine itself recorded as `succeeded`**. On a second machine the same class runs at **4.90%** on the build I left on.

**The timeline.**

**Before the switch, the engine caught its dead turns.** In the older engine's record I hold **18 aborted turns across 4,011** (0.45%), and every one is signed: a `message=cancel` line in the same session, **0 to 12 milliseconds** before the death. None of those were me: the nearest message of mine is 13 seconds from a death, most are 25 to 90 seconds away, and in **9 of the 18** the next message in the session is the plugin's own context injection rather than anything I typed. The cancels were the client's, and the client was at least still writing down what the engine did.

And the failure itself had already worn **four different models** in that era: big-pickle, hy3-free, phi4-mini and deepseek-flash. The output-duplication face of the failure was measured under the same agent on three of them — big-pickle repeating in **9 of 11** sessions, hy3-free in **6 of 7**, phi4-mini in **1 of 3** — while the same deepseek-flash under a clean agent repeated **zero times in 66 sessions**. The model was never the variable.

**2026-09-30 04:41 local.** The Copilot plugin's update ("OpenCode 2 in your vault", plugin 4.0.12, bundled engine 2.0.3) lands. Within forty minutes, **three agent sessions crashed** with `Internal error: Internal service failure`. After each crash the failed turn kept executing in the background: files were written minutes later. The chat stayed permanently locked: every new message returned `Internal error: Session already has an active ACP prompt: <session id>`. **This is the boundary the reporting dies at:** from this day, nothing asks, and nothing signs.

**2026-09-30, roughly 06:36.** A fourth session died mid-work. Its transcript stops mid-sentence while the uninstaller it had started kept running and finished on its own.

**2026-10-01 22:54.** First standalone session, engine 2.0.6, plugin removed. **271 turns, 0 aborts.** I read that as the fix working. It was the calm between two updates.

**2026-10-03 and 10-12.** The phone, engine 2.0.22, holds **7 dead turns in 691**: two on the 3rd, five on the 12th.

| build | assistant turns | aborted | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0.6 | 271 | 0 | 0.00% |
| 2.0.22 | 691 | 7 | 1.01% |
| 2.0.27 | 1,734 | 85 | 4.90% |

The 2.0.6 row is a bound, not a proof: 0 in 271 permits up to about 1.1% at 95% confidence. The other two rows are counts.

And the silence on 2.0.22 is documented, not inferred. Five of the seven deaths have the nearest message of mine more than thirty seconds away, several a minute or more out. At the death on 10-12 at 08:28, the engine's own `idle` line five seconds later records `outcome: interrupted` — the engine's own word, written at the death — with no message of mine within half a minute on either side, and the session's final record says `succeeded`. The turn after that death, answering my next message, tells the story the record does not: a tool call was aborted with the engine's phrase, "Tool execution interrupted", and my edit was left uncommitted. That narrating row carries no error field at all. Five of the seven dead rows wrote no token count and no cost. The engine told the model. It wrote nothing anywhere else.

**2026-10-07.** The desktop's own 2.0.22 era holds a specimen of the failure the counter cannot see at all. The store records a session created at **01:06** that no person opened, two minutes after work was queued for a fresh session at 01:03. By **02:14** that session had completed the queued task: **it rewrote the rule file that governs my entire system, in a pass nobody started, and no field in the record says it happened.** A write like that, done wrong, ends the project. The sessions around it are the only ones the engine recorded `interrupted` in that era — its own word for a turn that never got its answer — and the engine's log said nothing about any of it; the only report that existed was a census I ran myself against the store's columns. The session's stamp reads **version 2.0.22**. That is the class with no field, happening on this build, on this machine, while the abort counter reads zero.

**2026-10-08.** Obsidian removed.

**2026-10-13 through 10-15.** On the phone, engine 2.0.27: **11 aborts in 209 turns on the 13th**, and the class runs flat across the three days: **5.26%**, then **5.01%**, then **4.71%**.

**2026-10-16.** The desktop's worst day: **25 aborted turns** in one day, **15,135 log lines**, and not one of them an error.

| build | assistant turns | aborted | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0.22 | 1,522 | 0 | 0.00% |
| 2.0.24 | 2,404 | 2 | 0.08% |
| 2.0.27 | 1,598 | 25 | 1.56% |

The two 2.0.24 aborts are the two in `interrupted` sessions, the genuine class. **Every one of the 25 on 2.0.27 sits in a session the engine recorded as completed successfully.**

**2026-10-18.** The bridge and the engine removed. The deaths stopped.

The plugin belongs in this timeline for one reason: its update is my only link to the 2.x line, and the day it landed is the day the class began on my machines. What the plugin's team later assumed about fixes is their assumption, not your claim, and I am not here to hold you to it.

**Why it cannot be anything else.** I did not argue my way to the engine. I eliminated everything above it, in order.

1. **Not the person.** The nearest message of mine after any of the 27 deaths is **16 seconds**, the median **61**. An interrupt lands instantly. The only two aborts the engine labels `interrupted` are two of the 2.0.24 turns, and I would expect those: they are the genuine class, and your own field gets them right.
2. **Not the OS, not the surface.** Windows desktop and Android terminal, both affected. The surface moves the rate, not the class: 2.0.27 runs **1.56% on the desktop** and **4.90% on the phone**, same model, same agent.
3. **Not the plugin.** Removed 2026-10-01, scrubbed from every vault it touched, Obsidian out 10-08. The deaths continued in the standalone engine on the phone, with no plugin anywhere in the running system.
4. **Not the model.** The failure wore four models in the era before the switch, and the one it wears in 2.x is the only model in both stores. The rate still steps between builds on one phone with the model held fixed.
5. **Not the provider.** The frozen log holds **no provider errors from 09-26 through 09-30**, only the aborts. The 2.0.27 log holds 15,135 lines on the worst day and not one non-INFO. An abort writes no log line at all, so the log's silence cannot rule an outage in or out. What it can say is narrower and still useful: **in both eras the aborts travel unaccompanied.**

What is left is the engine, as the last layer standing, and its own record saying a turn was told to stop with no note of who told it. **The one thing that changed across the whole timeline was not the failure and not the model. It was the catching: the old era cancelled the dead turn and wrote a line every time. The new era does neither, and the turn hangs.**

**The record lost the words.** The `finish` field — the turn's visible end state — holds two values in the current stores, `tool_calls` and `stop`, and the raw finish never once says `aborted`. All **119** aborts I hold across both machines survive only in `error.type`. The older engine could write `unknown` (53 times), real error objects (29 of them), a content filter, an API error, and a cancel for every death. The current one has no field at all for the failures that never write an abort: the hang, the turn that never settles, the spinner with nothing behind it. I had all three, and all three are invisible to your store by construction.

**The session disagrees with the turn.** `idle_outcome` is the session's own verdict on itself, written at its end. Of the desktop's 27 aborted turns, **25 sit in sessions recorded `succeeded`**. The turn says the work was killed; the session says it finished; only one of them can be right. This is not new to you, even if the connection has not been made: #59051 is open on your tracker right now with the same field lying, a child session recorded `idle_outcome: succeeded` with real token usage while the parent receives an empty result. It is the same contradiction from the other end.

**The fog, published.** The opencode era also raised the only fog my project has ever had: duplicated sentences repeated inside model output. I published the full record of it: *Nothing Stayed Fog*, Zenodo, DOI `10.5281/zenodo.23632879`. Every fog reading in the project's history falls inside the opencode era, and none has occurred since the engine was removed. It is the same silence in a different voice: a failure the engine's own record could not show me.

**What it cost.** In the entire life of my project under opencode 2, I did not have a single stress-free day. Even after the plugin was out and the app gutted, there were ten more days, 10-08 to 10-18, spent tearing apart and rebuilding my entire system to make sure nothing of it was left. The project did not lose a single day across any of it; the cost landed in nights and rebuilds instead of downtime. This is a product sold as a full release, the second edition of one, and simply opening a session was enough to have my entire contract rewritten silently. One wrong move from total loss and restore state.

The ledger agrees with the days. Across that window the sessions your engine kept record **13,433,584 input, 3,038,094 output and 7,690,477 reasoning tokens**, all on my own key, all `deepseek-flash`, and your own cost ledger prices it at **USD 15.47** — a floor: the crash day and the entire 2.0.6 desktop era are in no store. I ran the cheapest model that can do this work. Your users are not all so lucky, and the failure was invisible on every one of them. And the ledger hides the dead turns: **98 of the 119 carry no cost record at all.** The price dies with the turn, the same as the word.

I am not filing this for compensation. I am reporting a loss, mental and financial, that traces directly to the decision to stop logging these failures at all. The next user deserves to know, before they install, that this can cost a lot more than dead turns with unlogged cost.

**What your tracker already knows.** Seventy-four issues and pull requests in your repo have the word aborted in the title. The shape has been in front of you since August:

- **#48850** (filed 09-13, closed 10-11): "Desktop randomly marks running turn as interrupted (AbortError: Aborted, no retry, no UI error)". This is the class, on your desktop build, filed by a stranger a month before I left. It was closed with "development is focused on V2", and the invitation: "if this is still relevant on 2.0, reopen this issue or open a new one with your 2.0 version."
- **#55130** (filed 10-13, closed 10-14): "[FEATURE]: record the abort origin — error=Aborted stack=undefined gives no source". The filer asks for the field this report documents the absence of, after a session stalled for 13 hours with no log event. Closed with the same invitation: open a new issue "with aborts that don't say what stopped the run" on v2.
- **#37852** (closed 10-11): "Aborted provider stream recorded as clean stop (finish=unknown, zero usage, no text)". The missing word, seen from the clean side.
- **#61694** (closed 11-05): when a streamed response fails after a tool call ran, the next request tells the model "User aborted the command" for a command that already ran. Your bot closed it saying v2.2.5 and later handle it correctly.
- **#61723** (closed 11-05): your own fix notes admit a run's outcome "could be missed" because the outcome was read from stored messages instead of the live stream.
- **#60487** (open): `provider.transport ECONNRESET` on large request bodies, triaged as a gateway limit. My desktop holds three ECONNRESETs of my own, on 10-10, 10-11 and 10-15. They are not the abort class; they are the same wire failing, and from my side they read as a spinner with nothing behind it.
- **[logancyang/obsidian-copilot#3444](https://github.com/logancyang/obsidian-copilot/issues/3444)** (the plugin's tracker, closed 11-06 by their triage bot): the crash side, with my logs. The closing note says it "has not recurred since OpenCode 2.0.22". My stores say otherwise, and the counts are above.

None of these threads connect the fields, and the two that asked for the missing word were closed without it being added in any build I ran. This report is the v2 specimen their closings invited.

**Your release notes.** Your live release feed carries twenty entries, newest 2026-11-10, and the word abort appears in it exactly once. I am not refuting a fix you announced: you never said a word about this either way. This report is the word.

**What I am not claiming.** I cannot see inside the engine, so I am not naming a cause. I never ran a build after 2.0.27, so this report does not cover 2.1 or 2.2, and it is possible some of this is already fixed. Every number here is a count in a store I still hold, and I will produce the store itself, not a summary of it.

**The three questions.**

1. **What writes `error.type = "aborted"` besides an explicit user interrupt?** A stream that ends, a session's own idle handling, a client that vanishes: any of those would explain the early deaths, the empty turns, the clustering and the cure by starting a new session at once. This is the question #55130 asked from the log's side, and it was closed before it reached you.
2. **Why does 2.x write no `message=cancel`, where 1.18.x wrote one for every abort it recorded?** The event is not new. It stopped saying who asked for it, and that is the single thing that kept this invisible.
3. **Does a session with an aborted turn report success on purpose, or is that the same missing word?** The 25 of 27 is the check, and #59051 is already asking the sibling question.

**Environment and evidence.** Windows desktop builds and Termux on Android; engine **2.0.6, 2.0.22, 2.0.24 and 2.0.27**; `deepseek/deepseek-flash` throughout. Both stores and the frozen log travel with this report. Name any row and I will produce it.

Toxx

issues.title: patch: case-only rename deletes the file on case-insensitive filesystems
issues.body:
### Description

On a case-insensitive filesystem (the macOS and Windows defaults), a patch that only changes the case of a file name deletes the file.

`packages/core/src/tool/plugin/patch.ts:185` treats the hunk as a move because `same.txt` and `Same.txt` are different strings. That check comes from #59197, which fixed moves onto the exact same path (`./same.txt`), but it doesn't catch a case change. The apply step then writes `Same.txt`, which overwrites `same.txt` in place, and removes `same.txt`, which is the same file (`patch.ts:233-239`). The tool then fails with:

```
Failed to read <dir>/Same.txt: file does not exist. Completed before failure: Same.txt
```

On a case-sensitive filesystem the same patch renames the file correctly.

The `v1` branch has the same write-then-remove in `apply_patch.ts` and no guard even for the exact same path (#45310 was closed, but its fix #45316 was not merged).

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

2.2.7 (dev at edfe6510d)

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a case-insensitive filesystem, create `same.txt` containing `before`.
2. Run the `patch` tool with:
   ```
   *** Begin Patch
   *** Update File: same.txt
   *** Move to: Same.txt
   @@
   -before
   +after
   *** End Patch
   ```
3. The directory is now empty and the tool returns the error above. Expected: `Same.txt` containing `after`.

I reproduced it with a test added to `packages/core/test/tool-patch.test.ts` (using `withTempTool` and `executeTool`), run with `TMPDIR` on a vfat mount. The same test passes on ext4.

### Screenshot

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS and Windows (any case-insensitive volume); reproduced on Linux with a vfat mount

### Terminal

_No response_

prs.title: fix(app): keep new timeline status below reports and shorten file lists
prs.body:
## What changed

All of this is behind the New timeline experiment. The old timeline renders as before.

- **Reports sit above the status line.** A subagent or shell report that the agent hasn't picked up yet ("Finished 1 subagent") used to show below "Waiting for shell", which read as if it happened after the current moment. A report is something that already happened, so it now joins the active turn above the status line, even when a steered prompt is waiting below.
- **Steered prompts still wait below the status line.** The agent hasn't replied to them, so the status line stays above them, as before.
- **"Move to background" no longer gets cut off.** When the status line sits in the `Activity` row above a waiting prompt, that row clips at its height and cut off the bottom of the 24px button. The lane there now keeps the 4px the button reaches past the line, always, so the waiting prompt doesn't move when the button comes and goes.
- **Edited names up to 2 files**, then says "Edited N files".
- **Read rows list each file once.** Reading one file in several chunks showed `patch.ts, patch.ts, patch.ts`. Each path now shows once (without line ranges when it was read more than once), and past 2 files the closed row says "Read N files". Opening it shows the full list. `CurrentReadToolGroup` only does this when it gets the new `names` prop, which only the new timeline passes.

No new flag. Every change only takes effect when the New timeline experiment (`newTimeline` setting) is on.

prs.title: feat(ai): add MiniMax video generation
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

I added MiniMax video generation to `@opencode/ai`: `MiniMax.configure(...).video(id)`, `videoModel`, and the `@opencode/ai/providers/minimax/videos` entrypoint, which core now loads. One entrypoint serves both `minimax` and `minimax-cn`; they differ only by `baseURL` (`https://api.minimax.io` or `https://api.minimax.cn`), which models.dev already sets per model.

**Two APIs, one selector.** MiniMax runs H3 on a v2 API and Hailuo on a v1 API. The two differ in body, statuses, result lookup and cancel, so they are two protocols (`minimax-video` and `minimax-hailuo-video`) in one file. models.dev lists every model under one `[api.videos]` table, and core loads one `/videos` entrypoint per model, so a separate selector can't be reached from the catalog. `video(id)` therefore picks the API by model family: Hailuo and `*-01` models go to v1 (a fixed legacy list), everything else goes to v2. `MiniMaxVideo.h3Model` and `hailuoModel` are exported for callers that want to choose explicitly. Video takes the API host without a version as `baseURL`, because the version is part of each API's path.

| Shared field | H3 (v2, `POST /v2/video_generation`) | Hailuo (v1, `POST /v1/video_generation`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `content[{type:"text"}]` | `prompt` |
| `start` / `end` | `image_url` items with role `first_frame` / `last_frame` | `first_frame_image` / `last_frame_image` |
| `references` | `image_url` / `video_url` / `audio_url` with `reference_*` roles | images to `subject_reference[{type:"character"}]` |
| MiniMax file refs | `mm_file://{id}` | not sent (v1 documents URLs and data URLs only) |
| `duration` | `duration` (seconds) | `duration` (seconds) |
| `aspect` | `ratio`; `auto` becomes `adaptive` | none |
| `resolution` | uppercased (`480P`, `2K`) | uppercased (`512P`, `768P`) |
| `sound` | none (always has sound) | none (always silent) |
| `providerOptions` | merged into the body (`extra`, `callback_url`, `response_format`, ...) | merged (`prompt_optimizer`, `fast_pretreatment`, `callback_url`, ...) |

Nothing gets a default. H3 requires `resolution` and `duration`, plus a `ratio` for text-only prompts (error 2013). If one is missing, MiniMax's error comes back typed.

**Rejected locally** (nothing to send them with): on H3, `sound: false` (I checked live that H3 ignores `generate_audio: false` and still adds sound). On Hailuo, `sound: true`, an explicit `aspect` other than `auto`, video or audio references, and MiniMax file refs.

**Status, result and cancel.** Statuses go through tables (v2: `queued`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled`; v1: `Preparing`, `Queueing`, `Processing`, `Success`, `Fail`). Unknown values stay `running`. Codes 1026 and 1027 become `ContentPolicy`, 1008 becomes `QuotaExceeded`, and 1002, 1004, 2013 and 2049 map to their reasons. v1 reports errors as HTTP 200 with a non-zero `base_resp`, and those are handled too. The H3 result is the task's `content.url` with `durationSeconds`, `usage` in seconds, and model, resolution, ratio and raw usage in `providerMetadata`. A Hailuo task returns only a `file_id`, so its result makes a second read to `/v1/files/retrieve` for the download URL, which expires after one hour (`expiresAt`). To support that, I added a `get(path)` to `MediaProtocol.PollContext`. It is a further GET with the same auth and headers, retried like the poll. Cancel on H3 sends `DELETE /v2/video_generation/{id}`, which MiniMax only accepts while the task is queued. Hailuo has no cancel and fails with `UnsupportedOperation` without a network call.

I checked fields against the official docs: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-create, https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-query, https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-v2-delete, https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-query and https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/video-generation-download.

No feature flag: this adds a provider protocol under the existing video API and changes no default behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New unit tests in `packages/ai/test/minimax-video.test.ts` cover body mapping for every shared field on both APIs, API routing by model, local rejections, JSON token round-trip, status tables including unknown values, result decoding, failures, moderation, and cancel.
- Video cases in `test/provider/media-entrypoints.test.ts` cover `minimax` (H3) and `minimax-cn` (Hailuo via `api.minimax.cn`).
- Recorded live: `MiniMax-H3-Lite` text-only at 480P, 4 s, 16:9, and `MiniMax-Hailuo-02` from a first frame at 512P, 6 s, including the file lookup.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `packages/ai`, `bun typecheck` and `variant.test.ts` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` at the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

N/A

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(ai): add Kling video generation
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

None. This is independent of the video tool in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63666. Like https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63680 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63681, it adds the shared `videos` cases to `media-entrypoints.test.ts` and `videos` to the package regex in `variant.test.ts`, so whichever lands second has a trivial conflict.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

I added Kling video generation to `@opencode/ai`: a `klingai-video` protocol, a minimal `KlingAI` facade with `.video(id)` and `videoModel`, the `@opencode/ai/providers/klingai/videos` entrypoint, and its registration in core's built-in packages, so models.dev's Kling video models can load it (https://github.com/anomalyco/models.dev/pull/13545).

Kling has one endpoint per mode and model. The protocol picks it from the inputs:

```
endpoint = providerOptions.endpoint
        ?? omni-only model (kling-3.0-omni, kling-video-o1)   -> /omni-video/<segment>
        ?? references and the model has an Omni endpoint       -> /omni-video/<segment>
        ?? start or end                                        -> /image-to-video/<segment>
        ?? otherwise                                           -> /text-to-video/<segment>
```

models.dev lists some models under Kling's older `model_name` values, so a small table maps them to path segments (`kling-v2-6` to `kling-2.6`, `kling-v2-5-turbo` to `kling-2.5-turbo`, `kling-video-o1` to `kling-o1`). Unknown IDs are used as the segment as-is. Every model, including 2.6 and 2.5 Turbo, has these bearer-key endpoints in the current docs, so I didn't implement the legacy `/v1/videos/*` routes, which need an AK/SK-signed JWT.

| Shared field | Kling |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `prompt` (text-to-video) or `contents[{ type: "prompt", text }]` |
| `start` / `end` | `contents` `first_frame` / `last_frame` (first frame first, last frame last) |
| image `references` | `contents` `refer_image` with ids `image_1`, `image_2`, ... |
| video `references` | `contents` `feature_video` with ids `video_1`, ... (URL only) |
| `duration` | `settings.duration` (seconds) |
| `aspect` | `settings.aspect_ratio`; `auto` is `adaptive`, left out on image-to-video where the frame sets the shape |
| `resolution` | `settings.resolution` |
| `sound` | `settings.audio`: `native` / `off` |

Inline images go as bare base64, as Kling asks. `providerOptions.endpoint` overrides the endpoint, `providerOptions.contents` adds native items (Elements, voices, `base_video`, `middle_frame`) before the last frame, and `providerOptions.settings` / `options` merge into the native objects (`settings.audio: "original"`, `settings.multi_shot`, `options.callback_url`, `options.external_task_id`, `options.watermark_info`).

Rejected locally, because the protocol has no field for them: reference audio (Kling takes voices only as `voice_id`), inline reference videos (URL only), references on models without an Omni endpoint (`kling-3.0`, `kling-3.0-turbo`, Kling 2.x), and frames or `providerOptions.contents` on an explicit text-to-video endpoint. Everything else, such as durations or aspect ratios a model doesn't list, goes to Kling and its error comes back typed.

Status and result read `GET /tasks?task_ids=<id>`. `submitted` is queued, `processing` running, `succeeded` (and the legacy `succeed`) completed, `failed` failed, and anything else stays running. The token is `{ taskID, createdAt }`. Kling keeps results for 30 days, so video URLs get `expiresAt` 30 days after the task's `create_time`. A task missing from the response after that window reads as `expired`; before it, it's an invalid-output error. Failed tasks carry Kling's `message` as `ProviderInternal`. Kling documents no failure codes on tasks and no exact moderation wording (only that `message` describes the reason, "such as triggering the content risk control"), so I don't map any text to `ContentPolicy`. A submit that Kling's content policy blocks (error code 1301, HTTP 400) comes back as Kling's HTTP error. Results carry `durationSeconds`, `usage` from `usage.output_duration` (Kling 4.0), and the task id, external id and billing in `providerMetadata`. Kling has no cancel endpoint, so `cancel` fails with `UnsupportedOperation` without a request.

No new flag: this only adds a library protocol and entrypoint; nothing in opencode loads video models until the video tool lands.

Sources: https://kling.ai/document-api/api/video/4-0/video-omni, https://kling.ai/document-api/api/video/3-0-omni/video-omni, https://kling.ai/document-api/api/video/o1/video-omni, https://kling.ai/document-api/api/video/2-6/text-to-video, https://kling.ai/document-api/api/get-started/authentication, https://kling.ai/document-api/api/get-started/error-codes

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/ai/test/klingai-video.test.ts`: body mapping for every shared field, endpoint and segment routing, the rejected inputs (no network call), errors returned typed, token JSON round trip, status table with unknown statuses, result decoding (URL, expiry, duration, usage, metadata), failed, pending, empty and expired tasks, and cancel.
- A `klingai` case in `media-entrypoints.test.ts` and `exports.test.ts`.
- `klingai-video.recorded.test.ts` uses `kling-v2-5-turbo`, 5 seconds at 720p. I had no `KLINGAI_API_KEY`, so it isn't recorded and skips without a key. Nothing here ran against the live API.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `packages/ai`, `bun typecheck` and `test/variant.test.ts` in `packages/core`, `bun run check` at the root.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(app): find in side panel previews
prs.body:
Cmd+F in the side panel did nothing on a Markdown, Mermaid, CSV or HTML preview: the code view's find bar only exists in the code view. This adds find to those previews, using the same bar, highlight colors and position as the code view, so switching between a preview and its source keeps the bar where it was.

The code view's find, and the session search, are unchanged. Nothing in `session-ui` changes; the previews render the existing `FileSearchBar`.

### How it works

```text
Mod+F with a file tab active (same handler as before)
  preview showing?   no  ─▶ code view's find, as before
                     yes ─▶ preview find, same bar
    Markdown / Mermaid / table ─▶ search the rendered text, mark matches with CSS highlights
    HTML (sandboxed iframe)    ─▶ postMessage to a small script added at the top of the page,
                                   which searches, marks and scrolls inside the frame and sends back the count
```

The HTML preview runs as an opaque origin, so the app can't read it. The script is added after the doctype and before the page's own markup, so a CSP the page declares later doesn't block it. It also passes Mod+F back to the app, since keys pressed inside the frame never reach the window's handlers. The app resolves the theme's highlight colors and sends them with each search, so the marks match.

I tried Electron's `webContents.findInPage` first. It searches the whole window, so it also counted the text in the find box and the conversation, and it moved focus into the frame after every search, which broke typing in the bar. So I didn't use it.

Limits: PDFs stay unsearchable (Chromium's viewer exposes nothing to the page). Matches don't span formatting, so "foo bar" doesn't match across `foo **bar**`. No feature flag: the window has no way to read server flags, and the change only adds find where Cmd+F did nothing before.

prs.title: feat(ai): add OpenRouter video generation
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Second video protocol after xAI, on the `ai.video` API from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63657.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds OpenRouter video generation (`POST /api/v1/videos`), which reaches 32 video models through one API: Veo, Seedance, Kling, Wan, Hailuo, Grok Imagine, HeyGen, FLUX and others. Use it with `OpenRouter.configure(...).video("google/veo-3.1")`, or from opencode through the new `@opencode/ai/providers/openrouter/videos` entrypoint.

| Shared field | OpenRouter |
| --- | --- |
| `start`, `end` | `frame_images[]` with `frame_type: first_frame / last_frame` |
| `references` | `input_references[]` as `image_url`, `video_url` or `audio_url` by kind |
| `duration: "6 seconds"` | `duration: 6` |
| `aspect` | `aspect_ratio`; `"auto"` is left out, which is how OpenRouter follows the input image |
| `resolution` | `resolution`, with `1k`/`2k`/`4k` written as `1K`/`2K`/`4K` |
| `sound` | `generate_audio` |
| `providerOptions` | merged into the body: `provider` (routing plus `options.<slug>` passthrough), `previous_job_id`, `seed`, `size`, `callback_url`, … |

Rejected before sending, because OpenRouter can't use them:

- Frames together with references. OpenRouter's docs say frame images take precedence and the request is treated as image-to-video, so the references would be dropped with no error.
- Reference videos that aren't http(s) URLs. OpenRouter rejects inline video, which I checked live earlier, and its Files API doesn't take video.

Everything else, including durations, resolutions and aspect ratios a model doesn't support, goes to OpenRouter, which returns a 400 listing the supported values.

Status and result:

- **Statuses:** `pending` → queued, `in_progress` → running, plus `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` and `expired`. Unknown statuses stay running.
- **Downloads:** the result's `unsigned_urls` are OpenRouter content URLs that only download with the API key (a request without it gets a 401, checked live). The protocol needs those headers, so `MediaProtocol.PollContext` gets a small `headers(url)` that returns the auth and deployment headers a GET to that URL would send. The result asset carries them for the download. `expires_at` becomes `expiresAt`, and the cost goes into `providerMetadata.openrouter`.
- **Failures:** a failed job fails `result` with OpenRouter's `error` text. Errors that mention a content policy or moderation map to `ContentPolicy`.
- **Cancel:** OpenRouter has no cancel endpoint (`DELETE /videos/{id}` and `/cancel` both return 404, checked live), so `cancel` fails as unsupported without a request.

### How did you verify your code works?

- **Live probes:**
  - an image `frame_images` entry sent as a data URL was accepted;
  - a 1-second 480p `x-ai/grok-imagine-video-1.5-lite` job completed, and the content URL downloaded a valid MP4 with the API key.
- **Recorded test:** `test/provider/openrouter-video.recorded.test.ts`, recorded live for $0.03. It drives start, status until done, then result, and downloads the video through the asset's headers. No signed URLs ended up in the cassette.

prs.title: feat(ai): add Google Gemini Omni video generation
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

The Gemini API Veo models shut down on 2026-10-22; Gemini Omni through the Interactions API replaces them. This lands on `dev` on its own, independent of the opencode video tool. Like https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63680 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63681, it adds the shared `sentVideo` helper and `videos` list to the media entrypoint test and `videos` to the reasoning-variant exclusion in `packages/core/test/variant.test.ts`, so whichever lands second has a trivial conflict.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

I added video generation for Gemini Omni (`gemini-omni-1.2-flash`, `gemini-omni-1.1-flash`) on the Gemini API. `Google.video(id)` returns a video model, `videoModel` and `@opencode/ai/providers/google/videos` expose it for opencode, and core registers the entrypoint.

The protocol (`packages/ai/src/protocols/google-interactions-video.ts`) reuses the Interactions auth, base URL and media lowering from the chat protocol (I exported its `mediaContent`).

How a job runs:

```
start   POST /interactions { background: true, ... }   -> token { interactionID }
status  GET  /interactions/{id}                          in_progress -> running, completed/incomplete -> completed,
                                                        failed, cancelled; anything else stays running
result  GET  /interactions/{id}                          the video content of the model_output step
cancel  POST /interactions/{id}/cancel
```

| Shared field | Sent as |
|---|---|
| `prompt` | last `input` part, `{ type: "text" }` |
| `start`, `end` | first and second image parts in `input`, plus `generation_config.video_config.task: "image_to_video"` |
| `references` | image or video parts after the frames, plus `task: "reference_to_video"` when there are no frames |
| `duration` | `response_format.duration`, `"3s"` |
| `aspect` | `response_format.aspect_ratio`; `auto` leaves it out so the model follows the input |
| `resolution` | `response_format.resolution`, lowercased (`"4K"` -> `"4k"`) |
| `sound: true` | nothing to send: Omni always generates audio |
| `providerOptions` | merged into the body (`previous_interaction_id`, `generation_config`, `response_format.delivery`, `service_tier`, `webhook_config`, ...) |

Omni has no role field for media: it reads one image as the start frame and two as start and end. The task hint makes that reading explicit when only frames or only references are sent. When both are sent I set no task and send them in order (start, end, references), because Google doesn't document how Omni combines them; the provider decides and its error comes back typed.

Rejected before sending, because there is no way to express them:

- `end` without `start` (a lone image is read as the first frame)
- `sound: false` (audio is always generated)

`aspect: "auto"` follows the same convention as xAI and OpenRouter: the ratio is left out. The Omni docs only say 16:9 is the default and don't say whether an omitted ratio follows a start image, so that part is unverified.

Reference audio is sent as an `audio` part. The docs say the current version doesn't accept audio inputs, but the wire format has them, so the provider's error comes back instead of a local rejection.

Results: `GET /interactions/{id}` returns the video inline as base64 (Google documents this even for `delivery: "uri"`), so the result is a bytes asset with no expiry. If a response ever carries only a Files API `uri`, I keep it as a `google` reference, since downloading it needs the API key. Usage maps to token usage, and `providerMetadata.google` carries the interaction ID, model and status. Failed interactions map their `errors[].code` (last URI segment) through a table: `INVALID_ARGUMENT`/`FAILED_PRECONDITION`/`OUT_OF_RANGE` to InvalidRequest, `PERMISSION_DENIED`/`UNAUTHENTICATED` to Authentication, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` to RateLimit, Gemini safety codes to ContentPolicy, and anything else to ProviderInternal.

Vertex serves `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` through the same Interactions API (global location only, base `https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1beta1/projects/{project}/locations/global`). This protocol should fit it with the Vertex base URL and auth, but I didn't wire or test it here.

### How did you verify your code works?

- I recorded `test/provider/google-interactions-video.recorded.test.ts` live against `gemini-omni-1.2-flash` at 360p, 3 seconds, 16:9. It completed in about 20 seconds and returned an inline `video/mp4`. The cassette is about 3 MB because the video appears in the final status read and the result read.
- `test/google-interactions-video.test.ts` covers body mapping for every shared field, task selection, the three rejections, a JSON round-tripped token, the status table with unknown statuses, inline and URI results, failure, cancelled, moderated and empty results, and the cancel endpoint.
- `bun test` and `bun typecheck` in `packages/ai`, `bun typecheck` and `test/variant.test.ts` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` at the root pass.

Not verified live: cancel, failure error codes (the docs only say they are URIs) and frames combined with references.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(desktop): pair with nearby phones over mDNS
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets the OpenCode mobile app pair with a desktop on the same network without scanning a QR code. The desktop announces itself over mDNS (`_opencode._tcp`), the phone lists it, and tapping it runs a key exchange. Both screens show the same 6-digit code, and only after the user confirms on both devices does the desktop send a pairing code, encrypted for that phone. The phone then redeems it the same way as a scanned QR code. The server doesn't change.

Guarded by the new **`nearby_pairing`** flag. Unlike other flags it's on in **local, dev and beta** builds, so beta testers can try it with the mobile app; stable releases keep it off until it graduates. The desktop main process has no Location config, so it reads the flag from `OPENCODE_FLAGS` and the build channel only; `experimental.nearby_pairing` in config doesn't reach it.

## How it works

- **Code exchange** (`exchange.ts`, whose header comment is the wire spec): X25519 with a commit/reveal step so an attacker in the middle can't search for matching codes, HKDF-derived keys for each direction, then AES-256-GCM sealed frames with counter nonces.
- **Prompt:** a request shows as a toast in every window, wherever the user is (Pair / Decline). If no window is focused, a system notification also shows, at most once every 30 s. Success or failure gets its own toast.
- **Abuse limits** (`gate.ts`): one request at a time; a device can replace its own request at most every 3 s; **Snooze This Device** (1 h) appears after 3+ requests from one address in 2 min, and **Snooze All for 15 Minutes** after 3+ addresses. Devices are told apart by network address, not the name the phone sends.
- **mDNS** (`mdns*.ts`): uses the system's own mDNS service. macOS runs `dns-sd -R`. Linux talks to Avahi over D-Bus (`dbus-next`). Windows uses `DnsServiceRegister` in `dnsapi.dll`, through a hidden PowerShell process. If the system service is missing or refuses, it falls back to `bonjour-service`. Using the system service avoids the host-name clashes (`macbook-2`, `-3`, …) that a second responder causes.
- **Settings › Pairing › Discoverable nearby** turns announcing off. It shows only while the flag is on, and turning it off and on again clears snoozes.
- **Remote access:** if the server only listens on this machine, the pairing payload turns on remote access and sends the tunnel URL, as the QR dialog does.

The iOS side is in anomalyco/opencode-ios, branch `nearby-pairing`, behind an off-by-default experiment.

## Testing

- `bun run check` passes, the 59 pairing tests pass (exchange with fixed test vectors shared with the Swift version, gate, mDNS backend choice and fallback), and the desktop production build bundles the new code.
- **macOS:** paired the dev desktop end to end with the iOS app on a phone and in the simulator. After porting onto the refactored pairing plugin, rechecked with a mock phone: discovery starts through `dns-sd` and the toast shows the code.
- **Linux:** Avahi path checked in a Debian container: publish, withdraw on stop, the "#2" rename on a duplicate name, and the fallback when Avahi is gone. Not yet tried on a real Linux machine on the same network as a phone.
- **Windows:** the PowerShell script parses and compiles under PowerShell 7 on Linux, but it hasn't run on Windows yet. It still needs a check on real hardware, including what the firewall asks about the pairing port.

- **Settings › Pairing:** the Discoverable nearby row renders on the refactored page, and toggling it stops and restarts the announcement.

A screen recording of the desktop and simulator flow is available on request (Brendan has it).

prs.title: feat(ai): add Seedance video generation for Volcengine and BytePlus
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. This adds a video provider on top of the job API from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63657.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

This adds ByteDance Seedance video generation through the Ark task API, served by two providers: `volcengine` (Volcengine Ark, `ARK_API_KEY`) and `byteplus` (BytePlus ModelArk, `BYTEPLUS_API_KEY`). Both use the same `POST /contents/generations/tasks` API on different hosts, so I wrote one protocol (`packages/ai/src/protocols/seedance-video.ts`) and built one instance per provider. That way `model.provider`, `Media.ref(...)` ownership and `providerMetadata` carry the right provider ID.

Neither provider had a facade in the package (their chat models go through openai-compatible), so I added small `Volcengine` and `BytePlus` facades with only `.video(id)`, plus `videoModel` and the `providers/volcengine/videos` and `providers/byteplus/videos` entrypoints, registered in Core's builtins.

Field mapping:

| Shared field | Ark body |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt` | `content[]` `{ type: "text" }` item (left out when the prompt is empty, since every media mode accepts no text) |
| `start` / `end` | `image_url` items with role `first_frame` / `last_frame` |
| `references` | `image_url` `reference_image`, `video_url` `reference_video`, `audio_url` `reference_audio` by asset kind; own `Media.ref` assets become `asset://<id>` |
| `duration` | `duration` (seconds) |
| `aspect` | `ratio`, with `auto` sent as `adaptive` |
| `resolution` | `resolution` as-is |
| `sound` | `generate_audio` |
| `providerOptions` | merged into the body; `draft_task: { id }` becomes a `draft_task` content item |

Rejected locally: nothing beyond what every protocol rejects (a `Media.ref` owned by another provider). Seedance rejects frames and references in the same task, but I send that combination and let the provider's error come back, as for limits and value ranges.

Status and cancel:

- Ark statuses map `queued`, `running`, `succeeded` (completed), `failed`, `cancelled`, `expired`; unknown ones stay `running`. Ark reports no progress.
- Failure codes are dotted (`InvalidParameter.TaskTypeConstraint`), so I classify by the first segment: `InvalidParameter`, `MissingParameter`, `InvalidArgumentError` and `InvalidImageURL` are `InvalidRequest`, `AuthenticationError` and `AccessDenied` are `Authentication`, `QuotaExceeded` and `RateLimitExceeded` are `RateLimit`, the rest `ProviderInternal`. Any `*SensitiveContentDetected*` code is `ContentPolicy`.
- The result is a URL asset with `expiresAt` 24 hours after `updated_at` (when the task finished), `durationSeconds` from `frames / framespersecond` or `duration`, token usage, and metadata (seed, ratio, resolution, fps, last frame URL, ...).
- `cancel` sends `DELETE /tasks/{id}`. Ark only cancels queued tasks: it refuses a running one (the error comes back typed) and deletes the record of a finished one. I documented that rather than reading the status first.

No feature flag: this only adds new provider entrypoints, and the video API they plug into is already shipped.

Sources: https://ai.byteplus.com/ark/region:ap-southeast-1/docs/create-video-generation-task-api (create), https://ai.byteplus.com/ark/region:ap-southeast-1/docs/get-video-generation-task-api, https://ai.byteplus.com/ark/region:ap-southeast-1/docs/cancel-or-delete-video-generation-tasks-api, https://ai.byteplus.com/ark/region:ap-southeast-1/docs/error-codes, and the Volcengine retrieve page https://www.volcengine.com/docs/82379/1521309, which has the same fields.

This PR also adds the `videos` case list to `media-entrypoints.test.ts` and `videos` to the regex in `variant.test.ts`. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63666 adds the same pieces for xAI, so whichever lands second has a small merge.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/ai/test/seedance-video.test.ts`: body mapping for every shared field, reference roles and `asset://` refs, `auto` to `adaptive`, frames plus references sent unchanged, `draft_task`, both hosts and provider IDs, token JSON round-trip, every status plus unknown ones, result decoding (expiry, duration, usage, metadata, mov), failed, moderated, cancelled and expired tasks, and cancel via `DELETE`.
- `media-entrypoints.test.ts` cases for both `/videos` entrypoints.
- `packages/ai/test/provider/seedance-video.recorded.test.ts` targets BytePlus with the cheapest settings (2.0 mini, 480p, 4 s). I have no Volcengine or BytePlus key, so it is not recorded and skips without `BYTEPLUS_API_KEY`. Nothing here has been run against the live API.
- `bun typecheck` and `bun test` in `packages/ai`, `bun typecheck` and `variant.test.ts` in `packages/core`, and `bun run check` at the root.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(desktop): persistent browser profile, extensions and agent tool fixes
prs.body:
The desktop's in-app browser was a signed-out, in-memory pane per attachment. Agents drove it through tools that failed on one call in five and ignored a configured `browser` deny. After this PR it is one persistent, encrypted profile with imported sign-ins, Chrome extensions and in-pane links. Its agent tools follow the user's permission rules and work on tabs that are not on screen. | Area | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Profile | Fresh in-memory partition per pane attachment | One `persist:opencode-browser` profile for the whole app | | Sign-ins | Lost on restart, tab close or a new session | Kept on disk; import from 14 browsers, Safari and cookie files | | Links | Web links open the system browser | Plain click opens the pane; Shift or other modifiers keep the system browser | | Extensions | None | Install from a store link, a browser profile or a folder; popups over the pane; per-extension verdict | | Ad blocking | n/a | uBlock Origin (MV2) and uBlock Origin Lite block requests | | Tool reliability | 20.7% of 14,974 measured calls failed | The top error groups are fixed or get a precise message (see Why) | | Hidden tabs | Screenshot refused, click fails with `UnknownVizError` | Screenshot, click and hover work while the tab is not on screen | | Permissions | Attach grant beats a configured deny; subagents and killed servers keep grants | Configured deny and ask win per operation; grants do not leak | | Cookie storage | Plain text (`EnableCookieEncryption` off) | Encrypted with the OS key store in packaged builds | https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1da061b9-3df7-448b-bf40-deb04bb14843 The video shows the original profile, import and extension flow. It was recorded before the extension APIs, tool, permission and macOS work below. | uBlock Origin popup over the pane | Dark Reader popup | | --- | --- | | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c77c4f42-95d0-446f-a99f-2f99847fc2ef) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e944604-6e32-4a82-8656-b05cd9db4a91) | ## Why ### Measured tool-call errors Browser calls from the session databases of four devices (adais and blade on Windows, air on macOS, vps on Linux with a remote desktop): 14,974 calls, 3,099 errors. | Error group | adais | blade | air | vps | Total | After this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `wait` without `condition` (Playwright-style `text`, `timeout`, `state`, `time`) | 70 | 2,033 | 2 | 33 | 2,138 | Condition read from the keys present | | `screenshot` "needs a visible tab" | 88 | 207 | 1 | 9 | 305 | Captures hidden tabs | | `evaluate` without `script` (`expression`, `code`) | 81 | 55 | 3 | 1 | 140 | Aliases accepted | | `[browser.disconnected]`, no desktop attached | 38 | 27 | 2 | 13 | 80 | Message names the next step (still an error) | | Page JavaScript threw | 16 | 52 | - | 12 | 80 | Top-level `return` and `await` now run; other script errors unchanged | | Caught by the script, message not stored | 8 | 64 | - | - | 72 | Code Mode stores `toolCalls[].error` | | Invalid browser URL (file path, `file:`) | 3 | 55 | - | - | 58 | Still refused; names the value and points to `preview` | | `click` `UnknownVizError` | 7 | 31 | - | 5 | 43 | Fixed (no forced `capturePage`) | | `tab_unavailable` | 5 | 16 | - | 1 | 22 | Lists the open tab IDs | | `wait` condition not met | 9 | 8 | - | - | 17 | Returns `met: false` | | `evaluate`, `tabs.open`, `preview` 60 s timeouts | 11 | 9 | 2 | 4 | 26 | Not addressed | - Estimate, not measured after the change: about 2,150 `wait` and 141 `evaluate` errors become successful calls, and about 160 more become one precise message. - Without the `wait` group, every device was at 6.8 to 9.1%. ### Community issues - **Sign-ins lost:** Fixes #60313, Fixes #55920. Addresses #53580 (imports all cookies of a browser; no per-site selection). - **User agent:** Fixes #55730. - **Permissions:** Fixes #54044, Fixes #53294, Fixes #56869, Fixes #61238, Fixes #61609. - **Agent tools:** Addresses #50781 (hidden-tab screenshot; macOS minimized or hidden windows still cannot be captured), #52407 (screenshot waits for a pending navigation and a fresh frame), #61625 (missing `preview` file now fails), #55795 (new no-desktop wording; tools still listed). - **Extensions:** Addresses #52419 (Bitwarden and 1Password load; autofill not verified). - **Network:** Addresses #62234 and #59722 for servers on the same machine, which no longer use the tunnel. - **Related, closed:** #50382, #63372, #62499, #62989, #52680, #59798. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR click["plain click on an http(s) link"] --> links["Links.open"] links -->|"browser LinkHandler"| tab["pane tab"] links -->|"modifier key or no handler"| system["system browser"] tab --> local{"server on this machine?"} local -->|yes| profile["persist:opencode-browser
cookies, site data, extensions"] local -->|no| remote["per-attachment partition
server tunnel"] remote <-->|"cookie mirror, both ways"| profile profile --> ext["extensions
Electron APIs + profile/extension-api"] ext --> popup["popup over the pane"] agent["agent browser.* call"] --> refuse["refuse: configured deny"] refuse --> lookup["tab and connection lookup"] lookup --> authorize["authorize: permission.assert
ask, tool.use policy, Allow always"] authorize --> gate{"extension page?"} gate -->|yes| refused["refused"] gate -->|no| tab ``` ## Profile and sign-in import - **One profile:** `PARTITION = "persist:opencode-browser"` in `packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/profile/index.ts`. Servers on this machine browse in it directly. - **Remote servers:** keep their own partition, because Chromium sets the proxy per partition. `link()` copies every profile cookie into it and mirrors changes both ways. Site storage and extensions stay with the profile. - **User agent:** the profile drops the `Electron/…` and app tokens, which sign-in pages such as Google's refuse. - **Import sources** (`profile/sources.ts`, `chromium.ts`, `firefox.ts`, `safari.ts`, `cookie.ts`): | Family | Browsers | Key | | --- | --- | --- | | Chromium | Chrome, Edge, Helium, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera, Chromium, Dia, Comet | DPAPI (Windows), Keychain (macOS), libsecret (Linux) | | Firefox | Firefox, Zen, LibreWolf, Floorp | none (`cookies.sqlite`) | | Safari | Safari | none (`Cookies.binarycookies`, needs Full Disk Access) | | Files | Netscape `cookies.txt`, Chrome-API JSON, Playwright storage state | n/a | - **Offer in the pane:** `import-prompt.tsx` shows a bar (a card on the new tab page) for the most recently used browser until the user imports or clicks "Not now". Settings › Browser is rebuilt around sign-ins, extensions and site data (`settings.tsx`). - **Chrome and Edge on Windows:** most cookies use app-bound `v20` keys that only the browser can unwrap. The import counts them and says to export with a cookie extension instead. A locked `Cookies` database (browser still running) is named too. - **macOS Keychain:** the Chromium key is read with `/usr/bin/security`, so macOS names "security" in the prompt. While it is open, the app says what it asks and to choose Allow, not Always Allow. - **Cannot save sign-ins:** at start, `cookiesPersist` writes one probe cookie (`cookie-check.opencode.invalid`), flushes and counts it in a copy of the `Cookies` database. If it is missing (Keychain key denied), Settings and the offer show a warning and imports are off. Extensions cannot see the probe cookie. - **macOS icons:** browser icons come from the Quick Look thumbnail of the resolved bundle path. ## Links - `createWebLinks` (`packages/app/src/runtime/plugin/render.tsx`) offers a plain left click on an `http(s)` link inside `[data-pane-row]` to `Links.open`. Modifier clicks, `download` links and links in dialogs keep the default. - The browser plugin's `LinkHandler` (`browser/renderer.tsx`, priority 5) takes it when the pane is available for that session and the setting is on. The file plugin no longer claims web links. - Terminal Ctrl+click on a URL goes through the same path (`terminal/terminal.tsx`). - Settings › Browser › "Open links in the browser pane" turns it off. ## Extensions - **Install:** a Chrome Web Store or Edge Add-ons link (CRX3, developer key pinned so the store ID is kept), a copy from a Chromium profile, or an unpacked folder. Loaded with `allowFileAccess: false`. - **Verdict:** `profile/compatibility.ts` reads the manifest and returns `supported`, `partial` (with the features that may not work) or `unsupported`. Unsupported only when a background needs an API with events nothing stands in for (`readingList`, `tabGroups`, `gcm`, `declarativeContent`, `debugger`, `ttsEngine`). An unsupported one needs "Add anyway". - **Results in a Windows dev build:** | Extension | Verdict | Background | Popup | Main feature | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | JSON Formatter 0.10.2 | supported | none declared | options page only | yes | | Dark Reader 4.9.135 | partial | starts | yes, shows the current tab | yes | | React DevTools 8.0.0 | partial | starts | yes | hook only; no DevTools panel in the pane | | Vimium 2.4.2 | partial, names its page features | starts | yes | no: content scripts lack `chrome.storage.sync` | | Bitwarden 2026.10.2 | partial | starts | yes, sign-in screen | vault and autofill not tried | | 1Password 8.12.44.33 | partial | starts | opens its welcome page as a tab | desktop app link refused (native messaging) | | uBlock Origin Lite 2026.1110 | partial | starts | yes | blocks (`ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`) | | uBlock Origin 2026.1108 (MV2) | supported | starts | yes, blocked count | blocks; badge in the menu | - **Popups:** `extension-api/popup.ts` anchors a view under the extensions button, sized from `preferred-size-changed` within 25x25 to 800x600. It closes on blur, Escape, and window blur, move or resize. - **API modules** (`profile/extension-api/`): a preload registered for frames and service workers defines the namespaces only in `chrome-extension://` documents. Main answers only the extension's own pages and worker, and only for namespaces its manifest has permission for. | Status | APIs | | --- | --- | | Real | `tabs`, `windows` (`remove` refuses), `action` / `browserAction` / `pageAction`, popup surface, `webNavigation`, `contextMenus` (in the tab's right-click menu), `cookies` (host permissions only), `notifications`, `storage.sync` (this device only, pages and workers) | | Partial | `permissions` (answers from the manifest; `request` grants nothing optional), `commands` (`getAll` only, no shortcuts) | | No-op | `sidePanel`, `identity`, `history`, `bookmarks`, `sessions`, `downloads`, `search`, `fontSettings`, `privacy.*` (`stubs.ts`) | | Electron's own | `storage.local/session`, `runtime`, `scripting`, `alarms`, `idle`, `offscreen`, `declarativeNetRequest`, MV2 `webRequest` | | Unsupported | `nativeMessaging`, DevTools panels, `storage.sync` in content scripts, MV3 worker `webRequest` listeners, `userScripts`, `tabGroups` | - **`file:` guard and request blocking:** any `session.webRequest` listener makes Electron skip the extensions' request proxy, so blockers saw nothing. `protocol.handle("file")` does not work either: with an extension listening it never runs and outside files load. `profile/file-guard.ts` and `file-guard-machine.ts` now register the listener only while a `file:` document can load something: ```ts // on: did-start-navigation to a file: URL, in any frame of any web contents in the partition // stay: while that page loads, and while any frame lives in a process that committed a file: document // off: only after did-stop-loading shows no such frame, or the page is destroyed; unknown states stay on ``` - It fails closed: a `file:` document's loaders are created after its navigation starts, and the listener stays until no frame can use them. - Cost: while a `file:` page is open, extensions do not block requests on other pages. ## Agent browser tools Server side in `packages/plugin-browser/src/{rpc,tools,files,machine,skill}.ts`. No wire or protocol change: an older desktop works with this server. | Call shape | Calls in the data | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `wait {tabID, text, timeout}` | 1,449 | `condition: Missing key` | Text wait, timeout capped at 30 s | | `wait {tabID, text, state: "visible"}` | 344 | same | Text wait (`hidden` gives `textGone`) | | `wait {tabID, selector, timeout}` | 24 | same | Polls until a match is visible | | `wait {tabID, timeout}` | 21 | same | Pause, capped at 30 s | | `wait {tabID, time}` / `{ms}` | 36 | same | Pause (`time` up to 60 counts as seconds) | | `wait {condition: "text"}` that timed out | 17 | Throws | `met: false` with `observed` | | `evaluate {tabID, expression}` / `{code}` | 141 | `script: Missing key` | Runs | | `evaluate` with top-level `return` / `await` | 8+ | Page `SyntaxError` | Runs as an async function body | | `find {tabID, query}` | 17 | `text: Missing key` | `query: Not a parameter of browser.find. Valid parameters: tabID, frameID, text.` | | `preview` of a missing path | unknown | Success | `browser.preview found no file at ` | | `preview` with no desktop | 37 | "Repeating … will not help" | Names the absolute path to give the user | ```js await tools.browser.wait({ tabID, text: "Saved", timeout: 5000 }) // before: Invalid arguments: - condition: Missing key // after: { ...tab, met: false, waited: "text", elapsedMs, observed: 'Text "Saved" did not appear within 5000 ms.' } ``` - **Unknown parameters:** each input is `StructWithRest(Struct(fields), [Record(not a field, always fails)])`. The JSON Schema drops `additionalProperties: false`, so core's input repair no longer deletes the guessed key before validation. - **Descriptions** on optional parameters now reach the model's JSON Schema (they were on the type side only). - **Code Mode:** `packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts` stores a failed inner call's message as `toolCalls[].error` (up to 2,000 characters), also when the script catches it. - **Hidden tabs** (`gui-plugins/src/browser/chromium.ts`, `capture.ts`, `page-machine.ts`): - `did-navigate` reapplies `setBackgroundThrottling(false)`, so a renderer that starts hidden still paints. - Viewport and element screenshots use `capturePage(rect, { stayHidden: true })` after any pending navigation and a fresh frame, under one 2.5 s deadline. - `click`, `hover` and `drag` wait for a double rAF instead of a forced `capturePage`. - `fullPage` keeps the CDP path and fails with a clear message when the tab is not on screen. - On macOS, `undrawable()` fails a screenshot at once when the window is minimized or the app is hidden. | State | Windows before | Windows after | macOS after | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pane open, tab in front | ok / ok | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Another tab in front | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Pane closed | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Tab opened with `focus: false` | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Another session in front | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Window covered by another window | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | ok / ok | | Window on another Space | n/a | n/a | ok / ok | | Window minimized | refused / `UnknownVizError` | ok / ok | "minimized" error in 1-3 ms / ok | | App hidden (Cmd+H) | n/a | n/a | "hidden" error in 1-3 ms / ok | Cells are screenshot / click. Hover matches click after the change. Captures were checked as current after a click, a timer and a redirect; macOS captures are at 2x. ## Permissions The attach grant is a session rule (`browser:* allow`) that core evaluates after every agent rule. It still exists; the plugin now decides from the rules the user configured. ```ts // packages/plugin-browser/src/tools.ts, execute yield* connection.refuse(tool, input.type) // configured deny only; before any file, tab or connection check // ...tab and connection lookup... yield* connection.authorize(tool, action.type) // permission.assert({ resources: [operation], save: [operation] }) ``` - **Deny and ask per operation:** a `permission.evaluate` hook (`connection.ts`) selects the rule for the operation from config, the agent definition and the session's own non-grant rules, with core's last-match semantics (`selectBrowserRule` in `machine.ts`). Deny gives `[browser.denied]`; ask gives the normal prompt. A read failure fails closed. - **`tool.use` policies** on `browser` now run, because every call goes through `permission.assert`. - **"Allow always":** calls pass `save: [operation]`. `packages/core/src/permission.ts` lets a saved approval answer an `ask` that a hook raised; denies are evaluated first and never overridden. - **Subagents:** a session `prompt` hook removes the inherited grant from a child with no attachment of its own, before its first prompt is admitted. - **Stale grants:** each grant is recorded in plugin storage with host, pid and location. At startup, before the RPC registers, `reconcileStaleGrants` revokes grants whose process is gone on this host. Another host's or a live process's grants stay. Builds on #61639 by @feiiiiii5. - **Extension pages:** `BrowserPage.execute` requires `origin: "agent" | "user"`. For agent calls, `agentRefusal` (`policy.ts`) refuses navigation to extension URLs and everything except navigate, back, forward and stop on an extension document. Extension frames are dropped from frames, snapshots and contexts, and a call that names an extension frame's `frameID` is refused. Screenshots still show their pixels. ## Cookie encryption ```ts // packages/desktop/electron-builder.config.ts, getBase() electronFuses: { enableCookieEncryption: true, resetAdHocDarwinSignature: true }, ``` - Keys: Keychain (macOS), DPAPI (Windows), libsecret or kwallet (Linux). Dev runs use the stock Electron binary and stay unencrypted. - `resetAdHocDarwinSignature` re-signs unsigned macOS builds after the flip, or Apple Silicon refuses to launch them. Signed builds are signed after the fuses anyway. - **One-way:** turning the fuse off, or a downgrade, cannot read encrypted cookies; users are signed out of sites. The app does not crash. - Existing cookies are encrypted when next written. Imported cookies are encrypted from their first write. - **Linux without a keyring:** Chromium falls back to a fixed key, which only obfuscates. A changed keyring signs users out. ## Notes for review - **Verified:** Windows dev build (profile, import, extensions and popups, ad blocking, the `file:` guard with extensions installed, the tool-call shapes, hidden tabs, deny / ask / Allow always, and the extension-page refusal, all over the real tool path). macOS dev and packed beta build on Apple Silicon (hidden tabs, links, import offer, Safari import, JSON Formatter, verdicts, fuse Enabled, "cannot save sign-ins"). Linux not tested. - **Not verified:** - The Chromium import "Allow" path on macOS (only Deny was clicked). - Encrypted cookie rows (`v10`) on macOS, and in the `persist:` partition on any OS. - Bitwarden and 1Password with a signed-in account; `chrome.cookies` with a real extension; context menus with a real right-click. - Extensions, popups and the API modules on macOS and Linux. - **Behaviour changes users will notice:** - A configured `ask` (including `"*": "ask"`) now prompts for browser calls while a desktop is attached. - `wait` returns `met: false` instead of throwing; scripts that used the throw as "not found" now continue. - Unknown tool parameters are rejected with the valid list. - Every browser tool's model-facing schema changes: one prompt-cache miss. - Web links open in the pane by default. Settings › Browser › "Open links in the browser pane" turns this off. - **Core change:** a saved "always" approval now answers a plugin hook's `ask` for every action, not only browser. - **Still listed:** a denied agent still sees the browser tools and skill while attached; every call is refused before anything reaches the desktop. Forks copy the grant. Grants written before this change have no ledger record and are not swept. - **Hidden agent tabs keep rendering** at the display rate. CPU and GPU cost of many hidden tabs is not measured. - **Keychain prompt names "security":** "Always Allow" would let any process read that browser's key, so the copy warns against it. The proper fix is an N-API addon calling `SecItemCopyMatching`, with signing and the `RunAsNode` fuse off. - **Remote servers receive the profile's cookies**, and their pages can write cookies back into the profile. - **#59477** (browser tools over client MCP, draft) deletes `packages/plugin-browser`. It would move the `wait`, `evaluate` and schema work and drop the grant, subagent and ledger fixes. - **No feature flag:** GUI plugins cannot read server flags, the fuse is a one-way build setting, and the server changes are fixes. ## Follow-ups - Per-session tool availability in core instead of a stored grant: hides tools from denied agents, covers forks. - Native Keychain read so the prompt names OpenCode. - Full-page screenshots of hidden tabs (scroll and stitch). - Per-site cookie import and clearing imported data (#53580). - Hide the browser tools, or report `connected: false`, when no desktop is attached (#55795). - Extension gaps: `storage.sync` in content scripts, native messaging, DevTools panels. - The first prompt after a fresh start does not see the browser tools: the Code Mode catalog is built before the plugin is active. - `packages/desktop/script/pack.ts` writes `app-update.yml` after signing, which breaks the local bundle seal. --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Fixes #53580 Related: #52419 Public API: adds experimental.approved to the permission.evaluate hook event and Wildcard.match to @opencode/schema; browser tools honour configured browser rules and reject unknown parameters; codemode toolCalls gain optional error

prs.title: fix(core): surface rejected config files instead of ignoring them
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54786

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A malformed or schema-invalid `opencode.json(c)` was only written to the server log and then dropped, so `opencode models` (and the other server-backed commands) ran with defaults without ever telling the user their config was ignored.

The config loader now keeps the rejected file as a `Config.Rejected` entry in the `/api/config` output, and the CLI reports rejected files on stderr when it resolves a local server:

```
Warning: Config file at /home/me/.config/opencode/opencode.json was ignored: CloseBraceExpected at line 1, column 2
```

The file is still skipped, so a broken config cannot take the server down; this change only makes the rejection visible. `opencode debug config` also shows rejected entries because it dumps `/api/config`.

When the final whole-document validation rejects a normalized config, the reason now names the failing field (`configuration is not valid: <path>`) instead of a generic message.

### Follow-ups

Two related surfaces are intentionally left for follow-up PRs:

- **TUI notice**: #54786 also asks for the TUI to report a rejected config. A stderr warning is invisible once the TUI owns the terminal, so that needs an in-app notice (for example a startup banner) and stays out of this PR.
- **Non-file sources**: rejections from well-known (remote) config and `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` are still dropped without a message. Surfacing them needs an optional `path` or a separate display-source field on the published `Config.Rejected` entry, which is better decided on its own.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: full suite matches `dev` before/after this change (identical pass/fail set, including the existing tests that lock config loading behavior).
- `packages/core`: new `test/config/reject.test.ts` covers the final-decode reason (failing field, generic fallback) and a valid document; the decode uses `SchemaParser.decodeUnknownResult` so the reason can later share #50832's formatter.
- `packages/server`: full suite 78 pass / 0 fail, including a new `/api/config` contract test asserting the rejected entry carries the file path and reason.
- `packages/cli`: new `server-connection` test asserts the stderr warning; `debug-config` tests still pass.
- Manual end-to-end on a source checkout: with `{"` in the global config, `opencode models --standalone` prints the warning above and still lists models; with a valid config it stays silent.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(tui): keep session tab busy while background shell runs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62505

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A session tab showed no spinner while a background shell in that session was still running, even though the shell row in the transcript kept spinning.

`SessionTabsProvider.status().busy` only looked at the session's `active` state and its non-synthetic pending items. It never looked at `data.shell`, so once the turn went idle after a shell was backgrounded, the tab indicator took the non-`runs()` path and showed nothing. `ShellDisplay` kept spinning because it checks `data.shell.get(id)` directly.

The fix adds the running shells of the session family to the busy check:

```ts
data.shell.listBySession(id).some((shell) => shell.status === "running")
```

Shell entries are removed from the store on `shell.exited` / `shell.deleted`, so `listBySession` reflects only the shells that are still running. The same `status()` feeds `createProgramStatus`, so the terminal title / program status is corrected by the same change.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `running background shell keeps its tab busy` in `packages/tui/test/context/session-tabs.test.ts`: it emits `shell.created` with `status: "running"` for a background tab and asserts `busy` flips to true, then emits `shell.deleted` and asserts it flips back.
- `bun test test/context/session-tabs.test.ts -t "running background shell"` → 1 pass, 0 fail.
- `tsc -b packages/tui` → clean.

prs.title: fix(core): tag subagent reports with pending background work as running
prs.body:
When a subagent goes idle while its own background work (a shell, an image, a nested subagent) is still going, the parent gets a report with a "Background work still running" list, and another report once that work wakes the child. The first report was tagged `state="completed"`, so models often read it as the final answer or decided the child had quit early and nudged it. This tags that report `state="running"` instead.

```diff
- <subagent sessionID="ses_A" state="completed" description="Run test suite">
+ <subagent sessionID="ses_A" state="running" description="Run test suite">
  I started the full test suite in the background; I'll report back when it finishes.

  Background work still running:
  - shell (sh_7): bun test
  </subagent>
```

Only the model-facing tag changes. The job row and the message metadata still say `completed`, so job bookkeeping and the TUI/app cards behave as before. Error and cancelled reports keep their state even with the list, and a report without the list is unchanged.

The outbox row only stores the formatted body, so `deliver` picks the label from the still-running list in the body. That keeps restart replay labelling the same way without storing anything new. A child answer that itself contains the exact `\n\nBackground work still running:\n` header would be labelled running too; I don't think that's worth a stored flag.

**Why `running`:** I replayed the parent's real request at that first report against 7 models with 5 labels, 10 trials per model, label and scenario (1,400 total, graded by rules plus a fixed-rubric judge).

| first report label | good next turn, weaker models (n=180) |
| --- | --- |
| `completed` (before) | 43% |
| **`running`** | **86%** |
| `waiting` | 71% |
| `completed` + "It will report again when this finishes." | 68% |
| `waiting` + that line | 80% |

Weaker models were GLM 5.3, DeepSeek v4.1 flash, MiniMax M3, Kimi K3, Qwen 3.6 Plus and Haiku 5.5; Opus 5.5 did well under every label. Unprompted follow-ups to the child dropped from 34 trials to 3, and no reply confused `running` with the launch result. It's a replay of the next turn only, so later turns weren't tested.

Checked: `subagent-completion`, `subagent-report`, `subagent-idle-e2e`, `tool-subagent`, `session-execution`, `job` and `session-background` tests (118 pass), `bun typecheck` in packages/core, `bun run check`.
