prs.title: feat(core): add agent instructions and use them for Plan mode
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62628. That loop came from Plan re-adding its reminder as a synthetic after each compaction, which woke the session again. This PR removes that code path, and after compaction the rules sit in the system prompt with no new message. The review bot ran the issue's mock-model repro with a 3,000-token context limit: on `dev` it never exits (1,873 requests in 40s), and with this PR it exits after 3 requests (title, one compaction, the answer).

Related: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62554 (this removes the one-off Plan reminder it lists; the other one-off prompts are unchanged).

Stacked on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63667 (its commit is the first one here); the revert case below depends on it.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Agents get an `instructions` field: text that's added to the default prompt while the agent is selected, without replacing the prompt like `system` does. Plan mode now uses it in place of its own reminder machinery.

Today a plugin can't add rules for one agent without trouble. Plan injects "you are in Plan mode" reminders as synthetic messages and repairs them on every request after compaction or a revert (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/42652). The internal orchestrator agent adds its rules to the system prompt in a context hook, so every agent switch rewrites the start of the prompt and loses the cache, and the rules aren't stored with the session.

Core already has the right mechanism: instruction sources, which are stored per session, shown once in the system prompt, and sent as an update at the next step when they change. This adds one source, `core/agent`, built from the selected agent:

```text
agent has instructions → value { id, name, text }
agent has none         → removed

first step             → text in the system prompt
switch in              → text as an update before the next prompt
switch away            → "The Plan agent is no longer selected. Its
                          instructions from earlier in this conversation
                          no longer apply."
switch between two     → one update: leave note + new agent's text
plugin edits the text  → "...instructions changed. These replace..."
```

Compaction, reverts, forks and storage all come from the existing instruction state. The source is last in the list because it changes most often.

`plan.ts` now sets `instructions` and drops the event subscription, the per-request repair hook and the reminder bookkeeping (about 60 lines). Its permissions and the error rewrite for blocked edits stay.

What changes for Plan, beyond the plumbing:

- The leave text is now the generic one above instead of "You are NO LONGER in Plan mode...". The enter text is the same, without the `<system-reminder>` wrapper, since it's now system content.
- The rules arrive as a system message (or in the system prompt), not as a user-role synthetic. In the timeline that shows as the standard "Instructions updated: core/agent" row.
- Switching away and back before the next step now sends nothing. Plan used to send both reminders.
- Sessions that are already in Plan when this ships still have the old reminder in history and get the rules once more as an update. That happens once per session.

The field is plugin-only for now. Agent config files have their own schema, and config already uses `instructions` for a list of file paths, so exposing this there needs a naming decision first.

### How did you verify your code works?

New runner scenarios under `agent instructions` in `session-runner.test.ts` use real agents and `switchAgent`: starting in an agent, switching in, switching to an agent without instructions, switching away and back, switching between two agents, a plugin editing the text, compaction, reverting past the switch in, and reverting between switching in and out. All pass, and the system prompt stays byte-identical across switches.

- `bun run check` from the root.
- Ran every core test file that touches history, compaction, forks, reverts, instructions, agents or Plan (179 files): 3,141 pass. The 33 failures are in shell, integration, provider and image test files and fail the same way on unchanged `dev` on my machine.
- Regenerated the client (`AgentInfo.instructions`).

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change; the timeline row is the existing instruction notice.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): seed missing event sequence from stored events and session messages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62523

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A session whose `event_sequence` counter row was missing started at seq `0`, while `session_message` already held seqs up to e.g. 318. The projector's `INSERT` then failed `UNIQUE(session_id, seq)` on every turn — permanently, because the low counter row is what the next insert reads.

`packages/core/src/bus.ts` treated a missing counter as `-1`, so the next durable event took seq `0`. The fix adds `persistedMax()`, which takes the maximum of the counter **and** the rows that are actually stored (`max(event.seq)`, and for sessions `max(session_message.seq)`), and uses `max(counter, persistedMax)` in `commitDurableEvent`, `publishAll` and `latestSequence`.

A missing or stale counter now resumes above the rows that exist, and the next write persists the healed counter through the existing upsert, so the session repairs itself. This also covers V1-migrated sessions whose events were deleted while their messages remained.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test in `session-projector.test.ts`: it seeds projected messages with no counter row and then delivers an inbox message. Before the fix this reproduced the `UNIQUE constraint failed` error from the issue; after it the message lands at seq `3` and the counter heals to `3`.
- `tsc -b packages/core` → clean.
- bus tests 64/64, projector tests 46/46 (including the new one), v1-migration + session-title + state-replay 60/60.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

prs.title: fix(util): convert synchronous spawn failure (ENOEXEC) to typed PlatformError
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62516

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

On macOS, `opencode upgrade` / `uninstall` crashed with `ENOEXEC: unknown error, posix_spawn '<prefix>/bin/pnpm'` when a package manager on `PATH` had no shebang.

`child_process.spawn` throws `ENOEXEC` **synchronously** for such a file, while a missing executable emits an asynchronous `error` event. `launchProcess` only handled the event, so the throw escaped as an Effect defect and `method()`'s `orElseSucceed` probe recovery never saw it — the upgrade aborted instead of trying the next package manager.

The fix wraps the `launch(...)` call in a `try`/`catch` and resumes as a typed `PlatformError`, the same handling the asynchronous `error` event gets and the same approach as #58722. A shebang-less `pnpm`/`yarn` is then treated as "not this one" and the detection continues.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/util/tsconfig.json` → clean.
- `bun --cwd packages/cli test test/updater-install.test.ts -t "method detection"` → 7 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.
- `bun --cwd packages/util test src/path.test.ts src/process-signal.test.ts` → 36 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(plugin): export Tool from the Effect plugin entry
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62367

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

`@opencode/plugin/effect` re-exports every schema (`Provider`, `Rpc`, `Skill`, `Vcs`, …) except `Tool`. An Effect plugin that wants to refuse a tool call with `Tool.Error` has to import from `@opencode/schema/tool` — which is not a declared dependency of a plugin — or define its own copy of the class, which the host does not recognise.

This adds the missing export:

```ts
export { Tool } from "@opencode/schema/tool"
```

so a plugin can write:

```ts
import { Tool } from "@opencode/plugin/effect"

ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", (event) =>
  event.tool === "shell" && blocked(event.input) ? Effect.fail(new Tool.Error({ message: "blocked" })) : Effect.void)
```

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `packages/plugin/test/effect-exports.test.ts` asserts `Tool.Error` is the same class the host uses (`Tool.Error === SchemaTool.Error`) and that `new Tool.Error({ message: "refused" })._tag === "Tool.Error"`.

- `bun test test/host.test.ts test/gui-host.test.ts test/gui-vite.test.ts test/gui-scope.test.ts` → 37 pass, 0 fail.
- `tsc -b packages/plugin` → clean.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep session tab busy while background shell runs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62505

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A session tab showed no spinner while a background shell in that session was still running, even though the shell row in the transcript kept spinning.

`SessionTabsProvider.status().busy` only looked at the session's `active` state and its non-synthetic pending items. It never looked at `data.shell`, so once the turn went idle after a shell was backgrounded, the tab indicator took the non-`runs()` path and showed nothing. `ShellDisplay` kept spinning because it checks `data.shell.get(id)` directly.

The fix adds the running shells of the session family to the busy check:

```ts
data.shell.listBySession(id).some((shell) => shell.status === "running")
```

Shell entries are removed from the store on `shell.exited` / `shell.deleted`, so `listBySession` reflects only the shells that are still running. The same `status()` feeds `createProgramStatus`, so the terminal title / program status is corrected by the same change.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test `running background shell keeps its tab busy` in `packages/tui/test/context/session-tabs.test.ts`: it emits `shell.created` with `status: "running"` for a background tab and asserts `busy` flips to true, then emits `shell.deleted` and asserts it flips back.
- `bun test test/context/session-tabs.test.ts -t "running background shell"` → 1 pass, 0 fail.
- `tsc -b packages/tui` → clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change in the visual sense; the tab strip animation is the visible effect.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(merman): parse inline edge labels written without spaces
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #63670

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Mermaid allows an inline edge label without spaces (`A--yes-->B`, `A==done==>B`). merman's edge regex required whitespace around the label for `--` and `==` links, though dotted links (`A-.yes.->B`) already worked without it. As a result, `A--yes-->B` was read as a node named `A--yes` (the ID pattern allows `--`), and with shaped nodes or `==` links the block failed as unsupported syntax.

The whitespace around the label is now optional. Two lookarounds keep the label form from starting inside another operator: the opening `--`/`==`/`-.` may not follow `-`, `=`, `.` or `<`, and may not be followed by `-`, `.`, `=` or `>`. So `-->`, `---`, `<-->`, `==>` and `-.->` still parse as before.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added "parses inline edge labels written without spaces" to `packages/merman/src/flowchart/flowchart.test.ts`. It fails on `dev` (`Unsupported syntax ... "B==done==>C[Done]"`, and `A--yes-->B` produces node `A--yes`) and passes with the fix.
- `bun run test` in `packages/merman`: 508 pass. The layout audit test times out at 40 s on my machine when it is loaded. Its summary is identical with and without the change, and a rerun with the change passed in 31 s.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/merman`: no errors. oxlint on the two files: clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

`renderFlowchartDiagram` output for `flowchart LR` / `A--yes-->B`, before and after:

```
before                          after
╭────────╮    ╭───╮             ╭───╮            ╭───╮
│ A--yes ├───▶│ B │             │ A ├─── yes ───▶│ B │
╰────────╯    ╰───╯             ╰───╯            ╰───╯
```

`A[Start]--yes-->B[End]` failed with "Unsupported syntax" before and now renders `Start ─── yes ───▶ End`.

prs.title: feat(plugin): add experimental model HTTP hooks
prs.body:
### Problem

Plugin HTTP hooks only run for Session requests. `generate` text, image and decision calls send provider requests that no hook can see or change (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62096). Anything that has to touch every model request, like the provider client certificates in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61832, has no single place to do it.

### Change

Adds `ctx.model.hook("experimental.http.request" | "experimental.http.response", ...)`. It runs for every HTTP request to a model provider, whichever Session or API makes it.

```text
who calls             kind                                     session
Session step       →  primary / compaction / title / generate  { id, agent }
generate.text      →  text                                     undefined   NEW
generate.image     →  image                                    undefined   NEW
generate.decision  →  decision                                 undefined   NEW
```

```ts
type ModelRequestScope = { model } & (
  | { kind: "primary" | "compaction" | "title" | "generate"; session: { id, agent } }
  | { kind: "text" | "image" | "decision"; session?: undefined }
)
// experimental.http.request:  ModelRequestScope & { request }
// experimental.http.response: ModelRequestScope & { request, response }
```

`session` is set for a Session's own model requests, so checking it narrows `kind`. A tool that calls Generate from inside a Session (like the built-in image tool) makes a Generate call with no `session`.

The session `http.request` / `http.response` hooks are unchanged and still only see Session requests. The docs recommend the model hooks. For a Session request, both run in one middleware, with the model hooks outside:

```text
model request hook → session request hook → send → session response hook → model response hook
```

How it's wired:

- `core/src/model-http.ts` builds the per-call middleware. It's moved out of `session/model-request.ts`, which now calls it.
- `Generate.text` passes it as `http` on `llm.generate`, the same option Sessions use.
- `Generate.image` and `Generate.decisions` pass it per call too. In `packages/ai`, the image/media and decision clients take an optional `{ http }` on each call, like `llm.generate` already does (new `RequestExecutor.withHttp`, which `RequestExecutor.middleware` now also uses). Downloading URL images afterwards still uses the plain executor, so those downloads aren't hooked.
- `PluginHooks` only gains the `model` domain.

`generate` calls through the HTTP API run in the global config location, so only globally configured plugins see them. That's noted in the docs.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif" font-size="9">
  <style>
    .dot{animation:go 2.4s linear infinite}
    .d2{animation-delay:.8s}.d3{animation-delay:1.6s}
    .ring{animation:pulse 2.4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes go{0%{transform:translateX(0);opacity:0}10%{opacity:1}90%{opacity:1}100%{transform:translateX(150px);opacity:0}}
    @keyframes pulse{0%,100%{opacity:.35}50%{opacity:1}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.dot,.ring{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <g stroke="none" fill="currentColor">
    <text x="4" y="18" opacity=".8">session</text>
    <text x="4" y="40" opacity=".8">text</text>
    <text x="4" y="62" opacity=".8">image</text>
    <text x="196" y="40" opacity=".8">provider</text>
  </g>
  <path d="M42 15H120M42 37H120M42 59H120" opacity=".3"/>
  <path d="M120 15Q130 37 140 37M120 59Q130 37 140 37M120 37H140" opacity=".3"/>
  <rect class="ring" x="140" y="27" width="30" height="20" rx="5"/>
  <text x="146" y="40" stroke="none" fill="currentColor">hook</text>
  <path d="M170 37H192" opacity=".5"/>
  <g stroke="none" fill="currentColor">
    <circle class="dot" cx="42" cy="15" r="2.5"/>
    <circle class="dot d2" cx="42" cy="37" r="2.5"/>
    <circle class="dot d3" cx="42" cy="59" r="2.5"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```

No feature flag: the new hooks are opt-in and named `experimental.*`, and the session hooks run for the same requests as before.

### Built-in provider plugins

Azure (Entra tokens), GitHub Copilot (auth and request metadata headers), Snowflake Cortex (env token, "conversation complete" handling) and OpenCode (the Console 401/403 explanation) now register model HTTP hooks instead of session ones. Before, their hooks skipped `generate` calls, so for example an Azure Entra model used through `generate.text` or the image tool was sent without its token.

### Out of scope

- Model-level WebSocket hooks. The session `experimental.ws.*` hooks are unchanged.
- `model.request` (baseURL and headers) and the `context` / `compaction` / `generate` hook split.

### Verification

- `bun run check`: passes.
- `packages/core`: new test in `generate.test.ts` with the real hook registry: `Generate.image` (a URL-image model) and `Generate.decisions` each run one request and one response hook with the right `kind`, the provider requests carry the hook's header, and the image download doesn't. Another new test in `session-model-request-hooks.test.ts` registers a model hook and a session hook. A `text` call runs only the model hook, a `primary` call runs both, and the session hook sees the model hook's header. A third test triggers the Azure hook with no Session and checks the Entra token is still applied (it fails before this change). The generate, session-hook, native-compaction, warming and provider plugin tests pass. Some plugin tests (Copilot classification, Cloudflare, ChatGPT, Claude agent) fail locally on `dev` as well.
- Ran `opencode serve` with a globally configured probe plugin that logs both hook types and adds an `x-probe` header:
  - `generate/text` (openai/gpt-5.4-nano): the model hooks fired with `kind: text` and no session, and the provider got the replaced request. `generate/image` (openai/gpt-image-2) and `generate/decisions` (opencode/jev-1.13-free) were checked the same way on the first commit, before the `session` field change.
  - A Session prompt on anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5: `primary` and `title` ran the model and session hooks with the session ID set.



---

_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Related: #62096

Public API: adds experimental `ctx.model.hook("experimental.http.request" | "experimental.http.response")` and optional per-call `http` middleware on the @opencode/ai image and decision clients (backwards compatible)

prs.title: feat(core): opt-in sqlite full-text index of session history
prs.body:
Adds an opt-in SQLite FTS5 index of session history that SQLite keeps current itself, plus a one-time background build over existing history and an experimental status endpoint for its progress. Off by default: set `experimental.sqlite_fts: true`. Nothing searches the index yet; search results with excerpts and cursors, and tools, come in follow-ups.

### Problem

Agents can't search past sessions. Scanning history without an index takes minutes per search on a large database (~2.5 min on a 37.5 GB one), so search needs an index that stays current without app code having to remember to update it on every write path.

### Change

```text
experimental.sqlite_fts: true in a loaded location
  (the server forks SessionSearchBuild.run like Schedule.run; an internal config plugin signals it while
   that location's config has the flag on, so global config turns it on everywhere; no polling)
  ─► ensure (once): pick a layout for this SQLite, create the FTS5 table, the source view and triggers
       SQLite 3.43+ ─► compact: contentless, contentless_delete      (~115 MB on a 37.5 GB DB)
       older        ─► text: FTS5 over session_search_document text   (~300 MB) e.g. macOS 13, 14.0–14.1
       no FTS5 / JSON functions ─► unsupported, nothing created
  ─► one-time build in the background (never blocks readiness), like the V1 import:
       newest first, ≤ 50 messages and ≤ 1 MiB stored bytes per transaction, cursor in kv,
       resumes after restart, skips rows that fail alone, records done/failed, never reruns once done
  ─► afterwards SQLite maintains it: source triggers queue the changed ID, the queue's trigger
       reindexes it from the session_search_source view and deletes the queue row
off (or the location unloads) ─► the build pauses between transactions; an existing index and its triggers stay and keep maintaining themselves
startup (a check search-index registers with the Database layer, run after migrations, before any write) ─► if search triggers exist but this
  SQLite can't run them (e.g. a compact DB opened on SQLite < 3.43), drop them so writes keep working
```

Indexed: session titles, user text, finished assistant text (part rows, then inline), completed compaction summaries, each capped at 64 KiB. Never indexed: tool calls and output, reasoning, files, synthetic/system/skill messages, running or failed compactions. Every message type is listed as indexed or not, so a new type fails typecheck until decided. Any-word BM25, `porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`.

`GET /api/experimental/migration/session-search` (`experimental.migration.sessionSearch.status`) returns `disabled`, `running`/`paused` with `{ label, numerator, denominator }`, `completed` with skipped rows, or `unsupported`/`error`. TUI and desktop UI for it are a follow-up.

```text
packages/core/src/session/search-index.ts   # layouts, view, triggers, startup check, ensure, build chunks, state
packages/core/src/session/search-query.ts   # BM25 any-word query over the index
packages/core/src/session/search-build.ts   # one-time background build and its status
packages/core/src/config/plugin/session-search.ts  # signals the build while a location's config enables it
packages/server/src/process.ts              # forks the build next to Schedule.run
packages/core/src/database/database.ts      # runs registered checks after migrations, before writes
packages/protocol/src/groups/migration.ts   # status endpoint
packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts  # sqlite_fts
```

### Measured

| | |
|---|---|
| Index size on a 37.5 GB DB (21.4 GB of it current data) | ~115 MB compact / ~300 MB text |
| One-time build on that DB | ~2–2.5 min (estimate from a 1% sample and a full read-only scan) |
| Extra cost per write, compact (in-memory, Bun) | user message +29 µs, finishing a 221 KB assistant +1 ms, streaming rewrite +71 µs |
| Agent benchmark: 27 questions x 12 models (search + read tools over this index design) | 93.7% pass, 18k median tokens, vs 91.5% / 31k for a no-index search and 57% / 99k for a page-by-page scan |

### Out of scope

- Search API with ranked per-session results, excerpts and transcript cursors; agent tools; client progress UI.
- Durable Objects: nothing forks the build there, so it never runs.
- A DB moved from SQLite 3.43+ to an older SQLite loses search on that machine (writes keep working).

### Verification

- `bun run check`: pass. `packages/core`: `bun run migration --check` pass; `bun test test/session-search test/config`: 303 pass, incl. both layouts across edits, renames, reverts and cascade deletes, streaming assistants indexed once finished, every message type decided, opening the database dropping triggers an SQLite can't run, triggers restored after a source-table rebuild, a newer index version left alone, the build resuming, byte cap, skipped rows, done/failed recorded and not rerun.
- CI: see checks.



---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Related: #54863, #60995

Public API: adds the opt-in experimental.sqlite_fts config key and GET /api/experimental/migration/session-search (experimental.migration.sessionSearch.status) (backwards compatible)

prs.title: fix(core): hide instruction updates a revert left behind
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/62027

Related: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/61550 is the same kind of contradiction in historical forks. This PR doesn't change forks, so that one stays open.

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After a revert, the model could see an instruction update that contradicts its own system prompt.

When a committed revert removes an instruction update, core throws away the instruction state, and the next step builds the system prompt again from current values. Updates that came before the revert point stay in history, though, and the model still sees them. So it gets the fresh system prompt plus an old update saying something else.

Reproduced on `dev` with the runner test harness:

```text
First → source turns on ("Entered mode") → Second
      → source removed → Third → revert to Second → Fourth

before: system prompt: no "Entered mode"
        messages: First, "Entered mode", Fourth
after:  messages: First, Fourth
```

This affects every instruction source: MCP guidance, Code Mode catalog, date, API entries. It would also affect a Plan-style "you are in Plan mode" source: after this revert the session is back on build, but the model is told it's in Plan.

The fix: the instruction state already records where its current system prompt starts (`epoch_start`), and every update before that point is already included in it. History now hides instruction update messages older than that point. If there is no state, as right after the revert clears it, the next system prompt is built fresh, so every older update is hidden.

The filter is in `messageEntries`, so the runner, `generate`, compaction, the compaction precompute and `session.context` all see the same history.

What else changes, and why it's safe:

- **Only sessions where a revert cleared the state behave differently.** In a normal session the epoch is the first instruction event, so nothing is hidden. Forks start their epoch at 0, so they're unchanged too.
- **The prompt cache.** Updates are only hidden when the system prompt is being rebuilt anyway. The one exception is sessions already in this broken state when this ships: their history shrinks once, which costs one cache miss.
- **After compaction**, updates before the checkpoint were already out of the window. When history falls back to an earlier checkpoint, the updates between the 2 checkpoints are now hidden too. The current system prompt already includes them, which matches what native compaction already does.
- **Clients still get every message.** The timeline doesn't read this path. Only the model context and `session.context` (documented as the active context messages) drop the stale update.
- **Cost:** one extra lookup of the session's instruction-state row by primary key per history read.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New scenario `hides an update a revert left behind once the source is removed`, and the existing `resyncs the instruction state when a committed revert removes an update` now also checks the messages. Both fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`.
- Ran every core test file that touches history, compaction, forks, reverts or instructions (147 files): 2,899 pass. The 34 failures are in 9 shell, integration, provider and image test files, and they fail the same way on unchanged `dev` on my machine.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): keep subagents in their current role on follow-ups
prs.body:
**A follow-up to a reviewer stays with the reviewer.** To use another role, start a new child. An explicit model choice still works independently of the role.

❌ **Before**
1. Start a reviewer and send it another request using the same session ID.
2. Name a different agent and the child silently takes on that agent’s instructions.

✅ **After**
1. Omit the agent or repeat the reviewer’s ID to continue the review.
2. Name a different agent and the call tells you how to start a fresh child. It does not queue the request or change the child’s model.

```diff
- use the agent named by every call; switch the child if it differs
+ new child: use the requested agent, or general if omitted
+ follow-up: use the child's agent; reject a conflicting request
+ check permission for that agent before sending the prompt
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Start without an agent | ❌ Missing required input | ✅ Uses `general`, subject to permission |
| Follow up without an agent | ❌ Missing required input | ✅ Keeps the child’s role |
| Ask a reviewer to continue as a different agent | ❌ Switches its instructions | ✅ Rejects the call; the next request still uses the reviewer’s system prompt |
| Ask for permission when no agent is named | ❌ Terminal labels the agent `general` | ✅ Terminal shows the agent the permission is for |

The running-child regression failed against unmodified `dev` and passes with the fix.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts` checks who owns the child before looking up its role. There’s no second built-in `task` executor to update on `dev`; the old name survives in migration and display code.

<sub>Requested behavior change · reproduced with a running child and a test model</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `packages/core`: `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-subagent.test.ts test/subagent-idle-e2e.test.ts test/config/command-subagent.test.ts` — 27 passed.
- `packages/tui`: `bun test test/util/permission.test.ts` — 2 passed, including the label when the agent is omitted or conflicts with the permission resource.
- `packages/core`, `packages/tui`, and `services/site`: `bun typecheck` — passed in all three.
- The running-child test covers both an omitted agent and an empty agent string.
- `packages/core`: `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-subagent.test.ts -t 'follow-ups to a running child return immediately'` — failed as expected with the original tool; it accepted the conflicting role.

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): only discourage unprompted subagent status checks
prs.body:
The subagent tool told the model not to "ask the subagent for status", with no exception. A strict model could read that as "never message a running child", even when the user asks what it's doing. The point of the rule is to stop the model checking in on its own, so this says that instead.

```diff
 tool output:
- DO NOT sleep, poll for progress, ask the subagent for status, or duplicate this subagent's work; avoid working with the same files or topics it is using.
+ DO NOT sleep, poll, proactively check on its progress, or duplicate this subagent's work.

 description:
- … Do not sleep, poll for progress, or ask the child for status.
+ … Do not sleep, poll, or proactively check on the child's progress.
```

I also dropped "avoid working with the same files or topics it is using". "Topics" is vague enough to stop the parent from doing related work like reviewing what the child changes, and the next line ("Work on non-overlapping tasks") already covers stepping on the child's files. The "you'll receive a `<subagent>` message" and "call subagent again with this sessionID" lines are unchanged, so the model still knows results arrive on their own and that messaging the child is allowed.

The mini TUI demo's copy of the launch text is updated to match.

Checked: `bun test test/tool-subagent.test.ts` (15 pass) and `bun typecheck` in packages/core.

prs.title: feat(ai): graduate video generation with start, status, result and cancel
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

No issue. Follows https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63634, which removed the dead Gemini Veo and Runway video protocols.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Video generation in `@opencode/ai` moves out of `experimental` and becomes a job you start and then check on yourself, instead of a call that blocks and polls for you. That's what opencode core needs: it decides when to poll, and it can pick a job back up after a restart from a stored token.

```ts
const job = yield* ai.video.start({ model, prompt, start, end, references, duration: "8 seconds", aspect, resolution, sound })
// job = { id, token }   token is plain JSON, store it with the model

yield* ai.video.status(model, job.token) // one read: { status, progress? }
yield* ai.video.result(model, job.token) // { videos, usage?, providerMetadata? }
yield* ai.video.cancel(model, job.token) // typed UnsupportedOperation where the provider can't cancel
```

The Promise client has the same calls under `ai.video`. Every call after `start` takes `(model, token)`, so recovering a job is the same as reading it normally.

What changed in the request:

- `frames: { first, last }` is now `start` and `end`.
- `references` takes any media kind; protocols route images, video and audio to their own fields.
- `durationSeconds: 10` is now `duration: "10 seconds"` (an Effect duration string, seconds only for now).
- `aspect` also accepts `"auto"` (follow the start image), `resolution` documents `480p | 720p | 1080p | 4k` and passes anything else through, and `audio` is now `sound`.
- `n`, `seed`, `negativePrompt` and the source `video` field are gone from the shared request. They're on too few providers; use `providerOptions`.

Removed: `generate`, `stream`, `resume` and the live handle (`await`, `events`, `refresh`) for video. There's no built-in polling loop and no queue position, since no video provider reports one. Other modalities keep `Generation` as is.

Enforcement: the package only rejects locally what a protocol has no way to send, such as a reference video on xAI. Values a provider may reject (durations, resolutions, reference counts, mixing frames and references) go to the provider and its error comes back typed. Spelling and routing differences are handled silently by each protocol.

How it works:

- `MediaRoute.queued` gets `attach(model, token, execute)`, which decodes a token into the route's status, result and cancel operations without a status read first. `resume` now uses it too.
- `VideoClient` is its own small service (`start`, `status`, `result`, `cancel`) on top of that, and `VideoModel` only accepts queued routes.
- xAI maps `start` to `image`, `end` to `last_frame`, image references to `reference_images`, audio references to `reference_audios`, `sound` to `generate_audio`, and leaves `aspect_ratio` out for `"auto"` when a start frame sets the shape. Edit and extend stay reachable with `providerOptions: { mode, video: { url } }`.
- `Media.Asset` gets `stream()`, and `Media.write` and the Promise `ai.write` now stream URL downloads to disk instead of buffering whole files.

Trade-offs:

- Callers that only want a one-liner now write a short polling loop. I'd rather add a helper later than bake a loop into the API core can't control.
- A request's `headers`/`http` overlay only applies to `start`. Status and result reads are rebuilt from the token, so they use the model's deployment settings, which is what a resumed job in another process gets anyway.
- `ai.experimental.video` is removed without aliases, since it was experimental. The release notes should mention that `ai.video` graduated with this shape.

No feature flag: this is a library API with no opencode runtime behavior yet.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` and `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/ai`
- `bun test` in `packages/ai`: 2073 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run check` at the root
- The recorded xAI test now drives `start`, then `status` until terminal, then `result`, and still replays the existing cassette: the request body is unchanged.
- New unit tests cover the xAI field mapping, `"auto"` aspect, edit and extend via provider options, rejecting reference videos and non-second durations before sending, token round trips and foreign tokens, status mapping and progress, result on pending, failed, expired and moderated jobs, unsupported cancel, read retries (503, 429 `retry-after`, no retry on 400) and `Media.Asset.stream`.
- The Promise tests that exercised the generic generation handle through video now use AssemblyAI transcription, which still has the handle.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR


---
<!-- opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->
_Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._

Public API: graduates video to `ai.video` (start/status/result/cancel), removing `ai.experimental.video` and renaming the request fields (breaking for experimental callers)
<!-- /opencode-github-bot:pr-section -->

prs.title: fix(core): rename instead of deleting when a patch only changes a file's case
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63126

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

A patch that moves a file writes the new name, then removes the old one. On macOS and Windows file names ignore case by default, so a move that only changes case (`same.txt` → `Same.txt`) wrote the file in place and then deleted it, and the tool failed with "file does not exist" on an empty directory.

```text
before: write Same.txt (= same.txt) → remove same.txt → file gone
after:  write same.txt → rename same.txt to Same.txt
```

A move now takes the rename path only when the two paths match ignoring case, the source is a regular file, and the new name already exists, which on a case-insensitive filesystem means it's the same file. Everything else keeps the write-and-remove path, so on Linux a move into a directory that differs only in case still creates it, and a symlink's target is left alone. If a different file with the new name exists on Linux, the rename ends the same way write-and-remove does: the new name holds the new contents and the old name is gone.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New test: `same.txt` moved to `Same.txt` leaves only `Same.txt` with the new contents. It fails on dev on macOS (the directory ends up empty).
- New test: `Foo/a.txt` moved to `foo/a.txt` succeeds. On Linux, where `foo/` doesn't exist, it failed with the first version of this PR.
- `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-patch.test.ts` in packages/core (44 pass), `bun run check`, and `typecheck:tsc` in packages/core.

### Checklist

prs.title: docs(zh-cn): 补上 keybinds 页面缺失的「绑定值」小节
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #57623

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The Chinese keybinds page is missing a section the English page has.

The English `keybinds.mdx` documents `## Binding Values`: a binding value may be one shortcut, several comma-separated shortcuts, an array, or an object with `key`, `event`, `preventDefault` or `fallthrough`. The `zh-cn` copy never got that section, so a Chinese reader has no way to learn from the docs how to configure more than one shortcut for a binding.

This PR adds the missing section to `packages/web/src/content/docs/zh-cn/keybinds.mdx`, in the same position it occupies in the English page (between `## 前导键` and `## 禁用快捷键`).

The terminology follows the page's existing choices and the `zh-cn` glossary: `keybind` / `shortcut` are 快捷键, and since `## Disable Keybind` is already 禁用快捷键 here, `## Binding Values` is 绑定值. The code block, the config keys and the schema URL are identical to the English page.

The reason the section is missing is the frozen locale sync described in #57623: `docs-locale-sync.yml` has its job disabled with `if: false`, so the Chinese copy stopped following the English one. I did not touch the workflow, because whether the sync should point at the v1 tree or the v2 tree is a question about which one is canonical, and #57623 already asks it. This PR just fills the specific gap.

### How did you verify your code works?

prs.title: docs: document the Windows Terminal ctrl+tab caveat
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #55606

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`session.tab.next` and `session.tab.previous` default to `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab`. On a default Windows Terminal neither key ever reaches OpenCode, so the advertised default silently does nothing.

The cause is in the terminal, not in the TUI. Windows Terminal binds `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab` to its own `Terminal.NextTab` and `Terminal.PrevTab` actions, and a terminal key binding consumes the key before the client application sees it.

I measured this on Windows Terminal 1.24.12741 with a probe process that logged every byte the terminal delivered. Same terminal, same run, `ctrl+tab` / `ctrl+shift+tab` / `tab`:

| encoding | `ctrl+tab` | `ctrl+shift+tab` | `tab` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default, no unbind | *(nothing)* | *(nothing)* | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, legacy | `0x09` | `ESC [ Z` | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, kitty requested | `0x09` | `ESC [ Z` | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, `win32-input-mode` | `CSI 9 ; 15 ; 0 ; 1 ; 40 ; 1 _` | `CSI 9 ; 15 ; 0 ; 1 ; 56 ; 1 _` | `CSI 9 ; 1 ; 9 ; 1 ; 32 ; 1 _` |

Three things fall out of that:

- While the terminal holds the binding, the key never arrives at all.
- Unbinding it is not enough on its own. Windows Terminal ignores the kitty keyboard protocol, so the terminal keeps sending the legacy encoding, where `ctrl+tab` is the same byte as `tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab` is a plain `shift+tab`. The Ctrl is gone either way.
- The only encoding that carries the modifier is `win32-input-mode`, and the `win32-input-mode` row is the one where the key-down arrives at all.

`alt+down` and `alt+up` are not reserved by the terminal and do arrive: they come through as `CSI 1 ; 3 B` and `CSI 1 ; 3 A`, which the parser reads as `down` and `up` with the alt modifier.

This PR adds a `### Windows Terminal` subsection under `## Sessions` in `services/www/src/docs/content/cli/keybinds.mdx`, next to the table that lists the session tab bindings. It says that the terminal reserves `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab`, points at `alt+down` and `alt+up` as the ones that work, and explains that unbinding the terminal's binding only helps once `win32-input-mode` is on.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Measured the terminal behaviour rather than inferring it, with a probe process inside Windows Terminal 1.24 that logs every byte the terminal delivers. The comparison that carries the argument is the one in the same run: a key the terminal binds, against one it does not, in each of the three encodings.
- For the rows that need the terminal's binding released, the probe added `{ "command": "unbound", "keys": "ctrl+tab" }` to the `actions` array of the terminal's `settings.json`, took a byte-exact backup first, and restored the file afterwards.
- Fed the exact bytes Windows Terminal sends for `alt+down` and `alt+up` (`CSI 1 ; 3 B` and `CSI 1 ; 3 A`) through the TUI's key parser and confirmed they resolve to `down` and `up` with the alt modifier set, so the alternative the new subsection points at is one that actually works.
- Checked the `settings.json` shape against the Windows Terminal documentation: `keybindings` was replaced by `actions` in version 1.4, and `"unbound"` is the value that releases a default binding.
- Ran `bun typecheck` and `bun run check:generated` from `services/www`: 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 hints over the 34 Astro files, and the generated-output check passes.
- Built the documentation site with `bun run build` from `services/www`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(core): connect model providers over a Unix socket
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

OpenCode can only reach a model provider over TCP. When a local server (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, a company gateway) already listens on a Unix socket, the only option today is a `socat` bridge that exposes a loopback TCP port. This adds a transport setting so provider traffic dials the socket directly: no port opened, no TCP handshake/overhead, no TLS encrypt/decrypt work, and access control is the socket's file permissions. OpenAI Chat Completions and the Responses API are covered on both the native and AI SDK paths.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature

### What does this PR do?

Adds provider-level `settings.socketPath`:

```jsonc
{
  "providers": {
    "local": {
      "package": "@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible",
      "settings": {
        "baseURL": "http://localhost/v1",
        "socketPath": "/run/llm.sock"
      },
      "models": {
        "local-model": {}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- The URL supplies the request path, method and headers; its host and port are ignored, like `curl --unix-socket`. It must be `http:`, because the transport is plain HTTP over the socket, with no TLS layer to encrypt or decrypt.
- `socketPath` is a named setting, so `Provider.nativeSettings` strips it from provider package options.
- Native path: `RequestExecutor.withTransport` is the one place that decides the transport. It builds the per-call middleware with `unixSocketFetch` (needed because the app graph pins its own fetch per response) and makes a configured socket win over a per-call `fetch`, so a new send site cannot accidentally go over TCP.
- AI SDK path: `prepareOptions` picks the socket fetch over `settings.fetch` and `outbound`, keeping the existing timeout and SSE wrapper.
- Runtime: Bun's `fetch(url, { unix })`. On non-Bun runtimes `socketPath` is rejected with a clear error instead of falling back to TCP; the first hand-written `node:http` fallback was removed during review because it was untested client code.
- Redirects are returned, not followed, because a redirect target would be TCP. `transport: "websocket"` is forced to HTTP, and media/decision models get the setting too.

Limitation: built-in Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio auto-discovery only probes HTTP URLs, so `socketPath` applies to explicitly configured providers and models. This is documented.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/ai/test/unix-socket.test.ts`: 8 tests against a real `Bun.serve({ unix })`, including a TCP decoy that must stay empty. Covers JSON POST, path/headers, streaming SSE before completion, abort while waiting for headers and while reading the body, redirects, https rejection, empty path, and a missing socket. Reran 10x.
- `packages/core/test/unix-socket.test.ts`: production app graph, not a mock. This test fails with the first implementation (which the reviewer caught) and passes now; the TCP decoy receives nothing.
- AI SDK path: `packages/core/test/aisdk.test.ts` sends a request through a socket while the model's base URL points at an unused host.
- `packages/core/test/provider.test.ts` asserts `socketPath` is stripped from native package settings.
- An empty `socketPath` is rejected at config decode; live, before the fix it silently hit a TCP decoy (HTTP 501), after the fix the decoy receives no request. A live TCP listener on the base URL port also receives nothing when a socket is configured, which exercises the provider-setting merge through `ModelResolver`.
- Live: `opencode run --standalone` with `baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:59999/v1"` (no listener on that port) plus `socketPath`, against a fake OpenAI-compatible streaming server on the socket. The model replied, so the request can only have gone over the socket.
- Typecheck passed for `packages/ai`, `packages/core`, `packages/schema`; full `packages/ai` suite 2056 pass / 0 fail; docs build succeeded; oxlint clean.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

_Implemented with AI assistance (OpenCode agent, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash). The submitter must review, comprehend and test every line._

prs.title: feat(read): attach audio and video files for multimodal models
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54491. Also covers #54049 (the video half) and #10531 (the umbrella request).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`read` attaches images and PDFs to the model, but rejects every other binary file. Audio and video are the visible case: `MEDIA_MIMES` in `packages/core/src/tool/read-filesystem.ts` lists only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and PDF, and `Mime.detect` in `packages/core/src/mime.ts` sniffs magic bytes for images and PDF only. An `.mp3` therefore detects as `application/octet-stream`, misses the set, and falls through to the text path, where the first NUL byte raises `BinaryFileError`.

The rest of the pipeline already handles them: `mimeToModality` in `packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts` maps `audio/` and `video/` to modalities and checks them against the model's declared `capabilities.input`. `read` is the only place that excludes them.

This adds the missing signatures to `Mime.detect` and the matching entries to `MEDIA_MIMES`, so a model that accepts audio or video input receives the file. It also adds `image/bmp` and `image/avif`, which `Mime.detect` already returns but the set was missing.

The 20MB `MAX_MEDIA_INGEST_BYTES` cap and the existing image/PDF/text paths are unchanged.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core/test/tool-read-filesystem.test.ts` covers the new formats, the `Mime.detect` verdicts, the ingest cap, and the unchanged text/image/PDF paths.

prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Closes #63631 ### Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [x] Documentation ### What does this PR do? This adds an `advisor` tool like the one in Claude Code. While the session model works, it can ask a second model the user picked for advice. Here it works with any provider, including local models. A lot of the developers I work with use Claude Code's advisor every day, and I've wanted this in OpenCode for a long time. How it works: - `/advisor` asks for Off, "Advisor" (the advisor sees the conversation) or "Advisor (secure)" (it only sees a short brief the agent writes, never the conversation), then a model from the `/models` list. The choice lives in plugin storage, like `/goal`'s state, and is read from there on every request, so it applies to every session and every open folder. - While it's on, the request carries the tool and a short system note saying it's there, when to ask, and to check advice before acting on it. While it's off, or the flag is off, neither is there and `/advisor` is hidden. - A call is one tool-less `session.generate` against the advisor's model. For that I added three optional inputs to the internal `SessionGenerate.generate`: a model override, `toolChoice`, and `transcript: false` for secure mode. A secure request also skips the session hooks, so only the advisor prompt and the brief are sent. Usage is recorded like other generate calls. - In the session it's one row ("Asking the advisor…", then "Advisor reviewed"). Clicking it shows what was shared and the reply. Sessions show a small "advisor" indicator; the home screen is unchanged. It's behind a new `advisor` flag, and the `bun run generate` output for the flag is included. The public API changes are additive. Desktop and web show the generic tool row for now. I'm very open to changing anything here: the design, names, splitting this into smaller PRs, moving parts to an external plugin, or adding desktop/web support. I'm happy to put in whatever work it takes to get this in. ### How did you verify your code works? - schema: `bun typecheck`, `bun test test/advisor.test.ts` - core: `bun typecheck`, `bun run script/test.ts test/tool-advisor.test.ts --rerun-each 10`, plus `session-generate`, `plugin`, `plugin-failure`, `plugin/goal` and `tool-todo` - tui: `bun typecheck`, `bun test test/session-advisor.test.tsx --rerun-each 10` (it clicks each row and checks the dropdown), and the full TUI suite. The one failure, `go-upsell-art.test.tsx`, fails the same way on `dev`. - root `bun run check` and `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `check:generated` in client and protocol, and the site build - By hand with `bun dev --standalone` and local models: calls in both modes, the choice surviving a restart, an unavailable model failing cleanly while the session carries on, and turning it off removing the tool and the note. ### Screenshots / recordings `/advisor`, then the model: A secure consultation in the session, expanded: The session indicator: ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Public API: adds the `experimental.advisor` flag, the `opencode.advisor` plugin RPC, the `@opencode/schema/advisor` module, the `advisor` tool and permission, and `/advisor` (backwards compatible)

issues.title: Bug: Cached models disappear after remote catalog metadata is reset to zero

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

Model `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-terra` intermittently disappears from `pi --list-models`, apparently after system sleep or VPN connectivity issues (or wrong country selection).

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
```

The model is still present in ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, but its catalog metadata changes:

Field | Before | After
-- | -- | --
lastModified | 1793193879000 | 0
checkedAt | 1793240351635 | 1793295007994
etag | Present | Missing
gpt-6.1-terra in cached models | Yes | Yes
Model visible in Pi | Yes | No

Even with PI_OFFLINE=1, the model remains hidden.

Running pi update --models restores it immediately. This has happened repeatedly.

# Suspected cause
In withRemoteCatalog(), HTTP 404/501 responses reset lastModified to 0 and clear etag, while preserving stored.models.

remoteModels() then rejects the cached models because their timestamp is older than the built-in catalog.

A successful response missing the Last-Modified header is another possible cause.

Source: [remote-catalog-provider.ts (v1.4.0)](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts)

---

- Pi 1.4.0
- Node.js 26
- Windows 11

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi update --models and verify gpt-6.1-terra is listed.
2. Allow a periodic catalog refresh, potentially during unstable VPN connectivity.
3. Observe that the model disappears while remaining in the stored model array.
4. Run pi update --models again. The model reappears.

The network trigger is intermittent; the exact HTTP response has not been captured.

### Expected behavior

A transient catalog endpoint failure should not invalidate a previously valid cached catalog or hide working models. The last known good catalog should remain available until a valid replacement is received.

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-6.1-terra                       500K     128K     yes       yes
```

### Version

1.4.0

issues.title: openai: ChatGPT sign-in still uses 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K account catalog
issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

An authenticated `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` using the stored `openai` OAuth access token returned HTTP 200 and:

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Anthropic message threads: thinking blocks dropped (prefix_binding_mismatch) on every thread_not_found resend after a string-typed numeric tool arg
issues.body:
### What happened?

With Anthropic message threads on (default for `api.anthropic.com` since 1.5.1), every full resend after a `thread_not_found` fallback warns:

```
Anthropic dropped 3 thinking blocks: prefix_binding_mismatch at messages.5.content.0; ...
```

The same blocks are dropped again on every later fallback. In one session that was 7 times, once per idle gap over ~5 min. Requests that continue a thread never show it.

What the session shows:

- Early in the session the model called `bash` with `timeout: "20"` (a string; the schema says number). It was the only string-typed numeric argument in that session.
- The dropped blocks are exactly the thinking blocks generated in that thread after that tool call. The thinking before it is kept.
- On the first fallback resend, cache read stopped at that assistant message (31,144 tokens vs 43,935 on the last request before the gap). Later fallbacks read the full prior prefix, so nothing new diverges. The original blocks are just dropped again each time.
- Two other sessions show the same pattern, each right after a string `timeout` in a bash call.

Hypothesis (I did not capture the request payload): pi keeps the parsed arguments as the model sent them (`"20"`) and replays them as `tool_use.input`. `validateToolArguments` only coerces a copy (`pi-ai/dist/utils/validation.js`). The server's thread copy of that turn seems to differ from what pi replays (maybe the input normalized to the schema type, maybe something else), so thinking bound inside the thread no longer matches the prefix on a full resend.

Impact is low: some old reasoning is lost, plus an extra 404 round trip per idle gap. But the warning repeats for the rest of the session.

Possible workaround (not tested): `models.json` → `providers.anthropic.compat.supportsMessageThreads: false`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Anthropic model with thinking, threads on (default).
2. Get the model to call `bash` with a string `timeout` (e.g. `"20"`), then do a couple more thinking + tool turns.
3. Stay idle for more than 5 minutes, then send another message.
4. The resend after `thread_not_found` reports `prefix_binding_mismatch` drops, and so does every later idle resend.

I haven't re-run this with `pi -ne` or built a minimal repro yet.

### Expected behavior

A full resend after a thread fallback should match what the server bound in the thread, so no thinking is dropped. That could mean storing the tool input the same way the server does (e.g. the schema-coerced args) or replaying it byte for byte. At minimum, the same drop shouldn't repeat on every fallback.

### Version

pi 1.5.2 (macOS), claude-sonnet-5-5, thinking high

issues.title: cacheWarming "idle" stops silently once an extension handles turn_end and the context holds a custom or compaction message
issues.body:
**What happened?**
With `cacheWarming: "idle"`, the idle warm never fires in our sessions: 507 `cache_warming_decision` events since September, all at `continuationProbability: 1`, none at 0.15. `/session` shows `Inactive (conversation context changed)` right after the run settles.

Cause: `cacheContextIsCurrent` (`core/sdk.js:214-222`) checks each captured message by object identity. When any extension has a `turn_end` handler, `_dispatchTurnEndBoundary` goes on to `_commitBoundaryDrafts`, which calls `_refreshFinalizedContext()` even with no drafts (`core/agent-session.js:492`, `:636`). `sessionEntryToContextMessages` (`core/session-manager.js:179-188`) builds new objects for `custom_message`, `branch_summary` and `compaction` entries on every projection. So `validateRun()` stops the warmer before any decision is emitted. Without a `turn_end` handler, idle warming works.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. `note.ts`: `pi.registerCommand("note", { handler: async () => pi.sendMessage({ customType: "n", content: "x", display: true }) })` plus `pi.on("turn_end", () => {})`.
2. `pi -ne -e note.ts` on an Anthropic model, `cacheWarming: "idle"`. Run `/note`, send one prompt, wait for it to settle.
3. `/session` → `Cache Warming … Inactive (conversation context changed)`.
4. Remove the `turn_end` line → `Decision in 4m …`, and the idle decision fires.

**Expected behavior**
The idle phase compares the prefix the provider saw: compare entry ids, or memoise the projected message per entry (entries don't change after append).

**Version**
1.2.0, Linux. Same symptom as https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10700; related to https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10515.

We run Pi Durable 1.5.2 for a guest assistant. A guest can ask us to erase their data (India's DPDP Act). Our transcripts hold masked text only, but we still need to delete a conversation's rows, not only make them unreadable.

Today a conversation cannot be deleted: there is no call on `Conversation` or `Harness`, and the storage interfaces have no delete for entries, tasks or documents. We work around it with one storage file per month, deleted 90 days after its last turn. That keeps conversations from being erased early on request.

issues.title: A lightweight entry point for defining extensions for pi-durable
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Add a subpath export, such as `@earendil-works/pi-durable/extension`, that exports the extension-authoring helpers (`defineDoc`, `defineExtension`, `hook`, `ToolTask`) and their types. It should not load the session runtime, storage or model code.

### Why?

These helpers are only on the root export, and importing the root loads the whole runtime. In 1.4.0, a module that only defines an extension pays about 180 ms and 742 modules for that one import. On Cloudflare Workers this cost hits every cold start. The package already has narrow subpaths (`./codemode`, `./env`, `./tools`, `./storage/*`, ...), so this fits the existing pattern.

Repro (Node 24, pi-durable 1.4.0):

```sh
npm i @earendil-works/pi-durable@1.4.0
node --input-type=module -e "const t=performance.now(); await import('@earendil-works/pi-durable'); console.log(performance.now()-t)"

# 513.1185280000001 (no disk cache)
# 165.471654
# 214.493499
# 185.04169
```

### How? (optional)

A new entry module that re-exports only the authoring helpers, plus an exports entry for it. Type-only imports stay as they are.

I’d be happy to implement this myself and open a PR if the subpath name and export set work for you.

issues.title: v1.5.2 exits with uncaught AbortError when a read tool stream is aborted after the run finishes

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

pi exited with `uncaughtException: AbortError` (code `ABORT_ERR`) mid-session, killing the whole process and the running work. All frames are in pi's own bundle (core read tool + built-in codemode worker); no third-party extensions are involved, so `pi -ne` would behave the same.

The read tool attaches the call's `AbortSignal` to the fs `ReadStream` (v1.5.2 `readLocalFileChunks` passes `signal` into `handle.createReadStream`). Here the abort came from `Execution.finish` when the codemode run finished while a `tools.read` was still streaming a file. The signal-aborted stream emitted an `error` nobody listens to, and the process exited:

<details><summary>Stack trace</summary>

```
AbortError: The operation was aborted
    at addAbortSignal (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:38:25)
    at ReadStream.Readable (node:internal/streams/readable:360:7)
    at new ReadStream (node:internal/fs/streams:258:3)
    at FileHandle.createReadStream (node:internal/fs/promises:408:12)
    at Object.readLocalFileChunks [as createReadStream] (chunk-VEJDBY3O.js:789:1792)
    at async selectLinesFromStream (chunk-VEJDBY3O.js:792:401)
  code: 'ABORT_ERR',
  [cause]: DOMException [AbortError]
      at AbortController.abort (node:internal/abort_controller:579:18)
      at Execution.finish (execute-L2EEDV3L.js:2:8423)
      at Execution.handleDone (execute-L2EEDV3L.js:2:6630)
      at Execution.handleMessage / Object.message / MessagePort (node:internal/worker)
```

</details>

This looks like the same crash class as #11956, but at a different point: the file was already open and streaming; the abort arrives when the run finishes, not during file open. main already removes the signal from the stream for #11956 ("No signal for the stream: one that aborts before the stream's iterator attaches makes the stream emit an 'error' no listener handles, which crashes the process"), which should cover this path too — but v1.5.2 is still the latest release, so released binaries keep crashing this way until that ships.

### Steps to reproduce

Happened twice so far, not reproduced on demand (macOS, v1.5.2): a codemode script was reading a large file (both times) via `tools.read`; the run finished while the read was still streaming, `Execution.finish` aborted the call's controller, and the aborted ReadStream crashed the process.

### Expected behavior

An aborted read tool call should cancel quietly and leave the process alive, as in the #11956 fix on main.

### Version

1.5.2 (latest release as of 2026-11-13)

issues.title: find: path globs match directories above the search path

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

`find` puts `**/` in front of patterns that contain a `/` and runs `fd --full-path`, which matches the absolute path. So a pattern can also match through the folders above the search path. If the project lives in `~/src/app`, `find src/**/*.ts` returns every `.ts` file in the project, because `~/src/` matches.

grep no longer works this way: #11895 anchored its glob at `path`, and lists "prefix `**/` ... as `find` does" as a rejected alternative because it matches lookalike folders (#10418). So the two tools now disagree on the same glob:

- `grep { glob: "src/**/*.ts" }` → `src/a.ts`
- `find { pattern: "src/**/*.ts" }` → `lib/b.ts`, `src/a.ts`, `test/c.ts`

#10418 reported this and was auto-closed; only its `./` part was fixed later (#12044).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create `/tmp/src/app/src/a.ts`, `/tmp/src/app/lib/b.ts` and `/tmp/src/app/test/c.ts`.
2. Run `cd /tmp/src/app && pi --tools read,bash,find` and ask: "Call the find tool with pattern `src/**/*.ts`."
3. It returns `lib/b.ts`, `src/a.ts`, `test/c.ts`.

In the pi repo, `find { pattern: "src/**/*.ts", path: "packages/coding-agent/src/core" }` returns 103 files instead of none.

### Expected behavior

Only paths below the search path match: `src/**/*.ts` returns just `src/a.ts`.

I'd like to fix this. One question first: inside the search path, should `find` stay unanchored (`src/*.ts` also finds `pkg/src/x.ts`, as today and as #12044 describes), or be anchored at the search path like grep's glob? Either way the fix is small: put the glob-escaped search path in front of the pattern passed to fd (fd matches the absolute path as given), with or without the `**/`. I have the unanchored version with a regression test working locally.

### Version

1.5.2, also on main (086028ecf). macOS, fd 10.5.2.

issues.title: forceSystemPrompt projection hoists later toolsAdded into the request tool list (prompt-cache miss after tool_search)
issues.body:
When any extension returns `systemPrompt` from `before_agent_start` (or sets `systemPromptOptions.forceSystemPrompt`), `AgentSession._installAgentForcedPromptProjection` (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts`, dist 1.0.3 `agent-session.js:1310-1326`) replaces all system messages with one head whose `toolsAdded` is `getCurrentSystemMessage(messages).toolsAdded`, i.e. the full current tool set. Later tool additions recorded by `tool_search` (`toolsAdded` on a mid-conversation system message) are folded into that head.

Providers with `compat.supportsAdditionalTools` (OpenAI Responses / Codex) rely on `resolveTranscriptTools` seeing the initial tools in system message 0 and the discovered tools in a later delta to emit `additional_tools` and keep the top-level `tools` (and so the cached prefix) unchanged. After the projection the top-level `tools` array grows instead, and the whole prefix after `instructions` is re-billed. Observed: 80k-115k token re-bills per discovery on a 37-turn session.

Repro: install any extension with
```ts
pi.on("before_agent_start", (e) => ({ systemPrompt: e.systemPrompt + "\n\nextra" }));
```
run on an `openai-codex-responses` model with `supportsAdditionalTools`, call `tool_search` once, and compare the two request bodies: `tools` grows and no `additional_tools` input item is present. Without the extension, `tools` is stable and `additional_tools` appears.

Suggested fix: keep later system messages that carry `toolsAdded`/`toolsRemoved` (dropping their content and sections, which the forced text supersedes); head = forced text + system message 0's tools. Alternatively, document in `docs/extensions.md` that returning `systemPrompt` also disables tool-addition anchoring.

issues.title: Branch summaries pay full fresh input on every navigate: summary request shares no cache prefix with live turns
issues.body:
## Problem

Every navigate with summarization sends a standalone request that shares no reusable prefix with the live turns it summarizes:

- System prompt is the generic summarization prompt, not the live session prompt.
- History is a serialized text blob, not the structured messages live turns send (tool results dropped).
- No tools attached, unlike the conversation being summarized.
- Uses `cacheRetention: "none"` with a random session id, so overlap cannot hit.
- Live thinking level is not forwarded as reasoning effort.

## Reproduction

On a branch with substantial history, navigate away with summarization on and check the summary request usage: cached input is ~0% while billed input covers the whole branch history, even though live turns were served from cache.

## Fix

Fixed in cad0p/pi#3 (fork; upstream PR to follow), which builds the summary request on the live prefix (live system prompt, tools, session id, thinking level, full history) and appends the summary instruction at the end. See cad0p/pi#3 for the mechanism and the prompt eval evidence (winner r5d).

## Verification

- Gate through shipped code: prefix match 100% / 100% / 99.9% across 3 held-out segments.
- Live check: cold navigate re-billed ~77k tokens ($0.0075); repeat on the warm overlapping prefix was cache-served ($0.0004).
- New unit tests pass; `tsgo` and biome clean.
- Zero tool calls in 126+ full-fidelity trial summaries with tools attached.
- Miss notice persisted on the entry and shown on the navigate path; silent when the setting is off.

Full eval comparison (rounds, head-to-head, per-round evidence) is in the cad0p/pi#3 description.

issues.title: Proposal: bounded retry for Gemini MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL

labels.name: untriaged

### What do you want to change?

Treat Google's `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` finish reason as eligible for bounded assistant-level retry, using the existing retry settings rather than a separate loop. I would like to implement this if maintainers agree.

### Why?

Gemini tool-use turns sometimes end with `Provider stopped with: MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` and require manual continuation despite auto-retry being enabled. I observed this with pi 1.5.0, `google-generative-ai`, through a local Google-compatible proxy.
