issues.body:
0.10.3 puts ACP (the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com)) first. This issue covers one direction: **Codewhale runs an installed agent CLI over ACP**, as a whole session that lives in Codewhale's sidebar, history and approvals. The other direction, an editor driving Codewhale, is #7280.

## Status

- **On main:**
  - A session can run on an installed agent.
  - Shutdown ends an agent that is still starting, restart recovery works, and approval answers are durable.
  - Discovery finds Windows `.cmd`/`.exe` shims and says *why* an agent is unavailable: missing, too old, or answering with another protocol.
  - The supported agents are listed in `crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs` (`AGENTS`): Claude Agent, Codex, DSH, Antigravity, OpenCode, Kimi, Mistral Vibe, Qoder, CodeBuddy and Grok.
- **How a session is started:** [docs/RUNTIME_API.md § Sessions on other agents](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/RUNTIME_API.md#sessions-on-other-agents-external-agent-threads), and `GET /v1/agents/external` for what was found on this computer.
- **Verification so far uses fixture agents.** No real installed agent has been qualified yet.

## Ways to help

**1. Try a real agent and report (no Rust needed).** Pick an agent you already have installed and comment with which one. Then:
- Start `codewhale serve` from a `main` build, check that `GET /v1/agents/external` lists your agent as runnable, and start a session on it.
- Send a prompt that edits a file and runs a command, answer an approval, cancel a turn, and quit and reopen to resume.
- Post the agent name and version, your OS, what worked, and the exact text of anything refused or broken.

Done when every step is reported for that agent.

**2. Add an agent that speaks ACP.** For example **Qwen Code** (`qwen --acp`) or **GitHub Copilot CLI** (`copilot --acp --stdio`), which are not in the registry yet. (Google's agent is already listed as Antigravity, `agy acp`; Gemini CLI was retired for personal accounts and is not added back.) This is a good first Rust contribution:
- Add one `ExternalAgent` row to `AGENTS` in `crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs`: `id`, `binary`, `acp_args` (how to start it in ACP mode), `min_version`, `upgrade`, `login` and `website`.
- Copy the shape of a neighbouring row. Fields you can't verify stay `None`; don't guess.
- Run `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/agents.rs registry`. `registry_rows_are_unique_with_verified_commands` must pass.
- Say in the PR how you checked the ACP flag against the agent's own docs.

**3. Improve the docs.** A user-facing page on running other agents inside Codewhale (install, sign in, start a session, what's supported) doesn't exist yet. A PR adding one under `docs/` is welcome, and a Chinese version under `docs/zh_hans/` even more so.

## Being built by maintainers right now

These are claimed, so please don't duplicate them:
- ACP options, capability refusals and agent-reported usage.
- Consolidating to one ACP client.
- Sending extra workspace directories to agents that support them.
- Projecting plan, mode, command and config updates from agents.

Steering, compaction, forking and images in an external-agent session are reported as unavailable unless the agent supports them.

## How to take a piece

1. **Comment here first** with the piece you want (for example "I'll take row 12" or "Windows journeys on ARM64"), so two people don't build the same thing. A maintainer replies to confirm.
2. **Build and test locally.** Setup: [Getting Started](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started); fast loop: [Fast local loop](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#fast-local-loop).
   ```bash
   CODEWHALE_BUILD_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" cargo build --locked -p codewhale-cli
   scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p <crate>
   scripts/dev-test.sh <crate-or-path> <test_filter>
   ```
3. **Open a PR that says `Refs #<this issue>`.** It merges as itself with you as the author, you are credited in the changelog and [CONTRIBUTORS](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/main/docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md), and a red check you didn't cause is ours to fix. Reports are contributions too: a test result posted here is credited the same way.

Questions are welcome here, in English or Chinese. Part of the overall [0.10.3 tracking issue](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/7284).

issues.title: Git status hides the source of a rename that leaves the workspace from the worktree side
issues.body:
### What happened?

`split_by_workspace` in `crates/app-server/src/runtime_api/git.rs` projects repository-root rows into the workspace frame. When a rename leaves the workspace, it synthesizes a `deleted` row so the source is still visible inside the workspace, but the guard for that is `row.index == "R"`.

Since #7310 the parser also returns a **worktree-side** rename, whose index column is a space. For that shape the guard is false, so the source path — which really has disappeared from the workspace — appears in no row of `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes` at all. The index-side equivalent shows a `deleted` row.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
git init -q -b main r && cd r
mkdir sub && echo one > sub/a.txt
git add . && git commit -qm init
git mv sub/a.txt outside.txt
git reset -q
git add -N outside.txt
git status --porcelain=v1 -z | od -c    # " R outside.txt\0sub/a.txt\0"
ls sub/a.txt                            # gone from the worktree
git ls-files sub                        # still sub/a.txt in the index
```

Open the workspace at `sub/` and request `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes`. `detail.files` is empty: `a.txt` is not listed, although it no longer exists in the workspace. With `git mv sub/a.txt outside.txt` and no reset, the same request returns one row for `a.txt` with `index = "D"`, `status = "deleted"`.

### Expected

The source is listed as a deletion in both cases. The column the change actually lives in differs, so the synthesized row should say so: a worktree-side rename deletes in the worktree (`worktree = "D"`, `staged = false`), and the index-side row keeps `index = "D"`, `staged = true`.

Staging safety is not weakened by the gap — the outside row still carries its root-relative `old_path` and `compute_tokens` covers it — so this is a listing gap, not a guard gap.

`C` should not synthesize a row at all: copying in either column leaves the source in place. Git reports a worktree copy as `A` in the first place (`-c status.renames=copies` still emits `A b.txt`), so that half is defensive only.

### Version

`main` at `f5a3dda97` (0.10.3 source).

issues.title: l10n(zh-Hans): ASCII punctuation in /router, label and usage strings; zh-Hans-only branches bypass the packs

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:sandbox
labels.description: Sandbox, container, or OS-level isolation behavior

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
## Summary

The zh-Hans pack uses full-width punctuation almost everywhere (540 `：`, 124 full-width parentheses around Chinese text), but a group of strings, mostly the `/router` setup and test screens, uses ASCII `:` `;` `,` `(` `)` next to Chinese text. On screen this reads as mixed typography, for example `费用:${cost} (提供商报告)`, `TypeSafe 已于 2026-09-22 暂停新用户注册;新用户默认使用 OpenRouter 路由。` and `删除该表(或运行 /router off),每个 Auto 回合都会使用默认模型。`.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, re
zh = json.load(open("crates/localization/locales/zh-Hans.json"))
for k, v in zh.items():
    if re.search(r"[一-鿿][:;]|[,;:(][一-鿿]|[一-鿿]\),", v):
        print(k, repr(v))
PY
```

On `main` this lists 54 keys. After the fix 9 remain, all deliberate: the parenthesized row suffixes below and the `enter:运行` key-hint notation in `ComposerSlashMenuHint`.

## Strings

- `/router`: `RouterPresetFastHint`, `RouterPresetUnavailable`, `RouterTypesafeSignupPaused`, `RouterTestSaveHint`, `RouterTestNotMade`, `RouterTestDecision`, `RouterTestChoice`, `RouterTestCostReported`, `RouterTestCostUnreported`, `RouterTestUsage`, `RouterTestFailing`, `RouterNotSaved`, `RouterRuntimeNotReloaded`, `RouterCurrent`, `RouterCurrentFailing`, `RouterCustomHelpIntro`, `RouterCustomHelpOutro`
- Labels and usage lines written as `标签: `: `StatusPickerInstruction`, `ConfigPreviewLabel`, `ConfigNoMatchesPrefix`, `ConfigEdit{Scope,Current,Hint,New}Label`, `ConfigSearchLabel`, `HelpFilterPrefix`, `CmdChangePreviousVersion`, `ProfileUsage`, `CmdQueueUsage`, `CmdQueueDraftHeader`, `CmdQueueMissingIndex`, `CmdQueueTip`, `HomeAgentModeYoloTip`, `ApprovalFieldWhy`, `ApprovalFieldStop`, `SessionsNewTitlePrompt`, `FleetDestPathLine`, `FleetDestUnavailable`, `FleetSavesToChip`, `FleetSavesToUndecided` (also has stray spaces in `此项目 或 个人`), `FleetModelRowBlockedNotice`, `AutomationUsage`, `AutomationListFailed`, `AutomationDeletedRunsDetail`, `AutomationDeletePreview`

`标签: ` becomes `标签：`. Both are two terminal columns wide, so label alignment does not move.

Left as they are: the `键=动作, 键=动作` key-hint footers (`ConfigFooter*`, `ConfigEditFooter`), whose commas separate key bindings rather than Chinese clauses, and short parenthesized row suffixes such as `(默认)`, where switching to full-width parentheses would change the column width.

The zh-Hant pack has the same `/router` strings and a pack-wide `標籤: ` style. That is a separate decision for zh-Hant reviewers, so it is not changed here.

## Related: zh-Hans-only branches outside the packs

Some TUI surfaces still pick their text with `match locale { Locale::ZhHans => "...", _ => "English" }` instead of going through `MessageId`. Every other locale, zh-Hant and ja included, sees English there. This goes against `crates/localization/locales/AGENTS.md` ("Do not add renderer-local language branches"). Main sites on `main`:

- `crates/tui/src/commands/groups/core/constitution.rs`: the whole `/constitution` command, 67 branches
- `crates/tui/src/tui/setup/mod.rs`: 44
- `crates/tui/src/tui/views/mod.rs`: 21
- `crates/tui/src/tui/views/help.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/handlers.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tui/ui.rs`: model-drafting status lines
- `crates/tui/src/tui/approval/previews.rs`: approval labels `Goal`/`Children`/... translated only for zh-Hans
- `crates/engine/src/tools/approval_summary.rs`

Moving these into the packs needs translations for all 14 non-English packs, so it is listed here as follow-up and not changed in this fix.

issues.title: ANSI stripping leaves the final byte of ESC ( B and swallows text after a stray CSI

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:macos
labels.description: macOS-specific behaviour

issues.body:
### What happened?

`strip_ansi_impl` in `crates/sanitize/src/sanitize.rs` (behind `strip_ansi_into`, `strip_ansi_keep_sgr_into`, `visit_ansi_text` and `sanitize_text`) treats every escape sequence that is not CSI/OSC/DCS as exactly two bytes, and lets a CSI run until any byte in `0x40..=0x7E`. Real output breaks both assumptions:

| input | output on `main` | expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ESC ( B ok ESC [ m` (what `tput sgr0` prints for `xterm-256color`) | `Bok` | `ok` |
| `ESC # 8 x` | `8x` | `x` |
| `a ESC ESC [31m b` | `a[31mb` | `ab` |
| `ESC [ 中文` (stray CSI introducer) | `` (CJK text swallowed until the next ASCII letter) | `中文` |
| `ESC 中` | `` (the CJK character is dropped) | `中` |
| `strip_ansi_keep_sgr_into("ESC [ ESC ( 0 m")` | the whole span, raw `ESC ( 0` included, is passed through as if it were SGR | only well-formed SGR passes through |

1. An escape sequence with intermediate bytes (`ESC ( B`, `ESC ) 0`, `ESC # 8`, `ESC % G`) is three bytes. Skipping two leaves the final byte as visible text, so tool output from scripts that call `tput sgr0` shows a stray `B` in the TUI transcript, exports and notifications.
2. `ESC ESC [31m` consumes the second ESC as the "final byte" and prints `[31m`.
3. A CSI keeps scanning through bytes that cannot appear in one (controls, another ESC, UTF-8). After a stray `ESC [` every following CJK character is eaten until the next ASCII letter, and with `keep_sgr` a span holding a raw ESC is emitted as "SGR".

### Steps to reproduce

```rust
let mut out = String::new();
codewhale_sanitize::sanitize::strip_ansi_into("\u{1b}(Bok\u{1b}[m", &mut out);
assert_eq!(out, "ok"); // fails on main: "Bok"
```

Or run any shell command whose output contains `$(tput sgr0)` with `TERM=xterm-256color` and look at the tool output card.

### Expected

Follow the ECMA-48 shapes: an escape sequence is `ESC`, any intermediates `0x20..=0x2F`, then one final byte `0x30..=0x7E`; a CSI ends at its final byte and is abandoned at the first byte outside `0x20..=0x7E`, so the text after it is kept. Only a well-formed SGR passes through `strip_ansi_keep_sgr_into`.

### Version

`main` at 4b8a30009 (0.10.3 source), macOS.

issues.title: Workflow authoring: words in strings reject a workflow, fleet TOML keeps single quotes, a host binding stays visible

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

issues.body:
### What happened?

Valid workflow inputs are rejected or misread, and one internal host binding is visible to Workflow scripts.

1. **Construct words inside strings reject the whole workflow** (`crates/workflow/src/js_authoring.rs`, `reject_unsupported_constructs`). The deny list is matched against the whole source, string literals included. The structured `workflow` tool plan also goes through this path: the engine wraps `plan.nodes` in `workflow({...})`. A goal or prompt such as `"Make the fetch handler async and fix the import paths"` therefore fails with `unsupported construct: async`. The same happens for text containing `import `, `await `, `open(`, `exec(`, `readFile`, and similar. The object is only parsed as JSON and never run, so matching inside strings protects nothing.
2. **Single-quoted fleet TOML strings keep their quotes** (`crates/workflow/src/named_fleet.rs`, `parse_fleet_toml_minimal`). `strip_toml_comment` already understands TOML literal strings, but the value step only trims `"`. `name = 'stopship'` gives the name `'stopship'`, and `load_named_fleet_file` then fails with a name mismatch. `explore = 'scout'` resolves the role to `'scout'`. Basic-string escapes are also kept: `"a \"b\""` is read as `a \"b\"`.
3. **`__workflow_slot_dropped` stays visible to scripts** (`crates/workflow-js/src/vm.rs`). The prelude deletes the other `__workflow_*` host bindings after capturing them, but not this one, and the inventory test leaves it out too. A script can call `__workflow_slot_dropped("parallel","agent",7)` to emit a `FanoutSlotDropped` event. The engine then records a clean run as Degraded.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `compile_javascript_workflow("w.workflow.js", r#"workflow({ "goal": "Make the fetch handler async", "nodes": [] });"#)` returns `UnsupportedConstruct { construct: "async" }`.
2. `parse_named_fleet("name = 'stopship'\n[roles]\nexplore = 'scout'\n")` returns the name `'stopship'` and the role `'scout'`.
3. Run a Workflow script that returns `typeof __workflow_slot_dropped`. It returns `"function"`.

### Expected

The deny list applies to code, not to string contents. TOML literal and basic strings are unquoted (and unescaped) the way TOML defines. No `__workflow_*` host binding is reachable from a script.

### Where

`crates/workflow` and `crates/workflow-js`, main at 4b8a30009.

issues.title: Skill install and import reject or mangle ordinary package layouts (GitHub tarball prefix, dotfiles)

labels.name: area:install
labels.description: Install, npm wrapper, release artifacts, Homebrew, winget, Docker, Nix

issues.body:
### What happened?

Skill install and import reject, or silently mangle, packages with ordinary layouts.

1. **The archive prefix is guessed from the first tar entry only** (`crates/skill-install/src/install.rs`, `scan_tarball`). The comment says the prefix is used when every entry shares it, but only the first entry is checked. A GitHub tarball starts with `pax_global_header`, and even without it the first entry is the bare `repo-main/` directory. In both cases the prefix becomes empty. As a result:
   - `repo-main/demo/SKILL.md` matches none of the documented layouts, so the install fails with `MissingSkillMd`. The layout is `<name>/SKILL.md`, which the docs list as supported.
   - A repository with a root `SKILL.md` plus `skills/other/SKILL.md` installs `other`. The docs say the repo-root `SKILL.md` comes first.
   - A direct tarball made with `tar czf s.tgz scripts/run.sh SKILL.md` gets the prefix `scripts`. Only `scripts/*` is extracted, flattened to the skill root, and `SKILL.md` is dropped. The install reports success, but the installed directory has no `SKILL.md`.
2. **Importing a skill that contains a dotfile always fails** (`crates/skills/src/mutation.rs`, `copy_dir_regular_files`). The copy skips every `.`-prefixed file and directory. `compute_package_digest` deliberately includes hidden files, so the copied package never matches the expected digest. Importing `~/.claude/skills/x` that contains `.DS_Store`, `.gitignore` or `.config/` fails with `imported content digest mismatch after copy; aborted`. The rollback is correct, so no data is lost.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `stage_tarball` on a gzip tar with entries `pax_global_header`, `repo-main/`, `repo-main/README.md` and `repo-main/demo/SKILL.md`. Result: `MissingSkillMd`.
2. Call `stage_tarball` on a tar with `scripts/run.sh` then `SKILL.md`. Result: the staged directory has no `SKILL.md`.
3. Create `.claude/skills/dotted/SKILL.md` plus `.claude/skills/dotted/.DS_Store`, then import it into the project scope. Result: digest mismatch error.

### Expected

The prefix is the first path component only when every entry shares it and it is a directory. Import copies the same files that the digest covers.

### Where

`crates/skill-install/src/install.rs` and `crates/skills/src/mutation.rs`, main at 4b8a30009.

issues.title: Git status panics or adds phantom rows on a worktree-side rename (non-ASCII original path)
issues.body:
### What happened?

`GET /v1/git` and `GET /v1/changes` misparse a worktree-side rename in `git status --porcelain=v1 -z`. When the original path starts with non-ASCII text, the request panics.

`parse_porcelain` (`crates/app-server/src/runtime_api/git.rs`) reads the extra original-path record only when the index column is `R` or `C`. Since Git 2.18, renames can also appear in the worktree column (`" R new\0old\0"`), for example when a moved file's new path is marked with `git add -N`. `porcelain_status` already maps `(_, 'R')` to `renamed`, but the parser treats the following `old` record as a status row of its own:

- With `old` = `ab说明.md`, `record[3..]` slices inside `说` and panics. The panic happens inside `spawn_blocking`, so every call returns 500 `git status failed` until the worktree changes.
- With an ASCII `old` such as `notes.txt`, a phantom row appears with index `n`, worktree `o` and path `es.txt`. It corrupts the file list, the staged and unstaged counts, and the row revision tokens.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
git init -q r && cd r
printf 'hello\nworld\n' > 'ab说明.md' && git add . && git commit -qm init
mv 'ab说明.md' new.md && git add -N new.md
git status --porcelain=v1 -z | od -c   # " R new.md\0ab说明.md\0"
```

Then open the workspace's Git/Changes view, or request `GET /v1/git`.

### Expected

The original path is read for a rename or copy in either column, and a short or malformed record never panics.

### Where

`crates/app-server/src/runtime_api/git.rs`, main at 4b8a30009. Git 2.53.

prs.title: fix(app-server): show the source of an outgoing worktree-side rename
prs.body:
## What and why

`split_by_workspace` projects repository-root rows into the workspace frame. When a rename leaves the workspace it synthesizes a `deleted` row so the source stays visible inside the workspace, but the guard was `row.index == "R"`.

Since #7310 the parser also returns a worktree-side rename (`" R outside.txt\0sub/a.txt\0"`), whose index column is a space. The guard is false for that shape, so the source — which really has disappeared from the workspace — appeared in **no** row of `GET /v1/git` or `GET /v1/changes`, while the index-side equivalent correctly produced a `deleted` row.

The guard now accepts a rename in either column, and the synthesized row carries the side the change actually lives in:

- worktree-side (`worktree == "R"`) → `worktree = "D"`, `staged = false`
- index-side → `index = "D"`, `staged = true` (unchanged)

The side is read from the worktree column instead of inferring it from `index == " "`. That is what keeps a copy out of this path by construction: only `R` synthesizes, because copying leaves the source in place and a `deleted` row for it would be false.

Staging safety is unchanged: the row still lands in `outside` with its root-relative `old_path`, and `compute_tokens` covers it. This is a listing gap, not a guard gap.

`docs/RUNTIME_API.md` and its `zh_hans` pair now say which side the synthesized row reports and that a copy is never shown this way.

## Where this came from

Closes #7324
Refs #7309

## How I tested it

Two new tests in the existing `runtime_api::git::tests` module.

`review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion` uses a real temporary repository, moves a tracked file out of the workspace from the worktree side (`git mv`, `git reset`, `git add -N`), and reads the workspace at its `sub/` subdirectory.

`outgoing_copy_keeps_its_source_inside_the_workspace` is a unit test on `split_by_workspace` with an index-side copy row, so the copy shape is pinned without needing a repository whose git config enables copy detection.

`cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- runtime_api::git` — **25 passed, 0 failed** (with `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`).

Both new tests fail on the shape they pin, which is the point of them:

- Before the fix, `review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion` fails because the source is in **no** row at all, not merely mislabelled:

```
thread 'review_outgoing_worktree_rename_exposes_source_deletion' panicked at
crates\app-server\src\runtime_api\git.rs:3256:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 0
 right: 1
```

- An earlier commit on this branch accepted `R` **or** `C` in the guard. On that version `outgoing_copy_keeps_its_source_inside_the_workspace` fails:


prs.body:
Refs #7250
Extracted from #7262

This is the maintainer-requested, opt-in verified evaluator slice. The evolutionary Draft PR remains separate and unchanged.

## Evaluator

- Freeze a versioned host spec, clean Git baseline, authorized write/protected scope, trusted public and held-out cases, executable identities, and a Linux bubblewrap capability probe.
- Accept completed Workflow worktrees; seal added/modified/deleted/binary/mode changes and replay from the sealed artifact after the writer worktree is gone.
- Run candidate commands in isolated processes and compare actual JSON output with the host oracle. Receipts bind spec, baseline, oracle, artifact/tree, sandbox and native binary identities. Public PASS requires public-plus-held-out replay.
- Wire the evaluator into the existing `operate_best_of_n` search Workflow only when `args.evaluator` is supplied. Results are `proposal_only`; there is no candidate apply, push, merge, policy genome, or mutation operator.

## Maintainer review fixes

- **Normal-user namespace creation:** the evaluator-specific `RLIMIT_NPROC` is 4096, and the probe reports that effective value. The old 32 limit counted all tasks owned by the Linux user. PID namespace isolation, `--die-with-parent`, cancellation, CPU/time bounds, filesystem/network restrictions and process cleanup remain in place.
- **Published-crate source identity:** the evaluator hashes the actual loaded Workflow source and compares it with a checked-in SHA-256 constant. The repository script path is referenced only by excluded test source. Exact checked-in content is accepted; a modified script fails closed. The update procedure is documented.
- **Evaluation deadline:** the aggregate budget counts active candidate evaluation and replay time, starting after generation. Receipts record effective start, elapsed time, deadline and stop reason; the delayed-generation regression passes.
- **Artifact capture:** a frozen policy records and excludes untracked root `target/` and `__pycache__/` outputs. Tracked and protected files remain checked, legitimate new source remains captured, and out-of-scope writes still fail. Exclusions appear in artifact and receipt provenance.
- **Descendant test and macOS:** the lifecycle test uses a writable in-sandbox marker, a surviving negative control, and timeout/cancellation cleanup checks. The non-Linux `UNSUPPORTED_ISOLATION` branch no longer has the unnecessary-return warning.

## Final validation at `61b889cf6ec10df5c048ef15715dbb272ccacf77`

- [Upstream PR CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43344788042): 10 successful jobs, 12 path-skipped, 0 failed. Workspace format, strict Clippy and Windows all-targets check passed. The PR view also counts the successful triage check.

A false PASS claim failed 2 public cases; the isolated candidate passed 2 public and 3 public-plus-held-out replay cases, ending `proposal_only`. No-evaluator and modified-source rejection controls passed. An independent verifier recomputed 7 case outcomes and 2 sealed tree hashes.

prs.title: fix(mcp,lsp): answer server requests instead of taking them as replies
prs.body:
## What and why

The MCP and LSP clients took a server's own requests for replies, and never answered them. Two commits.

- **Server requests taken as replies** (`crates/engine/src/mcp.rs`, `crates/lsp/src/client.rs`)
  - Root cause: a JSON-RPC message with a `method` is a request or a notification, never a reply. Both clients matched any message that carried an `id` against their own pending requests. Servers number their requests independently, so a server `ping` (MCP) or `workspace/configuration` (LSP) that shared an id with an in-flight request resolved that request with no result. The real reply was then dropped, and the server's request was never answered.
  - Fix: both clients skip messages with a `method` when they match replies, and answer server requests. MCP replies to `ping` with an empty result and to anything else with `-32601`. LSP replies `-32601` through the outbound queue, without blocking the dispatcher.
- **A failed answer no longer fails the request in flight** (`crates/engine/src/mcp.rs`, `crates/engine/src/mcp/http.rs`)
  - Root cause: in the first commit, the answer was sent with `self.send(reply).await?`. A failed send failed the `tools/call` it interrupted, although the server's real reply was still on its way, and marked the connection disconnected. Over HTTP, a 404/405/406/415/501 on that POST also made the transport fall back to legacy SSE and drop the Streamable HTTP messages still queued for the request in flight.
  - Fix: the answer goes through a new `McpTransport::send_reply`, which defaults to `send`. `HttpTransport` overrides it to report a refusal without changing mode. A failure is logged at debug level and not propagated, and the connection state is left alone.

## Where this came from

Closes #7306

## How I tested it

- New regression tests. Each one fails without this change and passes with it:
  - `call_method_answers_server_requests_instead_of_taking_them_as_the_reply` (MCP)
  - `server_request_sharing_a_pending_id_is_answered_not_taken_as_the_reply` (LSP)
  - `call_method_keeps_its_reply_when_answering_a_server_request_fails` (MCP)
  - `refused_reply_to_a_server_request_does_not_fall_back_to_sse` (MCP over HTTP)
- `cargo test -p codewhale-lsp`: 65 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib mcp::`: 373 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the changed crates: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (not applicable: bug fix only)

prs.title: fix(execpolicy): hold deny rules against rebound command words and more launchers
prs.body:
**This touches command deny rules, which CONTRIBUTING lists as trust-boundary surface (sandbox policy) that needs maintainer sign-off first.** I opened #7305 with the reproduction before this PR. Please confirm the direction before reviewing the code; I am happy to change the approach or close this if you prefer to handle it yourselves.

## What and why

With a deny rule for `rm`, these spellings ran `rm` and were allowed, including under `AskForApproval::Never` (`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs`). Two commits.

- **Rebound command words and launchers** (first commit)
  - `hash -p /bin/rm r; r x` (bash) and `hash r=/bin/rm; r x` (zsh) bind a new name to an executable. Now the `hash -p` path and the zsh `hash` value are expanded as code.
  - `alias qq='rm -rf'; eval qq /`: zsh expands the alias in code it parses later, and the alias value is code. Now alias values are expanded as code.
  - `=rm x`: zsh replaces a leading `=cmd` word with the path of `cmd`. Now a command word starting with `=` is known only at run time.
  - `parallel rm ::: x`, `parallel 'rm {}' ::: x`, `chpst -u nobody rm x` and `screen -dmS s rm x` run their operands as a command. `chpst`, `parallel` and `screen` are added to the wrapper table, and `parallel` joins its operands like `watch`. Only option values are listed for the new wrappers, so every other option is read both ways.
  - `at now <<< 'rm x'` and `echo 'rm x' | batch` run a script read from stdin, like `sh <<< ...`. `at` / `batch` stdin is now treated like a shell's: a heredoc body is expanded as the script, and other stdin is dynamic.
- **`parallel` with no command, and `at` job queries** (second commit)
  - **`parallel ::: `**: with no command of its own, `parallel` runs each input line, or each argument after `:::`, as a command line. `echo 'rm x' | parallel` and `parallel ::: 'rm x'` therefore still ran `rm`: the `:::` separator was taken as the inner command head, and nothing after it was checked. Now, when there is no real command after `parallel` (the separators `:::`, `:::+`, `::::` and `::::+` do not count as one), the line is dynamic, and each argument after `:::` / `:::+` is expanded as code. Arguments after `::::` / `::::+` are file names whose contents are not read, so they stay covered only by the dynamic marking.
  - **`at` / `batch` queries**: with the first commit, `at -l`, `at -r 3`, `at -d 3`, `at -c 3` and `batch -l` were treated as reading a job script from stdin, so these queries were refused next to any deny rule under `Never`. They only list, remove or print jobs, so they are exempt now.
  - **Why `at -q` is not exempt**: `-q QUEUE` only chooses the queue. `echo 'rm x' | at -q b now` still reads a job from stdin and schedules it, so it stays dynamic. `-q`, `-f` and `-t` take a value, which is skipped when looking for `-l`/`-r`/`-d`/`-c`, so `at -q a -l` is still a query and `at -qb now` is not. `at -f script.sh now` also stays dynamic. An option word that the shell rewrites at run time is not trusted, so it never makes a line exempt.

Still out of scope, as the issue says: `tmux new 'cmd'` / `tmux send-keys`, `screen -X stuff`, and other programs that take keystrokes or code in their own syntax.

## Where this came from

Closes #7305

## How I tested it

- New rows in `HIDDEN_RM` (`crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`), checked by `deny_rules_hold_against_runtime_resolved_and_reserved_word_spellings` and `file_rules_fail_closed_on_runtime_resolved_words`. All 19 new rows are allowed on `main` (both tests fail) and denied with the fix:
  - `alias qq='rm -rf'; eval qq /`, `hash -p /bin/rm r; r x`, `hash r=/bin/rm; r x`, `=rm x`
  - `parallel rm ::: x`, `parallel 'rm {}' ::: x`, `parallel -j 2 -- rm ::: x`, `echo 'rm x' | parallel`, `parallel ::: 'rm x'`, `parallel -j 2 ::: ls 'rm x'`, `parallel :::: cmds.txt ::: 'rm x'`
  - `chpst -u nobody rm x`, `screen -dmS s rm x`
  - `at now <<< 'rm x'`, `echo 'rm x' | batch`, `at now <<EOF ... EOF`, `echo 'rm x' | at -q b now`, `echo 'rm x' | at -qb now`, `at -f script.sh now`
- New rows in `ordinary_commands_stay_allowed_next_to_a_deny_rule`, which stay allowed: `alias ll='ls -la'`, `hash -r`, `parallel echo ::: a b`, `at -l`, `at -q a -l`, `at -r 3`, `at -d 3`, `at -c 3`, `batch -l`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-execpolicy`: 236 + 1 + 11 + 8 + 1 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-execpolicy --all-targets`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (not applicable: bug fix only)

prs.title: fix(sanitize): mask provider keys written next to CJK text
prs.body:
## What and why

The bare-token pass of `redact_secrets` and `redact_model_bound_secrets` (`crates/sanitize/src/redact.rs`, also the last step of `sanitize_text`) missed provider keys written in CJK prose:

- `密钥：sk-…`, `我的密钥是sk-…`, `（ghp_…）` and a key after U+3000 passed through unmasked.
- `sk-…，然后重试` was masked together with the Chinese text after it.

- **Root cause**: the pass split a line on ASCII spaces and trimmed only ASCII punctuation from each word. CJK text puts no space around a key, so the key and the text around it formed one word that matched no token shape.
- **Fix**: credential tokens are ASCII, so each word is now checked one ASCII run at a time, with the existing trims and token shapes. Each run that is a token is masked, and the non-ASCII text around it is kept. An ASCII-only word is a single run and is handled exactly as before.

Not covered here, as the issue says: keyed assignments with a full-width colon and a non-prefixed value (`password：hunter2`) and Chinese key names (`密码=…`). Those need vocabulary decisions, not a split fix.

## Where this came from

Closes #7301

## How I tested it

- New regression test `a_bare_token_next_to_cjk_text_or_full_width_punctuation_is_masked`. It fails on `main` (`密钥：sk-…` unchanged) and passes with the fix.

prs.title: fix(net): match network entries written as internationalized domains
prs.body:
**This touches network policy, which CONTRIBUTING lists as trust-boundary surface that needs maintainer sign-off first.** I opened #7302 with the reproduction before this PR. Please confirm the direction (compare entries and hosts in the IDNA ASCII form) before reviewing the code; I am happy to change the approach or close this if you prefer to handle it yourselves.

## What and why

A `[network]` entry written with a non-ASCII domain never matched (`crates/net/src/network_policy.rs`). With `deny = ["例子.com"]`, `https://例子.com/` was allowed under `default = "allow"` and prompted under `prompt`. `/network deny 例子.com` writes exactly such an entry. Allow entries never matched either.

- **Root cause**: hosts reach `NetworkPolicy::decide` from `Url::host_str`, which returns the IDNA ASCII form (`xn--fsqu00a.com`). `normalize_host` only lowercased ASCII, so an entry typed as `例子.com`, `*.中国` or `BÜCHER.de` was compared in a different form from the host.
- **Fix**: `normalize_host` converts a non-ASCII name to the URL parser's ASCII form, so entries and hosts use the same form. The `*.` / `.` wildcard prefix is kept. ASCII entries take the same path as before and are unchanged. A name the URL parser rejects is kept as written, as before.

## Where this came from

Closes #7302

## How I tested it

- New regression test `deny_entries_match_internationalized_domain_names` (`例子.com`, `*.中国`, `BÜCHER.de`). It fails on `main` (`https://例子.com/` -> `Allow`) and passes with the fix.

prs.title: fix(config): read every env alias chain through env_non_blank
prs.body:
## What and why

A variable exported empty (for example `CODEWHALE_MODEL=` from a compose `${VAR:-}` template) still hides its legacy alias. `CODEWHALE_MODEL= DEEPSEEK_MODEL=legacy-model` resolves to the default model instead of `legacy-model`.

- **Root cause**: `env_non_blank` exists so that a blank variable does not shadow its alias, but most of `EnvRuntimeOverrides::load` still read `env::var(A).or_else(|_| env::var(B)).ok().filter(non_blank)`. An empty `A` returns `Ok("")`, so the `or_else` never runs, the filter then drops the empty value, and the set `B` is ignored.
- **Affected**: every alias chain listed in the issue: `CODEWHALE_MODEL`, `CODEWHALE_BASE_URL`, `CODEWHALE_HTTP_HEADERS`, `DEEPSEEK_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and the NVIDIA, Volcengine, Wanjie, MiMo, Moonshot/Kimi, Hugging Face, Codex, Z.ai and StepFun chains, plus `CODEWHALE_FORCE_HTTP1` and `CODEWHALE_STREAM_OPEN_TIMEOUT_SECS` in `stream_timeouts.rs`.
- **Fix**: all of them read through `env_non_blank`.
- **Left alone on purpose**:
  - `CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT`: an empty value means "contact nobody".
  - `CODEWHALE_YOLO`: falling through to `DEEPSEEK_YOLO` would widen approval, so that needs its own decision.

**Note on the size of the diff:** the same commit also rewrites about 60 single-variable reads (`OPENROUTER_MODEL`, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL`, ...) from `env::var(X).ok().filter(non_blank)` to `env_non_blank(&["X"])`. `env_non_blank` does exactly that for one name, so those lines do not change behavior; they only remove the repeated filter chains (about 240 lines in total). If you prefer, I can split this into the alias fix and a separate cleanup PR.

`scripts/check-provider-registry.py` checked the Hugging Face base URL and model lookup order only as literal `std::env::var("NAME")` calls, so it failed once those chains read through `env_non_blank`. A second commit lets an `env_non_blank(&["HUGGINGFACE_BASE_URL", "HF_BASE_URL"])` list satisfy the check, since it states the same order; any other spelling still goes through the ordered `std::env::var` search.

Suggested changelog entry (kept out of the branch, as CONTRIBUTING asks):

> **Blank environment variables:** exporting a variable empty (for example `CODEWHALE_MODEL=` from a compose `${VAR:-}` template) no longer hides its legacy alias; `DEEPSEEK_MODEL`, `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, `KIMI_BASE_URL`, `DEEPSEEK_FORCE_HTTP1` and the other alias variables now apply as they do when the primary is unset (#7297).

## Where this came from

prs.title: fix(state,snapshot): keep index entries after a torn line and clamp prune age
prs.body:
## What and why

Two independent cases where on-disk state is lost, both from the linked issue. I can split them into two PRs if you prefer.

- **Session index: a torn last line swallows the next entry** (`crates/state/src/lib.rs`)
  - Root cause: a crash in the middle of an append leaves a final line with no trailing newline. The next `append_thread_name` wrote straight after it, so the new entry joined the fragment, the combined line failed to parse, and `session_index_map` skipped it. The name the caller had just saved was lost.
  - The existing torn-line test wrote its fragment with `writeln!`, so it never covered the unterminated case.
  - Fix: if the file is not empty and does not end in `\n`, the new entry starts on a new line.
- **Snapshot prune: a very large `max_age_days` deletes every snapshot** (`crates/snapshot/src/repo.rs`)
  - Root cause: the cutoff was `now - max_age.as_secs() as i64`. A `max_age_days` above about 1.07e14 (for example `9223372036854775807` as "keep forever") gives more than `i64::MAX` seconds, the cast wraps negative, the cutoff lands in the future, and every undo snapshot is pruned at startup.
  - Fix: clamp the age to `i64::MAX` and use `saturating_sub`.

This PR and #7317 (the fix for #7303) both touch `crates/snapshot/src/repo.rs`, in different functions. I checked that the two merge together without conflicts.

Suggested changelog entries (kept out of the branch, as CONTRIBUTING asks):

> - **Session index after a crash:** a session name saved right after a crash that cut off the previous index line is no longer lost; the new entry starts on its own line (#7298).
> - **Snapshot retention:** a very large `[snapshots] max_age_days` (such as `9223372036854775807` for "keep forever") no longer wraps around and deletes every undo snapshot at startup (#7298).

prs.title: fix: show non-ASCII paths as written in /diff and git mentions
prs.body:
## What and why

Two problems with non-ASCII file names from the linked issue.

- **Octal-escaped paths in `/diff`, `@git`, `@diff` and the Runtime API workspace diff**
  - Root cause: git quotes paths with non-ASCII bytes as octal escapes by default (`core.quotePath=true`). These readers passed that output on unchanged, so a file named `中文 目录/笔记 📝.md` reached the user and the model as `"\344\270\255..."`. The model-facing `git_status` / `git_diff` tools already pass `-c core.quotepath=false` (#1936).
  - Fix:
    - `Git::review_base` (`crates/dependencies`) sets `core.quotePath=false` next to its other runtime overrides. This covers `@git`, `@diff` and the Runtime API workspace diff.
    - The two `/diff` readers that do not go through it, the snapshot work-tree diff (`SnapshotRepo::work_tree_changes_since`) and the workspace git fallback (`workspace_git_diff`), pass `-c core.quotePath=false`.
- **Empty "Active paths" entry**
  - Root cause: the working-set path regex only matches ASCII segments. A message that carries the absolute path of a non-ASCII file (as an `@` mention does) stops at the workspace root, and `relativize_candidate` recorded that root as the empty path, shown as `-  (dir)` in `turn_meta`.
  - Fix: an empty relative path is no longer recorded.

This PR and #7316 (the fix for #7298) both touch `crates/snapshot/src/repo.rs`, in different functions. I checked that the two merge together without conflicts.

Suggested changelog entry (kept out of the branch, as CONTRIBUTING asks):

> **Non-ASCII file names:** `/diff`, the `@git` and `@diff` mentions and the Runtime API workspace diff now show paths with Chinese, emoji and other non-ASCII characters as written instead of as quoted octal escapes, and the turn context no longer lists the workspace root as an empty "Active paths" entry (#7303).

## Where this came from

- New regression tests. The first two fail on `main` and pass with the fix:

prs.title: fix(app-server): read the original path of worktree-side renames in git status
prs.body:
## What and why

The git status panel misread a rename that happened on the worktree side, for example a moved file after `git add -N`. Porcelain v2 `-z` output writes such a row as ` R new\0old\0`.

- **Root cause**: `parse_porcelain` read the original-path record only when the *index* column was `R` or `C`. For a worktree-side rename, the original path was left in the stream and parsed as a row of its own.
  - With an ASCII name, that row showed up as a phantom entry.
  - With a name that starts with multibyte text, such as `ab说明.md`, `record[3..]` panicked: `start byte index 3 is not a char boundary`.
- **Fix**: the original-path record is read when either column is `R` or `C`. The path slice uses `record.get(3..)`, so a record that is too short or not on a char boundary is skipped instead of panicking.

Closes #7309

prs.title: fix(app-server): read the original path of a worktree-side rename
prs.body:
## What and why

`parse_porcelain` in `crates/app-server/src/runtime_api/git.rs` read the extra original-path record of a rename/copy only when the **index** column was `R` or `C`.

Git reports a rename in either column, and since 2.18 the worktree column carries one when only the working tree moved — for example `git mv` followed by `git reset` and `git add -N`, which reports `" R new.md\0old.md\0"`. The original-path record was then parsed as a status row of its own:

- With a non-ASCII source (`ab说明.md`), `record[3..]` sliced at byte 3, inside `说` (`E8 AF B4`), and panicked. The panic happens inside `spawn_blocking`, so every `GET /v1/git` and `GET /v1/changes` returned 500 `git status failed` until the worktree changed.
- With an ASCII source, a phantom row appeared (`index = 'a'`, `worktree = '.'`, `path = "xt"`), corrupting the file list, the staged/unstaged counts and the row revision tokens.

The parser now reads the original path when either column reports a rename or copy, and slices the path through `get` before consuming the next field, so a malformed record is skipped instead of panicking and the record stream stays in sync.

## Where this came from

Refs #7309

## How I tested it

Two new tests in the existing `runtime_api::git::tests` module. Both use a real temporary repository and drive the same sequence the issue describes (`git mv`, `git reset`, `git add -N`), so neither mocks the parser input.

`cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- worktree_column_rename` — **2 passed, 0 failed**:

```
test runtime_api::git::tests::worktree_column_rename_reads_the_original_path ... ok
test runtime_api::git::tests::worktree_column_rename_with_non_ascii_source_does_not_panic ... ok
```

Before the fix the same two tests fail with exactly the reported symptoms:

```
thread 'worktree_column_rename_with_non_ascii_source_does_not_panic' panicked at
crates\app-server\src\runtime_api\git.rs:518:26:
start byte index 3 is not a char boundary; it is inside '说' (bytes 2..5 of string)

thread 'worktree_column_rename_reads_the_original_path' panicked at ...:
assertion `left == right` failed: the original path must not become a row: ["b.txt", "xt"]
  left: 2
 right: 1
```

The rest of the module, at the stack size this repository's tests need:

```
$ RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- runtime_api::git
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 756 filtered out
```

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` is clean. `cargo clippy -p codewhale-app-server --lib --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` is clean.

One unrelated note so it does not read as a gap: plain `cargo clippy -p codewhale-app-server ...` (with dependencies) stops on `codewhale-runtime` with `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` at `crates/runtime/src/...:723`. That error is present on `main` without this change, so I checked my crate with `--no-deps`.

## Adversarial review

An independent reviewer on a separate machine got the branch and tried to refute it without building. It confirmed the parser change against every porcelain v1 shape it could produce with git 2.39.5 — staged rename plus worktree delete (`"RD b.txt\0a.txt\0?? c.txt\0"`), chained `git mv` (`"R  c.txt\0a.txt\0"`), all eight conflict pairs, `!!`, `??` and `## ` — and found that porcelain v1 emits exactly one original-path record per rename/copy entry in either column, and that no non-rename entry ever carries `R` or `C` in either column. So the widened column test cannot over-consume or under-consume. `C` in the worktree column appears unreachable with current git (status rejects `--find-copies*`), which makes that half harmless belt-and-braces.

Two of its notes are addressed in the second commit:

- The `get(3..)` check is now above the `records.next()` call, so a record the parser cannot slice no longer consumes the next `\0` field first.
- `repo()` pins `status.renames=true`. The tests assert the rename shape git reports, but `Git::status_command` deliberately preserves global and system config so LFS filters keep working — on a machine with `status.renames=false` the tests would see ` D a.txt` plus `A b.txt` and fail for a reason unrelated to the parser.

One finding is left to a follow-up rather than widened into this PR, per the one-purpose rule:

- `split_by_workspace` (git.rs:564) synthesizes a `deleted` row when a rename leaves the workspace, but its guard is `row.index == "R"`. For a worktree-side rename the index column is a space, so the source path disappears from the listing entirely instead of being shown as a deletion. This is a pre-existing gap in the sibling path, newly reachable now that the parser returns such rows, and it does not weaken staging safety: the row still lands in `outside` with its root-relative `old_path`, and `compute_tokens` feeds outside rows into `members`, so the token still covers the source. It needs its own decision about the synthetic row's `staged` value.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`

- [x] Not a user-facing feature: no new flag or command, so `docs/features.toml` is unchanged

prs.body:
## What and why

Two zh-Hans display fixes, in separate commits. I can split them into two PRs if you prefer.

- **Full-width punctuation in the zh-Hans pack** (`crates/localization/locales/zh-Hans.json`, #7299)
  - The pack uses full-width punctuation almost everywhere, but 45 strings used ASCII `:` `;` `,` `(` `)` next to Chinese text. Most are the `/router` setup and test screens, plus `标签: ` labels and usage lines. Examples: `费用:${cost} (提供商报告)` and `删除该表(或运行 /router off),每个`.

  - Left as they are, as the issue describes: the key-hint footers and short parenthesized row suffixes such as `(默认)`, where full-width parentheses would change the column width.
  - Two existing tests that assert zh-Hans text, and one test comment, are updated to the new punctuation.
- **`/status` value column under CJK labels** (`crates/tui/src/commands/groups/config/status.rs`, #7304)

prs.title: fix(engine): honor env -S shebangs when resolving plugin interpreters
prs.body:
## What and why

`resolve_interpreter` in `engine/src/tools/plugin.rs` treats `#!/usr/bin/env <program>` specially and takes the first shebang argument as the program. A script that starts with `#!/usr/bin/env -S python3 -u` therefore spawned a program named `-S`, and the plugin tool failed to start. `env -S` (`--split-string`) is the usual way to pass interpreter flags through `env` on Linux and macOS.

The `env` branch now skips a leading `-S` or `--split-string` before it takes the program name. All other shebangs resolve as before.

prs.title: fix(tools): read every hunk line instead of stopping at twice the header counts
prs.body:
## What and why

`parse_hunk_header` in `crates/tools/src/patch_preflight.rs` stopped reading the hunk body after `2 * (old + new)` lines. Callers skip lines that do not start a header, so body lines past that cap were dropped without an error. `@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@` followed by five body lines kept only four, so the trailing `+e` was never applied. A header such as `@@ -1,18446744073709551615 +1,1 @@` also overflowed the multiplication: a panic in debug builds, and a wrap to a zero-length hunk in release.

The body loop now runs until the next `@@`, `diff `, file header or end of input. Every arm already consumes a line or breaks, so the loop ends. An under-counted hunk followed by prose now shows up as a context mismatch instead of a silent partial parse. The comment that described the cap is removed.

## Related issue (optional)

Refs #7274 (partial: the patch hunk item)

prs.title: fix(sanitize): strip whole escape sequences and keep the text after them
prs.body:
## What and why

ANSI stripping left stray characters in tool output and dropped text after a stray CSI.

- **Root cause 1**: `strip_ansi_impl` skipped exactly two bytes for every ESC sequence that is not CSI, OSC or DCS. Sequences with intermediate bytes are longer.
  - `tput sgr0` on xterm-256color prints `ESC ( B`, so tool output showed a stray `B`.
  - `ESC ESC [31m` printed `[31m`.
- **Root cause 2**: a CSI scanned through any byte until it found one in `0x40..=0x7E`.
  - After a stray `ESC [`, the following CJK text was dropped up to the next ASCII letter.
  - With `keep_sgr`, a span that held a raw ESC passed through as if it were SGR.
- **Fix**:
  - Other ESC sequences now consume their intermediate bytes (`0x20..=0x2F`) and one final byte (`0x30..=0x7E`). If no final byte follows, only the ESC is dropped.
  - A CSI stops at the first byte outside its parameter and intermediate range without a final byte. Nothing is emitted for it, and that byte is handled as ordinary text.

## Related issue (optional)

Closes #7300

## How I tested it

- New regression test `strip_ansi_consumes_whole_escape_sequences_and_keeps_following_text`. It fails on `main` (output `"Bok"` for `ESC ( B ok`) and passes with the fix.

## What and why

Three workflow authoring problems from the linked issue. They are independent, and I can split them into separate PRs if you prefer.

- **Construct deny list matched words inside strings** (`crates/workflow/src/js_authoring.rs`)
  - Root cause: `reject_unsupported_constructs` searched the whole source, string literals included. A goal or prompt that mentions "async", "import " or "open(" rejected the workflow. This also hit structured plans that the engine wraps in `workflow({...})`.

- **Fleet TOML kept quotes and escapes** (`crates/workflow/src/named_fleet.rs`)

- **`__workflow_slot_dropped` stayed visible to scripts** (`crates/workflow-js/src/vm.rs`)
  - Root cause: the prelude deletes every captured `__workflow_*` host binding from the global scope, except that `__workflow_slot_dropped` was missing from the list. A script could call it and emit `FanoutSlotDropped` events.

prs.title: fix(skills): detect the archive prefix from every entry and import hidden files
prs.body:
## What and why

Skill install and skill import rejected or damaged ordinary package layouts. This PR has two separate fixes from the linked issue. I can split them into two PRs if you prefer.

- **Install: archive prefix** (`crates/skill-install`)
  - Root cause: `scan_tarball` took the archive prefix from the first tar entry only. A GitHub tarball starts with `pax_global_header` or the bare `repo-main/` directory, so the prefix came out empty.
    - A repository laid out as `<name>/SKILL.md` failed with `MissingSkillMd`.
    - A nested `skills/<x>/SKILL.md` outranked the repository-root `SKILL.md`.
    - A flat tarball whose first entry was `scripts/run.sh` took `scripts` as the prefix and installed without its `SKILL.md`.
  - Fix: the first path component is the prefix only when every entry shares it as a directory. Global PAX headers are excluded. `SKILL.md` candidates are ranked after the prefix is known.
- **Import: hidden files** (`crates/skills`)
  - Root cause: import copied the package without `.`-prefixed files, but the package digest includes them. Any skill with a dotfile failed with "imported content digest mismatch".
  - Fix: the copy keeps hidden files. It skips the receipt markers (`.installed-from`, `.trusted`, `.system-installed-version`) only at the package root, which matches what the digest covers.

## Related issue (optional)

Closes #7307

## How I tested it

- New regression tests. Each one fails on `main` and passes with the fix:
  - `archive_prefix_comes_from_every_entry_not_the_first_one`

> AI-assisted report, requested by the affected user. Personal paths, addresses, account details and credentials have been omitted.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

During a macOS network investigation, two orphaned `ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'` processes in an OpenClaw source checkout were found; one was still receiving about 1.95 MB/s and the other had cumulatively received about 3.40 GB. **The process that originally launched them was not captured, so attribution to the OpenClaw updater or runtime is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.** This is a triage request based on an observed process-lifecycle/bandwidth problem, not a claim of malicious behavior or a confirmed current-release regression.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The incident was observed on one machine. The original invoking command/application and the moment the parent exited were not recorded. I have not reproduced this on a clean installation or the latest release, and do not want to present diagnostic commands as reproduction steps.

### Expected behavior

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Requested outcome: when a caller cancels or exits, any Git/SSH transfers it owns should terminate; update/status checks should avoid downloading unnecessary repository history. Whether the original caller was OpenClaw remains unverified.

### Actual behavior

Read-only process and network sampling showed:

| PID | Parent PID | SSH target / command | Cumulative received bytes, sample 1 → sample 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 17503 | 1 (`launchd`) | `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o SendEnv=GIT_PROTOCOL git@github.com git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'` | 3,399,071,394 → 3,399,071,394 |
| 72834 | 1 (`launchd`) | same command | 332,215,030 → 336,123,532 |

Samples were approximately 2 seconds apart. PID 72834 received 3,908,502 bytes during that interval (~1.95 MB/s); PID 17503 was idle during that interval. The 3.40 GB is a cumulative process counter, **not** an additional 3.40 GB downloaded during the sample and not a measured total VPN charge.

Both processes had the source checkout as their current directory. `lsof` showed stdout directed to `/dev/null`. FlClash independently attributed the active GitHub port 22 connection to an outbound proxy route. That connection's cumulative counter rose from ~104 MB to ~525 MB during the investigation.

### OpenClaw version

Installed npm-global CLI: 2026.6.11.
A separate local source checkout was also present at commit `105a6307cceb`.
Which executable/version initiated the SSH commands: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2, arm64

### Install method

npm global CLI plus a separate Git source checkout. The Gateway launch agent existed but was not loaded when inspected.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

Observed network path: SSH → github.com:22 → FlClash proxy route.
Model/provider path that initiated the operation: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Logs

```text
nettop cumulative bytes_in, about 2 s apart:
ssh.17503: 3399071394 -> 3399071394
ssh.72834:  332215030 ->  336123532

ps:
17503 PPID=1 ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'
72834 PPID=1 ssh ... git-upload-pack 'openclaw/openclaw.git'
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The figures above are transcribed from direct `ps`, `lsof`, `nettop` and FlClash observations on 2026-11-12. Raw screenshots include unrelated personal network details and are intentionally not attached.

### Impact and severity

Observed on one machine: sustained background transfer over a metered proxy, manual investigation and termination required. One process had received ~3.40 GB cumulatively; the other was actively receiving ~1.95 MB/s during sampling. Frequency and other affected versions/systems: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information

- Sending SIGTERM to both identified processes stopped them; a follow-up process check showed both absent.
- The user subsequently uninstalled the local installation. This report does not claim that stopping the Gateway alone would have stopped the SSH processes.
- Related but **not established as the same root cause**: #176152 (update checks fetching broad branch history) and #127591 (SSH descendant cleanup on termination).
- Could maintainers advise which diagnostics would distinguish an OpenClaw-owned update/fetch from an editor, agent or other tool operating on the checkout? If this cannot be attributed to OpenClaw, please reclassify/close rather than treating it as a confirmed updater bug.

issues.body:
# Draft — upstream issue: iOS node auth and connection state are opaque

**Status:** DRAFT — not posted. Tom to review before filing.
**Evidence collected:** 2026-10-24, Strix, OpenClaw 2026.10.3, iOS app `ui v2026.10.50` (node reports `v2026.10.30` — see §3).

---

## Summary

The iOS app reports a connected state that the gateway does not agree with, offers no visible way to
correct or re-enter gateway credentials, and renders no notification when a command is dispatched and
not delivered. Two distinct defects, one shared cause: **the app never tells the user what it is
actually doing.**

## Issue 1 — Paired node appears connected while authentication fails on every reconnect

**Observed.** With the app open and the user believing they were signed in:

```
[ws] unauthorized conn=5eb9ccb4… client=iPhone ui v2026.10.50 role=operator scopes=3
     auth=password device=yes platform=iOS 27.0.1
     reason=password_mismatch
     guidance=unauthorized: gateway password mismatch (provide gateway auth password)
     phase=auth_credentials_received cause=unauthorized handshake=failed
```

Immediately followed by a second connection attempt 6 minutes later, likewise rejected, with the node
command surface withheld.

Meanwhile `openclaw nodes describe --node iPhone` reported `paired · connected`, and
`openclaw nodes notify` returned `{"ok": true, "command": "system.notify"}`.

**Impact.** Every node-mediated capability silently degraded: notifications never rendered, APNs never
registered (`has no APNs registration (connect iOS node first)`), and a voice message dictated on a
paired Apple Watch never arrived. The failure is invisible from both ends — the app shows connected, and
the gateway CLI returns success.

**Asks.**

1. **Surface auth failure in the app.** A rejected handshake should put the device in a visible
   "not signed in" state, not an apparently-connected one.
2. **Provide a reachable credential entry point.** There appears to be no documented path to re-enter the
   gateway password once a device identity exists. The only way out was to make the node forget its
   session entirely.
3. **Do not report success for a command that was not delivered.** `nodes notify` returned `ok: true`
   while the journal recorded `node wake … connected=false reason=not_connected`. The CLI result
   described the request, not the delivery.

## Issue 2 — Connection and activity state are not legible

**Observed.** During the same session the user could not tell:

- whether the app was connected or merely paired;
- whether Talk Mode had an active session;
- whether a voice message had been submitted, was in flight, or had failed;
- whether a notification had been sent to the device.

The Talk Mode indicators and icons convey activity in a way the user could not interpret, and there is no
visible record of submitted-versus-delivered.

**Impact.** The user spent a morning on five separate channel attempts because nothing on screen
distinguished "waiting", "failed", and "delivered". This is not cosmetic: without a legible state the
user cannot self-diagnose, so every failure becomes a support request.

**Asks.**

1. **Distinct, labelled states** for paired / connecting / connected / auth-failed.
2. **A visible outbound log** in-app: what was sent, when, whether it was accepted by the gateway and
   delivered to the device.
3. **Talk Mode state made explicit** — listening, thinking, speaking, idle — with icons whose meaning is
   discoverable rather than inferred.

## Issue 3 — The same gateway is listed twice under one URL

**Observed.** "Manage Gateways" presents **two entries that both display `gateway.example-tailnet.ts.net:443`** —
identical name, identical port, no way to distinguish them.

**Ruled out as a host-side duplication.** `controlUi.allowedOrigins` contains exactly one origin
(`https://gateway.example-tailnet.ts.net`), `gateway.publicOrigin` is that same origin, and the gateway listens on
loopback `18789` behind one serve route. A second `tailscale serve` entry exists on `:10443`, but it proxies
to `127.0.0.1:8877` — a different service — and is not in the app's list. So the duplicate is **client-side
list state**, not two gateways on the host.

**Impact.** With two indistinguishable entries, a user has no way to know which is live. If one is a stale
cached record, picking it produces a connection that fails for no visible reason — and reinforces the
"it says Connected but nothing works" experience described above.

**Asks.**

1. **De-duplicate** on the resolved origin, or label entries when they resolve identically.
2. **Show which entry is live** (last successful handshake, auth state) rather than name only.

## Issue 4 — Three surfaces, three contradicting stories

Summarising the same moment on one device:

| Surface | What it said |
|---|---|
| App top bar | "Connected" |
| Manage Gateways | Two identical `:443` entries |
| Gateway journal | `password_mismatch`, `handshake=failed`, `connected=false reason=not_connected` |

None of the three agreed. This is the core of the report: the app is not merely vague about its state,
it is **self-contradictory**, which makes user-side diagnosis impossible.

## Reproduction

1. Pair an iPhone. Change `gateway.auth.password` on the host afterwards.
2. Open the app. It attaches a device identity and loops on `password_mismatch`, but presents as connected.
3. From the host: `openclaw nodes notify --node iPhone --body test` → returns `ok: true`; nothing appears.
4. `openclaw nodes push --node iPhone` → `no APNs registration`. `watch.notify` → `node not connected`.
5. Every attempt fails; the user sees success.

## Environment

- Gateway: OpenClaw 2026.10.3, Linux 7.0.0-38-generic, `mode: local`, `auth.mode: password`
- iOS app: reports `ui v2026.10.30` in `nodes describe`, `v2026.10.50` in the WS handshake log — the
  version disagreement is itself worth a look
- `gateway.auth.allowTailscale` unset; Tailscale Serve is in use at `gateway.example-tailnet.ts.net`

## Not claiming a clean-room reproduction

Reported from a single working installation, from the user's side of the app rather than from inside the iOS
codebase: no debugger, no Swift sources, no ability to instrument the handshake. The evidence offered is
what the client and gateway logs make visible. **A clean re-pair has deliberately not
been performed**: the setup currently works, and dismantling it to satisfy a review would convert a
working system into a broken one for the duration. If a maintainer needs that evidence, please ask and
say specifically what to capture (inbound session key, handshake log lines, or a fresh-pairing trace) —
it will be provided rather than guessed at.

## Possible mitigation on our side (not a fix for the asks above)

`gateway.auth.allowTailscale: true` lets Control UI and WebSocket sign-in use tailnet identity instead of a
shared password — documented as "no shared secret to distribute." This removes the drift class entirely,
but it is a workaround for an app that cannot report its own state.

---

*Draft notes for Tom: filed as observed behaviour from one working install. The "Not claiming a clean-room
reproduction" section sets that boundary explicitly and invites a specific evidence request rather than
offering a dismantle-and-rebuild. The four issues are separable, so a maintainer can act on one without
taking on all.*

issues.body:
## Use case

A shared Slack builder can start an authorized coding task and receive private child completion, but cannot persist a later CI/review checkpoint for the same conversation. The requester is an admitted Slack user, not a Gateway owner. We need this to survive Gateway restarts without granting workspace users control-plane administration.

## Observed on 2026.10.8

- Native Slack request; configured agent permits `automations` (`cron` alias).
- Requester is not a configured Gateway owner.
- Native tool discovery omits `automations`; a real Slack probe could not create a one-minute same-thread reminder.
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` includes `automations` in `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOOLS`, then `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS`.
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` applies that owner-only deny to the admitted non-owner turn. An ordinary allowlist does not override it.
- The automation tool and creator-authority code otherwise describe requester-scoped new-job creation. It is unclear which non-owner channel surface can reach that functionality.

Reproduction: admit a non-owner human to a Slack channel and an agent whose tool policy allows `automations`; ask it to schedule one reply in that thread after one minute. Inspect the actual tool catalog and accepted job, rather than accepting the model's promise. In our test, no automation tool or job was available.

The same ingress restriction remains in upstream `main` at `a8fe857038f62b209d7ef0b81e62b4a49fdfdbee`: `resolveGatewayScheduledToolAccess` exempts a verified scheduled occurrence's self-job tool, while ingress turns retain the owner-only rule. The newer `tools.gatewayPolicy.automations.scope: "caller"` restricts administrative grants; it does not itself expose this tool to non-owner ingress.

## Requested native capability

An explicitly enabled, caller-scoped schedule/checkpoint for an admitted conversation, with the runtime binding the creator, agent, account and original session. It should retain the caller's effective tool restrictions, permit cancellation/inspection only within that scope, and resume the original conversation for reconciliation and delivery.

This does not require command jobs, arbitrary destinations, cross-session wakes, global job administration, or making ordinary Slack users Gateway owners. Those can retain their existing restrictions.

## Acceptance cases

1. An admitted non-owner creates one bounded same-thread checkpoint and receives an accepted job ID.
2. Another requester/session cannot inspect, change, cancel or redirect it.
3. Restart preserves the accepted checkpoint and its caller restrictions.
4. On execution the original conversation reconciles current state and replies once; intermediate/raw child output is not announced independently.
5. Expiry, cancellation and completion stop the obligation without duplicate effects.
6. Command payloads, broader tool grants and foreign delivery targets remain unavailable.

## Related work

[Issue #41586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41586) was resolved by native child-completion delivery. That path works for us. This request concerns a later external-work checkpoint after the child is idle, rather than child completion.

We verified an operator-installed one-shot command calling native `wake` with delivery disabled as an operator maintenance procedure. It survives restart and returns to the parent conversation, but does not solve requester scheduling. We have not patched core, added a privileged CLI wrapper, or broadened channel users into owners.

Is a supported requester-scoped ingress path intended already, or should this be tracked as a separate native capability?

issues.body:
### Summary

On a single-operator gateway where agents coordinate with each other in chat, an agent cannot create its own scheduled jobs unless the turn was started by a configured owner (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`) or an authenticated Control UI administrator. The `automations` tool sits in `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS` together with `gateway`, `plugins`, `sessions`, `terminal` and others, so the only way to let an agent schedule its own work from a non-owner turn is to make that sender a full owner. That also grants config, restart and session control.

We'd like a narrower, documented permission: an agent can create, update and remove automations that it owns, for itself, without receiving any other owner-only tool.

### Current behavior (2026.9.7, read in source and docs; we have not built a fork)

- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts:55, 62–74`: `automations` is in `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_TOOLS`, which is part of `GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS`.
- `src/agents/tools/session-portal-target.ts:29–36`: for `senderIsOwner === false`, the whole owner-only list is denied, except that `automations` stays when the run holds an automation grant.
- `src/auto-reply/command-auth.ts` (owner resolution): owner = an explicit `commands.ownerAllowFrom` entry, or an internal channel with `operator.admin`. Channel allowlists and wildcards don't count (2026.9.5 release notes, "Automation owners and maintenance notices").
- `docs/automation/cron-jobs/managing-jobs.md` ("Conversational management"): creation from chat is for configured owners and fresh Control UI administrator turns. A `sessions_yield` continuation keeps management only.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.ts:104–105` and `tools/cron-tool.ts` (self-remove scope): a scheduled run can manage only its own job.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.policy.ts` (`SUBAGENT_TOOL_DENY_ALWAYS`): subagents never get `automations`.

Net effect: an agent can't schedule follow-up work for itself from its normal turns (a teammate's message, a peer agent, its own planning) unless a human owner starts that turn. The agent's runtime can still create jobs through the operator CLI, but an agent that follows the tool boundary as intended won't use the CLI to get around a withheld tool. So the result is no autonomous scheduling at all.

### Proposed behavior

A config-level, per-agent grant (name illustrative), for example:

```json5
agents: { list: [{ id: "main", automations: { selfManage: true } }] }
```

When it's enabled, that agent's turns receive the `automations` tool limited to:
- creating jobs whose target agent is itself (no `--agent` other than its own id);
- listing, getting, updating, running and removing jobs it created (by creator attribution);
- no access to other agents' jobs, and no other owner-only tool (`gateway`, `plugins`, `sessions`, `terminal`, …).

Requirements we'd consider essential:
- **Operator-controlled on/off.** The grant lives in gateway config, which only an owner or operator can write. An agent can never grant it to itself.
- **Revocation checked at commit.** Turning it off (or removing the agent's entry) takes effect for the next mutation: the grant is re-checked when it is minted and again before each create/update/remove commits, like the existing `isCurrent()` checks on owner grants.
- **Execution caps preserved.** Jobs created under this grant keep today's scheduled-execution rules: captured tool caps / `scheduledToolPolicy`, creator attribution, explicit `toolsAllow` where required. The grant controls who may create, not what a job may run.
- **Scheduled planning turns included.** A granted agent's own scheduled run (e.g. a daily planning job) may create and manage that agent's own jobs. That is the core of the requested autonomy. Today such runs are limited to removing themselves.
- **Subagents unchanged.** Subagent restrictions don't need to change for this request.

Every grant use is audited, as admin management already is.

### Why this matters

Multi-agent setups where agents plan their own work (daily planning, follow-ups, reminders) currently need either a human in every scheduling turn, or full owner rights for an agent account. The first defeats autonomy. The second is broader than needed and is exactly what the owner-only boundary exists to prevent.

### What we checked / didn't

Read the 2026.9.7 source and docs listed above. Keyword-checked the 2026.9.8 and 2026.9.9 changelogs for automation/owner/scheduling changes; none in this area found. Searched existing issues: no exact match found; related scoped-management requests exist (below). We did not test a patched build.

### Related

- #164880: a similar request for a narrow, sender-scoped authority (abort-only) instead of full owner rights.
- #158055: owner authority is not carried into `sessions_spawn` children, so delegated work loses owner-only tools.
- #138253: consistent owner verification across channels.
- #141201: one-time, scoped authorization for project automation management from Telegram forum topics, instead of repeating requests in the Control UI.

*Disclosure: this report was drafted by an AI agent that helps operate this gateway, at the operator's request, and reviewed by a second agent. The source references were read in the 2026.9.7 tree; no patched build was tested.*
