issues.body:
## Operator problem

An operator who drives OpenClaw from a shell cannot read an agent's workspace. The workspace is where durable agent output lands (`notes/`, plans, generated reports, screenshots), and today the only supported read paths are UI clients: the Control UI workspace browser and the mobile **Files** screens. `src/cli` and `src/commands` contain zero references to `agents.workspace.*`, so there is no `list` and no `get`.

The situation that hurts: the Gateway runs somewhere else (SSH on a shared host, a container, or a remote/bridged workspace where the workspace directory does not exist on the operator's disk). The operator wants one file out of an agent workspace — `openclaw agents workspace get notes/report.md > report.md` — and instead has to open a browser, click through the Control UI, and copy-paste. CI jobs and scripts cannot do that at all, and on a bridged workspace there is no local path to `ls`.

`openclaw agents files list/get` (issue #197715, PR #197814) does not cover this: it is deliberately limited to the fixed bootstrap filename set, and its `name` parameter is validated against `ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES`, so `notes/plan.md` is rejected as `unsupported file`.

## Existing-solutions preflight

1. **`openclaw agents files list/get`** — fixed bootstrap document set only (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `TOOLS.md`, …) with a `missing`/`expectedAbsent` classification. Nested workspace paths are rejected by the canonical handler, so it is not an alternative for browsing `notes/` or reading an exported image.
2. **Control UI / Android / iOS** — these are clients over the same two RPCs (`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/WorkspaceFilesScreen.kt`, `apps/ios/Sources/Design/AgentWorkspaceFilesScreen.swift`). They prove the RPC pair is the canonical read path for operator clients; they do not help shells, scripts, or CI. The CLI is the operator client that is missing.
3. **Reading the workspace from disk** — only correct when the CLI runs on the Gateway host with read access to the real workspace path. `docs/plugins/sdk-agent-harness/core-ownership.md` documents that a trusted host plugin can bind the existing `agents.workspace.*` RPCs to a provisioned remote workspace, so disk access is explicitly not the contract. Disk reads also bypass the handler's realpath confinement.
4. **`openclaw sessions ...`** — session-scoped. The workspace browser is agent-scoped (`agentId`), so session commands are not a substitute.
5. **A plugin that shells out** — would have to re-implement path safety (realpath confinement, symlink/hardlink escape rejection), the 5 MiB image cap, UTF-8 validation and the image MIME allow-list, and its output would not be bounded by the Gateway. The handler already owns all of that; a forwarding CLI command does not.
6. **A `gateway call` one-liner** — possible but not a surface: operators would have to hand-write JSON params, decode base64 themselves, and lose the table/byte-exact output. The repository treats first-class CLI verbs as the operator surface for existing RPCs (`sessions files`, `sessions artifacts`, `agents files`, …).

## Bounded outcome

Add two read-only verbs under the existing `agents` command group, forwarding to the canonical RPCs and formatting the responses:

- `openclaw agents workspace list [--path <dir>] [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--agent <id>] [--json]` → `agents.workspace.list`. Text mode prints a header (`path`, `totalEntries`, `offset`) plus a `name` / `kind` / `size` / `updatedAt` table; `--json` prints the RPC result unchanged.
- `openclaw agents workspace get <path> [--agent <id>] [--json]` → `agents.workspace.get`. Text mode writes the payload to stdout **byte-for-byte** (no appended newline, so `> file` redirection reproduces the Gateway-reported size) and puts `size`, `mimeType`, and `encoding` on stderr. `--json` prints the RPC result unchanged.
- Register `["agents","workspace","list"]` and `["agents","workspace","get"]` as exact `command-catalog` entries with `loadPlugins: "never"`, and `ownsProtocolStdout: true` on `get` because it owns stdout.
- Document both verbs in `docs/cli/agents.md`.

**Non-goals**: no write, delete, upload, or rename verb (`agents.workspace.set` does not exist and this change does not add one); no protocol change (no cursor pagination — `--offset` is the numeric offset the RPC already exposes); no change to the handler, schema, path-safety rules, or size caps; no new root command; no change to `agents files` or `agents.workspace` semantics for UI clients.

## Canonical owner and decision surface

- **RPC**: `agents.workspace.list` / `agents.workspace.get`, scope `operator.read`, descriptors at `src/gateway/methods/core-descriptors.ts:407-408` (family `agents-workspace`, since 2026.7).
- **Handler (owns every decision)**: `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-workspace.ts` — `limit` default 250 / max 500, realpath confinement under the workspace root, symlink and hardlink escape rejection, `WORKSPACE_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` text cap, 5 MiB image cap with a magic-byte allow-list, and the error codes `workspace_path_invalid`, `workspace_path_not_found`, `workspace_file_not_found`, `workspace_file_too_large`, `workspace_file_unsupported`.
- **Schema**: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-workspace.ts` (`AgentsWorkspaceListParams/Result`, `AgentsWorkspaceGetParams/Result`).
- **Contract doc**: `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md:159`.
- This change only forwards and formats. It does not re-validate paths, re-classify encodings, or invent cursor semantics. An explicit `--agent` is forwarded verbatim (the Gateway owns the configured-agent roster); an absent one is resolved with `resolveAgentOperationAgentId`, the same helper `agents bind` and `agents files` use.

## Acceptance

Verified against an isolated Gateway started on `--allow-unconfigured` with a fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, whose workspace contains `notes/a.md` (68 bytes), `notes/b.txt` (23 bytes, no trailing newline), and `notes/pixel.png` (67 bytes, 1x1 PNG). Baseline: current `main` at `0633f256350`.

- **before**: `openclaw agents workspace list` → exit 1, `OpenClaw agents has no command "workspace".`
- `openclaw agents workspace list` → exit 0; header `path: / · 1 entries · offset 0`, one row `notes` with `kind=directory`.
- `openclaw agents workspace list --path notes --json` → exit 0; `path: "notes"`, `totalEntries: 3`, entries `a.md` (68), `b.txt` (23), `pixel.png` (67) — the same sizes as on disk.
- `openclaw agents workspace get notes/b.txt` → exit 0; stdout is 23 bytes and byte-identical to the seeded file (SHA-256 matches; no trailing newline added); stderr reports the size, MIME type, and `encoding=utf8`.
- `openclaw agents workspace get notes/pixel.png --json` → exit 0; `encoding: "base64"`, `mimeType: image/png`.
- `openclaw agents workspace get ../etc/passwd` → exit 1, stdout empty, error surfaces the handler's path-escape rejection (`path escapes the agent workspace`, the `workspace_path_invalid` branch).
- `openclaw agents workspace list --agent ghost` → exit 1 with the Gateway's `agent "ghost" not found` (explicit id forwarded verbatim; roster validation stays server-side).
- `openclaw agents workspace list --limit 0` → exit 1 offline with `--limit must be an integer >= 1`, no RPC sent.
- A shell operator can therefore pull a file from a remote or bridged workspace with `> file` redirection and get the exact bytes the Gateway reported.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this? — Yes

issues.body:
## Version

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (macOS arm64, Node 24). Source checked on current `main`: `MAX_IMAGE_INPUT_PIXELS = 25_000_000` in `src/media/image-processor-config.ts` and the throw in `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts` are unchanged.
- Agent runtime: `claude-cli` backend, Feishu group channel.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an agent on the `claude-cli` runtime, connected to a chat channel (Feishu here).
2. Send it a full-page phone/desktop screenshot such as a 5120×10472 PNG (5.6 MB, ≈53.6 MP) or 5120×10090 PNG (6.6 MB, ≈51.7 MP). Both are below the 10 MB input byte cap.
3. The turn ends before any reply: `This turn ended before a reply: failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s) for CLI input`.

Screenshots of the same conversation at 1200 px wide, and wide images up to 5120×2818 (14.4 MP), go through fine and get resized.

Direct repro against the bundled sanitizer (2026.9.6 dist):

```js
const m = await import("./dist/tool-images-*.mjs");
await m.t([{ type: "image", data: <base64 of 5120x10472 png>, mimeType: "image/png" }], "test", { maxDimensionPx: 1200 });
// -> [test] omitted image payload: RastermillError: Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit: 5120x10472 (53616640 pixels)
```

## Gateway log (redacted)

```
[agent/embedded] Native image: dropped 1 image(s) after sanitization (prompt:images).
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=215 error=failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s) for CLI input
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:feishu:group:<chat> durationMs=225 error="failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s) for CLI input" errorName=Error
Embedded agent failed before reply: failed to hydrate 1 structured image attachment(s) for CLI input
...
[agent/embedded] Native image: dropped 2 image(s) after sanitization (prompt:images).
[agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=253 error=failed to hydrate 2 structured image attachment(s) for CLI input
```

## Source path (2026.9.6 dist / main)

1. `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts` (`prepareCliPromptImagePayload`, dist `helpers-*.mjs:292-306`) calls `detectAndLoadPromptImages(...)` and throws if `failedMediaCount > 0`.
2. `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/images.ts` (dist `images-*.mjs:50-68, 270-281`): `sanitizeImageEntriesWithLog` counts every image dropped by sanitization as a `failedMediaCount`.
3. `sanitizeContentBlocksImages` → `resizeImageBase64IfNeeded` (dist `tool-images-*.mjs:41-44, 87-130, 219-246`): `imageWithinLimits` correctly flags `width*height > 25e6`, then tries to downscale via `resizeToJpeg`, but the Rastermill processor itself is created with `inputPixels: 25e6` (`src/media/image-processor-config.ts`, `image-ops-*.mjs:24-40`), so decoding the source throws `Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit`, and the image is dropped.

So the downscale step that exists exactly for oversized inputs refuses to open them. `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx` / `imageMaxBytes` can't help, because they only shape the *output*. There is no config key for the input pixel cap.

## Expected behavior

- An inbound image that is within the byte cap but above the pixel cap should still be downscaled (to `imageMaxDimensionPx` / the model's max) before hydration, at least up to a bounded higher decode limit (e.g. 64–100 MP; tall full-page screenshots from modern phones/retina displays routinely hit 50 MP).
- If an image truly can't be admitted, the turn should degrade to text with a notice ("1 image was too large and was skipped") rather than abort. That second half is tracked in #137469.

## Related

- #156871 "Configurable bounded pixel limit for inbound agent images" — same root cause; closed as not planned by inactivity bot (not fixed). This report adds a fresh repro on 2026.9.6 with the claude-cli runtime.
- #137469 — failed hydration throws and kills the turn instead of degrading.
- #67031 — hardcoded image size limits not configurable.
- Note from #156871: for very tall text screenshots, tiling instead of one downscale would keep text readable; a 5120×10472 screenshot squeezed to 1200 px long edge loses most of its text.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary One transcript record with usage.usageReport.state = "unavailable" makes the entire /usage report unavailable, so the Control UI renders "unknown" for token totals that are already computed. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run an agent through OpenRouter until one turn fails or is aborted, which stores an assistant record with stopReason: "error" or a gateway-injected record carrying abortMeta. 2. Open Control UI -> /usage with the last 30 days selected. 3. Compare the totals row with `openclaw gateway usage-cost --json`. ### Expected behavior Token totals are displayed, because they are derived from complete usage token fields. Only the cost value is annotated as partial. This matches the bundled usage-tracking documentation: "A recorded zero-dollar cost is valid cost data." ### Actual behavior The Control UI shows "unknown" for both Tokens and Cost, while the same report contains complete numbers: totals.totalCost = 5.4021393748 totals.totalTokens = 296059881 totals.missingCostEntries = 2 totals.usageReport.state = "unavailable" ### OpenClaw version 2026.11.3 ### Operating system Raspberry Pi OS (Debian) 6.18.60+rpt-rpi-v8, arm64 ### Install method npm -g (Gateway running as a systemd user unit) ### Model openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 ### Provider / routing chain openclaw -> openrouter -> deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 ### Additional provider/model setup details Single OpenRouter API key. models.providers.openrouter.params.provider = { order: ["DeepInfra", "Cloudflare", "Together"], allow_fallbacks: true, require_parameters: true, data_collection: "deny" } ### Logs ```shell $ openclaw gateway usage-cost Usage cost (30 days) Total: unavailable (known subtotal: $5.28 · 287.3m tokens) Missing cost: 2 (openclaw/gateway-injected 1, openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 1) Latest day: 2026-11-13 · unavailable (known subtotal: $1.22 · 106.8m tokens) $ openclaw gateway usage-cost --json (trimmed) .totals.missingCostByModel.openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 = 1 .totals.missingCostByModel.openclaw/gateway-injected = 1 .cacheStatus.status = fresh .cacheStatus.pendingFiles = 0 .cacheStatus.staleFiles = 0 ``` ### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence Control UI /usage (30d) shows "unknown" for Tokens and "unknown" for Cost, with 8 sessions. Screenshot attached. The offending transcript record is a failed turn: { "model": "deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017", "stopReason": "error", "content": [], "usage": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cacheRead": 0, "cacheWrite": 0, "totalTokens": 0, "cost": { "input": 0, "output": 0, "cacheRead": 0, "cacheWrite": 0, "total": 0 }, "usageReport": { "state": "unavailable" }, "contextUsage": { "state": "unavailable" } } } A second entry is an internal gateway-injected record (totalTokens: 0, cost.total: 0) reported as openclaw/gateway-injected. ### Impact and severity Affected: any install whose selected range contains one failed or aborted turn. A single failed request is enough, so this is common in normal use. Severity: blocks reading token usage from the UI. The CLI/JSON path is unaffected. Frequency: persistent for any range containing such a record; later successful turns do not clear the state. Consequence: users conclude usage tracking is broken, even though usage-cost --json reports accurate totals. Monetary effect: none observed — both offending records carry totalTokens: 0. ### Additional information These records are written by OpenClaw's own code paths, not by corrupted or third-party data: 1. buildStreamErrorAssistantMessage (shipped bundle stream-message-shared) builds the failed-turn record with stopReason: "error" and usage: buildUsageWithNoCost({}), which writes cost.total = 0. 2. The transcript injector (shipped bundle chat-transcript-inject) builds gateway-injected records with provider: "openclaw", model: "gateway-injected", and usageReport/contextUsage set to "unavailable" when abortMeta is present. 3. stream.runtime marks usageReport unavailable whenever context usage is absent: usageReport: { state: contextUsage ? "available" : "unavailable" }. Both shapes still write cost.total: 0, but the cost rollup drops that value because the record is flagged unavailable, and counts it as a missing cost entry. This conflicts with the documented rule that a recorded zero-dollar cost is valid cost data. Workaround: `openclaw gateway usage-cost --json` reports correct totals; `/usage cost` in chat prints the known subtotal with a partial marker. Related issues: - #196737 — local ledger cannot reconcile with the provider bill (under-recording). Different cause: this report is about display state, not missing billing. - #180195 — one corrupt transcript event aborts the refresh. Different cause: the refresh here completes (cacheStatus.status = fresh) and produces correct totals. Suggested fixes, least invasive first: 1. Render token totals regardless of cost completeness; annotate only the cost value as partial. 2. Do not discard an entry whose usageReport.state is "unavailable" when it carries an explicit cost.total (including 0). 3. Exclude internal openclaw/gateway-injected records from cost-completeness accounting. No PR attached; filed for triage.

issues.body:
## Problem

In native Apple chat, a finished run folds its narration into the "Worked…" disclosure together with the tool steps. Only the final answer stays visible.

Narration often carries a large part of the reply: findings, caveats, intermediate results. Hiding it once the run ends removes content the reader was already reading while the run was live, and the visible answer then reads as incomplete.

## Reproduction

1. In the iOS app, send a prompt that makes the agent narrate between tool calls (for example "check X, then Y, and report").
2. While the run is active, narration bubbles stay in view; only tool steps fold.
3. When the run completes, the narration bubbles disappear into "Worked…". Only the final answer remains outside the fold.

## Cause

`apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatCompletedWork.swift`, on main at `e4fcf3020e8`: `isCollapsibleWork` treats every assistant message whose phase is not `final_answer` as collapsible work, which includes `commentary` (narration). The completed-turn projection then moves those rows into the disclosure.

## Expected behavior

After completion, fold only tool calls and tool results. Narration stays in the transcript, in order, as it was during the run. The web Control UI keeps narration visible inline.

## Affected platforms

iOS, iPadOS and native macOS chat (shared `OpenClawChatUI`).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`sessions.diff` for a sandboxed session on a managed worktree fails with `WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved` when any other worktree is created or removed at the same moment, although nothing about that session's worktree changed. The `sessions.diff` request then fails with `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE` instead of returning the diff.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build `main` (`bb97be6b37b`) from source and run a Gateway with isolated state, an agent workspace that is a git repository, and sandbox `mode: "all"`, `scope: "session"`, `workspaceAccess: "rw"` (Docker backend).
2. `sessions.create { agentId: "main", worktree: true }`, then `chat.send` one message and wait for the run, so the sandboxed local workspace is provisioned for the session.
3. Call `sessions.diff { sessionKey, scope: "all", summaryOnly: true }` for that session in a loop.
4. At the same time, loop `worktrees.create` (same repository) and `worktrees.remove { force: true }` for unrelated manual worktrees.

### Expected behavior

Every `sessions.diff` call for the session returns its diff; publications of other worktrees do not affect it.

### Actual behavior

Some `sessions.diff` calls fail with `WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved` (`errorCode=UNAVAILABLE`): 3 of 300 and 4 of 1000 calls, while 4 and 11 unrelated worktrees were created and removed. The diff of the same session right before returned `files: [], additions: 0, deletions: 0`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (main `bb97be6b37b`)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm build`)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (the failing call reads the session's worktree; no model is involved in it)

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway `sessions.diff` -> session worktree registry read

### Additional provider/model setup details

The session's one run used a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in model that answers `ok`; the failure is in `sessions.diff`, not in the run.

### Logs

```text
sessions.diff 300 calls:  {"ok":297,"contention":3,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 4/4
sessions.diff 1000 calls: {"ok":996,"contention":4,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 11/11
diff error WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved

[gateway] request handler failed: WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.diff 3ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Driver output and Gateway log above, from a WebSocket driver against an isolated Gateway.

### Impact and severity

Affected: operators with sandboxed sessions on managed worktrees who view a session's changes while other sessions or tools create or remove worktrees.
Severity: annoying. The diff request fails and has to be retried.
Frequency: intermittent; it needs a worktree publication during the diff's registry read (3 of 300 and 4 of 1000 calls in the loop above).
Consequence: the `sessions.diff` request fails with `errorCode=UNAVAILABLE` and a contention error although the session's worktree is unchanged.

### Additional information

`readLocalWorkspaceReviewBase` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-review.ts`) reads the registry by the session's known worktree id but captures the lifecycle read guard without a selection, so the guard watches every registry row. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197561 scoped the same guard in `resolveLocalWorkspaceOwner` and `expireLocalWorkspaceProjection` after the same kind of unrelated publication rejected sandbox startup.

`readLocalWorkspacePath` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-read.ts`), used by session file reads and Control UI assistant media reads of a sandboxed session, captures the same guard without a selection although it knows the expected worktree id. This was found by reading the code and reproduced in a unit test at that function, not driven through a Gateway.

issues.body:
Normal gateway `exec` with `host=node` rejects an already allowlisted Homebrew executable on macOS when the gateway's shell carrier prevents the node from binding the concrete executable file. A narrow local transport change restored the same command through the normal approval pipeline without changing grants.

### Environment

- Gateway: macOS, OpenClaw **2026.11.2**, build **b556fdf**.
- Node: macOS arm64, OpenClaw **2026.11.3**, paired/connected, advertising `system.run` and `system.run.prepare`.
- Affected agent requests exec in **allowlist** mode. Existing node rules cover `/opt/homebrew/bin/imsg` and its Cellar path, restricted to read subcommands (`chats`, `search`, `history`).
- `imsg` 0.4.0 is a two-line `#!/bin/bash` Homebrew wrapper executing `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/imsg/0.4.0/libexec/imsg`. Its resolved wrapper is owned by the current user; the relevant Homebrew parent paths are writable.

### Reproduction

Through the normal agent exec tool:

```json
{
  "host": "node",
  "node": "<paired macOS node>",
  "command": "/opt/homebrew/bin/imsg chats --limit 1 --json"
}
```

Expected: exit 0 and one newline-delimited JSON row. Private message data is omitted.

Actual before repair:

```text
INVALID_REQUEST: SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED: approval cannot safely bind this interpreter/runtime command
No approval request was created for this attempt; this is not a user denial. Retry a supported single executable with an absolute path through the normal approval flow. This node approval path cannot bind script/interpreter payloads nested in its shell wrapper.
```

This reproduced before and after a gateway restart. An administrative normal gateway-to-node read using unchanged pre-existing policy returned exit 0 and one valid JSON row, isolating the affected approval/binding path from node connectivity and iMessage database access.

### Source diagnosis

The gateway's `buildNodeShellCommand` sends macOS requests as `[/bin/sh, -c, command]`. The node's mutable-file policy requires stable binding for this Homebrew file, but the shell payload cannot provide a concrete file operand to snapshot. Direct executable-file argv already has a supported preparation path that snapshots/hashes the mutable file at `argv[0]`, including a shebang wrapper.

Relevant source: [node shell transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.3/src/infra/node-shell.ts), [mutable file operand](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.3/src/infra/system-run-mutable-file-operand.ts), [approval binding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.3/src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts), [command consistency](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.11.3/src/infra/system-run-command.ts).

### Verified local mitigation

The gateway transport builder now preserves direct argv only for canonical absolute ASCII literal commands on macOS, with exactly one space between tokens and an exact round-trip through the existing command formatter. Known interpreters/dispatchers and shell-sensitive or noncanonical inputs keep their previous transport. Other platforms are unchanged.

Normal `system.run.prepare`, its returned plan, exact argv/raw-command consistency, file snapshots/revalidation, allowlists, approvals and dispatch remain unchanged. No raw system.run invocation or permissive grant was added.

After the gateway loaded this change, the **same affected agent**, same command, same node version and same approval policy returned **exit 0, one valid JSON row, one nonempty output line**. The semantic approval policy hash is identical before/after (usage metadata excluded). Six focused tests pass, covering the canonical command, real raw-command consistency, literal arguments, platform preservation, shell grammar and interpreter fallback. The original builder failed the three direct-argv expectations.

### Version/rollback constraints

- The prepared **2026.10.3** node package could not be used: its read-only preflight supports database schema **20**, while current node state is schema **22**. It failed closed before opening state. No downgrade or state modification was attempted.
- Prepared **2026.11.5-beta.2** source retained the relevant binding behavior; it was not installed speculatively.
- Actual running versions remain gateway **2026.11.2** with the local transport hotfix and node **2026.11.3**.

Related historical reports: #66524 and #69251. This report supplies a current-version reproduction and an end-to-end verified transport mitigation while preserving binding and allowlist enforcement.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Media sent from a plugin tool via the sanctioned `toolContext.delivery.send({ mediaUrl })` capability (introduced in #127098) reaches the outbound channel but does not appear in the OpenClaw Control UI, while media produced by the built-in `image_generate` tool through `details.media.mediaUrls` appears in both.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a plugin whose tool factory receives `toolContext.delivery` and, in `execute()`, calls `delivery.send({ mediaUrl: <absolute-path-to-workspace-image> })` for one or more images.
2. Configure a chat channel (e.g. Telegram) for the agent so `deliveryContext` is populated with `channel`, `to`, `accountId`.
3. Invoke the plugin tool from a chat that has the Control UI open on the same session.
4. Compare the resulting turn on the chat channel and in the Control UI assistant reply.

### Expected behavior

The image that appeared on the chat channel also appears inline in the Control UI assistant reply for that turn — matching the built-in `image_generate` tool (`src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.execution.ts`), whose `details.media.mediaUrls` are ingested via `pendingToolMediaUrls` into the assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` that the Control UI renders.

### Actual behavior

Image is delivered to the chat channel. The Control UI shows only the text portion of the assistant reply for that turn; no image, no attachment entry.

Code trace on `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207` — `delivery.send` calls `runMessageAction` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false`. This is a live, ephemeral push through the core outbound owner and never populates the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102` — `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` is a hardcoded set. Plugin tool names are not members, so `details.media.mediaUrls` returned from a plugin tool is stripped by `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.
- Result: both established Control UI ingest routes (trusted tool-result media, or assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls`) are closed to plugin `delivery.send`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5 (main @ `c1ead4b71e0`)

### Operating system

macOS 12.7.6

### Install method

pnpm dev (source checkout of main)

### Model

Not model-dependent (defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, before the model round-trip)

### Provider / routing chain

Not routing-dependent

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A — the defect is in the tool-result → transcript pipeline, not in inference routing.

### Logs

N/A — no error is emitted; the media silently does not appear in the Control UI.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Code references above are sufficient for grounded verification against `main` @ `c1ead4b71e0`:

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts:161-207`
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts:102`
- `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.execution.ts` (baseline: native tool whose media does appear in Control UI)

### Impact and severity

- Affected: any plugin tool that returns media via the sanctioned `toolContext.delivery.send` capability from #127098.
- Severity: Behavior bug. Chat channel delivery works; Control UI users lose visibility of media the same turn produced.
- Frequency: Every invocation.
- Consequence: Control UI reviewers cannot see plugin-generated media without switching to the chat channel; degrades review, debugging, and audit workflows.

### Additional information

Follow-up to #120718. Of the three solutions proposed there, #127098 implemented Option C (a sanctioned `delivery.send` abstraction). Option A (extending `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` for plugins) was not implemented, and the Control UI path continues to depend on it.

Two directions that would close the gap:

1. Mirror `delivery.send`-sent media into the assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` for the current turn so the Control UI renders what the chat channel received.
2. Ship Option A from #120718 — allow plugins to declare a tool as trusted local-media producer so returning `details.media.mediaUrls` from the tool result also survives `filterToolResultMediaUrls()`.

Either would restore parity with the native `image_generate` tool's Control UI behavior.



---

**Update 2026-10-08 — still reproducible on `main`** (v2026.10.1-beta.2 @ `e73b64b7f62`):

- `src/agents/openclaw-plugin-tools.ts` still calls `runMessageAction` for `delivery.send` with `forceCoreDelivery: true, skipQueue: true, dryRun: false` — media never enters the tool-result media queue.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-media.ts` still exposes `TRUSTED_TOOL_RESULT_MEDIA` as a hardcoded set; plugin tools are not members, so `filterToolResultMediaUrls()` continues to strip plugin-tool `details.media.mediaUrls`.
- No mirror from `delivery.send` into assistant `ReplyPayload.mediaUrls` has landed on `main`. (See clawsweeper's 2026-10-08 review of this issue: `deliver-transcript.ts:45` passes `text` only, with mediaUrls flattened to filename text — confirming the mirror boundary is still the loss site.)
- Linked fix PR #156613 remains **open and unmerged**, blocked on merge conflicts (`mergeable_state=dirty`).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In existing project-parent sessions, sessions_spawn rejected DeepSeek or native Haiku during model validation, although the preserved Gateway model-list projection reported those models available; the same logical session later spawned working Children after text /reset

### Steps to reproduce

Historical operator-reported steps, supported by the attached selected records (not rerun for this report):
1. Use an installation where DeepSeek and native Haiku routes already work from a normal session.
2. Open a session attached to a registered non-worktree project outside the agent workspace.
3. Ask Main to invoke sessions_spawn explicitly with `deepseek/deepseek-flash` or `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.
4. Observe the preflight errors below.

Control: the existing SESSION-A history has failures at 13:57 KST, text /reset at 13:59 KST, then an accepted DeepSeek Child at 14:01 KST and later DeepSeek/Haiku assistant output. Project detachment at reset is operator-reported; no before/after project metadata snapshots were recovered. Do not treat /reset as the proposed fix. A clean-stock minimal configuration was not independently reproduced.

### Expected behavior

A model that works in a normal session should remain usable for Child validation when its parent is project-attached, without changing the project execution directory. The attached historical after-reset successes and related upstream inventory contract provide the control.


### Actual behavior

Two distinct historical errors were observed before Child execution:

```text
sessions_spawn model "deepseek/deepseek-flash" is not usable: Unknown model: deepseek/deepseek-flash. Found agents.defaults.models["deepseek/deepseek-flash"], but no matching models.providers["deepseek"].models[] entry. Add { "id": "deepseek-flash", "name": "deepseek-flash" } to models.providers["deepseek"].models[] to register this provider model. For custom or proxy providers, also set api and baseUrl so requests route to the intended endpoint. See https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/model-providers.
```

```text
sessions_spawn model "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5" is not usable: The selected account or native runtime is unavailable for anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5. Restore that account before spawning this model.
```

The native-runtime wording is an admission result, not evidence that the real credential expired. DeepSeek fails model resolution; Haiku fails availability evaluation inside the same outer preflight. These are not claimed to be identical inner failures.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.6 (`fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`), build 2026-10-22T08:54:27.830Z.

### Operating system

Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (OS Build 19045.7725), WSL2

### Install method

global-layout Node package in the managed Node v24.22.1 toolchain. Original installation command: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Model

Main observed: `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` and `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5`. Child failures: `deepseek/deepseek-flash`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`; Haiku case: `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` (not Haiku 5.5).

### Provider / routing chain

Gateway sessions_spawn -> resolveSubagentModelAndThinkingPlan -> prepareModelChoice -> prepared catalog owner/model/runtime evaluation. DeepSeek uses the installed global provider plugin; Haiku uses logical anthropic routing to the native claude-cli runtime. The rejected calls did not reach Child inference.

### Additional provider/model setup details

DeepSeek plugin manifest: enabled, global registration, `activation.onStartup=false`, `providerCatalogEntry=./dist/provider-discovery.js`, modelCatalog present. Earlier investigation recorded an empty inline deepseek model list; credentials and full config are intentionally not attached. A local project creation/recording maintenance plugin is installed but was not disabled; no clean-stock comparison is claimed. Project roots and session identifiers are aliased.

### Logs

```shell
See `01-child-spawn-evidence.zip`: `logs/child-failures.jsonl`, `logs/child-accepted.jsonl`, `logs/child-execution-identities.jsonl`, and `comparison/timeline.csv`. All event times use the original record timestamp, also rendered as KST. Only selected fields are exported; errors are verbatim.

The preserved models.list projection has 35 rows in agent-default, normal-session and project-session scopes: OpenAI 8, Anthropic 14, Claude CLI 11, DeepSeek 2. Selected DeepSeek and Haiku rows show available=true. It was collected later than the failures. The full raw 35-row response was not retained, and this RPC is not the Child validator owner.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

[01-child-spawn-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33901777/01-child-spawn-evidence.zip)

### Impact and severity

Affected: the reporter's project-parent workflow on this installation. Severity: blocks Child delegation while preserving project membership. Operator reports multiple projects and both Main routes affected. The attachment is a selected evidence set, not a complete failure-rate sample; population-wide frequency is NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

### Additional information

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/169205 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169539. The installed commit is not a descendant of merge `52885d96ffef88db68c56cb772840d23dcfaf150`; the installed lease code lacks inventoryInput. The upstream issue is analogous, not identical (it reported Main ingress failures). The PR repairs shared run leases; it does not directly cover sessions_spawn preflight.

Source-level candidate, NOT observed failure-owner state: project workspace owner lookup can miss a compatible published owner and fall back to a readOnly ephemeral build without runtime plugin facts. Owner keys also distinguish readOnly mode. Inspect `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.ts` owner selection and `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.ts::prepareModelChoice`, in addition to the lease fix. Preserve agent/auth/environment/generation isolation and execution cwd. No manual global-model-registration workaround is requested.

No Child/reset/restart/test or Core/config/DB/session mutation was performed to prepare this package. No failing-owner snapshot, clean-stock reproduction, or proof of a proposed patch is claimed. Last-known-good version: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

# Feature request

## Summary

When `gateway.publicOrigin` is configured and the Control UI is enabled, chat notifications for automation runs get an `Inspect: <url>` line appended (documented in `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`). The link itself is genuinely useful — one click straight to the exact run transcript. The problem: it is unconditional and unlabeled.

## Current behavior (2026.9.4)

- The `Inspect` line is appended to **every** cron announce, including routine "everything green" digests where it adds no value.
- The same pattern also appears on other announce paths (e.g. task/subagent completion notifications), not just cron.
- It is a bare URL with no label, so in chat channels it reads as noise rather than as a feature.
- There is no global or per-job toggle. The only way to remove it today is disabling the Control UI / `publicOrigin` entirely, which is not desirable.

## Request

1. A configuration option, e.g. `cron.announce.inspectLinks: always | errors | never` (default `always` to preserve current behavior), and/or a per-job delivery flag.
2. Ideally: attach the link only to failure/anomaly notifications (or make that the default), and render it as a labeled link (e.g. `Inspect run`) on channels that support markdown instead of a bare URL.

## Workaround

None short of turning off the Control UI.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d)
- Affected delivery: Discord channel announce (applies to all chat channels)

# Native Codex restricted completion handoffs repeatedly cold-start large history contexts

## Scope / relationship to existing issue

This is the remaining efficiency gap described under Limits in #143386, not another report of normal-chat binding replacement. The measurements below are from OpenClaw/@openclaw/codex 2026.9.3 on macOS Apple Silicon **with the local main-binding preservation/history-coverage fixes described in #143386 installed**. We have not reproduced these exact seven-call measurements on an unmodified 2026.9.4 installation. Please treat this as an efficiency/design follow-up, not an unsupported claim of a new stock-release regression.

The prior local fix preserves the main conversation across a restricted completion. Returning to ordinary chat was verified warm. However, each restricted completion still uses a new transient native conversation and loads a large history baseline.

## Observed impact

Seven recorded transient completion starts had seven opening model requests:

- Total uncached input on those opening requests: **566,057 tokens**.
- Each opening request contained approximately 86,000–89,000 total input tokens.
- Actual completion prompts were approximately 230,000–238,000 characters. A larger omitted-history marker was NOT injected text and must not be counted as such.
- All recorded requests in the seven completion conversations totaled **738,205 uncached input tokens across 70 calls**, excluding separate child conversations. This larger total includes subsequent useful work, not solely bootstrap overhead.
- Main-binding snapshots retained the ordinary native thread. The overhead here is in the completion surfaces, not evidence that main continuity protection failed.

Uncached input means input_tokens minus cached_input_tokens. These figures are not subscription-percentage or dollar attribution, nor population-wide estimates.

## Reproduction / measurement

1. Use a long-running native Codex parent conversation with ordinary owner-authorized tools.
2. Complete a bounded native child and deliver its result through non-owner internal completion provenance with the legitimate restricted tool catalog.
3. Preserve the ordinary binding as in the local mitigation in #143386; do NOT grant owner permissions to the restricted event.
4. Repeat with additional distinct child completions. Record transient native thread identities, first-request input/cached counters, context projection size, and ordinary binding identity.
5. Observe whether each restricted event starts a new native thread and reprojects the full retained parent baseline even when the restricted catalog is compatible with the previous completion.

Observed log: `dynamic tools unavailable; starting transient thread`. Source inspection shows this wording also covers catalog incompatibility, not necessarily unavailable/broken tools.

## Expected behavior / possible design

Provide bounded, safely reusable restricted completion context without losing original task intent, later user corrections, child results, or unfinished obligations. One possible implementation is a host-owned restricted completion slot alongside the ordinary binding, retaining all normal compatibility and authorization checks and projecting only history not already supplied to that slot. This is a proposed design, not a demand to bypass current security checks.

## What has been tested offline

An isolated native Codex protocol probe (CLI 0.144.1, synthetic local Responses provider and dynamic tools, no paid provider requests) verified:

- Separate ordinary and restricted native IDs.
- Restricted thread survives app-server restart and resumes by original ID.
- Restricted tools remain available; synthetic owner-only tools do not appear.
- Original task/result remain, while a later correction and second result are appended.
- Ordinary history remains separate.

This establishes native protocol feasibility, NOT working OpenClaw integration, external delivery, provider cache hits, or live savings.

## Host integration blockers found in source-coupled tests

1. Inventing a session-key suffix does not establish parent generation authority; the actual generation-authority helper treats an unregistered auxiliary key as ephemeral.
2. Current reset/retirement/deletion paths operate on one binding. A synthetic second row survives parent reset unless the lifecycle is extended explicitly.
3. Wall-clock completion time is not a truthful history admission boundary. A controlled source-level counterexample places a correction/result after admission but before completion; using completion time as coverage can skip that unseen input on reuse. This is a blocker for the proposed design, NOT proof that the exact loss occurred live.

A safe implementation needs real parent-owned multi-binding lifecycle, compatibility-sensitive slot selection, reset/delete/retirement cleanup, concurrent-event tests, and an actual admitted/projected source cursor with conservative fallback on gaps. Simply truncating history or disabling permission/catalog checks is unsafe.

## Related retry observation; not a deduplication fix claim

One announcement identifier was processed twice. The first handling logged `codex settled-turn finalization context is unavailable`; a later retry also logged `native prompt annotation conflicts with recorded provenance`. We have not established the full retry cause or proven duplicate visible delivery. Failed/unknown finalization must remain retriable; do not suppress solely by child ID.

No new reusable-slot patch is installed. Current mitigation is fewer, more complete child assignments. Please advise whether an existing upstream design addresses this remaining overhead. This report intentionally excludes private conversation text, credentials, native session identifiers, and local account paths.

## Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

With Codex `sandboxExecServer` enabled, a later turn in the same session can reconnect to a loopback listener that OpenClaw closed after the first turn, causing `Connection refused (os error 111)`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw `2026.9.3` with the official Codex plugin, managed stdio app-server, a Podman sandbox, and:

   ```json5
   {
     plugins: {
       entries: {
         codex: {
           config: {
             appServer: {
               experimental: {
                 sandboxExecServer: true,
               },
             },
           },
         },
       },
     },
   }
   ```

2. In a new Codex session, execute `pwd` with the native process tool. It returns `/workspace`.
3. After the turn finishes, execute `pwd` again in the same thread.
4. Observe `Connection refused` against the earlier exec-server URL. The sandbox remains running and was not OOM-killed.

## Expected behavior

Both turns should execute in the active sandbox and return `/workspace`.

## Actual behavior

The first turn succeeds; a later turn fails against the retired URL:

```text
exec-server connection attempt failed
Failed to connect to exec-server websocket ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/openclaw-<uuid>: Connection refused (os error 111)
```

## OpenClaw version

`2026.9.3` (`@openclaw/codex` `2026.9.3`, managed `@openai/codex` `0.153.4`)

## Operating system

Fedora Linux 44 Workstation, Linux `7.1.13-200.fc44.x86_64`, x86_64

## Install method

npm; official OpenClaw-managed `@openclaw/codex` plugin installation

## Model

`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`

## Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw Gateway -> official `@openclaw/codex` plugin -> managed local stdio Codex app-server -> OpenAI -> Codex native process tool -> OpenClaw loopback sandbox exec-server -> Podman sandbox

## Additional provider/model setup details

- Sandbox workdir: `/workspace`; `sandboxExecServer` is explicitly `true`.
- The managed app-server persists across turns. No host fallback is involved.
- Reproduced with Podman. Docker was not tested directly; the failing listener lifecycle precedes backend dispatch.

## Logs

```shell
exec-server connection attempt failed
Failed to connect to exec-server websocket ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/openclaw-<uuid>: Connection refused (os error 111)
```

## Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

- From 2026-09-08 through 2026-09-10: 45 matching failures across 19 Codex session transcripts, usually after a successful initial turn.
- The Podman sandbox remained running with `OOMKilled=false`.
- After the diagnostic lifecycle change, two consecutive `pwd` turns in one session both returned `/workspace` through one listener, with no Gateway restart or connection failure.

## Impact and severity

- Affected: sandboxed Codex sessions with the experimental exec-server.
- Severity: Moderate overall; workflow-blocking for affected sessions, but limited to the opt-in experimental sandbox exec-server configuration.
- Frequency: Repeated and deterministic in the observed configuration (45 failures across 19 transcripts over three days); prevalence across OpenClaw installations is unknown.
- Consequence: multi-turn coding and suggested-task workflows fail and require retries or runtime reset.

## Additional information

### Source-backed lifecycle analysis

Current `main` matches the installed `2026.9.3` lifecycle: OpenClaw derives a stable environment ID from `sandbox.runtimeId`, but uses an ephemeral port and random auth path. At `refCount == 0`, it removes and closes the current listener. A later acquisition can therefore register the same ID with a new URL while the observed thread still targets the retired URL.

This is consistent with Codex's sticky thread environments and `environment/status` probing without reconnection:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.ts
- https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/README.md

### Diagnostic workaround and proposed direction

A local diagnostic retained the current registry server at zero references. Orphaned servers still closed, and registry shutdown still closed retained servers. The two-turn verification then passed.

In simplified form, the diagnostic changed the current-server branch from delete-and-close to return-and-retain:

```diff
- if (current === execServer) registry.delete(runtimeId);
+ if (current === execServer) return;
  await registry.close(execServer);
```

This supports the lifecycle diagnosis but is not a complete production fix: indefinite retention could accumulate listeners or preserve stale sandbox context. A durable fix should align listener lifetime with its app-server/environment or sandbox runtime, clean up on invalidation/shutdown or bounded idle eviction, and add a two-turn regression test.

Related but not duplicate:

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/119125 — non-absolute cwd passed to Docker exec
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/115575 — `environment/info` and PathUri handling

## Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect state without crash). Beta release blocker: No.

## Summary
A restricted background-completion tool catalog replaces the persistent normal-chat Codex binding; returning to normal chat replaces it again, causing two cold history bootstraps across normal → completion → normal.

## Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (1391f7c), @openclaw/codex 2026.9.3; Codex 0.153.4
- Node.js 26.8.1; macOS 15.7.4 Apple Silicon; npm global, launchd Gateway
- Model: openai/gpt-6-astra; ordinary chat medium reasoning
- Route: Telegram direct chat → OpenClaw → Codex app-server → OpenAI subscription-backed authentication
- Measured independently after a local successful-delivery history-coverage correction made ordinary turns warm.

## Steps to reproduce
Observed on this installation; not claimed universal:
1. Settle an ordinary Codex-backed Telegram turn and record its native thread binding, coverage timestamp and dynamic tool fingerprint.
2. Run a bounded native child and allow its completion to arrive as non-owner internal `inter_session` provenance with source tool `agent_harness_task`.
3. Compare the normal binding with the completion binding. The observed ordinary catalog had 32 tools, completion 22; the difference includes owner-only tools and is legitimate.
4. Send another ordinary Telegram message with the original tool catalog, then compare thread IDs, history projection and first-request fresh input.

## Expected behavior
Preserve the ordinary compatible binding while servicing the restricted completion separately, without expanding its permissions. On normal return, resume the ordinary thread and reconcile the small unseen completion delta as quoted reference data. Our local candidate demonstrated this behavior.

## Actual behavior / evidence
Before handoff repair:
- Settled ordinary turns: 1,065 / 1,341 / 1,264 fresh input tokens, same normal native thread.
- Completion: new thread, 53,270 fresh input tokens and full history.
- Next ordinary message: another new thread, 49,559 fresh input tokens and full history.

First-request fresh input = input_tokens minus cached_input_tokens. These measurements do not establish subscription-quota percentages.

## Causal code path
In distributed `thread-lifecycle-D1pzRwHB.js`, `startOrResumeThread` rejects an incompatible immutable `dynamicToolsFingerprint` correctly. However, the existing transient preservation path recognizes no-tool turns but not a nonempty restricted completion catalog. `clearCurrentBinding` clears the ordinary binding, and fresh-thread startup commits the completion binding. Returning to the normal catalog repeats replacement.

Actual distributed lifecycle functions with the observed catalogs reproduce both replacements. Historical branch-level production logs/pre-clear snapshots were not captured, so this is a tested sufficient causal path corroborated by native rollouts and transcript metadata, not a captured mutation trace.

## Local repair and continuity requirement
We extended the existing transient lifecycle only inside the catalog-mismatch branch for explicitly non-owner internal inter-session completion provenance (`agent_harness_task` / `subagent_announce`). Earlier compatibility/security checks still run; the completion retains its real restricted catalog and cannot overwrite the ordinary binding.

A second change in the stale-binding history selector is necessary: native-mirrored completion rows from another thread must not be discarded as already present in the preserved ordinary thread. We infer turn/thread ownership from canonical transcript mirror keys, retain newer foreign completion input/results and fresh corrections, exclude proven same-thread mirrors/tool results, and preserve timestamp cutoff/current-request deduplication and quoted rendering. An unowned fresh mirrored user row is retained conservatively. Successful ordinary settlement then covers the delta. Transient completion settlement must not advance another thread's watermark.

## Verification
- Harness using actual distributed functions and observed catalogs: baseline performs two replacements; candidate retains/resumes normal binding.
- Tests cover fresh-thread persistence, transient cleanup, authority/supervision guards, coverage ownership, cancellation/failure gates, quoted rendering, and foreign-result/fresh-correction retention without bulk replay.
- Native RPC and delivery are mocked in the harness.
- Live post-patch test: original normal binding survived the child result; normal return reused it with 2,226 fresh input tokens, a small 6,326-character input envelope, and the child's new test phrase retained alongside a new user message.
- Next ordinary follow-up retained the thread, showed an advanced coverage timestamp and no replayed conversation-context block.

## Limits / impact
The local fix eliminates the unnecessary normal-return bootstrap in the measured test. The restricted completion itself STILL cold-starts. A reusable restricted-surface binding pool is broader lifecycle work, not implemented here. Other legitimate compatibility changes can still require new threads.

Observed on one long-running Telegram direct conversation; significant avoidable input overhead on the tested round trip. Population-wide frequency and exact quota cost: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO. No memory/context-budget reduction or permission relaxation. Local distribution edits may be overwritten by upgrades; no upstream fix claimed.

Related context-growth report: #84662. No private transcript, account identifier, native session ID or local machine path is included.

Companion successful-delivery coverage bug: #143385. The measurements here isolate the remaining handoff problem after that local correction.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw attach` reports a successful attach ("Attaching Claude Code to session ... (grant expires ...)…") and spawns Claude Code normally, but the local MCP bridge that `.mcp.json` points Claude Code at (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`) never starts listening — Claude Code gets zero MCP tools from the gateway session.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a client machine separate from the Gateway host, install the exact same OpenClaw version as the Gateway (`npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.2`).
2. Run: `openclaw attach --url wss://<gateway-host> --token <gateway-token> --session agent:<agentId>:<sessionKey>` (a fully-qualified session key is required when multiple agents are configured — separate minor rough edge: `--session agent:main` and `--session main` both fail with "no explicit owner", only `agent:<agentId>:<sessionKey>` from `openclaw sessions list --agent <id> --json` works).
3. CLI prints "Attaching Claude Code to session agent:main:main (grant expires <ts>)…" and spawns Claude Code successfully (interactive TUI opens, usable as a normal session).
4. Inside the spawned Claude Code session, no tool name starts with `mcp__` for an "openclaw" MCP server (checked via the session's own tool-search).
5. Inspect `~/.cache/claude-cli-nodejs/<cwd-slug>/mcp-logs-openclaw/*.jsonl` (auto-generated by Claude Code for this MCP server) — shows the client repeatedly trying `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` and failing.
6. Independently confirm nothing listens on that port on the client machine: `curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` → `Connection refused`; `ss -ltnp | grep <port>` → empty; `/proc/<openclaw-attach-pid>/net/tcp` → port absent.
7. Reproduced 3 separate times (3 independent `attach` invocations, one via `--print-config` two-step and two via direct `attach`), same result every time, different ephemeral ports each time (all consistently refused).

### Expected behavior

After a successful `attach` (grant minted, device already paired/approved, Claude Code spawned), the spawned Claude Code session should have the scoped MCP tools available via the `openclaw` MCP server defined in the generated `.mcp.json`, since that is the entire stated purpose of `attach` ("Attach Claude Code to a gateway session with scoped MCP tools").

### Actual behavior

The generated `.mcp.json` is well-formed and correctly injected via `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <path>`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "openclaw": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp",
      "alwaysLoad": true,
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${OPENCLAW_MCP_TOKEN}" }
    }
  }
}
```

But nothing on the client machine ever listens on `<port>`. Claude Code's own MCP client log shows 4 connection attempts (immediate + retries at +1s/+2s/+4s), all `ConnectionRefused` in 2-39ms each — not a timeout, an instant refusal every time, with no successful attempt in between:

```
{"debug":"Initializing HTTP transport to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp", ...}
{"debug":"Testing basic HTTP connectivity to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp", ...}
{"debug":"HTTP Connection failed after 39ms: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url? (code: ConnectionRefused, errno: none)", ...}
{"error":"Connection failed (ConnectionRefused): Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?", ...}
{"debug":"Transient ConnectionRefused on initial connect — retry 1/3 in 1000ms", ...}
... (repeats for retry 2/3 at +2s, retry 3/3 at +4s, all ConnectionRefused within 2-3ms each) ...
```

The `openclaw-attach` process tree stays alive the whole time (`openclaw` → `openclaw-attach` → `claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <path>`, verified via `ps aux`), so this is not a crash — the parent process simply never binds the local bridge port it told Claude Code to connect to.

Note: minting the grant itself works correctly — `openclaw attach --url ... --token ... --session ... --print-config` (the "exit without spawning" variant) successfully authenticates against the Gateway over the public WSS endpoint (behind a Cloudflare Tunnel) and returns a valid grant + `.mcp.json` + launch instructions every time. So the WS auth/grant-minting round-trip to the Gateway is confirmed working; only the local HTTP bridge that the *live* `attach` (non-print-config) is supposed to start for the spawned Claude Code process to talk to never comes up.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (3928bad)

### Operating system

Client: Linux Mint 22.3 (Ubuntu 24.04 base) x86_64. Gateway: Ubuntu 24.04 (Contabo VPS), reached over a Cloudflare Tunnel (`wss://<hostname>`), gateway itself binds loopback only.

### Install method

npm global, on the client: `npm install -g openclaw@2026.9.2` (Node v22.22.3 via nvm — the package's `engines` field requires `>=22.22.3 <23 || >=24.15.0 <25 || >=25.9.0`). Gateway side runs as a systemd user service, also installed via npm global (Node v24.x).

### Model

N/A — not model-routing related. The Gateway's own agent (`main`) uses `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-cli` runtime; this bug is about the `attach` CLI's local bridge, unrelated to model selection.

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (see above — this is a client-side CLI/transport bug, not an LLM provider routing issue).

### Logs

```
{"debug":"Initializing HTTP transport to http://127.0.0.1:35959/mcp","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.057Z"}
{"debug":"Node version: v26.3.0, Platform: linux","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.057Z"}
{"debug":"HTTP transport options: {\"url\":\"http://127.0.0.1:35959/mcp\",\"headers\":{\"User-Agent\":\"claude-code/2.1.236 (cli)\",\"Accept-Encoding\":\"identity\",\"Authorization\":\"[REDACTED]\"},\"hasAuthProvider\":false,\"timeoutMs\":60000}","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.057Z"}
{"debug":"HTTP transport created successfully","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.057Z"}
{"debug":"Starting connection with timeout of 30000ms","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.058Z"}
{"debug":"Testing basic HTTP connectivity to http://127.0.0.1:35959/mcp","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.058Z"}
{"debug":"Parsed URL: host=127.0.0.1, port=35959, protocol=http:","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.058Z"}
{"debug":"version negotiation probe failed on the http transport; reconnecting pinned legacy","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.075Z"}
{"debug":"HTTP Connection failed after 39ms: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url? (code: ConnectionRefused, errno: none)","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.096Z"}
{"error":"TypeError: Unable to connect. Is the computer able to access the url?\n    at async <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/cli:20817:8877)\n    at async <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/cli:20911:6045)\n    at async _send (/$bunfs/root/cli:1296:46528)","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.096Z"}
{"debug":"Transient ConnectionRefused on initial connect — retry 1/3 in 1000ms","timestamp":"2026-09-08T09:38:02.338Z"}
... (retry 2/3 at 09:38:03.339Z, retry 3/3 at 09:38:05.343Z, final attempt at 09:38:09.346Z — all identical ConnectionRefused within 2-3ms) ...
```

Independent confirmation nothing listens on the port at any point during the session's lifetime:

```
$ curl -sv http://127.0.0.1:35959/mcp --max-time 3
* Trying 127.0.0.1:35959...
* connect to 127.0.0.1 port 35959 from 127.0.0.1 port 57578 failed: Connection refused
* Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 35959 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server

$ ss -tlnp | grep 35959
(no output)
```

Gateway-side systemd journal (`journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service`) shows no error and no trace at all (no grant/bridge/attach/mcp/device-connect log lines) during the same window — nothing on the server side indicates a rejected or failed connection.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`ps aux` at the time, confirming the process tree is alive and not crashed:

```
openclaw           <pid1>  ...  openclaw
openclaw          <pid2>  ...  openclaw-attach
claude             <pid3>  ...  claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config /tmp/openclaw-attach-XXXXXX/.mcp.json
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Any user trying to use `openclaw attach` to bind a locally-spawned Claude Code session to a Gateway session for scoped MCP tool access — this appears to be the CLI's core advertised use case ("Attach Claude Code to a gateway session with scoped MCP tools").
- Severity: Blocks the feature entirely — the spawned Claude Code session is a normal, unattached session in practice (no scoped tools ever become available), even though the CLI reports a successful attach.
- Frequency: 3/3 observed attempts (2 via direct `attach`, 1 via `--print-config` + manual `claude --mcp-config` launch), each with a different ephemeral local port, same failure mode every time.
- Consequence: The Gateway-side agent cannot use the attached client's scoped tools at all; the feature silently no-ops instead of failing loudly (the CLI's own success message is misleading — it says "Attaching Claude Code to session ... (grant expires ...)…" even though the local bridge required for that attachment to actually work never starts).

### Additional information

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO for last-known-good version (this is the first version tested for this specific feature; no prior version was tested to compare against).

Workaround attempted: none found. `--print-config` (which explicitly documents itself as "exit without spawning") was tried as a two-step alternative (mint config, then manually launch `claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <path>` separately) — same result, since it also relies on the same local bridge that is never started by either code path.

Would be happy to provide `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` output or further logs if that helps narrow this down further.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add `--prompt-file <path>` to `openclaw infer model run` so a one-shot prompt can be read from a UTF-8 file instead of passed in process arguments.

## Problem to solve

`openclaw infer model run` accepts prompt text only through `--prompt`. Automation can build prompts larger than an operating system's command-line argument limit, so the process fails before OpenClaw can run the model. Prompt text in argv is also unnecessarily visible to local process inspection.

## Proposed solution

Support exactly one prompt source per invocation: the existing `--prompt <text>` or a new `--prompt-file <path>`. The file input should accept a UTF-8 regular file, reject missing, empty, and oversized inputs, and keep all current model-run behavior unchanged after the prompt has been read.

## Alternatives considered

Splitting a prompt into multiple model calls changes the one-shot request semantics. Calling the Gateway directly bypasses the configured local inference path and requires broader credentials than a local CLI invocation.

## Impact

Affected: operators and automation authors running one-shot model inference with generated prompts.

Severity: workflow-blocking once a prompt exceeds the platform argument-size limit.

Frequency: intermittent, depending on prompt size.

Consequence: automation fails before model dispatch and needs custom workarounds.

## Evidence/examples

Linux limits an individual exec argument independently of the total argument vector. A file-backed input avoids that boundary without changing the configured model, agent, authentication, transport, or response format.

## Implementation intent

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

issues.body:
# Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash). Whether it is a regression is unknown: no earlier version was tested.

# Beta release blocker

No

# Summary

When the stuck-session watchdog kills a cron run because a tool call is blocked waiting for an approval that can never arrive (isolated cron session, no interactive approver), the classification it acted on is discarded at the `abort()` call. The run history keeps the cause-free literal `cron isolated agent run aborted`, and on a chat route the failure alert degrades further, to `Check automation history for details.`

The information exists at abort time and is thrown away one layer above the formatter, so no amount of cron-side formatting can recover it.

**1. Recovery knows the cause.** `resolveSessionAttentionClassification` classifies exactly this state (`src/logging/diagnostic-session-attention.ts`):

```ts
    if (
      params.activity.activeWorkKind === "tool_call" &&
      (params.activity.activeToolAgeMs ?? 0) > params.staleMs &&
      lastProgressAgeMs > params.staleMs
    ) {
      return {
        eventType: "session.stalled",
        reason: "blocked_tool_call",
        classification: "blocked_tool_call",
        activeWorkKind: params.activity.activeWorkKind,
        recoveryEligible: false,
      };
    }
```

`isBlockedToolCallRecoveryEligible` (`src/logging/diagnostic.ts`) then admits that classification for recovery, and the activity snapshot in scope carries the active tool identity (`activeToolName` / `activeToolCallId`), already used in the recovery warn line.

**2. The abort drops it.** `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` passes a reason (`src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts:274`):

```ts
      const result = await abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun({
        sessionId: activeSessionId,
        sessionKey: params.sessionKey,
        settleMs: STUCK_SESSION_ABORT_SETTLE_MS,
        forceClear: true,
        reason: "stuck_recovery",
      });
```

`abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` accepts `reason?: string` and uses it for staleness bookkeeping, but calls the abort with the session id alone (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts:1292`, shipped as `dist/runs-DkiZS9mO.js:607`):

```js
		let aborted = abortEmbeddedAgentRun(params.sessionId) || expiredReplyRun;
```

`abortEmbeddedAgentRun` aborts with `opts?.reason`, which is `undefined` on that overload (`dist/runs-DkiZS9mO.js:379`):

```js
			handle.abort(opts?.reason);
```

The single-session overload cannot carry one at all — its signature is `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId: string): boolean`, and the `reason` parameter exists only on the `sessionId: undefined` overload, typed `reason?: "restart"`. So the classification and the tool identity never reach the `AbortSignal`.

**3. The operator gets a string with no cause.** With nothing attached, cron's finalizer falls to its literal (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run-finalize.ts:309`, shipped as `dist/isolated-agent-BbrXa1yO.js:279`):

```js
	if (finalRunResult.meta?.aborted === true && !cronPayloadOutcome.hasFatalErrorPayload) {
		const error = normalizeOptionalString(finalRunResult.meta.error?.message) ?? "cron isolated agent run aborted";
```

**4. On a chat route the alert does not even carry that string.** `emitFailureAlert` picks the detail lines by route (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts:326-332`): a webhook route prints `Last error: cron isolated agent run aborted`, while every chat route goes through `cronFailureDetailLines(errorReason, failureNotificationDetail)` (`src/cron/failure-notification-text.ts:18`). For this failure both inputs are empty — `errorReason` is `resolveCronRunErrorReason("cron isolated agent run aborted")`, which finds no `FailoverReason` (`src/cron/run-error-reason.ts`), and `failureNotificationDetail` only describes command/script payload failures, not an `agentTurn` one. So the notification body is the generic constant:

```ts
const GENERIC_FAILURE_DETAIL = "Check automation history for details.";
```

An operator watching the alert channel is told a named job failed and nothing else, while the cause was in the gateway's own diagnostics before the abort.

**A second, narrower gap on the same theme.** The immediate (non-hang) form of the same denial is also unclassifiable downstream. `deniedReason` for these is free text — `"allowlist-miss"` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts:1288`) and `"approval-timeout: allowlist-miss"` (`:627`) — while `resolveEmbeddedRunFailureSignal` only recognizes `FAILURE_SIGNAL_CODES = ["SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED", "INVALID_REQUEST"]` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/failure-signal.ts:14`), read off `result.details.errorCode` / `result.errorCode` by `extractToolErrorCode` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-tool-results.ts:445`). Those codes are produced by the approval-binding sites (`src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts:933`), not by the allowlist-miss path — so the coded failure-signal route that does surface a real reason never fires for the common denial.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Give an agent an enforced exec allowlist (`exec-approvals.json`, `security: "allowlist"`) whose default `askFallback` is `allowlist`, i.e. an unlisted command asks for approval.
2. Schedule a cron job for that agent with `sessionTarget: isolated` — no interactive approver exists in the run.
3. Have the job's prompt call `exec` with a command outside the allowlist.
4. Let the run sit until the stuck-session watchdog fires, and read the cron failure alert / run history entry.

# Expected behavior

The failure carries the cause the watchdog already classified: the blocking condition and the command it fired on, e.g. `blocked_tool_call: exec <command>`. Any other abort cause gets its own reason string instead of being flattened into the same text.

# Actual behavior

The run dies at ~150s and reports a cause-free string. Verbatim, from two of our incidents (gateway diagnostics and the cron run history):

```
11:01:23  stalled session  reason=blocked_tool_call  activeTool=exec  (no progress)
11:02:53  recovery abort_embedded_run → run aborted: "cron isolated agent run aborted" (152s)
```

The internal diagnostic names the cause (`reason=blocked_tool_call`, `activeTool=exec`) 90 seconds before the abort; the operator-facing failure never mentions it. Both of our incidents (2026-07-02 and 2026-07-05, same agent, different root command) were diagnosed only by reading the gateway journal by hand — the second one after the generic message had masked the real cause for weeks.

Scope of what was observed versus read: the `cron isolated agent run aborted` text and the diagnostic lines above are verbatim from those two incidents. The chat-route notification body (`Check automation history for details.`) is read from the code path in point 4 — we armed chat-route failure alerts fleet-wide only on 2026-09-04 and no failure of this class has fired since.

# Environment

- openclaw `2026.8.1 (ea80657)`, npm global install (`~/.local/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)
- Linux 6.17.2-1-pve x64, Node v22.23.2
- Verified unchanged on `main` at `d2a674a6c85` (paths and quotes above are from `main`; the two `dist/` quotes are from the installed 2026.8.1 bundle)
- Model-independent: the defect is in the abort/finalize plumbing, not in a provider path. Our affected runs were on `anthropic/claude-opus-5` and the `claude-cli` backend.

# Provider / routing chain

cron scheduler → `runCronAgentTurn` (isolated session) → embedded agent runner → `exec` tool → gateway exec-approval host → allowlist gate with no approver → stuck-session watchdog → `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` → `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` → cron `run-finalize` → `emitFailureAlert`.

# Additional setup details

Local customizations disclosed so they can be ruled out: one first-party plugin (`nexus-context`, prompt/context injection only — it does not touch cron, exec approvals or the embedded runner), per-agent enforced exec allowlists, and agent commands wrapped in shell scripts under `~/.local/bin`. No dist patch is applied for this defect; the quoted bundle lines are stock 2026.8.1.

# Impact and severity

- Every cron failure of this class reaches the operator with no cause. We armed `cron.failureAlert` on a chat route fleet-wide on 2026-09-04, across 31 scheduled jobs, so the generic body is now the default shape of a failure notification here.
- Time-to-notice is the cost: the alert fires immediately but says nothing actionable, so diagnosis requires reading the gateway journal for the `blocked_tool_call` line. In our second incident that gap ran for weeks of daily failures on a job that silently produced nothing.
- Each affected run also burns its full stall window (~150s of model/tool time) before dying.

# Fix shape

Thread the classification and the active tool/command from `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` through `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` → `abortEmbeddedAgentRun` → `handle.abort(reason)` as a real reason object (the single-session overload needs to accept one), and let cron's `resolveCronAbortReasonText` / `run-finalize` surface it as its own string rather than the generic aborted literal. A watchdog abort would then also have a classification to put on the chat route, which today can only print a cause it recognizes as a `FailoverReason`. Separately, attach a structured `errorCode` to allowlist-miss and approval-timeout exec denials so `resolveEmbeddedRunFailureSignal` can classify the immediate form too.
