issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

A recurring isolated cron job recovered from a tool error, successfully sent its Discord report, saved its checkpoint, and ended with `NO_REPLY`; the scheduler nevertheless recorded a tool-warning error and ran it again, producing a second report.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The observed production sequence is below. It has not been replayed in isolation, so these are observations rather than a claimed minimal reproduction.

### Expected behavior

The job explicitly sends and verifies its report before saving its checkpoint and returning `NO_REPLY`; an auxiliary error that it handled before completing should not turn that completed run into a failure. Merged #152165 describes this outcome for confirmed visible message-tool delivery and intentional silent completion.

### Actual behavior

On 13 November 2026 (UTC), with `agentTurn`, isolated session, `delivery.mode: none`, and a recurring 01:00 / 10:00 / 17:00 schedule:

- 01:13:28: `web_fetch` returned an error (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`). The agent continued; at 01:16:24 the native `message` send succeeded, the checkpoint write succeeded, and at 01:16:59 the final assistant response was `NO_REPLY`.
- 01:17:02: the run receipt recorded `error: "⚠️ Web Fetch failed"`. A second run started at 01:18:02, one minute later and well before the next scheduled slot.
- In the second run, a read-only `process` search exited 1 after returning paths; the agent continued and used a located result. At 01:25:01 its native `message` send succeeded, then its checkpoint write succeeded and at 01:25:14 it ended `NO_REPLY`.
- 01:25:19: the second receipt recorded `error: "⚠️ Process failed"`. The recipient received two reports; a failure-streak alert also fired.

The installed scheduler contains a one-minute transient retry at the applicable error count; the interval and schedule are consistent with a retry after the first false failure. The exact warning metadata and reason the delivery suppression did not apply have not been established.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3, official core commit `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`; no local source patches.

### Operating system

Windows 11 x64

### Install method

Official global npm package, native Windows Gateway.

### Model

Effective model identifier omitted.

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw cron → isolated agent turn → OpenAI Codex harness / Responses API → native Discord message tool.

### Logs and evidence

Times and outcomes above were read from the original session transcript events and scheduler receipts. Both session records show completed turns; the second scheduler receipt also records `delivered: true` alongside error status. Full private evidence has been retained; inbox content and private identifiers are omitted here.

The installed `resolveCronPayloadOutcome` excludes `NO_REPLY` from visible recovery text and can retain a structured tool warning as fatal. The finalizer can record a fatal run independently of message delivery. Those source observations are consistent with the receipts, but do not prove the warning's provenance or which delivery metadata reached the classifier in this Codex-harness run. No current-main reproduction has been run.

### Impact and severity

Two completed reports appeared in the same Discord channel for one scheduled slot, followed by an erroneous failure alert. This sequence was observed once across the original run and its repeat; broader frequency is unknown. Repeating an agent turn after it has performed side effects can repeat those effects.

### Additional information

Related: #155597 covers delivery status in failure alerts; #152165 addressed confirmed delivery followed by a silent finish; draft #180922 proposes broader recovery for silent turns after tool errors. This observation adds a confirmed native send and a repeat run with a second report. A useful regression target is a recovered tool error followed by confirmed native delivery, successful checkpoint, and `NO_REPLY`: record success and do not retry; preserve genuine runtime and delivery failures.

Prepared with AI assistance (Codex).

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

System-agent turns prepare agent-scoped memory/wiki context with the synthetic `openclaw` execution identity instead of the verified configured route owner.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure more than one agent, select one as the system-agent route owner, and enable an agent-scoped memory-wiki vault plus a non-legacy context engine.
2. Run a system-agent turn through an embedded harness such as Codex.
3. Observe context assembly attempt memory prompt preparation for agent `openclaw`.

### Expected behavior

Memory prompt supplements are prepared for the verified configured route owner while the system-agent transcript and tool policy remain isolated under the synthetic `openclaw` identity.

### Actual behavior

Context assembly falls back to pipeline messages because memory-wiki rejects the synthetic identity as an unknown configured agent.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1

### Operating system

macOS

### Install method

Source checkout, LaunchAgent gateway

### Model

OpenAI GPT-5.6 through the Codex embedded harness

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw system agent -> verified configured agent route -> Codex embedded harness -> OpenAI

### Additional provider/model setup details

The failure is independent of provider authentication. It occurs before the model request while preparing agent-scoped memory prompt supplements.

### Logs

```shell
context engine assemble failed, using pipeline messages: Error: Unknown memory-wiki agentId: openclaw.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

A focused regression test records the prompt-preparation input: before the fix it receives `agentId: "openclaw"` with `agentSessionKey: "agent:openclaw:main"` even though the verified route owner is a configured agent.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: operators using system-agent turns with agent-scoped wiki recall and a non-legacy context engine
- Severity: moderate; the turn continues, but compiled wiki/memory context is omitted
- Frequency: deterministic for the affected route
- Consequence: repeated warnings and degraded recall during system-agent turns

### Additional information

The Codex app-server thread/turn protocol does not own or transmit OpenClaw agent routing identity, so the canonical fix belongs at OpenClaw's verified system-agent route boundary. The synthetic execution identity must remain in place for transcript and tool-policy isolation.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.3 with `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, a Discord thread created by `/acp spawn claude` never delivers messages to the harness: every dispatch fails with `prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude`, the slash command replies "Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.", and the thread message is dead-lettered after 8 retries.

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (npm global) with the `discord` and `acpx` plugins enabled. `acp.enabled: true`, `acp.backend: "acpx"`, `acp.allowedAgents` includes `"claude"`, and the acpx plugin maps `agents.claude` to `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.63.0.
2. `agents.ownership: "explicit"` with several configured `agents.entries` (none of them named `claude` or `codex`). A Discord channel is routed to one of those configured agents through top-level `bindings`.
3. In that channel, run `/acp spawn claude` with a `--label`. OpenClaw creates a child thread, posts the "session active ... Messages here go directly to this session" intro, and stores a Discord thread binding with `targetKind: "acp"`, `targetSessionKey: "agent:claude:acp:<uuid>"`, `agentId: "claude"`.
4. Send any message in the new thread (or run another `/acp` slash command inside it).

Observed on one live spawn: 1 slash-command interaction failed and the follow-up message failed on all 8 spool attempts, then was dead-lettered. The same `agent:claude:acp:<uuid>` key shape is also produced for `codex`, so the harness name is not specific to Claude.

### Expected behavior

The thread message is dispatched under the channel's configured owner agent and forwarded to the bound ACP session. `docs/tools/acp-agents.md` states "Bound follow-up messages go directly to the ACP session until the binding is closed", and the closing comment on #136400 states that for a bound ACP target "reply dispatch uses the configured source agent's published runtime" (shipped in v2026.8.2).

### Actual behavior

No reply is produced and nothing reaches the harness. Gateway log (UTC):

- `19:04:31 discord/monitor | discord interaction handler failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude`
- `19:05:06 ... 19:07:33 channels/discord | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude` (8 attempts)
- `19:07:33 channels/discord | discord ingress: spooled update <id> on lane channel:<thread-id> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered`

`channel_ingress_events` holds the message with `status: failed`, `attempts: 7`, `failed_reason: retry-limit-exceeded`, `last_error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude`. The `acp_sessions` row for the spawned session stays at `identity.state: "pending"` and `state: idle`; no turn ever ran.

Unlike #136400, the lane did not stay blocked here: the event was dead-lettered (`failed`), not left `pending`, so no manual DB cleanup was needed. Subsequent messages in the same thread hit the same error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.3 (1391f7c). The cited source lines are unchanged at tag v2026.9.4 and on `main` @ fb2e68033c2634d15fd604255f167c3fc72463e7 (not re-tested live on those builds).

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2 (Apple Silicon), Node v26.5.0

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew Node), Gateway as launchd service

### Model

Not reached. Target was the ACP harness `claude` via `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` 0.63.0 (acpx backend); the failure happens in Gateway reply dispatch before any model/harness call.

### Provider / routing chain

discord -> openclaw gateway (thread binding, targetKind acp) -> acpx plugin -> @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp (never reached)

### Additional provider/model setup details

- `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, five entries under `agents.entries`; `agents.entries` contains no entry named `claude` or `codex`.
- `~/.openclaw/agents/claude` and `~/.openclaw/agents/codex` directories exist from earlier (pre-explicit-ownership) ACP sessions but are not configured entries.
- Discord thread bindings are stored by the discord plugin (`plugin_state_entries`, namespace `thread-bindings`); the record's `metadata` has `threadName/agentId/label/boundBy/introText` and no `pluginBindingOwner`, so it is not treated as plugin-owned.

### Logs

```shell
# gateway log, 2026-09-12 UTC, level info, hostnames/ids redacted
19:04:13 plugins           | embedded acpx runtime backend registered (cwd: ~/.openclaw/workspace)
19:04:13 plugins           | embedded acpx runtime backend ready
19:04:31 discord/monitor   | discord interaction handler failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:06 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:10 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:15 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:22 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:33 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:05:52 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:06:27 channels/discord  | discord message run failed: Error: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude
19:07:33 channels/discord  | discord ingress: spooled update <event-id> failed with non-retryable retry-limit-exceeded: prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude; dead-lettered
19:07:33 channels/discord  | discord ingress: spooled update <event-id> on lane channel:<thread-id> reached retry limit after 8 attempts; dead-lettered

# ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite (read-only), redacted
plugin_state_entries: plugin_id=discord namespace=thread-bindings
  {"targetKind":"acp","targetSessionKey":"agent:claude:acp:<uuid>","agentId":"claude","channelId":"<parent-channel>","threadId":"<thread-id>", ...}
channel_ingress_events: event_id=<event-id> lane_key=channel:<thread-id> status=failed attempts=7
  failed_reason=retry-limit-exceeded last_error="prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for claude"
acp_sessions: session_key=@acp:v1:<base64 of ["claude","agent:claude:acp:<uuid>"]> backend=acpx agent=claude
  identity_json.state="pending" state=idle last_error=null
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Source chain, verified on `main` @ fb2e680 (same lines present at v2026.9.4; line numbers from main):

1. `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-acp/lifecycle.ts:130` — `/acp spawn` keys the session as `` `agent:${spawn.agentId}:acp:${randomUUID()}` ``, i.e. the harness id (`claude`) sits in the agent-owner slot. The Discord thread binding stores that key as `targetSessionKey` with `agentId: spawn.agentId`.
2. `src/channels/plugins/binding-routing.ts:105-121` (`resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRoute`) — for a non-plugin-owned binding, core rewrites the inbound route to `sessionKey: boundSessionKey, agentId: resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey(boundSessionKey)`. `extensions/discord/src/monitor/route-resolution.ts:116-117` (`resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute`) does the same on the plugin side, and `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts` returns `baseSessionKey: effectiveRoute.sessionKey`. Result: `ctx.SessionKey = "agent:claude:acp:<uuid>"`, `ctx.AgentId = "claude"`; the channel's configured owner is no longer in the context.
3. `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.gather.ts:148-149` — `sessionKey = ctx.SessionKey ?? ctx.CommandTargetSessionKey` (already the ACP key).
4. `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.gather.ts:406-410` — the #136400 fix: `preparedReplyDispatchAgentId = boundAcpDispatchSessionKey ? resolveSessionAgentId({ sessionKey, config: cfg, fallbackAgentId: ctx.AgentId }) : sessionAgentId`. The comment says "Keep the source owner for Gateway dispatch", but `sessionKey` and `ctx.AgentId` are both the harness key/id by then, so the result is `"claude"`.
5. `src/agents/prepared-reply-dispatch-runtime.ts:46` publishes runtimes only for owners with `provenance === "configured"`; `:162-165` requires exactly one runtime with `runtime.agentId === agentId`, else throws `prepared reply dispatch runtime owner was not published for ${agentId}`. Under explicit ownership `claude` is not a configured agent -> 0 matches -> throw on every attempt.

Existing coverage: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-webchat-acp-binding.test.ts` exercises `resolveBoundAcpDispatchSessionKey` with `SessionKey: "agent:main:dashboard:<uuid>"` (source key preserved), which is the webchat path. The Discord path rewrites `ctx.SessionKey` to the bound ACP key before dispatch, so that test does not cover this case.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: Discord users who run `/acp spawn <harness>` on a Gateway with `agents.ownership: "explicit"` (the layout `openclaw doctor --fix` writes on the 2026.9.x upgrade) when the harness id is not itself a configured agent.
- Severity: blocks workflow — ACP thread sessions are unusable on Discord; the only user-visible signal is "Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details."
- Frequency: deterministic in code; 9/9 dispatch attempts failed on the observed spawn (1 interaction + 8 spool retries).
- Consequence: the user's message is dead-lettered after ~2.5 minutes and the harness never runs; each further message in the thread repeats the failure.

### Additional information

- Related: #136400 (same error, Slack `--bind here`; closed as shipped in v2026.8.2 — the shipped code is present here but is bypassed because the Discord route rewrite happens before it), #132502 (plugin-owned binding identity), #135152 (explicit ownership has no auto-owner fallback).
- Not tested: v2026.9.4 live, Slack/Telegram/webchat, `--bind here` on Discord, and the `agents.entries.<id>.runtime.type = "acp"` configuration. Only the Discord child-thread placement was observed.
- Earlier ACP thread sessions on this Gateway (created 2026-09-01/02, before the upgrade and before `agents.ownership: "explicit"` was written by doctor) reached `identity.state: "resolved"`. The exact last-known-good version was not recorded, so this is filed as a behavior bug rather than a confirmed regression.
- Possible directions (not implemented or tested): carry the pre-rewrite source route (parent channel's configured agent) into dispatch for bound ACP targets, or key spawned ACP sessions under the requesting configured agent as configured ACP bindings already do (`agent:<owner>:acp:binding:...` in `persistent-bindings.types.ts`).

issues.body:
## Summary
`message` tool inline buttons built with `action.type: "callback"` produce a `callback_data` prefixed with `tgcb1:<checksum>:<value>` (opaque plugin-only format). When tapped, the Telegram ingress handler drops the callback with `if (opaqueCallbackData) return;` because no plugin has registered the namespace. There is no fall-through path that delivers the callback back to the model as synthetic text, so button taps do nothing.

## Repro
1. Send a Telegram inline button via the `message` tool:
   ```json
   {"presentation": {"blocks": [{"type": "buttons", "buttons": [{"label": "X", "action": {"type": "callback", "value": "x"}}]}]}}
   ```
2. Tap the button. Nothing happens. Raw-update log shows the callback arrived; `answerCallbackQuery` fires; then silence.

## Root cause (v-current dist paths)
- Builder: `dist/button-types-B2h0t2EL.js:37` — `action.type: "callback"` → `buildTelegramOpaqueCallbackData(value)` → `tgcb1:<checksum>:<value>`
- Dispatcher: `dist/plugin-runtime-DAKxyCb0.js:59` — no plugin match returns `{handled: false}`
- Drop site: `dist/telegram-ingress-spool-Dd3cDhXe.js:3781` — `if (opaqueCallbackData) return;`

Compare `dist/button-types-B2h0t2EL.js:38` (raw `value` field) which uses `callback_data` unwrapped and falls through to synthetic-text delivery via ``genericCallbackText = `callback_data: ${data}` `` at ingress line 3540. That path works.

## Workaround
Use flat `{label, value}` shape instead of `{label, action: {type: "callback", value}}`. Callback arrives to the model as inbound text `callback_data: <value>`.

## Suggested fix
At `telegram-ingress-spool-…js:3781`, if `opaqueCallbackData` is present but no plugin handled it, fall through to the same synthetic-text delivery used by the raw-`value` path (`callback_data: <opaqueCallbackData>` inbound), instead of returning. Alternatively, only wrap in `tgcb1:` when the caller is a plugin with a registered namespace.

## Environment
- OpenClaw (npm global) — Pi5, Linux 6.18.39
- Node v22.23.2
- Telegram DM, `capabilities.inlineButtons: "dm"`
- Confirmed via raw-update log at 21:48:01 EDT on 2026-08-19

issues.body:
When an action in the Control UI Browser panel fails, for example a click on a link that the browser navigation policy blocks, the panel shows "Couldn't complete the browser action. Try again." for a moment and then the message goes away while the live view keeps streaming. The person is left without any sign that their action failed or why.

Steps:
1. Open the Browser panel on a page with a link to an address the navigation policy blocks.
2. Click that link in the panel.
3. Watch the error line above the page.

Expected: the error stays until the person does something else.
Actual: the error is cleared by the panel's own background work. Two passive paths clear it:
- the automatic viewport resize, which runs whenever the streamed page size drifts from the panel size;
- a panel refresh, which runs on presentation, context or session-tab changes.

Both go through code that clears the error before it starts, as if the person had started a new action.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After an in-process Gateway restart, one Telegram conversation on `claude-cli` stopped replying until the Gateway process was fully restarted. First every turn failed after ~185 s with `CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.`; then every turn hung with no output until stuck-session recovery aborted it ~6 min later. Stuck recovery reported `aborted=true drained=true released=0`, and the next turn hung the same way. Other conversations, including new `claude-cli` conversations, kept working. A full process restart (`systemctl --user restart`) cleared it immediately.

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproduced deterministically. Observed sequence (single host, timestamps IST):

1. A Telegram DM conversation pinned to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (claude-cli runtime) has a warm live session (`cli live session start ... activeSessions=1` at 07:27:21); turns at 07:27, 07:30 and 07:31 complete normally on it.
2. 07:31:42 the Gateway performs an in-process restart (`OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`, systemd user unit). Shutdown warns `Plugin google-antigravity-cli forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s)` and `shutdown completed in 5224ms with warnings`.
3. 07:32:19 the next turn on that conversation logs `cli exec: ... useResume=true ... reuse=reusable-drift:system-prompt` and no `cli live session start`. 185 s later: `lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:<hash> durationMs=185037 error="CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended."`
4. The same failure repeats for each turn at 07:35, 07:40 and 07:44 (each ~185 s, each `reuse=reusable`).
5. 07:47:38 the next turn logs `cli exec: ... useResume=false session=none reuse=none` and then nothing more from `agent/cli-backend`: no `cli live session start`, no `cli turn`, no error. Diagnostics report `stalled session ... lastProgress=embedded_run:started`, then stuck recovery aborts it.
6. Every later turn (07:58, 08:11, 08:17, 08:24, 08:35) logs only `cli session history ...` and then stalls the same way until recovery aborts it (`Reply operation expired as stale`, `released=0`).
7. 08:50 full process restart; the next turn on the same conversation completes in 5.8 s.

### Expected behavior

A Claude CLI live process left behind by an in-process restart, or a turn whose plugin iterator does not close in time, should be retired (killed and dropped) or should fail the turn quickly with an actionable error. It should not wedge one conversation until the Gateway process is replaced. When stuck recovery aborts the run, the conversation should be able to make progress on the next turn.

### Actual behavior

The conversation is permanently wedged. Each turn first fails late (~185 s) and then hangs silently until stuck recovery aborts it (~6 min). Recovery does not release anything (`released=0`), so every later message repeats the stall. Only a full Gateway process restart recovers.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1 (npm). Code paths below are unchanged on `main` @ 90dfe90f3c8.

### Operating system

Debian 13 (DietPi), Linux 6.12 x64, Node 26.13.0

### Install method

npm global, systemd user service

### Model

anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 via claude-cli (Claude Code 2.1.318)

### Provider / routing chain

Session override `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` -> bundled `claude-cli` backend (warm live session), Telegram DM.

### Logs

```text
07:31:14 agent/cli-backend cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 durationMs=10383 outBytes=928
07:31:42 Plugin google-antigravity-cli cleanup failed (instance): Plugin google-antigravity-cli forced retirement after 5000ms: 1 still-running call(s), 0 retained consumer(s); resource cleanup remains pending.
07:31:42 shutdown completed in 5224ms with warnings: plugin/acpx, plugin/google-antigravity-cli, plugin/parallel, plugin/tavily, plugin/typesafe
07:32:19 agent/cli-backend cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 promptChars=828 trigger=event useResume=true session=present resumeSession=<id> reuse=reusable-drift:system-prompt historyPrompt=none
07:35:24 diagnostic lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner:<hash> durationMs=185037 error="CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended."
07:35:24 agent/cli-backend cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 durationMs=187209 error=CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.
... (same at 07:38:31, 07:43:38, 07:47:05)
07:47:38 agent/cli-backend cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 promptChars=1238 trigger=user useResume=false session=none resumeSession=none reuse=none historyPrompt=none
07:57:50 diagnostic reply run stale takeover retained: sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:direct:<id> reason=stuck_recovery owner=awaiting_terminal_completion backend=attached
07:58:05 diagnostic stuck session recovery: ... age=614s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=false drained=false released=1
08:04:20 diagnostic stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
08:24:20 diagnostic lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:telegram:direct:<id> durationMs=384855 error="Reply operation expired as stale"
08:30:50 (same)
-- full process restart 08:50 --
10:17:38 agent/cli-backend cli exec: ... useResume=false ... reuse=none
10:17:38 agent/cli-backend cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 activeSessions=1
10:17:43 agent/cli-backend cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 durationMs=5848
```

No Claude Code transcript was written for this conversation after 07:31. A process listing at 08:36, during a stall, showed no `claude` process for this conversation.

### Impact and severity

One conversation (the user's primary Telegram DM) was unusable for ~80 min. Each message cost 3-6 min of silence. Nothing in the UI or logs points at a fix, and stuck recovery repeatedly reports success while the conversation stays wedged. Recovery needs a full process restart, which a chat user cannot trigger when `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` makes `/restart` in-process.

### Additional information

Code reading on `main` @ 90dfe90f3c8 (hypothesis, not proven by a repro):

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts` `finally` calls `closePluginIterator()`. After its 5 s budget (`execute-plugin-iterator.ts`) it throws `CLI plugin runtime did not close after its run ended.` but leaves `iterator.return()` running. In `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`, `executeClaudeCli`'s `finally` awaits `startup` and then `session.handle.waitForExit()`. If the transport startup or exit never settles (plausibly a process or MCP loopback tied to the retired plugin generation), that `return()` never completes.
- `restartCliLiveSession()` (`src/agents/cli-runner/cli-live-session-registry.ts`), used by fresh turns (`useResume=false`), awaits `closeLiveSession("restart")` and the owner's `retiredSessionCleanup` promise inside `runCliCleanup(..., "required")`. For Gateway chat runs `oneShotCliRun` is unset, so `runOwnedAgentCleanup()` (`src/agents/run-cleanup-timeout.ts`) awaits the cleanup with no timeout, and the wait is not raced with the run's abort signal. A `waitForExit()` that never resolves therefore blocks every later turn for that owner. Aborting the run does not release it, which matches `released=0` and the silent stall from 07:47.
- `register()` also refuses (`Previous CLI live session cleanup has not settled.`) while `retiredSessionCleanup` holds the stuck promise, so even a turn that got past the restart could not start a replacement.

Possibly related (both closed): #145378 (plugin hot reload mid-turn) and #112312 (SIGKILL teardown fallback).

## Summary

When `openclaw id rebind` commits the key move but the follow-up publication check fails with a **multi-line** error (for example the Gateway transport error carrying its remedy and connection lines), the CLI prints the whole message on one line with the newlines escaped as literal `\n` sequences.

## Root cause

`src/cli/id-cli.ts` `writeCommittedWarning` passes the entire error message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, which by design escapes control characters — including `\n` — for single-line rendering of untrusted values. Gateway transport errors are intentionally multi-line (`src/gateway/transport-error.ts`: message + remedy + connection details, plus a `Possible causes:` list for close code 1006), so the escaped output is unreadable.

Same bug class as the already-fixed #197255 (`sessions import`) and #197257 (`approvals get`).

## Reproduction

Trigger path: `openclaw id rebind` → `rebind_commit` succeeds → `waitForPublication` polls `openclawId.people` → the Gateway connection drops (or the Gateway stops) → the poll throws a multi-line `GatewayTransportError` → `writeCommittedWarning(..., error, "publication")`.

Observed output (driven through the real `createGatewayUnreachableTransportError` + `sanitizeTerminalText` modules, exact `writeCommittedWarning` text block):

```
Moved to new keys (committed).
Publication check failed: Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (ECONNREFUSED).\nStart it with `openclaw gateway run` or check `openclaw gateway status`.\nGateway ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (local), source: config file
Run openclaw id status to check remote access and publication. Do not repeat rebind: it rotates keys again.
```

The `--json` `publicationError`/`followUpError` values carry the same escaped text instead of the real message.

## Expected

Each line of the failure is sanitized separately and printed on its own line:

```
Moved to new keys (committed).
Publication check failed: Gateway not reachable at ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (ECONNREFUSED).
Start it with `openclaw gateway run` or check `openclaw gateway status`.
Gateway ws://127.0.0.1:18789 (local), source: config file
Run openclaw id status to check remote access and publication. Do not repeat rebind: it rotates keys again.
```

## Environment

- openclaw main @ b2c33ce071bb
- Windows 11, Node 24.16.0 (runtime-independent: formatting bug in shared CLI code)

A fix with a regression test is ready; PR incoming.

### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

### Summary

OpenClaw version: OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)
OS / channel: macOS 27.3 (arm64), webchat / Control UI
Steps to reproduce:
Open OpenClaw Control UI desktop app.
Move mouse to the sidebar bottom build chip (version/build info area).
Wait ~600ms for the hover card (sidebar-hover-card sidebar-build-hover-card) to appear.
Move the mouse from the trigger <a> onto the hover card content to read it.
Expected behavior: The hover card stays open while the mouse is over either the trigger or the card content, so the user has time to read the build info.
Actual behavior: The hover card flashes and immediately disappears as soon as the mouse leaves the trigger <a>, even if the mouse is moving onto the card itself. This makes the card unreadable.
Root cause:
In tooltip-7EQCaNdh.js, the interactionElements callback only returns the trigger element:
interactionElements: () => a.trigger ? [a.trigger] : []
The host element e (the whole openclaw-tooltip, which contains both the trigger <a> and the hover card slot content) is not included. The underlying popover therefore treats leaving the trigger as "mouse left the tooltip" and starts the closeDelay countdown immediately, regardless of whether the cursor is already over the hover card.
Additionally, in sidebar-build-chip-B-P5G6LE.js, closeDelay is set to only 300ms:
n.delay = 600, n.closeDelay = 300, ...
This makes the flicker especially severe — there is almost no time to cross the gap between trigger and card before the popover closes.
Affected files:
assets/tooltip-7EQCaNdh.js
assets/sidebar-build-chip-B-P5G6LE.js
Suggested fix:
Include the host element in interactionElements so hovering the card itself keeps the tooltip open:
interactionElements: () => {
  const t = [];
  if (a.trigger) t.push(a.trigger);
  if (e) t.push(e);
  return t;
}
Increase closeDelay in sidebar-build-chip-B-P5G6LE.js from 300 to at least 800–900 to give users a usable grace period when moving between trigger and card.

OpenClaw 2026.11.3; macOS; Codex runtime; Telegram DM.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Gateway intermittently becomes unresponsive on macOS and requires a restart. Two process samples taken during separate hangs show the main thread waiting for a write lock while closing a worker MessagePort.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The Gateway continues serving requests. Restarting the affected process restored service.

### Actual behavior

Three hangs were recorded on October 14–15. The process remained alive but the Gateway stopped responding. Samples from October 15 at 10:20 and 11:33 HKT show the same main-thread stack for every captured sample (1,808/1,808 and 1,360/1,360 respectively).

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3, local source build `f6cf7bbb60c` (includes local carries, not an unmodified release).

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.1 (25G76), ARM64. Node 26; the captured library is `libnode.147.dylib`. The sample reports do not record the exact Node patch version.

### Install method

Git/source build, Gateway supervised by launchd.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

These excerpts come from `/usr/bin/sample` captures of two separate Gateway processes. Paths and addresses are omitted.

```text
2026-10-15 10:20:52 +0800, pid 22909
1808/1808 main-thread samples:
  node::HandleWrap::OnClose(uv_handle_s*)
  node::worker::MessagePort::OnClose()
  node::worker::SiblingGroup::Disentangle(node::worker::MessagePortData*)
  uv_rwlock_wrlock
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_slow
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_wait
  __psynch_rw_wrlock

2026-10-15 11:33:39 +0800, pid 22320
1360/1360 main-thread samples:
  node::HandleWrap::OnClose(uv_handle_s*)
  node::worker::MessagePort::OnClose()
  node::worker::SiblingGroup::Disentangle(node::worker::MessagePortData*)
  uv_rwlock_wrlock
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_slow
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_wait
  __psynch_rw_wrlock
```

### Impact and severity

One macOS Gateway installation; intermittent complete loss of service, requiring manual restart. Three incidents were recorded over two days. Frequency on other installations is unknown.

### Additional information

Related: #169535 (continuous V8 stall flight recorder).

Disabling only the flight recorder was deployed locally on October 15. No recurrence was recorded during the following 3.5-day observation period. This is an uncontrolled workaround observation, not proof of causation; there is no deterministic reproducer or re-enable/reproduce test.

Both hang samples contain a `v8:ProfEvntProc` thread, mostly in `SamplingEventsProcessor::Run` → `ConditionVariable::WaitFor`. Its presence does **not** establish that the profiler is deadlocked or owns the MessagePort lock. The samples establish the main-thread lock wait, not the lock owner or root cause.

Please investigate the MessagePort-close lock wait on macOS and whether continuous profiling contributes. This report does not propose merging the blanket recorder disable as a fix.

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary
With the `claude-cli` backend, each final assistant reply is stored twice in the session transcript. The iOS app shows both copies, so every reply appears duplicated. The desktop Control UI does not show the duplicate.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf), self-hosted in Docker (Linux x64)
- Model: `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5`
- Client where it is visible: OpenClaw iOS app (`openclaw-ios`, mode `ui`)
- Client where it is not visible: desktop Control UI

### Evidence
Reading a finished iOS session with `sessions_history` shows two consecutive assistant text entries for the same turn, about 380 ms apart. The text is identical in the two entries, except that the second one also has the pre-tool-call commentary text prepended to it.

| | Entry A | Entry B |
|---|---|---|
| provider/api | `claude-cli` / `anthropic-messages` | `claude-cli` / `cli` |
| stopReason | `end_turn` | `stop` |
| origin marker | `__openclaw.importedFrom: "claude-cli"`, plus `cliSessionId` and `externalId` | `__openclaw.runId` and `idempotencyKey: "cli-assistant:<runId>"` |
| key | `externalId` (the CLI's own message uuid) | `cli-assistant:<runId>` |

Entry A looks like it comes from importing Claude Code's local JSONL transcript. Entry B looks like it comes from the live-run write. The two use different idempotency keys, so dedupe doesn't match them.

Not confirmed by me: the exact code path that writes each entry, and why only the iOS client renders both.

### Expected behavior
One stored assistant entry per final reply, or the clients dedupe the imported and live copies.

### Checked
- Still present on 2026.11.2. The 2026.11.3 release notes list no related fix.
- 2026.11.5-beta.2 notes mention duplicate-turn handling for retried committed input, which is a different problem (inputs, not replies). I have not tested it.

issues.body:
# Baseten Chat Completions: retained session emits orphan DSML; request a supported run-scoped capture path

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (8b18b55), Windows, built-in agent runtime.
- Provider endpoint: `https://inference.baseten.co/v1`, API `openai-completions`.
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, reasoning `max`, tools enabled.

## Observed failure

A retained agent session ended normally with an orphan `</｜DSML｜ parameter>` marker in text instead of a structured tool call. The final response contained no function name or arguments and invoked no tool. Response ID: `chatcmpl-59554d6ae7844e27a2cd4947bed19640`.

The gateway prepared tools, opened the provider stream and received HTTP 200. A smaller write-first continuation failed before its first tool, so we stopped retries. The installed adapter already recognizes DeepSeek model IDs and recovers complete DSML invoke blocks; there is no complete call to recover from the retained terminal fragment.

One earlier isolated raw-provider request using the same endpoint/model and max reasoning returned a valid structured `report_probe` call with `{"value":"ok"}` and `finish_reason=tool_calls`. The declared function was inert and never executed. This establishes clean-context endpoint capability only, not recovery or equivalence of the retained OpenClaw request.

The session had context pressure and many prior compactions. Neither has been established as the cause. No history reset, model switch or service/configuration change has been performed.

## Capture capability question

We need one supported, bounded retained-session capture of:

1. The final serialized Chat Completions request, especially complete tool schemas/choice and relevant history shape, with secrets removed.
2. Complete provider SSE events through the terminal finish reason, before DSML recovery/normalization.
3. The corresponding adapter-emitted text/tool events, correlated by run and provider response IDs.

Installed-source inspection found:

- `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_MODEL_PAYLOAD` and `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_SSE` are documented. Their inspected payload/preview call sites are in the Responses transport; the Baseten Chat Completions path uses `streamOpenAICompletionsRequest` and does not invoke those loggers. Full-redacted payload output is also capped at 8,000 characters; SSE peek captures five events, capped at 2,000 characters each.
- `diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled` records redacted pre-transport context/options but its stream-context snapshot does not include `context.tools` or the serialized provider response.
- `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` observes embedded assistant text/thinking, not a proven complete pre-adapter wire capture. Session `/trace raw` is likewise a reply diagnostic, not the wire request.
- The debug capture implementation has guarded-fetch request/response capture and a 16 MiB response limit. Its settings are process-scoped (`OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED`, capture session ID, optional proxy URL). `openclaw proxy run` configures a new child; wrapping a gateway RPC client does not instrument the already-running gateway. We found no documented retained-session-only switch and have not enabled capture, changed routing or restarted anything.

What supported operation captures these three boundaries for exactly one existing session/run, while preserving its model, history, direct provider route and unrelated sessions? If current support is process-wide only, please identify the minimal supported enable/disable procedure, content/redaction limits and completeness markers before we authorize a maintenance capture. A parser fix should not invent a callable from the orphan marker.

No credentials, raw prompts/history, private source, local paths, or attachments are included in this report. The original wire response was not captured, so provider-versus-adapter attribution remains unresolved.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Gemini 4 Hydrogen accepts Google's `XHIGH` thinking level, but OpenClaw refuses `--thinking xhigh` for it, and when `xhigh` comes from config it quietly sends `HIGH`, even for a model row that maps `xhigh`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a `google-vertex` provider with a `gemini-4-hydrogen` model row that has `thinkingLevelMap: { "minimal": null, "xhigh": "xhigh" }`. (Our run pointed the base URL at a local stub that records request bodies. A real Vertex setup behaves the same.)
2. Run `openclaw agent --model google-vertex/gemini-4-hydrogen --thinking xhigh --message "Reply with just: pong"`.
3. Set `agents.defaults.models["google-vertex/gemini-4-hydrogen"].params.thinking` to `xhigh` and run the same command without `--thinking`. Look at the request's `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`.

### Expected behavior

Google lists `xhigh` among Hydrogen's thinking levels ([model page](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-4-hydrogen); AI Studio calls it "Extra High"), and a direct Vertex call accepts it (see Logs). OpenClaw should offer `xhigh` for Hydrogen and send `thinkingLevel: XHIGH`.

### Actual behavior

- Step 2 fails: `Thinking level "xhigh" is not supported for google-vertex/gemini-4-hydrogen. Use one of: off, low, medium, adaptive, high, ultra.`
- Step 3 runs, but the request carries `"thinkingConfig": {"includeThoughts": true, "thinkingLevel": "HIGH"}`.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.1. Current `main` (`d30e45c3f48`) has the same code paths.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

### Install method

npm global

### Model

google-vertex/gemini-4-hydrogen

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw embedded runtime -> `google-vertex` (API key) -> Vertex AI. The repro used a local stub at the Vertex base URL.

### Additional provider/model setup details

The same applies to `google/gemini-4-hydrogen` from the bundled catalog that #197863 added.

### Logs

Direct Vertex calls on 2026-11-12 (`us` endpoint, `generateContent`, the same short reasoning prompt each time):

| model | thinkingLevel | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gemini-4-hydrogen | `XHIGH` | HTTP 200, 7,314 thought tokens |
| gemini-4-hydrogen | `HIGH` | HTTP 200, 542 thought tokens |
| gemini-4-carbon | `XHIGH` | HTTP 400 `Thinking level is unsupported: THINKING_LEVEL_XHIGH` |

So `XHIGH` is a real, deeper level, and support differs per model, not per Gemini family.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: users of Gemini 4 Hydrogen through the Gemini API or Vertex.
- Severity: annoying. The deepest reasoning level Google offers for this model can't be used, and the config path downgrades it without a warning.
- Frequency: always.
- Consequence: shallower reasoning than the user configured.

### Additional information

#197863 added Hydrogen to the catalog and deferred `xhigh` "for a separate change with a dated live probe". The table above is that probe. A fix PR follows: catalog rows opt in with `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh: "xhigh"`, which the bundled Hydrogen row then has. Rows without it keep today's behavior, which matters because Carbon rejects `XHIGH`.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Where `xhigh` is lost, at `d30e45c3f48`:

- `resolveGoogleThinkingProfile` (`extensions/google/provider-policy.ts`) offers off/minimal/low/medium/adaptive/high for Gemini 3 and 4 and never `xhigh`, so session and CLI validation refuse it. The generic layer (`getSupportedThinkingLevels`, `packages/ai/src/model-utils.ts`) already treats a row's `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh` entry as support; the Google profile ignores it.
- `getGoogleThinkingLevel` (`packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts`) has no XHIGH case, so `xhigh` falls through to `HIGH`.
- `resolveGoogleGemini3ThinkingLevel` (`src/llm/providers/stream-wrappers/google-thinking-payload.ts`) maps `xhigh` and `max` to `HIGH`. Two payload wrappers run it after the transport: the Google provider's `wrapStreamFn`, and `createGoogleThinkingPayloadWrapper`, which the embedded runner applies to every `google-generative-ai` request.
- `@google/genai` 2.32's `ThinkingLevel` enum has no `XHIGH` member, but the API accepts the string.

</details>

issues.body:
### Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.3 (59cb447)**, Homebrew Node 26.11.1, macOS 26.3 arm64 (Mac mini, 16 GB RAM)
- WhatsApp channel (Baileys), Gateway as LaunchAgent, scheduled command jobs run Python scripts that call the CLI

### What happens

**1. `openclaw message send` is slow to start, even with `--dry-run`.**
A WhatsApp dry run on an idle machine takes **16.7 s**; four dry runs started in parallel all finish together after **41 s** (they run concurrently rather than queueing). On the same machine a thin RPC client is fast: `openclaw automations status` 0.5 s, `openclaw gateway call send` (invalid params probe) 0.8 s.

```
openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target <group jid> --message "dry run" --dry-run --json   # 16.7 s
```

**2. In a scheduled command job the process sometimes keeps running for minutes after the message was delivered.**
The job calls `openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target <group jid> --message <text> --json` with a 120 s timeout. Four of its last six runs ended in the timeout; in the other two the CLI returned and the receipt was recorded. Gateway log of the 29 Oct 13:02 run (times local, UTC+8):

```
13:02:56.017 gateway/channels/whatsapp/outbound  Sending message -> sha256:...
13:02:56.993 gateway/channels/whatsapp/outbound  Sent message 3EB0... -> sha256:... (980ms)
13:02:57.042 gateway/ws  res ok send 1045ms channel=whatsapp bytes=187
13:04:39     the job kills the CLI at its 120 s timeout (started about 13:02:39)
```

The message was in the group at 13:02:57. So the Gateway answered the `send` request in about one second and the CLI was still running 100 s later. We do not know whether it had printed its JSON, because the caller discards the output on timeout. The script then recorded the send as failed and the scheduler recorded the job as failed (3 consecutive errors, error backoff), although every message had been delivered.

### Expected

`message send` should exit shortly after the Gateway reports the send, and a dry run should not need several seconds of CPU.

### Workaround that works for us

Call the Gateway method directly: `openclaw gateway call send --params '{"to":"<jid>","message":"...","channel":"whatsapp","idempotencyKey":"<unique>"}' --json` (0.8 s round trip for the validation probe; the docs say `gateway call` does not preload plugin runtimes).

### Related

Possibly the same cause as an earlier observation of `message send` returning only after 60 s although the message had been delivered. Our Gateway also logs many `slow SQLite transaction hold` warnings (see #176067), which may or may not be related.

### Summary

The iOS Share Extension can't deliver to a Gateway protected by Cloudflare Access via the interactive Access sign-in flow, even when the main app is signed in and connected. Sharing a URL + note fails with:

```text
Send failed: This gateway uses Cloudflare Access. Open OpenClaw and send from the app; your share stays here.
```

`docs/platforms/ios.md` ("Cloudflare Access sign-in") documents this as current behavior, so this is a feature request to close the gap rather than a regression.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Put the Gateway behind Cloudflare Access (interactive SSO login, no service-token headers).
2. In the iOS app, complete **Connect → Access sign-in → Continue**; the main app connects and chats normally.
3. In Safari, share a URL to OpenClaw, add a note, tap **Send to OpenClaw**.

### Expected

The share is delivered using the same Access session the main app already holds, like token/password Gateways.

### Actual

The extension refuses to send and asks the user to open the app. The only workaround is copying the content into the app by hand, which defeats the share sheet for every Access-protected Gateway.

### Proposed solution

Any of these would work:

- Bridge the app's Access session grant (scoped to the exact Gateway stable ID / Access host, kept in an App Group Keychain item) to the extension, under the same binding and clearing rules as the existing share-relay token/password.
- Or hand the share off: queue it in the App Group container and have the extension open the main app (or have the main app deliver it on next foreground), so the user gets one tap instead of manual copy/paste.

Related: #136103 (custom proxy headers for the Share extension, closed as stale) covers service-header Gateways; this covers the interactive Access sign-in path.

issues.body: ### Bug type Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash) ### Beta release blocker No ### Summary After a Codex-native parent has already received successful child results via wait_agent and produced its final response, OpenClaw can still create a second synthetic announce:codex-native Main that repeats the final answer; the same failure chain was independently observed through both Telegram and WebChat. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use an existing OpenClaw conversation/session backed by Codex. 2. Restart the OpenClaw Gateway / Codex app-server lifecycle. 3. Continue using the same conversation after the restart. 4. Send a request that first produces a normal user-visible progress message, then spawns one or more Codex-native children, waits for their terminal results with wait_agent, and produces a final answer after receiving all child results. 5. In the failing observations, the native child or children complete successfully and the original Main receives their results and produces the correct final answer. 6. Immediately afterward, inspect the gateway log. 7. In the failing runs, OpenClaw logs: Active requester session could not be woken for subagent completion; falling back to requester-agent handoff: active requester session could not be woken: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming 8. A separate announce:codex-native:::succeeded Main run is then created and produces the same final answer again. This sequence was independently observed once through Telegram and once through WebChat / Control UI. In the current WebChat case, immediately repeating an equivalent orchestration request in the same session did not reproduce the duplicate. The exact reproduction rate has not been established. ### Expected behavior When the active parent has already received the successful terminal child result through wait_agent and incorporated that result into its final response, the same child completion should not create another requester-visible Main execution. As a known-good comparison, an immediately repeated equivalent WebChat orchestration in the same session produced only one final response. ### Actual behavior The native child or children complete successfully, the original Main receives their results, and the original Main produces the correct final response. After that response is already complete, OpenClaw attempts to wake the requester for subagent completion. The wake fails with: queue_message_failed reason=not_streaming OpenClaw then falls back to a requester-agent handoff and creates a separate: announce:codex-native:...:succeeded Main run. That second Main produces the same final answer again. This is not one assistant message being rendered twice. issues.body:
### Summary

Settings → Talk sets up realtime voice (provider, model, voice) but not the speech-to-text model that Control UI dictation and Gateway-relay transcription use, and it has no way to add the provider key that model needs. Setting up Talk takes three pages today.

### Problem to solve

- Talk transcription (`talk.session.create({ mode: "transcription" })`, used by Control UI dictation) falls back to the media-understanding audio models in `tools.media.models` when no streaming transcription provider is configured. Those models are only editable in the raw `tools` schema editor under Settings → AI Agents.
- Picking which audio model wins means editing `tools.media.audio.preferredModel` by hand and making sure a matching, audio-tagged `tools.media.models` entry exists.
- An OpenRouter speech-to-text model (for example `openrouter/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo`) also needs an OpenRouter key, which is set on Settings → Models, not on Talk.
- `talk.catalog` already reports transcription readiness (`transcription.ready`, `activeProvider`, per-provider `configured`), but the Talk page doesn't show it, so a missing key or model only surfaces when dictation fails.

### Proposed solution

Add a "Speech to text" section to Settings → Talk, below Realtime voice, using only existing config paths and RPCs:

1. **Status:** readiness and active provider from the `transcription` group of the `talk.catalog` read the page already makes.
2. **Speech-to-text model picker:** lists the audio-tagged `tools.media.models` entries, plus "Automatic" and a free-text `provider/model` option. A pick writes `tools.media.audio.preferredModel`; a `provider/model` with no matching entry is first appended to `tools.media.models` with `capabilities: ["audio"]`. "Automatic" clears only the preference.
3. **OpenRouter API key:** a key field that saves through `models.authSetApiKey` (the RPC Settings → Models uses), for `talk.agentId` or else the default agent, then re-reads the catalog so readiness updates.

No new config options, RPCs or schema changes. The picks go into the same config the Tools editor shows, so both stay in sync. `tools.media.audio` also drives inbound voice-note transcription, and the section says so.

### Alternatives considered

- Link from Talk to the Models and AI Agents pages instead: still three pages, and the `tools.media` part has no curated UI at all.
- A Talk-only transcription config: a second owner for the same choice, and voice notes and dictation would drift apart.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone setting up Talk or Control UI dictation, especially with OpenRouter for speech-to-text.
- Severity: annoying; blocks setup for users who don't know the `tools.media` config shape.
- Frequency: every new Talk / dictation setup.
- Consequence: dictation fails until the user finds the raw config keys and the Models page.

### Evidence/examples

Config the new section writes for an OpenRouter model (same shape as `docs/providers/openrouter.md`, "Speech-to-text"):

```json5
{
  tools: {
    media: {
      models: [
        { provider: "openrouter", model: "openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo", capabilities: ["audio"] },
      ],
      audio: { preferredModel: "openrouter/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo" },
    },
  },
}
```

Readiness: `talk.catalog` → `transcription.ready` / `activeProvider`, with the OpenRouter provider's `configured` flag for the key.

Known limit: the key badge reflects that a credential is present, not that the provider accepts it (Settings → Models runs a provider check after saving; the Talk section doesn't).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

Related but separate: #192869 (Talk settings showing which login and billing each OpenAI transport uses).

**Version:** 2026.11.5-beta.2

On the Skills page, a skill counts as Ready only when `eligible && !blockedByAgentFilter`. Every other skill that isn't disabled lands in **Needs Setup**. **Observed:** an agent with a 50-skill allowlist showed 106 Needs Setup. Of those, 103 were eligible and filtered out only by the allowlist, and 3 had genuinely missing requirements. An agent with an empty allowlist shows every enabled skill as Needs Setup.

**Expected:** skills that are eligible but outside the agent's allowlist appear in a separate state (for example "Not enabled for this agent") or are left out of Needs Setup, and the tooltip names the reason. Needs Setup should list only missing bins, env, config or OS requirements.

**Repro:** configure two agents with different `agents.entries.<id>.skills` allowlists, open Skills, and switch agents. Compare the Needs Setup count with `openclaw skills list --agent <id> --json`, keeping only skills where `.eligible` is false.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the Control UI on desktop, **Search groups** in a session's **Move to group** menu shows "No groups match your search." when the group name and the typed query spell the same accented letter in different Unicode forms: precomposed `ü` (U+00FC) versus `u` followed by a combining diaeresis (U+0075 U+0308). The phone sheet's group search already matches these, and the docs describe that behavior for phones only.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Gateway from `main` (`4ab02e3c087`) with the Control UI enabled and open it on a desktop-width browser window.
2. Create a session and nine groups (the desktop menu shows **Search groups** above eight), one of them named `München` (decomposed `ü`) and one named `Café` (precomposed `é`), for example with `sessions.groups.create`.
3. Right-click the session in the sidebar and open **Move to group**.
4. Type `münchen` with a precomposed `ü` into **Search groups**.
5. Type `café` with a decomposed `é` (`e` + U+0301).

### Expected behavior

Each query shows its group, under the name as stored: `münchen` shows **München** (still stored as `M u U+0308 n c h e n`), and the decomposed `café` shows **Café** (stored as `C a f U+00E9`). An unaccented query such as `munchen` still shows no group, and an ASCII query such as `doc` still shows **Docs**.

### Actual behavior

Both queries show no group and the menu says "No groups match your search." The unaccented `munchen` also shows none, and `doc` shows **Docs**.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (main `4ab02e3c087`)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8), Chromium

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no model is involved; this is a Control UI menu)

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI -> local Gateway (`sessions.groups.create`, session list)

### Additional provider/model setup details

No provider is configured; no model request is made.

### Logs

```text
query (code points)      shown groups   "No groups match your search."
münchen (6d fc ...)      none           yes
café (... 65 301)        none           yes
munchen (ASCII)          none           yes
doc (ASCII)              Docs           no
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

`münchen` typed into **Search groups** with the group `München` (decomposed) present:

![Before: no groups match](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261112-196046-desktop-group-search-nfc/before-search-munchen.png)

### Impact and severity

Affected: desktop Control UI users with more than eight session groups whose names contain accented letters.
Severity: annoying. The group exists and is listed when the search is empty, but the search says no group matches.
Frequency: always, when the stored name and the typed text use different Unicode forms of the same letter.
Consequence: the group cannot be found through the search.

### Additional information

The desktop filter in `groupOptions()` (`ui/src/components/session-menu-view.tsx`) lowercases the query and the names but does not NFC-normalize them. The phone sheet's filter of the same list does, since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191945; the desktop **Search groups** field was added later by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197653. The Sessions list search on the Gateway side also NFC-normalizes when it matches a session's group (read in the source of the same `main`).

### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
Session-target scheduled checks repeatedly fail before inference for a missing recorded inference-account binding, but their scheduler outcomes replace the actionable refusal with `Session event execution failed`; a supervisor retried ten times and was disabled while independent worker continuations continued succeeding.

Related: #191936 (account selection/recovery UI), #193855 (explicit agent-account delegation). This report concerns error propagation and unattended failure visibility, not a request to bypass account authorization. #194441 concerns separate child-dispatch custody failures and is not the cause established here.

### Steps to reproduce
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

The following is a recovered production incident, not a newly executed minimal reproduction. Investigate this state combination: a scheduled agent turn targeting an existing orchestration session, no recorded job inference-account binding, and the Codex route resolving a stored configured account. Let a scheduled occurrence execute and compare its inner lane error with its outer scheduler outcome. No credentials should be removed or substituted to reproduce this.

### Expected behavior
The inner refusal already names the missing recorded account decision and a supported repair. Preserve that actionable cause in the scheduler's run outcome/diagnostics and disabled-job report, with appropriate account redaction. Keep the authorization guard intact. A separate worker's successful execution must not be interpreted as proof that its supervisory automation is healthy.

### Actual behavior
On November 7, 2026, the supervisor had ten correlated failures between 08:50 and 14:36 UTC+08, then was automatically disabled. Two one-shot checks also failed and were disabled. Their inner errors named the missing account binding; outer cron records and inspected job states reported only `Session event execution failed`.

The configured account was resolved, but its use was not recorded for these scheduled occurrences. This is not evidence of an expired login or unavailable credentials. The guard refused execution before model inference.

### OpenClaw version
Incident Gateway: 2026.11.1, commit b9d3e55ad90c4547308718feb5ef5f6f4d6a8d36. These are incident-time facts, not a claim about current main.

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.1 (25G76), arm64 (incident environment).

### Install method
Git checkout; local Gateway.

### Model
openai/gpt-6.1-sol; execution runtime reported as codex.

### Provider / routing chain
Gateway scheduled/session-event execution -> Codex runtime -> configured OpenAI stored account. Refused before inference.

### Additional provider/model setup details
Account identifier redacted as `openai:<configured-account>`. The existing account guard is working as written; the defect reported here is the loss of its actionable diagnosis across the session-event/scheduler boundary. Why these jobs lacked bindings, when that state arose, and whether creation/upgrade displayed a warning are not established.

### Logs
Recovered Gateway log correlation; all timestamps below are November 7, 2026, UTC+08. Job names are reduced to roles; unrelated jobs, account identity, hosts, paths, and conversation identifiers are omitted.

| Time | Job role | Outer scheduler error |
|---|---|---|
| 08:50:34.001 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 09:00:09.228 | Deadline check | Session event execution failed |
| 09:03:06.648 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 09:10:33.893 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 09:20:33.493 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 09:35:40.695 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 10:35:46.598 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 11:35:54.152 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 12:00:01.038 | Soak check | Session event execution failed |
| 12:35:59.889 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 13:36:05.487 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |
| 14:36:10.990 | Supervisor | Session event execution failed |

Representative paired records (same occurrence, correlated by adjacent timestamps; inner run ID and outer job ID are different identifiers):
```text
12:00:00.901 lane=cron-nested durationMs=62
  taskKind=cron
  error="Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime codex would run
  openai/gpt-6.1-sol with stored account openai:<configured-account>.
  Record the account with openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model
  openai/gpt-6.1-sol@openai:<configured-account>.
  For eligible host-managed accounts, openclaw doctor --fix can record it
  without pinning the model."
12:00:01.038 cron: job run returned error status
  jobRole=SoakCheck error="Session event execution failed"
12:00:01.038 cron: disabling one-shot job after error
  consecutiveErrors=1 reason="permanent error"

14:36:10.931 lane=cron-nested durationMs=38
  error="Automation has no recorded inference account. Runtime codex would run ..."
14:36:10.990 cron: job run returned error status
  jobRole=Supervisor error="Session event execution failed"
14:36:10.991 cron: auto-disabled job after consecutive run failures
  jobRole=Supervisor consecutiveErrors=10 error="Session event execution failed"
```
The original inner refusal is abbreviated only in the second example. The first example retains the repair wording with account identity redacted. Ten supervisor failures are ten occurrences, not double-counted inner/outer log records.

Inspected job snapshots corroborated disabled state and `consecutiveErrors=10` for the supervisor, and disabled state with one error for each one-shot. Its failure notification also recorded a separate delivery error requiring an explicit channel when multiple channels were configured; that secondary routing failure did not cause the inference refusal.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
No screenshot is attached or relied on for exact job attribution. The evidence above is a sanitized transcription of Gateway log records, corroborated by inspected automation state. The raw private log and local correlation JSON are retained locally; the relevant redacted evidence is included here so the report does not depend on inaccessible local links.

At the incident commit, the refusal condition is visible in:
- [run-prompt-executor.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b9d3e55ad90c4547308718feb5ef5f6f4d6a8d36/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts): `trigger === "cron" && !binding && authProfileId`, followed by `createUnrecordedScheduledAccountRefusal` before `runCliAgent`.
- [scheduled-unrecorded-account.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b9d3e55ad90c4547308718feb5ef5f6f4d6a8d36/src/agents/scheduled-unrecorded-account.ts): constructs the actionable refusal and stops fallback rather than silently switching accounts.

These source paths explain the inner refusal; the exact boundary discarding its cause has not been isolated or patched.

### Impact and severity
Affected: one local orchestration installation, its recurring supervisor, and two scheduled checks. Blocks unattended supervision/check execution. Twelve correlated account refusals are documented: ten supervisor occurrences and two one-shots. Frequency on other installations is unknown. Independent worker continuation successes do not restore the supervisory safety net.

### Additional information
Separate mechanisms were initially conflated during investigation and are explicitly excluded:
- Child-session state-change notifications caused repeated parent reconciliation acknowledgments. Those are not successful scheduled checks or proof of recovery.
- The worker continuation had independent successes and a separate setup timeout. No evidence establishes that timeout was caused by account binding.
- The five-model child-completion dispatch matrix associated with #194441 did not reproduce this account-binding path. It is not validation of these jobs.
- No claim that a fresh human message repairs a missing recorded account binding.

No production patch, account/configuration change, restart, credential substitution, or repair test was performed for this report. No deterministic red/green regression test exists yet. Last known good version and introducing commit: NOT_ENOUGH_INFO.

Suggested validation for a fix: exercise the real scheduled existing-session boundary with a missing binding; assert the run outcome and disabled-job diagnostics preserve a safe actionable cause; retain refusal and no-account-fallback assertions; separately verify an explicitly authorized binding can execute. Do not relax account-owner/revocation checks.

AI-assisted investigation and report, reviewed against the retained log timeline. Only relevant sanitized excerpts are published; the full conversation contains unrelated private information.

issues.body:
### Summary

Support Telegram Bot API 10.4 HTML widgets in the Telegram channel: send a widget, update its state in place, and receive/answer `widget_query` updates.

### Problem to solve

Bot API 10.4 (2026-11-09) adds HTML widgets: one self-contained HTML document (≤ 32 KB, ≤ 4 KB after zlib level 9) rendered inside the message bubble, running in a network-less QuickJS sandbox. The code is fixed at send time; only the state changes (`chat_data` / `public_data`, ≤ 1024 bytes each), and only the bot can write it. For agents this is a natural surface for status that should live in one message and change over time — e.g. a daily-brief or job-status card updated after each cron/heartbeat run — instead of a new message per run.

Checked on 2026.11.3 (`latest`) and 2026.11.5-beta.1, neither can use it:

- **No outbound path.** The `message` tool has no widget action, and the bundled grammY 1.46.0 has no methods/types for `sendWidget`, `editMessageWidgetData` or `answerWidgetQuery`.
- **No inbound path.** `resolveTelegramAllowedUpdates()` (`extensions/telegram/src/allowed-updates.ts`) sends an explicit `allowed_updates` list built from grammY `DEFAULT_UPDATE_TYPES`, which has no `widget_query` / `shared_widget_query`. So even a widget sent with `allow_queries` through a raw API call would never get its queries delivered to the Gateway.

### Proposed solution

Phased, smallest useful piece first:

1. **Outbound, no queries.**
   - `message` action (e.g. `widget-send`) → `sendWidget` with `html`, optional `width` / `height`, `chat_data` / `public_data`, `caption`, `reply_markup`; returns the message id.
   - `widget-edit` → `editMessageWidgetData(chat_id, message_id, chat_data?, public_data?)`.
   - Validate the 32 KB / 4 KB-compressed / 1024-byte limits locally with a clear error. `api.raw` calls are fine until grammY ships types.
2. **Inbound queries.** Add `widget_query` (later `shared_widget_query`) to allowed updates behind config and route it to the session as a structured event. Timing matters: `answerWidgetQuery` must be called within 15 s, and a user can send at most 5 queries per 5 s — shorter than a typical agent turn. Suggest the Gateway answers immediately (empty/deterministic answer, or a plugin hook for a deterministic handler) and the agent's real result lands later via `editMessageWidgetData`.
3. **Later.** Shared widgets (`sendSharedWidget`, `editSharedWidgetData`; public data editable at most once per second), plus the other 10.4 items if not already planned: `ephemeral_message_parameters` on callback replies and `quote_rich_texts` in `ReplyParameters`.

Capability gate: in production, widgets currently work only in the private chat with the bot (protected content, can't be forwarded or copied); groups, inline mode and forwards are test-server only. The action should fail clearly outside DMs instead of silently falling back.

### Alternatives considered

- **Mini App:** needs hosting, opens in a WebView on demand, not visible in the chat flow.
- **Re-sending a rich message each run:** works, but piles up messages and has no in-place state.
- **Calling the Bot API from a workspace script:** needs the channel bot token outside the Gateway, and still can't receive queries, because the Gateway's polling owns `getUpdates` with the restricted `allowed_updates`.

### Impact

- Affected: Telegram channel users who want persistent, in-place agent UI.
- Severity: feature gap, not a bug.
- Frequency: every cron/heartbeat-style status update is currently a new message.
- Consequence: chat clutter; no in-bubble interactive UI for agents.

### Evidence/examples

- Changelog: https://core.telegram.org/bots/api-changelog#november-9-2026
- Widgets guide: https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets
- Methods/types: [sendWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendwidget), [editMessageWidgetData](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#editmessagewidgetdata), [answerWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerwidgetquery), [WidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery)
- Existing Bot API 10.3 support: `docs/channels/telegram/rich-messages.md`

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

TON wallet query types (`WidgetQueryTypeSignData`, `WidgetQueryTypeSentTransaction`) and wallet cards are out of scope here. They involve user signing and transactions and probably deserve a separate, explicitly opt-in design.

issues.body:
I use Telegram's topics inside the private chat with my bot. With `channels.telegram.widgets: true`, I want to ask for a widget in one topic, see it there, and have its buttons continue that same conversation.

The support added in #196991 deliberately excludes topics because widget queries do not contain a thread ID. A normal private chat is supported; the same conversation inside a private-chat topic is not.

To reproduce:

1. Enable widgets for the Telegram account.
2. Open a topic in the private chat with the bot.
3. Ask the agent to show a small interactive widget.

The Telegram presenter rejects this context when the target or delivery context contains a thread ID, so the native widget route is unavailable. Source: [widget-presenter.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b22f35f7ed76552778bc185cc65a6177e8ad8b02/extensions/telegram/src/widgets/widget-presenter.ts#L71). Our running build is 2026.11.3 with local patches; this is source-confirmed rather than a clean-main client reproduction.

Telegram's [sendWidget API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendwidget) supports `message_thread_id` in private chats with bot forum mode enabled. [WidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) identifies the chat and message but does not include that thread ID.

The missing piece is the full round trip: retain the topic of a widget OpenClaw sent, use that trusted message binding when a query arrives, and update the original widget from the same session. Two topics in one private chat must stay separate. Missing or invalid bindings must not move a query into the root chat or another topic.

Plain private chats, the widget opt-in and current sender authorization should keep working. Group, channel, inline and forwarded widgets are outside this request. Local Bot API/proxy upgrades are separate work; upgrading those alone does not remove OpenClaw's topic guard.

Related: #196941 and #196991. I did not find a separate issue or PR for private-chat widget topics.
