### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When a Discord slash command's reply carries text plus an attachment that fails to load at delivery (a remote URL that answers 404, or a local path outside the allowed media roots), no follow-up message is sent for that reply: the text is lost and only a Gateway error log (agent reply) or a thrown error (plugin command) remains. Telegram keeps the text with a per-file receipt for the same failure since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186751.

### Steps to reproduce

The steps below are the expected live route; they were not run in a Discord client (bots cannot issue slash commands). What was observed came from the Discord plugin's slash-command entry points, as described under the provider details below.

1. Run a Gateway from `main` (`5d6a026e4375`) with a Discord bot account and slash commands enabled.
2. Run a slash command whose agent reply is `Report ready` plus `MEDIA:https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/docs/does-not-exist-609.png` (the URL answers HTTP 404).
3. Alternatively, run a plugin slash command whose reply is `Workspace report` plus a local file outside the allowed media roots.

### Expected behavior

The reply text arrives, followed by a receipt line for the file that could not be attached (`⚠️ does-not-exist-609.png: Delivery failed. Try sending this file again.`), as Telegram does since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186751. Attachments that did load are still sent.

### Actual behavior

Observed: the agent reply sends no follow-up message, and the Gateway logs `discord slash final reply failed: MediaFetchError ... HTTP 404`. The plugin reply sends no follow-up message and `LocalMediaAccessError` escapes the command handler.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (main `5d6a026e4375`)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout

### Model

Not model specific (the reply is fixed; no provider request is needed to reproduce)

### Provider / routing chain

Discord slash command -> agent reply or plugin command reply -> Discord interaction follow-up

### Additional provider/model setup details

Reproduced through the Discord plugin's slash-command entry points with the real reply pipeline and real media loading against the public 404 URL above; Discord's interaction API was recorded instead of called, and the model turn was replaced by one fixed reply carrying the URL as reply media, so `MEDIA:` parsing of a model reply was not exercised.

### Logs

```text
discord slash final reply failed: MediaFetchError: Failed to fetch media from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/docs/does-not-exist-609.png: HTTP 404 Not Found; body: 404: Not Found
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Agent slash reply on `main`: follow-ups sent: none. Plugin slash reply on `main`: follow-ups sent: none, error `LocalMediaAccessError: Local media path is not under an allowed directory`.

### Impact and severity

Anyone whose slash command reply names an attachment that cannot be loaded loses the whole answer text: no follow-up message is sent for it.

### Additional information

The reply is loaded in one step before the first follow-up, so one failed attachment aborts the whole reply.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On npm installs of 2026.11.5-beta.1 and beta.2, Gateway startup with Bonjour enabled logs `gateway discovery service failed (bonjour, plugin=bonjour): Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '.../node_modules/@homebridge/ciao/native.js'`, and the Bonjour advertiser fails to start. 2026.11.2 and 2026.11.3 import the package root instead.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Install into an unused prefix:
   ```sh
   PREFIX="$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc-beta.XXXXXX)"
   npm install --prefix "$PREFIX" openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.2
   ```
2. `grep -o 'import("@homebridge/ciao[^"]*")' "$PREFIX"/node_modules/openclaw/dist/advertiser-*.mjs`
   prints `import("@homebridge/ciao/native.js")`.
3. `ls "$PREFIX"/node_modules/@homebridge/ciao` prints only `LICENSE README.md lib package.json`. There is no `native.js`.
4. Start a Gateway from that install with a fresh state directory and default plugins:
   ```sh
   export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/oc-beta-state.XXXXXX)"
   export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
   "$PREFIX"/node_modules/.bin/openclaw config set gateway.mode local
   "$PREFIX"/node_modules/.bin/openclaw gateway --port 18852 --bind loopback --auth none
   ```
   The error appears during plugin startup, before any client connects.

### Expected behavior
The Bonjour advertiser starts. On 2026.11.3 the same chunk (`dist/advertiser-C86ADcfa.mjs`) imports `import("@homebridge/ciao")`, which resolves.

### Actual behavior
Logged at WARN on startup (beta.2):
```
[discovery] gateway discovery service failed (bonjour, plugin=bonjour): Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '<prefix>/node_modules/@homebridge/ciao/native.js' imported from <prefix>/node_modules/openclaw/dist/advertiser-DnCAXz4O.mjs
[gateway] http server listening (15 plugins: anthropic, bonjour, browser, ...)
```
The Gateway reaches `ready` despite the advertiser failure.

### OpenClaw version
2026.11.5-beta.2 (c0f42f6), also 2026.11.5-beta.1 (bc061f9). The same import remains on `main` (2035b0730f8). Earlier root-import versions: 2026.11.2 and 2026.11.3.

### Operating system
macOS 26.3.1 (arm64), Node 26.13.1

### Install method
`npm install --prefix <dir> openclaw@2026.11.5-beta.2`

### Model
N/A (not model-related)

### Provider / routing chain
N/A

### Impact and severity
Affected: npm installs of 2026.11.5-beta.1 and beta.2 with the default Bonjour plugin. Severity: the Gateway is not advertised over Bonjour; it still reaches ready. Frequency: reproduced on the beta.2 install above; the imported file is absent from the registry package. The same import remains on main.

### Additional information
#182826 (merged 2026-10-24, e77992dd) switched the advertiser to `@homebridge/ciao/native.js` (`extensions/bonjour/src/advertiser.ts:4` and `:186` on `main`). That entry only exists through `patches/@homebridge__ciao@1.3.12.patch`, which pnpm applies in the workspace. npm consumers get plain `@homebridge/ciao@1.3.12` from the registry:

- The `1.3.12` and `1.4.0` (current `latest`) tarballs both contain only `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `lib/` and `package.json`, with no `native.js` and no `exports` map.
- The root `openclaw` package declares `@homebridge/ciao` as a direct dependency, but its `bundleDependencies` do not include it, so npm installs the registry copy. `extensions/bonjour/package.json` does list ciao under `bundleDependencies`, but that only applies when the plugin is packed on its own; in the core package Bonjour ships under `dist/extensions/bonjour/`, which has no `node_modules`. In the published beta, `node_modules/openclaw/node_modules` holds only `chrome-devtools-mcp` and `playwright-core` (plus `.bin`).
- The published postinstall script does not install or patch ciao.

The published package needs to ship the patched ciao runtime that this import requires.

Searched openclaw/openclaw issues and PRs for "ciao native.js", "@homebridge/ciao", "bonjour ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND", "gateway discovery service failed", "native.js" and "bonjour"; found no report of this missing patched entry point. Related: #182826 (the change above) and #106699 (closed issue, "Bonjour: use the published ciao runtime contract").

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Optional post-turn memory maintenance can inherit the completed foreground turn's aborted asynchronous work scope and stop before finishing memory saving or compaction.

### Steps to reproduce

Synthetic regression against main `433a0c35850349620fbcb23cf6792f2e7d882fde`:

1. Use the existing `src/agents/session-maintenance/run.test.ts` fixture, which creates isolated session state and uses the real maintenance scheduler and admission path.
2. Call `scheduleSessionMaintenance` inside an `AsyncWorkScope`, holding its `afterOwnerSettles` promise.
3. Drain that foreground scope, then resolve the promise with `true` to represent a successfully completed foreground turn.
4. At the inert memory-effect boundary, call `getAsyncWorkSignal()?.throwIfAborted()`, as runtime readers and model preparation do when observing ambient cancellation.
5. Wait for maintenance settlement and check that both memory flush and subsequent compaction ran.

### Expected behavior

Post-turn upkeep has an independent lifetime after successful foreground completion. It must still honor its own deadline, foreground preemption, lifecycle and Gateway cancellation, and write admission.

### Actual behavior

The new regression fails on the original source: flush is entered once, but its inherited signal is aborted and compaction is not reached (`[1, 0]` rather than `[1, 1]`). The five existing tests in the file pass. No model or external service is called by this reproduction.

### OpenClaw version

Source main `433a0c35850349620fbcb23cf6792f2e7d882fde`.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2, arm64; Node 26.12.1 orchestration with the repository's pinned test runtime.

### Install method

Isolated upstream source checkout, pinned pnpm 12.15.0, frozen dependency install.

### Model

None. The regression uses inert model effects; it tests scheduler/admission lifecycle behavior.

### Provider / routing chain

None. No provider request is made.

### Evidence

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-maintenance/run.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

Before the fix: 5 passed, 1 failed. The new test's assertion is the intended failure, not a setup or dependency failure.

### Impact and severity

Optional memory processing can fail after an otherwise successful reply. The synthetic closed-foreground case is reproducible; prevalence across deployed configurations is not established by this test. This report does not claim loss of existing memories.

### Additional information

`runWithSessionControllerCleanup` exits session-controller custody, but preserves the separate asynchronous work context. `runWithGatewayIndependentRootWorkAdmission` creates a new Gateway root without detaching that context. The existing `runWithGatewayDetachedWorkAdmission` provides the required owned asynchronous lifetime without copying foreground tool grants or changing the maintenance owner's cancellation checks. This is separate from the caller-authority repair in #159353.

issues.body:
## Bug: backup SQLite header probe fails on large state trees due to fixed 64 MiB child-process buffer

### Summary

In OpenClaw 2026.11.1, `backup create --verify` can fail before archive creation when the state tree is large:

> Could not determine whether backup files are SQLite databases. Check that the backup worker can run and the source files are readable, then retry the backup.

The standalone SQLite header worker runs successfully. The failure occurs in the parent-side probe wrapper.

### Reproduction

On a Linux host running the installed 2026.11.1 bundle:

```text
openclaw backup create --output <staging-directory> --verify --no-include-workspace --json
```

Observed state-tree scale in the affected installation:

- 514,271 files/symlinks
- 56,892 directories
- approximately 98.5 MB of path data sent to the probe

The exact count will vary by installation.

### Expected behaviour

Backup creation should either classify retained candidates successfully regardless of state-tree size, or fail with a specific bounded-resource diagnostic that identifies the probe limit and remediation.

### Actual behaviour

The parent invokes the installed `sqlite-header-probe.worker.js` successfully for small inputs and for an 83-file SQLite candidate set. During the full backup, the child exits non-zero and the parent emits the generic worker/source-readability error.

The bundled `backup-sqlite-snapshot` implementation currently calls `probeSqliteDatabaseHeaders` with the full retained candidate/visited-path set and uses `spawnSync` with `maxBuffer: 67108864` (64 MiB). The affected probe input/path material is approximately 98.5 MB.

A process trace confirms that the header-probe child launches, the standalone worker succeeds independently, the full backup's probe child exits status 1, and no source permission failure is involved.

### Suggested fix

Preferred:

- avoid probing directories and non-candidate paths;
- chunk probe requests below the bounded worker limit, or stream requests/results;
- retain a clear error if a single request cannot be bounded.

Short-term mitigation:

- increase the buffer above the maximum expected path payload, although a fixed larger buffer remains fragile for larger installations.

Please also add a regression test with a synthetic state tree whose probe payload exceeds 64 MiB.

## Summary
A shared tab can disappear from `browser tabs` while the extension relay remains connected and the user still shares that tab. Attempting to use it then looks like a missing/disconnected tab instead of a Chrome debugger restriction.

## Reproduction
1. Share an ordinary web page through the browser extension.
2. Open a form whose focused field causes another extension to embed a protected `chrome-extension://` frame (observed with 1Password).
3. Chromium detaches/refuses the debugger with `Cannot access a chrome-extension:// URL of different extension`.
4. List tabs: the affected tab is omitted, despite remaining open and shared.
5. Dismiss/prevent the interfering menu: the same tab becomes controllable again.

The restriction is expected; the missing-tab diagnosis is not. No access to the protected frame's contents is requested.

## Expected behavior
Keep the shared tab in the user-facing inventory with a known attachment-blocked reason. Do not advertise it as an attached CDP page. Reject control with that reason and an actionable recovery instruction. After the restriction clears, acquire a fresh attachment/snapshot; never automatically replay an interrupted click or submission.

## Evidence and scope
- Observed in an existing Chrome 156 shared-browser session; the relay remained connected.
- Reproduced with Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, the real unpacked extension, a disposable profile and a synthetic foreign-extension iframe. No private website/account is required.
- Current main `565b3f99c21b` deliberately excludes exact Chrome refusals in `enumerateTargetInfos`. The public tab-list path projects only Playwright pages, losing the reason retained by neither output.
- #191578 fixes an additional refusal that previously broke the entire inventory. This request preserves its CDP exclusion behavior while making the user-facing inventory truthful. #193589 concerns discovery wait/ownership; #186674 concerns uninitialized pages. Those are separate from exposing a known blocked tab.
- Prevention via documented 1Password ignore attributes is a separate compatibility follow-up, not a proposal to disable extensions or relax Chromium protections.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On 2026.10.9, `openclaw message send` keeps running for about 10 s after the message has been delivered: stderr shows two CLI cleanup steps each timing out at 5000 ms (`agent-databases`, then `plugin-registration-resources`). Two real sends took 24.6 s and 22.8 s end to end; both were delivered and returned a message id.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run OpenClaw 2026.10.9 with the gateway as a service on the same Mac, so the gateway holds the agent stores open (eight agent stores here; six had `clean_close = 0`).
2. Run `openclaw message send` to an iMessage recipient (a plugin channel with direct delivery, so the CLI process loads the plugin and sends).
3. The message is delivered and a message id is returned. The process then keeps running, and stderr shows the two `CLI cleanup timed out: … after 5000ms` lines below.

### Expected behavior

The command returns shortly after the delivery result. On the same machine, commands that do not send return quickly: `--version` 0.1 s, `gateway call health` 0.6 s, `channels status` 1.0 s, `sessions list` 1.2 s, `status` 4.0 s.

### Actual behavior

- Two `openclaw message send` calls took **24.6 s** and **22.8 s** end to end. Exit status was fine both times.
- After delivery, stderr showed, in this order:
  - `CLI cleanup timed out: agent-databases after 5000ms`
  - `CLI cleanup timed out: plugin-registration-resources after 5000ms`
  - a `CLI cleanup deferred: shared-state …` line
- Before delivery there was also about 1 s per store with `clean_close = 0` (one logged `slow OpenClaw agent database open … 1069 ms`). That part is not the subject of this report.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.9 (8b18b55)

### Operating system

macOS 27 (Mac mini)

### Install method

npm global

### Model

N/A — no model call on this path

### Provider / routing chain

N/A — `openclaw message send` → iMessage channel plugin (direct delivery); gateway running as a service alongside

### Logs

```
CLI cleanup timed out: agent-databases after 5000ms
CLI cleanup timed out: plugin-registration-resources after 5000ms
```

### Impact and severity

Each CLI send takes 22–25 s. A caller with a deadline shorter than that reads a delivered message as a failure (we had three such deadlines written for 2026.9.x and had to raise them). Not urgent for us because of the workaround below; reported for other users of the CLI send path.

### Additional information

**Where the waits are** (paths relative to the npm package root, 2026.10.9):
- `dist/runtime-cleanup-BGkvU5QE.mjs` (region `src/cli/runtime-cleanup.ts`), line 5: `const DISPOSER_TIMEOUT_MS = 5e3;`. `runCliDisposer` (lines 37–51) races each disposer against it and prints the "timed out" line. We found no flag or environment variable that changes it.
- Wait 1: the `"agent-databases"` finalizer in `closeCliResources` (same file, lines 98–105), which awaits `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesAsync()`. Called from `dist/cli/run-main.js` line 1049.
- Wait 2: `runCliDisposer("plugin-registration-resources", …)` in `dist/cli/run-main.js` line 635 (region `src/cli/run-main.ts`), which awaits `resources.release()`.

**A reading of the shipped code (static; not confirmed by instrumenting).** The second wait looks like a consequence of the first rather than separate work:
- `closeCliResources` runs each finalizer through `pluginResources.runCleanup`, i.e. `work.track(…)` on the invocation's `AsyncWorkScope` (`dist/runtime-cleanup-scope-D7xyQUiE.mjs`, line 16).
- When `agent-databases` passes 5 s the CLI moves on, but that close is still pending in the same scope.
- `release()` then calls `work.runWhenIdle(…)` (same file, lines 53–57), which waits for every pending item in that scope, including the overdue `agent-databases` close. So it cannot finish before that close does, and it reports its own 5 s timeout.
- The later `shared-state` step already avoids this: it uses `runCliDisposerAfterPending`, whose comment says it should not make "the command wait again".

We did not find out what `closeOpenClawAgentDatabasesAsync()` was still waiting on for more than 10 s after a single send, and we did not account for the rest of the 22–25 s.

**Questions**
1. Is it expected that the agent-database close takes longer than 5 s after one `message send` while a gateway holds the same stores open? What is it waiting for?
2. Is the second 5 s wait (`plugin-registration-resources`) intended when the only thing it waits on is the already-reported `agent-databases` close? Could it defer the way `shared-state` does?
3. `docs/plugins/architecture.md` and `docs/cli/message.md` describe the five-second budget. Could it be made configurable, or shortened for one-shot commands whose result is already printed?

**Workaround.** Calling the gateway's `send` RPC (`openclaw gateway call send --params <json> --json`) delivers through the already-running gateway: **1.45 s** end to end for the same message on the same machine.

Possibly related: #186631, #191043.

issues.body:
## Problem
A page can be shared and controllable until focusing a field causes 1Password to inject a protected extension-origin frame. Chromium then refuses `chrome.debugger` access. Reporting that state accurately is tracked in #198002; this issue covers preventing that specific interference without reading password-manager content or disabling extensions globally.

## Tested cooperative path
1Password documents `data-1p-ignore` / `data-op-ignore` for individual fields and the document body:
https://www.1password.dev/web/compatible-website-design

Live shared-browser experiments on a disposable Example Domain tab, through OpenClaw's existing relay (not a substitute Playwright connection):

- A synthetic Name input with `autocomplete="name"` and `data-1p-ignore="true"` remained controllable. Snapshot, type, and readback succeeded.
- Removing suppression and refocusing the same field caused `Page closed before browser action completed`; tab inventory then omitted that still-open tab. A pre-armed reload restored the ordinary page.
- Adding the body-level attribute before opening a synthetic modal allowed its newly created/autofocused Name field to work. Open, snapshot, typing/readback, and Cancel succeeded.
- Removing body suppression after opening the modal preserved the open dialog and focused field in a fresh snapshot.
- Temporarily adding field suppression around typing, then restoring the original absent attribute, preserved both the entered text and focus in a fresh snapshot.
- Closing the modal, restoring normal attributes, and reopening without suppression reproduced the failure. Test tabs were closed afterward; no application, login, password field, or stored credential was used.

These are live feasibility results for the installed browser/1Password combination, not a guarantee for every vendor/version. An already-open protected menu cannot be assumed recoverable by a CDP-only hook: attachment may already be gone.

## Proposed scope
A separate, narrowly scoped compatibility change using the documented cooperation hook:

- Suppress the exact noncredential field when it is already known.
- The original modal-autofocus case needs prevention **before** the field exists; field-only wrapping of `type` does not solve that. A bounded page-level scope around the triggering action is the tested alternative, with the temporary effect on password-manager suggestions clearly documented.
- Restore the exact prior attribute state on completion/error without overwriting later page-owned changes. Preserve focus, form contents, and existing site attributes.
- Do not replay an interrupted action, read protected frame contents, remove extension containers, add broad extension permissions, or promise universal extension disabling.
- Keep existing blocked-state handling as the fallback when prevention was too late or interference recurs.

## Maintainer decision requested
Should this live-tested recipe remain an explicit automation workflow using existing evaluation, or become an extension-profile-specific action wrapper? The latter changes interaction policy and needs an agreed scope/lifecycle rather than a silent global default. No new public API or browser permission is proposed by the blocked-tab fix.

## Follow-up acceptance
Real relay proof of activation, same-document restoration (including preexisting values), navigation/error cleanup, repeated modal opening/refocus, and no interference with manual credential flows. Use synthetic forms and count/status-only evidence; do not export password-manager UI or vault data.

issues.body:
## Summary

A trusted tool policy (`api.registerTrustedToolPolicy`) that returns `requireApproval` without its own `pluginId` never reaches an approval surface. The Gateway rejects it with:

```text
signed plugin approval owner is unavailable
```

Ordinary `before_tool_call` hooks do not have this problem: the hook runner stamps the registering plugin's id onto the approval. The trusted-policy runner does not, so the owner is whatever the policy chose to put in the descriptor, or nothing.

This is the trusted-policy form of #137496 (Skill Workshop descriptor with no `pluginId`, closed). It is distinct from #163348, where the descriptor has an owner but a reused signed runtime identity drops it.

## Where (main 7cd1837be625)

- `src/plugins/hooks.ts:995`: the hook path sets `requireApproval: { ...next.requireApproval, pluginId: reg.pluginId }`.
- `src/plugins/trusted-tool-policy.ts:333-334`: the trusted path keeps `decision.requireApproval` as returned, with no `pluginId` from `registration`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval.ts:366-367`: `withGatewayToolApprovalOwner(approval.pluginId, ...)` attaches no owner when `pluginId` is absent.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-approval.ts:108`: a trusted agent-runtime request without `approvalOwnerPluginId` is rejected before any approval is created.

The SDK type makes `requireApproval.pluginId` optional (`hook-before-tool-call-result.ts`), and the trusted-policy docs (`docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md`) do not say a policy must set it. The repo's own fixture in `agent-tools.before-tool-call.trusted-approval.test.ts` sets it by hand.

## Reproduce

1. A plugin registers a trusted tool policy whose `evaluate` returns `{ requireApproval: { title, description } }` for some tool.
2. An agent run in the Gateway calls that tool.
3. `plugin.approval.request` is rejected with `signed plugin approval owner is unavailable`. No approval is shown on any surface, and the tool call is blocked.

Adding `pluginId: "<the policy's own plugin id>"` to the descriptor makes the approval appear.

Observed at v2026.11.2 / v2026.11.3. Those four files are byte-identical to the tags, and a unit run of `runBeforeToolCallHook` showed `approvalOwnerPluginId` undefined at the `plugin.approval.request` call. The same lines read the same way at main 7cd1837be625; that run was not repeated at main.

## Expected

The trusted-policy runner sets the approval owner from the registration, as the hook runner does: `approval = { ...decision.requireApproval, pluginId: registration.pluginId }`. A policy then cannot leave the owner empty, and cannot name another plugin as the owner.

## Possible fix

In `runTrustedToolPolicies`, stamp `registration.pluginId` when the first `requireApproval` is kept, with a test beside the existing trusted-approval tests that omits `pluginId` from the policy decision.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On an ordinary Discord user_request through the Codex app-server harness, OpenClaw concatenates recent-history context and the current request with only a blank line, without closing the history section or labeling where the current request begins.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a Discord guild text channel with the Codex app-server harness and at least one eligible recent-history entry. The historical message may legitimately be unseen discussion; no history-selection defect is required.
2. Send an ordinary current request (`inbound_event_kind: user_request`, not an ambient room event).
3. Inspect the model-facing user-role `response_item` in the native Codex rollout.
4. After the final attributed historical line, observe only two newline characters followed by the current request. There is no `[Current message - respond to this]` marker or closing history delimiter.

The production-function reproduction below feeds a synthetic, already-rendered history block into the exact Codex prepend helper and its real mention-sigil neutralizer. It reproduces that same layout, checks the no-context control, and verifies that historical skill sigils are neutralized while current-input sigils remain unchanged.

### Expected behavior

The current request should be explicitly distinguishable from preceding historical/quoted context, rather than depending only on whitespace and recognition of attributed history-line syntax.

The existing documentation at [docs/concepts/messages.md:92-113](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/docs/concepts/messages.md#L92-L113) states:

> When a channel supplies history, it wraps it with:
> - `[Chat messages since your last reply - for context]`
> - `[Current message - respond to this]`

It also says thread context uses the same current-message marker to keep the request separate, with an explicit exception for ambient room events. The observed Discord request is not that exception. The requested outcome is an unambiguous model-facing boundary on this path; it does not require promoting untrusted history to developer/system authority.

### Actual behavior

A retained native user-role record from November 11, 2026 at 20:35:18 UTC has this shape (IDs, timestamp within the history line, sender, and private bodies replaced; surrounding envelope omitted):

```text
Recent chat history: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#<history-id> <timestamp> <sender>: <historical body>

<current request body>
```

Direct readback confirms the separator is exactly two newline characters and the explicit current-message marker is absent. The current request follows the history; it is not itself a historical entry.

The synthetic production-helper output is:

```text
Recent chat history: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#100 2026-11-11 19:15:41 GMT+0 Alice: Earlier question.

This is the current request.
Its second paragraph stays current.
```

No incorrect model answer is claimed. The demonstrated defect is missing framing in the actual model-facing input, consistent with the user's reported ambiguity when inspecting the rollout.

### OpenClaw version

Production-source reproductions: **2026.11.3**, `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b`, executed November 13, 2026. The retained live incident occurred November 11; its exact installed build was not separately re-attested for this report.

### Operating system

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, Linux x64; Node v26.13.0.

### Install method

Source checkout with a built distribution; Gateway launched with Node against `dist/index.js`. Reproduction below reads the checkout without modifying it.

### Model

No model is invoked by the deterministic reproduction. The historical observation used an OpenAI model through the native Codex app-server harness; the exact model identifier is redacted. The demonstrated failure occurs in host-side processing before inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Historical observation: Discord guild text channel -> OpenClaw Gateway -> bundled Codex app-server harness -> OpenAI. Deterministic reproduction: local production-source functions with synthetic inputs; no provider or network request.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Ordinary admitted Discord guild `user_request`; a positive recent-history window and text-only current input. The reproduction exercises the Codex app-server prepend path, not the generic CLI runner or every channel/provider. No model sampling is needed to observe the formatting.

### Logs

The redacted native-input shape and exact synthetic output above are the relevant evidence. Full private rollouts are not attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

<details>
<summary>Self-contained production-source reproduction (Node 26)</summary>

Save as `reproduce.mjs` outside the checkout, then run `node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw` against the tested commit. No dependencies are installed and no product files are edited.

```js
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { stripTypeScriptTypes } from 'node:module';
const root = process.argv[2] ?? process.cwd();
const state = readFileSync(`${root}/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts`, 'utf8');
const projection = readFileSync(`${root}/extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts`, 'utf8');
const joinStart = state.indexOf('export function prependCurrentInboundContext(');
assert(joinStart >= 0);
const sigilStart = projection.indexOf('export function neutralizeCodexExplicitMentionSigils(');
const sigilEnd = projection.indexOf('\n}\n', sigilStart) + 3;
assert(sigilStart >= 0 && sigilEnd > sigilStart);
const code = stripTypeScriptTypes(projection.slice(sigilStart, sigilEnd) + '\n' + state.slice(joinStart)).replaceAll('export function', 'function');
const prepend = new Function(`${code}\nreturn prependCurrentInboundContext;`)();
const history = 'Recent chat history: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧\n#100 2026-11-11 19:15:41 GMT+0 Alice: Earlier question.';
const prompt = 'This is the current request.\nIts second paragraph stays current.';
const result = prepend(prompt, { text: history });
assert.equal(result, `${history}\n\n${prompt}`);
assert(!result.includes('[Current message - respond to this]'));
assert.equal(prepend(prompt, undefined), prompt);
assert.equal(prepend('run $current-skill', { text: 'Earlier: run $old-skill' }), 'Earlier: run ＄old-skill\n\nrun $current-skill');
console.log(JSON.stringify({scope:'Exact production join and sigil functions; synthetic already-rendered context, not full Gateway/model proof',input:result,currentMessageMarkerPresent:false,noContextUnchanged:true,historicalSigilsNeutralizedCurrentSigilsPreserved:true},null,2));
```
</details>

### Impact and severity

- Affected: directly observed in one Discord guild/Codex session and reproduced at the production joining helper.
- Severity: prompt clarity and auditability defect. No demonstrated security exploit, message loss, or incorrect model action.
- Frequency: present in the inspected historical input and deterministic for the supplied helper input; not a measured all-provider or all-channel rate.
- Consequence: determining where history ends and the current task starts requires inferring formatting conventions. Human inspection exposed the ambiguity; model-quality effects have not been measured.

### Additional information

#### Source explanation

- [src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts:595-631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts#L595-L631) emits a history heading and attributed lines, then joins context blocks. It does not close the history section.
- [src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts:190-207](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts#L190-L207) collapses whitespace in historical bodies. This limits the ambiguity: historical bodies are flattened into attributed single lines. It is not equivalent to an explicit current-request boundary.
- [extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts:120-130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts#L120-L130) joins context and current prompt with `join("\n\n")`. Sigil neutralization affects explicit skill mentions, not section framing.
- [extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-prompt.ts:360-370](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-prompt.ts#L360-L370) consumes this helper for the native prompt; [extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts:355-366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts#L355-L366) also uses it for steering.
- [extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.test.ts:49-66](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.test.ts#L49-L66) explicitly expects the blank-line concatenation. Those tests therefore preserve, rather than detect, the missing section boundary.
- [src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context-marker.ts:1-21](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context-marker.ts#L1-L21) documents `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` as a provenance/stripping marker, with no trust boundary depending on it. It is not a paired history delimiter or a current-message label.

#### Repair acceptance criteria

- For ordinary requests with history, explicitly identify the end of historical context and beginning of the current request. Reuse the existing current-message convention or an equivalent coherent framing mechanism.
- Preserve user-authored content, quoted-history status, sender attribution, mention neutralization, and the no-history case. Do not claim that a textual marker itself grants trust or authentication.
- Cover both native initial input and steering callers, multiline current bodies, quoted text resembling headers, and legitimate unseen history.
- Keep ambient room-event behavior distinct: do not accidentally turn optional-response context into a mandatory request.
- Validate the actual native input, not just isolated history selection. Preserve UI/history stripping compatibility and existing persisted conversation bytes.

#### Prior discussion and evidence limits

Earlier #188928 described decoration/body attribution ambiguity and was closed as a duplicate of #95279. That canonical request was later administratively stale-closed, explicitly without confirmation of a fix. This report supplies a current, narrowly reproducible **Discord/Codex history-to-current-request boundary** and the missing documented marker; it does not propose the broader trusted storage/deduplication metadata design.

The Codex prepend helper is byte-identical in upstream `main` at `6c32a15729f269d6ed44b89713eb6ae004f15ab1`; the relevant history-rendering block also retains this layout. No fresh live-provider A/B, prompt-injection exploit, or model confusion rate was tested. No product/configuration edits were made.

Saving an existing automation with no explicit agent fails even when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is configured.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Configure agents `main` and `worker`, `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`.
2. Open an existing agent-less agent-turn automation in the Control UI.
3. Leave **Agent** empty, change its name, and click **Save changes**.

The save fails with:

> invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner.

Saving should resolve the configured system agent without requiring an explicit Agent selection.

Reproduced on `81720a0ebe47` in a macOS VM with a disabled test automation named “Memory Dreaming Promotion.” On `f1bc59771d0`, the edit persisted after reload. A separate real-provider VM check saved and ran an agent-less job against Ollama and confirmed execution under the configured system agent, `worker`.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

When the Gateway accepts connections but does not answer, Ctrl-C during the status scan's Gateway probe does not stop `openclaw status` or `openclaw status --json`. The launcher force-kills the command about 2 seconds later (exit 137). With `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1` the command keeps the probe connection open, opens two more Gateway connections, and exits only about 55 seconds after Ctrl-C.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build `main` (`fc6c25e9156`) from source.
2. Use an isolated state dir and config with `gateway.mode` = `local`, `gateway.port` = a free port, and token auth.
3. Listen on that port with a TCP listener that accepts connections and never answers (stands in for an unresponsive Gateway).
4. Run `openclaw status --json` in a terminal and press Ctrl-C about 5 seconds after its first connection to the port. That lands about 2 seconds into the probe connection.
5. Repeat with `openclaw status`, and with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1 openclaw status --json`.

### Expected behavior

Ctrl-C stops the command promptly with the interrupt exit code (130) and closes the probe connection. The command then prints the CLI's stopping error, as it already does when the interrupt is finally honored without the launcher: in `--json` mode the `{"ok": false, "error": {"type": "cli_error", "message": "CLI stopping (SIGINT)"}}` envelope, then `[openclaw] The CLI command failed.` and ``[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.``

### Actual behavior

`status --json` and `status` print `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` (text mode also prints `■  Canceled`). The launcher kills them about 2 s later (exit 137) while the probe connection is still held. With `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`, the command holds the probe connection for another 28 s and opens two more Gateway connections. It prints the stopping error and exits 130 about 55 s after Ctrl-C.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (main `fc6c25e9156`)

### Operating system

Linux (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm build`)

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO (no model is involved; the command only talks to the Gateway)

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw status` CLI -> local Gateway WebSocket (unresponsive listener)

### Additional provider/model setup details

No provider is configured; no model request is made.

### Logs

```text
status --json                          exit 137 (SIGKILL)  2031.3 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held until the kill
status                                 exit 137 (SIGKILL)  2039.9 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held until the kill
status --json, OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1   exit 130           55041.5 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held 28.0 s after Ctrl-C, 2 more Gateway connections after Ctrl-C

# status --json, output after Ctrl-C
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
<killed>

# status, output after Ctrl-C
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
■  Canceled
<killed>

# status --json with OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1, output 55 s after Ctrl-C
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "CLI stopping (SIGINT)"
  }
}
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Terminal output above, from a PTY driver that records the exit code, the time from Ctrl-C to exit and each connection to the listener.

### Impact and severity

Affected: anyone running `openclaw status` while the Gateway is stuck or slow to answer.
Severity: annoying. The command cannot be stopped cleanly: it is force-killed, or keeps connecting for about a minute.
Frequency: every run. Each of the 3 variants above was run once on this `main`, and earlier once each on `main` `808c53a7a76`, with the same exit codes (137, 137, and 130 after 57 s).
Consequence: an interrupted status check holds Gateway connections open until the kill or until the probe budget runs out.

### Additional information

The status scan's Gateway readiness wait and probe (`resolveGatewayProbeSnapshot` in `src/commands/status.scan.shared.ts`) do not take the command's abort signal, so an interrupt waits for the probe's own timeout. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197758 passed that signal for `sessions list`. The other Gateway reads in the status command (the `--json` projection call, the overview's `status` and `channels.status` calls, the local `status` fallback) are changed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197909; this report is about the probe.

issues.body:
### Summary

Serve a static, non-agentic App Home card from the existing Google Chat webhook when an operator enables Google's **Support App Home** option.

### Problem to solve

Google Chat exposes a Home tab for apps that opt into App Home. The OpenClaw Google Chat plugin handles messages and approval-card callbacks, but has no synchronous Home response. Home events reach a message-oriented parser or an empty acknowledgement, so enabling the tab cannot display a useful OpenClaw welcome card.

This is present in v2026.11.3 and in the affected webhook owner on current `main` (rechecked November 12, 2026). A production-route regression reproduces HTTP 400 for native and initial add-on Home fixtures; this is local boundary proof, not a live Google UI observation.

### Proposed solution

Handle Home in the existing `@openclaw/googlechat` authenticated webhook:

- Keep existing native bearer/add-on token verification, body limits, and request limits ahead of the response.
- Recognize native `APP_HOME` and Google's documented initial add-on Home envelope.
- Return a static welcome card pointing the user to the Chat tab.
- Do not start an agent turn, create a session, enqueue a message, return a durable-acceptance marker, or disclose private configuration.
- Add no configuration, core API, SDK surface, forms, or action callbacks. Google's existing **Support App Home** checkbox remains the opt-in.

A [three-file candidate](https://github.com/clawSean/openclaw/tree/contrib/google-chat-app-home) is implemented and tested. This issue asks whether that deliberately narrow slice belongs in the maintained Google Chat plugin before proceeding with a PR.

### Alternatives considered

- Keep App Home disabled and use Chat exclusively: no code is needed, but the optional Home tab remains unsupported.
- Use a separate custom Google endpoint: works as a separate integration, but duplicates deployment/authentication ownership.
- Add configurable dashboards, help links, forms, or model-backed UI: larger product decisions, intentionally outside this first slice.

### Impact

Affected: operators who enable App Home and users opening that app's Home tab. The unsupported Home path is consistently affected; normal Chat/message use does not require it. This is an onboarding/discoverability improvement, not a claim that ordinary messaging is broken. The demand signal is operator setup experience plus Google's documented opt-in surface, not a claim of broad independent demand.

### Evidence/examples

- Current owner: [monitor-webhook.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed/extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-webhook.ts). Latest readback confirms the affected file is unchanged on `main` and v2026.11.3.
- Primary references: [Build a homepage](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/send-app-home-card-message) and [interaction event shapes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/receive-respond-interactions).
- Exact candidate: [`5b39e6b40be1f94c0bbbcbb2d624f1e21a971436`](https://github.com/clawSean/openclaw/commit/5b39e6b40be1f94c0bbbcbb2d624f1e21a971436).
- Native/add-on Home regressions fail on the base and pass after the change. The registered-route fixture exercises body parsing, authenticated target selection, synchronous response, invalid-token rejection, and absence of ingress/agent dispatch; external Google token verification and the ingress sink are mocked.
- All 272 owning-plugin tests pass, with targeted lint, typecheck, formatting, and diff checks. Independent source review found no actionable issues.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself. The small candidate above is already prepared; maintainer direction will determine whether to proceed in the maintained plugin.

### Additional information

Live Google Chat acceptance/rendering and before/after screenshots remain unverified. The Home guide's native-app prose requires a top-level `renderActions` field, while its nearby initial-Home sample returns bare `action`. The candidate follows the explicit native prose and the separate add-on `RenderActions` shape. That documentation inconsistency remains a live-canary question; local tests do not resolve it.

The next integration check needs an explicitly designated test Chat app whose Home endpoint can run the candidate, plus an allowed Workspace test user. It must verify the response shape accepted by Google, inspect the rendered card, and confirm no model/session turn is created. No deployment or authenticated Google account was changed to prepare this proposal.

issues.body:
### Summary

Realtime Talk agent consults (Control UI Talk / GPT-Live native delegation) ignore the per-model `agentRuntime` setting and the model fallback chain. When the agent's primary model is routed through a CLI backend (e.g. `anthropic/*` with `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"`) and there is no direct API credential for that provider, every consult fails immediately with an auth error, and it never falls back.

### Version

OpenClaw 2026.9.7 (c074824), macOS arm64, Node 24.19.0

### Config (relevant parts)

```json5
agents: {
  defaults: {
    models: {
      "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5": { agentRuntime: { id: "claude-cli" } },
      "openai/gpt-5.6-sol": {}
    },
    model: { primary: "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5", fallbacks: ["openai/gpt-5.6-sol"] }
  }
},
talk: { agentId: "main", realtime: { speakerVoice: "sol" } }
```

No `anthropic` auth profile or API key. `openclaw models status` reports `anthropic via claude-cli ... runtime-synthetic`. Normal chat turns in the same session work fine through claude-cli.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure as above (Anthropic only reachable through `claude-cli`, with a working OpenAI fallback).
2. Start Talk from the Control UI in the main session and ask something that triggers a consult.

### Expected

The consult runs through the same harness as a normal turn for that model (claude-cli), or at least uses the configured fallback (`openai/gpt-5.6-sol`).

### Actual

The consult fails in about 46 ms and the turn ends with no reply:

```
lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=46 error="Couldn't sign in to anthropic. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works. Run `openclaw models auth login --provider anthropic` ... (No API key found for provider "anthropic". Auth store: .../agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite ...)"
errorName=FailoverError runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: Couldn't sign in to anthropic ...
```

The message is also misleading. It says a saved login has expired, but the provider is intentionally CLI-only.

### Likely cause

`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` calls `agentRuntime.runEmbeddedAgent(...)` directly with the session's provider/model. It appears to skip both CLI-harness selection (`agentRuntime` per model) and the `runWithModelFallback`-style fallback that normal turns use, so a CLI-routed model goes to the embedded runner and needs a direct API credential. A `FailoverError` is raised but nothing acts on it.

### Workaround

Create a second agent on the same workspace with an API/OAuth-backed model and set `talk.agentId` to it. This only helps Talk sessions that aren't already scoped to an agent, and it splits conversation history. There's no `talk.consultModel`-style option to pick the consult model directly. Adding one would also help here.

Possibly related: #116058 (claude-cli / API path fallback inconsistencies).

issues.body:
### Summary

OpenClaw's default **heartbeat** now runs as a **Proactive check** in Automations. But it doesn't clearly explain how users or their agent should keep the heartbeat's list of things to check up to date.

For example: I ask my agent to keep an eye on something, then later say it's finished or no longer needed. Should the agent update the heartbeat checklist itself, or do I need to edit it manually? What happens if that conversation takes place while the check is paused?

### Affected docs path(s) or URL(s)

- [Heartbeat setup and checklist](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat)
- [Job scratch](https://docs.openclaw.ai/automation/cron-jobs/payloads#job-scratch-and-quiet-results) — the stored notes/checklist attached to an automation.
- The default `AGENTS.md` instructions given to the agent.

### Steps to reproduce / verify

1. Read the instructions for a newly set-up Gateway's default heartbeat (the Proactive check automation).
2. Look for how to give it an ongoing responsibility, change that responsibility, or tell it to stop checking something.
3. Look for whether the user or agent maintains that checklist, including when the job is paused and later resumed.

The docs explain how to edit the checklist, but don't connect those everyday requests to a clear maintenance workflow.

### Expected docs behavior/content

Explain one straightforward workflow to both the user and the agent:

- How an agreed ongoing check gets onto the list.
- Who updates or removes it when the request changes or ends.
- What to review before resuming a paused check.

If the intended behavior is manual editing, say so and show how. If the agent is expected to maintain the list, give it matching instructions. This doesn't require a new scheduler or automatic pause/resume feature.

### Actual docs behavior/content

The agent is told to keep checklists small and is given an editing command, but not when to add, update or remove individual responsibilities.

The heartbeat also uses conversation context, so it can still be useful without a checklist. Pausing and resuming preserves the existing checklist; it does not refresh its contents.

### Impact

Users can't easily tell whether an ongoing request has become part of the heartbeat, whether a finished task has been removed, or whether old instructions will still be there after resuming it.

### Evidence

<details>
<summary>Source references and verification limits</summary>

Inspected on November 12, 2026 at `7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d`:

- [Default job and prompt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d/src/cron/default-proactive-job.ts#L23-L54): creates an enabled check and asks it to review its checklist and conversation context.
- [Default agent instructions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d/docs/reference/templates/AGENTS.md#L115-L131): provides checklist/editing guidance, but not the add/change/remove workflow above.
- [Checklist documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d/docs/gateway/heartbeat.md#L190-L218): explains storage and editing.
- [Pause/resume command](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d/src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-simple.ts#L102-L126) and [existing-job update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7d014324876c9e2287cc10a472e5161cc244bc2d/src/cron/store/job-mutations.ts#L232-L275): change whether the job runs, not its checklist contents.

This is a source-based documentation finding, not an observed missed reminder or a test of how reliably a model maintains the list. No live Gateway or job was changed. Missing checklist notes allow a run; explicitly empty notes can skip it. That behavior is already documented and is not the defect reported here.

</details>

### Additional information

The heartbeat-to-Automations migration (#179387) is not being challenged. This issue is about keeping the heartbeat checklist current, not bringing back the retired heartbeat executor.

issues.body:
Related: #197394

## Summary

Consider rechecking the captured parent conversation’s lifecycle before an already-admitted automation performs an owner-only effect, including when the parent has no workspace binding.

This behavior already exists on main. #197394 lengthens the admission-to-execution interval through slot waiting; it does not introduce the behavior. This is a low-impact hardening follow-up, not a blocker for that PR.

## Evidence

A focused integration test at `1997e68` exercised this sequence:

1. Admit an owner-authorized automation linked to a parent without a workspace binding.
2. Let its condition fire and reach a durable run-slot wait.
3. Replace the parent’s session ID and lifecycle revision.
4. Release capacity and invoke `nodes approve` through embedded tool construction and in-process Gateway dispatch.

Both `node.pair.list` and `node.pair.approve` were dispatched. The assertion expecting no dispatch failed. The final pairing state was not recorded, so persisted approval is not established.

[Main’s prompt executor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/220ca12e0732ab599c5a9b6434ac699f6750728f/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L212) installs the parent-source guard only for workspace-bound children. Main also has asynchronous work between admission and execution without a slot wait; the corresponding main behavior was established by source comparison, not a fresh runtime reproduction.

## Impact and proposed hardening

An automation can retain permission to attempt an owner-only action after its parent is replaced. Requester-authority and pairing-scope checks remain separate; no privilege escalation or unauthenticated access was demonstrated.

Maintainers should decide whether a stale captured parent should prevent owner-only effects for that admitted occurrence. If so, reuse the existing parent-generation guard at the effect boundary and cover both ordinary admission-to-run delays and slot waits.

Preserve intentional behavior for future durable automation occurrences; avoid automatically disabling or deleting jobs merely because their parent was reset.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.11.3, the Claude Code/Codex sidebar intermittently alternates between populated paired-Mac sources and warning-only/unavailable sources; a Codex catalog request returned `NODE_INVOKE_FAILED` with `connected: true`, while the next full request succeeded.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on a Mac running both the local Gateway and the macOS companion app with its paired node:

1. Enable Claude Code and Codex session discovery and let the sidebar populate its local and paired-node sources.
2. Leave the sidebar visible through several normal discovery refreshes.
3. Observe the paired-node source groups disappear and reappear, with warning triangles at the Claude Code and Codex headings in the unavailable state. The local groups remain visible. The reporter observed this approximately every 20–30 seconds; both visual states were independently observed during diagnosis.
4. Compare metadata-only `sessions.catalog.list` responses while checking node connectivity. One request using the sidebar-style parameters below returned the Codex host error described under Logs. An immediately subsequent full query succeeded.

```json
{
  "agentId": "<current-agent>",
  "limitPerHost": 40,
  "progressId": "<unique-progress-id>",
  "allowPartialResults": true
}
```

This is intermittent, not a deterministic failure on every request. Later progressive requests also succeeded. The CLI comparison did not retain a WebSocket to observe subsequent progress events, so it does **not** establish that progressive mode causes the failure.

### Expected behavior

The paired-node sources should remain usable across routine discovery refreshes. Healthy pending refreshes should be distinct from actual host failures, as documented by the catalog pending/stale contract. Actual invocation failures should remain visible and be diagnosable without misleading users into assuming that their session discovery is disabled.

### Actual behavior

The sidebar repeatedly changes source availability and shows an amber warning suggesting that session discovery be configured. For Codex, an aggregate response actually contained `NODE_INVOKE_FAILED` for a host still marked `connected: true`; the same catalog was available immediately afterward. A successful standalone query therefore does not establish that the sidebar is stable.

Claude Code showed the same visual alternation, but **no failing Claude backend response was captured**. Its sampled requests succeeded. A common underlying cause for both providers has not been established.

### OpenClaw version

- Gateway/CLI: `2026.11.3 (847611d)`.
- macOS companion app: `2026.11.3`, build `2611000390`.
- Installed Codex plugin: `2026.11.3`.
- Node.js: `v26.12.1`.

No last-known-good version has been established for this installation; this is not a confirmed upgrade regression.

### Operating system

macOS `27.2.1` (`26B131`).

### Install method

npm-global OpenClaw Gateway/CLI, managed Codex plugin, and macOS companion app with its bundled node worker. Gateway and app node run on the same physical Mac.

### Model

Not applicable: session catalog enumeration, with no inference request needed to observe the issue.

### Provider / routing chain

Control UI sidebar in the macOS app → local Gateway → Claude/Codex session-catalog providers → paired macOS app node. Gateway-local catalogs are also present.

### Logs

Normalized metadata observations from the same diagnostic window on November 12, 2026; not verbatim complete payloads:

```text
Codex paired-node catalog, sidebar-style request:
  connected=true; error.code=NODE_INVOKE_FAILED; sessions=0
  request elapsed=0.809s

Immediately subsequent full catalog request:
  Codex paired-node sessions=9; no host error
  request elapsed=0.586s

Three earlier full requests at 21:51:40 / 21:52:00 / 21:52:21 UTC:
  Codex: local=9, paired-node=9, no host errors
  Claude: local=3, paired-node=3, no host errors
  request elapsed=1.140s / 0.570s / 0.770s

Three later requests at 21:56:06–07 UTC (progressive/full/progressive):
  all succeeded; Codex paired-node=9; Claude paired-node=3
```

The failing/immediately-successful pair was recorded in command output and the diagnostic notes, but has no individually retained timestamp or raw payload. The other samples have retained local timestamped metadata summaries.

During node status checks surrounding the investigation, the node remained connected with the same connection-start timestamp. This does not prove uninterrupted connectivity throughout the evening. A configuration reload and node reconnection occurred earlier; no causal link to the later periodic symptom has been established.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The reporter supplied two sidebar screenshots showing the alternating states. The same states were also observed during read-only app inspection. They are described here rather than uploaded because the screenshots contain private session titles.

Additional checks:

- Direct typed Codex and Claude list invocations both succeeded during diagnosis.
- Comparing metadata identifiers showed that local and paired-node routes enumerate the same nine Codex and three Claude sessions on this Mac; these are not newly created conversations. The duplicate-source presentation is background context, not a second issue being requested here.
- The previously repaired Codex CLI launcher still exists and resolves from the node; a missing executable was not reproduced.
- Installed UI code uses progressive catalog requests and a 30-second polling fallback, consistent with the reported cadence but not proof of the underlying exception.
- The installed Codex provider maps an invocation rejection to generic `NODE_INVOKE_FAILED` without exposing the underlying exception detail. The rejection category remains unknown.

No raw logs, transcripts, credentials, session identifiers/titles, private paths, node identifiers, or network endpoints are attached. No plugin/core instrumentation, authentication changes, reinstalls, or restarts were performed as part of this diagnosis.

### Impact and severity

Affected: Claude Code/Codex session discovery in the macOS app sidebar on this installation. Intermittent approximately 20–30-second source flicker and misleading warnings disrupt source selection and make the connection appear unstable. The local sources remain available in the observed states. No session deletion or data loss was observed.

### Additional information

Related reports, not proven to share this cause:

- #172473 (closed as completed): healthy `catalog_pending` was reported as an error. Here a sampled **host** error is `NODE_INVOKE_FAILED`, not merely a pending catalog flag.
- #130113 (administratively closed as not planned): same-machine local/node catalog duplication. That presentation context is present, but does not explain the invocation failure by itself.
- #166652 (open): concurrent node invocations and pairing-state failures. We have not captured those underlying pairing errors or established its concurrency trigger here.

Please triage the intermittent invocation failure and identify a privacy-preserving way to expose its underlying rejection category. The current evidence does not justify attributing it to OAuth, a timeout, a missing CLI, an update, or progressive-mode cancellation.

issues.body:
**Problem**
Talk transcription can come from three places, in this order: a Voice Call streaming provider (`plugins.entries.voice-call.config.streaming`), the `agents.defaults.voiceModel` default, or the media-understanding audio models (`tools.media.models` / `tools.media.audio.preferredModel`). The Gateway picks one in `buildTalkTranscriptionConfig`. `talk.catalog` only returns `ready`, `activeProvider` and the provider list, so a client can't tell which path was picked.

Settings → Talk can only state the precedence in its copy. When a streaming provider is in use, the page can mark the picked `tools.media` model's provider as "Not ready", even though Talk never uses it.

**Proposal**
Add an optional `source` to the `transcription` group of `talk.catalog`: `"streaming" | "voice-model" | "media-understanding"`. The Gateway sets it where it already picks the path. Gateways without this field keep working, and the protocol stays v4.

Clients then:
- name the path in the status line;
- check readiness against `activeProvider` when the path isn't media-understanding;
- say whether the picked model drives Talk dictation or only voice notes.

**Compatibility**
Older Gateways leave the field out. Clients that find it missing keep today's behavior and stated-precedence copy.

**Related:** #197906 (Settings → Talk speech-to-text model picker).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

Since 2026.10.10, delegating work to native Codex helpers fails roughly once for every helper launched.

The parent agent starts helpers and ends its turn (`sessions_yield`). When a helper finishes, OpenClaw opens a separate wake-up turn on the parent's Codex thread. Two things go wrong with that turn:
- it runs on authority borrowed from the turn that already ended;
- the parent's original Codex turn is often still live on the same thread.

The wake-up turn then fails ("agent harness host capability is no longer active"). The helper's result is lost, any active `/goal` is paused, and the user's next messages are rejected ("Codex session became active in another runner", "still has background work after waiting for cleanup").

This is the underlying problem behind a family of errors that have been reported separately. They are all symptoms of one lifecycle bug: OpenClaw ties authority and thread ownership to a single turn, while native Codex helpers and background work routinely outlive that turn.

### Impact and severity

**Severity: blocks the core workflow on every delegated task, and locks the user out of their own assistant.**

Delegating work to parallel helpers is the main reason to give an assistant a substantial job. On 10.10 and later, that is exactly the moment it breaks:

- **Work silently stops.** Helpers finish their work, but the results never reach the assistant. Nothing tells the user that progress has halted; the conversation just goes quiet.
- **Goals are paused out from under the user.** A failed wake-up pauses the active `/goal` with "Paused after an error." On native Codex sessions the operator cannot resume it ("requires the built-in OpenClaw runtime"), so the user has to notice the stall and re-establish the goal by hand.
- **The user is locked out.** Messages sent afterward are rejected with errors telling the user to "stop its running work and retry", meaning stop the very work they asked for. The user gets no reply at all; the rejected messages are simply dropped.
- **It recurs constantly.** In my installation this happened ~100 times a day on a single long-running task. The assistant becomes something to babysit rather than something that gets work done: every few minutes, check whether it is stuck, abort it, resend the message, re-set the goal.
- **The cost is spent and thrown away.** Helpers run to completion and consume usage, and then their results are discarded.

The experience is that the assistant falls over the moment it is asked to do anything ambitious, and that the user has to spend their time diagnosing and recovering it instead of getting the outcome they asked for. It is deeply frustrating, and it undermines trust in delegating anything substantial at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On 2026.10.10 or later (observed through 2026.11.2), use the native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`) for an OpenAI model.
2. In a channel session (Discord in my case), give the agent a long task that it delegates. The agent calls `spawn_agent` for one or more helpers, then `sessions_yield` while they run.
3. Let a helper finish after the parent's turn has ended.
4. Observe the following:
   - the completion "announce" turn fails;
   - any active goal pauses;
   - a user message sent shortly afterward is rejected with no reply.

### Expected behavior

- A helper's completion is delivered to the parent reliably: once the parent's Codex thread is idle, as a turn with its own valid authority.
- If delivery fails, it is retried. It does not lose the result or pause the goal.
- The user's messages are always accepted and answered (queued if necessary). They are never rejected with an instruction to stop running work.

### Actual behavior

A representative sequence from 2026-11-09 (times are America/Los_Angeles; one session; IDs shortened):

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 07:03:59, 07:04:05 | The parent calls `spawn_agent` twice. |
| 07:05:49 | The parent calls `sessions_yield`, ending its turn while both helpers run. |
| ~07:07:09 | A helper finishes. OpenClaw starts `announce:codex-native:<parentThread>:<childThread>:succeeded` on the parent thread. |
| 07:08:18 | `codex app-server notification ignored for inactive turn`, with `matchesActiveThread: true` and `matchesActiveTurn: false`. Codex is still emitting `item/started` and `item/completed` for the parent's original turn, while OpenClaw has already made the announce turn the active turn. Two turns are live on one thread. |
| 07:09:38 | `agent cleanup failed … step=codex-trajectory-flush error=agent harness host capability is no longer active`, then `lane task error … durationMs=148848 error="agent harness host capability is no longer active"`, then `Subagent completion direct announce failed`. The session goal changes to `paused`, with `lastStatusNote: "Paused after an error. Resume to continue. agent harness host capability is no longer active"`. |
| 07:14:09, 07:14:42 | Two user messages are rejected with `CodexAdoptedThreadActiveError: Codex session became active in another runner; wait for it to finish before continuing`. The log records `visible channel turn dispatched with no queued reply payloads … cause=error`, and the user receives nothing. |

Error counts in the gateway log:

| Error | 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-09 (until ~07:30) |
|---|---|---|
| `agent harness host capability is no longer active` | 56 | 131 |
| `Codex did not confirm unloading its previous configuration` | 28 | 76 |
| `still has background work after waiting for cleanup` | 20 | 27 |
| `Codex session became active in another runner` | 0 | 6 |
| `Session … placement authority changed` | 0 | 3 |

### Regression boundary: 2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10

I counted these errors per day in the agent's transcript events, alongside `spawn_agent`/`sessions_spawn` calls. The transcripts capture only a subset of the gateway-log errors, but the pattern is unambiguous:

| Period | Version | Helper launches/day | Errors/day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oct 8–21 | ≤ 10.9 | ~4 | ~0.5 |
| Oct 22–Nov 2 (proactive delegation enabled) | 10.9 | ~63 | ~2 |
| Nov 3–9 | 10.10 → 11.1 → 11.2 | ~97 | ~106 |

- Heavy delegation on 10.9 (~760 helper launches over 12 days) was essentially error-free.
- The first `host capability` / `background work` / `another runner` error in the entire history appears at 2026-11-03 11:16, a few hours after updating to 10.10 that morning. It has continued on every release since.
- Whatever changed between 10.9 and 10.10 in harness authority binding, announce delivery, or Codex thread retention is the most likely origin.

### Code-level observations (2026.11.2 dist)

- `bindHarnessHostSourceAuthority` (`src/agents/harness/host-source-authority.ts`) throws "agent harness host capability is no longer active" in any of these cases:
  - `attempt.admittedRunContext.operationalRunInstance` differs from the instance captured at bind time;
  - the captured admitted-run assertion fails;
  - the gateway is not current.

  The announce turn for a helper launched by an earlier turn appears to carry that earlier turn's delegated authority. It fails as soon as it touches a host capability, which in the trace above was the trajectory flush during cleanup.
- The announce turn is started while the parent's original Codex turn is still producing items on the same thread (see 07:08:18). That makes the follow-on errors expected:
  - "did not confirm unloading previous configuration",
  - "still has background work",
  - "became active in another runner".
- The `codex-trajectory-flush` cleanup failure has the same signature as #171197, which was closed as fixed in October. It is recurring on 2026.11.2.

### Suggested direction

The fix needs to be in the lifecycle model, not in individual guards:

- **The session, not the turn, should own outstanding helper work and background commands.**
- **Completions should be queued per session and delivered once the parent Codex thread is idle.** Simultaneous completions should be coalesced into one wake-up, instead of one competing announce turn per helper.
- **Wake-up turns should be admitted with fresh authority of their own,** rather than inheriting authority from the turn that spawned the helpers.
- **A failed delivery should be retried.** It should never discard the helper's result or pause the user's goal.
- **User messages should always be queued and answered,** never rejected with "stop its running work and retry".

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.2 (b556fdf); `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.2. The regression first appeared on 2026.10.10.

### Operating system

macOS 27.2 (Apple Silicon)

### Install method

npm global (Homebrew Node 26.13.0)

### Model

openai/gpt-6.1-sol

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw → native Codex runtime (`agentRuntime.id = codex`, codex-cli 0.164.0) → OpenAI

### Beta release blocker

No

### Additional information

Related reports that I believe are symptoms of this same underlying issue:
- #194403: helper-completion continuations lose authority and block conversations.
- #196061 and #196062: a silent turn with a retained command is falsely marked failed. That is one entry point into the stuck state, not the root cause.
- #171197: the `codex-trajectory-flush` "host capability is no longer active" failure, closed as fixed but recurring.
- #147759 and #167280: delayed or stalled prompts after native Codex handoff and stop.

Diagnostic signal: when the parent keeps its turn open and collects helper results with `wait_agent` instead of calling `sessions_yield`, the completion arrives inside the live turn and this path is not exercised. That is consistent with the announce/wake-up turn being the failure point.

## Summary

Offer an optional inline command trail in the Control UI for following coding tasks while they run.

## Problem to solve

Users following a coding task need to see commands, their status, and advancing output in conversation order. The grouped presentation emphasizes tool cards and details rather than a compact live trail.

## Proposed solution

Add a browser-local conversation view preference that presents commands, reads, and searches as compact inline rows during a running turn. Show advancing output and expandable details, preserve completed-turn folding, and keep grouped presentation as the default.

Reuse existing invocation state and session-message subscriptions. Output changes should update the relevant row without rebuilding unrelated conversation structure or the composer. Preserve ordering, recovery, output capture limits, authority checks, and shutdown settlement.

## Alternatives considered

The existing grouped view remains available. Expanding individual tool cards provides details but does not offer the same compact live trail. Replacing the agent harness is unnecessary for this presentation preference.

## Impact

Affected: Control UI users who follow command-heavy coding tasks, using either the native OpenClaw or Codex harness. The preference is optional; native mobile and messaging-channel presentation are outside this proposal.

## Evidence/examples

The implementation has been exercised in real OpenClaw deployments with both harnesses. Representative live views:

![Grouped command presentation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b53fb844-f9db-42e0-8550-80516db30d9c)

![Inline command presentation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77ae86f7-8f10-4221-9489-ae83542203db)

## Implementation intent

Yes, implementation and validation are complete locally; a PR follows.
