### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The durable `commitTurn` payload sends a closed turn's messages without their transcript entry ids, so a context engine stores the turn unanchored and cannot tie its rows back to the host transcript.

### Steps to reproduce

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.7 with `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.7, the context-engine slot set to lossless-claw 1.1.1, and an `openai/*` model on the Codex harness.
2. Run any turn, for example in a Slack thread.
3. Look at the `commitTurn` call the engine receives, or at the rows lossless-claw stored for that turn (`messages.transcript_entry_id`).

### Expected behavior

Each message in `commitTurn` carries the id of its transcript entry, so the engine can match stored rows to the host transcript.

- The host has the ids: each event in `transcript_events` has its own id in `transcript_event_identities`.
- lossless-claw reads an entry id only from per-message entry meta ([engine.ts L3727](https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/blob/v1.1.1/src/engine.ts#L3727)). Its forced budget recovery needs an id on every stored row of the current turn, and it can adopt ids later only for rows in its recent fresh-tail window (https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/issues/1228).
- If bare messages are intended, the `commitTurn` contract should say they are unanchored, so engines do not rely on ids there. #128509 is related contract work on the same payload.

### Actual behavior

- `readClosedTranscriptTurnInDatabase` reads the closed turn from `transcript_events` and keeps only `event.message` ([session-accessor.transcript-range.ts L276-L280](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.8/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript-range.ts#L276-L280)). The per-event id is not carried. The durable `commitTurn` payload therefore has bare messages, plus only the admission and terminal anchors ([context-engine-turn-outbox.ts L576-L591](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.8/src/agents/harness/context-engine-turn-outbox.ts#L576-L591)).
- lossless-claw stores those rows with `transcript_entry_id = NULL`. In this install, after the upgrade to 2026.9.7 + lossless-claw 1.1.1, 0 of 869 rows stored before the failure below had an entry id. The 34 rows stored earlier that day, before the upgrade, all had one, and 92-98% had one on each of the previous four days (OpenClaw 2026.7.1-2 with lossless-claw 0.15.3, before the durable `commitTurn` path). Both packages changed together, so these numbers alone do not show which side changed; the code above does.
- A short conversation created later that day ended up with 15 of 23 rows anchored, which fits lossless-claw adopting ids afterwards for its recent rows only.
- Effect: a 170-message Codex turn was stored with 0 of 170 rows anchored. On the next message lossless-claw declined the byte-fuse compaction, and the host dropped that message (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165460).

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (c074824), with `@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.7. Both source files above are unchanged in 2026.9.8 and on main (checked 2026-10-05).

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, Node 26.3.1

### Install method

npm global

### Model

openai/gpt-6-sol on the Codex harness

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw gateway -> Codex harness (`@openclaw/codex` 2026.9.7) -> OpenAI. Context-engine slot: lossless-claw 1.1.1, which receives each turn through the durable `commitTurn` outbox.

### Additional provider/model setup details

lossless-claw 1.1.1 with `freshTailCount` 64. Its `openclaw.compat.tested` lists 2026.9.4 and 2026.9.5, so 9.7 is an untested combination for the plugin.

### Logs

```shell
# lossless-claw rows with a transcript_entry_id, out of rows stored
previous 4 days (2026.7.1-2 + 0.15.3):      92-98% each day
upgrade day, before the upgrade:            34 of 34
after the upgrade, before the failed turn:  0 of 869
the 170-message Codex turn:                 0 of 170
```

### Impact and severity

- Affected: context engines that rely on per-message transcript entry ids from `commitTurn`. Here, lossless-claw on 2026.9.7.
- Severity: medium on its own. Stored rows lose their link to the transcript. Together with forced budget recovery it led to the dropped message in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165460.
- Frequency: every turn delivered through `commitTurn`.
- Consequence: engine features that key on entry ids (here, forced budget recovery) fail for these rows once a turn is longer than the engine's adoption window.

### Additional information

- Ask: carry each message's transcript entry id through `commitTurn` (for example as `{ entryId, message }` pairs), or document that `commitTurn` messages are unanchored.
- Not a clean regression: the earlier setup did not use the durable `commitTurn` path.
- Related: #128509 (`commitTurn` payload contract). On the same path `commitTurn` also arrives without `tokenBudget` or `modelContextWindow`; that is #158606 (fix in #158740), so it is not repeated here.
- Filed together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165460 (host: the dropped turn) and https://github.com/Martian-Engineering/lossless-claw/issues/1228 (lossless-claw: the refusal and the missing log line).

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With GPT-Live over Gateway-controlled WebRTC (`gateway-control-v1`, `brain: "agent-consult"`), about 40% of voice consults fail. The caller hears the filler ("I'll check that request."), then the failure prompt ("That didn't go through. Want me to try again?"). The agent never runs.

```
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=talk durationMs=4421 error="SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>" errorName=SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError taskKind=turn sessionKey=agent:main:<key> runId=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid>
[plugins] OpenAI GPT-Live delegation consult failed: SQLite transcript changed while preparing rewrite for <sessionId>
[gateway] terminal session persistence failed session=agent:main:<key> run=talk-realtime-consult-<uuid> error=Error: Terminal write owner changed before commit
```

A less frequent variant fails about 600 ms in with `Session transcript changed during context read` (`SessionTranscriptReadFenceError`).

This is the same family as #150530, on a path #150536 did not cover:
- #150536 exempted realtime-voice rows in `canRebasePreparedAssistantInTransaction`, for the gateway-relay consult (`talk-realtime-relay-consult`).
- This report is the native GPT-Live delegation: `extensions/openai/realtime-quicksilver-delegation-controller.ts` `runDelegation` → `runAgentConsult`, runId `talk-realtime-consult-*`.
- It still fails on 2026.10.4, and earlier in the run: the failed consult writes no transcript rows at all.

**Timeline of one failure**, from the session transcript. t = consult run start, i.e. error time minus the lane `durationMs`.

| t | seq | row |
|---|---|---|
| +0.00 s | | consult run starts |
| +0.49 s | 238 | `user` row, provenance `realtime_voice`/`talk`: the caller's question |
| +3.49 s | 239 | `assistant` voice row: "I'll check that request." |
| +4.42 s | | run fails with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`; no consult rows were written |
| +8.9 s | 240 | `assistant` voice row: "That didn't go through. Want me to try again?" |

**Timing across all failures**
- Failures land 0.6–5.4 s after the run starts.
- This matches gpt-live-1-codex calling the delegation before input transcription finalizes. #150530 reported the same pattern: the delegating utterance is saved 0.1–0.9 s after the consult starts.
- Retrying the same request works, because by then the utterance is already saved.

Our reading of the code, which may be wrong: the requester-final attachment (`registerRequesterFinalAttachment`) is only registered in `onRunStarted`. A caller final that lands between delegation acceptance and run start goes through the ordinary voice-transcript append, and the starting turn then conflicts with that row.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure `talk.realtime` with provider `openai`, model `gpt-live-1-codex` (ChatGPT OAuth), default transport.
2. Start a client-owned WebRTC session: `talk.client.create({ mode: "realtime", transport: "webrtc", brain: "agent-consult", sessionKey, capabilities: ["gateway-control-v1"] })`, then connect with an audio-only offer.
3. Ask a few questions that need the agent, for example "what's the hostname of the gateway?".
4. Watch the gateway log for `GPT-Live delegation consult failed`.

### Expected behavior

Speech finalized while an accepted consult is starting should not fail the consult. docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md says: "Speech finalized while an accepted consult is starting remains visible in history and does not prevent the agent from adopting that consult's recorded input."

### Actual behavior

- In one evening, 21 of 49 consults failed: 19 with `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError`, 2 with `SessionTranscriptReadFenceError`.
- Every failure happened before the run wrote anything, so no answer was produced.
- Each time, the caller had to say "try again".

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.4 (383c124cc32f). No related fix in release notes up to 2026.11.3 / 2026.11.5-beta.2.

### Operating system

Ubuntu, Linux 7.0 arm64, Node 24.18.0

### Install method

npm global, systemd user service

### Model

Realtime: openai/gpt-live-1-codex. Consult agent: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (embedded runtime).

### Provider / routing chain

Browser WebRTC (audio-only) → OpenAI GPT-Live, with the sideband owned by the Gateway (`gateway-control-v1`) → native delegation → `runAgentConsult` → embedded agent run.

### Logs

See Summary. Each failed consult logs the three lines shown there; the read-fence variant logs `Session transcript changed during context read` instead.

### Impact and severity

- **Who:** GPT-Live voice consults over `gateway-control-v1` on 2026.10.4.
- **Frequency:** intermittent, about 40% of consults.
- **Severity:** blocks voice workflows. The answer is lost, and callers can't tell whether the request ran (it never did).

### Additional information

Local workaround: retry the same delegation in `runDelegation` when the runner throws `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` or `SessionTranscriptReadFenceError`. Retries are limited to:
- failures within 10 s of the attempt start, before any tools can run;
- at most 3 attempts;
- starting only once the transcript has settled, at least 4.5 s after the delegation started.

This hides the symptom; the real fix is presumably to adopt or rebase realtime-voice rows that land while a consult is starting, as #150536 did for the relay path. We'll report back on how the workaround behaves.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On official OpenClaw 2026.10.6, two follow-up turns in an existing Feishu conversation each spent about 600 seconds in Codex `thread-lifecycle` startup, then failed without a new native task or output, while Gateway and plugin health checks passed.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed sequence on one affected installation, not a deterministic minimal reproduction:

1. Use an existing Feishu conversation routed to `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` through the Codex harness.
2. An earlier native task completes.
3. Send a follow-up. This attempt is later aborted by stuck-session recovery.
4. Send further short follow-ups in the same conversation. Two attempts hit the startup timeout below; the latter was only a short clarification question.

The triggering state and recurrence rate on clean sessions are not established.

### Expected behavior

The earlier task in this same conversation reached native `task_complete`. Subsequent messages should reach native execution and receive a reply, or identify a concrete local startup/admission blocker. A failed attempt should not leave ordinary follow-ups repeatedly waiting ten minutes without native progress.

### Actual behavior

Both later attempts failed after approximately 600,003 ms with `CodexAppServerStartupError` at `stage=thread-lifecycle`. The diagnostic snapshot reported no pending app-server request methods. The user received:

> The request took too long. Check the conversation for any completed work before trying again.

The inspected native history contained no new task or output after the earlier completion.

### OpenClaw version

Official 2026.10.6. Gateway runtime: Node.js 26.12.1.

### Operating system

macOS. The exact OS release is not included in this diagnostic record.

### Install method

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Model

`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`

### Provider / routing chain

Feishu -> OpenClaw Gateway -> Codex harness / local app-server -> OpenAI.

### Logs

Sanitized observation timeline for 2026-10-24, all times UTC+8. These are correlated diagnostic facts, not a concatenated raw log:

```text
20:18:59  Earlier native Codex task: task_complete
20:21:21  Follow-up received and dispatched
20:31:20  That attempt aborted by stuck-session recovery
20:41:21  Subsequent turn failed after approximately 600003 ms
20:51:24  Another turn failed after approximately 600003 ms
           (input was only a short clarification question)

Failure facts for the two ten-minute failures:
name: CodexAppServerStartupError
message: codex app-server startup timed out
code: CODEX_APP_SERVER_STARTUP_CANCELLED
stage: thread-lifecycle
timeoutMs: 600000
clientPendingRequestMethods: []
```

The associated 408 classification was synthesized locally; it was not an observed OpenAI HTTP 408 response. The inspected failure evidence did not show HTTP 401/403/429, a network error, or `tool_authority_mismatch`.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Read-only local inspection correlated Gateway diagnostics, conversation failure state, native history and binding-lease state. Gateway/plugin checks passed.

The conversation was marked failed. A binding lease was still visible around 21:00 and was no longer present by 21:02:52, without manual lock removal. Lease disappearance alone does not prove a successful subsequent reply; this report does not claim an ongoing deadlock or verified recovery.

The `thread-lifecycle` stage does not expose the particular internal await in the captured evidence. Queue, lease, recovery and configuration waits have not been distinguished.

### Impact and severity

One observed Feishu conversation was blocked from answering ordinary follow-ups. Two consecutive captured attempts each waited approximately ten minutes and returned an error without new native output. Behavior on other conversations and installations is unknown.

### Additional information

Related but not established as duplicates:
- #167280 describes post-Stop startup waits involving retired shared clients. This incident does not establish that specific wait or retirement cascade.
- #158127 includes Codex initialize/request startup timeouts on older macOS releases; this report narrows the observed stage to `thread-lifecycle` with an empty pending-request snapshot.

A separate Feishu final-delivery `300309` occurred after the earlier task completed and is noted on #152086. The order of events does not establish a causal relationship.

No manual lock deletion, timeout increase, model/auth change, or forced process termination was used to resolve these failures during diagnosis. No deterministic reproduction or validated fix is claimed. Account details, raw session/thread/run IDs, local paths and private conversation content are omitted.

Please advise which supported trace can identify the outstanding `thread-lifecycle` wait and verify that failed startup releases its ownership before a follow-up is admitted.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

After a macOS reboot changed the APFS volume device number, `openclaw update` is blocked with update-recovery-pending ("Package publication journal does not match its installation"). Every recorded identity differs only in device number (16777233 → 16777232); all inode numbers match.

`openclaw update repair` cannot settle the operation and fails with ENOENT because the activation anchor contains only `previous` (no `launchers` directory). The updating docs describe this layout as having no supported procedure yet.

### Steps to reproduce

1. An earlier `openclaw update` left a package publication journal under /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-da6bdffc3d964dca78e7c595 (anchor dated 2 Nov, contains only `previous`).
2. Reboot macOS. The APFS device number changes from 16777233 to 16777232.
3. Run `openclaw update` → fails with update-recovery-pending.
4. Run `openclaw update repair` → fails with ENOENT on <anchor>/launchers.

This was observed on an existing install. I couldn’t reproduce it from a clean setup.

### Expected behavior

`openclaw update repair` settles or retires the stale publication operation (inodes and paths are unchanged; only the device number drifted) so normal updates can proceed.v

### Actual behavior

openclaw update:
  Failed: update-recovery-pending — Package publication journal does not match its installation: parent (recorded 16777233:2431539; current 16777232:2431539; device number changed only); control dir (recorded 16777233:69160529; current 16777232:69160529; device number changed only); journal (recorded 16777233:69160537; current 16777232:69160537; device number changed only). Run openclaw update repair.
  Failing check at dist/package-update-activation-DaPvnr4e.mjs:324:36

openclaw update repair:
  ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-da6bdffc3d964dca78e7c595/launchers'

openclaw doctor also reports:
  Update f759a1b6-2824-42df-b7a2-64d665729842 remains abandoned: the target build was not recorded, so current version equality cannot prove this update completed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3 (847611d)

### Operating system

macOS, Apple Silicon (arm64) Install: npm global under Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw) Node: 26.13.1 (Homebrew) Gateway: LaunchAgent (ai.openclaw.gateway), loopback, healthy

### Install method

nom global

### Model

claude-opus 5.5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw

### Additional provider/model setup details

- Gateway is running and healthy on 2026.11.3; only updates are blocked.
- All recovery artifacts are preserved and untouched: the anchor, the .control journal, and the retained pre-migration snapshot .openclaw.package-backup-51149-1794494426198.databases (1.1 GiB). No identities were rewritten and no checks were bypassed.
- Fresh `openclaw backup create` taken.
- Docs (install/updating, "Recover an unfinished publication after a remount") list an anchor holding only `previous` with ENOENT on <anchor>/launchers as having no supported procedure.
- Related: #186527, #194291, #170203

### Logs

```shell
Anchor listing: only `previous` (drwxr-xr-x, 2 Nov 14:54). No `launchers` or `previous-launchers`.
The original update report was in $TMPDIR and was lost when the reboot cleared it.
```

issues.body:
## Current Status — November 12, 2026

Native [#168996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168996) merged destination-owned cron results. Stable [v2026.11.3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.3) now [contains that exact merge](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/e63e209ef4309c07c486e9e771d3ec9f9dd43a4a...847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f). Its [dispatcher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f/src/cron/isolated-agent/delivery-dispatch.ts) records confirmed destination results without the former implicit-isolated-to-main exclusion. Its result owner retains expected-generation and run-idempotency controls. Source containment is not installed-package or original-consumer qualification.

[#165802](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165802) remains **open and test-only**, now at `ce725d5882a837b18599597b1e0e56a792fbe91b`. The earlier `c1714fef` evidence below belongs to that prior head. Current GitHub metadata shows 53 successful, 74 skipped and one neutral check, no submitted human review, and a clean mergeability result. This metadata read is not a new test execution or maintainer acceptance.

issues.body:
## Problem

In the Control UI Browser panel you can watch and click in the agent's managed browser, but you and the agent act at the same time. If you step in to solve a CAPTCHA, finish a login or fix a form, the agent's next `browser` call can click, type or navigate over you. The only way to make it stop is to stop the whole run. The agent also has no idea that you are using the browser.

Desktops already handle this: while an operator holds control in the Desktop panel, computer input is refused with "Computer input paused while the operator has control" (`hasController` / `onControlChanged` in the desktop session registry, enforced in the worker computer transport). The browser has no equivalent.

## Proposal

Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't use it. Existing agents keep using the browser exactly as today.

- **A note, not a block.** When you click or type in the Browser panel, the agent's browser results over the next minute include a short note that you just used the browser, so it can check the page before acting.
- **Take control.** A button in the Browser panel toolbar. While your Control UI connection holds control of a browser profile, browser actions from anyone else (the agent's `browser` tool, the `openclaw browser` CLI, other Control UI windows) are not run. The agent's browser tool answers that you have taken over the browser. That answer is a normal tool result, not an error, so the agent's turn keeps going. Snapshots and screenshots still work. An action that had already started may finish.
- **It can't stay stuck.** Control ends when you click **Release control**, when the Control UI window closes or loses its connection, and after 5 minutes without input from you. The panel then says control was released.
- **Enforced in the real browser path.** The check sits in the browser plugin's shared route boundary that every caller goes through (agent tool, CLI, `browser.request`), not in extension or status state.

## No new setting

The feature does nothing until someone clicks Take control, and it lets go by itself after 5 minutes idle, so there is no behavior to turn off by default. A config option (for example to hide the button or change the idle time) can be added later if maintainers want it; per AGENTS.md that needs maintainer buy-in, so it is left out.

## Scope

- Browsers on the Gateway host only. Node-routed browsers are not covered (same gap as #166197 for node desktops).
- No new agent tool action to take control back.
- Relation to #143015 (mobile browser handoff): that PR reserves a profile for a handoff link and pauses automation. This is the simpler, same-machine case with the user's own Control UI connection as the controller; the handoff could reuse the same check.

Previous attempt: #44615 was closed because the lock lived in the Chrome extension and status state instead of the real browser command path.

issues.body:
# Windows node approval replay rejects with possible prepared-plan sessionKey inconsistency

Core 2026.8.2 (0965053), official Codex plugin 2026.8.2, Windows Hub 2026.7.1-3, Windows 10. Gateway is loopback-only; Windows command policy is allowlist/on-miss/deny, MXC sandbox enabled, host fallback blocked. The approved working directory has an explicit sandbox read/write grant.

A normal `node_exec` directory check (`cmd.exe /d /c cd`) with `timeoutSeconds=480` reached an authenticated Control UI approval prompt. The retained approval row records allow-once, resolver kind runtime, resolver label openclaw-control-ui, and no consumption. Gateway journal classification then shows `node.invoke` rejected with INVALID_REQUEST and `approval id does not match request`. The tool returns `failureKind=outcome-unknown`, null exit code, and warns against automatic rerun. We stopped; no new execution was attempted.

## Source trace and candidate cause

- Installed Core `prepareNodeSystemRun` in `bash-tools-BGTRNm2l.js` (2153–2181) supplies sessionKey inside nested `node.invoke.params`, without an outer sessionKey in that builder.
- Its `callGatewayTool` turn-source helper in `gateway-BLNBKneg.js` (191–202) does not add an outer sessionKey.
- Core `nodes-EjR1K851.js` (799) reads outer `p.sessionKey` for transport attribution.
- [Hub v2026.7.1-3 validator](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.7.1-3/src/OpenClaw.Shared/ExecApprovals/ExecApprovalV2InputValidator.cs#L98) uses `request.SessionKey`, deliberately not nested caller arguments; [prepare handler](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v2026.7.1-3/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/SystemCapability.cs#L200) returns that field in its plan.
- [Hub PR #1072](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/pull/1072), merged August 8, documents this trusted outer Gateway attribution contract and deliberately ignores nested sessionKey. This supports preserving that check; it is not a new repair for this Core/Hub combination.
- Installed Core `resolveSystemRunApprovalRequestContext` in `system-run-approval-context-B8Lhd3T8.js` (70–88) falls back from null plan sessionKey to request sessionKey. `resolveSystemRunApprovalRuntimeContext` (91–101) instead uses the normalized plan sessionKey directly.
- Exact binding comparison in `system-run-approval-binding-CBdJlfb5.js` (1075–1084) would then reject a session-context string versus null.

This is a source-supported hypothesis, not a captured comparison of the failed request. The durable operator approval row retains lifecycle/presentation but not the full expected binding or prepared plan. The scoped transcript also lacks those fields. The Gateway rejection branch precedes dispatch, but the tool reports the overall outcome as unknown. We have not weakened checks, directly invoked the reserved prepare RPC, or reused approval IDs.

## September 5 stable-source follow-up

Latest stable Core is now 2026.9.1; the affected installed Core remains recorded as 2026.8.2. We have not installed or reproduced the failure on 2026.9.1.

The tagged [2026.9.1 preparation code](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.1/src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.ts) still supplies nested sessionKey and retains the prepared plan while falling back separately to the request session. The [approval contexts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.1/src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts) still use request fallback for approval creation and the normalized plan field directly for replay. The [Gateway tool helper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.9.1/src/agents/tools/gateway.ts) attaches turn-source fields without adding an outer sessionKey in that helper. This focused static inspection does not prove that no other path repairs attribution in 2026.9.1; please clarify whether a supported correction exists elsewhere.

The [Hub 2026.7.1-4 comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/compare/v2026.7.1-3...v2026.7.1-4) was previously inspected without a relevant preparation/validation correction. No speculative update was installed.

## Requested guidance

September 7 follow-up: installed Core 2026.8.2 was rechecked. Focused tagged 2026.9.2 inspection still finds nested prepare sessionKey, outer-only Gateway session forwarding (`src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.invoke.ts:68,564–572`), approval request fallback (`src/infra/system-run-approval-context.ts:186`), plan-only replay (`:207`), and exact session binding comparison (`src/infra/system-run-approval-binding.ts:243`). Replay passes that plan-derived value into the matcher (`src/gateway/node-invoke-system-run-approval.ts:417–464`). Hub 2026.7.1-4 still reads the outer request.SessionKey and returns it in its prepare response. The separate webchat optional turnSourceTo comparison does not eliminate this candidate mismatch. We have not installed or reproduced the failure end to end on 2026.9.2; historical full bindings remain unavailable.

Please confirm whether the trusted outer session attribution should be propagated by Core's normal exec preparation path, and whether an official stable fix exists. If the trace is incomplete, what supported read-only interface can recover the exact expected/actual binding for an already resolved request without exposing environment values or replaying an uncertain command?

Please also clarify whether this known pre-dispatch approval rejection should be classified as a definite non-execution outcome rather than outcome-unknown. We need a safe reconciliation checkpoint before one fresh normal-policy test. Existing sandbox and approval checks must remain enforced.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

after upgrade from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.2, After a few minutes of normal use or idle time, the Control UI page enters a busy loop. The page's own JavaScript repeatedly calls `Element.getAnimations()`, and each call forces a full style recalculation. One renderer core sits at 100% or more, and the UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. Quitting and reopening the app clears it.

It happens in two different engines at the same time, the macOS app's WebKit WebContent process and a Microsoft Edge renderer, so it looks like a problem in the Control UI page code and not in one browser.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (gateway, CLI and macOS app all on the same release)
- macOS 27.0.1, MacBook Pro (Mac14,6, Apple M2 Max, 32 GB)
- Gateway running locally as the app-managed service, Control UI loaded from it
- Also seen in Microsoft Edge 152 against the same gateway
- Custom theme plugin enabled (the same plugin on a second gateway, running on mac mini, same version 2026.11.2, does not show the problem)

## Observed

- The hot process is the WebKit WebContent process hosting the Control UI (about 100% of one core, around 600 MB resident). A Chromium renderer for a tab on the same gateway shows the same pattern.
- The gateway process stays quiet (roughly 10% CPU) while this happens.
- System load stays low (about 18%), but WindowServer rises to roughly 50% CPU while the loop runs.
- A second gateway on the same release, used from the same app, does not show the problem.

## Stack (WebKit `sample`, main thread, 1,423 of 1,423 samples)

```
WebCore::Page::updateRendering()
  WebCore::AnimationTimelinesController::updateAnimationsAndSendEvents()
    JSC microtask checkpoint
      page JavaScript (microtask)
        WebCore::jsElementPrototypeFunction_getAnimations
          WebCore::Element::getAnimations()
            WebCore::Document::updateStyleIfNeeded()
              Style::TreeResolver::resolve()
                Style::TreeResolver::resolveComposedTree()
                  resetStyleForNonRenderedDescendants()
                    Node::isComposedTreeDescendantOf()
```

All time is in style resolution reached from `getAnimations()` inside a microtask during the rendering update. No other thread is busy.

## Suspected code

`dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-shared-Ihze6w_j.js` contains an overlay controller that polls animations on an element and reschedules itself while any are still running:

```js
function oe(){return a.getAnimations().filter(...)}
function ce(){return oe().length>0}
function le(e,t){
  ... requestAnimationFrame(()=>{
    ... Promise.allSettled(oe().map(e=>e.finished)).then(()=>{
      ... if(!i.isOpen(a)&&ce()){le(!1,t);return} ...
```

If an animation on that element never finishes or is replaced on each pass (for example, a looping or infinite animation, or one restarted by the theme), the condition `!isOpen && ce()` stays true. `le` then schedules itself again from a resolved promise on every frame. Each pass calls `getAnimations()`, which forces style recalculation. That matches the stack above. I did not run the page under a debugger, so this is the most likely loop and not a confirmed one.

## Expected

An idle Control UI should use no CPU. A loop that waits on animations should be bounded, or should stop when the element is hidden or the animation is infinite.

## Workaround

Quit and reopen the app.

## Not the cause (checked)

- Reduce Motion is off, so that setting does not explain it.
- The gateway is not busy, and its log shows nothing unusual during the spin.
- Page load alone does not trigger it. A normal load peaks briefly at about 84% CPU and then settles to idle.

### Steps to reproduce

The freeze is intermittent and I do not have a deterministic recipe. It has happened several times, each time in this pattern:

1. Run a local gateway as the app-managed service and open the macOS app with the Control UI connected to it ("Local Gateway").
2. Configure a second, remote gateway in the same app. Switch the app from the remote gateway to the local one.
3. Ask a question in an agent, or leave the app idle for a few minutes.
4. Switch to a different group or conversation, then choose **New session**.
5. The UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. The WebContent process sits at about 100% CPU until the app is quit.

Notes on reliability:

- Two runs that stayed on the local gateway the whole time, including a group switch and **New session**, did not freeze. A two-hour watch with normal use also did not freeze. The failing runs followed a gateway switch or idle time, and the freeze appeared within about a minute of a new WebContent process starting.
- Using the same app on the remote gateway on the same release has not frozen.
- To confirm it, watch the web process while you follow the steps: `ps -axo pid,pcpu,rss,command | grep WebContent | sort -k2 -nr | head`. A process at 100% for more than a few seconds is the loop. Then run `sample <pid> 3` and look for `Element::getAnimations` on the main thread.

### Expected behavior

An idle Control UI should use no CPU. A loop that waits on animations should be bounded, or should stop when the element is hidden or the animation is infinite.

### Actual behavior

he Control UI page enters a busy loop. The page's own JavaScript repeatedly calls `Element.getAnimations()`, and each call forces a full style recalculation. One renderer core sits at 100% or more, and the UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. Quitting and reopening the app clears it.


### OpenClaw version

2026.11.3

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (both Macbook and Mac mini)

### Install method

mac app

### Model

claude-sonnet_5.5, claude-opus_5.5, ChatGPT_6/Sol_5.5

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw (local gateway). openclaw (remote gateway)

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

_No response_

### Additional information

prs.title: fix(logging): keep refused commands and previews from changing state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes state changes caused by diagnostic logging during read-only update previews, rejected CLI commands, Doctor startup refusal, and a Gateway waiting for ownership.

## User Impact

Previews and refused commands preserve the selected state and do not create a profile merely to print an error. A refused Gateway contender no longer recreates logs while cleanup owns and removes that state. Console output, diagnostic events, error codes, and ordinary runtime file logs remain available. Terminal CLI error summaries are intentionally no longer duplicated into file logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197978 (`77fcbaa7`) correctly moved default logs into the selected state directory, exposing previously incidental file writes before state ownership. Keep that profile isolation and put the exception at the existing read-only diagnostic operations.

One operation-local async context in the logging owner omits only file transport before it prepares a target. Source-only config reads, preview presentation, startup-refusal and ownership-wait diagnostics, and both terminal CLI formatters use it. Command execution, custom error handlers, finalization, and acquired-ownership logging remain outside those scopes. Concurrent unrelated logs still persist. No schema, configuration, cache, retry, or timeout change is included. Production grows by 39 lines to express this shared boundary; tests +45 and docs +6.

## Evidence

On exact canonical main `88fb4154`, the original real CLI update and Doctor cases failed because their unchanged state snapshots acquired a dated log. The original cleanup cases also failed; an independent determining control proved the refused contender's new log caused the correct cleanup guard to refuse. With the repair, the selected update cases pass 12/12, Doctor startup-admission cases 10/10, and all 25 cleanup cases pass. The existing pristine-profile option-validation regression also failed before its terminal-formatter correction and passes afterward. No state assertions were weakened.

The new logging regression exercises real async file output and verifies console/diagnostic visibility plus concurrent unrelated persistence. Logging/browser-like import checks pass 40 cases; normal file transport/reload consumers pass 21 with 2 conditional skips; terminal runtime-helper checks pass 3. Cold TLS-free help and terminal JSON-console formatting pass. The Node browser-like check is not browser proof; the affected actual Playwright/Gateway consumer passes all 4 cases.

The complete 11-file candidate has a clean independent Codex P0–P2 review and completed test-audit/simplification. The original required `pnpm check:changed` run passed every stage except the two Talk exports repaired by #198056 and one redundant test type argument. After removing that argument, targeted lint passed. A normal integration of main `e711369e` includes the named export repairs; canonical production and full-tree export scans now pass with zero entries. All candidate TypeScript bytes are preserved, and the affected logging consumers pass 59 cases with 2 conditional skips against the integrated writer. The separate main documentation paragraph was retained. Two earlier one-second Git discovery timeouts did not recur in the final update proof; their cause remains unqualified. Exact PR CI and final hosted review remain required.

One proportional A/A/B cohort exercised ordinary persisted logging: 20,000 records across 1,000 synthetic sessionKeys, 20 batches and exactly 20,140,000 bytes per arm. A1/A2/fix wall times were 1313/1070/1106 ms; process CPU 1469/1267/1308 ms; main-thread CPU 1055/991/1013 ms; sampled main-isolate allocations 952.55/938.44/941.49 MB (32768-byte sampling, collected objects included). The fix lies within the A/A range; this is not a statistical performance claim. Imports and 1,000 warmup records were excluded. Already-active Git checkouts overlapped parts of the cohort; no tests or builds overlapped, and the cohort was not repeated.

prs.title: feat(agents): browse an agent workspace from the CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the missing CLI read surface for the canonical `agents.workspace.*` Gateway RPCs:

- `openclaw agents workspace list [--path <dir>] [--offset <n>] [--limit <n>] [--agent <id>] [--json]` → `agents.workspace.list`
- `openclaw agents workspace get <path> [--agent <id>] [--json]` → `agents.workspace.get`

Both commands are read-only forwarders. The Gateway handler keeps every decision (path confinement, size caps, encoding classification, error codes); the CLI only resolves the default agent, forwards params, and formats the response.

The RPC pair is not new: it backs the Control UI, the Android **Files** screen and the iOS workspace file screen, and it is documented in `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md:159`. What was missing is the operator surface for shells, scripts and CI — the CLI. `src/cli` and `src/commands` had zero references to `agents.workspace.*` before this patch.

Fixes #198068

## Linked context

- Issue: #198068 — `[Feature]: browse an agent workspace from the CLI (read-only)` (five-section body, acceptance written against `main` at `0633f256350`).
- Complementary, not duplicate: `openclaw agents files list/get` (#197715 / #197814) reads the **fixed bootstrap document set** (`AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `TOOLS.md`, …) and classifies `missing` / `expectedAbsent`. Its `name` parameter is validated against `ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES`, so it cannot address `notes/plan.md` or an exported image. This PR deliberately does not touch or widen that contract.
- Prior decisions that point at this contract: #100705 (mobile read-only workspace browser — shipped against these RPCs), #61368 (workspace file management API for remote/container deployments), #116494 (persisted-memory read side settled on `agents.workspace.list/get`). None of them asked for a CLI, and none of them is a duplicate of this patch.
- Dedup performed before opening: `gh pr list --state open --search "agents workspace"` → only my own unrelated #197814 plus bootstrap fixes; `gh pr list --search "agents.workspace"` → 0; `gh issue list --search "agents.workspace"` → #197715 (mine) and five closed decisions listed above.

## What changed (6 files, +503)

| File | Lines | What and why |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/agents.workspace.ts` | +197 | The two command implementations: numeric option validation, default-agent resolution, RPC forwarding, table/byte-exact/JSON rendering. |
| `src/commands/agents.workspace.test.ts` | +222 | 11 unit tests (default agent, verbatim `--agent`, offset/limit types, pre-RPC rejection, text table, JSON passthrough, exact stdout bytes incl. no-trailing-newline file, base64 passthrough, error path). |
| `src/cli/program/register.agent.ts` | +34 | Registers the `workspace` group under the existing `agents` command and imports the shared `addGatewayClientOptions` helper. |
| `src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` | +19 | One dispatch test that asserts both verbs resolve to the right command module with the right options. |
| `src/cli/command-catalog.ts` | +8 | Exact `["agents","workspace","list"]` / `["agents","workspace","get"]` entries with `loadPlugins: "never"`; `get` additionally sets `ownsProtocolStdout: true` because it writes the payload to stdout itself. |
| `docs/cli/agents.md` | +23 | `### agents workspace` section: options, the 250/500 Gateway limit, the byte-for-byte stdout contract, base64 images, and the nonzero exit for rejected paths. |

Design decisions worth calling out:

1. **`get` writes the payload with `process.stdout.write`, not the runtime writer.** The shared runtime stdout writer appends `\n` when the value does not end with one, which would corrupt `> file` redirection and make the local byte count disagree with the `size` the Gateway reported for the same read. This mirrors the existing precedent in `src/cli/register.cron-scratch.ts:58`.
2. **Missing/unsupported paths are the Gateway's errors, not the CLI's.** The command never pre-validates paths and never rewrites the message; `workspace_path_invalid`, `workspace_file_not_found`, `workspace_file_too_large` and friends surface verbatim, `--json` failures use the shared `formatCliJsonFailure` shape, and the process exits nonzero.
3. **`--agent` is forwarded verbatim**, including a blank value; the configured-agent roster check remains server-side (`resolveConfiguredAgentIdOrRespondError`). When `--agent` is omitted the CLI resolves the operation owner with `resolveAgentOperationAgentId`, the same helper `agents bind` and `agents files` use.
4. **`--offset` is the RPC's numeric offset, not a cursor.** No protocol change, no invented pagination semantics.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: a shell operator on a client machine can now browse and read an agent's workspace through the Gateway (`agents.workspace.list` / `agents.workspace.get`) instead of only through the Control UI or the mobile apps; `agents workspace get <path> > file` reproduces the Gateway-reported bytes exactly, and unsafe paths are rejected by the canonical handler with a nonzero exit.

**Real setup tested**: Windows 11, Node v24.22.1, OpenClaw source at this branch's head run through the repo's own tsx entry point (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`, reported version `2026.11.3`), against an isolated Gateway started from the same tree with `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-ws3 OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18816 … gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18816`. The workspace was seeded on disk with `notes/a.md` (68 bytes), `notes/b.txt` (23 bytes, no trailing newline) and `notes/pixel.png` (67 bytes, 1x1 PNG). No developer state (`~/.openclaw`) was touched, and no Gateway RPC was mocked.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**: five `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace …` processes against the isolated Gateway; exact argv below.

```bash
cd D:/IdeaWork/openclaw-worktrees/auto-feature
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-ws3
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18816
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18816

# each command below ran in its own process, stdout/stderr redirected to files
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace list --timeout 60000
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace list --path notes --json --timeout 60000
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace get notes/b.txt --timeout 120000 > ws-out-b.txt
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace get notes/pixel.png --json --timeout 120000
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents workspace get ../etc/passwd --timeout 60000
```

**After-fix evidence**: captured stdout, stderr and exit codes for the listing, the nested JSON listing, the byte-exact read, the base64 image read, the rejected traversal and the Gateway's operator connection line.

```text
# 1) directory listing at the workspace root  -> exit 0
$ openclaw agents workspace list
Agent workspace · main
path: / · 1 entries · offset 0
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+--------+--------------------------+
| Name                                                                 | Kind      |   Size | Updated                  |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+--------+--------------------------+
| notes                                                                | directory |        | 2026-11-13T03:30:01.665Z |
+----------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------+--------+--------------------------+

# 2) nested listing as JSON  -> exit 0
$ openclaw agents workspace list --path notes --json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "path": "notes",
  "parentPath": "",
  "entries": [
    { "path": "notes/a.md",      "name": "a.md",      "kind": "file", "size": 68, "updatedAtMs": 1794540601633 },
    { "path": "notes/b.txt",     "name": "b.txt",     "kind": "file", "size": 23, "updatedAtMs": 1794540601656 },
    { "path": "notes/pixel.png", "name": "pixel.png", "kind": "file", "size": 67, "updatedAtMs": 1794540601666 }
  ],
  "totalEntries": 3,
  "offset": 0
}

# 3) byte-exact file read  -> exit 0, stdout 23 bytes, stderr metadata
$ openclaw agents workspace get notes/b.txt > ws-out-b.txt
$ sha256sum ws-out-b.txt ; sha256sum <seeded notes/b.txt>
81b5ce080e6edb0f4f2b5ba0c78b59da021f82bda3efb8edd30b2b3609778b61  ws-out-b.txt
81b5ce080e6edb0f4f2b5ba0c78b59da021f82bda3efb8edd30b2b3609778b61  notes/b.txt   (23 bytes, no trailing newline)
$ cat ws-out-b.txt.err
Agent workspace file notes/b.txt, 23 bytes, text/plain, encoding=utf8

# 4) image payload as JSON  -> exit 0, base64 + mime type, no decoding by the CLI
$ openclaw agents workspace get notes/pixel.png --json
{
  "agentId": "main",
  "file": {
    "path": "notes/pixel.png",
    "name": "pixel.png",
    "size": 67,
    "updatedAtMs": 1794540601666,
    "mimeType": "image/png",
    "encoding": "base64",
    "content": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8AAAwAB/AL+2wAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
  }
}

# 5) traversal is rejected by the Gateway handler, not the CLI  -> exit 1, zero stdout bytes
$ openclaw agents workspace get ../etc/passwd
Agent workspace file failed: path escapes the agent workspace
$ echo "exit=$?"                                  # 1
$ wc -c < ws-out-escape.txt                       # 0  (nothing reached stdout)

# 6) server-side proof of the round trip (isolated Gateway log)
[ws] client connected conn=01a5e3ef-7886-4f23-ba3a-e2126b58297c client=cli name=cli mode=cli role=operator auth=device-token version=2026.11.3 platform=windows
```

**Observed result after the fix**: all read paths exit 0 and return the Gateway's real data (listing sizes 68/23/67 match the files on disk; the `get` payload is byte-identical to the seeded file with SHA-256 `81b5ce08…978b61`), while the traversal attempt exits 1 with the handler's path-escape rejection (`path escapes the agent workspace`, the `workspace_path_invalid` branch) and produces no stdout bytes.

**What was not tested**: (1) no `--json` failure-shape assertion against a live Gateway (covered only by unit tests and the shared `formatCliJsonFailure` path); (2) the `workspace_file_too_large` / `workspace_file_unsupported` error codes were not reproduced live (they need a >5 MiB image or a non-UTF-8 file seeded on the host; the handler owns those branches and this PR does not modify them); (3) no packaged-`dist` run — the evidence above is from the repo's tsx source entry point, not `pnpm build` output; (4) `--agent ghost` (a roster rejection) was exercised only in unit tests, not as a live CLI invocation; the live invalid-pagination runs in **Revision 2** cover the local-argument path, not the roster path.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: this Gateway build does not emit `⇄ res ✓/✗ <method>` lines for successful agent workspace reads, so the server side is evidenced by the `[ws] client connected … role=operator` line plus data that only the handler can produce (nested listing with on-disk sizes, byte-identical payload). The traversing request is rejected by the Gateway (not by the CLI), which is why no bytes reach stdout. The isolated Gateway took 389 s to bind and post-ready maintenance ran before the reads, so the first CLI process needed ~150 s to transform modules; that is local tooling latency, not command behavior.

## Before / after

Before (on `main` at `0633f256350` — the `agents` group registers `list`, `bindings`, `bind`, `unbind`, `add`, `team`, `set-identity`, `delete`, and nothing else; `git grep "agents.workspace" -- src/cli src/commands` returns zero hits):

```text
```text
$ openclaw agents workspace list
OpenClaw agents has no command "workspace".
Try: openclaw agents --help
Docs: https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli
$ echo "exit=$?"        # 1

# literal RPC token in the CLI layers on main
$ git grep -c "agents\.workspace\.list" HEAD -- src/cli src/commands
0
```
```

After (this branch, same isolated Gateway, same workspace):

```text
$ openclaw agents workspace list
Agent workspace · main
path: / · 1 entries · offset 0
… table …   # exit 0
```

## Tests and validation

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents.workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ |commands| lists a workspace directory and renders files next to directories
 ✓ |commands| forwards offset and limit as numbers, not strings
 ✓ |commands| rejects a non-numeric limit before calling the Gateway
 ✓ |commands| resolves the configured default agent when --agent is omitted
 ✓ |commands| forwards an explicit agent id verbatim, including a blank one
 ✓ |commands| emits the untouched list result as JSON
 ✓ |commands| writes the exact file bytes to stdout and metadata to stderr
 ✓ |commands| keeps a file without a trailing newline at exactly its own bytes
 ✓ |commands| writes base64 payloads unchanged and reports the encoding
 ✓ |commands| emits the untouched get result as JSON
 ✓ |commands| reports a Gateway path rejection and exits nonzero
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
 ✓ |cli| src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts > agent command registration > dispatches agents workspace list and get
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
   (shard wall time 530.34s)

$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json \
    src/commands/agents.workspace.ts src/commands/agents.workspace.test.ts \
    src/cli/program/register.agent.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts src/cli/command-catalog.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <the 5 ts files + docs/cli/agents.md>
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts
Test lines OK. Net test lines: +241; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.
```

Notes:

- No `config/test-lines-allocations/*` file is needed: the change adds 241 net test lines, under the current 400-line allowance.
- New-file assertion discipline: `src/commands/agents.workspace.ts` and its test contain zero `as` assertions. The only casts in the patch are none; option bags are constructed with explicit conditional spreads so `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` / `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` stay clean.
- The register test initially failed with `ReferenceError: addGatewayClientOptions is not defined` because the first revision of the branch used the helper without importing it; the import was added and the suite re-run (result above). This is the exact class of failure the local run catches before CI.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` touches only the six files above: no `pnpm-lock.yaml`, no `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` — additive only: two new read-only verbs under `agents`; no existing command, flag, output or error message changes.)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No` — no config keys, no schema/migration, no new state files; the commands read the same Gateway connection options as other `agents` subcommands.)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No` — the commands are `operator.read` forwarders over the existing WebSocket client. They do not read the filesystem themselves, do not bypass the handler's realpath confinement, symlink/hardlink rejection, 5 MiB image cap or UTF-8 classification, and they add no new network destination. `--token`/`--password` handling is the shared `addGatewayClientOptions` path.)

What is the highest-risk area? The **stdout byte contract** of `agents workspace get`: if any layer appended a newline (or decoded base64), `> file` redirection would silently corrupt saved files and disagree with the Gateway's `size`. The second risk is registering the verbs with the wrong command-catalog policy, which would either load plugins for a command that does not need them or let a plugin claim stdout.

How is that risk mitigated? `get` uses `process.stdout.write` and the implementation carries a comment explaining why the runtime writer is unsuitable; two unit tests assert the exact bytes for a file without a trailing newline and for an empty-body case, and the live proof compares the redirected stdout SHA-256 against the seeded file. The catalog entries are `exact: true` with `loadPlugins: "never"` and `ownsProtocolStdout: true` only on `get`; the register test asserts both verbs resolve to the workspace command module. Rejection behavior is proven live: the handler rejects `../etc/passwd` and the CLI exits 1 with no stdout.

## Revision 2 — the remaining actionable finding is fixed, with a real before/after

ClawSweeper's only actionable finding on revision 1 (`f5d64076b45`) was that local pagination validation bypassed the JSON-aware failure reporter:

> [P2] Preserve JSON failures for invalid pagination options — `src/commands/agents.workspace.ts:131-134`

`agents workspace list --limit 0 --json` and `--offset -1 --json` wrote a human message to stderr and called `runtime.exit(1)` directly, so `--json` produced **no stdout at all** instead of the `{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": ... } }` envelope that every Gateway failure already receives from `reportFailure`. Scripts lost the failure envelope exactly in the mode that exists for scripts.

**Fix (`580e8679255`)**: the pagination `catch` now calls the same `reportFailure(...)` helper as the two Gateway paths, so text and JSON modes share one failure owner, one exit path, and one envelope. The Gateway handlers, the protocol, and both command flags are untouched — this is a CLI-side reporting fix only.

Test follow-ups in the same commit:

- `agents.workspace.test.ts` now asserts **serialized** JSON (`JSON.parse(written())` against a runtime whose `writeJson` really stringifies) instead of spying on a mocked `writeJson`, so the assertions read the payload a script would see.
- The previous "default agent" case that only asserted a mocked resolver call is removed; agent selection is covered by the resolver's own tests and by the real CLI runs below.
- New coverage: invalid pagination in `--json` mode (envelope on stdout, exit 1, no RPC dispatched) and a Gateway path rejection in `--json` mode (envelope on stdout, exit 1).

### Before / after — same machine, same isolated state dir, same source-entry CLI

"Before" is this branch's previous head (`f5d64076b45`, the reviewed patchset); "after" is `580e8679255`. Both runs used `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-ws3` and the source runtime (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts`, **not** packaged dist), so the two runs differ only in the patch.

```text
# BEFORE  (head f5d64076b45)
$ openclaw agents workspace list --limit 0 --json
EXIT: 1
STDOUT: 0 bytes            <-- the defect: JSON mode loses the failure envelope
STDERR: Agent workspace list failed: --limit must be an integer >= 1

# AFTER   (head 580e8679255)
$ openclaw agents workspace list --limit 0 --json
EXIT: 1
STDOUT (58 bytes):
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "--limit must be an integer >= 1"
  }
}
STDERR: (empty)

# AFTER, text mode: human line on stderr, stdout stays empty
$ openclaw agents workspace list --offset -1
EXIT: 1
STDOUT: 0 bytes
STDERR: Agent workspace list failed: --offset must be an integer >= 0
```

The exit code, the message text, and the "no RPC is dispatched for an invalid flag" property are unchanged; only the machine-readable channel now matches the rest of the CLI.

### Validation for this revision

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents.workspace.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → **12 passed / 1 file / exit 0** (18.5s shard).
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/commands/agents.workspace.ts src/commands/agents.workspace.test.ts` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on both files → **pass**.
- `ocr review` (AI review over the working-tree diff) → **0 findings**.
- Diff for this revision: 2 files, +53/−22 (no `pnpm-lock.yaml`, no `CHANGELOG.md`, no allocation file — net test lines remain under the 400-line allowance).

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review. The patch is self-contained (read-only forwarders + tests + docs), the local gates (unit tests, oxlint, oxfmt, test-lines ratchet) are green, and the real-behavior proof above covers the happy path, a JSON path, the byte-exact path and a rejection path.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- CI on head `580e8679255` (re-running; the repository queue was ~1200 runs deep at push time). The previous head `f5d64076b45` had one red shard, `checks-node-changed-compact-small-33` -> `src/cli/help-exit.process.test.ts > does not scaffold a selected profile before option validation`. This PR touches neither that test nor the profile/port validation path, and the same shard also fails on #197814, a different branch with a different diff. The `workspace_file_too_large` / `workspace_file_unsupported` branches stay handler-owned and are declared untested rather than claimed. No packaged-`dist` run was made; the evidence is source-via-tsx and is labelled as such.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- ClawSweeper revision 1 (head `f5d64076b45`, overall gold, proof sufficient, 1 actionable finding): [P2] invalid pagination options bypassed the JSON failure reporter. Addressed in `580e8679255` by routing them through the shared `reportFailure` helper plus new JSON-mode coverage; the real before/after terminal output is in **Revision 2** above. ClawSweeper's low-value-test note is addressed too: the JSON assertions now read the serialized payload and the assertion-only default-agent case is gone.

## Update log

- `f5d64076b45` — initial revision: 6 files, +503. Rebased onto `origin/main` at `0633f256350` immediately before opening; the six anchor files (`register.agent.ts`, `register.agent.test.ts`, `docs/cli/agents.md`, `command-catalog.ts`, the handler and the schema) had zero drift from the draft base.

prs.title: fix(update): roll back activated releases that fail Doctor or Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What

Two gaps meant a bad release could stay installed after activation:

1. **Post-activation rollback never had a baseline without the candidate canary.** `captureUpdateActivationSchemas` read the pre-activation state schema versions only when the canary reported `candidateSchemaVersions`. Without that baseline, `rollbackFailedUpdate` returns `rollback-state-unverified` for every post-activation failure and leaves the bad release installed. The baseline is now read for every SQLite-backed update. PostgreSQL keeps the candidate-only read for now; reading a live PostgreSQL baseline before the owning Gateway stops is unproven.
2. **Updates that do not restart a service never booted the activated release.** The new `activated-gateway-startup` step boots it once on real state, with channels, providers, cron and watchers suppressed, and waits for `/readyz` (2 min budget, fails fast if the process exits). If the Gateway cannot become ready, the update fails into the existing post-activation rollback. The step is skipped, with an advisory, when a running Gateway owns the state, when the profile uses a remote Gateway, or when the Gateway serves TLS (the probe is plain HTTP). It is also skipped when the commit did not change or a service restart will verify readiness itself. Setup failures (port bind, lock read) fail the update into rollback instead of escaping it.

This PR does not remove the candidate canary. It makes the post-activation path safe enough that removing the canary can be evaluated in a follow-up.

## Evidence

Isolated git-checkout installs (synthetic state, `umask 077`), seeded bad releases, real `openclaw update --yes --no-restart`. The canary was skipped through a local-only experiment flag that is not part of this PR, so the post-activation path is what decides each outcome.

| Seeded fault | main, canary skipped | this PR, canary skipped |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway crashes at boot | `post-update-failed`; left on bad commit; Gateway dead | `activated-gateway-startup-failed` (12.4 s); rolled back to base; Gateway healthy |
| Doctor config transform writes an invalid value | `rollback-state-unverified`; left on bad commit | rolled back to base ("Previous package and configuration restored"); Gateway healthy |
| State migration adds a column, then throws | `rollback-state-unverified`; left on bad commit; Gateway dead | `doctor-failed`; rolled back to base; Gateway healthy |
| Clean update (no fault) | ok | ok; boot check 4.5 s |

On the exact head `1062ee4` with the candidate canary **on** (normal path): clean update ok (774 s); Gateway crash refused before activation by the canary (`runtime-verification-failed`), checkout stayed on base, Gateway healthy.

In the migration case the migration transaction rolled back, so the schema stayed at v39. The baseline comparison is what lets rollback see that.

## Tests

- `update-activated-gateway-check.test.ts`: ready, failed boot, live owner, and an untouched failed result.
- The execution fixture mocks the new boot check the same way it already mocks the canary, since both cross a process boundary.
- Five `update-cli.preactivation-inspection.test.ts` cases fail on main on this host as well; they are not affected by this change.

## Accepted edge cases

- **PostgreSQL state** keeps the previous canary-dependent baseline.
- **A plugin that fails during load** is non-fatal at Gateway startup, so the boot check accepts it, as the canary does.
- **TLS Gateways** with `--no-restart` are not booted; they are verified on their next restart.
- **A running Gateway** with `--no-restart` keeps serving the previous release until its own restart; the update reports that instead of booting a second Gateway on the same state.

## What Problem This Solves

A linked non-owner Telegram user with staff access can ask the bot to create a one-shot reminder without owner or elevated cron access.

The reminder is authorized only for the current accepted turn and its original delivery route. A managed child inherits that bounded authority. It grants no authority to create other jobs, redirect delivery, or use broader cron operations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Personal reminders need a narrow path that does not widen the caller's general job or cron permissions. Related context: [#187264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187264), [#168389](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168389), and [#141201](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141201). Those broader items are not fully closed by this PR.

## Evidence

Focused validation passed, including 121 media-path cases, 23 Gateway integration cases, core and extension type checks, 29 core-graph cases, lint/format checks, mock/export and assertion-safety checks, and timer-race coverage. An independent P2 review finding was fixed in the latest qualified source tree; the focused suite moved from 16 failures to 121 passing after correcting mock cleanup.

prs.title: feat(talk): report which speech-to-text path talk.catalog uses
prs.body:
Closes #197958

## What Problem This Solves

Talk transcription can come from three places, in this order: a Voice Call streaming provider, the `agents.defaults.voiceModel` default, or the media-understanding audio models (`tools.media`). The Gateway picks one in `buildTalkTranscriptionConfig`, but `talk.catalog` doesn't say which, so Settings → Talk (#197906) can only state the precedence in its copy.

The page's "Preferred model" warning has the same gap. Voice notes always use the picked `tools.media` model, but when Talk uses a streaming provider the catalog lists only streaming providers, and the page checks the picked model's provider against those. Their credentials are read from different config. A key added on Settings → Models still shows "Not ready" when the streaming entry of the same provider has no key, and a key only in the Voice Call settings shows no warning while voice notes have no key.

## User Impact

On Settings → Talk, the speech-to-text status names the path Talk uses, for example "Talk uses openai, the streaming transcription provider set in the Voice Call plugin." The speech-to-text model row says whether the picked model drives Talk dictation or only voice notes, and shows on the same row whether that model is ready, with the key hint and "Open Models" when it isn't. Readiness reflects whether voice notes can use the picked model.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Protocol:** the `transcription` group of `talk.catalog` gets two optional fields. `source` is `streaming`, `voice-model` or `media-understanding`. When `source` isn't `media-understanding`, `mediaProviders` lists the `tools.media` audio providers with their readiness. Both are additive and the protocol stays v4.
- **Gateway:** `buildTalkTranscriptionConfig` already picks the path, so it records which one it picked and the catalog passes that on. `mediaProviders` comes from `resolveTalkFileTranscriptionConfig`, the same readiness check the media-understanding path uses. `talk.session.create` is unchanged.
- **Talk page:** the status line uses `source` to name the path. The speech-to-text model row carries the picked model's Ready or Not ready state, and when it is not ready, the key hint and "Open Models", in place of the separate "Preferred model" row. Readiness is checked against `mediaProviders` when Talk uses another path, and against `providers` when it uses the media-understanding path. Gateways that omit the fields keep the stated-precedence copy and the existing provider check.
- **Docs:** `talk.catalog` in the Gateway protocol reference and the protocol package changelog describe both fields.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway with Chromium, made-up config and outgoing network blocked. Talk uses an OpenAI streaming transcription provider (Voice Call plugin settings), and the picked speech-to-text model is Deepgram `nova-3` in `tools.media`, with no Deepgram key.

Without this change (`main`): the status shows "Active provider: openai" and doesn't say Talk uses the streaming path; the model row states the precedence. The "Preferred model" row reads Deepgram's readiness from the streaming provider ("Deepgram Realtime Transcription").

![Settings → Talk, Speech to text on main: status Active provider: openai, Ready; model nova-3 with the stated-precedence description; Preferred model row says Deepgram Realtime Transcription can't transcribe yet, Not ready, with Open Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/d0e056098f6a1ba0de664cbbcbd1fc18fbef4e32/images/2026/11/dcdbfae3-accd-49e7-a256-b852339cf1cf.png)

With this change: the status says "Talk uses openai, the streaming transcription provider set in the Voice Call plugin." and shows Ready. The "Speech-to-text model" row shows nova-3 as Not ready with "Open Models", from the voice-note readiness check, and its description gives the key hint and says the model is used for voice notes only. There is no separate "Preferred model" row.

![Settings → Talk, Speech to text: status says Talk uses openai, the streaming transcription provider set in the Voice Call plugin, Ready; one Speech-to-text model row with the hint that deepgram can't transcribe yet and is used for voice notes only, Not ready, the nova-3 picker and Open Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9a78261cd8358ad12c50c2992eb1f708b06ff0db/images/2026/11/ad0f1f5c-93a7-4111-9747-3e8ec962db6f.png)

Tests: the Talk Gateway tests (`catalog.test.ts`, `file-transcription.test.ts`) assert `source` for all three paths and `mediaProviders` on the voice-model path, and fail without the Gateway change. Two cases in `talk-transcription.test.ts` give the streaming and voice-note Deepgram entries opposite readiness: with no voice-note key the model row shows Not ready, the hint and "Open Models", and with a voice-note key it shows Ready; neither case shows a separate "Preferred model" row. Both fail on `main`. 8 Talk Gateway and page test files pass (117 tests). UI and core typechecks, lint, formatting, `ui:i18n:verify` and the Gateway validator check are clean. `ui:i18n:check` reports locale fallback drift for the new English strings, which the `control-ui-locale-refresh` workflow translates after merge.

Not verified:

- Transcription with a real provider key. "Ready" means the provider has a credential, not that the provider accepts it.
- The `voice-model` path in a live Gateway; it is covered by the Gateway tests only.
- Native Talk clients, which don't read the new fields yet.

prs.title: feat(browser): let users take over the agent's browser from the Browser panel
prs.body:
Closes #197902

## What Problem This Solves

When you step into the Browser panel to solve a CAPTCHA, finish a login or fix a form, the agent can click, type or navigate over you in the same browser, and it doesn't know you are there. The only way to stop it is to stop the whole run.

## User Impact

- Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't click the new button. Agents keep using the browser exactly as before.
- When you click or type in the Browser panel, the agent's browser results over the next minute say you just used the browser, so it can check the page before acting.
- **Take control** in the Browser panel toolbar pauses browser actions from everyone else (the agent's `browser` tool, the `openclaw browser` CLI, other Control UI windows) on that browser. The agent gets a normal tool result saying you have taken over, and its turn continues. Snapshots and screenshots still work, and an action that had already started may finish.
- Control ends when you click **Release control**, when the Control UI window closes or loses its connection, or after 5 minutes without input from you. The panel then says control was released.
- Browsers on the Gateway host only. The button is hidden for node-routed browsers.
- No new config option.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check sits in the browser plugin's shared route boundary that every browser caller goes through (agent tool, CLI, `browser.request`), so the lock holds on the real action path rather than in status or extension state. It mirrors desktop computer control (`hasController` in the desktop session registry), including the wording "Browser input paused while the operator has control".

- **Who holds control:** the Control UI connection that took it. Its Gateway connection id already reaches the routes through `browser.request`. The agent's in-process calls and the CLI carry no connection id, so they are refused.
- **What it locks:** control belongs to the browser, not the profile name. Several profiles that reach the same browser through the same `cdpUrl` share one lock. Existing-session profiles without a `cdpUrl` key on their Chrome user data dir. Duplicate `cdpUrl` configs stay allowed.
- **What the agent sees:** the browser tool turns the route's refusal into a normal result (`status: "user_has_control"`) for tab actions and `start`/`stop`, so the turn is not treated as a failed tool call.
- **What counts as use:** the Browser panel marks its deliberate input (clicks, keys, text, scroll, back/forward, navigation, new tabs). Only marked input feeds the agent's note and keeps a takeover from going idle; the panel's automatic requests, such as page-metrics reads and viewport fits, do not.
- **What stays the same:** without a takeover, requests pass through untouched. The activity note is added only to host-local browser results.
- **State:** control is in memory. It ends with the browser runtime and does not survive a Gateway restart.

Relation to #143015 (mobile browser handoff): that PR reserves a profile for a handoff link. This covers the same-machine case with the user's own Control UI connection as the controller, and does not touch the handoff reservation; the handoff could reuse this check. #44615 proposed a lock kept in Chrome extension and status state.

Accepted edge cases, named instead of handled:
- One browser address spelled two ways (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1`) gives two locks.
- Session-scoped dashboard actions return the plain refusal message, not the friendly result.

## Evidence

Live run: an isolated Gateway with the managed browser (headless), the real Control UI and the real `browser` tool, with a local stand-in model that issues the tool calls.

Before, on `main`: the toolbar has no Take control button. The user clicked once in the panel, and the agent's click went through right after, with nothing telling the agent the user was there:

![Main: no Take control button; the agent's click lands while the user is in the panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ee34b743e036d49f3ab7f9a749910e22bb42e687/images/2026/11/03e31078-26a9-4889-a488-cd4b06c5fdfe.png)

With this change, the user clicked once in the panel. The agent's next click result carries the note:

![Agent's browser result notes that the user used the browser 5 seconds ago](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/dbeedc63-d215-4ec5-9b91-d62e97c3f9e9.png)

After **Take control**, the agent's click is not run. Its tool result says the user has taken over, the tool call isn't marked failed, and the page is unchanged:

![Agent told the user has taken over the browser; page unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/deb49a68-188a-4dfd-b228-eb25467449f7.png)

With no input for 5 minutes, control was released (after 297 s). The panel shows the notice and **Take control** again:

![Panel notice that control was released after 5 minutes without input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/692cd463-701f-4670-96f4-ef5d12169f59.png)

The agent's next click works ("Clicked 3 times"):

![Agent's click succeeds after the idle release](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/08284199534c706d53eeaeadd98a4a6925b5cf34/images/2026/11/2db5115d-a40f-4e77-bba3-f22d688e623a.png)

Tests through the real route dispatcher (`routes/operator-control.test.ts`) and the browser tool (`browser-tool.operator-control.test.ts`):
- Others' input is refused while control is held: act, navigate, open tab, stop. The holder's own input is admitted, and disconnecting releases control.
- Control is released after 5 minutes idle. Marked panel input restarts the window; automatic page-metrics reads and viewport fits don't.
- The panel keeps checking control across navigation and shows when the Gateway released it.
- A second profile name pointing at the same browser is held too. A profile on a different browser is not.
- Only a Control UI connection can take control.
- The tool answers `act` and `stop` during a takeover with `user_has_control`.
- The alias, idle-release, control-check and `stop` tests fail without their fixes.

Suites run: browser routes, browser Gateway handlers and browser tool: 422 + 52 passed; 55 skipped (existing opt-in Chromium suites). Browser panel UI tests: 274 passed. Typecheck is clean for the browser plugin, its tests and the UI; changed-files lint and the assertion-safety ratchet pass.
