prs.title: improve(ios): avoid reformatting unchanged parts of streaming replies
prs.body:
Related: #192232

## What Problem This Solves

iOS repeats Markdown formatting for unchanged parts of a reply as new text streams in, including unchanged list items.

## User Impact

The candidate removes redundant preparation without changing reply grouping, layout, reader anchors, sidebar animation, or word-fade timing. Native build, visual parity, and performance qualification are still pending; this must remain a draft until the exact candidate is tested on the Mac/iPhone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing streaming body now owns preparation for its mounted lifetime. Unchanged assistant segments retain their prepared snapshots; changed segments still run the complete Markdown parser, then reuse only positionally matching semantic blocks with matching completion state, reveal role, and localized default disclosure summary. Late references and structural changes therefore remain parser-owned.

This also removes throwaway initial reveal scheduling when SwiftUI reconstructs an already-mounted body. There is no incremental CommonMark parser, frozen prefix, global cache, new throttle, or word-timing change. A single growing prose block still requires full parsing and word scanning. Retained semantic inputs are limited to the current streaming snapshot, not a history of deltas. Static renderer initialization and image-list work belong to separate fixes. #198111 also touches the renderer and will need integration review; it is not included here, and no combined proof is claimed. The existing TimelineView ticks already render prepared snapshots: this is not a fix for whole-document reparsing at 60 Hz.

## Evidence

- Exact published candidate: `ed9258e79da94aac400d5f395339235258a726bc`; verified sole parent `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d` and all three published file blobs match the reviewed patch. The draft targets `main` and currently has integration conflicts; this pinned candidate has not been rebased.

- Pinned dependency/base: `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d` from #192232. This independent three-file candidate was reviewed before managed publication as patch SHA-256 `a1984c10d6bcd0415bd6075a1ce7f521d7a23e87c12d5aa04f1109dee1814c85`; #192232 itself is unchanged.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Complete changed sources and parser/reveal/list consumers inspected. Pinned swift-markdown 0.9.0 (`25cb61d3482054b09ae76ca4f281b1bfe7fe5a43`) still feeds and finishes a full document; no incremental-parser assumption is used.
- Added focused owner tests for unchanged-input publication, append timing, reasoning visibility, replacement, reveal-location changes, completion, localized summaries, late references, Setext headings, tables, and iOS nested lists. These have NOT been compiled or run. Baseline-red/candidate-green evidence, test duration, and CI seconds are pending. The shared-package suite is not automatically included by `pnpm ios:test`; macOS SwiftPM tests do not exercise the iOS-only list assertions. Native qualification must verify the actual test target and executed test counts.
- Author simplify pass: reused the existing streaming owner and semantic block equality, with no separate cache service or duplicate parser. Production delta: +151/-77 lines; test delta: +141 lines.
- Independent local `autoreview`, OpenClaw engine, pinned base through the complete local candidate, P0–P2: `scoped-clean`, no findings. This is source review, not native execution proof.
- Linux environment: `swift`, `swiftformat`, and `xcodebuild` are unavailable. No smoothness, frame-time, CPU, memory, or measured work-count improvement is claimed.

**Mac acceptance rule (before measurements):** compare the pinned base and exact candidate serially, ABAB, at least five samples per revision, cold and warm separately, on the same device/build settings. For a reply with 32 stable heading/prose sections and a changing final prose block, the source-derived expectation is 66 prose/heading preparations per changed input on the base versus 1 on the candidate after initial mount; full changed-segment parsing remains. Count actual calls before timing. Require unchanged rendered content/geometry/fade timing and reduced redundant preparation with no worsening median/p95 first-content latency, frame hitches, CPU, or memory. Treat any 20% regression as a stop; do not mark ready without native evidence. Include before/after video and representative screenshots from the exact heads.

Contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski and mikengyn.

prs.title: fix(skills): prevent missing transcription values from overwriting files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accidental output overwrites when a transcription option is missing its value: `transcribe.sh voice.wav --out --json` currently uploads the audio and overwrites a file named `--json`, instead of reporting the missing output path.

## User Impact

Malformed arguments now fail before uploading audio or writing a transcript, with a diagnostic naming the option. This also prevents silently consuming `--json` as a model, language, or prompt. A trailing value-taking option now prints a useful error instead of silently exiting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject a missing argument or an exact recognized option token before consuming a value; preserve other dash-prefixed literal values. The fix adds eight production lines and focused Python CLI regressions (44 lines); no parser framework or dependency change. There is no existing transcription argument test on this base. The new test uses the skills Python test lane and is outside the JavaScript/TypeScript test-line ratchet.

This follows the same missing-value/file-overwrite category as #196933, an external contribution merged by obviyus on November 11.

## Evidence

Executed the actual bundled Bash script with **real curl**, a synthetic WAV, an HTTP receiver on container loopback, Node response extraction, and real output files. The receiver returns a fixed transcript; this proves argument handling, request counts, and file writes, not hosted speech recognition. No paid API calls or user credentials were used.

```sh
# With a synthetic WAV, a local receiver returning {"text":"Local transcript"},
# and an existing ./--json file containing KEEP ME:
OPENAI_API_KEY=synthetic-local-key \
OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 \
  bash skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/transcribe.sh voice.wav --out --json
```

| Actual CLI case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out --json` | exit 0; 1 request; `./--json` overwritten with `Local transcript` | exit 2; 0 requests; `KEEP ME` preserved; `--out requires a value` |
| `--model`, `--language`, or `--prompt` followed by `--json` | exit 0 against local receiver; 1 unintended request | exit 2; 0 requests; option-specific error |
| Each of those four options at EOF | exit 1; empty stderr | exit 2; option-specific error and usage |
| Default text, `--json`, `--out -out.txt`, `--out ./--json`, or ordinary model/language/prompt values | exit 0; 1 request; expected output bytes | same |

All 15 actual CLI cases passed after the fix, including `--prompt "--- Meeting transcript ---"` and `--out --notes.txt`. Valid requests contained the exact synthetic WAV bytes. The five valid controls passed on both versions. For an intentional filename equal to a recognized option, use an explicit relative path, such as `--out ./--json`.

Focused verification: Bash syntax, repository-configured Ruff lint/format, and the committed Python regression passed. The missing-value regression failed on the original code in all 12 subcases; after the fix, `pytest -q -c skills/pyproject.toml skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/test_transcribe.py` passed (2 tests, 14 subcases; 0.86 s). Local checks ran in a secretless, network-disabled container capped at 256 MB and half a CPU. No full suite, macOS run, or hosted provider validation was performed. CI timing is pending.

<details>
<summary>Standalone reproduction from either checkout (Bash, curl, Node, Python)</summary>

```python
import os, subprocess, tempfile, threading, wave
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

script = Path("skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/transcribe.sh").resolve()
requests = []
class Receiver(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_POST(self):
        requests.append(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        body = b'{"text":"Local transcript"}\n'
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    def log_message(self, *_):
        pass

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp, HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Receiver) as server:
    root = Path(tmp)
    with wave.open(str(root / "voice.wav"), "wb") as audio:
        audio.setparams((1, 2, 8000, 0, "NONE", "not compressed"))
        audio.writeframes(b"\0\0" * 80)
    (root / "--json").write_text("KEEP ME")
    worker = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
    worker.start()
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(script), "voice.wav", "--out", "--json"],
            cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10,
            env={**os.environ, "OPENAI_API_KEY": "synthetic-local-key",
                 "OPENAI_BASE_URL": f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}/v1",
                 "NO_PROXY": "127.0.0.1"},
        )
        print("exit:", result.returncode, "requests:", len(requests))
        print("file:", (root / "--json").read_text())
        print(result.stderr)
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
        worker.join()
```

Observed on base: `exit: 0 requests: 1`, `file: Local transcript`.
Observed on this branch: `exit: 2 requests: 0`, `file: KEEP ME`, `--out requires a value`.

</details>

Independent Codex review covered the complete base `8830ff6d8ed6bbbc0ec15698428a7fcaaeb38deb` → head `fc565651b4a80d47f97843d18c8bc0f36f39498f` diff. One literal-value compatibility finding was fixed and covered before submission; final review found no remaining issues.

prs.title: fix: reduce Gateway stalls under filesystem pressure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reduces Gateway stalls when filesystem pressure makes synchronous pathname checks block request handling and maintenance. The incident included a 36.358-second main-thread stall; this change reduces the Gateway's exposure to that failure mode without claiming to fix the underlying host I/O pressure.

## User Impact

Session reads, workspace operations, skill preparation, database admission, and periodic cleanup move identified blocking work into existing asynchronous or worker owners. Lock exclusion, original-file identity, cancellation, FIFO ordering, and authority checks at the point of effect remain enforced.

This is an availability tradeoff: some operations take longer or allocate more. Normal cold plugin-root preparation remains unfinished: one measured fresh-root preparation makes **28 synchronous main-thread filesystem calls** (9 allocation/path calls and 19 staging/admission calls), with native SQLite I/O and retirement work uncounted. New generations can reenter this path; there is no once-per-process frequency claim, whole-runtime zero claim, or outage-immunity claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Repeated lock verification, duplicate database identity checks, discovery and workspace traversal, and synchronous work hidden behind asynchronous interfaces kept physical I/O on the Gateway thread. Existing preparation owners now perform that work and carry the original candidate, absence, and physical-identity facts to consumers. Live logical authority remains checked after awaits. Descriptor and loaded-native lifetimes stay with their existing owners, and accepted creation and completion work settles before services, ports, or capacity are released.

The complete migration is substantially larger than the original deletion-only expectation. Against integrated main `7d8875eb5f603e927ec42705eb05185437a97fac`, this PR adds **7,479 runtime lines**. The unique full-lane total is **9,175 runtime lines and two build lines**, including the 15 already-merged slices and counting readiness once. Canonical test growth is 10,683 lines with one 400-line allowance and 10,283 allocation credit. The growth supplies worker transport, physical custody, lifetime handling and complete caller migrations; it is not a net code reduction.

The integration also preserves upstream state-schema **39→40** and agent-schema **41→42** migrations. This lane adds no schema change of its own. Older code refuses the upgraded state, which changes the ordering and interpretation of the final compatibility measurements.

<details>
<summary>Already-merged prerequisite slices</summary>

Database and locks: [warm borrowing #197446](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197446), [writer admission #197461](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197461), [lock ownership #197455](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197455).

Discovery and credentials: [directory observation #197445](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197445), [credential reads #197460](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197460), [GitHub profile writes #197546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197546), [ClickClack reads #197545](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197545).

Execution and maintenance: [safe-bin preparation #197539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197539), [command preparation #197634](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197634), [installation observation #197584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197584), [readiness and diagnosis #197975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197975).

Logging, pricing, and measurement: [logging worker #197586](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197586), [default logging target #197742](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197742), [prepared pricing #197599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197599), [Gateway measurement #197504](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197504).

These fifteen PRs are merged; their evidence does not substitute for final combined-source qualification.

</details>

## Evidence

**Reviewed source:** commit `290f6cc1e647db3cd7065b6ea84f474c67769ec9`, tree `ce1b327c585ec51045fb766c2b2ba7cd4c68e0fa`, integrating exact main `7d8875eb5f603e927ec42705eb05185437a97fac`. The final two-file composition retains main’s scratch-cleanup command in the existing filesystem worker alongside the lane’s workspace, store-removal and refs-copy commands. This composition passed all 15 selected worker cases (10 scratch, four spool-removal, one refs-copy authority case; 13 other refs cases deselected), targeted core/infra types, lint, formatting and the exact-base test budget. One fresh complete-context Codex review found no actionable issue. Existing database, prompt and scoped UI proof remains bound to unchanged determining inputs; the prior UI bundle is not relabeled as a build of this head. The following qualification belongs to preceding commit `609f27bf3a760ccba9622c778192708679798b24` and is reused only for unchanged determining inputs. The final bounded conflict repair preserves main’s PostgreSQL page snapshot and the existing source-current guard. This successor passed 45 readonly/custody cases, all three real PostgreSQL snapshot cases, 89 prompt/prefix cases and one current-build public-reader E2E case (five others deselected). Core and four affected test type graphs, focused lint/format, and the exact-base test budget passed. Two fresh bounded Codex reviews found no actionable issue. The initial PostgreSQL attempt lacked a test-cluster extension and failed before history behavior; the corrected disposable cluster passed and was removed. No source or policy workaround was added. The following retained qualification belongs to preceding commit `424b1ed46af9621d9f8a45a3682bb40a14af530a` and is reused only for unchanged inputs. The integration preserves main's lazy status imports, awaits source reads before preparing resource identities, and retains the existing native-policy and cleanup owners. It passed 230 focused cases plus five browser and six public-session E2E cases. The 47-stage changed check retained 44 passing stages. Its three failed components are now closed: an unused internal CI benchmark export introduced by #195711 was made private (the identical repair subsequently landed on main in #198089), and the core/extension lint stages passed through the maintained native partitions after the 32 KiB changed-path transport limit triggered a whole-tree fallback. Complete changed-file coverage and the original failure remain recorded; no rule or baseline changed. The planner has four passing applicable tests and two platform skips. The exact-base budget passed. Five fresh bounded Codex assessments found no actionable issue; prior reviews cover unchanged source. Prior source-bound owner, worker, reader, packaged-worker and UI proofs remain valid only within their recorded scope; the previous session-worker file has composed coverage of all 30 cases, with its original failed command retained. Temporary diagnostics were removed without dropping original assertions. Review is separate from runtime proof.

**Measured owner behavior:** counters, timing, and allocation ran separately. The following are bounded synthetic source-mode measurements, not production syscall rates or compiled-Gateway latency. All adverse rows and A/A controls were retained.

| Owner workload | Synchronous calls | Material cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh native incarnation on an existing database, including release/drain | 27→0 per cycle | Paired elapsed +19.9%/+21.9% against A1/A2 (+776/+755 ms); source loading/startup is included. |
| Sharing acquisition | 10→0 per cycle | Paired sampled main allocation +31.6%/+22.5% against A1/A2. |
| Detached transcript fallback | 1,200→0 across the measured workload | Per read: +0.54–0.65 ms elapsed, +577–682 µs process CPU, +41–43 KB sampled main allocation. |
| Hourly cleanup, three synthetic artifacts | Warm full count 95→6; capture-owner subset 47→0 | Wall 6.578→246.209 ms; host+child CPU 8.357→296.053 ms; cumulative measured isolate allocation 1.008→118.113 MB. |

The first two rows are from 99 windows comparing the complete earlier implementation with the complete fix, not an isolated helper. Admitted hydration stayed 0→0 and supplies no deletion claim. Significant host load and A/A drift prevent a general CPU/latency speedup claim. Hourly cleanup's six warm residual calls are source-loader lookups; its first nonempty cold count increased **96→1,607**, mostly loader work. Allocation is not retained memory or RSS. The earlier APFS first-batch filesystem-API census fell **17,958→12,496** calls in its first window; that older five-owner result is not a final-union census.

**Prior CI failure disposition:** [the published 1d17 CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43354849847) ended with 122 successful jobs, 25 skipped, and three failed jobs (two test jobs plus aggregate). The current model-list failure reproduces unchanged on exact CI main `ba284782cf1705d7e5f1f085b9cdefbb55932af6`. Reversing only the nine-line accepted-catalog persistence addition from [#197784](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197784) makes the same original selector pass. This establishes the current inherited-main regression; it is a hunk counterfactual, not full historical-parent execution. No model runtime repair is included. Earlier failures predating #197784 remain unexplained. Follow-up must reconcile account replacement with durable shared-auth invalidation and the supported synchronous save/restart contracts.

The four continuation assertions are corrected to observe effects after the real transport guard: all 34 scenarios pass, and a negative control removing that guard fails the preserved no-write assertion. This is a fixture correction with no production change or weakened authorization requirement.

**Pending before landing:** the reviewed integrated commit still requires its canonical full-DTS artifact, compiled Linux/btrfs comparison, fresh-install and latest-stable upgrade/Doctor proof, final-head CI disposition, and final-head ClawSweeper with zero open items. No merge is requested while these gates are pending. The superseded pre-integration builds were canceled and joined before image export; no candidate measurement or Doctor run started from it. Linux ordering is A1→A2→candidate census→candidate timing, with both original-image controls before candidate fixture access. There is no post-upgrade baseline bracket, so aggregate CPU/allocation results remain observational across schema, packaging and startup-memory changes. prs.title: fix: honor session prefixes in media and link scope rules
prs.body:
Closes #190480

## What Problem This Solves

Media and link understanding apply session-prefix scope rules incorrectly: a `rawKeyPrefix` rule can block unrelated conversations, while an agent-stripped `keyPrefix` rule can fail to block its target.

## User Impact

Audio transcription, image/video understanding, and link processing honor the configured session prefixes. Existing full-key `keyPrefix` rules and first-match ordering are preserved. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fix the shared scope evaluator: match `rawKeyPrefix` against the full key and `keyPrefix` against either the full key or the request key returned by the existing session-key helper. Both fields must match when combined.

Credit to @yetval for the diagnosis and proposed repair in #190008, which was closed in favor of #190480 with an invitation to pick it up.

## Evidence

**Current submitted head:** `8b34a48361c454385aa721804aee678d6f9a5ea4`. [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41423465955) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41423465955/job/125208412058) passed for this exact head. The [current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191016#issuecomment-6574360819) reports sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Status checked November 11; runtime records below are retained, not new executions.

Real source CLI / Gateway before-and-after proof, using isolated state and synthetic sessions:

1. Start `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` with a single deny rule (first `rawKeyPrefix: "agent:main:blocked-raw:"`, then `keyPrefix: "blocked-short:"`).
2. Use `gateway call chat.send --params ... --json` to upload a valid one-second WAV to an unrelated session and the rule's target session. The configured local transcription CLI reads the actual uploaded file and records its invocation.
3. Wait with `gateway call agent.wait`, read `chat.history`, and inspect the local model endpoint's captured request. Require the completed reply to be persisted and the transcript's presence to agree with actual CLI execution.

Captured output (`CLI` means the transcription process ran; `providerTranscript` means its output reached the model request):

```text
before raw        allowed CLI=false providerTranscript=false modelCompleted=true
before raw        blocked CLI=false providerTranscript=false modelCompleted=true
before normalized allowed CLI=true  providerTranscript=true  modelCompleted=true
before normalized blocked CLI=true  providerTranscript=true  modelCompleted=true
after  raw        allowed CLI=true  providerTranscript=true  modelCompleted=true
after  raw        blocked CLI=false providerTranscript=false modelCompleted=true
after  normalized allowed CLI=true  providerTranscript=true  modelCompleted=true
after  normalized blocked CLI=false providerTranscript=false modelCompleted=true
```

The unrelated raw-prefix session was incorrectly denied before; the normalized-prefix target was incorrectly transcribed before. Both controls and both repairs pass after. Each phase ran separate raw/normalized Gateway configurations so the raw-rule bug could not mask the normalized-rule bug.

The Gateway, upload/media store, scope decision, process execution, model request, and persisted reply are real. Transcription text and model replies come from explicit local fixtures; this checks processing policy, not recognition quality. No live external channel, hosted STT, or hosted inference API was exercised. Image/video use the same evaluator and are covered by the existing media suite rather than separate live-device proof.

Focused validation on Node 24.22.2 in an isolated Debian container:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts src/link-understanding/runner.test.ts src/link-understanding/runner.transport.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-user-turn.audio-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **67 passed**. Before the fix, two audio-processing regressions and the normalized-prefix pre-fetch link regression failed for the reported reasons.
- Targeted format, type-aware lint, core typecheck, and changed-test typecheck passed; `git diff --check` passed.
- Focused test command wall time: 237.76 seconds including cold worker compilation and three shards. The modified media suite took 27.82 seconds total; its six new scope cases took 42 ms combined. The link suite shared a 146.42-second cold unit shard with the existing transport suite. The current-head hosted CI has since passed (linked above); no separate per-file hosted duration is claimed.

The broader suite is left to PR CI.

Completed `autoreview` (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, high, default P0 coverage) on the complete committed range `d9627ecb437b2a0fdaa2215137b291dbbc806137` → `8b34a48361c454385aa721804aee678d6f9a5ea4`: no accepted/actionable findings. Test-line allocation check also passed.

The author simplification pass retained one decision owner and no new state, wrappers, or configuration. The production change is +10 net lines. The +26 net test lines cover audio processing decisions and the separate pre-fetch link boundary; their allocation is recorded separately from the shared baseline.

prs.title: fix(agents): persona disappears after large inline avatar updates
prs.body:
Related: #127507 (remaining identity/avatar path; the ordinary workspace editor limit was fixed separately).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an agent loses its persona and custom identity instructions after saving a supported large inline avatar.

## User Impact

A supported 2 MiB avatar stays available for display while the agent continues receiving its name, persona, and instructions before and after the avatar field. Stored identity and avatar bytes remain intact. Ordinary workspace files and projected identity text retain their 2 MiB limits. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model receives a text projection with the inline image omitted. Identity publication and raw sandbox copies use the existing bounded 4 MiB identity allowance. Raw files and prepared identity text share the existing cache byte budget.

The implementation follows the canonical bootstrap file reader and preserves parallel read settlement, prompt order, source identities, and live workspace revocation. Extra-file discovery moves unchanged into its own module to keep the existing oversized workspace module from growing, retaining main's complete-file glob matching.

## Evidence

**Review target:** `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, comparison base `27f243756a45f02724b70597803571e2f0e1d020`. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159), including the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127820963084) and [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127823558387), passed. GitHub associates those checks with this exact head; the CI execution used the merge commit documented below.

| Revision | Evidence and scope |
| --- | --- |
| Current `8c251978` | 13 focused tests across projection, raw sandbox copy, and bootstrap cache; production-source filesystem probe preserves persona and exact raw copy, rejects an oversized ordinary file, and checks managed glob selection. Current-head hosted CI passed. |
| Previous `3034a560` | 224 tests, one existing skip, core typecheck and typed lint passed. Its CI ratchet failed on inherited debt. The recorded full-index PR patch is byte-identical to the current patch; this does not make its CI green. |
| Historical `4fd20c3` | Built Gateway/agent CLI and real host-model generation preserved four persona facts with a 2 MiB inline avatar. Separate base/candidate probes demonstrated the original loader and copy failures. These executions belong to that historical revision. |

The current candidate's recorded full-range independent review covers all 15 changed files, including the discovery extraction, bounds, cache, and publication owners, with no actionable findings. Its retained full-index diff SHA256 is `c76627e0c35fe7241bf1818f41e63e98807af184814b6ca211de00941b8ade0b`. This description update adds no code or new test execution. The [November 11 hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/173124#issuecomment-6192419182) now covers `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, with sufficient proof and no findings or before-merge actions. Its 4/6 proof assessment explicitly retains the historical-revision and model-bridge limitations below.

**Proof limits:** No full Gateway/model E2E was rerun on `8c251978`. The historical real-model proof used a manually orchestrated host-model bridge, not a genuine external Responses service compatibility test. Historical builds skipped declaration emission; skipped CI lanes are not build/test proof. The failed historical ratchets and unavailable local autoreview remain recorded below.

<details>
<summary>Retained verification records, commands/observations, and historical limitations</summary>

### Retained CI-repair verification (8c251978)

Candidate `8c2519786a3812cbd3b7b681164df33c51ce8edd`, base `27f243756a45f02724b70597803571e2f0e1d020`.

The previous hosted [run 42179630823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42179630823) failed its test-line ratchet by 25 inherited lines; its aggregate gate failed for the same reason. The new base has 35 lines of headroom. This rebase applies the identical PR patch to that corrected base: no tests removed, no shared-budget increase, and the PR's existing exact 213-line allocation is unchanged.

Current-head local results in secretless isolation:
- Native test-line ratchet: **6,534,770 lines / 6,534,805 ceiling; 35 lines slack**.
- **13 tests passed across 3 files**: identity avatar projection, raw sandbox copy, and workspace bootstrap cache. The canonical runner retained its completed compiler cache; dependency bundler directive warnings were nonfatal.
- Formatting of all 14 applicable changed files and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Production-source filesystem probe: decoded avatar **2,097,152 bytes**, raw identity **2,796,289 bytes**, model-facing identity **85 bytes**; persona before/after preserved; raw sandbox copy exact; oversized ordinary file rejected; managed glob selected only `packages/core/IDENTITY.md`.
- Hosted [CI run 42196349159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159) **completed successfully**, including [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127820963084) and the final [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42196349159/job/127823558387): 46 successful jobs, 30 skipped jobs. Skips are not counted as executed proof. Its actual merge `fc8aecc0d` combines this head with newer main `f6c70269845ce57772227801514d171d6c7c9642`; the native test-line gate reports **6,536,136 / 6,536,170, 34 lines slack**.

The prior head `3034a5608bb18de6dd60b47c99b1152229d49144` passed 224 tests (1 existing skip) across 11 files, core typecheck, typed lint and formatting. Those are prior-head results. Its hosted CI was not green because of the inherited 25-line deficit. The earlier real Gateway/model evidence below belongs to `4fd20c3`; it is historical evidence, not a new full Gateway/model E2E run on the current head. Selected current-head broad checks passed in the hosted CI run linked above; its skipped lanes, including build-artifacts, are not proof of a build or test run.

Fresh independent host-agent review of the complete 15-file committed range passed with no actionable findings. The review inspected current-base discovery extraction, raw/prompt bounds, cache and publication owners. Canonical full-index diff SHA256: `c76627e0c35fe7241bf1818f41e63e98807af184814b6ca211de00941b8ade0b`, byte-identical to the previous reviewed PR patch. Local autoreview remains unavailable as described in the historical evidence; no successful run of that tool is claimed.

### Historical behavior proof (previous head)

Historical validated candidate (before the CI repair): `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c`, based on `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738`. The exercised source tree is `7b65a7a8d7f77fd857869a90d2a2b9c57a86fb51`; the dirty candidate diff SHA256 is `6fbf623f75c8252beef335d43c1f11b2947fe6c2ec383443d9ce473815901cbc`.

- Historical focused tests: 224 passed and 1 existing/configured skipped across 11 files (124 Gateway + 100 agent tests), including prompt-prefix stability, managed/local reads, and file-publication boundaries. The canonical runner completed both serial shards in 290.94 seconds.
- Production core typecheck and all 29 affected canonical test-consumer typegraphs passed.
- Formatting, typed lint for all 13 changed TypeScript files, file-line-cap, and diff whitespace checks passed. Test-line accounting has the inherited failure described below.

Historical local test-lines result before this repair (superseded by the passing current-head result above): 6,434,192 lines against a 6,433,276 effective ceiling, over by 916. This PR adds 213 net regression-test lines and a separate allocation of exactly 213 for local/managed projection, raw sandbox copying, cache accounting, publication refusal, and alias bounds. The shared scalar is unchanged. Subtracting this PR's test growth and allocation leaves the same 916-line debt on the pinned base; this was an attributed inherited failure, not a passing gate at that old revision.

The supported built-CLI path passed (`node scripts/run-node.mjs --help`, 308.8-second cold build; declaration emission was skipped, so this is not full release-package/DTS proof). Its build input signature matched the exercised candidate. A normal built Gateway and agent CLI then produced:

```text
decodedAvatarBytes=2097152; persistedIdentityBytes=2796357
agents.update=ok; identity+roster avatar/name readback=exact
primaryResponsesRequests=1; personaMarkers=4; inlineAvatarInPrompt=false
providerReplyReturned=true; agent.wait ended=true; activeSessions=0
oversizedOrdinarySave=rejected; previousContents=retained
gatewayExit=0; nativeCleanShutdownReceipt=true; forcedKill=false
remainingOwnedDescendants=0; loopbackHttpOwner=joined
```

The stored identity hash stayed unchanged across the normal turn. The source hashes captured by this runtime match the historical committed tree; the build ran on the pinned base plus the exact candidate diff before the commit.

The model endpoint in this proof is a deterministic loopback Responses HTTP server inside a secretless network-isolated container, not an external model service. The ordinary built Gateway, normal agent CLI, CLI parser, and Gateway RPC paths are used. For the multi-megabyte update/save parameters only, a task preload replaces a short `--params` placeholder with JSON file contents before the unchanged CLI parser; this avoids Linux's single-argument size limit. CLI proof invocations provide the same `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning` Node flag that the CLI normally adds during startup, avoiding a second OS spawn after large JSON expansion. The product parser and RPC remain unchanged.

Independent host-session review of the complete 15-file committed range `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738..4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c` found no supported P0/P1/P2 findings. It independently matched all changed-file bytes and 21 runtime source hashes to the commit, and inspected the actual primary HTTP request, storage, session and cleanup observations. The full-index committed diff SHA256 is `179c31c174551d7f93be598ed59f9d64fc4c6525a8c324bd57beb8ee5a7c6fde`.

Local autoreview remains unavailable: the previously attempted helper rejects its configured `stream_max_retries` before sending a provider request. No successful autoreview of this final range is claimed; the independent source review above is the review actually performed.

Setup failures are retained separately: the first offline build needed two existing lock-pinned Darwin native asset archives; preparing the build owner's cache with SHA-512-verified archives allowed the isolated build to complete. The first CLI proof stopped before the update RPC with `E2BIG` during startup respawn; supplying the normal Node flag corrected the proof transport. Neither setup attempt is claimed as behavioral RED or a passing run.

Earlier proof and reviews on `c56a0e8d8d778478b950c11e2c9b6fde90d05b2c` remain historical; they do not establish validation of the conflict-repair candidate. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

### Historical red-on-base and candidate comparison (4fd20c3)

The same two probes ran through the canonical Vitest runner in separate detached source views: baseline `6b9a762375a4044ce7b69a626fa13d36c8f63738` and published candidate `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c`. Both used this PR's qualified read-only dependencies, separate initially empty compiler caches, Node 24.22.2 and secretless network-isolated containers. No candidate production source or root build output was supplied to the baseline.

```text
baseline: 2 failed / 1 passed
  loader: expected persona text, received [UNREADABLE: File exceeds 2097152 bytes]
  raw sandbox copy: destination IDENTITY.md absent (ENOENT)
  ordinary non-inline identity control: passed
candidate: 3 passed / 0 failed
both: native child completion; no remaining processes; dependency metadata unchanged
```

The copy regression is committed; the additional loader probe was a proof-only overlay with identical bytes in both source views. Their SHA256s are respectively `f62445e269ca926b068eda44be637a4c3205742cb1336547f7476b523650123b` and `c8b96210578a67b7d9fe192fd5dc91a8f4c5d0f4dc19424947a01201f29d593b`. This supplies actual behavioral RED, rather than treating setup failures as RED.

### Actual model generation through the built Gateway

A second supported build completed on the clean published `4fd20c3236043d4090b7e56bd7fa261a5134954c` HEAD (289 seconds, supported declaration-emission skip). The canonical build-input signature and buildstamp HEAD both matched. Its ordinary foreground Gateway and `agent` CLI, without `--local`, then completed this scenario:

```text
valid SVG decoded bytes=2097152; stored IDENTITY.md bytes=2796430
agents.update=ok; identity and roster name/avatar readback=exact
actual outgoing primary Responses requests=1; raw request bytes=56414
four randomized persona facts present; inline avatar absent from model context
fresh real host-model session answered all four facts correctly
ordinary agent CLI text=actual generated text byte-for-byte
agent.wait=ended; active sessions=0; stored identity SHA256 unchanged
gateway exit=0; native shutdown=clean; forced kill=false
remaining owned descendants=0; HTTP adapter owner=joined
```

The user question contained only the requested field names, with none of the random answers. The exact Gateway request (SHA256 `036e063250927a4afe3127cf3ddd3efa3fa637256db38de59a88392ea329ab74`) was supplied to a fresh host-model agent with no parent history or expected facts. Its actual final JSON was returned unchanged through the local HTTP envelope and ordinary agent CLI (generated-text SHA256 `d01a7d0e9cd910508731b1167f835a9e1a1d2a1ad2499fea5338862691f72753`). Delegation, actual model output, wire envelope, CLI output and natural cleanup records were retained.

This is **real host-model inference with a manually orchestrated bridge**. The host agent has its own system context; a transparent adapter asks it to read the complete actual Gateway wire context (system persona, user question and runtime context in `input`; there is no top-level `instructions` field). It is not a genuine external Responses service compatibility test. The underlying host model identifier and token usage are unavailable and are not claimed or fabricated. No canned answer, expected-answer injection, replay, or synthetic auxiliary response was used. Control UI was disabled in this isolated CLI/Gateway scenario. The earlier deterministic endpoint proof remains the source for the oversized ordinary-file save/refusal control only; it is not relabeled as real-model inference.

The first model-proof attempt stopped at the large-argument update CLI: an inherited Node compile-cache setting triggered a source-launcher respawn and Linux `E2BIG`. The corrected isolated invocation starts with the compile cache disabled, matching that launcher's ordinary cache-disable decision, and retains the pre-parser JSON argument transport described above. That failed attempt made no model request and is retained as a setup failure. A retained prior build lock was also archived only after checking that all associated task containers/build processes had ended; it is not a behavioral failure.

Historical-head hosted CI `41675209790` failed on the inherited test-lines debt and its aggregate check; the other checks for that historical head completed successfully. This evidence update does not make that failed ratchet a pass or claim that all CI is green.

An independent evidence audit matched the baseline/candidate observations and the actual host-agent, wire, storage, ordinary CLI and cleanup records. The base RED above proves loader/copy boundaries; the full real-model scenario ran on the candidate only. The isolated build used the supported Node fallback when offline Bun staging was unavailable, and a nonfatal page-cache warming `ENOSYS` diagnostic remains in runtime logs. Neither is presented as a full Bun/platform qualification.

Related: #198112

Stacked dependency: this patch is based on #198112 at `39c91efdee179c71f914d83d9f0cc94608fcc133`. Keep that event-admission change separate. The authored delta is exactly four files: the two queue owners and their two native test files; dependency changes are not new work in this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: native Gateway subscriber buffer overflows leave no diagnostic record when a consumer falls behind.

## User Impact

Operators can now see when a native subscriber overflows and how many deliveries it dropped during its lifetime. There is no UI or delivery/recovery change: buffer sizes, filtering, newest-event retention, grouped replies, sidebar animation, and word fade stay unchanged.

This is a diagnostics-only draft. Exact-head Mac/iOS builds, native tests, and log capture remain pending; no performance improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing subscriber owners now count actual AsyncStream drops, warn on the first one, and report at most one lifetime total on removal. A subscriber produces at most two content-free warning records and no records when it has no drops. Counts saturate rather than wrap and disappear with the subscriber. Normal delivery does not update counters, format logs, read a clock, or allocate diagnostic tasks.

The macOS owner applies this consistently to initial snapshots, ordinary pushes, and retirement publications. Existing admission filters and the separate realtime-audio overflow failure path remain intact. No replay, synthetic sequence gap, resubscription, configuration, storage, or public API is added. A process exit can prevent the final lifetime summary; no durable reporting is introduced.

## Evidence

- Added/extended real owner-stream regressions for admitted versus filtered traffic, independent fast/slow subscribers, newest-delivery retention, cancellation, replacement counters, zero-capacity initial snapshots, and retirement drops. Existing DEBUG push fixtures expose the actual counters; tests do not fabricate yield results.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): scope scratch binding protection to possible owners
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scratch cleanup globally deferred every checkout when one live execution lacked a session key, or a live session's checkout binding changed during refresh. Continuous activity could therefore starve expired scratch in unrelated idle worktrees.

## User Impact

Live runs protect roots they could own. Known session paths and session-owned worktrees remain protected while bindings refresh. When no checkout owner can be resolved, the run protects roots created since its admission, plus known agent directories; unrelated older roots remain eligible. Roots without a usable creation time stay protected under unresolved execution. Queued sources retain their bound paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scratch custody owner consumes existing run/controller identity, registry ownership and creation time. Project roots use their filesystem birth time. It keeps previously known paths during refresh instead of discarding them, resolves a missing session key through the existing execution controller when possible, and replaces the two global throws with root-local protection. Refreshes still occur at the existing preparation boundary; no config, schema or durable state is added.

Production delta: +49 lines for root ownership and admission-time classification. Tests +76, benchmark +43. The indexes are derived once from the existing pass inventory; no extra registry scan or persistent cache.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the exact parent in both production cases: missing-key preparation throws, and continuously invalidated bindings produce zero removals / three deferred roots. The candidate's 13 custody tests pass, including an unmapped known session key, possible-owner preservation, release of protection, queued bindings, lease isolation and restart ordering. The 10 scratch consumer tests also pass. Independent Codex P2 review is scoped-clean. Changed checks and full owner measurements are in progress; this remains a draft.

Measurement contract, recorded before the first measured run: use the committed `scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts` with two 62,000-file workspaces, 5,000 synthetic session rows, one complete 62,000-file expired clone, 255 expired small entries and 256 fresh entries. Run two A/A controls followed by five serial interleaved parent/candidate pairs for each `--scratch-binding missing|stale` condition. Accept parent starvation and candidate completion of the 256-entry scratch budget with all fresh files preserved. Report wall, main/total CPU, main allocation, loop p99/max, counts and host load. Zero-work failures are not per-removal CPU controls. Source-mode APFS hardlinks and accelerated waits do not establish production btrfs throughput or chat latency.

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts \
  --source /path/to/62000-file-synthetic-source --output /path/to/new-fixture \
  --worktrees 2 --scratch-order --scratch-clones 1 --scratch-binding missing
# Use stale for continuous binding publications; --reuse-scratch-order for later arms.
```

Baseline arms use the existing sparse-source overlay support with only `src/gateway/scratch-maintenance-custody.ts` from parent `1110e81c7b93da2eb1a8b3ba26f70cf4a9660553`. Worker scan/delete and atomic claiming remain identical in both arms.

prs.title: fix: preserve native inline widgets during revalidation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes inline widgets unnecessarily losing their loaded page when a retained native chat row starts resource resolution again.

## User Impact

Same-owner widgets can keep their interactive state while their current source is re-resolved. Layout, grouped replies, sidebar animation, and word fade are unchanged. True row destruction still releases the WebView.

This is a draft candidate: the Apple build, native regressions, exact-head iOS performance measurements, and before/after media are pending. No speedup or memory improvement is claimed yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain the mounted document during same-path revalidation instead of clearing it first. Continue resolving on every ready task appearance, and replace or retire the document when resolution changes or fails. Existing model identity and session target/generation bound the widget's SwiftUI identity, so a retained row cannot reuse its browser across chat owners.

Keep the current TLS, navigation, script, capability-refresh, snapshot, and bounded-retry policies. Refresh retained failure callbacks and recovery metadata, serialize a browser failure behind in-flight resolution, and invalidate snapshots whenever the load generation changes. An unchanged URL/TLS binding with new recovery metadata keeps the document and updates its callbacks; a recovery that returns the same failed resource now retires the dead page. No global WebView pool, skipped resolution, new route-fencing protocol, or public API change is introduced.

## Evidence

- Inspected the candidate against base `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`; `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent Auto Review of the complete local candidate, including untracked lifecycle tests, returned `scoped-clean` for P0–P2. This is static review, not native execution.
- Added, but have not executed, production-boundary tests hosting the real chat bubble and WKWebView against the existing ephemeral loopback HTTP fixture. The retained-page assertions exercise a readiness false→true task restart while the resolver is pending, not literal scroll disappearance/reappearance. Scope replacement uses the production bubble with fixture identity tokens, not full IOSChatViewModelOwner hydration. Both real flows remain pending on the Mac/iPhone. The tests also cover failures during revalidation, callback/recovery-metadata updates, suspended resolution, and changed/missing source results. Existing resolver/TLS/snapshot tests remain in place.
- Native tests, compilation, SwiftFormat, and SwiftLint could not run: this Linux environment has none of those Apple/Swift tools. Baseline-red/candidate-green proof, test wall time, and CI seconds are pending the exact-head Mac build loop.
- Simplification: no new loader/manager or cache. Production delta: +52 net lines; test delta: +340 net lines, including constructor updates and reuse of an existing HTTP fixture.

**Performance acceptance rule, before measurement:** use a synthetic transcript with 30 widgets; separate cold mounting from 20 retained reappearance/scroll cycles. Interleave at least five baseline and candidate samples on the same iPhone/build configuration. On confirmed retained same-owner/same-resource reappearance, require continued resolution with zero additional WKWebView creations or document GETs after the first load, and preserved interactive state. Real destruction may create a new browser. Report creation/navigation counts, frame time and CPU median/p95, and peak/settled memory. No unbounded retained-browser growth or user-facing regression is acceptable. These measurements are not yet available.

Contributor credit: @vyctorbrzezowski and @mikengyn.

prs.title: fix(state-migrations): allow OAuth dirs reached through a state-dir alias
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` is spelled through a symlink alias of the copied state directory, the legacy state migration plan refuses it as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` even though its real path is inside the snapshot. The containment check compares two lexical spellings, so a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through an alias fails closed.

Precedent: #195061 (path containment through a canonical spelling owner). That PR audited 53 files combining path resolution with containment comparison and explicitly deferred this exact wrong deny: "**`infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` OAuth-dir check.** It compares two lexical spellings, so `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` spelled through a state-dir alias is refused as `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`. This is a minor wrong deny that fails closed."

Related: #195061

## Why This Change Was Made

The plan's `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` predicate compares `callerOAuthDir` against `requestedSnapshot.stateDir` with `isPathInside`, which is purely lexical (`@openclaw/fs-safe/path`). `resolveOAuthDir` expands `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR` with `resolveUserPath` (tilde + absolute, no realpath), so an alias that resolves inside the snapshot is judged outside.

The fix resolves both sides through `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (the same helper the sibling endpoint check at `listMigrationEndpointsOutsideRoot` uses) before the containment comparison. The admission lives in `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`, next to the plan-env owner (`createLegacyStateMigrationPlanEnv`); `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` consumes the admission. This re-spells the OAuth dir to its real location, so an alias inside the snapshot is admitted while a genuinely external directory stays refused.

No new validator, option, config, or persistence policy. The refusal path is otherwise unchanged.

The assignment that feeds later discovery also changes: it now stores the already-resolved canonical identity rather than the raw alias spelling. Admitting a path and then handing the unverified spelling to later directory I/O would leave a window where retargeting the alias redirects reads outside the admitted snapshot. Resolving once and reusing the checked result closes that window without adding a second resolution site.

Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32` (new admission owner), `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3` (net +3 physical lines; counted lines stay under the base 2805 — the file is grandfathered over its line cap and the ratchet rejects any growth, which is why the admission lives in `plan.ts`).

Classification: `behavior-completing` (completes the path-containment canonicalization that #195061 landed).

## User Impact

Operators who keep their OAuth credentials inside a symlinked state-dir alias no longer get a spurious `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` refusal from the migration plan; the read-only doctor/startup plan now recognizes the directory as snapshot-bound. Truly external OAuth directories are still refused, and the security boundary that rejects symlinked state snapshots (`captureLegacyStateSnapshotIdentity`) is untouched.

## Evidence

### Shipped CLI proof (source entry, same argv as the packaged CLI)

Proven through the shipped CLI entry `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json` (argv tree is identical to the packaged `openclaw` binary), with a real filesystem fixture: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials` where `alias` is a symlink to the copied state dir, and `operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json` inside it. No credentials involved.

```text
# BASE (production without the fix): the shipped CLI refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": {
    "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot",
    "message": "Configured OAuth migration directory is outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials"
  }
}

# HEAD (this fix): the shipped CLI no longer refuses it (planner proceeds to its normal
# staged-candidate identity refusal; no oauth-dir-outside-snapshot anywhere)
$ OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-* --json
{
  "outcome": "refused",
  "refusal": { "code": "candidate-artifact-digest-required", ... }   // planner's fixed artifact guard, unrelated to OAuth
}
```

No wrong allow — the same shipped CLI still refuses both a genuinely external OAuth dir and a **reassigned** alias (alias retargeted to an outside dir). Re-verified on the current head after the refactor:

```text
# HEAD, OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=/ws/proof-external/operator-credentials (outside the snapshot)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof-external/operator-credentials" } }

# HEAD, alias reassigned to point outside (/ws/proof/alias -> /ws/proof-external)
{ "refusal": { "code": "oauth-dir-outside-snapshot", "message": "...outside the copied state snapshot: /ws/proof/alias/operator-credentials" } }
```

### Directory I/O confinement after admission (alias retargeted)

The admitted plan must not leave later discovery reading through the alias spelling: retargeting the alias afterwards would redirect directory I/O outside the snapshot. The plan records the OAuth source in the `channel-pairing` step, so that step is the readback boundary.

Same fixture (alias `.../alias` -> `.../state`, `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=.../alias/operator-credentials`), same shipped CLI, only the assignment under test differs:

```text
# BASE (assignment keeps the raw alias spelling)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/alias/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json

# HEAD (assignment stores the resolved canonical identity)
channel-pairing source: /ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
```

Re-verified on the current head: `channel-pairing` source is the canonical `/ws/proof2/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json`. BASE resolves through the alias for the containment check but then re-spells the env var with the alias, so a retarget after admission moves the recorded source outside the snapshot. HEAD records the checked canonical location, so the same retarget cannot change where the admitted plan reads.

### Retarget between admission and directory I/O (same run)

The two runs above retarget the alias between invocations. The stricter case retargets *inside one plan run*, after the containment check admits the directory and before `detectLegacyChannelPairingState` enumerates it.

Instrumentation is a `--import` preload on the shipped entry, hooking `fs.readdirSync`: when the OAuth directory is first enumerated, it repoints the alias to an outside directory and then performs the read, tracing the actual path. The outside directory holds `discord-pairing.json`, which the snapshot copy does not, so any external read shows up in the plan itself.

```text
# BASE trace
RETARGET before readdir of /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials
RETARGETED /ws/rt/alias -> /ws/rt/outside
READDIR /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials          <- reads outside the snapshot
plan refs: /ws/rt/alias/operator-credentials/{telegram,discord}-pairing.json

# HEAD trace
READDIR /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials          <- reads the admitted snapshot dir
plan refs: /ws/rt/state/operator-credentials/telegram-pairing.json
external-only "discord-pairing" occurrences in plan: 0
```

On BASE the retarget lands, the plan enumerates through the alias and picks up the external-only `discord-pairing.json`. On HEAD the alias spelling never reaches the directory read: the admitted plan reads the canonical snapshot directory and the external-only file never appears.

Reproduce: `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR=<alias>/operator-credentials node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --import <preload> src/entry.ts update migration-plan --snapshot-home <h> --snapshot-config <c> --snapshot-state <s> --json`, with `alias` a symlink to the copied state dir and the preload retargeting it on the first `readdirSync` of the OAuth directory.

The regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` asserts exactly this: on the base it fails on the canonical path mismatch (it previously asserted the alias spelling), on this head it passes.

Red (base) / green (head) / external-rejection (head) all captured on the same fixture and CLI. Current head: `37dec884e1cb` — `state-migrations.plan.ts` sha256 `b99eae1f52f0e978fe42fc5cab12fe0ef4fc357523547d701dc7d2ba9979a697`, `state-migrations.doctor.ts` sha256 `3c5c11494159520e8b3cd04c083c0e433a20d265324aa4ea530d5b34a571cac1`.

### RED -> GREEN

The alias case is covered by a new regression test `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias` in `src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts`. On the base with production WITHOUT the fix and the test WITH the alias case, the test fails with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot`; on this head it passes.

- Baseline (RED) SHA: `cdcef6c25f75fd7e2e2ddea93636a0ff629ce45a` (the branch's original base) + alias regression test → test FAILs. `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` and `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts` are unchanged between that base and current `main` (`3e9d22d51026`), so the RED verdict still holds on current main.
- Head (GREEN) SHA: `37dec884e1cb` (this branch) + alias regression test → test PASSes
- Production entry: `planLegacyStateMigrationsReadOnly` in `src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts`; admission owner: `resolveSnapshotOAuthDirAdmission` in `src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts`
- Decision surface: `oauthDirOutsideSnapshot` / `OPENCLAW_OAUTH_DIR`
- Recorder/readback boundary: plan `refusal.code` and `channel-pairing` step `source`

```text
# RED (base cdcef6c25f + alias test): plan refuses the alias-spelled OAuth dir
FAIL: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
  AssertionError: oauth-dir-outside-snapshot refusal present

# GREEN (head 37dec884e1cb + alias test): plan admits the alias-spelled OAuth dir
PASS: preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory reached through a state-dir alias
```

### Legal control (no over-broadening)

- `refuses an OAuth migration directory outside the copied state without inspecting it` — still PASSes (external dir kept refused)
- Retargeted-alias control: after the alias is repointed outside, the shipped CLI still refuses with `oauth-dir-outside-snapshot` (see above)
- `preserves a snapshot-bound OAuth directory in the read-only plan` — still PASSes (direct inside path unchanged)
- Security boundary `rejects a symlinked state snapshot before migration detection` — unchanged, untouched code

### Verification

Current head `37dec884e1cb` (rebased onto current `main` `3e9d22d51026`), all re-run after the line-cap refactor:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/state-migrations.caller-mode.refusal.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 23/23 pass.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts src/infra/state-migrations.plan.ts` — passes.
- `node scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` — OK (`no new violations or over-cap growth`; doctor.ts no longer grows).
- `node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main` — OK (`Net test lines: +28; allowance: 400`).
- `npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on both changed production files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested locally: `tsgo:core` (the pinned `tsrs` native binary needs GLIBC 2.34; this host's libc is older — environment limitation, not a code verdict) and the full repository suite. PR CI covers both.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC vs base: `state-migrations.plan.ts` `+32`; `state-migrations.doctor.ts` `+22/-3`; Test LOC: `+28`.
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `resolveIdentityPathViaExistingAncestorSync` (same helper as the sibling endpoint check) and `isPathInside`; no new validator or resolution primitive.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none beyond admitting alias-spelled snapshot-bound OAuth dirs (the intended fix); external dirs and symlinked-snapshot defenses unchanged.

### Line-cap: admission owned by the plan module

`src/infra/state-migrations.doctor.ts` is grandfathered over its line cap (2805 counted lines, cap 700), and the checks-fast-baseline-ratchets line-cap job rejects **any** growth on such files (`allowed = max(cap, base count)`). The containment + canonical-assignment logic therefore cannot stay inline without shrinking `doctor.ts`. prs.title: fix(agents): web_fetch results are wrapped twice in Code Mode and Tool Search
prs.body:
Closes #198109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Code Mode cell or Tool Search `dispatch_action` returns `web_fetch` fields, the result wrap sanitizes the tool's own envelopes as if they were spoofed, so the model gets `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]` frames and a second warning sentence, and whole pages go over the 20,000-character result budget.

## User Impact

User impact: agents using Code Mode or Tool Search see fetched titles and text as content inside one untrusted-content envelope, and a `{ title, text }` page result comes back inline instead of as a saved-result reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

`web_fetch` and `web_search` wrap their own fields with `wrapExternalContent`, and Code Mode guests keep that wrapper as documented. `renderToolSearchControlText` then wraps the whole result again, and `replaceMarkers` cannot tell the tool's envelope from a spoofed one.

This PR folds only envelopes OpenClaw issued, never syntax alone:
- `wrapExternalContent` now remembers a SHA-256 digest (over UTF-16 code units) of each envelope it issues for the `web_fetch` and `web_search` sources, keyed by its random id (bounded to 4,096 entries per process).
- Before the outer wrap, `foldIssuedExternalContent` looks up each start marker's id, decodes the candidate (raw or JSON-encoded up to three levels), and folds it into its body only if the decoded envelope, start marker through end marker, matches the stored digest. The warning line that `wrapExternalContent` puts directly before an envelope is removed with it; it is fixed text and not part of the digest.
- Anything else stays for the outer wrap to sanitize as before: a well-formed envelope with an unknown id, an issued id with changed bytes, an envelope from another source, a clipped envelope, or one evicted or issued before a restart.
- The outer wrap and the 20,000-character model cap are unchanged. The fold reads only the first 200,000 characters of a result, which is a new bound; nothing past it folds. Guest values and tool `details` are untouched.

**Why this is not #78521.** #78521 skipped the outer wrap when tool output already contained marker strings, so attacker text with fake markers went out unwrapped. Here the outer wrap always applies, and a fold requires the exact bytes the runtime produced, including its random id and its already-sanitized body. The tests and the live run below check that a copy of a real envelope with a fabricated id stays `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]`.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- A cell that slices a wrapped string (`res.text.slice(0, 300)`) clips the envelope. A clipped envelope does not match its digest, so it is sanitized as today; the whole `title` field in the same cell folds.
- The Code Mode result fit measures through the same function, so results that the duplicate framing pushed over budget now come back inline. Results that still don't fit are saved with a preview, as before.
- `web_search` builds its fields with the same wrapper, so it gets the same fold. I tested `web_fetch` live, not `web_search`.
- #194934 (open) edits the same function for a configurable limit. The overlap is small; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, real Gateway.** Fresh state dir, loopback port, real `web_fetch` of `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_pelican`. A scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint stands in for the model, so no vendor model is involved: it issues one tool call and records the tool result it receives. `main` is unmodified source at db4b2edd6d0; the PR column is this branch. Each run made 2 model requests, and the result was inside one outer envelope.

| Run | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Code Mode, issue cell: `{ title, textStart: text.slice(0, 300) }` | 979 chars; 3 sanitized markers; `title` = `\n[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]\nSource: Web Fetch\n---\nBrown pelican\n[[END_MARKER_SANITIZED]]` | 900 chars; `"title":"Brown pelican"`; the clipped `textStart` keeps 1 sanitized marker (expected, see scope notes) |
| Code Mode, whole fields: `return { title: res.title, text: res.text }` | Over budget, so saved: the model got a 1,018-char reference and a preview that cuts off inside the title's wrapper, no page text | 20,216 chars inline, no `[truncated]`, 0 sanitized markers, 1 warning sentence |
| Code Mode, `{ title, forged }` where `forged` is the title with its id replaced by `0123456789abcdef` | n/a | `"title":"Brown pelican"`; `forged` stays `\n[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]\nSource: Web Fetch\n---\nBrown pelican\n[[END_MARKER_SANITIZED]]` |
| Tool Search `dispatch_action` to `web_fetch`, Code Mode off | 20,187 chars, truncated; 3 sanitized markers; 2 warning sentences | 20,307 chars, truncated (the page is longer than the limit); `"title":"Brown pelican"`; 0 sanitized markers; 1 warning sentence |

**Tests**
- New `code-mode.output.test.ts` case: a network tool returns `web_fetch`-wrapped fields, and the cell returns them plus a copy with a fabricated id. It fails on `main` (db4b2edd6d0) with 3 `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]` and passes here with exactly 1, the forged copy; the guest value keeps the original wrapper.
- New `external-content.test.ts` cases: issued raw, JSON and nested-JSON envelopes fold, including a body that ends in a backslash. A fabricated envelope, an issued id with a changed body, a clipped envelope, an `api`-source envelope and an issued envelope with a changed lone surrogate are returned unchanged, and the outer wrap sanitizes them.
- Randomized check, outside the suite: 20,000 bodies (15,003 distinct) built from backslashes, quotes, newlines, emoji, U+2028, a lone surrogate and marker fragments, each raw and JSON-encoded 1 to 3 times (80,000 cases). Every issued envelope folded to the same encoding of its body, and the folded JSON parsed. No forgery folded: fabricated id, another issued id, changed body, changed metadata, `api` source, and a changed lone surrogate where the body has one. With a UTF-8 digest instead, the surrogate forgery folds and the new surrogate test fails, which is why the digest hashes UTF-16 code units.
- `pnpm test` on `src/security/external-content.test.ts`, the Code Mode suites (`code-mode.{output,result-budget,wait,integrated,auto-results,mcp,agent-loop}.test.ts`, `code-mode.test.ts`, `code-mode-json.test.ts`), all `src/agents/tool-search*.test.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/web-{fetch,search}*.test.ts`: 774 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are `web-fetch.sandbox.test.ts > stages read-only output` and `web-search-provider-common.test.ts > redacts short reason credential`, which fail the same way on unmodified `main` on this macOS host (`stat -c`, local credential redaction).
- tsgo on `tsconfig.core.json` (the `pnpm tsgo:core` project), `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` and `tsconfig.core.test.other.json`, `run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched files, and oxfmt (`--stdin-filepath` per file): clean.
- Adversarial timing for the 200k scan: at most 3.2 ms for 4,000 issued start markers with one far end marker (the per-call cap of 64 digest checks bounds this), under 2 ms for a 16 MiB string.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep every session prefix append-only on every route
prs.body:
## What

Make "the session prefix never changes mid-session" a guarantee for every provider route, not a per-route option.

Builds on #197925, which pinned the system prompt on every Anthropic Messages route.

- **Every route pins the session system prompt.** The `pinnedSystemPrompt` transcript-policy flag from #197925 is removed. `prepareSessionSystemPrompt` now runs for every route: Chat Completions, Google, Bedrock and any other transport. Later changes go out as appended deltas: an in-history system message where the route accepts one (`inHistorySystemUpdates`), otherwise the existing user-role note. The tool-pin-only checkpoint path (`persistSessionToolSurface`) is removed because every session now writes the combined checkpoint.
- **Runtime-context carriers are append-only on every route.** Routes without `appendOnlyRuntimeContext` stripped the previous turn's carrier. On Anthropic Messages that also changed how that turn's user message merged with the carrier. Both rewrote earlier messages on every turn. The new e2e found this; it is fixed in `resolveTranscriptPolicy`.
- **Rebuild points are a closed list** (in code on `prepareSessionSystemPrompt` and in `docs/reference/prompt-caching.md#session-prefix-stability`):
  - a new session (`/new`, `/reset`);
  - an explicit compaction;
  - a model or provider switch (API, base URL, system-message capability, or selected personal profile).
  - `/compact` and `/new` are the operator refresh points. There is no separate refresh command.
- **Enforcement.**
  - The prompt-cache tracker now also asserts on `systemPrompt` and `systemPromptSuffix` changes, as well as history and tools. Only a declared series rebuild is exempt.
  - `test/setup.shared.ts` turns on `OPENCLAW_PROMPT_CACHE_ASSERT=1` for the whole test suite. The two observability suites that change prefixes on purpose opt out explicitly.
  - Production logs one `[prompt-cache] prefix changed within session outside a rebuild point: <component>(...)` warning per session and component.
  - Only the immediate request-to-request difference is enforced. Changes carried as unmeasured cache evidence stay attribution data.
- **Gateway e2e** (`test/prompt-cache-prefix-stability.{anthropic,openai-completions}.e2e.test.ts`). One session goes through a user turn, an exec completion wake, a subagent settle, `sessions_send` from another session, a skill add, a workspace `AGENTS.md` edit and `sessions.compact`. It runs against fake `anthropic-messages` and `openai-completions` providers. Every provider request must extend the previous one byte for byte (cache markers ignored; a string equals a single text block). The only allowed break is at the compaction. Each route has its own e2e file, because Gateway state is process-wide. Both pass.
  - Before the carrier fix, the same e2e found 8 breaks outside the compaction on `anthropic-messages`.

## Upgrade behavior

- No schema change. The series checkpoint is the existing `openclaw.system-prompt` custom transcript entry. A session that has no checkpoint starts its series on its first turn after the upgrade. That turn sends the freshly rendered prompt, the same request it sends today.
- On routes that previously stripped runtime-context carriers, those carriers were never stored (the runtime-replay suite covered that case). Old history therefore replays unchanged, and only new turns store their carriers.

## Real-route proof

The same journey runs on one target session through a real Gateway: user, exec wake, `sessions_send`, skill add, workspace edit, subagent settle, final user. A logging proxy records each provider request and its usage. Before is `main` before #197925. After is this change on top of #197925's head, measured before the rebase onto current `main`.

**Anthropic Messages through a custom base URL proxy** (Claude Opus 5.5, `cacheRetention: short`), target-session requests:

| | requests | prefix breaks | cache write | cache read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 11 | 5 (all system prompt) | 149.2k | 212.7k |
| after | 11 | 0 | 77.7k | 397.8k |

**OpenAI Chat Completions** (`openai-completions`, gpt-5.4-mini, automatic prompt caching), target-session requests:

| | requests | prefix breaks | uncached input | cached input |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 11 | 3 (all system prompt) | 39.9k | 176.1k |
| after | 10 | 1 (see below) | 24.9k | 218.1k |

The remaining break is an edge case. The exec-wake reply was silent, so replay has no assistant message after that turn. This route merges consecutive user turns, so the next turn's input merged into that turn's trailing prompt-update note. Routes that merge consecutive user turns (strict Chat Completions compatibility, Google, Bedrock) can break once in this way. It happens only when a silent turn also carried a prompt update.

## Not covered

- **Remote worker turns** still render the system prompt each turn. Pinning them needs two things: the Gateway must read the session checkpoint from the worker's model-context view (it omits custom payloads), and the checkpoint must be written after the worker commits its `prompt-update` entry through the worker transcript-commit path. That is a follow-up.
- **The `appendOnlyRuntimeContext` policy field is now always true.** Its non-append-only branches are dead code. Removing the field and those branches touches about 40 call sites; that is a mechanical follow-up kept out of this diff.
- **Silent turns on merging routes:** see the Chat Completions note above.
- **Settled-turn finalization after custody revocation:** the suite-wide assertion found that this request is observed against the conversation's baseline. `settled-turn-finalization.borrowed.test.ts` keeps the warning path, and a comment names the gap. Request-admission and cache-observation suites change prefixes on purpose and opt out the same way.
- **Tool additions:** a tool the session has never sent still extends the tool pin once. That is one break, and the tracker declares it. Freezing additions would hide tools from a session whose first turn had a narrow tool grant.
- I did not measure Bedrock or Google on a real route. Their pin is covered by `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts`; their delta note uses the same user-role shape that runtime-context carriers already use on those routes.
- The first-to-second-turn cache miss on the proxy route with byte-identical prefixes (noted in #197925) is unchanged. It is visible as request 2 above in both runs.
