prs.title: fix(ios): Gateway password typed in Settings is ignored after onboarding pairing
prs.body:
Related: #182723

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after pairing iOS from onboarding (setup code or QR), typing the Gateway password in Settings did nothing. The password was never saved, so Reconnect and later launches kept sending the old device token and the app stayed on "Gateway password is out of date".

## User Impact

User impact: when the Gateway rejects the saved credentials, typing the correct password in Settings and tapping Reconnect connects. The password is also kept for later launches.

## Why This Change Was Made

Settings saved the Gateway Password and Gateway Auth Token fields under the manual-host endpoint. Onboarding pairing never fills the manual host, so the save target was empty and the save was silently skipped (`Fields.persist` returns when the target is nil). The fields still showed the typed text, so it looked saved.

Now, when no manual host is set, the fields load from and save to the active saved gateway, the same entry Reconnect connects to. A manual host still wins when one is set, and fields already bound to a gateway are unchanged. Saving writes token and password together, so a new `Fields.edit` first loads the target's stored credentials into unbound fields; typing a password can no longer erase the stored token.

**Accepted edge (as on `main`):** after switching gateways from the sidebar while Settings stays open, an edit still saves to the gateway the fields were last bound to, until Settings syncs again on appear or foreground.

## Evidence

**Simulator (iOS 27, isolated local Gateway with password auth):** pair from onboarding with a setup code, revoke the device's tokens on the Gateway so the app shows "Gateway password is out of date", type the correct password in Settings → Gateway Password, tap Reconnect, then relaunch.

| Build | Gateway log after Reconnect | After relaunch |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`73c6cbf00f9`) | operator and node: `authProvided=token authReason=password_mismatch` | same; still "Gateway password is out of date" |
| this PR | operator: `client connected auth=password` | operator and node `auth=password`, app Connected |

The node role first needs Gateway approval because its device token was revoked ("Additional approval required" on the device). After approval it connects with the password.

**Test:** `a credential typed after onboarding pairing saves to the active gateway`. It fails with the active-gateway fallback removed (the password is not saved) and with the load-before-save step removed (the stored token is erased). It passes with both. `RootTabsSourceGuardTests` and `GatewayConnectionControllerTests`: 98/98.

**Review:** two second-model rounds. Round 1 found the token-erasing write and a test that could not fail; both are fixed. Round 2: ready.

prs.title: improve(ios): reduce repeated work while reading long chats
prs.body:
Related: #192232

## What Problem This Solves

Reading long chats can repeatedly prepare the same transcript during unrelated view updates and scroll callbacks.

## User Impact

Reduces redundant transcript preparation while preserving the current chat design, grouped replies, reader position, sidebar animation, and streaming word fade. Native build, device behavior, and measured performance are still pending; this is a draft for the Mac verification loop, not a ready-to-merge performance claim.

**Stacked dependency:** Vyctor accepted stacking this new PR on #192232 at `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`. The inherited dependency changes shown against main are not this fix. The authored delta against that immutable head is exactly five shared chat files. This PR does not modify #192232, does not duplicate #194235 composer isolation, and requests no merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

One mounted chat now retains one immutable prepared transcript for its actual message, narration, reader-history, display-policy, session/model, run, and tool inputs. Rendering and scroll callbacks share its rows, footer metadata, groups, iOS cells, and turn anchors; split-row actions reuse the already-projected full current message instead of projecting history again per part.

The existing rendering, grouping, visibility, and scroll policies remain the owners of behavior. The cache is bounded to one preparation per view, reads observed dependencies even on hits, and does not rely on timeline notifications alone. This does not implement changed-delta incremental Markdown or remove the existing live-text reconciliation work. Input comparison and retained preparation have a CPU/memory cost that still needs device measurement.

Simplification removed duplicate callback preparation and the forwarding grouping wrapper. Against the dependency head: production +208/-132 lines (net +76); tests +241 lines for four distinct owner contracts. The retained growth supplies the one-entry owner and its invalidation/reuse proof; no durable state, schema, setting, or dependency change is authored here.

## Evidence

- Published head: `da48e3f1521eb2ddab73783fc529771c79b0c794`. Remote GitHub commit/compare reads verify its sole parent is `7618f4311be932aadf7a06d18e28fbfe806c407d`, it is exactly one commit ahead, and all five changed remote blobs match the inspected local files. Both required human coauthor trailers are present. GitHub currently reports conflicts against main (`mergeState: dirty`); the accepted dependency base is intentionally preserved for this draft build loop, not rebased.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary native chat work when a Gateway sends events that chat never uses; those events also compete with useful updates in bounded queues.

## User Impact

Unrelated Gateway activity no longer enters the iOS/macOS chat event queues. Chat presentation, grouped replies, sidebar animation, word fade, and supported chat effects are unchanged. Snapshot-only onboarding and sidebar-catalog observers also stop queuing unrelated server events.

**Draft build loop:** native compilation, runtime verification, and before/after measurements are still pending on the exact candidate commit. No measured speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared chat codec now owns one event-name registry used for both subscription admission and exhaustive payload dispatch. iOS uses the existing filtered subscription with explicit cleanup; macOS adds the same opt-in filter at its existing queue owner. Lifecycle publications bypass the macOS event predicate.

Filtering does not inspect a mutable agent/session selection, payload, reason, or stream. New reasons and stream variants under supported event names remain admitted. Unknown names and bounded narration tails already mapped to no chat effect; their transport-frame decoding is unchanged, but they no longer occupy chat queues or trigger chat mapping attempts.

## Evidence

- Added a real GatewayNodeSession subscription/mapping regression: 16 relevant fixture events followed by 250 unrelated events. Assertions require all 16 effects in order, 16 filtered mapping attempts versus 266 for an independent all-events subscriber, and no post-cancel delivery. These are **expected assertions, not executed measurements**.
- Added macOS queue-boundary coverage for retained health/snapshot events, sequence gaps, disconnects, and unaffected unfiltered subscribers.
- Executed: `git diff --check` passed; 13 embedded JSON fixtures parsed, including 8 fixtures validated against their canonical producer schemas.

- Not run: Swift/Xcode compilation, Swift tests, SwiftLint, SwiftFormat, real transport cancellation/reconnect/route-switch smoke, device performance, or video capture. All four native tools are unavailable on the Linux worker. Test wall time and CI seconds remain pending.
- Simplification: no cache, batching, new recovery state, or UI changes. Production delta: +72/−33 lines; tests: +270 lines.

### Performance acceptance — pending

Use the committed queue workload above for operation counts. On a qualified Mac, compare the pinned base and exact candidate with the same isolated Gateway and synthetic chat workload, alternating at least five samples each; separate cold and warm runs. prs.title: fix: prewarm sandbox dependency templates between sessions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first sandboxed session after a default-base lockfile change builds a missing dependency template on its startup path. The existing idle prewarm now prepares that base before the next session arrives. In the native fixture, median first-session preparation falls **41.475 → 9.752 seconds (76.5%)**.

## User Impact

Recently used sandbox repositories prepare dependencies and the default projection manifest during idle time. Later sessions reuse the ready generation; a session arriving mid-build joins the existing preparation. The serial pass repeats 60 seconds after settlement and respects foreground, host I/O, memory and disk pressure. An immediate arrival or sustained pressure can still require foreground preparation.

Existing template records select repositories actually used for sandboxed sessions, including role-required project sandboxes. Background access preserves foreground `lastUsedAt`; eligibility expires at the existing seven-day idle window. Configured-but-unused repositories are excluded. Each pass resolves the newest base, and publication of a superseding base cancels obsolete background work before another pass. Existing mutation leases, cleanup settlement and four-generation retention remain authoritative.

No new config, schema, persistent state or cache. Production delta against integrated main is **+157/−67 = +90 LOC**: +62 for recurring selection/identity reuse/manifest preparation, +25 for recency/supersession bounds, +2 for the lightweight shared retention constant, +1 for generation-age ordering when foreground-use timestamps tie. Configured-unused selection and the eager execution import were removed. No changed module is imported by the Control UI.

## Evidence

Integrated head `d97bc512a917976a3f24e9b8aad7e498be15efe7`: **131 focused tests passed** (94 template/base owner cases, 37 scheduler/import cases). Earlier retention/import consumer proof passed 193 cases with one platform skip. Regressions fail before their fixes, including recency and unused headless cold imports. Codex autoreview of the integrated change is clean through P2. Main #197801's memory gate and both test sets are preserved; its one-shot timer drain was adapted to await observable first prewarm calls.

Final head `4620cd0dc17bcc8793ca75ad509717c09815af7e` review follow-up: **52 focused tests pass**, including a regression that fails before the one-line age tie-break (five equal-recency generations, reversed UUID order, newest retained and reused without installation). The existing v2026.11.2 raw-table fixture loads, selects, and refreshes successfully without staging fields or migration. `created_at` already exists in that released schema. Fresh Codex review of this delta is clean through P2.

The slow-startup summary already records `template.select`, `template.build` and `template.clone`; the regression verifies those child phases through the real diagnostics summary. Native phase detail also names them. No additional production logging patch was needed.

`pnpm build` passed on the cold-import head before integration. Final `pnpm check:changed --base c74c7a977c06` passes every stage except the unused `runPlannerFlow` export in `scripts/bench-ci-planner.mts`. The same Knip 6.40.0 command fails with exactly that finding on main parent `c74c7a977c060678604b01968547b45c4997cd7c`, using matching frozen dependencies and no resolution errors. Introduced by **#195711 / `ba284782cf170`**; its owners are unchanged here. This is a newly appearing main regression, not noise. The older production dead export is fixed in integrated main. Prior-head [CI 43365293062](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43365293062) completed green (60 successful jobs, 28 expected skips). The final retention correction is separately gated by exact-head CI.

## Native performance and accepted tradeoff

Fourteen completed arms: two interleaved A/A pairs and five A/B pairs, ordered AA, AB, BA, AA, AB, BA, AB. Linux/btrfs, 8 CPUs / 16 GB RAM, 64,608 tracked files / 1.10 GB, the real public frozen dependency graph and lifecycle scripts, and an original physically allocated 34.64 GiB database with 10,000 synthetic sessions. No production data was copied. Each measured arm advances the base with a lockfile change and starts one session 120 seconds later. Thus CPU/allocation below are **per base advance and per started session**, including background work; the untimed seed is excluded.

| Measurement | Baseline median → candidate | Empirical p95 before → after | Largest A/A difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup preparation | 41.475 → 9.752 s | 45.477 → 11.596 s | 6.389 s |
| Main-thread CPU | 4.124 → 4.322 s | 4.622 → 5.080 s | 1.588 s |
| Process CPU | 31.200 → 32.863 s | 35.396 → 35.591 s | 8.539 s |
| Whole-VM active CPU | 90.850 → 93.280 s | 98.900 → 100.280 s | 13.740 s |
| Main-isolate allocation | 498.672 → 514.178 MB | 508.487 → 532.820 MB | 8.026 MB |
| Loop p99 | 10.953 → 10.953 ms | 11.108 → 11.133 ms | 0.238 ms |
| Maximum loop pause | 282.067 → 322.175 ms | 298.320 → 382.992 ms | 37.880 ms |

Empirical p95 is the maximum of five samples per variant, not a population-tail estimate. Startup ranges are 30.836–45.477 s before and 9.389–11.596 s after. Paired median main CPU delta is +0.263 s versus 1.588 s A/A variation; process +1.663 s versus 8.539 s. Paired p99 delta is +0.025 ms versus 0.238 ms. Allocation rises 3.1% by medians. Maximum observed loop pause rises; no worst-pause parity is claimed. The recorded acceptance rule uses p99, which holds, and the maintainer explicitly accepts consumed build CPU moved into idle time.

**Attribution:** every arm builds exactly one dependency template and the session consumes that commit. Every candidate finishes preparation before arrival and performs zero foreground installs. There are no unused builds in this used-base fixture; that does not estimate a production waste rate. Recently used eligibility, no recency renewal, serial newest-base selection and supersession cancellation bound unused work independently.

Consumed cold-template/build/clone intervals have candidate medians **2.162 s main / 11.798 s process CPU**, versus **1.904 / 10.445 s** before. Main-isolate profiles place the same template/filesystem work and associated GC earlier; no extra installer appears. Added eligibility, scheduling and **all extra ready-template lookups** are conservatively charged to overhead: median **0.130 s main / 1.426 s process**, maxima **0.238 / 2.112 s**. One candidate has a second ready-only idle pass; it is included, not discarded. Residual paired median delta is **+0.029 s main / −0.209 s process**, within residual A/A bands **1.075 / 6.299 s**. Consumed owner work dominates background cost; bounded orchestration remains small. Interval observations are not exact causal CPU samples, and the whole process delta is not relabeled as moved work. Profiles corroborate main-isolate execution; resource counters include workers, and VM counters additionally include Git/broker/installer children.

The complete campaign meets the predeclared revised rule. All 125 artifacts (129.7 MB) were copied and SHA-256 verified; native cleanup unmounted btrfs, detached the loop and removed scratch without errors.

Reproduce each arm with the committed `scripts/perf/sandbox-template-prewarm-measure.ts`, using the synthetic fixture/state/image and a fresh output directory; add `--baseline-dir` containing the five original owner files for baseline arms. The measured revision is `a81d266e`, with original parent `7d014324`. Final changes to measured owners are loading-only imports/constant relocation and main's pre-scheduling memory gate, outside capture. Six of eight measured files are byte-identical. The later retention correction adds a secondary `created_at` sort to the existing worker query: only equal-recency generation selection changes; the measured single-advance fixture never exceeds four generations. Its red/green collector regression and released-schema compatibility proof cover that delta. Final main also contains independently owned database/lazy-import changes; compatibility is covered by final owner tests and separately gated by exact-head CI. These are scoped owner-path measurements, not an exact-final-head native run.

Earlier adverse evidence remains recorded: the tiny-graph campaign regressed 33.547 → 75.288 s and exposed missing projection-manifest preparation, now fixed. The first full-graph campaign improved 66.311 → 10.614 s and 39.362 → 13.015 s but stopped on +36% main / +29.3% process CPU. Both old arms built one consumed template; old profiles expose GC and synchronous fixture verification but cannot retrospectively partition worker/process CPU. The qualified rerun excludes fixture assertions from capture, waits for actual one-time handler settlement, and records disjoint intervals plus aligned profiles. No exact numerical attribution of the old process delta is asserted.

prs.body:
Re-export the host's session chat-type classifier from the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/routing` subpath so plugin tool factories can gate on `ctx.sessionKey` without re-implementing the session-key rule by hand.

**What changed**
- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.ts`: add `deriveSessionChatTypeFromKey` (value) and `type SessionKeyChatType` re-exports from `../sessions/session-chat-type-shared.js`, alongside the existing `parseAgentSessionKey` export from the same subpath.
- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.test.ts`: new unit-fast test locking the host classification through the SDK subpath (direct/dm/group/channel, legacy `group:`/`channel:`/`@g.us` shapes, unknown, and plugin-supplied legacy fallback).

**Why**
A plugin tool factory receives `ctx.sessionKey` but no chat type. A tool that should only be offered in a direct chat (e.g. one that shows the owner something a group or channel shouldn't see, since group/channel replies are read by everyone) currently has to copy the host's canonical parsing (`agent:<id>:` prefix strip, `direct`/`dm` vs `group`/`channel` tokens). That copy drifts from the host's peer-shape parsing with legacy and plugin-supplied fallbacks. With this export, plugins call the host's function and drop their copy.

**Verification**
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` — passes.
- `src/plugin-sdk/routing.test.ts` via vitest unit-fast config (Bun runtime) — 14/14 pass.
- `run-oxlint` on the two files — clean.
- `run-format --check` — formatted.
- `plugin-sdk:check-exports` — synced.

Closes #194467

prs.title: fix(cli): cancel interrupted hooks status reports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw hooks list`, `info` and `check` keep waiting for `hooks.status` after interruption, then print a misleading RPC timeout error.

## User Impact

User impact: Interrupted hook reports promptly close their read connection and exit quietly with the normal SIGINT/SIGTERM code.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing command signal through the shared report reader, skip offline discovery when that read was aborted, and suppress canceled output in both report actions. The default/list/check path and info are covered together; enable/disable keep their config mutation owner.

## Evidence

Product HEAD: `3477ef2c5a7fd1fb1df3598c218733a17a0fbec0`; acceptance-red BASE: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`.

- **Actual CLI → real Gateway:** clean normal QA builds run `node openclaw.mjs hooks list --json`, `hooks info proof-hook` and `hooks check --json` in a controlling PTY. A transparent proxy forwards the real handshake/request and holds the successful real `hooks.status` reply before delivering terminal Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. It records the exact held connection and actual terminal/stderr readback.
- **Same frozen red/green scenarios:** All three BASE interruptions eventually exit130/143 after **1793–1901ms**, with a spurious timeout banner. This is a quietness/timeliness failure, not a harness kill. HEAD naturally exits **130/143 in 78–92ms**, closes the held read connection within **5–9ms**, and leaves no owned CLI/Gateway/proxy process. No timeout banner or late report after the normal interruption notice. No collector watchdog fires.
- **Legal controls:** Five controls on both revisions: list JSON, named info and check JSON exit0 and include the actual configured workspace hook; a missing hook and wrong-token authentication still exit1. Configuration bytes stay unchanged and the real Gateway/proxy clean up normally.
- **Focused regression:** BASE has two intended public-output failures and12passing controls; HEAD has **36 passing tests across two files in 33.977s**: `pnpm test src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts src/cli/hooks-cli.toggle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. These include existing ownership-refusal, enable/disable, legacy fallback and ordinary-error controls. Targeted types, typed lint and formatting pass. Clean exact-HEAD QA build: 271.756s. Independent adversarial review: PASS, no findings. Two cold worker generations took125–126s and exceeded an unchanged toggle test’s120s budget. After retaining the final generated compiler outputs, the unchanged36-test command passed without timeout or assertion changes.

Reproduce with the [unchanged collector](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/47409c0bd2011c9b51aba8b0183d0d3ee51abb3d/cli-read-proof-v2.py): `python3 cli-read-proof-v2.py CHECKOUT FRESH_OUTPUT NODE26 EXPECTATION hooks`. prs.title: fix(doctor): Ctrl+C during the Gateway health check hangs and reports a false health failure
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198086

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor` does not stop when Ctrl+C is pressed during its Gateway health check.

When the Gateway is starting, unreachable or slow to answer, the default launcher force-kills the CLI about 2 s after Ctrl+C instead of letting it exit with 130; without the launcher wrapper Doctor waits out the read (30 s here) and then reports the cancelled check as `Gateway health check failed` with a repair step.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl+C during Doctor's Gateway health check ends Doctor at once with exit code 130 and no health finding for the check the user cancelled. Runs that are not interrupted behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw health` and `openclaw channels list` already pass the command's cancellation signal to their Gateway reads (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196655, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197815); Doctor's health check was left out. This change passes the same signal to the Doctor health check's readiness wait, its `status`, `channels.status` and `diagnostics.stability` reads, the re-probe it runs when the `status` read fails for missing credentials, and the `doctor.memory.status` probe, and lets the cancellation end the check where an error used to become a finding (after the parallel channel/stability reads and in the check's catch). Doctor's contribution loop already stops on that cancellation.

## Evidence

Head `fc5c5bd86994ca5d2c0bd52707d287bbb5f2276b` (based on `main` `95a6cfe79b2ec1ef65d17c310499b13c2f6a0b7c`). The real runs below ran at `063a591cbc27060016b9a2a6304998cddcd42904`, Linux, Node 24.22.1; the head adds only a test change on top of it, so the production code is the same.

The built CLI ran `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` with an isolated state directory, config and home, and a local Gateway config pointing at a stand-in on `127.0.0.1` that accepts TCP and never answers. A small driver sent SIGINT 3 s after `Doctor: Gateway health` appeared and recorded the time from SIGINT to exit. Each side ran once with the default launcher and once with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`.

Before (excerpt; `main` `9cfa4b5ff744da4e7133c53dfea287abdba1c223`; the commits between it and the base above do not touch the changed or calling Doctor files):

```text
# default launcher
  16.14 >>> SIGINT sent
  16.14 Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
  18.19 >>> exit code -9
>>> SIGINT to exit: 2.05 s

# OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1
  16.13 >>> SIGINT sent
  16.13 Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
  23.14 Doctor: Gateway health (10s elapsed)
  33.17 Doctor: Gateway health (20s elapsed)
  43.19 Doctor: Gateway health (30s elapsed)
  46.35 Fix now:
  46.35 - Gateway health check failed: Health check failed: AbortError: CLI stopping (SIGINT)
  46.44 >>> exit code 130
>>> SIGINT to exit: 30.30 s
```

After (excerpt; this PR at `063a591cbc27`):

```text
# default launcher
  17.02 >>> SIGINT sent
  17.02 Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
  17.05 Doctor: maintenance release
  17.08 CLI stopping (SIGINT)
  17.21 >>> exit code 130
>>> SIGINT to exit: 0.19 s

# OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1
>>> SIGINT to exit: 0.19 s   (exit code 130, no "Gateway health check failed")
```

Observed result: before, the launcher force-kills Doctor (signal 9) or Doctor waits 30 s and prints a false health failure; after, Doctor exits with 130 within 0.2 s and prints no finding. A run without SIGINT, also at `063a591cbc27`, printed the same output before and after apart from timings, process ids and the Control UI assets line (the assets were built in the test checkout between the runs), with the same readiness failure after the 60 s wait.

Regression test: `cancels the pending %s read on Ctrl+C without reporting a finding`, one case per read (readiness, `status`, `channels.status`, `diagnostics.stability`, `doctor.memory.status`, and `probe`, the credentials re-probe). All six fail on the base and pass with the fix. Reverting any one of the eight signal or re-raise lines alone turns at least one case red. The `doctor.memory.status` case pins only that the cancellation reaches that read: `probeGatewayMemoryStatus` turns any error into an "unavailable" result, and Doctor's contribution loop is what ends Doctor on the cancellation.

Sibling test: the cancellation case in `src/commands/doctor-gateway-installation-replacement.test.ts` (from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174060) closed the work scope and expected the live check to stay healthy. A closed scope now ends the check, so its normal case expects the closure reason after the unavailable-history note (it fails on the base); the lint case is unchanged; and a new `unavailable` case keeps an unreadable history, without cancellation, from changing a healthy result.

Checks at the head above: `pnpm test src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts src/commands/doctor-gateway-installation-replacement.test.ts` (43 passed), the other test files that import or mock the changed module (7 files, all passed), `pnpm check:changed --base 95a6cfe79b2` (all 35 steps ok, including format, typecheck of core and core tests, lint of the changed files and the dead export scan), and the test-lines ratchet (net +52 test lines, within the allowance: the six-case regression and the sibling test update); the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file                                                      | `--maxWorkers=1` wall, warm cache | CI seconds (`063a591cbc27`)                                                |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts`                   | 7.5 s                             | 5.8 s                                                                      |
| `src/commands/doctor-gateway-installation-replacement.test.ts` | 18.8 s                            | 98.8 s (80% transform; the case that failed there is the one updated here) |

Not covered:

- The real Gateway was not run. The stand-in holds only the readiness wait (it never completes a handshake), so the `status`, `channels.status`, `diagnostics.stability`, `doctor.memory.status` and credentials re-probe holds are covered by the unit test only.
- After a failed `status` read the check inspects the installed Gateway service's state paths (`noteInstalledGatewayStateDirectory`) without the cancellation signal: that step is bounded to 3 s and only writes notes.
- Sibling Doctor Gateway reads with the same gap are left as they are: the Gateway probe in the Doctor lint path (`collectGatewayHealthFindings`, used by `doctor-core-checks`), and the best-effort `secrets.reload` / `models.authStatus` refresh after auth-profile repair (3 s each, errors ignored, no finding).
- `Doctor: maintenance release` still runs after Ctrl+C, as before.

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `95a6cfe79b2ec1ef65d17c310499b13c2f6a0b7c` to head `fc5c5bd86994ca5d2c0bd52707d287bbb5f2276b`, priority P0–P1: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

prs.title: fix(channels): make answered-history lookup candidate-aware and bounded
prs.body:
Closes #197995

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously requested `candidate count * 2` projected canonical text rows. Candidate messages, physical platform rows, and projected canonical text rows are different units. An internal user-role runtime input plus assistant `NO_REPLY` can consume that evidence budget without adding a channel-history candidate. A selected, unchanged, previously answered request then resurfaces in later model context because its completion evidence fell outside the lookup.

The conservative behavior on genuinely unavailable evidence is intentional and remains. This is not a missing-final-answer report or a requirement to suppress unproven input. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured.

## What the branch changes

- The recent-history omission owner passes the selected transport message IDs to its existing private canonical turn reader instead of prescribing a two-row ratio.
- The shared SQLite/memory transcript projector follows those IDs until each has been encountered, the active transcript ends, or an existing safety ceiling is reached: 10,000 physical canonical message rows and 64 MiB of captured serialized transcript data.
- Both ceilings are reused from the existing transcript reader constants. The byte count bounds captured payload data, not process heap usage; parsed objects and page metadata add overhead.
- A byte-limited page can contain older sparse rows. Only its newest contiguous suffix is used, and lookup stops at the first omitted physical row. It never bridges a potentially missing user barrier.
- All intervening user rows remain barriers, including image-only/textless users represented as `text: ""` only in the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text reader retains its old nonempty-text behavior.
- The private facade captures options and clones candidate IDs before awaiting acquisition. Caller mutation cannot silently change the evidence request after it starts.

The final omission decision still requires exact transport-ID/body equality and completed-answer evidence. Attachment-bearing, changed, unseen, unfinished, and unproven requests remain eligible. Existing active-session/agent scoping and snapshot/worker ownership are retained. There is no new schema, index, configuration, background archive, public SDK option, or arbitrary larger multiplier.

### Performance and bounded fallback

An unseen or too-old selected ID can require searching the whole permitted tail, unlike the old short heuristic. The explicit row and cumulative byte ceilings cap that additional work, and lookup stops early once all selected IDs are found. A missing ID, oversized barrier, unavailable transcript, or exhausted bound can therefore still leave an answered request quoted conservatively. This is an accepted bounded-evidence limitation, not an assertion that every historical answered request will disappear.

The direct projector's 10,000-row synthetic scans ran in 2-3 ms in the supplemental test run. These pages contain already decoded small fixture rows; this is not a SQLite/JSON-decoding benchmark, a production latency guarantee, or a memory measurement.

## Reproduce the original failure independently

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197995-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783640/openclaw-197995-evidence.zip)

Use Node 26.12.1+; the portable helper was executed with Node v26.13.0:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs > observed.json
```

No repository checkout, npm install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway is required. The helper resolves its bundled source relative to itself, not the current directory. Copying the package outside the checkout and running it from `/` produced the identical output.

`SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled baseline owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package version `2026.11.3`) with exact source hashes and its MIT license. `reproduction-output.json` is the fresh baseline result. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior at the fix branch's newer upstream base.

The helper's optional checkout argument is for reproducing this baseline contract:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It prints the actual checkout commit/hash and does not label differing source as the pinned baseline. Its assertions intentionally encode the old behavior, including the bug. It is not a green-on-fix acceptance script; use the branch's real owner tests below for the new reader contract.

The executed fixture has exactly six unchanged ID-bearing channel candidates, each with a directly following completed answer. There is no steering fixture:

1. Six ordinary U/A pairs: 12 projected rows, requested limit 12, retained `[]`.
2. Add one internal U/NO_REPLY pair after the oldest answered pair: 14 projected rows, same candidates and requested limit, retained `[target]`.
3. Give the unchanged algorithm all 14 rows: retained `[]` again. This reader override isolates coverage; it is not a repair.
4. Separate controls retain all candidates without evidence and preserve independently edited text, attachments, and incomplete answers.

These are synthetic production-function probes with an injected chronological reader. They do not exercise the real projector, persistence, channel/Gateway, prompt renderer, or model. Passing them must not be called a live end-to-end result.

## Implementation verification

`persisted-baseline-red.txt` records the actual pre-fix SQLite/reconciliation failure on the current upstream base: three tests passed; adding the internal U/NO_REPLY pair retained `target` and failed the expected-empty assertion. This was a real owner assertion failure, not the earlier cold-compiler infrastructure failure.

The final implementation passed:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/coverage-final-cache \
  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- SQLite owner: 4/4. Real persistence and `runPreparedChannelTurn` rendering cover the six-candidate control/failure, edited text, attachments, unseen discussion, incomplete output, unrelated internal text users, image-only user barriers, and unchanged public text projection.
- Private projector: 5/5. Covers paging past 250 rows, the exact 10,000-message edge, candidates beyond it, and zero/one-row newest-contiguous suffixes after oversized omissions.
- Provider prefix stability: 14/14.
- A supplemental cumulative-byte-budget regression was added after that integration run; the updated projector suite passed 6/6 in 3.36 seconds (7.69 seconds including the wrapper). Production source is unchanged. The new case uses two contiguous pages reporting 32 MiB each, verifies requests of 64 MiB then 32 MiB, and prohibits a third read. Its config-cli test-leaf typecheck, dedicated-core lint, formatting, and diff check also passed. This is a private byte-budget contract, not a SQLite memory benchmark.
- Final command: 23 tests passed across three shards, 413.35 seconds including a 160.54-second cold worker compilation. SQLite test bodies totaled about 7.6 seconds; projector bodies about 37 ms. CI seconds are not available because no PR CI was run by this work.
- An earlier candidate passed the unchanged non-recent channel suite, 9/9; that unaffected-path evidence is reused, not presented as an exact-final-head rerun.
- Core production typecheck, plugin-sdk/config-cli test-leaf typechecks, dedicated-core targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `FIX-VERIFICATION.json` records exact tested source hashes and verification scope.

Independent review found and corrected the textless-user barrier and pre-await request-capture defects. Re-review found no further material findings in the reviewed scope. This is not a claim of an automated scoped-clean review.

## Owner and upstream implementation pointers

Pinned baseline source prefix: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/>

- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`: selected candidate identities and conservative final omission.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, `readRecentUserAssistantTurnsForSession`: private active-session/agent facade; public text projection stays separate.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts`, `readRecentTranscriptConversationText`: shared SQLite/memory projection and candidate stopping/coverage.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-visible-cursor.ts`: existing 10,000-message/64 MiB ceilings.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-active-events-read.ts` and `session-actor-memory-history-facts.ts`: byte-bounded page and contiguous-suffix contracts.
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.recent-history.ts`: physical platform-row budget, distinct from filtered candidates and canonical rows.
- `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md`: bounded completion confirmation and conservative retention contract.

## Evidence and submission files

`LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the successful November 13 candidate-only run. A real isolated Gateway, native Codex runtime and configured provider produced one older answered request followed by seven non-platform user-source RPC turns with seven `NO_REPLY` responses. These are real persisted turns, not fabricated transcript rows, but they are not internal-system events or scheduled automation. Historical production evidence separately covers the original internal-event example.

With six selected history candidates, core dispatch removed the older answered request and retained all five unrelated unanswered candidates. The newly submitted native input contains each retained candidate once and does not quote the older request again. Independent review matched all nine submitted bodies to native and provider requests, verified the 16-row pre-lookup canonical transcript, and separated eight auxiliary recap calls. Retained native conversation history is intentionally not erased.

The canonical `build:runtime` command passed; exact source/build/runtime/Codex provenance is in `live/build-provenance.json`. The fixture uses a restricted native-tool profile and a synthetic authenticated local channel, not Discord transport. Both disposable homes were removed. This is not a fresh live baseline/fix A/B comparison or a full package/declaration/PR-CI run.

The ZIP includes the headerless `fix.patch`, verified `BRANCH.json`, regression receipts, original baseline helper/source/license, sanitized historical observation, live observations, and exact executed harness source. `SHA256SUMS.json` covers the payload. The separate Markdown is byte-identical to this file inside the ZIP. The branch is based directly on the stated upstream commit, not on another fix branch.

## Exact limits

- A separate shared-renderer API migration renames `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` to `buildInboundUserContext` returning `{ text, hasHistory }`. If that migration lands first, migrate this branch's added SQLite rendering-test call to the new API and select `.text` where the old string result was consumed. A mechanically clean merge does not establish type compatibility; rerun the focused tests and typecheck after rebasing.
- This is a standalone branch, not a pre-integrated series. A mechanical combination with the separately prepared completed-run attribution change conflicts in the shared projector, SQLite tests and Discord documentation. If that change lands first, rebase and reconcile those owners before landing this branch; combined behavior has not been tested here.
- Recorded historical observations and the fresh synthetic-channel proof are separate. Neither implies this branch was installed on the production Gateway.
- No regression-from-known-good release, population-wide incidence, or end-to-end performance rate has been established. The historical observation and deterministic fixtures do not prove such claims.

prs.title: fix(channels): use completed-run identity to reconcile steered request history
prs.body:
Closes #197994

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously credited a completed assistant answer only to the nearest preceding user row. With full transcript coverage of `original user -> accepted steering user -> completed final`, the steering row received credit but the original could be re-quoted in a later model input, even when the completed run had answered both requests.

This can duplicate an already-answered request in context. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured. The demonstrated case is an attribution problem, not a missing delivered final or insufficient lookup coverage.

## Implemented behavior and owners

The fix reuses producer-owned canonical metadata and the existing reconciliation owner:

- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts` adds `runId` and user `steerTargetRunId` only to the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text projection does not gain those fields.
- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`, walks the returned chronological rows backward. A completed assistant records its known run ID. A user is attributed to `steerTargetRunId` when present, otherwise its own `runId`, and can be covered by a later completed answer of that run.
- Known conflicting run identities do not qualify through the nearest-user fallback. When either side lacks usable run identity, the legacy immediately preceding-user behavior remains; the code tracks unidentified completed replies separately from known completed runs.
- Every projected user resets the adjacency-only completion state. Private evidence now retains textless/image-only users as `text: ""` barriers, so an unrelated final is not paired across an invisible user row. Public recent text still excludes empty user text.
- Final omission still requires the same transport ID and unchanged trimmed body. Attachments, edits, unseen discussion, incomplete replies, earlier unrelated runs, and missing completion evidence remain eligible in the tested cases. Session/agent scope and the existing completion classifier are unchanged.

This does not remove the conservative reset, mark all consecutive users answered, create a second completion owner, add schemas/configuration, or change steering admission. The branch also documents the run-aware behavior in `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md`.

### What completion and acceptance mean here

This is host-side completed-run bookkeeping, not semantic answer grading. Accepted steering metadata alone is insufficient: the reader must also observe a completed assistant answer with the relevant run identity. Conversely, a host completion flag is not a generic guarantee that an answer's content satisfies every request. No semantic-answer detector was added.

The historical collector separately inspected the combined final's content. The regression fixtures supply canonical metadata and a final classification to exercise reconciliation; they do not themselves prove real steering admission or semantic coverage.

## Evidence: historical observation versus new verification

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197994-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783568/openclaw-197994-evidence.zip)

`historical/observation.json` is a sanitized read-only reinspection of retained production canonical records and the native rollout. Its event date is November 11, 2026, and collection date is November 13. It reports:

- Original input and accepted steering belong to the same completed run.
- The final stopped normally and carries terminal-run metadata.
- The collector inspected two corresponding final-answer sections; the full final body is omitted from the public excerpt.
- The original request was subsequently quoted in a native recent-history input.

Run membership was copied separately from canonical metadata; the baseline projector did not expose these identity fields. The collector used the real retained events as an injected read-only page, not a fresh storage/channel/Gateway experiment. Its installed/source commit labels are provenance fields, not a new attestation that this fix ran on the historical date.

**Fresh fixed-branch proof passed at the exact commit above**, completing at `2026-11-13T03:55:07.004Z`. A synthetic authenticated local channel exercised the real Gateway/core dispatch, canonical storage, native Codex and configured provider. A declared read-only tool held a checkpoint while a second actual inbound request was admitted through native steering; the gate was released only after a correlated steering acceptance. Original `runId`, steering `steerTargetRunId` and completed-final `runId` agree in the persisted transcript. A subsequent request supplied both inputs plus an unrelated ambient candidate: core removed the two answered inputs and retained only the unrelated candidate.

The executed harness required exact submitted-body matches for all three primary native requests and all three newest provider-user inputs. One native conversation and one separate auxiliary recap were observed. The newly appended input does not repeat the answered requests; their earlier retained native history is not deleted. The build completed with exit zero in 354 seconds and exact build/runtime/Codex provenance verified. Fixture and runner cleanup succeeded. `LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the raw synthetic records, exact executed harness and verification scope. This is a candidate-only synthetic-transport live test, not Discord transport, a fresh live base/fix A/B, or a production deployment.

## Red-on-baseline and green-on-fix validation

The integrator ran the current 15-test persisted SQLite suite against the two original production owner files from the base, then restored the fixed source. `attribution-persisted-red.log` records **5 failed, 10 passed**:

- Completed original plus accepted steering remained eligible incorrectly.
- Two explicit run-mismatch/steering-target-precedence cases incorrectly omitted a pending input.
- Empty-user and image-only-user barriers incorrectly allowed omission of an earlier unanswered input.

These are owner assertion failures, not the earlier compiler setup failure. `attribution-source-restored.json` records the restored production hashes; both match the committed source reviewed here.

`attribution-final-green.log` records **38 passed** across three files on the final source:

- SQLite reconciliation: **15/15**. Covers successful shared-run completion; error, abort, truncation, commentary, and unsettled native output; explicit mismatch; steering-target precedence; missing-identity fallback; edited text; attachments; textless/image-only barriers; and unchanged public text projection.
- Provider prefix stability: **14/14**.
- Channel context runtime: **9/9**.

The final wrapper took 274.83 seconds, including 124.87 seconds of cold worker compilation. The SQLite file took 155.47 seconds including preparation/transform; its test bodies totaled about 6.6 seconds. CI timings are unavailable because this handoff did not run PR CI.

The prepared commit has the same four source/doc hashes as the reviewed tested candidate; the commit's formatting hook did not change them. `candidate-review.json` records those hashes and review scope. Core production and plugin-sdk test-leaf typechecks, dedicated-core lint, four-file formatting and diff checks passed; the bounded static receipts are included under `attribution-static/`.

### Re-run the fix tests

From the prepared branch with repository dependencies installed according to `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/steering-attribution-cache \
  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For the persisted baseline comparison, use a separate checkout at the base commit and apply only the regression-test file from the prepared commit, leaving production files at the base. Then run the SQLite test file alone. Do not overwrite a running checkout's source or reuse another run's active dependency installation.

## Portable reproduction of the original mechanism

The unchanged bundled baseline helper requires Node 26.12.1+ and no checkout, install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs > observed.json
# Optional baseline checkout comparison:
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It resolves `source/` relative to itself and was verified after copying the package outside the checkout and running from `/`. `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package `2026.11.3`) with its exact hash and MIT license. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior on the newer base.

The seven executed baseline cases include full coverage (limit four, all three rows returned, original retained), an ordinary single-input completion, a larger candidate budget that does not repair attribution, incomplete output, an unrelated earlier unanswered request, and independent edit/attachment controls.

These are exact production-function probes with a synthetic bounded reader. They do not exercise persistence, admission, the real projector, prompt rendering, or a provider. The helper's assertions deliberately describe the old bug. It is not a green-on-fix acceptance script: its synthetic rows do not carry the newly required run identities. Use the persisted branch tests for the implemented contract.

## Limits and submission state

- The existing `candidate count * 2` read budget remains in this branch. Run attribution only uses returned evidence; older or unavailable evidence can still cause conservative re-quotation. This handoff does not claim unconditional all-history suppression or alter lookup policy.
- The persisted regressions verify storage, projection and `InboundHistory` reconciliation; the separate fresh live records establish real native steering acceptance and next-input behavior. Neither is semantic answer grading.
- The independent branch has no dependency on another fix branch. `BRANCH.json` pins the published head and verified remote ref; `fix.patch` is the exact base-to-head diff. `UPSTREAM-MERGE-CHECK.json` records a clean mechanical merge check against a newer upstream head, not tests on that merged result.
- This is a standalone branch, not a pre-integrated series. A mechanical combination with the separately prepared candidate-coverage change conflicts in the shared projector, SQLite tests and Discord documentation. If that change lands first, rebase and reconcile those owners before landing this branch; combined behavior has not been tested here.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passed with the supported 4352 MiB heap budget. This is the runtime build, not a full package declaration build or all-repository test run.
- No known-good multi-input release, population-wide rate, production latency, or token-cost improvement was established. Do not label this a bisected regression.
- No PR publication, issue comment, release or running-service deployment was performed. The branch and this evidence are for a separate upstream submission.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): explicitly separate recent history from the current request
prs.body:
Closes #197996

## What problem this solves

An ordinary Discord `user_request` through the Codex app-server harness can place attributed recent history immediately before an unlabeled current request, separated only by a blank line:

```text
Recent chat history: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#100 2026-11-11 19:15:41 GMT+0 Alice: Earlier question.

This is the current request.
Its second paragraph stays current.
```

All values above are synthetic. The issue also describes a retained native user-role input with this layout; that earlier observation's exact installed build was not independently re-attested. The bundled replay freshly reproduces the formatting at its separately pinned baseline source revision, without invoking a Gateway or model.

The demonstrated impact is prompt clarity and auditability: where historical reference data ends and the active request begins must be inferred from whitespace and attributed-line syntax. No incorrect answer, exploitation, message loss, or model confusion rate is claimed. Historical bodies are flattened into attributed single lines, limiting ambiguity without supplying an explicit current-request label. Legitimately unseen discussion suffices; a selection defect is not required.

The requested outcome is an explicit, coherent model-facing boundary after historical context, without promoting quoted data into instruction authority. The exact legacy literal is not a universal requirement for every prompt; an existing explicit inline current-message header is also valid framing.

## Candidate mechanism and scope

The candidate extends the existing shared reply-envelope boundary rather than adding a Discord-specific or Codex-only text parser:

1. `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts` now builds `{ text, hasHistory }` through `buildInboundUserContext`. The producer sets the history fact only where attributed history/chat-window lines actually emit, after limits, suppression and empty-line filtering. Raw `InboundHistory.length` is not used as a substitute for rendered history.
2. `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts` consumes that fact at its existing thread-boundary owner. History-bearing ordinary requests acquire one `[Current message - respond to this]` **runtime-instruction fragment** after assembled source context. A simultaneous thread note uses the same marker, not a second marker.
3. Existing internal callers and test fixtures migrate to the richer result. There is no compatibility wrapper, new configuration, public SDK seam, state store, header inference, or second history renderer.
4. Raw current text, queued text and saved user transcript text remain separate from runtime context. Codex's existing prepend and mention-sigil neutralization functions are unchanged and serve both initial native input and steering.

Verified ordinary-request model-facing shape:

```text
Recent chat history: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#100 2026-11-11 19:15:41 GMT+0 Alice: Earlier question.

[Current message - respond to this]

This is the current request.
Its second paragraph stays current.
```

### Preserved exceptions and constraints

- Empty, disabled or nonrenderable history does not create an orphan marker. Reply-target metadata alone does not change behavior.
- An existing Telegram inline current-message header keeps its header/body adjacency and does not acquire a competing history-only marker.
- Contexts using optional room participation, including ambient `room_event` and optional bot-authored message-tool-only requests, get no response-directing current-message marker, whether their context contains history or a thread note. The same existing participation predicate owns both the delivery directive and this exclusion.
- Bare resets keep their existing startup/metadata assembly; history alone does not create normal per-turn context on that path.
- Existing thread-note boundaries and queued-goal ordering remain in place.
- Historical sender attribution, quoted-data status, current user bytes and historical/current mention-selection behavior must remain intact. The marker is formatting, not authentication or permission.
- No history selection, retention, channel permission, model policy, or stable system/tool prefix change is intended.

## Source ownership

These baseline links explain the defect and surrounding contracts. Candidate source must be reviewed at the final verified branch head, not assumed identical to these earlier revisions.

- [Structured inbound rendering](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts#L595-L631): history heading and attributed lines, without the current-message literal.
- [Shared envelope/thread boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts#L638-L647): existing runtime-only marker policy, extended by this candidate.
- [Codex prepend](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-state.ts#L120-L130), consumed by [initial input](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-prompt.ts#L360-L370) and [steering](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-active-turn.ts#L355-L366): neutralizes historical explicit mention sigils, then joins context and current prompt.
- [Separate plaintext wrapper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/history.ts#L23-L37): already contains `CURRENT_MESSAGE_MARKER`; it is not the structured renderer.
- [Context-engine projection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/extensions/codex/src/app-server/context-engine-projection.ts#L229-L240): already closes its own `conversation_context` and labels `Current user request:`.
- [Inbound provenance marker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context-marker.ts#L1-L21): `⟦openclaw:ctx⟧` supports provenance/stripping, not a paired section or authority boundary.

## Historical intent, briefly

This is not described as a restoration PR having simply "forgotten the marker."

- The [February sender-spoofing split](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/53273b490b3a7fe30c9348d751194ca37502068a) deliberately separated clean Discord current text from structured history. [May's prompt-local refactor](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80275) and [Codex restoration](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c529ab29c2228fa37ddf1a8e76b0559805e16d59) preserved that separation; the Codex prepend neither removed nor created the literal.
- [July #100366](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100366) deliberately replaced fenced JSON history with attributed prose. Its QA parser explicitly ended history at the next blank line; a negative control put a current-request sentinel after that boundary and required it not to count as historical evidence. The [maintainer praised that control](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100366#issuecomment-4888653814). Implicit paragraph framing was consciously tested, but deterministic parser checks do not establish model interpretation.
- [September #153075](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153075) reused structured prose for native restart-history recovery while retaining the current-message marker in the separate plaintext wrapper. The marker was not generally rejected.
- [October #169817](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169817) explicitly addressed thread requests being mistaken for starter/history context, adding the existing runtime marker after nonempty thread notes and excluding ambient events. Its metadata-only no-thread absence test did not establish a deliberate exception for history-bearing ordinary requests.
- [Ambient deduplication #119860](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/119860) concerned `[OpenClaw room event]`/`Current event:` duplication, not removal of the ordinary current-message literal.

The evidence supports inherited divergence between framing routes and an intentional blank-paragraph convention, not an explicit prohibition on labels for ordinary structured history. The candidate improves that convention using an existing owner and preserves its real exceptions.

## Portable baseline replay

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197996-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783694/openclaw-197996-evidence.zip)

Requirements: Node 26 with built-in `node:module.stripTypeScriptTypes`; the recorded replay used Node v26.13.0. No packages, network, provider or model are required.

```sh
node reproduce.mjs
# Or verify the same baseline functions in a checkout:
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw
```

The default resolves `source/` relative to the script, independent of working directory. `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` records the two complete source files, SHA-256 hashes and upstream paths at **baseline `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b`**, not the newer fix-branch base or candidate head. Both invocation modes verify those file hashes before executing only the extracted join and mention-sigil functions. Different bytes fail the pin check. Node's experimental stripping warning can appear on stderr; evidence JSON is stdout.

`reproduction-output.json` is synthetic production-function replay: exactly two newlines between supplied history and current text, no marker created by the join helper, no-context/whitespace controls unchanged, historical skill sigils neutralized, current skill sigils preserved, and an already labeled projection retained. It does not execute Discord admission, history rendering, shared envelope preparation, native submission or inference.

**This baseline helper replay is not an A/B test of the fix.** The candidate changes the shared producer/envelope, not these two Codex functions; passing this script cannot show the repaired production composition.

## Regression evidence

The new table in `src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts` composes the real `prepareReplyRunContext` with runtime prompt assembly and checks the boundary plus unchanged current/queued/transcript bytes.

Verified baseline-red run on original production bytes at branch base `ee465500a4575d90bf62446765233b9c01c8703d`:

- Four history-bearing cases failed specifically because the runtime marker was absent: recent history, pending history, media-only history and selected chat-window history.
- Four controls passed: disabled history, blank entries, reply-only metadata and no history.
- No setup failure was counted as a defect result. Fixed source bytes were restored and verified afterward.
- Wall time: 335.398 seconds; Vitest duration: 310.83 seconds, dominated by cold transformation (91%), not test-body runtime. CI seconds are not yet available.

Before the final optional-participation correction, the fixed-source owner run passed all **5 files / 243 tests** across the canonical wrapper's three shards (70 fast tests, 119 media-only/queue tests, 54 inbound-metadata/envelope tests). Total wrapper wall time was 648.63 seconds, including the cold source generation and existing large suites. That run covered history plus thread note emitting one marker, empty chat windows, existing inline headers, reset-with-history behavior, ambient controls and queued-goal ordering. A subsequent migrated-consumer/prefix run passed **8 files / 119 tests** in 745.32 seconds. The later review found that optional bot requests use the same room-participation policy; the final candidate now excludes the marker there too, including for thread notes. The final full `prompt-prelude.test.ts` rerun passed **26/26 tests**, including optional-bot history/thread controls and an ordinary human message-tool-only positive control. Wrapper wall time was 129.33 seconds; Vitest duration was 124.31 seconds (94% transformation). The three new policy cases took 9, 7 and 8 ms respectively. The earlier results are not presented as execution of that final correction; the 26-case rerun is its direct runtime proof. An earlier deliberately interrupted attempt is not counted as passing evidence.

Static gates completed on the source bound to the local fix commit (with the later test-only extraction checked separately below):

- Production core typecheck passed (`pnpm tsgo:core`, 46.55 seconds).
- The canonical core test-boundary guard passed. prs.title: fix(ios): avoid UI pauses while loading large session lists
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses UI pauses while a large iOS session roster loads: source inspection confirms that typed page decoding currently runs on MainActor. The user-visible latency impact has not yet been measured.

## User Impact

Moves roster-page and same-sidebar-model dashboard decoding to an explicit concurrent executor, without changing the existing sidebar animation, grouped replies, word fade, pagination, offline fallback, or partial-roster presentation. Broad chat-history decoding is outside this PR. This draft still needs an exact-head Mac build and device performance verification; no measured speedup is claimed. No migration or user configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A network await did not move the subsequent synchronous JSON decode out of the MainActor-isolated roster loader. The existing payload-decoding owner now offers an explicit Swift `@concurrent` Data decoder with Sendable results and cancellation checks, also used by the same sidebar model’s usage/cron request helper. State application stays on MainActor. Both successful and failed page decodes revalidate their captured physical connection before the pagination owner consumes them.

This relocates necessary decoding; it does not remove total decoding work or add a cache, detached task, persistent worker, or new refresh policy.

## Evidence

- Local `git diff --check` and reverse patch-application check: passed.
- Simplification/source review completed; production delta is +23/-3 lines, tests +206 lines.
- Independent autoreview: P0–P2, `scoped-clean`, no findings, complete local candidate against `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`. This is source review, not native runtime proof.
- Added a decoder executor/responsiveness check and cancelled-caller check, plus real roster-owner tests using the existing WebSocket fixture for paged payloads, malformed first/later pages, and agent/gateway/connection/cancellation interruptions. The executor test covers the decoder; it does not by itself prove the real roster uses no main-thread decoding.
- **Pending:** exact-head Swift 6.3/Xcode 27.1+ compilation and validation of `@concurrent` executor behavior and route/cancellation semantics, SwiftFormat/SwiftLint, all new and affected native tests, base-red/head-green executor evidence, exact-head device profiling, before/after video, test wall time, and CI seconds. This Linux environment has none of Swift, Xcode, SwiftFormat, or SwiftLint.

Mac focused validation (repository root, Xcode 27.1+ and its required iOS/watchOS toolchains):

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD # Record and verify the exact published PR head before testing.
xcodebuild -version
xcrun swift --version
pnpm ios:test ChatSessionsCodingTests RootSidebarRosterLoadingTests RootTabsPresentationTests RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests CronJobsListLiteTests \
  "OpenClawTests/GatewayConnectionControllerTests/chat cache remains isolated when active gateway switches"
```

Source-bound workload: `RootSidebarRosterLoadingTests` exercises `NodeAppModel.loadChatSessionRoster` through the existing WebSocket fixture with 401 rows/three pages; `RootTabsPresentationTests` retains the 1,205-row/seven-page and 50-page/10,000-row-bound contracts. The live Mac run below must exercise `NodeAppModel.loadChatSessionRoster` and `RootSidebarModel.request`, not an isolated decoder benchmark.

Performance acceptance rule, declared before measurement: use the same isolated Gateway and synthetic 1,205-session roster, page size 200, device/build configuration, sidebar open/refresh interaction, and concurrent synthetic streamed reply. Interleave baseline/candidate at least five times each; keep cold and warm results separate. Count roster RPCs (seven), typed page decodes (seven), and typed page decodes on MainActor (target zero, baseline to measure). Record median/p95 UI stalls, refresh latency, total CPU, peak memory, and host/device load. Confirm grouped replies, sidebar animation and word fade remain visually unchanged. Require a demonstrated main-thread reduction without worsened user-facing metrics; investigate any 20% regression rather than dismissing it as spread. Fill in the measurement table and attach the before/after video before readiness.

Human contributors: Vyctor Brzezowski and mikengyn.

prs.title: improve(ios): avoid duplicate storage recovery on cold activation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When iOS activation opens its local databases, it immediately repeats the storage recovery that opening them already performed.

## User Impact

Cold activation performs one recovery pass instead of two. Later activations still retry pending cleanup and legacy imports, including after permission dialogs or Control Center. The UI and recovery safeguards are unchanged.

This is a draft for exact-head Mac validation, not completion of the broader resume-performance goal. Ordinary warm activations, including Control Center returns, remain unchanged and synchronous. No responsiveness improvement has been measured yet. If initial recovery fails transiently, the next activation retries it instead of immediately repeating it in the same activation; unresolved removal markers continue to block writable access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The database initializer already resolves pending gateway removals before importing legacy state. Activation now either opens that owner or recovers an existing owner, rather than doing both. Existing-owner quarantine checks and retry ordering are retained. There is no new cache, worker, schema, permission, or persistence contract.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Auto Review of the local candidate against `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`: P0–P2, scoped-clean, no findings. Static review only.
- Added native owner-boundary coverage through `NodeAppModel.setScenePhase` and real SQLite/Keychain fixtures: registered stages cancel, forgotten gateways remain excluded, preserved sources retry on inactive → active, and imports do not resurrect forgotten state.
- Native compilation, SwiftFormat/SwiftLint, test execution, test wall/CI time, device traces, and before/after video are pending. Linux has no Swift or Xcode. The added test protects recovery semantics; it is not a measured work-count regression or a claimed red-on-base result.

**Mac acceptance rule, before measurement:** compare the pinned base and candidate with identical synthetic fixtures. Cold activation that opens the container should invoke one registry read, one pending-removal pass, and one import pass rather than two; warm activation retains one of each. These are source-derived expectations, not observed measurements. Run at least five interleaved base/candidate samples each, separate cold and warm flows, and report main-thread and total work plus median/p95 activation duration and frame hitches. No regression in recovery, foreground latency, cold launch, CPU, or memory is accepted; investigate any 20% metric regression. Keep pending until exact-head native proof is available.

Co-authored with Vyctor Brzezowski and mikengyn.
