prs.title: fix(apple): avoid rebuilding chat for voice meter updates
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary chat-surface invalidation when microphone or voice-playback levels change in iOS or native macOS Chat.

## User Impact

The change is intended to keep live voice meters updating without rebuilding the enclosing chat surface. It preserves the current UI, grouped replies, sidebar animation, word fade, and capture/session ownership. **This is a draft for Mac/Xcode validation; native compilation, visual equivalence, and performance gains are not yet verified.** No migration or user configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Apple chat hosts read live meter values while creating shared voice controls; iOS also reads them in the header avatar. Defer the control values until the existing waveform consumers render, and move header metering into an internal avatar view. The optional main-actor level providers preserve existing mutable scalar inputs and scalar callers. Recording actions, handoff guards, phase precedence, and the header's nil-playback animation fallback remain unchanged.

This deletes the eager metering dependency rather than adding a cache, throttling samples, or changing transcript rendering. The existing platform control builders take their owners explicitly so regressions exercise production construction rather than copied test adapters. macOS keeps its primary-Gateway-only control guard, pause/status behavior, input selection, and Talk action. Production delta: +137/-92 lines; test delta: +153/-2 lines; generated localization inventory: one unreachable string removed.

## Evidence

- Base: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`; no unrelated base refresh.
- Passed: `git diff --check`, whitespace check of the new test file, and `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; complete source/diff inspection. The first localization check found the removed unreachable macOS status string; `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` regenerated exactly that one inventory deletion, then verification passed. No translation memory was edited.
- Independent bound Auto Review: `local` against the base above, including the untracked test and unchanged owner/caller context; OpenClaw engine, P0–P2, three completed evidence batches on the extended candidate, `scoped-clean`, no findings. Static review does not replace native proof.
- Added regression coverage (not run): actual tab control construction must not subscribe to meter-only changes; the real Talk glyph and header avatar bodies must subscribe and receive new values. The existing dictation lifecycle test now checks its production control builder and activity-row observation, then finishes through the unchanged control action. Scalar compatibility tests retain mutable levels without a provider. The macOS regression uses the existing inactive voice-owner fixture and the real chat adapter/glyph: microphone/playback changes must invalidate the glyph, not control construction; pause remains observable and secondary-Gateway controls remain absent.
- Missing: Swift/Xcode build, native tests (including baseline-red/candidate-green), SwiftFormat/SwiftLint, screenshots/video, and measured invalidation/frame-time/CPU results. This Linux environment has none of those native tools. Test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available. Keep this PR draft until the Mac build loop supplies exact-head evidence.

### Sibling audit

- **Same cause, fixed here:** the bundled macOS caller in `WebChatSwiftUI.swift` eagerly read `TalkModeController.level` while constructing `MacChatSurface → OpenClawChatWindowShell → OpenClawChatView`. It now uses the same deferred provider. All bundled Talk/dictation constructors and shared consumers were traced; scalar test/smoke callers stay compatible.
- **Already isolated, unchanged:** `VoiceNoteComposerViews.swift` reads recorder levels only in the recording row. `VoiceLiveActivityCoordinator.swift` separately observes meter and presentation changes; `LiveActivityManager.updateVoiceLevel` coalesces ActivityKit samples at 500 ms and uses a bounded 24-sample buffer. These do not rebuild chat. The Activity Widget consumes that bounded payload.
- **Different bounded surface, unchanged:** `TalkOverlayView.swift` owns the voice orb, not a chat transcript; its visible-only level writer and orb-scale animation remain intact.
- **Distinct owners, not claimed fixed:** `VoiceWakeOverlayView.swift` observes a value-type overlay model shared with its draft display; `WatchRealtimeCallView.swift` reads its call controller's 100 ms input meter alongside the latest two transcripts. Neither uses the shared chat control contract. Profile overlay body/NSView updates and Watch call-view/text updates before considering separate fixes; no speculative owner split was added here.

### Mac verification

From the repository root on a qualified, task-owned Mac/simulator:

```sh
/usr/bin/time -p pnpm ios:test ChatVoiceObservationTests NodeAppModelInvokeTests OpenClawTypographyTests
swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter 'ChatTalkControlTests|ChatDictationControlTests|ChatTalkTranscriptStripModelTests'
```

For the macOS app, build and run the focused native test **only inside a disposable macOS VM/CI runner**, following `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md#run-native-tests-safely` (a temporary HOME or a filter alone is not isolation):

```sh
swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests
node scripts/test-macos-native.mts named --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --skip-build --filter TalkModeControllerPublishingTests
scripts/lint-swift.sh macos
```

The iOS test entry point generates/builds the app and runs its existing source lint gates. Capture the tested SHA, Xcode version, simulator/device, full test result bundle, timing, and any native format/lint repair.

Before measurement: use the same synthetic long conversation (100 user/assistant pairs, grouped assistant text and a code block every tenth reply) on baseline and candidate. With no new transcript events, measure 30-second listening, playback, and dictation intervals; repeat serially in interleaved baseline/candidate order at least five times each. Separate first-open from warm runs; record host/device load. In SwiftUI Instruments count ChatProTab/OpenClawChatView and MacChatSurface/OpenClawChatWindowShell updates attributable only to meter changes and confirm the visible meters still react. Record median/p95 frame duration, CPU and memory alongside the counts. Acceptance: meter-only parent invalidations become zero; visual/control semantics remain unchanged; no measured user-facing metric regresses. Results remain pending, not claimed here.

Also exercise stop/start, mute/unmute, dictation Done/Cancel, session/gateway handoff with an owned attachment, idle and nil-playback states; compare before/after video while scrolling grouped replies, opening the sidebar, and streaming word fade. Distinguish legitimate phase/transcript updates from pure meter updates.

Human contributor credit: @vyctorbrzezowski and @mikengyn.

prs.title: fix(ios): avoid sidebar reloads on chat switches and brief interruptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: switching same-agent chats or briefly opening Control Center needlessly restarts the iOS sidebar's roster, dashboard reads, and session subscription.

## User Impact

User impact: switching conversations and returning from a temporary inactive overlay no longer invalidate unrelated sidebar data. The current UI, selected-row presentation, sidebar animation, grouped replies, and word fade are unchanged. This draft still needs native build, runtime request-count, and before/after device evidence; no speedup is claimed yet. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The selected chat is a presentation input, not an input to these shared reads. Remove it from the refresh identity and retain an already-admitted foreground task lifetime through `.inactive`. One scene-local Boolean starts false, admits work on `.active`, and closes it on `.background`; cold or background-to-inactive transitions cannot start work. Gateway, agent, connectivity, and authority changes still invalidate the tasks.

Observer visibility remains **active-only**. Permission refreshes, microphone/capture gates, discovery, reconnect checks, and storage recovery are unchanged. RootTabs' separate branding/agent overview refresh still runs on activation: this does not eliminate all activation traffic. Event-driven updates and the ten-minute refresh remain; if an overlay stays inactive that long, the periodic read can still run until actual background. No new timer, debounce, cooldown, cache, or manager.

Contributor credit: @vyctorbrzezowski and @mikengyn.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b98dedd-1923-4f79-837e-5d48ac84b6c4)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b12bdfba-cb0b-43f7-a2f5-ca17649c42bc)

## Evidence

- Base: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`.
- Source trace: roster requests use Gateway and agent, dashboard requests use Gateway scope, and approval inbox reads use the authenticated Gateway route. None consumes the selected chat key. Selection remains observed directly by `RootSidebar`.
- Added an opt-in UI regression that launches the real app against the existing synthetic loopback Gateway, warms one chat, then switches five times between two same-agent chats. It records requests and requires zero additional root roster reads, dashboard reads, or global subscriptions while both histories still load. Chat's separate 50-row metadata reads are intentionally permitted.
- Added `RootSidebarLifecycleTests`: mounted real RootTabs with serialized requests captured at the existing Gateway test socket. Covers initial inactive/first active, three inactive/active cycles, active-only visibility, event consumption while inactive, background cancellation, background-to-inactive staying closed, and foreground restart. It controls scene phases; actual Control Center and permission-sheet transitions remain device-proof gaps.
- `git diff --check`: passed. New-file whitespace check and packaged-patch reverse check: no diagnostics.
- Local autoreview, OpenClaw engine / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2, complete three-file uncommitted candidate against the base above: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Native execution remained explicitly unverified. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the required final-range review/publication route remains parent-owned.
- Simplification: one invalidation input removed and one scene-local admission Boolean retained by the existing owner; no model, rendering, decoder, storage, or voice changes. Production delta: +16/-5; test delta: +271 lines. The mounted boundary test adds no production test hook.
- **Pending:** Xcode build, SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, red-on-base/green-on-candidate UI and mounted-lifecycle regressions, affected native suites, physical-device performance and before/after video. This Linux host has no Swift or Xcode toolchain. Test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

### Acceptance rule (set before native runs)

Use the same isolated Gateway, synthetic chats, device, appearance, and workload on base and candidate. After initial load, switch between two same-agent chats five times. Per switch, candidate must issue **zero** extra sidebar `sessions.list(limit: 200)`, `usage.cost`, `cron.list`, or `sessions.subscribe` calls; selected history and selected-row presentation must remain correct. The synthetic fixture proves outgoing requests, not successful usage data or real-Gateway performance.

Then keep the sidebar visible and open/dismiss Control Center five times without going Home. Establish the actual scene sequence in Xcode: inactive/active-only cycles must produce zero additional shared calls, while observer visibility follows true/false/true. Separately background and return: shared work must restart. Verify first activation, owner/authority changes during inactivity, retained session events, and permission updates. Compare this extension against original draft head `6d8fcadbd7eac451cf4d042f10ce4d2edd4a6b85` as well as the full base.

Keep cold and warm runs separate. For device timing, collect at least five interleaved base/candidate samples, record host load, median/p95 and spread for tap-to-history completion and animation hitches, and report CPU/memory changes. Reject regressions or obtain explicit acceptance; investigate any 20% regression. Verify agent/Gateway switches, reconnect, authority changes, foregrounding, session events, and the periodic refresh still refresh their scopes.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extra root roster/dashboard/subscription requests over five warm switches | Pending | Pending; required 0 |
| Extra shared requests over five inactive/active-only cycles | Pending | Pending; required 0 |
| Background/active refresh and active-only visibility | Pending | Pending; required retained |
| Tap-to-history median / p95 | Pending | Pending |
| Animation hitches / CPU / memory | Pending | Pending |

Native workloads: `IOS_SIM=<owned-simulator-udid> pnpm ios:test RootSidebarLifecycleTests RootTabsPresentationTests RootSidebarModelSessionEventsTests RootEventSubscriptionTests`, then `IOS_SIM=<owned-simulator-udid> pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/SidebarRefreshUITests` with the existing loopback fixture and `TEST_RUNNER_` environment described in the implementation session. Use a task-owned simulator; preserve request attachments and record test wall time/CI seconds when available.

prs.title: fix(google): Gemini 4 Hydrogen refuses xhigh thinking or sends it as HIGH
prs.body:
Closes #198001

## What Problem This Solves

Gemini 4 Hydrogen can't use Google's deepest thinking level: `--thinking xhigh` is refused, and `xhigh` set in config is sent as `HIGH`, although Google accepts `XHIGH` for this model.

## User Impact

A Gemini model row that maps `thinkingLevelMap: { xhigh: "xhigh" }` now offers `xhigh` and sends `thinkingLevel: XHIGH` (Interactions: `thinking_level: "xhigh"`). Rows without that entry are unchanged, so Gemini 4 Carbon, which rejects `XHIGH` with HTTP 400, keeps sending `HIGH`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The generic thinking layer already reads a row's `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh` as support, but the Google profile never offered `xhigh`, the transport had no `XHIGH` value, and both Google payload wrappers rewrote `xhigh` to `HIGH`. Each now honors the row's opt-in, so the level menu, validation and the request agree.

The bundled Hydrogen catalog row is left as is: released installs read that row from the hosted catalog and would offer `xhigh` while still sending `HIGH`. Its `xhigh: "xhigh"` entry can follow once a release sends `XHIGH`.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5: change details</summary>

- `googleSupportsXHighThinking(model)` (`packages/ai/src/transports/google-thinking-level.ts`): true when `thinkingLevelMap.xhigh === "xhigh"`.
- Transport (`google-shared.ts`): `getGoogleThinkingLevel` returns `XHIGH` for `xhigh` (and `max`, which clamps to it) on an opted-in Gemini 3/4 thinking-level row. Gemma 4 and Gemini 2.5 rows that carry the entry keep `HIGH` and the high budget.
- Payload wrappers: `sanitizeGoogleThinkingPayload` takes the row's map; the Google provider `wrapStreamFn` and the embedded runner's `createGoogleThinkingPayloadWrapper` both pass it. The deprecated `resolveGoogleGemini3ThinkingLevel` keeps its signature (Gemini Live indexes the SDK enum with it).
- Profile: `resolveGoogleThinkingProfile` appends `xhigh` for an opted-in Gemini 3/4 row.
- Tests (red on the base, green here): `extensions/google/thinking.test.ts`, `provider-hooks.test.ts`, `provider-policy-api.test.ts`, and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner-extraparams-google.test.ts`.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** throwaway Gateways on 2026.11.3 and on this branch, with a real Vertex key and a `google-vertex` row as a Vertex user writes it (`gemini-4-hydrogen` with `thinkingLevelMap: { minimal: null, xhigh: "xhigh" }`, `gemini-4-carbon` with `{ minimal: null }` as the control). Each turn sends the same short reasoning question with `openclaw agent --model <ref>`. Google bills thinking as output, so output tokens show how hard the model thought; every completed turn gave the same correct answer.

| Vertex row, output tokens | `--thinking high` | `--thinking xhigh` | `params.thinking: "xhigh"` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen, 2026.11.3 | 1,540 | refused: `"xhigh" is not supported` | 999 |
| Hydrogen, this PR | 608 | 5,250 | 4,900 |
| Carbon, 2026.11.3 | 4,302 | refused | 4,268 |
| Carbon, this PR | 3,793 | refused | 4,009 |

Tested on 90cfb370a0c.

- Request bodies, against a local stub that records them: 2026.11.1 sends `"HIGH"` for `xhigh` from config; this branch sends `"XHIGH"` on `google-vertex` and `google-generative-ai`, `"xhigh"` on `google-interactions`, and `"HIGH"` for Carbon. Google's side: a direct Vertex call with `XHIGH` returns 200 for Hydrogen and 400 for Carbon (#198001).
- Checks: the focused tests above pass (112), `pnpm tsgo:core` and the Google plugin typecheck pass; `pnpm check:changed` passed on the previous head (this commit only edits tests, docs and the manifest) except two lanes that fail the same way on the base (Plugin SDK surface budget, dead export scan).
- Gap: the real-model turns show the effect, not the request bytes; those come from the stub run and the unit tests.

prs.title: improve(ui): show project icons in the New Session project picker
prs.body:
Requested by @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d0da0223-3f95-4864-b576-136e6b6b99f3)

## What Problem This Solves

The New Session project picker shows the same generic glyph for every project, while the chat header already shows a project's own icon.

## User Impact

User impact: registered projects show their own favicon in the picker rows and on the picker trigger. GitHub search results, recent repositories and a selected GitHub repository show the filled GitHub mark. The trigger's default icon is now `folder-git-2`. Projects without an icon keep a generic glyph.

## Why This Change Was Made

Picker rows have no session yet, so the existing session-keyed workspace icon route can't serve them. A sibling Gateway route, `/__openclaw__/project-icon/<projectId>`, resolves a project through the existing requester-specific visibility owner and reuses the existing workspace icon scanner and cache. The browser only names a project ID it can already list, never a host path. The route requires `projects.list` read access, applies the same per-project visibility policy as the project list, revalidates authority before responding, and keeps the remote-workspace exclusion from the session route. Hidden project IDs return 404 before scanning their checkout.

The UI reuses the existing `openclaw-workspace-icon` element, which now accepts a fallback glyph. The chat header and the picker share one route/auth helper, replacing the header-only version. The session menu's stroke reset was hollowing filled brand marks into outlines, so filled icons now keep their fill there and on the picker trigger. The boot manifest was regenerated because New Session now loads the icon element.

## Evidence

- Maintainer correction: the original route returned private registered-project artwork to a read-only caller. The HTTP regression fails on the original code and passes with requester-aware resolution, including after a writer warms the icon cache.
- 38 focused Gateway/UI tests pass. Core/UI TypeScript, scoped lint/stylelint/formatting, and the test-line check pass. A scoped 144-line allocation covers reviewed project-icon access and selection regressions; the global baseline is unchanged.
- The production UI was tested against an isolated real Gateway with two real registered Git checkouts. The SVG returns 200 and decodes in both the picker row and selected trigger. The project without artwork returns 404 and retains its fallback. Desktop and 390px captures: [maintainer proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197607#issuecomment-6828294550).
- Production UI build completes. Strict CSS/boot budget warnings remain reported separately; no budget limit or approved visual value was changed.
- Independent P0–P2 review of the corrected candidate found no actionable issues.
- Original matched mock-Gateway screenshots below show the visual change. They are the author's before/after pair; the real-Gateway captures above validate the corrected source separately. No live model/provider call is claimed.

![Before: project picker with generic icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34d74322-f6ce-43eb-b68b-798ea162febb)

![After: project picker with project artwork and GitHub marks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97b9757d-d560-4e17-9e63-9e7469ab907f)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: fix: report size mismatches in OpenAI subscription image generation
prs.body:
Closes #192061 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Image generation silently returns different dimensions with an empty ignoredOverrides list when OpenAI subscription auth uses the Responses image tool. ## User Impact User impact: OpenAI subscription image results identify size hints that do not match the generated files while still returning those files. ## Why This Change Was Made The OpenAI provider already normalizes and forwards size, but the runtime only reports overrides dropped before generation. The runtime now compares returned dimensions with the size it sent to the provider and reports mismatches in ignoredOverrides. Completed images remain available when dimensions differ or cannot be read. (Maintainer update: the added extension test and its allocation were removed; the behavior is covered by the end-to-end proof linked below.) ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: the reported gpt-image-1 size case failed before the fix with ignoredOverrides: []; five controls passed. - `pnpm test extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.usage.test.ts extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.test.ts src/image-generation/runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 90 passed after the fix. - `pnpm test:extension openai`: 1252 passed. - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json src/image-generation/runtime.ts extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.usage.test.ts`: passed. - `pnpm format:check src/image-generation/runtime.ts extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.usage.test.ts docs/tools/image-generation.md` and `git diff --check`: passed. - `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base HEAD --staged`: failed on inherited test-budget debt; the added regression has a matching allocation. - 8 focused test files under `extensions/openai` re-run before opening: passed - Local review: autoreview (openclaw/agent-skills, source sha256 ea4d34), branch mode, base 3c43252c0, head deecae436, max priority P2: clean. ### Real behavior proof (head `deecae4360fc`) Runs openclaw infer image generate (OAuth, codex-responses), unpatched vs this branch: a 2048x1152 request returning 1536x1024 now lists size in ignoredOverrides. ```text $ openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt "A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall" --size 2048x1152 --output before-size.png --json # unpatched before size: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses before size: dimensions=1536x1024 before size: ignoredOverrides=[] before size: promptRewritten=true $ openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt "A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall" --output before-ordinary.png --json # unpatched before ordinary: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses before ordinary: dimensions=1536x1024 before ordinary: ignoredOverrides=[] before ordinary: promptRewritten=true $ openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt "A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall" --size 2048x1152 --output after-size.png --json # this branch after size: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses after size: dimensions=1536x1024 after size: ignoredOverrides=[{"key":"size","value":"2048x1152"}] after size: promptRewritten=true $ openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt "A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall" --output after-ordinary.png --json # this branch after ordinary: provider=openai mode=oauth transport=codex-responses after ordinary: dimensions=1536x1024 after ordinary: ignoredOverrides=[] after ordinary: promptRewritten=true ``` | 3. Unpatched subscription Responses image with explicit size 2048x1152 | 3. Unpatched subscription Responses image with size omitted | 4. Patched subscription Responses image with explicit size 2048x1152 | 4. Patched subscription Responses image with size omitted | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | | | | | - 3. Unpatched subscription Responses image with explicit size 2048x1152: `node before/openclaw.mjs --log-level info infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt 'A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall' --size 2048x1152 --output before-size.png --json` - 3. Unpatched subscription Responses image with size omitted: `node before/openclaw.mjs --log-level info infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt 'A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall' --output before-ordinary.png --json` - 4. Patched subscription Responses image with explicit size 2048x1152: `node openclaw/openclaw.mjs --log-level info infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt 'A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall' --size 2048x1152 --output after-size.png --json` - 4. Patched subscription Responses image with size omitted: `node openclaw/openclaw.mjs --log-level info infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-1 --prompt 'A red bicycle leaning against a plain white wall' --output after-ordinary.png --json`
Notes for reviewers - The check applies to all size-capable image providers. Sizes the runtime already snapped to a preset are compared with the snapped size, so `normalization` alone reports them. - Dimension inspection is best effort and does not discard completed images.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): scribe retries repeat the request after a lost response
prs.body:
Related: #197391

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate scribe update turns when **Try again** reaches the Gateway but its response is lost, and the update is sent again.

## User Impact

Owners can retry automatic updates and run-message replacements after a lost response without starting a second turn for the same attempt. No stored-data format, permissions, generated run-message bytes, or visual presentation changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final review of #197391 identified two P2s: late retries discarded their failed request identity, and new Granola instructions lacked an incident citation. This follow-up retains each retry identity until its send succeeds and adds the citation. The existing attempt map and replacement closure remain the owners; no new retry machinery or helpers.

The real-Gateway proof below found a third path: in the Control UI a lost response arrives as a dropped connection, and the page reconnects with a new plugin host. Attempts and pending updates were kept per host, so the reloaded page forgot the unsent retry and sent the update again under a new identity. They are now kept per Gateway (the Control UI base path), and Try again sends through the page that asks.

## Evidence

Unit and static checks at `02995e6c49e7`:

- Lost-response regressions fail on the unmodified base, then pass. The reconnect regression (new host, same Gateway) fails on `457d4aa` ("Updating…" with a third send) and passes with the fix.
- 43 scribe-state, scribe-view and skill-packaging tests pass; extension source/test typechecks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, test-lines ratchet, baseline ratchets and `git diff --check` pass.
- No visual change: the notices and buttons are the same; only which requests they send changed.

### Real-Gateway proof on the Mac Studio

Isolated Gateways on loopback ports 19821–19823, each with its own state directory and token; real model turns through ClawRouter; headless Chromium driving the Control UI. The live fsn1 Gateway and the Studio's own Gateway were not touched. Builds: `v2026.11.3` (`847611dc`), pre-#197391 main (`69b3f27b`), this PR (`457d4aa` and `02995e6`). Each upgrade stopped the old Gateway, ran the new build's `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive` on the same state, then started the new build.

**1. Released scheduler storage → this PR (`v2026.11.3` → `02995e6`).** Created through `v2026.11.3`'s `cron.add`: a `session:<key>` cron job with tz, stagger, pacing, trigger, model, thinking, timeout, fallbacks, `lightContext`, `toolsAllow` [2 tools], delivery none and failure alert {after 3, cooldown, includeSkipped}; a paused isolated interval job with `toolsAllow: []` and failure alert off; a main-session `at` reminder. A forced run succeeded on `v2026.11.3`. After the upgrade, all three jobs compared field-for-field equal (excluding run state and revision), the paused job stayed paused, and forced runs succeeded on the new build: the session job answered in `agent:main:kn-lane1-target`, the tool-less isolated job in a fresh `cron:…:run:…` session. (The built-in `heartbeat-main` record migrated to its current form, as main does; not touched by this PR.) `v2026.11.3` has no Knowledge plugin, so this lane exercises scheduler storage only.

**2. Pre-#197391 Scribes → this PR (main to main; run twice, on `457d4aa` and on `02995e6`).** On `69b3f27b`, the Scribes page started *Knowledge Consolidation* (setup prompt edited to save model, thinking `low`, timeout 900, active hours, failure alert after 3 with a 2 h cooldown) and *Learn from conversations* (a hand-edited run message plus model, thinking, timeout, `lightContext`, exact `toolsAllow` of 6 tools, `idleOnly`, pacing and a trigger), each on `session:<key>`; both first runs succeeded, then Conversations was paused. After the upgrade, the first load of the Scribes page:
- paired both automations with their conversations and sent exactly one update turn to each conversation;
- moved both to `current`; replaced Consolidation's unedited generated run message; left the hand-edited Conversations message byte-identical;
- kept every saved option above, the pause, the owner, and the account-mode scheduled tool policy (field-for-field comparison).

Then on `02995e6`: **Run now** on Consolidation ran in a fresh `agent:main:cron:<job>:run:<id>` session, called `knowledge_status` (owner store, writes enabled), and the page showed its status line with an **Open run** link read from run history. **Repair** on Conversations after archiving its conversation restored the conversation, turned the automation on and sent no turn.

**3. Lost response on a real Gateway, both late retry paths.** The page's `chat.send` frame was sent, then its WebSocket was closed before the answer (a lost response); on `02995e6` the conversation was also kept busy with a 90 s turn so the update stayed late; the page clock was advanced 3 minutes once the page showed "Updating…". Counted by update messages that reached the scribe conversation:

| Path | Build | Identities sent | Inputs accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Automatic update → Try again → response lost | `457d4aa` | X, Y (lost), **Z (new, sent by the reconnected page)** | 3: Y and Z duplicate one retry |
| Automatic update → Try again → response lost | `02995e6` | X, Y (lost), Y again | 2: X and Y |
| Replace with new → Try again → response lost | `02995e6` | A, B (lost), B again | 2: A and B |

### Out of scope

- **Granola outcome status** was not exercised here. This PR's only Granola change is the 5-line citation in `scribe-runs.md`; it changes neither generated run-message bytes nor outcome-status behavior, which shipped in #197391 and is covered by its prompt and status tests. Its live check is the next Granola scribe run after the maintainer's rebuild. No private Granola account was used.

### Follow-up

- In one Replace run, the model re-declared the automation keeping an owner note from an earlier turn in the same conversation instead of writing the new run message exactly. The page correctly did not mark the replacement applied (it compares the saved message with the new one) and kept offering Try again. Making the replacement turn write the message exactly is a separate follow-up.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): move scratch tree cleanup off the Gateway thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large expired scratch clones consume minutes of Gateway-thread CPU and tens of gigabytes of V8 allocation during background reclaim, competing with chat even after cleanup starvation is fixed.

## User Impact

Recursive scratch inspection and deletion run in one filesystem worker. The Gateway retains expiry, custody, and identity decisions. A new run can reuse the original scratch path while cleanup finishes on the expired tree. Interrupted cleanup remains recoverable after restart without a new journal, configuration option, or schema.

The requested low-millisecond / tens-of-KB main-thread cost per clone remains unmet. The complete six-clone phase now uses a median 0.975 seconds and 154.7 MiB on the main thread, including fixed owner work and 250 small-file removals. The remaining per-128-file host pacing and pressure checks are retained. Accepted tradeoff: the owner explicitly approved landing this measured result and the +219 production lines. Dividing the complete six-clone window evenly gives about 163 ms of main CPU and 25.8 MiB of main allocation per clone, including fixed owner work and 250 small-file removals, versus about 36.8 seconds of main CPU per clone before. The remaining gap to the low-ms/tens-of-KB target is accepted for this PR; no claim is made that the original target was achieved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway verifies current custody and the expiry scan's exact device/inode, atomically renames each expired directory within scratch, and passes that identity to the existing filesystem worker for rechecking. This transfers the expired tree out of task custody before asynchronous deletion; new work uses the original name. Interrupted claims remain ordinary scratch entries and are rediscovered by the existing expiry owner.

The worker streams traversal and deletion with the existing depth/scan/removal budgets, symlink handling, hardlinked Git-object expiry, cancellation joins, and 100 ms pauses after every 128 removals. The host samples IO pressure at those pauses. It reuses the filesystem worker entrypoint, task pool, and mutation-authority relay. The unique pause IDs already landed in #197986 remain unchanged.

Production delta is +219 lines for the worker boundary, bounded receipts, cancellation settlement, and atomic custody transfer; tests +45, benchmark +17. No extra scheduler API or cache. Top-level enumeration and bounded plain-file deletion remain on the Gateway thread. Direct `.openclaw/<name>` and contributor landing clones remain owned by their creating task's closeout.

## Evidence

Five serial interleaved before/after pairs on the same six 62k-file clone-shaped trees, two 62k-file workspaces, 5,000 synthetic session rows, 250 expired small entries, and 256 fresh files. Every arm removed **6 clones / 256 top-level entries / 372,274 filesystem entries / 6,856,707,876 logical bytes**, preserving all fresh-file contents. All timings were retained.

Values are median / sample p95 (nearest rank; with five samples, p95 is the maximum).

| Measurement | Main-thread cleanup | Worker cleanup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scratch phase wall, seconds | 360.290 / 450.946 | 208.935 / 299.790 |
| Total process CPU, seconds | 279.015 / 310.608 | 188.072 / 253.036 |
| Main-thread CPU, seconds | 220.796 / 248.759 | 0.975 / 1.245 |
| Cumulative main-V8 allocation, MiB | 30,530.027 / 30,654.485 | 154.700 / 168.780 |
| Owner-probe loop p99, ms | 19.251 / 26.411 | 13.279 / 13.967 |
| Owner-probe loop maximum, ms | 130.154 / 190.185 | 23.970 / 43.123 |
| Reclaim, clones/minute, median (range) | 0.999 (0.798–1.968) | 1.723 (1.201–2.135) |

Main CPU falls 99.56% and allocation 99.49%. This relocates the recursive work; total process CPU is reported alongside main CPU. Two preceding equal-work A/A controls measured main CPU 200.565 / 252.251 seconds and allocation 32.348 / 32.307 GB (0.13% allocation spread), demonstrating substantial timing noise. Those controls used the prior synthetic metadata fixture version; all final pairs use the same current base and fixture version in both arms.

- 85 focused scratch, custody, maintenance, and scheduler tests passed. Identity replacement has red/green proof against the parent. The new-work-at-original-path case is red on the earlier worker prototype and green after atomic claiming. Cancellation joins the worker, and a subsequent pass finishes the partial claim.
- All 10 scratch tests passed with fs-safe native helpers disabled. The final physical-removal assertions also pass in the focused 10-test suite.
- `pnpm build` passed. `pnpm check:changed --base 0e771727076e7fa5e059a61d8a75876a1ecb2105` passed all checks except the nine attributed inherited dead exports below.
- Codex P2 review of the complete staged correction was scoped-clean. A separate review of the final proof-only adjustment was also scoped-clean.
- The final full-size expired root was independently verified empty, including hidden claims; the fresh root contained exactly its 256 files. The benchmark now counts every remaining top-level directory, so renaming a clone cannot masquerade as reclaim. That post-timing counter adjustment was validated on a smaller behavior-only fixture; it changes neither production code nor timed statements, and its production source digest matches every full-size candidate arm.

<details>
<summary>Individual paired samples, command, and limits</summary>

| Pair | Total CPU seconds, before → after | Main CPU seconds, before → after | Loop p99 ms, before → after | Loop max ms, before → after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 310.608 → 188.072 | 228.349 → 0.917 | 26.411 → 12.558 | 190.185 → 17.121 |
| 2 | 168.445 → 152.995 | 140.878 → 0.688 | 12.198 → 12.313 | 26.493 → 12.919 |
| 3 | 167.504 → 187.161 | 138.636 → 0.975 | 12.337 → 13.279 | 29.540 → 23.970 |
| 4 | 279.015 → 253.036 | 220.796 → 1.245 | 19.284 → 13.967 | 130.154 → 43.123 |
| 5 | 308.663 → 212.874 | 248.759 → 1.055 | 19.251 → 13.287 | 133.300 → 24.986 |

The shared host's load changed between arms; pair 3's higher total CPU and p99 are retained above. APFS hardlinks, accelerated waits, and Node 26.12.1's exact allocation counter limit production extrapolation. The synthetic database is 4.48 MB. This is distinct from the earlier Linux/btrfs 35-GiB pressure qualification, and is not a live chat or production Node 24 latency proof. Logical unlinked bytes are not physical freed space. Fixture preparation is excluded. The benchmark ends at scratch completion and intentionally cancels subsequent worktree GC.

Reproduce with the committed workload after preparing a 62,000-file source (`--prepare --files 62000 --file-bytes 18432`):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts \
  --source /path/to/synthetic-source --output /path/to/synthetic-fixture \
  --worktrees 2 --scratch-order --scratch-clones 6 --reuse-scratch-order
```

prs.title: fix(ui): Browser panel blanks its live view after every agent action on the same tab
prs.body:
Related: #148187 (context only: remote viewport sizing for the same panel) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the Browser panel's live view goes blank and reconnects after every successful agent browser action, even when the agent stays on the tab the panel is already streaming. ## User Impact User impact: while an agent works in the tab shown in the chat's Browser panel, the live view keeps streaming instead of blanking after each action. Seen with a remote attach-only CDP browser, where each rebuild took 1 to 2 seconds, so the panel went blank every few seconds; on slower links it never recovered between actions. Switching tabs, changing browser route, choosing a browser card, and the screenshot fallback behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made Each successful browser tool call gives the chat's preferred tab a new revision, and the panel follows it with `selectTab(targetId, route, { focusBrowserTab: false })`. `selectTab` only returned early for the no-route case, so a session result for the tab already being streamed still invalidated the view: it closed the screencast socket, cleared the view, listed tabs, minted a new screencast, and waited for a first frame. A live screencast already shows the agent's changes, so a session result for the tab the stream owns now leaves the stream alone. Screenshot fallback still recaptures, because there the reselection is what refreshes the picture. Card choices (which focus the tab) are unchanged. ## Evidence - New tests in `ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-stream.test.ts` ("following session results"): a newer result for the streaming tab keeps the socket, the view and the request count; a result for another tab, or for the same tab on another route, still closes the stream and mints one for the new target. - New Control UI e2e test `ui/src/e2e/browser-panel-session-follow.e2e.test.ts` (mock Gateway with synthetic data and a real screencast WebSocket): with the Browser panel streaming page A, a new agent browser result for page A causes no second `/screencast`, the stream socket stays open, and the live view stays rendered with no empty state; a result for page B still mints a stream for B, closes the first socket, and shows B. On the base `selectTab` the same-tab case fails (`expected [ ... ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`: a second `/screencast`); with the fix both pass via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/browser-panel-session-follow.e2e.test.ts`. - On the base `selectTab`, the same-tab unit test fails: `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (the screencast socket is closed). The other two pass on both. - `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-stream.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 42 passed. - `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser --maxWorkers=1`: 276 + 6 passed (2 shards). - `pnpm tsgo:ui`: passed. `pnpm format:check`: passed. - `pnpm check:changed` (with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_SKIP_DEADCODE=1`): all lanes passed, including typecheck core tests, typecheck UI and lint of changed files. The dead export scan, when run, reported only `scripts/bench-ci-planner.mts: runPlannerFlow`, which this change does not touch. Full `pnpm lint` reports existing `max-lines` errors in unrelated files and nothing in the changed files. - Reproduction on 2026.10.9 with a remote attach-only CDP browser: with the panel open on a tab, each new preferred-tab revision for the same tab logged a client close (1000) of `/browser/screencast`, then `GET /tabs` and `POST /screencast`, with a blank view until the new stream's first frame (about 330 ms on a local link; about 5.9 s with 300 ms added round trip between the Gateway and the browser). With the equivalent change applied to the built panel, 6 revision bumps kept 1 stream open with 0 closes and 0 blanks, also at 300 ms added round trip. - Before/after screenshots of the e2e scenario (synthetic data), taken 800 ms after the same-tab agent result: on main the panel shows the loading placeholder instead of the page; with this change the live view stays. **Before (main):** **After (this PR):** - Still to do: live proof through a real Gateway with a real agent and model.
Repro 1. Open the Browser panel in a chat session on a tab the agent is using, with live streaming working. 2. Let the agent run several browser actions on that same tab (equivalently, give the panel's `preferredTab` a new revision for the same tab). 3. Before the fix, each action closes the screencast socket with code 1000 and the panel is blank until a new stream's first frame arrives.

prs.title: fix: keep native chat images stable while replies stream
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary image recreation when a native chat reply containing inline data images is prepared repeatedly during streaming.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is stable inline images while native iOS and macOS replies stream, without changing layout, supported formats, fallback labels, grouped replies, sidebar animation, or word fade. Actual mounted-identity reuse and UI equivalence still require Mac/device execution. No configuration or migration is required.

This is a draft for the exact-head Mac build and device-proof loop. Native compilation, runtime decode counts, performance measurements, and before/after video are still pending; no measured speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Markdown preparation previously decoded every inline data image and generated a new UUID on every pass. Even the user-message metadata sanitizer paid that decoding cost before discarding the images.

Preparation now records the source and a forward occurrence index, so duplicates remain distinct and appended copies do not change earlier IDs. The existing image-list consumer owns decoding in a retained SwiftUI StateObject, once per mounted image identity. Changing the source creates a new identity; current labels still update. Removal releases view-owned state, subject to SwiftUI's normal lifecycle. Remounting can decode again.

There is no process-wide cache, eviction policy, disk storage, URL fetch, or new image-size restriction. The encoded slice refers only to an image source, not to a growing reply. The same platform decoder and existing remote-image flattening remain in use. The separate managed-attachment thumbnail path is unchanged. The metadata sanitizer still discards inline user images exactly as before; this patch removes the wasted decoding, not that existing behavior.

Human contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski and Mike Nguyen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6b98dedd-1923-4f79-837e-5d48ac84b6c4)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2966d896-f850-4e02-9a34-98b9c2a3562f)

## Evidence

- Base: 0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4.
- Passed: git diff --check; complete local diff/source and sibling-call-site inspection; author simplification pass.
- Auto Review: OpenClaw engine, effective model openai/gpt-6.1-sol, complete local candidate against that base, P0–P2, scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed patch SHA-256: a7a0172cf4ce576191a6916d66a3ce1274ccbfadb28bd95ccfc6c04aaa5a51f6.
- Added identity regression for appended text, duplicate copies, interleaved sources, changed labels, and replacement sources; retained malformed-data fallback and existing decode assertions at the production decode boundary.
- Not run: Swift unit tests, red/green baseline proof, Swift typecheck/build/lint/format, iOS simulator/device checks, macOS rendering, frame/CPU/memory measurements, and video. This Linux environment has no Swift, Xcode, SwiftLint, or SwiftFormat. Test wall time and CI seconds are unavailable.
- Simplification: no cache manager or metadata-cleaning flag. Production delta +40 lines; tests +35 lines. Renderer algorithm and streaming owner are untouched; only the image-list consumer is adapted.

### Native proof acceptance rule (pending)

Use the same synthetic inline PNG reply on base and candidate, append 100 text updates with the image mounted, append a duplicate, replace one source, and remove/reinsert the image. Inspect actual platform-decoder calls and retained allocations through the real native view. Candidate must do zero decodes during text-only metadata cleanup, one decode per newly mounted occurrence, no further decodes while its mounted identity survives, and fresh decoding after source replacement. Duplicate images and invalid-image labels must remain correct.

Compare five interleaved base/candidate runs on the same device with cold and warm samples separated. Record decode counts, main-thread/total CPU, median/p95 frame time, initial appearance latency, and retained memory. No visual or user-facing metric regression is accepted; a 20% degradation is a stop for investigation. Keep the draft until exact-head builds/tests, lifecycle counts, and user-supplied before/after evidence are recorded.

<details>
<summary>Exact pending Mac verification plan</summary>

Use a task-owned checkout and simulator, Swift 6.3/Xcode 27.1+, xcodegen, and the pinned Watch toolchain described in apps/ios/README.md. Follow docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md#run-native-tests-safely; do not use operator Gateway state. Record the published full head SHA and clean status before testing. Set IOS_SIM to the selected task-owned simulator UDID.

    git rev-parse HEAD
    git status -sb
    git diff --check
    swift --version
    xcodebuild -version
    scripts/check-swift-tools.sh
    swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --scratch-path .openclaw/tmp/inline-image-swift-build --filter 'ChatMarkdownPreprocessorTests|ChatMarkdownRendererTests|ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests|ChatMarkdownDisplayPreprocessorTests|ChatCompletedWorkTests'
    scripts/lint-swift.sh ios
    scripts/format-swift.sh ios
    IOS_DEST="platform=iOS Simulator,id=$IOS_SIM" pnpm ios:build
    IOS_SIM="$IOS_SIM" pnpm ios:test OpenClawTypographyTests

SwiftPM exercises AppKit; the iOS build checks UIKit. Record test counts, wall time and CI seconds. These tests do not prove StateObject allocation counts.

For baseline red/green, copy only keepsImageIdentityAcrossStreamingUpdatesAndDuplicateAppends into a separate base checkout's existing preprocessor suite. Do not copy candidate decode() API conversions onto base. The UUID-based base must fail same-source identity equality, rather than compilation/setup.

Count actual platform-decoder entries using Xcode/Instruments: base ChatMarkdownPreprocessor.inlineImage; candidate InlineImage.decode() via InlineImageView.DecodedImage.init. Disable breakpoints for timing. Use identical synthetic pixel PNG and 1024x1024 PNG bytes across A/B runs.

1. Append 100 text updates through the real grouped-reply/word-fade path: no new decodes while the same image subtree remains mounted.
2. Append an identical source: two visible occurrences, with only the new occurrence decoding.
3. Replace a source with visibly different pixels: the replacement decodes; existing images remain correct.
4. Change an invalid image's label: current fallback text updates without another same-source decode.
5. Interleave replies/sessions: no global cache or cross-session retained image sharing.
6. Remove/navigate away, then reinsert: release follows SwiftUI lifecycle and remount decoding is expected. Record ancestor-induced remounts rather than claiming process-wide reuse.
7. Exercise stripInboundMetadata/decodeMessages: unchanged cleaned text and zero candidate decodes, preserving its existing inline-image discard behavior.
8. Cover remote URLs, escaped/fenced/inline-code examples, Unicode, CRLF, invalid base64, GIF/JPEG/PNG: unchanged rendering/fallback and no remote Markdown-image fetch.
9. Check managed artifact images' unchanged detached 2048px thumbnail path.

Capture actual iPhone and shared macOS before/after screenshots/video with synthetic content, including scrolling, duplicates, replacement, grouped replies, sidebar animation and word fade. Consult .agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/media.md and .agents/skills/proof-video/SKILL.md first. No credentials or unrelated sessions in evidence. Apply the five-run acceptance rule above; no runtime result is claimed yet.

</details>

- @mikengyn
- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: feat: recognize personal identity across enrolled devices
prs.body:
Related: #162164

## What Problem This Solves

People using paired browsers, native apps, and interactive CLI credentials cannot consistently use the same personal profile across their Gateway.

## User Impact

People can optionally enroll approved operator clients into one Gateway-local profile, see their effective access, and retain that identity through normal rotation and reconnect. Skipping setup preserves Shared Owner; existing devices are not silently converted and historical authorship is not rewritten.

**Migration:** state schema advances from 39 to 40, with unsafe older readers refused rather than discarding personal bindings. Rollback requires supported backup/restore. No external account or new login provider is required, and enrollment does not expand device or personal permissions.

This contributes to the native-identity umbrella without claiming its outstanding physical iOS/macOS acceptance is complete.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse canonical profiles, existing pairing and credential lifetimes, role policy, and worker-owned storage instead of adding a parallel identity or permissions system.
- Apply personal identity consistently to WebSocket and supported HTTP requests, browser/CLI enrollment, native/mobile operator handoffs, and OpenClaw ID adapters. Keep node, unattended-service, membership/root, and independent maintenance authority separate.
- Keep setup and recovery in existing onboarding, Profile, Devices, and QR surfaces. Missing or revoked personal authority requires recovery rather than silently becoming Shared Owner.
- Consolidate repeated policy selection, enrollment checks, profile options, and TUI connection setup: the final cleanup removes 51 production lines without dropping a client or recovery path.

## Evidence

**Publication head:** `68103b49aa27b5b022d3411d459e8bbb5778df59` (tree `8680223f7f1445fc083086d2806c4017f24d918f`). The normal commit hook, core typecheck, targeted lint/format, and diff checks passed after the mechanical publication fixes. Transpiled JavaScript was byte-identical across the four TypeScript files touched by those fixes.

**After the simplification:** core and UI typechecks, targeted lint/format, production UI build, all eight browser enrollment/QR E2E cases, real-Gateway enrollment/reconnect/HTTP/WebSocket/revocation, corrected recovery fixture (4/4), personal bootstrap producers (8/8), and TUI connections (12/12) passed. UI startup remains **92,135 B / 92,137 B**, with no budget increase.

The independent all-severity review of the cleanup snapshot found no actionable issues. Its reviewed snapshot was `143afdcd723097dcb8f027fa634846f6feaccc56`; subsequent changes were a three-line recovery-fixture setup correction, exact test-allocation bookkeeping, an equivalent local-variable rename for lint, Markdown quoting, and unchanged type declarations relocated to existing CLI/TUI modules to satisfy file-size checks. This review covers the cleanup, not the entire feature.

**Retained pre-cleanup product proof:** actual packaged-Gateway browser/CLI lifecycle and a generated, persisted, rendered personal local-model reply; published `2026.11.3` schema-22 state upgraded normally to candidate schema 40 with older-reader refusal; and one actual uninstrumented Linux/Tauri recovery fixture. In that native fixture, rotate → revoke → refused Connect → maintenance restoration → Connect recovered the same running app and identity without restart/reload/token reseeding. Native routing tests passed 54/54; terminal/setup tests passed 122 cases across 11 files. These receipts belong to pre-cleanup tree `85ce39b173b744453e691f8e51afba3892d8f3be`, not a new full-tree certification. The full feature also received five completed P0-only Auto Review chunks on that tree; this is not all-severity or CODEOWNER approval.

**Known failures and gaps:**

- One unchanged browser-pair expiration test still expects an expired request to remain pending although it is removed; expiry refusal succeeds. No baseline replay or unrelated production repair is claimed.
- Six Devices UI tests have identical missing-provider failures before and after the cleanup; 46 focused UI unit tests pass.
- Seven lines of inherited test-ratchet debt and three unchanged core max-lines findings remain. The original 4,330-line feature allocation is unchanged; the cleanup adds only its exact 12 test lines of scoped allocation, not a shared baseline increase.
- `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` completed with exit 1: eight generated Rust-target JavaScript artifacts and three tracked files byte-identical to the base (`scripts/bench-pr-dependency-cache.mjs`, `scripts/pr-lib/dependency-lifetime-inherit.cjs`, and `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-transport.test-support.mjs`). None of the 243 candidate paths in scanned tree `56b959e799b05f3204a1d31e15ff37aacb8037c2` was reported; the aggregate check remains red.
- Current-main integration is outstanding: a nonmutating merge probe against `d4577ec4b31ea0126ca1bc1ede0bdd16c0186ed1` found 26 conflicts, including schema/version, identity admission, recovery, and Profile UI. This PR preserves the validated candidate on base `c37e3897be60e2db9db3aefba9cee92bcb193b51`; it is not merge-ready and conflict resolution will require affected requalification.
- Existing UI size-warning categories remain. No aggregate-green/full-repository claim is made.
- No new live hosted-ID/channel, Apple, physical-mobile, cross-platform, or stress certification. Historical native/upgrade proof is retained with its original scope. The no-model native fixture's initial Home-unavailable shell is not counted as a pass; subsequent Profile/Debug use established usability.

Current-head CI will be reported by the PR checks; local evidence does not imply that CI or required owner review has completed.

These are inspected historical captures from the pre-simplification feature candidate. They illustrate the original feature/recovery proof, not newly captured visual parity for the cleanup. All people and Gateway names shown are synthetic fixtures.

prs.title: fix(ui): remove automatic browser preview cards
prs.body:
Related: #197528

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated page-preview cards cluttering the conversation whenever the agent browses during a task.

## User Impact

Browser tool calls keep their normal expandable results without automatic preview cards, including inside expanded work. Deliberately shared links, images, and widgets remain unchanged. The Browser panel remains available through its existing controls and retains the session’s latest successful browser target. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Following the requester’s design direction, this removes the card rather than hiding it or introducing a replacement. @vyctorbrzezowski plans to redesign browser activity as a better chat-transcript experience in separate work. The renderer, styles, thumbnail capture/cache, preview-placement selectors, transcript plumbing, unused copy, and obsolete card tests are removed. Browser target selection remains because the existing panel still uses it.

A follow-up review of adjacent code also removed the card-only `browserTab` field from Browser panel open requests. No other producer sends it; panel controls, Gateway panel commands, native links, and session-result routing are unchanged. Browser, settings, security, and configuration documentation no longer describes the removed card or its menu and page-preview behavior. Stale card paths are removed from CI owner metadata and benchmark checks. External-link hover previews keep their existing setting.

The generated boot manifest and config-documentation hash are refreshed; no new state owner or compatibility path is added.

## Evidence

- The removal regression failed in both light and dark themes before the card was removed; it passes afterward.
- After merging current `main`, **3,553 of 3,555 tests passed across 316 of 317 UI unit files** covering chat components, Browser panel, menus, clipboard, and native links. The two failures were mobile session-menu timing tests outside this change; that file passed **17/17 twice** in isolation.
- **30 production-bundle browser tests passed** across 6 suites: light/dark expansion and reload, draft retention, repeated visits at desktop/mobile widths, social URLs, delivered widgets, and host/node Browser panel routing.

prs.title: fix(cli): keep multi-line id rebind warnings readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw id rebind` commits the key move, then checks publication. When that follow-up fails with a multi-line error, the
CLI prints the whole message on one line with the newlines escaped as literal `\n` sequences:

```
Moved to new keys (committed). Follow-up check failed: gateway transport failed: refused\n  remedy: …
```

Gateway transport errors are intentionally multi-line (message, remedy, connection details, sometimes a `Possible causes:`
list), so the escaped form is the least readable case that shows up right after a successful key move.

## Why This Change Was Made

`writeCommittedWarning` passed the whole message through `sanitizeTerminalText`, whose contract is *single-line* rendering of
untrusted values — it maps `\n` to the two characters `\` + `n` on purpose so a value cannot break a line.

The message here is not a bare untrusted value: the transport builds it as several text lines and the layout is ours. The fix
sanitizes each line and rejoins them, which is the idiom already used for the same reason in
`src/infra/control-ui-assets.ts:269` (`split` → `map(sanitizeTerminalText)` → join). Control characters inside a line are
still stripped, so nothing regains the ability to inject escapes or raw control bytes.

## User Impact

A failed publication check after `id rebind` now prints the transport error as the several lines it was written as: the
message, the remedy, and the connection details stay separately readable while the "committed, don't repeat" framing is
unchanged. Single-line errors render exactly as before.

## Evidence

New case in `src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts`: a three-line follow-up error with a trailing `\u0007` control byte, asserting
the output keeps the newlines, contains no escaped `\n`, and drops the control byte.

- base (`main` @ `6b22db7fa32`): **1 failed | 9 passed** — `expected 'Moved to new keys (committed).\nFollo…' to contain
  'refused\n  remedy: …'`.
- with this change: **10 passed**.
- `oxlint` on both touched files: no findings.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change and its evidence.

prs.title: fix: queued follow-ups drop the implicit reply target
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:

below this comment.

type: user-facing description
-->

Closes #142268

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Queued follow-up answers on resolver-less channels (Telegram after restart, no live dispatcher) dropped the implicit reply target, so `reply_to_message_id` was missing.

This PR restores that injection for same-channel external/legacy turns. It does **not** claim ordinary overlapping-turn parity through a live Telegram Test Server run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Queued follow-up delivery already stores `messageId` / `originatingReplyToId` at admission. Payload resolution only applied reply tags and never ran the same implicit-injection helper the live path uses.

Queued payloads now go through `resolveReplyThreadingPayloads`. Implicit `currentMessageId` is injected only for resolver-less channels, with the same origin/provenance exclusions as `routeReply` (same-channel external or legacy user turns). Channels that own `resolveReplyTransport` keep correlation at `routeReply`, so empty/`replyToId` opt-outs survive. Restart-sentinel still keeps `originatingReplyToId`. Explicit `replyToId` still wins. `replyToMode` `off` / `first` / `all` stay authoritative.

## User Impact

On resolver-less transports, queued follow-up answers reply to the triggering same-channel message. Cross-channel and internal/inter-session IDs are not forwarded. Channels with a transport resolver still decide correlation at final routing.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` as a single commit. Head SHA: `c6f38a93c8f7f9266efe7d3b39dbfd1aa799494b`. Marker: `PROOF_OK_c6f38a93`.

Focused Vitest after this revision (`test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts`): `followup-delivery.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.channel.test.ts` + `followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts` + `followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts` + `followup-turn-admission.test.ts` — **137 passed**.

Coverage:

- same-channel queued `messageId` still injects `replyToId` on resolver-less channels
- Discord-origin / Slack-destination IDs are withheld at decision time
- inter-session child announcements stay unthreaded
- restart-sentinel keeps `originatingReplyToId`
- explicit `replyToId` survives excluded implicit IDs
- empty `replyToId` opt-out survives decision and delivery through the real channel resolver
- decision-to-delivery matrix matches those exclusions through the real channel resolver
- core tests use a fixture channel; they no longer import `extensions/qa-channel`

Sabotage: switching decision injection back to unguarded `resolveFollowupCurrentMessageId` turns the foreign-channel and inter-session tests red.

Runtime observation on `ba68eaeb` used the real Gateway + Telegram transport after restart and recorded the queued answer referencing message 11. That remains the dispatcher-less recovery proof. Telegram Test Server E2E for ordinary overlap was **not** rerun (no Convex QA broker credentials on this fork).

## Maintainer refresh — September 14, 2026

Refreshed onto `82a9bef596011a6145d7f639d9773ff5e7267f7d`, preserving the original patch and contributor authorship. Current candidate: `6d592e236f8d40d33c911391ad795ed59062b439`.

Fresh review exposed an empty-target regression on channels without a transport resolver. The shared threading owner now distinguishes an absent reply target from `replyToId: ""`; the latter remains an explicit opt-out. Inline explicit-reply directives still override that implicit-threading opt-out. This is an owner-level condition change, not a follow-up-specific workaround.

Verification:
- Added regressions failed on the pre-repair candidate: **3 failed, 46 passed**.
- Repaired candidate: **183 passed across 7 suites**, covering queued delivery, channel boundaries, admission/provenance, resolver delegation, shared threading, empty/false opt-outs, inline override, first-reply slot accounting, and deduplication.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.channel.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.implicit-reply.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery-payloads.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-plumbing.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-threading.test.ts`
- `git diff --check` passed. The repair adds one net production line (an explanatory comment) and 61 test lines. Full changed-surface static checks and hosted CI are tracked separately; this section does not claim they have completed.
- This is deterministic owner/channel-boundary proof, not new authenticated live-channel proof.

Review adjudication: the fresh autoreview returned four reports, not a scoped-clean result. The index-only empty-target finding is resolved in the committed candidate. Two resolver-owned issues were verified as unchanged baseline behavior and recorded as follow-ups: **resolver-owned empty/false opt-out consistency** and **separating explicit inline current-message resolution from implicit correlation policy**. The reported QA dedupe mismatch was not established: that resolver returns a native message reference without `threadId: null`, while the dedupe owner treats `replyToId` as a conversation thread only for the explicit-null transport contract. No new unresolved P0–P2 regression was independently confirmed in this candidate.

prs.title: fix: keep native chat math warm when caches fill
prs.body:
Related: #198080 (same eviction pattern; this change does not depend on that PR).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unnecessary repeated math parsing and image rendering in native chat when adding an expression fills the existing math caches.

## User Impact

Previously rendered expressions can remain warm as more math arrives, without changing typography, grouping, sidebar animation, word fade, or raw-source fallbacks. No configuration or migration is needed. Native build, performance measurements, and before/after video are still pending; keep this PR in draft for the Mac validation loop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both 80-entry math caches currently discard all entries on the next miss. They now evict only the oldest entry. Cached parse failures still occupy a bounded slot, and hits do not reorder entries or add bookkeeping work. FIFO deliberately keeps the fix small; a working set larger than 80 entries can still miss.

The image key also includes the display scale already used by its pixel-budget guard, so a scale change cannot reuse an image without rechecking that budget. Font size and resolved color remain part of the key. Parser guards, source-byte limits, bitmap bounds, SwiftMath configuration, and baseline calculation are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Base: `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`. Inspected the complete math owner, its display/inline consumers, and pinned SwiftMath 1.7.3 image/label implementations.
- `git diff --check` passed. Author simplification retained two short owner-local FIFO queues, with no generic cache framework or test-only production hooks. Production delta: +13/−4 lines; test delta: +77/−0 lines.
- Two new owner-boundary regressions exercise the real parse and image caches across capacity, including bounded cached failures, bitmap identity/baseline reuse, font/theme separation, and the non-ASCII Kelvin-sign fallback. The existing pixel-budget test also checks the same logical size at 2× and 3×.
- Independent autoreview (OpenClaw engine, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) completed with no findings on the local candidate against that base. Reviewed patch SHA-256: `d9678f29aa1f195a4470a30c73499683df55c7b4473692edddc41f1ee169485f`. This is static review, not native execution.
- **Pending:** Swift 6.3 compilation, native red/green regression runs, SwiftFormat 0.63.1 / SwiftLint 0.65.1, iOS simulator/device build, scale-transition checks, before/after video, and performance timing/memory evidence. This environment is Linux and has no Swift/Xcode/native formatting tools. Test wall time and CI seconds are not measured.

Source-bound acceptance workload: `ChatInlineMathTests` admits one unknown-command failure followed by 80 distinct `x_{910000…910079}` parses, then repeats the failed parse 80 times; the image case admits 81 distinct `x_{920000…920080}` renders at 12 pt and revisits the preceding render after every insertion, then interleaves 18 pt and dark-theme requests. Both call the actual cache owners and use object identity as the no-recompute oracle, without test-only production hooks. Test runtime and CI cost, including real native math rendering, are unknown.

Acceptance rule for the Mac run: run these committed capacity-crossing regressions plus the same synthetic transcript containing more than 80 distinct completed expressions, revisiting recent neighbors as new math arrives. A newly inserted expression must retain the preceding warm parse/image object; cached failures and total capacity must stay bounded. Run the real transcript workload on base and candidate interleaved, at least five cold and five warm samples per revision; record parser/render work counts, median/p95 and spread, main-thread time, frame hitches, and memory. No appearance or user-facing performance regression is acceptable. Source inspection predicts 79 unaffected entries retained instead of zero at a full-cache miss; native counts and timing remain unmeasured.

Focused Mac commands (record the exact checked-out candidate SHA; Xcode 27.1+ / Swift 6.3):

```sh
git rev-parse HEAD
xcodebuild -version
swift --version
./scripts/check-swift-tools.sh
SRC=apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatInlineMath.swift
TEST=apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Tests/OpenClawKitTests/ChatInlineMathTests.swift
swiftformat --lint "$SRC" "$TEST" --config config/swiftformat \
  --unexclude "$PWD/$SRC,$PWD/$TEST"
node scripts/run-swiftlint.mts --strict --config apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml "$SRC" "$TEST"
/usr/bin/time -p swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit \
  --filter 'ChatInlineMathTests|ChatMathBlockViewTests|ChatMarkdownRendererTests|ChatMarkdownBlockSegmenterTests'
IOS_DEST="generic/platform=iOS Simulator" pnpm ios:build
```

For baseline-red proof, apply only the test-file diff to a separate checkout at the recorded base and run `ChatInlineMathTests`; expect an object-retention assertion to fail, not a build/setup failure. The user's Mac agent supplies exact-head compilation/test results and before/after video. Compare light/dark, Dynamic Type, display scale, raw-source fallbacks, baseline alignment, grouping, sidebar animation, and word fade. No speedup is measured or claimed here.

Human contributor credit: Vyctor Brzezowski and Mike Nguyen.
