prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

## Browser evidence

Existing sanitized synthetic captures illustrate shorthand and desktop/mobile Settings presentation; they are not live OAuth or current-head runtime qualification.

prs.title: feat(message): recommend one exact ClawHub plugin in chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Template setup needs to recommend the exact plugin its author named, rather than a fuzzy search result. Server-started setup can also publish a card before live chat adopts its run ID; that card was saved but dropped from the live view.

## User Impact

Agents can show one exact ClawHub plugin card by package name, including during server-started setup without reloading. Official plugins keep Install; community plugins offer View details for normal review. Unknown packages show no card.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an exact-package option alongside existing ClawHub search, keeps intermediate card publication non-final when requested, and admits only native sequenced producer-owned intermediate replies before local run adoption. This is the foundation of the chat-based Template Add stack.

## Evidence

- Initial exact-card layer: 61 focused tests pass; five integration cases fail without the production change.
- Live admission repair: recorded-row regression changes zero cards to one; repository-standard integrated runner passes 65/65 across four files. UI typecheck and focused lint/format pass.
- [Real full-stack before/after and View details proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198065#issuecomment-6843632949): real model, Travel Copilot 0.2.8, isolated Gateway. One community card appears in the original chat without reload, and View details opens the correct review page. No plugin installation or enablement occurs.
- Pending chat 120ms; durable admission event 6.28s; first visible reply 56.5s. These are different timing boundaries.
- The recorder preserved a stale-selector harness error after successful live-card assertions; screenshots confirm navigation. Intermittent screencast-size corruption means clean final-head video proof is still pending, not claimed complete.
- Aggregate changed-file validation has inherited dead-export findings; it is not reported green. Production Gateways were unchanged.

prs.title: fix(gateway): session diff and file reads fail when another worktree is created or removed
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198061

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `sessions.diff` for a sandboxed session on a managed worktree fails with `WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved` when any other worktree is created or removed during the diff's registry read, although the session's own worktree did not change. Session file reads and Control UI assistant media reads of a sandboxed session have the same guard and the same failure.

## User Impact

User impact: reading a sandboxed session's diff, its files, or assistant media from its workspace no longer fails because another session or tool created or removed a worktree at the same moment. A removal of the session's own worktree during the read still fails it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readLocalWorkspaceReviewBase` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-review.ts`, used by `sessions.diff`) and `readLocalWorkspacePath` (`src/gateway/worker-environments/local-workspace-read.ts`, used by session file reads and assistant media reads) both know the session's worktree id before they read the worktree registry, but captured the lifecycle read guard without a selection. The guard then watched every registry row, so any unrelated publication during the read rejected it. Both now pass the same `{ id, ownerKind: "session" }` selection that https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197561 passed in `resolveLocalWorkspaceOwner` and `expireLocalWorkspaceProjection` for the same failure in sandbox startup. `readLocalWorkspacePath` reads by path and already rejects a row with another id, so the selection only drops the watch on unrelated rows.

## Evidence

Tested at this PR's head (base `main` `bb97be6b37b`).

A real Gateway on Linux x64 with isolated state and config: the agent workspace is a one-commit git repository, sandbox `mode: "all"`, `scope: "session"`, `workspaceAccess: "rw"`, Docker backend, and a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in model that answers `ok`. A WebSocket driver creates a session with `worktree: true`, sends one message and waits for the run (this provisions the sandboxed local workspace), then calls `sessions.diff { scope: "all", summaryOnly: true }` 1000 times on that session while two other lanes loop `worktrees.create` and `worktrees.remove { force: true }` for unrelated manual worktrees in the same repository.

Before (base `main` `bb97be6b37b`):

```text
sessions.diff 300 calls:  {"ok":297,"contention":3,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 4/4
sessions.diff 1000 calls: {"ok":996,"contention":4,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 11/11
diff error WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved

[gateway] request handler failed: WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved
[ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.diff 3ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved
```

After (this PR):

```text
sessions.diff 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 12/12
sessions.diff 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 8/8
sessions.diff 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 9/9
```

Observed result: with the same driver and setup, the diff calls fail with the contention error on base (3 of 300 and 4 of 1000) and none of 3000 fail at the head; the Gateway log at the head has no contention line and no failed `sessions.diff` response.

Session file reads, same setup and driver, reading `README.md` with `sessions.files.get` (this reaches `readLocalWorkspacePath` through `prepareSessionFileReadPath`) 1000 times per run, each run on a new session, under the same churn of unrelated worktrees. Before is a Gateway built at base `bb97be6b37b` in a separate clean worktree; After is the head build used above.

Before (base `main` `bb97be6b37b`):

```text
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":989,"contention":11,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 26/26
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":993,"contention":7,"other":0}    unrelated worktrees created/removed 21/21
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":996,"contention":4,"other":0}    unrelated worktrees created/removed 21/20

[ws] ⇄ res ✗ sessions.files.get 4ms errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=WorktreeRemovalContentionError: Worktree owner or binding changed; checkout preserved
```

After (this PR):

```text
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 26/26
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 22/22
sessions.files.get 1000 calls: {"ok":1000,"contention":0,"other":0}   unrelated worktrees created/removed 21/21
```

Observed result: the file reads fail with the contention error on base in 22 of 3000 calls and in none of 3000 at the head; the head Gateway log has no contention line and no failed `sessions.files.get` response. On base, one unrelated `worktrees.remove` in the churn failed on its own removal guard, which this PR does not change, and left one unrelated worktree behind; at the head the churn hit that worktree's leftover branch once per run on `worktrees.create` and went on.

Checks: `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/registry-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (13 passed). The new "scopes the local workspace %s read across %s" cases call `readLocalWorkspaceReviewBase` and `readLocalWorkspacePath` and, while their registry read is in flight, publish an unrelated worktree or remove the selected one.

- With the base versions of both production files, the two unrelated-publication cases fail (`promise rejected "WorktreeRemovalContentionError: ..." instead of resolving`). With only `local-workspace-read.ts` from base, the path case fails the same way, from `readLocalWorkspacePath`.
- The selected-removal cases pass on both sides. With the guard dropped from both readers, both selected-removal cases fail (`promise resolved ... instead of rejecting`), so they pin that the scoped guard still rejects a change to the session's own worktree.
- The changed-file lint and the test-lines ratchet pass. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `bb97be6b37b` to head `3dc0f274521`, priority P0–P1: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"bb97be6b37b1fe14fc74a38a904efce340cdef91","head":"3dc0f274521dbd4906ab9c545da45b4b7118052c","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

| Test file                                       | `--maxWorkers=1` wall                         | CI seconds         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `src/agents/sandbox/registry-authority.test.ts` | 30.1 s (the four new cases 1.6 s each)        | after this PR's CI |

Test lines: +39 net (68 added, 29 removed), within the ratchet allowance. The interleave helper moves out of the existing unrelated-publication test and takes the registry reader to intercept, so all three owners use it. Production: +4 / -1 in each of `local-workspace-review.ts` and `local-workspace-read.ts`.

Not covered:

- Control UI assistant media reads go through the same `readLocalWorkspacePath` but were not driven through a Gateway; the session file read runs and the unit test cover that function.
- When no registry row is at the read path, `readLocalWorkspacePath` keeps its read guard, now scoped to the expected id; a different worktree created at that same path afterwards is no longer watched by it.
- Guards of other kinds without a selection (record, exact-owner, exact-snapshot, publication, source-record, session-owner) protect other invariants and are not changed here.
- The publications in the proof come from manual `worktrees.create` and `worktrees.remove`; another session starting its own managed worktree goes through the same registry insert but was not driven.
- Linux with Docker only.

prs.title: fix(ci): avoid full lint for declaration words in comments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mentioning `declare` in a comment or runtime string can make a small PR run full type-aware lint instead of its affected files and consumers.

## User Impact

CI retains focused lint for these changes. Real declarations, declaration files, unsupported syntax, and parse failures still retain full lint. No application behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ambient-impact check matched raw text. Use Node's existing syntax-erasure API to distinguish preserved comment/string text from erased TypeScript syntax, checking every original match at its preserved offset. This avoids another hand-written lexer and keeps uncertain inputs conservative.

A concrete source example is the opening comment in `src/media/input-files.extract.test.ts`; its import graph has no consumers, but the old text match still requests full lint.

## Evidence

- The new regression failed on the base: expected the changed file and its consumer, received full fallback.
- All 31 tests in `test/scripts/ci-changed-lint.test.ts` passed in 8.51s (wrapper 9.46s).
- Scripts and tooling-test typechecks passed.
- Targeted lint and format checks passed.
- Independent diff review found no blockers. Local ClawSweeper completed on `cf00ecdeebd557e28a683da646094ecdb31b6a8d` with no blocking findings; it did not receive the separate execution evidence above.
- Linux proof: [Blacksmith Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43362016862), using the focused 2-vCPU profile.

Scope-verification acceptance rule, declared before measuring the real-file plan: five serial base/candidate comparisons of the committed `scripts/ci-check-plan.mts` entry point for `src/media/input-files.extract.test.ts`. Require the base's full core lint fallback to disappear while the candidate still selects the changed file, with the declaration and parse-failure regressions green. Count planned work; do not infer wall-time or invoice savings from it.

All five comparisons passed the scope rule:

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full core lint rows | 5 | 0 |
| Core/extension lint matrix rows | 5 | 2 |
| Explicit core files | full stripes | 1 changed test |
| Extension stripe selections | 3 | same 3 |
| Planner median / p95 | 0.298s / 0.302s | 16.935s / 17.213s |

The candidate pays about 17 seconds for dependency discovery that the old early fallback skipped. These are planner timings, not complete CI timings. The eliminated full-core passes are the intended work reduction; no end-to-end speedup or billing saving is claimed.

The initial probe incorrectly assumed one total matrix row and stopped at the retained extension owner. The completed probe checks unchanged extension selections instead; production code and the acceptance rule did not change.

prs.title: improve(postgres): read each chat history page from one database snapshot
prs.body:
Closes #197313
Related: #188956, #190129 (#188956 tracks the worker queueing in front of `chat.history` on PostgreSQL, which #190129 addresses)

## What Problem This Solves

On PostgreSQL, some `chat.history` pages open a new read-only transaction for each step of the page read instead of one: a sparse page (few visible replies among many silent ones) takes three `BEGIN ... READ ONLY` / `ROLLBACK` round trips over the database bridge, and a Claude CLI session after a provider switch takes seven. When the database is across a network hop, every extra round trip adds to the page's response time.

## User Impact

User impact: each `chat.history` page on PostgreSQL is read from one database snapshot. Sparse pages and Claude CLI sessions after a provider switch now take one transaction for the page instead of three or seven, which makes those pages faster when PostgreSQL is not on loopback: with about 3.4 ms added round trip, median latency drops by 14 to 26 ms for a sparse page and about 40 ms for a Claude CLI session after a provider switch (see Evidence). Pages that already took one transaction read the same rows with the same SQL, but cost more on a loopback database: the history worker spends about 0.25 ms more per request at 1 and 8 clients, which shows as 9.5 to 12.9% lower throughput alone and 13.5% lower at 8 clients with #190129, with higher p95 and p99 (see the pair bench under Evidence). Returned messages and pagination are unchanged, and SQLite is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker runs one task at a time, and no read snapshot outlives a task. The `chat.history` page task now holds one PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot from its first read until the page is assembled. That covers the Claude CLI import check (revision read and, after a provider switch, its tail read) and every page and tail-scan read. Every read still goes through the read scope's admission (`acquire`), so validation and path checks run per read as before. A failed read rolls the held snapshot back and the next read opens a fresh one. A failed rollback retires the connection, as `runPostgresTransactionSync` does, and the snapshot uses the same `BEGIN` and read-snapshot scope.

Scope: this changes the page task only. The pending-input read that the handler issues before the page is its own worker request with its own snapshot, and the history reader cap (#169110) is untouched. It keeps the eager read-only `BEGIN` (the deferred `BEGIN` in #188952 was closed unmerged).

Scope: this closes #197313 (one read snapshot per history page). The worker queueing in #188956 is separate and is #190129; the two changes touch different files and are measured on their own. This one removes 2 or 6 read-only transactions (4 or 12 round trips) per affected page with no other behavior change.

### Accepted decision: PostgreSQL latency tradeoff

On November 13, 2026, @Patrick-Erichsen instructed landing after the network-hop benefits and measured dense-loopback regressions were disclosed in the [review and landing discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/89f4bf42-824d-42df-a83d-8715b2bd5292). This records acceptance of the current one-snapshot-per-page proposal and its disclosed tradeoff, including one-client throughput of 159.0 to 138.55 calls/s and p99 of 12.85 to 15.84 ms, and eight-client p99 of 26.26 to 55.06 ms when paired with #190129. It is not a universal performance improvement. The linked discussion is for team reference and requires sign-in.

No code or benchmark data changed for this decision. Existing proof keeps its actual executing revisions and the coverage limits below.

## Evidence

Evidence files: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/assets/pg-r2-l3c-history-snapshot-evidence/current-source (paths below are relative to it; `README.md` there describes each file). PostgreSQL 17.11, isolated Gateways built with `pnpm build` from each tree.

Original experimental acceptance rule (the dense-loopback exception is explicitly accepted above): through a running Gateway, sparse and Claude CLI provider-switch pages read in one page snapshot with the same reads and messages; with a real network hop, their p50 and p95 drop by roughly the saved round trips times the round trip time; pages that already use one snapshot do not change; no metric moves the wrong way.

- **Gateway A/B with a network hop** (`network-hop/`). Base `3c130c7268e` (this head's `main` parent), fix `213409bf` (same PR source as the current head). The Gateway reaches PostgreSQL through toxiproxy with 1 ms latency toxics on each stream. Measured `SELECT 1` round trip: 0.44 ms without the toxics, 3.77 ms before the runs and 3.85 ms after (`network-hop/rtt.txt`). The store was seeded through the Gateway's own RPCs. It has a sparse session (1 visible reply, 250 silent replies, 1 visible reply) and a Claude CLI session made by one real `chat.send` turn through a stub `claude` binary on `PATH` (the stream-json stub from `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/reply-run-plugin-reload.product-proof.e2e.test.ts`, no API key), followed by 250 silent replies and a visible one, and then switched to the default OpenAI model with `sessions.patch`. Both use `limit: 2`. There were 5 runs per arm in ABBA order (base fix fix base base fix fix base base fix). Each run restores the same database template and boots the arm. It warms, traces 3 calls per session, then runs a 20 s closed-loop `chat.history` load per session at concurrency 1 and 8 after a 5 s warmup, with statement logging off. A run starts only when the 1-minute load average is below the 32 cores (`network-hop/load-gates.txt`).

  Read-only transactions per call (`network-hop/SUMMARY-snapshots.txt`; runs N4 to N10 carry a statement trace, N1 to N3 latency only):

| shape | arm | runs x calls | page snapshots | page reads | pending-input snapshots |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sparse session | base | 4 x 3 | 3.0 | 11.0 | 1.0 |
| sparse session | fix | 3 x 3 | 1.0 | 11.0 | 1.0 |
| Claude CLI session after a provider switch | base | 4 x 3 | 7.0 | 23.0 | 1.0 |
| Claude CLI session after a provider switch | fix | 3 x 3 | 1.0 | 23.0 | 1.0 |
| 4 imported Claude Code threads | base and fix | 7 x 12 | 1.0 | 3.0 | 1.0 |

  Latency, median of the 5 per-run values (range) in ms, no errors in any run (`network-hop/SUMMARY-latency.txt`, per run in `network-hop/runs/*/load-*.json` with the 1-minute load recorded at start and end):

| shape | concurrency | arm | p50 | p95 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sparse | 1 | base | 89.54 (86.70 to 100.37) | 101.18 (93.17 to 116.49) | 115.00 (93.91 to 121.88) |
| sparse | 1 | fix | 75.69 (71.11 to 85.72) | 103.37 (83.60 to 116.78) | 112.35 (90.50 to 212.93) |
| sparse | 8 | base | 171.09 (157.09 to 175.80) | 192.44 (168.67 to 233.24) | 234.65 (214.77 to 264.21) |
| sparse | 8 | fix | 144.65 (135.19 to 167.16) | 162.76 (153.67 to 248.04) | 195.39 (162.52 to 273.79) |
| Claude CLI after switch | 1 | base | 174.21 (164.71 to 179.52) | 234.17 (204.74 to 284.76) | 249.55 (211.94 to 421.65) |
| Claude CLI after switch | 1 | fix | 132.55 (119.25 to 138.00) | 171.47 (127.20 to 229.39) | 196.63 (136.80 to 269.81) |
| Claude CLI after switch | 8 | base | 246.90 (245.67 to 277.02) | 326.56 (323.03 to 373.99) | 356.10 (342.10 to 424.84) |
| Claude CLI after switch | 8 | fix | 207.56 (198.27 to 219.93) | 262.89 (257.81 to 285.03) | 274.96 (265.30 to 314.48) |

  The sparse page saves 2 `BEGIN` and 2 `ROLLBACK` round trips, about 15 ms at 3.8 ms each, and its p50 drops by 13.85 ms at concurrency 1 and 26.44 ms at concurrency 8. At concurrency 1 the sparse p95 is flat (101.18 vs 103.37, within the run ranges), and at concurrency 8 it drops by 29.68 ms. The Claude CLI page saves 6 and 6, about 46 ms, and its p50 drops by 41.66 and 39.34 ms and its p95 by 62.70 and 63.67 ms. The runs started below the core count, but the 1-minute load during them ranged from 4.3 to 37.0 because the host is shared. No cell got worse beyond its range.

- **Running Gateway statement trace on loopback** (`gateway-trace/`, previous head `27ab37717af` vs its `main` parent `7c2ff8f775a`, same code): sparse session 3.0 vs 1.0 page snapshots (7 x 3 calls per arm, reads 11 = 11); imported Claude Code threads and a 12-session `limit: 100` shape stay at 1.0 on both arms. On loopback the latency did not move (`gateway-trace/SUMMARY-latency.txt`), as expected when a round trip costs well under a millisecond.
- **Regression test** (new, live PostgreSQL), red on base and green with the change (`tests/conformance-red.log`, `tests/conformance-green.log`). Read-only `BEGIN`s for one page, base vs fix: sparse page 3 vs 1, Claude CLI session after a provider switch 7 vs 1. A third test checks that a failed statement inside the held snapshot is rolled back and the next read works.
- **Live PostgreSQL conformance** (PostgreSQL 17.11): the new test plus the bridge, read-facts, reuse, publication, hydration, agent and state database suites, 15 files and 165 tests pass on head `213409bf` (`tests/conformance-green-new-head.log`) and again on head `5af7f878` merged into current `main` `10592dacdc6` (`ci-lanes/conformance-merge-into-main-10592dac.log`). Consumer unit tests for the changed modules pass on the previous head, 16 files and 223 tests (`tests/unit-fix.log`). `pnpm check:changed` on the previous head merged into `main` `638a1851e7e` (`ci-lanes/check-changed-merge-into-current-main.log`): typecheck, format, lint (0 errors), Knip (0 unused exports) and the guards pass. The one failure is `changelog attributions` on existing `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `CHANGELOG/2026.7.1.md` entries, which fails the same way on that `main` (`ci-lanes/changelog-attributions-current-main.log`).
- **CI lanes**: the red lanes on head `5af7f878` came from the `main` that CI merged it into (`4ca233c908c`), not from this branch, which touches no `ui/` files and allocates exactly the 146 test lines it adds.
  - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` failed only `test-lines` (`over by: 50; net delta: +146`, `ci-lanes/ci-run-42356893636-excerpt.txt`). Plain `main` `4ca233c908c` is already over by 50 with no change at all (`ci-lanes/test-lines-plain-main-4ca233c9.log`), and the CI merge tree reproduces the CI result (`ci-lanes/test-lines-ci-merge-5af7f878-into-4ca233c9.log`). `main` reconciled the ceiling in #194509. Merged into current `main` `10592dacdc6`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes all 10 checks (test lines slack 21; `ci-lanes/baseline-ratchets-merge-into-main-10592dac.log`).
  - `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)` failed one test, `ui/src/e2e/gateway-fresh-visit.http.e2e.test.ts:175` ("Matcher did not succeed in time"). It fails the same way on plain `main` `4ca233c908c` (`ci-lanes/ui-e2e-gateway-fresh-visit-plain-main-4ca233c9.log`) and was fixed on `main` by #194504. Merged into current `main`, that file passes 3 of 3 (`ci-lanes/ui-e2e-gateway-fresh-visit-merge-into-main-10592dac.log`), and the other 18 files of that shard pass (`ci-lanes/ui-e2e-shard1-files-merge-into-main-10592dac.log`; the one WebKit test there needed WebKit installed locally and then passed 2 of 2, `ci-lanes/ui-e2e-mcp-fullscreen-webkit-rerun-merge-into-main-10592dac.log`).
  - `openclaw/ci-gate` only aggregates the two lanes above.

- **Pair bench on current `main` `82210a2bbdb0`** (`pair-bench/`): four builds from one `main` (`main`, `main` + this PR, `main` + #190129, `main` + both), four runs each in interleaved order, PostgreSQL 17.11, closed-loop `chat.history` at 1, 8, 16 and 32 clients. Gate results on the same `main`: PostgreSQL conformance 15 files / 165 tests pass with this PR and with both PRs (3 tests fail on plain `main`); unit 16 / 224 with this PR, 28 / 386 with both (`pair-bench/tests/`). This store has dense pages only, which already read in one page snapshot on `main`, so the database work is the same on all four builds (`BEGIN` 2.00 per call at 1 client, statements per call within 0.1, `pgss.tsv`). End to end, this PR is slower on it at 1 and 8 clients, alone and together with #190129. Medians of 4 runs (`medians.tsv`), p50 / p95 / p99 in ms and calls/s:

| clients | `main` | + this PR | + #190129 | + both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.01 / 10.47 / 12.85 / 159.0 | 6.9 / 11.79 / 15.84 / 138.55 | 6.31 / 12.75 / 21.33 / 136.4 | 7.24 / 13.3 / 20.23 / 125.6 |
| 8 | 19.65 / 32.55 / 46.48 / 385.0 | 20.75 / 37.58 / 54.23 / 348.35 | 13.84 / 20.29 / 26.26 / 555.25 | 15.21 / 26.02 / 55.06 / 480.2 |
| 16 | 41.94 / 70.81 / 95.38 / 362.05 | 40.14 / 66.81 / 89.35 / 361.05 | 29.21 / 52.3 / 67.81 / 506.85 | 29.57 / 45.42 / 81.27 / 507.3 |
| 32 | 79.41 / 112.25 / 199.78 / 372.35 | 79.47 / 113.22 / 202.16 / 376.1 | 58.09 / 67.92 / 88.81 / 545.0 | 58.06 / 91.12 / 128.55 / 529.4 |

  Moved the wrong way with this PR, against `main`: at 1 client p50 +15% (6.90 vs 6.01 ms), p95 +13% (11.79 vs 10.47 ms), p99 +23% (15.84 vs 12.85 ms) and throughput -12.9% (138.55 vs 159.0 calls/s); at 8 clients p50 +6% (20.75 vs 19.65 ms), p95 +15% (37.58 vs 32.55 ms), p99 +17% (54.23 vs 46.48 ms) and throughput -9.5% (348.35 vs 385.0 calls/s); at 32 clients p50, p95 and p99 within 1.2%. Against #190129 alone, with both PRs: at 1 client p50 +15% (7.24 vs 6.31 ms), p95 +4% (13.3 vs 12.75 ms) and throughput -7.9% (125.6 vs 136.4 calls/s); at 8 clients p50 +10% (15.21 vs 13.84 ms), p95 +28% (26.02 vs 20.29 ms), p99 from 26.26 to 55.06 ms (also above `main`, 46.48 ms) and throughput -13.5% (480.2 vs 555.25 calls/s); at 16 clients p99 +20% (81.27 vs 67.81 ms); at 32 clients p95 +34% (91.12 vs 67.92 ms), p99 +45% (128.55 vs 88.81 ms) and throughput -2.9% (529.4 vs 545.0 calls/s).

  Host load: at 8 clients, this PR alone is slower than `main` in 3 of 4 rounds, but `main` started those arms at lower load (3.8 to 4.4 vs 5.5 to 10.1, `arms.tsv`), so these rounds alone do not rule load out. With both PRs it is slower than #190129 alone in 4 of 4 rounds, including round 3 where it started at lower load (6.7 vs 12.8) and round 2 at about equal load (6.1 vs 5.9). In the profiled runs below, this PR started both 8-client runs at lower load than `main` (6.5 and 8.0 vs 8.6 and 9.3, `cpu-profile/run-order-and-load.txt`) and was still slower (p50 28.72 and 28.88 vs 26.78 and 28.14 ms, `cpu-profile/runs-h8.txt`).

  The database runs the same statements on all builds; the extra time shows in the history worker. Worker time per request (`worker-time.tsv`) is 2.043 vs 1.804 ms at 1 client and 2.630 vs 2.373 ms at 8 clients against `main`, 3.741 vs 3.229 ms at 8 clients against #190129 alone, and equal at 16 and 32 clients. A CPU profile of the history workers at 8 clients (2 runs per build, `cpu-profile/`; profiling slows every build, so only the difference is used) shows the workers busier by 123 µs per worker request with this PR. Of that, 62 µs is waiting for database replies to the same statements, about 10 µs is garbage collection, and the rest is spread thinly, with no other function moving by more than 6 µs. With statement counts unchanged, the average wait per statement is longer; why was not isolated, and the profile does not separate database time from bridge transport time. The saving on sparse and provider-switch pages, which grows with the database round trip, is measured in `network-hop/` above.

### Gaps

- The network hop is simulated with toxiproxy on one host, not a remote database. The saving scales with the real round trip time.
- This fixes #197313 only. The worker queueing in #188956 is #190129, and the two changes touch different files. The acceptance rule above is not met on the pair bench: on a loopback database with dense pages only, this PR costs about 0.24 to 0.26 ms of history worker time per request at 1 and 8 clients alone (throughput -12.9% at 1 client and -9.5% at 8 clients) and about 0.51 ms at 8 clients with #190129 (throughput -13.5%). The trade is still worth taking when PostgreSQL sits behind a network hop: each snapshot this PR removes saves two round trips (about 7.6 ms at the measured 3.8 ms round trip, 15 ms per sparse page, 46 ms per Claude CLI page after a provider switch), while the added cost on this bench is under 0.6 ms of worker time per request with identical SQL. Whether that cost grows with the round trip was not measured: the profile puts part of it in waiting for replies, so it may. It is not worth it for a loopback database that serves only dense pages. Ending the snapshot right after the last read was not tried: the page code interleaves reads with projection (tail scans project between reads, and reply attachment can read), so there is no single point after the last read without restructuring the page reader.
- After a provider switch, the Claude CLI import check still reads the tail twice (now inside one snapshot). This is a possible follow-up, as is sharing a snapshot with the pending-input request.

prs.title: fix(talk): subagent launches fail during direct agent consults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes operator-owned Talk agent consults losing the Gateway binding needed for subagent launches when no ambient Gateway request scope is available.

## User Impact

Talk consults retain their original Gateway for delegated tools instead of hitting `Operator subagent spawn requires its current Gateway binding`. No configuration changes, permission expansion, or migration is needed; the spawn guard and source/abort lifetime checks remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Talk runtime already receives the owning resolver but does not bind it to the admitted execution context. Bind it through the existing `onAdmitted` callback, as other ingress paths do, without adding an ambient/global fallback or tying accepted work to the audio transport. The production repair remains four lines.

One three-row regression extends the existing spawn production-boundary suite and shared support, replacing the weaker resolver-only assertions in the terminal-write tests. It enters the production Talk consult runner with a retained authenticated operator, invokes the actual `sessions_spawn` tool without ambient Gateway request scope, and uses real Gateway dispatch and child admission.

- Authorized caller: the original Gateway admits the child; its real admitted run, RPC source, and registry/session ownership are observed.
- Caller revoked after Talk admission and child preparation: real device-source invalidation rejects dispatch before child admission/registration.
- Gateway replaced after Talk admission and child preparation: dispatch rejects, with neither original nor replacement facade admitting child work.

## Evidence

- Red control: remove only the four production-fix lines. The authorized operator case fails at `subagent-spawn.ts:148` with `Operator subagent spawn requires its current Gateway binding`. Production bytes are restored afterward.
- Corrected final fixture: all three Talk child-admission cases pass. Command wall time: approximately 78s including cold compilation; test bodies total approximately 11.23s. The real dispatch/admission composition, not inference, is the required proof boundary.
- Existing Talk terminal-write/abort contracts remain intact: final rerun 3/3 pass, approximately 19s wall. The earlier three-file Talk sibling run passed 24/24, approximately 102s wall.
- Targeted lint, formatting, scoped test typecheck, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh isolated independent AutoReview of the complete corrected candidate: no actionable P0-P2 findings.

### CI import-cycle follow-up

Removed the new result-helper back-import from the shared spawn support, keeping the two deterministic result fixtures local and equivalent. No tests or production behavior were added or changed. The exact failing Madge check went from one cycle to zero; all three affected Talk cases pass again (approximately 91.58s wall, including cold compilation). Targeted lint, format, scoped typecheck, and a fresh independent review of this small repair pass. Current-head hosted CI is separate from this local verification.

### Investigated local failures

The broader spawn owner-file run before the final operator-fixture correction had 80 passing and six failing existing native Stop cases (approximately 313s wall). All six also fail with the owner tests restored to unchanged published-head versions: `preserves routed native Stop authority and existing receipts` for `retained-exact`, `consumed-channel`, `consumed-command-handler`, `consumed-session`, `consumed-generation-replaced`, and `consumed-active-revoked`. Assertions concern existing command-exit/source-abort behavior; these failures remain unresolved and are not reported green. After the fixture correction, only the affected three rows, terminal-write tests, and static checks were rerun; the broad file was not repeated.

## Real-provider after-fix Talk smoke

PASS on exact head 04ec91b6213af1085b6f9878ce4f21f9079fb05e, source-built runtime/UI with matching build identity, isolated fresh-state Gateway. One persistent signed/authenticated public Gateway SDK connection called the shipped Talk relay create/audio/close endpoints. Synthetic spoken input was transcribed by the real voice provider, which initiated the native Talk agent consultation. No chat.send substitution, direct consult helper, inference mock, or driver-issued child spawn was used.

Observed native consult run: talk-realtime-relay-consult-d17cbe3e-5402-4034-a5c5-9adfbb78990d. The real backing model invoked sessions_spawn and received accepted child run c2d42987-f809-40b6-98ec-2124a63fc392. It then invoked agents_wait, which returned that same child as done with exactly TALK_CHILD_OK. Independent child history confirmed the exact output. A reduced/redacted event capture is supplied in the PR discussion; credentials, endpoints/IPs, binary audio and model identifiers are omitted.

One create attempt, no retries. The same owner connection closed Talk successfully. The temporary Gateway shut down cleanly and its container/listener were removed; all 11 task-private databases pass integrity checks. Original Gateway process identity and config/runtime/native-auth hashes remain unchanged.

## Main-merge compatibility repair

After main was merged into this branch, upstream's Talk refactor had relocated resolveTalkAgentConsultAuthority into client-tool-authority.ts. The added boundary fixture still imported it from client-gateway-control.ts, causing the same missing-export/setup error in the three Talk cases and both production/test typechecks. Commit d923b93eb6f537b7da0f7750dc1db1c74aaa46ce changes only that one test import to its current owner.

On the synchronized source, the three focused Talk cases pass (83 unrelated owner-file cases intentionally skipped), both tsconfig.core.json and the agents-sessions test typecheck pass, and one-file lint/format/diff checks plus fresh independent review pass. Production code and test assertions are unchanged. Fresh hosted CI is pending; the earlier accepted live capture remains evidence for its explicitly pinned 04ec91b6 revision, not a new runtime trial.

## Current-main conflict reconciliation

Merge commit 602ceecc042e76350945b53fd4a188551d913b91 incorporates pinned main 904703bef63222ab459cbabdd7556bdb3e542fec. The two manual test conflicts retain both upstream Access-case registrations and all three Talk authority cases, and adopt upstream terminal-write import/type cleanup without restoring tests upstream removed. The terminal-write file matches pinned main exactly. Net PR changes against that main are three files, +254 lines; the only production change remains the four-line admission binding.

Fresh production, agents-sessions, and gateway-other typechecks pass, as do lint/format/diff checks for the resolved files. Independent review of the complete net PR candidate found no actionable P0-P2 defect. Current-main runtime tests are NOT reported green: compiled-subprocess preparation was killed twice by kernel-confirmed host-wide OOM before collecting/executing any tests (exit 137); terminal-write preparation was stopped to prevent another OOM (exit 143). No assertion verdict or current-head runtime proof is claimed. A heap-budget alternative was denied by execution policy and not bypassed. Fresh hosted CI owns runtime verification for this merge; prior passing runtime evidence is pinned to its older revision.

GitHub reports this pushed head mergeable rather than conflicting. Additional upstream movement was checked without editing the branch using merge-tree and was conflict-free; checks/reviews remain separate from mergeability. Nothing was merged into upstream or deployed.

## Proof Limits

Automated regression inference is deterministic and mocked; the separate after-fix Talk relay smoke below used real provider speech/delegation and real backing/child model execution. It is headless relay proof with synthetic speech, not browser UI, microphone, acoustic-playback, native-app, WebRTC, or deployed voice-recovery proof. Exact admitted binding is source-traced through the shipped native Talk path, not a runtime admission-object audit dump. Automated revocation/replacement is triggered immediately before real child dispatch, not exhaustively at every internal suspension. Maintainer/security-review acceptance remains separate. Nothing was merged, deployed, or changed in the running installation.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): converge NFD titles to the canonical page and preserve released identities
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A memory-wiki page whose title contains accented characters, typed in a different Unicode normalization form than an existing page, silently creates a **second** page file instead of linking to the existing one — so `[[Café]]` written in NFC and `[[Café]]` written in NFD resolve to two different `.md` files and the link is broken. The first fix NFC-normalized the shared `slugifyWikiSegment` helper, which repaired the new-vault case but broke **released** vaults: an already-published decomposed (`cafe` + U+0301) page was renamed to `café` on upgrade, orphaning its hand-written Notes and frontmatter ID. This revision keeps machine-derived identity byte-stable (the shared helper is untouched) and resolves a released page by **canonical (NFC) equivalence** across *every* normalization form — NFC, fully decomposed NFD, or a mixed spelling such as `café-naïve` — so both the original bug and the upgrade regression are fixed without changing released identities.

- Problem: `slugifyWikiSegment` lowercases but never NFC-normalizes, so NFC vs NFD editions of one visual title produce two distinct slugs/files, and `[[links]]` in the other normalization form cannot resolve.
- Solution (this revision): new pages derive their stem from the NFC-normalized title, but before writing we enumerate the published pages and **reuse any existing stem whose NFC-normalized slug equals the incoming title's** — regardless of how that released page was originally normalized. The comparison layer (`related-pages.ts`, `lint.ts`) NFC-normalizes on both sides so cross-form links/backlinks resolve. The shared `slugifyWikiSegment`/`slugifyWikiPageStem` helpers are unchanged.
- What changed: `vault-page-write.ts` (`resolveWikiPageIdentity` now lists published stems and matches on NFC equivalence), `ingest.ts` / `apply.ts` (reuse the existing `id` when an equivalent page exists), `related-pages.ts` / `lint.ts` (NFC in `normalizeComparableTarget` / `normalizeLintTarget`). `markdown.ts` is unchanged from released behavior.
- What did NOT change: the shared slugify helpers' outputs (imported identities in `bridge`/`unsafe-local`/`okf` keep their released filenames and `id`s, so their sync state survives); title display; the rest of link parsing/serialization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The smallest complete repair (per review direction "normalize *new* slug generation and relevant comparisons while reusing existing page paths and IDs") is to keep the machine-derived identity primitive byte-stable and move canonicalization to the new-page decision and the graph-comparison owner. A single decomposed candidate was rejected because it missed **mixed-form** released pages (`café-naïve` where `café` is composed but `naïve` is decomposed) and would still create a duplicate on re-ingest. Enumerating published stems and comparing on NFC equivalence is the only approach that catches all forms. Preserving released bytes also means no migration mechanism is required; a released vault is read back exactly as it was written.

## User Impact

- New vaults: a title typed as `café` (NFC) and the same title typed as `café` (NFD, e.g. from a macOS paste) now land on one page (`sources/café.md`) instead of two.
- Upgrades: a vault already holding `sources/cafe` + U+0301 `.md` (released NFD) **or** `sources/café-naïve.md` (released mixed form) is reused on re-`ingest`; its path, frontmatter `id`, and hand-written Notes are preserved — no duplicate page, no lost annotations.
- `[[wiki links]]` resolve regardless of normalization form: a page titled `Café` (NFC) is correctly back-linked by `[[Cafe` + U+0301 `]]`.

## Evidence

### Behavior addressed

Unicode normalization-form divergence causing (a) duplicate page files for one visual title and (b) broken cross-form `[[links]]` / backlinks, plus (c) a regression where the original NFC-on-helper fix renamed released decomposed/mixed pages on upgrade.

### Real environment tested

- OS: Linux (x86_64); Node: v22 (same CI runtime). Branch: `fix/wiki-slug-nfc` at PR #197950. Configured vault `renderMode: obsidian` for link display.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

The regression tests added/updated in this PR drive the shipped entry points directly:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/ingest.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.related-index.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts
```

A throwaway script additionally drives the production `ingestMemoryWikiSource` (page write) and `compileMemoryWikiVault` (link resolution) entry points, writing real vault files to a temp dir and reading them back.

### Evidence after fix

Real terminal output (production functions, real files on disk):

```console
[new-vault]   NFC -> sources/café.md / source.café (created=true)
[new-vault]   NFD -> sources/café.md / source.café (created=false)
[new-vault]   source files: ["café.md"]
[released-nfd]   NFC -> sources/café.md / source.café (created=false)
[released-nfd]   notes preserved: true
[released-nfd]   source files: ["café.md"]
[mixed-form] NFC re-ingest -> sources/café-naï.md / source.café-naï (created=false)
[mixed-form] notes preserved: true
[mixed-form] source files: ["café-naï.md"]
[cross-form] backlink resolved: true
```

Regression tests (shipped entry points) — all green:

```console
✓ ingest.test.ts > ingestMemoryWikiSource > maps precomposed (NFC) titles onto one canonical source page
✓ ingest.test.ts > ingestMemoryWikiSource > maps decomposed (NFD) titles onto one canonical source page
✓ ingest.test.ts > ingestMemoryWikiSource > reuses a released decomposed page instead of creating a duplicate
✓ ingest.test.ts > ingestMemoryWikiSource > reuses a released mixed-form page (café-naïve) when re-ingested in any normalization
✓ compile.related-index.test.ts > compile related blocks > resolves a decomposed backlink against a canonically titled page
✓ markdown.test.ts > keeps published slug bytes stable across Unicode normalization forms
```

### Before / after matrix (real behavior, three versions)

| Scenario | `origin/main` (base) | reviewed head `3c1f6a82` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| New vault: NFC then NFD title | two files (`café`.md + `café` NFD.md) | one file `café.md` | one file `café.md` |
| Upgrade released `cafe`+U+0301 page, NFC re-ingest | duplicate `café.md`, Notes lost | duplicate `café.md`, Notes lost | reuses `cafe`+U+0301 `.md`, Notes kept |
| Upgrade released `café-naïve` (mixed) page, NFC re-ingest | duplicate `café-naïve`(NFC), Notes lost | duplicate `café-naïve`(NFC), Notes lost | reuses `café-naïve`.md, Notes kept |
| Cross-form `[[Cafe`+U+0301`]]` → NFC page | no backlink | no backlink | backlink resolved |
| Published slug bytes (imported identities) | unchanged | **changed** | unchanged |

The reviewed head fixed the original duplicate-file bug but introduced the upgrade regression (`merge-risk: compatibility`); this PR fixes all forms while keeping released identity bytes stable.

### Observed result after fix

1. NFC and NFD editions of one visual title converge on a single canonical page (`sources/café.md`); the second `ingest` reports `created=false`.
2. A released decomposed page (`sources/cafe` + U+0301 `.md`) and a released mixed-form page (`sources/café-naïve.md`) are both reused on re-`ingest`: same path, same frontmatter `id`, and hand-written Notes survive (`created=false`, exactly one `.md` in `sources/`).
3. A `[[wiki link]]` written in the opposite normalization form resolves to the NFC-titled page and produces a correct backlink.

### Hash-truncated released page (the P1 ClawSweeper flagged)

A title at/over the 240-byte slug cap is truncated with a content hash. A
released page built from the NFD spelling stores that hash-truncated stem;
re-ingesting the same visual title in canonical (NFC) form must reuse it.
Filename matching alone cannot recover it (NFC vs NFD truncate to different
points and hashes, and the directory listing normalizes the stem), so the
resolver also reads the released page's frontmatter `title` and matches on NFC
equivalence.

| Check | PR head `70735826c34` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `reuses a released hash-truncated NFD page when re-ingested in NFC form` | FAIL (`created: true`, duplicate page) | PASS (`created: false`, reused) |

The regression test writes the released NFD hash-truncated file, then re-ingests
the NFC form; this PR reuses it (path, frontmatter `id`, and hand-written Notes
all preserved), the unfixed head creates a second page.


### What was not tested

The end-to-end CLI surface (`openclaw memory ...` binary invocation) is not driven live; the shipped module entry points (`ingestMemoryWikiSource`, `compileMemoryWikiVault`) are exercised directly instead. GUI editor / OS-level normalization behavior (macOS NFD paste) is assumed from Unicode semantics, not reproduced in a live UI.

prs.title: docs: containerized gateway networking, host model servers, and rootless Podman troubleshooting
prs.body:
Related: #194988

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a containerized gateway cannot reach model servers running on the host, and nothing in the docs explains why published ports go unreachable, config edits get rejected, or container starts fail on SELinux hosts — operators reverse-engineer error strings like `Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address` and `cannot verify Gateway ownership from this process`.

Affects anyone running the gateway in rootless Podman or Docker with local models (llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM) or scripting a hosted-primary + local-fallback setup.

## User Impact

Users can now: point a local provider at a host model server from inside a container (with the SSRF-guard caveat and both fixes explained), understand why `loopback`/`tailnet` binds strand published ports and what to use instead, script the non-interactive hybrid setup (hosted primary, local fallback), and self-recover from three rootless-Podman failure modes (config ownership lock, keep-id mismatch on one-off commands, SELinux relabel denial).

## Why This Change Was Made

The documented behavior is incomplete, not the code: bind modes, the config ownership lock, exact-origin SSRF trust, and onboarding flag handling all behave as designed, but the containerized-gateway docs describe host-centric semantics only. Each section documents observed behavior — verified against source and reproduced on a real rootless Quadlet deployment — rather than proposing changes.

## Evidence

- Source verification: bind fallback semantics in `src/gateway/net.ts`; ownership-lock error text and the 90-second heartbeat in `src/infra/gateway-lock-payload.ts`; link-local exclusion from exact-origin trust in `src/agents/provider-network-policy.ts` and `src/infra/net/ssrf.ts`; `--custom-*` flags ignored beside a hosted `--auth-choice` in `src/commands/onboard-non-interactive/local/`.
- Real deployment: all three troubleshooting failure modes reproduced on Fedora rootless Podman with the Quadlet; the alias `baseUrl` is rejected while a LAN-IP `baseUrl` works.
- Docs checks: `pnpm docs:check-links` passes (16,476 links, 0 broken); `docs:check-links:anchors` shows only two pre-existing failures that reproduce unchanged on the unmodified upstream tip; `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` passes (the json5 patch fence validates); `oxfmt` clean on touched files.
- Issue: #194988 (with closed predecessors #68684, #79850, #163315 — code paths fixed, docs gap remained).

<details>
<summary>Commits in this PR</summary>

- `docs(podman): reach host model servers from a containerized gateway` — alias setup, link-local SSRF caveat, both fixes, cross-link from local-models
- `docs(local-models): add non-interactive hybrid setup recipe` — hosted-primary + local-fallback scripting sequence
- `docs: warn that container bind modes strand published ports` — Quadlet note, Docker networking note, troubleshooting entry
- `docs(podman): add rootless container troubleshooting` — ownership lock, SELinux relabel, keep-id entries

</details>

Closes #181772

## What Problem This Solves

prs.title: feat(sessions): show per-session token and cost usage from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #192616

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway records per-session token and cost attribution and the Control UI shows it, but the terminal could not: `openclaw gateway usage-cost` prints one aggregate number, so a headless operator could not see which session, agent, or model burned the tokens.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions usage [sessionKey]` prints one row per session (label, agent, model, messages, tokens, cost) plus range totals, with `--agent`, `--all`, `--range`, `--start/--end`, `--max-rows`, and `--group-family` selectors. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.usage` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `sessions.usage` owner and only shapes output: conflicting selectors are rejected before dispatch, and the report's `partial` status is printed instead of hidden, so a time-budgeted answer is never mistaken for "no usage".
- The row cap flag is `--max-rows` rather than `--limit`, because the parent `sessions --limit` list-row cap owns that name (the sibling search command follows the same naming after review feedback).
- Registration rejects the parent list selectors, matching the other gateway-backed verbs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-usage.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and run against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000 --json
{ ..., "startDate": "2026-10-06", "endDate": "2026-11-04", "cacheStatus": {"status": "partial"},
  "partial": { "reason": "time-budget", "message": "Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; ..." } }

$ openclaw sessions usage --timeout 120000
Session usage (2026-10-06 → 2026-11-04)
No session usage recorded in this range.
Totals: $0.0000 · 0 tokens · in 0 / out 0
Partial report: Usage request exceeded its 15-second budget; narrow the date range or select a session.

$ openclaw sessions usage --agent x --all          → exit 1 (conflict)
$ openclaw sessions usage --end 2026-10-31         → exit 1 (missing --start)
$ openclaw sessions usage --max-rows 500           → exit 1 (cap exceeded)
```

The live response's `partial` reason surfacing in text mode is the behavior the review asked to prove: an incomplete answer is labeled, never silent.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, ledger, or config changes.
