prs.title: improve(memory): drop embedding cache copies the published index already serves
prs.body:
Refs #168777

## What Problem This Solves

The memory embedding cache keeps a second full copy of every vector the published memory index already holds, so most of a large cache (64% of a 50,000-row cache in #168777) is duplicate data.

## User Impact

User impact: memory databases stop growing a second copy of published vectors. On a 4096-dim store the cache table drops from 32.9 MB to 0.95 MB after the first full rebuild, with no new embedding calls. The cost: text copied into a different memory file, and switching back to an earlier provider or model, are embedded again (details below). No schema change and no user action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stage 1a (#185968) lets ordinary memory-file edits reuse vectors from the published index. The embedding cache still keeps its own copy of every vector it wrote, so most cache rows duplicate a published chunk. This change deletes those copies after a successful publication, in two commits:

- **1b** (`perf(memory): retire cache rows a publication already serves`): after an ordinary sync publishes its memory files, and after a full rebuild publishes, the cache rows that run wrote are deleted when the published index holds the same bytes.
- **Step 2** (`perf(memory): retire existing cache duplicates after a full rebuild`): after a full rebuild publishes, older rows that the new index holds are deleted too. This commit can be dropped on its own (the "1b only" option below).

### Accepted decision: both-stage cache retirement

On November 13, 2026, @Patrick-Erichsen instructed landing after the retention alternatives and their re-embedding costs were disclosed in the [review and landing discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/89f4bf42-824d-42df-a83d-8715b2bd5292). This records acceptance of the current proposal: **both 1b and step 2**, including the three re-embedding costs below. The linked discussion is for team reference and requires sign-in.

This is the maintainer acceptance of the intentional valid-cache retention change required by `docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md`, "Review checkpoint for material changes". No source or retention semantics were changed to obtain acceptance.

**Alternatives considered:**

- **Accept both commits (recommended).** New duplicates are deleted after each clean publication, and existing duplicates after the next full rebuild. In the upgrade run below, a forced rebuild takes the cache from 977 rows on base to 14 on head, with 0 embedding inputs and the same published vectors.
- **Accept 1b only.** Drop `perf(memory): retire existing cache duplicates after a full rebuild`. Rows written after the upgrade are retired as in A. Rows already in the cache stay until the cap prune evicts them. Not measured separately.
- **Reject.** Close this PR. The cache keeps every duplicate up to the cap, and none of the costs below apply.

**Why both:** each cost below is paid as one embedding call per affected chunk, like any cache miss today; switching back to an earlier provider or model can re-embed the whole store. None changes what is published or searched: chunk checksums and search hits match base after every step below. The savings grow with the store: 64% of a 50,000-row cache in #168777, and on the upgraded 2026.11.2 store below the cache vectors go from 500,224 B on base to 7,168 B on head. Rolling back to the newest build without this PR needs no repair: base works on a cleaned store with the same inputs and results as on its own store (table under "Rolling back"). Accepting 1b only keeps an existing store's duplicates until the cap prune reaches them.

The accepted policy:

A cache row of the active primary embedding identity is deleted after a successful publication when every published chunk carrying its text hash holds exactly the same bytes, at least one of those chunks belongs to a memory file, and the published index metadata binds the same provider, model, provider key, input format and dimensions. Nothing else is deleted:

- a row whose vector differs from any published copy (non-deterministic providers, ambiguous hashes) is kept;
- unpublished rows, rows for session-only text, alias identities and other identities are kept;
- a disabled cache keeps its rows;
- failed, partial and deferred runs keep every row they wrote. The skipped run's start carries to the next sync that finishes cleanly, which deletes those rows only after its publication holds the same bytes.

Accepting this means accepting these re-embedding costs, which the cache used to absorb:

1. **Text copied or moved into a different memory file.** Read-through from 1a is scoped to the file being indexed, so a retired vector for text that appears in another file is embedded again.
2. **Switching back to a previous provider or model.** After a full rebuild under identity A, A's cache rows are gone. Rebuilding under B and then back under A embeds everything again. On main, A's rows could survive in the cache up to the cap.
3. **Downgrading to a build without published read-through** (before 198b761c325). Unchanged chunks of edited memory files are embedded again, because the cache no longer has them.

### How it runs

- New `cache.retire` command on the SQLite publication worker and the PostgreSQL binding. One write transaction handles one page of up to 256 candidates in `(updated_at, hash)` order on `idx_memory_embedding_cache_updated_at`, with one chunk read per page. The caller yields between pages and stops while closing.
- Fences:
  - Ordinary sync: rows written since the sync started, or since the oldest earlier sync that did not finish cleanly.
  - Full rebuild: rows written since the rebuild started (1b), then rows written before it started (step 2). The two fences meet at the rebuild start.
- Gates: it runs only when the cache is enabled, and on ordinary syncs only when the memory sync returned normally with no dirty or full-retry state.
- It runs before the cap prune, after publication, outside every publication transaction. Publication transactions gain no work. A retirement error is logged and never fails the sync, marks retry state or records a reindex failure.
- No schema change and no new index. The 1a metadata gate is shared through `readMemoryPublishedVectorMeta`.

## Evidence

### Measured costs

On a fresh store, the CLI proof drove the built `openclaw memory index` and `openclaw memory search` through a loopback `/v1/embeddings` stub with 64 and 4096 dimensions. It ran on 120 memory files with 965 distinct chunks, comparing base 476cce7a8a3 against this head. Chunk checksums are identical between the two builds after every step.

| step | base: inputs embedded | head: inputs embedded | base: cache rows | head: cache rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| initial full index | 940 | 940 | 940 | 0 |
| prepend a paragraph to 10 files | 20 | 20 | 960 | 0 |
| copy 10 indexed paragraphs into other files | 0 | **10** | 960 | 0 |
| failed run (3 of 15 files written) | 12 (6 ok) | 12 (6 ok) | 966 | 6 |
| retry | 24 | 24 | 990 | 6 |
| full rebuild | 0 | 0 | 990 | 0 |

With 4096 dimensions, the same sequence leaves a 32,952,320 B cache table on base and 4,096 B on head. The failed run's 6 rows stay until the full rebuild here, because each CLI command is a new process. A long-lived manager deletes them at its next clean sync.

**Upgrading an existing store** (head run on the base store above): ordinary syncs leave older rows in place. The first full rebuild takes the cache from 990 rows to 28, the 28 that no published chunk holds, and embeds nothing. At 4096 dimensions the table goes from 32,952,320 B to 946,176 B.

**Time and lock hold** (synthetic SQLite store, 4096 dimensions, both passes run back to back):

| store | cache table | rows retired | pages | total | page p50 | page p95 | page max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 22,000 chunk rows, 23,000 cache rows | 765 MB to 173 MB | 17,800 | 91 | 7.6 s | 75 to 91 ms | 124 to 158 ms | 182 ms |
| 44,000 chunk rows, 46,000 cache rows | 1.53 GB to 346 MB | 35,600 | 181 | 24.9 s | 113 to 159 ms | 162 to 262 ms | 395 ms |

Each page holds the writer for well under the 5 s busy timeout discussed in #143640. The cost per page grows with the chunk table, because chunks have no hash index and each page reads the chunks for its 256 hashes. The database file does not shrink: freed pages are reused by later writes, as after any delete.

### Upgrade from latest stable (openclaw@2026.11.2) and data-model compatibility

All runs use the shipped CLI (`openclaw memory index/status/search`, `openclaw doctor --fix`, `openclaw database port`) in isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`HOME` directories, with no Gateway process. Embeddings come from a loopback `/v1/embeddings` stub (64 dims, deterministic except for one step). PostgreSQL is 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.7 in a local container bound to 127.0.0.1.

Builds:

- **stable**: `openclaw@2026.11.2` from npm (dist-tag `latest` on 2026-11-08).
- **head**: this PR, 9c16f4e8084, built from source. Later commits change no production code: 8b5b0f0a18c adds a test and the test-line allocation, and 6a7323d419e merges main 277e32c668a (one import conflict in a test file). The production diff against main is line-for-line the same as at 9c16f4e8084.
- **base**: control at the merge-base 476cce7a8a3, built from source. Every head run is repeated with base on an identical copy of the same store. That separates this PR from what main already does to a 2026.11.2 store.

#### The existing store, written by 2026.11.2

| | |
|---|---|
| Contents | 120 memory files, plus the workspace files and one session transcript from a local agent turn (loopback chat stub) |
| Steps | full index (951 inputs); prepend a paragraph to 10 files (20); copy 10 indexed paragraphs into other files (0); copy 5 paragraphs into a new file with the cache disabled and a non-deterministic provider (5 inputs, random vectors) |
| Agent DB `user_version` | 27 |
| Chunks | 996 (995 memory, 1 session); 5 hashes carry two different published vectors |
| Cache rows | 971 rows (497,152 vector bytes): 956 equal to every published copy, 5 differ from a published copy, 10 have no published chunk |

#### SQLite: 2026.11.2 store upgraded to head, with base as control

Head and base both refuse the v27 store until it is migrated: `uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 41 before using it.` This PR adds no schema change and touches no `.sql` or `src/state` file, so the 27 to 41 migration is main's. Each arm ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`, then the steps below.

| step | inputs embedded (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2026.11.2 store | | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| `doctor --fix` (v27 to v41) | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| `memory status` | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| 3 searches | 1 query each | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| index, no edits | 0 / 0 | `80149dab` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files, index | 6 / 6 | `ea07cfb0` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `ef7fdec9` | **14** / 977 |
| 3 searches | 1 query each | `ef7fdec9` | 14 / 977 |

Final cache vector bytes: 7,168 on head and 500,224 on base.

- **Existing data loads and works.** After the migration, the chunk checksum (decoded vectors, path, line, hash) and the cache checksum equal the 2026.11.2 store. Status, the no-edit index (0 inputs) and all searches work. Every search returns the same hits as 2026.11.2: 6 for a marker in 10 edited files, 1 for a marker in one original file, and 1 for a phrase only in the session transcript.
- **Head and base publish identical data.** Chunk checksums match at every step, and a per-row compare of the final stores shows 999 of 999 chunk vectors identical. Among all 76 agent-DB tables, only `memory_embedding_cache` differs in row count, and the schema is identical.
- **Settings are unchanged.** `memory_index_meta` is byte-identical before and after every step on both arms. `doctor --fix` rewrites `openclaw.json` as JSON and adds `meta`, `wizard` and `skills` entries on both arms. The `memory`, `models`, `plugins`, `gateway` and `agents.defaults` blocks are semantically identical to the 2026.11.2 file.
- **Duplicates are retired only as described above:**
  - Migration, status, search and the no-edit index delete nothing: 971 rows stay through all of them.
  - The 3-file edit writes 6 rows, and head deletes them after publication. Base keeps them.
  - The forced rebuild deletes the older duplicates. Head keeps 14 rows: the 13 whose hash no published chunk carries, and the 1 whose text exists only in the session transcript. All 14 are also in base's final cache.
  - The 5 rows that differed from a published copy are kept through every ordinary sync. On the forced rebuild, both builds republish those 5 chunks with the cached vector (the same 999/999 identical chunks), so the rows stop differing and head retires them.

#### Rolling back

- **To 2026.11.2: refused, with or without this PR.** 2026.11.2 refuses the head-upgraded store and the base-upgraded store with the same error: `OpenClaw state database <state>/state/openclaw.sqlite uses newer schema version 39; this build supports 22. ... To use an older build, restore your pre-update backup created with openclaw backup create.` Once main has migrated a store, 2026.11.2 cannot open it, so its missing read-through (below) cannot re-embed anything on that store. Going back means restoring the pre-update backup, which still holds the full 2026.11.2 cache.
- **To base 476cce7a8a3, the newest build without this PR:**

| step | base on head-cleaned store | base on its own store |
|---|---:|---:|
| index, no edits | 0 inputs | 0 inputs |
| edit 3 files | 6 inputs | 6 inputs |
| forced rebuild | 0 inputs | 0 inputs |
| final chunk checksum | `3d677fde` | `3d677fde` |
| searches | same hits | same hits |

**Published read-through (198b761c325) is not in 2026.11.2.** The evidence:

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 198b761c325 v2026.11.2` exits 1.
- v2026.11.2 (b556fdf457b) branched from main at 459cad76530 (2026-10-14). 198b761c325 was committed on 2026-10-27.
- The first tag containing 198b761c325 is v2026.11.5-beta.1.
- The 2026.11.2 `CHANGELOG.md` has no #185968 entry.

#### PostgreSQL

**2026.11.2 has no PostgreSQL memory store, so a stable PostgreSQL upgrade does not exist.**

- Its shipped `docs/reference/database-engines.md` says: "Workboard is currently the only PostgreSQL-supported store. Shared state, agent/session storage, and other stores continue using SQLite."
- The memory tables live in the agent store.
- PostgreSQL memory landed in 163e18fa89e (#174183) and 89557502c7c (#174374), and v2026.11.2 contains neither.

Two substitutes were run instead.

**1. Existing PostgreSQL store written by base 476cce7a8a3, upgraded to head.** The fixture steps match the SQLite store, including the session transcript and the non-deterministic copy. The store was then copied with `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` so head and base each start from identical data.

| step | inputs (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| existing store (schema_meta 41) | | `e33dad37` | 971 / 971 |
| status, 3 searches, no-edit index | 0 / 0 (plus 1 per query) | `e33dad37` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files | 6 / 6 | `b9636702` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `addc9f90` | **14** / 977 |

- Final cache vector bytes are 7,168 on head and 500,224 on base.
- schema_meta stays 41, and `memory_index_meta` is unchanged.
- Of the 10 memory tables, only `memory_embedding_cache` differs in row count between head and base.
- Every search returns the same hits as the SQLite runs.

**2. The 2026.11.2 SQLite store moved to PostgreSQL the supported way, then upgraded to head.** The steps: `doctor --fix`, then `openclaw database port --to postgres --dry-run`, then `openclaw database port --to postgres` (run with base). The port completed with 0 embedding inputs and rebuilt the memory index on PostgreSQL (996 chunks).

- After the port, the PostgreSQL store holds 996 chunks and 971 cache rows. The cache checksum equals the 2026.11.2 store's.
- 991 of 996 chunk vectors are identical to the 2026.11.2 store. The other 5 are the non-deterministic copy, which takes the cached vector in the port's rebuild. That is main's port behavior.
- Status and all searches work.

Head and base then ran on copies of the ported store:

| step | inputs (head / base) | chunk checksum (head = base) | cache rows (head / base) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| ported store | | `7ead0c53` | 971 / 971 |
| status, 3 searches, no-edit index | 0 / 0 (plus 1 per query) | `7ead0c53` | 971 / 971 |
| edit 3 files | 6 / 6 | `50edc75f` | **971** / 977 |
| forced rebuild | 0 / 0 | `50edc75f` | **14** / 977 |

Across all SQLite and PostgreSQL arms, 57 search runs return the same hits as 2026.11.2. The session file id is normalized for the store written on PostgreSQL.

#### Not covered

- **Rollback to 2026.11.2 after the upgrade.** 2026.11.2 refuses any store main has migrated (above), so only base was used as the older build.
- **A stable PostgreSQL upgrade.** 2026.11.2 has no PostgreSQL memory store.
- **Gateway processes.** Each command is a separate CLI process; no long-lived Gateway process was exercised.
- **Real providers.** No real embedding provider was used, and these runs use 64 dims. The 4096-dim measurements are in "Measured costs".

### Tests

- `manager-embedding-cache-retire.test.ts` and `manager-embedding-cache-retire.postgres.test.ts` cover the kernel on SQLite and PostgreSQL:
  - the full predicate;
  - metadata refusals (provider key, dimensions, input format, fts-only, unreadable metadata);
  - both fences and paging with the cursor;
  - an EXPLAIN guard that later pages search one `updated_at` range. A bare OR keyset sorted the remaining rows on every page under the step-2 fence.
- `manager.cache-duplicate-retirement.test.ts` covers the manager:
  - ordinary edits and full rebuilds;
  - a failed edit whose retry reuses its rows;
  - a failed edit whose text another file already publishes;
  - a skipped sync retired by the next clean sync;
  - a cached vector that differs from the published one;
  - a cleanup error that leaves publication and retry state alone;
  - a disabled cache whose existing duplicate rows survive an edit and a forced rebuild;
  - existing duplicates retired only by a full rebuild.
- Each predicate, fence, gate and call site was mutated (19 mutants). Every mutant fails the suite.
- Existing tests that read generated vectors back from the cache as a probe now hold retirement with `keepPublishedCacheDuplicates`, and their assertions are unchanged. They cover reindex recovery, chunk publication retry, source and session races, legacy-format upgrade, declared-dimension repair, and PostgreSQL rebuild reuse. `manager-cache-rebuild.test.ts` re-seeds the rows an older build kept, and expects only superseded rows after a published rebuild.

The new PostgreSQL 1/3 execution ran both conformance and the previously interrupted PostgreSQL 16 Gateway cron smoke successfully, followed by a successful aggregate gate. Passing lanes reused from attempt 1 retain their original execution. The original whole-job deadline cancellation and failed aggregate are preserved as historical evidence; successful recovery supplies missing coverage, not proof that an infrastructure cause was repaired. The [post-CI Security Review publisher](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43311418885) published successful CI, security-sensitive and dependency statuses for this exact head. No CI was rerun for the later acceptance or for age.

The earlier shipped-CLI, SQLite/PostgreSQL upgrade/port/rollback measurements below retain their stated executing revisions. Current-main composition is conflict-free, with the production patch unchanged from the completed source review.

prs.title: feat(agents): explain the effective tool set for a session
prs.body:
Closes #192712

## What Problem This Solves

When a tool the agent expects is missing, the operator had to guess why. The Gateway already computes the full effective tool set for a session — each tool's status plus the profile, deny, allowlist, session, or runtime rule behind every decision — through the canonical `tools.effective` RPC, but no CLI verb exposed it.

## User Impact

`openclaw agents tools <sessionKey>` prints the effective profile, the Gateway's filtering notices, and one row per tool with its status and the deciding reasons; `--json` returns the raw diagnostics.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owner and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and transport failures exit non-zero in both output modes.
- Registered under `agents` because the `tools` root is deliberately reserved.
- The command defaults its runtime to `defaultRuntime`, matching the other agents commands that are invoked without an explicit runtime from the registration wrapper.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents-tools.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` → 32/32 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`). The first live run exposed a real defect (the command was invoked without a runtime, crashing the error paths) which was fixed before this head; the fixed build shows the correct failure contract:

```text
$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "unknown session key \"agent:main:main\"" },
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:main" }            (exit 1)

$ openclaw agents tools "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Tools diagnostics failed: unknown session key "agent:main:main"
                                                (exit 1)
```

The Gateway log confirms both live requests (`⇄ res ✗ tools.effective ... errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown session key`). The isolated store has no sessions, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, tool-policy, or config changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope image capability discovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- scope attachment image-capability fallback to the selected provider instead of rebuilding every provider catalog
- keep runtime-only models by using the existing request-scoped live catalog path
- retry the complete Gateway projection when its published runtime owner is replaced during scoped discovery

## Root cause and owner

Attachment admission first reads the lifecycle-published catalog. When a selected runtime-only model is absent or has provisional text-only metadata, current main falls back to `readOnly: false`, which rebuilds the full cross-provider catalog inside the request. The provider-scoped catalog machinery exists, but this Gateway caller did not use it.

The canonical owner is the Gateway catalog projection. The second read now carries the selected provider into the existing prepared request-scoped live catalog. The projection checks the published owner before and after the asynchronous scoped read and reacquires the full owner on replacement, so catalog, config, agent identity, and auth projection never mix generations.

## ClawSweeper findings

- Early owner replacement: fixed by retrying at the Gateway projection boundary; the regression replaces the owner during scoped discovery and proves only the replacement catalog returns.
- Final provider I/O fence: the old branch tried to turn generation liveness into a public provider-auth revocation contract, but that was incomplete and added a large cross-plugin surface. This port removes that contract. Published-generation liveness governs whether results may publish; it does not retroactively revoke already-started provider requests. Results from a retired generation are discarded and the owner is reacquired.
- Runtime-only models: retained. An independent P1 review caught and rejected an intermediate static-only rewrite; the final branch uses the existing scoped live mode.
- Test-cost evidence: recorded below for the new image-capability file and the combined focused Gateway set.

## Scope

Seven Gateway files changed against integrated main: 222 insertions and 60 deletions. Reuses the existing scoped catalog owner; no provider/plugin implementation changes, new configuration, or cache.

## Validation

- Integrated main: `1f01f4944d45eb265081f8bfbf8d3e8e54ff4266`; resolved conflicts while retaining current static-capability and projection owners.
- Three focused Gateway suites: 86 tests passed (image capability, catalog projection, session utilities).
- Core production typecheck and targeted lint passed; `git diff --check` clean.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the seven-file candidate diff. Surrounding loader implementations were not included in the isolated reviewer bundle; integration assurance also relies on focused tests and source inspection.
- Previous validation counts and hosted evidence were for the old head and are not current-head proof.
- No new real-channel/live-provider proof was run.
- CI follow-up: the new catalog mock now accepts the loader's optional argument. The affected Gateway-server test-type leaf passed; 16 catalog tests passed. Current head: `8a7567d2df5d`. Replacement exact-head CI is pending, not claimed green.

Agent transcript omitted.

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit E2E file targets still created full test-fixture workers even when their downstream runner supported production-only workers.

## User Impact

Qualified E2E target rows compile fewer worker files while running the same selected tests. E2E build prerequisites, isolation, cleanup, unknown-target fallbacks, and build-dependent group fallbacks stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing E2E qualification inventory in CI's parent selector and qualify the real Gateway exec-approval test. Builds on merged https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197980, which preserves the selected preset through CLI shims. This PR now targets main.

## Evidence

- Regression-only baseline: 3 expected failures / 150 passes. Fixed: 153/153 focused tests; targeted tooling typecheck, lint, formatting and native syntax pass.
- Same 4-vCPU, 16.56-GB Linux Testbox, Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun; the real CI shard command ran all three approval cases in both modes, zero skips, with completed worker cleanup. [Qualification run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43335307757).

| Worker preparation | 36.620s | 23.390s |

The payload difference is observed, not a causal fleet or billing estimate. Largest-child RSS was 6,003,624/6,263,452 KiB; neither run failed or skipped a case.

prs.title: ci(i18n): add non-publishing native locale refresh
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where maintainers cannot refresh secret-backed native translations for review without also creating and arming an auto-merge generated PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an explicit non-publishing dispatch mode that runs the existing bounded locale matrix and validation, then uploads an allowlisted binary patch artifact. The default publishing path remains unchanged.

Secret-backed non-publishing runs execute only from the trusted `main` workflow. The operator supplies an exact source SHA; that SHA must be the current head of one open, non-draft PR targeting `main` with GitHub's current review decision `APPROVED`. Each locale worker revalidates the exact PR head and current approval immediately before the translation-secret step. Branch-selected preflight support was removed: guards inside branch-controlled YAML cannot independently guarantee secret isolation. Manual runs use the trusted main workflow definition.

## User Impact

No direct user-facing change. Maintainers gain a review-only native translation refresh path that cannot push, open a PR, or enable auto-merge, while non-publishing source selection requires current exact-head review approval.

## Evidence

### November 2 review-readiness repair

- Removed the branch-selected preflight mode and restored the main-only dispatch contract, addressing the P1 workflow-boundary finding without adding another execution path.
- Focused workflow contract regression: fails on the previous head at the branch-admission condition; passes after the repair (1 test, 4.97s runner wall).
- Workflow validation passed, including pinned tooling fallback and zizmor.
- Changed-surface checks passed: formatting, root-test typechecks, dependency/coercion/dead-export guards, and script/test lint. `git diff --check` passed.
- Repair delta: 12 insertions / 37 deletions across workflow and guard test; removed the separate preflight input, scheduling branch, and branch-dispatch route.
- Local autoreview of this repair against `7bf16b8fd47f07612777b4957b1a14bbc66eba42`: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.
- Remaining integration proof: no new credentialed translation run was dispatched. The earlier hosted translation/artifact run predates the current approval checks, so it does not prove approved and revoked-source behavior for this head. That remains an explicit pre-merge validation gap.

prs.body:
Related: #142663

## What Problem This Solves

`/tools verbose` advertises automation creation during management-only turns, even though execution rejects `add`. Inventory construction has no run ID, so deriving its description and schema from an exact-run execution grant incorrectly falls back to the unrestricted surface.

## User Impact

Discovery inside an admitted management-only turn no longer advertises creation. Fresh remote administrator turns retain creation through the existing `callerScopedCreation` distinction. Execution authorization is unchanged.

This fixes the discovery mismatch only; the reported Telegram creation rejection is not claimed fixed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `resolveCronToolManagementMode` reads admitted scope, deployment policy, liveness, and any supplied run ID without requiring an execution grant.
- `bindCronManagementGrant` reuses that classification while retaining its exact-run, live caller authority and operational-instance checks.
- Automation descriptions, schemas, and compact summaries use the admitted mode. Summary wording stays in the existing description-presets owner, keeping `cron-tool.ts` within its line limit.
- Discovery outside an admitted turn still describes the configuration surface, not per-turn execution authority.

## CI Repair

Rebased onto upstream `24e758688a6db34e1f9079f65faff3269bf15978`, which contains [#181647](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181647), `05d779c0c931c8c0bbccf9cce93a47fbb54e6ef9`. That upstream repair distinguishes the admitted restart source ID from the interrupted execution run ID, addressing the three failures previously reproduced on CI's upstream base without this PR.

Removed this PR's duplicate exact action-enum assertion, which had become stale when upstream added `bind`. The real command-handler regression remains; existing schema and authority tests protect permitted actions and the creation boundary. No upstream assertions, skips, retries, or approval gates were changed by this PR.

## Evidence

- Real command-handler regression covers `/tools verbose` in an admitted management-only scope. Authority coverage distinguishes discovery from execution grants and preserves fresh remote creation.
- 128 focused tests passed using repository-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 20 restart-continuation cases plus 108 authority, tool, inventory, and prefix-stability cases across the six affected suites.
- [New-head native CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40344290316), including `checks-node-changed-5` and the native `openclaw/ci-gate`. The final rollup had 66 passing checks and none pending; only the maintainer-approval commit statuses remain red.
- Standalone command smoke outside Vitest, with isolated state and synthetic admitted scopes: management-only output omits `add job`; fresh remote creation output includes it. This is command-boundary proof, not a live Gateway/model session.
- Targeted production and touched-test typechecks, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks.
- Fresh independent review was attempted, but both reviewer processes failed at service capacity; no fresh review verdict is claimed. The authority implementation is unchanged from the previously reviewed patch. This update rebases that patch, removes the duplicate enum assertion, and relocates the unchanged summary expression.

The security-sensitive guard still requires current-head approval from a maintainer with `maintain` or `admin` access. A previous-head approval would not carry over after this rebase.

prs.title: fix(codex): retain native thread reasoning effort
prs.body:
## Summary

- retain Codex App Server's effective reasoning effort from thread start, resume, and fork responses
- update the same live and durable binding from matching `thread/settings/updated` notifications
- report the effective native setting through the existing `turn_starting.effort` diagnostic when a supervised turn intentionally has no per-turn collaboration override

## Root cause and canonical fix

OpenClaw's manual response types and durable session binding omitted Codex's response-backed reasoning effort. The notification controller also discarded settings notifications emitted before `turn/start` returned a turn id. Supervised attempts therefore reported a null effort even when the native thread had an effective setting.

The repair records the fact where Codex owns it: start/resume/fork responses initialize it, and `thread/settings/updated` changes it. All binding writers carry the same nullable field. Existing generation and thread guards prevent stale clients from moving live or durable state.

This current-main rewrite does not add `thread_ready.reasoningEffort` or another event field. It fills the long-standing `turn_starting.effort` field only when the per-turn request intentionally omits an override. The live harness independently verifies the effective native effort and the absent collaboration override.

## Dependency contract

The integrated plugin pins `@openai/codex` 0.164.0. The sibling Codex source was inspected directly at commit `fdf23b4097bf19adf2286c64316da2d2a9fedae6`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs` defines response-backed nullable `reasoning_effort` for thread start/resume and `ThreadSettings.effort` for settings updates. Native thread facts remain separate from per-turn overrides.

## Coverage and change shape

Regressions cover response capture across start/resume/fork and supervised materialization, pre-turn settings updates, durable-owner rejection, effective turn-start diagnostics, and the live supervised/native assertion boundary.

No new configuration surface, schema migration, protocol version, fallback, or parallel path. The positive production delta propagates one native fact through the existing binding writers; notification writes use the connection's current authority.

## Validation

- Current head: `ae1b83e6b0bd`; integrated main: `1f01f4944d45`.
- 89 tests passed across three affected files during conflict repair.
- After the final current-authority adaptation: all three reasoning-effort regression cases passed; extension production types and targeted lint passed.
- Fresh autoreview against integrated main, P0–P2: no actionable findings in the supplied candidate diff; unchanged surrounding source was unavailable to the isolated reviewer.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- No fresh credentialed live Codex run. Historical CI and hosted review are not current-head evidence.
- Exact-head CI pending after publication; not claimed green.

prs.title: feat(system-agent): let the system agent report backup status
prs.body:
Fixes #192657

## Summary

The system agent could report `health`, `status`, `doctor`, `models`, and `plugins`, but had no way to answer backup questions ("when did the last backup run, did it succeed, are the offsite schedules working?"). The Gateway already summarizes that through the canonical `backup.status` projection; only the model-facing surface was missing.

This PR adds a read-only `backup-status` system-agent operation plus the `backup_status` tool action, wired through the same four-step chain the `health` action established: operation type → executor case → tool action enum + `SIMPLE_ACTIONS` → assistant-prompt lists. The executor reuses the projection's own helpers (`readBackupRuns`, `summarizeBackupTargets`, `summarizeBackupSchedules`, `listStorageLocations`, `buildBackupStatusValue`), so no new projection or state access is introduced. The typed-command parser accepts `backup status` / `backup` / `backups`.

Revision 2 (`2118837348c`) closes the remaining P2 from the earlier review: when the selected Gateway is not this host (`gateway.mode=remote`), the loader now asks that Gateway's `backup.status` handler for the projection instead of reading the client's own SQLite ledger, cron partition, and storage registry. The rendered headline now states where the rows came from (`Source: local process state` or `Source: selected Gateway ws://…`), so an operator can tell which host answered.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: the `backup_status` system-agent operation now renders the recorded backup-run ledger — freshness headline, per-target `kind/target/status/age` table, enabled schedules, storage locations, plus the existing backup doctor hints — instead of having no action at all; and with `gateway.mode=remote` it renders the selected Gateway's projection rather than the client's local one.

**Real setup tested**: Windows 11 host, OpenClaw run from TypeScript source on this PR's head (`2118837348c`). Two isolated state directories, no user state touched: Gateway host `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix` (real pre-existing `state/openclaw.sqlite`, 2.0 MB, with two recorded runs) and remote client `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote` whose own ledger holds **0 rows**. The Gateway ran on `ws://127.0.0.1:18817` with token auth, started only for this proof and stopped afterwards.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1, invoked as `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` (no `dist` rebuild, so the tree under test is exactly this branch's source)
- **Selected-Gateway transport**: the shipped `backup.status` RPC over the real Gateway WebSocket, exercised through the shipped `createSystemAgentTool()` object and its `backup_status` action (not by calling `backupStatusCommand` directly, and not through a stubbed transport)

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
# Gateway host: isolated state with real ledger rows, real Gateway on 18817
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18817

# Local mode (no gateway.mode): the same tool object the agent calls
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts     # createSystemAgentTool({surface:"cli"}).execute({action:"backup_status"})

# Remote mode: client has gateway.mode=remote -> backup.status on the selected Gateway
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote"
export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-b-remote/openclaw.json"
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-backup-status.ts

# What the client's own ledger contains (0 rows), so the two rows below can only
# have come from the Gateway's backup.status response
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs .proof-ledger-rows.ts
```

The two probe files contain no stubs: they build the shipped tool with `createSystemAgentTool({ surface: "cli" })`, prepare runtime config through `captureRuntimeConfigAsyncReader`, and print the tool's real text result.

**After-fix evidence**:

```text
# local mode, isolated state with two recorded runs (newest first)
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: local process state
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# gateway.mode=remote, client ledger has 0 rows — rows come from the selected Gateway
Backup status last attempt failed 20h ago (external)
Source: selected Gateway ws://127.0.0.1:18817
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| Kind     | Target                                                             | Status | Age     |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
| external | nas-b                                                              | failed | 20h ago |
| external | nas-a                                                              | ok     | 20h ago |
+----------+--------------------------------------------------------------------+--------+---------+
----- tool result meta -----
{"ok":true,"parts":1}
```

```text
# the remote client's own ledger, proving the two rows above crossed the RPC boundary
{"clientLedgerRows":0,"targets":[]}
```

The local-mode run took 254.6 s and exited 0; the remote-mode run took 142.6 s and exited 0. Both are real terminal runs, not test output.

**Observed result after the fix**: the headline moves from `Backup status none recorded` to `last ok` / `last attempt failed`, the table lists every recorded target newest-first with the ok row still visible behind a later failure, and in remote mode the same rows are rendered from the Gateway while the client's own ledger is empty. Exit code is 0 for the populated, single-row, and empty cases alike — the empty state is a normal state, not an error. `Source:` makes the answering host explicit in both modes.

**What was not tested**: no live LLM agent turn was run (this host has no model credential wired for a paid run), so the model's own tool-selection step — choosing `backup_status` and formatting its answer — is covered only by the contract assertions in `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts`, not by an executed agent session. Schedule rows were not exercised in this session: the isolated state has no cron backup jobs, so the "Schedules:" line did not appear (the code path is the same helper the `health` action already uses). The remote run used a loopback Gateway with token auth; a TLS/tunnel Gateway was not exercised.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: the runs used TypeScript source via the `tsx` loader rather than a `tsdown`-built `dist`, so the evidence is byte-identical to this branch's source but not to a packaged release artifact. The Gateway was started for the proof only and stopped afterwards; the isolated state directories and the loopback token never touch the user's real `~/.openclaw`.

## Gateway-target fix (revision 2)

| Scenario | Before this revision | After this revision |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.mode=remote`, client ledger empty, Gateway has a failed `nas-b` run | client prints `none recorded` (its own empty SQLite ledger) | client prints `last attempt failed … nas-b`, `Source: selected Gateway ws://…` |
| Transport used | none — local file reads only | canonical `backup.status` on the selected Gateway (`callGateway`, `operator.read`) |
| Failure mode when the Gateway is unreachable | silently wrong local answer | explicit error naming the Gateway URL; no silent local fallback |
| Doctor hints | built from the client's local ledger | built from the same projection the headline/table used |

`isImplicitLocalGatewayTarget(config)` chooses the path: implicit local keeps today's local reads (no Gateway required for CLI use), `gateway.mode=remote` routes to `backup.status`. `loadBackupStatusSnapshot` is the only decision point; `renderBackupStatus` and the hint builder are shared, so both modes describe one projection.

## Tests and validation

- Unit tests landed with the PR (recorded when the branch was pushed, not re-run in this evidence session): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` → 114/114 passed, covering the new `backup status` parse rows and the schema/description assertions.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/commands/backup-status.ts src/commands/backup-health.ts` → 0 warnings / 0 errors; `oxfmt --write` applied to both files.
- Type checking: a workspace-wide `tsgo` run in this checkout is red on pre-existing `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` dependency drift (`src/acp/*`, unrelated to this branch); it reported exactly one error in the touched files on the first pass (`OpenClawConfig` imported but unused), which is fixed in the pushed head.
- The end-to-end behaviour above is production code (tool dispatch → executor → projection → renderer → Gateway RPC), not a unit-test fixture.
- Read-only throughout: no backup runs, schedules, storage writes, or Gateway mutations; the operation returns `{ applied: false }` like the other reporting actions.

## Risk checklist

- **Does this change user-visible behavior?** Yes, but only additively: the system agent gains one read-only action (`backup_status`), the tool description grows by two words, and every rendered status now carries a `Source:` line. No existing action semantics change.
- **What is the release/rollback risk?** Low. The new code path is a branch inside one loader; reverting it returns to local reads without touching the ledger, the cron store, or the RPC, which remain the canonical owners.
- **Could this corrupt state or break an existing surface?** No state is written. In remote mode the command now performs a read-only `backup.status` RPC with the configured client credentials; the local path is unchanged. A defect would surface as wrong output or an explicit connection error, not as data loss.
- **Auth/secret handling**: the Gateway token is read from the existing `gateway.remote` config through `buildGatewayConnectionDetails`/`callGateway`; it is never printed, logged, or embedded in the body.

## Current review state

- **Addressed in revision 2**: the P2 "Read backup status from the selected Gateway" — `gateway.mode=remote` now routes through the selected Gateway's `backup.status`, and the evidence above shows the empty-client-ledger scenario the review described (2 rows from the Gateway, 0 rows locally).
- **Addressed in revision 1**: the "Add real behavior proof" blocker — populated, single-row, and empty states were already shown; revision 2 additionally shows the actual system-agent tool dispatch and the selected-Gateway transport the earlier review asked for.
- **Still open (author-known)**: no live LLM agent turn, no cron schedule rows, and no packaged-`dist` run (see What was not tested).
- **Next step**: maintainer review. I will not claim the remote path is release-proven until a packaged build runs against a non-loopback Gateway.

## Before / After

| State | Before this PR | After this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Agent action | no `backup_status`; fallback guidance lists doctor/status/health only | `backup_status` registered; parser maps `backup status` / `backup` / `backups` |
| Operation type | `operation-types.ts` has no backup case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | `{ kind: "backup-status" }` (1 hit) |
| Executor | no `backup-status` case (0 hits on `origin/main`) | dispatches to `backupStatusCommand` (2 hits) |
| Rendered output | — | freshness headline + source + per-target table + schedules/locations + doctor hints |
| Remote Gateway | local ledger read regardless of `gateway.mode` | `backup.status` on the selected Gateway; explicit error instead of a silent local answer |

prs.title: fix(android): keep inline code in markdown plain-text extraction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat renders remote Markdown images as plain alt text (no image fetching on this path). `buildPlainText` in `apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/ui/chat/ChatMarkdown.kt` handled `Text` and line-break nodes but fell through to the generic `else` branch for the leaf `Code` node, which recurses into `firstChild` — always `null` for a commonmark `Code` node — so inline-code literals were silently dropped.

Concretely, an alt like `![Open **`setup.json`** now](https://example.com/diagram.png)` rendered as "Open  now", and a code-only alt produced an empty string, falling back to the generic `image` label.

Fixes #196086

## Solution

Append the `Code` node's `literal` directly in `buildPlainText`, matching how the rendering path (`appendInlineNode`'s `is Code` branch) already handles inline code. The `org.commonmark.node.Code` import was already present.

## Impact

Inline-code literals in remote-image alt text now appear in the rendered placeholder text, including code-only alts which previously degraded to the generic `image` fallback. No other plain-text consumers change behavior: every non-leaf node still recurses as before.

## Evidence

### Before / after (Android chat, production markdown pipeline)

Captured on a local Android 16 (API 36) emulator from the app's built-in screenshot fixture mode (`openclaw.screenshotScene chat`, no Gateway or credentials involved). The fixture chat was temporarily extended with the two labels from the linked issue on both builds; that local scaffolding is not part of this PR. Both screenshots show the same seeded message rendered through the real `ChatMarkdown` pipeline:

![Before (main): label reads "Open  now" and the code-only alt falls back to "image"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-before.png)

![After (this PR): label reads "Open setup.json now" and the code-only alt shows "config.yml"](https://github.com/Heetisk/openclaw/raw/proof/196086-screenshots/proof-after.png)

- Before: mixed label reads "Open  now" (inline code dropped); code-only alt falls back to the generic "image".
- After: mixed label reads "Open setup.json now"; code-only alt shows "config.yml".
- Both builds otherwise identical (`origin/main` + the same local fixture vs. this branch + the same fixture).

### Tests and CI

- Two focused regressions in `ChatMarkdownTest` exercise the user-visible path from the issue (`buildChatInlineMarkdown` → `appendInlineNode` → `MarkdownImage` → `buildPlainText`):
  - `imageAltTextKeepsInlineCodeLiteral`: mixed bold + inline-code alt extracts `Open setup.json now`.
  - `imageAltTextKeepsCodeOnlyFallback`: code-only alt extracts `setup.json` instead of falling back to `image`.
- CI green on head `1e79292b4`: `android-test-play` (runs these regressions), `android-ktlint`, `android-test-third-party`, both `android-access-native` lanes, `native-i18n`, `security-fast`, and `PR context and evidence`.

prs.title: fix(memory): reduce constrained Gateway startup pressure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory-constrained Gateways load unused runtimes during startup and can run out of memory before their first agent reply.

## User Impact

Defer optional execution and skill-status runtimes until their owning operation needs them, and emit smaller runtime JavaScript while preserving names, module provenance, update recovery and standalone code generation.

**This is an incremental startup-memory improvement, not Cardputer qualification. The 768 MiB service still OOMs before its first reply; the original issue remains open for follow-up.**

## Why This Change Was Made

- Narrow startup imports for agent, CLI, Code Mode, cron and execution review. Preserve configuration capture, cancellation, deadlines, authority and parent-owned cleanup.
- Reuse the startup publication reader, avoid database imports for disk scans, and skip optional warmups when a constrained process has at most 20% memory available.
- Compact emitted JavaScript while preserving module labels and source-map positions. Update existing provenance readers and keep declaration output outside the JavaScript hook.
- Defer both skill-status import paths. Keep per-workspace environment ordering and serialize completed worker results.
- Load cron read handlers only for cron queries, removing the redundant predicate while preserving preparation before fresh database admission.
- Load the OpenAI SDK only inside model-request work. Keep synchronous client factories in their existing construction owner and preserve SDK error identity.
- Update build/recovery tests and the native PR-wrapper inventory for the changed output.

No new configuration, dependency, persistence contract or cleanup owner is added. Net runtime production growth is 60 lines; net test/helper growth is 400 lines against the 400-line allowance, without allocation credit or an allocation file.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `333572898b080f5c6082d7da8d1a42b49eae1ef2`, based on `d90d52cc`. Current-head native packaging, ARM construction and image qualification pass. The original-cap runtime still fails as detailed below.

- Five runtime chunks shrink from 2,256,643 to 1,873,728 bytes (16.97%); all 176 module labels, declaration owners and cooked literals remain equivalent. The packaged skill-discovery static graph shrinks from 293 chunks / 1,456,375 bytes to 248 chunks / 1,269,523 bytes. These are source-size measurements, not RSS savings.
- Import/build regressions fail before their fixes and pass afterward. All 121 targeted skill, remote-host, resource, install, snapshot and worker tests pass. Retained proof covers unchanged execution-review cancellation/cleanup, prompt-prefix stability, build markers, provenance, update deadlines and package replacement. Four scoped typechecks, lint and formatting pass. The existing external-buffer accounting test has an investigated baseline failure; its assertion was not weakened.
- The cron-reader repair passes 53 focused state, cron and lifecycle tests. Its import-boundary regression fails on the prior head and passes after the fix; core/state typechecks, lint and formatting pass. Independent review found no actionable defects. The conservative startup-reader graph removes 70 modules / 408,991 source bytes, falling to 11 modules / 58,463 bytes after the proactive reader is used; no sustained RSS saving is claimed.
- The SDK import regression fails before its fix and passes afterward. All 188 selected Responses/Completions tests pass, as do response-hook, session-header and prompt-prefix stability suites. Core and package-test typechecks, lint, formatting and the 400-line test budget pass. Fresh independent review found no actionable defects. Packaged AST inspection confirms the 910,807-byte SDK chunk and its 2,330-byte construction owner stay outside the five AI entry points’ static import closure; all five deferred imports remain inside request work.
- Fresh full-range independent review of `d90d52cc..33357289` inspected all 88 files and found no actionable correctness or security regressions. Current-head native packaging passes (241.35s, 11 joined commands), ARM64 construction passes (59.59s, 21 joined commands), and immutable-image/native-module checks pass (10 joined commands). The source checkout is clean.
- [CI run 43351311520](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43351311520) remains failed: two Node jobs and one UI job. Its actual merge checkout is `ca062042`, with main parent `a83f7437`. The admission and invalid-profile assertions inherit [#197978](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197978): the unchanged logger now creates `stateDir/logs`; test data and the logger are identical to the actual main parent. Stored config, database and credential hashes remain unchanged.
- The UI failure is the Mermaid blocked-frame request count remaining zero. Source review attributes it outside this PR: the complete UI and renderer trees, dependency inputs and E2E entrypoints are unchanged, and the fixture builds and serves isolated Vite assets through a mocked Gateway. It does not run the changed Gateway/tsdown output. The shared singleton change adds only an uncalled export; the changed CLI-worker build entry is not served to the browser. This is scoped unrelatedness attribution, not a matching-main-failure claim; the exact scheduling/renderer cause remains unknown. Both focused UI cases pass locally, which is nonreproduction only. The separate failure-capture exporter also lacked `python`. Landing uses the native attributed-CI exception under the operator's standing instruction, with these failures retained rather than marked green.
- The current-head original runtime test fails: service OOM exit 137, client exit 1, outer peak 857,219,072 bytes (817.51 MiB), zero swap/restarts, no verified reply or soak. Parent-local max/OOM/kill counters stay zero; descendant OOM counters and the service exit identify the service-side limit. Ready-time RSS is 734.8 MiB. All 25 commands join and owned cleanup passes.
- A preceding-head diagnostic captures 30 worker creations and 20 exits around readiness, including repeated reader, SQLite, logging and discovery replacements. The service reaches its 768 MiB cap before readiness and is later OOM-killed. This identifies churn but does not establish an active-work ownership violation or satisfy acceptance. All 25 commands join and owned cleanup passes.

Physical-device readiness still requires a real OpenAI `CARDPUTER_GATEWAY_OK` response and 60-second healthy soak, with a 1 GiB outer limit, 768 MiB service limit, one CPU, original 256 MiB old-space / 4 MiB semi-space flags, zero swap/OOM/restarts, and outer peak at most 928 MiB. Larger diagnostic runs do not satisfy that gate.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

prs.title: feat(agents): keep absolute workspace paths out of cached system-prompt prefix (#191485)
prs.body:
Closes #191485

## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents configured with identical instructions (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md) run in separate isolated workspaces, their system prompts diverge before character 2,200 due to absolute workspace paths in injected file headings and the `## Workspace` section, preventing prefix prompt cache sharing at the provider.

## User Impact

User impact: Multi-agent setups using shared template instructions across separate workspaces can now benefit from prompt-prefix cache reuse at providers supporting prompt caching (e.g. Anthropic prompt caching, OpenAI prefix caching), reducing input token latency and inference overhead for templated multi-agent deployments.

## Why This Change Was Made

1. **Workspace-relative headings**: Files located inside the agent workspace now render their prompt headings as workspace-relative paths (`## AGENTS.md` instead of `## /abs/path/AGENTS.md`), while files outside the workspace retain their original paths.
2. **Symlink and canonical alias support**: Recognizes canonical workspace identity when workspaceDir is supplied as a symlink or alias (e.g. `/tmp/alias` -> `/tmp/real`), ensuring context files reporting resolved paths render relative headings while genuinely external files stay absolute.
3. **Missing-file marker normalization confined to prompt preparation**: The exported harness SDK loader (`buildBootstrapContextFiles` / `buildBootstrapContextForFiles`) keeps its existing `[MISSING] Expected at: <absolute path>` marker text — the SDK consumer contract is unchanged. The loader only flags generated markers with a new `missing: true` metadata field, and the prompt preparation layer (`prepareContextFilesForPrompt`) renders workspace-relative markers (`[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md`) for cache parity, including budget-clamped spellings, while preserving genuine loaded file content that begins with missing-file text.
4. **Directory section placement**: The `## Workspace` and `## Directory Roles` sections containing absolute workspace paths were moved below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` adjacent to `## Runtime`.
5. **Cache key identity**: The stable prefix cache key now tracks `headingPath` and file `contentHash` via `projectStableContextFiles` rather than raw file objects with absolute paths, enabling cross-workspace cache hit evaluation while preserving invalidation upon content changes and keeping `system-prompt.ts` within its line cap.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Workspace Loader & Native Runtime Provider Request Trace

Executed end-to-end through OpenClaw's shipped workspace loader (`resolveBootstrapContextForRun`) reading real files from isolated temporary directories on disk, followed by the native runtime turn executor (`createNativeRuntime` + `rt.withTurn`) capturing actual serialized HTTP request payloads sent to the provider model endpoint:

```
================================================================================
  OPENCLAW SHIPPED WORKSPACE LOADING & PROVIDER REQUEST PROOF TRACE
================================================================================

Step 1: Isolated Disk Workspaces Created
  - Agent A: /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1/
      * AGENTS.md: "# Agent Instructions\nBe helpful."
      * SOUL.md:   "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise."
      * IDENTITY.md: "# Identity\nv1.0"
      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk
  - Agent B: /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX/
      * AGENTS.md: "# Agent Instructions\nBe helpful."
      * SOUL.md:   "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise."
      * IDENTITY.md: "# Identity\nv1.0"
      * Absent BOOTSTRAP.md: left unwritten on disk

Step 2: Shipped Workspace Loading (resolveBootstrapContextForRun)
  - Loader A reads files from /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1 on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker
  - Loader B reads files from /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX on disk
      * Preserves genuine SOUL.md content starting with missing-file text
      * Detects absent BOOTSTRAP.md -> generates missing marker

Step 3: Native Runtime Turn Execution (createNativeRuntime -> rt.withTurn)
  - Runtime A bound to workspace /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1
  - Runtime B bound to workspace /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX
  - Model requests captured at mock provider endpoint (POST /v1/chat/completions)

================================================================================
  SERIALIZED PROVIDER REQUEST PARITY (Before Directory Section)
================================================================================
Request A System Prompt Length:    1,918 chars
Request B System Prompt Length:    1,918 chars
Working Directory Marker Offset:   Index 1,700 in both requests
Shared Prefix A (0..1700):        1,700 chars
Shared Prefix B (0..1700):        1,700 chars
Exact Byte Parity (A === B):      TRUE (100% BYTE-IDENTICAL MATCH)

================================================================================
  INJECTED HEADINGS, MARKERS & PRESERVED INSTRUCTIONS (Outgoing Provider Payload)
================================================================================
Heading AGENTS.md:                "## AGENTS.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading SOUL.md:                  "## SOUL.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading IDENTITY.md:              "## IDENTITY.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Heading BOOTSTRAP.md:             "## BOOTSTRAP.md" (clean workspace-relative)
Preserved User File Content:      "[MISSING] Expected at: /old/TOOLS.md\n# Soul\nConcise." (retained)
Generated Missing Marker:         "[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md" (normalized at prompt preparation)
Absolute paths in Headings:       NONE (0 occurrences of /tmp/ws-*)

================================================================================
  DYNAMIC SUFFIX & DIRECTORY FACTS (Preserved after cache boundary)
================================================================================
Directory Section Offset:         Appears after prompt cache boundary
Request A Directory Content:      "Working directory: /tmp/ws-a-9F2kL1"
Request B Directory Content:      "Working directory: /tmp/ws-b-4mN8vX"
Cross-contamination:              None (A contains only wsA; B contains only wsB)
================================================================================
```

### 2. Shipped CLI/Gateway Proof (Real Gateway Child, Real Turns)

Requested by review: the fix proven through the **real shipped product path** — a Gateway child spawned via the repo CLI entrypoint (`scripts/run-node.mjs`), two configured agents (`alice`, `bob`) with **byte-identical** `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md` instructions in **distinct isolated workspaces**, two real chat turns driven over the Gateway RPC (`chat.send`), and the outgoing provider request bodies captured at the mock provider (`mock-openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, OpenAI Responses API; system prompt in `instructions`).

Proof script: `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/workspace-prefix-proof.ts` (committed; runs end-to-end in ~90 s).

```
=== SHIPPED GATEWAY PROOF ===
captured provider requests: 2
prompt A length: 54188 | prompt B length: 54180
prompt A === prompt B: false                      <- expected: directory facts differ
A contains '## AGENTS.md': true                   <- relative heading
A contains alice workspace path: true             <- only on its Working directory line
B contains bob workspace path: true
byte-identical prefix before 'Working directory:' line: true
first differing char index: 32134                 <- divergence starts exactly at the
                                                      per-workspace directory path
A around first diff:
  "Working directory: C:\...\openclaw-qa-suite-tTGxOb\workspace-alice\n## Runtime\n..."
B around first diff:
  "Working directory: C:\...\openclaw-qa-suite-tTGxOb\workspace-bob\n## Runtime\n..."
```

What this establishes end to end through the shipped Gateway:

- The first **32,134 bytes** of both outgoing provider requests are **byte-identical** despite completely distinct workspace paths — exactly the property providers need for prefix-cache reuse.
- The first divergence is the per-workspace `Working directory:` fact, which the fix moved **below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`** (immediately before the `## Runtime` section).
- Workspace file headings render workspace-relative (`## AGENTS.md`); no absolute `## <drive>:\...` or `## /abs/...` headings appear anywhere in the prompt.
- The run was observed through the Gateway's own terminal event (`chat.send` → `final`), not a synthetic adapter.

### 3. Base vs. Head Comparison

| Metric | Before Fix (Base) | After Fix (Head) |
|---|---|---|
| **Early Prefix Divergence** | Diverges at character 2,081 (`Working directory:`) | **100% byte-identical** before directory section |
| **Injected Headings** | `## /abs/path/to/ws-a/AGENTS.md` (absolute) | `## AGENTS.md` (workspace-relative) |
| **Missing File Marker (SDK loader output)** | `[MISSING] Expected at: /abs/path/BOOTSTRAP.md` | Unchanged — SDK contract preserved |
| **Missing File Marker (rendered prompt)** | `[MISSING] Expected at: /abs/path/BOOTSTRAP.md` | `[MISSING] Expected at: BOOTSTRAP.md` (normalized at prompt preparation) |
| **Directory Roles** | In stable prefix (prevents cache reuse) | In dynamic suffix (below cache boundary) |
| **Symlink Aliases** | Aliased workspace paths diverge | **Canonical roots unified into relative headings** |
| **Provider Request Cache** | Distinct prefixes across separate workspaces | **Potential prompt-prefix cache reuse across isolated workspaces sharing template instructions** |

### 4. Automated Verification
- **Provider request test**: `src/agents/cross-workspace-provider-cache.test.ts` writes real files to isolated temporary workspaces on disk, invokes the shipped `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` loader, exercises real file preservation and absent bootstrap marker normalization (`missing` flag -> prompt-relative marker), executes the native runtime turn, and asserts byte-for-byte prefix parity in outgoing provider requests. Passing after the SDK-marker restoration.
- **Unit tests**: `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` and `src/agents/system-prompt.blind.test.ts` verify relative heading rendering, placement of directory facts below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`, and symlinked workspace alias resolution.
- **SDK contract test**: `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts` confirms the loader keeps `[MISSING] Expected at:` markers (absolute path spelling) within bootstrap budgets — passing unchanged.
- **Inherited CI failure aligned → superseded by main**: this branch previously aligned `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-hook-relay.test.ts` with compact JSON tool results per #196756. Current main has since fixed its own copy, so the rebase onto main (conflict in that test) resolved by taking **main's side** and dropping the now-redundant branch change; 12/12 passing locally via `test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`.
- **Quality Ratchets**:
  - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: **PASS** (108 test lines allocated matching net delta; 0 slack).
  - `check-line-cap-ratchet`: **PASS** (0 violations or over-cap growth).

prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197783

## What Problem This Solves

Narrow compiled test workers lose their runtime/tooling preset when the native test CLI launches its implementation, so the child incorrectly treats the same artifact directory as full.

## User Impact

CI and local test children retain the selected worker scope and its compatibility checks. Full workers and ordinary CLI arguments keep their existing behavior. This is a correctness fix; no additional runtime or billing saving is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing non-full preset through the CLI shim's bootstrap arguments. Extend the existing three-preset child probe through the real shim, without adding test cases or compiler preparation.

## Evidence

- Before the fix: runtime and tooling arrive as full; 2 failures / 4 passes in the six-case worker suite (0.857 s).
- After the fix: all 31 tests across the worker-owner and local-runtime suites pass (2.86 s combined). Descriptor, original arguments and managed child cleanup are exercised. No additional timing or billing improvement is claimed.
- Root-tooling typecheck, scoped lint, formatting, native syntax and diff checks pass.
- Fresh independent review: no actionable findings. Complete committed-range local ClawSweeper review: no actionable findings (confidence 0.96), same base/head below.

Validation base: `02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba`; head: `2d4a5ca1b383ad34f168f15d0a48510e729ab3e7`.

CI run43333627352 failed only the wrapper archive closure checks: six OpenClaw ID protocol sources were missing from the existing inventory. The inventory, failing tests and import owners are byte-identical to captured main base02f29597. This was fixed separately on main in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197976 (2035b073). prs.title: perf(ios): stop redrawing the model menu and buttons on every keystroke
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Editing a draft makes the clean chat composer observe draft changes outside the editor and primary controls, causing unnecessary parent work on each keystroke.

## User Impact

Draft edits stay within the draft-dependent composer sections. The existing Send, Talk, placeholder, and model-picker layout is unchanged. This does not claim a measured typing-latency improvement.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing `ChatComposerSection` observation boundary for the editor overlay and clean primary controls. No new state, renderer, or cache is introduced. The change adds 11 net production lines and 53 test lines; the small wrappers are necessary observation boundaries.

## Evidence

- Baseline regression compiled and failed: outer draft observation invalidations were 1, expected 0.
- Patched focused suite: 15 tests in 2 suites passed. A strengthened assertion also verifies the deferred primary-controls body still observes draft changes; that run passed all 15 tests in 0.077 seconds.
- Simulator: compact composer/draft growth and Stop availability while drafting during an active response passed. Rotation/sidebar test skipped because the simulator lacked expanded window space (2 passed, 1 skipped).
- Inspected recording frames show the rendered follow-up draft and keyboard during an active response. No device or typing-latency proof is claimed.
- Same-family Codex and cross-family Grok reviews found no production correctness defect. Addressed coverage findings by adding positive child-body observation and narrowing the test name. The observation test does not claim to exercise rendered menu invalidation or the Talk branch.
- Scoped SwiftFormat: 0/3 files require formatting. Scoped SwiftLint: no errors; one pre-existing `empty_string` warning at line 219 of the parity test.
- Simplification: retained the existing observation owner and no duplicate rendering path; every production hunk serves draft isolation.

AI-assisted implementation and review.
