prs.title: feat(message): let operators confine group-turn sends to the current conversation
prs.body:
Related: #190557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a group turn's `message` send can reach the owner's DM or another chat when the operator wants group turns kept in their own conversation, because the existing `crossContext` switches confine every kind of turn or none.

## User Impact

User impact: existing configs behave exactly as on main; no default changes. An operator who sets `tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes: ["group", "channel"]`, globally or per agent, gets group and channel turns that can only send to their own conversation. Any other target, on the same provider or another one, fails with `message_cross_context_denied` before a transport call. DM turns keep their current permissions. Separately, under the existing `allowWithinProvider: false`, a Telegram forum-topic send or poll that names the chat id with the current topic's `threadId`, or inherits it, is no longer denied. Other actions from a topic turn, such as renaming a topic, still have to name the current topic, as on main. Two deliberate tightenings apply under `allowWithinProvider: false`, or when group turns are confined. A turn in a Telegram forum topic can no longer create a forum topic in that chat, even through its own topic target, which main allows; the new topic is a sibling conversation in the base chat, and a turn bound to the chat itself still can. Telegram topic creation and topic edits that name another chat through `chatId`, `chat_id` or `channel_id` are denied. In every mode, a target that disagrees with one of those fields is refused as conflicting input. A numeric `target`, `to` or `channelId` is now read as its string, so it follows the same rules as the string: with a target the target wins, and alone it is the destination the check judges. Before, a numeric `channelId` skipped the check and Telegram acted on it, and a numeric `to` or `target` was dropped for the current conversation. A number that is not a safe integer is refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision (4b90fc67b80) flipped the shipped `allowWithinProvider` default to deny. That was the wrong shape. It reversed a deliberate default (#149875, #150157), it broke the required-delivery and context-isolation fixtures, and it changed bound broadcasts. My claim in the old body that broadcasts were exempt was wrong: child sends carry `toolContext` into the same check. Review also found a real matcher bug: the same-provider check ignored `threadId`, so a same-topic Telegram send could be denied.

This revision keeps the default and adds an opt-in inside the existing owner, `enforceCrossContextPolicy`:

- `confineChatTypes` keys on the conversation kind the host reports for the turn (`toolContext.currentChatType`). A listed kind may only target its own conversation; this overrides both `allowWithinProvider` and `allowAcrossProviders`. Unlisted kinds, and turns with no reported kind, keep those flags. A `POST /tools/invoke` call bound by the conversation headers reports the bound target's kind, so it is confined like a turn from that conversation. A per-agent list replaces the global one through the existing per-agent merge; `[]` lifts it.
- Broadcast child sends already go through this check, so a confined broadcast delivers the current conversation and reports a denial for every other target. There is no runner change.
- When same-provider sends are restricted, the check resolves the thread the send will actually use, with the same `resolveAndApplyOutboundThreadId` that delivery uses (on a copy of the params), and names the destination with the channel's own `resolveCurrentChannelId`. Policy and delivery now judge the same destination. Only `send` and `poll` are judged by that thread alone, because the runner delivers them into it. Other guarded actions only hand the thread to the plugin, so they are judged on their requested target as on main, and a thread they carry can only narrow that. `topic-create` must also name the current conversation through its parent chat, resolved with the channel's own conversation grammar (core's `resolveSessionConversation`, which asks `messaging.resolveSessionConversation`), because Telegram creates the topic in the base chat whatever topic or thread the request names. Telegram declares `chatId`, `chat_id` and `channel_id` as delivery-target aliases for `topic-create` and `topic-edit`, because its handler takes the chat from them ahead of the target. Normalization therefore canonicalizes them before the check, the same way the thread spellings are folded. Normalization also stringifies exact integer values of `target`, `to` and `channelId` before folding them: Telegram's chat reader accepts numbers, while the fold and the check read only strings.
  - When a Telegram target's encoded topic and an explicit `threadId` disagree, the check follows Telegram's delivery precedence: the explicit thread wins. Telegram's `resolveCurrentChannelId` now goes through `formatTelegramDeliveryTarget`, the helper Telegram already uses to name a delivered send (moved unchanged into `targets.ts`).
  - The shared param readers accept each key's snake_case form, and Telegram's handler reads `messageThreadId` or `message_thread_id` before `threadId` or `thread_id`. Action normalization now folds every one of those four spellings into one string `threadId` before any check, including a numeric `threadId`, which core's string reader would otherwise skip. Values that disagree are refused, and so is any value alongside an explicit `threadId: null`. On any channel, an action carrying only an alias, or a numeric `threadId`, gets that value as its string `threadId`.

What changed since `1cb5e029db3` (2026-11-10): `POST /tools/invoke` now reports the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, so `confineChatTypes` applies to header-bound direct calls as it does to a turn from that conversation (`9aadc2bbc5c`). The Bot API traces at `1cb5e029db3` showed the gap: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the topic-A headers, all nine direct calls were delivered, including a `sendMessage` to the owner DM and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on it. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` now sets `currentChatType` on the direct-invocation surface from the bound target, with the resolver outbound target resolution already uses, `inferChatTypeFromTarget` (now exported from `src/infra/outbound/targets.ts`; for Telegram it asks the plugin's `parseTelegramTarget`). Calls without the headers, the RPC `tools.invoke` and the MCP loopback surface are unchanged. `src/gateway/tool-resolution.direct-invoke-confinement.test.ts` fails on `1cb5e029db3` (`promise resolved "{ content: [ { …(2) } ], …(1) }" instead of rejecting` for a sibling-topic send from a header-bound call) and passes on this head; `92aee940aa8` raises the test-line allocation by its 62 lines.

On this head the Gateway logs each refusal. Under `confineChatTypes` it ends with the confinement reason, for example `MessageActionDeniedError: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target="<group>:topic:99" while bound to "telegram:<group>:topic:42" (channel=telegram). tools.message.crossContext.confineChatTypes keeps group turns in their current conversation.`; the `to`, `topic-edit` and `topic-create` rows name `target="telegram:<owner-dm>"`. The HTTP caller gets `500` with `{"type":"tool_error","message":"tool execution failed"}` for a refusal, on main as well.

What these runs also showed, and what they do not cover:
- At `1cb5e029db3` the `confineChatTypes` column was all delivered: with only `confineChatTypes: ["group"]` set and the same headers, all nine calls went out, including a `sendMessage` to `<owner-dm>` and `editForumTopic` and `createForumTopic` on `<owner-dm>`, because `/tools/invoke` reported no conversation kind. `9aadc2bbc5c` makes it report the kind of the conversation its headers bind it to, which gives the refusals above.
- Without the conversation headers, `/tools/invoke` has no current conversation on either build (`Action send requires a target. This turn has no current conversation; pass an explicit target, or reply in normal text.`), so no `crossContext` switch applies. This is unchanged by `9aadc2bbc5c`: in both runs on this head, under `confineChatTypes`, a `threadId` of 99, string or number, went to topic 99, as it does on main. `topic-edit` with `channelId` `<owner-dm>` acted on `<owner-dm>` as a string on both builds, and as a number on this head; main refused the number with that "requires a target" error.
- The Bot API is a loopback, not Telegram. The traces show what the Gateway sent, not how Telegram would answer.

prs.title: fix: avoid repeated grouping during tool-heavy turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes main-thread stalls during tool-heavy turns: finishing a nested tool rebuilt the presentation graph for every active and completed tool in the run.

## User Impact

Tool progress retains the same grouping, order, and outcomes while completion work scales with the affected ancestry. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The live presentation owner now records nesting at tool start, propagates visibility when a tool finishes, and publishes only newly hidden wrappers. This removes whole-run grouping, global active-tool enumeration, and repeated searches for completed wrapper metadata. History snapshot grouping and transcript cloning are unchanged.

The graph preserves late parents, ambiguous reused IDs, cycles, failed/cancelled tools, routine hidden calls, immutable published events, and compaction resets. Production code grows by 103 lines: the retained topology replaces the repeated scan while preserving those existing semantics. Tests add 170 lines; the rerunnable measurement script is separate.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: identical snapshots/deltas, zero unrelated activity reads, linear turn work, lower CPU/allocation at 100/500/1000 calls, and no worse maximum segment. Five counterbalanced A/A and A/B pairs, three turns per sample; timing and allocation runs are separate. The synthetic workload has 20-call groups, completed wrappers, late parallel child results, and routine/failed outcomes.

| Calls/turn | Base A1 CPU ms | Base A2 CPU ms | Candidate CPU ms | Base → candidate sampled allocation |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 10 | 0.107 | 0.120 | 0.044 | 164 KB → below sampling resolution |
| 100 | 6.428 | 6.386 | 0.195 | 12.69 MB → 65.7 KB |
| 500 | 118.654 | 122.149 | 0.900 | 255.48 MB → 395 KB |
| 1000 | 500.625 | 528.413 | 1.815 | 1006.84 MB → 906 KB |

Values are medians. At 1000 calls, CPU p95 is 574.353 ms before and 3.583 ms after; the per-sample maximum segment median/p95 is 19.898/127.221 ms before and 0.022/3.853 ms after. Wall tails varied on the loaded host. This is exact-owner proof with synthetic lifecycle bookkeeping on Node 26.12.1/macOS arm64, not a whole-Gateway latency claim. This owner performs no database or workspace I/O. Allocation sampling includes collected objects at a 32-KiB interval; a zero small-workload sample does not mean zero allocation.

At 1000 calls the baseline groups 951,000 call records in 951 invocations; the candidate makes zero live grouping calls. CPU profiles identify `groupToolCalls` as the dominant baseline owner frame. All measured snapshots and emitted delta sequences match.

Reproduce: `node --expose-gc scripts/perf/tool-activity-presentation-measure.mjs BASE_ROOT HEAD_ROOT`.

The subscribed-pipeline regression fails on the exact base with 102 reads of an unrelated completed activity, and passes with zero. The focused owner, tool ordering, tool handler, lifecycle, compaction, and history suites pass all 189 tests after correcting the partial lifecycle fixture. The new owner fixture also passes its focused typecheck after adding required activity fields. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. Unused-file checks pass with zero entries. `check:changed` found unrelated unused exports that reproduce on clean exact parent `db4b2edd6d0882dd93ce2fdc670a5861e42621f3`: `runPlannerFlow` in `scripts/bench-ci-planner.mts` (introduced by #195711, `ba284782cf170`) and `resolveTalkTranscriptionSelection`/`TalkTranscriptionCatalog` in `ui/src/pages/config/talk-transcription.tsx` (introduced by #197906, `c4ec183648940`). These are main validation regressions, not ignored noise. Patch-caused fixture type/lint errors were corrected; the complete core test typecheck and changed-file lint reruns pass. All remaining changed-check guards pass. Benchmark brace-style lint findings were also fixed and its targeted lint rerun passes.

The changed runtime modules have no imports under `ui/src`; this change does not alter the browser import boundary or rendered presentation.

prs.title: fix(ios): keep Talk replies below the spoken turn that prompted them
prs.body: Closes #197129 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: iOS Talk sometimes saves the assistant's reply above the user's spoken turn when the user's speech transcription finishes after the reply's transcript. ## User Impact User impact: in iOS Talk over a client-owned OpenAI realtime session, chat history keeps each spoken turn above the reply it prompted, whichever transcript finishes first. ## Why This Change Was Made Each turn now reserves its place in the conversation when it starts, and finished transcripts are sent to the Gateway in that order instead of arrival order. A turn that never finishes cannot block the conversation: later transcripts are sent after 5 s anyway, a failed or interrupted turn releases its place at once, and stopping Talk or starting a voice consult first sends every held transcript. This covers both standard OpenAI realtime events and the frameless `gpt-live-1-codex` events. Web Talk has the same arrival-order behavior but is not changed here; it can follow separately. ## Evidence Real iPhone (OC 102499, OpenAI `gpt-live-1-codex` over WebRTC, November 11): the assistant's "Hey Peter." was saved above the user's earlier "Hey, Chatting." The two finals reached the Gateway 65 ms apart (`talk.client.transcript` at 04:59:25.077Z and 04:59:25.142Z). iOS simulator run (Xcode 27.2), with lint phases skipped in that local run; CI runs lint. - **Unchanged `main` + the new race tests only:** both race tests fail with the bug's exact symptom, for standard and frameless events: ``` TalkRealtimeTranscriptOrderTests.swift:21: error: testLateUserTranscriptionPersistsBeforeTheReply : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("["assistant", "user"]") is not equal to ("["user", "assistant"]") TalkRealtimeTranscriptOrderTests.swift:34: error: testLateFramelessUserTurnPersistsBeforeTheReply : XCTAssertEqual failed: ("["assistant", "user"]") is not equal to ("["user", "assistant"]") Executed 3 tests, with 4 failures (0 unexpected) ``` - **With the fix, all Talk realtime tests:** `Executed 19 tests, with 0 failures` (XCTest: transcript order, stall/release cases, consult cancellation) and `Test run with 5 tests in 2 suites passed` (Swift Testing: event decoding, transcript write queue). - The stall tests cover the 5 s fallback, failed and interrupted turns, stop and consult sending held transcripts, reply text arriving after its completion event, and no item limit per session. Not yet shown: a run of the fixed build on a physical phone. The original bug was seen on a phone (screenshot in #197129). AI-assisted: written and tested by an AI agent (OpenClaw, Claude Opus 5.5 with Opus and codex review passes), directed and checked by @Marvinthebored.

prs.title: perf(gateway): keep static Control UI HTTP independent of media imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Serving ordinary Control UI HTML/assets eagerly loads assistant-media policy, playback and message-media dependencies, and reaches unrelated runtime code through a broad HTTP-auth barrel. This makes static HTTP serving depend on optional media capabilities it does not use.

Move the existing assistant-media HTTP handler into its existing message-media owner, load it only for the current matching media URL, and import authorization directly from its authoritative lightweight owner. All internal consumers move together; there is no compatibility re-export, new cache, configuration option, or policy.

## User Impact

Ordinary Control UI HTTP serving avoids unnecessary media/runtime import work. Media requests keep their existing authorization, tickets, query/method validation, streaming/cancellation and resource-custody behavior, including media access when dashboard hosting is disabled. Plugin-rewritten URLs are classified before loading the optional media owner.

This is a measured reduction in preexisting work, not a claim that the current hosted CI setup timeout has been fixed. The remaining hosted 85–90-second postcompiler interval is unqualified.

## Why This Change Was Made

The eager media-policy edge was introduced by #138856 (`7b1217e2e79e5b489ea542e3019f9e86c281529a`); the media-read and message-association cuts followed in #170540 and #172202. The lightweight auth owner was split in `b02cca4e00cdda9df4dc5bbeabdc3efddbf58d2f`, while the Control UI binding through the broad barrel dates to #126200 and its bootstrap copy to #179449. These owner files are unchanged between the last known green full run at `bb78f2bd` and this repair's pinned parent `49c99cf91a4df477fc4bd986701cee643cd9d36b`: they are not attributed as newly introduced hourly-CI regressions.

The cutover removes the old message-media module/export and keeps one media HTTP owner. The existing no-cache JSON response implementation moves into the existing lightweight Control UI HTTP utility so it is shared without duplication. Production changes are +20 lines; test changes are +20, and two obsolete registry entries are removed. Growth is the optional media loader's current-URL admission and cross-module imports; no new authorization or retained state is added. The media loader selects the receiver-independent handler through the existing named-export primitive. The routing owner now adapts the current raw HTTP request to its existing classifier, using the base path already normalized by the request owner. This brings the request router below its absolute 700-line limit without adding eager dependencies to generic module loaders, probes, upgrades or session routes.

Open #196180 separately moves stored-filename decoding into its shared owner. This change preserves the current implementation and does not copy that unreviewed proposal; its corresponding import now belongs to the media HTTP module.

## Evidence

- Exact-parent negative control: the existing real auto-root HTTP suite fails at the eager assistant-media policy import when that unrelated capability is unavailable. The candidate passes all four existing HTTP cases.
- All 137 existing media/security/routing sibling cases pass, including dashboard-disabled media, explicit-allow POST, current authority, tickets, roots, response cancellation and the plugin URL-rewrite boundary.
- The unchanged four-case route-assets browser flow passes in both baseline controls and the candidate through canonical bundled UI setup and the real production HTTP/file-worker path. All three arms use the runtime compiler preset and regenerate 12,678 inputs and 7,629 outputs.

| Metric | Baseline A1 | Baseline A2 | Candidate B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Setup wall |36.445s|25.452s|25.022s|
| Setup process CPU |3.508s|2.449s|1.978s|
| Sampled estimated V8 allocation |661.10MB|665.39MB|531.43MB|
| Setup RSS increase |417.09MB|421.78MB|351.78MB|
| Whole command wall |73.49s|59.72s|59.31s|
| Whole command user+system CPU |121.53s|98.22s|97.66s|
| Whole command maximum RSS |3.316GB|3.429GB|3.398GB|

Allocation and RSS changes exceed their A/A spread; wall and CPU improvements do not. These are three bounded fresh-process diagnostics with retained transform/build state and lane-local quiet only, not a cold-disk/hosted-runner or median/p95 campaign. Allocation is sampled V8 bytes, not exact or all-subprocess allocation; sampler overhead is shared across arms. Static graph reduction 3,925→3,045 counts repository modules reachable through static edges, not runtime evaluations.

The required full build and the direct Chromium stale-build consumer passed before the final raw-request adapter relocation. Their reuse is explicitly qualified by unchanged static/media/loader bytes, the same request-classification predicate and exact equality of all six affected import-root sets; they were not rerun or relabeled as executions of the final patch. The final four-case HTTP boundary suite and 20 existing routing cases pass after the raw-request adapter cutover. Fresh independent Codex review covers the complete final 17-file diff and supplied unchanged owner context and is scoped-clean through P2.

The initial `pnpm check:changed --base 49c99cf91a4df477fc4bd986701cee643cd9d36b` exited 1. All corrected final applicable stages pass: line-cap, wrapper, format, core types, all three export scans, canonical core/scripts lint, sidecar-loader and import-cycle checks. Successful max-lines/mock-export checks and unrelated guards are reused with unchanged relevant contracts. No final aggregate `check:changed` exit 0 is claimed, and no gate, allowance, assertion or deadline was relaxed.

prs.title: fix(doctor): recognize git checkouts whose root ends in whitespace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` classifies the install root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` before offering the git update path. The result was `.trim()`ed, so a checkout whose directory legitimately ends in whitespace (for example `/srv/openclaw `) had its meaningful trailing space stripped, failed the root comparison, and was reported as "not a git checkout". The operator then got the package-manager guidance note and no git-update offer, even though the install is a source checkout. The same root-cause shape was approved for `openclaw update status` in #196654 and already shipped in `src/projects/project-checkout.ts`.

Precedent: #196654 (same one-line predicate fix at the update-check call site; this PR covers the doctor sibling)

## Why This Change Was Made

`detectOpenClawGitCheckout` in `src/commands/doctor-update.ts` now removes only Git's final LF record terminator (`replace(/\n$/, "")`), preserving filesystem characters in the checkout path, exactly matching the approved #196654 wording. Ordinary checkouts, aliases, separate Git directories, and non-checkouts keep the current classification and messages.

Production LOC is `+2/-1` in one file.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

A source checkout under a whitespace-suffixed directory is now recognized by `openclaw doctor`, so the "Update OpenClaw from git before running doctor?" prompt (and the resulting git update flow) appears as it does for ordinary checkouts. Ordinary paths are byte-for-byte unaffected; a path that merely looks similar after trimming no longer misclassifies.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `4ec78cebcf3b`
- Current-main RED baseline: `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`
- Production entry: `maybeOfferUpdateBeforeDoctor` → `detectOpenClawGitCheckout` in `src/commands/doctor-update.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `detectOpenClawGitCheckout` at `src/commands/doctor-update.ts:32-34`
- Decision surface: the `"git" | "not-git" | "unknown"` classification that gates the git-update offer and the package-manager guidance note
- Recorder/readback boundary: `maybeOfferUpdateBeforeDoctor` return value plus the mocked `confirm`/`updateCommand` calls in the existing `src/commands/doctor-update.test.ts` harness
- Acceptance RED: on current main, a root of `/repo/source ` with `show-toplevel` returning `/repo/source \n` classifies as `not-git`: the offer resolves `false`, `confirm` is never called, and the package-manager note is printed
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, the same inputs classify as `git`: the offer resolves `true`, `confirm` is called once, and `updateCommand` receives `sourceUpdate: { root: "/repo/source " }`
- Legal control: the pre-existing table (another checkout, not-a-repository, missing git, inspection failure, host-owned install, non-interactive/non-TTY/declined gates, update-in-progress recursion) all passes unchanged — 11/11 prior cases green
- Cleanup: isolated vitest temp dirs only; no production Gateway, session, token, or config was touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Vitest shard on the real runner (Node 24.22.1, docker `lexiflow-all`):

```text
# BASE (76024435027d) + new test, via node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
FAIL src/commands/doctor-update.test.ts > offers the git update for a checkout whose root ends in whitespace
expected false to be true  (offer resolves false; confirm never called)
Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

```text
# HEAD (4ec78cebcf3b), same command
Tests  12 passed (12)   Duration ~100s (compiled-worker preparation dominates)
```

```text
# Legal control on HEAD: pre-existing classification/guidance table + interaction gates
Tests  12 passed (12)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-update.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 12/12 passed on exact head; RED reproduced on current main with only the new test
- Superseded: an earlier interactive-run gap was closed by the shipped-CLI proof below (produced on an unrestricted host with a real TTY); the vitest red/green at the classification boundary still stands.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+2/-1` (src/commands/doctor-update.ts)
- Test LOC: `+12` (src/commands/doctor-update.test.ts)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `resolveComparablePath` comparison and the approved `replace(/\n$/, "")` predicate from #196654; no new helper or export
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none (read-only discovery)

## Real behavior proof (shipped interactive CLI)

The review asked for terminal evidence from a physical whitespace-suffixed checkout. Reproduced with the compiled CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`, dist built from the pinned trees) running from a real Git checkout whose path ends in a meaningful space (`/tmp/oc-proof-doctor/leg2-head/openclaw-src `), inside a real TTY (tmux), with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and a real Git identity. The checkout's branch tracks an offline bare remote one empty commit ahead, so the offered update could actually fast-forward.

Base — current main `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`:

```text
◇ Update ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  This install is not a git checkout.                                   │
│  Run `openclaw update` to update via your package manager (npm/pnpm),  │
│  then rerun doctor.                                                    │
```

Doctor withholds the Git update offer and routes the operator to package-manager guidance.

Head — this PR `4ec78cebcf3b7a5b35ae8ec4ac00d18428fdbb0f`, same checkout shape and harness. The interactive prompt now appears (tmux capture):

```text
Doctor: maintenance admission
│
◆  Update OpenClaw from git before running doctor?
│  ● Yes / ○ No
```

Answering `Yes` enters the shipped source-update flow (same capture, after the answer):

```text
◇  Update OpenClaw from git before running doctor?
│  Yes
Doctor source update requires the accepted Git checkout.
```

That final line is the update flow's *second* install-kind probe (`src/infra/update-check.ts:278`, `result.stdout.trim()` — the same pathname-loss family). It is owned by the already-open, same-shape fix #196654 (`result.stdout.replace(/\n$/u, "")`); it is deliberately not duplicated here. With #196654 landed, the offered update fast-forwards this exact checkout. Classification — the boundary this PR changes — is proven at the real CLI: base routes to package-manager guidance, head offers the Git update from the same physical whitespace-suffixed checkout.

Not tested here: the completed `git pull` inside the update runner (blocked by the separately-owned #196654, disclosed above, not by this diff).

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Maintainer edits allowed: yes — address review comments directly on this branch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready: one-line predicate aligned with the already-reviewed #196654; proof is red/green on the real test runner.
- Alternative: fold into #196654 as a second commit; kept separate because doctor-update and update-check are different owners.
- Scope declaration: behavior-completing only; no change to update execution, only to the doctor discovery predicate.

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): capture published catalog for read-only setup probes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Setup inference (`openclaw.setup.verify`) loses the configured agent's published subscription routes and rejects a usable OAuth profile with `Explicit auth order for openai has no usable profiles.`

`acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime` (used by setup inference and isolated completion probes) runs an ephemeral `readOnly` prepared model runtime. Its catalog capture comparison in `prepared-model-runtime-lease.ts` compared `ownerKey()` values that still included the read-only execution identity and the gateway subagent-binding capability. Because a setup probe is `readOnly: true`, uses the projected execution config, and does not request the subagent-binding capability, its key never matched the configured owner published at Gateway startup — so the probe captured an empty static catalog and lost the configured agent's OAuth subscription rows. Auth planning then found no usable profile and failed with the explicit-order error.

## Solution

Compare the catalog source with the read-only identity and the gateway subagent-binding capability excluded, so a read-only probe captures the configured agent's published catalog while keeping its own execution owner. This:

- **does not weaken the execution `ownerKey`** — the probe still runs under its own ephemeral read-only owner;
- **does not grant subagent-binding authority** — the configured owner's `allowGatewaySubagentBinding` is not copied onto the probe;
- **does not change auth policy** — auth still resolves through the probe's own read-only profile store.

The fix follows the same "execution purpose isolates plugins, not the configured agent's published inventory" precedent already used to exclude `loadRuntimePlugins`/`runtimePluginPurpose`/`runtimePluginSelections` from the catalog-source comparison, extended to the read-only projection dimensions.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** `prepared-model-runtime.test.ts > captures the configured agent's published catalog for a read-only setup probe`: red on the base (empty catalog, `expected [] to include 'openai/gpt-5.5'`), green with the fix (captures `openai/gpt-5.5`), and asserts the probe keeps its own scratch workspace (execution isolation).
- **Related suites pass** (71 tests): `prepared-model-runtime.test.ts`, `prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts`, `prepared-model-runtime.catalog-owner.test.ts`.
- The existing `keeps an isolated setup probe exact after a gateway replacement` test stays green — read-only probes still keep their own execution owner.

Fixes #196817

prs.title: fix(subagents): report the failing context cleanup phase
prs.body:
Related: #197335, #197990.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading subagent context-cleanup diagnostics: failures while loading a registry, resolving an engine, checking ownership, or disposing resources are all reported as an `onSubagentEnded` failure, even when the default legacy engine has no such hook.

## User Impact

Operators can identify the failing step from the warning's new `phase` field: `registry`, `resolve`, `authority`, `notify`, or `dispose`. Error identity, best-effort handling, plugin isolation, retry behavior, and cleanup ordering stay unchanged. This is diagnostic preparation; the reported production closed-scope failure remains unresolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track the phase within each notification attempt, resetting it when plugin replacement retries delivery. Preserve the first failure's phase if disposal also fails. No configuration, schema, cache, or new log stream is added.

The lifecycle investigation overlaps #197335. The separately reproduced Tool Search `agent_end` failure is covered by #197990; neither is duplicated here. The diagnostic change adds 17 production lines because the existing catch lacks the information needed to distinguish its five operations.

## Evidence

- New warning-attribution cases on the original code: 5 fail, 10 existing tests pass. The cases cover all five phases, including a notification failure followed by a secondary disposal failure.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the system prompt stable when task suggestions are not granted
prs.body:
## Problem

A Control UI (or TUI) session renders one system prompt for the user's own turns and a different one for turns that arrive from elsewhere: `sessions_send` from another session, subagent settle, cron, wakes. Every alternation re-writes the whole conversation at Anthropic cache-write price.

On a production gateway the `[prompt-cache]` detector repeatedly reported `systemPromptSuffix` changes in the **Tooling** and **Session routing** sections on `trigger=user provenance=inter_session:*` turns. A fix that merged earlier for completion wakes (run-granted `skill_library`) covered part of the Tooling difference; it did not cover this one.

## Root cause

`suggest_task` and `dismiss_task` are offered only when the turn's **requesting client** is an operator UI with `operator.admin` and the `task-suggestions` capability:

- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-request.ts` (`supportsTaskSuggestions`) and `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.ts` set `taskSuggestionDeliveryMode: "gateway"` from the client connection.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` adds the two tools only in that mode.

A turn without that client (inter-session, cron, wake) does not have the tools. The cached system prompt changed in two places:

1. The deferred-tool directory in **Tooling** lost the `suggest_task` / `dismiss_task` rows.
2. **Session routing** (`src/agents/delegation-guidance.ts`) lost its `suggest_task` bullet.

## Fix

Use the mechanism that already exists for run-granted tools:

- Both tools are marked `runGranted` in `core-tool-facts.ts`, like `skill_library`. The cached directory omits them, and the turn that holds the grant lists them in its own runtime context ("Deferred tools granted for this turn"). The flag also stops "unavailable core tool" allowlist warnings for them, which is correct because they are absent on some turns by design.
- Session routing no longer renders the `suggest_task` bullet. The tool's own description already carries that guidance (records a card only; not for explicit requests to start a session).

Which turns get the tools does not change. The Codex app-server thread prompt, which renders its own delegation section, is not changed.

## Proof

**Real route, before vs after.** Isolated throwaway Gateway (scratch state, no channels), real Anthropic-compatible provider route, `cacheRetention: short`. A logging proxy recorded the provider's own `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` and the system-prompt digest. User turns were sent as an operator UI client (TUI identity: `operator.admin` + `task-suggestions`, through `chat.send`), the same gate the Control UI passes. Target session: UI turn, UI turn, then another session's `sessions_send` into it, then a UI turn.

| target-session request | before: read / write | after: read / write |
|---|---|---|
| UI turn 1 | 11,640 / 19,589 | 11,640 / 19,623 |
| UI turn 2 | 12,785 / 19,411 | 12,921 / 19,445 |
| **`sessions_send` turn** | **12,785 / 20,310** | **32,366 / 1,097** |
| UI turn 3 | 32,196 / 2,065 | 33,463 / 1,307 |

- Before: 2 system prompts in the session. The `sessions_send` turn's prompt differed exactly by the two `suggest_task`/`dismiss_task` directory rows and the Session routing bullet (diffed from captured bodies), and re-wrote 20.3k tokens.
- After: 1 system prompt for every target-session request. UI turns still list both tools in their own runtime context. The `sessions_send` turn does not.

Separate from this change, the second request of a fresh session (UI turn 2 above) re-wrote ~19k in both arms. I reproduced it with plain UI turns and no inter-session input, and found no byte difference in system, tools, parameters or message prefix. It happens once per session, on this route only. I did not investigate it further here.

**Focused tests:**
- `tool-search-directory.test.ts`: the cached directory is identical with or without each run-granted tool (`skill_library`, `suggest_task`, `dismiss_task`). The grant is listed separately.
- `delegation-guidance.test.ts`: Session routing renders the same with or without the task-suggestion grant.

## Not covered

`Skills`-only suffix changes in production also happen on ordinary user turns (8 of 15 with no provenance). They track environment changes (skill catalog edits and the remote-node availability line inside the Skills section), not the trigger. Separate follow-up.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep provider history append-only across runs
prs.body:
## Problem

The Anthropic prompt cache of a long session broke at the first request of a new run, even with no compaction and no config change. The existing `[prompt-cache]` detector reported:

```
[prompt-cache] message N (assistant) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only;
changed fields: content.length, content[k].type, content[k].id, content[k].name, content[k].arguments
```

and sometimes `content[0].thinking/thinkingSignature` or `envelope.api/provider/model`. On a production gateway over 2 days there were 23 of these. Each re-wrote the whole conversation (up to ~500k tokens) at cache-write price.

I matched every event to its session transcript. Each one comes from one of two writes that put different bytes into the transcript than the live run sent to the provider.

## Root cause

1. **Unknown tool calls were dropped at persistence** (~16 of 23 events). `src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.ts` (`guardedAppend`) sanitized each assistant message with the run's tool allowlist before persisting it. The model sometimes calls a tool name that does not exist, often in parallel with a valid call. The live run answers that call (`Tool X not found`) and keeps it in provider history. But at append time the result does not exist yet, so the guard treated the call as incomplete and removed it from the transcript. The next run replayed the transcript: that assistant message lost a block (`content.length`, `content[k].*`), and the orphaned result was dropped. Replay sanitization (`sanitizeToolCallInputs`) already keeps *completed* calls and applies the allowlist only to calls without results ("Completed replay facts survive capability removal"). The append-time filter predates that rule and contradicted it.

2. **Publication receipts were inserted mid-history** (~7 of 23 events). `src/gateway/github-publication-transcript.ts` appends the `gateway-publication` receipt (a model-visible assistant row) when the publication finishes. That often happens while a run is active, for example between a tool call and its tool result. The live run never sees the row. The next run replays it in the middle of history, so every later message shifts (`envelope.api/provider/model` changes, and the "thinking changed" variants are the same shift). Background automation results already handle this case: during active work they are written as pending rows, and the live run's next request places them at the end (`openclaw.background-result-placement`). Receipts did not use that path.

## Fix

- The guard no longer filters persisted tool calls by allowlist. The live run and the transcript now hold the same assistant message. Replay still drops unknown calls that never got a result. Format checks (missing id/input, invalid names, partial JSON) are unchanged. The now-unused `allowedToolNames` guard option and its plumbing (including a perf probe script) are removed.
- A publication receipt that lands while the session has active work is written as the existing pending background-result row (`automation-result`, `excludeFromContext`, `openclawModelPlacement: "pending"`). It keeps its `github-publication:<requestId>` response id. The placement predicates do not change, and this adds no new stored shape: current and older versions already place these rows. A receipt written while the session is idle is unchanged.

## Proof

**Real route, before vs after (cause 1).** Isolated throwaway gateway (scratch state, no channels), real Anthropic-compatible provider route, `cacheRetention: short`. A logging proxy recorded the provider's own `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens`. Opus does not call an undefined tool on request; production calls are spontaneous. So the proxy renamed the second of two parallel `exec` calls in the provider's first tool response to an unknown name (`mesh_process`, a name seen in production). Every request after that, and all cache numbers, are the real provider's.

| request | before: read / write | after: read / write |
|---|---|---|
| turn 1 | 11,640 / 20,813 | 11,640 / 20,813 |
| turn 1, tool results | 32,453 / 240 | 32,453 / 240 |
| **turn 2** | **12,260 / 20,759** | **32,693 / 493** |
| turn 3 | 33,019 / 406 | 33,186 / 408 |

- Before: the gateway logged `message 2 (assistant) differs from the previous request … changed fields: content.length, content[1].type, content[1].id, content[1].name, content[1].arguments` and `cache read dropped 32453 -> 12260`. This is the production signature.
- After: no `[prompt-cache]` warnings. Session cache writes fell from 42.2k to 22.0k. In production, each such event re-wrote the full conversation.

**Cause 2** has no isolated trigger: a receipt needs an accepted GitHub publication, and the throwaway gateway refuses before acceptance. It is covered by an integration test through the real session manager and SQLite transcript (below). The production mapping above is the field evidence.

**Focused tests:**
- `attempt-session-tool-call-persistence.test.ts` (new; fails on the base, passes here): through the production `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSessionManager` path, a parallel call to an unknown tool and its results persist exactly as the live run sent them.
- `background-session-result.test.ts` (fails on the base, passes here): a publication receipt that lands during a tool call appears after the tool result in the live request, and the cold replay prefix equals that request.
- `agent-session-code-mode-source.test.ts`: updated. The answered unavailable call now stays in the persisted message, as the provider saw it.

## Not covered (follow-up)

`systemPromptSuffix` changes on inter-session turns (`sessions_send`, subagent settle) in **Session routing** / **Tooling**. `suggest_task` is offered only when the triggering client is a Control UI operator client with the task-suggestions capability (`chat-send-request.ts`, `agent-run-execution-phase.ts`). Inter-session, cron and wake turns have no such client, so the tool and its Session routing bullet appear and disappear by trigger. This PR does not change it.

prs.title: feat(ui): traverse sessions with bracket shortcuts
prs.body:
Closes #197878
Related: #87662. Attention-based navigation in #182559 is intentionally out of scope.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators reviewing neighboring sessions need a direct previous/next action without repeatedly searching the command palette or using the mouse.

## User Impact

Users can press **Cmd+[ / Cmd+]** on macOS, or **Ctrl+[ / Ctrl+]** elsewhere, to move up/down the loaded sidebar session tree, wrapping at its ends. Filters, collapsed sections/children, ordering, and normal session selection remain owned by the existing sidebar; repeated appearances are visited once. If the current session is absent or there is no neighbor, nothing is selected.

Typing, IME composition, dialogs/menus, and embedded-frame focus are protected. A held chord performs one traversal and suppresses browser-history repeats until release. Gateway/digit shortcuts and command-palette behavior are unchanged.

**Mac app shortcut change:** its existing Back/Forward menu equivalents also occupied Cmd+[ / Cmd+]. They move to **Cmd+Option+Left/Right Arrow**; Previous/Next Session use the bracket chords and the same web-side guards. The native bindings require a rebuilt Mac app plus the updated Control UI; this PR does not alter an installed app.

## Why This Change Was Made

This narrows the stale-closed, locked #87662 to cyclic session navigation instead of positional digits. [The Discord follow-up](https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1458141495701012561/1570229010242347169) advised refiling and submitting an implementation, explicitly without a guarantee of acceptance. This is community guidance, not a claim of maintainer product approval.

The shortcut handler delegates to the existing sidebar projection and selection path. It adds no session list, persistent preferences, pagination requests, or alternate route owner. The existing shell owner tracks only the claimed held key and releases it on keyup, blur, or shell disconnect. Native menu commands re-enter at the focused element; frame boundaries are not crossed. The simplification pass retained this state only to prevent the independently reviewed browser-history regression.

## Evidence

### Current readiness — `5ba0a13799444ff0a8f9c3d796b899c833e80304`

**Current-head CI is green:** [run 43359427211](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43359427211) completed successfully on this exact head: 45 successful jobs, 25 skipped. The CI gate, performance, and all four previously failed jobs passed. Skips are not verification. Still not a full runtime/product-ready or 6/6 claim. Prior CI run [43337663926](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43337663926) failed four root jobs. This head includes the reviewed clipboard-isolation repair, sidebar-dismissal completion assertion, and upstream integration through `0633f256350b5580a5bdbcd8a6a5782750de03d4`. New Session recovery and raw-details transcript anchoring **did not recur in current-head CI**; their original transient root causes remain unproven. This is current-head passing evidence, not a claimed deterministic repair of those two failures.

- **Clipboard:** the account-menu suite owns a private Chromium process. Its real-clipboard regression fails with a competing writer on the shared browser and passes with isolation. No clipboard mock or global serialization.
- **Sidebar:** the test waits for reactive removal separately from synchronous focus restoration. Updated WebKit file passed 20/20; Chromium follow-up passed 38/38 across three projects/files. Original WebKit failure is retained; no local red reproduction is claimed.
- **Animation:** adopted upstream's permitted reduced-motion duration assertions rather than maintaining a duplicate local fix.
- **Latest integrated candidate:** four production-bundle E2E files pass **19/19**, including account-menu, clipboard competition, New Session recovery/revisit, and transcript disclosure. These use a synthetic Gateway, not a real model. Existing focused type/lint/format checks passed before the mechanical upstream integration.
- **Review:** canonical local Codex autoreview of the complete staged/unstaged candidate against `01c9fc93632fe3fcba5749388967ba1112fc3972` completed scoped-clean at P0–P2. Subsequent integration adopts upstream's animation assertion verbatim and preserves the reviewed repair hunks. Reviewer did not execute code and lacked unchanged implementation context; integration testing remains separate evidence.
- **New-base performance gap:** candidate production build succeeds. The local comparison against `0633f2563` could not build the archived base because filesystem file-identity validation failed. Its fallback absolute-budget check is red; no valid new-base differential result is claimed. Earlier differential passes below belong to their stated bases. The exact-head remote performance job subsequently passed, qualifying the gate against the actual CI base; the failed local comparison is not presented as a pass.
- Physical Mac shortcuts/main-menu interaction, latest-stable app upgrade behavior, completed real-model browser proof, and maintainer approval of bracket/history reassignment remain open. No merge, deployment, or recurring watcher.

### Historical repair evidence

The following results apply to their stated earlier bases/heads, not automatically to the current head.

### CI remediation

- Integrated the failing CI comparison base `4dea0383ed44f6d19c6fd648d16d8d128085750f`, then upstream `2035b0730f826f8f431c69c8737f89c70a1fe8c4`. The latter contains the official wrapper inventory repair in #197976; the branch adds no independent inventory change against that base. The intervening upstream commits do not change UI, package, toolchain, or UI-performance inputs.
- **Upstream table resolution:** #197954 landed as `6c32a15729f269d6ed44b89713eb6ae004f15ab1` while the first repair push was publishing, causing one stylesheet conflict and preventing CI from starting on that intermediate head. The final merge adopts upstream's typed `--chat-table-outset`/clamp implementation verbatim and removes the duplicate local table repair. There is no stylesheet diff against the new base. Independent resolution review found no actionable P0–P2 findings; all 47 affected table, bubble, and mobile-gutter browser cases pass.
- **Performance:** the original exact-base failure reproduced Chat 1,310,444 → 1,310,814 B gzip (+370 B). Twelve external-session menu strings now register synchronously at the existing lazy sidebar-menu boundary. Hot view-only reasons stay eager; no keyboard event handling moved. The serialized canonical comparison passed against `4dea0383`: Chat **1,310,444 → 1,310,265 B gzip (−179 B)**; New Session **811,729 → 810,931 B (−798 B)**. After the table merge, a fresh serialized comparison also **passes against `6c32a1572`**, with candidate Chat **1,310,265 B gzip** and New Session **810,931 B gzip**. The largest-shared-JS and CSS differential gates pass; limits and 64 B variance are unchanged. These are differential passes over an already-over-budget base, not claims that absolute caps pass. Canonical English ordering and namespace identity are retained; foreign translation memory, fallback metadata, and raw-copy baseline are unchanged against the integrated base.
- Fresh independent source review of the final repairs found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The author simplification pass retains existing owners and loading boundaries; no new runtime state, event deferral, test skip, retry allowance, or relaxed performance limit was introduced. The earlier CLI autoreview authentication failure is not presented as a clean review. The independent source reviewer did not rerun the author's builds or tests.

prs.title: fix(cron): cancel interrupted edit-job reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: interrupting `cron edit <id>` leaves its pending `cron.get` read running until the CLI launcher forcibly kills the process about two seconds later.

`cron edit` loads the existing job through `readCronJobForEdit`, which called `callGatewayFromCli("cron.get", ...)` with no abort signal. #197315 introduced `callCronReadFromCli` and routed the other cron read commands (`status`, `get`, `runs`, read-only `scratch`, `list`, `show`) through it, but the edit path was missed. The edit read is the one remaining cron read that Ctrl-C/SIGTERM cannot cancel.

## User Impact

`cron edit` now stops its pending job read promptly on Ctrl-C/SIGTERM and exits via the normal interrupt path instead of hanging until the launcher emergency-kill. Interrupted edits report no late result or error. Mutations still wait for and report their receipts (unchanged).

## Why This Change Was Made

Same shape as the accepted cron-read cancellation from #197315 (which followed #187726): reuse the existing `callCronReadFromCli` helper so the read participates in the CLI async-work cancellation scope. One call-site change plus import; no new RPC, cancellation policy, option, config, protocol/schema, permission or upgrade change.

## Evidence

Discriminator test red on base, green on head:
- BASE (`28d20f9532f4`): the new `cancels cron edit reads` test fails — after `scope.beginClose(SIGINT)`, the pending `cron.get` promise never settles (the read has no abort signal), so the tracked command never resolves and no output/exit is produced.
- HEAD (`8b653df77506`): `src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts` passes in full — **72 passed**, including `cancels cron edit reads`. The read is now wired to the async-work signal, so the abort rejects the pending read and the command settles exactly once with no stdout/stderr/exit side effects.

Command: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/cron-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (Linux, Node 24.22.1).

Proof ceiling: a shipped source-CLI PTY probe against a loopback held-response peer does not separate base from head, because the CLI launcher's top-level SIGINT handler terminates the process in both cases; the observable difference is whether the pending read is cancelled, which the focused discriminator test captures directly (base read never settles / head read aborts). This mirrors the unit-level cancellation proof used across the already-merged cron/CLI interrupt family (#197315, #197491, #197747, #197758).

Production: +2/-1 lines in `register.cron-edit.ts` (one call-site swap + one import). Tests: +36 lines in the existing `cron-cli.test.ts`. No new files.

Precedent: #197315 (same helper, same file family). Collision check: #197704 touches `register.cron-edit.ts` but only adds a `--clear-access` option declaration in a different region; no overlap with the `readCronJobForEdit` read path.

Built CLI and Gateway proof (main vs candidate, two rounds each, SIGINT and SIGTERM, plus controls): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198012#issuecomment-6842414738

prs.title: feat(agents): support required manual-step handoffs in chat
prs.body:
Related: #192713 (effective-tool CLI diagnostics, not chat recovery).

## What Problem This Solves

An agent cannot represent a required human-only step through its structured question tool, so a blocked task falls back to prose or an optional decision whose cancellation says to proceed with best judgment.

## User Impact

The existing chat question panel can explain the observed blocker and supported manual step, with an optional **Open link** action, while the original turn waits. The user does not repeat the task. **Ready to recheck** returns to that turn for a fresh check—not a declaration of success, authentication, or permission. **Stop this task**, Skip, and expiry return an explicitly unresolved outcome instead of the optional-decision fallback.

Existing sign-in, approval, native-permission, and desktop-ownership flows remain authoritative. No new approval prompt or automatic takeover is introduced. This is not a universal recovery framework, a scheduler-level lock on other work, or a durable restart ledger. The agent must verify the prerequisite through its owning tool before continuing effects; unavailable capabilities and unsuccessful checks remain blockers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared question contract already supports URL navigation separately from answering, exact-run attribution, human-input waiting, cancellation, expiry, and reconnect recovery. Its model-facing adapter and result semantics were decision-only. Add an opt-in `requiredAction` to that existing `ask_user` owner; ordinary decisions and the delegated channel/model/setup guard are unchanged.

This replaces the earlier plugin-only candidate with the shared-owner fix. The previous implementation remains in commit history, not the current diff. Production changes are confined to three existing agent modules (+105 net lines), without a new manager, protocol, storage, UI renderer, or configuration option.

## Evidence

### November 13 redacted regression fixture

Published head [`723eef051b8954c7ff62686a6a8f2c768884de34`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/723eef051b8954c7ff62686a6a8f2c768884de34) preserves original PR history and differs from `ac614097` by one test-fixture value only. prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.
- Shared failed factory: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` sanitizes the failure `message` before building `contentItems`.
- Regression: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts` spies `readLoggingConfig` with nonmatching `redactPatterns` `[String.raw`\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\b`]`, asserts `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` still contains the synthetic bearer (before), and asserts model-visible `contentItems` do not (after `sanitizeToolResult`). Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

```text
Product head: 67505f4ca5c482f9eac9474cd0a6f25bf4afc2bd
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.thrown-error-redaction.test.ts --reporter=verbose
PASS redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items under custom logging patterns
```

Configures logging.redactPatterns=["never-match-custom-redact-pattern-141271"] via isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH so formatToolExecutionErrorMessage still contains the synthetic bearer (defaults bypassed), then asserts the bridge response does not.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Thrown dynamic-tool error content could include unsanitized credentials when diagnostic redact patterns replace defaults.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.
- **Boundary crossed:** Extension dynamic-tool error content → shared `sanitizeToolResult` from plugin-sdk agent-harness-runtime (model-visible policy merges built-ins).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused existing `sanitizeToolResult`; no new helper.
- **Real environment tested:** Local diagnostic harness against production `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` + `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse` under custom `logging.redactPatterns`. **Live Codex binary was NOT used** — this records the actual protocol response object returned toward Codex, not a full app-server binary round-trip.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text
# Codex dynamic-tool thrown-error redaction diagnostic
# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)
# Proof surface: createCodexDynamicToolBridge → handleToolCall catch path
#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)
# Synthetic credential only — non-usable fixture.

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;
 model-visible sanitizeToolResult merges built-ins.)

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

sanitizeToolResult(formatted) alone (model-visible built-ins):
{
  "sanitizedAlone": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
}
contains synthetic credential: false

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server
toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse(createCodexDynamicToolBridge.handleToolCall(...)):
{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"
    }
  ],
  "success": false
}

success: false
contentItems text contains synthetic credential: false
contentItems text contains "Authorization: Bearer": true

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.
- After sanitizeToolResult on the catch path, protocol contentItems do NOT contain it.
- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

- **Vitest (distinguishing regression):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts -t 'redacts credentials from thrown' --reporter=verbose
 ✓ |extension-codex| extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts > createCodexDynamicToolBridge > redacts credentials from thrown dynamic tool error content items 38ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 172 skipped (173)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 25.56s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Under custom nonmatching `redactPatterns`, diagnostic formatting still contains the synthetic bearer; protocol `contentItems` after the catch-path sanitizer do not (`Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890`).
- **What was not tested:** Live Codex app-server / `@openai/codex` binary round-trip. Proof surface is the real bridge + protocol response object.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
