prs.title: fix(templates): Template review and publish fail when the name or description has stray spaces
prs.body:
Related: #196644 — that PR edits the same four lines for a different reason; this PR is written against `main` so neither depends on the other, and the combined shape is in Evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: reviewing or publishing a Template fails with a field-less `invalid_manifest` error when its display name or description carries leading or trailing whitespace.

`prepareTemplateDraft` copies the review selections and the authored draft text straight into the CLAW.md manifest, while the manifest owner (`nonEmptyString` in `src/templates/schema.ts`) rejects any value with leading or trailing whitespace. A padded name or description therefore made `templates.drafts.review` and `templates.drafts.publish` fail with `invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.` — an error that names no field, no source and no remedy, so the Template could not be published until someone guessed which string to retype.

- Problem: whitespace around a value that already passed the review-schema gate was re-rejected by the manifest schema, turning cosmetic padding into an unrecoverable publication failure.
- Solution: normalize the name and description at the boundary that assembles the manifest (`src/templates/draft.ts`), so the schema owner stays authoritative and the review keeps working with the text the reviewer accepted.
- What changed: one production file (`src/templates/draft.ts`, +4/−2) plus regression coverage folded into two existing cases — `src/templates/draft.test.ts` (owner lane) and `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts` (Gateway handler lane for `templates.drafts.publish`, driven against a real loopback `node:http` ClawHub registry). Net test lines: +6, no new test file, no allocation entry. The product entry point itself is evidenced below with a built Gateway process reached over a real WebSocket, outside the test runner.
- What did NOT change: `nonEmptyString` and every other manifest schema rule, the review-choices protocol schema in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/template-drafts.ts`, the slug-derived title-cased default, the `@publisher/name` package id, what a review may exclude, and every other Template field (skills, plugins, mcpServers, automations, workspace files).

## User Impact

User impact: a Template whose name or description carries stray spaces now reviews and publishes, keeping the text the reviewer accepted, instead of failing on every attempt with an error that names no field. This also unblocks the most common trigger — an agent-authored draft description ending in a space, which failed before any selection was made. A whitespace-only display name falls back to the readable title-cased default instead of blocking publication.

Risk: published manifests now carry the trimmed form of a string the reviewer saw with padding — the value the review already intended, and the only other reader of these two fields is the manifest validator itself. In-range, unpadded values are byte-identical to before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The authoring surface and the consumer surface disagree about the same string. `TemplateDraftDocumentSchema.description` is `Optional(Text)` (no trim rule) and `ReviewChoices.displayName` is only `minLength: 1`, so padded text is legal right up to the moment `prepareTemplateDraft` writes it into the manifest — and the draft text is what an agent writes into a chat-authored proposal, so `"…brief. "` reaches publication with no user ever typing a space. Following the repo rule to fix invalid state at the producer and validate untrusted input once at its trust boundary, the normalization belongs where the manifest is assembled, not in the schema.

- Best fix: trim the two strings where they are read (`displayName`, and the whole `choices → authored → manifest` description chain), then let the existing owner validate. A whitespace-only `displayName` falls back to the existing slug-derived title-cased default, because that is already the answer to an absent name.
- Alternative rejected: relaxing `nonEmptyString`. That refinement is shared by other manifest fields and is still being extended — open PR #197402 reuses it for `conversationStarters` — so loosening it would let padded text into published CLAW.md files that other readers compare verbatim.
- Alternative rejected: a friendlier `invalid_manifest` message. That still leaves the user with a Template they cannot publish and a field they cannot edit, because the Control UI shows the text as-is and sends it back unchanged (`ui/src/pages/templates/creator-flow.ts:359` reuses the previous review result as the next `choices`).
- Risk: one 4-line producer change with no schema, protocol or UI contract touched; both shipped entry points are red on `main` and green on this head, at the product entry point and in the folded regression cases.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Gateway entry point (the real product path)

Two throwaway checkouts, each built from its own head with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts runtime` and each verified by the shipped bundle itself:

```console
$ node dist/index.js --version                       # checkout at origin/main
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (02f2959)
$ node dist/index.js --version                       # checkout at this PR head
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (0aaa1c0)
```

Each lane then runs that bundle as its own OS process and talks to it over a real WebSocket — nothing is imported in-process:

- server: `node dist/index.js gateway run` with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, `gateway.mode=local`, `gateway.auth.mode=token`, `gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates=true`, `tools.profile=minimal`, `plugins.slots.memory=none`, ready on `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` after `/readyz` answers;
- registry: the ClawHub endpoints are a loopback `node:http` stub (`OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, `CLAWHUB_TOKEN` set to a synthetic value — no real credential is used anywhere). `/api/v1/whoami` returns handle `maker`; `/api/v1/packages` receives the real upload, keeps the `clawpack` bytes and echoes back the reviewed digest, so `published` is confirmed against the artifact this run actually produced;
- client: the shipped `GatewayClient` (`src/gateway/client.ts`, the same client class the CLI uses) with `role=operator` and the `operator.admin` scope — the scope `templates.drafts.*` requires (`src/gateway/methods/core-descriptor.ts`), so `draftAuthority` is satisfied by a live socket rather than a constructed context;
- input: the same research-brief draft the product writes, saved through `templates.drafts.save`, then reviewed with `displayName: "  Engineering Partner  "` and `description: " A collaborative engineering partner. "`.

| step, over the real Gateway socket | `origin/main` `02f29597c10` | this head `0aaa1c0bc63` |
|---|---|---|
| `templates.drafts.create` | `draftId=<uuid>` | `draftId=<uuid>` |
| `templates.drafts.save` (padded-prone draft body) | ok | ok |
| `templates.drafts.review` with padded choices | `INVALID_REQUEST: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.` | ok — `displayName="Engineering Partner"` `description="A collaborative engineering partner."` |
| reviewed `CLAW.md` agent fields | never produced | `name: Engineering Partner` \| `description: A collaborative engineering partner.` |
| `templates.drafts.publish` with the review token | unreachable — review never returns a token | `publicationStatus: "published"` for `@maker/research-brief@0.1.0` |
| `CLAW.md` inside the uploaded `.tgz` artifact | — | `name: Engineering Partner` \| `description: A collaborative engineering partner.` |

Raw output, base lane (`origin/main` `02f29597c10`, its own `dist/`):

```console
[base] built dist/index.js gateway ready on ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
[base] real WebSocket operator connection established (token redacted)
[base] templates.drafts.create -> draftId=db612157-ad5f-4963-883c-f9646c569931
[base] templates.drafts.save -> research-brief draft stored through the Gateway
[base] templates.drafts.review choices={"name":"research-brief","displayName":"  Engineering Partner  ","description":" A collaborative engineering partner. ","excluded":[]}
[base] FAILED at unknown: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.
[base] gateway stopped (exit null); scratch removed
```

Raw output, candidate lane (this head `0aaa1c0bc63`, its own `dist/`):

```console
[candidate] built dist/index.js gateway ready on ws://127.0.0.1:<port>
[candidate] real WebSocket operator connection established (token redacted)
[candidate] templates.drafts.create -> draftId=eeec717e-a6d4-4ece-9c0e-5911fe04cae9
[candidate] templates.drafts.save -> research-brief draft stored through the Gateway
[candidate] templates.drafts.review choices={"name":"research-brief","displayName":"  Engineering Partner  ","description":" A collaborative engineering partner. ","excluded":[]}
[candidate] review OK -> displayName="Engineering Partner" description="A collaborative engineering partner."
[candidate] reviewed CLAW.md agent fields: name: Engineering Partner | description: A collaborative engineering partner.
[candidate] publish -> {"name":"@maker/research-brief","version":"0.1.0","url":"http://127.0.0.1:<port>/maker/templates/research-brief","publicationStatus":"published","attemptId":"proof_attempt"}
[candidate] artifact uploaded to the loopback registry: /tmp/…/uploaded-template.tgz
[candidate] uploaded archive package/CLAW.md agent fields: name: Engineering Partner | description: A collaborative engineering partner.
[candidate] gateway stopped (exit null); scratch removed
```

The two lanes differ only in `src/templates/draft.ts`; the Gateway bundle, the config, the draft document, the choices and the registry stub are identical.

### 2. Owner-level behavior matrix

Same scratch checkout, `origin/main` `02f29597c10` vs candidate `0aaa1c0bc63`, with only `src/templates/draft.ts` swapped. The probe drives the shipped owner `prepareTemplateDraft` — the function `templates.drafts.review` and `templates.drafts.publish` call at `src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.ts:214` and `:251` — and prints the CLAW.md agent fields it produced.

| input | `origin/main` `02f29597c10` | candidate `0aaa1c0bc63` |
|---|---|---|
| review `displayName: "  Engineering Partner  "` + padded `description` | `FAILED: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.` | `name: Engineering Partner` \| `description: A collaborative engineering partner.` |
| review `displayName: "   "` (whitespace only) | `FAILED: invalid_manifest: …` | `name: Research Brief` (slug-derived default) |
| review `description: ""` — control, semantics must not change | `displayName="Research Brief" description=""` | `displayName="Research Brief" description=""` |
| authored draft description `"…cited brief. "`, **no review choices at all** | `FAILED: invalid_manifest: …` | `description: Compare primary sources into a cited brief.` |

Raw output, frozen `origin/main`:

```console
review choices: padded displayName + padded description
  -> FAILED: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.
review choices: whitespace-only displayName
  -> FAILED: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.
review choices: description cleared by review (control)
  -> displayName="Research Brief" description=""
  -> CLAW.md agent fields:   name: Research Brief
authored draft only, no review choices: padded description
  -> FAILED: invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.
```

Raw output, candidate:

```console
review choices: padded displayName + padded description
  -> displayName="Engineering Partner" description="A collaborative engineering partner."
  -> CLAW.md agent fields:   name: Engineering Partner |   description: A collaborative engineering partner.
review choices: whitespace-only displayName
  -> displayName="Research Brief" description="padded."
  -> CLAW.md agent fields:   name: Research Brief |   description: padded.
review choices: description cleared by review (control)
  -> displayName="Research Brief" description=""
  -> CLAW.md agent fields:   name: Research Brief
authored draft only, no review choices: padded description
  -> displayName="Research Brief" description="Compare primary sources into a cited brief."
  -> CLAW.md agent fields:   name: Research Brief |   description: Compare primary sources into a cited brief.
```

### 3. Regression tests, same test files on both heads

The Gateway lane is a handler-lane test: it invokes `templatesDraftsHandlers["templates.drafts.publish"]` with the method's own params validator and asserts the client-facing RPC outcome (`ok` / `errorShape`), against a real loopback `node:http` ClawHub registry — it does not open a socket, which is why section 1 runs the same flow against a real Gateway process.

Before (frozen `origin/main` production file, candidate tests kept):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/templates/draft.test.ts --run
 ×  unit  src/templates/draft.test.ts > agent-created Template drafts > keeps the package slug while showing a title-cased agent name
   → invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.
      Test Files  1 failed (1)
           Tests  1 failed | 16 passed (17)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts --run
 ×  gateway-methods  … > Template draft reviewed publication > publishes exactly the reviewed selections under the personal publisher
   → {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace."}: expected false to be true
      Test Files  1 failed (1)
           Tests  1 failed | 29 passed (30)
```

After (candidate head):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/templates/draft.test.ts --run
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  17 passed (17)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/templates-drafts.test.ts --run
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on all three changed files; `check:line-cap-ratchet --staged --base HEAD~1` OK (3 changed source files, no new violations); `check:test-lines-ratchet --staged --base HEAD~1` OK — net test lines +6 against the 400 allowance, no allocation added; `check:test-mock-exports` OK; `check:assertion-safety-ratchet` OK. `oxlint` and the declaration/typecheck lanes could not run on this host: the worktree shares a symlinked install and both abort with `Declaration input escapes checkout … shared installs and external symlinks are unsupported`. The change only wraps expressions that already typecheck on `main` in `.trim()` / `||`, and CI's lint and type lanes run on the PR head.

CI note: the one red lane on the first revision, `checks-node-compact-small-1` (`test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`, missing `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/*` in `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`), is base drift introduced by merged #197697 and was fixed by #197976 (merged 2026-11-13 00:12 UTC); it reproduced identically on unrelated PRs and touched none of these three files. This head is rebased past it.

### 4. Proof image — the padded input and the stored result, base vs candidate

![Base rejects the padded draft at review; candidate trims the display name and description, publishes, and stores the trimmed CLAW.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-clickclack-proof/main/pr-197979/template-draft-trim.png)

Both panels are the captured console output of two isolated lanes (base `02f29597c10`, candidate `0aaa1c0bc63`, each with its own built `dist`) driven by the shipped `openclaw gateway call` client through the same sequence: `templates.drafts.create` → `templates.drafts.save` with a draft whose description is `" A collaborative engineering partner. "` → `templates.drafts.review` / `templates.drafts.publish` with `displayName: "  Engineering Partner  "` and the same padded description. The base lane stops at the review with `invalid_manifest: Value must not have leading or trailing whitespace.`; the candidate lane reviews to `"Engineering Partner"` / `"A collaborative engineering partner."`, publishes `@maker/research-brief@0.1.0` (the ClawHub stub echoes the uploaded `clawpack` digest, which equals the Gateway's `payload.expectedArtifactSha256`), and the uploaded `CLAW.md` carries the trimmed values. It is deliberately an open-artifact view rather than a Control UI screenshot: the padded values live in the draft document and in the review `choices`, so the surrounding chrome would not show what changed. Artifacts and provenance: https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-clickclack-proof/tree/main/pr-197979

Relationship to #196644: that open PR edits these same four lines to keep an authored CLAW.md name verbatim and to stop an empty review description from erasing the manifest description. The two fixes answer different questions — #196644 chooses *which* text reaches the manifest, this PR normalizes *whitespace* around whatever text is chosen — so they can land together, and this PR is deliberately written against `main` so it does not depend on #196644. If #196644 merges first, the combined shape is:

```ts
const displayName =
  choices?.displayName?.trim() || draftManifest.agent.name || titleCaseTemplateName(draftName);
const description = (
  choices?.description ?? (authored.description || draftManifest.agent.description) ?? ""
).trim();
```

This PR keeps `??` for `choices?.description`, so `description: ""` continues to mean "the reviewer cleared it" — the semantic #196644 pins in its own test — and uses `||` only for `displayName`, so an all-whitespace name falls back to the existing default instead of failing. The control row in section 2 shows that cleared-description behavior is byte-identical on both heads.

Open PR collision check (2026-11-13 snapshot, re-run after the rebase): swept the changed files of the 60 newest open PRs; this PR is the only one touching `src/templates/draft.ts` or either test file. #197924 touches `src/templates/conversation.workspace.test.ts` (zero overlap); #196644 remains open on the same four lines with the combined shape above; #197402 touches `src/templates/schema.ts` but only adds a field that reuses `nonEmptyString`, and does not change the trim rule this PR relies on. #196427 (merged 2026-11-11) introduced the review-choices path that carries the defect, and no commit since then normalizes these fields — the bug still reproduces on `02f29597c10`.

What was not tested: no live Control UI session with a real model authoring a draft — section 1 reaches the Gateway over its real WebSocket with the shipped client, but the browser page itself is not driven, and the padded values enter at the two contract boundaries the product uses (the draft document saved through `templates.drafts.save`, and the `choices` object sent to `templates.drafts.review` / `templates.drafts.publish`). Other manifest fields are untouched, so a padded workspace file name or skill ref still hits the schema rejection — this PR fixes the name and description path that the review surfaces feed.

prs.title: fix: reach the configured owner on project-parent sessions_spawn preflight
prs.body:
Closes #182467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: project-attached `sessions_spawn` rejects a plugin-resolved child model (`deepseek/*`, native `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) as `Unknown model` or `selected account or native runtime is unavailable`, even though the agent's configured owner knows the model and a normal session on the same installation accepts it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Child spawned from a project-parent session resolves provider-plugin and native-runtime models the agent's configured owner already knows, without the operator having to detach the project or `/reset` the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A project-parent read supplies the project workspace to `withPreparedModelCatalogOwner({ readOnly: true })`. `resolveReadOnlyPublishedModelCatalogOwner` builds two candidates (`full`, `activationFull`); both carry the explicit project workspace, so the resolver's exact-key lookup misses the single configured owner published at the agent's workspace. The configured-workspace fallback inside `resolvePublishedOwner` is also gated on strict workspace equality, so it misses too. The code then falls through to `acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime`, which builds a runtime-free ephemeral catalog without the provider plugin registry — the plugin's `resolveDynamicModel` hook is never invoked and the model is reported as unknown.

This change narrows the preflight to a third read-only candidate that probes at the agent's **known configured workspace** (resolved via `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir`, not any arbitrary workspace) with every other identity dimension carried from the caller and `env` bound to the effective process environment so the resolver's env match stays exact instead of degrading to the wildcard branch. If the configured workspace is not resolvable, the fallback is suppressed and the existing ephemeral read-only path takes over, preserving the prior behavior for that shape.

Agent, agent-directory, inherited-auth, environment, and generation isolation are preserved exactly. Writable publications and non-read-only paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage in `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:
  - Positive: project-parent read falls back to the configured workspace with agent, agent-dir, env, and workspace identity verified in the fallback input; the fallback carries a plugin-provider model that is absent from the ephemeral read-only snapshot.
  - Negative: when a competing publication matches by workspace but diverges on agent / agent-dir / env, the fallback rejects it and the ephemeral read-only path takes over.
  - Suppression: a workspace-less caller does not synthesize a second workspace-less probe.
  - Guard: when the agent's configured workspace is unknown, the preflight skips the project-parent fallback and lands on the ephemeral read-only build.
- Full targeted test suite (6 files, 119 tests) passes locally:
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.workspace.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.plan.test.ts`

<details>
<summary>Review notes</summary>

Marked draft pending maintainer sign-off on scope. ATX reviews surfaced a residual architectural suggestion to gate configured-workspace reuse behind an explicit, validated project-parent predicate; introducing such a predicate expands scope beyond the acceptance criteria recorded in the issue's Codex review ("preserve agent, account, environment, and generation isolation"; "a focused inventory-owner correction"), so it is deferred.

</details>

prs.title: fix(tts): speak an answer that carries a picture instead of dropping its voice
prs.body:
Closes #142188

> **Rebased onto current `main` again (2026-11-02, `796b1471345`).** The branch was
> ~4,800 commits behind. One conflict, in `dispatch-from-config.tts.test-support.ts`:
> kept the media guard in the mocked synthesizer, because the supplement tests depend on
> it. Two rebase adaptations beyond the mechanical ones:
> - `main` replaced `resolveStatusTtsSnapshot` with `resolveTtsSettingsSnapshot`, which
>   changed the captioned-final deferral: with `tts.auto` unset it now reads `off`, so the
>   streamed-answer test sets `tts.auto: "always"` explicitly. Behaviour is unchanged.
> - Upstream growth pushed `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` over the 700-line cap, so
>   `withInheritedSupplementMetadata` and `resolveMediaFinalTtsText` moved to the sibling
>   `dispatch-from-config.media-tts-supplement.ts`.
>
> Local on this head: targeted suites 407/407, core and core-test typechecks, line-cap
> ratchet and lint green.

### Current status (2026-11-02)

ClawSweeper re-review: **0 code findings**, `proof: sufficient`, patch 4/6.

CI on `89672c0`: 64 pass. The only red lanes are `main` regressions, not this diff:
- `checks-node-changed-compact-small-7` — the lease fixture in
  `deliver-queue.lease-integration.test.ts` (`preserves lost ownership during provider`),
  already being fixed upstream in #190934;
- `checks-node-changed-boundary` — the boundary scan flags
  `test/decision-baseten-admission.integration.test.ts` (main commit `91f4975` imports
  `extensions/baseten/decision-provider.runtime.js`); this PR changes neither file.

This branch's own lanes pass. Waiting on the owner decision below. The branch already
carries the live-only behaviour; on approval of option 2 I will add the restart test
that proves a recovered queue never replays the audio (and name the signal if the review
wants it separate from `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with auto-TTS enabled would receive no voice message at all
when the assistant's answer carried an attachment. A reply that says something *and*
shows a chart arrives silent: no audio, no error, nothing in `doctor`. The same text
without an attachment is spoken normally, so the feature disappears exactly when the
assistant illustrates its answer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`maybeApplyTtsToPayloadCore` skips synthesis whenever the payload already carries media.
That guard is correct and stays: on success the same function writes the audio into
`mediaUrl`, so removing it would overwrite the picture. One message carries one media
set — `ttsSupplement` holds only `spokenText` and a flag, not a second set.

So the answer is spoken by a **second message** instead. A final that carries non-audio
media is delivered untouched; afterwards its text is synthesized separately and sent as
an audio-only payload marked
`markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement(…, { visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true })`. This is the
mechanism `dispatch-from-config.finalize.ts` already uses for deferred final text; only
the entry condition is new.

Audio versus non-audio is decided by `hasNonAudioMediaReference`, built on the shared
media table (`isAudioFileName`), so a reply that already carries a voice note gets no
second one. Legacy `MEDIA:` directives participate in that classification and are
stripped from the spoken copy while staying in the visible message. Only speech-related
metadata (`tts`, `ttsExplicit`, `commandReply`) is inherited by the synthesized payload,
so command replies stay silent and delivery ownership is not transferred.

Boundaries: the ACP delivery coordinator has its own synthesis application and is not
touched here; the same branch can be added there if maintainers want it.

**Note for channel authors:** this makes a case reachable that previously only appeared
on channels with captioned-final delivery — a final that carries media and no text.
Such a payload is marked `visibleTextAlreadyDelivered` and must not be read as "no answer
was produced". Our own VK channel plugin did read it that way and deleted the message
holding the answer; the flag is what tells them apart.

## Supplement lifetime: live-only

The supplement is optional audio that repeats an answer already delivered, and its writer
fence is the in-memory `sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority` it inherits. Durable recovery
cannot rebuild that fence — the supplement owns no pending-final completion of its own —
so a persisted row could replay the audio after the writer was replaced.

It therefore carries `ttsSupplement.liveOnly`, and the queue boundary in
`deliver-queue.ts` refuses to persist such a payload, next to where `skipQueue` is
consumed. That placement is layer-independent: both the routed and the channel-local lane
reach it, as does any caller of `deliverOutboundPayloads`. The normalizer
`getReplyPayloadTtsSupplement` preserves the flag, since delivery reads the lifetime from
the normalized supplement.

What this costs: a Gateway restart between the picture and its voice loses the audio. The
answer it repeats has already been delivered and recorded, so nothing the user needs
disappears. The alternative — an independently fenced durable completion — would need a
second owner of the session's pending final, which is a change to session delivery
ownership for the sake of optional audio; that decision is the maintainer's.

## User Impact

An answer that comes with a picture is now also spoken: the picture arrives in its own
message, the voice follows in the next one. Answers that already carry audio, command
replies, and replies without attachments behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**The guard is unconditional — real synthesis path, no channel, no TTS mocks**
(`src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts`, synthetic speech provider):

| payload | synthesis called |
|---|---|
| text + PNG / JPEG / PDF / MP4 / Opus | no |
| text + several attachments | no |
| text + legacy `MEDIA:` line | no |
| **same text, no attachment** | **yes** — control |

**Delivery, through `dispatchReplyFromConfig`** — 19 attachment formats plus edge cases:
mixed attachments, audio-only sets, a caption-less picture, `isError` payloads, non-final
TTS modes, two finals in one turn, a streamed answer ending in a picture, command replies
with and without an explicit speech request, and synthesis failure. Every case first
asserts the visible message survives untouched.

**The regression test fails without the fix:** stashing only `finalize.ts` turns
"speaks a picture answer as a separate voice message" red while the rest stay green.

**Writer authority is preserved and enforced.** A settled final can carry
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, and an absent authority reads as authorized at every
check, so the supplement inherits it — while transcript and completion ownership stay
with the visible message. Three dispatch tests pin the boundary:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| writer still holds the turn | picture, then its voice supplement |
| writer replaced while the supplement is being synthesized | picture only — the audio is rejected before transport |
| replaced writer, ordinary settled final (pre-existing test) | not dispatched, unchanged |

The middle case is the one this PR had to earn: the first attempt attached the authority
to the synthesis input instead of the delivered payload, and since that metadata lives by
object identity it never reached the send path. The test failed until the authority moved
onto the payload that is actually sent.

**Speech comes from the prepared text.** `sendFinalPayload` now reports the text it
prepared for delivery — normalization applied and deferred block text merged, TTS not yet
run — and the supplement synthesizes that, reading it after the media pass so a rewritten
or cleared caption is what gets spoken. A recording cannot be normalized after the fact.

**A supplement follows only a message the recipient can see.** Eligibility is decided by
the outcome of preparation and delivery, not by the raw reply:

| situation | supplement |
|---|---|
| final delivered (queued or routed, settled) | yes |
| final deduped against a block that was delivered | yes |
| block vetoed by the channel (`channel-transform`) | no |
| visible answer failed to route | no |
| preparation cleared the caption (media pass, channel transform) | no — an empty prepared text says "say nothing" |
| queued answer cancelled in `beforeDeliver` | no |
| queued answer suppressed as a channel transform | no |
| answer delivered but not visibly (`visibleReplySent: false`) | no |
| settlement could not complete within its bound | no |

Admission is not visibility, so eligibility is decided after `turnLedger.settleQueued`,
the same bounded wait the no-visible-reply gate uses — but this gate fails closed. The
neighbouring gate treats admission as the strongest fact because uncertainty there must
not produce a duplicate message; here uncertainty must not produce a voice note that
arrives alone. Both answer "stay quiet"; only the reasoning differs, and the code says so.

**Runs** (Node 24.20.0):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:changed` | pass |
| `auto-reply-reply` shard | 223 files, 5474 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/tts/tts-entry-delivery.test.ts` | 11 tests, 0 failures |
| `src/media/audio.test.ts` | 13 tests, 0 failures |
| `pnpm build`, `pnpm check` | pass |
| `autoreview` (claude, P2) | no accepted findings |

**Live traffic**, one install, before and after (redacted, hashed peer ids):

```
before   11:36:01  deliver kind=final len=758 media=true
         11:36:02  vk upload ok kind=photo
         11:36:03  vk upload ok kind=photo          ← no synthesis in the turn

after    15:43:54  deliver kind=final len=621 media=true
         15:43:55  vk upload ok kind=photo
         15:43:57  tts synthesize: format=ogg, size=385395
         15:43:57  deliver kind=final len=0 media=true
         15:43:59  vk upload ok kind=audio          ← voice as its own message
```

Docs updated: `docs/tools/tts.md` described the old behavior in both the rule list and
the decision tree.

## Plugin compatibility

Channel plugins see a new message shape: a final that carries media and no text. It is
marked `ttsSupplement.visibleTextAlreadyDelivered`, which is exactly the signal that tells
it apart from "no answer was produced".

Our own VK plugin got this wrong at first and deleted the message holding the answer,
because its progress-draft finalizer read an empty final as "no answer came". The repair
was to check the flag — not to work around the core — and it is a five-line guard plus
seven regression tests in that plugin. We report it because it is the upgrade risk a
reviewer should weigh: plugins that infer "no answer" from empty final text need that
one check. Plugins that only deliver what they are given need nothing.

## Open question for maintainers: durable recovery of the supplement

This is the one finding we have not implemented, because both ways to close it change a
contract that is yours to set. Everything below is what we traced; we are happy to build
whichever you choose.

**The gap.** `buildRecoveryDeliverParams` installs the writer fence
(`assertDirectAdapterHandoff` / `onPlatformSendDispatch`) only when the queued entry has a
`pending-final` `deliveryCompletion`, and reads the authority from that record alone. The
supplement carries its authority in payload metadata, which is process-local, and has no
completion of its own. If the process stops after the supplement is enqueued and the
session writer is replaced before recovery runs, the recovered audio sends unfenced.

**Why the supplement has no completion.** Reusing the visible answer's receipt would give
a second message the first one's delivery ownership — the mistake this PR was already
corrected for in an earlier round. So the choice is a new receipt or no recovery at all.

**Option 1 — give the supplement its own `pending-final` completion.** This is more than a
field: a completion is a durable record with a lifecycle (`prepared` → `queued` →
`delivered` / `suppressed` / `unknown`, settled through `settlePendingFinalDelivery`).
Minting one per supplement means new rows in that store and a new owner obligation to
settle them on every path, including failure. `AGENTS.md` asks contributors to agree
material persistent-store changes before implementing them, which is why we stopped here
rather than guessing at the shape.

**Option 2 — keep the supplement out of durable recovery.** Our preference, and the one
ClawSweeper now recommends ("Approve live-only supplements: add a narrowly scoped
non-recoverable delivery path"). A voice note lost to a restart is a small loss, while one
that outlives its writer is exactly what the fence exists to prevent.

We re-checked whether an existing signal already expresses it, so the ask is not for
something already there. `OutboundDeliveryQueuePolicy` is `required | best_effort`, and
`best_effort` is about how a failure is treated, not about persistence: recovery carries
the policy forward (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts` reads `entry.queuePolicy ?? "best_effort"`)
and replays such entries like any other. There is no admission bypass for an optional
send. So live-only needs a new signal, however small, and that is a contract addition.

**What is already fenced.** The live path: the supplement inherits
`sessionWriterDeliveryAuthority`, it is attached to the delivered payload rather than the
synthesis input, and a replacement during synthesis is covered by a regression test. Only
the recovered path is open.

Tell us which option you want — or a third we have not seen — and we will implement it in
this PR. If you approve option 2, we will add the narrowest signal that expresses "do not
recover this send", thread it from the supplement through admission, and cover it with a
restart test that asserts the recovered queue never replays the audio.

## Related

- #42539 asks for text and voice as separate messages as a general Telegram delivery
  option. Different problem — there the answer is spoken and the split is a preference;
  here synthesis never runs. The mechanism is the same one, so that option could be
  built on this branch.
- #132736 (closed) covers auto-TTS supplement messages on Signal — separate voice
  messages are an existing shape in the core, not a new one.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep a Browser panel action's error visible through passive refreshes
prs.body:
Closes #198052

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Browser panel's error for a failed action, such as a navigation blocked by policy, disappears while the page keeps streaming, because the automatic viewport resize and passive panel refreshes clear it.

## User Impact

User impact: when an action in the Browser panel fails, its error stays visible until the person acts again, retries or refreshes, instead of vanishing on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The automatic viewport sync runs as a passive action and no longer clears the shown error before it runs.
- A panel refresh keeps an error that came from the person's own action; it still clears errors from its own snapshot work.
- The person's next action, and an explicit Retry or Refresh, still clear the error, and any new error replaces it.

## Evidence

![The Browser panel still shows "Couldn't complete the browser action. Try again." about 10 seconds after a blocked navigation, while the page keeps streaming](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/f64e3f00b94ba3938400a5d18acea436e3af2aed/images/2026/11/ae8525d1-2aa6-4ac6-b259-5971ed3cf493.png)

Live run in an isolated VM, on a build that contains this change: about 10 seconds after a navigation blocked by policy and an automatic viewport resize, the panel still shows "Couldn't complete the browser action. Try again." while the page keeps streaming (live frame counter running). The expanded "Show details" text, which names the policy block, was not checked in that run.

Tests:
- New Browser panel streaming tests: an action's policy error survives 10 seconds of viewport sync and of a panel refresh while frames stream; both fail without this change. A second new test shows an explicit Refresh still clears an action's error.
- Control UI Browser panel tests: 283 passed. Lint and the UI typecheck are clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep bootstrap completion in long sessions
prs.body:
Related: #154923

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, the workspace instructions are sent again in a long session, even though the first full turn already completed.

## User Impact

Long sessions keep skipping the workspace instructions after the first turn, as the setting promises. Reset and compaction still re-arm the instructions. Short sessions are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The check for "full bootstrap already done" only read the last 500 transcript events. Once the marker was older than that, the check said "not done" and the instructions were injected again.

Now the check asks the transcript reader for the latest marker, reset or compaction on the active branch. The query uses the existing projection snapshot and read fence. It reads only small navigation data and does not unpack message bodies. It works on SQLite and PostgreSQL and keeps the last-duplicate-key rule of `JSON.parse`. There is no new schema, writer or database connection.

#154923 made the marker get written. This PR fixes how the marker is found again later.

## Evidence

Built product (`pnpm build`), driven by a small script. The script uses a temp HOME and a temp state dir, makes a real session with `SessionManager` and calls the built `hasCompletedBootstrapTurn`. SQLite only.

| Session | main (`5cbed85ff94`) | this PR (`a103a25bb17`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| marker, then 5 messages | true | true |
| marker, then 501 messages | **false** | true |
| reset, marker, then 501 messages | **false** | true |
| marker, 501 messages, then reset | false | false |
| no marker, 501 messages | false | false |

Tests (focused files, run with `--maxWorkers=2`):

- Red on main, green here. `bootstrap-files.test.ts`: 2 new tests fail on main, 39 of 39 pass here. `session-actor-memory-history.test.ts`: 7 new tests fail on main, 23 of 23 pass here.
- Core type check, test type check shards, oxlint and format check pass on the touched files.

<details>
<summary>Exact script output</summary>

Before (main):

```
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=true | marker, then 5 messages (expect true)
UNEXPECTED  | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | marker, then 501 messages (expect true)
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | marker, 501 messages, then reset (expect false)
UNEXPECTED  | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | reset, marker, then 501 messages (expect true)
as-expected | hasCompletedBootstrapTurn=false | no marker, 501 messages (expect false)
```

After (this PR): all five rows as expected (true, true, false, true, false).

</details>

Not tested:

- PostgreSQL was not run. The PostgreSQL branch of the query uses the existing `jsonPathValue` helper and was only type checked.
- No full gateway run with a real model.
- A cold-storage restore test was left out to keep the test file under its line cap.

prs.title: fix(codex): chat rows that arrive during a native turn are never sent to Codex
prs.body:
Related: none found (no open or closed issue or PR covers this).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat message that arrives while a Codex turn is running is never sent to Codex, because the next turn thinks the thread already saw it.

## User Impact

User impact: Codex now gets every chat message exactly once. Before, a message saved during a running turn (and not steered into it) was silently lost for Codex on the next turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a turn, the thread binding stored "history seen up to <turn end time>". A row saved mid-turn has an older time, so the next turn skipped it.

Now the binding also stores the exact chat row that was sent with the turn (thread id, run id, row key). The next turn resumes after that row. Rows steered into that run are skipped. If the row is not found (for example, history was compacted), the old time check is used, so nothing gets worse.

Size: 4 files, about 60 lines of code plus one test.

## Evidence

Real code path, fake app-server, real SQLite session store. This is the production attempt code run through the repo test harness (source, not a built bundle). No real OpenAI call, no credentials.

The test runs two turns on one resumed thread. A chat row is saved during turn 1 and not steered. Then turn 2 starts. It checks the text sent to Codex in turn 2.

| | Base (`5cbed85ff94`) | This PR (`47b8294779d`) |
|---|---|---|
| Row saved during turn 1 appears in turn 2 input | 0 times (lost) | 1 time |
| History from before turn 1 appears in turn 2 input | 0 times | 0 times |

- New test is red on base: `expected [ Array(1) ] to have a length of 2 but got 1`. Green here.
- `run-attempt.bounded-continuity`, `session-binding`, `run-attempt`, `run-attempt.durable-context`, `run-attempt.generation-finalization`: 5 files, 181 tests pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the 4 files.

Not tested: a full `pnpm build` and a real gateway with a real Codex app-server. The "steered row is not sent again" and "row not found, use old time check" paths have no new test. A turn run without a user-turn recorder keeps the old time check.

prs.title: feat(update): new releases run their own pre-update rehearsal
prs.body:
Related: #145252

## What Problem This Solves

A fix to the pre-update rehearsal cannot help the update that needs it. The installed updater runs its own copy of the state snapshot, Doctor rehearsal, test Gateway, and their time budgets before the new release takes over, so a corrected check only reaches users one update later.

## User Impact

User impact: once an installation runs a release with this change, later releases rehearse themselves, so rehearsal fixes and budget changes take effect on the update that ships them. A successful update otherwise looks the same, apart from one output line saying the candidate ran its own checks.

- Updates from releases published before this change behave as they do today. Those updaters ignore the new marker.
- This adds a package marker, `openclaw.updateRehearsalProtocol: 1`, and a hidden `openclaw update rehearse` command. **The marker is a protocol addition and needs maintainer approval before merge.**
- If the candidate's rehearsal crashes, goes silent, times out a check, fails its state copy, or returns an invalid result, the updater names the reason in its output and runs its own rehearsal. The worst case is that the rehearsal runs twice.

## Why This Change Was Made

After staging, the updater runs the candidate's `openclaw update rehearse --request <file>` in place of its own rehearsal. The candidate receives the config source the updater resolved in a private `0600` file, holds no update authority, and touches copied state only.

A candidate refusal stays binding, and the candidate refuses only when its Doctor rehearsal or its private Gateway fails on the copied state. A pass grants nothing: the installed updater still owns drain, activation, verification, and rollback.

Two existing guarantees carry across the process boundary:

- **Committed progress before forward work.** The candidate sends each progress and step receipt, then waits for the updater's answer on its stdin before it continues. The updater answers only after its ledger write has completed. A refused receipt or a lost updater stops the candidate before the announced check. This keeps the contract from #162098.
- **Custody of check processes.** Each rehearsal check runs in its own process group, which stopping the candidate does not reach. The candidate reports those processes, and the updater stops any still running after the candidate exits, crashes, or is forced to stop. It signals a process only while it still has the start time it had when reported.

| Update | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Any published updater to a release with this change | Unchanged. The old updater runs its own rehearsal. |
| Updater with this change to a candidate with the marker | The candidate rehearses itself and the updater applies its verdict. |
| Updater with this change to a target without the marker | The updater runs its own rehearsal. This is the downgrade case. |
| Candidate rehearsal ends without a usable result | The updater logs the reason and runs its own rehearsal. |

Tradeoffs worth a reviewer's attention:

- The updater does not impose a work deadline on the candidate. It detects a dead or blocked candidate by silence: the candidate sends a heartbeat every 15 seconds, and 15 minutes without any output returns the rehearsal to the updater. An explicit `--timeout` still ends it.
- On cancellation the candidate gets five minutes to remove its temporary state copies before it is forced to stop, matching the existing cleanup allowance.
- The immutable activation path keeps the updater's own rehearsal. `updatePreflightProtocol` and the external-supervisor `update preflight` command are unchanged.

## Evidence

All Docker runs used `scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh` locally (linux/arm64) with packages built by `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`.

**Both sides marker-aware, packaged.** This run predates the rebase onto `a83f743`; `git range-diff` shows both commits unchanged by it. The installed updater was this branch at `27f3c52`, and the candidate was a second build of the same tree with a different build identity. The harness is written for a published updater, so I seeded this build through its driver seed cache, using the same in-container `npm install --global --prefix` step that CI uses to seed a published release.

```text
PASS published 2026.11.3 → candidate 2026.11.3 (c1c7f08eb4e854981e572b287be391aaf9fac7b2): finished, readyz=200, running version verified
```

The label says "published" because that is the harness's wording; the updater was the local build. The update's output contains `The candidate release ran its own update checks.` once and no fallback line. All eight rehearsal steps were relayed with exit 0, the run finished `succeeded`, and the harness's durable and incognito session checks before and after the update passed.

**Published updaters to this change.** On the pushed head `758582e`, one cell per published updater, plus two control cells with unmodified `main` at `a83f743` as the candidate:

| Candidate | Published updater | Result | Recorded steps | Updater's own rehearsal |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| this branch | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway verified | 139.1 s | 21.0 s |
| this branch | 2026.11.2 | PASS, Gateway verified | 138.0 s | 21.3 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.9 | PASS, Gateway verified | 171.4 s | 32.7 s |
| this branch | 2026.10.1 | PASS, Gateway verified | 168.1 s | 29.2 s |
| this branch | 2026.9.9 | FAIL, `post-update-failed` | 178.3 s | 24.2 s |
| `main` | 2026.11.3 | PASS, Gateway verified | 141.3 s | 21.9 s |
| `main` | 2026.9.9 | FAIL, same step and message | 180.0 s | 23.8 s |

Each published updater ran its own rehearsal, as designed: `The candidate release ran its own update checks.` appears in no output of these cells.

The `2026.9.9` failure is not caused by this change. Both candidates fail at the same step after the package swap, with the same message:

```text
openclaw doctor --fix: Shared state migration did not finish: expected schema 40, found missing.
```

In both runs the new Gateway serves the candidate version with `readyz: true`, the run is recorded as failed, and rollback is not attempted (`state-migrated-no-rollback`). The cause is not established.

**Focused tests.** Before the rebase, 174 tests in 8 files passed. On `758582e`, the five test files this change touches pass (58 tests). Four cases use a real child process: acceptance, fallback, a refused receipt stopping the candidate before its announced check, and the updater stopping a check process that a crashed candidate left running. I removed each guarded behavior in turn (exit-status and document agreement, commit-before-answer, the refused-receipt stop, silence detection, the inconclusive-outcome rule, and process custody) and confirmed tests fail each time.

**Checks.** On `758582e`: `pnpm tsgo:all`, the mock-export ratchet, and the test-line ratchet pass. Format and `oxlint` on the changed files passed before the rebase and were not rerun. `pnpm check:changed` on the first commit reported two failures that this change does not cause: `max-lines` lint errors in files it does not touch, and the Plugin SDK surface budget.

**Review.** An autoreview pass (Codex, P0 and P1 scope) found that the candidate treated a timed-out check or failed state copy as a binding refusal; fixed in the first commit. ClawSweeper then found the two lifecycle gaps described above; the second commit fixes both.

**Gaps.**

- Windows and macOS service managers were not exercised, and process custody after a candidate crash is untested on Windows.
- No extended-stable updater was run. The harness accepts only updaters that classify as `stable`.
- The two-sided cell was not rerun after the rebase.
- The advisory step `post-activation doctor inspections` exits 1 in every passing cell, including the `main` control. Its JSON is identical between the branch and `main` runs with `2026.11.3` apart from duration and a temporary directory name. It reports 12 `info` findings and no errors or warnings.

<details>
<summary>Test notes</summary>

- Net test lines are +719, above the 400-line allowance, so this adds `config/test-lines-allocations/update-candidate-rehearsal.txt` for 319 lines. The excess covers the updater-side fallback table (nine invalid-result shapes), receipt acknowledgement ordering, liveness and cancellation timing, inconclusive candidate outcomes, and the real-subprocess cases.
- Touched test files, each read in full: `update-candidate-delegated-rehearsal.test.ts` (new), `update-candidate-canary-process.test.ts`, `update-command-preflight.test.ts`, `run-main-update-admission.test.ts`, and `update-command-candidate-validation.test.ts`. No existing case was removed. In `run-main-update-admission.test.ts`, two inline per-command conditionals became one lookup table.
- Step timings from the two-sided cell's update run, small fixture state: 177 s of recorded steps in total, of which the candidate-owned rehearsal was 25.5 s.

</details>

prs.title: fix(context): keep an answered candidate when internal rows spend the read budget
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recent-history reconciliation asks the transcript for two rows per platform candidate — one user row and one reply. That is the floor for a candidate pair, not the number of rows a real tail contains: internal runtime inputs and their `NO_REPLY` pairs sit between candidate pairs and spend the same budget. When they do, a read that hits its limit stops before an older candidate pair and the already-answered platform message becomes eligible again, so it comes back under `Recent chat history:` on a later turn.

`omitAnsweredRecentHistory` now extends the read by exactly the rows it saw that cannot answer a candidate (no `messageId`, or an id that is not in the candidate set) and reads again. The extension is bounded to three attempts, so a candidate that never entered this session — answered in another session, or in a window that no longer exists — cannot widen the read without limit. Nothing else changes: the walk, the completed-answer requirement, and the text-equality guard are untouched.

Closes #197995

## Evidence

Deterministic, from the fixture in the report: six ID-bearing candidates, each with its own adjacent completed answer, plus one internal runtime input and its `NO_REPLY` between the oldest pair and the other five. That is 14 canonical rows for a 12-row budget.

- **Red** (`omitAnsweredRecentHistory` unchanged, new test added): `1 failed | 9 passed` in `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts`. The retained entry is `m-target` — the `target` candidate whose pair fell outside the read.
- **Green** (this patch): `10 passed` in the same file, `2 passed` in `session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts`.

```
› ../../.tools/node-v24.22.2-win-x64/node.exe scripts/test-projects.mts \
    src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Validation on this head (`329028dc3`, base `a83f74375`):

- `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` on both files: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json`: no diagnostics for either file (the four remaining `@openclaw/fs-safe` / `DirectoryMode` errors are the known local `node_modules` drift and appear on unmodified main).

prs.title: fix: leaked DSML tool markup shows in visible assistant replies
prs.body:
Related: #169728, #175058 (these fix transport parsing only; this PR does not touch transport)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: raw DeepSeek DSML tool-call markup shows up in the visible assistant reply when a model leaks it as text, in both batch and streamed replies.

Example reply text: `Let me check. <｜DSML｜tool_calls>...rm -rf /tmp/x...</｜DSML｜tool_calls> Done.`

## User Impact

Users no longer see raw tool-call markup, or the command inside it, in chat replies. Code examples that show DSML tags in backticks or code fences are still shown as written.

## Why This Change Was Made

#169728 and #175058 recover real tool calls in the transport. They do not clean the final visible text, so any leaked envelope still reaches the reader. Upstream `main` has no DSML handling in `src/shared/text`.

The visible-text filters now hide DSML envelopes (`tool_calls`, `tool_call`, `function_calls`, `tool_use_error`; `|`, `｜` and `｜｜` delimiters).
- Code spans, fenced blocks and indented code are left alone.
- Quoted JSON inside an envelope cannot end it early.
- An envelope split over stream chunks is hidden once it is recognized.
- An unfinished or mismatched envelope hides the rest of the text, so private payload is not shown.
- Nothing is executed or recovered here.

## Evidence

Tests, in `src/shared/text`:
- On plain `main` (5cbed85ff94): 20 new tests fail (19 in `assistant-visible-text.test.ts`, 1 in `assistant-internal-scaffolding.test.ts`).
- With this change: `pnpm test src/shared/text` passes, 226 tests in 5 files.
- `tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the 6 touched files are clean.

Real built modules (`pnpm build`, then a small script imports the built visible-text and text-projection chunks from `dist` and feeds them leaked text). No model, gateway or provider was run.

| Input | Before (main) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Batch: `Let me check. <DSML envelope with exec command> Done.` | envelope and command shown | `Let me check.  Done.` |
| Stream, envelope split over 4 chunks | full envelope shown | `Let me check.` then `Let me check.  Done.` |
| Batch and stream: code example in backticks | kept | kept |

In the stream case, the first chunk can show a partial opener (`<｜DS`) until the next chunk arrives.

<details>
<summary>Raw output</summary>

Before:
```
batch   delivery | leaked envelope: "Let me check. <｜DSML｜tool_calls><｜DSML｜invoke name=\"exec\"><｜DSML｜parameter name=\"command\" string=\"true\">rm -rf /tmp/x</｜DSML｜parameter></｜DSML｜invoke></｜DSML｜tool_calls> Done."
stream  chunk 2 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check. <｜DSML｜tool_calls><｜DSML｜invoke name=\"exec\">"
stream  chunk 4 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check. <｜DSML｜tool_calls>...</｜DSML｜tool_calls> Done."
batch   delivery | code example: "Use `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>example</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` literally."
```
After:
```
batch   delivery | leaked envelope: "Let me check.  Done."
stream  chunk 1 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check. <｜DS"
stream  chunk 2 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check."
stream  chunk 3 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check."
stream  chunk 4 | envelope split across chunks: "Let me check.  Done."
batch   delivery | code example: "Use `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>example</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` literally."
stream  chunk 2 | code example split across chunks: "Use `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>example</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` literally."
```
Environment: Linux, Node v26.13.1, build of 5cbed85ff94 (before) and 128f37add52 (after).
</details>

Not tested: a live gateway or channel with a real DeepSeek model, and the full `pnpm lint` and full test suite (left to CI).

prs.body:
## What changes

Public shared conversations retain a 64px ghost rail and a 272px ghost session list with the OpenClaw wordmark, current conversation, and fading rows. The right ghost panel and its reserved space are removed. The 720px conversation column is centered in the remaining area; the desktop title aligns with conversation text, actions stay at the viewport’s right edge, and the jump button stays centered on the column. The list row’s spinner indicates live activity; the desktop top bar retains the title, Public session badge, and state text without a visible Live indicator. At 761–1080px only the rail remains. Loading and access failed share the left frame.

On phones up to 760px wide, the 56px header shows the OpenClaw mascot and wordmark on the left, with quiet Log in and primary Get started actions on the right. The conversation title wraps as a 22px heading above the Public session badge and Live indicator. Earlier and delayed state text and actions retain their placement below that line. The circular ghost button and duplicate login link are removed. Loading and access failed use the same left-aligned wordmark, with their existing actions and centered content. The request and publication owners are retained. The inline script synchronizes titles and status across the frame, exposes delayed-update recovery, and updates the scroll jump control while retaining refresh/reconciliation, login-hash forwarding, and copying.

prs.title: fix(cli): let interrupted session listings exit promptly
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw sessions list` acknowledges interruption while waiting on an unresponsive local Gateway's model catalog, but keeps the connection alive until the launcher forcibly kills the command.

## User Impact

User impact: interrupted session listings close their Gateway connection and exit normally for SIGINT/SIGTERM, without publishing a late table/JSON result or an offline-fallback warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass the existing command signal to the cached catalog read. Once interrupted, skip its saved-catalog fallback and final result publication. Normal unavailable-Gateway fallback and explicit offline store reads retain their current behavior.

## Evidence

Product HEAD: `1c7a491f44ba3e38ea9d84b2d521752c6c6313fd`; acceptance-red BASE: `b48d16bf6e98f0b9c1e110548fc46b3b35f2becd`.

- **Actual CLI → real Gateway/SQLite:** normal clean `qaRuntime` builds run `node openclaw.mjs sessions list` through a controlling PTY. Setup persists a real session through the canonical SQLite accessor and starts the actual Gateway. The task-owned Gateway is suspended to reproduce an unresponsive connection; `/proc` verifies the actual CLI's established socket before Ctrl-C/SIGTERM.
- **Same frozen red/green scenarios:** both BASE cases reach the launcher's emergency SIGKILL after **2035–2043 ms**. **HEAD exits 130/143 within 148.61 ms; its owned socket closes within 34.18 ms.** No late JSON/table/warning after the existing interruption notice; no collector watchdog or owned CLI survivor. This proves the pending connection/handshake, not a held authenticated RPC reply.
- **Three controls on both revisions:** normal JSON/text exit 0 with the real stored session and synthetic model; JSON capacity is 8192. Explicit `--store` succeeds while the Gateway is suspended and opens no Gateway socket. Config stays unchanged; Gateway cleanup succeeds.
- **Focused regression:** BASE has one intended unwanted-output failure and 26 passing controls. HEAD: **44 tests / two files pass in 324.775 s**: `pnpm test src/commands/sessions.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. This includes 133.686 s canonical worker preparation and SQLite fixtures. Targeted types, typed lint, formatting, normal exact-HEAD build and independent review pass.

Reproduce with the [unchanged collector](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/sessions-read-proof-v2.py): `python3 sessions-read-proof-v2.py CHECKOUT FRESH_OUTPUT NODE26 EXPECTATION`. [Environment and observations](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/EVIDENCE.md), [BASE receipt](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/base-receipt.json), [HEAD receipt](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/head-receipt.json), [actual output](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/head-streams.txt), and [independent review](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/blob/c82e62dcab440086354268a195af17d1d2f91bec/independent-review.md).

Production +9/−0 lines; tests +22/−0 lines, two files. Uses the existing command/RPC lifetime; no new configuration, protocol/schema, permission, dependency or migration requirement. Upstream CI is checked after publication.

Not tested: holding a completed authenticated catalog reply, provider/model execution, production user data, Windows/macOS or production load. Native proof covers a pending real connection; regression tests separately cover cancellation rejection, fallback and public output.

prs.title: fix(config-cli): say the running gateway self-restarts, and name the deadline
prs.body:
## Summary

`config set` on a restart-required path always prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`, regardless of `gateway.reload.mode`. With live reload at its default that hint is wrong about **who** restarts, and silent about the fact that the restart has a **deadline**.

What actually happens when live reload is on:

1. The CLI writes the config file and prints `Restart the gateway to apply.`
2. The running Gateway's config watcher independently detects the change.
3. It classifies the path as restart-required and defers, waiting for active work to drain.
4. After `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` (5m) it **force-restarts anyway**, aborting whatever is still in flight.

So the operator is told to perform a restart that is not theirs to perform, and is not told that an automatic one is already scheduled with a hard cut-off. If the edit was made from inside a long-running agent turn, that turn is aborted by its own config write.

## Reproduction

On a running Gateway with default `gateway.reload` settings:

```console
$ openclaw config set plugins.load.paths '["/path/to/my-plugin"]' --strict-json
Updated plugins.load.paths. Restart the gateway to apply.
```

The operator does nothing, believing the change is inert until they act. Five minutes later, unprompted:

```
[reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (plugins.load.paths)
[reload] config change requires gateway restart (plugins.load.paths) — deferring until 1 operation(s), 1 reply(ies), 1 embedded run(s), 1 gateway request(s) complete
[reload] restart still deferred after 30330ms ...
[reload] restart timeout after 300053ms with 1 operation(s), ... still active; forcing restart
[gateway] forced restart requested; skipping active work drain
[shutdown] aborted 1 active run(s) during restart shutdown
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=<redacted> durationMs=1504983 error="agent run aborted for restart"
```

A ~25 minute agent run was aborted. Nothing in the CLI output suggested that was coming.

`plugins.load.paths` is not special here — it has no hot-reload rule, so it takes the default in `buildGatewayReloadPlan`:

```js
const kind = rule?.kind ?? "restart";
```

Any restart-required path reaches the same outcome.

## Fix

Split the hint by who owns the restart:

| `gateway.reload.mode` | hint |
| --- | --- |
| default / `hybrid` | `A running gateway restarts itself to apply this: it waits for active work to drain, then aborts in-flight runs after 5m. Restart manually if no gateway is running.` |
| `off` | `Restart the gateway to apply.` (unchanged) |

The deadline is read from `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs()` rather than hardcoded, so the message tracks the value the Gateway actually enforces.

Hot-appliable paths under `reload.mode: "off"` keep the manual hint — live reload is disabled, so the Gateway will not pick them up on its own.

## Tests

`src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` — 243 passed.

- Two new cases pin both branches: the self-restart wording including its deadline, and the unchanged manual wording under `reload.mode: "off"`.
- Five existing assertions updated; they asserted the manual hint for restart-required paths running with live reload on, which is the behaviour being corrected.
- `docs/cli/config.md` hint table updated.

## Scope

This changes the `config set` / `config patch` / `config unset` hint only. `plugins-cli.runtime.ts` and `plugins-uninstall-command.ts` print their own copies of the same string and have the same ambiguity — left for a follow-up to keep this diff reviewable.

This is a message-accuracy fix. It does not change restart behaviour: the 5m deferral is still hardcoded and its timeout intent is still `force: true`, so a restart-required config write can still abort an in-flight run. Making that window configurable (and non-forcing by default) is a separate discussion I'm happy to open if maintainers want it.

prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. prs.title: improve(ios): polish native chat, floating composer, and sidebar
prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.
