prs.title: fix(channels): cancel pending channels.stop on Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels remove <account>` ignores the Ctrl+C / SIGINT cancellation signal while it is stopping the running channel gateway (`channels.stop`) before deleting the account config. If the user hits Ctrl+C during that in-flight gateway call, the command swallows the abort and still writes the deletion to disk, so an interrupted removal partially or fully mutates the config even though the user asked to cancel.

- Problem: `channelsRemoveCommand` never reads the ambient async-work signal (`getAsyncWorkSignal()`), never forwards it into `callGateway({ method: "channels.stop", ... })`, and never re-checks `signal.aborted` after the stop attempt. The gateway call therefore has no way to be cancelled, and the subsequent `applyChannelAccountRemoval` / config write proceeds regardless of the abort.
- Solution: capture `const signal = getAsyncWorkSignal()` at command entry, abort early if already aborted, forward `signal` into the `channels.stop` `callGateway` call, and re-check `signal?.throwIfAborted()` both after a failed stop and after the stop completes, so a cancellation during or after the gateway call aborts the command before any config mutation.
- What changed: `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` (import `getAsyncWorkSignal`; entry guard; forward `signal` to `channels.stop`; two `throwIfAborted` guards). `src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts` (one regression case folded into the existing "normalizes a listed deletion" test).
- What did NOT change: the `list` command (separate gap in the original bug report, not addressed here), the gateway transport, `applyChannelAccountRemoval`'s own logic, and the non-gateway removal path (no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) which still skips the stop entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Best fix: propagate the already-existing ambient cancellation signal that the CLI SIGINT handler installs via `AsyncWorkScope`, rather than adding a new bespoke cancellation mechanism. This mirrors the canonical pattern already used by sibling commands (e.g. the status interrupt-cancel fix, PR #197815). It is the minimal, owner-reusing change and keeps the interruption contract consistent across commands.

Alternative considered and rejected: aborting only after `applyChannelAccountRemoval` (too late, config already mutated); or catching `AbortError` in `callGateway` and silently succeeding (loses the user-visible "you cancelled" semantics).

Risk: a consumer that relied on `channels.remove` ignoring Ctrl+C and completing the deletion will now see the command abort on cancel. This is the intended fix; no compatible contract depended on the old (buggy) swallow. Non-goal: this does not add graceful rollback of a partially-stopped gateway runtime, it only prevents the config write after a cancel.

## User Impact

When a user presses Ctrl+C while `openclaw channels remove <account>` is stopping the channel's running gateway, the command now aborts cleanly and does NOT write the account deletion to config. The user's "cancel" is honored instead of being silently overridden. The success path is unchanged: a removal that completes without interruption behaves exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Before / after comparison (interrupt handling in `channels remove`)

| Behavior | Before (pre-fix) | After (post-fix) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ctrl+C during in-flight `channels.stop` | Abort ignored; command continues and writes the account deletion to config | Command aborts; `writeConfigFile` is never called |
| `signal` forwarded to `callGateway({ method: "channels.stop" })` | Not forwarded (gateway call cannot be cancelled) | Forwarded (`signal` from `getAsyncWorkSignal()`) |
| Guard at command entry (`signal?.throwIfAborted()`) | None | Aborts immediately if already cancelled |
| Guard after the stop attempt (`signal?.throwIfAborted()`) | None (only logs the error) | Re-throws the abort reason and skips the config write |
| Stop fails (gateway error) then user cancels | Error logged, deletion still written | Abort re-thrown, config NOT written |
| Successful removal (no interrupt) | Deletes account, writes config | Identical (unchanged) |
| Non-gateway path (no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) | Skips stop, deletes config | Unchanged |

### Behavior matrix (interrupt during `channels.stop`)

```text
scenario                                  => pre-fix result                 => post-fix result
Ctrl+C during in-flight channels.stop      => swallow + still writes config  => command aborts, config NOT written
already-aborted signal at command entry    => proceeds to gateway stop      => aborts before any gateway/stop call
stop fails (gateway error) then Ctrl+C     => logs error, writes config     => throws abort reason, config NOT written
normal completion (no interrupt)           => deletes account, writes cfg   => identical (unchanged)
```

### Live module-level check (real `node`, real AbortSignal, no mock)

The production cancellation signal is a genuine `AbortSignal` produced by `AsyncWorkScope`, which is exactly what the CLI SIGINT handler installs:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e 'import("./src/shared/async-work-scope.js").then(m => { const s = new m.AsyncWorkScope(); console.log("signal is AbortSignal:", s.signal instanceof AbortSignal); const r = new Error("x"); s.beginClose(r); console.log("aborted:", s.signal.aborted, "reason:", s.signal.reason && s.signal.reason.message); })'
signal is AbortSignal: true
aborted: true reason: x
```

### Pre-fix: failing test (source reverted, test kept)

The regression case asserts the ambient signal is forwarded to `callGateway` and that no config write happens on abort. Without the fix it fails (the `signal` argument is absent from the `callGateway` call):

```console
$ vitest run src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts -t "normalizes a listed deletion"
 FAIL   commands  src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts > channelsRemoveCommand > normalizes a listed deletion before stopping runtime, running lifecycle, and persisting
AssertionError: expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ ObjectContaining{…} ]

- Expected
+ Received

  [
    {
-     "signal": AbortSignal {
-       Symbol(kAborted): true,
-       Symbol(kReason): Error { "message": "channels remove interrupted" }
+     "clientName": "gateway-client",
+     "config": { ... },
...
```

### Post-fix: passing

The signal is a REAL `AbortSignal` from the production `AsyncWorkScope` (not a mock). The test wraps the command in `scope.run(...)`, aborts the scope mid-`channels.stop`, and asserts both that `callGateway` received `signal` and that `writeConfigFile` was never called.

```console
$ vitest run src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts -t "normalizes a listed deletion"
 ✓  commands  src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts > channelsRemoveCommand > normalizes a listed deletion before stopping runtime, running lifecycle, and persisting 4945ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

The discriminating assertions (drive credible failure):

```ts
expect(gatewayMocks.callGateway).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(
  expect.objectContaining({ signal: scope.signal }),
);
expect(configMocks.writeConfigFile).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```

Mutation check (proves the test is not vacuous): deleting the `signal,` line from the `callGateway` invocation in `remove.ts` makes this exact test go RED with the `ObjectContaining` assertion above, i.e. the test catches the regression.

### What was not tested

- The `list` command's separate interrupt gap mentioned in the original bug report is NOT covered by this PR (tracked separately).
- No live end-to-end CLI subprocess + real SIGINT was exercised; the proof drives the production `AsyncWorkScope`/`AbortSignal` path directly, which is what the CLI SIGINT handler installs. A real `openclaw channels remove` SIGINT run would additionally require a live gateway account and is out of scope for this regression test.
- The non-gateway removal path (plugin with no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) skips the stop entirely and is unchanged; its existing tests still pass.

### Open PR collision check

Searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` and `src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts` (today's snapshot). Two open PRs touch the same files but fix different bugs in different regions:
- #187514 "scheduled automations keep running after their Telegram account is removed while a binding remains" touches `remove.ts`/test in the automations/binding area, not the `channels.stop` signal path.
- #134060 "deleting an account leaves its stored inbound events behind" touches `remove.ts`/test in the inbound-events area, not the signal path.

Neither modifies `signal`/`throwIfAborted`/`callGateway`/`channels.stop` in `remove.ts`, so there is no duplicate-fix overlap; only a possible future merge-time file coordination on the shared test file. No open PR addresses the Ctrl+C cancellation gap fixed here.



E2E proof (built CLI + Gateway, SIGINT/SIGTERM during a slow channels.stop): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198019#issuecomment-6841689898

prs.title: fix(cli): surface failed systemd dueling-scope probe in `status --deep`
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway status --deep` on Linux could report a healthy Gateway while the systemd dueling-scope check had never run. When the deep probe threw, `findSystemdGatewayInstallation(serviceEnv).catch(() => null)` turned the failure into `null`, so the result carried neither a warning nor an error: "the probe broke" and "no dueling scope found" printed the same thing. The service-mode startup path in `gateway-cli/run.ts` swallowed the same failure.

- Problem: a failed systemd dueling-scope probe was silently dropped on both paths.
- Solution: keep the redacted probe error on the status payload, print it next to the dueling-scope warning it belongs to, and log it during service-mode startup.
- What changed: `status.gather.ts` records `gateway.duelingScopesWarningError`; `status.print.systemd.ts` renders it; `run-systemd.ts` logs it. The print/inspect code moved into sibling modules to stay inside the line-cap ratchet.
- What did NOT change: a successful probe still prints the existing dueling-scope warning; no new flags, config keys, exit codes, or extra probes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Silence is the wrong default for a diagnostic whose job is to catch a misconfigured host; this is the same silent-swallow class as #195977.

- Best fix: carry the error beside the warning it invalidates, redact at the egress boundary with `redactSupportDiagnosticLine`, and print both from one owner so `status` and startup agree.
- Alternative: rethrow and fail the whole `status` command. Rejected: status is a read-only health report, unrelated checks should still print, and the operator needs the partial result plus a named remedy.
- Risk / non-goals: the probe still only runs on Linux with a native service target (default install identity, no port override, healthy service inspection); this does not widen when it runs.

## User Impact

Operators on Linux now see `Could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: <reason> The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; run openclaw doctor for the full check.` instead of a silent gap, and the startup log names the same reason and remedy.

## Evidence

Before/after on one machine (Linux, systemd 255, Node 24.19, non-root uid 1000). The failure is real, not mocked: `/etc/systemd/system/openclaw-gateway.service` exists while the system manager does not know it, so the probe throws `ServiceInspectionError: busctl --system call: exit 1; Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded.` A real `openclaw gateway run` serves port 18899, then a second real `openclaw gateway run` starts in service mode and evicts it:

| Same scenario, real CLI | Before (`46350da`) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Startup evicts a stale gateway, probe throws | eviction logged, inspection failure dropped | eviction logged **and** the inspection warning |
| `gatherDaemonStatus` + real printer, probe throws | error undefined, nothing printed | error recorded, warning printed |
| `gateway status --deep`, probe succeeds | no inspection warning | unchanged: no inspection warning |
| `gateway status --deep`, probe fails mid-run | probe access denied, nothing printed | same denied access, warning printed |

```
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=1 openclaw gateway run --port 18899   # 46350da
[gateway] service-mode: cleared 1 stale gateway pid(s) before bind on port 18899
```

```
$ OPENCLAW_SERVICE_MARKER=1 openclaw gateway run --port 18899   # this branch
[gateway] service-mode: cleared 1 stale gateway pid(s) before bind on port 18899
[gateway] service-mode: could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: busctl --system call: exit 1; Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded. busctl --system could not be inspected. The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; check read access to the reported unit and run openclaw doctor for the full check.
```

Focused tests, same test file, base source vs this branch:

```
# 46350da source, this branch's tests
× surfaces a dueling-scope inspection error when the systemd probe fails
  → expected undefined to be defined
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 53 skipped (55)
```

```
# this branch
✓ reports dueling systemd diagnosis for its native target
✓ surfaces a dueling-scope inspection error when the systemd probe fails
      Test Files  1 passed (1)
           Tests  2 passed | 53 skipped (55)
```

The focused tests above drive the shipped `gatherDaemonStatus` and the shipped `printDaemonStatus`: only the systemd boundary is stubbed, so the collector-to-printer wiring is the real code.

`gateway status --deep` reaches its own probe only after a healthy service inspection, so a mid-run host change is what separates the two failures. Reproduced with the shipped CLI and no stubs: traversal on the user-unit directory was revoked right after the service audit's second `systemctl --user show`, and `strace` shows the deep probe's own discovery call denied 23s later, with no failed inspection in either run.

```
# identical probe syscall, 46350da and this branch
access("/home/…/.config/systemd/user/openclaw-gateway.service", F_OK) = -1 EACCES
```

```
$ openclaw gateway status --deep      # 46350da
Service: systemd user (enabled)
Runtime: running (pid 280115, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0)
Last shutdown: gateway.stop at 2026-11-10T02:12:06.107Z
```

```
$ openclaw gateway status --deep      # this branch
Service: systemd user (enabled)
Runtime: running (pid 280115, state active, sub running, last exit 0, reason 0)
Last shutdown: gateway.stop at 2026-11-10T02:12:06.107Z
Could not inspect the systemd gateway installation: EACCES: permission denied, access [redacted-path]. The dueling-scope diagnosis was NOT checked; run openclaw doctor for the full check.
```

Per review: use the real daemon-status types instead of a narrow printer type, drop the redundant baseline test, and give the startup warning a recovery step.

prs.title: fix: keep Gateway runtime checks off the main thread
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway-wide stalls when a runtime executable lookup blocks during readiness checks or child-process failure diagnosis.

## User Impact

Gateway readiness, health, startup, and recovery can wait for filesystem I/O without blocking unrelated requests. Missing or replaced runtimes still trigger the existing unavailable-runtime and recovery behavior. Public synchronous APIs retain their contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing child-runtime owner now prepares physical facts asynchronously and carries them to publication, where callers also consult current logical state. Native asynchronous diagnosis stays separate from the failing command runner. Child processes retain independent physical-close settlement, so delayed or rejected diagnosis cannot release cleanup custody early. The broker shares one terminal diagnosis while preserving its already-ready failure behavior. No new cache, configuration, schema, or recovery manager is introduced.

This is an availability tradeoff, not a speedup. On a synthetic real-HTTP readiness workload (44 channels, 176 accounts), measured median overhead was approximately 0.013 ms wall, 8.15 µs main-thread CPU, 27.32 µs parent-process CPU, and 2658 sampled allocation bytes per request. All medians increased; loaded-host A/A variability and paired increases are retained below. Production code grows 315 lines to preserve the named synchronous interfaces and separate physical-close from asynchronous diagnosis. One import-time executable stat and explicit synchronous SDK/OOM/SQLite entry points remain.

## Evidence

- Real Gateway HTTP-server/TCP clients: while executable `fs.promises.access` completion is held, `/readyz` remains pending and concurrent `/healthz` returns 200. Changing drain state before release produces `/readyz` 503 with `gateway-draining`. This exercises the production HTTP server/router/request lifetime; it is not a full model/plugin startup claim. The existing main-thread fs spy also passes.
- Integrated candidate: both HTTP tests and the complete agent/environment/artifact RPC flow pass; a source-matching canonical build and three real restart cases pass (original crash/partial-shutdown resume, direct child continuation, and continuation after requester completion). The three previously failed wrapper closure/resolution selectors also pass.
- Canonical Madge reproduced the owned static type cycle on the previous head. Readiness contracts now live in the existing health type owner; both static and runtime-value cycle guards pass. The new Windows diagnostic module is included in the wrapper inventory.
- `pnpm check:changed --staged --base 2035b073` completed **39/40 stages**: all types, lint, format, ratchets and other guards passed. Its dead-export stage reproduces identically on clean exact `2035b073`: a test-only trusted-proxy helper export introduced by #196867 (`f4f290c52`) and eight live lazy-UI capability exports introduced by #197466 (`d90d52cc`). These are separate main regressions, not suppressed or treated as noise; no unrelated UI rewrite is included here. `pnpm deadcode:unused-files` passes with zero production/full-tree entries.
- Affected Chromium routing (5) and post-deploy E2E (6) pass on the integrated candidate, with a current production UI build and joined Chromium exit. Fresh four-pass Codex P2 review against `2035b073` is scoped-clean; it was static with partitioned supplied context, not four independent complete-context executions. Prior owner 131-case, restart/startup and Windows/Workshop proofs remain explicitly scoped to their recorded predecessor source.
- Regression guards cover readiness `accessSync` 2→0 for two requests, cached-health 2 sync→1 async observation, and diagnosed failure `accessSync` 1 + `statSync` 1→0 sync with asynchronous observations. These are owner API-call counts, not kernel syscall counts.

The main integration is pinned to `2035b073` for two named CI prerequisites: the `createWithRequest` producer and merged #197976 protocol inventory repair. Two missed fixture migrations are repaired with exact-parent red/green evidence: #197875 (`9ecae401`) omitted the artifact API fixture, and #195420 (`924a3bc9`) intentionally preserved unclaimed yielded work after requester completion while the restart fixture still expected failure. The corrected yield case positively joins requester completion and then proves a later real turn resumes and completes the same child. No timeout or authoritative status was weakened.

Two failures remain investigated uncertainties. An unchanged SPA fallback test timed out on its first HTML request in the initial multi-file run; candidate and exact-parent isolated replays passed at the original timeout. CI also failed the partial-shutdown resume case with unavailable principal facts; its original selector passed once on exact CI main parent `20237d956` and once on the integrated candidate. Neither passing comparison is presented as a fix, flaky diagnosis, or inherited-failure proof.

<details>
<summary>Measurement scope and integration notes</summary>

Thirty separated timing/allocation rows used five rotated A1/B/A2 triplets, each with 5 warm requests and 60 measured requests. macOS Node 26.12.1; load 15.55–18.42. Pooled A→B medians per 60 requests: wall 9.403979→10.165292ms, main CPU 9.246→9.735ms, parent CPU 15.923→17.562ms, sampled allocation 2456500→2615984bytes. Paired increases reached 28.78% wall, 24.75% main CPU, 22.04% parent CPU. A/A ranges were −56.22% to +15.13% wall, −53.13% to +13.36% main CPU, −50.51% to +11.27% parent CPU, and −3.31% to +2.84% allocation. All 30 owned process groups drained naturally; no repeated or discarded rows. Allocation is sampled main-isolate V8 allocation, not total native/worker memory. Parent CPU excludes the source compiler child; setup/import and failure-probe costs are outside the window. The matched frozen source campaign measures this owner delta; exact-main correctness is qualified separately.

Overlapping open work observed during preparation: #157693 readiness cleanup projection/raw readiness fixture, #181390 health observedAt, and #196773 schema child-close waiters. No unrelated peer features were transplanted. Future composition must retain prepared-readiness fixtures and independent physical-child-close settlement.

</details>

prs.title: fix: compaction fails for sandboxed sessions with selected skills
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sandboxed conversations can stop answering when required compaction reads a persisted selected-skill snapshot, reporting that the conversation could not be shortened.

## User Impact

Long conversations can proceed through the affected automatic and direct/manual compaction paths without resetting the conversation or dropping selected skill instructions. No configuration, storage migration, or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session persistence intentionally omits runtime skill catalogs. Required preflight was replacing the hydrated current-turn snapshot with that persisted projection, causing `Selected skill snapshot must be hydrated before sandbox delivery` before summarization.

Reuse the prepared turn snapshot, and hydrate persisted-only snapshots through the existing skill-snapshot owner before direct compaction prepares its sandbox. Pass that same snapshot into sandbox delivery and runtime preparation. Retain pinned revisions, source roots, cancellation checks, and the existing sandbox guard; do not persist runtime catalogs or refresh already-hydrated snapshots.

## Evidence

### Current revision

- Current head: `f1ee3b98c3b41aa7e3fcf307f7aa94e8e5944d86`. obviyus integrated current main and consolidated the regression into the existing preflight test; the earlier standalone persisted-skill test/harness is no longer part of this revision.
- [Built-Gateway red/green proof by obviyus](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198029#issuecomment-6842306282): repeated automatic and manual compaction failures on main, successful compaction and subsequent replies on the candidate, retained selected skills, unchanged persisted snapshots, and non-sandboxed/no-selected-skill controls. Real SSH sandbox and controlled model endpoint; the final head adds only a test type line to that executed candidate.
- [Supplementary real-Docker/local-model output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198029#issuecomment-6842515520): automatic count 0 → 2, manual count 2 → 3, subsequent semantic reply, pinned R1 delivered after R2 publication, and unchanged snapshots across each compaction. Executed original head `8de1ea816cc`; the production repair and relevant runtime paths are byte-identical at the current head. Small-model summary degradation flags and failed exploratory attempts are disclosed in the receipt.
- [Hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198029#issuecomment-6841634287) accepts the runtime proof on the current head: no findings, no before-merge items, ready for maintainer review.
- [Exact-head CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43355835344): success, including dependency and security-sensitive review statuses. Merged as [`35949a1cea37`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/35949a1cea3738db01efca48db08c75b8939b2b5) on 2026-11-13. Deployment is not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Historical local validation on original head 8de1ea816cc (before test consolidation)</summary>

- Red/green automatic-preflight regression reaches the real sandbox resolver and reproduces the exact error on the base; the full preflight suite passes (47 tests).
- Persisted-selection regression exercises real SQLite projection/reload, Library revision pins, skill hydration, filesystem delivery, and container-path mapping. It verifies revision R1 is delivered after R2 exists, compaction succeeds, and the stored snapshot is unchanged. The selected-revision and explicit-empty regressions both pass. The selected-revision test body took 6.59s; the empty-selection case took 0.14s. Together with the four existing sandbox policy/cancellation cases, the command took 109.48s including 63.02s cold worker preparation; Vitest duration was 41.26s. This is an integration boundary requiring the host-owned database broker.
- Prompt-prefix stability suite: 14 tests pass. Cold worker compilation dominates its 155.99s command time; the full preflight command also incurred cold compilation. CI seconds are not yet available.

- Independent native code review of the complete delta against `14feaef71db35cd1b4b2627314ee997a883b156b`, P0–P2 coverage: one P2 (explicit empty snapshots unexpectedly discovering skills) was reproduced and fixed; re-review found no remaining P0–P2 issues. This was a read-only native reviewer, not the CLI helper or a hosted approval.
- Simplification: existing hydration owner reused, no new production helper/cache/schema; two oversized test fixtures were moved into their existing support modules without dropping assertions. Production delta +45/-2 lines; regression/support growth stays below the 400-line test allowance. Line-cap and mock-export ratchets pass.

- Final consolidated run: **53/53 tests pass** across preflight, selected/empty skills, and sandbox policy/cancellation suites (151.50s command wall time, 74.97s Vitest; cold worker preparation 70.33s). Production and both affected test typecheck leaves, touched-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Structural duplication scan over the affected runtime/reply roots found no >=0.8 candidate involving either changed production function. Complexity was measured without coverage; no CRAP or mutation score is claimed. The bounded mutation run was stopped when the independent review found the empty-selection defect; its red/green regression is retained.

Scope limits: model completion and container provisioning are scripted in the integration fixture; live server recovery, native CLI compaction, and deployment are not claimed. The local autoreview CLI was attempted but failed authentication and produced no review verdict.

</details>

prs.title: fix(bonjour): npm installs fail to start Bonjour discovery with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
prs.body:
Closes #198010

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: On npm installs, Bonjour discovery fails at Gateway startup with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for `@homebridge/ciao/native.js`, so the Gateway does not advertise.

## User Impact

User impact: an npm install of the packed package advertises `_openclaw-gw._tcp` over Bonjour, so LAN clients can discover it. Source installs are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#182826 moved the advertiser to `@homebridge/ciao/native.js`. That entry only exists in our pnpm-patched copy of ciao. The root package depends on ciao but does not bundle it, so npm installs get the registry 1.3.12, which has no `native.js`. The Bonjour plugin's own `bundleDependencies` only applies when the plugin is packed on its own. In the core package it ships under `dist/extensions/bonjour`.

This adds `@homebridge/ciao` to the root `bundleDependencies`, the same way `acorn` and `playwright-core` ship their patched runtimes. The tarball check now requires ciao to be bundled, like `chrome-devtools-mcp`, when the package's `dist` references `@homebridge/ciao/native.js`, so a future unbundle fails package validation rather than discovery at runtime. The `patches/README.md` note now says the root package bundles it too.

The packed tarball grows by about 418 KiB (ciao plus `debug`, `ms`, `fast-deep-equal`, `source-map-support`, `source-map`, `buffer-from`, `tslib`).

The checker also validates published and frozen candidates in Package Acceptance. Releases before #182826, such as 2026.11.3, import the ciao package root, which registry ciao satisfies, and do not bundle it. The requirement is therefore scoped to packages that use the patch-only entry, so those releases keep their shipped dependency contract, as #158098 did for the MCP patches.

This changes root `bundleDependencies`, so the dependency guard will ask for a maintainer `/allow-dependencies-change`.

## Evidence

I packed this commit the way `scripts/npm-prepared-bundle.mjs` does (`pnpm run prepack`, then `pnpm pack --config.node-linker=hoisted`, plus the `@openclaw/ai` tarball). prs.title: feat(exec): keep durable background commands running across Gateway restarts on macOS
prs.body:
Fixes #197443

## What Problem This Solves

Durable background commands are unavailable on macOS, preventing sessions from keeping work running across Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

macOS users can run Gateway-host background commands with `durable: true` and resume observing their output and completion after a Gateway restart. This requires a logged-in GUI session; logout and reboot still end the jobs. Descendants that leave the command's process group are outside its timeout and stop handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use transient launchd jobs behind the existing durable-process registry. A wrapper tracks the command's process group, enforces its timeout, and records its outcome and duration. Failed job observations remain unknown and are retried. The launch environment is stored in a private spec file and removed before command execution. Doctor excludes these jobs from its stray-service scan.

The existing completion-notification crash window remains: a Gateway crash immediately after recording notification settlement can lose the completion wake.

## Evidence

Reused implementation evidence, inspected for publication:

- Focused tests: 52 passed across three files, covering launchd, systemd, and exec-target selection; no failures in the final run.
- Test lines: the PR adds 174 net test lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/197474-durable-exec-macos.txt` allocates 174 lines for launchd supervisor states, wrapper failure, process-group cleanup, and timeout regression coverage.
- Regression checks: process-group observation and wrapper-loss cases fail with the hardening removed and pass with it; the command-stop case fails with the prior wrapper and passes with the fix.
- Recorded build completed successfully; targeted lint and formatting checks passed. The recorded core typecheck produced no diagnostics.
- Isolated macOS VM: a durable command survives a Gateway restart and delivers its completion wake; killing the wrapper preserves the running command and subsequently reports an unknown outcome; timeout enforcement works while the Gateway is down and retains the measured duration.
- Publication check: `git diff --check` passes. Tests and live scenarios were not rerun for publication; broad CI, Linux live execution, logout/reboot behavior, and macOS privacy-permission behavior were not checked here.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agent creation returning a post-commit error when the config watcher observes the agent's own newly written config before the writer finishes.

Separate the prepared config's lifetime from the caller's authority. The existing synchronous pre-publication guard checks prepared settings immediately before the write becomes visible. prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

## Verification

Current author head: `b61e37141b7760e0933aedd671d9ee9f73a78b55`. prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

<!-- forone-adoption-decision-20261102:start -->
## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02

The Slack-owner decision remains whether to expose the compatibility-preserving `requireExplicitBotMention` opt-in. The current submission section below owns the latest head and CI status; maintainer edits remain enabled. Owner acceptance is still outstanding.

The historical [advisory review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177555#issuecomment-6274222081) reports no actionable findings and sufficient recorded isolated-Gateway output, and recommends accepting the opt-in. It does not record Slack-owner acceptance. Its two outstanding checklist entries both concern that same public-contract decision. The review is scoped to `39d01116dd2d5e01fa7f8ab50dbb1e44613a0e9a`; the earlier12-input comparison was bound to8fa0cc0d85711ab2ee19e488ec9e325309a476c2. That earlier integration retained11 byte-identical inputs; access-control documentation only adds accepted official Slack read-bound guidance. The strict opt-in authored delta and committed Gateway scenario are retained. The older proof retains its original head; that earlier head's CI supported its integration. No fresh live Slack run or current employee acceptance is claimed.

Recorded official distribution evidence confirms that the need remains after the implicit-thread silence repair: unmodified Core/Slack **2026.10.10-beta.5**, build `7e15622f37bd0ced194a3b0fccacb4ad6bc78d85`, still admits untagged bot messages through both `bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot` in the isolated distributed-function/compiled-gate fixture. The same 20-case matrix passes 17, with these two strict-admission requirements and the separate optional-completion policy remaining. Package integrity and the scope are recorded in the [release follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621). This is not a new live Slack incident or a claim that existing documented defaults were silently changed.

**Decision requested from the Slack owner:** accept or reject this optional public setting at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Omitted/false keeps existing implicit bot handoffs. With `allowBots: "mentions"` and the opt-in enabled, untagged bot activation is rejected while explicit bot requests, implicit human follow-ups, DMs, authorized commands, and existing sender restrictions retain their controls. This is the compatibility-preserving alternative to #160752's default change; no new default change is requested here.

This PR decides **admission**, not whether an already admitted explicit bot notification may finish empty. That latter product-policy question remains separate in #186514. A scoped acceptance/rejection of this opt-in is the missing adoption decision; existing code/proof work is not being represented as owner approval. No new review command or redundant behavior replay was added for this mechanical integration.
<!-- forone-stable-adoption-evidence-20261103:start -->
### 2026-11-03: the same admission requirement remains in stable2026.10.10

Official npm/latest Core/Slack **2026.10.10**, distributed Core build`7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be`, was checked with the unchanged20-case synthetic matrix: **17PASS / 3FAIL**. The two untagged-bot admission cases (`bot_thread_participant` and `reply_to_bot`) still admit the bot under existing mentions-only behavior. The two implicit-thread optional/silent conditions from merged #164877 nowPASS in stable; the third remaining failure concerns #186514's separate explicit-bot completion policy.

The [stable distribution follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164877#issuecomment-6266458621) fixes the verified immutable Core/Slack hashes and execution scope. This is actual distributed Core-function / verbatim compiled Slack-gate evidence, with unchanged cases/assertions and shipped package bytes. The existing native Gateway proof retains its original binding. This paragraph updates distribution evidence only; the current PR head and compatible opt-in proposal remain unchanged. Slack-owner acceptance or rejection remains unrecorded.

prs.title: feat(slack): render streamed reasoning as task cards, with continuation messages for long streams
prs.body:
## Decision requested

This PR adds one optional setting, `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "narration" | "cards"` (channel and per-account scope), and one additive compositor option (`reasoningLine`) used only by the Slack plugin. Default is unchanged (`narration`, today's behavior). `cards` is opt-in, there is no migration, and existing configs are untouched. It needs a maintainer's yes or no on the setting; the rendering code is only reachable once it is set.

Rebased onto current main, which already contains the first companion fix (#143879, merged); the second (#143880) is being landed by a maintainer. Two commits for review: the first renders reasoning as task cards on a single message; the second adds continuation messages, the byte ledger, and recovery when Slack rejects an oversized append. They ship together: the rendering half is not safe on its own for long turns, which is why an attempted split (#144256) was folded back.

## What Problem This Solves

With `agents.defaults.reasoningDefault: "stream"` (an existing operator opt-in), OpenClaw streams the model's reasoning while the reply is generated. On Slack's native progress card (`streaming.mode: "progress"`, native task cards, which is the default) the plugin keeps one compacted reasoning line, filters it out of the task list (`resolveNativeProgressLines`) and appends it to the stream's narration text (`resolveNativeProgressNarration`). The first sentence of the reasoning therefore lands at the top of the reply as plain prose, later reasoning is appended to that prose as further snapshots arrive, and a long think shows as an unlabeled paragraph above the card rather than as the thought it is. There is no setting that renders reasoning in the card itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one opt-in, `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "narration" | "cards"` (default `narration`, today's behavior unchanged). In `cards` mode the Slack plugin renders streamed reasoning as task rows in the plan block:

- The plugin accumulates the reasoning text through the compositor's existing merge (`mergeReasoningProgress`, core semantics: an explicit or detected snapshot or a prefix extension replaces, otherwise the delta is appended) and splits it into segments of about 240 characters at word boundaries. Cuts depend only on preceding text, so a segment already shown never changes as the text grows. Each segment is one task row with a stable id (`reasoning:<n>`), label `Reasoning`, a 🧠 prefix, and `status: completed` for every segment but the newest. Row titles are capped at 250 characters; Slack documents 256 characters per `task_update` field ([chat.appendStream](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.appendStream/)).
- One streamed message holds only so much. Slack's plan block renders at most 50 tasks ([plan block](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/plan-block/)), and `chat.appendStream` rejects further content with `msg_too_long` once a message that carries text holds about 10,600-11,300 UTF-8 bytes of titles, `details` (about double) and text (undocumented; measured, see Evidence). A long think therefore continues in a new message: the plugin keeps a per-message ledger of everything it has put on the current stream message (task titles, `details` and `output` weighted 2x, the plan title, streamed text, all in UTF-8 bytes; `extensions/slack/src/stream-size.ts`) and, before a send, splits the update into what still fits and what does not. New rows are admitted while the message stays under 6,000 weighted bytes of rows and 50 rows; streamed text while the total stays under 9,000. Segments are cut in the same unit (at most 240 bytes, never splitting a code point), so a card with its 5-byte prefix is at most 245 bytes and an emoji- or CJK-heavy segment can no longer be truncated by the title cap. When something does not fit, the current message is finished with `chat.stopStream` carrying the plan title `Thinking, continued below` and every open row marked complete, and a new native stream starts in the same thread for the same recipient with the title `Thinking, continued`, a fresh reconcile snapshot and the deferred rows; no task id carries over. Card numbering continues (`reasoning:<n>`), later tool rows land on the newest message, and the answer plus the `Thought for …` title land on the message that is current when the turn ends. Before the answer is appended the same check runs for closeout plus answer; if they would not fit, the think closes on its message with `Thought for …` and the answer streams as its own message in the thread. The reasoning runtime seals the cards that landed on a finished message at their current cut (`rolloverSlackReasoningCards`) while the compositor keeps merging the same phase, so cumulative snapshots neither repeat nor lose text.
- `msg_too_long` is now classified (`SlackStreamMessageTooLongError`, a `SlackStreamNotDeliveredError`): the stream is healthy, nothing from the rejected call landed, and the SDK's retained text is discarded before the message is stopped. In `cards` mode a rejected card update or streamed text rolls to a continuation and is retried once; a rejected answer finishes the think and retries the answer as its own stream; if the retry is rejected as well, the stream is stopped and the answer goes through the normal reply path. Every mode gains the last part: a `msg_too_long` on the answer no longer leaves the message `in_progress` without it.
- A tool call (`onToolStart`, phase `start`) and the end of a reasoning phase (`onReasoningEnd`) seal the open segment, so thinking after a tool result starts a new row below the tool row instead of extending the one above it. The seal runs before the tool row is admitted, which fixes the row order in the same append.
- Reasoning stays out of the narration text in this mode; commentary still streams as text.
- At completion the plan title becomes `Thought for <n>s, <k> tool call(s)` (part of the same mode rather than a second setting; easy to split if preferred). An explicit `progress.label` still wins, and while running the headline never borrows a reasoning row's text: it keeps the newest tool row's title or falls back to `Thinking`.
- Cards are ordinary compositor lines, so they share the existing one-second coalescing loop (`createDraftStreamLoop({ throttleMs: 1_000, coalesceInFlight: true })`), the delayed start gate and the native reconciler with tool rows: one `chat.appendStream` call per batch carrying every changed row, and no throttle of its own. Because each card occupies one line of the compositor's rolling window, `cards` mode raises the effective window to at least 64 lines (`progress.maxLines` raises it further); with the default of 8, a burst of more than eight new segments between two sends would evict a card before it was ever sent. Rows that leave the window later are already complete in Slack and stay there.
- Per-turn state (segments, the rolled prefix of the open phase, tool count, start time, the message chain and its ledger) resets with the rest of the progress turn state.
- `cards` applies to the detailed native card (`progress.toolProgress: true`); the quiet card keeps its single summary row and shows reasoning as narration, as today.

Layout: the pure segmentation/planning helpers live in `extensions/slack/src/progress-reasoning.ts`, the per-turn runtime in `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch-progress-reasoning.ts`, the per-message size ledger and fit planner in `extensions/slack/src/stream-size.ts`, the stream chain (snapshot, narration state, rollover, `msg_too_long` retry) in `dispatch-progress-stream.ts`, and `progress-blocks.ts` gains the 250-character title for reasoning rows plus the headline rule. `dispatch-streaming.ts` records streamed text in the ledger, accepts a thread override for continuations and a `msg_too_long` retry hook; the transport accepts a thread override. Core changes are limited to the config type, the UI-hint label and the regenerated bundled channel metadata. `narration` mode never enters the rollover paths (`rollover: false` skips every fit check and hook); the regression proof below shows its chunk sequence is byte-identical to `upstream/main`, and the dispatch tests assert one start, two appends and one stop for both the narration fixture and a short `cards` think.

Config surface: this adds one channel config key (`channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning`, also under `accounts.*`), so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json` `channel` moves from 3710 to 3712. Per AGENTS.md this is a conscious budget raise for an owner decision: the alternative of overloading `nativeTaskCards` or `style` would change the meaning of existing values.

Alternative considered: streaming the reasoning into the reply text instead of the card. Not chosen because a native stream is append-only, so every reply would carry its thinking permanently in the message body; task rows can be marked complete and collapse with the card, and the final answer stays the message text.

## User Impact

Operators who set `reasoningDefault: "stream"` can add `channels.slack.streaming.progress.reasoning: "cards"` (with `progress.toolProgress: true`) and see the model's reasoning as a sequence of 🧠 rows in the plan block, interleaved in order with tool rows, with the card titled `Thought for <n>s, <k> tool calls` when the turn finishes. A think longer than one message holds continues in a second (third, …) message in the same thread titled `Thinking, continued`, the previous one ending as `Thinking, continued below`; the answer follows the last one. In any mode, a `msg_too_long` on the answer now ends with the answer posted normally instead of a message stuck in streaming state. Everyone else sees no change: the default is `narration`, and with `reasoningDefault` off (the default) nothing is rendered either way. The setting validates as an enum; other values are rejected by the strict Slack schema.

Root cause, one mechanism: core fires `onReasoningEnd` and `onAssistantMessageStart` best effort (`runBestEffortCallback`, not awaited). With a live model the `onReasoningEnd` handler is still waiting on the seal's in-flight append when the run ends and the final reply is dispatched; `deliverNativeFinal` cancels the pacing loop, which was the only guard on `beginNewProgressTurn`, and opens the compositor's `beginNewTurn` via `markFinalReplyStarted`, so the late boundary ran a turn rotation under the final: it stopped the stream (short turn: the answer then opened its own stream) or, in the long turn, hit the window between the roll's stop and the continuation's start, clearing the compositor and the reasoning runtime (no `Thought for`, headline kept). Fix: a non-forced `beginNewProgressTurn` now waits for the in-flight final delivery (`finalDelivery`) before it acts, so the answer and the summary title land on the card message and a genuine next assistant message still rotates afterwards. ### 4. Source of the limits

- 50 tasks per plan block: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/plan-block/ (hence the 50-row rollover bound; the API accepts more ids and renders 50, see the probe).
- 256 characters per `task_update` / `plan_update` text field: https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.appendStream/ (hence 240-character segments and the 250-character title cap).
- Per-message size: not documented for `chat.appendStream`; `msg_too_long` measured 2026-09-09/10 against Slack as above: the check runs once the message carries text and counts titles, `details` (about 2x) and text in UTF-8 bytes, ceiling about 10,600-11,300 bytes (text-only 9,064 accepted / 12,054 rejected; 48 rows of 11,215 title bytes rejected a 92-byte answer; 24 emoji rows of 10,418 bytes rejected a 3,045-byte answer; 50 emoji rows of 22,900 bytes with no text accepted; with 100-character details 8,471 accepted / 8,821 rejected; the API accepts task ids beyond 50 but renders 50).
- Corroboration only: on a downstream build of this behavior against `@openclaw/slack@2026.8.1-beta.3`, a 62-second turn with one tool call rendered 30 cards in Slack (observed 2026-09-09).

### Design: bounded admission

The reasoning runtime no longer hands every planned card to the compositor. It admits a card only while the message being built can still take it, rows and bytes, on top of everything already admitted for that message (the chain's `admitsRow` runs the production fit planner over the current draft plus the candidate against the current ledger, or a fresh one before the first start; tool and plan rows count the same way). Cards the message refuses queue in order inside the runtime and are released when the chain rolls to a new message. A card counts as queued only when the message refused it for room, not while a render is still waiting behind the send in flight, and a release is deferred while a compositor flush holds the gate's start promise on that send (releasing there would wait on itself). Nothing is evicted: the compositor's rolling window stays disabled in cards mode as a safety net, because the default window (eight lines) is smaller than one message's row budget; with admission bounded, at most one message's rows are unsent at any time.

Every message of the chain after the first is opened by one function (`openMessage`): it fits the opening under a fresh message's budget, text first (or room reserved for the text the caller appends next), then rows in order, defers the rest to the compositor and records only what Slack accepted. The send loop, the narration rollover and the rejected completion before a separate answer all open through it; `transport.start` has no other call site in the chain.

`send()` now reports `{ sent, settled }` (settled: nothing queued, every row of the draft on a message) and keeps going past a full message on its own, bounded by the work in hand (queued cards plus unsent rows, two rounds each) instead of a fixed round count. The terminal paths drain until settled: a final that does not stream, the silent closeout, turn rotation, and the queued cards before an in-stream answer (previously skipped when the answer fit). If the compositor refuses a release after the passes, the remainder is placed straight from the queue on budgeted messages, so no completion append or stop ever carries an unbudgeted batch; the turn's status (error/complete) still lands on the last message.

Guard: every dispatcher test charges each accepted start, append and stop to its message with the production `SlackStreamMessageLedger` and fails in `afterEach` if any message passes 50 rows or the 9,000-byte budget; the thresholds are read back from the exported fit planner at load time, so no production export exists for them (knip production scan: 0). It is on for all dispatcher cases and no scenario needed it off.

### 13. Deferred compositor rows not counted as unsettled

Scenario: more distinct tool rows inside one throttle window than a message can hold (120 in the test; 60 do not reach the case, because the first message and its roll absorb a budget's worth before any fresh opening has to defer), then an immediate error final. `openMessage` admitted only the rows that fit, but `send()` declared the result settled because only queued reasoning cards were counted, so `drain()` returned and the terminal completion appended the remaining rows unbudgeted.

Fix: `openMessage` reports whether the opening deferred rows, and `send()` settles a fresh opening only when no card is queued and nothing was deferred; the deferred rows go out on further messages through the existing roll path. A second defect surfaced by the regression: a message that overflowed with rows it could not take must not carry its running rows along (round 3's rule), or every continuation re-admits the same running rows ahead of the deferred ones and the chain never converges; such a message freezes its rows as before round 3, while a roll for queued cards, narration or the answer still carries running tool rows.

Test: `drains tool rows the compositor admitted past the budget before an error closeout` (120 distinct tool starts, error final): every row reaches Slack once across at least three messages, the last message ends with a stop carrying the error status, the final is delivered once, and the budget guard stays clean.

Before:
```
× drains tool rows the compositor admitted past the budget before an error closeout
  → expected 2 to be greater than or equal to 3
  → "append: message holds 120 rows and 1452 weighted bytes (budget 50 rows, 9000 bytes)"
```

After: passes.

### 14. Tool rows overtaking queued reasoning

Scenario: a 60-segment snapshot queues reasoning beyond the current message, and a tool starts before the next paced send; `seal()` returned with cards still queued and the tool row went straight into the compositor, so Slack showed the tool above the reasoning that preceded it.

Fix: `noteToolCall` flushes the queued cards through the chain (`drain`, joined to the transport order) before the tool row is admitted, so admission order is shared: reasoning that preceded the tool reaches its messages first. The chain's `releasePending` now waits for a pending compositor flush to settle unless the caller is the pacing loop's own send (which defers to the next paced send, avoiding the self-wait), so a tool-boundary drain queued behind the startup send never falls through to direct placement.

Test: `keeps a tool row behind the reasoning cards queued before it` (60 cards, tool start before the next send): the first appearance of every row in transport order is reasoning 1-60 then the tool, across the messages the cards need.

Before:
```
× keeps a tool row behind the reasoning cards queued before it
  → expected [ 'reasoning_1', 'reasoning_2', …(59) ] to deeply equal [ 'reasoning_1', 'reasoning_2', …(59) ]
    (tool_1 after reasoning_24, before reasoning_25)
```

After: passes.

### Design note (knip)

The guard no longer needs a production export. `SLACK_STREAM_MESSAGE_BUDGET` is private again; the dispatcher test derives the thresholds from the exported planner at load time (the row cap is how many tiny rows a fresh message admits, the byte budget the longest text a message already holding text still takes: 50 and 9,000). `scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` reports 0 entries for the production, script and full-tree scans.

### Results (this revision)

- Before (head `484b37b4`), the two new cases: `Tests 2 failed | 214 skipped (216)`.
- After: dispatcher `216 passed (216)` with the guard on; `extensions/slack` whole suite `Test Files 158 passed, Tests 2983 passed`.
- Knip unused-export scans (production, script, full-tree): 0 entries. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware`, `tsgo` for `tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, `git diff --check` pass. Part 1 (`e3fa7957`) unchanged; branch base `25a6148d1`.

### Not tested (this revision)

- A tool started while cards are queued and a compositor flush is pending (the startup send): the wait path in `releasePending` is exercised only indirectly.
- Running tool rows on an overflowing message whose result arrives later: by design they are frozen on that message; no test asserts the frozen state.

### 15. Later results for running rows frozen by an overflow roll

Scenario: a burst of tool starts larger than one message rolls the chain; a tool on a rolled message then fails. The overflow rule from the previous revision kept that running row out of `carried`, so its id entered `rolledTaskIds`, running and completion rendering both filtered it out, Slack kept the synthetic completed row, and the real result was never delivered.

Fix: running rows on an overflowed message are now frozen rather than plainly retired: `planSlackMessageRetirement` (extracted to `dispatch-progress-stream-rows.ts`) records each such row with its rendered state (title, status, details, output) alongside retiring it, so continuations still do not fill up with unchanged running rows. Before each render, `thawChangedRows` compares the frozen rows' current rendered state with the recorded one; a row whose state changed (a failure, output, a terminal status) leaves both the frozen register and `rolledTaskIds`, renders whole on the current message through the normal budgeted path, and is settled by the turn's completion there. Unchanged frozen rows stay frozen, so the non-convergence case remains fixed.

Test: `delivers a later result for a running row frozen by an overflow roll` (120 tool starts, paced sends roll the burst, then `command_output` with exit 1 for the first tool): the first message closed with the row painted complete, the current message receives the row with `error` and the completion settles it as `Recovered: …` complete, the answer lands there, no normal-reply fallback. The earlier non-convergence test (`drains tool rows the compositor admitted past the budget before an error closeout`) still passes.

Before:
```
× delivers a later result for a running row frozen by an overflow roll
  → expected [] to include 'error'
```

After: passes.

### Results (this revision)

- Before (head `c807766e`), the new case: `1 failed | 216 skipped (217)`.
- After: dispatcher `217 passed (217)` with the budget guard on; `extensions/slack` whole suite `Test Files 158 passed, Tests 2984 passed`.
- Knip unused-export scans (production, script, full-tree): 0 entries. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` (including the 700-line cap on the stream chain, which motivated the extraction), `tsgo` for `tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, `git diff --check` pass. Part 1 (`e3fa7957`) unchanged; branch base `25a6148d1`.

### 16. Continuation capacity behind a full plan

Scenario: a plan update with about 50 short steps fills the native row budget by itself; once reasoning queues, every rollover kept all `plan_step_*` rows eligible and every continuation opened with those plan rows first, leaving no slot for a card, so the send and drain loops produced plan-only messages until their bounds and direct placement returned with the cards still queued.

Fix (in `dispatch-progress-stream-rows.ts`, wired from the stream chain):

- Every message of the chain after the first is opened through `planSlackMessageOpening`, which budgets plan rows: it fits the rows that must carry and the queued cards first (the cards the runtime will release next are reserved by fitting their chunks without sending them, and only the reserved cards that actually fit count, since the planner defers everything after the first row that does not), then gives the remaining slots to plan rows in priority order: running steps, then steps not started, then completed steps (already visible on an earlier message), and within each group steps no message has shown yet before steps shown before. The plan rows a message shows are fixed for that message (`messagePlanStepIds`); later sends update their statuses in place and do not add plan rows, so they cannot compete with cards. Plan rows left out are never counted as deferred work; they wait for the next continuation.
- Steps shown on any message are tracked (`shownPlanStepIds`, recorded when a message retires), so the remainder paginates forward across continuations while running steps stay visible on each.
- At the closeout, `admitPlanForCompletion` lets plan rows the current message left out onto it, in the same priority order, as far as they fit beside what the message holds and the answer to come (`prepareForAnswer` reserves the answer text; the non-streamed and silent closeouts reserve nothing). Completed steps are therefore elided on a message only when the plan does not fit beside the rows already on it (for the final message: beside the cards it carries and the answer). This is broader than "only when the plan alone exceeds the row budget": on the last message the plan competes with the cards that landed there, and Slack's 50-row render cap cannot be exceeded either way. The first message still shows the whole plan.
- Cards refused for room now schedule the paced send themselves (`noteQueued`); previously nothing reached the compositor in that case, so the roll waited for an unrelated later event.

Tests: `leaves continuation capacity for queued cards behind a plan that fills the row budget` (50 pending steps, 30 queued cards: every continuation carries cards, 2-4 messages, each card once, answer on the last message, guard clean) and `keeps plan progress visible across budgeted continuations and settles it at completion` (50 steps progressing from step 1 to step 2 while the cards go out: the running step opens each continuation, its completion and the next step's start land on the message current at that time, and the closeout settles the running step). The existing rollover and plan tests pass unchanged.

Before:
```
× leaves continuation capacity for queued cards behind a plan that fills the row budget
  → expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(30) ]
× keeps plan progress visible across budgeted continuations and settles it at completion
  → expected 'complete' to be 'in_progress'
```

After: both pass.

### Results (this revision)

- Before (head `7498b866`), the two new cases: `2 failed | 217 skipped (219)`.
- After: dispatcher `219 passed (219)` with the budget guard on; `extensions/slack` whole suite `Test Files 158 passed, Tests 2986 passed`.
- Knip unused-export scans (production, script, full-tree): 0 entries. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --type-aware` (the stream chain stays under the 700-line cap; opening, retirement, thaw and completion planning live in `dispatch-progress-stream-rows.ts`), `tsgo` for `tsconfig.extensions.json` and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json`, `git diff --check` pass. Part 1 (`e3fa7957`) unchanged; branch base `25a6148d1`.

### Not tested (this revision)

- A plan larger than one message (more than 50 steps) on the first message: the first message still shows the whole plan and relies on Slack rendering the first 50 rows; only continuations budget plan rows.
- Plan rows added by a later plan update while a continuation is open appear on the next continuation or the closeout, not on the open message; no dedicated test.
