prs.title: fix(skills): retain source context in review cancellation diagnostics
prs.body:
## Current author acceptance — 2026-11-12 JST

Head `951ecd02e1c6a36936787ca62abace6062b49cce` normally merges official main `a87a4bf29d3638afa7565715962067bd7ca38359`. Official #197082 corrects the worker-permission/compact-JSON expectations and #197210 corrects the preparation-time Bun fence expectations while retaining final admission and settlement assertions. These are official test-owner repairs; no assertion, timeout, allocation or runtime guard was locally relaxed. The merge has no conflicts and no hand-edited source.

Fresh source-pinned OpenClaw Bun verification on Darwin arm64 passes **143/143** cases: 140 permission/feature/changed-owner sibling cases and three context-engine cases. Generated config, prepared-main ratchet (6,660,793 / 6,660,800; slack 7), targeted format, type-aware core lint, core typecheck and whitespace checks pass.

Fifteen of the eighteen contribution paths retain their preceding head's exact bytes. Main changes three production contexts: admitted principal snapshot/access ownership, bounded session-fork transcript reading, and context-engine replay exports. The preceding isolated Gateway proof remains evidence for its original bytes; it is not transferred as fresh Gateway acceptance for this merge. The first [native CI43058686770](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43058686770), attempt1, is terminal **SUCCESS**: all92 jobs are settled (65 succeeded,27 skipped,0 failed/pending), on checkout `7664542cab3339cb209365ce8f1076f737c031f9` with exact main parent `c324818cbf86074f34578d07f381b0d2835955a1` and this head. Both `subagent-completion-direct-fallback` and `subagent-empty-completion-recovery` explicitly pass in their own same-run QA logs. This accepts these scenarios on the new native checkout; it does not identify the QA root repair or establish equivalence with the old Darwin baseline. No CI rerun or employee/runtime-delivery acceptance is claimed.

Maintainer adoption, official distribution and employee deployment remain separate.

## Previous author acceptance — 2026-11-11 JST

The mixed-failure review is addressed: a fence is unwrapped only when the existing cancellation owner classifies the complete cause/aggregate graph as expected cancellation. An independent close/database failure remains a warning.

The positive fence, mixed aggregate, and cause-wrapped mixed cases are retained. All 23 focused plugin/scheduler cases pass. The two owned test fixtures now reuse fork settlement and diagnostic extraction, removing 29 further test lines without dropping assertions, diagnostic fields, the 400-character/four-item mask limits, real idle/compaction/provider/continuation checks, or timeout/budget controls. Targeted format/type-aware lint and a fresh independent review pass.

The same compiled isolated Gateway scenario passes with the new test bytes: 10 ordinary turns, background provider admission, public compaction, source-correlated DEBUG cancellation without a failure warning, and an 11th ordinary turn. Delivery is disabled and the owned Gateway has stopped. Production bytes are unchanged from the preceding repair head.

Changed-head native CI 42841905084 completed all 90 jobs on merge b80a7de86e372f3fb1f344180327aec5270ea425 (main parent 54261842119e5c1d069e53b901bd12bd10a21268). The unchanged ratchet now passes: 6,629,534 test lines / 6,629,543 ceiling, net delta +424 and slack 9. The full gate remains failed: two stale worker-permission expectations, two Bun fence assertions, and the direct/empty QA handoff scenarios. All 28 inspected owner/tooling blobs are identical in the actual main/merge and preceding bb91/4515 frame. On exact bb91, the pinned Bun reproduces both undefined-fence assertions; both selected QA scenarios also complete with the existing 60-second failure. Direct-fallback reaches terminal/ok with delivery pending; empty-recovery does not retain enough detail to select one of its three wait predicates. These Darwin baseline observations are not Linux CI equivalence, passing CI, or proof that every PR interaction is harmless. The owned regression and real Gateway proof remain valid; broad native acceptance is still open. No CI rerun, limit change or unrelated main repair is hidden in this evidence.

Maintainer adoption of the bounded mismatch fields/source fingerprint and the existing SDK diagnostic contract remains separate. This contribution does not deploy a private runtime build or claim official distribution/employee acceptance.

## What Problem This Solves

A rejected Workshop experience review loses the source correlation and collapses every anchor mismatch into the same error. Operators cannot distinguish a rewritten completed turn from an unavailable anchor projection after the queued candidate is discarded.

Refs #156948, #164279. [Observed diagnostic limit and bounded scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/156948#issuecomment-6288213684).

## User Impact

Existing cancellation/failure logs identify the first failed anchor field (or `unavailable`) and a source fingerprint. No new raw identity, transcript value, conversation key, path or message content is recorded. Expected cancellations remain DEBUG; actual failures remain warnings.

The historical refusal cannot be reconstructed. This is diagnostic repair, not a claim that the historical refusal was incorrect or that the broader issues are resolved.

## Change

Reuse the existing comparison owner in SQLite and committed-actor readers. Every prior predicate, exact actor scope check, and physical database-path alias rule remains. The scheduler adds SHA256(JSON.stringify([agentId, sessionId, entryId])) to its existing log. `unavailable` means no usable anchor was returned; it does not assert deletion.

No schema, config, SQL query, retry, re-anchoring, acceptance policy or authority relaxation. Maintainer decision requested: accept the fixed field names and bounded source fingerprint in these existing diagnostics. No approval is assumed.

## Evidence

**Historical acceptance checkpoint:** `664ad5a34b5b479b03c8294b38d09bffde60f3c2` remains **not accepted** for the strict native cancellation diagnostic. Its first native CI budget/ratchet gate now passes; the remaining diagnostic failure is reported below. Older component/Gateway/CI proof keeps its original head.

- Baseline `39fb90fb35d5ae628a0316fe40cd9b7b9bbbe055`: real SQLite validation lacks mismatch reasons; five scheduler cancellation/failure cases lack source correlation. The committed-actor diagnostic also failed before its change.
- After resolving the real GitHub conflict against official main `3213e3e542c5658f4095d08942f2636e6a40153e`, all **35 focused cases pass**. Main's actor-fixture simplification is retained, together with the generation diagnostic assertion. Existing lifecycle, permissions and SQL-statement controls remain.
- **Historical head `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2`: running compiled Gateway proof passed**, using standard source-QA plugin staging and loopback synthetic inference. Ten ordinary `chat.send` / `agent.wait` turns reach the unmodified review threshold. Public `sessions.compact` changes the transcript before the real idle timer runs the queued review. Its actual cancellation log has the expected bounded reason and independently calculated fingerprint at **DEBUG**. An eleventh ordinary turn succeeds. The owned Gateway exits. No scheduler callback or logger is mocked in this proof; no internal cancellation hook is injected.
- The reproducible opt-in scenario is `extensions/qa-lab/src/workshop-anchor-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts`. Its body takes **48.284s**, Vitest **78.10s** including compilation, wrapper **82.31s**. It retains the real 30-second product idle interval; the existing unit/SQLite suites own the cheaper predicate matrix. This opt-in E2E timing is local; hosted CI supplies the broader integration proof.
- Targeted proof types, lint, format, whitespace and outgoing-content gate pass. Fresh independent P0-P2 review is recorded separately; it does not execute the project.
- Prior head `bc5d003f689caafa456049d1e640d9029505dd8c` completed hosted production/test types, lint stripes, selected tests, security checks and aggregate CI successfully. Final head `5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2` completed [hosted CI run 39413661817](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39413661817) with **SUCCESS**, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. Production/test types, selected tests, lint, boundary, QA and security checks passed. Readback shows no failed or pending checks.

Captured terminal result from the isolated Gateway scenario (allowlisted fields only):

```json
{
  "candidateHead": "5c99913874a641bc1091941508801aa0e98ec9c2",
  "seconds": 82.31,
  "gatewayStopped": true,
  "foregroundTurnsCompleted": 11,
  "rewriteCompacted": true,
  "mismatch": "unavailable",
  "sourceFingerprint": "f294355d59610236b23c6f8e24d3298dd94d8a2446e70ceae7c8c17a4c88ccda",
  "sourceCorrelationMatches": true,
  "cancellationObserved": true,
  "severity": "DEBUG",
  "failureWarningAbsent": true,
  "ordinaryTurnAfterCancellation": "ok",
  "realGateway": true,
  "model": "loopback-synthetic",
  "delivery": false
}
```

The initial proof harness used the wrong log-accessor name; it was corrected. A packaged-plugin preparation attempt separately stopped in update-repair before readiness, while same-checkout static tooling held artifact ownership. Neither setup failure is used as a product verdict. The successful proof uses the supported source-staging route and runs serially after static checks, without bypassing a lock. This demonstrates the running diagnostic path, not package installation, stable-upgrade compatibility, live-provider behavior or official-release equivalence.

The integrated first head exposed a private test-helper import in the new proof fixture. Both failing boundary checks are addressed by using the existing public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-env` re-export of the exact same functions. The 20-case extension-boundary suite, corresponding static boundary check, lint, focused independent review, and the running Gateway proof all pass after this correction. No helper/export or guard exception was added.

No production employee runtime, downstream private patch/package, customer data, configuration or external delivery was changed.

<!-- upstream-integration-2026-10-27:start -->
### Current official budget-fix integration — 2026-11-06 JST

Current head: `664ad5a34b5b479b03c8294b38d09bffde60f3c2`; prior head: `45275b5ba429737dda9ee0739db82b32f137ded1`. A normal merge of pinned official main `6cb1db786257582b364a8a28de16515294e10e71` incorporates the approved inherited-budget reconciliation #193183. There is no author-written scalar, checker, allocation, assertion or timeout change. The existing 424-line allocation is retained exactly. Native counter after this merge commit uses that exact main comparison base: **6497128 lines /6497170 ceiling, slack42**.

All11 owned feature inputs remain byte-identical, including the424-line grant. Config-doc and whitespace checks pass. [First native CI42065424687, attempt1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42065424687) is terminal:52 successful,2 failed and27 skipped jobs. The native baseline-ratchet job **passed**. The sole originating failure remains [checks-node-changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42065424687/job/127378950477), reporting the false-to-true assertion at `workshop-anchor-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts:250:6`; the dependent CI aggregate also fails. The reported position matches the prior failed assertion, but no retained structured cause/phase payload was found, so hosted root-cause equivalence to earlier local authority warnings remains unverified. The existing #156948 and draft/unmerged #182121 remain the applicable upstream context, not adopted repairs. Strict native acceptance is still open; no timeout/assertion relaxation, unchanged local variant replay or CI rerun is used to turn it green. No local Gateway diagnostic variants were replayed, and no fresh runtime/Gateway success or employee acceptance is claimed.

### Previous fixture correction and CI — 2026-11-05

Head `45275b5ba429737dda9ee0739db82b32f137ded1` contains a scoped fixture repair over `2595d2a71d2334577a070aa24be09d80c8679670`. Production diagnostics, authority checks, cancellation controls, the real 10-turn threshold and 30-second idle interval, strict assertions and timeouts are unchanged.

The mock provider now identifies the latest actual `Background skill review.` request using the existing input helpers and native optional timestamp grammar. It no longer assumes provider request 11 must be that review; daily maintenance shares this provider. Ten ordinary foreground turns replace the repeated foreground tool calls. The actual review response is held once after admission, then compaction and the strict diagnostic check run. The dedicated allocation decreases from **425 to 424 literal LF**, matching the final net test growth. No shared ceiling or other allocation changes.

Fresh targeted format, type-aware lint, canonical extension-test TypeScript and whitespace checks pass. The official compiled Gateway build passes. Fresh independent source review found and closed a P2 timestamp-prefix mismatch; no findings remain on the two final file blobs. This review is source-only, and prior component-suite results retain their original production-source scope.

The current local native Gateway proof **fails**: ten ordinary turns finish; the actual background review reaches the provider; compaction and held-response release occur. There are zero bounded cancellation records and two failure warnings with `admitted run authority is no longer active`. The fingerprint appearing in another log is insufficient. Ordinary continuation after cancellation is not reached. All strict assertions remain, and this is not a diagnostic PASS.

Current [CI 41960922463](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41960922463), **attempt 1**, is terminal: **50 succeeded, 3 failed, 27 skipped**. All PostgreSQL conformance shards and the build-artifact job succeeded. Originating failures remain:

- `checks-node-changed-2`: the fixture now fails the `expected false to be true` assertion at annotated position `workshop-anchor-diagnostics.e2e.test.ts:250:6`; the earlier foreground-status error is absent from this job. Hosted output retains no structured stage/cause payload or generic authority signature. Root-cause equivalence with the local native failure is therefore still **unverified**.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,478,914 LF / 6,478,828 allowed, excess **86**, native net **+424**. Exact native comparison base `d189a5541541e1641a544d6a60b411387f1698af` independently counts 6,478,490 / 6,478,404, the same excess 86. Both candidate total and allowance rise exactly 424; this is inherited budget debt, not a missing grant for this PR.
- The third failed job is the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, reflecting those two originating failures.

The local native line counter against pinned original base `55a554e78a83af031760ef247e26d5be9e24329d` is 6,462,756 / 6,462,696, excess 60, net +424. Its unmodified base is also 60 over; the final grant covers exactly the added lines. The failed counter is not waived.

The preceding [CI 41954004221](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41954004221), attempt 1, on 2595d2a is terminal: **50 succeeded, 3 failed, 27 skipped**. Its node fixture failed at foreground status `error` instead of `ok` (annotation line 152). Its native ratchet comparison base `e531410a397e5cdb3c839ce69ac10283a70bcb21` contains 6,477,519 LF / 6,477,468 allowed, excess 51. The hosted candidate is 6,477,944 / 6,477,893, also excess 51; both rise exactly 425. This exact source count supersedes a job-name-only triage suggestion that main's ratchet was clean. Raw CI logs were not retained. A global quarantine occurrence lacked this fixture's context and is not attributed to it.

Earlier integration `0ce7d97ba68f7406ade22d9b0d2a957bf99b5f44` and its independently built pinned-main control already reproduced the generic authority-failure path; that evidence remains scoped to those original sources and fixtures. Existing #156948 and draft/unmerged #182121 cover lost-cause/reason classification. The official consumer and admitted-run owner histories were rechecked; no applicable merged repair was found. The merged process-startup/shared-process-lineage and GitHub-worker authority repairs are different paths. No draft, overlapping authority patch, string-based cancellation exception, weaker assertion or increased timeout was introduced.

No CI rerun or new review request was issued. Native diagnostic acceptance remains open; resume when an applicable official cause-owner repair or a concrete maintainer request supplies new evidence. This update does not establish upstream adoption, package qualification or employee runtime acceptance. The historical Gateway PASS below belongs to its original head only.

<details>
<summary>Previous integration evidence; original head scope</summary>

### Current submission status — 2026-10-31 JST

Current head: `49938254dd47869c1d65bec737fa91e045ce7c1b`. Normally merged reviewed parent `a5b3f5f0c9d298c64b19051ea6dafa36ae02298c` with fixed official main `4d76d1d82f705391c461268a5d6b8190b889066b` to reconcile the scheduler and its tests with upstream #178145. Main's Stop propagation, interrupted-turn eligibility and cleanup-failure classification are retained exactly. The existing SHA-256 source calculation and bounded debug/warn suffix remain; no new disclosure, retry or acceptance behavior was added. This preserves the existing bounded anchor mismatch/source correlation diagnostic.

Fresh independent source review found no remaining actionable finding and verified that removing the retained diagnostic addition reproduces the selected main scheduler. Earlier Gateway evidence retains its original-head scope; this integration does not claim a fresh external E2E run. The official scalar and allocation tree match the selected main exactly; no allowance, assertion, timeout, checker or permission was weakened.

Fresh proof on Node 24.22.1: **53 focused cases passed**, with targeted format/lint and the allocation-aware counter: **Test lines OK: 6323044; ceiling: 6353167; slack: 30123.** The diff and secret gates pass. Current-head hosted CI **passed**: [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41172821235), read back at `2026-10-31T05:31:18.128407+00:00`. The complete latest check-run inventory has zero failed or pending lanes.

Product/contract adoption remains with the upstream owner. Older dated evidence blocks retain their original-head scope. No employee runtime, private patch or package distribution changed.
</details>

prs.title: improve(ci): measure complete planner CLI flows
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/154108.

## What Problem This Solves

The CI planner has partial internal timers but no repeatable baseline for the complete manifest and check-planning CLI flow.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(telegram): stop Plugin SDK deprecation warnings blamed on the bundled Telegram plugin
prs.body:
Closes #191786
Closes #191785
Related: #174937, #190243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway logs `[DEP_PLUGIN_SDK]` warnings blamed on "Plugin telegram", and the Plugins catalog marks Telegram as using APIs that retire on Dec 31, 2026, when the bundled Telegram plugin loads, or when a Telegram group message from another member steers an active run under collaborative steering.

## User Impact

User impact: Telegram operators no longer see the startup deprecation warning, the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warning on steering, or the retiring-API notice those two cause. A Telegram group message that steers another member's run under collaborative steering still logs `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`, and those still show as a catalog notice; that read is out of scope here (see "Not in this PR"). Discord, Slack, Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp sessions now list `nativeApprovals` in the agent Runtime capabilities, and Telegram keeps it. Approval authorization, routing and delivery are unchanged. For those 8 channels the Runtime line gains one token, so their system prompt changes once after upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Telegram was the last bundled caller of the sync `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability`. It now uses `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapabilityAsync`, as #174937 did for Discord; `isNativeDeliveryEnabled` wraps the same check.
- `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` read only `native` and `nativeRuntime`. The async factories expose `nativeAsync` and `nativeRuntimeAsync`, so moving Telegram alone would have dropped `nativeApprovals` for Telegram, as it already had for 8 channels. The check now reads all four.
- `prepareFollowupRunToolAuthorityFingerprint` re-read its prepared fingerprint through the deprecated plugin-facing `fingerprint()`. Steering runs in the channel plugin's frame, so the warning and the deprecated-API record landed on Telegram. Core now uses a module-private reader with the same checks; plugin callers of `fingerprint()` still warn.
- Not in this PR: core's sync placement `getMany` (10 call sites, several inside synchronous commit guards; its warning has no fixed removal date), and the collaborative steering read that still calls `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Both need their own core reader and proof.

pr-simplify: no production code removed. One test assertion on a statically defined factory output was removed. No new state, exports or test-only hooks. Production +30 -11 in 3 files; tests +117 -4; three test-line records totaling exactly the 113 net added test lines.

## Evidence

### Gateway run (2026-11-09)

A real Gateway from a built `dist` (`node --trace-deprecation dist/index.js gateway run`, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64; Vitest also on Node), a local fake Telegram Bot API that grammY talks to as its transport, and a scripted Responses provider that records the `Runtime:` line of every request. Base: main `3855c896edd`. Head: this PR merged onto that main (`git merge-tree --write-tree 3855c896edd d096fe01a3c` = `8f366fba0b5`, no conflicts, same patch-id as this PR's diff). `messages.queue.mode: "steer"`. `channels.discord` and `channels.slack` are `{ enabled: true }` with no tokens, so the Gateway loads both plugins (`5 plugins: discord, memory-core, qa-lab, slack, telegram`) and `channels.status` shows both accounts `configured: false, running: false`. Two runs per scenario per build.

Steering. A run is held open at the provider and a second Telegram message arrives while it is active. In every run the second message is injected into that run (session controller `injection-outcome: consumed`, no "steering rejected" record), the provider gets it in the same session, and Telegram receives both answers.

| scenario | build | DEP_PLUGIN_SDK warnings, all "Plugin telegram" | `plugins.list` notices (of 268 plugins) |
|---|---|---|---|
| group, a second member steers, `allowCollaborativeSteering: true` | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup); at the steer `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 4 APIs |
| same | this PR | at the steer `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`, `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` | telegram, those 2 APIs |
| DM, the sender steers their own run | main | `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability` (startup) | telegram, that 1 API |
| same | this PR | none | none |

Stacks from `--trace-deprecation` on main:
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint`: `fingerprint <- read <- prepareLegacyReplySteeringAuthority <- prepareReplyMessageJoin <- runActiveReplySteer`. Gone here.
- `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`: `<- read <- prepareCurrent <- prepareCurrent <- beginPreparedReplyMessageInjectionTarget`. Same stack here.
- `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project`: called from inside that `projectToolAuthorityFingerprint`. Same here.
- Startup: `createApproverRestrictedNativeApprovalCapability <- channel-*.mjs` module load. Gone here.

Two things this shows that the description had wrong or left out:
- On main, a message from the run's own sender does not reach `fingerprint()` at all. A plain message is a `continue-existing` steer, which goes through `prepareReplyMessageContinuation` (since #177698) and never calls the deprecated reader. The fingerprint warning needs the legacy steering path, which a second member's message reaches under collaborative steering.
- On that collaborative path this PR leaves two warnings in place, `replyOperation.projectToolAuthorityFingerprint` and `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.project` (the second comes from inside the first), and both still put a retiring-API notice on Telegram in the catalog. The first is the collaborative read already listed under "Not in this PR".

Runtime capabilities. The provider's view of `channel=<id> | channel_capabilities=...`, the same in every run of a build. Discord and Slack turns come from the Gateway `agent` RPC with `channel` set and `deliver: false`, on fresh sessions:

| channel | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| telegram (DM and group turns) | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` | `inlinebuttons,nativeapprovals` |
| discord | `threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` | `nativeapprovals,threadbound-acp-spawn,threadbound-subagent-spawn` |
| slack | `none` | `nativeapprovals` |

Telegram keeps `nativeApprovals` after moving to the async factory, and Discord and Slack gain it.


- At this head the three changed test files pass 37 of 37 (26 + 7 + 4). With the three source files from `19aff5bfd42`, they fail 1 of 26, 5 of 7 and 1 of 4.
- Red on base, green here, each with only that commit's source file reverted:
  - `extensions/telegram/src/approval-native.test.ts`: 5 failed / 2 passed vs 7 passed; the new test receives the deprecation message.
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.test.ts` (follow-up read): fails with the `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` usage record vs passes.
  - `src/channels/plugins/approvals.test.ts`: `expected false to be true` vs 4 passed. Dropping either async field alone fails its own assertion.
- `--trace-deprecation` over the message-join and fallback-steering suites (101 tests): `ReplyToolAuthoritySnapshot.fingerprint` warnings 3 -> 0.
- All 9 bundled approval capabilities: `channelPluginHasNativeApprovalPromptUi` true for 1 of 9 on base, 9 of 9 here.
- Prompt consumers 16 files / 174 tests, Telegram and Discord approval suites 9 files / 218 tests, core steering and authority suites 19 files / 371 tests: all pass. `pnpm run tsgo:all`, oxlint, oxfmt, line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass against `19aff5bfd42`. If CI's test-lines job is red, that is main's own overage (main has been over its ceiling since `2a32ab046f2`, #191638); this branch adds 113 test lines and 113 lines of allocation.
- Test cost (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Bun, the local default, macOS arm64, two runs each): `approval-native.test.ts` 26.1 s (cold worker cache, 20.2 s of it compiling) and 6.6 s wall, 413 ms and 376 ms of tests; `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 8.8 s and 7.8 s wall, 1.3 s and 1.2 s of tests; `approvals.test.ts` 10.0 s and 6.2 s wall, 11 ms and 9 ms of tests. CI run 41606285186, Bun: `approval-native.test.ts` 744 ms of tests in a shared run (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1`); `reply-tool-authority.test.ts` 9.0 s Vitest duration, 1.6 s of tests (`checks-node-changed-7`); `approvals.test.ts` 50.1 s Vitest duration, 17 ms of tests (`checks-node-changed-channels`).
- Not covered end to end: real Telegram, Discord or Slack. The Discord and Slack sessions above came from the Gateway `agent` RPC with their plugins loaded and no accounts running, not from those services. Matrix, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, iMessage, Signal and WhatsApp were not run.

prs.title: improve(ci): keep stale packages out of hosted dependency caches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hosted Linux CI jobs download old packages carried forward through pnpm cache prefix restores. One sampled job downloaded a 2.25 GB cache in 52.9 seconds, then installed its current dependencies in 8.6 seconds. New cache generations inherit that baggage.

## User Impact

Future hosted Linux cache generations contain a fresh installation of the required dependencies. Existing immutable exact entries stay in use until the next missing dependency-store key. There is no immediate production savings claim. Blacksmith, macOS, pull-request cache authority, cache keys, reader fallback, and independent code warming retain their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before saving a new hosted Linux generation, the existing protected publisher preserves authenticated pnpm bootstrap archives, clears its private store and importer modules, then runs the unchanged frozen installer. Both existing dependency saves follow successful rebuilding. It adds no jobs, runners, concurrency, or cache writers.

The publisher pays an extra cleanup and cold install once per new generation. In the hosted probe, that cold install took 14.97 seconds; production cleanup and transfer must still be observed. This trades one producer rebuild for smaller repeated reader restores. A prune attempt was rejected because it removed required offline package snapshots; fresh installation preserves them.

## Evidence

Five sequential baseline/fresh-store pairs on one hosted Linux job, after one excluded warmup pair. Every install preserved the complete package-directory/lock inventory and authenticated bootstrap hashes. Timed consumers were strictly offline; online repair was blocked before execution.

| metric | inherited store | fresh store |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| compressed archive |2,244,425,757 B |957,104,890 B |
| extraction+offline install, median |31.535s |12.211s |
| extraction+offline install, sample p95 |31.917s |12.798s |
| CPU, median |23.41s |13.80s |
| CPU, sample p95 |23.626s |13.836s |
| max-child RSS, median |200208 KiB |195704 KiB |
| max-child RSS, sample p95 |200516.8 KiB |197647.2 KiB |

Archive bytes fell 57.36%; median local extraction/install fell 61.28%. This measures local archive extraction and installation, excluding module/store cleanup between samples. It does not measure WAN transfer, PR completion time, aggregate VM memory, or billed savings. Five samples provide limited tail evidence.

- Passing run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43347110114/job/131629016507 at 7341d6891a168f657dfd8744f41c6d1f58cbd7cc. Committed probe source remains available at that revision; temporary probe code is removed from the final diff.
- Before-run rule:≥20% payload reduction; first measured pair≥5% wall gain; stop on≥20% adverse wall/CPU/RSS; require five measured pairs,≥5% median wall gain, no worse sample p95 wall/CPU/RSS, and unchanged offline inventory/bootstrap bytes. All passed.
- Rejected prune run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43346380443/job/131626640210. No shared cache was published by either probe.
- Production source 8733d477e9a693a24931a4e90062bbbd080e5a1f (final head 1a454ee50469408a80fe79c4f7b9f818ccc1c407 only adds lint-required test braces): fresh independent full-source review and complete-delta local autoreview at P0–P2 found no actionable findings. The latter included the full installer, but not every unchanged workflow/action context; independent source review covered those contracts. Neither executed tests.
- Production shell fixture passed cleanup, bootstrap preservation and frozen-installer admission. Formatting, docs inventory and diff-whitespace checks passed. One regression covers runner/hit eligibility and the actual cleanup shell.
- Final-head focused regression and all six built-source scenarios passed (7 tests) through the normal repository wrapper; targeted lint passed. Tooling typecheck and workflow validation passed on unchanged inputs. The new regression fails against the old workflow for the intended missing step.
- Native full guard suite on the prior production head: 209 passed, 8 skipped, 2 failed. Both untouched built-source fixtures expect empty NODE_OPTIONS while the native PR wrapper reinjects its dependency lifetime preload. All six scenarios pass through the normal test wrapper, including on final head. This diagnoses the environment interaction; it does not fix or erase the original failures.
- Exact-head [PR CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43351190582). Squash merged as [2c821b44743e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c821b44743e31119bb2029126ea8646cc1a986b). The merge-push cache warmer was skipped, so the actual publisher's next normal generation and resulting reader transfer remain post-land observation gaps. No full-suite local green is claimed.

prs.title: fix(logging): keep log tailing from stalling Gateway chats
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat stalls when a client tails a busy Gateway's JSON logs. Scalar redaction and historical private-key context scanning ran on the same event loop as every chat.

## User Impact

The Logs tab and `openclaw logs --follow` now read and redact through a bounded background reader. Returned bytes, ordered custom patterns, newly registered secrets, PEM context, line limits, rotation, and byte cursors keep their existing behavior. No configuration or storage migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing file-log worker entrypoint with a separate serial reader pool, so tail CPU cannot queue file writes. Keep one read/redaction implementation; pass the resolved file target, current pattern policy and exact registered-secret membership to the worker. The queue admits at most eight pending reads. File writes remain raw, and redaction remains an egress responsibility.

The reader already selects its capped return window and skips completed bytes at a valid cursor. A cold read may scan older bytes for cross-window private-key context; that scan now also stays off the Gateway thread. No result cache or weaker pattern policy was added. The worker is demand-started and retires under the existing pool lifecycle, trading one additional isolate and initial startup latency for responsive chats.

## Evidence

Acceptance fixed before the candidate run: UI-shaped 500-line / 250,000-byte cursor polls every two seconds over a synthetic >=300 MB day log; five interleaved A/A controls and five A/B pairs; byte-identical responses; warm main segments below 20 ms and at least 80% lower; main CPU/allocation lower; report total CPU, latency and cold startup separately.

On Node 26.12.1/macOS, the serial run uses a 320,636,800-byte file, 9,109-byte scalar-rich JSON lines, synthetic URL tokens and an exact registered secret. Every poll in all four isolated readers produced the same SHA-256 of the complete response. Values below are median / p95 (five warm samples per arm, p95 is the maximum):

| Per-poll metric | Direct reader | Worker reader |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main callback segment, ms | 73.246 / 99.474 | 0.198 / 0.303 |
| Main CPU, ms | 75.320 / 95.767 | 0.571 / 0.723 |
| Whole-process CPU, ms | 88.718 / 143.328 | 88.568 / 117.854 |
| Wall time, ms | 76.133 / 101.784 | 63.951 / 75.146 |
| Exact main allocation, bytes | 100,734,784 / 103,332,016 | 416,424 / 466,280 |

A/A medians: wall 68.595 vs 70.083 ms, main CPU 68.272 vs 69.572 ms, process CPU 79.708 vs 82.504 ms, allocation 100,116,136 vs 101,193,512 bytes. Host load varied; these are synthetic owner measurements, not a production deployment claim. An earlier run overlapping compilation is retained: wall p95 73.398 → 89.563 ms (+22%), while main segment p95 fell 72.332 → 0.266 ms. The serial rerun specifically resolves this concurrent-compilation uncertainty; no failure or slow sample was discarded from either run.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/logs-tail-main-thread-measure.ts <new fixture directory>`. The script cleans up its processes and fixture. The existing direct reader remains the baseline because CLI-local/filtered callers use the same unchanged owner without blocking a Gateway.

Cold first read (single sample, includes historical PEM scan and worker start): wall 298.7 → 865.0 ms; main segment 98.8 → 2.53 ms; main CPU 268.9 → 4.25 ms. Warm process RSS medians are 141.8 → 208.2 MB. This is deliberate CPU isolation, not eliminated redaction work: one reader isolate costs ~66 MB here and ~0.57 s on the first request; subsequent median total CPU is effectively unchanged. Only main-isolate allocation is measured, not total worker allocation.

CPU profiling confirms `readScalarTokens` in `src/logging/redact-json-tokens.ts`: 11.325 ms sampled self time across the direct-reader run, zero on the candidate main thread. Main-thread pattern scanning and PEM scanning likewise disappear. Add `--cpu-prof --cpu-prof-dir=<existing directory>` to the benchmark's Node invocation to retain per-process profiles.

Packaged real-Gateway proof: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/logs-tail-gateway-proof.ts <new fixture directory>` after `pnpm build:runtime`. prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.

prs.title: feat(cron): size automation run slots from the agent limit
prs.body:
Related: #196859

Depends on #197340 for condition-check admission.

## What Problem This Solves

Due automations wait behind a fixed eight-run cap even when the host has unused agent capacity.

## User Impact

- Automation admission uses `agents.defaults.maxConcurrent` minus active conversation turns, with a floor of eight.
- Conversations start without waiting for automation. Running automations are not interrupted, so combined activity can temporarily exceed the agent limit.
- Waiting jobs are reconsidered when a run ends and within a minute while demand remains.
- No new setting is added. The default agent limit is `max(8, available CPU parallelism * 4)`.
- Condition checks remain three wide; hook dispatch remains eight wide.
- A requester who loses owner status during a slot wait starts the payload as a non-owner, without owner-private memory or owner-only tools.

Larger automation bursts can reach provider limits sooner. This PR does not add provider backoff.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing run queue decides how many automations may start from the conversation lane’s configured width and active count. Automation lanes are wide enough to serve those admissions. Keeping the budget at queue admission lets conversations start immediately.

The requester’s owner status is rechecked when the payload starts. Owner-only tools also recheck requester authority at each call. Memory audience is resolved at run start.

Accepted tradeoffs:

- Only conversation-lane turns reduce automation’s share; subagents, restart-recovery turns, and hooks do not.
- The eight-run floor can exceed a configured agent limit below eight.
- Lowering the agent limit during active automation can delay hooks until the shared budget drains.
- The automation lane also carries internal session events, plugin-hook turns, and channel join intros.
- Waiting demand causes a periodic queue recheck, including when another admission condition prevents a run.

For automations whose parent has no workspace binding, parent replacement can still permit owner-authorized work on main. The [main prompt executor installs its parent-source guard only for workspace-bound children](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/220ca12e0732ab599c5a9b6434ac699f6750728f/src/cron/isolated-agent/run-prompt-executor.ts#L212). The slot wait lengthens that interval; it does not introduce this behavior. Maintainers may choose to harden it separately. This observation is not a blocker for this PR.

## Evidence

At `1997e68`, an isolated macOS Gateway with an agent limit of 12 produced 12 overlapping model requests from 12 scheduled agent-turn jobs. All 12 finished `ok`.

A focused integration test verified allowed continuation after a durable fired-condition slot wait and cancellation following human-owner reassignment. Its parent-replacement case dispatched `node.pair.list` and `node.pair.approve`; the strict no-I/O assertion failed, but source comparison identifies that result as existing main behavior. The final pairing state was not captured.

The VM used a synthetic model server; the focused test exercised real queue, occurrence, parent-storage, tool, and pairing-handler paths.

The [recorded PR context and evidence check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43286855181/job/131422419242) passed.

## Validation Limits

Requester revocation remains inconclusive because of a fixture error. Stored-data upgrade, real providers, config reloads, hook reservations, and the full suite were not checked. The reported `ops-lifecycle.start-arm.test.ts` timeout remains unresolved by this validation.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): keep scribes current after updates, with fresh runs and clear update prompts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after an OpenClaw update, Knowledge scribes keep running the run message they were set up with and an ever-growing conversation. They miss new scribe behavior and follow stale copies of skill text; one consolidation conversation reached about 590k tokens, and a weekly run read about 13M. On main, scribes already switched to `sessionTarget: current` are not paired with their conversations on the Scribes page. Learn from Granola could also stop with meetings left `pending` for no external reason and still report `on`.

## User Impact

Opening the Scribes tab brings existing ongoing scribes up to date. Each run now starts in a fresh session of the scribe's conversation, and an earlier generated run message that is unchanged is replaced with the new one. A saved run message that differs from what this version generates is never overwritten. When it still carries replaced wording, the scribe shows **New run instructions**, and **Replace with new…** shows only the lines that change. After an update, Replace or Repair turn, the scribe shows **Updating…** and refreshes when its automation changes, with a visible note if nothing changes within 3 minutes. The last-run summary shows only real scheduled or Run now results, never setup, repair or update answers. A Granola run that leaves meetings pending without an outside reason now reports **Needs attention** instead of On.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Versioned run message.** `scribes-catalog.ts` keeps every wording a released run message was generated from in `RUN_WORDINGS`. `checkRunMessage` classifies the stored message as:
  - `current`
  - `custom`
  - `outdated`: an unchanged earlier message, upgraded automatically
  - `differs`: carries replaced wording, so new instructions are offered

  Adding the Granola needs-attention rule added a wording entry, so unchanged Granola messages upgrade too.
- **Fresh run per session: `current` session target.** Each run is a new `cron:<job>:run:<id>` session. The automation still belongs to the scribe conversation, so the Scribes page pairs them, and Run now, Pause, Turn off and Repair act on the same job. Run transcripts no longer land in the conversation, so the page reads a run's status line from `cron.runs` / `cron.history` and links runs to Automations. Resetting the conversation before each run was rejected: it changes the conversation's lifecycle revision, which unlinks the automation and denies private Knowledge access.
- **The Scribes page owns the upgrade, through a turn in the scribe's conversation.** A direct `cron.update` would drop the job's operator source on an executable edit and lose owner-private access. Instead the conversation re-declares its automation with the owner's turn authority, as setup does. The page asks once per automation revision, then watches `cron.inventory.changed`, with a 10s poll and a 3-minute bound, until the revision changes *and* the change landed. A target-only intermediate write doesn't count as done or trigger a second turn. Pending updates are tracked per Gateway connection and per agent. The watch stops when the tab is left or the page is closed.
- **Re-declaration keeps what it doesn't set, and stays in this agent.** Re-declaring through `applyDeclarativeJobSpec` replaces the payload and drops omitted `activeHours`, `pacing` and `idleOnly`. Update and repair prompts therefore pass the automation's saved options back exactly as written: payload model, thinking and other run options, an explicit `toolsAllow` passed with `toolsAllowMode: "exact"` so it is not broadened (a generated default list is left to its owner), `activeHours`, `pacing`, `idleOnly`, `trigger`, `delivery` and `failureAlert`. An existing automation keeps its delivery and failure alert instead of getting new-job defaults. The cleanup step lists automations for the Runtime agent only, and leaves another or missing owner agent untouched. This applies the #196224 scoping (same wording as #196238), which matters more now that opening the tab can send the turn. A send that fails is retried on the next load. A turn that left the automation unchanged shows **Try again** after 3 minutes. Try again sends the turn as a new request (fresh idempotency identity), so the Gateway can't answer it from the first request's record. A transport retry after a failed send keeps the same identity, for automatic updates and for confirming **Replace with new** again in the same dialog. An update that is still landing is never asked twice.
- **Last-run result vs. state.** The state still follows the newest answer, so a failed repair shows Failing. The shown result comes only from a run: the latest run's own transcript, or for legacy in-session jobs a status line answering a `Scheduled run of the Knowledge scribe` turn.
- **Granola pending rules** (`knowledge-meeting-ingest/references/scribe-runs.md` and the Granola run message):
  - `pending` is only for reasons outside the run: still recording, no transcript yet, or verification that still fails after a fix attempt.
  - Acquiring or digesting a meeting is not a stopping point.
  - Checkpoint lines record outcomes, never resume notes or plans.
  - A run with only unexplained pending meetings ends `Scribe status: needs attention`, which the page parses as a new state.

  No "stop when context runs short" rule is reintroduced (#197890).

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway (separate state and port, real model), driven through the Control UI. **Before** is the previous PR build; **after** is this head with the same state.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Scribes list: last-run summary | ![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/599767bf-d535-45f5-917b-945d31fa15e7) | ![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f37ab3d5-0235-4c26-b5d5-effba0182331) |

Before, Learn from conversations showed an update turn's answer ("each run's message now has the updated access check…") as its last result. After, it shows the scheduled run's counts and **New run instructions**. Consolidation's earlier claims-only message was upgraded to the five-step one when the tab loaded.

Saved message that differs (earlier access wording plus one added line):

![detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b1da31b-5ed6-4998-a336-a2bf97d0fd8a)

**Replace with new…** shows only the changed lines:

![dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05ff9ead-0b7c-4ca2-8b55-98eac75688fe)

After confirming, the page shows **Updating…**:

![updating](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/509e5481-1da2-4a46-b3c1-ed9592a722ad)

The conversation re-declared the automation. The page refreshed on the cron change and cleared without a manual reload. The job now has the new message and `sessionTarget: current`.

![settled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24b5e192-20dd-41f3-a845-f29b31382ee2)

(Model values redacted.)

Checks:
- `scribes-state.test.ts`, `scribes-view.test.ts` and `skill-packaging.test.ts` pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- oxlint on the touched files, oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.
- `sync-skill-references.mjs --check` passes.
- The test-lines ratchet passes (+220 net within the allowance, so the allocation file is removed).

Upgrade compatibility on existing data: the isolated Gateway's state came from the previous PR build, and the jobs began as earlier releases created them (legacy `session:<key>` target, earlier generated messages, and one changed message). On this build they loaded and paired, then migrated or offered **New run instructions** as shown above, keeping schedule, enabled state, operator source and silent delivery. Scheduled runs succeeded both before and after.

ClawSweeper's review of `615bd0e` found three issues, all fixed with regression tests:
- P1: cleanup was not scoped to the agent.
- P1: re-declaration dropped saved options.
- P2: a failed send was never retried.

The re-review of `6e8156c` added two more issues, both fixed with tests:
- P1: trigger and delivery were not carried over.
- P2: an unchanged update was not retried after reopening.

The re-review of `16825c7` found that reopening reused the same request identity. Retry is now an explicit **Try again** with a new identity, and the test asserts the second key differs.

The re-review of `3c29bd4` found two more issues, both fixed with tests:
- P1: an explicit `toolsAllow` cap could be broadened.
- P2: a re-confirmed Replace used a new identity. This test fails without the fix.

The re-review of `c743638` found that a failed Try again send was shown as Updating. It now stays late, with the error, and can be tried again. The test fails without the fix.

The failed-send test fails without the fix. The CI assertion-safety ratchet failure was caused by this PR and is fixed (typed `choicesOf` with a SAFETY note). The `eager-import-closure` tooling-shard failure is inherited: `#197697` broke the PR-wrapper inventory on main, `#197976` fixed it, and it passes locally on current main (`6c32a157`).

Independent review found three P2 issues in the update watcher, all fixed:
- It kept running after the page closed.
- Viewing another agent dropped this agent's pending updates.
- A target-only intermediate write could trigger a second update turn.

Accepted edge cases:
- Scribes from the earliest setup (Oct 27, JSON setup) have model-authored run messages that can't be recognized; they read as custom.
- If the model doesn't follow an update turn, the job stays unchanged. The page then says so after 3 minutes, and asks again once the page is reopened.

prs.title: fix(agents): continuation-skip turns tell the model its workspace instructions were removed
prs.body:
Related: #196122

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with `contextInjection: "continuation-skip"`, every continuation turn on routes that pin the system prompt (direct Anthropic, official OpenAI Responses) tells the model that AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md and every heading inside them were "(removed)".

## User Impact

On those routes, skipped turns keep the workspace instructions the model already has, without a system update revoking them. Skipped turns still send no workspace files, and an explicit `contextInjection: "never"` still announces the removal. Sessions that already received a false removal from an earlier skipped turn get their files redelivered once on the next skipped turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

A skipped continuation withholds files that the pinned prompt prefix still carries, but the prompt series diffed the file-less prompt against that prefix and reported each Project Context section as removed. The bootstrap stage now reports that it withheld already-delivered context, and the pinned series reuses its own Project Context block for that comparison, placed inside the framed stable region (before `<!-- /openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->`, or the cache boundary when unframed). If the saved comparison state already lost the block, the block comes from the admitted prefix, which still has it.

Scope: this does not change what unpinned routes (OpenRouter, most OpenAI-compatible providers) receive on skipped turns. Whether those routes should keep workspace files under `continuation-skip` is the separate product question in #196122; this PR leaves the #154923 behavior as is.

## Evidence

- Regression in `session-prompt-state.test.ts` built from real `buildAttemptSystemPrompt` output (with STABLE/DYNAMIC framing): on a pinned series, a withheld turn emits no update; redelivering unchanged files emits nothing; a removal without the withheld flag reports `(removed)` for the file and its inner headings; a comparison state that already lost the files redelivers them (`Be brief.`) once.
- Mutation checks: ignoring the STABLE terminator makes the "no update" assertion fail; dropping the admitted-prefix fallback makes the redelivery assertion fail.
- `session-prompt-state.test.ts`: 36 passed. `tsc` for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`: no errors in changed files or for `workspaceContextWithheld`. `check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with the allocation. `oxfmt --check` / `oxlint` clean.
- Evidence gap: I have not captured a live provider request on a pinned route. Pinned routes require a direct Anthropic or official OpenAI endpoint with a real key, so the existing loopback Gateway fixture (`gateway.continuation-skip-bootstrap.integration.test.ts`) resolves as unpinned and cannot show this path. `attempt-bootstrap-prepare.test.ts` hits `EMFILE` on Windows for 14 cases, identically on unmodified `main`.

prs.title: fix(release): report malformed --manifest JSON with a one-line diagnosis
prs.body:
Related: #139736 (introducing commit fd22d08e2dd, which moved this CLI into `scripts/`)

## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.mjs` reports a bare JSON parse error with no context when the `--manifest` file contains malformed JSON (script landed at `scripts/` with the tooling move bundled into #139736, commit fd22d08e2dd):

```
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
```

Every other bad input in this script already reports a named one-line diagnostic — `--manifest is required` from `readArgs`, `Usage: plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence --manifest <path> ...` for argument-shape errors, and `Plugin SDK API ...` messages from the validators — so a manifest body that fails JSON parsing is the one remaining input shape that skips the diagnostic path.

Fixes: malformed `--manifest` files now exit 1 with `--manifest is not valid JSON (<reason>)` on stderr, naming the offending flag and keeping the parse reason. Filesystem failures (missing file, unreadable file, directory path) stay outside the new diagnosis: the manifest is read before the parse try block, so `ENOENT`/`EISDIR` errors keep the raw filesystem message they have always had instead of being mislabeled as invalid JSON.

## Why This Change Was Made

`main()` parsed the manifest with a bare `JSON.parse`, so a malformed body surfaced as a raw `SyntaxError` message before `validatePluginSdkApiReleaseEvidence` could classify it. The CLI's top-level handler already prints one-line messages and exits 1; this change only routes the manifest parse failure through the same wording style the script's own `readArgs` uses (`${flag} is required` → `--manifest is not valid JSON (...)`). Follow-up to review: the first version wrapped `readFileSync` and `JSON.parse` in one catch, which mislabeled `ENOENT`/`EISDIR` as invalid JSON; reading the manifest text before the try block restores the original meaning of filesystem errors.

## User Impact

Anyone running the release-evidence CLI (release workflows and contributors following `docs/reference/RELEASING.md`) with a truncated or garbage manifest now gets a diagnosis naming `--manifest` as the offending input instead of a context-free parse error; a wrong or missing path still shows the plain filesystem error. No schema, defaults, argument handling, or exit-code behavior changes.

## Evidence

Real environment tested: Linux x86-64, Node v26.12.1, this checkout; the script itself with local manifest files; no mocks, no production credentials, no network.

Exact steps or commands run after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.test.ts
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base
node scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.mjs --manifest <malformed file> --head <sha> --workflow-sha <sha>
node scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.mjs --manifest <missing file> --head <sha> --workflow-sha <sha>
node scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.mjs --manifest <directory> --head <sha> --workflow-sha <sha>
```

Evidence after fix: at head 860cc734ae, vitest 12/12 passed with exit 0 (test/scripts/plugin-sdk-api-release-evidence.test.ts), including the `reports a malformed release-evidence manifest with a named diagnostic` case (RED on base b48d16bf6e9, GREEN since 9f457fef84e) and the new `keeps filesystem failures out of the malformed-JSON diagnostic` case (RED on 9f457fef84e, which mislabeled ENOENT as `--manifest is not valid JSON (ENOENT: ...)`, GREEN on 860cc734ae); test-lines ratchet OK (allowance 400). Shipped CLI runs at head 860cc734ae, all exit 1:

```json
{"malformed": "--manifest is not valid JSON (Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2))", "missingFile": "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/tmp/definitely-missing-manifest.json'", "directory": "EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read", "exitCode": 1}
```

Observed result after fix: with a manifest file containing `{`, the CLI exits 1 with the one-line `--manifest is not valid JSON (...)` diagnosis; with a missing file or a directory path it exits 1 with the raw `ENOENT`/`EISDIR` message and no invalid-JSON wording. Same malformed-JSON command on base b48d16bf6e9 exits 1 with the bare parse error and no indication of which input is at fault. Control: a well-formed empty manifest `{}` still reaches the existing validator and reports `Plugin SDK API release evidence is missing or invalid` (exit 1), so the new branch only claims the malformed-JSON shape.

What was not tested: the GitHub workflow invocation path end-to-end (unchanged by this patch). The default `tsrs` type-checker binary aborts on this EL8 host (glibc 2.28 < required 2.32), so `tsgo:core` is left to CI lanes. `oxfmt --write` ran clean locally; `oxlint` aborts on this host with a Rust allocator panic (fixed_size.rs) under current memory pressure — an environment limitation, left to the CI `check-lint` lane, which was green at 9f457fef84e and the diff since then adds only a test case mirroring the adjacent one.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the fixture write into the helper's existing `try/finally`. All eight test declarations and 13 expanded cases remain unchanged; production and support code are unchanged. This is a small follow-up in the authorized repository-wide test audit.

- The original helper leaves a real temporary directory after an injected `ENOSPC` write failure. The repaired helper removes it; both preserve the exact error and never call the config reader.
- Native CLI suite: all 13 cases pass on the base and repair. The isolated filesystem fault check executes the actual helper with an injected write failure; no new production hook or permanent test is added.

prs.title: feat(providers): add XingChen-AGI provider plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds the **XingChen-AGI** provider plugin for OpenClaw, exposing the **Xing4.1-Preview** model (China Telecom AI Technology Co., Ltd.) through its OpenAI-compatible API.

- Provider id: `xingchen-agi`
- Package: `@openclaw/xingchen-agi-provider`
- Auth env var: `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`
- API: `openai-completions`
- Base URL: `https://api-maas.teleai.com.cn/v1`
- Default model: `xing4.1-preview`

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw user who wants to use Xing4.1-Preview currently has to hand-configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and model metadata. This PR adds a ready-made provider plugin plus documentation, so the model becomes selectable as `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` once the plugin is installed and `XINGCHEN_API_KEY` is provided.

## What's included

- `extensions/xingchen-agi/` - provider plugin (`index.ts`, `openclaw.plugin.json`, `package.json`)
- `docs/providers/xingchen-agi.md` - provider docs page
- `docs/providers/index.md` - registered in the provider directory

## Manifest

Uses the current provider schema (`setup.providers[].envVars`, declarative `modelCatalog` with `discovery: static`) and the `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-entry` SDK entry point.

## Model

| Model ref | Input | Context | Max output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview` | text | 192,000 | 192,000 |

- Reasoning: supported (deep-thinking mode; no `reasoning_effort` tiers exposed)
- Pricing (USD / 1M tokens, off-peak): input $0.11 / cached input $0.0022 / output $0.45 (peak = 2x)

## Verification

- Endpoint reachable over HTTPS from outside mainland China (tested: TCP 443 / TLS / HTTP 200, median latency ~120 ms)
- Auth is standard `Authorization: Bearer` (unauthenticated request returns a business 401, not a signature error)

## Evidence

Validation was run end-to-end on OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`), Windows, Node `v24.18.0`, with the plugin from this PR installed. All output is redacted (the API key is masked as `sk-****`). Two layers are covered: local one-shot inference through the plugin, and a full Gateway agent turn using a saved credential profile with the standard plugin set loaded.

### Real behavior proof

Verified end-to-end against OpenClaw `2026.11.3` (`847611d`) on Windows, Node `v24.18.0`. The plugin from this PR was installed in link mode, the model catalog resolved, credentials resolved from `XINGCHEN_API_KEY`, and real one-shot model turns returned responses.

**1. Plugin installed and enabled**

```
$ openclaw plugins install --link ./extensions/xingchen-agi --accept-capabilities
Saved for the next Gateway start

$ openclaw plugins list
@openclaw/xingchen-agi-provider | xingchen-agi | openclaw | enabled | ...\extensions\xingchen-agi\index.ts | 2026.11.3
```

**2. Model present in the catalog**

```
$ openclaw models list --provider xingchen-agi --all --plain
xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview
```

**3. Credentials resolve for the provider**

```
$ openclaw models status --json
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "effective": { "kind": "env", "detail": "sk-****" },
  "env": { "value": "sk-****", "source": "env: XINGCHEN_API_KEY" }
```

**4. Real inference through the plugin**

```
$ openclaw infer model run --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --local --json \
    --prompt "Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: XINGCHEN-OK-2026"
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "model.run",
  "transport": "local",
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "model": "xing4.1-preview",
  "outputs": [ { "text": "XINGCHEN-OK-2026", "mediaUrl": null } ]
}
```

```
$ openclaw infer model run --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --local --json \
    --prompt "A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 8 run away. How many sheep are left? Answer with just the number."
{
  "ok": true,
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "model": "xing4.1-preview",
  "outputs": [ { "text": "8", "mediaUrl": null } ]
}
```

### Gateway agent turn (saved credentials, standard plugin set)

Beyond the local runs above, a full **Gateway** agent turn was exercised with the API key **saved as an auth profile** (not an environment variable) and the standard plugin set loaded.

**1. Credential saved as a profile**

```
$ openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider xingchen-agi
Auth profile: xingchen-agi:manual (xingchen-agi/api_key)

$ openclaw models auth list
Agent: main
Profiles:
- xingchen-agi:manual [xingchen-agi/api_key]

$ openclaw models status --json
  "provider": "xingchen-agi",
  "effective": { "kind": "profiles", "detail": "~\\.openclaw\\state\\openclaw.sqlite" },
  "profiles": { "count": 1, "apiKey": 1, "labels": [ "xingchen-agi:manual=sk-****" ] }
```

(No `XINGCHEN_API_KEY` environment variable was set during this run.)

**2. Gateway running**

```
$ openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured
[gateway] ready

$ openclaw gateway health
Gateway Health
OK (8ms)
```

**3. Agent turn through the Gateway**

```
$ openclaw agent --model xingchen-agi/xing4.1-preview --json \
    --message "Reply with exactly this string and nothing else: XINGCHEN-GATEWAY-OK"
{
  "status": "ok",
  "summary": "completed",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [ { "text": "XINGCHEN-GATEWAY-OK", "mediaUrl": null } ],
    "meta": {
      "agentMeta": {
        "provider": "xingchen-agi",
        "model": "xing4.1-preview",
        "agentHarnessId": "openclaw",
        "credentialSource": { "kind": "profile" }
      }
    },
    "executionTrace": {
      "winnerProvider": "xingchen-agi",
      "winnerModel": "xing4.1-preview",
      "attempts": [ { "provider": "xingchen-agi", "model": "xing4.1-preview", "result": "success", "stage": "assistant" } ],
      "fallbackUsed": false
    },
    "requestShaping": { "authMode": "auth-profile" }
  }
}
```

Gateway log confirming the turn was served over the gateway transport:

```
[ws] -> res agent 1342ms runId=909023f7-bb83-48cc-96ef-6b0968d56cf9
[agents/agent-command] [agent] run 909023f7-bb83-48cc-96ef-6b0968d56cf9 ended with stopReason=stop
```

The run executed with the normal plugin set loaded (42 of 70 built-in plugins enabled, 23 skills and the standard tool surface present), not an isolated single-plugin environment.
