prs.title: fix(audit): report malformed bulk advisory JSON with a one-line diagnosis
prs.body:
Related: #139736

## What Problem This Solves

`scripts/pre-commit/pnpm-audit-prod.mjs` aborts with a bare JSON parse error when the npm bulk advisory endpoint answers HTTP 200 with a body that is not valid JSON (introduced with the script in #139736):

```
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
[pnpm-audit-prod] FAILED (exit 1)
```

The user cannot tell whether the local lockfile, the request, or the registry response is at fault. The script already reports empty bodies (`Bulk advisory response body was empty`) and structurally invalid payloads (`Invalid bulk advisory response: expected a package map`) through the same boundary — a body that fails JSON parsing is the one remaining malformed-response shape that skips the diagnostic path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readBulkAdvisoryJson` parsed with a bare `JSON.parse`, so a malformed 200 body escaped as a raw `SyntaxError` before `validateBulkAdvisoryResponse` could classify it. The module's own contract comment requires malformed responses to remain blocking; this change keeps that exact behavior (non-retryable, exit 1) and only routes the failure through the existing diagnostic wording owner: `Invalid bulk advisory response: ...`, matching the sibling message emitted by `validateBulkAdvisoryResponse`.

## User Impact

Anyone running the pre-commit audit (or the CI job that calls it) against a registry that returns a truncated/garbage 200 body now gets a one-line diagnosis naming the bulk advisory response as the source, with the underlying parse reason retained. No schema, defaults, retry policy, timeout, or exit-code behavior changes.

## Evidence

Real environment tested: Linux x86-64, Node v26.12.1, this checkout; the script itself with a loopback registry; no mocks, no production credentials, no network.

Exact steps or commands run after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/pnpm-audit-prod.test.ts
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main --no-merge-base
NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:<port> node scripts/pre-commit/pnpm-audit-prod.mjs --min-severity high
```

Evidence after fix: vitest 24/24 passed with exit 0 (test/scripts/pnpm-audit-prod.test.ts), including the new `reports malformed response JSON without a traceback` case; test-lines ratchet OK (+8, allowance 400). Loopback run (head 3b1289fa611): exit 1, stderr:

```json
{"stderr": "Invalid bulk advisory response: not valid JSON (Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2))", "exitCode": 1, "attempts": 1}
```

Observed result after fix: with `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` pointed at a loopback server that answers the bulk advisory POST with `200` and body `{`, the audit now exits 1 with the one-line `Invalid bulk advisory response: not valid JSON (...)` diagnosis and no stack frames, after exactly one request (still non-retryable, still blocking). Same command on base b48d16bf6e9 exits 1 with the bare parse error `Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)` and no component context; the new test is RED on base and GREEN on head (RED/GREEN pinned by commit SHA 3b1289fa611).

What was not tested: real hosted-registry malformed responses (the loopback server stands in for the transport, so this proves the response-boundary behavior, not hosted npm behavior). The default `tsrs` type-checker binary aborts on this EL8 host (glibc 2.28 < required 2.32), so `tsgo:core` is left to CI lanes; oxfmt + oxlint + colocated vitest ran green locally.

prs.title: fix(ci): finish readiness fixture retries within the virtual deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a macOS readiness fixture that can hang while holding the shared test-isolation lock when readiness needs a second retry.

## User Impact

There is no runtime behavior change. Native CI can finish the fixture's existing readiness and maintenance-timeout cases without leaving unrelated tests waiting on its isolation lock.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manual-clock conversion in #197407 (`8608f8810a8e7dfee7575d36426124d6cd5102b5`) advanced only one retry in the successful-maintenance case. A legitimate second retry then slept on a clock that nobody advanced, including the owner's deadline.

The fixture now coordinates each real probe and retry through its existing clock and gates. It preserves the one-second virtual budget, all persisted-credential and readiness assertions, and cancels and joins the clock driver before cleanup. The final probe timeout and retry share a deadline, so their timer registrations are distinguished explicitly. The existing testcase now retains one transient unavailable health response so that the second retry is regression coverage. Production changes: 0 lines; test changes: +21/-7.

## Evidence

On exact canonical main `49c99cf91a4df477fc4bd986701cee643cd9d36b`, the old clock driver with the committed transient-health condition registered the second retry at 600 ms and remained blocked until an external 60-second process limit killed and joined it. The final candidate rebuilt and passed both maintenance outcomes in 44 ms with the same condition. Only the temporary phase witness was removed; the regression condition remains in the committed test. The unmodified fixture pair was also verified before retaining the regression condition. All local execution used synthetic state inside the audited headless sandbox, with no operator Gateway, Keychain, windows, or network access.

Required `pnpm check:changed` passed on that canonical base. Independent Codex review of the complete owner context found no actionable P0–P2 findings; test-audit and simplification review are complete. No temporary diagnostics or new production test seam is included.

The cancelled native run [43326355293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43326355293) had both this readiness fixture and an authentication test unfinished. This proves the readiness fixture defect; the exact cause of that hosted authentication timeout remains untraced. Full native CI remains the integration proof.

prs.title: fix(cron): retry versioned HTTP server status errors
prs.body:
Closes #197710

## What Problem This Solves

Cron's text fallback misses transient HTTP server errors when the status line includes a protocol version and no reason phrase.

## User Impact

Cron can use its existing retry policy when a transient server failure is reported as `HTTP/2 502` or a similar status line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize protocol versions in the existing 5xx pattern, following the version handling already used for rate limits and overload. Keep the status boundary so longer numbers and unrelated prose do not trigger retries.

## Evidence

- Ran the production classifier against the three versioned cases on main and reproduced the missed classifications.
- Six focused Vitest cases passed in an isolated configuration. Seven direct assertions also passed, including the existing overload category for HTTP 529. Formatting and Git whitespace checks passed.
### Gateway reproduction

I ran a one-shot **main-session** cron system event through the built Gateway on Windows with an isolated state directory. The Ollama-compatible fixture listened on loopback, served the model discovery endpoints, and returned HTTP 200 with the following NDJSON line on every /api/chat request:

```json
{"error":"HTTP/2 502"}
```

I created the job with `openclaw cron add --name "retry proof" --at +10s --session main --system-event "Reply OK"` and read the resulting job state with `openclaw cron list --all --json`. The test computed the retry delay from the persisted next-run timestamp minus the run start and duration.

| Runtime | Provider requests observed | Stored error | Stored error reason | Job enabled | Retry delay |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Same Gateway bundle with the parent regex from `794a6a806` | 6 | `HTTP/2 502` | absent | false | none |
| PR head `b45b2a6ef` | 4 | `HTTP/2 502` | absent | true | 30,000 ms |

Both runs used the same fixture and job settings. The control temporarily substituted only the parent regex into the loaded Gateway bundle. That regex is the sole production-code difference between the two commits. The Gateway test passed against the expected state in each run. The broader cron suite was not rerun.

Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, and focused verification.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid redundant GitHub action authority work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

GitHub PR actions repeat requester, session and plugin authority work between admission and already-guarded operations. Large session and role inventories amplify that work on the Gateway main thread.

## User Impact

PR metadata reads and edits use less main-thread CPU and allocation. Cross-user restrictions, current-authority checks before GitHub writes, callback isolation and final-disclosure checks remain intact. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing retained plugin grant, keep one session reader per distinct target, and remove intermediate assertions duplicated by transport or disclosure guards. Requester-incarnation lookups retain the original registry-ordered candidates and consume the existing live latest-child index instead of rebuilding an index of every retained run. Scope APIs are unchanged.

Production code is net +2 lines: the prepared-index argument preserves the existing registration-order contract without adding a cache or owner. The measurement script records actual owner calls using pinned baseline/candidate function bodies and separate census, timing and allocation passes. Existing callback tests now inject revocation through the retained authority's live assertion instead of requiring another grant resume.

## Evidence

Synthetic inventory: 2,000 persisted sessions, 20,000 live retained subagent runs and 2,000 role assignments; real visitor-access policy, session storage and registered action handler. Five A/A pairs and five alternating A/B pairs after warmup. GitHub transport is synthetic. Source publication separately exercises the durable coordinator with real local Git and a changed source file per request.

Predeclared acceptance: warm metadata-edit CPU and allocation improve at least 20%, no measured user-facing metric regresses 20%, and work census confirms fewer redundant entries/assertions and no requester-wide index rebuild.

| Warm operation | Main-thread CPU median / p95, ms | Wall median / p95, ms | Timer gap median / p95, ms | Sampled allocation median / p95, MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Read-only edit | 45.04 / 45.96 → 22.75 / 24.78 | 46.64 / 47.47 → 24.10 / 26.71 | 25.02 / 26.57 → 15.40 / 16.89 | 47.93 / 50.30 → 22.48 / 22.94 |
| Metadata edit | 67.44 / 68.17 → 28.41 / 37.18 | 68.86 / 69.65 → 29.65 / 37.24 | 47.86 / 48.24 → 16.18 / 18.27 | 75.23 / 77.19 → 28.96 / 29.89 |
| Requester run lookup | 3.27 / 4.45 → 0.09 / 0.09 | 3.30 / 5.44 → 0.08 / 0.09 | 3.32 / 5.47 → 0.10 / 0.11 | 5.48 / 5.85 → 0.03 / 0.03 |

Metadata-edit census: plugin entries **60 → 20**, gateway scope entries **63 → 23**, source assertions **432 → 159**, role selections **247 → 92**, sharing filters **84 → 29**. Requester-run lookup full-index builds **1 → 0**. Counts are stable across pairs; metadata A/A median timing differences are 3.2% or less.

Full source publication is a narrower result: plugin entries **799 → 580**, but source/role assertion counts are unchanged. CPU median/p95 is **401.01/405.60 → 390.83/404.62 ms**, wall **793.10/830.84 → 783.97/865.58 ms**, timer gap **27.33/28.32 → 27.29/29.67 ms**. Sampled publication allocation is 333.79/337.92 → 331.32/334.39 MiB (median/p95). This does not establish a material publication latency or allocation improvement. Timer gaps include scheduling; sampled allocation is collected separately from timing at 32 KiB intervals. No production data, live GitHub writes, btrfs or production stall-magnitude reproduction is claimed.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts --freeze-source <capsule> --revision 02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba`, then `node scripts/perf/github-action-scope-measure.ts --capsule <capsule> --output <new-directory>`. Run separate passes with `--counts`, `--allocation`, and `--publication` as needed. Synthetic throttle-window maintenance is outside the timed action; normal RPC admission still runs.

228 focused tests pass, including cross-user requests, revocation between read and write, synchronous alias/role mutation in plugin callbacks, accepted-push reconciliation, grant renewal/expiry/restart, base refresh and requester registration order after row replacement. The grant-resume and full-index work regressions fail on the exact parent and pass with the fix. The extended real-registry replacement-order test fails on the initial PR head and passes with the preserved ordered lookup. Codex Auto Review is scoped-clean. Changed-file format, lint, production/test/script typechecks pass.

`pnpm check:changed` has inherited unused-export failures reproduced on the exact parent `02f29597c1075`: `resolveTrustedProxyGitCoauthor`, introduced by [#196867](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196867) (`f4f290c52f961`), and inline-command UI exports introduced by [#197466](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197466) (`d90d52cce941c`). These are main regressions, not dismissed noise. Initial benchmark tuple/curly errors were fixed and their type/lint gates rerun successfully.

prs.title: fix(telegram): forum approval drops the topic when the live turn omits it
prs.body:
Closes #125166

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin approval started in a Telegram forum topic is sent to the approver DM when the live turn has the group id and the topic exists only on the stored session.

## User Impact

User impact: the approval prompt stays in that forum topic instead of falling back to the approver DM. A live turn that names a different topic still does not route into the stored topic.

## Why This Change Was Made

Origin matching treated a missing thread as a disagreement with the stored topic and returned no origin. Delivery then preferred the approver DM. When the chat matches and only one side has a thread, the side that has the thread is used.

## Evidence

I understand this code. Origin resolution is `resolveApprovalRequestOriginTargetFromDelivery`. Telegram supplies `reconcileDivergentTargets`. Delivery uses that origin target, and a null origin is what selects the approver DM.

`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/approval-native.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

8 tests passed. The omitted-thread case expects `{ to: "-1003841603622", threadId: 928 }`. Reverting the non-test files makes that assertion fail with null. The conflicting-thread case stays null. I did not run a built Gateway against a live Telegram forum topic.

prs.title: fix(ui): manage agent GitHub accounts in Profile
prs.body:
Closes #196136

## What Problem This Solves

In Settings → Profile → GitHub accounts it is hard to see which GitHub account each agent uses, what changing "System GitHub" affects, or how to give one agent its own account (for example a token limited to a fork): only the selected agent is shown, and its own account sits behind "Advanced: agent GitHub override" in Agents → Tools.

## User Impact

Profile → GitHub accounts lists My GitHub, the shared agent account and every agent with the account it uses, and every account change happens there:

- **My GitHub** keeps its own section and is used only when you publish a PR with it.
- **Shared agent account** (replacing the "System GitHub" label) is used by every agent without its own account. Its button counts the agents a change affects, for example "Change for 2 agents" (agents without `agents.entries.<id>.tools.github`).
- **One row per agent** shows the GitHub username it uses and either "Uses the shared agent account" or "Own account · Personal access token". An agent's account, own or shared, serves its commands, its dashboard GitHub data, and Publish PR unless you choose My GitHub.
- **Per-agent actions:** an agent on the shared account has **Give its own account**; an agent with its own account has **Change** and **Use shared account**. Setup opens inline under that agent ("Own account for {agent}", "Save for {agent}"), with GitHub authorization or a fine-grained PAT whose hint explains choosing only selected repositories with Contents and Pull requests read and write.
- **Rows stay current without a reload.** `tools.github.configure` replies once the Gateway runs on the saved account, so every agent that inherits a changed shared account shows the new account right away.
- **Agents → Tools** shows the agent's account read-only with **Manage accounts in Profile**; the duplicate override setup is removed.
- Reconnect hints (the `screen` action `github_identity_settings`, the `github_identity_status` hint, the publication-failure next step) open Settings → Profile → GitHub accounts. The Publish PR picker and the chat publication report line use the same names ("Shared agent account", "Own account").

Permissions and account behavior are unchanged: agent rows and their actions need `operator.admin`; saving uses the same `tools.github.configure` calls (`scope: "agent"`, `managed` or `inherit`); the "Use the shared agent account for new replies?" confirmation stays, and changes apply to new replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The roster reuses the existing scoped identity owners (`tools.github.status` with `selectedScope: "agent"` per agent, `tools.github.configure`), so there is no new Gateway method, record or config shape. Profile becomes the one place to view and change every agent's GitHub account, and Agents → Tools only shows it. That product choice, which ClawSweeper's review of #196136 also raises, needs a maintainer's yes.

Clients re-read every inheriting agent as soon as the configure reply arrives, while the config hot reload applies the write a few hundred milliseconds later. `tools.github.configure` therefore attaches the existing config-write application receipt (the one `agents.*` methods already wait on) and replies after the Gateway runs on the written config. A saved identity that is not applied immediately still replies with its saved status and logs a warning.

The reconnect screen action loads its Profile destination on demand (`ui/src/app/github-accounts.ts`), so the boot bundle does not carry it. The unused startup strings "For me" and "For the system" are removed.

**Relationship to #192350** (open; moves GitHub repository integration into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin): this PR changes presentation and where an agent's account is set, not owners, records, methods or config shape, so both can coexist, but they conflict mechanically (17 of these 37 files are also changed in #192350). If #192350 lands first, this rebases onto the plugin: the Profile component, strings and tests move to `extensions/github-repositories/browser/`, the agent count reads `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config.agents.<id>`, and the read-only Agents → Tools change goes into the plugin's Agent tools contribution. If this lands first, #192350 carries the presentation along and points the count at the plugin config path.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway with real GitHub accounts

Isolated Gateway started from this branch, built Control UI, three made-up agents, read-only fine-grained PATs for two GitHub accounts. Tokens never appear in screenshots or logs; Gateway profile IDs are shown as `<profile-A/B/C>`.

1. The shared agent account is set up with a PAT for `@lamp-connection-test`. Only `tools.github` is written (`<profile-A>`); no agent entry changes. Main, PR Irrigator and Release Notes show `@lamp-connection-test` · "Uses the shared agent account", and the shared button reads "Change for 3 agents".

   ![Shared agent account set up](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/c45077d9d700e7f40aa3a035bedf80bdedf3ad2d/images/2026/11/67166aab-1221-464b-ac23-fe8214cdcf9d.png)

2. **Give its own account** for PR Irrigator, saved with a PAT for `@daniel-lxs`. Only `agents.entries.pr-irrigator.tools.github` is written (`<profile-B>`); `tools.github` stays `<profile-A>` and the other agents have no entry. PR Irrigator shows `@daniel-lxs` · "Own account · Personal access token", Main and Release Notes keep `@lamp-connection-test`, and the shared button reads "Change for 2 agents".

   ![PR Irrigator with its own account](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/c45077d9d700e7f40aa3a035bedf80bdedf3ad2d/images/2026/11/000d1940-99c8-4f3a-b6ca-26063326380b.png)

3. The shared agent account is replaced with a new PAT. `tools.github` moves to a new profile (`<profile-C>`); `agents.entries.pr-irrigator.tools.github` is still `<profile-B>`. Main and Release Notes use the replaced shared account; PR Irrigator still shows `@daniel-lxs` · "Own account".

   ![Shared account replaced, own account kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/c45077d9d700e7f40aa3a035bedf80bdedf3ad2d/images/2026/11/64850373-f77c-4b76-bded-f43f42fa65bb.png)

Saved config after each step:


prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(channels): unblock ingress after a transient shutdown release failure
prs.body:
Closes #193019

## Main compatibility refresh — 2026-11-06

Published merge head `3e7a10e467cf355f5a02d71b899efa3eb4068832`, integrating main `b11b610d173cc6ff87eb026b6506c20fc7e5fd62` without rewriting PR history. The single `ingress-drain.ts` conflict is resolved preserving upstream failure callback extraction, queue-cap drops, selective custody retirement and test consolidation.

**Updated scope:** main #193423 already mitigates the old indefinite hold by retiring failed drains and permitting recovery of known never-adopted claims after disposal. This PR retains the bounded, token-fenced native cancellation-release retry before disposal; it does not claim current main remains indefinitely blocked. Pinned-main production overlay fails the focused retry regression (one release instead of two). Exhaustion coverage now follows upstream recovery after joined disposal; uncertain outcomes remain fenced.

**New-head verification:** 180 tests across 13 affected files passed; final worker handoff rerun 12 passed, coordinator independent rerun 12 passed. Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, source-line ratchet and scoped whitespace passed. Independent exact-head semantic review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Frozen pnpm 12.15.0 install used target-identical manifests/lockfile. Test-line ratchet retains main's 25-line debt: pinned main is 25 over, candidate is 25 over, and the PR adds exactly its existing 182-line grant. No shared ceiling was changed. New-head CI is not claimed green.

**Proof provenance:** all Telegram/Claude live evidence below remains historical at `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. Writer bytes are equivalent, but upstream custody/disposal, dependencies and test contracts changed; no live-proof equivalence or new-head live run is claimed. No production restart or new Telegram traffic occurred.

Later observed main `c63b3a2e58c45e82ea4d4955c1ac3bbb6a275d2e` also merge-probes cleanly; intervening changes are iOS tooling, so no additional merge was introduced.


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: queued channel messages remain blocked when a pre-adoption cancellation release fails once during shutdown and the retained old drain continues holding its claim.

## User Impact

A transient known release failure can recover automatically so a replacement monitor can deliver the queued conversation. Cancellation preserves delivery retry history. No configuration or database migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retained cancellation after abort now joins at most three token-fenced release attempts, with 1s and 2s backoffs. The existing settlement owner holds custody throughout. Explicit disposal prevents another attempt; failed completion, ordinary abandonment, standalone drains, and uncertain write outcomes keep their existing safety behavior. Exhaustion or an uncertain cancellation write remains observable and retains custody. The bounded retry can add up to three seconds of backoff to shutdown, plus storage I/O.

## Evidence

- A real production ingress monitor stop/restart with an actual isolated SQLite-backed queue fails on the unchanged base and passes with the repair. One known failure is injected before the native release write; the lifecycle callback is invoked only once. The replacement processes same-lane events in order, rejects stale-token writes, and does not replay already-adopted unrelated work.
- Focused drain, monitor, handoff and claim-owner suites: 73 tests passed. Added checks cover exhausted retries, nested uncertain outcomes, explicit disposal during backoff, takeover during retry, standalone cancellation and ordinary abandonment. Existing failed-completion and retry-history controls pass.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, lint, format, line-cap/test-line ratchets and whitespace checks are recorded in the local handoff.
- Independent shared autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium reasoning, P0–P2, one pass over the complete uncommitted candidate against `06d4059a3d06` and supplied unchanged owner context; no actionable findings. This is evidence-based review, without a repository mount or test execution in the reviewer sandbox. Subsequent test edits only added required braces and an explicit already-completed return and removed a redundant default type argument. The coordinating parent independently inspected the final source and clean commit and reran all 10 boundary cases successfully.

**Initial test scope (historical; supplemented by the real Telegram/model run below):** proof here is the owning monitor/SQLite boundary with a synthetic pre-write failure. Actual SQLite locking, a complete Gateway process, a real agent/model, and Telegram transport were not exercised; no live outage reproduction is claimed. Exact live Gateway channel stop/restart under an actual storage lock remains a broader integration gap. No external API or transport contract changes here.

The dedicated allocation grants exactly 182 added test lines for this recovery regression and its distinct custody bounds; the shared baseline is unchanged. The change reuses existing owners and removes redundant release wrappers; production code grows by 12 lines. The four-suite run took 41.92s including worker preparation; the final boundary file took 4.63s in Vitest (50.61s wrapper including compiler preparation), and the parent independently measured 4.92s (53.90s wrapper). CI timing is unmeasured before publication.


## Additional shipped-entry-point evidence — 2026-11-05

The earlier Evidence section describes the initial monitor tests. This additional run used the real built CLI/Gateway, its plugin loader, and the public `channels.stop` / `channels.start` RPCs. It was **not another in-process monitor test**. The channel was a task-only local diagnostic plugin (`ingress-proof/default`), not Telegram. Its delivery callback deliberately calls synthetic `onDeferred` / `onAdopted`; **no real agent/model response or external transport was exercised, so this does not claim the root real-agent/model E2E gate is fully satisfied**.

**Isolation and provenance.** Separate task HOME, config, SQLite state, workspace and loopback ports; only the diagnostic plugin enabled; no provider credentials copied, no production Gateway restart/config/state change, no real-channel messages. The same fixture and one-shot fault wrapper ran against head `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2` and runtime inputs from base `06d4059a3d06e1a34a3cacfd3f635b93fe803a38`. For the base run, only the two owner files were temporarily restored byte-for-byte from the base and rebuilt through the CLI; all other runtime inputs matched base (only the new test/allocation differed). This was a documented base-runtime overlay in the head checkout, not a Git checkout whose HEAD changed. Original source was restored afterward.

The external plugin uses public SDK `createChannelIngressMonitor` and `api.runtime.state.openChannelIngressQueue`. It throws exactly once **before** calling the native release operation, logs refresh only after the real queue returns `true`, and reads the committed queue via the public API. There is no SQLite method mock, SQL reset, forced owner retirement, manual second cancellation callback, or claimed actual `SQLITE_BUSY`. The fixture SHA-256 is `d1d039654e952e53eff1e39baa8680360637a26f3e8cf0bad372773df0b7fcb3`.

**Base observation.** Real Gateway PID `95449`: the channel stop RPC reported `stopped: true`, but the internal joined monitor stop rejected the injected error. Starting the replacement channel did not drain its lane. Only `unrelated` was synthetically adopted; `task` remained claimed and `waiting` pending. Committed `claimedAt` values advanced at `2026-11-05T11:03:19.612+09:00`, `2026-11-05T11:03:21.614+09:00`, and `2026-11-05T11:03:58.706+09:00`; heartbeat commit counts were `[4, 6, 43]`. This is a bounded observation of continued old-owner renewal, not an empirical claim that it can never recover.

```text

11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-abort","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":95449,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-rejected","generation":1,"pid":95449,"message":"Error: Synthetic known cancellation release failure before native write","ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback-returned","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:18 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":1,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
11:03:21 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":2}

11:03:58 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"heartbeat-committed","generation":2,"pid":95449,"ownerGeneration":1}
```

**Head observation.** Real Gateway PID `93148` remained the same across channel generation 1→2. One cancellation callback caused one known pre-write failure, then release attempt 2 committed about one second later and joined stop succeeded. The replacement synthetically adopted `task`, then `waiting`; the already-adopted `unrelated` was not replayed. The old token's release/complete/refresh all returned `false`, the successor token differed, and re-enqueue of `unrelated` returned `completed`. Final pending and claimed sets were empty.

```text
10:58:29 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-started","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:58:59 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"adopted","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"unrelated","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"cancel-callback","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":1,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:55 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"injected-known-prewrite-failure","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-attempt","generation":1,"pid":93148,"attempt":2,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"release-result","generation":1,"pid":93148,"id":"task","committed":true,"ownerGeneration":1}
10:59:56 INGRESS_PROOF {"event":"channel-stop-joined","generation":1,"pid":93148,"ownerGeneration":1}

```

**Shipped command path.** Under each task-only environment: `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`; then `corepack pnpm openclaw gateway call` with `--expect-url` pinned to that task's configured loopback Gateway, using `ingressProof.seed`, `ingressProof.arm`, `channels.stop`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, `channels.start`, `ingressProof.snapshot`, and `ingressProof.dedupe` (head). Public lifecycle params were `{"channel":"ingress-proof","accountId":"default"}`. All these RPC commands exited 0; the base's reported stop success is distinguished above from its monitor failure. Both task Gateways later handled SIGTERM and exited 0 with clean shutdown. No commit/push was required for this instrumentation.

**Interpretation and limits.** A generally slow model cannot explain this comparison because no model runs; identical fixture, queue, lane and fault behavior plus the advancing native timestamps distinguish a retained old-owner claim from a delayed initial read. However, the fixture deliberately supplies deferred/cancelled work and observes its own callback receipts. Its synthetic adoption is not evidence of agent execution, outbound send, Telegram acceptance, or user-visible response. It does not prove an actual database lock, indefinite blockage beyond the observed interval, every channel adapter, or a whole-Gateway process restart. It proves a real Gateway-hosted local channel stop/replacement through shipped entry points with actual SQLite persistence. Whether this layer satisfies the requested real-behavior gate remains for review; the broader real agent/model/transport gap is explicit.


## Real Telegram and real model recovery evidence — 2026-11-05

**Observed result:** recovery eventually succeeded through the production Telegram adapter, real Claude CLI agent/model, and Telegram Bot API. It did **not** succeed on the first replacement: the task relay refused two overlapping local polls and the adapter automatically restarted twice before both replies completed. The human operator confirmed in the Telegram client that the replies arrived in A → B order. Per-event counts below are backed by the queue, transcript and Bot API receipts; the human confirmation specifically establishes client-visible order.

Pinned PR head: `934ca4166ec58d9dc24deaf248051da44392a0a2`. The requesting user confirmed their dedicated bot was unused elsewhere, then sent a fresh exact handshake and prescribed A/B prompts manually in the verified private DM. No automated user account or team QA pool was used. The isolated Gateway had task-owned config/state/workspace/ports. A parent-owned, destination-bound protected HTTPS relay consumed the stored token sentinel; no credential value was extracted or copied into the Gateway. The operator Gateway was untouched.

Temporary instrumentation held only A before real admission and injected one known error before the original claim's native cancellation release write. It never invoked synthetic adoption. Native cancellation, the PR's existing bounded writer retry, real Telegram replay, real agent/model execution and outbound delivery remained production paths. Setup `deleteWebhook` was a recorded local no-op after verified empty webhook; no upstream webhook deletion or queue flush occurred. Command-menu deletion attempts were refused locally.

Measured timeline, KST:

```text
13:31:16.764  A held before native adoption
13:31:58.907  bound B observed by real Telegram poller
13:32:36.938  read-only task SQLite: A claimed, B pending; same lane; attempts=0
13:32:38.283  one known pre-write release failure for original A token
13:32:39.285  second release attempt for that same token (+1002ms)
13:32:40      manual channel replacement starts
13:32:41      local concurrent-poll refusal; automatic restart scheduled
13:32:47–48   first automatic restart also hits local poll guard
13:32:58      second automatic restart starts
13:32:59.308  real A adoption/completion write commits with new claim token
13:33:03.954  Telegram accepts final A response
13:33:04.053  real B adoption/completion write commits
13:33:06.414  Telegram accepts final B response
```

The old long-poll request remained in the relay until its bounded upstream request returned after the downstream client was cancelled. The relay's single-poll guard refused the two successor attempts rather than starting another upstream poller. This was task relay lifecycle behavior, not a second bot consumer or a newly fixed PR behavior. No queue reset, forced retirement, manual second cancellation callback or failed-send retry was used to recover.

Final read-only SQLite inspection found exactly A and B, both `completed`, both attempts=0, with no pending/claimed work. The real agent transcript contains exactly two assistant records matching the prescribed A and B responses in order, both `provider=claude-cli`, `api=cli`, with actual usage: A input10/output181/cache-write11936; B input10/output81/cache-read11936/cache-write710. Telegram returned two distinct accepted message receipts, A then B; no duplicate-send refusal or uncertain-send event occurred. Native launch/probe/maintenance subprocess counts are not misrepresented as exactly two model requests. The separate one-shot provider setup qualification is excluded from this recovery proof.

The native Claude child used its existing login without copying credentials, with global home file writes denied by an OS policy, tools/customizations and native session persistence disabled. Gateway/OpenClaw state stayed task-owned. This was a real provider, not mock-openai or synthetic `onAdopted`. Source instrumentation was restored byte-for-byte, Git was clean at the pinned head, and the uninstrumented head build completed successfully. The Gateway logged a clean shutdown in82ms; its launcher group received SIGTERM and reported-15, so that wrapper is not reported as exit0. Parent verified the protected relay ended code0 and both task ports closed. No live task processes remain; persistent review Remote is retained.

**Client observation:** on 2026-11-05 at 13:43 KST the human operator confirmed the replies arrived in order. This is a human client observation, not an inference from Bot API acceptance.

**Limits:** Actual SQLite locking, every transport/provider, and whole-Gateway restart were not tested or required for this known pre-write failure. The earlier base/head Gateway comparison and existing safety regressions are separate supporting evidence. This run establishes eventual real-channel/model/outbound recovery with the explicit transient relay failures above; it is not presented as a clean first-restart run or proof of all client-rendering behavior.

prs.title: improve: render chat composer mentions inline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected people should behave as whole inline mention chips, not an avatar followed by an independently editable name or a painted overlay. Earlier revisions also lost recipient identity during some editing/history operations.

## User Impact

Chat and New Session show one atomic avatar-and-name chip using the sent-reference styling. The caret cannot enter its letters; selection and deletion respect the whole chip. The extra “Will notify” strip is removed. Raw messages and clipboard text remain canonical `@Name` text with selected recipient spans. No new dependency or configuration change.

Straight and curly possessives attach directly after selecting a person. Read-only/disabled composers reject rich paste and composition mutations. Undo/redo preserves recipient identity for repeated names and across the first native-to-editor handoff, including same-text selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing lazy CodeMirror editor owns layout, selection, history, clipboard, and composition. The hidden textarea is only the established raw-value/controller port; it is not a visible overlay. Current-main integration preserves the moved dictation owner and lazy reply preview, and routes remaining focus/selection callers through the shared editor bridge.

Requested by @Patrick-Erichsen, with @vyctorbrzezowski’s atomic-editing and manual-testing requirements. The possessive issue was reported by @vincentkoc.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion and initial implementation with @Patrick-Erichsen and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/31236f32-4426-45a7-be8f-b1aed8f96632)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/e42589fc-b3f8-4478-8032-adc37344a926)

## Author response to the acceptance report

Current head: `a7bb4e2d44ef41de71f8451f761ab7dcbe214973`. The report below was run on `4ae188c3` and is unchanged. Two commits follow it: `005d8712` fixes the report's three findings, and `a7bb4e2d` applies an independent review. Neither has been retested in the macOS app, in Safari or on a phone.

### The report's three findings

| Finding | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Backspace also navigates back (macOS app) | The editor forwards each key to the hidden textarea as a copied event. Copying the whole event also copied WebKit's legacy `keyIdentifier`, and WebKit runs default actions for an untrusted keydown that carries it: Backspace goes back in history, Tab moves focus. | Forwarded keys are built from named fields only. |
| 2. Safari drag moves part of the selection | WebKit delivers a fast first `mousemove` before `dragstart`. CodeMirror treats a move of 10 px or more as a new selection, so the drag started with a smaller selection. | The editor remembers the selection that was grabbed and restores it at `dragstart`. A press that ends without a drag forgets it. |
| 3. Long names clip at 320/390 px | Chips were `white-space: nowrap`. | A chip is one inline box. It moves to the next line whole, and a name wider than the composer wraps inside it. |

Long name in a narrow composer, before and after:

![Before: long mention name clipped at the composer edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5edf0b50-02d9-4329-aa3c-489397527a31)

![After: long mention name wraps inside its chip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d481a99-32c8-4822-a3df-31574e28a837)

### Independent review

An isolated read-only reviewer agent read `cda0b61a..005d8712`, focused on the code changed since the earlier full review and on iOS and WKWebView risks. It ran nothing. Outcome: no P0, two P1 and eight P2. This was not a local ClawSweeper or autoreview run; a hosted ClawSweeper review is still due when the PR leaves draft.

Fixed in `a7bb4e2d`, each with a test that fails on `005d8712`:

- **Backspace dead key.** Backspace beside a separator the chip needs put the caret back where it was, so every further press did nothing. It now steps over the separator.
- **Unreadable selection.** Selected text in the rich editor used CodeMirror's light default, which is light on light in the dark theme. It now uses the app selection color, focused and blurred.
- **Mobile resting capsule.** After sending a message with a mention, the retained empty editor kept its full height in the one-line capsule. It now rests like the textarea.
- **Undo after send.** A native snapshot from before the owner cleared a sent draft could seed undo history when the next mention was inserted without typing. A snapshot is now used only when the selection replaced it. Accepted edge: a sent draft ending in a plain `@word` still passes.
- **Stale grabbed selection.** A tap inside a selection could leave a selection for a later touch drag to restore.
- **Dragged move reported as typing.** A move now reports `insertFromDrop`.
- **Scrollbar.** `scrollbar-width: thin` made Chromium ignore the app's 8 px scrollbar that the overflow padding assumes. With real scrollbars the old head measured a 10 px bar against 8 px of padding; the new head measures 8 against 8. This one has no automated test, because headless Chromium hides scrollbars.

Selection in the dark theme, before and after:

![Before: selected text is light on a light highlight](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4df4a82-7956-42fb-b964-8dfc47d4330a)

![After: selected text on the app selection color](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c6a4acc-038e-4783-aa6f-8eeadf61d144)

Rejected, with reasons:

- **"Programmatic focus into the editor never sets mobile editing" (P1).** The editor's content element carries `contenteditable="true"`, which the existing check already matches. Confirmed in a browser.
- **"A paste replayed after the editor chunk loads can land in the next draft" (P2).** This needs a first-ever recipient paste, a slow chunk load and a send in between. The result is visible and recoverable, and a guard would add always-loaded code.

Named by the review as worth checking on a device, not confirmed as bugs:

- IME composition next to a chip on iOS keyboards.
- Whether the software keyboard stays up when the first mention mounts the editor on iPhone.
- Caret position in the macOS app, where each selection change also writes to the hidden textarea.

### Proof on this head

- 124/124 unit cases and 145/145 Chromium browser cases passed, with UI types, lint, CSS lint, format and the test-line ratchet.
- **WebKit 27.2 (Playwright's Linux build, not Safari or the macOS app)**, using the shipped editor module: Tab from the editor lands on the next stop (two stops away on `4ae188c3`), and the reported drag moves the whole selection (`A@Alice Morgan  right-side-endBC ` on `4ae188c3`). Finding 1 was not reproduced as back navigation, only through this shared Tab mechanism.
- The repository's WebKit browser-test lane could not connect on this host, so the browser suites ran in Chromium only.

### Asset size

- Against the branch base `cda0b61a`, `pnpm ui:check-performance:base` passes: Chat boot JS +693 B, New boot JS +819 B, total CSS +40 B gzip and +50 B raw.
- **Against main `5cef30a3` it fails** (local trial merge, not pushed):
  - Chat boot JS measures 1,303,841 B against a 1,303,711 B limit, 130 B over. This PR adds 882 B there.
  - New boot JS on main alone measures 806,388 B against its 805,886 B cap, so only 64 B of growth is allowed. This PR adds 623 B.
- No thresholds were raised. This needs an owner budget decision or a reduction before the PR can pass that check. Local sizes can differ from CI by a few hundred bytes.

### Other points from the report

- **Twelve-ID synthetic clipboard.** Intended. The composer cannot hold more than 10 recipients, so it never writes such a clipboard. Foreign metadata that claims more than 10 is rejected as a whole and pastes as plain text. Pasting into a draft that would exceed 10 keeps the existing recipients and binds only up to the limit, which is the 10+2 case that passed. The original handoff wording for item 6 was wrong.
- **Attachment focus (item 15).** Also on main, as the report says. Not changed here.

<!-- maintainer-acceptance-2026-11-12:start -->
## Inline composer mentions — full test report

**Two editing regressions and one visual regression were confirmed against main. I would not consider the tested head ready to merge.** No fixes were made during testing. These results apply to the exact revision below, not automatically to later changes.

### Scope and environment

- Candidate: `4ae188c349e1ba45e9ef7a9e5bfcdabd482e52eb`, branch `roboclaw/composer-inline-mentions-20261103`.
- Matched main: `fb83d658cf3b6257a43b322c1e701ba757a0d546`.
- **Real isolated Gateways**, authentication, sends, durable history and authenticated recipient Inbox reads. **Only the model was a local response stub.** Provider/model behavior was not validated.
- 24 synthetic profiles covered a crowded picker, duplicate display names, a long name, non-Latin names, photos/initials and a failed-photo fallback. Recipient IDs, not just display labels, were checked.
- Chrome **157.0.8103.39 headless** on macOS **27.0.1**, plus Chrome **157.0.8103.79** with real OS keyboard/mouse in a disposable macOS **26.6.2** VM.
- Firefox **160.0**: headed native-OS lanes plus separate headless WebDriver lanes. Safari **26.6.2**: actual Safari, native-OS and separate WebDriver observations.
- Actual macOS app **2026.11.3, build 2611000390**, built at candidate, on macOS 26.6.2. Native A/B held the executable constant while UI/Gateway switched between main and candidate. SHA-256: `a1d2188e763cd2bdb3ed1708dd5e90b89173ac7396a05e0f3c446f199bb1ac89`. No `apps/macos` source difference exists between the compared revisions.
- The app's shared-password **Owner** fixture cannot send bound human mentions without a signed-in human. Main has the same policy. Native delivery items 1/2/21 remain unqualified; this does not excuse unrun editing/layout tests.

### Coverage

**92 rows: 23 handoff items × 4 surfaces**, each with Chat and New Session results. These are coverage cells, not test-execution counts.

**PASS:** applicable subcases supported. **FAIL:** contrary result observed; notes identify pre-existing behavior. **NT / partial:** whole item remains not tested, but some subcases passed. **NT:** not qualified as a whole, including blocked setup. **N/A:** explicitly inapplicable. Partial coverage never becomes a whole-item pass.

Across 184 cells: **67 PASS, 7 FAIL, 110 not tested**, including **6 N/A**. Seven failing cells represent the three new findings and the pre-existing Chrome attachment-focus behavior in both contexts, not seven new defects.

New Session has no conversation prediction/history or pre-creation split-pane surface. No dedicated focus-composer shortcut was identified in the inspected catalog. Mention/slash/skill menus use composer-wide anchors; emoji uses the caret. These applicability/design facts are not failures.

The undo acceptance sequence was: type `hi @al`, select Alex, undo back to `hi @al`, then redo the same recipient chip; separately cut/undo a chip and verify that undo after sending does not resurrect the sent draft. Boundary checks used `'s`, `’s` and an immediately following letter. Clipboard checks distinguish copied chip metadata from plain external `@Name` text. For IME, only observed marked composition and its committed result counted.

### Chrome

| # | Handoff item | Chat | New Session | Evidence boundary / remaining gap |

| 1 | Pick and send | PASS | PASS | Correct recipients, durable sends and authenticated Inbox receipts. |

| 8 | IME composition | NT | NT | Before/after/restored marked composition unqualified. |
| 9 | Unavailable editor / recovery | NT | NT / partial | Chat unqualified. New healthy chip observed; cache and pairing-dialog focus prevent qualified 404 fallback/recovery. |
| 10 | Atomic chip editing | FAIL | FAIL | Backspace also navigates backward in both (finding 1). Arrow jump/whole-chip selection pass. |
| 11 | Possessive / letter boundaries | PASS | NT | Chat possessives/following-letter space pass. New not run; final-new filenames actually identify Chat in AX. |
| 12 | Send keys, prediction, history | NT | NT | Send-setting/newline set not run; Chat prediction/history not run, not applicable to New. |
| 13 | Menus with a chip | NT | NT | Complete keyboard menu set not run. |
| 14 | OS text services | NT | NT / partial | New spelling/substitution/speech menus and visible autocorrection observed; dictation, replacement and OS emoji picker missing. Chat not run. |
| 15 | Focus and tab order | NT | NT | Click/type-to-focus, tab order and menu/attachment return incomplete; no dedicated focus-composer shortcut identified. |
| 16 | Growth and scrolling | NT | NT | Growth/scroll/lateral movement not measured. |
| 17 | Narrow / landscape / short panes | NT | NT | 320/390, landscape and very short pane not run. |
| 18 | Placeholder | NT | NT | Hide/restore placeholder not run. |
| 19 | Pending, locked, themes, Incognito | NT | NT | Pending/locked, themes and Incognito set not run. |
| 20 | Draft persistence | NT | NT / partial | New reload retains chip/text; Forward restores draft after back navigation. Other transitions missing; Chat sequence not run. |
| 21 | Queued mentions | NT | NT | Bound queued delivery unqualified: shared Owner needs signed-in human. |
| 22 | Large drafts and paste | NT | NT | Large paste, later typing and error observations unqualified. |
| 23 | macOS-only interactions | NT | NT / partial | New spelling menu and Cmd+Z/Shift+Cmd+Z observed; external text/file drag missing. Full Chat set not run. |

### Finding 1 — Backspace also navigates backward in the macOS app

**Severity: major. Surface: actual macOS app; Chat and New Session.** Versions and exact candidate/main heads are above. This is a navigation/editing regression, **not demonstrated permanent text loss**.

1. Visit a Chat, then open New Session so Back has a previous destination.
2. Type `ab @Ali`, choose **Alice Morgan** through the real picker, then append `cd`. Complete draft: `ab @Alice Morgan cd`.
3. Focus the native accessible text area and put the caret immediately after the mention (exported AX caret `[16,16]`).
4. Press native **Backspace** without modifiers. A control also used a CGEvent with empty modifier flags.
5. Repeat in Chat with New Session as its preceding history entry. Use **Forward** to inspect the retained draft.

**Expected:** remove the whole mention and remain editing on the same screen.

**Actual:** the chip is removed **and the app navigates to the previous page**. Deleting an ordinary character with the rich mention editor active also reproduced navigation.

**Frequency/control:** candidate **2/2 New Session, 2/2 Chat**. Main stayed in the current screen in both controls. Executable, shared-password setup and enabled prediction were held constant. Main's older text representation deletes a character rather than a chip; the matched invariant is **no navigation**, not identical token deletion.

Native state:

```text
Before: ab @Alice Morgan cd
After Forward: ab  cd
New case AX label: "What should this session work on?" → "Chat composer".
Chat case: inverse navigation.
```

Forward recovered the edited draft. No send occurred. AX observations/screenshots support this result; **no equivalent DOM dump or JavaScript console capture exists for this exact sequence**. Cause was not isolated or fixed.

Receipt identity: `native-backspace-ab/receipt.json`, candidate/main before-and-after AX records, and matched images.

![Native Backspace: matched main and candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7f5eae6-1845-427b-a61f-8d4ad8124d9e)

### Finding 2 — A native Safari drag moves only part of the selection

**Severity: major. Safari 26.6.2 on macOS 26.6.2; Chat; real OS input and real Gateway.** Candidate/main heads are above.

1. Select **Alice Morgan** through the real picker and create exactly `ABC @Alice Morgan  right-side-end`, with two spaces before `right-side-end`.
2. Select exactly `ABC @Alice Morgan`, including the chip. Verify the selected string through the OS clipboard.
3. Drag this selection to the end of the same composer without modifiers.
4. The reproduced native gesture uses **empty flags, clickState 1, an 800 ms mouse-down hold, then 35 straight-line movements 40 ms apart**.
5. Repeat on main, adjusting coordinates to the actual input position.

**Expected:** move the entire selected prefix. Matched main produced ` right-side-endABC @Alice Morgan`.

**Actual:** candidate produces `A@Alice Morgan  right-side-endBC `. Only `BC ` moves. The full selection remains after mouse-down, then becomes `BC ` in the early-drag AX sample.

**Frequency:** candidate **3/3** with this gesture; main **2/2** moves the complete prefix.

```text
Before value:       ABC @Alice Morgan  right-side-end
SelectedClipboard: ABC @Alice Morgan
AXSelectedText:    ABC @Alice Morgan
Candidate result:  A@Alice Morgan  right-side-endBC [trailing space]
```

This is **gesture-specific**. Another native helper passed on candidate but differed in event fields as well as trajectory: no explicit flags/clickState and an initial 60 px horizontal segment. It does not invalidate the failing matched route. Chrome using the same failing-Safari helper passed in **New Session**; do not generalize this Safari defect to Chrome.

**Recipient loss is not established as a new regression.** Both revisions' later sends lacked `humanMentions` and matching Inbox items; main also crossed navigation before final send. Initial main picker/bound-recipient state was independently checked. This comparison establishes incorrect text movement, not candidate-only loss of notification. The specific drag sequence has AX/clipboard/image evidence, not a DOM metadata or console dump.

Receipt identities: `79-candidate-straight-result.json`, `79-candidate-third-drag.json`, `79-main-straight-result.json`, `79-main-repeat-result.json` and separate final-send receipts.

![Safari drag: matched full-selection control and partial candidate movement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eae1c9b5-bb3a-45c7-8f72-c5fe6a294fbb)

### Finding 3 — Long names clip abruptly in narrow composers

**Severity: minor, visual. Chrome 157.0.8103.39 on macOS 27.0.1; Chat and New Session;320 px and 390 px widths.**

1. Open Chat or New Session at **320 px** or **390 px** viewport width.
2. Type `@` and select **Alexandra Beatriz de Albuquerque Monteiro-Silva**.
3. Inspect the name inside the composer; compare a fresh matched main page at the same width.

**Expected:** readable wrapping or deliberate truncation.

**Actual:** the chip exceeds the usable text region and the name is cut abruptly without ellipsis. Main wraps the complete text at 320 px and fits it at 390 px.

**Frequency:** confirmed in both contexts at both widths, with fresh main controls. The evidence does not record a repeated-trial denominator for all four combinations; no additional N/N rate is claimed.

Captured candidate state (synthetic profile):

```json
{
  "value": "@Alexandra Beatriz de Albuquerque Monteiro-Silva ",
  "mentions": [
    {
      "profileId": "c79569c7-5552-4825-ace5-ecddcac62c75",
      "start": 0,
      "end": 48
    }
  ],
  "richEditor": true
}
```

Full text and recipient metadata remain in the draft. **This is not text/recipient loss.** Initial resize-transition captures were replaced by fresh controls; the visual defect does not imply a console exception.

Evidence: fresh long-name Chat/New images, `long-name-before-after.png` and matching draft/geometry records.

![Long-name clipping: matched main and candidate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f444f861-7c38-4d81-b36f-b40ea52ac8bc)

### Important boundaries and excluded conclusions

**Normal overflow versus a synthetic 12-ID clipboard.** Copying ten real mentions and pasting into two existing mentions retained twelve names with ten bindings. This is not one clipboard containing twelve distinct bindings pasted into an empty editor. The UI does not itself produce a twelve-binding clipboard. A separate synthetic OS-clipboard producer supplied twelve valid IDs: text survived but **all bindings were rejected**; its ten-ID control was accepted. Keep this literal-handoff discrepancy separate from normal UI copy/paste. It is not established as a new regression, and the synthetic diagnostic was not repeated in every surface/context.

**Unavailable editor: picker selection and paste are different.** The fault target was `composer-editor-mentions-*.js`, including identity/gzip/Brotli representations. Cache hits do not qualify as induced load failures.

- Chrome New qualified the source clipboard, empty prestate, blocked load, plain paste with no binding, normal send with no `humanMentions`/matching Inbox, and same-payload recovery after unblocking/reload. Chrome Chat lacks its own blocked-native-paste subcase.
- Safari New case **83** showed visually plain paste during genuine 404 and a chip after exact restoration plus same-tab reload. **No metadata read or send receipt proves absence of a recipient for that paste**; item 9 remains partial.
- Safari case **84** chose a person through the picker while the asset was missing. Its send retained **Alice[17,30]** and generated **one authenticated Alice Inbox receipt**. A plain-looking fallback does not imply missing recipient metadata. This positive picker receipt cannot substitute for a negative paste receipt.
- Firefox hard reload retained cached rich editor during server 404, and later recovery paste was unqualified. The native app likewise retained its rich chip and a pairing dialog interfered with focus. **Neither has a qualified fallback/recovery transition or a product-failure verdict.**
- Initial fault setup still served gzip from memory and was aborted; only verified 404 windows counted. Exact hashes and HTTP 200 were restored afterward. These recovery claims require **explicit reload**, not automatic recovery.

**Other controls and invalidated attempts:**

- Initial headless partial-drag and unsuccessful mouse-transfer observations were not treated as native OS regressions. Safari's later matched OS gesture is the separate confirmed finding above.
- An early paste copied the address-bar URL rather than the intended selection and was excluded. The later empty-prestate/clipboard-controlled result is counted.
- Initial queue probes had empty draft/unsettled handoff. Only final hold→queue→release→recipient receipt counts.
- Early skill probes expected a hyphenated raw slug. Canonical normalization produces `mention_fixture_skill`; corrected keyboard selection passed.
- Immediate-reload suffix loss did not reproduce in three controlled blocked-chunk trials. Initial main-only-selector mistakes and a session-switch probe that stayed in the same logical session were excluded.
- Attachment removal focusing BODY and attachment-menu Escape focusing its trigger also occur on main. They are reported in coverage, not attributed to this PR.
- Bound mentions prevent Incognito sending on main too; this restriction is not new.
- IME required real marked composition, not merely a Japanese input source producing Latin letters. Safari's independent textarea failed qualification. A later invalid Firefox attempt does not erase earlier genuine composition evidence.
- Delaying a real local `sessions.create` request showed **Starting** and a new composer, not a remotely pending placement lock. No UI property was altered to fabricate this state. The real `users.setRole` read-only result applies only to the Chrome run that executed it.
- Large-paste checks prove preservation and continued input with error/geometry observations where stated. They are not comparative latency benchmarks or a blanket performance guarantee.

### Actionable retest list

1. Investigate native Backspace navigation and Safari partial drag, then repeat these exact gestures on the proposed new head and main. Hold executable, focus, selection, modifier/event fields and page-history prerequisites constant. Cover chip deletion and ordinary-character deletion, and inspect Forward-restored text.
2. Recheck long names at 320/390 px in both contexts using settled layout/fresh controls; inspect full draft text and ID.
3. Qualify native bound delivery/queueing with an **authenticated synthetic human**, not shared Owner. Verify durable message IDs and intended recipients' authenticated Inbox records, including duplicate names.
4. Close remaining item 9 cells with verified cache eviction/404, empty prestate and known clipboard contents. Prove paste metadata/negative recipient receipt separately from picker selection. Restore exact assets and show same-origin/same-payload recovery.
5. Resolve intended behavior for the twelve-ID synthetic clipboard before treating it as a natural UI regression; keep the ten-ID control and normal 10+2 case.
6. Complete remaining OS text services, internal Chrome Chat drag, other drag contexts, Safari post-send undo, focus/tab/attachment-return sequences, immediate-letter boundaries, remote pending placement, persistence transitions and true narrow/short-pane cells. Reuse valid passes rather than rerunning them only because another lane did not duplicate them.

### Evidence retention and closeout

The three comparison images are the visual evidence for the findings. Raw JSONs retain exact draft/selection/geometry and authenticated receipts where stated; AX limitations are explicit. The privately retained raw archive contains **1,069 files / 351,623,607 bytes**, SHA-256 **`c26739c11c098dabc449eb0cc05fade92cabc6b61b948ff02d7f52bb79edf939`**. No public archive-download availability is implied.

Native evidence manifest SHA-256: **`4516f5dc2f3b19c57beebec22da263156ccdef7fae4ec0ddb31080eb4a0d171f`**. Invalidated attempts remain distinguishable from counted proof. Disposable test services, checkouts and VM were cleaned up after preservation; shared resources were preserved. No fixes, commits, pushes or merge were performed during the test campaign.

Public comparison images use synthetic profiles. The device name is redacted in the native comparison; no product behavior is altered.

<!-- maintainer-acceptance-2026-11-12:end -->

## Author-supplied evidence before the acceptance pass

Current head: `4ae188c349e1ba45e9ef7a9e5bfcdabd482e52eb`. It merges main `cda0b61ac4d23fb0a5fa5530e37f9e74ce3face5` (two conflicts, in the boot-module manifest and its generator script) and adds one commit with the fixes from a whole-code review. Ancestry is preserved; nothing was force-pushed.

Changed in this update:

- Pasting more than 10 recipients keeps the first 10 and leaves the rest as plain text. Previously all were dropped.
- Enter and Shift+Enter insert a plain newline, without code-style auto-indent.
- Spellcheck, autocorrect and autocapitalize stay on once a mention exists.
- Undo can no longer bring back a draft that was already sent.
- Fixed a lazy-load race that kept chips from mounting, separators inserted on owner sync, and mobile composer rules that never reached the rich editor.
- Recipient paste and drop have one owner, the rich editor. If the editor cannot load, the transfer lands as plain text and binds no recipient.
- The editor is listed in the textarea's existing geometry selectors, and editor-only rules live in its lazy theme. Unrelated transcript CSS from earlier revisions is back to main.

Local proof on this head:

- **124/124 unit cases** in 4 files and **139/139 Chromium browser cases** in 11 files passed, covering the editor, production callers, native drag-and-drop, mobile gestures and overflow. Composition events test the editor transaction contract, not an OS IME.
- UI types, CSS lint, format, whitespace and the test-line ratchet passed. Targeted lint reported 0 errors and 5 Solid reactivity warnings.
- Not rerun on this head: the production-UI E2E suites, WebKit and Firefox, a native OS IME, real devices, and live notification delivery.
- The last round of changes (paste/drop ownership, CSS consolidation, the eager bridge trim) has not had an independent review yet. An earlier independent review of the full diff found the issues listed above, which are fixed.
- CI for this head has not been observed. Main has advanced since `cda0b61a`; a trial merge with current main was clean.

### Startup gate — passing locally

`pnpm ui:check-performance:base cda0b61ac4d23fb0a5fa5530e37f9e74ce3face5` exited 0 on Node 26.12.1 / Vite 8.3.5. This measures shipped asset counts and bytes, not live latency.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Startup JS gzip | 92,209 B | 92,156 B | −53 B |
| Chat boot JS gzip / requests | 1,302,904 B / 20 | 1,303,597 B / 20 | +693 B / 0 |
| New boot JS gzip / requests | 804,259 B / 15 | 805,078 B / 15 | +819 B / 0 |

| Total CSS gzip | 331,131 B | 331,167 B | +36 B |

Chat boot JS is 114 B under its 1,303,711 B limit, so growth on main can still push it over. Base CSS already exceeds its absolute ceiling; this head stays inside the 64 B growth allowance. No thresholds were raised.

### UI (captured on an earlier head)

Mobile:

[Earlier matched before/after layout evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192242#issuecomment-6619285884) remains available for that earlier avatar-layout revision.

## Limitations and Scope

**Keep this PR draft.** The maintainer acceptance report above found two editing regressions and one visual regression on `4ae188c3`. Head `a7bb4e2d` fixes them and applies an independent review (see the author response). It awaits a retest, including on a phone, together with the coverage gaps the report lists. The asset-size check against current main is also open. The evidence below this report remains historical author-supplied context.

The screenshots above were captured on an earlier head with the real production UI and synthetic Gateway profiles. They were not recaptured for this update.

Accepted edge: the composer focus frame also shows while keyboard focus is on a suggestion button inside the input area, not only while the text field has focus.

An earlier renderer CPU comparison on a prior candidate showed typing in a 64 KiB draft about 5% faster at the median and a 256 KiB paste about 3% slower. It was not rerun on this head.

Against main `cda0b61a`, UI production source adds 2,073 and removes 323 lines, and tests add 2,007 and remove 170. Net test-line growth is allocated explicitly (1,965 lines on the current head) rather than raising the shared ceiling. The existing CodeMirror dependency is reused; manifests and the lockfile are unchanged.

## Maintainer integration repair

Current head: `6628c6bec069f9b314aaef85616483ba61b53564`. The input component remains a separate, draft-keyed component but now lives in its parent module, eliminating the static import cycle. Its function body is unchanged. The existing composer options type lives in a type-only leaf module, and the boot inventory was regenerated. The editor cleanup method explicitly declares its existing `this`-free contract.

CI fixes complete the existing test doubles, use native Command/Control history shortcuts, and make the loader-refresh fixture retain the same requested draft. Duplicate test setup was consolidated without dropping the first/second-person, undo/redo or read-count scenarios. No new tests, product behavior changes, or budget increases were added.

Validation: 106 editor/lifecycle tests, 135 view/paste tests, and five route tests passed; the final consolidated caller file passed all 27 cases. UI and UI-chat types, scoped type-aware lint/formatting, the import-cycle guard and the test-line budget passed. The UI build succeeded with asset-size warnings. Independent review of the complete repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The history tests now emit uppercase `Z` with Shift for redo and test apostrophe normalization as one atomic edit, without assuming two keystrokes arrive within the history grouping interval. The stale exact-padding assertion was removed; the complete selected production-build E2E case still checks text, avatars, overflow and scrolling and passes. All 83 affected history/editor cases pass locally. The explicitly requested CI rerun completed. - Chat and New Session: insert a person, continue typing, and preserve the mention.
