- Selected text remains readable in light and dark themes. A long name wraps inside the phone composer.
- Chat send clears the draft. Inserting another mention and undoing does not restore the previously sent message. An outside tap returns the empty composer to its one-line capsule.
- The native Done accessory leaves the empty editor expanded in this simulator, but the same gesture also does that on base `cda0b61ac4d23fb0a5fa5530e37f9e74ce3face5`; it is not introduced here.

Limits: this simulator did not expose its software keyboard. CJK IME, predictive-keyboard behavior, dictation, software-keyboard persistence, touch selection dragging, and the native macOS app were not qualified by this run.

All 44 focused mention-ownership tests passed on this head. Fresh complete-diff independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The synthetic fixture was restored and the task-only simulator/server were removed or stopped after testing.

The user-requested second attempt of [CI run 43273739723](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43273739723/attempts/2) completed. The other previously timed-out shard passed. The fixture, suite owner, state factory, HTTP harness and cleanup owner have identical blobs in the incoming source, published head, actual CI merge 7f0d10d, and live main c4ec1836.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse verified prepared snapshots and worker code
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fresh cloud sessions repeat completed snapshot setup and worker-code extraction instead of reusing verified prepared content.

## User Impact

Fresh, unpinned default-branch sessions can reuse a compatible completed snapshot only when its revision belongs to admitted default-branch history. Explicit refs and pinned sessions retain exact-source preparation. Seed-only requests prepare the requested revision without running an unauthorized setup recipe. The actual completed base reaches preparation, inspection and binding; current repository access remains required.

Verified worker packages are reused through exact aliases; damaged or missing code falls back to verified archive installation. Legacy peers retain registration-time verification. Only negotiated peers defer verification to first binding with its full timeout; exact binding replay preserves private edits.

**Status:** `3825a67…` is published for **proof**, not landing. Broad CI, shared Swift-kit Periphery and OpenGrep precise scan **attempt 2 succeeded** after separately diagnosed download failures. At the November 9, 16:41 UTC readback, all **167 latest check runs were terminal: 124 success, 42 skipped, one neutral**, with no failed or pending checks. OpenGrep's parser-coverage limitations are recorded below. AUTH-2, UPGRADE-3 and dependency #193873 remain open. No consumer merge or server deployment occurred.

**Landing dependency:** older-snapshot behavior requires [managed publication recovery #193873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193873). Publication is not dependency acceptance. Capture normalization and diagnostics are separately covered by #193776.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing admission, prepared-workspace and installer owners serve this flow. Strict registration requests exclude receipt-only fields. Negotiated verification stages preserve old/new peer compatibility without a protocol-version bump. Actual-base propagation, main's preparation callback, memoization, capture verification and diagnostics remain intact.

The admitted repository/account owner checks snapshot ancestry. Missing or oversized comparisons decline optional reuse only after repository/account revalidation; authentication, revocation, cancellation and transport failures still fail closed. The metadata size limit is unchanged.

Original PR and contribution: @galiniliev. Workflow recovery and contributor-credit support were requested with @vyctorbrzezowski. Automated repair and qualification: @roboclaw-bot.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev and @vyctorbrzezowski](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1f24e3f3-e7d6-4966-b666-e5868987619d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/70153122-6ab4-4eea-96e9-a8b689da6467)
- [Implementation and verification — first-bind and seed-only regressions](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/649d3ef7-7e03-41fc-b728-f1e3cc134da1)
- [Implementation and verification — mixed peers and snapshot lineage](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/acd66058-9c68-4d20-bd3e-3bb4b94b466b)
- [Implementation and verification — comparison fallback boundaries](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/b0bc6b4e-8b23-422c-85ab-e11a9c70d9f7)
- [Implementation and verification — main conflict resolution](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2c3657af-b6ae-4a02-9b36-e12ca377884a)
- [Implementation and verification — landed native workflow prerequisites](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4e21df81-705a-4c4f-8051-ce41b210e29d)
- [Verification — authenticated baseline candidate](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/94d52650-602b-4d45-952b-682817c03e9e)

## Evidence

### Published source

- **Head:** `3825a67949692994c8c09733379bcda88992df5e`; **tree:** `d689db82d1bd50a160e0086c818371eace8753ab`.
- Native proof publication fast-forwarded `e67f9b520ca4c19fb34a01e5a5bb7080e9181661` to this exact candidate. Receipt: `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, `PUSH_REPLACED_HOSTED_ANCESTRY=false`, pending `AUTH-2,UPGRADE-3`.
- The sole new blob is `config/test-lines-allocations/prepared-snapshot-residual.txt`: **3 owned LF**, reconciling complete PR growth **1,019** against prior grants **1,016**. Tests, runtime, checker and shared scalar are unchanged. Exact hosted composition reproduced red **6,593,452 / 6,593,449**, then green **6,593,452 / 6,593,452** with this record. No inherited-debt credit or padding was added.
- Independent remote readback verified the full tree, changed blob, parent, signature and both exact Galin/Vyctor trailers. Earlier hosted ancestry, `b6faccd…` and all signed main merges remain ancestors.
- The prior native baseline `c7266a4…` preserves `b6faccd…` as first parent and authenticated `1bc50e0…` as second parent. It used landed #195476/#195662 tooling without changing signing trust or rewriting history.

### Source-pinned local proof and review

These are separate executing-source receipts, not a summed final-head suite:

| Source | Completed proof |

| `32b13317…` | **93-test** correction proof and immutable bundle. |

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the real-Gateway Profile test failing when Personal instructions finishes loading during its first screenshot.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The browser fixture captures the loaded Profile page while preserving its identity, editing, and admin-approval checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

#196867 ([f4f290c5](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f4f290c52f9614cdac8e8d95322b96590dc1b96e)) added an earlier identity screenshot before the Personal instructions readiness wait established by [c5b1f555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c5b1f5558e53fc861900dde148594d576553cbd7). Move that existing wait before the first capture; retain the later wait after role promotion. The strict screenshot guard and all authorization assertions remain unchanged. Production LOC: 0; test LOC net: 0 (+1/-1).

## Evidence

[CI 43332707251](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43332707251) failed on tested merge ea118ee7 with unchanged identity-card bounds but ancestor height growing 199.53125 px during capture. Holding and then delivering one real `users.personalFile.get` response reproduced the exact expected/received geometry strings. Inspected before/after images show the editor appearing and Saved accounts moving below the viewport.

The controlled old case failed when the held reply was delivered at screenshot entry. The controlled repaired case verified that no screenshot started while the reply was held, then delivered it and passed the complete flow. These are deliberately different release schedules: the corrected wait prevents reaching screenshot entry while the reply is held. No response substitution, timeout change, capture retry, or production hook was used; the experiment proves the mechanism, not the exact hosted transport timing.

The original local flow passed once, which is not flake proof. With all temporary probes removed, the final real-Gateway case passed in 40.496 s on canonical main 6c32a157, with actual screenshot capture enabled. Its 265.01 s wrapper time includes build preparation and is not a speedup claim. After integrating the named #197992 export repair, the final original flow also passed on main 49c99cf9 in 20.519 s (220.71 s including preparation); the newer main contains Gateway/schema changes, so this additional run verifies that context. Fresh Codex P2 review is clean and its changed-file/owner inputs remain byte-identical. All unaffected changed-file gates passed; the only failure was nine known exports, now resolved with all three canonical export scans at zero. The affected UI E2E type graph also passes on 49c99cf9.

prs.title: feat(ui): choose the speech-to-text model from Settings → Talk
prs.body:
Fixes #197859

## What Problem This Solves

Settings → Talk has no speech-to-text setting: the model Talk dictation and transcription use lives in the raw `tools.media` config under AI Agents, and nothing on Talk says whether speech-to-text is ready or what is missing.

## User Impact

On Settings → Talk, users can see whether speech-to-text is ready and pick the speech-to-text model. Status shows the catalog’s readiness and active provider. If the preferred model’s provider is unavailable, a separate "Preferred model" row explains that it may need a key or may not support speech to text, and links to that provider on Settings → Models. The page says which setups take precedence over the picked model for Talk.

## Why This Change Was Made

The new "Speech to text" section uses only existing config keys and Gateway methods. It adds no config options, RPCs, schema or key entry:

- **Status:** readiness and active provider from the `transcription` group of the `talk.catalog` read the page already makes. The row can show "Ready" with "Active provider: openai" even when the preferred model’s provider is unavailable.
- **Preferred model:** appears only when the catalog lists the preferred model’s provider as unconfigured. It shows "Not ready", explains that the provider may need a key or may not support speech to text, and offers an "Open Models" button for that provider on Settings → Models.
- **Speech-to-text model:** lists the audio-tagged `tools.media.models` entries, plus "Automatic" and a free-text `provider/model` option. A pick sets `tools.media.audio.preferredModel`; a `provider/model` with no matching entry is first added to `tools.media.models` with `capabilities: ["audio"]`. "Automatic" clears only the preference. These are the same config values the AI Agents → Tools editor shows, and they also drive inbound voice-note transcription.
- **Precedence:** this picker is the file-transcription preference. A streaming transcription provider (Voice Call plugin) or a speech-to-text voice-model default takes precedence for Talk dictation, and the row says so. The page states this rather than detecting the active override, because `talk.catalog` does not report which path the Gateway chose and that choice depends on the provider registry.
- **Validation:** a custom value that isn't `provider/model` (for example `openrouter/`) is refused with an inline message, and the saved preference stays unchanged.

Provider keys stay on Settings → Models. "Ready" reflects the catalog’s local availability checks, including transcription support and credential configuration; it does not verify that the provider accepts the credential.

The new code loads only with the Settings → Talk page; it adds nothing to the startup, chat or New Session bundles.

## Evidence

Live runs against an isolated Gateway, with temporary state and a made-up Gateway token, driven in headless Chromium. The upgrade run used a synthetic OpenAI credential. The saved config file was read after each step.

Before (`main`, same isolated setup): Settings → Talk has Realtime voice and the raw Talk settings, with no speech-to-text setting.

![Settings → Talk on main: Trigger words, Realtime voice, and the raw Talk settings editor; no speech-to-text section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/a9d73258befcf996f825677216392687ce7a7922/images/2026/11/345afd8f-7372-439e-8077-85a6e10f8bd1.png)

Catalog readiness and preferred-model warning (`709411d`): in one isolated macOS VM, with a dummy OpenAI key and no OpenRouter key, the catalog reported `ready: true` and `activeProvider: openai` while the saved OpenRouter model’s provider was unconfigured. Status showed "Ready" and "Active provider: openai"; the separate "Preferred model" row showed "Not ready", the "can’t transcribe yet" explanation, and "Open Models". No transcription session was started.

![Speech to text: Status Ready with active provider openai, saved OpenRouter model, and a separate Preferred model Not ready warning with Open Models](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/7f2bbaa5e87f1087acb0116c61d6c648e932320f/images/2026/11/2bcd4799-4fee-42cc-b7d2-32f729304445.png)

Upgrade preservation: in one disposable macOS VM, upgraded published v2026.11.3 to a fresh build of `95f74aa`. Before picker edits, both existing audio entries, the `openai/whisper-1` preference, the other audio settings, and the synthetic OpenAI credential profile and key bytes were preserved. Doctor added authorization metadata and an empty local auth row; the full auth store is not identical.

Saved and reloaded: selected the existing `openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` entry, then added `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe` through "Other model (provider/model)". Each selection survived Settings autosave and reload. Both original entries and their options, the other audio settings, and the credential profile and key bytes remained intact. The final preference is intentionally `openai/gpt-4o-transcribe`. Redacted config and credential snapshots cover the baseline, the upgraded state before edits, and both picker edits.

Malformed reference: typing `openrouter/` shows the inline message, and the config file still holds the previous preference.

Automatic: choosing "Automatic" removed `preferredModel` and kept both audio entries; after a reload the picker shows Automatic.

Tests: `talk.test.ts`, `talk-device.test.tsx` and `settings-search.test.ts` pass. Speech-to-text coverage is in `talk-transcription.test.ts`, including tests that catalog readiness stays separate from the unavailable preferred provider’s "Not ready" warning and "Open Models" link, and that a malformed custom reference is refused without writing config. The shared Talk test helpers find the realtime model picker by its label, since the page has two model pickers. UI typecheck, lint and formatting are clean, and the i18n raw-copy baseline is verified.

Not verified:

- Provider authentication and transcription with a real provider key. "Ready" reflects local availability checks, not a successful provider request. The upgrade run used only made-up credentials and made no paid provider calls.
- A setup with a streaming transcription provider or voice-model default configured; the precedence is stated in the UI, not detected.
- Native Talk clients (macOS, iOS, Android) and Settings search entries for the new rows.

prs.title: improve(sessions): cover the current-turn walk and opaque first-kept resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/config/sessions/session-entry-navigation.ts` is the one navigation owner behind the runtime session manager and the streaming transcript operations, and it had no test file — none of its exported symbols appeared in any `*.test.ts`.

The load-bearing part is where the current-turn walk stops. `walkSessionCurrentTurn` feeds `resolveCurrentTurnEntryId` and `prepareCurrentTurnReplaySelection` (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-current-turn.ts:87`, `:138`), so a wrong stop position changes which entries belong to the live turn:

- An unresolvable row, an id mismatch, and an untraversable row all stop the walk. Skipping any of them would splice unrelated history into the current turn.
- The ancestor budget ends the walk by handing back the next id, not the last one visited. That is what makes the caller's `entry?.id !== userId` check reject a budget-truncated walk instead of accepting a partial one — no test protected that.

`resolveOpaqueSessionFirstKeptEntryId` decides what a keep marker points at once opaque entries are involved; returning the wrong id silently changes the replay window after a compaction or reset.

## What Changed

- `src/config/sessions/session-entry-navigation.test.ts` — 8 cases: the four stop conditions plus the ancestor-budget boundary, and the three resolution paths of the opaque first-kept resolver.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/session-entry-navigation.txt` — 115 lines.

Deliberately left out: `SessionEntryNavigation`'s reset-boundary bookkeeping and `normalizeSessionContextEntryBoundaries`. Both need entry fixtures that survive the persisted entry schema, and asserting them with hand-built records would test the fixture rather than the module. They belong in a separate change.

## Why This Way

Covering it through `SessionManager` instead was rejected: the existing manager tests exercise the happy path, so none of the four stop conditions ever executes there and their exact outcome is asserted nowhere.

## Evidence

All eight cases run through the project's lane dispatcher, `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/config/sessions/session-entry-navigation.test.ts`:

```text
✓ walks the whole parent chain when the budget allows it
✓ stops on the row it could not resolve instead of skipping over it
✓ stops when the resolved row belongs to a different id
✓ stops at a row marked untraversable
✓ does not walk past the ancestor budget
✓ returns a first-kept id that is already canonical
✓ follows the opaque chain to the canonical ancestor
✓ falls back when the first-kept id is not part of the branch
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  8 passed (8)
```

`oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The file matches the pinned formatter output byte-for-byte, verified through `oxfmt --stdin-filepath` because in-place formatting writes are blocked in this environment.

## Related

Closes #190424

prs.title: fix(reply): carry the queued chat identity into follow-up tool context
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #184730.

A message drained as a native `followup` rebuilt its turn template context from the queued run's routing facts, but never restored the chat identity the source turn was addressed at. `buildEmbeddedContextFromTemplate` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.ts:288-290`) derives the tool-run `chatId` from `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId`, and `buildEmbeddedAttemptToolRunContext` projects that field as `nativeChannelId` for V2 plugin tools. A queued turn supplied neither field, so V2 plugin tools saw requester / channel / account facts with an absent `nativeChannelId`, while the same message as an immediate turn carried it (and the CLI candidate path already passed `followupRun.originatingChatId` as `chatId`).

The queued run already carries the value: `get-reply-run-execute.ts:501` captures `originatingChatId` as `NativeChannelId ?? ChatId` at enqueue time, and the drain preserves it. Only the follow-up template projection dropped it.

- `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.ts`: `buildFollowupTemplateContext` now publishes `ChatId: queued.originatingChatId`. The shared embedded context keeps its existing preference for `NativeChannelId` and only falls back to `ChatId`, so the follow-up projects the same native conversation as an immediate turn.
- No inference from prompt text, session-key parsing, route relaxation or extra session lookups: a queued turn without an originating chat id still projects none, so an absent identity keeps failing closed.

## Evidence

Red first, on the real follow-up execution owner. Regression added in `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts`:

```text
FAIL  src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts > executeFollowupTurn > carries the queued chat identity into the follow-up turn's tool context
AssertionError: expected undefined to be '-1001234567890' // Object.is equality

- Expected:
"-1001234567890"

+ Received:
undefined

 Tests  1 failed | 32 passed (33)
```

The case drives `executeFollowupTurn` with a queued `originatingChatId` and asserts both hops the issue is about: the turn template's `ChatId`, and the `chatId` that `buildEmbeddedRunContext` feeds into the tool-run context (which `nativeChannelId` is projected from). It also asserts the requester stays separate (`SenderId` unchanged), and a second case fixes the fail-closed side: with no queued chat id, both hops stay `undefined`.

Green after the change:

```text
 Tests  33 passed (33)          # src/auto-reply/reply/followup-turn-execution.test.ts
 Tests  37 passed (37)          # followup-runner.test.ts + agent-runner-utils.test.ts
```

Verification on this host (`node scripts/...`, portable Node 24.22.2):

- `scripts/test-projects.mts` for the three files above — all passing.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on both changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors (259 rules).
- `scripts/run-format.mts --check` — all matched files use the correct format.
- `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json` — no diagnostic in either changed file. This workspace's installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` is older than current main, so the run stops on four pre-existing errors in unrelated files (`src/agents/host-file-write.ts`, `src/config/io.audit.ts`, `src/infra/private-dir-mode.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.agent-dir-receipt.ts`).
- The e2e lane (`agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts`) needs a full build, which this host cannot produce (`ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE: mode 'preserve'`), so end-to-end shipped coverage is left to CI.

Test-line growth is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/followup-tool-chat-identity.txt` (32 net new test lines, measured after formatting).

prs.title: test(ui): honor reduced-motion transition timing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The OpenClaw ID menu E2E test requires zero animation objects under reduced motion, although the stylesheet permits 0.01 ms CSS transitions. Resetting copy feedback can create four such transitions after the earlier idle check and fail the final snapshot assertion.

## User Impact

Restores browser coverage of the existing menu without changing application behavior or styling. The remote-access completion repair already landed separately in #197998; this PR preserves those canonical ceremony assertions unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Check each actual animation effect's duration and delay against the existing reduced-motion limit. Preserve the earlier idle check and all geometry, focus, clipboard, publication and close assertions. No extra retries, longer timeouts, production helpers or new test cases.

## Evidence

- The assertion and CSS contract were introduced by #196688 (`5a371b71d80eb1572ede712e70c8821aee7193d8`). Controlled real keyboard Copy and its unchanged 2,200 ms feedback reset reproduced four CSS transitions, each with duration and delay of 0.01 ms. The original zero-count predicate failed; the corrected timing contract passed the existing viewport/theme/sign-in matrix. Temporary diagnostics are excluded. prs.title: feat(browser): open Chrome settings pages from the Control UI Browser panel
prs.body:
Closes #197837

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI Browser panel can't open Chrome's settings pages. For example, typing `chrome://settings/payments` to add a payment card fails with `Navigation blocked: unsupported protocol "chrome:"`.

## User Impact

The operator can open `chrome://settings` and `chrome://password-manager` pages from the Browser panel's address bar, then view and use them like any other tab. The agent still can't open, list, read, capture or interact with those pages, including while the operator has one open. Other `chrome://` pages stay blocked for everyone.

This works for locally managed and CDP-attached Chromium profiles on the Gateway host. It isn't available for node-routed browsers, Chrome MCP existing-session profiles, the browser extension, or Chrome's headless shell, which has no settings pages.

## Why This Change Was Made

These pages hold saved payment cards and passwords, so access follows who is asking, not which tool is used:

- **Who counts as the operator.** The Gateway marks a `browser.request` as the operator's only when it comes from an authenticated Control UI connection (`authenticatedControlUi`, recorded at handshake) that isn't one of the Gateway's own internal clients. The agent's browser tool, the `openclaw browser` CLI and node proxies never qualify.
- **What changes for the operator.** For those requests only, tab listing, opening a tab, focus, close and every tab route (screencast, screenshot, `act`) accept `chrome://settings` and `chrome://password-manager` targets. Every other caller keeps the existing target filter and navigation guard.
- **New tab only.** These pages open only in a new tab, never by navigating an existing one, so a tab the agent already holds can't turn into a settings page.
- **Kept away from the agent.** These tabs get no `t1`-style alias, never become the implicit tab for targetless agent calls, and aren't recorded as session tabs.

The panel's address bar opens any `chrome://` URL in a new tab, and the Gateway decides whether it's allowed. Docs: a "Chrome settings and passwords" section under the Browser panel in `docs/tools/browser/profiles.md`.

`GET /snapshot` isn't extended. The panel doesn't call it, so the operator gets a 404 there too.

## Evidence

The Browser panel in a real isolated Gateway built from this branch, with headless managed Chrome and a temporary profile. The address bar opened `chrome://settings/payments` in its own tab, and the panel streams it:

![Control UI Browser panel showing the chrome://settings/payments page in a new Settings tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9188e39dab3e00f8bde7a32f3668dfdfcb0c9371/images/2026/11/a36c6853-6849-43e7-8227-dad21a5fba81.png)

Tests:

- `routes/operator-pages.chromium.test.ts` runs against real Chromium. Without an operator requester, the agent can't open or navigate to the page. While the operator has a `chrome://settings/payments` tab open, the agent can't see it in `/tabs` and gets 404 for snapshot, screenshot, screencast, click, key press, navigate, focus and close on it. A targetless agent snapshot still uses the agent's own tab. The operator can open, list, stream, press keys in and close it. The test fails on `main` (the operator's open is refused) and passes here. It's gated by `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_OPERATOR_PAGES_E2E=1` like the other `*.chromium.test.ts` files. It runs in the Browser MCP contract workflow (`pnpm test:e2e:browser-mcp` and its Bun job), whose Chromium install includes the full Chromium build this test needs.
- `gateway/browser-request.operator-pages.test.ts` checks who counts as the operator. Only an authenticated Control UI socket is marked. An internal client (including one carrying a Control UI marker), a CLI operator socket and an unauthenticated Control UI id are not. 5 of 5 pass.
- Existing tests for the changed files: 19 files, 296 tests pass. These cover the navigation guard, target ids, tab selection, tab routes, remote tab ops, Playwright page creation guards, CDP, `browser.request`, session tab scope and the Browser panel controller and toolbar.
- Typecheck (extensions, UI), format and `git diff --check` are clean.

Not covered: a headed (visible) Chrome window, and Chrome's own device-password prompt before it reveals a saved password. That prompt appears on the computer running the browser, not in the panel.

prs.title: fix(status): cancel pending Gateway reads in status on Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status` did not pass its abort signal to the Gateway `status` and `channels.status` reads, so Ctrl-C or SIGTERM while one of those replies was pending left the read running: the CLI hung until the cleanup deadline force-killed it (exit 137), or the read timed out and the report printed late.

#197969 already covers the readiness wait and probe in the same command and stops `status` and `status --json` quietly when the scan fails only because of the interrupt. This change covers the reads after the probe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `status` read in the status scan, the `channels.status` read, the `status --json` projection read and the local fallback `status` read now take the command's abort signal, and their existing catch paths rethrow the abort before their usual fallback, so the scan ends through #197969's quiet interrupt path. Uninterrupted scans, unreachable-Gateway output, JSON shape and exit codes are unchanged. No new text.

## Evidence

Built CLI in a secretless node:24.22.1 container, real `openclaw gateway run` behind a relay that answers readiness and the probe normally but holds the `status` or `channels.status` reply. Main twice, candidate twice. On main, `status` (SIGINT), `status --json` (SIGTERM) and `status --deep` with `channels.status` held (SIGINT and SIGTERM) all ended in exit 137 about 2 s after the signal. With this change they exit 130 or 143 within 0.1 s, close the held socket at the signal, and print only the existing interrupt line, nothing on stdout. A healthy Gateway, no listener, and uninterrupted held replies give the same output on both. The deep status scan test in `src/commands/status.scan.test.ts` now also interrupts the scan while the `status` or `channels.status` read is pending: both cases fail on main (the scan resolves) and pass here, at 0 net test lines. Details: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197909#issuecomment-6840859476.

prs.title: fix(sessions): confirmed deliveries record a false delivery-failed when media cannot be embedded
prs.body:
Related: #196616

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a confirmed outbound send is recorded as `delivery-failed` in the destination conversation when the media cannot be embedded into transcript history, and the underlying preparation reason is discarded.

## User Impact

An agent or UI reading a conversation no longer sees a false "delivery failed" card for media a channel already delivered; the delivered media name stays visible in the display text; the underlying preparation reason now appears in gateway logs instead of a generic "could not be prepared" message. Unconfirmed (internal) commits keep their honest failure cards.

## Why This Change Was Made

After a channel accepts a payload, `commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` projects the delivered media into history. When embedding then fails (unreadable media, size/type limits, trust refusals), `createManagedOutgoingMediaBlocks` records an `attachment_error` with `code: delivery-failed` — a delivery outcome that did not happen. Separately, `getSanitizedManagedImageAttachmentError` replaced every non-managed prepare error with a generic "could not be prepared", so operators could not tell a trust refusal from a content-type error.

This change:
- Retains a named media reference (not a failure card) in the confirmed-result projection, but only for a false `delivery-failed` outcome produced while embedding the accepted media. Independently meaningful preparation outcomes such as `unsupported-format` keep their recovery guidance, and failures recorded before the channel send (for example a rejected `file://` source removed by reply-media normalization) keep their failure cards — they are never converted into delivered references for media that never reached the channel.
- Keeps the delivered name visible in the UI: the reference name is appended to the display text block (the UI renders text blocks even though `message-normalizer-attachments.ts` drops a reference `attachment` that has no URL).
- Preserves the underlying prepare reason on the sanitized error as a `cause` unconditionally (no private-path heuristic), and routes the cause-bearing warning through the shared error-coercion formatter (`formatErrorMessage`) instead of the WebSocket `formatForLog`, so a long attachment label no longer truncates the cause away and the message is not pre-redacted before file logging. Logs are written raw and redacted at egress.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway transport send accepted** (real `openclaw` Gateway server + webchat transport, `installGatewayServerChatTestSuite`): a `chat.send` is accepted by the webchat transport (`{"ok":true,"payload":{"runId":"proof-196812","status":"started","messageSeq":1}}`) and the reply reaches terminal `final`. This demonstrates the shipped Gateway and its transport accept a send in this environment.
- **Shipped outbound delivery → confirmed → destination history** (real `deliverOutboundPayloadsCore` through the `recordConfirmedTranscript` path in `deliver-core.ts:684`, a channel adapter confirms each part, real SQLite state store): the adapter accepts the send (`delivery results: [{"channel":"telegram","messageId":"msg-1"}]`) and the destination session history is committed with the delivered text. This is the exact shipped pipeline that internally calls `commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` after an accepted send — no manual `deliveryConfirmed` assertion.
- **One shipped trace connecting accepted delivery → embedding failure → destination-history readback → ordinary cause in the warning.** Run through the shipped commit path `commitConfirmedVisibleMessage` (the function `deliver-core.ts:684` calls after an accepted send) → `commitBackgroundPayloadsToSession` with `deliveryConfirmed: true`, against a real SQLite state store. The delivered media is a valid base64 `image/png` data URL whose image content cannot be read back, so the embedding failure happens in the real image-processing step (`getImageMetadata` in `managed-image-attachments.ts`), not in input parsing or sanitization:

  ```
  === PROOF 196812: shipped confirmed-delivery -> history projection (ordinary cause) ===
  1) channel accepts the payload (deliveryConfirmed): 'Voice note' + image accepted
     commit result: {"ok":true}
  2) transcript embedding fails for an ordinary reason (the delivered image is present
     but its dimensions cannot be read), and the destination history records:
     [
       { "type": "text", "text": "Voice note\nGenerated image 1" },
       { "type": "attachment", "attachment": { "kind": "image", "label": "Generated image 1" } }
     ]
     false delivery failure present: false
  3) preparation warning logged with the underlying reason:
     logWarn: webchat media embedding skipped attachment: Managed image attachment
              "Generated image 1" is missing readable dimensions
  === END PROOF 196812 ===
  ```

  The four required elements sit in this one shipped flow: the channel accepts the delivery, the subsequent embedding fails, the destination history reads back a visible name with no false `delivery-failed`, and the warning carries an ordinary preparation cause (not an invalid-input/sanitization error). The media-embedding failure runs through the shipped projection (`prepareWebchatReplyMediaForDisplay` → `createManagedOutgoingMediaBlocks`) inside `commitConfirmedVisibleMessage`; the outbound delivery layer strips raw media from the recorded payload, so the projection is the authoritative path for this failure.
- **Confirmed-delivery projection regression test** (`src/sessions/background-result-payloads.test.ts`, routed through the SQLite broker shard): a confirmed media payload that cannot be embedded records a named `attachment` reference, no `attachment_error`, the name in the display text, and `logWarn` carries the underlying reason. An unconfirmed payload keeps the honest failure card. These assertions failed on the base and pass with the fix.
- **Pre-delivery failures keep their failure cards** (`src/sessions/background-result-payloads.test.ts`): a payload whose reply-media normalization rejected one source (recorded as `delivery-failed` in `assistantMediaFailures`) while a delivered image fails to embed records the delivered image as a visible reference **and** keeps the rejected source's `attachment_error` failure card — the pre-delivery failure is not converted into a delivered reference for media that never reached the channel. This guards the conversion in `buildResultDisplayContent` (`background-result-payloads.ts`).
- **Pre-delivery failure cards survive with no remaining embeddable media** (`src/sessions/background-result-payloads.test.ts`): a confirmed payload with text plus a rejected `probe.mp3` source and no embeddable media takes the no-embedding return path in `buildResultDisplayContent` and still keeps the rejected source's structured `attachment_error` card (previously the card disappeared with the cleared `assistantMediaFailures` metadata). The normalization-appended textual receipt (e.g. `⚠️ probe.mp3: Delivery failed…`) is stripped from the display text so it is not duplicated beside the structured card. This covers the early-return branch and unconfirmed internal commits alike.
- **Text-reference fallback and narrowed conversion via the public commit path**: a confirmed media-only payload (no text block) gets a prepended `text` reference; a confirmed SVG payload (`unsupported-format`) keeps its recovery-guidance failure card rather than being rewritten into a delivered reference. `retainDeliveredMediaReferences` stays private to `background-result-payloads.ts`.
- **Cause preservation** (`src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.errors.test.ts`): managed errors are unchanged; the original error (including path-bearing refusals) is always preserved as `cause`.
- **Full cause in the warning for long labels** (`src/gateway/server-methods/chat-reply-media.test.ts`): a confirmed payload with a 200+-character attachment label that cannot be embedded records the failure block and a warning whose sanitized wrapper alone exceeds the old 240-char display limit — the distinct underlying cause (`requires an explicitly trusted reply payload`) still survives in the warning via the shared error-coercion formatter. This assertion failed against the previous `formatForLog` path and passes with the fix. It exercises the exact `onManagedMediaPrepareError` callback in `chat-assistant-content.ts` that produces the warning, demonstrating that an ordinary (non-bypassing) preparation cause is preserved end to end.
- **UI visibility** (`ui/src/lib/chat/message-normalizer-attachments.test.ts`): text blocks survive normalization while a URL-less reference `attachment` is dropped — proving the text path is the consumer-supported form. Validated by `checks-ui` (the local UI vitest run hangs environmentally).
- **Test-line ratchet**: `config/test-lines-allocations/pr-196812-confirmed-delivery-media-embedding.txt` is set to the exact merge-tree regression delta (428; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes with zero slack).
- Affected suites pass via the repo runner: `background-result-payloads.test.ts` (6), `managed-image-attachments.errors.test.ts` (3), `chat-reply-media.test.ts` (15), `confirmed-visible-message.integration.test.ts` (10), `managed-image-attachments.recovery.test.ts`.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui` (typecheck), oxlint on changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.

## CI

Checks are green on head `659bd9a9d7f3` (pre-delivery failure preservation). CI is in progress on the latest head `5a7b2b6970f0` (pre-delivery failure cards on the no-embedding branch, receipt dedup); no failing checks so far (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`, `checks-node-changed`, `checks-ui`, `checks-ui-e2e`, `check-lint-core`, `TypeScript contracts`, `ci-gate`, `security-sensitive-review`, `dependency-review`).

prs.title: perf(agents): reuse sealed nested tool-result payloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Tool-heavy sessions repeat deep normalization when persisting nested Tool Search results that are already sealed JSON.

## User Impact

Tool-result persistence reuses safe immutable payloads with less normalization work and identical stored transcripts. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Nested Tool Search target results are JSON-round-tripped and deeply frozen before acceptance, but their sealed children did not carry existing transcript ownership. The real guarded append therefore walked and copied those children again.

Record the already-established child ownership after the existing freeze, allowing transcript admission to reuse immutable JSON. Keep the envelope unowned: its intentional `details: undefined` marker still needs omission at admission. Direct built-in, Code Mode, Tool Search control, MCP/plugin, error and replacement payloads retain normal ingress unless they already carry immutable ownership. Same-process admitted replay keeps its existing fast path.

Production grows by eight lines for the existing ownership import and a shallow, nonallocating direct-child loop. The recursive freezer and its array fast path are unchanged. No new flag, cache, configuration, schema, session-row projection or provider-request change.

## Evidence

### Performance

Synthetic Linux btrfs fixture: 35.189 GiB agent DB, 5,000 sessions / 198,545 messages, and 62,000 workspace files / 1.14 GB. Six-way tool-heavy history covers built-ins, Code Mode, search controls, nested plugin/MCP snapshots and errors. Producer construction is included; appends use the real tool-result guard, SessionManager and SQLite. No production data.

Five A/A and five counterbalanced A/B pairs per metric. Allocation: 240 warmup / 1,200 measured appends. CPU: 2,400 warmup / 6,000 measured. Final whole-append comparison alternates serial 100-append batches between two prepared processes. Every A/A control met the predeclared ±10% bound for total CPU, main CPU, active wall and latency p95; all A/B gates passed. Stored message JSON hashes are identical in every pair.

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Normalization CPU (ms/1,000) | 137.357 | 94.116 | -31.48% |
| Normalization allocation (MiB/1,000) | 70.062 | 44.707 | -36.19% |
| Whole-append total CPU (ms/1,000) | 11,086.644 | 10,380.521 | -6.37% |
| Whole-append main CPU (ms/1,000) | 3,608.754 | 3,333.811 | -7.62% |
| Whole-append active wall (ms/1,000) | 9,167.653 | 8,588.766 | -6.31% |
| Whole main-isolate allocation (MiB/1,000) | 539.835 | 514.270 | -4.74% |
| Per-append latency p95 (ms) | 15.079 | 14.237 | -5.58% |
| Recursive normalization visits / 1,000 | 121,833.333 | 82,333.333 | −32.42% |

Paired total-CPU changes have median −1.75% (range −6.37% to −1.50%); A/A total-CPU changes range −4.45% to +2.75%. Both normalizer and native-JSON preflight recursion drop by the same count; root normalization calls remain unchanged. Allocation is V8 sampled allocated bytes, **not retained heap**. Whole-append differences are small relative to A/A variation; this establishes no material regression, not a large end-to-end speedup. The synthetic producer mix does not establish the affected production fraction.

An earlier time-separated whole-append campaign **failed** acceptance (total CPU median +43.86%, main CPU +53.68%, wall +48.36%, latency p95 +39.63%). Landing stopped. One stronger bounded serial-batch experiment was declared before execution, with all earlier results retained; it did not reproduce the regression under qualified controls. Production code did not change between campaigns. The benchmark also replaces an inherited sub-millisecond owner-clock precision defect with a Linux thread CPU clock; strict compiler, monotonicity and real-append checks pass.

### Validation

- Two producer → guarded append regression cases fail on base and pass with the fix, preserving stored bytes and sealed-child identity while raw undefined/NaN still normalize.
- 65 focused tests and 14 prefix-stability tests pass.
- `pnpm check:changed` and incremental changed checks pass, including final source. Independent Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped-clean.
- Controller smokes pass for A/B, reverse A/A with partial batches, and missing-seed failure propagation.
- Exact-head CI [43339720070](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43339720070) passes on `68cce6b374fd6babbc2065b4c33c507345edbd4d`. ClawSweeper final-head review has zero open items.
- No changed production module is imported by the Control UI. Existing shared ownership is browser-safe and unchanged.

Earlier-head CI exposed a separate main regression introduced by #197697, reproduced on the exact main parent and attributed to its introducing commit. Upstream repaired it in #197976. Final-head CI is green; no rerun or admin exception is needed.

prs.title: fix(browser): keep shared tabs visible when Chrome blocks automation
prs.body:
## Merge Brief

Shared tabs can disappear when Chrome correctly refuses debugger access to a protected extension frame. This keeps the tab visible with the native refusal and prevents the agent from diagnosing it as disconnected. The existing CDP exclusion contract is unchanged; there is no permission, extension-package, or persistent-state change. The fix is backed by red/green regressions and a real unpacked-extension recovery run. Please review the separation between user inventory and attachable CDP targets. Temporary 1Password suppression is deliberately separate (#198004).

Closes #198002.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a still-shared browser tab disappears from the agent's inventory when Chrome blocks debugger attachment, so using it reports a missing tab rather than the actual restriction.

## User Impact

User impact: the tab remains listed with `automationBlockedReason`; control reports Chrome's refusal and asks for a fresh snapshot after the restriction clears. Healthy tabs remain usable. This does not read protected extension content, disable another extension, dismiss website forms, or replay interrupted actions. No new extension release is required; the change is Gateway-side.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bridge already omits exact Chrome refusals from attachable CDP discovery. That is appropriate for Playwright, but it is not a complete inventory of the user's shared tabs. Record the refusal on the existing tab state, expose it through the existing descriptor endpoint, and retain those records in the user-facing list. The attachment owner records the observation for every failed acquisition, not just enumeration. Successful reattachment, URL change, or extension replacement clears it.

A retired Playwright Page can remain unresolved after its native target disappears from discovery. When the authoritative native inventory is already completely accounted for, that stale Page must not make the whole listing fail. Missing native targets and unrelated transient failures still fail instead of being reported as a complete partial list.

The patch follows the existing refusal classifier from #191578. It does not implement #193589's discovery timeouts or #186674's pending-navigation transport changes. No new manager, config setting, browser permission, or recovery loop is introduced. The additional files carry one output field through its type/schema/formatter/selection consumers.

## Evidence

- Identical focused regressions on base `565b3f99c21b`: **7 expected failures, 68 passes**. With the fix: **75/75 pass** across bridge refusal/recovery, profile inventory/selection, page enumeration, and model-facing output.
- Real Chrome for Testing **153.0.8010.12**, real unpacked OpenClaw extension, disposable profile, synthetic foreign-extension iframe: native `target_closed` detach and protected-origin refusal; blocked tab retained with reason; after removing the fixture frame, fresh snapshot, typing/readback, and Cancel all succeeded **through the repaired OpenClaw relay**, not a substitute browser connection. The protected fixture sentinel was absent from inventory output.
- Canonical production extension typecheck and `pnpm build:runtime` pass. Focused formatting, type-aware lint, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent local autoreview with owning source context identified a P2: focus/close could still dispatch a placeholder and report target-not-found. Both now use the same blocked-tab check, with regressions passing. No claim of whole-repository review.
- Author simplification: reuse the existing tab state and descriptor request; no additional polling, identity registry, or action-replay path. Negative coverage retains near-match refusals/transient failure behavior and unresolved native-target completeness.

Native proof is limited to the tested Chromium build and synthetic protected frame. Separate live Chrome 156/1Password experiments are documented in #198004; no claim is made that this branch was installed into that daily-use browser or production Gateway. The final native run observed one transient inventory error during detach propagation, followed by a successful separate settled-state read and complete recovery. Immediate transition reads are not claimed to be atomic; transient failures still fail the complete request. Earlier failed attempts are not counted as passes. Broad cross-platform checks are delegated to PR CI.

Release note: browser extension profiles now report shared tabs blocked by Chrome debugger restrictions instead of presenting them as missing/disconnected; restore control only after normal attachment succeeds.

prs.title: feat(agents): inspect workspace documents from the CLI
prs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `openclaw agents files list` and `openclaw agents files get <name>` to the existing `agents` command group.
- Forwards the two canonical read RPCs that already back the Control UI's **Agents → Files** view (`agents.files.list`, `agents.files.get`); the Gateway keeps every policy decision (bootstrap-name allowlist, `missing` vs `expectedAbsent`, 2 MiB read bound, symlink/hardlink refusal).
- `list` prints a terminal table (`name`, `state`, `size`, `updatedAt`); `get` writes the document body to stdout byte-for-byte — no trailing newline is added, an empty document stays empty — and metadata (bytes + SHA-256) goes to stderr. Both support `--json`, which prints the RPC result unchanged.
- A missing bootstrap document is **not** a CLI failure: it stays the Gateway's `missing` / `expectedAbsent` classification and exits `0`. A rejected name (e.g. `../etc/passwd`) is a Gateway error and exits non-zero with the Gateway's message.

Fixes #197715

## Linked context

- Issue: #197715 — bounded CLI forwarding surface for the already-shipped read RPCs.
- Canonical owner: `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-files.ts`; protocol schemas `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-files.ts`.
- Existing consumers that prove the contract is live: Control UI `ui/src/pages/agents/files.ts:143`, e2e feature set `ui/src/e2e/agent-file-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts:85`, docs `docs/gateway/protocol/rpc-talk-config-and-agents.md:157`.
- Prior scoping issues reviewed: #116494 (closed) settled the *persisted memory* read side on `agents.workspace.*` and explicitly did not cover bootstrap documents; #75236 (closed) would add cursor pagination to `agents.files.list`, which this PR deliberately does not touch.

## What Problem This Solves

An operator who runs a headless or remote Gateway (VPS, container, another host) and works over SSH can see an agent's bootstrap documents in the Control UI, but the native CLI has no `files` verb. Today the only CLI path is the generic escape hatch:

```bash
openclaw gateway call agents.files.list --params '{"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

That requires knowing the RPC name and exact camelCase params, is not discoverable from `openclaw agents --help`, and returns a raw JSON envelope instead of the document the operator asked for. Reading the workspace directory directly is wrong for bridged/remote workspaces and bypasses the canonical owner's validation. This PR adds the missing surface without reimplementing any of that policy.

Agent selection follows the neighbouring `agents` commands: when `--agent` is omitted, the CLI resolves the configured agent from the local CLI config (`resolveAgentOperationAgentId`, the same helper as `agents bindings`); an explicit `--agent <id>` is forwarded verbatim without local validation, so an operator pointed at a Gateway with a different agent roster can name the target agent and let the Gateway's roster check decide.

Placement: the verbs live in the existing core `agents` group because the forwarded methods are core `agents.*` read RPCs; no new root command, plugin, export, or config key is introduced. The command module (`src/commands/agents.files.ts`) is self-contained, so a plugin-owned placement remains possible later without changing the RPC contract.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: On `origin/main` (`0518869e94e`) `openclaw agents files …` does not exist; after this patch the two read verbs connect to a real Gateway, forward the canonical RPCs, and format the results, including the missing-file and rejected-name paths.

**Real setup tested**: Node v24.22.1 on Windows. The after-fix pass below runs the **packaged build** from this branch — `pnpm openclaw …` drives the repository's own tsdown build (`dist`), built and stamped at commit `c0bd12b0999`; the CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (c0bd12b)`. The before-fix pass ran the same command against pristine `origin/main` (`0518869e94e`) through the repo's tsx loader. Isolated state dir `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-feature`, Gateway started with `gateway run --allow-unconfigured` on port `18812`; CLI connects through `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT` (no `--url` override). Workspace seeded with `SOUL.md` (2561 bytes, unique marker `PROOF-MARKER-AGENTS-FILES-7f3a`, sha256 `53ffd041…31482e`) and `AGENTS.md` (84 bytes); `USER.md`/`IDENTITY.md` were auto-created by agent admission.

**Revision 2 (review P2) setup**: the byte-for-byte fix at head `4987f2d4d84` was verified against a **fresh** isolated state dir `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-bytes` (no prior update intents) whose workspace contained a single `SOUL.md` of exactly 5 bytes, `hello`, **without a final newline** (sha256 `2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824`). The CLI ran through the repository's tsx loader — `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts …` (`source via tsx`, 6 s cold start, **not** a packaged `dist`; this is stated so the evidence is not read as a build claim). Gateway `gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18812` on the same state dir. Every stdout capture used `cmd /c "… > file"` so PowerShell could not normalize the bytes.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR="D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-feature"
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18812
# (a) before this patch, on pristine origin/main (source-run, no new verb):
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents files list
# (b) after this patch, packaged build from this branch:
pnpm openclaw agents files --help
pnpm openclaw agents files list
pnpm openclaw agents files list --json
pnpm openclaw agents files get SOUL.md > soul.out      # stdout captured byte-for-byte
pnpm openclaw agents files get MEMORY.md               # expected-absent document
pnpm openclaw agents files get ../etc/passwd           # rejected by the Gateway
# (c) revision 2 — byte-for-byte stdout check against a fresh isolated state:
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agents files get SOUL.md --agent main > out.bin
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```text

# Gateway-side receipt for the same call (real RPC round-trip, not a local stub):

# --json mode (RPC result printed unchanged, exit 0)
$ pnpm openclaw agents files list --json

# get: document body verbatim on stdout, metadata on stderr (exit 0)

# 53ffd041525d9eea635add2286518cd1369e4509f6e031dc0643f81ba531482e — identical to the seeded file):
```

```text
# (c) REVISION 2 — the P2 fix, same mechanism the review flagged, real Gateway, fresh isolated state.
# seed: proof-state-bytes/workspace/SOUL.md = "hello" — 5 bytes, NO final newline

        ^ byte-identical to the document; revision 1 emitted 6 bytes here
stderr: Agent file SOUL.md, 5 bytes, sha256 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824
# Gateway receipt for the same call:
[ws] ⇄ res ✓ agents.files.get 1913ms bytes=400 conn=78e4fa58…6a23 id=2:02a549eb-7…df66

# The pre-fix writer that revision 1 used for document bytes, reproduced directly (real RuntimeEnv, no mocks):
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-newline.mts hello > w.bin      # defaultRuntime.writeStdout("hello")
stdout: 6 bytes · 68 65 6c 6c 6f 0a   ("hello\n" — one invented byte, the reported P2)
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-newline.mts --empty > e.bin    # defaultRuntime.writeStdout("")
stdout: 1 byte  · 0a                 ("\n" — an empty document became one newline)

# Revision 2 no longer routes document bytes through that writer; the command writes them raw:
$ git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- src/commands/agents.files.ts
 src/commands/agents.files.ts | 174 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
# src/commands/agents.files.ts: writeDocumentBytes() -> process.stdout.write(content)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The new verbs are discoverable from `agents --help`, resolve the configured default agent on their own, and complete a real RPC round-trip against the isolated Gateway (`⇄ res ✓ agents.files.list` logged for the list call; the rejected `get` logged as `⇄ res ✗ agents.files.get`; the successful `get` is proven by the returned bytes: 2561 bytes, SHA-256 identical to the seeded file). Text mode renders the same file set the RPC returns (`MEMORY.md` classified `optional` because it is an expected-absent bootstrap file, `IDENTITY.md` absent because the list filter excludes it). `get SOUL.md` emitted the file bytes unchanged (sha256 matches the seeded file) and kept decoration off stdout. The rejected name produced `unsupported file "../etc/passwd"` and a non-zero exit — the CLI added no validation of its own. The `--json` form returns that same canonical object unchanged (content + hash for `SOUL.md`; `missing: true` + `expectedAbsent: true` for `MEMORY.md`), and an explicit `--agent ghost` is forwarded as-is and rejected by the Gateway (`agent "ghost" not found`, exit 1), so an explicit selector is never silently replaced by local config. In revision 2 the same `get` also emits exactly the document bytes: the 5-byte seeded file produced a 5-byte stdout with an identical sha256 (the pre-fix writer produced 6 bytes for the same read), the Gateway logged `⇄ res ✓ agents.files.get`, and the unit suite asserts the exact bytes handed to `process.stdout.write` for a document without a final newline, an empty document (0 bytes), and a result returned without `content` (no synthetic write).

**What was not tested**: (1) A completely fresh empty state dir was not exercised against the Gateway; empty-state rendering is covered by the unit test (`lists workspace documents with missing and optional classification`). (2) Remote transport via `--url/--token/--password` was not exercised, and a remote Gateway with a different agent roster was not exercised positively; the commands use the same `addGatewayClientOptions` / `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport` path as the neighbouring `agents bindings` command, and the `--agent ghost` run shows an explicit id is forwarded and validated by the Gateway, not by the CLI. (3) Symlinked workspace files (#136485) remain the Gateway's existing refusal — this PR does not change that policy. (4) Non-Windows hosts were not run; packaging was exercised only on win32-x64. (5) The pre-fix CLI binary was not re-run end-to-end at revision 2; the trailing-newline defect was reproduced directly through the real `defaultRuntime.writeStdout` writer that revision 1 used (5-byte input → 6 bytes; empty input → 1 byte), while the end-to-end run above is the fixed CLI at `4987f2d`. (6) The revision-2 byte capture ran the source tree through the repository's tsx loader, not a freshly built `dist`; revision 1's packaged-CLI evidence still stands for registration and formatting.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: The evidence came from a Windows host over loopback against a packaged build of this branch (`pnpm openclaw` → tsdown `dist`, commit `c0bd12b0999`); packaging on Linux/macOS was not exercised. The `--json`/`--agent` runs above were captured through the same packaged entry invoked directly as `node scripts/run-node.mjs` (the command `pnpm openclaw` delegates to). The Gateway logged a runtime-only auth token for the isolated state dir. No mocks, stubs, or unit-test output are used as behavior proof above.

## Before / after

- **Before** (pristine `origin/main`, `0518869e94e`): `OpenClaw agents has no command "files".` — exit 1. The only path was `gateway call agents.files.list --params '{"agentId":"main"}' --json`.
- **After**: `agents files list` renders the canonical file set as a table (or raw JSON), `agents files get SOUL.md` streams the document bytes with size/hash on stderr, `agents files get ../etc/passwd` exits non-zero with the Gateway's `unsupported file` message, and `agents files get MEMORY.md` keeps the canonical `optional` classification instead of inventing an error.
- **After (revision 2, review P2)**: `agents files get` output is now byte-identical to the workspace document: a 5-byte file with no final newline yields exactly 5 bytes (before the fix the shared runtime writer appended one, yielding 6), an empty document yields 0 bytes (before: one newline), and a document that already ends in a newline is unchanged.

## Tests and validation

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/agents.files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ✓ lists workspace documents with missing and optional classification
  ✓ resolves the configured default agent when --agent is omitted
  ✓ forwards an explicit agent id verbatim, including a blank one
  ✓ emits the untouched list result as JSON
  ✓ writes the exact document bytes to stdout without appending a newline
  ✓ keeps an empty document at zero bytes
  ✓ leaves a document that already ends with a newline unchanged
  ✓ does not synthesize bytes when the Gateway returns no content
  ✓ treats an absent optional document as a normal state
  ✓ reports a rejected document name and exits nonzero
  ✓ emits the untouched get result as JSON
  Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 11 passed (11) · duration 23.04s · exit 0 (post-rebase)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ✓ dispatches agents files list/get
  Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 27 passed (27) · duration 407.37s · exit 0

node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json <5 files>
  Found 0 warnings and 0 errors. (4 TS files, 8 threads)
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <5 files> (4 TS + docs/cli/agents.md)
  All matched files use the correct format.
```

- `pnpm openclaw agents files --help` on the packaged build printed the registration above (`get` / `list`), confirming the command path is wired in the built CLI, not just in source.
- No new `as` assertions in the new files; the RPC result type comes from the protocol schema via the generic `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport<T>`.
- Registration test file `src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts` was extended with `dispatches agents files list/get` and re-run on this branch: 27 passed.
- No protocol/schema changes, no new config keys, no retention changes, no docs JSON changes.
- `src/cli/command-catalog.ts` registers `agents files list|get` with `loadPlugins: "never"` and `ownsProtocolStdout: true`, matching the neighbouring `agents bind/bindings/unbind` entries. Without this the new verbs inherited the broad `["agents"]` policy (`loadPlugins: "always"`), and a startup doctor notice could be printed to the same stdout that `get` uses for document bytes.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)
- Yes: two new read-only subcommands under `openclaw agents files`. No existing command or output changes.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)
- No new config keys, env vars, migrations, or state layout.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`No`)
- The commands reuse the existing authenticated Gateway client options (`addGatewayClientOptions` + `callGatewayFromCliWithTransport`). They do not read workspace paths from the local disk, do not widen the Gateway's name allowlist, and add no write path. The write RPC `agents.files.set` stays UI-only in this proposal.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Surface drift: a CLI that re-implements or contradicts the Gateway's bootstrap semantics (allowlist, `expectedAbsent`, hidden `IDENTITY.md`) would confuse operators. Secondary: `get` growing decoration on stdout and breaking piping into files.

How is that risk mitigated?
- Zero duplicated validation: the CLI forwards `agentId`/`name` and formats the typed result; reject/missing decisions stay in `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-files.ts`. Document bytes are written with a raw `process.stdout.write` (the shared runtime writer appends a missing trailing newline, which would corrupt redirection), metadata goes to stderr, and `--json` prints the result unchanged (covered by tests that assert the exact bytes handed to stdout). Missing files keep exit 0, matching the schema's explicit "absence is a normal workspace state" contract.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review of the (unchanged) feature direction; the one author-actionable finding from the first review is fixed in revision 2 (`4987f2d`).

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- CI on the pushed head and the maintainer owner decision. Nothing is waiting on me for correctness: the P2 output defect is fixed and covered by a test that asserts the exact bytes handed to stdout.

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- ClawSweeper first review (`c0bd12b`, gold shrimp 3/6) — `[P2] Preserve document bytes without adding a final newline` (`src/commands/agents.files.ts:166`): fixed by writing the document with a raw stdout write instead of the newline-terminating runtime writer.
- ClawSweeper note `Low-value test src/commands/agents.files.test.ts`: the mocked-`writeStdout` assertion was replaced with assertions on the bytes actually handed to `process.stdout.write`, covering empty content, content without a final newline, and a document returned without content.
- ClawSweeper `Decision needed` (owner approval for a new core agents surface): outside author control; the PR stays bounded to forwarding the two existing read RPCs and waits on a maintainer decision.

## Update 2026-11-13 — the only red check is resolved by an upstream fix; branch rebased

The previous head (`4987f2d4d84f`) had exactly one failing job: `checks-node-changed-compact-small-31` → `src/cli/help-exit.process.test.ts > CLI help process exit > exits naturally after precomputed root help`, aborting with `Error: CLI help imported TLS from .../src/cli/one-shot-exit.ts` (the repository's `forbidTlsImport` guard). I reproduced that exact child process **outside vitest** (single `node --import tsx --import forbidTlsImport.mjs src/entry.ts --help` invocation, 2.7 s) on pristine `origin/main` and on this branch's base, and traced it to `src/entry.ts` importing `./cli/one-shot-exit.js` before the root-help fast path while `src/cli/one-shot-exit.ts` value-imported `node:tls`.

Upstream fixed the root cause in `d30e45c3f48` — `fix(cli): restore lightweight help and cleanup test startup (#197936)`: `TLSSocket` is now acquired lazily inside the exit watchdog via `process.getBuiltinModule("node:tls")`, keeping the precomputed help path free of TLS initialization. This branch is now rebased onto `origin/main` (`d30e45c3f48`, new head `31cf7923107`), and the rebase changed **none** of this PR's files: `git diff --stat <base>..origin/main -- src/commands/agents.files.ts src/commands/agents.files.test.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.ts src/cli/program/register.agent.test.ts docs/cli/agents.md src/cli/command-catalog.ts` was empty before the rebase.

After the rebase the same 3-second reproduction exits 0 and prints the full root help with no TLS guard trip:

```text
$ node --import tsx --import file:///D:/IdeaWork/openclaw/.scratch/helprepro/forbidTlsImport.mjs src/entry.ts --help
ELAPSED_S: 29.6  EXIT: 0  STDOUT_LINES: 139

OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (31cf792) — All your chats, one OpenClaw.

Usage: openclaw [options] [command]
```

The guard file used above is byte-for-byte the one the failing test installs (`guardSources.forbidTlsImport`). This confirms the red check was never caused by this patch (the pre-fix run of the same command on unmodified `origin/main` failed with the guard error; see the 2026-11-12T21:36Z comment on this PR) and that the new head should pass that shard.

prs.title: fix(ui): desktop group search misses accented group names typed in another Unicode form
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197982

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on desktop, **Search groups** in a session's **Move to group** menu shows "No groups match your search." when a group name and the typed query spell the same accented letter in different Unicode forms (precomposed `ü` versus `u` plus a combining diaeresis).

## User Impact

User impact: desktop **Search groups** finds accented group names typed in either Unicode form, as the phone sheet already does, and keeps showing and assigning the name exactly as stored.

## Why This Change Was Made

The desktop filter in `groupOptions()` (`ui/src/components/session-menu-view.tsx`) lowercased the query and the names but did not NFC-normalize them. It now normalizes both sides of the comparison, the same way the phone sheet's filter of this list has since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191945; the desktop field was added later in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197653. The menu still labels and selects the stored name, and an unaccented query stays distinct. The docs line that limited this behavior to phones now covers both.

## Evidence

Tested at `4acf06f92b1` (base `main` `4ab02e3c087`).

A real Gateway started with isolated state and the Control UI built from each side, driven in Chromium at 1200x844 by a temporary browser test (not part of this PR). It creates one session and nine groups through `sessions.groups.create`, including `München` (decomposed) and `Café` (precomposed), opens **Move to group** from the session's context menu, types each query into **Search groups**, and records the shown labels with their code points.

Before (base `main` `4ab02e3c087`):

```text
query (code points)      shown groups                        "No groups match your search."
münchen (6d fc ...)      none                                yes
café (... 65 301)        none                                yes
munchen (ASCII)          none                                yes
doc (ASCII)              Docs                                no
```

After (this PR):

```text
query (code points)      shown groups (stored code points)   "No groups match your search."
münchen (6d fc ...)      München (4d 75 308 6e 63 68 65 6e)  no
café (... 65 301)        Café (43 61 66 e9)                  no
munchen (ASCII)          none                                yes
doc (ASCII)              Docs                                no
```

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: münchen shows no groups](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261112-196046-desktop-group-search-nfc/before-search-munchen.png) | ![After: münchen shows München](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261112-196046-desktop-group-search-nfc/after-search-munchen.png) |

Observed result: both canonically equivalent queries now show their group under its stored form; the unaccented query and the ASCII search behave as before.

Checks: `pnpm test ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (54 passed). The changed "searches long group lists" case now holds a decomposed `"Mu\u0308nchen"`, expects the decomposed query `"mu\u0308nchen"` to show it, then types the precomposed `"m\u00fcnchen"` and expects the move to the stored name. Removing either side's `.normalize("NFC")` makes it fail; on base it fails with `Expected enabled menu action in an open panel: move-to-group:Mu%CC%88nchen`. Changed-file lint, `oxfmt --check` and the test-lines ratchet pass. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI `checks-node-compact-small-1`, and `openclaw/ci-gate` that aggregates it (no other job failed): the 2 failures in `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (the PR wrapper inventory is missing six `packages/openclaw-id-protocol` files) also fail locally on this PR's base `main` `4ab02e3c087` without this change, with the same missing-file list; this PR does not touch those files.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui/src/components/session-menu.test.ts` | 4.8 s | 5.5 s (`checks-ui (2/3)`, 6.4 s with setup) |

Size: production +2/-2 in one function, test lines net 0 (one existing case reuses its group list, input step and selection step), docs +2/-2. No helper or state was added; the inline normalization matches the other Control UI search filters.

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `4ab02e3c087` to head `4acf06f92b1`, priority P0–P1: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed","head":"4acf06f92b16f015f6fc296bd43c02e4d48034c7","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

Not covered:

- Other Control UI searches that lowercase without NFC are left out because an open PR changes each file: the desktop **Assign to…** owner search (`ui/src/components/session-menu-details-solid.tsx`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189518), the personal session group dialog's filter (`ui/src/components/personal-session-group-dialog-view.tsx`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195407), the file preview filter (`ui/src/components/file-preview-modal.tsx`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191694), and the chat context panel filter (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-context-panel.tsx`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192350). That PR also changes `session-menu.test.ts` and `sessions-and-sidebar.md`, in other sections than this one.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep Gateway shell usable on restricted continuation turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authorized continuation with a finite tool allowlist can no longer call its registered Gateway shell tools after a native-shell turn.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateway command execution and process follow-up remain available under the continuation's current tool policy, without enabling unrestricted native Code Mode. This is distinct from the automation receipt-read permission proposal in #197551.

## Why This Change Was Made

A finite allowlist disables native Code Mode. The shell builder also required native Code Mode before constructing `gateway_exec` and `gateway_process`; a retained catalog advertised these names but excluded the replacement raw `exec`/`process` names. The resulting bridge had no admitted shell binding.

Remove only the native-enabled prerequisite for the existing host-owned, Gateway-pinned aliases. Preserve current allowlist filtering, exclusions, sandbox/node separation, and command approval. No new policy option, credential handling, or permission grant.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the original implementation: the retained bridge contains only `message`, not `gateway_exec`.
- Candidate passes the 82-test dynamic tool suite. After independent review corrected the new test's Unix-only command, its portable command/output and message-only denial control pass again.
- The focused test builds an unrestricted catalog, applies a finite `exec`/`process`/`message` cap with native tools disabled, reuses the registered catalog, executes a real `echo` command, then verifies a message-only cap denies execution.
- Scoped type-aware lint, extension typecheck, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent source review found no production defect; one test portability finding was fixed.

Limits: this is production host/tool-builder/bridge proof, not a naturally triggered end-to-end completion or live installation verification. It reproduces a mechanism consistent with the reported continuation failure; the historical turn's exact effective cap was not recovered. No installed Gateway, scheduler jobs, or customer data changed. Draft for upstream review; no merge/release claim.
