prs.title: fix(agents): plugin agent_end hooks fail after a turn that called dispatch_action
prs.body:
Closes #197940

Related: #197947 is an open draft for the same issue; this PR carries the regression test and Gateway proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every plugin `agent_end` handler fails with `Plugin invocation scope is closed` after an embedded turn in which the model called a tool through Tool Search `dispatch_action`.

## User Impact

User impact: plugins that keep memory, logs or telemetry at `agent_end` (including bundled `skill-workshop`) run again after Tool Search dispatch turns, which is the default tool surface. Turns that call tools directly already worked and behave the same.

Risk: low. Only the bundled asynchronous `agent_end` path changes ordering, and only when a message loader is bound. A slow transcript read now delays the end of the run instead of losing every handler.

## Why This Change Was Made

A turn with nested tool activity (only `dispatch_action` records it) hands `agent_end` its messages through a loader that reads that activity back from the transcript store. `runAgentEndSideEffectsAsync` started hook delivery in a detached launcher, so it returned before the read finished. The run then released its prepared plugin invocation scope, and when the read completed, each handler's admission hit the closed scope and threw. Turns without nested activity got their messages after one microtask, before the release, which is why direct tool calls were fine.

`runAgentEndSideEffectsAsync` now awaits the message hydration (new internal `startAgentHarnessAgentEndHook`) and then starts handlers without waiting for them, so they are admitted while the turn's scope is still open. Handler execution stays fire-and-forget with unref timeouts, as before. The closed-scope check, caller context, the SDK-exported `runAgentHarnessAgentEndHook` and `awaitAgentHarnessAgentEndHook`, and the deprecated synchronous `runAgentEndSideEffects` are unchanged.

Cost: on a dispatch turn with an `agent_end` subscriber, finalization now waits for that one transcript read, which previously ran right after it. `before_agent_finalize` already awaits the same read in the foreground. No read happens when no plugin subscribes.

`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` loses the `agent-end-side-effects.test.ts` entry because that mock now carries a `// mock-isolation:` reason; the mock export ratchet requires the stale entry to be removed.

## Evidence

Regression test, real plugin admission (`src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.test.ts`): a real plugin instance, a retained `PluginInvocationScope` and a real hook runner with a wrapped `agent_end` handler. The message loader resolves after a macrotask, and the scope is released as soon as `runAgentEndSideEffectsAsync` returns, as the embedded run does.

- Base `4efd662cc2c` with only the new test: 1 failed, 9 passed. The handler is refused with `[hooks] agent_end handler from agent-end-probe failed: Plugin invocation scope is closed`.
- Head: passes.

Tests on head (`pnpm test <files>`, 18 files, 312 tests passed): harness lifecycle helpers, agent-end side effects, plugin invocation scope, embedded-runner nested tool activity, phase lifecycle, stream finalize/settle/prepare, execution and session settle, attempt result, Tool Search executor, code-mode continuation and bridge lifecycle, and CLI `agent_end` paths. The suggested `vitest.unit.config.ts` invocation matches none of these files, so they were run through `pnpm test`, which routes them to the agents and plugins configs.

`pnpm check:changed --base 4efd662cc2c`: typecheck (core and core tests), lint, format, mock export ratchet, import cycles and the other lanes pass. The dead export scan reports `src/gateway/trusted-proxy-git-coauthor.ts: resolveTrustedProxyGitCoauthor`, which this change does not touch; `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports the same on clean `4efd662cc2c`.

Real Gateway run: one fresh isolated Gateway per row (`/v1/chat/completions`, loopback, local OpenAI-compatible model). Two `agent_end` handlers were registered: a fixture plugin and bundled `skill-workshop`.

```
base-dispatch  turn=dispatch tools=tool_search,session_status,dispatch_action(openclaw:core:session_status) agent_end=FAILED handler_failures=2
head-dispatch  turn=dispatch tools=tool_search,session_status,dispatch_action(openclaw:core:session_status) agent_end=ok handler_failures=0
base-direct    turn=direct tools=session_status agent_end=ok handler_failures=0
head-direct    turn=direct tools=session_status agent_end=ok handler_failures=0
```

The dispatch rows use Tool Search at its default. The direct rows set `tools.toolSearch: false` and call `session_status` directly. On base, both handlers log `failed: Plugin invocation scope is closed`. On head there are no handler failure lines, and the fixture records `agent_end` with 8 messages. `skill-workshop` does not log on success, so on head its result is shown only by the absence of a failure line.

prs.title: feat(agents): let the gateway tool read update status
prs.body:
## Summary

- The agent-facing `gateway` tool can now read the Gateway's update state with `{ action: "update.status" }`, forwarding to the existing read-only `update.status` RPC through the same `callGatewayTool` path that already backs `config.get` / `config.schema.lookup`.
- `update.status` stays available when `allowConfigReads` is false. The restricted tool variant is the one that schedules `update.run`, so it is the one that most needs the read: "why did my update fail?" is a question the restricted agent is expected to answer without handing it config read authority.
- No new RPC and no new write authority: the action is read-only, `update.run` / `restart` / `update.cleanup` admission is untouched, and the change is a single enum + dispatch branch in `src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts`.
- The tool description and the Codex prompt snapshot that mirrors it (`codex-dynamic-tools.telegram-direct.json`) move together, per the prompt-prefix contract. Both variants were shortened to 165 chars ("Owner/operator:" replaces "Owner request/operator schedule:") so the tool directory no longer truncates the description.

Fixes #188320

## Linked context

- Issue: #188320 — the `gateway` tool could schedule `update.run` and restart the Gateway but could not read the update state it was about to change.
- Review history on this PR: the 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper round raised three P2s (signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit). All three are fixed on this head.
- **This revision answers the one remaining reviewer ask** — *"Provide a successful real agent invocation of `update.status` with configuration reads allowed and withheld; the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body"*. The previous revision's `tools.invoke` capture aborted on agent-database admission, so the new forwarding branch never ran. This body replaces that capture with **two successful executions of the real tool object, one per variant**, against a live Gateway (see below), and explains honestly why the `tools.invoke` wrapper path is still blocked on this host.

## Revision note (rebase)

The capture below was taken at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`. The branch has since been **rebased onto `origin/main` to clear a merge conflict** (`mergeable: dirty`), so the current head is `8862cfd8bddc482a2ddfbe7caa208b2a9d0fbfd2`. The patch content is unchanged — same 8 files, `+63 −22` — and the only bytes that moved were the generated prompt-snapshot fixtures, which were regenerated with `scripts/generate-prompt-snapshots.ts --write` rather than hand-merged (`Prompt snapshots are current (6 files)`). Because the captured `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is literally the checkout's HEAD at capture time, it reads `3c654c1b48f…` and not the post-rebase sha; that is the expected consequence of the rebase and is called out here instead of being silently edited.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Before this patch the assembled `gateway` tool's action enum contained `config.get`, `config.schema.lookup`, `update.run`, `restart` and `update.cleanup` only, so `{ action: "update.status" }` was rejected at the tool boundary and an agent could not read the update state it was about to change or diagnose a failed update. After the patch the same call forwards to the canonical read-only `update.status` RPC and returns the recorded state, and it does so in **both** variants — including the restricted one that has configuration reads withheld.

**Real setup tested**: Windows host, Node v24.22.1, branch `feat/agent-update-status` at head `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, TypeScript sources executed directly through `scripts/tsx.mjs` (source runtime, not a packaged dist), **brand-new** isolated state directory `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` (empty before this run, so the agent database is created and migrated from scratch rather than reused), Gateway bound to loopback port 18815 with `--allow-unconfigured`, reaching `post-ready.startup-maintenance` at total 387.0 s before any RPC was issued.
- **Runtime**: node v24.22.1 + `scripts/tsx.mjs` loader (source runtime); no packaged `dist` build was used for this capture.

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:

```bash
export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2
export OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=18815
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port 18815

# (1) Ground truth: the canonical RPC the new branch forwards to.
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway call update.status --timeout 180000 --json

# (2) The changed code path itself, exercised once per variant against the same
#     live Gateway. This is a throwaway harness (NOT part of the patch); it
#     imports the production factory and calls the production tool object.
#     Variant selection is the same input the real assembly passes:
#       src/agents/openclaw-tools.gateway.ts:23 ->
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `update.status` now executes through the tool object in **both** variants and returns the live Gateway's real update state — `schedule.install.git.currentSha` is `3c654c1b48f51618882032bc33e2ed832a6ed39d`, which is exactly `git rev-parse HEAD` of this checkout, and `repositoryUrl` is this fork. That SHA is read out of the running Gateway's own install state, so the payload cannot be synthesized by the calling process. The two action enums are the direct, structural answer to the reviewer's question: the restricted schema is `["update.run","restart","update.cleanup","update.status"]` — `update.status` is present while `config.get` and `config.schema.lookup` are absent — and the full schema is the six-action superset. The restricted variant ran much faster (210 ms vs 8079 ms); the likely explanation is a warm connection on the second call, and I am not claiming more than that — both executions are real calls against the same Gateway, which the per-variant backend connections in (4) corroborate. `lastRun` / `activeRun` are absent because no update was ever run in this fresh isolated state directory; that is the honest shape of a clean Gateway, not a filtered field.

**What was not tested**: a packaged `dist` build of this head (both captures use the tsx source runtime); the **`tools.invoke` wrapper path end-to-end** — it is still blocked on this host by `Agent database execution admission is closed` (see the limitation section below), which fires inside the Gateway's agent-database admission *before* the tool body runs, so it cannot exercise this patch either way; a full model-driven agent turn on Discord/Telegram that selects this action from the model's tool list; a real update run producing `lastRun` / `activeRun` records (no update was deliberately triggered in a throwaway state directory); and any `openclaw update status` CLI surface, which does not exist for this action.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints**: The `tools.invoke` RPC (which is how the previous revision tried to reach the tool) is gated by the Gateway's agent-database execution admission. On a brand-new state directory that admission still ends in a schema handshake failure — `agent database remains degraded agentId=main … reason="Agent database execution admission is closed"`, with the Gateway log advising `Use the newer install that supports schema 41 or newer`. The `repairHint` is `openclaw doctor --fix`, which is out of scope for this run (it mutates a deliberately throwaway state directory and is not something a contributor should run to manufacture proof). Rather than stop there, the capture above drives the **same production tool object** the assembly builds, so the new forwarding branch genuinely executes and returns Gateway-served data — but it is invoked directly instead of through an agent-mediated turn, and that distinction is stated rather than blurred. Note also that a **successful** `update.status` does not emit a `⇄ res ✓ update.status` line in this build (only failures and the outer `tools.invoke` RPC are logged at that level), so the round-trip evidence here is the backend connection log plus the self-referential `currentSha`, not a `⇄ res ✓` line — I did not fabricate one. No secrets, tokens or real user state were used: every command ran against `D:/tools/openclaw-proof-state-prfix2` on loopback port 18815.

## Tests and validation

- Baseline regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on this head → **`Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 15 passed (15)`, duration 368.90 s, exit 0**. This is the pre-existing suite around the changed file, so it covers "did the patch break the existing actions" rather than only the new branch; the run includes the pre-existing `preserves update diagnostic Unicode in tool results` case alongside the new `update.status` assertions.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts` → **0 warnings, 0 errors**.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check` on the same four files → **All matched files use the correct format.**
- CI on head `3c654c1b48f`: **110 check runs, 0 failures** (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` pass, `openclaw/ci-gate` pass, `pr-failure-report` skipped as expected). The compiled agents-tools suites are covered by CI, not by this Windows host.
- Unit coverage added on this branch: `gateway-tool.test.ts` ("reads update status even when config reads are withheld" — calls the tool with `allowConfigReads: false` and asserts the forwarded method), `gateway-tool.assembly.test.ts` (action present in the coding profile and in the full profiles after `config.schema.lookup`; grants matrix), `tool-search.test.ts` + prompt snapshot (new description text).

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`)

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes`)

What is the highest-risk area?
- The risk is the agent tool surface: one more action becomes reachable from a model-driven turn, and that action crosses the Gateway boundary. The action is read-only, but it does expose update channel/schedule state to the restricted tool variant that previously could not read it — the capture above shows exactly that enlarged surface (`update.status` inside a schema that still withholds `config.get`).

How is that risk mitigated?
- The action maps to the existing `update.status` RPC with no parameters and no write admission; it does not touch `update.run`, `restart` or `update.cleanup`. It is enumerated in the schema (no free-form method passthrough), so an unknown action still fails closed at the tool boundary. The restricted-profile availability is intentional and asserted in tests; the full-profile grants matrix keeps the owner/config-read boundary unchanged. The dispatch branch sits *before* the `allowConfigReads` guard rather than inside it, so the read is available without widening the config-read gate.

## Current review state

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review (owner decision) on the bounded status action. No author action is pending on the code; this body rewrite is the author action for the proof gap the review named.

What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof?
- Waiting on the maintainer decision requested by the review. Open external proof, stated plainly: a packaged `dist` capture, a model-driven turn that picks the action, and the `tools.invoke` wrapper path (blocked by the agent-database schema handshake on this host).

Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed?
- 2026-10-30 ClawSweeper P2s: signal/result assertions, assembled-tool contracts, directory description limit — all fixed on this head.
- The 2026-11-12 review's single "Before merge" item ("add real behavior proof … the supplied invocation aborts before the changed tool body") is addressed by the two successful per-variant executions above; the stale "not producible in this checkout" note is retracted.

## Before/After

- **Before**: `{ action: "update.status" }` was outside the tool's action enum in both variants, so the tool boundary rejected it and an agent could only schedule updates, never read their state. The captured "before" is structural — the four-action / five-action enums on `origin/main` — because a live pre-patch build capture would require reverting the patch on a second host.
- **After**: the same call forwards to the canonical `update.status` RPC and returns `{sentinel, updateAvailable, effectiveChannel, schedule}` in both the full variant (6-action enum) and the restricted variant (4-action enum), with `schedule.install.git.currentSha` matching this checkout's HEAD.
- **Boundary**: the action is enumerated in the Zod schema (`stringEnum`), not a free-form method passthrough, so an unknown action still fails tool-input validation before any Gateway call is made — the enum is closed and the new action is an explicit addition, visible in the two enum dumps above.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): report physical line number for malformed JSON manifest rows
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `source-manifest.mjs` reads a JSONL manifest and one row is malformed, the operator gets V8's `JSON.parse` position instead of a location:

```
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
```

`line 1 column 2` is the position *inside that row*, not the row's position in the file. On a dump with hundreds of rows the diagnostic points nowhere.

- Problem: `snapshot` and `loadManifest` call `JSON.parse` directly inside the line loop; the syntax error propagates to the top-level handler, which prints only `error.message`.
- Solution: count physical lines (blank lines included) while iterating and rethrow as `<file>:<line>: line is not valid JSON`. The raw row is deliberately not echoed: manifests carry private payloads (message text, author fields), and the file plus physical line already locate the fault.
- Changed: `extensions/knowledge/skills/knowledge-source-ingest/scripts/source-manifest.mjs` (both `JSON.parse` sites) and one regression folded into the existing `source-manifest.test.ts` case.
- Unchanged: valid-manifest behavior, output format, exit codes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The manifest tool is the ingest boundary; naming the exact offending line is the minimal correct diagnostic. Wrapping only the two `JSON.parse` sites keeps the change surgical and preserves the existing per-row validations (header checks, `Item N has no stable string id`, ...) that still throw their own messages.

- Best fix: local try/catch rethrow with the counted physical line, reusing the existing top-level `console.error(error.message)` path.
- Alternative rejected: a whole-file validating parser — larger change, different error ordering and timing.
- Risk: only the error text for malformed input changes; it deliberately omits row contents.

## User Impact

A malformed JSON row now reports the file and physical line, e.g. `-:3: line is not valid JSON`, so the offending row is directly locatable without echoing its contents (or others' private payloads) to stderr.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry point: base vs this branch

One capture, real CLI runs. Base = `main` at `28d20f9532f`, whose `source-manifest.mjs` blob is identical to the PR base `4efd662`; head = this branch at `de40cbd80ca`. Fixture `run/bad.manifest.jsonl` is two blank lines followed by `{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}` — a malformed row on physical line 3. The marker is a synthetic canary: it must never reach stderr.

```text
$ node source-manifest.mjs plan --current run/bad.manifest.jsonl    # base: main 28d20f9532f
exit 1
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
$ node source-manifest.mjs plan --current run/bad.manifest.jsonl    # head: de40cbd80ca
exit 1
run/bad.manifest.jsonl:3: line is not valid JSON
$ printf '\n\n{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}\n' | node source-manifest.mjs snapshot --input - ...   # base
exit 1
Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1 (line 1 column 2)
$ printf '\n\n{bad "PRIVATE_LEAK_MARKER_9f3c" json}\n' | node source-manifest.mjs snapshot --input - ...   # head
exit 1
-:3: line is not valid JSON
```

`-` is the stdin filename. Same raw log: [terminal-capture.log](https://github.com/shuisadev/openclaw-pr-197722-proof/blob/main/terminal-capture.log).

### Media proof ✨

![source-manifest line number before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shuisadev/openclaw-pr-197722-proof/main/source-manifest-line-number-proof.svg)

### Regression

The existing `source-manifest.test.ts` case already ran the malformed-row check through `snapshot` only. It now runs one fixture through **both** changed call sites and asserts, per case, that the message names physical line 3 and that the canary is absent:

- `snapshot`, stdin — `-:3: line is not valid JSON`
- `plan --current`, file — `malformed.manifest.jsonl:3: line is not valid JSON`

Both assertions use `expect.soft`, so each case reports independently instead of hiding the second behind the first.

Base (main's `source-manifest.mjs`, blob `63f33e4d`, with this test) — both cases fail:

```text
→ expected 'Command failed: ...' to match /-:3: line is not valid JSON/
→ expected 'Command failed: ...' to match /malformed\.manifest\.jsonl:3: line is…/
Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)
```

Head — `npx vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts extensions/knowledge/src/source-manifest.test.ts`: `Tests 3 passed (3)`.

Open PR collision check: searched the latest open PRs' changed files for `source-manifest.mjs`; none touched it. The sibling entry about `--input -` UTF-8 decoding errors (`encoded data was not valid`) is a different failure and is unchanged.

Closes #195802

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a scheduled session turn that fails shows only `Session event execution failed` in run history and disabled-job diagnostics.

## User Impact

User impact: operators see the real cause (for example the missing account binding and its repair command) when a scheduled automation fails.

The generic placeholder was recorded first, so the failed operation's own cause was never used. The placeholder now only applies when no cause exists.

prs.title: fix(tlon): align nickname mention boundary with ship pattern
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a Tlon group, mentioning the bot by its nickname with markdown formatting or a trailing `:` / `;` (e.g. `**nimbus** hi`, `nimbus: hello`) was silently dropped — the bot never replied, with no error or log — while the same mention by ship (`**~zod** hi`, `~zod: hello`) was answered normally.

```text
- Problem: `isBotMentioned` runs two parallel regexes — one for ship, one for nickname. #197037 widened the ship branch boundary to `(^|[\s*~])...(?)$|[\s*~,.!?;:])` so the `*`/`**`/`~~` markers that Tlon renders around bold/italic/strike text (and trailing `;`/`:`) don't break matching. The nickname branch was left at the narrow `(^|\s)...(?=\s|$|[,!?.])`, so the same user action that the ship branch accepts is dropped by the nickname branch.
- Solution: Align the nickname pattern's leading and trailing boundary character class with the ship pattern's, so both branches share `(^|[\s*~])` ... `(?=$|[\s*~,.!?;:])`.
- What changed: `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/utils.ts` — one regex literal in `isBotMentioned`; `extensions/tlon/src/security.test.ts` — extended the existing `it.each("detects mentions in Story")` table with `nimbus:`/`nimbus;`/bold/italics nickname stories.
- What did NOT change: ship matching, `stripBotMention`, `@all` handling, and the `nimbusy`/`prenimbus` non-match guards all keep their existing behavior.
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The ship and nickname branches live in the same function and represent the same user action (pointing at the bot); keeping two different boundary character classes is the latent inconsistency that #197037 left behind. The minimal, owner-aligned fix is to reuse the ship branch's already-reviewed boundary class for the nickname branch, instead of inventing a third class or a shared helper that would change more surface area. `~` in the leading class is harmless for nicknames (it only widens, never matches literal nickname chars) and keeps the two branches literally identical, so the next widening happens once in both branches.

- **Best fix**: yes — reuse the ship branch's already-merged boundary class so there's a single notion of "mention boundary" in this function.
- **Alternative**: extract a `mentionBoundary(needle)` builder so both branches share one owner. Rejected for this PR — it would rewrite the ship branch too and expand the diff/risk for no behavioral gain; the two literals are now byte-identical and easy to follow.
- **Risk**: low. The `nimbusy` / `prenimbus` guards still pass (verified), and the new class only adds `*`/`~`/`;`/`:` which are not legal nickname characters.

## User Impact

Tlon users who address the bot by its nickname (set from the bot's own Urbit profile) in the common chat forms `nimbus:`, `nimbus;`, `**nimbus**`, `*nimbus*` now get a reply, matching how `~zod:` and `**~zod**` already worked. No behavior change for non-mention text or for the existing `nimbus,`/`nimbusy`/`prenimbus` cases.

## Evidence

Regression test folded into the existing `it.each("detects mentions in Story")` table in `extensions/tlon/src/security.test.ts` (bold/italics nickname + `:`/`;` suffix stories). On the fix branch:

```text
✓ |extension-messaging| extensions/tlon/src/security.test.ts > detects mentions in Story [["nimbus: hello"],["nimbus; hello"],[{"bold":["nimbus"]}," hi"],[{"italics":["nimbus"]},"?"]]
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  25 passed (25)
```

On `origin/main` (production reverted, test kept) the same case fails:

```text
FAIL |extension-messaging| extensions/tlon/src/security.test.ts > detects mentions in Story [["nimbus: hello"],["nimbus; hello"],[{"bold":["nimbus"]}," hi"],[{"italics":["nimbus"]},"?"]]
AssertionError: expected false to be true
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 24 skipped (25)
```

Admission owner proof: the same probe drives the shipped `prepareTlonGroupAdmission` (the group ingress admission owner that calls `isBotMentioned`) and reports `isAdmissionAllowed()` — `true` is the exact condition under which `index.ts` dispatches the agent reply (`isAdmissionAllowed?.() === false` skips; otherwise `core.channel.inbound.dispatch`). HEAD (`df6116ffcaf`) run, current head:

```text
PASS | ship ~zod: hi (baseline) => admitted=true (expect true) text="~zod: hi" mentioned=true
PASS | nickname nimbus: hello (colon) => admitted=true (expect true) text="nimbus: hello" mentioned=true
PASS | nickname nimbus; hello (semicolon) => admitted=true (expect true) text="nimbus; hello" mentioned=true
PASS | nickname **nimbus** hi (bold) => admitted=true (expect true) text="**nimbus** hi" mentioned=true
PASS | nickname *nimbus* ? (italics) => admitted=true (expect true) text="*nimbus*?" mentioned=true
PASS | nimbusy guard => admitted=false (expect false) text="nimbusy" mentioned=false
PASS | prenimbus guard => admitted=false (expect false) text="prenimbus" mentioned=false
ALL PASS
```

Against `origin/main` `utils.ts` (production reverted, probe unchanged) the colon case fails — bug reproduced:

```text
FAIL | nickname nimbus: hello (colon) => admitted=false (expect true) text="nimbus: hello" mentioned=false
FAILED
```

Open PR collision check: no open PR touched `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/utils.ts`. #197057 (the only recent PR editing this file) was merged 2026-11-11 and its hunks sit at `renderInlineItem`/`extractInlineText` (lines 173+), with zero overlap with `isBotMentioned` (lines 46-76).

prs.title: fix(subagents): keep delegated tools and results working after yield
prs.body:
Related: #196199, #190670, #170562, #194024.

## What Problem This Solves

Our earlier Gateway logs showed children losing tool access or failing to return results after the parent yielded. Accepted work could still inherit the plugin call that had just ended.

**Current-main status:** the maintainer's real Telegram test with a Codex parent and child passed. Merged #197658 fixes a separate failed-child announcement path and is already installed here. A normal user-path reproduction for the broader failure on current main is still missing.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(memory): CLI-backed sessions never flush memory before native compaction
prs.body:
Related: #137613

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sessions on a CLI backend (for example `claude-cli`) never save durable memory before Claude's native auto-compaction, because the pre-compaction memory flush is skipped for CLI runtimes.

## User Impact

User impact: CLI-backed agents now write their pre-compaction memory notes the same way embedded sessions do, re-arming every 256 KiB of transcript growth. Native compaction stays owned by the backend. Existing sessions need no migration; rows written before this change never suppress a flush.

## Why This Change Was Made

Branch rewritten on current `main` (the previous head was ~27k commits behind and conflicted with the memory-flush restructure).

- Reply and command turns reach the flush only through the preflight-compaction `beforeCompaction` hook, and preflight returned before calling it for CLI sessions. CLI sessions now run that hook before returning to native compaction (codex and other non-CLI native owners are unchanged).
- CLI compaction counts never advance, so the compaction-cycle dedup would lock after one flush. CLI sessions dedup on a transcript-byte window persisted as `memoryFlush.cliRearmBucket`; only a `succeeded` record suppresses.
- The flush dispatches through the CLI backend with a `read`/`write` allowlist, and the host-minted `memoryFlushWritePath` is carried through CLI dispatch → loopback grant → gateway tool resolution, so the writer stays append-only to the prepared target (a memory trigger without one still fails closed). Provider-owned tool plans keep the original skip.
- The private flush prompt stays out of the CLI dispatch transcript.
- Threshold and CLI byte-window rules live in `memory-flush-cycle.ts` so `agent-runner-memory.ts` does not grow past its line cap.

## Evidence

**Live run** (OpenClaw 2026.11.2 with the equivalent change applied to the packaged dist, `claude-cli` runtime, Claude Code 2.1.296, `forceFlushTranscriptBytes` temporarily set to 4096 for the run):

```
15:48:13 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user          # turn 1, transcript below threshold
15:48:19 dispatching embedded run through CLI backend: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5
15:48:19 ... unavailable here: memory-triggered compaction runs expose only read and append-only write.
15:48:19 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-sonnet-5-5 trigger=memory      # turn 2: flush via CLI
15:48:22 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true
15:48:25 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true   # turn 3: no flush (same window)
session memoryFlush: {"kind":"succeeded","compactionCount":0,"cliRearmBucket":0}
```

Before the preflight-hook change, the same three turns produced no `trigger=memory` run. The flush model chose not to write for that filler transcript, so this run shows the bounded grant but not an actual append; the append-only writer is covered by the existing writer tests.

**Tests:** `agent-runner-memory.cli-flush.test.ts` (flush through CLI dispatch with the bounded grant; flush from the preflight hook without compacting — fails without the hook change; same-window suppression; re-arm on a new window; failed records do not suppress), `memory-flush-cycle.test.ts`, session-shape round trips for the bucket (including bucket-free older rows), CLI dispatch and grant-context forwarding. 48 related test files / 538 tests pass; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, oxfmt and the line-cap ratchet pass.

**Limits / decision needed:** this still needs the maintainer call from the earlier review — recurring CLI memory maintenance at a fixed 256 KiB re-arm interval. Each re-arm costs one flush turn on the configured memory-flush model.

prs.title: fix(slack): recover Socket Mode 3.2 native reconnect failures
prs.body:
Fixes #197952. Thanks @jorge-monalee for the report, the root-cause analysis and the deterministic repro.

## Problem

A Slack plugin installed from ClawHub (an unbundled archive) resolves `@slack/socket-mode` 3.2.0 at install time. In 3.2.0 the SDK's close handler calls `delayReconnectAttempt(() => this.start(), signal)`, and a Slack refresh (`disconnect` warning) calls `this.start()` directly. OpenClaw's native reconnect observer only treated a failure as a start failure when `callback === client.start`, which only matches the 3.1 call shape. With 3.2.0, a failed native reconnect (for example `apps.connections.open` failing during a network outage) was rethrown inside the SDK's async listener and logged as `Non-fatal unhandled rejection (continuing)`. `unable_to_socket_mode_start` was never emitted, the reconnect loop stayed parked, `channels status` kept saying `connected`, and inbound events stopped until a manual channel restart.

## Fix

`extensions/slack/src/monitor/provider-support.ts`:

- Observe failures at the start itself. The SDK's own starts (native reconnect and refresh replacement) now report failures through the existing `unable_to_socket_mode_start` event, which the existing recovery loop already handles (status, backoff, retry). Bolt's `receiver.start()` still rejects to its caller as before.
- Stop during a pending reconnect: 3.2's `disconnect()` doesn't clear the reconnect timer the way 3.1's did, so the observer clears it, and the waiter settles quietly when the SDK passes its lifecycle signal. A stopped channel never reconnects.

No new retry policy, timing, config or text. The interop tests now drive the 3.x call shapes (net -4 test lines).

## Proof

End-to-end proof (built Gateway, ClawHub-shaped plugin install with socket-mode 3.2.0, local Slack API/WSS stand-in): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198007#issuecomment-6840631381

prs.body:

Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.

Avoid implementation details such as:

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```
 src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts   Tests 10 passed, Duration 42.94s
 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both

("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. prs.title: fix(channels): cancel pending channels.stop on Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels remove <account>` ignores the Ctrl+C / SIGINT cancellation signal while it is stopping the running channel gateway (`channels.stop`) before deleting the account config. If the user hits Ctrl+C during that in-flight gateway call, the command swallows the abort and still writes the deletion to disk, so an interrupted removal partially or fully mutates the config even though the user asked to cancel.

- Problem: `channelsRemoveCommand` never reads the ambient async-work signal (`getAsyncWorkSignal()`), never forwards it into `callGateway({ method: "channels.stop", ... })`, and never re-checks `signal.aborted` after the stop attempt. The gateway call therefore has no way to be cancelled, and the subsequent `applyChannelAccountRemoval` / config write proceeds regardless of the abort.
- Solution: capture `const signal = getAsyncWorkSignal()` at command entry, abort early if already aborted, forward `signal` into the `channels.stop` `callGateway` call, and re-check `signal?.throwIfAborted()` both after a failed stop and after the stop completes, so a cancellation during or after the gateway call aborts the command before any config mutation.
- What changed: `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` (import `getAsyncWorkSignal`; entry guard; forward `signal` to `channels.stop`; two `throwIfAborted` guards). `src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts` (one regression case folded into the existing "normalizes a listed deletion" test).
- What did NOT change: the `list` command (separate gap in the original bug report, not addressed here), the gateway transport, `applyChannelAccountRemoval`'s own logic, and the non-gateway removal path (no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) which still skips the stop entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Best fix: propagate the already-existing ambient cancellation signal that the CLI SIGINT handler installs via `AsyncWorkScope`, rather than adding a new bespoke cancellation mechanism. This mirrors the canonical pattern already used by sibling commands (e.g. the status interrupt-cancel fix, PR #197815). It is the minimal, owner-reusing change and keeps the interruption contract consistent across commands.

Alternative considered and rejected: aborting only after `applyChannelAccountRemoval` (too late, config already mutated); or catching `AbortError` in `callGateway` and silently succeeding (loses the user-visible "you cancelled" semantics).

Risk: a consumer that relied on `channels.remove` ignoring Ctrl+C and completing the deletion will now see the command abort on cancel. This is the intended fix; no compatible contract depended on the old (buggy) swallow. Non-goal: this does not add graceful rollback of a partially-stopped gateway runtime, it only prevents the config write after a cancel.

## User Impact

When a user presses Ctrl+C while `openclaw channels remove <account>` is stopping the channel's running gateway, the command now aborts cleanly and does NOT write the account deletion to config. The user's "cancel" is honored instead of being silently overridden. The success path is unchanged: a removal that completes without interruption behaves exactly as before.

## Evidence

### Before / after comparison (interrupt handling in `channels remove`)

| Behavior | Before (pre-fix) | After (post-fix) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ctrl+C during in-flight `channels.stop` | Abort ignored; command continues and writes the account deletion to config | Command aborts; `writeConfigFile` is never called |
| `signal` forwarded to `callGateway({ method: "channels.stop" })` | Not forwarded (gateway call cannot be cancelled) | Forwarded (`signal` from `getAsyncWorkSignal()`) |
| Guard at command entry (`signal?.throwIfAborted()`) | None | Aborts immediately if already cancelled |
| Guard after the stop attempt (`signal?.throwIfAborted()`) | None (only logs the error) | Re-throws the abort reason and skips the config write |
| Stop fails (gateway error) then user cancels | Error logged, deletion still written | Abort re-thrown, config NOT written |
| Successful removal (no interrupt) | Deletes account, writes config | Identical (unchanged) |
| Non-gateway path (no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) | Skips stop, deletes config | Unchanged |

### Behavior matrix (interrupt during `channels.stop`)

```text
scenario                                  => pre-fix result                 => post-fix result
Ctrl+C during in-flight channels.stop      => swallow + still writes config  => command aborts, config NOT written
already-aborted signal at command entry    => proceeds to gateway stop      => aborts before any gateway/stop call
stop fails (gateway error) then Ctrl+C     => logs error, writes config     => throws abort reason, config NOT written
normal completion (no interrupt)           => deletes account, writes cfg   => identical (unchanged)
```

### Live module-level check (real `node`, real AbortSignal, no mock)

The production cancellation signal is a genuine `AbortSignal` produced by `AsyncWorkScope`, which is exactly what the CLI SIGINT handler installs:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e 'import("./src/shared/async-work-scope.js").then(m => { const s = new m.AsyncWorkScope(); console.log("signal is AbortSignal:", s.signal instanceof AbortSignal); const r = new Error("x"); s.beginClose(r); console.log("aborted:", s.signal.aborted, "reason:", s.signal.reason && s.signal.reason.message); })'
signal is AbortSignal: true
aborted: true reason: x
```

### Pre-fix: failing test (source reverted, test kept)

The regression case asserts the ambient signal is forwarded to `callGateway` and that no config write happens on abort. Without the fix it fails (the `signal` argument is absent from the `callGateway` call):

```console
$ vitest run src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts -t "normalizes a listed deletion"
 FAIL   commands  src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts > channelsRemoveCommand > normalizes a listed deletion before stopping runtime, running lifecycle, and persisting
AssertionError: expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with [ ObjectContaining{…} ]

- Expected
+ Received

  [
    {
-     "signal": AbortSignal {
-       Symbol(kAborted): true,
-       Symbol(kReason): Error { "message": "channels remove interrupted" }
+     "clientName": "gateway-client",
+     "config": { ... },
...
```

### Post-fix: passing

The signal is a REAL `AbortSignal` from the production `AsyncWorkScope` (not a mock). The test wraps the command in `scope.run(...)`, aborts the scope mid-`channels.stop`, and asserts both that `callGateway` received `signal` and that `writeConfigFile` was never called.

```console
$ vitest run src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts -t "normalizes a listed deletion"
 ✓  commands  src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts > channelsRemoveCommand > normalizes a listed deletion before stopping runtime, running lifecycle, and persisting 4945ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
```

The discriminating assertions (drive credible failure):

```ts
expect(gatewayMocks.callGateway).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(
  expect.objectContaining({ signal: scope.signal }),
);
expect(configMocks.writeConfigFile).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
```

Mutation check (proves the test is not vacuous): deleting the `signal,` line from the `callGateway` invocation in `remove.ts` makes this exact test go RED with the `ObjectContaining` assertion above, i.e. the test catches the regression.

### What was not tested

- The `list` command's separate interrupt gap mentioned in the original bug report is NOT covered by this PR (tracked separately).
- No live end-to-end CLI subprocess + real SIGINT was exercised; the proof drives the production `AsyncWorkScope`/`AbortSignal` path directly, which is what the CLI SIGINT handler installs. A real `openclaw channels remove` SIGINT run would additionally require a live gateway account and is out of scope for this regression test.
- The non-gateway removal path (plugin with no `startAccount`/`logoutAccount`) skips the stop entirely and is unchanged; its existing tests still pass.

### Open PR collision check

Searched open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `src/commands/channels/remove.ts` and `src/commands/channels.remove.test.ts` (today's snapshot). Two open PRs touch the same files but fix different bugs in different regions:
- #187514 "scheduled automations keep running after their Telegram account is removed while a binding remains" touches `remove.ts`/test in the automations/binding area, not the `channels.stop` signal path.
- #134060 "deleting an account leaves its stored inbound events behind" touches `remove.ts`/test in the inbound-events area, not the signal path.

Neither modifies `signal`/`throwIfAborted`/`callGateway`/`channels.stop` in `remove.ts`, so there is no duplicate-fix overlap; only a possible future merge-time file coordination on the shared test file. No open PR addresses the Ctrl+C cancellation gap fixed here.

Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

prs.title: feat(ui): show and edit each agent's utility model on the Agents page
prs.body:
Closes #197866

## What Problem This Solves

An agent can have its own utility model (`agents.entries.<id>.utilityModel`), but the Control UI only shows it in Advanced raw config. **Agents → Overview** lists the primary model, fallbacks and decision model, but not the utility model. **Models** shows the shared utility default and says agent settings override it, without naming which agents do. A broken per-agent override stays invisible, and changing the shared default leaves those agents on their own setting with no hint.

## Solution

**Agents → Overview** gets a **Utility model** row between Fallbacks and Decision model. It uses the same model picker as the primary model and offers:

- **Inherit default (…)**: names the shared default (a model, Automatic, or Disabled) and removes the agent's own primary.
- **Disabled for this agent**: saves an empty primary, which turns utility routing off for this agent.
- Any model from the catalog. A configured model that is unavailable stays shown and selected.

The agent's own `utilityModel.fallbacks` are kept, in order, for every choice. Choosing inherit on an agent that has its own fallbacks saves `{ fallbacks }`, which inherits the shared primary and keeps the fallbacks. The row lists those fallbacks under its description. Editing them stays in raw config.

![Forge after saving a new utility model and reloading: the picker shows gpt-5-mini and the row lists its own fallbacks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ec0a5addc2bcd13cf2fcc7ae92ac02a1ef507a2a/images/2026/11/79d7e25d-c20d-4e6d-8d62-0a0030250757.png)

**Models → Utility model** lists every agent that has its own utility settings, with its model (or "Disabled" or "default model") and its fallbacks. Each name opens that agent's Overview.

![Models page naming Forge, its utility model and fallbacks, with a link to Forge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/ec0a5addc2bcd13cf2fcc7ae92ac02a1ef507a2a/images/2026/11/a3afec00-4d37-4412-a80f-0e1cb9107ae5.png)

An agent that picks a model and has no fallbacks of its own saves a bare model string. As documented in [models](https://docs.openclaw.ai/concepts/models), an explicit per-agent primary without `fallbacks` does not use the shared utility fallbacks. Raw config edits already behave this way.

## Impact

- Per-agent utility models can be seen and changed without raw config.
- No config shape or Gateway change: the UI writes the existing `utilityModel` string or `{ primary, fallbacks }` shape through the existing agent config save.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/settings.md` describes where to set it and what each choice saves.

## Evidence

- Live, against an isolated Gateway built from this branch just before a lint-only refactor of the Models link (keyless, synthetic config): Forge started with `{ primary: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6", fallbacks: ["anthropic/claude-opus-4-8", "openai/gpt-5.4"] }`. Picking `gpt-5-mini` on Agents → Overview saved `{ primary: "openai/gpt-5-mini", fallbacks: ["anthropic/claude-opus-4-8", "openai/gpt-5.4"] }` to the config file. After a page reload the picker and the fallback line showed the saved values, and the Forge link on Models opened `/settings/agents/forge`. The red "couldn't refresh some models" notice in the screenshot comes from the test Gateway having no provider keys.
- Tests: `ui/src/pages/agents/model-config.test.ts` (the fallback test fails without the fallback-keeping write), `panels-overview.test.ts`, `model-providers/data.test.ts`, `view-defaults.test.ts`, `view.test.ts`, `model-providers-page.test.ts`, `model-providers-page.presentation.test.ts`: 7 files, all passing.
- `tsgo` (UI project), oxlint on the changed files, stylelint, `ui:i18n:baseline` (no baseline change) and `ui:i18n:verify` all pass.
- Not covered live: the inherit and disable choices (unit tests only), and a Gateway with real provider credentials.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep agent_end preparation within the turn lifetime
prs.body:
Closed in favor of #197990, opened by the issue author for the same fix. No merge or author-delivery completion is claimed for this Draft.

Related: #197940

## What Problem This Solves

After an embedded turn calls `dispatch_action`, deferred terminal-message hydration can outlive the plugin invocation scope. The reply succeeds, but plugin `agent_end` handlers fail before executing.

## User Impact

The candidate hydrates terminal messages within the awaited turn preparation owner, then starts handlers without waiting for their completion. Existing admission checks, no-subscriber behavior and best-effort failure handling remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

Implementation head: `3e27ee9c18fd0dde03f0fb5539292df5583c0056`. The repair stays in `runAgentEndSideEffectsAsync`. This Draft is being closed because the issue author is carrying the same repair in #197990.

## Evidence

Actual named-base failure and exact-head post-fix proof were executed through `ocpr prove`:

- Base `4efd662cc2c6f9f2afa8330ac813e48c9bd9b0a2`: built isolated Gateway, existing local Ollama `qwen3.6:35b-a3b`, and two real plugin registrations. The chat-completions request returned HTTP 200 after `tool_search` → `dispatch_action` → `session_status`; neither terminal handler executed, and both logged `Plugin invocation scope is closed`. Required-hook assertion exited 1.
- Head `3e27ee9c18fd0dde03f0fb5539292df5583c0056`: the same shipped entry executed both terminal handlers exactly once, each receiving 8 messages, with zero closed-scope errors. A fresh direct-tool control executed both once with 5 messages. Both task-owned Gateways were terminated and joined. The formal post command exited 0.
- Deterministic real `PluginInstance` / `PluginInvocationScope` regression: baseline failed with zero handler entries; candidate passed. Pending handlers do not block foreground completion. No-subscriber and rejected-hydration controls passed.
- Six affected test files / 55 tests passed; changed-test type graph, targeted lint and format passed. Gateway `qaRuntime` build passed. Independent local P0–P2 review reported no actionable findings.
- Coverage is the isolated local embedded Gateway/model path. Other providers, channels and operating systems were not exercised. Final hosted proof re-review, Ready CI and author WATCH gates were not completed.

Executed runtime driver commands (each starts the built Gateway using `pnpm openclaw gateway run`):

prs.title: fix(logging): isolate Gateway logs by state directory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes test Gateways and real Gateways with separate state directories appending to the same host-wide daily log, contaminating operator diagnostics.

## User Impact

Default logs follow the selected state directory: `logs/`, with the existing safe-directory fallback kept inside that same state tree. Harness-created temporary state automatically owns its logs. Explicit `logging.file` overrides remain unchanged. External file collectors using `/tmp/openclaw/` must switch to the new path or use `openclaw logs`; old logs are not imported. The macOS app now prefers the selected state's structured log (including its safety fallback), preserving separate launchd stdout files, the existing `OPENCLAW_LOG_DIR` override, and discovery of pre-upgrade logs. macOS clawlog reads unified logs and is unaffected.

## Operator migration note

The default rolling log moves from `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-YYYY-MM-DD.log` to `<stateDir>/logs/openclaw-YYYY-MM-DD.log`. With the default state directory, the exact path is `$HOME/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-YYYY-MM-DD.log`; a Linux system service uses the **service user's home**, for example `/home/openclaw/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-YYYY-MM-DD.log` when that user's home is `/home/openclaw`. `openclaw logs` and macOS discovery follow the new location. Any external watcher tailing `/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-<date>.log` must switch to `openclaw logs` or the new path. Explicit `logging.file` settings are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file-log I/O owner already receives the state directory but previously used it only after shared-temp safety failure. Select it at that owner for normal and fallback paths. No new setting, environment variable, cache, schema, or per-harness convention.

## Evidence

Acceptance before measurement: two real Gateway processes must report distinct files through `openclaw logs`, contain their own startup record, and contain no sibling startup record. Default-root selection must not scan workspace/session/database contents. Measure five A/A controls and five serial A/B samples of 100 root qualifications on a synthetic 62k-file/1.1-GB workspace with 3k session placeholders and a sparse 35-GiB opaque database placeholder. Report wall time, CPU and exact Node allocation separately from full Gateway behavior. This is an isolation fix, not a performance speedup claim; additional safety-check cost must be reported.

The regression fails on base `d30e45c3f48eaa570df1f4528bcc50e7b28e6c77` and passes after the fix. All 43 focused logging cases passed; the final 13-case path regression replay passed in 20.40 s wrapper / 13.86 s Vitest. One earlier cold-worker compilation run timed out while the runtime build was also running (17 other cases passed); this is retained as a local validation limitation, not claimed as an inherited product defect. Both runtime builds passed. The final bounded state-creation correction passed 26 tests (two Linux-only deleted-directory cases are skipped on macOS), targeted typecheck and lint. The two real Gateway proof passed again after rebuilding the final correction, and the transport proof reports zero main-thread synchronous filesystem calls, one worker, safe fallback, rollover, reload, refusal, and forced rescue.

The initial `pnpm check:changed` run passed every stage except dead exports outside this change. The final run retained those nine failures and also timed out in the unrelated cached x64 Bun staging fixture; its descendant remained in a macOS uninterruptible execution wait after termination. That host cleanup failure remains unresolved, and is not claimed as an inherited product failure. No second fixture or host restart was attempted. Other changed-file stages passed. All nine signatures reproduce in a clean checkout of exact base `d30e45c3f48eaa570df1f4528bcc50e7b28e6c77`: `resolveTrustedProxyGitCoauthor` was introduced by `f4f290c52f961` / #196867; the eight inline-command UI export signatures were introduced by `d90d52cce941c` / #197466. These are newly observed main regressions, not noise; their owners and relevant source inputs are unchanged by this PR. Final independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. No changed module is directly imported by Control UI.

Per 100 default-root qualifications, five alternating A/B samples:

| Metric | Before median / p95 | After median / p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Wall ms | 2.764 / 2.861 | 5.441 / 5.586 |
| Main CPU ms | 2.779 / 2.872 | 5.505 / 5.604 |
| Process CPU ms | 5.052 / 5.257 | 8.551 / 9.272 |
| Exact main allocation bytes | 1,336,488 / 1,975,152 | 2,335,088 / 2,560,184 |

A/A wall/main/process medians differ 1.3%/0.03%/2.2%; allocation differs 1.2%. No directory/content scans occur in either arm. State-path ancestor qualification adds six `lstat` operations, one `stat` and one `mkdir` per preparation. Accepted correctness cost: about 27 µs wall/main CPU, 35 µs process CPU and 10 KB allocation per qualification, retained by the existing transport across ordinary records and date rollover. This is not per-record work. Local Node 26/APFS, host load ~16.6; no btrfs or whole-Gateway performance claim. Synthetic fixtures and both Gateways were cleaned up.

Production growth is 16 physical lines: five in the core owner to keep initial and later discovery consistent, and 11 for native discovery across the relocated primary/fallback paths while preserving launchd and pre-upgrade logs. Existing bounded directory creation is reused; no recursive-mkdir retry hazard is introduced. No new owner, cache, schema, production option, or export.

Rebuilt two-Gateway terminal output (temporary root abbreviated; all fixtures synthetic):

```json
{"name":"log-production","file":"<temporary>/openclaw-test-state-log-production-TVxcVM/home/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-2026-11-12.log","port":30000,"cliExit":0,"ownStartup":true,"siblingStartup":false}
{"name":"log-test-harness","file":"<temporary>/openclaw-test-state-log-test-harness-sFKjSz/home/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-2026-11-12.log","port":30008,"cliExit":0,"ownStartup":true,"siblingStartup":false}
```

Reproduce after `pnpm build:runtime` with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/gateway-log-isolation.ts`. Both live Gateway processes are read using the real `openclaw logs --json` command. The script verifies the resolved file and startup contents, then cleans both processes and states.

Native correction: added a regression covering two selected state directories and state-local safety fallback; existing override/stdout coverage remains. Swift formatting, SwiftLint (435 files, zero violations), and a source compilation of the locator/path owner pass. The ordinary PR planner skips macOS Swift jobs. A sandboxed compiled-source probe therefore exercises the actual `LogLocator` and `OpenClawPaths` owners, with only the unused default-profile identity supplied by the fixture. It fails on the prior locator and passes on the corrected one for two state directories, safety fallback, existing override and launchd path. Initial custom-sandbox setup attempts aborted; the supported repository sandbox profile plus a physical temporary root succeeded. No full app or native test suite was launched against operator state.


Latest-stable upgrade proof used the registry's current stable `2026.11.3`, then the rebuilt candidate against the same isolated state and unchanged explicit `logging.file` setting. Both actual Gateway starts and CLI reads passed:

```text
2026.11.3: explicitFilePreserved=true cliExit=0 file=<fixture>/home/.openclaw/explicit/retained.log
candidate: explicitFilePreserved=true cliExit=0 file=<fixture>/home/.openclaw/explicit/retained.log
native prior locator: exit 1, FAIL selected-state log discovery: production/logs
native final locator: exit 0, PASS production/logs, test/logs, state-local fallback, launchd paths, OPENCLAW_LOG_DIR override
```

The native probe uses `scripts/macos-health-render.sb`, denies child forks, and supplies a test-owned HOME/root. Original HOME, preferences/Keychain IPC, shared Keychains, network and filesystem writes outside that root are denied. Its source fixture controls only the default profile stub; selected-state resolution and log enumeration are production code.

The later symlink-fallback review concern was reproduced against this exact head and disproved: Foundation's URL-based `contentsOfDirectory(at:includingPropertiesForKeys:options:)` returns POSIX `ENOTDIR` for the primary directory symlink, so the locator selects the active fallback. A path-based enumeration control on that same valid symlink lists the old log. No additional guard was retained.
## Landing qualification

Final head: `74d4ff4dd364d978af196203556718a98fcfd118`. Codex autoreview is clean; the published ClawSweeper review on this head has zero findings/open checklist items, and both code-review threads are resolved.

[CI run 43335003904](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43335003904), attempt 1, tested merge `c257f03c1b69f2d6dfee88a080c584233e6f6831` against main parent `bb97be6b37b1fe14fc74a38a904efce340cdef91`. The wrapper import-closure failures reproduce on that exact main parent and trace to `fc6c25e91564ca1f757d04c5b4676dcab6f66aaa` / #197697, which added a runtime protocol import without updating the wrapper inventory. This is a main regression requiring its owner's repair.

The other failure was the fresh-browser HTTP suite's 180-second setup hook, before all three test bodies, with no assertion failure. The saved log was reused. At the maintainer's direction, the exact test was replayed on direct head parent `da4776053295fbe088df07d25584292c1a326787`: all three cases passed in 101.20 seconds. That qualifies one scoped hosted retry under the explicit landing instruction; only the failed UI job was requested through the protected job-rerun endpoint. No source change, timeout relaxation or broad CI retry was made. Attempt 2 completed: UI job `131608414381` passed, security-fast passed, and the only remaining failed job is the inherited wrapper closure (`131608417407`), with its downstream aggregate `131612623668`. This qualifies the explicitly authorized pinned-head admin merge; CI is recorded as failed, not relabeled green.

The unrelated cached x64 Bun staging fixture's uninterruptible process is left alone as directed. Its earlier timeout/cleanup failure remains an investigated local limitation; it is not claimed fixed or as inherited product behavior.

prs.title: fix(telegram): suppress duplicate replies in the originating topic
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate Telegram replies when a message tool sends to an encoded topic target but the originating conversation carries its topic ID separately.

## User Impact

Replies already delivered to the originating topic are deduplicated correctly. Different-topic replies remain intact, and an encoded origin topic takes precedence over a separate thread ID. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This standalone fix carries the resolved origin thread ID through the existing channel suppression callback and uses it as Telegram's normalized fallback. The new SDK field is optional. Telegram derives its parameter type from that SDK contract instead of repeating the shape locally.

The change adds one net production line and 64 net regression-test lines, with an allocation for exactly that test growth. The regression exercises the real Telegram plugin through both immediate and queued payload preparation.

## Evidence

### Regression and build checks

- Before the fix: two expected same-topic failures; seven other cases pass. After the fix: 95 focused tests pass, with one Windows-only skip.
- After the type simplification: all nine regression cases pass, including numeric/string thread IDs, different-topic controls, and encoded-origin precedence. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-payloads-transport-dedupe.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Core, extension, and messaging-test type checks, targeted lint/boundary lint, formatting, test-line budget, line-cap ratchet, and commit hooks pass. Extension types and affected lint/format checks were rerun after the type-only change.
- Full package build and [CI run 42589003974](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42589003974) pass at `c99a0840418571a09d1a1347d8005ce207cd271f`.
- Independent local review against `9a26486062c8` found no actionable findings; that review covers the equivalent type simplification. Shared autoreview was unavailable.

### SDK compatibility

An external consumer of the built public SDK passes strict TypeScript checking with the original callback declaration, unchanged adapters, and calls omitting `originThreadId`. Negative controls reject a numeric thread ID, a missing required origin target, and an implementation requiring the new optional field.

Twenty-five built-runtime compatibility cases pass, including five real-core calls into a legacy callback, unchanged Slack/Discord comparisons, and Telegram calls using the old argument shape. The additional property is observable to reflection or exact-key validators; the checks establish compatibility for those consumers, not every third-party plugin. SDK-owner review of the additive optional field is requested.

### Gateway and Telegram observations

An isolated Gateway built from this PR, with Telegram polling and local Bot API/deterministic model fixtures, suppresses the duplicate same-topic final. The transcript confirms a nonempty model final. A negative control removing only `originThreadId` forwarding reproduces two identical same-topic answers.

That replay also exposed a separate completion-accounting issue: after deduplication, the Gateway emitted “No answer was returned”. It independently reproduces in ordinary chats without topic routing and is addressed in [PR #195909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195909). The route-matching correction here and that general completion-accounting correction have separate reproductions and separate changes.

An additional integration replay applying both fixes produced one answer with no notice for the same-topic case and one answer per topic for the different-topic control. Both transcripts contain nonempty model finals. These Gateway replays use local transport/model fixtures.

A separate live Telegram run on a deployed 2026.11.2 Gateway confirmed one answer in each topic for the different-topic control. Its Telegram matcher and target-thread resolver are byte-identical to this PR's build; the origin normalization difference is idempotent for admitted inputs. Its same-topic runs had empty model finals and are not counted as successful deduplication proof. This comparison covers the suppression functions, not equivalence of the entire released Gateway.

### Inspectable standalone Gateway trace (2026-11-09)

The following is newly captured output from a standalone build of **this topic-matching PR only**, without #195909. The process ran `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port 19842` with isolated state and Telegram polling enabled. The Bot API and Chat Completions endpoints were local deterministic HTTP fixtures; this is production-path Gateway evidence, **not a live Telegram or live-model run**. All chat IDs, topic IDs, message text, and message IDs below are synthetic fixture data. No production credentials or conversations were used.

Build identity from `dist/build-info.json`: `c99a0840418571a09d1a1347d8005ce207cd271f`, built `2026-11-09T08:42:30.357Z`. The current rebased PR commit is `1e0c7b3e8518580b1d264c0162468620a3a500b5`; `git range-diff 9a26486062c8..c99a08404185 1e0c7b3e8518^..1e0c7b3e8518` reports `=` (identical patch). This replay uses the earlier build, not an asserted rebuild of the rebased head.

Both input updates originate in private chat `12345`, topic `77`. The fixture first requests a real `message` tool send with `final:false`; after receiving the tool receipt, it returns the same text as a nonempty automatic final. Streaming is disabled on the Telegram channel, not on model inference.

| Case | Tool destination | Nonempty model final | Actual Bot API answer sends |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Same topic | `12345:topic:77` | `TOPIC_PROOF_SAME` | Exactly one, to topic `77` |
| Different topic | `12345:topic:88` | `TOPIC_PROOF_CROSS` | Exactly two, first to topic `88`, then to origin topic `77` |

These records were captured at the HTTP fixture boundaries. `model_request_tool_receipts` is the actual tool result the Gateway submitted in its next inference request. `bot_api` contains the actual Gateway request and the fixture's success response. The trace includes every `sendMessage`/`editMessageText` observed during both cases, including the separate missing-reply notice; it is not a hand-written expected transcript. The same-topic case has one answer and the pre-existing “No answer was returned” notice (record 7). That notice is the separate completion-accounting defect addressed by #195909; it does not undo the observed suppression of the repeated answer. The extra model tool-call response in record 6 occurs during finalization and produces no additional answer send. The different-topic case retains both intended answer deliveries without that notice. No completion fix was applied to obtain these results.

<details>

After stopping the isolated Gateway, a read-only query of `transcript_events` for the origin session selected assistant messages with `stopReason: "stop"`. The records below retain the stored sequence, role, content, and stop reason; unrelated transcript fields are omitted.
