prs.title: fix(macos): offer OpenClaw ID recovery after this Mac is removed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After **Settings › Remove this Mac**, the Mac forgets its OpenClaw ID enrollment and clears its primary connection, but then leaves the person stranded. The dashboard shows the generic "Dashboard unavailable · Gateway not configured" page with a Reload button that cannot help, Settings › Connection hides the OpenClaw ID section entirely, and the menu bar says "Gateway not configured". Found in the live sign-in-first test on 2026-11-12: there was no in-app way back short of a fresh profile. A Mac removed from another device ends up in the same place, with no explanation.

## User Impact

- The dashboard window shows a calm page instead of an error: "This Mac was removed from <claw>" (or "no longer has access", when another device removed it), with **Sign in with OpenClaw ID…**, **Set up a different connection** and **Close**.
- Settings › Connection always offers **Sign in with OpenClaw ID** when the build has an OpenClaw ID configuration, with a removal note when one applies.
- The menu bar offers **Sign in with OpenClaw ID…** when unconfigured and shows the removal.
- All entry points open the same sign-in → claw picker → approval flow.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `MacOpenClawIDDeviceStore` owns one local-retirement path for both a local removal and a verified remote one: stop the operator route, deselect the node, forget enrollment/session/keys, clear the primary connection, and record `{hostname, time, origin}`. The record is display context only, never authority; it clears on a new enrollment or when another primary connection is configured.
- A remote removal is recognized only from a verified snapshot that no longer admits this Mac's owner key (`notAdmitted`). Missing local trust data now reports `trustUnavailable` instead of `notAdmitted`, so it is not mistaken for removal; network errors never retire.
- A removal in progress on this Mac keeps "here" wording even when its lost-response verification observes the removal first.
- The sign-in sheet moves from the Settings model to one shared presenter used by Settings, the dashboard page and the menu.

Stacked on #197630.

## Evidence

- Real SwiftUI/HTML renders with fixture data (screens below).
- MacBook Pro (macOS 26.5.1, Xcode 26.6), isolated HOME/state, sandbox: `swift build --build-tests` passed; `OpenClawIDRemovalTests`, `DashboardFailurePageTests`, `StatusMenuDescriptorTests` 26 tests passed; `OpenClawIDRemovalRenderTests` passed.
- Pinned SwiftLint strict (macOS config, and iOS config for the shared file): 0 violations. SwiftFormat: clean. `pnpm native:i18n:verify`: passed.
- Not yet proven live: the OAuth → picker → approval round trip from each entry point, and a real remote removal. Both are in the next live test.

prs.title: feat(workboard): record optional claims, observations, and verification
prs.body:
Fixes #197450
Supersedes #161618

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard needs to distinguish worker claims, observed run outcomes, and checker verdicts without making evidence a requirement for completing work.

## User Impact

Workers can include optional claims when completing a card, and checkers can record what they checked and whether it was confirmed, disputed, or inconclusive. Completion and dependency scheduling keep their existing behavior, including for cards without evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Store the three record types separately with their source identities. Session lifecycle sync owns observations, and generic metadata writes cannot forge or remove evidence. Records are bounded to the newest four per kind within 6 KiB, and evidence only uses room the card's other records leave: near the 24 KiB card budget it drops its own oldest entries and never evicts proof, attempts, comments, or artifacts. `workboard_verify` returns an error when its record cannot fit; claims and observations that cannot fit are dropped without failing completion. No database migration is required; older versions may drop this optional evidence when writing a card.

## Evidence

- Regression test `store-evidence.test.ts`: fails on `63808cadb49` (a verification on a card near its budget evicted existing artifacts) and passes on this head. It also covers forged evidence through raw metadata and evidence surviving a later metadata write.
- Workboard suites: 192 tests passed across seven files (store, tools, lifecycle sync, plugin registration, Gateway, attempts, evidence). Extension and extension-test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, the line-cap ratchet, and the test-line ratchet passed locally.
- Test lines: the PR adds 27 net test lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/197471-workboard-result-evidence.txt` allocates the 9 lines past the ceiling; the regression test lives in its own file because `store.test.ts` is over its line cap.
- Isolated Gateway scenario with a stand-in model: completion with and without records, lifecycle observation from a real session run, checker verification, and rejection of forged observations through generic metadata. Not run against a live external model; the budget-fitting behavior is covered by the regression test, not this scenario.

prs.title: fix(automations): let authenticated owners inspect run receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an authenticated configured channel owner can load an existing automation with `get`, but its `runs` request loses management authority and can return “Automation not found” for that same job.

## User Impact

Owners and Control UI administrators can inspect execution receipts for automations they can already manage, without changing job ownership or creating replacement jobs. Ordinary caller restrictions remain unchanged.

**Draft for permission-contract review:** existing admission tests explicitly exclude `cron.runs` from management. This proposes changing that contract; maintainer approval is needed. Transcript access (`cron.history`) remains excluded. No live installation or deployment is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

The management grant allowlist includes `cron.get` but excludes `cron.runs`. The tool therefore sends run-history requests without the method-bound management grant. This adds run-receipt reads to that existing mechanism and aligns management-only schema/help, retaining run/method binding, single-use redemption, live-authority checks, expiry, revocation, and self-job restrictions.

The regression was reproduced on the affected 2026.11.3 source revision `847611dcaa3bf0e2783335f961dd1fd0580e4d9f`. The candidate has now been replayed onto upstream main `f817a8b3eb1` to resolve the diverged release-line conflicts, preserving newer automation policy checks and binding behavior. It does not alter the scheduler or claim to repair worker-memory failures.

## Evidence

- New tool-boundary regression calls `get` followed by `runs` for configured-owner and Control UI admin contexts. Both cases failed on the original code: the owner path omitted the grant, and management-only execution rejected the action.
- Candidate: **97 targeted tests passed** on the updated candidate across tool management (14), grant security (29), tool schema (45), and creator-context admission (9). This supersedes the 59-test result on the release-based candidate.
- Existing admission expectations were explicitly updated for the proposed run-receipt permission; transcript history remains a negative control. This policy adjustment is not represented as independent evidence that the prior restriction was accidental.
- Scoped type-aware lint, core TypeScript checking, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Updated-main verification: the initial four-file run identified two stale management action/error-text expectations; those were corrected and the affected file passed (14 tests, 7.98s command wall time). The other three files passed unchanged.
- **Independent local review unavailable:** default reviewer preflight found no standalone Codex CLI; the documented OpenClaw reviewer returned `reviewer_unavailable` (exit 1, no report). The requester explicitly approved submitting this draft with that limitation. This is not a clean review claim or a waiver of upstream review.
### Receipt-disclosure follow-up

Added `cron.management-receipts.integration.test.ts` in response to the review of `b03f3f418b73`. It reuses the admitted-run fixture but calls the production Gateway request router, method-bound grant redemption, CronService, SQLite receipt persistence, and worker-backed receipt hydration. No Gateway call, authorization decision, or receipt payload is mocked.

- Control UI administrator and configured channel-owner: `cron.get` then per-job `cron.runs` returns the persisted synthetic receipt from a different creator conversation.
- Ordinary non-owner: both requests fail with not-found and no response payload.
- Configured owner removed during an awaited receipt read: the test delegates to the real storage reader, pauses only its return, removes the owner from the runtime config, and resumes. The Gateway returns an authority error without disclosing the hydrated receipt.
- Negative control: temporarily removing only `cron.runs` from the management allowlist makes both authorized cases fail (admin receipt request denied; owner grant mint rejected). The ordinary non-owner denial still passes. The production allowlist was restored afterward.
- Focused integration test: 3/3 passed; test time 2.33s, runner duration 9.07s, command wall time 11.23s on the first successful warm run. CI seconds not yet available.
- Final adjacent suite: **33/33 passed** across receipt visibility, requester continuation, and the new management receipt integration (83.54s command wall time, including compilation).
- Gateway-methods test TypeScript shard and scoped type-aware lint passed. The requester-continuation test's existing help-text expectation was updated to match the proposed action list.
- Test-line allocation covers only this branch's net 165 test lines. The new cases close the storage/disclosure gap not reached by the original mocked-Gateway tests; no new production hook or authorization path was added.

**Limits:** this is isolated in-process Gateway integration proof using synthetic admitted-client facts, not a network login, live model/channel session, or installed-release E2E. Full CI and post-install verification remain outstanding. Maintainers still need to approve cross-conversation receipt access. No live authorization controls were patched or bypassed.

AI-assisted implementation; submitted for upstream review, not automatic merge.


## Authenticated shipped-entry-point proof (head 2a6431e1b58)

Built this candidate in an isolated Gateway and used real Control UI browser authentication (trusted-proxy synthetic identities), actual chat composer, and the shipped automations tool. No management grants were manually minted or injected.

| Authenticated caller | get | runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator, new chat session | Exact existing job returned | One persisted successful receipt and its unique summary returned |
| Ordinary member, separate chat session | Not found | Not found; receipt summary absent |

The job was created and executed through real Gateway RPC outside the administrator chat session; it is foreign to that chat session, not owned by another human. The receipt is produced by the isolated scheduler execution, not inserted as a fake row.

Committed reproduction: `ui/src/e2e/cron-management-receipt-proof.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (registered in UI E2E routing).

```text
Authenticated automation receipt tool proof
reads foreign receipts as admin and denies an ordinary non-owner through authenticated chat tools
Test Files 1 passed
Tests 1 passed
Scenario 6.327s
```

Runtime build (including Control UI), scoped type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and test-line budget checks passed. Independent review inspected both the fixture and saved actual tool outputs. Browser/Gateway cleanup completed.

Limits: deterministic loopback provider, not live external model inference; configured Discord-owner ingress remains unproved. This browser test was not repeated on the original permission implementation; earlier in-process red/green controls remain separate. No installed Gateway or billing watch changed. Maintainer permission-scope approval remains required.

prs.title: fix(agents): honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR in claude-cli transcript resolution
prs.body:
<!--
Closes #145309
-->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the `claude-cli` backend with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set (e.g. a second Claude login on the same host) would lose session continuity on every cold turn and silently fall back to the next model with no history after any config hot-reload. The bundled `claude-cli` transcript resolver looked for project JSONL files under `$HOME/.claude/projects/…` and ignored `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so every transcript check missed — even though the session catalog scanner, provider-auth resolver, and Claude Code itself all honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` as the projects tree root.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two resolvers were hardcoding `~/.claude/projects` instead of honoring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`:

1. **`resolveClaudeCliProjectDirForWorkspace`** (`src/agents/command/claude-cli-project-dir.ts`) — used by the transcript probe (`claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent`) and the doctor health check. A miss here triggers `reason=missing-transcript` session resets on every cold turn.

2. **`resolveClaudeProjectsDir`** (`src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`) — used by `resolveClaudeCliSessionFilePath` and `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed`. A miss here means the fallback prelude has no harvested context, so a fallback-model re-run starts with zero conversation history.

Both now follow the same pattern as the existing `resolveClaudeCliConfigDir` in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-claude-compat.ts` and `configuredClaudeConfigDir` in `extensions/anthropic/session-catalog-scan.ts`: when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set and non-blank, resolve project transcripts under `<resolved config dir>/projects`; otherwise fall back to `<homeDir>/.claude/projects` as before.

## User Impact

Users who set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (for a second Claude login, a dedicated profile, or a Docker-mounted config directory) will no longer experience:
- Cold-turn session resets (`reason=missing-transcript`) that discard the stored Claude session id.
- Warm-turn silent fallback to a different model with no conversation history after a config hot-reload.
- The cascading failure where the fallback process occupies the same live-session owner key, blocking the primary model from reusing the slot.

The existing workaround (symlinking `$HOME/.claude/projects/<key>` → `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/<key>`) is no longer needed.

## Evidence

### Production-path behavior proof

Exercises the **production exported functions the Gateway actually runs** — `claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent` (the session-continuity probe used on cold turns) and `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed` (the fallback-history recovery reader) — against a real `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` tree containing a Claude Code session JSONL (one user/assistant exchange):

```
[setup] CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = /tmp/oc-proof-prod-swqXxG/claude-config
[setup] transcript written to /tmp/oc-proof-prod-swqXxG/claude-config/projects/-tmp-oc-proof-prod-swqXxG-workspace-demo/prod-proof-session.jsonl

[1] production transcript probe (transcript under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR):
    claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent() = true
    -> session stays LIVE, no missing-transcript reset: true

[2] production fallback history reader (readClaudeCliFallbackSeed):
    recentTurns = 2
    turn[0].role = user
    turn[1].role = assistant
    -> fallback re-run recovers the conversation from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects

[3] negative control (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset):
    probe = false (expected, no reset-triggering miss leak)
    seed = undefined (expected)

Result: production probe + production history reader both honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
```

What this demonstrates:
- The **production transcript probe** finds the existing Claude session under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…` and returns `true` — the stored session id stays live across a cold turn instead of being reset with `reason=missing-transcript`.
- The **production fallback history reader** recovers the full recent-turn history (user + assistant roles) from `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…` — a fallback-model re-run starts with the actual conversation instead of no context.
- The **negative control** (env var unset) shows the same session id resolves to `false`/`undefined` under the default `<homeDir>/.claude/projects` tree — the fix is selective, not a lookup leak.

(The one `v4 miss` warn line in the trace is the negative-control run emitting its expected structured miss for the default-tree path — the same warn Gateway operators would see before this fix on every turn.)

### CI

All 169 jobs green on head `d3d5304a5c` (run 34682440091, `openclaw/ci-gate` SUCCESS). Earlier runs hit two unrelated infra flakes — a `resolve-auth.test.ts` 1000ms timeout and a runner-preempted `checks-fast-bundled-protocol` job (0 steps executed) — both cleared on rerun; no test failure was ever traced to this patch.

### Resolver unit tests (4/4 passed)

```
✓ resolves under <homeDir>/.claude/projects by default
✓ resolves under $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects when configured
✓ falls back to <homeDir>/.claude/projects for a blank CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
✓ resolves a relative CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR against the process working directory
```

### Test-suite coverage (189/189 passed locally)

- **Transcript probe test** (`attempt-execution.test.ts`, 21 tests in the probe suite): writes a transcript under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/…`, verifies `claudeCliSessionTranscriptHasContent` returns `true` inside the env override and the file is absent from the default tree outside it (direct path check, no probe side-effects).
- **Fallback seed test** (`cli-session-history.test.ts`, 168 tests): writes a session JSONL under `configDir/projects/demo-workspace/`, verifies `readClaudeCliFallbackSeed` finds it with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set (2 turns, correct roles) and returns `undefined` without it.

### Patch history

- `6d11eda` — initial fix + tests
- `7c3d4f` — switch 6 synchronous `withEnvAsync` callbacks to `withEnv` (typecheck)
- `9205926` — avoid probe grace-period side-effects in the new test's negative assertion
- `4ee3802` / `5fce660` / `d3d5304` — empty CI-rerun commits for unrelated infra flakes

prs.title: feat(telegram): roll Telegram's native dice from the message tool
prs.body:
Closes #137110

## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw bot cannot take part in a Telegram dice roll. Sending 🎲 as text posts a static
emoji: no animation, no roll, no value. Telegram's `sendDice` is the only way for a bot to
trigger the real thing, and it was unreachable — the message tool exposed no action for it.

The distinction matters because Telegram picks the outcome server-side. Nobody in the chat,
agent or operator, can influence or fake it, so a roll everyone watches land is credible in a
way a number the agent typed is not.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dice` joins the core action vocabulary with target mode `to` and no conversation read — it
is an outbound send to an explicit target. That vocabulary is closed by design ("Plugins add
names through a core PR; runtime registration is intentionally unsupported",
`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a third-party plugin cannot add this and
the core entry is the intended path.

Scoped tool schemas prune parameters the selected actions do not use and merge the surviving
groups into one flat object. Dice therefore gets its own `diceEmoji` key rather than reusing
the reaction group's `emoji`: sharing that name would retitle the reaction parameter for
`react` whenever both actions are enabled. The group is also part of the full schema, so the
six faces are advertised in both scoped and unscoped tool surfaces.

The Telegram runtime wraps `sendDice` and returns `messageId`, `chatId`, `emoji` and the
rolled `value` in the same tool result, so the agent learns the outcome without a second
round-trip. Input is validated against Telegram's documented allowlist before the API call,
after stripping the emoji presentation selector (⚽️ vs ⚽) the same way the plugin's reaction
path does — that form is what most keyboards and models emit.

No new configuration key. Dice rides the existing `sendMessage` gate: permission to post in a
chat already governs it, and a roll is an ordinary outbound message to a chat the bot may
already post in, so a dedicated toggle would guard nothing. `sticker` is gated because it also
enables `sticker-search`, which reads external sticker packs; dice has no such surface, which
puts it with `edit`, `delete`, `reactions` and `topic-create` — all enabled without a toggle.
Disabling `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` withdraws dice too, and a test asserts that.

Accepted tradeoff: the returned `emoji` echoes the validated request rather than
`result.dice.emoji`. Telegram's contract returns the requested face, and reading it back
would add a branch for a state the API does not produce; the rolled `value`, which the API
alone decides, is read from the response.

Inbound dice are a separate defect and ship in their own PR (#137112); this one is outbound
only.

Opened so the product decision on #137110 has a concrete diff to judge rather than a
description. The gate shape here follows the recommendation in that issue's review — dice under
the existing send gate, no new configuration key. If maintainers decide against the capability,
closing this costs nothing.
`sticker` and `poll` have `openclaw message` subcommands and `dice` does not; CLI parity
is a small follow-up rather than part of this change, since most action names have no
subcommand either.

## User Impact

Telegram operators can have their agent roll Telegram's native animated dice — 🎲 🎯 🏀 ⚽ 🎳 🎰 —
and act on the result in the same turn, with no configuration to discover or enable. Operators
who have disabled Telegram sending are unaffected: dice is withdrawn along with `send`.

## Evidence

- **Live**: run on a live gateway against a real Telegram bot.
  `{"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲"}` returned
  `{"ok":true,"messageId":"944","emoji":"🎲","value":6}`, a real animated roll landed in the
  chat, and the agent reported the value in the same turn with no chat re-read between the
  call and the reply. The model picked the `diceEmoji` key unprompted, from the schema
  description alone. That run predates the gate change below; the send-gate coupling is
  covered by a test rather than by that session.
- **Live**: ⚽ with the presentation selector (`U+26BD U+FE0F`) was accepted and reached
  `sendDice` as the bare face, returning `{"emoji":"⚽","value":1}`. That form was rejected
  before this change.
- **Live**: the stale-key case behaves as documented — `{"action":"dice","emoji":"🎯"}` with
  no `diceEmoji` rolls 🎲, since `emoji` remains a legal key belonging to reactions in the
  same flattened object. This is why the separate key is load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
- **Live, earlier revision**: an earlier form of this action ran for a week on a live
  instance before the rename and the selector handling.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0 (oxlint 0 errors, `tsgo:all`, assertion/max-lines ratchets,
  Knip dead-export scan, import cycles, plugin boundaries, generated-metadata check).
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — exit 0.
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels` — 13 files, 32 tests passed.
- Focused: dice send tests (default face, all six faces, presentation selector, rejection
  before the API call, missing dice payload) and schema-scoping tests, including a regression
  test that `emoji` keeps its reaction description when `react` and `dice` are both in scope.
- Gate coupling: `ties dice availability to the send gate` asserts dice is offered under an
  ordinary config and withdrawn when `channels.telegram.actions.sendMessage` is `false`.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — exit 0 as its own job, confirming the generated bundled
  channel metadata matches the schemas now that no dice key exists.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Note on the telegram lane: three cases in `bot/body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` (inline-code
whitespace normalization) fail on this branch, and they fail identically on a clean
`upstream/main` checkout with the file byte-identical to upstream. They are unrelated to dice —
not Node-version specific (same on 24.20.0 and 26.8.1) and not locale specific (same under
`C.UTF-8`). Nothing in this PR touches that file or its subject.




## v2

Rebased onto current `main` first: `annotateSourceDelivery` was refactored there after the
review, which absorbed part of the second repair and made the rest smaller.

- `dice` is declared `GUARDED_ACTION` in `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_ACTION_DEFINITIONS`
  (`src/channels/plugins/message-action-names.ts`), so a roll addressed by `to` clears the same
  cross-context check as every other recipient-visible send. As a plain targeted action it
  carried no `crossContext` fact, and the guard returns early for such actions, which is why the
  gap was silent rather than a build error. Deliberately not `"marker"`: that decoration writes
  into `params.message`, which dice never sends.
- A successful roll now sets `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered`. The fact was neither
  produced nor trusted, so the repair has two halves:
  - Produced: `source-reply-mirror.ts` carried the "which actions address their conversation by
    target" rule twice — once inside `isCurrentSourceConversation`, once in the `default` arm of
    `isDeliveredCurrentSourceReply`, where it compared `params.action` raw while the switch head
    compared it normalized. Both now read one `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` set that includes
    `dice`, since a roll addresses its conversation by target exactly like a send. Net zero
    production lines in that file (+11/-11), one duplicate policy gone. Transcript mirroring
    shares the predicate and needs no second gate: a roll carries no text or media, so it drops
    out on the existing empty-payload check.
  - Trusted: `isDeliveredMessageToolOnlySourceReplyResult`
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.ts`) re-derived eligibility from an
    action-name list (`["reply", "thread-reply", "poll"]` plus the send names) even when the
    producer had already recorded the route, so it still rejected dice after the marking landed.
    It now reads the recorded fact. This is more permissive in exactly one direction: a result
    the producer stamped `current-source` is trusted regardless of action name, and only results
    that passed the target comparison carry that stamp — nothing that did not deliver visible
    content to this conversation can reach it. The `allowExplicitSourceRoute` path, where no such
    stamp exists, still requires the name list.
- Mirrorable payload eligibility is now separate from current-source delivery classification.
  The message tool's argument object is flat, so `{action: "dice", message: "You rolled a six"}`
  passes validation; Telegram ignores `message`, but `mirrorDeliveredSourceReplyToTranscript`
  reads text and media straight out of `actionParams` and would have recorded assistant text no
  recipient ever saw. A `MIRRORABLE_SOURCE_ACTION_NAMES` set (currently `send` alone) gates the
  mirror, while `TARGET_ADDRESSED_ACTION_NAMES` keeps covering delivery classification. The same
  hole already existed for `poll` — its params can carry `message` too — so the regressions cover
  dice text, dice media and poll text; all three fail without the gate.
  Both halves are in core rather than in `extensions/telegram/src/channel-actions.ts` where the
  finding was reported: a channel plugin cannot classify itself into a core delivery decision,
  and the classification has to hold for any channel that grows an equivalent send.
- `silent` is read in the dice handler and forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram`, matching the schema
  the action already advertises.

Named follow-up, not changed here: `sticker` is likewise absent from `MESSAGE_TOOL_SEND_ACTIONS`
and the reply-name list, so it does not set `messageToolOnlySourceReplyDelivered` either. Whether
that is the same gap or deliberate — a sticker may not answer the question, so the fallback reply
is wanted — is a product call this PR does not make. Stickers behave exactly as before.

### Dependency contract

The review recorded that it could not inspect the `sendDice` contract (dependency sources absent,
DNS blocked). From the installed tree:

- `grammy@1.46.0`, `node_modules/grammy/out/core/api.d.ts:470` —
  `sendDice(chat_id: number | string, emoji: … | "🎲" | "🎯" | "🏀" | "⚽" | "🎳" | "🎰", other?, signal?): Promise<Message.DiceMessage>`.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `methods.d.ts:927-935` — payload is `chat_id`, `message_thread_id?`,
  `emoji?` restricted to the same six faces, and `disable_notification?`, which is what `silent`
  maps to. This is the upstream source of both the allowlist and the silent option.
- `@grammyjs/types@5.0.0`, `message.d.ts:878-883` — `Dice` is `{ emoji: string; value: number }`,
  with value ranges documented as 1-6 for 🎲 🎯 🎳, 1-5 for 🏀 ⚽ and 1-64 for 🎰. The roll is
  server-decided, which is why `value` is read from the response while `emoji` echoes the
  validated request.

### v2 evidence

- Regressions, each verified by reverting its own fix and rerunning:
  - cross-context denial for `dice` (`src/infra/outbound/outbound-policy.test.ts`) — without the
    policy entry: `expected [Function run] to throw an error`.
  - current-source marking for a target-addressed send
    (`src/infra/outbound/message-action-execution.reply-action.test.ts`, plus the negative case
    for another conversation) — without the set entry:
    `expected { ok: true, …(2) } to match object { sourceReplyRoute: 'current-source' }`.
  - the classifier accepting a recorded route it does not enumerate by name
    (`src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts`, plus the unconfirmed negative)
    — without the fix: `expected false to be true`.
  - `silent` forwarded to `sendDiceTelegram` (`extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`)
    — without the fix: `expected undefined to be true`.
- `pnpm check:changed` — exit 0.
- `pnpm tsgo` — exit 0.
- Vitest over `src/infra/outbound`, `src/agents/tools`, both source-reply suites,
  `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts` and `extensions/telegram` — the only failures are
  the three pre-existing `body-helpers.inbound.test.ts` whitespace cases noted above. Both that
  test and the module it covers are byte-identical to `upstream/main` on this branch.
- `autoreview` (skill) — `scoped-clean`, no accepted findings.

Repair commit alone: production +20/-9 (net +11), tests and test support +114/-3. The
`source-reply-mirror.ts` half is net-neutral (+11/-7 replacing a duplicated action list with one
set). Whole branch versus `main`: production +285/-62, tests +185/-3, docs +16/-1.

Test-line budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-dice-action.txt` allocates the
branch's net +182 test lines. They hold the contracts no cheaper layer proves: the dice
authority gates, silent and topic delivery at the Telegram sender, cross-context and delivery
classification in outbound policy, and source-reply ownership in the agent.

The branch is a linear series of six commits on current `main`, with no merge commits.

### Live proof

Captured against a real Telegram bot on `dfa0fb6`, an earlier head of this branch. Later
revisions rebased and compressed it without changing the behaviour on the proven paths. The run used a gateway built from this
branch, agent model `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`. Chat identifiers are redacted as `<chat-a>` (the
conversation the run is bound to) and `<chat-b>` (a different configured chat).

**Cross-context egress.** With `tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinProvider: false`, a
direct message-tool call from the session bound to `<chat-a>`:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","target":"telegram:<chat-b>","diceEmoji":"🎲"}
toolResult Cross-context messaging denied: action=dice target="telegram:<chat-b>"
           while bound to "telegram:<chat-a>" (channel=telegram).
```

Nothing reached `<chat-b>`. Before this change `dice` carried no `crossContext` fact, so the
guard returned before it ever compared targets.

**Terminal delivery.** With `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`, a roll in the bound
conversation:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","final":true}
toolResult {"ok":true,"messageId":"…","emoji":"🎲","value":4,
            "sourceReplyRoute":"current-source"}
```

`sourceReplyRoute: "current-source"` is the marking this PR adds; the operator observed
exactly one message in the chat — the animated roll — with no fallback text after it.

**Silent.** The call carried the option and the roll was delivered:

```
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲","silent":true}
```

The forwarding is covered by the sender-boundary regression above and by
`extensions/telegram/src/send-special.ts:183`, which maps `silent` to the
`disable_notification` field `@grammyjs/types` declares for `sendDice`.

**Forum-topic roll.** Captured on the current head `6b6731dd31c` with a Gateway built from
this branch in an isolated state directory, agent model `litellm/deepseek-v4-flash`, and
`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies: "message_tool"`. `<forum>` is a forum supergroup; the
request was a user message in its topic 14 that mentioned the bot and asked for a roll there.

```
session    agent:main:telegram:group:<forum>:topic:14
toolCall   message {"action":"dice","diceEmoji":"🎲"}
toolResult {"ok":true,"messageId":"727","chatId":"<forum>","emoji":"🎲","value":5,
            "receipt":{"threadId":"14"},"sourceReplyRoute":"current-source"}
delivery   {"createdThreadIds":["14"],"status":"settled","sourceReplyDelivered":true}
```

The call named no target or thread: the roll landed in the topic the request came from, and
the receipt in the result reports that topic. The tool result ended the turn (`terminate: true`,
stop reason `toolUse`); the model was not called again, no assistant text was produced, and the
Gateway sent nothing after the roll. The operator observed the animated die, face 5, in topic 14
with no message after it.

Follow-up, not changed here: the trajectory recorder labels this turn
`non_deliverable_terminal_turn` (`status: error`). `finalizeEmbeddedAttempt` in
`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-finalize.ts` counts a tool-use turn as delivered
only through `messagingToolSent*` evidence, which neither `poll` nor `dice` records. The runtime
terminal check, `hasAttemptTerminalState` in `attempt-terminal-evidence.ts`, also accepts
`didDeliverSourceReplyViaMessageTool`; delivery and fallback follow that check, so only the
trajectory label is affected. A turn that ends with `poll` takes the same path.

An earlier attempt at the cross-context case did not exercise the guard: the model routed
around it with `sessions_send`, asking the session already bound to `<chat-b>` to roll in its
own conversation, where no cross-context target exists. The proof above is the direct call.

prs.title: fix(auth): suggest sign-in for missing OAuth credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OAuth-only providers with inline model definitions recommend `paste-api-key` when no matching sign-in is available.

## User Impact

Missing-sign-in errors show the provider's login command and agent-selection guidance. API-key recovery stays unchanged for custom endpoints, explicit API-key routes, and providers offering both methods.

## Why This Change Was Made

Choose recovery advice from declared authentication methods and native endpoint metadata after credential resolution fails. Existing provider-specific messages and the profile-specific failed-refresh diagnosis retain precedence. Prepared direct attempts still disable profile discovery while receiving accurate static recovery advice.

## Evidence

- Integrated main `02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba`, retaining its failed-refresh sign-in regression. Only the original three PR files differ from that base.
- **93 targeted tests pass**, including the upstream ended-sign-in case, canonical/alias/direct OAuth login, and the API-key controls:

  ```sh
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.synthetic-fail-closed.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
  ```

  Captured runner summary: `47 passed` in the profiles suite and `46 passed` in the other two suites; runner wall time 97.16 s. The changed test file completed in 24.89 s locally. Per-file CI timing was not available in the narrowly inspected CI records.
- Core and affected test-group typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, test-line budget (+129 / 400), source CLI build, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- [CI passed for the current head `7dd816184`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43336431021). CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, and the macOS Periphery report also passed. The separate security-sensitive approval is still awaiting a maintainer.

<details>
<summary>Recorded regression tests before and after the fix</summary>

The added tests from `7dd816184fab943018289820053df8a050a56a08` were run against the integrated base `02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba` production code, then against the restored current head. The two production files were restored byte-for-byte; HEAD and the test file stayed unchanged.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'missing provider auth recovery'
```

- Base production code: `3 failed | 6 passed | 38 skipped`. All three OAuth cases fail because the real resolver returns `paste-api-key` instead of the expected provider login command. All six API-key controls pass.
- Current PR head: `9 passed | 38 skipped`. The filter excludes the other 38 tests; the broader 93-test run is recorded above.

Captured base assertion:

```text
Expected: "models auth login --provider fixture-oauth"
Received: "No API key found for provider \"fixture-oauth\". ... Configure an API key (openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider fixture-oauth; ...)"
```

The received line is abbreviated here; only the diagnostic relevant to the assertion is shown. An earlier restricted-host attempt stopped before test execution with `EPERM: operation not permitted, write`; that setup failure is excluded from these results.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Captured actual local CLI commands and output — updated head</summary>

Captured `7dd816184fab943018289820053df8a050a56a08` at `2026-11-13T00:16:48.011Z`. These are new executions of the supported CLI, using a fresh isolated HOME/state/workspace for each case and no credentials. The synthetic OAuth plugin declares `appGuidedAuth: "oauth"` and a native catalog endpoint matching the inline model. The control provider is unowned and requires an API key. Only temporary filesystem paths are redacted below.

Both commands intentionally exit **1** because credentials are missing. The checked behavior is the recovery command in the actual JSON error. Neither a login handler nor model transport ran; the no-forwarding network guard stayed enabled.

**OAuth-only inline model**

```sh
pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent reporter --session-key agent:reporter:auth-recovery --model oauth-fixture/sample --message 'Synthetic missing-auth check.' --json --timeout 30
```

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "No credentials found for provider \"oauth-fixture\". Auth store: <auth-store> (agentDir: <agent-dir>). Sign in (openclaw models auth login --provider oauth-fixture; add --agent <id> to select the affected agent)."
  }
}
```

**Unowned API-key control**

```sh
pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent reporter --session-key agent:reporter:auth-recovery --model custom-fixture/sample --message 'Synthetic missing-auth check.' --json --timeout 30
```

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "No API key found for provider \"custom-fixture\". Auth store: <auth-store> (agentDir: <agent-dir>). Configure an API key (openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider custom-fixture; add --agent <id> for a non-default agent) or copy only portable static auth profiles from the main agentDir."
  }
}
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): compact Talk consult sessions after over-budget turns
prs.body:
Closes #195509

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a voice-heavy Talk session that grows past the prompt budget is never compacted. Every later consult re-sends a windowed copy of the whole history, which also misses the prompt cache, until someone runs `sessions.compact` by hand.

## User Impact

User impact: once a Talk consult leaves its session over the compaction threshold, OpenClaw compacts it the same way it already does after typed turns. Later voice questions fit the budget again and reuse a stable prefix. Consults under the threshold are unchanged: the upkeep runs, finds nothing to do, and returns.

## Why This Change Was Made

Typed replies and `openclaw agent` runs schedule optional post-turn session maintenance (memory flush, then compaction if needed). Anthropic attempts rely on that owner: with compaction replay on, they defer in-attempt threshold compaction to it. Native Talk consults (`talk-realtime-consult-*`) call the embedded agent directly, so nothing schedules that maintenance, and the preflight only logs `route=compact_only` and windows the prompt, by design.

The Gateway Talk consult adapter now schedules that same maintenance after a completed consult. It uses the reply path's eligibility gates: the OpenClaw harness, a successful auth observation, no in-run compaction (read from `agentMeta.compactionCount`, so the runner keeps owning durable compaction accounting), not aborted, yielded or errored, and compaction not disabled. The follow-up carries the consult's conversation tool policy, auth-pin provenance, compaction request budget, and the session's lifecycle revision and generation, read while the turn is still admitted. The context window comes from the route's provider-scoped thinking catalog, so it uses the model's real window, not the 200k default. Optional preparation failures are swallowed so they never replace the consult's answer. Upkeep is scheduled outside the consult's async work scope: when the consult returns, that scope drains and would abort the upkeep, which the real-Gateway run below caught. Maintenance takes its own root work and writer admission, as it does for typed turns.

Non-goals: the preflight's diagnostic-only heuristic route (deliberately not turned back into a compaction trigger), consult retention and prefix policy (#179236 / #179237), the daily reset for voice sessions (#185942), and chat-backed `talk.client.toolCall` consults, which already go through the reply pipeline.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway, native consult path, base vs head.** I ran a real Gateway child from this worktree with an isolated temp state dir on a free port, using qa-lab's Gateway harness. The agent model was a local Anthropic Messages stub: 36k context window, usage reported as request size / 4. The Talk provider was a fixture browser realtime provider requesting `gateway-control-v1`. For each turn the fixture emits a final ~9k-char spoken user transcript plus an `openclaw_agent_consult` call on the Gateway-owned control, so each turn is a native `talk-realtime-consult-*` run. Both arms ran the identical driver for 8 consults. Base is the production file from `8d269eb63c9`, rebuilt.

| | base (`main`) | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| memory flush / compaction summary calls | 0 / 0 | after consult 6 / 2 after consult 7 |
| consult 8 pre-prompt history | `messages=21`, no summary | `messages=13 ... compactionSummary:1` |
| consult 8 prompt estimate | 60,702 | 42,517 (was 58,494 at consult 7) |
| published session tokens after consult 8 | 29,982 (threshold 27,000) | 22,930 |

Head numbers were reproduced unchanged on the final squashed commit (`f50c391e7a9`, rebased on current `main`).

Base logged the reporter's line on every turn, e.g. `admitted provider attempt ... route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=60702 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=27000`, plus a `[prompt-cache] message 0 ... history must be append-only` rewrite.

**Control: head with `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false`.** Same driver, same built head. It matches base exactly: no memory flush, no summary calls, history reaches `messages=21`, and totals are `12776 → 29982`. The new upkeep respects the existing opt-out.

<details>
<summary>Verbatim driver output (base, head, control)</summary>

The driver prints each consult's stub-call kinds and the persisted session entry. The session id is the same for every consult in an arm.

```text
[base] consult 6: toolResults=6 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"2c5f951a-…","totalTokens":25066}
[base] consult 7: toolResults=7 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"2c5f951a-…","totalTokens":27524}
[base] consult 8: toolResults=8 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"2c5f951a-…","totalTokens":29982}
[base] FINAL arm=base consults=8 stubNonSummaryCalls=8 compactionSummaryCalls=0 totalTokens=29982

[head] consult 6: toolResults=6 stubCalls=consult,consult entry={"sessionId":"9f339ff0-…","totalTokens":25066}
[head] consult 7: toolResults=7 stubCalls=consult,summary,summary entry={"sessionId":"9f339ff0-…","totalTokens":26933}
[head] consult 8: toolResults=8 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"9f339ff0-…","totalTokens":22930}
[head] FINAL arm=head consults=8 stubNonSummaryCalls=9 compactionSummaryCalls=2 totalTokens=22930

[head-compaction-disabled] consult 7: toolResults=7 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"ef3a4162-…","totalTokens":27524}
[head-compaction-disabled] consult 8: toolResults=8 stubCalls=consult entry={"sessionId":"ef3a4162-…","totalTokens":29982}
[head-compaction-disabled] FINAL arm=head-compaction-disabled consults=8 stubNonSummaryCalls=8 compactionSummaryCalls=0 totalTokens=29982
```

The extra `consult` call after consult 6 on head is the memory-flush turn. The two `summary` calls after consult 7 are compaction.

Gateway log, pre-prompt history and preflight per consult (each line is logged twice, once per attempt record):

```text
base   consult 7: messages=18 roleCounts=assistant:6,custom:6,user:6 | route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=58494 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=27000
base   consult 8: messages=21 roleCounts=assistant:7,custom:7,user:7 | route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=60702 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=27000
head   after consult 6: memory flush dispatched
head   consult 7: messages=18 roleCounts=assistant:6,custom:6,user:6 | route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=58494 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=27000
head   consult 8: messages=13 roleCounts=assistant:4,compactionSummary:1,custom:4,user:4 | route=compact_only estimatedPromptTokens=42517 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=27000
control consult 8: messages=21 roleCounts=assistant:7,custom:7,user:7 (no memory flush, no compaction)
```

</details>

While building that proof, an earlier version of this patch scheduled the upkeep but never compacted. The memory flush aborted at `async-work-scope beginClose` ← `gateway-work-admission runWhenAllIdle`, the consult's own work scope draining. That is why scheduling now happens outside it.

**Regression.** `src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.terminal-writes.test.ts` runs a consult through the real Talk admission with a mocked model core. It asserts that the completed consult hands the session to `scheduleSessionMaintenance` with its session, provider, model and auth, and that the call happens outside the consult's work scope.
- `origin/main`: fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times`.
- Without the work-scope detach: fails with `expected true to be false`.
- Head: 4/4 pass.

**Checks.** `check:changed` passes core typecheck, core-test typecheck, changed-file lint and format, and the import-cycle and ratchet guards. Its dead-export scan fails only on `src/agents/runtime/index.ts: BashExecutionMessage`, an export this change does not touch. The test-line ratchet passes without an allocation.

**Review.** One default Codex pass came back clean. Four `gpt-5.6-sol` max-effort passes raised eight findings. Seven are fixed here:
- compaction accounting stays with the runner;
- the conversation tool policy is forwarded;
- a failed session read can't fail the consult;
- the real catalog window is used;
- the lifecycle fence and catalog are read inside the admitted turn.

The test-mocking finding is answered by the real-Gateway run above.

One P2 is still open, disclosed here: the catalog read runs right after `runEmbeddedAgent` resolves, still inside the admitted turn but after the attempt's own runtime scope has closed. If the model catalog refreshes, or the account switches, during a consult, the upkeep could budget against a slightly different window than the attempt used. The worst case is compacting one turn early or late. The reported case, an Anthropic route with a stable catalog, is unaffected. A follow-up could have the attempt report its resolved window, so the upkeep reuses it. I kept that out of this PR because it widens the runner's observer surface.

prs.title: fix(agents): native Codex chats get plugin MCP tools that use OpenClaw OAuth
prs.body:
Closes #197763 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a plugin-provided MCP server that uses OpenClaw-managed OAuth (for example Atlassian) shows as authorized in Settings, but a Codex-backed chat never gets its tools. The native Codex thread config carries the server URL with no credential, so Codex fails `initialize` with `invalid_token`. ## User Impact User impact: once a plugin's MCP connection is authorized, its tools are available in native Codex chats, the same as an `mcp.servers` entry authorized with `openclaw mcp login`. When the saved token can't be read, the server is skipped with a warning, matching configured servers. Remote Codex app servers still never receive OpenClaw-managed bearers. ## Why This Change Was Made The native Codex projection has two inputs. Owner-configured `mcp.servers` go through `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig`, which reads the saved OAuth token and projects it as an `Authorization` header. Plugin bundle servers went straight to normalization, and normalization drops `auth: "oauth"`, so they reached Codex with only a URL. `loadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfigCore` now sends the bundle's static OAuth servers through that same resolver, with the guards the configured path already uses: - Literal projection is only for local app servers. Both native callers pass `allowLiteralOAuthProjection: connectionClass !== "remote"`, and on a remote connection the server is omitted and reported. - A server whose token can't be resolved is omitted and reported through the existing `skipping unavailable MCP OAuth server` warning. - Read-only native fork preparation refuses, with the same message as the configured path, rather than projecting a server without its credential. - Requester-scoped servers are skipped before resolution. They never reach the native projection, so no operator token is read for them. - A plugin server shadowed by a same-named `mcp.servers` entry gets no bearer. Thread configs are deep-merged, so the configured URL would otherwise inherit the plugin's `Authorization` header. - The run's (or App session's) abort signal reaches the token lookup. A cancelled lookup rejects instead of being reported as an unavailable server. - App-session preparation logs skipped OAuth servers through the same warning as model turns. Relation to #197868, which targets the same issue: that PR adds the resolver call without the remote-app-server and same-name shadowing guards above. Without them the plugin's literal token reaches remote Codex app servers, and a different configured URL inherits it through the deep merge. It also reads operator tokens for requester-scoped servers. Non-goals: the Codex CLI backend, refresh-exchange behavior, and plugin auth state in the UI. Known limit, unchanged from configured servers: a warm App session (one whose native client is still live) keeps the bearer its thread started with until the next model turn rotates the thread. Configured `mcp.servers` OAuth bearers behave the same on `main`. Refreshing a live thread's credential from an App request would mean letting warm App acquisition take preparation authority and replace the session's thread, so I left it for a follow-up. ## Evidence **Real Gateway chat, real agent and model, base vs head.** Each arm ran a separately launched, built Gateway (`pnpm build:runtime`, then `node openclaw.mjs gateway run`) with: - an isolated, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; - a free loopback port and token auth. The setup per arm was: - **Agent:** the default agent on `openai/gpt-6-astra`, with `models.providers.openai.agentRuntime.id: "codex"`. Turns ran in the native Codex harness (installed `codex app-server` 0.166.0). - **Model credential:** an `openai/oauth` profile imported from the local Codex login with `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`. - **Plugin:** a Claude-format bundle installed with `openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities`. Its `.mcp.json` declares only `atlassian: { type: "http", url, auth: "oauth" }`. There is no `mcp.servers` entry. - **OAuth token:** saved in the isolated profile's MCP OAuth store through the real client provider (`provider.saveTokens`). - **MCP server:** a local streamable-HTTP server on a free port. It returns `401 invalid_token` unless it gets that bearer, and exposes a read-only `getJiraIssue`. The prompt was the same in both arms and went through `openclaw gateway call chat.send`: > Use the getJiraIssue tool from the atlassian MCP server to read issue PROOF-1 (read-only). Then reply on one line exactly: PROOF-197763 RESULT=. If no atlassian getJiraIssue tool is available to you, do not search or improvise; reply on one line exactly: PROOF-197763 NO-TOOL and end your turn. | | base (`main` production files) | head (`d50872fb32b`) | | --- | --- | --- | | requests the MCP server received | `POST auth= rpc=initialize` (401), nothing else | `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call tool=getJiraIssue`, each with `auth=` | | agent tool discovery (`ALL_TOOLS` lookup) | no `atlassian` tool | `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue` | | agent tool call | none | `atlassian.getJiraIssue {"issueKey":"PROOF-1"}` → `Issue PROOF-1: summary="PROOF-197763 marker issue", status="In Progress"` | | final assistant reply (`chat.history`) | `PROOF-197763 NO-TOOL` | `PROOF-197763 RESULT=PROOF-197763 marker issue` | The base arm is a scratch commit on this branch that reverts only the six production files to the merge base, then rebuilt. Both arms' `dist/build-info.json` match the commit under test: `8bcd48064d3` for base, `d50872fb32b` for head. Tokens are redacted. No live or shared Gateway or real Atlassian account was used.
Head transcript (from chat.history, trimmed) ```text user: Proof check. Use the getJiraIssue tool from the atlassian MCP server to read issue PROOF-1 (read-only) ... assistant: exec const t = ALL_TOOLS.filter(x=>/getJiraIssue/i.test(x.name)&&/atlassian/i.test(x.name)); text(t); tool: [{"name":"mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue","description":"Read a Jira issue by key (read-only). ..."}] assistant: atlassian.getJiraIssue {"issueKey":"PROOF-1"} tool: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Issue PROOF-1: summary=\"PROOF-197763 marker issue\", status=\"In Progress\""}]} assistant: exec text(await tools.mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue({issueKey:"PROOF-1"})); tool: {"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Issue PROOF-1: summary=\"PROOF-197763 marker issue\", status=\"In Progress\""}]} assistant: PROOF-197763 RESULT=PROOF-197763 marker issue ``` Base transcript: ```text user: Proof check. Use the getJiraIssue tool from the atlassian MCP server ... assistant: exec const t = ALL_TOOLS.find(x => /getJiraIssue$/i.test(x.name) && /atlassian/i.test(x.name)); if (t) { text(t); } else { text("NO-TOOL"); } tool: NO-TOOL assistant: PROOF-197763 NO-TOOL ```
**Real Codex app-server, base vs head (loader boundary).** A proof driver in a fresh Node process used an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, plus a temp `CODEX_HOME`. It set up: - a real Claude-format plugin installed under the isolated profile, declaring `atlassian: { type: "http", url, auth: "oauth" }`; - a local streamable-HTTP MCP server on a free port, returning `401 invalid_token` unless it gets the saved bearer; - the token saved through the real MCP OAuth client provider (`provider.saveTokens`). It then called the production `loadCodexBundleMcpThreadConfig` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`. The result went to a real `codex app-server` (codex-cli 0.166.0) as `thread/start` config, and the driver read `mcpServerStatus/list` for that thread. | | base (`main`) | head | | --- | --- | --- | | projected `atlassian` fields | `url` | `http_headers,url` (`Authorization: Bearer `) | | what the MCP server saw | `POST auth=`, `GET auth=` (401) | `POST auth=saved-bearer` | | Codex `mcpServerStatus` for `atlassian` | `tools: []`, `authStatus: "unsupported"` | `tools: ["getJiraIssue"]`, `authStatus: "bearerToken"` | **Regression.** `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts` saves a token in the real MCP OAuth store, then loads a plugin-declared OAuth server. It checks that: - the projection carries the saved bearer on a local app server; - a remote app server omits the server and reports it; - fork preparation refuses; - an aborted signal rejects the load rather than omitting the server; - a same-named configured server does not inherit the plugin bearer. The file moves to the database-worker project, because the real token store needs the host SQLite broker. - `origin/main`: fails with `AssertionError: expected { Object (mcp_servers) } to deeply equal { Object (mcp_servers) }` (no `http_headers`). - Head: 9/9 pass, including a server literally named `__proto__`, which keeps its own data property. The neighbouring `mcp-app-session-preparation`, `run-attempt-client-prewarm` and configured-path `bundle-mcp-codex.user-config` suites pass unchanged. **Checks.** `check:changed` passes core and extension typecheck, core-test and extension-test typecheck, changed-file lint and format, the SQLite worker ratchet (the test file joins the database-worker list), and the import-cycle and ratchet guards. Its dead-export scan fails only on `src/config/sessions/session-pending-input-source.ts: readPendingInputSource`. This change does not touch that file, and the export has no production consumer on the base commit either. **Review.** A default Codex pass came back clean, then four `gpt-5.6-sol` max-effort rounds. Every finding they raised is fixed here, and the fourth round was clean: - same-name shadowing could leak the plugin token; - cancellation now reaches both OAuth and auth-profile token refresh; - App-session preparation reports skipped servers; - `__proto__` server names survive the merge. One finding is disclosed rather than fixed: the warm App-session limit described above. Touching `src/agents/mcp-auth-profile*.ts` places this PR in the credentials security-review tier. prs.title: perf(ci): share compiler answers across database guards
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The database-worker and personal-credential guards use the same immutable compiler snapshot but separately ask it to resolve some of the same aliases and module exports. A full inventory of the frozen baseline made 11,088 repeated requests across those two methods.

## User Impact

Experiment rejected and closed unmerged. It removes repeated requests, but did not pass the published full-command speed screen. No change was landed and no CI or billing savings are claimed.

## Why

Keep raw compiler answers with the existing compatibility inspection owner and pass them to the credential guard. Each guard still applies its own forwarding rules and target classification. The maps live for one snapshot; module-export arrays are exposed read-only. No caller approval, credential boundary, diagnostic, or policy exemption changes.

Two production files: 29 additions / 18 deletions. The small growth gives both guards one owner for raw answers; the credential guard's duplicate alias map disappears. Release-note context belongs here; the changelog is release-owned.

## Evidence

- Baseline: `02f29597c1075c0db5193fe2e3f2d5409593cfba`. Candidate: `de0979ee421100e7cda24bfe0b05335685b453ec`.
- Full committed workload: `node scripts/database-worker-inventory.mjs --json`. Count profiling on the baseline completed successfully: alias requests 95,588 / unique 85,897 / repeated 9,691; module-export requests 4,532 / unique 3,135 / repeated 1,397. Instrumentation was temporary, excluded from speed measurements, and restored afterward.
- Native TypeScript client inspection confirmed each invocation makes an RPC; its method cache does not cache answers.
- `git diff --check`, targeted formatting, and normal commit hook passed.
- Fresh independent source review and full local ClawSweeper committed-range review of the exact baseline-to-candidate range found no actionable findings. ClawSweeper was correctness-focused; it did not execute tests or establish performance.
- Candidate counts: aliases 85,897 / unique 85,897 / repeated 0; module exports 3,135 / unique 3,135 / repeated 0. Exactly 11,088 repeated requests removed.
- All five completed benchmark invocations (count probe, two excluded warmups, measured baseline and measured candidate) produced the same complete decoded inventory, matching the baseline count probe. Original candidate bytes were restored afterward.
- The first measured pair failed the published screen; stopped without five pairs, tail-statistics claims, fixture execution, tooling typecheck or lint. No readiness or landing qualification.

### Result — rejected at the first measured pair

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Full inventory wall time | 60.078 s | 71.182 s | +18.48% |
| Total child CPU | 103.88 s | 120.50 s | +16.00% |
| Maximum child RSS | 5,917,180 KiB | 5,888,348 KiB | -0.49% |

This is one prespecified early-rejection pair, not an estimate of the general regression or production tail latency. It failed the required 5% wall-time improvement. Excluded warmups were baseline 65.513 s and candidate 58.542 s; their favorable candidate result did not replace the measured pair.

Environment: configured Boat/ascii-box provider, requested standard profile with the normal OpenClaw fast-tier mapping; observed 8 CPUs/affinity 8, 15.62 GiB physical RAM, Node 24.22.1. Cgroup CPU/memory limit files were not visible. Starting benchmark load was 0.268/0.127/0.192. Setup and transfer are excluded. This direct run has no hosted portal URL.

The workload completed and restored source before the wrapper reported a cleanup failure (exit 7, provider absence during release). A separate blocking native stop confirmed the task resource absent (exit 0). No host-key or source guard was relaxed.

### Acceptance rule — published before candidate timing

Use the same frozen source inputs, installed dependencies, Node version, and machine. Record available CPU/affinity, memory/quota visibility, and host load. Each inventory invocation starts a fresh compiler; excluded baseline/candidate warmups warm filesystem caches. Run serial, interleaved baseline/candidate pairs.

1. Count first, outside timing. Candidate must remove the repeated raw queries and preserve the complete decoded inventory.
2. First measured pair is an early rejection screen: require at least 5% less wall time, otherwise stop and close unmerged. Stop immediately for any metric at least 20% worse.
3. A qualifying screen proceeds to at least five measured pairs. Report median, nearest-rank p95 (the maximum with five samples), range, total child CPU, and maximum child RSS. Require at least 5% median wall-time gain, with p95, median CPU and median maximum-child RSS no worse. These small samples do not establish production tail latency or total process-group peak memory.
4. Every complete decoded inventory must match, and the existing negative guard fixtures plus targeted tooling typecheck/lint/format must pass before readiness or landing. Reject or fix any changed behavior; do not weaken guards.
5. Setup, source transfer, dependency reconciliation, count probes, and warmups are excluded from the speed table. Do not extrapolate to all PRs or Blacksmith spend without actual job-selection and runner evidence.

## What Problem This Solves

Agent-less automations fail to save on multi-agent Gateways even when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` is set. Use the scheduler’s existing owner resolution during inference-account capture so creation, editing, and execution agree on the effective agent.

## Evidence

Verified the save regression in a private macOS VM: with Agent empty, the Control UI save failed on parent `81720a0ebe47` with “no explicit owner” and persisted after reload on `f1bc59771d0`. A separate VM then saved and ran an agent-less automation through the Control UI against real Ollama `qwen3:0.6b`, with `worker` configured as the system agent. It completed successfully, returned the marker from worker’s workspace, and stored its transcript only under worker. Coverage confirmed that the changed capture owner-resolution statement executed. Ollama processed 2,550 input tokens and generated 9 output tokens in one native `/api/chat` request. The focused host run passed 105 cron/auth tests across four files; two relevant cases also passed inside the VM, and the new regression failed on the parent for the expected owner error. This verified Ollama’s supported local, accountless path without reading or copying a host key. Personal OAuth sign-in and hosted providers were not exercised.

Based on @DasX’s work in #194890.

Closes #197905

prs.title: fix(status): Ctrl-C does not stop openclaw status during the Gateway probe
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/197968

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Ctrl-C does not stop `openclaw status` or `openclaw status --json` while the Gateway probe waits on a Gateway that accepts connections but does not answer; the launcher force-kills the command about 2 seconds later (exit 137), and without the launcher the command keeps connecting for about a minute before it exits.

## User Impact

User impact: Ctrl-C during the Gateway probe stops `openclaw status` (text and `--json`) within about a quarter of a second with the interrupt exit code (130, or 143 for SIGTERM) and only the existing stopping line, instead of a forced kill or another minute of Gateway connections.

## Why This Change Was Made

The status scan's Gateway readiness wait and probe (`resolveGatewayProbeSnapshot` in `src/commands/status.scan.shared.ts`) did not take the command's abort signal, so an interrupt waited for the probe's own timeout. Both now take the ambient command signal, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197758 passed it for `sessions list`. An interrupted probe resolves as "aborted"; the scan now stops right after the probe instead of rendering that result as Gateway state.

## Evidence

Tested at this PR's head (base `main` `fc6c25e9156`).

Built CLI on Linux x64 with isolated state and config. The configured Gateway port is a stand-in TCP listener that accepts and never answers (an unresponsive Gateway). A PTY driver sends Ctrl-C 5 s after the CLI's first Gateway connection, which lands about 2 s into the probe connection, and records the exit code, the time from Ctrl-C to exit and each connection to the listener.

Before (base `main` `fc6c25e9156`):

```text
status --json                          exit 137 (SIGKILL)  2031.3 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held until the kill
status                                 exit 137 (SIGKILL)  2039.9 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held until the kill
status --json, OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1   exit 130           55041.5 ms after Ctrl-C, probe connection held 28.0 s after Ctrl-C, 2 more Gateway connections after Ctrl-C

# status --json, output after Ctrl-C (launcher)
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
<killed>

# status, output after Ctrl-C (launcher)
^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
■  Canceled
<killed>

# status --json with OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1, output 55 s after Ctrl-C
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "type": "cli_error",
    "message": "CLI stopping (SIGINT)"
  }
}
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

After (this PR): see the proof comment https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197969#issuecomment-6840048382. The interrupt exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) about 0.1 s after the signal, with only `Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` on stderr and nothing on stdout. `status` and `status --json` return quietly when the scan fails with the command's own abort reason; other scan failures keep their report.

Checks: `pnpm test src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (22 passed; the new test fails on base because the scan resolved instead of rejecting with the abort reason). The changed-file lint and the test-lines ratchet pass. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, high), base `fc6c25e9156` to head `4fbbb6b8883`, priority P0–P1: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

<!-- openclaw-preflight:v1
{"v":1,"repo":"openclaw/openclaw","base":"fc6c25e91564ca1f757d04c5b4676dcab6f66aaa","head":"4fbbb6b8883f99822d01093acb519317292d8425","tool":{"name":"autoreview","version":"source-a120e048f9fc"},"completion":"complete","summary":"Threshold P1; lower priorities not assessed; status scoped-clean; accepted 0; priority-filtered 0; scope/attribution-rejected 0; missing-required 0. Self-reported; see native report."}
-->

| Test file                                 | `--maxWorkers=1` wall                    | CI seconds                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/commands/status.scan.shared.test.ts` | 8.5 s (warm); 44.9 s on a cold first run | 10.5 s (`checks-node-changed`, 11.8 s with setup) |

Line deltas against main: production +34/-4 (`status.scan.shared.ts`, `status-runtime-shared.ts`, `status.command.ts`, `status-json-command.ts`); tests +19/-20 (the two no-fallback cases are folded into one table), no allocation file.

Not covered:

- A Ctrl-C during the readiness wait (the first Gateway connection, about 3 s) was not driven; every run's Ctrl-C lands in the probe. The unit test mocks the readiness wait, so the signal on that call is covered by reading the source only.
- The other Gateway reads in the status command take no signal here: the `--json` projection call, the overview's `status` and `channels.status` calls, the local `status` fallback, and `status-runtime-shared.ts`. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197909 changes those calls. A Ctrl-C that lands after the probe has returned, during one of them, is not changed by this PR and was not driven here.
- In a scan that still has an earlier phase pending (the update check under `--all`, or a deep scan), an interrupted probe can reject before the scan awaits it. The CLI may then print `[openclaw] Suppressed AbortError: ...` on stderr; the exit is the same. This comes from reading the source and was not observed. It is accepted and not coded.
- The update check and the Tailscale lookup in the same scan do not take the signal; both are bounded (the 10 s status timeout and 1.2 s).
- Linux only.

prs.title: fix: resume overlapping worktree cleanup waits independently
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Overlapping worktree-maintenance waits can cancel one another's scheduler wakeup, leaving cleanup pending until shutdown.

## User Impact

Each cleanup wait now resumes at its own deadline. Pacing, pressure thresholds, shutdown cancellation and scratch retention remain unchanged; no configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler replaces jobs with the same ID. Giving every pause its own ID preserves each promise's wakeup using the existing scheduler and UUID import. Production LOC is unchanged; the regression adds 22 test lines.

The resume job deliberately keeps its existing phase: the maintenance phase rounds deadlines and would change short pacing delays. Inspection found serial awaits in the current GC, template and scratch callers. This fixes the demonstrated overlapping-wait defect; it does not establish that overlapping callers caused the reported parked production pass.

## Evidence

The regression overlaps a 60-second removal wait with a one-second checkpoint wait through the maintenance owner's callbacks and real scheduler. The parent only settles the checkpoint; the fix settles both at their respective deadlines. All 65 maintenance and scheduler tests pass. Codex autoreview found no actionable findings. Changed-file formatting, lint, core/test typechecks and all other guards passed. `pnpm check:changed` reports unrelated unused exports in trusted-proxy co-author code (#196867) and inline-command UI code (#197466); both failures reproduce on exact main parent `20237d956bb5df8147144e6ea5fb0195c78d78ff`. Their introducing commits are `f4f290c52f961` (#196867) and `d90d52cce941c` (#197466). These are main regressions, not failures introduced by this two-file change.

Related: #197941, #197898, #197772.

prs.title: fix(release): warn when diagnostic receipts cannot seal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation can spend time running cross-revision diagnostics before rejecting their child receipts. The CLI previously printed the selected commits without explaining this limitation.

## User Impact

Operators now see a warning before dispatch, during dry runs, and when reconciling a retained request. Matching candidate and tooling revisions keep their existing output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing selection formatter now explains that cross-revision diagnostics cannot produce candidate-sealed child receipts and may fail release verification even when workloads succeed. Dispatch, receipt validation, and publication rules are unchanged.

The missing warning was observed in [this diagnostic run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43254031797), whose receipt publisher rejected different candidate and tooling revisions.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing warning against the base formatter; the same direct Node contract check passes with this change.
