prs.title: fix(anthropic): Claude Fable 5.2 is missing from the bundled catalog
prs.body:
Related: #196248

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `claude-fable-5-2` has no bundled catalog row. Live discovery can make the model visible, but its price, limits, and short aliases come only from the bundled manifest, so they are missing.

## User Impact

User impact: `anthropic/claude-fable-5-2` appears in the bundled catalog with its price, limits, and `fable-5.2` / `fable-5-2` aliases.

The bare `fable` alias is unchanged and still selects Fable 5.1.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR now covers item 1 of #196248. Item 2 (the Claude Code identity floor) is fixed on `main` by #196693, which adopts the version Anthropic names in a `claude_code_version_too_old` rejection and stores it, so the floor constant no longer needs a bump per model. An earlier revision of this PR raised the constant to 2.1.290; the merge of `main` drops that change and keeps #196693's design. Item 3 was fixed by #196459.

The docs describe Fable 5.2 as it behaves on `main`: always-on adaptive thinking, native fast mode, no assistant prefill, server-side refusal fallback, and the 1M window. They also note that the Claude CLI runtime needs an installed Claude Code 2.1.290 or newer, because that CLI sends its own version.

## Evidence

Catalog values (`$8/$40`, cache read `$0.20`, 5-minute cache write `$10`, 1M context, 128K output, always-on adaptive thinking) come from Anthropic's [Fable 5.2 overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview) and [pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing).

Evidence for the Claude CLI 2.1.290 note in the docs: a live check against `api.anthropic.com` with a Claude subscription token and the same identity headers OpenClaw sends, changing only the reported version:

| `user-agent` | `claude-fable-5-2` result |
| -- | -- |
| `claude-cli/2.1.280` | 400 `invalid_request_error`: "Claude Code 2.1.280 does not support this model; version 2.1.290 or newer is required." |
| `claude-cli/2.1.289` | 400, same message |
| `claude-cli/2.1.290` | 200, `stop_reason: end_turn` |
| `claude-cli/2.1.311` | 200, `stop_reason: end_turn` |

Tests:

* `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.test.ts` and the model contract cases cover the new row; `provider-model-id-normalization.test.ts` covers the `fable-5.2` / `fable-5-2` aliases and the unchanged bare `fable`.
* On this head (`f64e988a1df`, Linux, Node 24.22.2, 4 vCPU), each run with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, all passing: `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `cli-migration.test.ts`, `cli-process.test.ts`, `cli-version.test.ts`, `forward-compat-generation.test.ts`, `stream-wrappers.test.ts`, `claude-code-version-requirement.test.ts`, `fast-mode-unsupported.test.ts`; `packages/model-catalog-core/src/provider-model-id-normalization.test.ts`; `packages/ai/src/anthropic-client-identity-parity.test.ts`, `anthropic-cache-transport-parity.test.ts`, `transports/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`.
* `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` pass; `oxfmt --check` on the six changed files and `oxlint` on the changed code files are clean; `git diff --check` against `main` is clean.

Gaps:

* No end-to-end Gateway run. The live proof above is at the HTTP boundary only.
* Bedrock's long-cache matcher (`extensions/amazon-bedrock/bedrock-options.ts:93`) does not recognize Fable 5.2 yet. Not changed here.
* Item 4 of #196248 (tool-use ids changing on replay) is not addressed. From source: an unowned custom `anthropic-messages` provider gets `buildAnthropicReplayPolicyForModel` without `preserveNativeAnthropicToolUseIds`, so `toolu_…` ids in assistant messages without a thinking block are rewritten to alphanumeric form (`src/agents/tool-call-id.ts`), while messages with a thinking block keep theirs. The rewrite is deterministic for the same history, so on its own it does not explain a change between turns; I could not reproduce it live.
* PR CI on this head: the only failing job is `checks-node-compact-small-2` (and so `openclaw/ci-gate`). It fails in `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` because the PR wrapper inventory does not include `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/statements/validate.js`, newly imported by `src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts` in #197697. This PR does not touch those files; the same failure appears in an unrelated PR's run ([43329469130](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43329469130)), and #197976 (now merged) adds the missing source to the wrapper inventory. I classified this by hand from the job logs and `gh` API reads; `pnpm test:ci-failed 196605` was not run. On the previous head (`53a28733766`), the red job was the `anthropic-messages` prompt-cache case tracked in #196682; the changed-test selection lines of this head's run do not include that test.

Related: #197555

## What Problem This Solves

Rapid-MLX users need a named setup and memory-search provider in OpenClaw.

## User Impact

User impact: choose **Rapid-MLX** during setup, discover local chat models, and use `rapid-mlx/<model-id>` or an explicitly served embedding model for memory search. Rapid-MLX is an open-source local LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the bundled oMLX provider in #173327, reusing OpenAI-compatible transports with optional authentication and a default URL of `http://localhost:8000/v1`. Includes provider and memory docs, navigation, generated inventories, tests, official app/onboarding icons, and an existing generic activity glyph. No new external dependencies or changes to oMLX.

## Evidence

Before/after: real Control UI → Models → Add account → On this Gateway, with isolated local state. The before capture uses the same shared build with the new Rapid-MLX plugin omitted; the after capture includes the provider and its official-site onboarding icon. Both images were inspected and contain no personal data.

![Before: local provider list without Rapid-MLX](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/before.png)

![After: Rapid-MLX entry, official icon, and Connect server action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/after.png)

- Fix pass: onboarding metadata/auth-choice tests passed (25 tests); the browser capture asserts Rapid-MLX is absent before and present after, with a decoded icon and a Connect server action. Inventory/config-baseline and scoped format checks passed.
- `pnpm test:extension rapid-mlx`: 56 tests passed. The two files took 56.51s and 71.12s locally, including first-run compilation; CI timing is unavailable.

The 1,050-line allocation preserves the existing provider's auth and embedding boundary coverage.
- `pnpm build` passed; production and full-tree Knip unused-file checks found zero entries. Build emitted advisory UI bundle-budget warnings.
- Live at `http://127.0.0.1:8477/v1`, with isolated OpenClaw state: noninteractive onboarding saved the keyless connection; `pnpm openclaw models list --provider rapid-mlx --refresh --json` listed two models with status `ready`; `pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-id rapid-mlx-smoke --message 'What is 19 + 23? Reply with just the number.' --thinking off --json` returned `42` through Rapid-MLX. Direct streaming also returned `42` with usage metadata.

Broader checks exposed inherited failures: missing label rules for `celeris`, `fastino`, and `nace`, and a missing `celeris` icon. The provider/embedding contract tests themselves passed (49 tests). Live embeddings were not tested because the local Rapid-MLX server serves a chat model. Feature request: #197555.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed and tested locally.

## Verification (review follow-up)

Live on Apple Silicon against a local Rapid-MLX server:
- CLI setup, fresh-process model discovery and agent chat succeed. A saved connection stores no generated model rows.

- 140 focused tests and 8 package-boundary contract tests pass, along with scoped lint, a targeted typecheck, formatting and docs-link checks. I did not run a full release build or a repo-wide typecheck.

The `@openclaw/plugin-sdk` workspace devDependency and its lock entry are required by the extension package boundary contract, the same as the bundled oMLX extension.

prs.title: feat(ui): search Google from the Browser panel address bar
prs.body:
Closes #197895

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI Browser panel address bar does nothing when you type a search phrase and press Enter, and turns a single word such as `bitwarden` into `https://bitwarden/`. Unsupported addresses such as `javascript:` are also dropped with no message.

## User Impact

User impact: the address bar works like a browser omnibox. Text that is not an address, such as words with spaces or a single name like `devbox`, opens a Google search in the panel's browser. Addresses keep their current handling, including spaces in a path or query: explicit `http(s)://` URLs, hosts with a dot or port (`example.com/a b`, `devbox:443`), `localhost` and IPv6 literals. While a single name is typed, an option under the bar opens it as an address instead (**Go to `https://devbox/`**); Enter still searches:

![Browser panel address bar with "devbox" typed and the option "Go to https://devbox/" under it](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/f045699e4b9f25bce230ee266355b6ced553478c/images/2026/11/da141412-1dd9-42ed-bdad-6ba47c74cf48.png)

Input that can be neither opened nor searched (`javascript:`, `file:`) keeps focus and shows a hint under the bar:

![Browser panel address bar keeps "javascript:alert(1)" with a red outline and the hint "Only web addresses (http or https) or search text can be opened here."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2fa5a8e585e848a5b347a0d140dd1b977f312687/images/2026/11/f82b65e8-ce18-4f44-b5a2-e5f756b88b67.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

Search uses Google because none of the browsers the panel drives exposes its default search engine to OpenClaw: Chrome has no CDP or Chrome DevTools MCP access to its omnibox or engine, `chrome.search` is available only to extensions, and WKWebView has no default engine. Google is also the default of a fresh managed `openclaw` profile in most regions. Using the browser's own engine where an extension makes it possible can follow separately.

Address-versus-search parsing stays in `browser-url.ts`; reload keeps the existing URL-only normalization. The host part of the input (before the first `/`, `?` or `#`) decides whether spaces make it a search, and an explicit port is read from the typed text because URL parsing drops the https default. The "Go to" option appears exactly when the URL-only normalizer would open the text but the resolver searches it, which is the single-name case. The hint is toolbar state rather than the panel error line, because background panel refreshes clear that line within a second. The hint clears when the text is edited or the field loses focus, and it keeps the address input's IME composition handling.

## Evidence

- Typing `openclaw browser panel search` and pressing Enter in a local build, against an isolated Gateway with the managed headless Chrome, opened `https://www.google.com/search?q=openclaw+browser+panel+search` in the panel. Google answered that automated browser with its reCAPTCHA page rather than results:

  ![Address bar with the search text typed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2fa5a8e585e848a5b347a0d140dd1b977f312687/images/2026/11/90253ceb-34d6-4fa3-81d7-4b790dce158d.png)

  ![Panel after Enter, showing Google's reCAPTCHA page for the search request](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/2fa5a8e585e848a5b347a0d140dd1b977f312687/images/2026/11/09067991-f4f1-400c-a1e0-0f29013d7a49.png)

- In the same build, `javascript:alert(1)` showed the hint above, which was still visible 16 seconds later, with the field still focused.
- The "Go to" option screenshot above comes from the Control UI end-to-end harness against a mock Gateway, with `devbox` typed into the address bar.
- `browser-panel.test.ts` and `browser-panel-toolbar.test.ts`: 51 tests pass. New tests cover the address-versus-search cases, addresses with spaces in the path or an explicit default port, the "Go to" option (clicking it opens `https://devbox/`, Enter searches) and the hint; the hint and address tests fail without this change.
- `tsgo` (UI project), `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, oxfmt, stylelint on the panel CSS and `git diff --check`: clean. The one oxlint warning (Solid reactivity in the toolbar's "copy URL" action) is also present on `main`.
- Not exercised: the native macOS and Tauri hosts (WKWebView bridge), extension-attached Chrome, a Google results page, and picking "Go to" against a real browser (covered by the toolbar test).

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.title: feat: add an opt-in usage-ranked tool index
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large tool catalogs can crowd frequently used tools out of the bounded Code Mode index and Tool Search directory.

## User Impact

Adds an **off-by-default** Labs option, `agents.defaults.experimental.usageRankedToolIndex`, that gives frequently and recently used OpenClaw tools priority in those indexes. Protected core tools remain included, selected entries retain canonical rendering order, and ranking never grants tool access. Empty/off cold starts preserve the existing output.

Operators can inspect, bootstrap, or clear learned usage with `openclaw tools usage status|import|reset`. The matching Gateway methods require `operator.admin`. This is limited to the built-in harness; the MCP directory and Codex harness are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Count successful, actually executed native calls by catalog ID, not dispatch or Code Mode wrappers. Exclude errors, cancellations, running/pending work, client handoffs, and incognito sessions.
- Accumulate in memory per run. For canonical agent transcript stores, admission and count deltas share the existing transcript actor transaction, FIFO, and final live-authority grant; they add no separate usage writer request. Custom/shared stores and late completions use the existing retained settlement writer. Scores use a 14-day half-life.
- Let the existing session prompt-state owner freeze ranking in its checkpoint. Only session/reset, committed compaction, model/route, or harness/surface boundaries refresh it; normal turns and configuration refreshes preserve the surviving order. Child sessions inherit a filtered preference, not authority.
- Reserve 20% of each index's character budget for recently discovered tools without usage history. Unused reserve returns to ranked entries.
- Import the configured transcript store independently of the canonical counter database, including custom/shared stores. Preserve disjoint coverage intervals and exclude inherited history, duplicate nested dispatches, and live-managed runs. Size-omitted nested results are reported as unknown outcomes, not inferred to be successful.

**Config inventory:** the core count increases by exactly one (2,645→2,646) for the explicitly approved Labs setting; channel/plugin counts and hashes are unchanged. The inventory was regenerated, not hand-edited.

**Storage/update behavior:** agent schema 41→42 adds an initially empty STRICT `agent_tool_usage` table, with SQLite backup/rollback coverage and a PostgreSQL migration. Usage rows contain IDs, scores, and timestamps—not arguments, results, or per-call records. Existing metadata holds bounded import windows and 90-day run-participation receipts. Expired usage is excluded from reads and physically pruned on writes and hourly maintenance, even with the lab disabled. Retention skips closed Gateway admission and drains with its lifecycle owner. Reset fences pending writes without rewriting frozen prompts or transcripts. Crashes/failed flushes can lose unflushed counts; import does not replay live-managed runs.

## Evidence

All execution proof ran in isolated workspaces and state, on the Mac Studio or on AWS Crabbox. No live Gateway or operator database was modified.

### Upgrade compatibility from v2026.11.3 (Mac Studio, Crabbox)

Build of `039a1f3fac69` (rebased onto `origin/main` `e3502d33aa08`). Run on the Mac Studio through Crabbox (`CRABBOX_CONFIG=~/.config/crabbox/studio.yaml`, lease `studio-usage-ranked-tool-index`, run `run_56d0c35d8d2eceb904d0c3020b794513`). The test used one isolated state directory (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` under `~/crabbox-work/urti-proof/up-state`), Gateway port 18941 bound to loopback, and a synthetic OpenAI Responses provider on 127.0.0.1:18942 that scripts Code Mode tool calls. No live Gateway, credentials or operator data were involved. I used the synthetic provider rather than a real model, because the ranking checks need deterministic tool calls.

**Before the upgrade, on v2026.11.3** (`npm install openclaw@2026.11.3`, `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (847611d)`):

- Config: synthetic `openai` provider with models `gpt-a`/`gpt-b`, `agents.defaults.model.primary`, `tools.codeMode.enabled`, the Responses endpoint, plus `openclaw config set agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds 900`. `config validate` passed.
- Sessions with history: `hist-a` (`sessions_list` ×3 and `session_status` ×1 through Code Mode, then a follow-up turn; 16 history messages), `hist-b` (`sessions_list` ×1) and `hist-c` (plain chat).
- Automation: `openclaw cron add --name urti-nightly --cron "0 3 * * *" --message "synthetic nightly automation"`, alongside the built-in `heartbeat-main` job.
- Databases: agent `openclaw-agent.sqlite` at `user_version=27`, state `openclaw.sqlite` at 22.
- Gateway stopped, then the standard pre-upgrade backup ran: `openclaw backup create --verify` produced a verified archive (`2026-11-12T13-26-26.862-08-00-openclaw-backup.tar.gz`, 24.5 MB).

**Upgrade.** `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran with the PR build, as candidate Doctor does in `openclaw update`. It exited 0, saved pre-migration SQLite backups for both databases (`*.pre-startup-migration-ff67a46b-….bak`), and migrated the agent database 27→**42** (`agent_tool_usage` present) and the state database 22→39. The PR Gateway then started on the same directory with no errors.

**Everything loads intact.** Results were captured through the running Gateway (`config get`, `sessions.list`, `chat.history`, `cron list --all`) and compared with the v2026.11.3 capture:

| Data | v2026.11.3 → PR build |
| --- | --- |
| 4 settings (`timeoutSeconds`, primary model, Code Mode, Responses endpoint) | identical |
| Session list (keys, session IDs, models) | identical |
| `hist-b`, `hist-c` history | identical (message-by-message digest) |
| `hist-a` history | all 16 earlier messages preserved in order; the 2 new messages are the post-upgrade turn |
| `urti-nightly` automation | identical name, schedule, enabled state and message |

`heartbeat-main`'s payload is rewritten by main's existing heartbeat migration (Doctor's "heartbeat migration backups" step). The cron capture from main `e3502d33aa08` on the same snapshot is byte-identical to the PR's.

**Lab off: no recording, prompt unchanged.** I restored the v2026.11.3 snapshot and ran the same Doctor and the same first turn in upgraded session `hist-a`, once with main `e3502d33aa08` and once with the PR. Instructions, the full tool schemas (10,697 B) and the Code Mode index (21 rows, 38 omitted) were byte-identical. The 50 KB input differed only in the `Docs:` checkout path and the minute in the turn timestamp. A further lab-off turn calling `sessions_list` twice left `tools usage status` at `enabled: false, rowCount: 0`.

**Lab on: ranking from pre-existing history.** After `openclaw config set agents.defaults.experimental.usageRankedToolIndex true` and a Gateway restart:

- `openclaw tools usage import --agent main --since 90 --dry-run --json` reported `applied: false` with 2 candidate rows: `sessions_list` 6.0 (3 + 1 from v2026.11.3 history, plus 2 from the lab-off turn) and `session_status` 1.0. `status` still reported `rowCount: 0`.
- `tools usage import --agent main --since 90` applied the same 2 rows, and `status` then showed them.
- In a new session, the Code Mode index grew to 31 rows (28 omitted) and now lists `sessions_list` and `session_status`, which the cold 21-row index omitted. Rows keep canonical order. `status --session` shows the frozen snapshot `orderedToolIds: [sessions_list, session_status]`.
- Pre-existing v2026.11.3 session `hist-c` got the same ranked index and the same frozen snapshot on its first turn with the lab on.
- The agent database stayed at 42 throughout.

**Downgrade.**

- **v2026.11.3 on the upgraded directory:** the Gateway refuses to start and Doctor refuses to run, both before touching anything. The first incompatibility it reports is main's state database (39 > 22): "Gateway refused startup because 1 OpenClaw database schema(s) are newer than this build … Run a build at least as new as the writer …, or stop the service and restore your pre-upgrade backup created with openclaw backup create."
- **Main `e3502d33aa08` (agent schema 41) on a copy:** startup is refused with "agent database for agent main … uses schema 42; this build supports 41".
- In both cases the database versions were unchanged afterwards. Rolling back means restoring the verified pre-upgrade backup, the same as for any other schema bump.

Logs observed in the upgraded Gateway, not caused by this PR: the `skill-workshop` `agent_end` warning "Plugin invocation scope is closed" appeared 3/3 tool-call turns on both main and the PR on the same upgraded state, plus macOS-only config watcher and scratch-root notices.

### Rebased head `73448cf482e9`

The current head is `73448cf482e9`, on `origin/main` `4efd662cc2c6`. Two generated-only rebases followed the `039a1f3fac69` gate run:

- Onto `2a1914519f65`: the config baseline and Gateway predicates were regenerated.
- Onto `4efd662cc2c6`: `package.json` `schemaVersions` now keeps main's new `state: 40` alongside the PR's `agent: 42`. Main's agent schema is still 41.

On `73448cf482e9`, local checks passed:

- `pnpm tsgo:all`, `config:docs:check`, `gateway:validators:check`, `db:kysely:check`, `db:postgres:check` and `sqlite:sessions-schema:check`.
- 42 focused test files: both conflicted files' consumers, the ranking, Tool Search, Code Mode and tool-usage tests, and every non-PostgreSQL `src/state` migration test.

The upgrade proof above ran on the `039a1f3fac69` build. Neither later rebase touched PR runtime code.

The first rebase, onto `origin/main` `e3502d33aa08` (136 commits ahead of `544e5c37f780`), produced the head that the AWS gates and Studio proofs below ran on. Its conflicts:

- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`: regenerated (`pnpm config:docs:gen`). Core count is main's +1, for the Labs setting.
- `src/agents/tool-search-directory.ts`: kept main's run-granted exclusion (#197594's run-granted tool directory) and the PR's ranked native rows. Both `isCoreCodingSurfaceToolName` and `isRunGrantedCoreToolId` are imported, and main's new `buildRunGrantedToolDirectory` now filters with the PR's `NativeToolDirectoryRow` type. `tsgo` caught a predicate mismatch here that Vitest did not, and it is fixed in the same commit.
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-system-prompt-prepare.ts`: kept main's `buildRunGrantedToolDirectory` import and runtime-context listing alongside the PR's `ToolUsageRankingSnapshot` input to `prepareToolPrompt`.
- Agent schema: main is still at 41 (`openclaw-schema-versions.ts`), so the PR's 42 still follows main's latest. No renumbering was needed.

Gates on AWS Crabbox lease `cbx_e47e618961fa` (real git checkout at the exact head):

- Passed: `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, `pnpm tsgo:all`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm gateway:validators:check` and `pnpm protocol:check`.
- 56 focused test files passed. They cover both conflicted files' consumers (`attempt-system-prompt`, `attempt-tool-search-prompt`, `attempt-session-runtime-prepare`, `attempt-prompt-phase`), Tool Search directory/MCP/discovery, `tool-usage-ranking`, Code Mode, tool-search executor, the tool-usage Gateway/session tests, the CLI policy tests, the wrapper-inventory tests and every `src/state` migration test.
- `pnpm check:changed --base e3502d33aa08` (run `run_f9115a2a559fe176dd0cca7c7d7d3946`): typecheck, lint (848 s) and 37 lanes passed, including the dead-export scan, which main has fixed since the previous head. Only the Plugin SDK surface budget failed (entrypoints 163 > 162, exports 3888 > 3867, callable 2243 > 2236, wildcard reexports 1 > 0). `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` on a clean `e3502d33aa08` worktree on the same box fails with identical numbers, and this PR does not touch the Plugin SDK.

### CI follow-ups

**Head `6aa74a2f8959`** (rebased onto `origin/main` `d30e45c3f48e`; generated `predicates.js` regenerated). Its CI failures on `73448cf482e9` and this head:

- **`server-maintenance.telemetry.test.ts`, PR-caused, fixed in `test: keep tool usage retention out of the telemetry maintenance fixture`.** The PR schedules a `tool-usage-retention` maintenance job, and in the worker-free telemetry fixture it tried to launch the registry-listing worker ("tool usage retention failed: Worker-free Gateway fixture attempted to launch a worker"). The fixture now stubs `pruneRegisteredAgentToolUsage`, as it already does for the other storage sweeps; retention keeps its own scheduler test in `server-maintenance.test.ts`. The CI red was timing-dependent and did not reproduce locally before the fix. After it, both maintenance test files pass under Node and the pinned Bun fork on the Mac Studio, and locally.
- **`help-exit.process.test.ts` (precomputed root help): fixed on main.** #197936 (`d30e45c3f48e`) replaced the static `node:tls` import in `src/cli/one-shot-exit.ts`. On this rebased head the file passes on the Mac Studio under Node and Bun.
- **`extensions/codex/src/node-app-server.runtime.test.ts` ("gates native resource readiness…"), inherited on Linux.** The command proof returns `exitCode: 1, stdout: ""` instead of `worker-command-proof`. It fails identically on clean `4efd662cc2c6` and `d30e45c3f48e` worktrees on Linux, while the PR head passes it on the Mac Studio (Node and Bun). This PR touches no Codex files; the shard is selected by changed-core dependency.
- **`test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` (PR wrapper inventory), inherited.** It reports six missing `packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/*` imports reached through `src/gateway/openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts` (main's OpenClaw ID work, #197628/#197697). The same test fails identically on a clean `origin/main` `02f29597c107` worktree; none of those files are touched here.

**Full CI on `6aa74a2f8959`:** 208 checks passed (including all PostgreSQL conformance shards) and 43 were skipped. Two test jobs failed, both inherited (above), which also fails the `openclaw/ci-gate` aggregate: `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1-3` (the Codex runtime test) and `checks-node-compact-small-8` (the PR wrapper inventory). The telemetry and help-exit failures from earlier heads did not recur. CI was not rerun.

**`native-hook-relay.test.ts` 120 s timeout: not reproduced.** Run on the Mac Studio (darwin-arm64), whole file, interleaved main `e3502d33aa08` / PR head, 25 runs per cell:

| Runtime | main | PR head | Target test duration (min / median / max) main · head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node 24.22.1 | 25/25 pass | 25/25 pass | 157 / 161 / 163 ms · 158 / 160 / 163 ms |
| Pinned Bun fork `openclaw-v1.4.4-20261026-191755ec11` | 25/25 pass | 25/25 pass | 158 / 162 / 167 ms · 158 / 161 / 188 ms |

The CI failure was on a Linux x64 Bun shard. The Bun runs here used the same pinned fork tag (confirmed from the running process path), but on darwin-arm64. That's 0/100 failures in total, with no difference between main and the PR, so I recorded it as a non-reproducing CI timeout, not a PR defect.

**Latency acceptance.** On 2026-11-11 Josh reviewed the Studio latency benchmark and judged the overhead not meaningful (about +2 ms paired median, in his words), which settles the no-meaningful-overhead acceptance criterion. The instrumented 300-pair table below is kept as recorded.

### Earlier rebased-head behavior proof (AWS Crabbox)

Proof build `9eac6b2e24a1` (runtime tree identical to `01679c308c1d`; the later CI fixes change prompt finalization only for settled-tool runs and the `tools` CLI root), rebased onto `origin/main` `544e5c37f780`. Both trees were built with `pnpm build` on AWS Crabbox lease `cbx_43da335fa37d` (c7a.8xlarge, eu-west-1). The run used one isolated Gateway (`--port 18931 --bind loopback`, its own `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/`HOME`) and a synthetic OpenAI Responses mock on `127.0.0.1:18932` that scripts Code Mode `exec` calls. Turns went through `POST /v1/responses`. Status came from `openclaw tools usage status --json [--session <key>]`. No live Gateway, credentials or operator data were involved. The surface is Code Mode, whose 8,000-character index omits 37–38 of the 58–59 catalog tools on this config.

**Feature off: same as main.** The same config and state path ran against both builds, and the first provider request was compared byte for byte. `tools` was identical (16,830 B), and so was the Code Mode index (21 rows, 38 omitted). The rest of the 45,060 B input differed only in two checkout-path lines (`Docs:`/`Source:` pointing at the two worktrees). With the lab off on the head build, `sessions_list` was used three times and then a fresh session was opened. The index was unchanged, and `tools usage status` reported `enabled:false, rowCount:0`.

**Feature on.** The Gateway clock was shifted 20 days back (`libfaketime`, `FAKETIME=-20d`, for the Gateway and its CLI), and `update_goal` was denied:

| Step | Observed index / state |
| --- | --- |
| Session A, cold. `sessions_list`×3 + `session_status`×1 in one turn (5 requests) | All 5 requests: 21 rows, 37 omitted, same index bytes (`6c8dba94…`). Neither tool listed. Snapshot `orderedToolIds: []` |
| Session A, next turn | Same index bytes. Usage now `sessions_list` 3.00, `session_status` 1.00 |
| New session B (fresh prefix) | 31 rows, 27 omitted. Now lists `sessions_list` and `session_status`. Snapshot `orderedToolIds: [sessions_list, session_status]` |
| Session A after `sessions.patch` model gpt-a→gpt-b (prefix break) | Index refreshed to B's selection. Snapshot re-read, newcomer first-seen times preserved |
| Gateway restart at the same faked clock | `rowCount: 2`, scores 2.99997 / 0.99999 before and after (only decay over ~10 s) |

**Real clock, `update_goal` allowed again** (newly added tool):

| Step | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Restart, status | Usage survived. Scores decayed by 20 days at the 14-day half-life: 1.1145 / 0.3715 (3×2^(−20/14)) |
| Session A, same prefix | Ranking stayed frozen (`at` still 20 days ago). The catalog refresh admitted `update_goal` as first-seen now, without rereading scores |
| Session A after a model change gpt-b→gpt-a (prefix break) | 32 rows. `update_goal` (unused, now the only tool inside the 14-day newcomer window) entered the reserved newcomer slot. `progress_card` (unused, earlier id, first seen 20 days ago) left. Ranked tools stayed |

The proof scripts (mock, config writer, driver) and raw logs are kept off-repo as task artifacts. Ports, state dirs and the lease were cleaned up after the run.

**Rebase and gates.** After the first rebase, check:changed found four PR-owned failures, and commit `fix: classify tool usage SQL as worker-owned` fixes them:

- The database worker ratchet flagged 13 main-thread T1 calls in `tool-usage.kernel.ts`, plus 3 inherited in `session-cold-storage-chunks.ts`. Fix: reviewed worker/purge classifications, and `tool-usage-read.worker.ts` registered as worker-only.
- The first-party mock-export ratchet flagged a mock without an isolation note.
- The dead-export scan flagged two unused exports.

The second rebase, onto `544e5c37f780`, resolved a conflict in `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.ts` with #197594: the GitHub publication tool-listing pin now refreshes the lazily prepared, ranking-aware prompt. That PR's new test was adapted to `prepareSystemPrompt`. Generated config baseline and Gateway predicates were regenerated (main's committed `predicates.js` lacked `inheritedDefault`). Agent schema 42 still follows main's 41; no renumbering was needed.

On AWS Crabbox (real git checkout at the exact head):

- Passed: `pnpm check:changed --base 544e5c37f780` lanes including typecheck-all and lint (914 s), `pnpm tsgo:core:test` after the test-type fix, `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm check:no-conflict-markers`, the database-worker and mock-export ratchets, and targeted Vitest for the conflicted and ranking-owner files. The earlier Studio run passed all 33 PR test files.
- Inherited red on main, unchanged by this PR: the Plugin SDK surface budget (identical failure on main), the dead export `scripts/lib/mac-runtime-portability.mjs: auditMacAppPortability` (from #197383), and `db:worker-inventory:check` (stale on main; not a CI gate).


**First full CI run (head `01679c308c1d`).** Six PR-caused failures were fixed in `d627ff5e0f54` (`fix: complete tool usage cutovers for CLI, prompt finalization, and CI inventories`):

- `attempt-prompt-phase.test.ts` (settled-turn finalization): the PR had switched the prompt-commit choice to `inHistorySystemUpdates`, so settled finalization, which has no active prompt series, committed a pending prompt. The commit now also requires the active series updater, restoring main's contract while ranking-only runs still persist the tool surface. Red under Node before, green after.
- `root-command-descriptions.test.ts`: `tools` was a reserved, unregistered root and a root-help alias, but this PR registers it as a built-in command. `tools` is now a normal built-in root (it keeps its fast, plugin-free startup policy); only the legacy `tool` stays reserved. `openclaw tools --help` now shows the tools help instead of root help.
- `check:madge-import-cycles`: the moved `createHeldModelRun` helper created a cycle between two spawn test-support files. It now lives in the leaf `subagent-spawn.held-model-run.test-support.ts`.
- `openclaw-agent-memory-revision-migration.test.ts`: the v30→current migration now creates `agent_tool_usage`, so it joins the declared scope (as earlier version steps did).
- `eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `pr-worktree-provision.test.ts`: `src/state/openclaw-agent-tool-usage-schema.ts` was missing from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`.

Inherited from main, not caused by this PR: `help-exit.process.test.ts > exits naturally after precomputed root help` fails identically on clean `544e5c37f780` (`src/entry.ts` → `src/cli/one-shot-exit.ts` → static `node:tls`, from #197382; neither file is touched here). On AWS Crabbox lease `cbx_8ed4d01ea875` (run `run_ebde532cef8556f10fef50b0f986c57b`), the fixed head passed `check:madge-import-cycles`, 42 focused test files (including every non-PostgreSQL migration test in `src/state`, both wrapper-inventory tests and the production spawn boundary), and `check:changed --base 544e5c37f780` typecheck, lint (851 s) and ratchets. Only the main-inherited Plugin SDK budget and dead-export lanes remain red.

**Full CI on `d627ff5e0f54`:** complete. 215 checks passed (including all PostgreSQL conformance shards) and 49 were skipped. Two test jobs failed, which also fails the `openclaw/ci-gate` aggregate:

- `checks-node-compact-small-8`: only the main-inherited `help-exit.process.test.ts > exits naturally after precomputed root help` failure described above.
- `checks-node-changed-compact-large-8`: one 120 s timeout in `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.test.ts > keeps replacement pending PermissionRequest approvals when stale approvals settle`, while awaiting a session-entry write. It does not reproduce: the whole file passes locally at this head (97 tests in 49.5 s, Node and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`), and the PR does not touch that test or its entry-write path. CI was not rerun.

### Transaction co-commit repair and current limitations

**Publication status:** the PR left draft so full CI could run. The measurements in this subsection were taken on pre-rebase head `6710d304b90a`. Josh accepted the latency result on 2026-11-11 (about +2 ms paired median, not meaningful); see "Latency acceptance" above.

- Every tool-usage kernel mutation declares the existing empty session write scope. Usage writes no longer invalidate unrelated retained session facts; a real replica regression fails without the scope and passes with it, retaining the session-mutation negative control.
- Canonical transcript appends carry usage admission and count deltas inside their existing actor transaction. Removed the standalone begin operation and turn-end flush request. Generation checks, FIFO ordering, final live-authority checks, rollback, incognito exclusion, and the default-off flag remain intact. No schema, retention, permissions, or dependency changes in this repair.
- The admitted logical-target binding is carried through both manager and direct-message append paths. A real logical-store regression covers both paths; it does not relax target matching. Custom/shared transcript stores retain canonical counter ownership and use the existing run-settlement writer. A crash before that foreign-store receipt may leave the run importable.
- Imports exclude active recorders as well as durable live-run receipts. Independent read-only review found one verified P2: settlement could relabel captured pre-reset rows with a newer generation across an awaited import. The red/green regression now captures the generation with its rows before yielding. No other verified P0–P2 finding in that review.
- Studio core types passed (**1.42 s**), the agents-sessions test graph passed (**2.30 s**), changed-file lint passed (**7.02 s**, zero warnings/errors), and changed-doc MDX passed (**0.29 s**). **100 tests across 10 affected files passed in 105.44 s**. prs.title: fix: dashboard stays on the shared token profile after Tailscale Serve recovers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the macOS dashboard switches to the Gateway's shared token profile (default theme, no pinned shortcuts) and stays there until the app is relaunched, after managed Tailscale Serve briefly drops and recovers.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Tailscale restart or Serve recovery, the dashboard returns to the Serve sign-in address and the user's own profile on its own. During the outage it still falls back to the shared token profile, so it keeps working. No data was lost before this fix either: the user's profile rows stayed intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway advertises `controlUiIdentityUrl` in an operator hello only while a managed Serve route is published. When the route is withdrawn or replaced, it already closes identity-bearing operator sockets with 1012 so they reconnect and get a fresh hello. The reverse case had no equivalent. A hello sent while Serve was unpublished, during startup or a recovery, kept its identity-less answer for the life of the connection. The Mac app reconnected during the outage, correctly rebuilt the dashboard with native token auth, and never received another hello once Serve came back.

Eligible identity-less hellos now bind to a "next Serve publication" signal owned by `tailscale-published-origin.ts`. When managed Serve publishes again, those connections close with 1012 and reconnect with the identity route. On the Mac side, the existing reconnect path already moves the dashboard back to browser identity (`remote dashboard uses verified browser identity across tunnel reconnects`), so no Swift change is needed. Only operator hellos that could actually use Serve identity subscribe: `auth.allowTailscale` set, auth mode not `none`, Control UI enabled, and no origin published at all. Trusted-proxy, funnel, node-role and `allowTailscale: false` connections are untouched.

Accepted edge case: for the length of the outage, the dashboard shows the shared token profile. The Gateway has no way to tell a transient outage from an intentional removal, and a working dashboard is the better fallback. Telling the two apart would need a protocol addition.

## Evidence

**Incident (2026-11-12, Mac app 2026.11.2, Gateway 2026.11.3), from read-only log inspection:**
- 20:38:02Z: Gateway logged that the `serve route claim exited`; all `auth=tailscale` browser sockets dropped, along with the app's native operator socket.
- 20:38:02.9Z: the app's native socket reconnected while Serve was still down, so its hello carried no identity URL. At 20:38:03.6Z a new dashboard page connected as `client=openclaw-macos … auth=token`.
- 20:38:11Z: Gateway logged `serve enabled`. Nothing renewed the app's hello, so the page stayed on the token profile.
- WebKit's log shows the old WebContent process was not a crash. Its page was closed by the document replacement and WebKit reaped it about 10s later. The crash-recovery path (`webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate` → Reload) wasn't involved in this event. It resolves through the same `windowConfiguration(for: .primary)` as launch.

**Regression test (real WebSocket, real `startGatewayTailscaleExposure` publication):** `renews a hello announced while managed Serve was unpublished once its route returns`. An operator gets an identity-less hello, managed Serve then publishes, and the test expects a 1012 close followed by a renewed hello carrying `https://gateway.tailnet.ts.net/`.
- Red on base `4efd662`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 1012, Anything ]`, 0 calls.
- Green with the fix.

**Overreach control:** the existing `advertises the personal dashboard for resolved $mode auth with $tailscale` table publishes a Serve origin after each hello and expects no close for rows that cannot use Serve identity. I checked it by mutation: subscribing every operator hello fails 6 of those rows.

**Checks on this head:**
- `pnpm vitest run` on every consumer of the published-origin and identity modules (`server-tailscale`, all `server/ws-connection/*`, `mcp-app-standalone`, `portal-service`, `provider-browser-auth/*`, `models-auth-login`): 41 files, 611 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: format, lint and the other guards OK. The dead-export scan reports `src/gateway/trusted-proxy-git-coauthor.ts`, which is already on main and unrelated.
- Typecheck: the guarded `tsgo` lanes refuse to run in this worktree because the compiler resolves through the shared pnpm store, outside the checkout. Running the pinned compiler directly (`tsrs -p tsconfig.core.json`, plus the `gateway-server` and `gateway-root` test projects) found no errors under `src/`. CI's guarded typecheck is the authoritative result.
- `git diff --check` clean.

**Review:** local autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode `origin/main`..`42e197d`, the pre-rebase head with the same patch, max priority P2): `scoped-clean`, "patch is correct (0.87)", no remaining findings. It ran on the operator config's ChatGPT route because the environment's `AUTOREVIEW_CODEX_CONFIG` provider override doesn't match the operator config, and the helper refuses that combination before launch.

**Not run:** an end-to-end proof with the Mac app and a live managed Serve route. It needs a disposable macOS VM with its own Tailscale Serve, and I didn't touch the only Serve route available (the user's live Gateway). The Gateway behavior is proven over a real socket through the real publication path. The Mac reconnect consumer is covered by its existing test.

<details>
<summary>Test audit</summary>

- `connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` (whole file audited): the socket server and hello delivery from the existing withdrawal test now live in a shared `withHelloSocketServer` helper used by both Serve socket tests. Assertions are unchanged (real hello methods, 1012 close, renewed identity URL). Added the regression above. No cases removed.
- `server-tailscale.test.ts` (whole file audited): `expectNoControlUiIdentity` now checks `?.url`, because an unpublished-route answer may carry a renewal signal without a URL. All callers still assert that no identity is advertised.
- Production delta: `tailscale-published-origin.ts` +19/−3, `control-ui-identity.ts` +13/−3, `connect-hello.ts` +9/−6. One docs paragraph in `docs/platforms/macos.md`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(talk): pick a working transport when switching voice providers
prs.body: Related: #195149 AI-assisted: Yes. [OpenClaw session log](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/9c586bbec4eaf7eb2f14a270dc39ffd9). ## What Problem This Solves Talk settings retain Gateway relay when switching from xAI to OAuth-only OpenAI, so Talk fails until the user manually chooses WebRTC. ## User Impact Changing the provider or model, including resetting the model to its default, selects WebRTC for OpenAI without Platform credentials when the target model supports WebRTC. Accounts with Platform credentials retain a compatible relay selection. ## Why This Change Was Made The catalog now exposes OpenAI Platform credential availability separately from its selected-provider `configured` flag. Settings uses that fact to apply the OAuth/WebRTC policy on provider and model changes. This does not remove OAuth support from the relay runtime or introduce a startup fallback. Model-family transport restrictions still apply. This does not override provider-reported compatibility — it meets it. `configured=true` answers "can OpenAI be selected" (yes, via OAuth/WebRTC). `platformAuth=false` answers "can gateway-relay serve it" (no: relay needs a Platform key — both the Nov 8 iPhone and Nov 10 prod `talk.session.create UNAVAILABLE: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured` failures prove it). Switching to WebRTC follows the provider's own capability report. ## Evidence - Live Gateway with this head (`30053f31244`), November 11, ChatGPT OAuth and no Platform key: in Settings → Talk, switching the provider from xAI (Gateway relay) to OpenAI with the default `gpt-live-1-codex` set Transport to **WebRTC** without manual editing. Then, on the same Gateway from the iOS app (OC 102499): after switching xAI to OpenAI, Talk started straight away over WebRTC with no further settings edits. Gateway log: config change at 05:05:36Z, `talk.client.create` ✓ at 05:05:45Z, then two `talk.client.transcript` ✓. | OpenAI selected, default `gpt-live-1-codex` | Talk listening over realtime WebRTC | Live voice turn transcribed | |---|---|---| | | | | - Physical iPhone, November 8: switching xAI → OpenAI (`gpt-live-1-codex`, subscription OAuth without a Platform key) retained relay. Starts at 09:03:51 and 09:04:21 returned `talk.session.create ✗ UNAVAILABLE: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured`. Manually choosing WebRTC at 09:06:47 led to successful `talk.client.create` at 09:09:37. [Redacted device trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192876#issuecomment-6719676687). - Production Gateway, November 10 at 07:26:10.909 UTC: the same Codex/OAuth/relay case returned `talk.session.create ✗ UNAVAILABLE: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured`. WebRTC session creation succeeded on the same Gateway at 01:27, 02:00, and 07:23 UTC. - Regression against the previous PR head: provider-switch and model-change UI assertions failed (2 failed, 38 passed); the targeted catalog assertion failed (1 failed, 19 skipped). The new assertions require a `webrtc` form write despite `configured: true`, and separate Platform credential availability from relay readiness. - Patched focused suites: catalog **22 passed**; Talk Settings UI **41 passed**. Coverage includes Platform credentials present/absent, a rejecting auth predicate, provider switching, explicit model changes, and resetting the model to its default. - Commands: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/talk/handlers/catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/config/talk.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, both under `nice -n 15`. - No persisted configuration fields or migrations change. `platformAuth` is an optional catalog response field. - Fresh install from this head (`30053f31244`, clean build): a new Gateway with generated config has no authored `talk` values (runtime defaults apply). `talk.catalog` reports OpenAI `configured: false`, `platformAuth: false`, `supportsBrowserSession: true`, transports `[webrtc, gateway-relay]`; xAI `configured: false`, transports `[gateway-relay]`. No realtime provider is configured (scratch carries no voice credentials by policy). - Fresh install, bug scenario in Settings → Talk: picking xAI Grok Voice saves `{provider: xai, transport: gateway-relay}` (gateway log: `config change detected … (talk.realtime.provider, talk.realtime.transport)`). Switching the provider to OpenAI Realtime Voice then saves `{provider: openai, transport: webrtc}` with no manual transport edit — the auto-WebRTC switch: - Latest-stable (`v2026.11.3`, commit `847611dcaa3`, clean build) upgrade: a Gateway created from stable with `{provider: xai, transport: gateway-relay}` saved, then moved to this head and restarted, keeps `{provider: xai, transport: gateway-relay}` (config unchanged apart from the code dir). Switching the provider to OpenAI after the upgrade saves `{provider: openai, transport: webrtc}` — the same auto-flip. - Behaviour contrast on stable (pre-PR): the same xAI → OpenAI switch preserves `transport: gateway-relay` (only `talk.realtime.provider` in the change log). `talk.client.create` then rejects with `INVALID_REQUEST: talk.client.create is client-owned; use talk.session.create for gateway-relay`, and `talk.session.create` with OpenAI + relay returns `UNAVAILABLE: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured` — the reported November 8/10 failures, reproduced on stable. On this head the same `talk.client.create` passes transport validation and stops only at provider credentials (`UNAVAILABLE: Realtime voice provider "openai" is not configured`). Scratch Gateways carry no OpenAI OAuth or Platform key by policy, so the live voice leg rests on the November 11 prod proof above (same head, ChatGPT OAuth, no Platform key: `talk.client.create` ✓ plus transcripts). - Redacted gateway logs (config changes, both `talk.*.create` outcomes): [fresh install](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/evidence/195156-fresh-upg-20261112/evidence-195156/fresh-6-gateway-excerpt.log), [stable bug behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/evidence/195156-fresh-upg-20261112/evidence-195156/stable-7-gateway-excerpt.log), [upgrade base→head](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/evidence/195156-fresh-upg-20261112/evidence-195156/upg-3-gateway-excerpt.log). prs.title: feat(gateway): role definitions no longer turn on named-role enforcement without a default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway cannot hold role definitions without also switching on named-role enforcement for every operator sign-in. The presence of `gateway.roles` refuses device-token and setup-code sign-ins that have no verified identity, turns off browser-code pairing and owner ingress, and caps Tailscale and trusted-proxy users at the default role. OpenClaw ID needs role definitions on a personal claw without changing how its other sign-ins behave.

## User Impact

User impact: none for existing Gateways. Every valid config already has `gateway.roles.default`, so it keeps enforcement exactly as before.

`gateway.roles.default` is now optional. A config with `definitions` and no `default` defines roles as data and otherwise behaves like a Gateway with no `gateway.roles`.

Required action to be aware of: removing `default` from a team Gateway's config now turns named-role enforcement off, where it used to fail validation. `assignments.byGithubLogin` without a default is a validation error.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Named-role enforcement applies only when `gateway.roles.default` is set. One helper, `src/gateway/operator-role-enforcement.ts`, answers that question, and every enforcement gate that tested for `gateway.roles` now uses it: sign-in and pairing, owner and person ingress, HTTP profile requirements, session sharing, cron, web push, `send`, questions, tool invocation, and the bundled `mcp-relay` and `visitor-access` plugins.
- Code that reads definitions as data (model catalogs, role-name validation) still reads `gateway.roles.definitions`.
- Change detection still compares the whole `gateway.roles` object, so adding or removing a default reloads and re-checks connections.
- With no default, a profile resolves to no named role. `users.setRole` with a role name is refused and names `gateway.roles.default`; clearing with `null` works in every state.
- OpenClaw ID member policy is unchanged in all three states.

## Evidence

- New tests with definitions and no default: setup-code and device-token-only operator connects succeed; browser-code start and approval work; owner ingress is allowed; Tailscale identity scopes are not capped; `users.setRole` is refused and `users.list` shows no effective role; config validation accepts definitions alone and rejects an unknown default and assignments without a default.
- Focused run: 13 files, 387 tests pass. A broader 22-file run passed except one fixture that relied on definitions alone enabling enforcement; it now sets a default and its refusal assertion is unchanged.
- Four existing expectations changed, each only because `default` is no longer required: the schema rejection of definitions alone, role resolution with no default (denied to none), and two fixtures that gained an explicit default.
- Targeted typechecks, lint, format, config schema and docs checks, SDK boundary checks and line ratchets pass.
- An independent review listed 162 non-test references to `gateway.roles` across 66 files and found no missed or wrongly switched enforcement gate, and no P0 or P1.

Known gap, found by that review (P2): two Doctor checks in `src/commands/doctor/cron/execution-context-check.ts` and the replay script `scripts/dev/cron-context-replay.mts` still test for the presence of `gateway.roles`. With definitions and no default, Doctor can wrongly report that an automation will lose owner access. It only reports; it repairs nothing. #197785, later in this stack, fixes it.

Not run: the full repository suite and a live Gateway test.

prs.title: fix(slack): match canonically equivalent names in allowlist resolution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An allowlist entry written in NFC form (e.g. `@Renée`, precomposed) fails to resolve a Slack profile whose display name is stored in NFD form (`Rene\u0301e`, decomposed), and vice versa. The two strings compare unequal under `===` even though they are canonically equivalent, so the user is reported `resolved: false` instead of being matched.

The same omission predicate affects the user's exact-name comparison against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, and `profile.real_name`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSlackUserAllowlist` in `extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts` compares the allowlist entry name against profile names with `===` on lowercased strings. Lowercasing does not canonicalize Unicode, so NFC/NFD-equivalent spellings of the same name never match. Both sides of the comparison are now normalized with `normalize("NFC")`.

This is the same shape already accepted for the feishu sticker-search path (`#190043`, `extensions/feishu/src/sticker-catalog.ts`) and the slack/feishu/msteams directory lookups that normalize query and candidate before matching.

**Security guard (P1):** canonical matching is a fallback, never a replacement. Exact (lowercased) spelling stays the primary comparison, preserving the pre-existing principal selection. If two active humans have display names that differ only by normalization form (one NFD, one NFC), the configured name resolves to the exact-spelling match even if the canonically-equivalent user appears earlier in the directory. This prevents NFC normalization from displacing the configured principal with a different Slack user id.

Production LOC is `+28/-3` across one file. No new validator, option, config item, or persistence strategy is added.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Allowlist entries that differ from the stored profile name only by Unicode normalization form now resolve to the correct user id instead of being reported unresolved. Matching for already-canonical names is unchanged. NFC normalization is a canonical-equivalence relation used as a fallback only: it never merges two distinct names, and it can never displace an exact-name match, so it cannot admit a different principal than the one the configured name denotes.

## Evidence

### Shipped entry-point proof (production WebClient over local fixture)

The real exported `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` is exercised through its production `createSlackLookupClient` WebClient path against a local `users.list` fixture, using the existing `SLACK_API_URL` seam the plugin itself supports. No Slack client is mocked: the same code path that ships resolves entries over the fixture.

- Product head SHA: `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`
- Current-main RED baseline: `632dced4affb7a338d0def2b7059c246ed33b0af`
- Production entry: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` (`extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.ts:99`) over the production `createSlackLookupClient` (`extensions/slack/src/client.ts:47`) and its `users.list` fetch.
- Decision surface: allowlist entry name matched against `user.name`, `profile.display_name`, `profile.real_name`.
- Recorder/readback boundary: the `resolved` flag and resolved `id`/`name` in `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` output.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
  - both NFC/NFD cross-form resolve cases fail (resolved: false)
  - both canonical-direction admission cases fail (no derived grant, sender denied)
  - competing-principal case fails (active grant never derives, intended sender denied)
  - removal case fails (first turn never admits)
  - exact-name / accent-stripped / same-form / ASCII controls pass
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
 ✓ resolves NFC entry against an NFD profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ resolves NFD entry against an NFC profile through the production WebClient and local users.list fixture
 ✓ keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 ✓ does not admit a different principal (accent-stripped) through the production path
 ✓ keeps same-form and ASCII controls unchanged through the production path
 ✓ name-derived grant through production admission > admits the canonical sender for NFC/NFD entries through production ingress
 ✓ ... > rejects the competing principal while the canonical grant is active
 ✓ ... > denies a different sender (unresolved accent-stripped name) before any agent/provider I/O
 ✓ ... > denies subsequent messages once the name-derived grant is removed
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
 [test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

### Shipped CLI trace (`openclaw channels resolve`)

The shipped CLI entry point is executed against the same local `users.list` fixture through the plugin's own `SLACK_API_URL` seam (loopback only; the fixture logs every request). No Slack client, transport, or resolver code is mocked or substituted: the command runs the real bundled slack channel plugin (`plugin.resolver.resolveTargets` → `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the production WebClient). One CLI invocation is one directory-query batch; the fixture serves a fixed directory per scenario and logs `POST /api/users.list` for each run.

Setup (synthetic token, loopback fixture, nothing public):

```text
$ export SLACK_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:47891/api/        # local users.list fixture on loopback
$ export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=$PWD/proof/openclaw.json    # channels.slack.botToken="xoxb-synthetic-proof" (synthetic)
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs channels resolve --channel slack --kind user <entries>
$ node --version   # v24.22.1
```

Base (`resolve-users.ts` at current main, same tree minus this PR's slack files):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved             # cross-form NFC entry vs NFD-stored profile: the defect
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name: control
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match (pre-existing behavior)
@Renée -> unresolved            # cross-form NFD entry vs NFC-stored profile: the defect
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence (pre-existing on base)
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Head (this PR, head SHA `0e25f23c568a73ea54c92cb926e7ea39bce2225b`; built from a tree whose slack files are byte-identical to the head SHA):

```text
# directory: one user, display name stored NFD (decomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée' '@Renee'
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFC entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFD_STORED (Renée)   # same-form exact match unchanged
@Renee -> unresolved             # accent-stripped distinct name still unresolved
# fixture: [fixture][nfd-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: one user, display name stored NFC (precomposed)
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée' '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)   # cross-form NFD entry now resolves (fixed)
@Renée -> U_NFC_STORED (Renée)    # same-form exact match unchanged
# fixture: [fixture][nfc-stored] POST /api/users.list

# directory: NFD-stored user listed FIRST, NFC-stored exact spelling second
$ channels resolve --channel slack --kind user '@Renée'
@Renée -> U_INTENDED (Renée)     # exact-name precedence intact: the canonically-equivalent
                                 # earlier directory entry never displaces the exact-spelling match
# fixture: [fixture][precedence] POST /api/users.list
```

Both NFC→NFD and NFD→NFC directions resolve on head and were unresolved on base; same-form matching, the accent-stripped control, and exact-name precedence are unchanged. IPs are loopback, the token is synthetic, and no non-public endpoint is touched.

### Authority-chain proof: production DM ingress through final effect

The authority chain no longer stops at the resolver return value or a bare admission boolean. `createMonitorTestContext` returns a context whose `readRuntimeContext` is the real `createSlackRuntimeContextReader`, so awaiting it runs the production `resolveWorkspacePolicy` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/runtime-policy.ts:239-250`), which resolves the allowlist names through the real `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` over the local `users.list` fixture and merges the derived ids into `ctx.allowFrom` via `mergeAllowlist`. The resolved policy context is then handed to the production DM ingress entry point `prepareSlackMessage` (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts`), the function the monitor calls for every inbound message; it runs the DM admission gate `authorizeSlackDirectMessage` and, on admission, returns the exact `PreparedSlackMessage` object the monitor dispatches to the agent/provider. No admission helper, Slack client, or dispatch seam is mocked.

- **Both canonical directions admit the intended Slack ID at final effect.** `@Renée` (NFC) against an NFD-stored profile, and the NFD spelling against an NFC-stored profile, each resolve to `U_ACCENT` through production policy reload, the id lands in the allow-from list, and `prepareSlackMessage` returns a non-null `PreparedSlackMessage` for sender `U_ACCENT` — the object that reaches agent/provider dispatch.
- **The competing principal is rejected while the canonical grant is active.** With `@Renée` derived to `U_ACCENT` and present in allow-from, a message from `U_OTHER` — a distinct sender with its own fixture display name and identity, resolved per user id exactly as production resolves sender names (`prepare.ts:381`) — returns null: the DM gate drops the event before any agent/provider I/O. The derived grant admits exactly the resolved principal and never a different Slack user id.
- **A distinct name is denied before any agent/provider I/O.** With the accent-stripped `@Renee` configured (unresolved), `U_ACCENT` never becomes a derived grant and both `U_ACCENT` and `U_OTHER` are dropped before dispatch.
- **Removing the name-derived grant denies subsequent messages on the same runtime policy reader.** First turn `@Renée` resolves and `U_ACCENT` is admitted at final effect. The published config is then replaced with one whose only entry is the stale `@Renee`; the same reader rebuilds policy on its next read (`runtime-policy.ts:116`, `current.cfg !== cfg`), the derived id leaves allow-from, and a subsequent message from `U_ACCENT` is dropped before dispatch — the same live-policy-change path the monitor uses, no reconnect or fresh monitor.
- **Exact-name principal is preserved (P1 regression).** With `U_OTHER` (NFD display name) before `U_INTENDED` (NFC display name) in the directory, `@Renée` resolves to `U_INTENDED`, not the canonically-equivalent earlier entry. This test fails on the pure-canonical head (selects `U_OTHER`) and passes on this head.

Base (`resolve-users.ts` without `normalize("NFC")`):

```text
 Tests  6 failed | 4 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Pure-canonical head (without exact-first guard):

```text
 × keeps exact-name matches ahead of canonically-equivalent directory entries
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
 FAILED (exit 1)
```

Head (this PR):

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
 [test] passed 1 Vitest shard
```

### Focused unit regression

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed on this head. The NFC/NFD cross-form cases are covered by the production-WebClient live-proof group instead of duplicated mocked-client cases; the focused unit suite retains its existing mocked-client coverage of resolution inputs and outputs.

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.live-proof.test.ts` — 10 passed, 1 shard, ~50s wall.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/slack/src/resolve-users.test.ts` — 9 passed, 1 shard.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Not tested: no live Slack API call and no full gateway process boot. `resolveSlackUserAllowlist` resolves names to IDs from a `users.list` response; the fixture drives the real WebClient through the plugin's own `SLACK_API_URL` seam. The authority chain runs the production policy reload and the production DM ingress over the fixture; the remaining runtime path (socket-mode event reception) is exercised by existing monitor tests, not re-driven here.

## Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+28/-3`
- Test LOC: `+390/-0` (live-proof integration, including the authority-chain group); the focused unit suite is unchanged (added NFC/NFD mocked-client cases were dropped per review as duplicates of the live proof).
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `normalizeLowercaseStringOrEmpty` helper already used in this file; adds only `normalize("NFC")` on both comparison sides, matching the accepted feishu sticker-search fix (#190043).
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. NFC normalization is a canonical equivalence used as a fallback only — it collapses only spellings of the same name and never displaces an exact-name match, so it cannot widen admission to a different principal; the P1 two-id regression and the accent-stripped control prove distinct names are still denied, the competing-principal case proves the derived grant rejects every other sender identity at the production ingress boundary, and the same-reader removal case proves the grant is revoked by the same live-policy path that created it.
