prs.title: fix(ui): preserve table expansion across reaction containers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Flat-chat Markdown tables lost their ability to use spare transcript width after #197823 (`0d602b36cb3fd5ea7b3b5645e314421e88a51660`). The new message query container correctly positions reaction tabs, but the inherited, untyped table-outset calculation then resolves its container units against that narrower message container.

## User Impact

Wide assistant tables can use the surrounding transcript space again, while preserving avatar clearance, bubble containment, mobile scrolling, Details reservation, and expanded-table interactions. Reaction placement is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register the existing `--chat-table-outset` property as an inherited length so its row producer resolves the transcript-relative calculation before descendants inherit it. Its initial zero preserves the existing unset/mobile behavior, and the bubble override stays zero. This retains the reaction container and adds no new setting or layout policy. The registered initial value also removes three redundant variable fallbacks; an equivalent clamp simplifies the producer calculation. Production net growth is four lines for the existing property's type contract.

## Evidence

The original three table cases reproduce on the actual failed CI merge `e4405e4a99cd311d35b7e93b14d22c60558d9243` and on clean main parent `8608f8810a8e7dfee7575d36426124d6cd5102b5`: widths 668 equal 668 twice and 768 equal 768 once, instead of exceeding prose width. The original assertions and tests are unchanged by this PR.

- All three focused original cases: parent red and candidate green in Chromium. The two leading-table cases also passed in WebKit. The temporary three-case adapter run used **two WebKit cases plus one Chromium desktop/mobile case**, not three WebKit cases.
- Table interactions, bubble activity, and reaction E2E siblings: 25/25 passed.
- Content-column and reaction browser siblings: 12 Chromium cases passed; the four admitted WebKit reaction cases passed.
- Existing short-assistant name/action geometry cases passed at 320px and 1366px.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed on the final simplification. Fresh independent Codex review of the complete one-file PR: no actionable findings. The final simplification passed 25 Chromium E2E cases, 12 Chromium browser cases, four WebKit reaction cases, and both leading-table WebKit cases.

Initial exact-head CI `43324932729` was red. Its CSS regression is repaired: the canonical paired bundle check against `fc6c25e91564ca1f757d04c5b4676dcab6f66aaa` now passes at **+63 raw CSS bytes / +59 gzip bytes / zero JavaScript byte change**, within the unchanged 64-byte raw CSS allowance (initial candidate: +78 bytes). Existing absolute main asset overages are not waived or changed.

The separate raw-tool disclosure-anchor case reported a 129px shift. That identical signature also occurs in CI merge `5490dd7aef01931636b48ca656e895451ad0678d`, which lacks this CSS registration; causal attribution remains open. The original case, a predecessor-order probe, and a temporary geometry-only observer passed locally on exact failing merge `9ec2b6e2e0ba8acb8935b407572ca6116e8fb3f6`; these are non-recurrence, not a fix or proof of flakiness. Original assertions and deadlines were preserved, and diagnostic edits were restored. Final exact-head CI [43332049762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43332049762) passed at `4fa659dc6abc7c74a71c1a221dd318ab700a24d0`, including the performance gate and all six selected ordinary UI E2E shards. This changed-source run does not attribute the earlier disclosure failure; no rerun-to-green is claimed. Final-head ClawSweeper review has zero open items and no actionable findings.

Synthetic before/after screenshots were inspected at 1600×1000. They show restored table width with the avatar and surrounding UI unchanged. The fixture uses only synthetic messages and service data. No runtime performance claim is made from these correctness runs.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep assistant process chatter out of Dreaming candidates
prs.body:
Closes #80664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Dreaming admits assistant scratch notes such as `Need commit PR.` and `Now inspect.` as durable session-corpus candidates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared session scanner rejects whole-body assistant chatter before candidate construction, leaving generic transcript export and existing admission/provenance controls unchanged.

This preserves the focused approach from #80666 and #111922 by @ArthurNie, including @vincentkoc's durable-signal boundary refinement. The October 13 update merges current main and resolves the scanner conflict without expanding the three-file contribution.

## User Impact

User impact: Dreaming and session backfill exclude narrowly defined assistant process notes while retaining user text and assistant evidence containing PR numbers, commit SHAs, or results. Previously ingested memory is not rewritten.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `dc71f9a026c25135b26e068ad3fd78af4d3f15c2` (merged main `983f4a3bdbf7`). Fresh main `7c1b789ca5b` has no intervening changes to memory-core or the applicable contribution policy; the candidate merges cleanly. Local timings/results below apply to the candidate, not a synthetic merge with newer main.

- Current-main production baseline: both new regressions fail because all three reported scratch notes enter candidates.
- With the filter: both complete touched test files pass, **34/34**. This includes actual canonical SQLite-backed backfill, user lookalikes, durable assistant results, scan progress, provenance and recovery coverage.
- Independent Claude review on this exact head: clean, no findings. A final one-file autoreview of the test typing correction also returned clean; earlier merge-snapshot autoreviews did not certify attribution.
- Production and test extension typechecks, targeted type-aware lint on all three changed files, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed. The conflict update preserves both current-main scanner helpers; the backfill fixture now obtains its type from the canonical transcript helper instead of a removed alias.
- Broader memory-core run: **1,600 passed, four skipped, one failed** in the first 171-file batch; the wrapper did not proceed to the two remaining files. The failure is `manager-provider-probe.test.ts`, which observed one leftover fake timer after a successful embedding probe. The test, fixture and production probe owner are byte-identical to the checked base. One isolation rerun reproduced it, the base-scanner control passed, and the restored final candidate passed **4/4**. This establishes intermittency, not a proven repair; the broad run is not claimed green and no timer assertion was weakened.
- Aggregate changed checks also found pre-existing max-lines suppression/dead-export problems outside the three-file patch. Targeted typed lint timed out during SDK preparation on its first attempt; one normal retry completed preparation and lint successfully, without changing the wrapper or deadline. The aggregate run is not claimed green; exact-head PR CI remains required.

Measured touched-file wall times: ingestion **17.42s**, canonical backfill **48.97s**. The new backfill regression itself took **423ms**; the complete file also exercises existing SQLite worker, provenance and recovery contracts. CI durations for this new head are not yet available.

The earlier merge-snapshot autoreview's whitespace suggestion does not apply because snippets are normalized and trimmed before the predicate. No filter broadening, timeout increase, assertion weakening, or unrelated cleanup is included.

<details>
<summary>Historical production CLI proof on the original reviewed head</summary>

The original `0e9f75e2aaa9` head was exercised through an isolated real session-backfill CLI. This is historical evidence, not a new CLI run on the October 13 merge.

```text
seeded messages: 5
openclaw memory session-backfill --agent main --from 2026-09-12 --to 2026-09-12 --json
candidateCount: 3
topCandidates:
  User: Keep the durable release note for the memory candidate filter.
  Assistant: Commit 9f2a3b1 passed CI.
  User: Now inspect.
stagedEntries: 0
```

The assistant messages `Need commit PR.` and `Now inspect.` were excluded. The new merge also has fresh canonical-store regression proof as reported above.

</details>

AI-assisted implementation; the author owns the code, scope, and evidence.

prs.title: fix(channels): opt-in NFC normalization for config directory queries
prs.body:
<details>
<summary>maintainer-edits</summary>

Maintainers may push to this branch to finish or adjust the change; "Allow edits by maintainers" stays enabled. The touched files are one shared helper plus its test, and seven channel config files each gaining a single `normalizeUnicode: true` line — a maintainer can re-point or narrow without rebasing anything else.

</details>

<details>
<summary>maintainer-options</summary>

- **Land-ready**: opt-in NFC normalization in the shared config-directory helper; shipped-CLI base/head receipt on IRC (NFD query matches NFC key on head, empty on base) plus NFC control; `+13/-2` production in one file, `+2` per channel config file, zero new files, zero config/schema/auth/storage surface.
- **Alternatives considered**: (a) patch each channel lister with inline NFC like whatsapp/feishu-live already do — rejected, nine config-driven listers funnel through `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` and would re-derive the same predicate; (b) rewrite stored config keys to NFC — rejected, that mutates user data; (c) make NFC the unconditional default — rejected, that is the `merge-risk: compatibility` label on #189988, this PR avoids it by keeping the default unchanged.
- **Scope**: `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts` + `.test.ts` + 7 channel config files (`irc`, `telegram`, `discord`, `line`, `zalo`, `googlechat`, `feishu`). No `plugin-sdk` export-list change (`scripts/lib/plugin-sdk-shipped-surface.json` untouched), no lockfile change.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query <NFD café> --json` returns `[]` even though `channels.irc.groups["#café"]` is configured. The config-driven directory filter lowercases both operands and never normalizes Unicode, so a decomposed (NFD) query misses a composed (NFC) key — and the reverse misses too. The same predicate covers every config-driven directory listing: `irc`, `line`, `reef`, `signal`, `telegram`, `zalo`, `zalouser`, plus the config halves of `feishu`, `matrix`, `discord`, `slack` and `msteams`.

Seven channels that use the shared helper are affected: **irc**, **telegram**, **discord**, **line**, **zalo**, **googlechat**, **feishu**. Six other channels (whatsapp, feishu-live, slack-live, matrix-live, msteams-live, signal) already do NFC normalization in their own directory filters, proving the fix pattern.

Precedent: whatsapp `directory-config.ts:92`, feishu `directory.ts:45`, slack `directory-live.ts:82`, matrix `directory-live.ts:146`, msteams `directory-live.ts:68`, signal `aliases.ts:154`. This PR closes the gap for config-driven directory listings.

Related: #189988 (same bug, different approach — makes NFC unconditional, currently stalled with `merge-risk: compatibility`).

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` is the single owner of config-driven directory query matching. A new optional `normalizeUnicode` parameter, when `true`, normalizes both operands to NFC after lowercasing. The default remains unchanged (no NFC), preserving backward compatibility for any caller that relies on the current behavior.

Seven channel configs opt in by passing `normalizeUnicode: true`. Stored ids, returned entries and spelling, `limit`, empty-query behavior and non-matching queries are unchanged. No validator, option, config key, schema, dependency or persistence change; the `plugin-sdk` export list is untouched.

Production LOC is `+13/-2` (one file) + 7 one-liners in channel configs.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

An operator who types or pastes `#café` in either Unicode form now gets their configured group back from `directory groups list` for the 7 affected channels. Same-form queries and non-matching queries behave exactly as before, and accent folding is **not** introduced (`#cafe` still misses `#café`).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `d171cef73311`
- Current-main RED baseline: `c7962d6a108c`
- Production entry: real source CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel irc --query <NFD> --json` (argv/command tree identical to the packaged CLI), Node 24.22.1 in a `lexiflow-all` container
- Canonical owner exercised: `applyDirectoryQueryAndLimit` in `src/channels/plugins/directory-config-helpers.ts:20-25`
- Decision surface: `--query` on `directory groups|peers list` for config-driven channels; fixture is a generated `channels.irc.groups` keyed by channel name

prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

Tested on `upstream/main` `20237d956bb` (2026-11-12) before, and `c50d8b26e1e` (this PR head, rebased onto it) after. Real built CLI, local fake MCP servers on loopback, isolated temp HOME and state dir. Ubuntu 26.04, Node 26.10.0.

`node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning|error`. Exit codes: warning threshold / error threshold.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy server (remote or stdio) | no finding; exit 0 / 0 | no finding; exit 0 / 0 |
| Remote outage: connection refused, HTTP 503, HTTP 401, hang past the 10 s deadline | error; exit 1 / 1 | warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 0 |
| Remote invalid catalog (bad tool entry, repeated cursor) | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Stdio failure: crash at start, missing executable, invalid catalog | error; exit 1 / 1 | error; exit 1 / 1 |
| Remote 503 and stdio crash in one config | error + error; exit 1 / 1 | error + warning `mcp-service-unavailable`; exit 1 / 1 |

Upgrade check (published `openclaw@2026.10.8`, then this build, same temp state dir, remote HTTP 503): at the error threshold 2026.10.8 gave error, exit 1; this build gave no finding, exit 0. State files stayed byte-identical. Not the `openclaw update` command.
Unit tests (4 files, `--maxWorkers=1`): 55 of 55 pass, including the stdio Doctor tests.
Not tested: real `openclaw update`, a running Gateway, real third-party servers, OAuth, legacy SSE, TLS, human-readable Doctor output, Windows, macOS.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(test): worktree recovery fixture loses its checkout to startup cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway worktree recovery test (`worktrees.test.ts`, "fences recovery relocation through real paired requester and workspace authority") fails with `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` when startup worktree cleanup runs before the fixture has published the sessions that own its checkouts.

Observed on scheduled main [run 43310185262](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43310185262) (head `21479e2b10`), job `checks-node-compact-large-15` (131504632303).

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This is a test-fixture-only fix that restores the `checks-node-compact-large-15` main CI shard; no production code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197898 (`e3502d33aa08`) made startup managed-worktree cleanup run immediately. The recovery fixture created its `recovery` and `replacement` checkouts before writing the session entries that own them, so cleanup correctly treated those checkouts as orphaned and removed one. The later `prepareLocalSandboxWorkspace` call then saw the owner change and rejected.

The fixture now publishes both live session entries first, then creates the worktrees and binds the recovery entry to its checkout. The cleanup behavior is intended and unchanged. Every existing requester revocation, session replacement, worktree rebinding, file-integrity and authorized-recovery assertion is kept.

## Evidence

Proof ran on an AWS Crabbox (c7a.2xlarge, Node 24.22.1, [run_cc81f18c5e9ea631870710a46d79d312](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cc81f18c5e9ea631870710a46d79d312)) against base `4efd662cc2c`, using a patch byte-identical to this PR's diff (same base, same file blob):

- **Controlled reproduction:** a temporary, uncommitted proof gate held only the first real startup `managedWorktrees.gc` until the first checkout existed, then released it and let the real cleanup finish. No fake owner, sleep, timeout change or product seam was added.
  - Base: exit 1. Cleanup removed the fixture checkout and reproduced the exact `Local sandbox managed workspace owner changed` failure.
  - Fix: exit 0. The checkout was kept and the same recovery-authority case completed.
- **Uninstrumented** `src/gateway/server-methods/worktrees.test.ts`: 9/9 pass.
- Scoped tsgo, oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Independent autoreview (P0–P2) over the diff: no actionable findings.

Limits: proof is on base `4efd662cc2c`. Main has moved since then, and no runtime qualification on later heads is claimed; PR CI on this head is the broad proof. A later scheduled main run will confirm the shard is fixed.

prs.title: feat(plugins): tell agent hooks when the turn read network content
prs.body:
Closes #197881

Related: #107069, #196857

## What Problem This Solves

A plugin that stores turn content (memory, logging) cannot tell whether the turn read network-sourced tool results, so it stores text from a fetched web page with the same trust as text the user typed. Core already tracks this per turn and records its own memory writes as `untrusted` when it is set.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can read `ctx.turnTainted` on agent hooks and lower trust or skip storing content from turns that read network-sourced tool results. The field is optional and read-only. Nothing changes for plugins that do not read it, and there is no new enforcement. Until #197940 is fixed, `agent_end` handlers do not run after turns that call Tool Search `dispatch_action`; `before_agent_finalize` and `llm_output` carry the field on those turns.

## Why This Change Was Made

The field reuses the one per-turn flag core already keeps (`createAgentTurnTaintState`), the same getter that makes memory writes record `untrusted` (see "Freeform edits and quarantine" in `docs/concepts/memory-provenance.md`). There is no second tracker. This implements the minimal informational contract recommended in the issue triage; the coverage and semantics below are the proposal for the SDK and security owners.

- `PluginHookAgentContext.turnTainted?: boolean` (readonly). The embedded runtime reads the flag each time it builds a hook context, so the value matches the turn at that point. It is set on `before_prompt_build`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_finalize`, `agent_end`, and the run loop's own `before_compaction` / `after_compaction`.
- The shared harness context builder (`buildAgentHookContext`) now forwards the field. It copies fields one by one, so without this `agent_end` and `before_agent_finalize` would not receive it. External harnesses that use the same SDK helpers can pass it too.
- It is absent, not `false`, when the runtime does not report it: CLI backends, other harnesses that do not pass it, and the session-level compaction hook that only carries `sessionKey`. So the issue's `before_compaction` ask is met for compaction the run loop owns, not for that session-level hook.
- Memory-flush maintenance runs (`trigger: "memory"`) start with the flag `true` when the source turn was tainted or the sender was not the owner, so on those runs `true` does not require a network tool result in that run. The flag stays set across retries of the same turn.
- `false` is not a trust attestation. It only means core saw no network-sourced tool result in this turn. The user's own message, channel input, and tool results not marked as network content leave it `false`. The docs and the type comment say to treat the flag as informational provenance.

Shape differs from the issue sketch (`turnTaint: { untrustedContent, sources }`). Core records only "a non-presentation tool result had `resultContentSource: "network"`", not which source, so a `sources` list would need new tracking. The boolean keeps the name core already uses (`turnTainted` in transcript metadata). A structured object can still be added later if core starts recording sources.

Not changed:
- When the flag is raised. #196857 (Code Mode catalog search raising it with no network call) still applies, and plugins now see the same value core uses, which makes that case visible.
- Input provenance. `ctx.inputProvenance` is unchanged; #107069 is separate.
- Tool hooks. The issue asks for them too, but they take a different context type (`PluginHookToolContext`), and a per-call value needs its own timing rule (before or after this call's result is counted). That is left for a follow-up, so this PR covers the agent hooks only.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on each side: built from the tree, isolated state, loopback, a local OpenAI-compatible model, and a small fixture plugin that logs whether `turnTainted` is present on each hook. Two turns through the Gateway's `/v1/chat/completions`: one asks for `web_fetch` of `https://example.com/`, one asks for `read` of a workspace file. The `after_tool_call` rows show which tools ran (tool hooks are not changed, so they never carry the field).

origin/main (7602443):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null
```

This branch (8f0bbfa; the current head 6417045 adds only docs and a type comment):

```
turn=network  hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=web_fetch
turn=network  hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=dispatch_action
turn=network  hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=network  hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=true
turn=local    hook=before_prompt_build  has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=after_tool_call      has_turnTainted=false turnTainted=null toolName=read
turn=local    hook=before_agent_finalize has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
turn=local    hook=agent_end            has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false toolResults=read
turn=local    hook=llm_output           has_turnTainted=true  turnTainted=false
```

Known limitation, tracked in #197940: in our runs (2/2), after an embedded turn that called Tool Search `dispatch_action`, plugin `agent_end` handlers failed with `Plugin invocation scope is closed` before running. That is why the `web_fetch` turn above has no `agent_end` row: the model also called `dispatch_action`. With Tool Search off, `web_fetch`, `read` and `session_status` alone each ran `agent_end` normally.

This blocks the issue's main use case, retaining at `agent_end` after a network turn, whenever the turn used `dispatch_action`, until that bug is fixed. Tool Search is on by default, so that is common. The new field itself is correct on `before_agent_finalize` and `llm_output`, which run after the tools and are not affected, and a plugin can use those meanwhile. The `hook-context` test below covers `agent_end` getting the field from the shared builder, and the `read` turn above shows it live on `agent_end`.

Tests (red on origin/main, green here):
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/agent-hook-context.test.ts`: the hook context reports the real `createAgentTurnTaintState` flag (false, false after a local result, true after a network result), and omits the field when the runtime gives no getter.
- `src/agents/harness/hook-context.test.ts`: the harness builder forwards `turnTainted` (the path `agent_end` and `before_agent_finalize` take).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts`: run-loop compaction hooks read the flag when they fire (false before, true after).

Gates on 6417045:
- `pnpm test` on the three files above plus `turn-taint-state`, `lifecycle-hook-helpers` and `agent-end-side-effects` tests: 6 files, 35 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 7602443`: passed (core and core-test typecheck, lint and format of changed files, import cycles, dead exports, ratchets).
- `pnpm build`: passed.
- `pnpm check:docs`: passed.
- `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff --base 7602443 --head 6417045`: exit 0. The only declaration change is the added `readonly turnTainted?: boolean;` on `PluginHookAgentContext` (2 reachable declarations, 183 exports that reach the type). Additive, no removals.

Risks: low. It is an additive optional field on a hook context. A plugin that treats a missing field as "not tainted" would be wrong on CLI backends; the docs say the field is absent there. A plugin that treats `false` as "trusted" would also be wrong; the docs say `false` only means no network-sourced tool result was seen.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let manifest configSignals test a config value
prs.body:
Closes #197882

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors cannot hide a tool while its config flag is `false`, because manifest `configSignals` can only test whether a value is present. The tool is still offered to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can list a tool only while a feature is actually on, for example `"equals": { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true }`, so the model no longer sees tools the plugin will refuse to run. Existing manifests behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `configSignals` entry now accepts an optional `equals` map from a dot path to a literal string, number, or boolean. It follows the issue triage: literal equality only, with inequality left out until a plugin needs it. The issue is marked as needing a product decision; this PR implements the recommended contract so that decision can be made on concrete code.

The contract, stated in the docs and covered by tests:

- **Missing value:** a missing or `null` path fails. Comparison is strict, so `"true"` does not equal `true`.
- **Overlays:** paths are read from the same effective config as `required`, after `overlayPath`. With `overlayMapPath`, each map entry is checked on its own, so `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry.
- **SecretRefs:** never resolved. A path holding a SecretRef does not equal any literal, even when the secret has that value.
- All fields of one signal must pass together. `required`, `requiredAny`, and `mode` are unchanged, so `false` still counts as present for `required`.

Generation provider metadata shares the same evaluator, so it gets the same field. Docs cover the field, its rules and a flag-gating example.

## Evidence

Real Gateway run (`openclaw gateway run`, isolated state, `tools.profile: "full"`) with a small fixture plugin that registers two tools unconditionally:

- `kb_search`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", equals: { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true } }]`
- `kb_status`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", required: ["knowledgeBase.enabled"] }]` (presence only, unchanged control)

`tools.effective` for a fresh session:

| Build | `knowledgeBase.enabled` | `kb_search` | `kb_status` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (`8608f8810a8e`) | `false` | listed | listed |
| this branch | `false` | not listed | listed |
| this branch | `true` | listed | listed |

On main, `equals` is an unknown field, so the signal is dropped and the tool fails open. The presence-only `kb_status` shows the original gap, because `false` counts as configured. On this branch, `kb_search` follows the flag and `kb_status` is unchanged. No model turn was run: `tools.effective` reads the same manifest availability filter the run uses to build its tool list.

Regression tests (red on main, green here):

- `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts`: on main 8 failed, 23 passed (31). Covers `true`, `false`, the string `"true"`, `null` and a missing path; `overlayPath`; `overlayMapPath` where `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry; a SecretRef that is never resolved; and a tool-level check that the presence-only signal still lists the tool when the flag is `false`.
- `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts`: on main 1 failed, 65 passed (66). The normalizer keeps `false` and `0`, trims paths, and drops non-scalar values, empty paths and a signal whose only `equals` entry is invalid.

Checks run on this branch applied to main `8608f8810a8e`:

- `pnpm test` on the two files above plus consumers (`tools.optional`, `tools.inspection`, `manifest-command-aliases`, `tool-policy`, `tool-policy-pipeline`, `tools-effective-inventory` (3 files)): 10 files, 261 tests passed.
- `src/cli/plugins-authoring-command.test.ts` does not depend on this change and is not in the count above. It passed 31 of 31 on both main and this branch here, but its symlink project root test can fail in some environments, and when it does it fails the same way on main.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm build`: pass.
- `pnpm lint:core`: fails with the same output on main and on this branch (existing UI findings); no findings in touched files.

Risks: low. The field is optional and additive, and no existing branch of the evaluator changed. Older hosts drop the unknown field and keep listing the tool, which is today's behavior.

prs.title: fix(ui): stop the flat assistant group from clamping table width
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`main` is red: `ui/src/e2e/chat-markdown-table-interactions.e2e.test.ts` fails three cases (12 pass), which is what #197944
reports. Two shapes of the failure are the same symptom — the table is exactly as wide as the prose above it, so the
"table is wider than the surrounding text" assertions cannot hold:

- `tableBounds.width > textBounds.width` receives `668 > 668`;
- `denseWidth > prose` receives `768 > 768`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197823 added `container-type: inline-size` to the flat assistant message group:

```css
.chat:not(.chat--bubbles) .chat-group.assistant:not(.chat-group--forwarded) > .chat-group-messages {
  container-type: inline-size;
}
```

Inline-size containment makes that element a query container **and** applies layout containment, so its children stop
contributing their intrinsic inline size: the group becomes exactly as wide as its parent, and a table that used to grow
past the prose column is clamped to the same width.

Nothing in the tree consumes that container — no `@container` query and no `cqw`/`cqi` unit references the
`.chat-group-messages` container (`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message-reactions.css` uses plain pixel anchors), so
the declaration only cost the containment side effect. This removes it and leaves the reaction layout of #197823 intact.

## User Impact

Markdown tables in flat assistant messages size to their content again instead of being pinned to the prose width, and the
desktop table layout assertions pass. Bubble messages (`chat--bubbles`) and forwarded groups were never affected and are
unchanged.

## Evidence

Both runs use the same command on this branch's base and head:

- base (`main` @ `d90d52cce94`): `chat-markdown-table-interactions.e2e.test.ts` → **3 failed | 12 passed**
  (`expected 768 to be greater than 768`, `expected 668 to be greater than 668`).
- with this change: same file → **15 passed**.
- regression check for the change that introduced the declaration: `chat-flow.reactions.e2e.test.ts` → **4 passed**.

`oxlint` reports no findings for the touched file.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report; the author reviewed the change and re-ran both suites.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): member roles come from gateway.roles.definitions
prs.body:
Stacked on #197712, which is stacked on #197697. Review only the top two commits.

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway hardcodes what the OpenClaw ID member roles `operator` and `viewer` allow, so an owner cannot change them or add a role of their own.

## User Impact

User impact: an owner can edit what Operator and Viewer members may do, and can define more member roles, by editing `gateway.roles.definitions`. OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and is off by default; with it off, nothing here runs.

Changes an owner will notice:

- Turning on OpenClaw ID, or starting a Gateway with it on, writes missing `operator` and `viewer` definitions into the config file. It writes no `default`, so the claw's other sign-ins behave as before. **This rewrites the config file as JSON and removes JSON5 comments**, as every config write does.
- Viewer members are limited to conversations (`operator.sessions.read`). They no longer read logs or the user directory.
- A member whose role has no definition cannot connect. Deleting a definition cuts off its members until an owner gives them another role.
- A member role has no ceiling in code. A definition that includes `operator.admin` or `operator.pairing` gives its members those scopes. No preset includes them.
- `users.setRole` with a role name is refused for an OpenClaw ID member's profile. A member's role comes from membership.

Known limit: a Viewer cannot open the Access page, because loading plugin pages needs `operator.read`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A member's role name is looked up in the current `gateway.roles.definitions` on every admission and authority check: WebSocket connect, Gateway HTTP, the tunnel API, retained and recovered runs, sandbox streams and session continuations. Editing or deleting a definition closes the affected members' connections and stops their retained work.
- The membership role takes precedence over any named role, default role or GitHub mapping on the member's profile.
- Presets are ordinary definitions. They are written only when missing, never overwrite an edited preset, and are not written again after an owner deletes one until OpenClaw ID is next turned on or the Gateway restarts.
- At startup the presets are installed before the runtime config is published, so existing members keep access after upgrade in every reload mode. If a running Gateway cannot apply the saved definitions (`gateway.reload.mode: "off"`), the OpenClaw ID status says a restart is needed.

## Evidence

- New tests cover: edited presets and custom roles; unknown role refused on all surfaces; Viewer can read conversations and cannot read logs, list users or send; a custom admin role gets admin scopes; live eviction when a definition is edited or deleted; retained runs and sandbox streams losing an edited role's authority; preset writing on activation and at startup, with existing definitions, default and assignments preserved; nothing written with OpenClaw ID off; `users.setRole` refused for members.
- One unmocked Gateway test proves that turning on OpenClaw ID does not refuse a device-token-only reconnect.
- Focused runs: 281 backend tests in 21 files and 85 UI tests in 4 files for the first commit; 61 tests in 6 files for the second. Targeted typechecks, lint, format and ratchets pass.
- Independent review of the first commit found no P0, one P1 and two P2. The second commit fixes the P1 (with config reload off, presets written at startup could reach disk without reaching the running Gateway, leaving existing members refused until another restart) and one P2 (a profile merge during `users.setRole` could skip the member check). The other P2 is the comment removal stated above. A second review of the fix commit found nothing.

Test lines: this PR adds 1,305 net test lines, 905 over the 400-line allowance. The allocation record is `config/test-lines-allocations/member-role-definitions.txt`. The tests cover separate transport, retained-authority and config-lifecycle boundaries, each of which can fail on its own.

Not run: the full repository suite, a live relay or deployed Gateway, and browser end-to-end tests.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): guest member role with sandboxed session tools
prs.body:
Stacked on #197739. Review only the top two commits.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw ID members are either Operators, whose sessions run tools on the Gateway host, or Viewers, who cannot start work. An owner has no role for someone who should be able to work with the session's tools kept in a sandbox.

## User Impact

User impact: turning on OpenClaw ID also writes a `guest` role definition. A guest member reads shared sessions and starts their own work, and the exec and file tools of their sessions run in a per-person sandbox. Operator stays the default invite role. OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and is off by default.

Important limit: a required sandbox contains a session's exec and file tools only. It does not contain Code Mode under the default `node` executor, CLI backends, or direct `node.invoke` calls by a role that also has `operator.write` or `operator.admin`. These limits apply to every sandbox-required role, named roles included, and are listed in `docs/gateway/operator-scopes.md`. With default settings a guest can reach the first two. Whether to close them for sandbox-required sessions, or to give the guest preset stricter defaults, is an open maintainer decision; this PR changes none of those paths.

A guest needs a Docker or Podman sandbox backend. Without one their runs fail; they never fall back to the host. The invite form warns when a sandbox-required role is selected and no backend is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The `guest` preset is `sessions.others: "view"`, `agents: "*"`, `scopes: ["operator.sessions.write"]`, `sandbox: "required"`. It is written with the other presets, only when missing.
- A member's sandbox requirement comes from the membership role, so it holds when named-role enforcement is off (definitions without `gateway.roles.default`), which is the normal state of a personal claw.
- Sessions a guest creates are stamped sandbox-required at creation. Forks, rewinds, spawned children, cron jobs and recovered runs keep the stamp. A guest cannot start a run in an existing host-execution session.
- The connection decides the role: a person who is a guest member and also has a non-sandboxed named role gets a sandboxed session over the member connection and an unsandboxed one over the other sign-in.
- The People data marks which roles require a sandbox and whether a backend is available. The backend probe runs only for that owner-only view.

## Evidence

- Focused runs: 127 Gateway tests, 36 cron tests, 24 UI tests and 23 People projection tests pass, with targeted typechecks, lint, format, docs checks and ratchets.
- New tests cover the preset being written; a guest's session stamped sandbox-required with enforcement on and off; forks, rewinds, children, cron and recovery keeping the requirement; refusal to run in a host-execution session; fail-closed with no backend; an operator member's sessions staying unsandboxed; and the two-sign-in case.
- These tests prove stamping, propagation and admission. They do not run a tool inside a real container.
- An independent review found the membership propagation consistent on every surface it listed, and reported the three uncontained paths above. The second commit corrects docs, UI copy and test names so nothing claims a guest has no host access.

Not run: a live Docker or Podman model run, a real restart and recovery cycle, the full repository suite.

prs.title: fix(backup): keep whitespace-suffixed git backup repository roots adoptable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw backup git init --repository <path>` verifies an adopted backup repository by comparing `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` against the requested path. The shared `requireGitCommand` helper trims the output, so a backup repository whose directory legitimately ends in whitespace (for example `/mnt/backups/openclaw `) had its meaningful trailing space stripped; the subsequent `fs.realpath` then failed with ENOENT (or compared against a different directory) and initialization refused a valid operator-owned repository. The same root-cause shape was approved for the update path in #196654 and already shipped in `src/projects/project-checkout.ts`.

Precedent: #196654 (same root cause at the update-check call site; this PR covers the git-backup adoption check)

## Why This Change Was Made

`assertGitRepository` in `src/snapshot/git-backup.ts` now reads the top level through the existing `executeGitCommand` + `requireGitCommandOutput` owners and removes only Git's final LF record terminator (`replace(/\n$/, "")`), preserving filesystem characters in the repository path. The shared `requireGitCommand` helper is intentionally untouched (many callers rely on its trimmed output for non-path values); only this path-typed call site changes. The probe a few lines below already used the untrimmed `runGit` result, so the two checks are now consistent.

Production LOC is `+5/-1` in one file.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Adopting a Git backup repository under a whitespace-suffixed directory now verifies and initializes correctly, including the follow-up `remote add` and first commit. Ordinary repository paths are byte-for-byte unaffected. Creation of a not-yet-existing whitespace-suffixed directory remains owned by `@openclaw/fs-safe` and is out of scope for this in-repo fix (the regression test pre-creates the private root, which is also the supported adoption flow for existing directories).

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `51820d5e6db4`
- Current-main RED baseline: `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`
- Production entry: `initializeGitBackupRepository` → `assertGitRepository` in `src/snapshot/git-backup.ts` (CLI surface: `backup git init --repository <path>`)
- Canonical owner exercised: `assertGitRepository` at `src/snapshot/git-backup.ts:162-171`
- Decision surface: whether the adopted repository verifies as the Git worktree root (gates init/remote/commit)
- Recorder/readback boundary: real filesystem + real `git` subprocess end-to-end in the existing `src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts` harness (the test initializes, configures identity, commits a file, and reads it back)
- Acceptance RED: on current main, a pre-created private root named `repository ` fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '<tmp>/repository'` (the trimmed path) thrown from `assertGitRepository`
- Acceptance GREEN: on exact head, the same flow initializes, commits `note.txt`, and reads back its contents — 10/10 tests pass
- Legal control: the nine pre-existing ownership/restore/prune tests (missing/corrupt payloads, symlink escape, legacy refs, staging hygiene) all pass unchanged
- Cleanup: isolated vitest temp dirs only; no production Gateway, session, token, config, or real backup repository was touched

### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace

Vitest shard on the real runner (Node 24.22.1, docker `lexiflow-all`):

```text
# BASE (76024435027d) + new test, via node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
FAIL src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts > initializes and commits in a repository path that ends in whitespace
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '/tmp/.../git-backup-trailing-space-*/repository'
 ❯ assertGitRepository src/snapshot/git-backup.ts:164
Tests  1 failed | 9 passed (10)
```

```text
# HEAD (51820d5e6db4), same command
Tests  10 passed (10)   Duration ~146s
```

```text
# Legal control on HEAD: pre-existing ownership, restore, prune, and symlink-escape cases
Tests  10 passed (10)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 10/10 passed on exact head; RED reproduced on current main with only the new test
- Not tested: `openclaw backup git init` end-to-end via the packaged CLI against a live Gateway was not run on the proof host (kernel 3.10 blocks the Gateway runtime); the verified boundary is the real `initializeGitBackupRepository` path with real `git` and real filesystem, matching the proof style of the sibling snapshot/backup tests.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+5/-1` (src/snapshot/git-backup.ts)
- Test LOC: `+13` (src/snapshot/git-backup-ownership.test.ts)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses the existing `executeGitCommand`/`requireGitCommandOutput` owners and the approved `replace(/\n$/, "")` predicate from #196654; the shared `requireGitCommand` signature is unchanged
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none (adoption-time read-only verification)

<details>
<summary>Maintainer edits</summary>

- Maintainer edits allowed: yes — address review comments directly on this branch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready: five-line owner-local change aligned with the already-reviewed #196654; proof is red/green on the real test runner with real git.
- Alternative: change the shared `requireGitCommand` helper for every caller; rejected because non-path callers rely on the trimmed output (matches the #196654 review direction of per-call-site, path-typed fixes).
- Scope declaration: behavior-completing only; no change to backup contents, encryption, or restore behavior.

</details>

prs.title: improve(gateway): reduce Control UI PR subscription allocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI PR subscriptions still recheck every audience after timestamp-only session writes, and repeat reader assertions during delivery, despite the passive-poll reduction in #197840.

## User Impact

Reduce Gateway allocation and CPU for PR subscriptions while preserving cross-user isolation, revoked-access denial, and credential ownership on delivery. No configuration, schema, or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Consume the session writer's existing unchanged-sharing fact instead of recapturing every unrelated root. Keep root-source reconciliation and one synchronous warm-recipient assertion through broadcast; asynchronous preparation still requires its final assertion. Remove redundant pre-load/post-load audience passes and empty nested target guards. Preserve the compact identity snapshot introduced by #181890 to avoid retaining replaced row graphs.

Production diff: +22/-27, net **−5 lines**. One real-writer regression adds 20 test lines. The existing measurement harness gains identical-source controls, real metadata writes, and separate allocation/CPU passes on one large fixture.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on exact parent `4efd662cc2c6f9f2afa8330ac813e48c9bd9b0a2`: an unrelated timestamp write recaptures the watched root. It passes with the patch and retains root reconciliation and subsequent PR delivery.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): approve an app's node together with its owner device
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mac app is moving to sign-in-first OpenClaw ID enrollment: the owner signs in and approves the Mac as an owner device. Its node (running tools on the Mac) should come from that same approval, not a separate node invite and six-digit ceremony.

## User Impact

- When an owner approves a new device that also asks to run tools, the Control UI approval dialog names the claw and says "<device> will also be able to run tools for <claw>: <surface>. Its own permissions still apply." One compared number and one click approve both the device and its node.
- Approval copy now says "device" instead of "browser".
- Owners get a toast when the recovery kit was used to add a device ("Your recovery kit was used to add <device>"), with a link to Your devices.
- Your devices tags such a device "Runs tools". The remove confirm says its node goes too.
- Access lists the node as "<device> · Your device", with a visible **Stop using for tools** action. That removes only the node; the device stays.

## Why This Change Was Made

Protocol (unshipped v1-draft):
- `MembershipChange` `add_owner_device` gains an optional `node { peer_key, label, description }`. The node is listed in `node_peer_keys` (tunnel and relay admission unchanged) as `NodeRecord { owner_device: fp(D) }` with no `invite_id`. Auto-pairing is bounded by the approved `description`, as for invited nodes.
- The node key can never be a human key (R, any D, any owner or member peer key, including the new device's) or another node's key. A device has at most one node.
- `remove_node` removes only the node. A re-add with `node` turns it back on.
- Revoking the device (directly or through the device that approved it) or dropping it for inactivity removes its node.
- SAS `start` gains an optional `node { peer_key, description }`, covered by the commitment and transcript, so the compared code binds the node key and the surface shown. Starts and changes without `node` are byte-identical to before.
- The node is in the change rather than the owner cert because the approved surface could push the cert past Discovery's 16 KiB owner-certificate header limit.
- `isNodeDescription` is exported for approvers.

Gateway: the owner link view exposes `ownerDevice` on nodes and `nodePeerKey` on owner devices.

Supersedes the operator-key approach of #197413 (closed). Discovery re-vendor: openclaw/discovery#13. Design: sign-in-first Mac enrollment (Josh, 2026-11-11).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: 224/224.
  - New `owner-device-node.test.ts`: binding, human-key refusal, remove_node keeps the device, self re-add, revocation and approver cascade, inactivity cascade, kit path with `kit_used`, and a stolen node key.
  - SAS commitment binding test.
  - New fixture vector "owner approves a device with its node".
- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/owner-approval.test.ts`: 15/15. New: node approved in the change; browser unchanged; malformed node ignored; kit-used notice names the device.
- openclaw-id UI, lib, access-extension and Gateway authority/people suites: all pass.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:extensions` clean. `pnpm check:changed`: pass (exit 0).
- Not yet: the Mac side (stacked separately), live staging proof, and Control UI screenshots (mockup renders exist; real before/after screenshots will be added before ready).

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): retain callback owners in heap summaries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Heap profiles that exceed the inline size limit hide callback owners behind `[...]` because summary stacks retain only eight frames.

## User Impact

Heap summaries retain up to 32 frames, making intermediate listeners and plugin callers visible while preserving outer application owners. The complete response remains capped at 1 MiB; wider stacks may leave room for fewer ranked entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

Increase the existing bounded stack depth and document it. Frame redaction, allocation accounting, and summary ordering are unchanged. The stall formatter uses separate stack and 2 KiB report limits and does not share this constant. Production LOC delta is zero.

## Evidence

- Heap and stall focused suites: 44 passed, four runtime-gated skips.
- Both extended deep-stack regression cases fail on the parent because listener frames are missing. They pass with the fix and verify outer caller retention, recursive compression, the 32-frame bound, and the 1 MiB result cap.
- Codex autoreview of the full local change against `4efd662cc2c6f` completed clean at P0–P2.
- `pnpm check:changed`: every check passed except the production unused-export scan for `resolveTrustedProxyGitCoauthor` in `src/gateway/trusted-proxy-git-coauthor.ts`. The same single failure reproduces on exact parent `4efd662cc2c6f9f2afa8330ac813e48c9bd9b0a2` with all workspace configs resolving. `git log` identifies introducing commit `f4f290c52f961` (#196867). This is a newly identified main regression, unrelated to the summary change.

CI run 43329164621 (attempt 1) also exposes a newer, unrelated main regression: both wrapper inventory/extracted-dependency cases in `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` fail identically on the exact CI main parent `d30e45c3f48eaa570df1f4528bcc50e7b28e6c77`. Commit `fc6c25e91564ca1f757d04c5b4676dcab6f66aaa` (#197697) introduced the runtime protocol import without its six transitive inventory entries. Reproduced with the pinned Bun runner; no diagnostic files participate in that failure. This is a main regression requiring its own owner repair.

Changelog

Sourced from addressable's changelog.

Addressable 2.9.1

  • fixes denial of service in Addressable::URI.normalize_path, which took quadratic time on paths with many dot segments; URI#normalize, #join, #== and #=== were affected (GHSA-qq38-m9mg-xjj5)
  • fixes Addressable::URI.normalize_path keeping segments that a .. should have removed after a .. above the root, e.g. /../../public/x/../../secret normalized to /public/x/secret instead of /secret (GHSA-8gmh-2hhj-2hv9)
  • fixes Addressable::URI.normalize_path treating a raw line feed as a segment boundary, e.g. joining ..\n/secret onto /public/ gave /\n/secret
  • deprecates Addressable::URI::RULE_2A, RULE_2B_2C, RULE_2D and RULE_PREFIXED_PARENT, which are no longer used; they will be removed in 2.10.0
  • fixes denial of service in Addressable::Template#match and #extract, which still backtracked exponentially in 2.9.0 for exploded /, ., ;, ? and & expressions (e.g. {/path*}) on regex engines without match memoization, such as JRuby, TruffleRuby and MRI before 3.2; match results are unchanged (GHSA-j82w-28jv-3pmj)
  • fixes denial of service in Addressable::Template#match and #extract, which backtracked polynomially or exponentially on the same regex engines for expressions with several variables (e.g. {/owner,repo,ref}, or {+a,b,c} with many variables), for ; expressions, and for adjacent expressions (e.g. {+a}{+b}{+c} or {+a}{b}); match results are unchanged (GHSA-9f42-57jx-vpp3)
  • fixes denial of service in Addressable::Template#match and #extract, which backtracked polynomially for expressions with several exploded variables (e.g. {+a*,b*}), including on MRI 3.2; match results are unchanged (GHSA-4w5q-wg7v-w6gp)
  • fixes Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode in the pure-Ruby backend decoding Punycode labels that aren't valid A-labels: labels that decode to only ASCII characters (e.g. xn--google- decoded to google) and labels that don't convert back to themselves; such a label is now returned unchanged, as with libidn, so Addressable::URI#display_uri no longer shows a host that differs from #normalized_host (GHSA-9crm-g4mf-wc5j)
  • fixes Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode decoding Punycode labels with characters that change how a host displays without being visible themselves, such as bidi overrides and isolates (e.g. U+202E and U+2066), zero width characters and control characters; such a label is now returned unchanged, so Addressable::URI#display_uri no longer shows them. The pure-Ruby backend also no longer decodes labels with other characters that nameprep prohibits, as with libidn (GHSA-539f-xcgw-2gjg)
  • fixes Addressable::URI#route_from and #route_to raising InvalidURIError when the route's first segment contains a colon (e.g. /a:b from /a); the route is now ./a:b (#625)
  • fixes Addressable::IDNA.to_unicode raising in the pure-Ruby backend for Punycode labels that are too long, overflow the decoder, or decode past U+10FFFF; the label is now returned unchanged, as with libidn, so Addressable::URI#display_uri no longer raises for such hosts (#620)
  • fixes Addressable::URI#display_uri raising InvalidURIError for URIs

prs.title: docs: propose update generations and staged candidate handoff
prs.body:
Related: #145252

## What Problem This Solves

Update reliability work has no written plan for its two structural causes: package updates replace files in place, and the installed updater drives the whole run, so a fix in a new release cannot help the release that is failing.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This is a design proposal for maintainers to accept, change, or reject. It adds one page under `docs/reference/` and changes no behavior.

The page asks for decisions, including two that this repository reserves for explicit approval: a typed descriptor in the activation journal, and a retention rule for release directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

#197922 implements the first slice of this plan, and reviewers of that PR have no place to see where it leads. The page records:

- The recommendation: package generations on OpenClaw-owned prefixes, built into the existing package update path, plus a staged transfer of update work to the candidate.
- Two approaches that were considered and rejected, with the source facts behind each: a launcher in the npm package, and extending the immutable installation owner to user installations.
- Step timings from two published-driver cell runs.
- Four rules that came out of reviewing #197922 and that later handoffs should keep.
- What was not traced or measured.

It follows the form of the existing `team-immutable-update-design.md`. Like that page, it is not listed in `docs/docs.json`.

## Evidence

Docs-only change. Run against this page:

- `pnpm docs:check-mdx`: passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-links`: `broken_links=0`.
- `scripts/format-docs.mts --check` with the page tracked: clean.
- `markdownlint-cli2` with the repository config: 0 issues.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

`pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` fails on two existing pages that this change does not touch (`/tools/acp-agents-setup` and `releases/2026.10.1.md`). The three anchors this page links to exist.

The design itself is from reading source. The page's "Evidence limits" section lists what was not traced, including how the update path rebinds a service to a different package root end to end.

prs.title: fix: provider plugins cannot route summaries by session
prs.body:
Closes #197932

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: provider plugins cannot reliably assign session affinity or cache keys when compaction and branch summaries run alongside other sessions.

## User Impact

Provider plugins can use the owning session's identity in stream wrappers and summary requests. Calls without a session remain supported; no configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the existing session ID/key through foreground, side-question, and compaction wrapper setup, and the session ID through compaction and branch-summary completion options. Optional parameters preserve the public summary APIs; the host does not create new identities.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: **298 passed across 11 files**, using `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` (381.55 seconds locally). Covers concurrent core/safeguard compaction, summary and branch requests through both completion paths, split-turn summaries, wrapper ID/key context, identity-less callers, and existing provider, compaction, side-question, and prompt-prefix contracts. The three new core regressions failed with undefined IDs on the base before the fix. Final fixture cleanup rerun: all five core/host regressions passed.
- Typecheck: `pnpm tsgo:core` and canonical changed-test graphs (`agents-other`, `packages`, `agents-sessions`) passed. Targeted oxlint passed with zero warnings/errors; formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed in 11m 42.4s, including package/runtime bundles, declarations, 105 plugin distributions, SDK exports, and the Control UI. The UI build reported six informational size-budget overruns; UI source is unchanged and no base comparison was run.
- Container validation used Node 24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0 with a frozen lockfile. All locked npm versions passed a three-day publication-age audit; upstream's stricter install policy also passed. Used the documented Node/oxfmt/oxlint alternatives; the pinned Bun download was outside the registry-only network allowance.
- Local review gap: autoreview and local ClawSweeper are not installed in the available tool/skill locations. Author simplification/diff review completed for `614924dc4ad6daf6f59bc2c2a84c44e7e6986258..96cd062ca3569c528a78225645b1edcbf60efde3`; the change keeps existing owners and adds optional identity pass-throughs.
- Boundary inventory: current `check-plugin-extension-import-boundary.mts` passed. The wider `check-src-extension-import-boundary.mts` command documented in CONTRIBUTING.md is absent on this base; that inventory could not run.
- No live model/Gateway validation. CI results and CI seconds are pending.

<details>
<summary>Changed test-file timing</summary>

Vitest wall time from the focused local runs; compilation/import time is included.

| File | Wall time |

| `session-identity.test.ts` | 3.32 s |
| `agent-session-summary-identity.test.ts` | 234.67 s |
| `extra-params.lifecycle.test.ts` | 33.31 s |

The host identity file's cold run spent 209.16 seconds preparing the repository's shared subprocess entry set; its two tests took 678 ms. The existing wrapper and compaction consumer suites include their existing runtime/bootstrap fixtures. Added test code stays below the 400-line budget.

prs.title: fix(update): skip unreadable foreign directories during update capture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Original-state capture and full backups abort when a workspace contains an unreadable foreign entry, such as the root-owned `.fseventsd` directory on a mounted APFS volume. Reported by @BorClaw.

Fixes #191855.

## User Impact

Capture and backup can finish around unreadable foreign entries, with one warning per omitted path and explicit manifest omissions. Unreadable owned files, explicitly selected resources, canonical databases, and present private-capture markers still refuse. The running updater needs this repair for original-state capture; installing a corrected candidate cannot change the older updater's capture code.

## Why This Change Was Made

At base `8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004`, [`update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts:312`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-recovery-baseline-capture.ts#L312) calls the privacy classifier before enumerating a directory. [`update-capture-paths.ts:18–23`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004/src/infra/update-capture-paths.ts#L18) probes the marker inside that directory and refuses on EACCES. The original-capture caller catches this as a continuation warning; it is not itself the stopping validation exception.

The other walks are agent scratch discovery, backup SQLite inventory, and payload tar traversal. The installed v2026.10.10 updater's broad [`backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts:183`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/v2026.10.10/src/infra/backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts#L183) reaches the same privacy check through `isTraversable`; its directory failures also propagate at line 192. Supplemental candidate-state discovery calls that owner during validation, inside the broad package-update catch. This is a source-supported validating-phase failure path, not identification of the report's discarded exception. Main already narrows supplemental discovery to declared plugin resources (`4a393be419f3`), so an unrelated workspace subtree need not be visited there. Capture and full-backup omission handling were still missing on main. Classification and exception-retention work belongs to #194160.

One shared permission/UID policy now serves the walkers. The backup inventory retains skipped paths across discovery and archiving, and checks deferred scratch-scan failures after all explicit includes are known. SQLite readability probes use descriptor-free access checks to preserve existing POSIX database locks. Capture records omissions in its existing `excludedRoots`; backup records `unreadable-foreign` entries in its existing `skipped` manifest. Mount traversal policy is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix owner-boundary reproduction: both `captureUpdateRecoveryBaseline` and `createBackupArchive` failed with the reported marker `lstat` EACCES. The focused reproduction took 44.53 seconds including subprocess fixture preparation.
- GREEN narrow proof: `CI=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/backup-tar-walk.test.ts src/commands/backup-resource-inventory.test.ts src/infra/update-capture-paths.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **21 passed**, 4.78 seconds wall time. Covers permission-denied readdir/open, owned-file refusal, late explicit-resource protection, and privacy/symlink safeguards.
- Committed capture and archive/manifest regressions are in the existing Doctor capture and backup ownership suites. They use real chmod-000 denial and synthetic foreign UID metadata, skip root/Windows, and include foreign SQLite plus owned-file refusal. Their complete GREEN runs and typecheck/build are pending [remote CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42232892038), dispatched with `target_ref=5438a832520be89cde6799215b99a711fc039950`; preflight confirms that checkout SHA and passed. Build and test jobs are running; their results remain pending. CI seconds are pending. The first dispatch was cancelled after preflight rejected `validation_tier=main` for a cross-revision target; the linked replacement uses the supported default inputs.
- Touched-file lint passes with `config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`; formatting, `git diff --check`, and commit hooks pass. A separate **200-line** regression allocation preserves inherited test-line debt and leaves the shared scalar unchanged.
- Local autoreview: Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3, base `8dd41fc95291553e5885fec09992bd41c3038004` to local production changes, full affected production modules supplied. Explicit-resource and SQLite-probe findings were resolved; final production review is **scoped-clean**. Subsequent test fixture type guards and relocation into the existing ownership suite were mechanical.
- Simplification: the permission/UID decision has one shared owner; existing manifests carry omissions without a new format or version. Necessary production growth connects the capture, discovery, and archive boundaries; net test growth is 200 lines.

**Blockers / Crabbox receipt:** provider `blacksmith-testbox`, Linux lease `tbx_01m6rjrhygjtsk58zyh6kgayr3`. The requested main build (`pnpm build:ci-artifacts`) queued before payload execution; no build or CLI update ran. The lease was stopped, then reconciliation confirmed the exact GitHub run cancelled and `crabbox inspect` confirmed `state=completed`, `ready=false`, `hasHost=false`. Built-CLI main/branch RED/GREEN with a real root-owned 0700 workspace directory remains unproven. The initial named integration/lint entrypoints unexpectedly prepared broad worker fixtures/declarations; this wrapper expansion was not repeated after recognition. Subsequent checks used the narrow walkers and source-backed touched-file lint. This PR stays draft for the missing CLI proof and remote build/typecheck/capture-suite results.

prs.title: fix: reclaim older scratch before fresh worktrees after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: expired scratch remains untouched across repeated Gateway restarts when recently created worktrees consume the first cleanup budget.

Related: #197772, #197898.

## User Impact

Scratch cleanup reaches older managed checkouts on its first pass after restart. The existing 24-hour expiry, live/queued-run custody, filesystem identity checks, and bounded scan/removal budgets remain authoritative. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry publishes newest-created worktrees first. Scratch target preparation inherited that presentation order, so every restart could inspect the same 256 fresh candidates and stop before reaching old clones. The scratch owner now traverses that existing result oldest-first, without another query, filesystem census, cache, or array copy.

Production code grows by two lines: backward traversal plus its explanation. The additional benchmark code corrects the earlier fixture's missing fresh prefix and makes each clone contain the full workspace file count. It also allows serial reuse of its explicitly generated synthetic fixture outside measured intervals.

## Evidence

- A regression through target preparation and real filesystem cleanup fails on the parent with 0 removals. The fix removes 256 expired entries, then the remaining 2 after discarding the cursor and restarting; all 258 fresh entries survive.
- Focused custody, scratch, and maintenance coverage: 55 passing tests. The final custody rerun passes all 10 tests; its new regression takes 188 ms (50 s command wall, primarily compilation).
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2 with complete owning-module and benchmark context.
- Final `pnpm check:changed` passed. Exact-head CI passed: [run 43320491424](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43320491424). The final serial timing campaign is complete; results are below.

The benchmark's acceptance rule is 0 to 6 full-sized clone removals in the first scratch phase, 256 total expired top-level entries removed, and all 256 fresh entries preserved. It uses two 62,000-file/1.14-GB synthetic workspaces, six 62,000-file clone-shaped trees, 5,000 real synthetic session records, serial A/A controls and five interleaved before/after pairs. The source parent is `10285cd35ca7d696957430bbc6c8556f55af79fe`; only the custody owner is overlaid for baseline runs.

```
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts \
  --source <new-synthetic-source> --prepare --files 62000 --file-bytes 18432
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts \
  --source <synthetic-source> --output <new-synthetic-arm> \
  --worktrees 2 --scratch-order --scratch-clones 6
```

Later serial arms may add `--reuse-scratch-order` for that completed synthetic output. Timings cover the real maintenance owner through scratch completion at GC entry. Pacing is accelerated and immutable fixture files are hardlinked; this measures ordering, counts, CPU and allocation, not physical btrfs throughput or production chat latency. The prior pressure-gate experiment is not repeated. No production data is used or changed.

### Built Gateway restart proof

Built `e21dbced74ce6fda110607f7f87a505f0536e195` with `pnpm build`, then launched the shipped `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <leased-port> --bind loopback` in isolated synthetic state. Created older and newer managed roots through `openclaw worktrees create ... --json`. The older root contained six real Git clones plus 252 expired files; the newer root contained 258 fresh files. Each restart started a new Gateway process with no retained scratch cursor.

```text
restart 1: ready 8.917 s; 256 expired entries removed 1.922 s after ready; 2 remain
restart 2: ready 52.110 s; remaining 2 removed 2.059 s after ready; 0 remain
both: 258 fresh files preserved with identical SHA-256; no forced process cleanup
```

All three lifecycle shutdowns logged completion; the existing settled-exit watchdog then exited via SIGTERM for lingering MessagePorts. The harness originally assumed exit code zero and stopped during setup; the corrected assertion checks the lifecycle log, process exit and absence of forced cleanup. These are actual launched Gateways, not owner-module substitutes. Startup timings reflect a busy shared host and are not a startup-performance comparison. No production data or live service was touched.

### Completed ordering measurements

Five serial interleaved parent/candidate pairs on the corrected harness, with two same-harness A/A parent controls. Fixture preparation is outside the owner timing. Every parent and A/A arm removes zero entries and leaves all six full-sized clone-shaped trees. Every candidate removes all six clones, 256 total top-level entries and 372,274 filesystem entries, unlinks 6,856,707,876 logical bytes, and preserves all 256 fresh files byte-for-byte.

Values are median / sample p95, followed by minimum–maximum; with five samples, sample p95 is the maximum.

| Measurement | Parent | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Scratch owner wall, s | 2.612 / 10.089 (1.821–10.089) | 382.098 / 753.254 (248.888–753.254) |
| Process CPU, s | 2.633 / 6.254 (2.054–6.254) | 285.558 / 420.523 (230.193–420.523) |
| Main-thread CPU, s | 0.058 / 0.139 (0.042–0.139) | 228.169 / 315.692 (188.525–315.692) |
| Cumulative main-V8 allocation, MiB | 15.521 / 21.496 (13.122–21.496) | 31005.468 / 31021.641 (30844.852–31021.641) |
| Owner probe loop p99, ms | 13.099 / 31.359 (12.042–31.359) | 26.051 / 56.918 (12.034–56.918) |
| Owner probe loop maximum, ms | 14.524 / 98.566 (12.886–98.566) | 135.135 / 334.758 (35.815–334.758) |

Candidate reclaim rate: 0.942 clones/min median (0.478–1.446), versus zero on the parent. This is the accelerated owner fixture rate, not a prediction of physical production throughput. A/A owner wall: 3.357 and 3.818 s; CPU: 2.332 and 3.024 s; main allocation: 19.043 and 15.660 MiB.

The candidate now performs the formerly blocked recursive scan and deletion; its CPU/allocation cost is reported rather than presented as a speedup. The backward traversal adds no per-entry filesystem work. These unequal-duration owner probes on a busy shared host do not establish unaffected live transport latency; one candidate overlapped the separate build qualification, and that slow sample is retained. Allocation is cumulative main-V8 allocation, not retained heap or RSS; process CPU includes worker threads but excludes Git children. Early pilot timings that also advanced unrelated recurring maintenance were excluded after the benchmark correction.

This ordering fixture has 5,000 real synthetic session rows in a 4,472,832-byte agent database. It does not repeat or replace the earlier physical 35-GiB Linux/btrfs pressure-gate experiment; this owner change does not read transcript bodies. APFS, hardlinked immutable payloads, accelerated pacing, shared-host load, and logical-byte accounting limit the throughput/latency conclusions. The shipped Gateway proof above separately verifies real startup and restart behavior without accelerated timers.
