prs.title: fix(agents): keep a local Codex owner refusal from cooling the shared credential
prs.body:
## Head update — sixth mechanical integration (2026-11-12 23:17Z)

`main` regenerated the Gateway predicate again at `4ab02e3c0879aa5efb51e664b5e57c092144c9ed` (+6247/−6222 in `predicates.js`), which returned this PR to `CONFLICTING` on that one generated path — the same single-file recurrence documented below. Resolved the same mechanical way: integrated `main`, took main's clean `predicates.js`, re-ran `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and committed the generator output. The approvable head is now **`14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`** — a fast-forward of `06a288a4b05` (one merge commit, zero semantic change; every hand-written file and both proof e2e files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head, only the generated table moved). Both `session_authority` and `route_unavailable` are verified present in the regenerated table (one occurrence each), the generator exited 0, an ESM import smoke passed, and `mergeable` is back to `MERGEABLE` (`blocked` on the two maintainer actions only). Every `/allow-security-sensitive-change` reference below keys to this new SHA; any push re-keys it.

The CI and mergeability tallies in the historical sections below are snapshots of earlier heads, not claims about this one. On the previous head one lane stayed red for a PR-owned TypeScript error at `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts:143` (`.map(readRunFailureNotice)` callback signature, TS2345); that file is byte-identical on this head, and the finding is recorded in the integration comment rather than silently folded into a mechanical integration.

---

Closes #191473

## Needs from a maintainer (nothing is waiting on the author)

Two one-line actions, neither of which CODEOWNERS routes to anybody — which is the mechanical reason they have been waiting since Nov 3:

1. **`/allow-security-sensitive-change`** for head `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699` — this is the conflict-resolved head the re-derived review now names; `e960518954b` is one merge behind it, and approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. This is maintainer-tier, not SecOps: matched against the repo's own security policy, the gate covers **one** non-test production file (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`) and **3 lines** in it. The gate is live and correctly keyed, verified from the shipped logic: `scripts/github/security-review-rollout.mjs` returns mode `enforced` for this PR (rollout pull 152415 merged 2026-09-19, this PR created 2026-11-03), and `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` triggers on `issue_comment` created/edited plus a ten-minute reconcile schedule — so posting the command is picked up on its own, with no push or re-run needed from anyone. The exact acceptance predicate is `scripts/github/guard-review.mjs:525-552`, with the command grammar at `scripts/github/guard-shared.mjs:128-138`, and four of its clauses fail silently - worth quoting before anyone posts, so the first attempt sticks: (i) the comment must be created **after** the guard's current approval request, because any push re-keys it; (ii) **every** non-empty trimmed line must be one bare command from the closed set (`/allow-security-sensitive-change` or `/allow-dependencies-change`) - `lines.every(...)` means prose wrapped around the command makes the parser return nothing at all; (iii) the comment must **never have been edited**, since `updated_at !== created_at` disqualifies it, so tacking a clarifying note onto an already-posted command silently revokes that approval; (iv) the author's own comment is ignored and the poster must hold `maintain` or `admin`. Two intuitive choices that do **not** work: a GitHub Review - Approve satisfies nothing here (no review state is read anywhere in these files), and re-editing the command comment is equivalent to deleting it. The same function also closes the loop on the #193250 comparison quoted above: when the PR author's own repository role is `maintain` or `admin`, `findMaintainerApproval` returns an author-kind approval immediately and no command is required at all.
2. **A yes/no on the `Decision needed`**: whether `session_authority` joins the closed failover vocabulary. The review's own recommendation is to approve it; the measured alternative is that a refused scheduled run's cause is dropped to `undefined` by the run-history reader's own enum (`z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)`), because the writer already emits the value. Who can answer: the repo requires explicit approval for protocol changes (`AGENTS.md` — “Protocol/version bumps … need explicit approval; fix/ship authority ≠ release authority”) but names no owner for them — `CODEOWNERS` is 23 lines covering only `openclaw-secops` and `openclaw-release-managers`, has no catch-all, and lists nothing for `packages/gateway-protocol/**`; searching `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` for a protocol/vocabulary owner returns nothing. So this is waiting for any maintainer, not for a specific team that has been silent. Measured so the decision is framed correctly: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` has **exactly two commits in its entire history** — created whole by #121334 (2026-08-10, `3d5f916523d`) after duplicated reason lists had drifted and worker live events were rejecting `tls_certificate` payloads, and touched once since by #158222 (2026-09-26, `3c449bd35be`), a refactor that preserves the contract. **That framing was accurate when written and is now obsolete — and the correction is the most useful paragraph in this body.** `6f69195cd6b` (#193250, landed 07:24:45Z the same day) added `route_unavailable` to this very list, so `main` is at 17 members and this PR would make 18. That commit is the precedent the reviewer said did not exist, and it is nearly line-for-line the same change: it touched `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` with a **one-line addition to the same no-cooldown-write list** (`main` now reads `params.failoverReason === "route_unavailable" ||` at line 35, immediately beside this PR's line 41), updated the same formatter files (`user-copy.ts`, `assistant-request-failure-copy.ts`, `probe-status.ts`, `failover-error.ts`), regenerated the same predicate (`+3187/−3185` — the ordinal shift described above), added its own `config/test-lines-allocations/clawrouter-credit-immediate-fallback.txt`, and merged. Its final state: **`rating: 🦐 gold shrimp` (3/6)** — the same rung this PR sits on — with **`status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`**, carrying `security-sensitive-changed`, and **zero** `/allow-security-sensitive-change` comments anywhere in its comments or timeline. Two consequences stated plainly: the vocabulary is extendable by exactly the mechanism used here, so a yes points at an in-repo template rather than setting a precedent; and a 3/6 rating has never been this repo's merge bar. (Verified 15:14:10Z against `main`; the gate asymmetry recorded here as unexplained **is now explained, from source**. #193250's guard comment states verbatim: "No secops approval is required. This comment is informational because the PR author has Maintain or Admin access.", names `Repository role: admin` for its author, and matches **the same file** this PR does (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`). The shipped predicate is `scripts/github/security-review-event.mjs:309`, which drops a PR from the review queue when the author's repository role is `maintain` or `admin` — so the exemption keys on the author's permission on the repository, not on the scope of the change. Both PRs do report `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR` in REST, which is exactly the field that misled the earlier version of this paragraph: the workflow does not read it. Two consequences, stated separately so neither overreaches: this PR cannot borrow that zero-approval path, because the command is genuinely required for a contributor-author change; and the rating argument is unaffected, because #193250 still merged at 🦐 3/6, which is why 3/6 is not this repo's merge bar. The `status:` difference is explained by the same mechanism plus the review's own definition - it labels `👀 ready for maintainer look` when it has no contributor-facing blocker left, and `⏳ waiting on maintainer` when an explicit approval or decision is outstanding, which is precisely the state the enforced gate plus the recorded vocabulary decision create here.) The two options, and their costs, both quotable from shipped code. **Option A** is this PR: name the state (`session_authority`) so every consumer that already keys on the vocabulary says the same thing - the 403 mapping (`src/agents/failover-error.ts:191`), the cron run-history cause (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`), and the four exhaustive copy maps. **Option B** is the narrower alternative the question implies: keep classifying the refusal as `auth` and only suppress the profile-health write, so no public member is added. Its cost is user-visible and specific: under `auth`, the shipped copy at `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:621-622` reads "Couldn't sign in to ${provider}. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works.", and `auth` additionally carries cooldown copy (`:652` → `AUTH_PROFILE_COOLDOWN_COPY.auth`) - so a local relay that never spoke to the credential would still tell the user their saved login is broken, which is the false statement these reports are about (#162119's own diagnostics log `reason=auth` for exactly these 403s). Option A's copy instead reads "refused this request before sending it. Start a fresh request with /new." (`:625-626`), true whether or not the credential works. `VISION.md:99` states the repo's preference for this shape of change - "Once several independent PRs or requests wire in the same kind of capability, the right response is a contract, not a queue of merges" - and three independent P1 reports (#162119, #165739, #191473) wire this one. VISION does not decide enum membership, so this remains a human ask rather than a citation that answers itself.

Head moved twice since the last review: `main` regenerated the one colliding generated path, first in 513c12703ad and again in d0e78b07144, each time flipping this PR to CONFLICTING and stopping CI, so the branch was re-integrated and the predicate regenerated — `e960518954b` (main `9cb29007ed1`, 56 commits) was the head to approve at that point (superseded twice since; item 1 names today's); `a58d99c1fbc` is one merge behind it, the durable review quotes `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges behind, and the historical notes below still name `23ba4def295`. Re-verified on the newest merge: all five validator checks; the protocol registry, generation, native `--check` and since guards; the core test typecheck; the seven touched suites (45, 25, 13 and 72 passed across four shards); and the test-line ratchet with 15 lines of slack. On the previous merge the same set passed with the touched suites at 72, 13, 42 and 25. One environment caveat carried forward: `codex-app-server:protocol:check` cannot run here because it wants a sibling `openai/codex` checkout at `rust-v0.164.0`, and no workflow references it, so it is a dev-time sync check rather than a gate. One measured caveat: on that earlier merge `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` reported the tree 7 lines over the ceiling, and the identical 7 is `main`’s own overage (same checker, same throwaway-index method: `Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`), while this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292. Nothing was trimmed to hide it; the shared scalar is untouched.

Current state (03:08:18Z, head `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`): **mergeable, and CI is red-free** — the run is **complete and red-free** (re-read 12:07Z): 111 succeeded / 72 skipped / 1 neutral (`CodeQL`), zero failures, zero cancellations, nothing in progress, and 3 checks that never report. `mergeable` is **MERGEABLE**, with `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` only on the two approvals above. Drift is measured as one full sweep plus hourly increments: the full head-to-`main` sweep at 07:07Z (66 `main` commits, 680 distinct changed paths) and every hourly window since (this round: 8 commits, 95 paths against `main` @ `9f5e8175577`) intersect this PR's 21 files in **0** paths, and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` is still blob `c5df64e150ac` on that tip, identical to this branch's merge base - so no regeneration is pending and `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699` is a head that can be approved and merged as-is today. Concretely: `check-lint-core-1..5` all green, `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)` and `(3/4)` green, both `android-access-native` matrix cells green, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` green, the `openclaw/ci-gate` mirror green, and all 20 `checks-node-changed-*` shards — the family that runs the Gateway product proof — green. That clause is now a citation rather than an inference: in job `127671424815` (`checks-node-changed`, log fetched 21:20Z) the shard log shows `[shard:bun:test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts] begin` at 02:30:35Z, then `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 77.48s` and `end (exit 0)` at 02:31:53Z, and the neighbouring `gateway-codex-refusal-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` reports `Test Files 1 passed (1)` at 02:33:21Z. So both refusal-proof e2e files execute in CI on this head - the first is this PR's own, and the second predates it (same blob `50f493f86ad9` on `main`, first added by #136194 on 2026-09-04), which also means this PR does not disturb the lane that already covers the sibling refusal shape. Proof confidence 🦞 5/6 ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 5/6, zero open findings, no remaining rank-up moves, and the reviewer's `Before merge` has collapsed from two items to one. The two lanes that *were* red on earlier heads cleared exactly as attributed below (upstream repaired both), so what follows is kept as a measurement trail, not as open work:

- `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)`, `(3/4)` — Control UI copy assertions broken by upstream `f1a317d4674` ("chore(ui): refresh control ui locales", landed 17:50Z, i.e. after this branch's previous integration). All seven failing spec files (`cron-search`, `cron-filters`, `cron-run-completion`, `cron-run-suppression`, `boot-module-boundaries`, `settings-layout`, `new-session-page.workspace-memory`) are byte-identical to `main` here — `git diff 77c263b9fa1 HEAD -- <file>` is empty for each — and none is in this change's surface.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — the tree is 7 lines over the test-line ceiling, and `main`'s own tree is over by the same 7 under the same checker and method (`Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`); this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292.

Head `a58d99c1fbc` then merged main past `9938e65a609`, the upstream commit that realigned those e2e expectations with the refreshed locales, and past the test-line reconciliation: on this merge the ratchet measures 25 lines of slack rather than 7 over, and the seven UI spec files are byte-identical to a `main` that contains its own repair. Measured on this merge: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `checks-ui-e2e (3/4)` turned green, exactly as those two upstream reconciliations predict. Two lanes stayed red there for a **different** copy drift that the e2e-alignment commit did not cover: `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.device-dispatch.e2e.test.ts` still expects `No worker slots are available` while the UI renders `No session slots are available. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Codex owner refusal (HTTP 403 produced by the in-process inference relay, before any provider request) was classified as a provider authentication failure, which cooled down the shared OpenAI OAuth profile and interrupted every other agent using that credential.

## User Impact

User impact: one refused run no longer logs an entire profile out. Sibling agents on the same credential keep working, the model fallback chain is not consumed for a refusal that says nothing about the model, API clients receive a permission rejection instead of a retryable server error, and the message no longer tells operators to sign in again — it tells them to start a fresh request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is generated locally, so the credential answered nothing; the 401/403 rule in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` could not tell the two apart. The fix preserves the local refusal's identity instead of exempting HTTP 403 or the `model_permission_denied` code globally, so genuine provider permission errors keep their exact current handling.

- The local relay's own refusal copy is the identity carrier. Codex's transport drops the relay's JSON body and renders only `error.message` as `unexpected status {status}: {message}, url: {url}` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, `UnexpectedResponseError::display_body` / `Display`), so the copy is the part that survives to the runner.
- A new run-scoped `session_authority` failover reason carries it: `src/agents/auth-profiles` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` record profile health only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, and `billing`, so the shared credential is never cooled.
- The reason resolves to `coordination` in `resolveModelFallbackError`, the owner that already stops the chain when "changing models cannot repair" the failure. Another model cannot re-establish the refused run's owner, so the chain surfaces the refusal instead of blaming a candidate, which is what the issue's "should not consume the model fallback chain" requirement asks for.
- `FAILOVER_STATUS` projects the reason as `403` with `permission_error`, so OpenAI-compatible clients stop seeing an unmapped reason fall through to a retryable `500`.
- Operator-facing copy for the reason avoids sign-in advice on both the assistant and auth-profile surfaces.

Second, this exercises loading and migrating existing stored data, not the packaged update lifecycle: no `openclaw update` install/replace and no managed-service restart is involved, so the container lane (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`) stays the authoritative version of that claim.

That was wrong — the guard only failed closed because I isolated state by overriding `HOME`, which stops it inspecting the local service. Using the repo's own `OPENCLAW_HOME` normalization, the check runs on the host.

### Blast radius of the new member, measured rather than asserted

The concern worth answering for the vocabulary decision is whether a new canonical reason could change credential behavior somewhere unintended. The repo already encodes that boundary in types, and every number below is checkable in-tree:

- **There are two closed lists, and the canonical one is deliberately wider.** `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` holds 17 members on this head; `AuthProfileFailureReason` in `src/agents/auth-profiles/types.ts:85` — whose own doc comment says it is the set of "Closed reasons that drive cooldown, disable, and failure counters" — holds 13 and **already excludes three canonical reasons** (`server_error`, `tls_certificate`, `context_overflow`). So "a reason exists in the vocabulary" has never implied "a reason can cool a profile"; `session_authority` becomes the fourth member in that existing class rather than a new kind of thing.
- **One producer, zero casts.** `resolveAuthProfileFailureReason` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts:17`) is the only function that converts a canonical reason into a cooldown reason, and it returns `null` for `session_authority` at line 41. All four profile-health writers route through it and bail on `null` before calling `markAuthProfileFailure`, whose parameter is the narrow union (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:555`): `run/auth-controller.ts:318`, `run/failover-retry-controller.ts:134`, `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-run-settlement.ts:148`, `src/agents/simple-completion-profile-failover.ts:44`. Grepping production code for `as AuthProfileFailureReason` returns **no hits**, so there is no path — including no escape hatch — by which the new member can reach cooldown bookkeeping.
- **Stored history stays total.** `src/agents/auth-profiles/profile-usage-stats.ts:33` normalizes persisted reasons against `AUTH_PROFILE_FAILURE_REASONS`, so an unrecognized value in old data degrades to "not a cooldown reason" instead of throwing or cooling.
- **Wire and rollback tolerance, measured — and why it holds is the part worth reading.** The live telemetry schema *is* strict: `WorkerLiveFallbackAttemptSchema.reason` (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/worker-admission.ts:421`) and `fallbackStepFromFailureReason` (`:458`) are a union of one literal per member (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/failover-reason.ts:10-12`), so an older peer's schema literally cannot name `session_authority`. But nothing enforces them on ingress: the worker live-event receiver (`src/gateway/worker-environments/live-events.ts`) validates credential ownership, sequence and window state rather than payload shape, and the only production files that import the generated predicates at all are `src/chat/sender-identity.ts` and `src/config/sessions/session-participant-identity.ts`. So a newer worker reporting this reason to an older Gateway is not rejected, and stored values written by a newer build degrade tolerantly (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`). Flagging the caveat explicitly: that tolerance is **incidental to the absence of inbound validation, not designed in** — if these payloads ever gain boundary schema enforcement, widening this enum becomes a downgrade hazard that would need negotiation or a tolerant reader first. (Checked 12:15:13Z on this head.)
- **The structural contract passes with the member added.** `test/type-contracts/agent-runtime-plan.ts:40` asserts the runtime plan's failover projection `toEqualTypeOf<(typeof FAILOVER_REASONS)[number]>();`; that file is compiled (the `test-root-other` shard includes `test/**/*.ts` via `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json`, confirmed by `--listFilesOnly`), and running it on this head is clean: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json` → exit 0 at 07:19:32Z.

- **Copy completeness is enforced by the compiler, not by my diligence — and every behaviour-enabling list is opt-in.** The four user-facing maps are declared `satisfies Record<FailoverReason, …>` (`src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:647`, `src/agents/failover/assistant-request-failure-copy.ts:100`, `src/agents/failover/probe-status.ts:22`, `src/gateway/openai-compat-errors.ts:37`), so a forgotten member is a type error rather than an `undefined` at runtime; CI's green typecheck is the proof, not my claim. The single table the compiler cannot check, `FAILOVER_STATUS` (`src/agents/failover-error.ts:181`), is carried by hand at line 190 (`session_authority` → 403) with a dedicated branch at `src/agents/failover-error.ts:745`. In the other direction, the three allow-lists that *grant* user-visible side effects all omit the new member deliberately, which is what makes "no re-login prompt" a measured property rather than an intent: re-login recovery (`src/auto-reply/provider-login-recovery.ts:58`, whose members are `auth`, `auth_permanent`, `session_expired`), session model auto-revert (`src/agents/session-model-auto-revert.ts:30`) and profile-recovery affordances (`src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:656`). Sets like these are invisible to the build, so a maintainer reviewing the vocabulary question can read the three line numbers above as the whole behavioural surface.

- **Every other branch on the reason takes the safe default, and the reason for that is checkable: the new member is simply absent from them.** Grepping these files for `session_authority` returns nothing, so it falls through each predicate rather than being special-cased: `src/agents/failover-policy.ts:12` (the transient cooldown-probe-slot predicate) does not list it, so a refused local run can neither consume a probe slot nor be treated as transient; the provider-runtime diagnostic gates its auth/401 chat copy on `failoverReason === "auth"` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-runtime-failure.ts:160`), so the new reason cannot be labelled an authentication problem on that path either; and the realtime relay's switch (`src/gateway/talk/relay/issues.ts:54`) reaches its `default` at line 68, producing a generic provider error rather than a credentials instruction — the same no-re-login rule the four maps this change *does* update follow.

None of this answers the *policy* question — the reason a human still has to decide is persistence: the value is written into cron run history and read back through `z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)` (`src/cron/run-error-reason.ts:6`, `src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`), so the vocabulary and the stored cause must agree. It does, however, bound what a yes costs on the credential side: the cooldown surface cannot receive the new reason.

**The user-facing blast radius is also not one issue, and it predates this PR.** A repo-wide search for the refusal string returns three open P1 reports: #162119 (2026-09-30) records what the classifier did, verbatim from the reporter's own diagnostics — "For each 403, OpenClaw classified the result as `reason=auth`, `attempt=1`, `retry=0`, `rotations=0`, `next=none`" — which is precisely the write path this PR stops; #165739 (2026-10-05) names the producer, `CodexInferenceAuthorizationError("owner")` surfacing as a 403 `model_permission_denied`; and #191473, the issue this PR closes. #176311 merged on 2026-10-23 against the *startup* variant of the native-child path and #165739 is still open, so the classification half was never taken by it. Neither reporter claimed a profile cooldown — that inference is mine, and it is the mechanism the fix exists for — but the `reason=auth` attribution they do record is what routes into `markAuthProfileFailure`, and it has been recorded against this message for five weeks.



**Two completeness questions a reviewer would reasonably ask about this member, each answered from source rather than from intent.** (1) *Does an added reason have to appear in every copy site?* Only in the maps written as `satisfies Record<FailoverReason, …>`, and those are the four the compiler already forces this PR to fill. `src/cron/failure-notification-text.ts` is deliberately **not** one of them: `cronFailureDetailLines` (`:18`) special-cases four members - `billing`/`server_error` at `:22`, `route_unavailable` at `:31`, `model_not_found` at `:37` - and the remaining 14 of the 18 render as the bare `Cause: <token>` at `:43`. A refused scheduled run therefore notifies `Cause: session_authority`, the same shape as today's `Cause: rate_limit` or `Cause: timeout`; giving this reason its own cron guidance is a product choice of the kind #193250 made for `route_unavailable`, not a completeness requirement this PR is missing. (2) *Does an added member require a protocol-version bump?* The repo's own history says no. The negotiated surface is `packages/gateway-protocol/src/version.ts:2-8` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4`, `MIN_CLIENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 4`, `MIN_NODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`, `MIN_PROBE_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`), read today from `main` @ `8dd41fc9529`; `#193250` added `route_unavailable` without touching that file and neither does this PR. The four strict wire positions consuming the enum (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/cron.ts:460` and `:740`, `schema/worker-admission.ts:421` and `:457`) are unions over the same generated list, and the published SDK declaration bundles are gitignored (`packages/*/dist/`, `.gitignore:45`), so there is no second in-repo artifact that can go stale with the vocabulary.

## PR surface

The `size: XL` label on this PR is generated code, not review surface. Of `+3499/-3153` across 21 files, `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` accounts for `+3155/-3153` by itself: the generator renumbers its internal check identifiers when the vocabulary grows, so adding one enum member rewrites the whole file. It was produced by `pnpm gateway:validators:gen` and verified by `pnpm validators:check`, never hand-edited. The reviewable part is `+41` production lines across 11 files and `+299` test lines across 8 files — which includes the 188-line Gateway-turn product proof — plus a 4-line `config/test-lines-allocations` record.

Regeneration is also the whole merge resolution, and the merge is now done. `main` @ `be881a7f8b1` (2796 commits) is merged into this branch, and the generated predicate was the only colliding path: the six hand-written files both sides touch (`message-patterns.ts`, `failover-error.ts`, `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, `classify.test.ts`, `model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`, `scripts/lib/vitest-build-prerequisites.mts`) auto-merged, and `3cee3643e13` publishes the regenerated output on top of main's numbering.

Because `build-artifacts` and the ratchets run on `refs/pull/191562/merge` — this head merged with whatever `main` is at that moment — the generated predicate can merge cleanly as text and still be stale as output. That was the first `build-artifacts` failure on this PR: `main` had advanced 25 commits, none of them under `packages/gateway-protocol/src`, and the merged tree no longer equalled the generator's bytes. Reproduced locally on that merge, fixed by regenerating against it (`23ba4def295`), and re-verified with `validators:check` + `protocol:check`. So regeneration is the last step before pushing, not a step that finishes once.


Integration also caught one stale assertion, which is the point of landing on a current base: `main` added a `model_fallback_chain_stopped` record for local coordination stops (`src/agents/model-fallback-runner.ts:597`), so the chain-stop case now pins that stop event and its `local_runtime_coordination` reason instead of asserting an empty record list. The behavior the case proves is unchanged and was re-verified on the merged base: the refusal rejects with the original error, `run` is called once, no fallback step fires, and no candidate is consumed. Re-ran green on the merge: `validators:check`, `protocol:check`, `tsgo:core:test`, the touched agent/gateway suites, and the Gateway refusal proof above (real build, `Tests 1 passed (1)` in 31s).

Two contributor-side items from the review are now also closed: the redundant helper-level refusal case in `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` was removed as suggested (its classification, chain-stop and HTTP-status assertions are each pinned at their own owner boundary, and `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError` is only a wrapper over the chain resolution), and the cooldown assertion reads the store's own predicate.

## Remaining Gates

For a quick pass, in order of cost:

1. **Approve** — post `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for head `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699` (the conflict-resolved head; the review's `Before merge` names this same SHA). Every push resets this approval, so it has to be keyed to whatever head you land.

   What the gate actually covers, so the approval is scoped: matching this PR's real file list against the repo's own `.github/security-review-policy.yml` (using the repo's `minimatch`, with the policy's own exclusions applied) yields **exactly one** security-sensitive non-test file — `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`, reached through the `credentials` glob `src/agents/**/*auth*.ts`. The production diff there is 3 lines that add `session_authority` to the condition returning `null`, i.e. "write no credential-health state for this run". That policy file's own header declares it the *maintainer-review tier* and says SecOps-only paths remain in CODEOWNERS — and `src/agents/**` has **no** CODEOWNERS entry, so clearing this needs a maintainer's command, not a security team member. The same gap explains why this has been sitting: `packages/gateway-protocol/**` is also unlisted in CODEOWNERS, so the vocabulary decision has no routed owner at all and is picked up only by whoever reads this.

2. **Decide** — the recorded `Decision needed`: whether `session_authority` joins the public failover vocabulary. The reviewer now recommends approving it **and has retracted its own earlier premise** — "the merged route_unavailable precedent establishes that the vocabulary can expand, correcting the earlier immutable-vocabulary premise, but no maintainer has approved this particular addition" — so what is missing is a written maintainer decision, and the readiness cap is now stated as that decision "independently of the enforced security approval".
3. **CI** — complete on `14a2d9eb5098ad67b28bf48c3990a7afb6ba3699`: re-read 12:07Z, 111 succeeded / 72 skipped / 1 neutral, **zero red at all**, both `android-access-native` matrix cells included. (The disk-exhaustion note below is from head `23ba4def295`, kept because it records how that lane was ruled out rather than fixed.) `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` exhausted the disk while unzipping the 16 KB page-size system image (`You are running out of disk space … Free space left: 0 MB`, then `No space left on device`) before any instrumentation ran, and its `(4096, google_apis)` sibling passed on the same head; `openclaw/ci-gate` mirrors that single job. The two lanes that were genuinely red on the previous head — `build-artifacts` (generated predicate stale against a `main` that had moved again) and `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — are both green here.

Checked whether that red can block you: it cannot. The `16384/ps16k` variant is **skipped** on other recently landed PRs and never reports on `main` push commits, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is not a required status check either — PR #192499 landed with `openclaw/ci-gate` red on its merge commit. So this lane needs a re-run by someone with write access to be green, not a code change from me; nothing about it reflects the tree.

The latest review marks this explanation as contributor-supplied because its own log download was redirected to a blocked host, so here are the two lines verbatim from `gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/jobs/126253990114/logs` (re-fetched just now, both still present): `##[warning]You are running out of disk space. The runner will stop working when the machine runs out of disk space. Free space left: 0 MB` at `22:42:12`, then `Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package 16 KB Page Size Google APIs Intel x86_64 Atom System Image: No space left on device.` at `22:42:20`. The job died inside SDK/emulator provisioning — the only earlier steps were Java setup and that `sdkmanager` download, and no Gradle build or instrumentation task had run yet — so the lane cannot be reporting anything about this diff. GitHub’s own record corroborates it without the log CDN: the annotations endpoint for that check run reports `No files were found with the provided path: apps/android/app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/**`, i.e. the job produced no Android test results at all, which is only possible if it stopped before instrumentation.
4. **Optional** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` to cover the packaged update lifecycle, which the host-side checks deliberately do not claim.

As of the latest recorded review (re-keyed to `23ba4def295`), evidence is not the constraint and neither is code: proof confidence is graded 🦞 diamond lobster ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 diamond lobster with **no actionable findings and no remaining rank-up moves**, and overall readiness is held at 🦐 only by owner direction on the public vocabulary — the review states that in two places, so the sub-scores cannot lift it on their own. The two items that remain are maintainer-only: the security-sensitive approval for `23ba4def295` (any push resets it) and the recorded `Decision needed` on adding a member to the closed failover vocabulary, for which the review's own recommendation is to approve the additive reason. This section is kept as a record of what was produced locally and what a container would still add, not as a claim that more evidence is required.

Currency check, re-run at 10:04:12Z against today's `main` @ `43654d5fcea` (09:56:52Z) — still no competing repair. `session_authority` occurs **0** times, on that tip, in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` (344 B), `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` (18,768 B), `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` (16,997 B) and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` (3,543 B); the byte counts are quoted because a truncated or empty read would print the same zero. `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` on `main` already carries the `route_unavailable` exclusion (1 occurrence) and not this one, and a repo-wide code search for `owner of this model request` on `main` returns **exactly one path** — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`, the relay that emits the refusal — so nothing on the classification side mentions it. Earlier reads (at `be881a7f8b1`, then `8209e020b8c`) said the same; today's is the one that matters. So the misclassification is live on `main` as of now, and this PR remains the only fix.

Hook integrity was checked pre-merge against `df9d3240e52` because CI could not run while the branch was unmerged; the merge makes that reasoning moot and the live code is now the evidence. Between the old base and `be881a7f8b1` exactly one commit touched the classifier files this repair hangs off (`7e4bdf2f607`, provider deadline timeouts reported as auth failures), and after the merge the classification still resolves the refusal prose to `session_authority` (`classify.test.ts`), the profile policy still skips the health write (`run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts`), and the Gateway proof still shows the shared profile serving the next turn.

The one stronger form not reproducible on this host:

- **Latest-stable upgrade with existing state** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPECS="openclaw@2026.10.10 openclaw@2026.9.36"` (current `latest` and `extended-stable` from the registry) against this PR's candidate package; Package Acceptance resolves the same lane from `source=ref`, and the QA Lab scenario id is `docker-upgrade-survivor` (`qa/scenarios/runtime/docker-upgrade-survivor.yaml`, script `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`). Checked before writing this: every existing-state upgrade scenario the repo ships (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `docker-release-upgrade-user-journey`, `docker-update-channel-switch`, `docker-update-migration`, `docker-update-restart-auth`) routes through `docker-e2e-lane.ts`, so there is no host-runner equivalent to substitute — this is the one gate that genuinely needs a container or a runner rather than more local evidence. That is the check that a pre-existing install still loads its stored cron, auth-profile and session state after moving onto this build. The additive-vocabulary probe above shows existing reason values still validate, but it is not the upgrade run the review asked for.

Correction worth recording: the Gateway-turn gate did **not** need a container. It runs on the host through the shipped QA product harness (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `--runner host` semantics), and the earlier claim that this sandbox could not exercise a Gateway turn was wrong. The survivor lane genuinely is container-only (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` hands off to `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh` inside the harness image) and this machine has no running Docker daemon; starting one, or using a credentialed remote runner, is a host-level action that needs the operator's go-ahead, and remote execution is maintainer-authorized. I still tried the host route today, and it stops on a guard that should not be bypassed: published `openclaw@2026.10.10`, run in an isolated `HOME` on its own port, created real durable state (a seeded cron row, canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, config journal), and this branch's CLI then refuses to load it with `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`, because the machine has a LaunchAgent-managed Gateway. That refusal is correct behavior on a live install, so the existing-state upgrade check needs a container or a runner without a live service rather than a workaround. One ordering detail matters for whoever runs it: until `main` is integrated, this branch's own version reads `2026.10.9`, which predates the `2026.10.10` stable baseline, so a meaningful upgrade run has to follow the merge rather than precede it. Integration is complete, and the blocker was local configuration rather than the link: this machine's global `http.lowSpeedLimit=1` aborted the fetch during the v0 full-ref advertisement ("expected flush after ref listing"), which is what the earlier failures looked like. `git -c protocol.version=2 -c http.lowSpeedLimit=0 fetch` pulled the whole pack at 9-11 MB/s. The merge itself was one generated file plus `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and the branch version now reads `2026.10.10`, so a survivor run pairs a published `openclaw@2026.9.36` baseline against this build rather than treating `2026.10.10` as the newer side.

prs.title: fix: honor access changes for queued worker deletion
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Queued cloud-worker deletion can reach acceptance after the requester loses access.

## User Impact

Ordinary and forced deletion honor access changes before acceptance. Cleanup that was already accepted continues through retries and disconnection. Upgrading ordinary cleanup to forced discard requires its own current authorization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing request assertion through the deletion queues into the existing guarded persistence operations, including prepared-worker cancellation. Terminal workers use the same forced-discard acceptance path. Requests for missing environments return the existing error without discarding placement data; internal maintenance retains its dangling-placement cleanup.

The environment lifecycle remains the cleanup owner. No schema, configuration, or protocol changes are required.

## Evidence

- **103 tests passed across seven focused files**, covering queued ordinary/forced deletion, prepared cancellation, forced-discard upgrades, terminal and missing workers, timeout/restart recovery, and accepted cleanup after requester removal. Regressions failed on the preceding code for the intended behavior.
- Production and both affected Gateway test typechecks, targeted lint, format parity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- **Full `pnpm build` passed**, including unified declarations, plugin builds, and Control UI assets.
- **Two compiled-app Chromium scenarios passed**, ordinary and forced. Each exercised normal sign-in and device removal through the real issuer, Discovery, Loader, Gateway, and native tunnel. After canonical removal and socket closure, an independent FIFO queue barrier completed with no deletion acceptance, allocation lookup, or provider deletion. Authorized deletion, no-deletion, and independent-cleanup controls passed.
- Source and served assets were independently verified against retained manifests. The 64,531-input build/runtime snapshot matches commit `3cac1d2b48552e6a99c17df60ff921aae8b6cbdf` byte for byte; build metadata retains base commit `043dfcbf4ccdd983189d09de51f4b4297b3716c4`.
- Local Codex autoreview covered the complete candidate against that base through **P0–P2**, with no remaining actionable findings. The reviewed source matches this commit. [Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197961#issuecomment-6838996994) completed for this exact head with no code findings. Its request for inspectable application evidence is addressed by the sanitized receipt below.

App qualification used pinned supporting service sources, a source-built native binding and reused Loader WASM/glue assets, and a synthetic loopback provider. It proves the application flow, without claiming real-cloud deletion, runnable-worker execution, npm-package, or deployed-service qualification. Live services were unchanged.

## Application receipt

Sanitized field projection from the two compiled-app receipts, checked against the retained source/asset manifests and provider event history. Identifiers, endpoints, keys, and browser error stacks are omitted. The barrier is a completed same-key replay using a different profile, which exits at the existing profile-mismatch check after earlier queued work. Independent local-owner cleanup runs after that barrier.

## CI status

Six `openclaw-id-protocol` runtime files are missing from `wrapper-components.txt`, leading to an unresolved `statements/validate.js` import. prs.title: fix: node directory listing pages until the gateway stops
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node directory listing stops after 32 pages so one oversized directory cannot pin the gateway. Bootstrap discovery used that stop to skip the directory, then still loaded a sibling, but it recorded no diagnostic. A configured `*/AGENTS.md` file inside the oversized directory disappeared with `diagnostics: []`.

## Evidence

Head `b06896ea3a7` on macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1. The production trace below was run on `055d09e2943`. `b06896ea3a7` merges current main and adds the 112-line test grant. It does not change the listing or the diagnostic. A real directory held 131073 empty names, which is one past 32 pages of 4096. Its sibling `keep/AGENTS.md` contained `kept instructions`. Production `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` listed that tree. Each `dir.list` call went to production `handleDirList` on that directory, not a scripted page payload. `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` then loaded `*/AGENTS.md`.

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 stat=0 fetch=1
```

`dir.list` ran 34 times: one page for the root, 32 pages for the oversized directory, and one page for the sibling. `file.fetch` read the sibling once. The oversized directory is named in the diagnostic and its instructions were not loaded.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Bootstrap discovery skips one directory after the real 32-page listing cap, records that skip, and still loads a sibling `AGENTS.md`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin arm64, Node v26.12.1, head `055d09e2943` in `/tmp/oc-165805`, then merged forward as `b06896ea3a7` without changing the listing or the diagnostic. The directory was a local folder with 131073 names. The node command handler and the gateway bridge ran in one process.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Created the oversized directory and `keep/AGENTS.md`. Called `createNodeWorkspaceBridge` with `invoke` dispatching to `handleDirList`, `handleFileStat`, and `handleFileFetch`. Called `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` for `*/AGENTS.md`.
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that production path:

```console
OK: files=kept instructions diagnostics=[{"dir":"fat","reason":"io","detail":"Directory listing exceeded 32 pages"}] dirList=34 fetch=1
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sibling file was loaded. The oversized directory produced one `io` diagnostic, `Directory listing exceeded 32 pages`, after 32 real listing pages.
- **What was not tested:** A second OS process enrolled as a node over the gateway websocket. The same handlers ran in-process.

## Summary

A directory past the listing page budget is still skipped, and its sibling still loads. The skip is now a diagnostic instead of a silent omission.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): bound the sandbox scp transfer with a deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Sandbox media staging shells out to `scp`, and that spawn had **no deadline**: a hung transfer (dead peer, wedged ssh, a dropped TCP session that never resets) left the child process alive indefinitely and the caller awaiting a promise that never settles — one leaked `scp` per stalled staging attempt, with no bound on how long the turn could hang.

This gives the transfer a bounded deadline **through the shared process-lifecycle runner rather than by owning the spawn directly**, which is the direction #98141 was closed toward: that PR was closed as "superseded by the current process-lifecycle architecture, not because the linked defect is fixed" — so the timeout belongs on the existing runner call, not on a locally-owned `child_process.spawn`.

## Evidence

The change is two files:

```
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts          |  8 +-
src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts | 101 ++++++++++++++++++-
```

- `stage-sandbox-media.ts` derives the per-transfer budget (`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()`: size cap / supported throughput, 30s floor, `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` override) and passes it as `timeoutMs` on the existing shared-runner invocation — the runner already owns deadlines and descendant-tree termination.
- The test suite asserts the deadline reaches the runner (`expect.objectContaining({ timeoutMs: SCP_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT_MS })`) so the wiring cannot silently regress, and adds a real-process hang case: a fake `scp` on `PATH` that spawns a descendant, ignores `SIGTERM`, and never exits. The assertion is that the transfer is rejected by the deadline and **both the parent and the descendant are gone afterwards** (via the repo's existing `test-utils/process-tree` helpers), plus a negative control that a normal transfer still succeeds unchanged.

```
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --no-file-parallelism
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  13 passed | 2 skipped (15)
```

## Verification

The deadline wiring and the normal-transfer assertions run and pass here; the two skipped cases are the POSIX-only hang cases (`it.runIf(process.platform !== "win32")`) — this machine is Windows, so the process-tree termination assertion itself is **not exercised locally**. I am stating that rather than implying it: it needs a POSIX CI lane to run, and that is the one part of this change I could not observe directly.

Partial fix for #98468: the deadline wiring, the revised budget, and real timeout recovery (process tree + temporary cleanup) are verified here; the remaining unobserved part is a real multi-hour suspend/transfer scenario on a POSIX lane, which CI's Linux lane runs via the committed cases.

## Context worth knowing before review

- Three prior attempts exist on this issue: #98141 (closed as superseded by the lifecycle architecture — see above), #101473 (long review loop, closed), #132552 (merged, but that was the *cancellation* half of staging, not the transfer deadline).
- The issue currently also carries `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`. If the automated fix lane produces a PR for the same deadline, take that one — the intent here is to have the fix available in the architecture the maintainer pointed at, not to race a bot.

## Revision 2 — revised transfer budget + real transport proof (head `8707115c920`)

**Decision answer (the question the review asked): revise the deadline instead of an unconditional 30s cutoff.**
`resolveScpTransferTimeoutMs()` derives the per-transfer budget from the size cap and the slowest throughput still called supported, keeps it bounded, and is overridable:

| Case | Budget |
|---|---|
| 50 MiB cap at the 256 KiB/s supported floor | **200s** |
| review example: 40 MiB at 1 MiB/s (~40s) | **160s** (the old fixed 30s could never allow it) |
| small transfers | 30s floor |
| `OPENCLAW_SANDBOX_SCP_TIMEOUT_MS` | operator override (tests use it to reach the deadline in seconds) |

The deadline remains an absolute, bounded value owned by the shared runner, so an unattended hang still dies; it just no longer kills a slow-but-healthy copy. A deadline kill is also no longer retried (one bounded wait instead of three): retrying a copy that stopped progressing only re-waits the whole budget. If maintainers want a different number, or a config field instead of the env override, name it and I'll switch it.

### Real behavior proof (no mocks: real spawned transport through staging, Windows)

A compiled stand-in transport is spawned through the same argv/PATH path the runner uses, so the real spawn, deadline, tree kill, and temp cleanup all execute:

```
[proof] slow transfer staged=1 elapsed=7965ms
[proof] staged bytes=real transport bytes
[proof] hung transport pid=22892 alive=true
[proof] descendant pid=54128 alive=true
[proof] reaped by deadline: parent=true descendant=true
[proof] surface={"value":{"staged":{}}}
[proof] attempts="attempt\n"
[proof] temp dir removed=true
 ✓ windows real transport proof > publishes a real slow transport that finishes inside the budget 8044ms
 ✓ windows real transport proof > kills a real hung transport tree on the deadline without retrying 8507ms
```

Both Windows-native cases pass (17 passed | 3 skipped with the scratch cases in place) and the same file without them is **15 passed | 3 skipped, exit 0**; `oxfmt --check` clean on both files. The three skips are the POSIX-gated cases (they spawn a shebang script), which is why the Windows run above uses a compiled stand-in. `oxlint` produced no verdict for explicit paths in this junction worktree, so I am not claiming a lint verdict — CI's lint lane judges.

The new committed cases: the derived-budget unit math (including the 40 MiB / 160s case), a real slow transfer that publishes, and the hung tree + descendant reaped on the deadline with one attempt and the temp dir removed.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `818eee92049`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 368ae1dc | v2026.10.8 | 17:47:36 | 17:47:37 | 17:48:06 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| a7d22a6f | v2026.10.8 | 17:48:15 | 17:48:16 | 17:48:49 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 49b062ca | v2026.10.8 | 17:49:07 | 17:49:08 | 17:49:09 | completed | completed |
| 8fea48a4 | 2df6212 | 22:12:37 | 22:12:38 | 22:13:28 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 05f267e5 | 2df6212 | 22:13:34 | 22:13:35 | 22:13:55 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 0a54b7ad | 2df6212 | 22:14:01 | 22:14:02 | 22:14:37 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| c96579c8 | 2df6212 | 22:14:51 | 22:14:52 | 22:14:53 | completed | completed |
| 28ab70e0 | 2df6212 | 22:15:40 | 22:15:42 | 22:16:14 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |
| 70f2a343 | 2df6212 | 22:24:50 | - | 22:24:53 | completed | completed |
| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

prs.title: fix(discord): honor provider interruption policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord realtime playback currently admits a fresh receive stream only when local `bargeIn` is enabled (or output is continuous). With `bargeIn: false`, that prevents provider-side VAD from hearing a new speaker turn even when `interruptResponseOnInputAudio` is enabled. The provider therefore cannot perform the interruption policy it was configured to own.

## Merge brief

- **Root cause:** receive admission during playback was coupled only to local raw-audio barge-in policy.
- **Fix:** retain the resolved provider interruption flag on the realtime speaker session and include it in `canReceiveDuringPlayback()`.
- **Preserved boundary:** raw local audio still does not stop playback when `bargeIn` is disabled; provider input must qualify speech and own the interruption.
- **Protected mode:** when both local and provider interruption are disabled, capture during playback remains blocked.
- **Scope:** one Discord voice source file and two test files; no new config or public API.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/voice/transcripts-readiness.test.ts extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-session.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **51/51 passed** on head `4dbdf05f2f53a6ee5864366761aa50d2c2b89fe9`.
- Positive regression: provider interruption enabled + local barge-in disabled admits capture without stopping the player locally.
- Closest negative regression: both interruption paths disabled rejects capture during playback.
- Adjacent readiness regression: provider-owned bidi capture during playback reaches the provider while STT/TTS and protected paths retain their prior expectations.
- `pnpm check:changed` — passed, including formatting, Discord extension tests/typechecks, lint, dead-export, boundary, and import-cycle checks.
- `git diff HEAD^ --check` — passed.
- Independent P0/P1 review found no actionable issues.
- Baseline comparison: the new provider-only lifecycle regression was run against base `231fae1903a04b51df073b25b20906fb4d58799e` in an isolated worktree with matching frozen dependencies. It failed because `receiver.subscribe` was called zero times during playback. On candidate `4dbdf05f2f53a6ee5864366761aa50d2c2b89fe9`, that positive case and the both-off negative case both pass (2/2 selected tests). This is in-process proof, not acoustic proof.

### Proof debt

Live acoustic Discord proof is not included. The repository has QA voice join/authorization scenarios, but this contributor environment cannot reach its leased-bot broker: `qa discord --doctor` stopped before readiness because no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair was available. Those scenarios also do not by themselves exercise acoustic interruption. The contributor's voice bot is attached to a production Gateway; the candidate was not connected in parallel or deployed there. A sanitized real Discord trace still needs to show mic admission during playback with `bargeIn: false` and provider interruption enabled, provider-owned interruption without local cancellation, and both-off protection. The in-process lifecycle regressions do not establish acoustic provider behavior. No repository rule requires that proof before PR publication, but ClawSweeper requests it before merge.

## Non-goals

- Changing speech qualification thresholds or VAD behavior.
- Enabling local raw-audio cancellation when `bargeIn` is false.
- Changing non-realtime Discord voice handling.
