prs.title: fix(telegram): first DM message lands in root chat when the client creates the topic separately
prs.body:
Closes #169443

## Deployment status — 2026-11-12

The downstream [Threaded Mode kit for OpenClaw 2026.11.3](https://github.com/aspalagin/openclaw-threaded-mode-hotfix) leaves DM-topic adoption disabled. We disabled the local patch after the November 9 `BOT_TOPIC_WRONG_HOME` regression: newly created private topics could reject bot writes, so adopting a threadless opener could route its reply into an unusable topic. [Telegram Bot API issue #944](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api/issues/944) was closed on November 10; this note does **not** assert that the Telegram defect is still present.

The November 5 evidence below remains historical evidence for the specified head. The downstream 11.3 kit release did not revalidate this upstream PR head against current Telegram behavior; its compatibility checks must not be read as new live validation of this proposal.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Telegram threaded mode (`has_topics_enabled: true`) the user's first DM message is answered in the root chat and the topic the client just created stays empty, when the client sends `forum_topic_created` and the message as two separate updates.

Telegram for Android (observed since 2026-10-09, 12 of 12 attempts, reproducible on demand) creates the topic and then delivers the message **without** `message_thread_id`:

```json
{"message_id": 500, "date": 1760000000, "chat": {"id": 1001, "type": "private"}, "from": {"id": 1001, "is_bot": false},
 "message_thread_id": 500, "is_topic_message": true,
 "forum_topic_created": {"name": "hello", "icon_color": 0, "is_name_implicit": true}}
```

```json
{"message_id": 501, "date": 1760000000, "chat": {"id": 1001, "type": "private"}, "from": {"id": 1001, "is_bot": false},
 "text": "hello"}
```

`resolveTelegramMessageThreadSpec` resolves the second update to `{ scope: "dm" }` without an id, so the turn runs in the root DM session, the reply goes to the main chat, and the user later opens an empty topic and continues without the original message. Clients that deliver the first message inside the topic (with `message_thread_id`) were never affected.

## User Impact

User impact: a new DM conversation started from such a client now runs in the topic the client created. The session key, reply, typing indicator and auto label all target that topic, the same as when the first message arrives inside the topic.

Scope of the adoption is deliberately narrow:

- private chats only; group/forum and channel Direct Messages resolution is unchanged;
- the `forum_topic_created` service message must come from a human user (bot-created topics are ignored);
- the adopted message must come from the same user, have a larger `message_id` than the service message, and arrive within 3 seconds by `date`;
- a message that arrives inside the topic clears the pending adoption (normal clients);
- the decision is made **once per bot account at ingress admission** and persisted with the spooled update, so lane key, authorization, message context, session and delivery all read the same topic fact, before and after a restart;
- a `forum_topic_created` update whose window was already spent never rearms adoption when it is inspected again (drain, retries);
- both per-account maps are bounded (512 entries).

## Why This Change Was Made

The receiving bot account's ingress monitor (`createTelegramIngressMonitor`, one per account in polling and webhook transports) is the only place that knows the account and sees every update exactly once at admission, before the lane key is derived. The adoption state (`pending` by `chat:user`, `consumed` by `chat:createdMessageId`) therefore lives in that monitor's closure (`extensions/telegram/src/dm-topic-adopt.ts`); there is no module-level state shared between accounts, so a topic observed by bot A can never admit a root message sent to bot B (and `requireTopic`/topic allowlists for bot B keep rejecting it exactly as on `main`).

The decision is recorded on the message object (`WeakMap`) and written to the durable spool payload as the optional field `adoptedDmThreadId` (payload version unchanged). `deserialize` and `deriveLaneKey` restore it before lane inspection, so a replay after restart derives the same `telegram:<chat>:topic:<id>` lane as the stored claim and the row is dispatched instead of being rejected as `TelegramIngressPayloadError`. `resolveTelegramMessageThreadSpec` only reads that fact (`getTelegramAdoptedDmThreadId`), so every consumer behind the resolver (session key, authorization, message context, native commands, delivery) sees the topic without any further derivation. `bot/helpers.ts` gains the lookup call only.

## Evidence

- Inbound handler regression (`bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts`, "client-created DM topic adoption through the inbound handler"): the real account ingress monitor admits `forum_topic_created` 500, root message 501 and a later root message 502 from a private chat **without** `chat.is_forum` (so `withResolvedTelegramForumFlag` copies the message before `authorizeInboundMessage`); 501 reaches the model with session key `agent:main:main:thread:42001:500` and its reply is sent with `message_thread_id: 500`, while 502 runs in the root DM session and is sent without a thread. With `direct.<chat>.requireTopic: true`, 501 is admitted into topic 500 and 502 is dropped before any outbound call (the adopted topic feeds the same `requireTopic`/topic-config gate as a native `message_thread_id`). Before this revision the adopted fact lived in a `WeakMap` keyed by the admitted message object and was lost on that copy.
- Redelivery after a failed durable append (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "keeps the adopted topic for a redelivery after every durable append attempt failed"): the account monitor admits `forum_topic_created` 500, then every spool append attempt for root message 501 fails (the transport fails closed and Telegram redelivers); the redelivered 501 is a freshly parsed object with no symbol/WeakMap association, and it is still admitted into lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` with `adoptedDmThreadId: 500`, resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }` and dispatches once, with no failed rows. The decision is recorded per account by `chat:message_id` (bounded map) in addition to the message object. Unit case (`dm-topic-adopt.test.ts`, "adopts a redelivered copy of the decided message after a failed durable append"): the redelivered copy is adopted while the next root message stays root. The helper-level per-account case was removed in favour of the two-account ingress test.
- Service message retirement (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "does not rearm adoption when the service message is redelivered after a native topic message"; unit case "does not adopt when the first message arrives inside the topic"): service 500 → native 501 inside topic 500 clears the pending adoption and marks 500 consumed, so a redelivered service 500 inspected again at admission does not rearm the window and root message 502 within three seconds stays `{ scope: "dm" }`.
- The restart replay regression waits on owned signals (a dispatch-entered promise resolved inside the dispatch callback and the owner's `AbortSignal` abort event) instead of polling, and releases its gate and stops the monitor in `finally`. Helper-level cases duplicated by the ingress and inbound-handler regressions (redelivery after failed append, happy-path adoption and never-adopted root) were removed; the normalization/serialization contract stays.
- Durable row compatibility (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "replays legacy spool rows without adoptedDmThreadId unchanged and restores it from new rows"): a spool row written before this change (no `adoptedDmThreadId`) replays in lane `telegram:1001` and resolves to `{ scope: "dm" }` with no failed rows; a row carrying `adoptedDmThreadId: 500` replays in lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` and resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }`. The payload version is unchanged: the field is optional and old rows are read as before (live: a `claimed` root row and a `pending` topic row written by the npm release `2026.11.1` replayed in their original lanes and answered by this head, see the v2026.11.1 upgrade section; additionally a `claimed` row written by a custom `2026.10.10` build, section 4). An older reader ignores the field; a row that is still pending in an adopted-topic lane when the binary is downgraded does not reconcile with the pre-PR lane derivation and is dead-lettered as `invalid-event` with a reason (fails closed, not re-routed) — see the downgrade note in section 4.
- Normalization and serialization (`thread-spec.test.ts`, "keeps the adopted topic on normalized message copies but not in serialized JSON"): the fact survives `withResolvedTelegramForumFlag` (a spread copy) and is absent from `JSON.stringify` and `structuredClone` output, so durable rows carry it only as explicit payload metadata.
- Account isolation (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "scopes client-created DM topic adoption to the receiving bot account"): bot A admits `forum_topic_created` 500 from user 1001; the same user's root message 501 admitted by bot B within the window stays in lane `telegram:1001` and resolves to `{ scope: "dm" }` (no topic fact reaches bot B's authorization), while bot A's copy of 501 lands in `telegram:1001:topic:500`.
- Restart replay regression (`telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts`, "adopts a client-created DM topic at admission and keeps it through restart replay"): admit 500, admit 501 → claim lane `telegram:1001:topic:500` with payload `adoptedDmThreadId: 500`; abort the owner before dispatch, close the state database (fresh monitor, fresh adoption state, re-parsed update objects) → replay dispatches 501 once in lane `telegram:1001:topic:500`, resolver returns `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }`, no failed rows. With the durable restore removed, this test fails (the replayed row never reaches dispatch), so it demonstrates the failing base and the passing head.
- Idempotency (`dm-topic-adopt.test.ts`, "does not rearm the window when the consumed service message is resolved again"): resolve 500 → adopt 501 → resolve 500 again (fresh object too) → 502 within the window is not adopted.
- Resolver boundary (`thread-spec.test.ts`): adopted root message resolves to `{ id: 500, scope: "dm" }` on repeated resolution; the next root message and a never-adopted message stay `{ scope: "dm" }`. The former duplicated unit cases were removed; unit tests keep only the edge cases (message inside the topic, 3 s window, older/lower `message_id`, bot-created topic, other user, group chat, bounded maps, per-account state).
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/dm-topic-adopt.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/thread-spec.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-drain.test.ts --reporter=dot` → 3 files, 42 passed (after the duplicate removals); `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.native-pipeline.test.ts -t "client-created DM topic adoption"` → 2 passed. `oxfmt` and `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on the touched files clean.
- Local full `pnpm check:changed` was not completed because the development host hit its memory limit; the full verification is the CI run on this PR.
- Provenance / durable transport admission (f7786a16cfe: polling offsets and webhook acknowledgments follow committed spool writes, with shared replay and retry ownership): this change keeps that contract and intentionally adds one admission-time decision. The receiving account's ingress monitor decides once, during admission inspection and before lane derivation, whether a root DM message belongs to the topic its author just created; the fact is stored in the durable row as the optional `adoptedDmThreadId` field and restored before lane inspection and authorization on replay, so acknowledgment still follows the committed append and replay/retry ownership is unchanged. The reason is the client behaviour in #169443: the topic is created by a separate service update and the first message arrives at the root chat without `message_thread_id`, so the fact cannot be derived from the message alone at replay time. Decisions are also retained per account by `chat:message_id`, so a redelivery after a failed append (transport fails closed) reaches the same topic.
- Live behavior: see **Live candidate proof, head `0ca998590e8e`** below — this branch built and run as the shipped Gateway (not a dist patch of an older release): topic session, reply, typing and labeling for the adopted first message; another account with `requireTopic` rejecting the inherited adoption; topic-access revocation before durable replay producing no Telegram I/O; and the state written by `2026.10.10` loaded and drained by this head. Upgrade from the latest stable npm release: see **Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.1 (npm) to this head** below — settings, sessions and two pending ingress rows written by `openclaw@2026.11.1` are migrated with the documented `doctor --fix`, kept, drained and answered in the root chat and in the topic, and a new adoption works on the upgraded state. The Telegram Test Server userbot was not available to the author; the proof is on the production Bot API with the user's own client account as the witness.

- Security boundary (final-effect authorization): the persisted assignment is scoped to the receiving bot account and is only a topic fact for the existing gates. Live: another account with `requireTopic` receiving the same user's root message right after the topic was created at the first account blocks it before any outbound call (section 2); a row persisted with `adoptedDmThreadId` whose topic is disabled while the Gateway is down is blocked at replay by the ordinary topic-config gate, with no `sendMessage`/`sendChatAction` and nothing visible to the user (section 3). Without the persisted assignment the same replayed root message would have fallen back to the root DM session and been answered there.

### Upgrade from latest stable v2026.11.1 (npm) to this head (2026-11-05)

Release side: the official npm package `openclaw@2026.11.1` (`dist-tags.latest`, `https://registry.npmjs.org/openclaw/-/openclaw-2026.11.1.tgz`, integrity `sha512-2pSbt/taBKM/…VXptw==`, `openclaw --version` → `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)`), installed with `npm i openclaw@2026.11.1` (npm 11.19.1, Node 24.22.2) on the same WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 host. Candidate side: this head built from source (`OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (0ca9985)`, `dist/build-info.json` commit `0ca998590e8ec657766553054037cb060debc856`). One profile and one state directory for both binaries (`--profile stand-169444-rel`, fresh state created by the release's own `onboard --non-interactive`), Gateway on loopback, polling transport, the same two bot accounts as above (account `a` = `@openclaw_stand_proof_c_7960_bot`, account `b` = `@openclaw_stand_proof_b_7973_bot`); only one Gateway polled these bots at any time. Witness: the user's own Telegram account over MTProto (Telethon), as in the sections above. Redaction: user id → `<user>`, host/home paths → `<host>`/`<home>`, Gateway token and bot tokens removed.

**Settings, sessions and pending rows written by v2026.11.1**

- Settings (release CLI: `config patch` + `config set`, validated): `channels.telegram` with account `a` and account `b` (`dmPolicy: allowlist` with one user, `groupPolicy: disabled`, `tokenFile`, account `b` with `direct.<user>.requireTopic: true`), `logging` (`level: debug`, `file`, `consoleLevel: info`), `agents.defaults.model` (LM Studio, local), `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault: off`, `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: "0m"`, `tools.profile: minimal`, `gateway.port`/`bind`/`auth.mode`. Snapshot taken with `config get <key> --json` per key.
- Sessions (release Gateway, replies read back by the witness): root DM `p3 rel root one` (`1936315`) → `ack: p3 rel root one` (`1936316`, root, `reply_to: None`) in `agent:stand:main` (`sessionId e4c4c4fe-…`); a DM topic created by the client with the first message **inside** the topic (`1936318` + `1936319`, not an adoption) → `ack: p3 rel topic one` (`1936320`, `reply_to_top_id = 1936318`) in `agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936318` (`sessionId ace51559-…`). `sessions list` (2 sessions), `sessions.describe` and `chat.history` (2 messages each) recorded through the release Gateway.
- Pending ingress rows: the client sent a root message `p3 rel pending root` (`1936332`) and a message inside topic `1936318` (`p3 rel pending topic`, `1936333`) back-to-back at 20:17:22Z. A watcher polling `channel_ingress_events` every 4 ms sent SIGSTOP + SIGKILL to the release Gateway as soon as both rows existed (no reply had been sent; the witness saw no typing and no bot message):

| row | status (written by v2026.11.1) | lane | payload keys | message |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0000000348475071` | `claimed` by the killed release process (`attempts: 0`) | `telegram:<user>` | `[receivedAt, update, updateId, version]` | bot `message_id 45`, `message_thread_id: null` |
| `0000000348475072` | `pending` | `telegram:<user>:topic:1936318` | `[receivedAt, update, updateId, version]` | bot `message_id 46`, `message_thread_id: 1936318` |

Neither row carries `adoptedDmThreadId` (the release does not know the field).

**Upgrade**

1. The candidate started on that state directory refuses to start before any channel work: `OpenClaw agent database … uses schema version 27; stop active agents and run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to schema version 40 before using it. Sessions remain unavailable.` and `agents.defaults: Unrecognized key: "heartbeat"`. Nothing is drained or sent (spool unchanged, witness silent). Both migrations come from `main` since the `2026.11.1` release branch point, not from this PR (its 11 files: Telegram extension sources and tests — `dm-topic-adopt`, ingress spool payload/drain, `bot/helpers.ts`, thread spec — plus one doc paragraph and one test-lines allocation file).
2. `openclaw --profile stand-169444-rel doctor --fix --non-interactive` (candidate binary), exactly as the message says: `Saved pre-migration SQLite backup` for the agent and state databases, `Upgraded agent database schema …: v27 -> v40`, `Retired heartbeat configuration after ordinary automation data was verified`, `Updated config` (backup `openclaw.json.bak`); `config validate` → valid. The spool is not touched by the doctor (`claimed 1, pending 1, completed 3` before and after).
3. Candidate Gateway started on the migrated state: `channels status` → accounts `a` and `b` running/connected; health RPC `ok: true`, `channels.telegram` lifecycle `ready`, no error codes.

| | v2026.11.1 (before) | this head after `doctor --fix` |
|---|---|---|
| `channels.telegram` (both accounts, allowlists, `requireTopic`, token files) | `config get --json`, sha256 `f3e5c6551b81…` | identical (`f3e5c6551b81…`, read by the head's CLI) |
| `logging`, `agents.defaults.model`, `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, `tools.profile`, `gateway.port`/`bind`/`auth.mode`, `agents.list` | snapshot | identical value for every key |
| `agents.defaults.heartbeat.every: "0m"` | present | retired by the doctor's heartbeat migration (`main`, not this PR); the key no longer exists in the head's schema |
| sessions (`sessions list`, `sessions.describe`, `chat.history`) | `agent:stand:main` (`e4c4c4fe-…`), `agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936318` (`ace51559-…`), 2 messages each | same keys and session ids, read by the head (`session-init store-load … session=agent:stand:main` / `…:thread:<user>:1936318`); the replayed turns are appended to the release-written transcripts (`chat.history` 2 → 4 messages in each: the release's exchange followed by the replayed message and its reply) |
| pending row `…071` (root, `claimed` by a dead process) | not answered | taken over from the dead release process and dispatched in `agent:stand:main`; typing `top_msg_id: null`; reply `1936355` `ack: p3 rel pending root` in the **root** chat (`reply_to: None`, 20:46:52Z); row `completed` (20:40:05.370Z, `attempts: 0`) |
| pending row `…072` (topic `1936318`, `pending`) | not answered | dispatched in `agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936318`; typing `top_msg_id: 1936318`; reply `1936356` `ack: p3 rel pending topic` **in topic `1936318`** (`reply_to_top_id = 1936318, forum_topic = True`, 20:52:28Z); row `completed` (20:40:05.427Z, `attempts: 0`) |
| rows without `adoptedDmThreadId` | — | both replayed in the lanes the release derived (`telegram:<user>`, `telegram:<user>:topic:1936318`); `failed` 0, no dead-letter, no `invalid-event` |
| new adoption on the upgraded state | — | topic `1936352` created with an implicit name + root message `1936353` sent 0.000 s later with `reply_to: None` → `adopted root DM message into client-created topic {chatId: <user>, messageId: 48, threadId: 1936352, topicCreatedMessageId: 47, delaySec: 0}`; rows `…073`/`…074` in lane `telegram:<user>:topic:1936352`; session `agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936352`; typing `top_msg_id: 1936352`; reply `1936373` `ack: p3 up adopt root` **in topic `1936352`** (`reply_to_top_id = 1936352, forum_topic = True`, 20:58:06Z); `chat.history` of the new session: 2 messages |
| spool | `completed 3, claimed 1, pending 1` | `completed 7` (3 release rows, the 2 replayed rows, 2 adoption rows), `failed 0` |

Run note (stand model, not the head): the stand answers with a local LM Studio model on a desktop GPU that was busy with another application during this run, so prompt processing ran at ~20 tokens/s. The first candidate start after the doctor (attempt 1) drained both rows the same way (rows `completed`, typing in the root chat and in topic `1936318`, the release session ids reused) but the model call stalled; that Gateway was stopped before any reply was sent (witness: nothing delivered), and steps 2–3 were repeated from a byte copy (`cp -a`) of the state directory taken after the release was killed and before the candidate first touched it. The table above is that second run; the doctor output was the same (`v27 -> v40`, heartbeat retired, spool unchanged). Attempt-1 logs are kept with the rest of the raw material.

Raw material (release and candidate debug logs, console log, both doctor outputs, spool dumps before/after, config before/after, per-key `config get` snapshots, `sessions list`/`sessions.describe`/`chat.history` snapshots, watcher log, user-side JSON dumps, scripts) is kept by the author, redacted as above.

### Live candidate proof, head `0ca998590e8e` (2026-11-05)

Isolated Gateway built from this PR head (`dist/build-info.json`: `2026.11.1`, commit `0ca998590e8ec657766553054037cb060debc856`, `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`) on a clean WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04 host, polling transport, `logging.level: debug`, `autoTopicLabel` left at its default (enabled). Production Bot API (the Telegram Test Server userbot was not available to the author). Two fresh bot accounts in the same Gateway, both with BotFather **Threaded Mode** on (`getMe.has_topics_enabled: true`):

- account `a` (receiving account): `@openclaw_stand_proof_c_7960_bot`, `dmPolicy: allowlist` (one user), `groupPolicy: disabled`;
- account `b`: `@openclaw_stand_proof_b_7973_bot`, same policy plus `direct.<user>.requireTopic: true`.

Client side: the user's own Telegram account over MTProto (Telethon 1.44, layer 227) acting as the client: `messages.createForumTopic` in the DM with the bot, then `messages.sendMessage` to the same chat **without** `top_msg_id`, 0.000 s after the topic — the two-update sequence from #169443 (`forum_topic_created` with `message_thread_id`, then the text with no `message_thread_id`). A control run sends the first message inside the topic. Independent witness: the same user account reads the DM back (bot messages with `reply_to.forum_topic` / `reply_to_top_id`, `UpdateUserTyping` with `top_msg_id`). Redaction: user id → `<user>`, host → `<host>`, home → `<home>`; bot usernames kept. Client-side message ids are the user's (`1936xxx`); the bot sees its own small ids (`message_id` 1, 2, …).

#### 1. Authority chain on the shipped Gateway: topic created → threadless first message

| step | fact |
|---|---|
| client | topic `1936192` "proof topic S1" created 18:49:55Z; message `1936193` sent in the same second with `reply_to: None` (no `top_msg_id`) |
| Gateway, account `a` | service update = bot message 1 with `message_thread_id: 1936192`, `forum_topic_created`; text = bot message 2 with no `message_thread_id`. Debug log: `adopted root DM message into client-created topic {chatId: <user>, messageId: 2, threadId: 1936192, topicCreatedMessageId: 1, delaySec: 0}`. Both spool rows in lane `telegram:<user>:topic:1936192`. Session `agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936192` (`session-init store-load … session=agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936192`), model turn `outcome=completed`, `message processed: … messageId=2 sessionKey=agent:stand:main:thread:<user>:1936192 outcome=completed` |
| witness | typing from the bot with `top_msg_id = 1936192` at +1.2 s, +5.4 s, +9.4 s, +13.2 s, +17.9 s; streamed progress message `1936194` and the final reply `1936195` both carry `reply_to_top_id = 1936192, forum_topic = True`; the root chat received nothing |
| repeat after restart (S1b) | topic `1936201` / message `1936202` → `adopted … messageId: 9, threadId: 1936201`; typing `top_msg_id = 1936201`; reply `1936206` ("ack: …") in the topic |
| labeling | `autoTopicLabel` is on by default and the label step runs for the adopted topic after the reply. Run S1c (topic `1936229`, adopted `messageId: 29`, reply `1936231` in the topic): `auto-topic-label: generated label (len=21)` followed by `auto-topic-label: topic name changed, skipping rename` — the client had given the topic an explicit title, so the existing title-preservation guard kept it. In the runs that created the topic with an implicit name (`title_missing`, as the Android client does: `1936233`, `1936241`; both adopted and answered in the topic) the stand's local utility model (LM Studio Qwen, thinking model) returned no usable label (`conversation label generation failed (utility, primary fallback)`), so the `editForumTopic` rename itself is not shown here; the label call is downstream of the resolver and unchanged by this PR |

#### 2. Another account with `requireTopic` rejects the inherited adoption

| step | fact |
|---|---|
| client | topic `1936196` created in the DM with bot `a` at 18:52:28Z; 0.025 s later a root message `1936197` sent to bot `b` |
| Gateway, account `b` | `Blocked telegram DM <user>: requireTopic=true but no topic present` at 18:52:28.604Z; no `dm-topic-adopt` line for account `b`; its spool row is in lane `telegram:<user>` (no topic) and completes without dispatch; no outbound call |
| witness | 35 s of listening: no typing and no message from bot `b`; the DM with `b` holds only the user's message |

#### 3. Topic access revoked before durable replay → no final Telegram I/O

| step | fact |
|---|---|
| client | topic `1936198` + root message `1936199` at 18:54:50Z |
| freeze | a watcher polled `channel_ingress_events` every 4 ms and sent SIGSTOP + SIGKILL to the Gateway as soon as a pending row carrying `adoptedDmThreadId` appeared: row `0000000348475049`, `status: pending`, lane `telegram:<user>:topic:1936198`, payload keys `[adoptedDmThreadId, receivedAt, update, updateId, version]`, `adoptedDmThreadId: 1936198`, `message_id: 7`, `message_thread_id: null`; the service-message row `…048` was still `claimed` by the killed process. No reply had been sent (readback: only the user's two messages) |
| revoke | Gateway down: `channels.telegram.accounts.a.direct.<user>.topics.1936198.enabled = false` via the config CLI (validated) |
| replay | Gateway restarted on the same state: both rows replayed and completed (18:55:34.789Z / .802Z); log `Blocked telegram topic <user> (unknown) (topic disabled)` twice — the `unknown` is the forum-only `resolvedThreadId` in the log text, the topic config was looked up by the adopted DM thread id (without the persisted assignment the root message would have resolved to the root DM session and been answered there). No `sendMessage` / `sendChatAction` after the restart |
| witness | listener spanning the restart (75 s): no typing, no bot message; the topic still holds only the user's two messages |
| redelivery | Telegram re-sent update `348475049` by polling after the restart (the kill preceded the offset commit); it was deduplicated against the completed row — no second admission, still no I/O |

#### 4. Additional: data-model compatibility with a custom `2026.10.10` build (supplementary; the release upgrade is above)

Base = OpenClaw `2026.10.10` (`cac84a8fe91e`, main + #131347, without this PR), started on a copy of a state directory that build had been using all day (35 sessions), same two bots.

| step | fact |
|---|---|
| base behaviour (the bug) | topic `1936208` + root `1936209` → typing with `top_msg_id: null`, reply `1936210` in the **root** chat (`reply_to: None`), session `agent:stand:main`, lane `telegram:<user>` |
| base control | topic `1936212` + first message inside the topic → typing and reply `1936215` in the topic |
| legacy pending row | root DM `1936216` admitted by the base and left `claimed` by killing it: row `…057`, lane `telegram:<user>`, payload keys `[receivedAt, update, updateId, version]` (no `adoptedDmThreadId`) |
| upgrade | candidate started on a copy of that state: the legacy row replayed in `agent:stand:main`, reply `1936218` delivered to the root chat (19:08:35Z), row completed, no failed rows; 35 sessions listed through the candidate; old completed rows unchanged. Same state, new topic flow: `adopted … messageId: 23, threadId: 1936221`, reply `1936224` in the topic; the new row is written with `adoptedDmThreadId` (seen pending in the next step) |
| upgrade note (not this PR) | the copied state carried duplicate session rows for one key from an earlier unrelated load test on that host; the head reports `SESSION_CANONICAL_KEY_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` on the health RPC while channels, replay, delivery and `sessions list` work; `doctor --fix` did not clear it in this run |
| downgrade (informational) | a pending row written by the candidate (`…061`, `adoptedDmThreadId: 1936225`, lane `telegram:<user>:topic:1936225`) replayed by the `2026.10.10` build (started with `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1`; the config guard refuses an older binary otherwise) is dead-lettered: `spooled update 348475061 on lane telegram:<user>:topic:1936225 failed after 1 attempts (invalid-event): Telegram ingress row 0000000348475061 changed update identity.` — the pre-PR lane derivation yields `telegram:<user>`, the stored topic lane does not reconcile, and the row fails closed with a reason instead of being re-routed; the older build reads the remaining 9 completed rows and 36 sessions normally. So an older reader ignores the field, but an in-flight adopted row does not survive a downgrade |

Raw material (user-side JSON dumps, redacted Gateway debug logs, spool dumps, watcher logs, scripts) is kept by the author; the Gateway log lines above are quoted verbatim apart from the redactions.

prs.title: fix(telegram): defer transcript echo until message admission
prs.body:
Closes #146311

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users running multiple bot accounts in a mention-gated group would see transcript echoes from every bot after sending one voice note, even though only the addressed bot admitted the message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram now uses the shared deferred preflight-audio behavior: transcription remains available before mention detection, but the user-visible transcript echo is held until the message passes the existing command and mention admission gates. Direct messages and admitted group messages retain the configured echo behavior and account/topic routing.

## User Impact

Only the Telegram bot that admits a voice message echoes its transcript. Unaddressed bots can still inspect the transcript for mention detection without leaking a duplicate reply into the group.

## Evidence

- `bot-message-context.body.test.ts`: 40/40 passed, including admitted group, rejected group, DM, and forum-topic routing cases.
- `bot-message-context.group-body.test.ts`: 24/24 passed.
- `media-understanding-runtime.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- Oxfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Portfolio preflight completed with no BLOCK; its two WARNs were the expected pre-push missing tracking branch and seven intentional replaced lines.

prs.title: fix(mcp): report a missing stdio launcher command instead of a generic transport close
prs.body:
Fixes #146268

## What Problem This Solves

A stdio MCP server whose launcher command isn't installed (the common case: a plugin's `mcpServers` entry runs `uvx <package>` and `uv`/`uvx` was never installed on the host) fails with no actionable signal. The spawn fails, the JSON-RPC handshake never happens, and the only thing that surfaces — and only once something actually tries to connect — is a generic `MCP error -32000: Connection closed`. Nothing in that message points at "the command doesn't exist."

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw mcp doctor` already has exactly the right check for this (`commandExists` in `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts`, resolving a stdio server's `command` against `PATH`/`cwd`), but it only runs as a separate, opt-in diagnostic — the actual runtime connection path (`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`'s `loadCatalog`) never checked this before attempting to connect.

This PR:
- Extracts that PATH-resolution check out of `mcp-cli.ts` into a shared `src/agents/mcp-stdio-command-check.ts` module (`stdioCommandExists`), so there's one implementation instead of two.
- Threads the resolved stdio launch config (`command`/`cwd`/`env`) through `resolveMcpTransport`'s return value (a new optional `stdioLaunch` field, only populated for stdio transports — no behavior change for SSE/streamable-HTTP).
- Lets `ensureSessionConnected` run first, exactly as before this PR, on every platform and every launch config. Only if it throws does `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts` check whether the launcher is missing and, if so, replace the generic `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` with `stdio command not found or not executable: <command> — is it installed and on PATH?` (the original error is preserved via `Error.cause` and still included in the formatted diagnostic).

This design deliberately enriches a connection failure after it happens rather than gating one before it happens. `stdioCommandExists` is a best-effort approximation (it can't fully replicate every platform's real launch semantics — Windows PATHEXT/shim/node-entrypoint resolution, symlink traversal, etc.), so it never vetoes an attempt: a false negative can only affect the wording of an error a working server never reaches.

## User Impact

Anyone installing a `uvx`-based (or any stdio) MCP server plugin without the launcher binary installed gets a clear, actionable error in the gateway logs immediately, instead of a generic JSON-RPC error code with no indication of the real cause. Existing working configurations, on every platform, are unaffected — the check never runs unless a connection has already failed.

## Evidence

Real, executed test run (not fabricated) — `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/agents/mcp-stdio-command-check.test.ts` on the exact head of this branch:


prs.title: feat(ui): add optional inline command trail
prs.body:
Closes #197463

## What Problem This Solves

Following a coding task requires commands and their advancing output to remain visible in conversation order.

## User Impact

Choose **View → Inline command trail (this browser)** in the conversation menu for the new, optional inline presentation. Command, read, and search rows show status and expandable details. Command previews show the newest output within **three visual rows**, including wrapped text, without an omission label. Expanded details retain the captured beginning. Grouped presentation remains the default, and completed dashboard turns retain **Worked for…** folding. The preference stays in this browser for this Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stable conversation structure and changing invocation output use separate publications from existing owners. Command rows subscribe narrowly, avoiding unrelated pane and composer work. Native OpenClaw tool progress and opt-in Codex stdout delivery use the existing tool/session-message contracts and bounded in-flight recovery.

Accepted updates, ordering, live disclosure authority, cancellation, terminal retirement, recovery, and shutdown settlement remain enforced. Capture limits and publication cadence are unchanged. Native mobile live-output adoption and messaging-channel presentation remain outside this change.

## Evidence

### Screenshots

The same conversation in an actual OpenClaw deployment, captured at different instants during one command and cropped to the conversation.

**Before — original grouped presentation:**

![Original grouped command presentation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73e2d293-6e57-479f-abd2-20cacdcd8e4d)

**After — new, optional inline presentation:**

![New, optional inline presentation with three visual output rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d66d385-0674-4560-b9ac-cedcf7884d79)

### Performance

Candidate performance qualification used Linux AWS guests with 4 vCPU/8 GiB and 8 vCPU/16 GiB, a real Gateway/native harness, served production UI, and 512 × 4,096-byte output updates at 20-ms cadence per 10.24-second output turn. Each candidate mode ran for one hour per hardware profile, alongside 20 matched warm rounds per profile. The table reports only candidate results; latency cells are p95 / maximum in milliseconds.

| Candidate observation | 4 CPU grouped | 4 CPU inline | 8 CPU grouped | 8 CPU inline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complete key response, ms | 33.5 / 83.9 | 33.4 / 75.5 | 33.4 / 81.5 | 33.4 / 58.2 |
| Scroll onset, ms | 69.5 / 80.9 | 56.0 / 73.4 | 63.2 / 79.5 | 55.9 / 72.5 |
| Live preview, ms | N/A | 86.6 / 126.2 | N/A | 86.4 / 128.1 |
| Active product RSS p95, GiB | 4.398 | 4.371 | 4.362 | 4.325 |
| Renderer CPU, % of one core during fixed work | 14.00% | 14.98% | 11.84% | 13.88% |
| Complete lifecycle CPU, core equivalents | 0.8330 | 0.8623 | 0.7877 | 0.8463 |

RSS sums product processes and can double-count shared pages. Minimum available RAM in the 4-CPU inline run was 2.634 GiB. These bounded runs support the tested workload, not indefinite leak freedom or universal performance. The smaller guest has limited renderer CPU margin; this is not a CPU-reduction claim. Separately, one grouped startup Send event took 104 ms; the table describes sustained interaction. The sustained measurements are retained from feature runtime `e654f9288f4a`; the output/rendering hot path is unchanged by the final startup-loading repair. The sustained measurements also predate the three-row CSS cap and final integration; the cap adds no JavaScript measurement or output state. Current-head asset and functional validation is reported separately below; this is not a fresh sustained-performance run.


### Validation

The repair integrates the exact main used by the failed CI merge, `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`. It keeps the failed-only footer in Chat boot and the general outcome renderer in its existing deferred details owner, and consolidates identical stylesheet declarations. No new state, module, cache, or output scheduling was added.

- **56 focused UI owner cases:** expanded outcomes, standalone failure footers (undefined/zero/nonzero exit code), advancing previews, and captured output. The obsolete omission-label expectation is corrected.
- **9 model-control browser cases:** canonical session facts survive descriptor refresh. The original fixture fails deterministically when that refresh is exercised; the corrected fixture preserves the visible reasoning-slider and route assertions. No runtime or timeout change.
- **5 inline-trail browser scenarios:** three-row wrapping/newest tail, expansion, preference changes, completion/reload folding, recovery/Stop, and reader hold/rejoin all passed in exact-head hosted CI. The earlier local run passed every assertion but hit a Chromium teardown watchdog afterward; the hosted pass is separate evidence, not a claimed repair of that local teardown.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, Stylelint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Net test growth is **5,098 lines**, within the unchanged 400-line allowance plus 4,976 lines of existing feature allocation credit.
- Fresh isolated review of the corrected repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. A separate before/after check through the production hover guard verified identical complete computed styles and geometry across 60 hover/focus, desktop/touch, light/dark and viewport states; diff addition signs remain visible. Retained real Gateway/model, default/grouped behavior, disclosure-authority, output fidelity, lifecycle, and published-browser upgrade proof applies to unchanged contracts. The three-row cap adds no JavaScript geometry measurements or output state.

Reviewed, signed repair: `ea5bf507ef76f41a32c1a6200a9bc069574cd1dc`. Fresh paired production builds against the exact main above pass every asset gate without allowance changes: startup JavaScript is **90,870 normalized gzip bytes across three requests**, and total CSS is **331,553 normalized gzip bytes**, within the unchanged paired limit of 331,560 bytes. Existing total-CSS fixed-ceiling warnings remain visible under the checker’s paired rules. These are asset-size results, not a new runtime latency or CPU measurement.

### CI disposition

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43319887516) completed for `ea5bf507`, tested as merge `9cf6a2c` with main `4efd662`. All three UI unit/browser shards, the performance gate, asset checks, model-control cases, all five inline-trail scenarios, and all five Gateway restart-resume scenarios passed. ClawSweeper's exact-head review found no findings; the native review is validated.

CI remains **red** with five failed jobs. No branch-caused failure was identified:

| Failure | Attribution |
| --- | --- |
| Oversized Codex skill read expectation | Unchanged inherited test expects refusal after upstream changed reads to bounded text with explicit continuation. The 14 relevant owner/test inputs match main and the prior causal proof. |
| Yielded-child restart finish expectation | Unchanged inherited expectation conflicts with the updated requester/paused-child contract. The six relevant owner/test inputs match main and the prior main reproduction. |
| Three Markdown-table sizing assertions | [The exact main-parent job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43319824287/job/131538049277) has the same three failures. A focused exact-main run also reproduced them; all 15 cases passed on the published feature head. |
| OpenClaw ID completion locator | [The exact main-parent job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43319824287/job/131538049183) has the same stale **Done** locator failure after the completion action changed to **Close**. A focused exact-main run reproduced it. |
| Browser shard 6 aggregate timeout | [The exact main-parent job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43319824287/job/131538049185) also exhausted the unchanged 20-minute action limit. Both runs were still advancing without a reported assertion failure. All 11 cases across the three incomplete/unreached suites passed in a focused run of the actual CI merge, with a clean browser exit. This closes scenario coverage; it does not repair the full-shard timeout or establish runtime equivalence between different shard memberships. |

The automated classifier used an older completed main run and labeled browser shards 1/3 new, the node failures unknown, and shard 6 pre-existing by job name only. The completed exact-parent jobs and source/runtime attribution above provide the more specific disposition. No CI retry, timeout increase, exclusion, or allowance change was used.

The earlier Home and Gateway restart-resume failures remain unreproduced; current passing checks do not establish their cause or erase those failures. Sustained-performance and local-teardown limitations remain as described above. **Merging remains pending; auto-merge is disabled.**

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): member roles are opaque names in the protocol
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw ID members can only be `operator` or `viewer`, because the protocol package fixes that list and ranks the two. Owners need roles between those two and roles of their own, which a closed, ordered list in the signed protocol cannot carry.

## User Impact

User impact: none yet. Operator and viewer members, owner devices and nodes behave as before, and the Access page still offers Operator and Viewer. A member whose role name the Gateway does not know is refused access.

OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and its protocol is an unreleased v1 draft, so this changes the draft schema with no version bump. Discovery and the claw loader carry their own copy of the protocol and must update before any claw publishes a role other than `operator` or `viewer`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- A member role is now an opaque name in the protocol: 1 to 64 characters, lowercase ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter. The same validator covers invites, the `add` and `set_role` operations, and membership snapshots.
- Role ranking is removed. Approving an invite must use the invite's exact role; before, an approval could grant a lower role than the invite named.
- The Gateway still gives meaning only to `operator` and `viewer`. Any other role name is refused at WebSocket connect, on Gateway HTTP, on the tunnel API (`/_openclaw-id/v1/*`), and for retained and recovered runs. Stored membership keeps the name, so a later change can define what it allows.
- The Access page and account menu show an unknown role by its name.

This is the first step of customizable member roles. Resolving role names from `gateway.roles.definitions` comes in a follow-up.

## Evidence

- Protocol package: 29 files, 224 tests pass, including new cases for valid and malformed names in all four signed fields and for exact invite-role matching in both directions.
- Gateway: `tunnel-principal`, `tunnel-api`, `remote-signout` (21 tests), `server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts` (20) and `operator-run-recovery.test.ts` (41) pass. New tests cover refusal of an unknown role at connect, HTTP, every tunnel API route and recovery.
- UI and Access page suites for the changed files pass.
- `tsgo` for core, UI and extensions, scoped lint, format and the line ratchets pass.
- An independent review found one P1, that the tunnel API skipped the unknown-role check (a member with an unknown role could call sign-out). The second commit fixes it and adds a regression test over every tunnel API route.

Not run: the full repository suite, a live tunnel or Discovery end-to-end test, and browser screenshots (no visible UI change for existing roles).

prs.title: docs: propose retained protection and native Codex coding lane
prs.body:
Related: #187891, #189827, #189600, #185406, #189112, #190147
Related work and context; inclusion does not imply a hard dependency or endorsement

Related: #189522 — clarifies per-turn Codex instruction replacement scope; relevant to instruction handoff and same-thread continuity, not a storage/protection prerequisite.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw already lets people with different permissions work in one shared Gateway. But an agent's work can be saved or delivered after the session that started it is gone. Before someone reads that result, OpenClaw needs to know where it came from, what protection it originally required, and whether that person is allowed to read it **now**. Shared session access or an old permission must not silently become a grant to read retained content.

A native Codex coding task makes this concrete: work runs on an authorized host, returns findings to a conversation, and may need a revision on the same native thread. The retained-content question can also matter to other background work in a shared Gateway. This proposal builds on existing identity, storage, and permission owners rather than adding a second permission system. It does **not** claim a demonstrated vulnerability in the deployed product.

## First decision requested

**May a separately reviewed, inactive original-identity and retained-policy storage foundation proceed as an implementation PR?** It would keep the original identity and protection requirements with retained results after the live session is deleted. We need storage, security, and compatibility owners to decide whether that is the right first boundary, including:

- How retained original policy survives deletion while every later read still checks current grants.
- Whether an affected protected store should refuse *all* serving, including ordinary content stored alongside protected records, until its consumers are ready; unrelated ordinary stores would remain usable.
- How its storage format can coexist with experimental layouts and existing upgrades. No experimental format number is reserved by this proposal.

This first slice would **not** activate protected origination or serving, change approval wire/SDK formats, or launch the Codex lane. If this is the wrong boundary, please suggest the alternative or route us to the owner who can decide it. [Issue #187891](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187891) remains the end-to-end tracker; merging a design document would not complete the feature.

## User Impact and later decisions

The goal is useful coding results and same-thread revisions without making protected content visible to an unauthorized participant. That workflow is **not implemented or proven end-to-end** by this documentation PR. Parent visibility and consent, protected serving, native execution, and the eventual all-payload approval wire/SDK transition need separate acceptance and proof, including real two-user and recovery workflows. The two synchronous legacy reads in the writer-fence candidate are a separate compatibility question, not the decision on this first foundation.

**Design-review proposal only: no runtime behavior changes, implementation readiness, activation authority, or maintainer acceptance is claimed.** Implementation should proceed through independently useful fixes and safely verifiable prerequisite/dependent changes; final PR decomposition remains subject to maintainer acceptance.

## Detailed contract and evidence limits

The eventual design intentionally breaks legacy content-bearing approval wire/SDK formats for ordinary and protected payloads together. That break belongs to later activation and compatibility decisions, not the proposed first inactive slice. Complete replacement human reads and ordinary remote publication, retirement, restore and rollback qualification must land before activation. Protected remote redistribution is unsupported; authorized human reads do not create publication custody. Retained original protected-lineage policy permits authorized reads after live-session deletion; original execution authority does not survive by implication. Existing-parent visibility changes require consent, with an explicit protected coordinator when in-place promotion is unsafe.

The [November 1 inactive foundation proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187893#issuecomment-6558684429) records a locally qualified original-identity and retained-policy storage boundary. It remains a proposed feature boundary, not an upstream-accepted landing plan. Protected origination and serving remain disabled: protected retained records or scopes cause whole-store serving refusal, including co-resident ordinary content, while unrelated ordinary stores remain usable. This slice removes no approval-wire or public SDK interface. Schema coordination and maintainer acceptance remain unresolved. The [sanitized evidence packet](https://gist.github.com/ekinnee/8e9842b6d80d8c62d57c2446d10d69be) supports only its stated local foundation boundary.

**Current prerequisite decision (November 7):** the separate affected-relation writer-fence work now has a concrete compatibility question for the later native-binding cutover. The [existing compatibility request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187893#issuecomment-6635883406) asks whether its existing synchronous V1 transaction/rollback owner may retain two bounded original-value reads, and which existing execution-owner interface should classify them while new modern main-thread SQL remains rejected. [Inspectable review packet](https://gist.github.com/ekinnee/53bcc4917c05a18431c6a4c817baef93) · [ZIP](https://gist.github.com/ekinnee/53bcc4917c05a18431c6a4c817baef93/archive/3acb7944b7adcd479e32a1a55d6fd5217394725c.zip). The candidate and verifier extension remain frozen and unaccepted; no implementation approval or schema allocation is claimed.

The committed design and November 1 foundation evidence remain dated design/evidence snapshots. This supplement adds the writer-fence compatibility decision; it does not claim a maintainer-approved change to the foundation boundary or landing order. Their experimental format numbers are not upstream reservations. Related #192623 (async bundled binding/approval reads) and #125913 (Codex capacity recovery) are separately owned work, not prerequisites or answers to this V1 compatibility decision.

A separate local integration candidate remains unaccepted. Whole-candidate review and packaged native coding, useful result delivery, and same-thread revision proof remain outstanding; intermediate checks do not establish end-to-end readiness.

## Why This Change Was Made

Early owner feedback can resolve the public protocol, retained-policy, parent UX and migration trade-offs before implementation is presented as ready. The document reuses existing storage/sharing, approval/delivery, startup/restore, plugin/harness, binding and paired-node transport owners; it does not introduce a parallel dispatcher or grant service.

The dated native design and subsequent coding-lane contract select owned direct stdio, superseding the earlier shared-daemon proxy proposal. The later retained-policy contract also supersedes the earlier deny-on-live-session-deletion alternative. This draft preserves those decisions while requesting maintainer assessment; it does not make new upstream acceptance claims.

## Evidence

- **November 7 compatibility supplement:** the [public packet](https://gist.github.com/ekinnee/53bcc4917c05a18431c6a4c817baef93) contains approved source excerpts and sanitized historical receipts for the unaccepted C3 candidate. It is not a complete source release or new runtime proof. The final canonical guard failed with nine semantic diagnostics before producing counts; 141 passing verifier fixtures do not establish production closure. Historical worker/legacy controls retain their stated snapshot/reuse limits. No new tests, verifier work, build or review was run for this evidence publication.
- The PR diff contains one documentation file only: `docs/design/protected-content-native-codex-lane.md`, including dependency order, alternatives, review questions, and a claim/evidence limitations map. No implementation code, raw log, credential, private path or advisory transcript is part of the PR diff.
- Focused oxfmt formatting/check passed; repository MDX checker passed for the one document; staged `git diff --check` passed; public-sensitive-string scan returned no matches.
- Independent document/security-claim review found no actionable P0–P2 finding in its scoped pre-final draft. The lead subsequently corrected retained-policy wording against the later acceptance contract and added dated transport provenance. That review is not claimed to cover those later edits or constitute runtime security certification.
- Prior source-pinned fixture/design reports are summarized only as **reported evidence**. Failed checks and unvalidated corrections remain explicit; no compiler-green, whole-lane, two-user, old-helper, or deployed-runtime proof is claimed. Private reports are not presented as accessible artifacts. Full accessible sanitized exact-head proof remains required for the later implementation PRs.
- This documentation refresh passed focused formatting, one-document MDX and whitespace checks, plus authored PR-context validation. Independent exact document/body review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Canonical autoreview (P0–P2, pre-commit snapshot matching the document) and local ClawSweeper reviewed the change from `b317d9e53035` to `7660a70e5901` with no actionable findings; neither establishes implementation readiness or verifies the linked runtime evidence.
- No full test suite/build/runtime campaign was run for this documentation-only proposal. The [existing hosted ClawSweeper assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187893#issuecomment-6508139872) reviewed `b317d9e53035` and remains prior-head evidence; it requested maintainer direction with no actionable findings. No current-head review or CI acceptance is claimed. This PR remains a design proposal for maintainer feedback.

Review requested on existing owner seams, the all-payload compatibility break, retained policy after deletion, parent consent/coordinator behavior, and completeness of first-party consumer/restore/rollback acceptance requirements.

prs.title: feat(cron): make automation inspect links configurable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves Implements #150029 by adding the strict config option `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with values `always`, `errors`, and `never`. The default is `always`, preserving existing behavior. This supersedes #175817, which was closed unmerged. The approach is rebased onto current `main` and additionally proves that the policy applies to isolated agent-run announcements through the shared delivery append path. ## Behavior - `always`: include Control UI `Inspect` links on successful completion announcements and failure alerts (backward-compatible default). - `errors`: include links only on failure alerts. - `never`: omit links from both successful completion announcements and failure alerts. - Applies to isolated/direct cron completion delivery, successful completion announcements, failure alerts, and isolated agent-run announcements that share `sendCronAnnouncePayloadStrict`. - Webhook delivery is unchanged; the setting only governs chat announcement links. ## Changes - Add `src/cron/inspect-links.ts` with the policy resolver and `shouldIncludeCronInspectLink`. - Add the strict `cron.announce.inspectLinks` schema under `cron`. - Apply the policy at the shared delivery append path in `src/cron/delivery.ts`, with an explicit completion/error kind for failure alerts. - Gate link generation in `server-cron-completion.ts`, `server-cron-notifications.ts`, and isolated agent delivery dispatch. - Document the option in `docs/gateway/config-automation.md` and `docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md`. - Refresh generated config baseline hashes/counts. - Add `config/test-lines-allocations/194794-cron-inspect-links.txt` (126 lines, exact measured net test LF growth) for the test-lines ratchet. ## Evidence Focused tests: ```text pnpm vitest run src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/cron/delivery.failure-notify.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.delivery-awareness.test.ts src/gateway/server-cron-completion.test.ts Test Files 4 passed (4) Tests 59 passed (59) ``` Schema / generated baseline: ```text pnpm check:base-config-schema [base-config-schema] ok pnpm config:docs:check OK docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256 and docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json ``` Type checks: ```text pnpm tsgo:core # passed node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.services-cron.json ... node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json ... # passed ``` Formatting / whitespace: ```text oxfmt --check All matched files use the correct format. git diff --check # passed ``` ## Review notes - Branch is one commit on top of base `56eb6f3fe2e6b3056727094d22add3c02322215d`; current head `67123e2245a348373f2d3a01df041fc3e739a82c`. Only generated baseline outputs changed during this rebase. - No merge is requested here; this PR is ready for maintainer review. ## Shipped-entry-point proof: 2026-11-08 Sanitized extract. Originals remain local. Contains only synthetic fixture data and `control.example` URLs. Placeholders replace credentials, ports, identifiers and paths. ### Scope Proves on the real shipped CLI entry point (`openclaw.mjs gateway run`) that the cron scheduler appends the Control UI run-inspection link according to `cron.announce.inspectLinks` with default `always`: | Mode | Completion | Failure alert | | --- | --- | --- | | `always` (explicit) | link present | link present | | `errors` | link absent | link present | | `never` | link absent | link absent | | omitted (default) | link present | link present | Transport is a **local simulated Bot API over loopback** implemented for this proof. It is **not** real Telegram, not Telegram's network, and not a real bot account. prs.title: fix(cron): keep condition checks running when all run slots are busy
prs.body:
Related: #196859

Builds on #197099, which is on main.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: conditional automations stop being checked while eight long automation runs are active.

A condition check takes one of the scheduler's eight run slots before it starts. When eight long runs hold those slots (work loops, long agent turns, manually started jobs), no check can start until one of them ends, so a watcher that should look every few minutes goes unchecked for as long as the long work lasts.

## User Impact

- Scheduled condition checks keep running, three at a time, however many long runs are active. A check is short and uses no model; run slots are for the work a fired condition starts.
- When a condition fires and all eight run slots are busy, the run waits for the next free slot and then runs its payload on the result of that one check. The condition is not evaluated a second time. The automation shows as running while it waits, and the wait does not count against the run's time budget.
- Freed run slots go to waiting payloads and queued runs in due-time order. A run due before the condition's check starts first; a fired condition starts before runs due after its check.
- A cron config change keeps a fired condition waiting: the scheduler that takes over hands it the next free slot, as runs already executing keep going across the change (#197606). A Gateway stop or restart ends the wait without running the payload.
- Unchanged: the limits themselves (three checks, eight runs). A check started by a manual or stream run, and the check of a job with a script payload, takes a run slot first.

## Why This Change Was Made

The run queue counted a run against the eight run slots from activation, including the opening phase in which it only evaluates its condition. A timed check counts against the three-check limit only, and the run counts against the eight once its condition fires.

A fired timed condition then holds neither kind of capacity. The queue drain, which already hands out run slots in due order, hands the next free slot to it or to an older queued run, so the wait is ordered with queued runs instead of jumping ahead of them. The run asks the queue again each time it moves; a failed request for the slot is logged and asked again the same way. Keeping the first result, instead of checking again when a slot frees, preserves the existing rule that an evaluated condition consumes its occurrence: a condition script may act, so it must not run twice for one occurrence.

After the wait the run checks its active hours again, and it starts no payload while scheduling is paused, while the Gateway is draining for a restart, or after the service stops.

A cron config change hands scheduling to a new scheduler and retires the old one without aborting its runs. The wait ends only when the run is aborted or its scheduler stops, not when it hands over; a stop wakes waiting runs so they end at once. Waiting runs wake whenever any scheduler on the same store hands out slots, and while a handed-over scheduler still has runs waiting, a freed slot also makes the live scheduler go through the queue, since the handed-over one no longer does.

Script payloads are excluded because their time budget cannot pause during the wait; a script-payload watcher that waited longer than its budget would fail with a timeout.

Accepted edges: a Gateway restart during the wait interrupts the run like any run in flight, and the condition is evaluated again afterwards. During the wait the run keeps the job definition it started with, as any active run does. A condition that fires after the new scheduler has loaded its jobs, during a cron config change, may get its slot at that scheduler's next tick instead of the next freed slot.

## Evidence

**Live Gateway with eight long jobs holding every run slot.** Isolated Gateways in a macOS VM, no model, no channels. Three quiet watchers and one watcher whose condition always fires, all on a one-minute schedule; eight scheduled command jobs of 240 seconds each start at +70 s and end at +310 s. Both builds ran side by side.

| Build | Quiet watchers checked at | Longest time without a check | Firing watcher: checks at | Its payload ran at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #197099 head `92e0afa` | 1, 60, 311, 360 s | 251 s | 2, 62, 312, 372 s | 3, 63, 313, 373 s |
| This branch at `d0b24c0` | 1, 60, 120, 180, 240, 300, 360 s | 60 s | 2, 62, 122, 361 s | 3, 63, 310, 363 s |

The condition that fired at 122 s waited for a run slot and its payload started at 310 s, when the long jobs ended, without another check in between. This live run used commit `d0b24c0`, which reserved slots for waiting conditions ahead of queued runs; it has not been repeated on head `2c1c192`, where the drain hands out slots in due order. No queued run was due during that wait, so the table does not exercise the ordering.

**Tests** (targeted, not the full suite), on head `e783d56`: 223 passed in 13 cron and Gateway cron test files, none skipped. They include:

- a scheduler test in which eight payloads hold every run slot: two conditions are checked anyway, the one that fires waits holding neither a slot nor a check, and when one payload ends its payload runs with the condition evaluated once. It fails when checks take a run slot (`expected [] to deeply equal ['quiet', 'fires']`); it runs in about 0.15 s;
- queue rows: three checks start with every run slot taken, a fired condition frees its check for the next waiting condition, and it takes the next slot that opens;
- queue rows for the order: with every slot taken, a run due before a fired condition gets the first freed slot, the condition the second, and a run due after it the third. It fails when waiting conditions reserve slots ahead of queued runs (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'older' ]`);
- a scheduler test with a fired condition waiting behind eight payloads, in two cases. After a cron config change hands over to a new scheduler and a payload ends, the waiting payload runs; without the reload handling it fails (`expected false to be true`: the payload never runs). After a stop the wait ends and the payload never runs.

Formatting, lint, both typechecks (core and cron tests), the test-line budget and `git diff --check` pass.

Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/196859-checks-off-run-slots.txt` records 161 lines, the exact net growth. The regression needs the real scheduler, the queue and eight blocked runs together, which no existing smaller test exercises.

**VM proof at `e783d56`:**

- A live agent-turn payload using Haiku 4.5 through OpenRouter: one condition check while all eight run slots were occupied, model execution after capacity returned, and one tool effect with the original receipt finishing successfully.

- A live cron config reload while a fired condition waited: the same receipt survived handover and its payload ran once after capacity returned.

- A Gateway restart during the wait: the original run was interrupted, the condition was rechecked after recovery, and its payload ran once. The source-bound queued continuation also resumed.

See the recorded proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197340#issuecomment-6836478279

**Not tested:**

- A failed request for the slot followed by a retry (no test injects that failure).
- The active-hours check after the wait, and the hold while scheduling is paused or the Gateway drains.
- Several Gateway processes sharing one store.
