prs.body:
## Merge Brief

- **Problem:** a Discord realtime consult can yield for delegated work, but the eventual child final is only written to the text/session lane and never reaches the requesting voice turn.
- **Why now:** this causes the live voice agent to report failure or uncertainty even when the delegated worker completed successfully.
- **Value:** delegated research results return to the active Discord voice conversation that requested them.
- **Smallest complete fix:** register a trusted requester-final sink for agent-proxy consults, preserve overlapping yielded turns, and queue valid late finals through Discord's existing exact-speech path.
- **Scope:** core requester-final attachment bookkeeping, trusted plugin-runtime plumbing, and Discord realtime delivery.
- **Risk:** late or stale delivery; mitigated by exact agent/session/run matching, provider-epoch checks, lifecycle cleanup, and untrusted-ingress stripping.
- **Proof:** focused lifecycle and serial-continuation regressions pass, both new compaction cases pass, and final `pnpm check:changed` exits 0 on head `0b95d74b9dfe8a03a051874506e9805588c90546`. The reviewer-reported failure is reproduced against the prior PR head.
- **Non-goals:** no delegation redesign, restart persistence, new user configuration, or cross-channel behavior change.
- **Owner decision requested:** this adds an optional field to the PluginRuntime command parameter type, exported through the Plugin SDK, and permits overlapping yielded attachments. Please confirm that shared contract direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord realtime voice routes forced consults through the agent-proxy ingress. If that agent turn yields while delegated work continues, the later child final is delivered to the session/text lane but has no registered path back to the requesting realtime voice session. The voice agent can therefore continue without the answer even though the delegated work succeeded.

Browser Talk already attaches requester finals for this lifecycle. This change applies the same ownership model to the trusted Discord realtime consult path. The callback is stripped from untrusted command ingress, but the trusted PluginRuntime parameter type is exported through the Plugin SDK.

## What Changed

- add a host-owned `requesterFinal` sink to trusted agent command options and strip it from public ingress
- register and clean up requester-final attachments around trusted agent-proxy command execution
- bind registration to the session accepted after preflight compaction and carry it through later committed rotations
- allow multiple overlapping yielded requester turns to coexist instead of replacing one another
- revoke every matching pending attachment when a session ends
- send a valid delayed final through Discord's existing exact-speech queue only while the same realtime provider epoch remains active

## Scope Boundaries

- no change to child-agent execution or yield semantics
- no persistence across restart
- no new user configuration; the optional trusted PluginRuntime parameter type is SDK-visible
- no delivery to a replaced or inactive realtime provider session

## Evidence

- focused lifecycle suite: **48/48 passed**
  - delayed delegated final returns to the active Discord realtime requester
  - overlapping yielded requester turns deliver independently
  - session revocation removes all overlapping attachments
  - forged public-ingress requester sinks are stripped
- serial requester-wake E2E selection: **3/3 passed**, including delegated-final transfer across a successor requester turn
- exact-head `pnpm check:changed`: passed
- core, core-test, extension, and extension-test typechecks: passed
- format, lint, deprecated-API, schema, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guards: passed
- exact-diff autoreview: no actionable P0/P1 findings

The reviewer-reported compaction P2 is reproduced on the prior PR head `7699d8cade7700ff2cae0e55ab51ee2f505a7c71`: the new compact-then-yield regression exits 1 because the delegated-final callback is called zero times after a successor session is accepted. On the repaired branch, that regression exits 0. A second regression covers in-run committed compaction. These are in-process lifecycle tests, not live voice proof.

After fixing an unused destructured variable caught by the first local changed-scope run, the final full `pnpm check:changed` rerun exits 0. The two new compaction tests pass together (2/2) on the published head.

Live acoustic Discord proof is not included: the exact branch has not been connected to a real Discord voice session. The repository has QA voice join/authorization scenarios, but this contributor environment cannot reach its leased-bot broker: `qa discord --doctor` stopped before readiness because no authenticated Convex launcher or broker environment pair was available. Those scenarios also do not by themselves exercise an acoustic delegated final. The contributor's voice bot is attached to a production Gateway and was not replaced or restarted for this PR. A sanitized real consult-yield → child-completion → spoken-once trace remains proof debt. Deterministic lifecycle tests are not presented as a substitute.

The first hosted run exposed a serial continuation regression: transfer lookup accidentally required the successor turn ID before replacing the prior turn ID. The lookup now selects the existing attachment by batch/session identity first; the exact failed E2E and the original 48 focused tests pass on the updated head.

prs.title: fix(agents): private CLI completions lose delivery under restrictive profiles
prs.body:
Related: #121661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a private subagent result can fail to reach the user when the requester uses a restrictive tool profile such as `coding`, or a CLI backend that does not retain the full requester tool surface.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified private completion can relay its result to the requesting conversation through `message`, while its final answer stays private. Explicit tool denies, frozen policies, channel action gates, and grant revocation remain authoritative.

An additional completion messaging grant is restricted to sends in the original channel, account, conversation, and thread, and cannot become general messaging authority for spawned children or cron jobs. Existing requester permissions are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already restores the normal Claude CLI requester tool surface. The remaining repair uses the explicit `privateCompletion` flag, carries source restriction independently of automatic final-reply delivery, and keeps the admitted completion allowance through the actual Gateway tool projection. The same policy merge helper preserves explicit denies and frozen allowlists at both stages.

The earlier destination-scope rationale in this PR was incorrect. This revision uses the existing source-reply guard for the additional grant. It also follows the current media contract: #176594 permits source-conversation photos and attachments through normal media validation; this PR does not restore the obsolete text-only restriction.

Integrated main at `650091daacdc10aa374e82a6327e8beffe136072` to resolve the stale branch conflicts and preserve current runtime selection and requester-tool retention.

## Evidence

At `bed203a26ff9c7aac301f0bff632b97d23895318` (tree `30b8d9d69f3d1a9983b45bc4f12f445b877763dc`):

- Production typecheck passed (`tsconfig.core.json`).
- Focused typecheck of all four changed test entrypoints, extending the repository root-test configuration, passed. It caught and fixed the current-main MCP startup API change.
- Type-aware lint passed for changed production files, tests/support, and the CI inventory; formatting, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The test-line ratchet still reports **51 inherited lines over budget**. At the integrated base the measured total is 6,551,687 and the effective ceiling is 6,551,636. This change adds exactly 663 test/support lines and a separate 663-line allocation, preserving that pre-existing difference. No shared baseline increase is included.

The complete Gateway → private parent completion → CLI runner → minted MCP grant → message tool → Telegram transport fixture passed **5/5** in [CI job 128116367053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116367053). Only model decisions and external Bot API responses are synthetic. CI checked merge `328504c21532c5402858ade03a23c749cf1aa84e`, combining this head with main `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc`.

| Scenario | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary private completion | Exactly one send containing the child result |
| Coding profile | Exactly one allowed send; other chat/thread and non-send probes rejected |
| Explicit operator deny | No completion message tool or child-result send |
| Disabled Telegram send action | Tool error and zero child-result sends |
| Revoked grant | HTTP 401 and zero child-result sends |

The five reported case durations total 122.7 seconds. This expensive composition stays in the release-only tier except for changed-file CI because admission-only tests miss authority lost between projection and dispatch.

The [CLI attempt suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366616), including the new private/coding/other-CLI cases, and [MCP grant-context suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366918) also passed. CI lint and all five core test-type stripes passed.

Full CI is red on an unrelated current-main defect: [production type checking](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116569548) and some asset-building jobs cannot resolve `extensions/deep-research/browser/client.js`. The browser directory has identical filenames and blob SHAs in main `9651d634` and the tested merge; both lack that module. This PR does not change those files.

The [CI baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116365654) also confirms the same inherited test-line debt on main `9651d634`: total 6,552,688, ceiling 6,552,637, over by 51, PR net delta +663. The separate allocation covers exactly the PR's +663; all other ratchets passed.

Local runtime attempts did not start tests: the worker compiler exceeded a 3 GiB cgroup limit, including a retry with a smaller Node heap; a narrow unit selection needed the same compiler and was stopped. The CI run supplies current-head GREEN proof. A fresh full-flow RED control, a real Gemini process, and Telegram Test Server were not run; the older-head live trace is not treated as evidence for this implementation.
Independent Codex source review covered the production and regression changes against `650091daacdc`: no actionable findings. This was an independent source review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper execution. The existing private-delivery owner cases cover suppression of nonempty private final text; the new integration fixture itself returns `NO_REPLY`.

Simplification retained the existing runtime-selection and policy owners and removed unused photo/document assertions. Against the integrated base: production +38 net lines, regression tests/support +663. prs.title: feat(ui): customize agent welcome descriptions and conversation starters
prs.body:
Related: #196643 (Template description preservation is tracked separately; this PR does not fix that publishing issue).

## What Problem This Solves

Purpose-built agents and agents added from Templates show generic new-chat suggestions instead of explaining their purpose and offering relevant first prompts.

## User Impact

Users can see what the selected agent does and start a relevant conversation with one click. Authors can optionally reuse `description` and define `conversationStarters` in regular agent configuration or under `agent` in `CLAW.md`. Unset fields keep existing defaults; no greeting or automatic message is introduced. No migration is required.

Example template configuration in `CLAW.md`:

```yaml
agent:
  id: project-briefing
  description: Follows your repositories and briefs you on meaningful changes, proposals, and decisions.
  conversationStarters:
    - Set up a repository
    - Brief me on recent changes
    - Show my tracked projects
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the two optional fields through the existing config, Template Add, agent-list response, and shared welcome renderer. Template settings remain in `CLAW.md`; retired profile files are not revived. Custom starters remain visible beside recents and on phones, while incognito does not expose recent chats. Terminal targets retain their own guidance, and model setup still takes precedence.

The change adds no framework, owner, or greeting concept. Production delta is +61/−26 lines; the growth is the optional metadata path and presentation. Existing defaults, permission-aware suggestions, and recent-session lifecycle remain covered.

## Evidence

### Review follow-up (November 12)

The four original review findings are addressed:

- The config parser test asserts the parsed structure without dereferencing optional data or an unchecked record key.
- The canonical generator refreshed the config hash and counts for the one new optional setting (two additional core schema paths); no generated artifact was hand-edited. A generated-hash conflict with current main was resolved by regenerating again.

- Description copy now uses inherited typography and the existing muted style. Against refreshed base `0b04511ee505`, total CSS is **1,704,720 → 1,704,779 bytes (+59 raw bytes)** and **331,496 → 331,507 bytes (+11 gzip bytes)**, within the existing 64-byte raw-CSS variance allowance. No CSS budget was raised. The already-selected agent supplies the renderer directly; no second roster lookup or memo is needed.

Current-base validation: all `pnpm tsgo:test:src` shards, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, 34 config tests, 15 Template schema tests, 10 welcome/draft tests, config docs generation/check, the exact-base test-line ratchet, and the five focused production-built browser E2E scenarios pass. The final direct-metadata handoff also passes the custom-welcome and terminal-retargeting browser scenarios. Focused config test time was under one second; UI component test time was under three seconds per file and browser cases under two seconds each (the production UI build is shared). **Remaining performance gate:** newer main already exceeds the New Session JS cap: base **806,389 B gzip** versus the **805,886 B** cap. This candidate is **806,576 B (+187 B gzip)**, above the unchanged 64-byte variance allowance. The full performance check is therefore **not green**. No JS budget increase or unrelated paydown is included; accepting the small feature cost requires an explicit budget decision. Startup JS is unchanged.

- Reproduced missing descriptions and custom starters on the original welcome implementation; the UI regression fails on the base and passes with the change.
- Focused config, Template Add, schema, protocol, agent-list, and agent-resolver tests pass.

- Production-built Control UI browser E2E passes for desktop/phone/narrow-phone custom prompts, incognito, default suggestions, guest prompts, existing mobile composer behavior, and retargeting from an agent to a native terminal.

prs.title: feat(identity): accept co-author credit from trusted-proxy headers
prs.body:
Related: #196845

## What Problem This Solves

A shared OpenClaw Gateway behind Keycloak identifies separate users, but ordinary Keycloak profile claims do not establish the verified GitHub identity needed by existing automatic commit credit. Publication credentials serve a separate purpose.

## User Impact

An administrator can map authenticated proxy headers to a co-author name and email, with an optional email-verification header. HTTP and WebSocket profile admission import that pair into protected profile metadata. Profile shows the pair read-only and requires explicit consent before publishing the email in commit history.

This proposal is **proxy-only**. There are no editable co-author name/email fields, manual identity preferences, custom overrides, or custom-before-default precedence. Existing GitHub-derived credit remains the fallback. These claims do not link a GitHub account or change the authenticated principal, permissions, or publication credentials. Independently verified, host-selected GitHub identities remain available for mentions; proxy claims never create GitHub mentions. Updating alone does not reset existing Cloudflare/Tailscale GitHub credit when the new organization mapping is not enabled.

The related OIDC Profile fix prevents issuer-qualified sign-in subjects from appearing as default display names or linked email addresses, including after name/avatar saves. The underlying authentication aliases, binding IDs, profile IDs and role inputs remain intact. A deliberately chosen display name with the same HTTP(S)-URL-plus-subject shape is also hidden, without deleting its stored value; it can be replaced with a human-readable name. No database schema migration is introduced.

The implemented attribution layout shows the selected name/email inline beside the consent control, removes the separate Credit source row and the paragraph below the pair, and explains that Linked emails serve sign-in/profile linking rather than determining commit credit. Organization details use existing protected metadata. Verified public-GitHub credit uses a read-only self-profile projection derived from the verified account ID/login, sharing the actual trailer's noreply formatter. Enterprise commit addresses remain excluded from profile responses. Consent defaults and publication selection are unchanged.

### Deployment compatibility

For existing Cloudflare Access and GitHub-backed Tailscale team Gateways, this remains additive when configuration is unchanged: updating alone does not require relinking or re-enabling existing Git co-author credit. Enabling the new organization mapping intentionally selects a new address source and requires disclosure consent. [Current deployment-scope report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196867#issuecomment-6827282472).

The feature is configuration-gated, not exclusively multiplayer-gated. A single-person trusted-proxy deployment may opt in, and shared Profile UI/API and OIDC presentation improvements can affect single-user profiles too. Ordinary token/password owner installations gain no new personal co-author identity or authentication permissions. We do not claim zero changes outside multiplayer mode or a newly performed live Cloudflare/Tailscale upgrade test.

## Why This Change Was Made

Our Keycloak proxy maps authenticated `name`, `email`, and `email_verified` claims to overwritten upstream headers while preserving the issuer-qualified subject. OpenClaw accepts them only after successful trusted-proxy authentication. Missing/invalid configured claims clear imported details.

Imported details are bound to their principal/credit-header mapping. A replacement mapping withholds previously imported details and requires renewed consent after refresh. Enabling credit atomically checks the organization details observed in Profile, including their absence. Inactive stored metadata does not block GitHub-fallback consent or silently revive later. Updates under an unchanged mapping retain the existing profile-wide preference.

The existing preference, profile, and attribution owners preserve merge opt-outs, participant/delegated attribution, incognito exclusions, publisher separation, and publication-time checks. One protected organization-metadata slot remains outside the 128 user-preference allowance.

The OIDC presentation repair addresses the misleading identity fields observed during live validation of this same Keycloak flow. Presentation normalization stays in the existing server profile owner; the shared browser display-name helper remains unchanged. Canonical authentication data is not filtered. The attribution layout reuses the existing Profile and settings components, with no new module, stylesheet, persistent state or authentication path.

## Review Repairs

- Bind stale-view consent to the observed organization pair using atomic preference preconditions, and bind imported metadata/consent to the current proxy mapping.
- Reconcile proxy changes in already-open Profile pages, including notifications received during a pending save.
- Preserve independently verified public and Enterprise GitHub mentions/account IDs when organization details supply the trailer address.
- Keep public-email context in the organization-credit control's description, with detailed explanation in the existing help popover.
- Repair runtime-policy, worker, typed-event and callback fixtures without weakening production guards or assertions.
- Keep opaque OIDC subjects out of default names and Linked emails across catalog reads, presence projections and mutation responses. Hide the empty Linked emails row.
- Preserve the original 1,003-line, review-repair 464-line and OIDC/Enterprise 63-line regression allocations. The layout/API/browser-fixture regressions have a separate 107-line allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Current integration: `0164d66f9c4d3c17c3d42f7fa8b8b1944842de56`

Rebased onto canonical main b10c9e1c00cb801841dfafc131d7105a44dfb2a0 to resolve the generated config-baseline conflict. The owning config-documentation generator regenerated the conflicting hash artifact and its canonical check passed; no hash was hand-computed or edited. Range-diff preserves all four contributor patches and the cleanup patch unchanged. The only feature-patch difference is the generated baseline hashes reflecting current main. Contributor authorship/sign-offs and Sally’s credit are preserved. Cleanup remains separate as [0164d66f9c4d](https://github.com/russellb/openclaw/commit/0164d66f9c4d3c17c3d42f7fa8b8b1944842de56), following feature-repair commit 4870fb50eaef8d0.

**Rebased-head verification:** 84 focused tests passed across eight files (attribution 11, documentation 10, import/admission 18, canonical profiles 13, Profile UI 32; 75.94 s wrapper wall time). Canonical config-documentation/protocol checks, UI typecheck and whitespace checks passed. The source checkout is clean. GitHub reported the new head mergeable after the exact-lease push; CI and security approval remain separate gates, not an all-green claim.

#### Earlier cleanup/main-integration checkpoint: b89c163bb68b

The five approved cleanups are published in a separate commit, [8ef6995e9398](https://github.com/russellb/openclaw/commit/8ef6995e939809b6e53c9bb0f3adf047e5933ca2). It removes 11 production lines and 102 test lines across seven paths: temporary config-artifact emission is removed and the four documentation-key checks share the existing renderer; consent becomes local to the Profile identity read; protected object/null denial uses the canonical preference test; quota/admission cases retain 128 saved preferences, both transports, cross-transport refresh and consent preservation; and both GitHub-backed/organization-only UI cases retain the stronger consent assertions. Main at 0001c18108e9f13426bbc9eaedd656e4bd86cef6 is included by merge commit b89c163bb68b094ae9d316b61bfc37e9091654fd, without rewriting the existing contributor or feature commits. There were no overlapping changed paths or merge conflicts; the exact lockfile remained unchanged. The cleanup commit is intentionally not squashed.

Integrated-head verification: **59 focused tests passed across six files** (documentation 10, canonical profiles 13, admission 4, Profile UI 32; 70.96 s wrapper wall time). UI types, targeted lint, formatting/whitespace, canonical gateway:validators:check and config:docs:check passed; the generator checks changed no committed files. Fresh independent review found no actionable cleanup issue. These checks preserve the distinct contracts rather than deleting failed behavior tests. Broad new-head CI remains separate; importing main does not claim the earlier CI failures are fixed.

The PR now changes 62 paths versus the integrated main, down from 63 before cleanup. The published UI copy/layout is unchanged by cleanup; the general raw-Git prompt issue remains deferred to #197860.

The preceding 7fb8a615 revision changed only the Git co-author help wording from 7e57878990ef, retaining the upstream sentence structure while including organization-provided details. Keyless i18n, formatting and both public/Enterprise help browser scenarios passed again; the UI bundle built successfully. The layout/API source and earlier focused proof are otherwise unchanged. The separate no-credit prompt repair was considered but is not included, at Sally’s request to keep this PR focused.

The approved attribution layout is now implemented, not just a design preview. Independent source review found one stale assertion for the removed row; it was repaired to check the disabled switch, configuration guidance and absence of an inline identity. No additional correctness, privacy, Solid-reactivity or mutation-retention finding was reported. The browser fixture was also brought into line with the existing organization preference read and atomic consent precondition, and its public/Enterprise scenarios then passed.

After explicit task-scoped authorization, dependencies were installed offline from the exact frozen lockfile in the independently owned task checkout, without lifecycle scripts or changes to shared installs/live Gateway state. Earlier focused proof on 7e57878990ef, before the cleanup and integration checks above:

- `users.test.ts`: 45 passed; 45.73 s Vitest duration, 49.24 s tool wall time. This includes compiled-result validation for public-GitHub details and Enterprise-address exclusion.

Refreshed implemented-layout/OIDC screenshots and live results for 7e57878990ef, before the help-copy-only revision above, are recorded in the [existing maintainer evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196867#issuecomment-6827494086), replacing the earlier run. [Refreshed evidence and inspected synthetic-identity screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196867#issuecomment-6827494086) now cover `7e57878990ef52f77a5314cbd36eff81aa9b2ade`, replacing the prior-head run. The failure did not require mid-session revocation.

The original docs/ratchet failures were PR-caused stale generated metadata, not upstream noise. Four core documentation entries change 2,647 to 2,651. [Owning integration job 131196831664](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43222121225/job/131196831664) emitted the exact canonical hash/count bytes used in the committed files; they were not manually calculated. prs.title: fix(test): isolate built-source worker cleanup fixture
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a flaky built-source worker-cleanup assertion in main CI when another invocation reuses the disposed generation’s local cache directory.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. The CI fixture now observes only its own worker generation; runtime cache reuse, cleanup assertions and test deadlines are unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The built-source fixture removed CI settings and unintentionally enabled the reusable local worker cache. It now sets `CI=1` and clears inherited `OPENCLAW_VITEST_WORKER_CACHE` for that route, so the generation has a unique invocation directory. Existing compiler, IPC, shared-borrower and disposal assertions remain intact; production cache behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

Main run 43300241896 (`e8ff306f74133486c302f9358296fb43ecb52cd3`), job 131469978137, failed `built-source runner owns worker preparation through ready`: the disposed generation path still existed at the cleanup assertion. Proof used fresh-main base `0468e1d3cfa0f0dc8ee607a7d8068cda38aa78b2` on AWS Crabbox:

- A controlled successor using the real `createVitestWorkerRun` reproduced the exact assertion on the base: original and successor both used `run-cache-0`, although the original manifest was already removed. With the fix, the original used a unique `run-*` directory and the successor used `run-cache-0`; all original assertions passed. Probe instrumentation is not committed.
- Uninstrumented batch and cache-lifecycle files: 57/57 passed. Scoped typecheck, type-aware oxlint, oxfmt and diff checks passed. Independent local autoreview found no P0–P2 findings.
- The unchanged six-file shard replay passed 307/307. This did not reproduce the original concurrent CI failure, and the competing CI process identity was not captured; the controlled interleaving establishes the fixture-isolation error, not a spontaneous hosted recurrence.
- No retries, skips, weaker assertions, deadline increases or baseline changes. The AWS lease is released with cleanup complete. Exact-head PR CI and natural scheduled-main qualification remain pending.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

## Worked on by

- @obviyus
- @steipete

prs.title: fix: PR auto-fix stops following review and CI feedback
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes enabled PR auto-fix missing fresh review feedback, repeating already-handled work, and losing attempt state when a scheduled payload fails.

## User Impact

PR auto-fix follows fresh feedback and exact-head checks for the selected PR, and reconciles pending publication requests without replaying them. AutoFix, AutoMerge, and AutoArchive remain separate opt-ins; enabling repairs does not grant merge authority. Existing jobs require explicit re-enabling to install the new revision—there is no implicit migration.

**Status:** open and ready for review, not merged. The real isolated Gateway/model repair→publication→original-request reconciliation→fresh same-PR feedback flow and sanitized UI captures remain unproven. Native GitHub Bot/App eligibility is the integration boundary; a separate branded RoboClaw deployment is not an additional requirement. Local boundary regressions use synthetic GitHub/model I/O and do not close the live-proof gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing native Cron, selected-PR reader, publication receipt, and retry-history owners rather than introducing another watcher. Feedback remains untrusted data. Authority, cancellation, revocation, selected-target checks, and self-only cleanup are retained. App feedback is eligible only with same-head, same-repository native evidence; an outside human PR author is verified by stable integer account ID, not login spelling.

Successful no-op and explicit not-actionable feedback remain deduplicated until the exact revision changes or an observed resolved-to-unresolved thread transition requires reassessment. Both bounded inventory and mandatory fresh rereads reconcile the existing exact-revision receipt owners, including when inventory has advanced to a different thread. Fired payload-failure attempts, retries, and cooldowns survive at the scheduler boundary while cancelled, interrupted, and stale-owner runs remain excluded.

The change verifies the complete attempt-head→accepted-published-head changed-file range and freshly paginates exact-head check contexts beyond the first 100 with bounded consistency/failure handling. Repeated checks from the same App retain one eligible App identity rather than overflowing persisted trigger state; all check records and paging/count/head/repository qualification remain intact. Explicit authenticated Control UI enable of a historical source-less job uses the existing authority-capture owner. Loading or disabling that job does not capture authority, and there is no implicit migration.

## Current Evidence — November 12, 2026

- Published head: `ef15fdcc57cd51e3c8ed34c77fa7f6b2a633e364`, sole parent source commit `5695262a3f9432b28d11a6fc060d44b2811f980b`. The ordinary two-parent source merge preserves first parent `1716c4ca7cc62d6573b9baa697015cfcb44418ec` and integrated-main second parent `17140700d7b54ac2d960863123273528d1e77553`. Source and publication share reviewed tree `8d2df54907a78b6b76db15e1ff438f4e5dc90bfb`; the bookkeeping commit changes no files. Native request `1c982466-f0cd-450c-98db-5f7573feaa8b` is terminal `published` on this original PR, branch and binding. The earlier request `a2b015da-b67a-4d7b-a08f-5c23f5396090` remains historical. No replay, force-push, replacement PR or rebinding.
- Source author/committer: Jason (Json). Native bookkeeping author/committer: verified linked account `fuller-stack-dev`, ID `263060202`. Both commits use `263060202+fuller-stack-dev@users.noreply.github.com`; both are unsigned, not GitHub/web-flow platform commits. Normal commit hooks preserved the exact reviewed tree.
- Independent canonical API review completed **4/4 passes**, exit 0, native `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P3 findings. Review covered the complete **29-file candidate, +3949/-357 against integrated main**, with all **49 context datasets** supplied completely. Earlier accepted findings were repaired and independently re-reviewed. This is source/test review, not live integration acceptance.
- Reopening regressions were demonstrated red before production edits and green afterward through the real authenticated dispatcher, native Cron scheduler and SQLite persistence. Quiet no-op and explicit `not_actionable` threads reassess unchanged reopened feedback, including the two-thread inventory-cursor gap. Non-thread praise, unchanged-revision dedupe, edited revisions and native scheduler reload controls remain intact.
- Prior frozen preparation passed **39/39 Cron tests**, including all **11 comparison/pagination fault controls** (Vitest **208.88s**, wrapper **228.37s**, exit 0). The final App-dedupe repair passed **4/4 affected cases** covering 1-check and 800-check matrices, edited feedback/head/CI reruns, and App-bot eligibility/spoof controls (Vitest **75.31s**, wrapper **94.64s**, exit 0). The large matrix failed before the fix and now persists one App identity and bounded cursor progress across actual scheduler reload without dropping checks or replaying quiet batches. The final run replaces proof for three changed scenarios and adds one matrix case; **this is not a full 40-test rerun on final inputs**.
- Final three-file type-aware lint passed (**9.53s**), as did supported formatting and staged diff checks. Exact-main staged test-line ratchet passed **6,669,545 / 6,669,545 LF**, slack **0**, with the existing **2040-line allocation unchanged**. The final matrix test/fixture delta has zero net test-line growth; no cases/assertions were removed and no budgets/timeouts raised.
- Exact accepted-candidate `pnpm build:runtime` passed (**exit 0, 2m 2.4s**), including 102 plugin runtimes, Control UI, metadata and CLI/worker bootstrap guards. Native `pnpm openclaw --help` returned 0 and identified `ef15fdc`; both actual build stamps recorded this exact HEAD with `inputsClean=true`. Preparation used frozen, canonical-store filtered repairs of missing declared importer links, with no source, dependency declaration or lockfile changes. This runtime profile **omits standalone declarations**; it is not a current default `pnpm build`, standalone typecheck or clean performance-gate result. Reported warnings remain explicit: startup JS **92276 > 92137 gzip bytes**; all CSS **331109 > 326575 gzip bytes** and **1705287 > 1682231 raw bytes**; chat boot **1304054 > 1303711 gzip bytes**. Generated outputs were consumed and removed after identity and consumer checks.
- [CI 43114235628, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43114235628) completed successfully: **55 successful / 24 scope-skipped job records**. Checkout was merge-ref `b40429dd15f7421876be1e392a7fb137a4e34fa8`, incorporating the reviewed head; it is not direct reviewed-tree qualification. Build/native/real-Gateway UI/published-driver lanes were scope-skipped, not passed. Required `openclaw/ci-gate` check `130850982828` is successful. [Final security 43118053117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43118053117) supplies successful exact-head dependency-review, security-sensitive-review and aggregate statuses.
- A protected CI-owner read at **2026-11-12T21:36:55Z** confirmed this unchanged head OPEN and ready for review, with mergeability **UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN**, not a CLEAN qualification. There was no merge, review, review request, thread or new comment. Complete check pagination returned **100 + 100 + 26 = 226 check records: 79 success, 146 skipped, 1 neutral, none failed or running**. These check records are distinct from the original CI's 55/24 job counts. Exact-head required check `130850982828` (App `15368`) and the latest security statuses from `43118053117` remained successful. Subsequent complete ownership qualification found **none of the 29 changed paths matches a CODEOWNERS rule**. CODEOWNERS is identical at target base, accepted head and current main (blob `cf711f7a1cbb26f49074824ed5c54b18ff88f1bd`); applicable sensitive-review policy also introduces no listed-owner requirement for this diff. The earlier generic code-owner evidence gap is withdrawn, not a request for unnecessary SecOps/release-manager signoff.
- Local boundary proof uses real isolated local Git, authenticated dispatcher, Cron scheduler, publication coordinator and SQLite owners with **synthetic GitHub/model I/O**. Revocation-before-transport, queued-request receipt/reset and no-replay evidence remains bounded to its recorded inputs, not a live remote/model repair flow.

## Prior Evidence — Not Current-Tree Qualification

- [Manual qualification 42984984292, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42984984292) belongs to historical head `1716c4ca7cc62d6573b9baa697015cfcb44418ec`. It ended in terminal failure on **2026-11-11T09:12:42Z**: **128 success, 16 failure, 2 cancelled, 14 skipped / 160 jobs**, with failed `ci-gate`. Selected types, lint, ratchet and security-fast checks passed; the overall run did not. Mixed/unknown failures and cancelled phases are not waived, and a 35-minute aggregate build cancellation was not established as a TUI defect.
- [Historical draft CI 42984313132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42984313132) skipped preflight, build, broad tests and `ci-gate`; its 5-success/76-skipped summary is not qualification. [Older manual qualification 42909361914](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42909361914), bound to `2bd1377f2820b6c317ee4b370791de22ed99ee67`, also failed. Neither supplies a blanket inherited-failure waiver.
- Historical default `pnpm build` passed with declarations, 102 external plugins, 162 public SDK subpaths, Control UI and startup metadata (**2m 50.8s**). It used the documented temporary checkout-local virtual-store exception with pinned pnpm, frozen lock, canonical v11 content store and `packageImportMethod=auto`, without compiler/admission bypass or manifest/lock changes. It was **not rerun after main integration and these repairs**. Standalone `tsrs` was not rerun and is not reported passed; external-realpath declaration admission remains an explicit standalone gap.
- The historical unchanged public built-CLI real-PTY canary passed one selected case (**7.369s**, invocation **43.50s**, 11 unselected), using a loopback mock with zero provider requests. It is not live model proof or a full CI-shard pass. Historical 14-pass UI evidence is not fresh screenshot qualification.
- The UI geometry result **14.109375px > 13px** was reproduced, but causation by this PR was not demonstrated; heading alignment belongs to [#196632](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196632), canonical [#196716](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196716). The abort diagnostic, historical gzip warnings and unused `memory-wiki` preparation import were not passing qualification or proven product verdicts.

## Remaining Proof Gaps

- Real isolated Gateway/model repair→publication→original-request recovery→fresh same-PR feedback remains unproven. The historical local attempt returned HTTP401 during catalog discovery **before Gateway startup or inference**. It used a separate configured literal, **not the protected team-store credential**, so it does not show that stored key is invalid. Jason subsequently approved **one coordinator-backed AWS Linux lease**. Coordinator authentication verified GitHub account `263060202` in organization `openclaw`; the `c7a.xlarge` lease became ready on a public network, with no instance role and restricted SSH ingress. The native 0.83 protected grant and sentinel bridge started, but the [bounded catalog-first run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_dd4ff2f4e9d21c4f60322dd0dbf67e5a) returned **HTTP403, terminal exit 21**, before any model request or Gateway startup. Retained records contain no response headers, body or attributable proxy audit: **origin remains unknown between local host denial and upstream/edge refusal; no invalid-key conclusion follows**. No new model/catalog request or credential replacement was authorized or attempted after that refusal. Lease stop was verified, exact retained-resource inventory showed zero matching resources, and the task runtime was removed. No raw-secret transfer or live configuration change was used.
- Creation of **one disposable private fixture** is approved but **not performed**. It requires one private base-only repository and its only PR through an actual isolated native conversation's own publication and binding. Historical installed-CLI startup/config validation passed, but an assistant-imposed blank HOME hid native credential admission: tools.github.status returned credentialState unavailable, account null and evidence none, with no credential-verification probe—not a GitHub /user refusal or the AWS/catalog 403. The corrected preflight preserved native HOME and opaque gh/Octopool selectors unchanged while isolating state, config, workspace, TMPDIR, cache and handoff SQLite. Actual installed-runtime prestartup guards reported allowsProcessHomeSessionScan=false and isDefaultInstallIdentity=false; configuration validation exited 0. Native tools.github.status then succeeded as available/native/system-detected for account fuller-stack-dev, evidence github-api, with gitAuthor Jason (Json) <263060202+fuller-stack-dev@users.noreply.github.com>. Numeric account ID was not returned, scopes were empty and grants unknown; no reconnect was indicated. The account-options read was forbidden with 'GitHub publication session was not found' because no actual owning session existed—not credential failure or GitHub403; no binding was fabricated. This proves **installed-CLI native admission only**, not accepted-source feature behavior or publication/write authority. The test Gateway stopped with exit 0, its endpoint closed and private roots were removed. No lease/model/catalog or fixture writes occurred. The model403 and actual UI-policy/approvals-owner blockers remain; no copied profile, receipt, live association or PR196839 test mutation substituted for the missing fixture.
- Sanitized before/after UI captures remain unproved. Host Chrome MCP access failed; the separately admitted paired extension could list tabs but refused actual localhost fixture navigation by policy. Temporary exact `127.0.0.1` trust across all ports was approved but **not applied**: the actual paired Mac app owner's effective policy remains unverified. Its node-provenance read was **denied before execution** because the native approvals owner's selected CLI did not recognize `--stdin`; no fallback or weakened approval policy was used. The running browser intentionally preserves its SSRF policy during refresh, and an owner-bound supported no-restart apply-and-restore route remains unverified. No current UI fixture or screenshots exist, and no restart, deployment or proxy change was performed.
- Standalone typecheck qualification remains explicit. Current CI/security and runtime-build success do not establish that outcome or the live repair flow.

Consumed task-only live-test, visual-fixture/cache, temporary Crabbox runtime and current runtime-build artifacts were removed after consumers finished; accepted source, compact evidence and canonical dependencies remain. This is an evidence-only metadata refresh: no source publication, CI rerun, review request, merge, live deployment or Gateway restart.

prs.title: fix(update): updating from 2026.11.3 fails when Workboard is installed
prs.body:
Closes #197320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update` from the published 2026.11.3 fails when Workboard is installed. With Workboard on SQLite, the second Doctor reports `Agent database migration did not finish: …/plugins/workboard/workboard.sqlite; expected schema 41, found 0` and rollback is refused. With the 2026.11.1-era `database.engine: "postgres"` (Workboard-only) setting, the candidate snapshot refuses with `Existing SQLite state data cannot switch engines`.

## User Impact

User impact: installs on 2026.11.3 with Workboard, on SQLite or PostgreSQL, can update with `openclaw update` again, and their Workboard data is kept. Rollback still refuses when Workboard changes after capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 2026.11.3 driver is already installed, so the fix is on the candidate side.

- **Schema rows.** The 2026.11.3 driver checks every non-shared row the candidate worker returns against the agent schema. The candidate answers callers that omit `includeLocalStoreVersions` (2026.11.3 and older) with only shared and agent-owned rows: owners, registered paths, and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR`/`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. That is the same set the 2026.11.3 worker publishes itself. Rows are selected by ownership, not by file name. Replies to current launchers, which send the flag and verify agent databases by ownership, are unchanged. Discovery, capture, backup and generation checks still include Workboard and other plugin stores.
- **Config.** Released drivers send config that they read without the candidate's normalization. The worker applies the existing `normalizeLegacyWorkboardDatabaseConfig()` to that config, using the source state directory, so the Workboard-only PostgreSQL setting keeps shared state on SQLite, as ordinary config reads already do.
- **Rehearsal config.** Rehearsal state is private SQLite images, never live PostgreSQL anchors. Current drivers write that into the rehearsal config, but 2026.11.3 copies the source database selection unchanged, so the candidate doctor read the copied shared state as PostgreSQL and refused it. When the update rehearsal contract is present, the candidate's config read applies the same projection to SQLite.

These compatibility paths for released drivers can be removed once 2026.11.3-era drivers are no longer supported upgrade sources.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced live:** in an isolated macOS VM, unmodified `openclaw@2026.11.3` from npm with Workboard cards, updated with `openclaw update`, fails with `Agent database migration did not finish: …/plugins/workboard/workboard.sqlite; expected schema 41, found 0.`, and rollback is refused (`state-migrated-no-rollback`).
- **Inspectable SQLite upgrade:** [Captured output](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34735466/sqlite-upgrade-redacted.txt). An unmodified npm `openclaw@2026.11.3` installation updated to `9216824` through `openclaw update --channel dev --yes --no-restart`. Candidate Doctor, configuration validation, startup rehearsal and activation checks exited 0; the updater exited 0 and durable history recorded `succeeded`. All three synthetic Workboard cards and their persisted data were retained, and the saved timeout remained 321.
- **Inspectable PostgreSQL upgrade with stable-ported data:** [Captured output](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34735469/postgresql-upgrade-redacted.txt). Published 2026.11.3 created three SQLite cards and ported Workboard to PostgreSQL 17.11 with its own `database port --to postgres`. The same installed updater completed the upgrade to `9216824`: candidate Doctor and activation checks exited 0, updater exit was 0, and history recorded `succeeded`. Workboard's store ID, namespace, card contents and data hash were retained across 18 captured tables. PostgreSQL engine selection and timeout were retained; a fresh post-update Workboard CLI read returned the same cards. The outer proof script exited 1 because its connection-equality assertion read the CLI's redacted display value. The attachment separates that harness assertion from the native update result. Raw persisted connection-string equality was not captured.
- **Fresh candidate installation without the rehearsal contract:** [Captured output](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34735468/fresh-install-redacted.txt). A package built from `9216824` was installed in a fresh macOS VM with empty OpenClaw state and no update/rehearsal selectors. Ordinary Doctor commands exited 0, the config read and validation passed, and the Gateway reached `ready=true`, `coreReady=true` with RPC health `ok=true`. A separate fresh PostgreSQL 17.11 profile retained `database.engine=postgres` outside rehearsal; ordinary Doctor, PostgreSQL state/Workboard selection, and a card write/read passed. The run ended `FRESH_INSTALL_PROOF=PASS`.
- **Tested candidate and reviewed head:** [Source identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34735467/candidate-head-equivalence.txt). All three live runs targeted `9216824`, the commit containing the final rehearsal config-read fix. All six production files changed by this PR are byte-for-byte identical at reviewed head `d9fc286`. The runs are prior-head evidence; they are not presented as executions of the entire rebased repository.
- **Regression tests,** each failing without the fix and passing with it:
  - `update-candidate-state.local-schema.test.ts`: legacy and modern callers with a Workboard store at `user_version 0`. Legacy replies omit the row; modern replies keep it; Workboard is still inventoried and copied.
  - Same file: with the 2026.11.3 verifier's rule applied to a legacy reply, wrong-schema agents (default, `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` and registered) are still flagged, and Workboard is not. Without the fix, Workboard is flagged too.
  - `update-candidate-state.postgres.test.ts`: a snapshot under the Workboard-only PostgreSQL setting keeps shared state on SQLite and preserves the Workboard row, and the candidate doctor's database preflight then reads the rehearsal config a 2026.11.3 driver writes and selects SQLite for shared state and Workboard. Without the fixes, the snapshot fails with `cannot switch engines`, and the preflight fails with `Doctor cannot repair this state: shared state database is unreadable`.
- **Guard test:** `update-database-restore.test.ts` checks that rollback refuses when Workboard is written after capture, and passes with and without the fix.
- `update-candidate-state.online-backup.process.test.ts` sends the flags current launchers send, so it keeps asserting the supplemental schema row.
- **Wider runs:** 33 related update test files passed (about 370 tests), plus `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` (all 10 checks), core and infra-test typecheck, lint and format.
- **Test cost:** new cases take 1–4 s each. Test-line growth is +194, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/197320-released-driver-schema-rows.txt` for these regressions.

The [test-line ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43166484725/job/131009863399) reflects inherited base debt: this PR adds 194 test lines and allocates exactly 194, leaving the base's existing 27-line excess. The same excess appears on [another PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43167503452/job/131013377627), while [newer main reports 25 over and passes with zero test-line growth](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43169008291/job/131017935084). The [PostgreSQL shard failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43166484725/job/131009863499) is a file-change rejection in unchanged memory-search code, outside the introduced diff. That exact case [passes on newer main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43169008291/job/131017935232); a matching inherited-main failure has not been established. No updater failure is identified by that job's diagnostic. [Selected CI evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34735465/ci-attribution-redacted.txt).

prs.title: fix: guide agents to reuse shared repository checkouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents preparing another checkout or a batch of PR reviews can clone a repository that is already available in their workspace, creating an independent object store that survives until later cleanup.

## User Impact

Shared agent instructions now tell agents to reuse the existing checkout or create a shared-object checkout through the repository workflow or native Git worktrees, and to report inaccessible shared paths before creating an independent clone. This is guidance, not an enforced clone restriction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native PR provisioning already shares objects. Its documentation and maintainer skill require discovery, while Code Mode deliberately defers tool descriptions and permits calling tools directly when their arguments are clear. The native harness also builds its base prompt separately from the regular renderer. Putting one copy of the guidance in their existing shared Care section makes it visible before the checkout decision in both paths without adding another tool, command rewriting, repository-specific URL, configuration option or cache.

The instruction adds 383 bytes to each prompt: synthetic regular 8,177 → 8,560 bytes; native harness base 6,051 → 6,434 bytes. Production grows by one static text line plus one source comment citing the scratch-clone incident (#197663). No executable branch or I/O is added. New sessions/rendered contexts receive the guidance under the existing prompt lifecycle.

## Evidence

- Six new cases fail on the original shared owner and pass with the fix: ordinary, Code Mode, minimal subagent, CLI-backend, native harness and minimal native harness prompts expose shared checkout guidance without reading a skill or tool description.
- Focused prompt, configured prompt, tool-prefix stability and native harness thread-prompt suites: 145 tests passed.
- Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings on the complete shared-owner patch. Final-scope `pnpm check:changed --base 0181ef700d4aaaf75a5d72c9ac95092cd132996c` passed, including snapshot drift, typechecks, lint, dead exports and runtime boundaries. ClawSweeper’s incident-citation finding is addressed in the adjacent source comment.
- Prompt construction across 5,000 synthetic sessions, five interleaved pairs: median wall 226.823 → 234.575 ms (+3.42%), CPU 257.417 → 266.292 ms (+3.45%), sampled cumulative V8 allocation 219.77 → 221.88 MB (+0.96%, about 422 bytes per fresh prompt). A/A wall drift was 0.054%. These are prompt-construction costs, not model-choice or clone-throughput measurements.
- The complete synthetic regular and native harness prompt diffs each contain exactly one added paragraph. No production model-compliance or disk-reclamation result is claimed.

CI found prompt-snapshot drift on the first shared-owner head. The same two-file mismatch reproduced locally; both the canonical fixture and its hash-bound delta were regenerated with `pnpm prompt:snapshots:gen`, and `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` passes (6 files). A fresh Codex autoreview of the complete patch, including the generated fixtures, found no actionable P0–P2 issues. This was a PR-caused failure, not an inherited-red exception.

Before: the shared prompt policy has no checkout reuse instruction; checkout documentation and deferred tool descriptions require discovery.

After:

> Repos already in the workspace: reuse the checkout, including multi-PR batches. For another checkout, use the repo's checkout workflow or `git worktree add` from the existing repo to share its object store. Do not clone the same repo into task scratch or copy/hardlink its Git objects. If shared paths are inaccessible, report the scope blocker before creating an independent clone.

prs.title: fix(config): repeated $include entries make config loading take minutes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config loading takes minutes when config files include the same child file several times across a few levels of `$include`.

## User Impact

User impact: a config tree with repeated includes now fails fast with a clear `Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded` error, so the CLI, the Gateway and config reloads stop spending minutes on it. Real configs stay far below 1024 include file loads.

## Why This Change Was Made

`$include` already has a depth limit of 10 and a cycle check, and each file is capped at 2 MB. Both checks look at one include chain. A file may still list the same child file several times (`"$include": ["./b.json", "./b.json", ...]`), and each repeat reads, parses and merges the whole subtree below it again. The work grows as fan-out to the power of depth. Nine levels that each include the next level four times load 349,524 files, built from eleven files of about 100 bytes.

The include resolver now counts file loads in one resolution and throws a `ConfigIncludeError` once it reaches 1024 loads. The check sits next to the depth check in `loadFileSync`, and the error flows through the same config validation path as the depth and cycle errors. The docs list the new limit next to the depth limit.

## Evidence

The proof script generates nine levels where level i includes level i+1 F times, then runs `openclaw config validate` from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config validate`) with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at that tree. Wall time includes about 30 s of dev-mode CLI startup on this machine.

| Fan-out | Include file loads | main `00b62dd` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 | 28.0 s, Config valid | 31.0 s, Config valid |
| 2 | 1,023 | 30.0 s, Config valid | 30.8 s, Config valid |
| 3 | 29,524 | 67.3 s, Config valid | 29.7 s, include error |
| 4 | 349,525 | 389.9 s, Config valid | 30.9 s, include error |

Branch output for fan-out 4:

```
Config needs correction: .../fan4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json
```

Calling `resolveConfigIncludes` directly on main for the same trees took 0.56 s, 7.3 s and 80.3 s for fan-out 2, 3 and 4. On this branch fan-out 2 resolves in 0.39 s and fan-out 3 and 4 throw the include error.

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/includes.test.ts src/config/includes.top-level-key.test.ts src/config/include-write-boundary.test.ts src/config/mutate.agent-delete-include.test.ts`: 41 passed. On main the two new tests fail. The budget test resolves 1025 loads without an error, and the fan-out test runs for 101 s and resolves without an error. On this branch they take 660 ms and 352 ms.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK, net +34 test lines within the allowance.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive wrapper-inventory lookup work contributing to baseline-proof timeouts in main CI.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible runtime change. Developers running the native PR workflow spend less time resolving wrapper inventory; trust checks, baseline authority and the 120-second test budget remain unchanged. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper repeatedly resolved thousands of revision:path entries from the commit root. One tree walk now produces the same ordered object-ID vector through the existing dispatcher. Missing entries still fail closed. This removes measured overhead without relaxing any trust comparison or baseline-admission assertion.

## Evidence

Main run 43290071255 (`7602443502`) exceeded the unchanged 120-second budget in the retained-baseline case. Proof used fresh-main base `0181ef700d4` on AWS Crabbox with pinned Bun:

- Existing baseline-proof file: 28/28 pass. The affected case took 72.5 seconds with the change versus 94.7 seconds unchanged on the same machine. These are single end-to-end observations, not a reproduced hosted timeout or a guarantee against future flakes.
- Wrapper-trust selection: 10/10 pass, including canonical substitution, materialized anchors, omitted components, symlinks, tampered sources and spoofed refs.
- Five interleaved resolver measurements returned byte-identical ordered hash vectors: tree walk 76–107 ms versus per-path lookup 738–757 ms.
- Bash and embedded-JavaScript syntax checks pass. ShellCheck has the same 18 inherited diagnostics. Independent local autoreview found no P0–P2 findings.
- Current PR CI and later natural scheduled-main qualification remain pending. The AWS lease is released with cleanup complete.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.title: fix(text): streaming Markdown checkpoint must settle after a closed legacy bracket block
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant reply delivered to the user contains a *closed* legacy bracket tool-call block (`[TOOL_CALL]…[/TOOL_CALL]`), the streaming Markdown checkpoint never settles — `settledLength` stays 0 for the entire reply. Because the Gateway runs stream processing synchronously on its event loop, every appended chunk re-scans the whole prefix, so a 64KB reply blocks other conversations for ~73.7s and a 128KB reply for ~191s (same failure class as #186667 / #192831 / #187400, and it corrupts no text).

- Problem: `findTextCheckpoint` treats any line containing `[` as needing the full paragraph context and returns `offset = retainStart` (= 0); and `scanLegacyBracketToolCallBlocks` sets `pending` from the last `[` anywhere in the reply, so an ordinary unmatched bracket (e.g. `Array index [0`) also keeps the reply pending. Both pin the checkpoint boundary at 0.
- Solution: a completed `[TOOL_CALL]`/`[TOOL_RESULT]` tag line with no other open bracket or link is allowed to settle immediately; and `pending` is narrowed so only a partial `[TOOL_(CALL|RESULT)` header keeps the reply pending.
- What changed: `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` (`findTextCheckpoint`) and `src/shared/text/assistant-text-transforms.ts` (`scanLegacyBracketToolCallBlocks`), plus one regression row in `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: unclosed labels, reference definitions, inline code, and link targets still force the conservative full-paragraph fallback; a genuinely partial `[TOOL_C` header still keeps the reply pending.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two guards conflated "contains a bracket" with "needs full context". Only the legacy tool tag line is provably closed on a single line, so it is the only bracket line eligible to settle early. The `pending` heuristic is narrowed (not removed) so a stray `[` no longer blocks settlement. This is the best available fix: minimal, no new abstraction, and no behavior change for real open labels/links. Risk: none observed — the full `src/shared/text` suite (664 tests) is green, including the existing batch/streaming consistency contracts.

## User Impact

Streaming replies that contain a closed legacy bracket tool-call block now settle their prefix incrementally instead of stalling the Gateway event loop. Operators see no text change; they avoid multi-minute stalls on 64KB+ replies.

## Compatibility

- Preserved: unclosed bracket labels, reference definitions, inline code, and link targets retain the conservative full-paragraph fallback; partial `[TOOL_(CALL|RESULT)` headers still keep the reply pending.
- Related: same failure class as #186667 / #192831 / #187400 (streaming re-scan stalls), fixed at the checkpoint/legacy-bracket layer.
- Not claimed: a reply whose trailing line ends with a genuinely unmatched open bracket `[` (e.g. `Array index [0`) still keeps that final line un-settled — that is intentional conservative behavior, not part of this fix.

## Evidence
### Before → After (summary)

| Observable | Before fix (`origin/main`) | After fix (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| Reply prefix settles (`settledLength` / source) | 0 / 4,096 (0%) | 3,949 / 4,096 (96.4%) |
| Re-scan work over the whole stream (`scannedChars`, in-process) | 12,025,421 | 1,332,715 (≈9× lower) |
| Gateway event-loop stall on 64KB / 128KB reply | ~73.7s / ~191s | none |
| Streaming preview == final text (shipped, 32KB workload) | — (pre-fix not exercised on the shipped path) | ✅ 32,706 chars, byte-for-byte |
| Gateway responsiveness mid-stream (shipped) | — (pre-fix not exercised on the shipped path) | ✅ health avg 4ms; peer RPCs ≤9ms, 0 failures |

### Shipped Gateway streaming proof (isolated run)

Isolated Gateway started through the production `startGatewayServerCore` entry point, with an independent local OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider and a real WebSocket client subscribed to the `agent` stream. The provider streams the regression workload — a *closed* legacy bracket block followed by ordinary prose — as 4-character SSE deltas, so the reply arrives through the shipped provider/subscriber path (not a direct helper call). No stubbed runtime, no clock instrumentation.

- Workload: `[TOOL_CALL]{}\n[/TOOL_CALL]\n` + ~32KB of prose, 4-character deltas.
- The accumulated `agent` stream deltas are reconstructed into the preview and compared against the final assistant text for the whole reply.
- Gateway responsiveness is measured concurrently by loopback `/health` probes and by a **second, independent WS session** issuing real Gateway RPCs while the workload streams (the cross-conversation case).
- Host paths, loopback addresses, ports, tokens, and local-only credentials are redacted below.

```console
$ vitest run --pool=forks src/gateway/pr-193871-shipped-stream-proof.test.ts

[proof] gateway ready after 58856ms
[proof] provider request 1: stream=true
[proof] replyChars=32707 finalChars=32706 previewChars=32706
[proof] previewEqualsFinal=true
[proof] finalSettledMs=49301 requestError=none
[proof] healthProbes=892 avgRttMs=4 maxRttMs=101 slowProbesGt500ms=0
[proof] peerSessionRpcs=36 peerAvgRttMs=4 peerMaxRttMs=9 workloadPeerFailures=0 warmupPeerRtts=143 warmupPeerFailures=0
[proof] providerRequests=[{"stream":true,"messageCount":3}]
[proof] deltas=100 snapshots=0
[proof] finalTail="fix.\nThe guard rejects the call when values differ.\nIt keeps the settled prefix."

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The reconstructed streaming preview equals the final assistant text byte-for-byte (32,706 chars, no loss or duplication), and the reply tail is intact. During the whole run the Gateway stayed responsive: 892 health probes averaged 4 ms with a 101 ms maximum and zero probes over 500 ms, and the second session's Gateway RPCs in the workload window completed in ≤9 ms with zero failures. This is the cross-conversation property the in-process harness could not establish.

The performance delta of the fix itself (pre-fix re-scans the whole prefix on every append) is quantified by the in-process harness directly below, since the shipped provider/subscriber layer batches deltas and is not where the O(n^2) re-scan lives.

### Regression: red on pre-fix main, green on this head
Live runtime check of the regression shape (source = `[TOOL_CALL]{}\n[/TOOL_CALL]\n` + 4096 chars of ordinary prose, streamed in 4-char chunks via `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")`):

```console
$ node --import tsx <script>.mts
PRE-FIX (origin/main):  scannedChars=12025421 settledLength=0     sourceLen=4096 settledPct=0.0   textMatches=true
POST-FIX (this branch): scannedChars=1332715  settledLength=3949  sourceLen=4096 settledPct=96.4  textMatches=true
```

Behavior matrix (regression shape):

```text
input form                               => pre-fix                                => post-fix
closed [TOOL_CALL]…[/TOOL_CALL] + prose  => scannedChars 12,025,421; settled 0%    => scannedChars 1,332,715; settled 96.4%
```

`scannedChars` is the total characters fed to `RegExp.prototype.test` across the whole stream — a direct proxy for the re-scan cost. Pre-fix re-scans the entire ~4KB prefix on (almost) every append; post-fix stays bounded (~1.33M total, ~9× lower). The regression test `bounds ordinary legacy bracket block streaming work` asserts `settledLength > 90%`, `scanned < 512× source length`, and `markdownOwnershipWork.scannedCharacters < 16× source length`; it is RED on origin/main and GREEN on this branch.

- What was not tested: a reply whose trailing line ends with a genuinely unmatched open bracket `[` (e.g. `Array index [0`) still keeps that final line un-settled by design; this is the correct conservative behavior and is outside the scope of this fix.
- Open PR collision check: searched open PR topics and changed-file lists for `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts`, `src/shared/text/assistant-text-transforms.ts`, and `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts`; no open PR touched these files. My open PRs at push time = 19 (< 20). Branch rebased onto latest `origin/main`.

prs.title: fix(oc-path): preserve the first line in newline-only JSONL files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw path resolve` cannot address the first line of a JSONL file containing only one newline, and reports an append position of line 1 even though appending writes to line 2.

## User Impact

Files containing a single LF or CRLF now resolve `L1` as a blank line and `+` as line 2. Empty files still append at line 1, and append preserves the existing bytes and newline style.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removing the final line separator made a single blank line indistinguishable from an empty file. Check whether the original input is empty before splitting it into lines.

## Evidence

Verified through the built CLI on Windows with Node 24.22.1, isolated configuration, and only `oc-path` enabled. Compared base `a3d5baaabd` with `078970ecd6`:

| Input | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One LF or CRLF | `L1` is unresolved; `+` reports line 1 | `L1` resolves; `+` reports line 2 |
| Empty file | `L1` is unresolved; `+` reports line 1 | Unchanged |

The final CLI checks also verified an actual append followed by resolving `L2`, byte-preserving dry runs, literal `find L1`, and that `*`, `$first`, and `$last` still skip blank lines. Nine baseline commands and sixteen final commands passed their assertions.

With `oc-path` enabled, the LF reproduction is:

```sh
python -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('events.jsonl').write_bytes(b'\n')"
pnpm --silent openclaw path resolve oc://events.jsonl/L1 --json --file events.jsonl
pnpm --silent openclaw path resolve oc://events.jsonl/+ --json --file events.jsonl
```

- Regression proof: LF and CRLF cases fail on the old parser; all 61 tests in the owning test file pass with the fix. Empty input and consecutive blank lines are covered too.

prs.title: feat(automations): preview impact before changing default models
prs.body:
Related: #188761

## What Problem This Solves

Changing a default model can leave existing automations blocked by model policy or account/runtime compatibility, with no warning at the point of change.

## User Impact

Models and Agents settings show automation impact before changing the primary model, and ask for confirmation when enabled jobs have blockers or unknown compatibility. CLI and agent callers can inspect the same read-only result. Existing overrides, account ownership, permissions, schedules, and expired work are not changed.

This is an advisory metadata preview—not proof that inference, fallback attempts, tools, or delivery will succeed. Missing personal/native observations remain unknown. CLI models set preserves offline save behavior when assessment is unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

One cron-owned assessment reuses scheduled model selection, account-route availability, and runtime checks. The UI, CLI and automation tool share it instead of maintaining separate compatibility rules. This is the agreed preview-and-guidance first stage; bulk editing automation overrides remains deferred. No migration or new configuration option is required.

The November 12 rebase preserves current main’s account semantics: a recorded account constrains only its own provider. An inherited default moving to another provider selects credentials/runtime live, so preview reports that case as **unknown**, not incompatible. Model policy still applies.

## Evidence

Current head: **3a8fdc135e9c9a2041b03f7f8c6da79199d36a3b**, rebased onto main 1ca34955022cadc5900793cebeab6c89a2a652ba. The five prior bot-authored commits, including two merge-resolution repairs, were consolidated with an exact tree-equality check before rebasing; human attribution is retained. Current-main Agents settings access, page-data ownership, save feedback, and provider-aware inference behavior are preserved.

- **Real isolated Gateway:** 2/2 browser tests pass (183.26s including fresh private-QA runtime and production UI preparation). The wire result reports unknown / execution-path-not-assessed for the cross-provider change. Cancel preserves config and jobs. Accept changes only the default model; all job/account metadata remains unchanged and the scheduler remains disabled. No mocked WebSocket or live inference.
- **UI:** 137 owner tests across 12 files and 4 impact/recovery browser tests pass. Production, UI-page-test and UI-E2E types, scoped lint and format pass. The mock fixture now advertises the read capabilities required by main’s settings-access owner; no access rule or assertion was weakened.
- **Domain and runtime:** 16 tests cover preview and both scheduled-run cross-provider paths; 26 catalog/account/plugin-auth tests pass. Two temporary negative controls fail at the real preview boundary: restoring the old provider blocker, and dropping the provider argument that preserves the captured runtime. Both controls were restored byte-for-byte; the final 8-test domain suite passes. Synthetic loopback transport is not upstream-provider proof.
- **CLI/tool/Gateway:** 193 tests across six affected files pass, including automation tool, CLI, model-selection, registered-Gateway-dispatch, request-start and prompt-prefix consumers. The 10-test models-set E2E suite also passes (230.79s including ordinary current-source runtime preparation, without skip-build or stale-dist reuse). The first attempt was interrupted by a Gateway restart before tests; the resumed supported run completed successfully.
- **Static contracts:** core, commands, Cron, Gateway and CLI types pass. Canonical Gateway validators, six prompt snapshots, protocol registry/introduction-train and native Swift/Kotlin determinism checks pass. An import-order lint failure was corrected without changing schema values. Final scoped lint/format, whitespace, line-cap and test-cost gates pass.
- **Test cost:** +1,490 literal test LF lines; current policy’s 400-line allowance plus a 1,090-line feature allocation covers the exact growth. This supports distinct selection/account, private-session visibility, transport and real-Gateway/UI cancellation/config-only boundaries. No shared limit or unrelated debt adjustment.
- **Fresh independent review:** Local autoreview completed all 3 P0–P2 passes against base 1ca34955022cadc5900793cebeab6c89a2a652ba, reviewing the full staged candidate (tree 348baf5bbfaa254387b1f504f0e55a436a24b2c8). Zero accepted/actionable findings; no partial attempts; final source verification passed. This is not a new hosted ClawSweeper verdict.

**Remaining qualification:** the standard UI build succeeds but reports five performance-budget overages (startup JS, CSS gzip/raw, chat boot JS and new boot JS). Strict performance-gate success is not claimed; exact-head CI will classify these. The old missing deep-research client preparation blocker is gone on this base. No upstream credential-acceptance, live scheduled execution or WebKit claim. November 6 CI/review results below are historical, not current-head evidence.

### Current real-Gateway interaction

Synthetic data, desktop/light. Both frames are from the same freshly built rebased candidate: before selecting the model, then after opening the impact warning. This is an interaction comparison, not two historical source builds.

**Before**

![Before selecting the new model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1d3b7c2-36f8-4fdd-ad47-effaf50ab26b)

**After**

![Cross-provider compatibility warning on the real isolated Gateway](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/527a27f7-aa40-411f-81d3-adc8c7680141)

<details><summary>Historical captures retained for context</summary>

### Historical November 6 fixture screenshots

Inspected synthetic browser fixtures captured at `84b7f294`: desktop/light and agent-scoped mobile/dark. The follow-ups change no UI runtime behavior: they restore erased type contracts, correct introduction-train metadata, and relocate an unchanged Gateway error classifier. These are historical captures, superseded by the current real-Gateway warning above. These show the automation warning review modal, not an isolated settled InlineAlert notice. Actions and text remain legible; job details intentionally scroll.

![Historical November 6 automation warning, desktop light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/838567e2-9b67-49da-b0e8-577452cadde7)

![Historical November 6 automation warning, agent mobile dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9369a369-6a74-4700-b130-634ebc992960)

### Before (original baseline)

![Original Models settings before selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93c06eaa-00ed-494d-b1dd-b67dba68ba4c)

### After (original published head)

<details><summary>Actual isolated Gateway interaction</summary>
