prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
Long conversations kept reloadable transcript bodies resident as more history was opened. This change bounds the resident window, reloads older/newer history on demand and retires evicted presentation data while preserving navigation and reader position.

**Signed integration candidate: 1a8742cdb7377d9e7a8d6b051422b7b4ce165f0c**, tree 614b5c96e0a711e010358218ef1c605b84130977, on frozen application baseline 9ca7932563ff3a8d2d3eca37e50d6ea7b031a527. Native C materialization and the signed D allocation-only follow-up preserve the reviewed integration. **NEEDS WORK; R4 asset disposition and R5 ordinary landing gates remain open.** No READY, merge, deployment, Firefox crash-recovery or whole-browser RSS claim.

**Proof publication completed:** native exit 0; uncached GitHub reads confirm exact signed D/tree above. The native receipt records `PUSH_PURPOSE=proof`, review 2821037447cfb0fcb19b8ed5ce0739898e2af80d and pending R4/R5. This supplies no ordinary READY qualification, CI success or merge admission.

Source review covers the prior signed H candidate, all eight explicit conflict resolutions, all 25 clean joins, canonical Gateway generation and all 304 materialized C postimage/mode comparisons. No mismatch was found. The D child only removes an obsolete five-line historical test allocation; production and test source are C-identical. The canonical test-lines ratchet passes: delta 14,570, credit 14,241 plus allowance 400, spare 71. B-to-D semantic accounting across 303 paths is authored production +4,416 lines, generated production −12, test/support +14,604 and metadata +38. Positive production growth owns bounded, reloadable transcript residency and lifecycle retirement. Extracted module size is not treated as new algorithm size; a 4,712-byte matcher body is unchanged from B.

**Exact-D proof:** native isolated receiver source/tree/origin/clean guards passed with Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3. The complete CI-artifact build passed, including SDK declarations and 163 export checks. The selected 32-operand focused command passed 630 tests in 31 files, with two native Playwright footer cases skipped. Real Chromium geometry added 32 passing cases; the single config-save E2E file added six distinct passing cases. Total: **668 distinct passes, two skips**. The skipped executable-dependent footer cases include Firefox; Chromium success is not Firefox proof. Node packet/cache collection controls passed at their actual runtime scope.

The [full-build and strict fixed-b59 run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43288240720) completed application phases but exits 1 for four asset budgets. Both candidate and fixed-b59 builds completed; b59 itself passes. Current full-pack D reports:

| Metric | Actual | Limit | Over |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup gzip | 92,224 B | 92,137 B | 87 B |
| Chat gzip | 1,310,678 B | 1,303,958 B | 6,720 B |
| CSS gzip | 331,494 B | 326,575 B | 4,919 B |
| CSS raw | 1,704,670 B | 1,682,231 B | 22,439 B |

New and largest-JS pass. No cap, fixed-base policy, compressor or fallback was changed.

A [separate canonical matched D:B diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43291958563) uses the same Settings-only preparation on both revisions, from guarded fresh output directories. It also exits 1; it is diagnostic attribution, not a replacement strict gate. Both builds completed:

| Metric | D | B | D minus B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup gzip | 92,224 B | 92,231 B | −7 B |
| Chat gzip | 1,310,332 B | 1,303,228 B | +7,104 B (+0.5451%) |
| New gzip | 789,545 B | 806,389 B | −16,844 B (−2.0888%) |
| CSS gzip | 331,494 B | 331,492 B | +2 B |
| CSS raw | 1,704,670 B | 1,704,684 B | −14 B |
| Largest JS | 548,589 B | 565,419 B | −16,830 B |

B itself exceeds startup, CSS and New limits. These inherited failures are not a baseline PASS or a waiver. Fresh Settings-only D Chat is 346 B below full-pack D; preparation scopes remain separate. Owner review found no justified deletion or deferral that preserves the bounded-history, action-custody and native-scroll contracts. Owner disposition remains pending; current merge CI below provides a separate comparison.

Both task-owned Testboxes were stopped and independently observed completed, with owned local processes joined. Their linked Actions workflows were cancelled by native cleanup; those statuses do not convert payload exit 1 into success or supply ordinary PR CI. Transport carrier identities remain separate from exact application D.

**Ordinary hosted evidence:** [CI attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43310038296) is testing merge c0310e0bc40d9d71018e4eb0830f48bd3c9b3d2a (tree 4e1ef328dd32fd0f2b5eab19c592e749e03b7bc8), with actual comparison base 10285cd35ca7d696957430bbc6c8556f55af79fe and application parent D. Preflight and performance logs record that execution identity; it is distinct from standalone D and the event base field B. The tested merge contains the canonical separately landed service-worker blob 39707d3984a9be810550e6b653cde3b75d0d2d69. The artifact build, six selected Control UI browser shards, browser-extension bootstrap in the artifact build, and both Android variants have passed their actual steps; the attempt has completed with 83 successful jobs, 21 intentionally skipped jobs and two failed checks. The aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` log attributes its failure solely to `control-ui-performance`; all other selected groups succeeded. The completed performance job fails a new Chat violation: merge/base Chat 1,310,557/1,303,259 B, **+7,298 B (+0.5600%)**. New improves 16,650 B, startup improves 7 B and CSS gzip grows 2 B. Base Chat passes the 1,303,958 B cap, so this failure is not inherited debt and cannot use an inherited-only exception. These actual merge measurements do not replace the separate D:B or full-pack scopes above.

[Security Review attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43310037851) completed successfully for exact D, including its enforcing step. [ClawSweeper revision 9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187440#issuecomment-6490746062) reviewed exact D with no actionable code findings and no rank-up moves; it holds for explicit maintainer asset disposition. The previous two source findings are repaired. This clears neither the new Chat failure nor final native admission.

**Remaining admission:** explicit owner acceptance of the measured current Chat growth, followed by its reviewed canonical budget disposition (or an unchanged-cap reduction), complete ordinary CI disposition and final independent READY/native qualification. Owner acceptance alone cannot clear the fixed Chat source ceiling; no cap has been changed. Historical manual run 43219943464 executed 0cc, not D, and retains its original scope. The three prior ClawSweeper source-oracle files remain outside the original 668-case pack. Current merge CI explicitly records 11 passing file-link cases and one passing PDF case. An additional focused exact-D run of `test/scripts/control-ui-engine-page-scenarios.test.ts` passed all 11 cases on Node 26.7.0 through the repository wrapper; the checkout remained clean. These scopes are separate.

**Proposed owner disposition (not implemented):** accept the observed +7,298 B (+0.5600%) Chat gzip tradeoff for bounded, reloadable history. Increase only the existing fixed Chat ceiling from 1,303,958 to **1,311,256 B**: the prior ceiling plus the measured matched growth, preserving the prior base headroom. Keep startup/CSS/New limits and canonical measurement unchanged. After explicit owner acceptance, record it here, make the source/rationale-only budget adjustment, and obtain fresh focused checks, ordinary CI, exact-head review and native qualification before squash landing. No acceptance or passing result is inferred.

Historical real SQLite/actor, Stop/Gateway, loading, generation and browser evidence below retains its original source and execution scope. It is not relabeled as D runtime proof. Named follow-ups remain separate: GlobalAbsenceProofAgentScope, HistoryDepthBoundedResidentVerification and DelegatedProviderPreflightBeforeSourceMirror. No new timing cohort, speedup or deployment claim.

## What Problem This Solves

Long chat sessions retain more transcript bodies as readers page. This change bounds reloadable resident history, releases evicted bodies from presentation caches, and keeps older/newer navigation reversible.

## User Impact

Ordinary residency targets **400 entries / 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units / eight source segments**. Source atomicity, the current reader packet and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one bounded staged packet is separately charged. These are retained-body targets, not a whole-pane RAM ceiling.

Readers can move older/newer, return to Latest and restore semantic bookmarks. Search states its loaded-window scope; export loads complete history separately. Capacity/unavailable outcomes are visible. A local command after an authoritative empty-history read stays before the first later turn, including after resident-prefix retirement and older-page admission. Unloaded or unknown history never implies the beginning. Command replies retain transient custody and retire rather than entering persistent raw history.

**Tradeoff: bounded residency makes a full 900→1→900 traversal perform more pagination and rendering work. Historical matched comparisons remain rejected, with substantial wall-time and renderer-CPU regressions disclosed below. The owner accepts that product tradeoff after investigation; this is no numerical benchmark pass or speedup claim.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical source/packet/cursor ownership controls trimming, reopening, continuity and retirement. SQLite and actor-memory reads certify same-snapshot Stop continuation; UI admission revalidates a fresh selected packet. Numeric adaptive budgets cross awaits, prepared bodies do not. One synchronous owner performs final prefix fit and accepted-prefix receipt adoption. Visible fitting reads commit without an unnecessary fallback/staged read, while sparse/raw progress, smaller-envelope retries and cancellation retain their existing contracts.

Accepted raw source facts and one canonical publication owner govern local-output placement; empty views, stale reads, pending inputs and unavailable outbox storage do not confer authority. Local occurrence placement preserves consecutive command order without inventing durable sequence zero. Edge-only history traversal advances navigation while preserving the original held packet bodies, certificate and opaque endpoints; actual cuts or body changes still revoke that custody.

One native offset producer supplies paging/follow facts before callback-induced rendering, preserving input/link ownership and anchor ordering. Its accepted reader-policy baseline is independent of geometric synchronization: measuring the current position before scroll capture cannot consume upward paging intent. Presentation-owned partial retirement releases dormant bodies while preserving safe survivor seeds. One shared weak derivation owner preserves exact digest bytes for fresh immutable stream/snapshot envelopes and per-source reactions. Reply-preview revisions follow final lookup facts; releasing nonempty quote bodies still invalidates their previews.

prs.title: fix(logging): preserve stuck-session recovery classification in automation failures
prs.body:
Related: #138528

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled run that the stuck-session watchdog stops reports no reason: automation history keeps the mechanical effect (`Reply operation stalled`) and the failure alert ends with "Check automation history for details". The cause the attention layer already computed for that stall is dropped one layer above every operator-facing surface, so a run killed behind a tool call that never progresses is indistinguishable from one killed by a provider outage or an attempt deadline.

Fixes: the stop's classification reaches automation history and the failure alert, with recovery guidance.

## User Impact

An operator reading a stopped scheduled run now sees *why* it was stopped — in `lastError` / `cron runs` and in the chat alert's `Cause:` line plus a one-line recovery step — instead of a cause-free line. A run stopped while the provider is rate-limiting still reports the provider's own recovery text: the mechanical watchdog label never replaces it. Cancellation, restart and rate-limit handling, scheduler merge re-admission, abort signatures and alert routing are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session controller owns the stop; cron owns the operator-facing projection. The object connecting them already exists: the controller-owned `ReplyOperation` that `finalizeCronRun` reads. `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession` commits the attention classification onto that operation (`recoveryClassification`) before it drives `watchdog.tick()`, and a stop performed by the watchdog tick records its own decision reason there instead. One owner, no diagnostic-owned store, nothing to keep in sync.

Cron projects that one field twice: as the run-history error when the run failed without a descriptive message, and as a typed `agent-stall` `CronFailureNotificationDetail` that the alert renders as `Cause: <classification>` plus guidance. Rate-limit precedence lives in one helper (`resolveCronRecoveryClassification`): `abortForStall` records a stop during provider backoff as `rate_limited` and `describeStop()` keeps the provider text, so no classification is projected.

Accepted edge case, named instead of coded around: whichever owner performs the stop decides the label. The watchdog timer usually fires its own quiet-tool allowance first, so a hung tool call reports the mechanical `semantic_stall`; when the diagnostics recovery request lands the stop, it reports the precise `blocked_tool_call` (§1). Both labels are recorded facts, and both now reach the operator.

Scope: cause attribution only. #138528 also asks for immediate exec-denial classification and the blocking tool identity inside the alert; neither is here, so `Related:` rather than `Closes:`.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped Gateway, real chat alert

Shipped `openclaw.mjs gateway --dev` (isolated state dir, loopback), the shipped plugin installer registering a plugin whose `hang_forever` tool never settles, a local OpenAI-compatible provider that answers the first turn with that tool call, and the shipped `cron` CLI creating a recurring isolated job with `--timeout-seconds 0` so no attempt deadline can mask the block. `cron.failureAlert` = `{"enabled":true,"mode":"announce","channel":"qa-channel","to":"dm:operator"}` against a local qa-lab bus. No stubbed runtime, no clock instrumentation.

The attention layer classifies the in-flight tool call every heartbeat; the run ends when the quiet-tool allowance (15 min) is exhausted:

```
08:51:40 [diagnostic] stalled session: … state=processing age=685s
         reason=blocked_tool_call classification=blocked_tool_call activeWorkKind=tool_call
         activeTool=hang_forever activeToolAge=684s cronJob="watchdog-chat" recovery=controller_owned
08:55:16 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested durationMs=909760
         error="Reply operation stalled" errorName=AbortError taskKind=cron
```

The alert as the bus recorded the outbound message (ids and ports removed):

```
Automation "watchdog-chat" failed 1 times
Cause: semantic_stall
The agent made no semantic progress before the stall deadline.
Review the run transcript and simplify the task, then rerun.
```

Same moment, persisted history: `"lastError": "semantic_stall"`, `"lastDurationMs": 917358`, `"consecutiveErrors": 1`. Delivery status stayed `"unknown"` — the qa-channel fixture does not ack the announce send, though the bus recorded the text.

The precise label, when the recovery request lands the stop (same stack, webhook alert): run record `"error":"blocked_tool_call"`, alert `Last error: blocked_tool_call`.

### 2. Regression: red on pre-patch main, green here

`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.watchdog-cause.test.ts` drives the real cron finalizer with a controller-owned operation:

| code state | persists the cause | rate-limited stop keeps provider text |
|---|---|---|
| pre-patch `main` (`f75bd97cda9` / `8ac4e19d206`) | **fails** | passes |
| reviewed head (`639c0970838`) | passes | **fails** |
| this head (`e02bc6f1ada`, on main `8ac4e19d206`) | passes | passes |

### 3. Acceptance on this head

```
vitest run run.watchdog-cause / failure-notification-text / diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery-cause
                             → 3 files passed · 17 tests passed
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main → Test lines OK: 6456838; ceiling: 6456859; slack: 21
oxfmt --check, oxlint --type-aware (12 code files) → formatted · 0 warnings, 0 errors
git diff --check                                     → clean
```

Rebase onto main `8ac4e19d206`: one conflict, the renderer table where main added `billing`/`server_error` guidance beside the agent-stall cases — both kept, and the production hunks are byte-identical to the reviewed head. The formatter-only aborted-branch assertion is dropped; cause propagation stays guarded by the recovery and cron-boundary cases.

Gap: local type checking cannot run in this worktree (the `run-tsgo` boundary guard rejects the shared install's symlinks), so CI's `check-prod-types` and `check-test-types-*` own that lane. The proof stack stays outside the repository (~16 min/run).

prs.title: fix(github): recover saved repository publications
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repository-backed sessions can publish against their selected source branch instead of the current default branch, and saved publication requests cannot recover from pre-effect outages or retained-worker reconnects. Native integration also forwarded the selected personal publisher credential to the worker instead of using the normal execution identity. Capture failures could bypass bounded recovery and leave a request pending indefinitely.

## User Impact

Publication integrates the accepted checkpoint with one observed target tip in private worker Git state while preserving later edits, the editing index, the original request and existing PR metadata. Explicit retries revalidate the original requester and publisher; they never force-push or adopt an unmatched external head.

Repository-only publication requires the normal worker execution account to read the source/head and target/base roles: one repository in the common case, or fork and upstream when applicable. Actual read checks remain mandatory. My GitHub stays Gateway-held for final API/ref/PR writes and attribution. Missing execution credentials or access fail closed without personal-token fallback, anonymous fallback, new App requirements or broader grants. Ordinary worker Git/PR/issue capabilities are unchanged.

New capture still requires authoritative disk custody. Live private-provider/model acceptance and installed-upgrade qualification remain incomplete.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing checkpoint, receipt, placement/runtime recovery, transfer and native Git owners. Capture holds editing custody; merge work stays private. Failure receipts retain bounded transport facts, not command output. Worker execution credentials have a bounded publication-operation lifetime independent of the API publisher, with acquisition rotation, committed selection, expiry, requester and placement checks. Native drain joins private publication and awaited cleanup outside the editing queue.

Reclaimed recovery carries the publication's existing live startup reader through the normal placement owner, without fabricating a chat turn or substituting credentials after denial. Capture errors now use the existing cooldown and three-attempt/one-hour terminal policy. Healthy checkpoint waits remain exempt; busy work preserves previous failures. Terminal settlement rereads the current receipt under workspace exclusion without recapture or Git replay. No database schema, protocol-version extension, broader grant or new recovery owner was added.

prs.title: fix: preview plugin and personal themes with their own colors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin and personal theme cards show the selected theme’s colors instead of their own in Settings → Appearance.

## User Impact

User impact: users can compare each theme’s background and accent colors before selecting it, in either light or dark mode. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing connection-scoped theme catalog cache to load and preview every listed palette. Single-mode themes retain their available palette, accent overrides do not recolor previews, and failed preview reads use the existing Retry action. Built-in cards and the browser-local import slot keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced in Chromium on the base: both synthetic catalog themes incorrectly displayed Knot’s background and red/gray accents. The same production-UI regression passes with the fix.
- 50 focused tests pass: 18 theme-catalog, 4 Appearance catalog lifecycle, 4 theme-token, 5 theme-picker browser, 18 Appearance browser, and 1 production-bundle Chromium E2E. E2E covers dark/light palettes, single-mode fallback, accent override isolation, selection/cache reuse, plugin refresh, and inactive-preview failure/Retry.
- Initial E2E test time: 2.9 s; wall time including production UI build: 14.5 s. Focused owner/lifecycle wall time: 3.2 s; theme-picker browser: 1.0 s; Appearance browser: 1.1 s. Hosted CI time is not yet available.
- UI typecheck, targeted Oxlint/Stylelint, formatting, diff checks, controller guards, and staged test-line budget pass. The sandbox needed task-local Chromium libraries and fallback fonts; no live Gateway or shared dependency installation was changed.
- Independent Auto Review (OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2: no findings on the complete staged candidate against base `17140700d7b54ac2d960863123273528d1e77553`. Candidate patch SHA-256: `2632cbe1d5725c602b7238617cc361c7ff8b3d3df532441c9499080743281dcf`. Review inspected code; runtime proof was run separately.

### ClawSweeper follow-up

Addressed the [CSS-budget finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197388#issuecomment-6808052002) from `bc6ccd204cd041f6d5ba047fbcc71a26cbd7dfdd`: neutral unloaded-preview values now come from the existing swatch style memo, not an added stylesheet rule. The budget and baseline are unchanged.

- Paired production builds on the same toolchain: total CSS **1,705,417 → 1,705,287 raw bytes (−130 B)** and **331,126 → 331,109 gzip bytes (−17 B)**. Startup, chat, and new-session boot bytes are unchanged. This removes the full 130-byte increase identified by CI.
- The native performance checker passes comparing the repaired build with the reviewed-head build. The full archived target-base wrapper exceeded this sandbox’s 1 GiB temporary filesystem; exact target-base CI remains the authoritative fresh-head check.
- Added a held plugin-palette read to the existing E2E: both chips stay neutral while loading, then switch to the theme’s own palette. The E2E and 23 affected browser cases pass; unchanged owner/token proof is reused. Fresh E2E: 1.3 s test time, 13.8 s including build; browser suite: 1.4 s.
- Fresh UI typecheck, targeted lint/stylelint, formatting, test-line guard, and independent P0–P2 Auto Review pass. Existing screenshots are retained because the intended appearance is unchanged. New-head CI is pending.

### Visual proof

Synthetic themes in the production UI; Knot remains selected in both dark-mode captures.

**Before**

![Before: plugin and personal themes inherit Knot’s red and gray palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2411bf4b-1c37-43f2-9858-1c391a5cb35f)

**After**

![After: Evergreen uses green and gold; Lavender keeps its light-only purple palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc2683e7-1521-4f2a-8c3d-5cf9ce336ae8)

<details>
<summary>Light-mode preview</summary>

![Light mode: Evergreen switches to its light palette while Lavender retains its only palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7af80906-f04f-42de-aa38-4bba2da384a6)

</details>

<details>
<summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

The existing catalog remains the only palette cache; no second request/state owner was added. Removed the shared active-palette rendering path for catalog cards. Production delta: +42 lines; regression-test delta: +203 lines, recorded in a dedicated test-line allocation. No new effects, imperative DOM queries, native listeners, or controller/owner escape hatches.

</details>

Reported by Jacqueline Henriksen.

prs.body:
Idea and direction from @jjjhenriksen and @vyctorbrzezowski.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jjjhenriksen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b2da1949-0fe2-4875-baa4-194927f1e6ba)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/bb931058-ecfd-42d9-8501-3413e9a00c0d)
- [Source and patch review](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/28bd033a-23a0-4996-b7ae-753a1ae83101)

Stacked on #197388 until it merges; base: openclaw/glow-langoustine-2 at b1501b63c14ebc85c31cd19d5a314fd4fb51d78d. Draft only; no merge requested.

## What Problem This Solves

Installed theme-plugin details do not show what their themes will look like before users select them.

## User Impact

Users can inspect each installed theme’s colors and mode-specific artwork in a compact OpenClaw chat preview without changing their current theme or sending a message. A single-purpose, single-theme plugin uses the same palette chip as Appearance; multi-theme and mixed-capability plugins retain their normal identity artwork. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Share the existing palette chip and a narrow compact-chat renderer while keeping palette readiness, supported-mode selection, artwork loading and retry with their existing owners. Recommended prompts reuse the window without changing their buttons, onSelect, busy/disabled state or unsent-draft launch behavior. Their superseded RGB-mask renderer and six exclusive artwork files are removed. There is no new palette cache, loader, route or catalog feature, and the preview does not fabricate a reply.

## Evidence

- Production Control UI with an isolated mock Gateway: public Artemis Canopy 1.0.2 plus Travel Themes palettes and authored light/dark background assets. Appearance chips remain unchanged. No operator Gateway was touched.
- The installed-preview reproduction is red on the exact base and green with this change. Its production-UI regression also verifies dark-only mode fallback, palette failure/owner Retry, no perpetual skeleton, no theme mutation and no chat send.
- Focused owner/detail checks: 33 passed. Browser checks cover Appearance, SVG artwork, recommendation layout and contrast; 24 affected cases were rerun after consolidation. All 10 recommendation-action E2Es pass. Latest installed-preview E2E: 1.5 seconds test time / 13.8 seconds wall including production build; focused detail unit file: 2.4 seconds wall. Hosted CI timing is not yet available for this draft.
- UI build, UI typecheck, targeted Oxlint/Stylelint, formatting, i18n verification, controller guards, diff checks and staged test-line budget pass.
- Exact-base paired asset check passes without raising budgets: total CSS 1,705,287 → 1,705,349 raw bytes (+62) and 331,109 → 331,126 gzip bytes (+17), within the existing 64-byte variance allowance. Startup JS is unchanged. Shared chip rules live in the existing settings-control sheet: startup CSS +280 gzip bytes, still one request and within its existing growth allowance. The standalone chip stylesheet and duplicate preview chrome are gone.
- Fresh independent Auto Review (OpenClaw, GPT-6.1 Sol), P0–P2, reports no findings on the complete candidate against the exact stacked base. Reviewed staged-patch SHA-256: 864e60b65bcc5f55cf7c53cd3b73a27f1f634e850b77b507c9329b46cd7438fe. Parent source review covered the chip, artwork flag, eligibility, mode fallback and narrow rendering contract. Runtime proof was run separately; broad CI and live Gateway installation are not claimed.

- Publication follow-up: the managed publisher retained only @jjjhenriksen’s commit co-author trailer; @vyctorbrzezowski’s trailer still needs publisher-side repair. Both idea contributors are credited above.

<details>
<summary>Size and simplification</summary>

26 files: +792/−268 textual lines, plus four removed PNGs. Tests/helpers +309/−24 (net 285, scoped allocation); logic/projection wiring +29/−4; UI renderers +299/−96; CSS +140/−128; docs +1/−1; English/baseline/allocation +14/−0; retired artwork source notes/SVG −15. Production growth serves the new preview and retry flow; no controller, effect, cache or request owner was introduced. Existing contrast and prompt-action proof is retained while obsolete mask-geometry assertions are removed.

</details>

### Visual proof

Public theme data in the real production UI with an isolated mock Gateway.

prs.title: fix(node-host): Windows node commands cannot use the allowlist or auto-review because of the cmd.exe wrapper
prs.body:
Closes #157930

## What Problem This Solves

On a Windows node host, every `system.run` command is wrapped as `cmd.exe /d /s /c <command>`. The node intentionally treats that wrapper as an allowlist miss (`windowsShellWrapperBlocked`), because cmd.exe changes the meaning of quotes and builtins. As a result, no allowlist entry or durable approval can ever apply on a Windows node: every command needs a human approval, even an absolute-path executable that is explicitly allowlisted.

## User Impact

An operator can now allowlist an executable on a Windows node (for example `C:\Users\me\.local\bin\claude.exe`) and the agent can run it with varying arguments without an approval each time. Commands that genuinely need cmd.exe (operators outside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat` scripts) keep the existing wrapper and the existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

#157930 suggests binding and reviewing the inner command of the canonical wrapper. This PR takes the narrower route of not sending the wrapper when it is not needed: when a Windows command has no cmd.exe operator outside quotes, no builtin as its first word, and no `.cmd`/`.bat` target, the Gateway sends it to the node as a direct argv. The `windowsShellWrapperBlocked` rule is untouched, and the node's existing direct-argv path, allowlist and approval binding apply unchanged.

Splitting follows both Windows command-line rules (`CommandLineToArgvW` and the current C runtime) and only accepts a command when both yield the same argv; otherwise it keeps cmd.exe. Characters such as `& | < > ^ ( ) % !` and newlines are literal inside quotes and stay on the direct path; `%VAR%` is not expanded there, and the approval card shows the exact argv that runs. The Gateway approval precheck evaluates that same argv, so it never authorizes more than the node does.

## Evidence

- Unit tests for the splitter: eligible commands, every cmd.exe metacharacter inside and outside quotes, escaped quotes and backslash runs, doubled quotes, newlines inside quotes, builtins, `.cmd`/`.bat`, shell wrappers.
- Gateway tests for the argv sent to the node on both paths and for equality between the approved text and the executed argv.
- Real Windows integration test through the node handler: the child receives `a & b | c < d > e ^ f (g) 50% %PATH% !x! say "hi"` plus a newline exactly; `allow-always` is offered for an ordinary executable and reused.
- Real behavior proof: on a Windows 11 node paired with a Linux Gateway, with `claude.exe` in the node allowlist, the agent ran `claude.exe -p "<prompt with ( ) & % ? and accents>" --permission-mode plan` with no approval prompt, and Claude Code answered the full prompt. Before this change, the same calls required an approval each time and logged `Exec auto-review skipped: dispatch chain cannot be bound`; after it, that line no longer appears.
- Not run locally: the full test suite.

prs.title: feat(backup): omit Doctor migration originals from archives on request
prs.body:
Closes #183277

**Decision:** Option A, approved in the [maintainer review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194823#pullrequestreview-5829109969).
`openclaw backup create` keeps Doctor's retained pre-migration originals by default, and
`--exclude-migration-backups` omits them. This follows the existing opt-in `--exclude-worktree-templates` flag
(#190822). All four items from that review are addressed (see "Why This Change Was Made").

## What Problem This Solves

Full backup archives carry every retained Doctor original as raw bytes next to the live database snapshot.
That makes archives much larger and slower after each update, with no way to leave the originals out.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can run `openclaw backup create --exclude-migration-backups` to leave Doctor's retained
pre-migration originals out of an archive. Each omitted file is listed as `excluded`. Archives made without the
flag are unchanged.

A restored archive made with the flag cannot roll back the last migration with those originals. The docs say
so. The flag never deletes or changes the originals on disk; `openclaw update cleanup` still owns their
retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The flag matches only the exact names Doctor writes beside the shared state database and each registered
  agent database:
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak` (full SQLite original)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.scoped.bak` (scoped SQLite original)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.postgres.bak` (PostgreSQL backup directory, omitted as a whole
    and listed once)
  - `<database>.pre-startup-migration-restart-recovery-<uuid>.bak` (SQLite original saved before a
    restart-recovery session repair)

  Look-alike names and other `.bak` files stay included. A repo-wide search found no other
  `pre-startup-migration` producers.
- The exclusion goes through the backup resource plan, like `--exclude-worktree-templates`. Each omitted file
  appears in `skipped` (kind `migration backup`, reason `excluded`) in the dry-run plan, the text and JSON
  output, and the archive manifest. The reason is not `regenerable`, because these files are recovery
  artifacts.
- Doctor's original names are built and classified in one module,
  `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.ts`, next to `doctor-migration-backup.ts`. All four producers
  (`doctor-migration-backup.ts`, `doctor-postgres-migration.ts`, `doctor/shared/session-entry-rewrite.ts`)
  build their names there, and backup planning and the restore manifest classify names there, so the matcher
  cannot drift from the writers. The rule is not in `doctor-migration-backup.ts` itself because the restore
  manifest importing that file creates an import cycle (`doctor-migration-backup` ->
  `doctor-migration-backup-artifacts` -> manifest) and pulls SQLite worker code into backup planning.
- The restore manifest still accepts only the full and scoped SQLite originals, the only formats Doctor
  records in manifests. PostgreSQL and restart-recovery paths are rejected there, as before.
- `docs/cli/backup.md` documents the flag, every omitted format and the rollback tradeoff.
  `repair-and-recovery.md` points to it.
- The final test-line allocation is 214: 88 naming-test lines plus 126 archive-regression lines.
  The added coverage protects retired-store discovery and lexical/physical database aliases; current-head CI remains required.

## Evidence

### Follow-up: retained stores and physical aliases

The [signed correction](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/commit/88285352f5994b9b8f4e554b1868776fd3c64859) preserves the original contributor ancestry and fixes two additional discovery omissions without changing Option A:

- Reuse the existing complete agent-store discovery owner, including disk-only retired stores and retained registry-only custom paths, rather than only the configured roster.
- Match originals beside both lexical database locators and physical file-alias targets, matching Doctor’s canonical SQLite naming while preserving lexical-name support.
- Extend the same create/verify/archive-member/restore regression with both unconfigured-store routes and an alias-only registration. Exact archive paths prevent shared-basename false positives. Defaults, source originals, look-alikes, manifest reporting, whole PostgreSQL-directory omission and live database restoration remain covered.

The unconfigured-store defect fails on published `230674856fe149723df1b81585f277821ac2c3c4`; the physical-alias defect separately fails with the first repair already applied. Both fail at the actual archive-member omission assertion, then pass after the complete repair. Secretless focused proof passes **32 tests across four files**, focused formatting/lint, core typecheck and infra-test typecheck. The wrapped test command takes 84.01 s including cold worker preparation; the primary archive scenario takes about 6 s because it creates, verifies and restores real archives.

Local Auto Review covered the complete staged candidate against `5a2b6e131c309f6986e44509e95ee659302caab9` at P0–P2 and was scoped-clean; the staged bytes were committed unchanged as `88285352f5994b9b8f4e554b1868776fd3c64859`. A separate fresh independent source review found no likely/high-impact P0–P2 findings. The initial local review’s two INDEX-only findings were resolved by staging the already tested repairs; that earlier incorrect-index verdict is not called clean.

The optional full `check:changed` remains **failed** at the dead-export scan: the same normalized set of 58 reported exports is reproduced on a fresh unmodified copy of `230674856fe149723df1b81585f277821ac2c3c4`. All other selected checks completed successfully; no skip or baseline exception was enabled. [Exact new-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43303668867) remains the required broad proof; the local attribution does not waive it. Synthetic PostgreSQL originals exercise directory omission, not live PostgreSQL capture; Windows was not newly exercised.

The original CLI/upgrade measurements and command receipts below retain their original executing revisions and are not relabeled as executions of the corrected head.

**Shipped CLI, real Doctor originals.** On an isolated state directory, OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (latest stable)
created an agent. Current main's `openclaw doctor --fix` then migrated the databases (agent schema 27 to 41,
state 22 to 39), which left three real originals: one agent `.bak`, one state `.bak` and one state
`.scoped.bak`. Doctor writes the other two formats only during PostgreSQL migrations and restart-recovery
repairs, so I added one of each with Doctor's exact names (a restart-recovery copy of the agent database and a
`.postgres.bak` directory with a 4,096-byte file), plus two look-alikes that must stay
(`...pre-startup-migration-notauuid.bak`, `...pre-startup-migration-<uuid>.bak.old`). Each run below is
`node openclaw.mjs backup create` from a `pnpm build` of main dc0ab0240fa or of this branch rebased on it.

| Run | Members | Uncompressed bytes | Doctor originals in archive | Compressed bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main, default `--verify` | 63 | 5,381,400 | 5 (3 real, 2 added) | 180,402 |
| this PR, default `--verify` | 64 | 5,494,001 | 5 | 197,093 |
| this PR, `--exclude-migration-backups --verify` | 58 | 2,648,564 | 0 | 134,488 |

- Main rejects the flag: `OpenClaw does not recognize option "--exclude-migration-backups".`
- Default archives have the same member names on main and on this PR. The one extra member on this PR,
  `state/openclaw.sqlite.seal` (112,601 bytes), is the state database's clean-close seal. It appeared on disk
  between the two runs and is unrelated to this change.
- On this PR, the flagged archive lacks exactly six members compared with the default one: the three real
  originals, the restart-recovery file, and the PostgreSQL directory with its file. Both look-alikes stay.
  The manifest grows by 1,283 bytes for the five new `skipped` entries (the directory is listed once).
- Main and the default run each warn five times about SQLite files archived as opaque bytes, four of them for
  the originals. The flagged run keeps only the unrelated warning.
- `backup restore` of the flagged archive into a fresh target returns `ok: true` and
  `sqliteInventoryVerified: true`, and restores 58 entries. The only `pre-startup-migration` names in the
  target are the two look-alikes. The restored agent and state databases pass `PRAGMA integrity_check` at
  `user_version` 41 and 39, the same as live.
- Every `pre-startup-migration` file on disk has the same SHA-256 before and after all runs.

<details>
<summary>Text output with the flag</summary>

```
Skipped 9 paths:
- workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace (missing)
- agent: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent (covered by ~/.openclaw)
- plugin skills: ~/.openclaw/plugin-skills (regenerable)
- managed state: ~/.openclaw/tmp (regenerable)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555.postgres.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-cc3f463f-378c-4112-812f-e4bf675240eb.scoped.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-e9a1d31a-6dfc-8015-86ba-d688b1710ad5.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-e9a1d31a-6dfc-8015-86ba-d688b1710ad5.bak (excluded)
- migration backup: ~/.openclaw/agents/work/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite.pre-startup-migration-restart-recovery-11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555.bak (excluded)
```

</details>

**Regression tests.** In `src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts` ("backup Doctor migration originals"),
a default archive contains full, scoped and restart-recovery agent originals, a full state original, and a
PostgreSQL backup directory with nested content. A flagged archive omits exactly those and keeps look-alike
names. It lists each one as `excluded` in the result and manifest, and lists the directory only once. The
archive restores, and the originals stay on disk. With only this test file applied to main dc0ab0240fa, it
fails (`AssertionError: expected true to be false` on the first flagged archive member check); with this
change it passes. In `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.test.ts`, every produced name round-trips
through the classifier and look-alikes are rejected. A restore manifest accepts full and scoped originals and
rejects PostgreSQL and restart-recovery paths.

**Checks run** (rebased on main dc0ab0240fa)

- `pnpm test src/infra/backup-create.ownership.test.ts src/commands/doctor-migration-backup-names.test.ts`:
  15 and 3 passed.
- Consumers of the changed plan, names, manifest and CLI: `backup-resource-inventory`, `backup-shared`,
  `doctor-migration-backup`, `doctor-session-sqlite-recovery-inventory`, `doctor-session-entry-state`,
  `update-command-missing-originals`, `update-cleanup.stored-manifests`, `update-automatic-cleanup`:
  8 files, 102 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`: OK (slack 0). Main dc0ab0240fa alone is 6 lines over its ceiling.
- `pnpm check:import-cycles`, `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm lint:docs`: pass.
- `pnpm check:changed`: formatting, core and test typechecks, lint, ratchets, import cycles and the other
  guards pass. The dead export scan fails on 17 files this PR does not touch (for example
  `src/process/linux-oom-score.ts`, `extensions/knowledge/src/tool-results.ts`). `pnpm deadcode:exports` on main dc0ab0240fa fails with the identical list.
- The CI `check-lint-core-4` failure on the previous head was a `no-shadow` error in
  `ui/src/e2e/sidebar-rail-alignment.e2e.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; main has since fixed it.

Not covered: an end-to-end run against a live PostgreSQL server (the directory exclusion is covered by the
regression test and the hand-made directory above) and Windows.

prs.title: fix(clawrouter): edit uploaded images with the selected OpenAI model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: uploaded reference images are rejected when users select a supported OpenAI image model through ClawRouter.

## User Impact

Users can edit authorized PNG, JPEG, or WebP references with the exact selected ClawRouter OpenAI image model and credential; text-only generation stays unchanged.

The companion JSON edit route in [openclaw/clawrouter#1002](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/pull/1002) is also merged; deployment has not been verified. It does not deploy or activate that service, change credentials or grants, or relax budgets. Existing hard-budget policies still reject edits because reference-image input tokens do not yet have a safe reservation upper bound, unless an explicit fixed policy tariff already applies. Existing soft/unmetered policies can proceed and settle complete, consistent measured usage; this change does not alter those policies. References are limited to 16, 4 MiB decoded each, and 8 MiB for the whole JSON request. Masks, remote reference URLs/file IDs on the wire, and streaming remain unsupported.

## Why This Change Was Made

Hannes requested OpenAI image editing through ClawRouter and explicitly authorized both the backend and this plugin change. The previous generation-only scope intentionally rejected edits; this change adds the separately granted edit route rather than assuming that generation access also allows editing.

The existing plugin now admits exact qualified models, requires a same-key edit capability and offer, and sends inline references to the edit endpoint. Existing request deadlines, cancellation, SSRF/download guards, secret-safe failures, and non-retrying paid requests remain shared with generation. No core production code, new configuration, SDK surface, or provider substitution is added.

Requested by @hannesrudolph; co-author credit is included in the commit.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(signal): print reply author state degradation on the console
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running the gateway in a container and watching `docker logs -f openclaw-gateway`, a Signal account whose persisted reply-author state cannot be opened or written showed no console output at all: the channel looked healthy while every inbound Signal reply silently lost its quoted-reply author context and fell back to in-process memory. All three degradation warnings in `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts` went through `ctx.runtime.logging.getChildLogger(...)`, and in production that logger only writes the file log, so nothing ever reached stdout/stderr. They now go through the console-capable `createSubsystemLogger("signal/reply-author-state")`.

- Problem: reply-author persistence failures were recorded only in `~/.openclaw/logs/openclaw-*.log`; operators watching process output never saw that Signal had degraded to the memory-only fallback on every message.
- Solution: route the three warnings to the channel subsystem logger that owns the console sink, keeping message text, `{ error }` metadata, control flow, and fallbacks.
- What changed: `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts`, console regression coverage in `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.test.ts` (net +28 test lines), and its allocation `signal-reply-author-console.txt`.
- What did NOT change: store open/write/read paths, memory fallback behavior, warning text, and the deliberate file-level pre-gate in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-logging.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal already sends its other operator-facing warnings through this owner (`createSubsystemLogger("signal/approvals")`, `signal/daemon`), so the reply-author paths were the exception; the same per-site shape shipped for Telegram media failures (#193256) and is open for ClickClack (#193951).

- Best fix: change the sink at each degradation site. The plugin-runtime child logger deliberately only writes the file log (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-logging.ts` pre-gates on `isFileLogLevelEnabled` before `getChildLogger`), and that boundary is shared by every plugin, so the bug belongs to the three call sites that need operator visibility.
- Alternative rejected: a console transport inside `createRuntimeLogging()` — it would duplicate every plugin's file-log line into the console, turning a per-site visibility fix into a core-wide behavior change.

## User Impact

Operators now get one line on the same stream they already watch for channel status, for example `[signal] persistent reply author state unavailable error="Error: state database is locked"`, instead of having to find it in the file log after replies lose quote context. Signal keeps replying and keeps in-process reply context; only persistence is degraded, and that degradation is now visible at the moment it starts.

## Evidence

Shipped Gateway, real channel turn. `openclaw gateway` from this branch (CLI entry `src/entry.ts` via `scripts/tsx.mjs`; the local `dist` build is blocked by an optional Control-UI devDependency missing here), with the real `extensions/signal` plugin, a real HTTP/JSON-RPC + SSE signal-cli peer on loopback, and a real agent turn against a local OpenAI-compatible model. Two inbound DMs from `+15550002222`:

1. healthy store: no console line, and `plugin_state_entries` gets the reply-author row for `id=1794225433653`;
2. store write rejected for the `signal.reply-authors.v1` namespace: the gateway console prints the degradation line, the turn still completes, and the outbound RPC still quotes the author.

```console
2026-11-09T20:03:01.682+08:00 [signal] persistent reply author state failed error="PluginStateStoreError: Failed to register plugin state entry."
2026-11-09T20:03:22.476+08:00 signal rpc send {"message":"Acknowledged.","recipient":["+15550002222"],"quoteTimestamp":1794225780868,"quoteAuthor":"+15550002222","quoteMessage":"State store failure message"}
# plugin_state_entries, account=default|to=+15550002222|id=1794225780868
[]   # the failed registration never persisted; the quoted author came from the memory fallback
```

The write rejection is a temporary SQLite trigger on `plugin_state_entries` for that namespace only — the fault-injection shape `src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.prepared.test.ts` uses — dropped 4 s after the message arrived, so the rest of the turn ran on a healthy store. Store path, transport, and reply flow are unmodified production code; other messages kept persisting in the same run.

Regression test, red on base with the test kept, green with the fix:

Console regression coverage — base = the same test file run against `origin/main`'s `reply-authors.ts` (3 failed), PR = green. The lookup case fails while registration reads the existing entry; it does not exercise the separate resolve-time lookup catch:

| warning site | base | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| store open fails | silent (file log only) | `[signal] persistent reply author state unavailable error="…"` |
| register fails | silent (file log only) | `[signal] persistent reply author state failed error="…"` |
| lookup during registration fails | silent (file log only) | `[signal] persistent reply author state failed error="…"` |

Shipped Gateway run, healthy vs rejected store write (same process, consecutive messages):

| | healthy store | write rejected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| console line | none | `[signal] persistent reply author state failed error="…"` |
| `plugin_state_entries` row | 1 (`id=1794225433653`) | 0 (`id=1794225780868`) |
| outbound `send` quote | `quoteAuthor=+15550002222` | `quoteAuthor=+15550002222` |
| turn outcome | replied | replied |

```console
$ npx vitest run extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
$ FORCE_COLOR=1 npx vitest run extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.test.ts   # CI forces color
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

`watchConsoleWarnings()` matches visible text only: `lines()` runs `console.warn` output through `stripVTControlCharacters` from `node:util`, the same normalization `src/gateway/health/collector.session-store-path.test.ts` uses, so the cases hold with and without SGR styling.

Consumer tests of every other caller of the module (`media-access`, `core`, `event-handler.inbound-context`, `event-handler.mention-gating`): `Test Files 4 passed (4) / Tests 89 passed (89)`.

Gates: `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json` 0 warnings/0 errors; `oxfmt` clean; `check:test-lines-ratchet` reports `Test lines OK` with this PR's allocation. `tsgo` cannot run on this host (native binary needs GLIBC 2.29), so type checking used `tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json`: 0 errors in `extensions/signal/**`.

Not tested: no real Signal account, hosted signal-cli, or container (the peer speaks the same JSON-RPC/SSE contract on loopback); console assertions cover `consoleStyle: "compact"` only, not `pretty`/`json`.

No duplicate: `gh search prs` for "reply-authors", "reply author state", "createSubsystemLogger" and "operator console warning" finds only #193951 (ClickClack, different file); the open Signal quote PRs (#195752, #195044, #195105) do not touch `extensions/signal/src/reply-authors.ts`.

prs.title: fix(clickclack): show discussion attachment failures on the console
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When ClickClack discussion routing fails to persist a refreshed discussion binding, the inbound message is dropped for that turn and the only record of why goes to the plugin log file. Nothing reaches the console.

`resolveClickClackDiscussionRoute()` catches a throw while resolving the discussion route (`extensions/clickclack/src/discussions/routing.ts:75-81` on `main`), warns, and returns the revoked state. That state is a hard gate: `access.ts:186` records it and `access.ts:440` refuses dispatch. A transient storage error — `SQLITE_FULL`, a locked database, a brief I/O failure — silently stops the bot from answering in that conversation.

The warning itself is fine; its *destination* is not. `runtime.logging.getChildLogger()` only attaches the core file transport (`buildLogger()` in `src/logging/logger.ts`), so a container or systemd operator watching stdout sees nothing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix routes this one warning through the console-capable subsystem logger the plugin SDK already exports.

`createSubsystemLogger()` comes from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` and writes to both file and console, honouring `consoleLevel`. This is the same correction shape as the sibling site in `inbound.ts` (#193951). No new logging surface, no config option, and no change to how `revoked` is computed.

- Warning text, `String(error)`, and `return { state: "revoked" }` are unchanged — egress only; fail-closed delivery is still the right answer.
- `"clickclack/discussions"` mirrors the previous `{ plugin, feature }` context. `createSubsystemLogger` reuses the same file logger via `getChildLogger({ subsystem })` (`src/logging/subsystem.ts:357`).
- `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-logging.ts` is untouched — changing `getChildLogger()` itself would alter every plugin's output at once.

The regression test now asserts on `console.warn`, not the `getChildLogger` call record: the call-record check passed on broken code. No open PR touches these files; #190322, #189977, #193951 and #164122 are file-disjoint.

## User Impact

Operators running ClickClack discussions in containers or as a daemon now see the failure on stdout instead of a silent bot. Delivery behaviour is unchanged (the message is still not dispatched), and there is no config, migration, or log-path change.

## Evidence

Head `dbd72c83d465de32eb82c4ce6894ed3527656082`. Everything below was measured, not stubbed: no logger mock and no injected transport.

### Isolated running Gateway (before vs after)

Both arms use the shipped entry (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run`) on loopback with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`/config and a local ClickClack protocol peer. The persisted discussion binding carries a pre-reset `sessionId`, so the next refresh must write; the stored binding value sits over the plugin-state 1 MiB write limit, so that write throws `PluginStateStoreError: plugin state value exceeds 1048576 byte limit` while reads and ingress keep working. The event (`message.created`, `msg_proof_1` in `chn_proof`) arrives over the real WS, and the Gateway then fetches `GET /api/messages/msg_proof_1`.

Before — `main`'s `routing.ts` restored in the worktree, same seed, same event. Console has no warning; only dispatch denial:

```
2026-11-09T21:11:23.975+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (21 plugins: … clickclack …; 230.4s)
2026-11-09T21:12:16.335+08:00 [clickclack] [default] skipped ClickClack message before agent dispatch: kind=group requireMention=false wasMentioned=false hasAnyMention=false commandAuthorized=true
```

After — this branch, same seed, same event:

```
2026-11-09T20:54:49.292+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (21 plugins: … clickclack …; 181.3s)
2026-11-09T20:55:34.707+08:00 [clickclack] discussion attachment refresh failed for channel chn_proof: PluginStateStoreError: plugin state value exceeds 1048576 byte limit
2026-11-09T20:55:34.727+08:00 [clickclack] [default] skipped ClickClack message before agent dispatch: kind=group requireMention=false wasMentioned=false hasAnyMention=false commandAuthorized=true
```

| Observable | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Warning lines on stdout | 0 | 1 |
| Dispatch-denial line on stdout | 1 | 1 |
| `POST /api/channels/chn_proof/messages` | none | none |
| Agent turn (`taskKind=turn`) | absent | absent |
| Persisted binding row | `value_bytes=1200561`, stale `session_id` | same, unchanged |

### Regression test (red → green)

New `console.warn` assertion against `main` production code, in this file's lane (`test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`):

```
 FAIL  extension-database-workers  extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.mention-gating.test.ts > ClickClack inbound mention gating > records attachment persistence failures before dropping inbound delivery
AssertionError: expected '' to match /discussion attachment refresh faile…/su
+ Received:
""
 ❯ extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.mention-gating.test.ts:209:56
 Tests  1 failed | 53 skipped (54)
```

Same command on this branch:

```
 ✓ extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.mention-gating.test.ts > ClickClack inbound mention gating > records attachment persistence failures before dropping inbound delivery 45ms
 Tests  54 passed (54)
```

Affected shards (`node scripts/test-projects.mts --changed origin/main`): `extension-database-workers` 4 files/108 tests, `extensions` 7 files/72 tests, 503.99s. `oxfmt --check` clean; `oxlint` 0 warnings and 0 errors; test-line ratchet 1 line slack; line-cap ratchet 2 changed source files. Net production delta +2 lines; no new test file, allocation, or baseline change.

prs.title: fix(cli): let image TTL sweep recur within a long-running process
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running a long-lived OpenClaw process with CLI image prompts — after the first image write to a cache root, stale files are never pruned again, even if the process stays up for weeks and new files exceed the 7-day TTL. The cleanup only runs after a restart. The fix replaces a one-shot Set guard with a Map that tracks the last-sweep timestamp per root, gated by a 24-hour recurrence interval, and clears the timestamp on I/O failure so the next call retries.

- Problem: `sweptCliImageRoots` was a `Set<string>` that permanently marked each cache root as "swept once". Once added, `Set.has()` always returned true and `sweepCliImageRoot` returned early forever — within a single process lifetime, TTL pruning effectively ran at most once per root regardless of wall-clock elapsed since the first sweep.
- Solution: Replace the permanent boolean Set with `lastCliImageRootSweepMs: Map<string, number>` and a `CLI_IMAGE_SWEEP_RECURRENCE_MS = 24h` gate. A sweep re-runs whenever `nowMs - lastSweep >= 24h`. On I/O failure inside the sweep, clear the timestamp so the next caller retries instead of carrying a stale mark.
- What changed: `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts` — two constants + one Map at module top, and the first ~20 lines of `sweepCliImageRoot`. A focused vitest proof case was also folded into the existing `writeCliImages` describe.
- What did NOT change: The 7-day `CLI_IMAGE_SWEEP_TTL_MS` used by `fileStore().pruneExpired`. The sweep call site (`writeCliImages` → `sweepCliImageRoot`) and the I/O call itself (`pruneExpired({ ttlMs })`) are untouched. No other file was modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the smallest possible surgical fix: swap the in-process deduplication primitive from a permanent Set to a timestamped Map with a well-chosen recurrence window. A hard-coded 24-hour interval (next to the 7-day TTL constant) balances two concerns — we do not want to re-scan the image cache on every single CLI prompt, but we also do not want stale files to live past the 7-day TTL simply because the process survived longer than one day. Catching the pruneExpired I/O failure and deleting the timestamp matches a minor defect noted at discovery time: the previous code also carried the "swept" mark past the failure, and subsequent calls silently skipped.

**Alternatives considered**:
- `Set` + `delete()` on a ticker — requires a background timer and increases lifecycle surface area; rejected.
- `process.once("beforeExit")` — the bug is the opposite (long lifetime, not short); rejected.
- Per-root next-sweep-at pre-computation — semantically identical to timestamp-plus-interval, just expressed differently; kept the timestamp form because it also surfaces on-disk debugging ("last swept at X").

**Risk boundaries**:
- The Map grows without bound if the process keeps writing to an unbounded number of distinct `imageRoot` values. In practice these map to a small finite set (each workspace's `.openclaw-cli-images` plus a global tmp dir); still worth calling out.
- `Date.now()` drives both the recurrence gate and the TTL inside `pruneExpired` (`@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.27.1 compares `Date.now()` against `stat.mtimeMs`), so both gates read the wall clock. A backward jump of X delays the next sweep by X + 24h rather than "until the next wall-clock drift in the opposite direction". That is still bounded — too-frequent sweeps are harmless, and an overdue sweep is bounded by the next forward drift — so there is no correctness break, but the timing does shift with wall-clock changes. If the recurrence gate ever needs to be immune to clock jumps, `monotonicNow()` in `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts` is available; the caveat is that the libfaketime proof runs with `FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC=1`, so a monotonic gate would no longer move in that harness.

## User Impact

Users and operators running long-lived OpenClaw processes now get periodic TTL cleanup of the CLI image cache every 24 hours. Stale files stop accumulating after the first 7 days of process uptime. No user-visible behavior changes in the happy path — the change is purely about when cleanup happens, not whether image prompting continues to work. Operators should observe `.openclaw-cli-images/` directories staying bounded in size without requiring a process restart.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `66df5fcbbce` (fix + proof test, squashed onto current `main`)
- Baseline main SHA: `437b1571fd5` (pre-fix parent of this commit; Set guard present)
- Production entry: `prepareCliPromptImagePayload` → `writeCliImages` → `sweepCliImageRoot` (the guard lives here)
- Canonical owner exercised: `sweepCliImageRoot` (not exported; reached through `prepareCliPromptImagePayload`, which IS exercised by existing vitest infrastructure)

### Behavior matrix (before / after)

| Scenario | Input | Baseline (Set guard, main) | Fixed (Map + 24h interval) |
|---|---|---|---|
| First sweep, fresh root | Stale file (8d old, exceeds 7d TTL) | sweep runs → file removed ✅ | sweep runs → file removed ✅ |
| Second sweep within 24h of first | New stale file | `Set.has = true` → skipped → file remains ⚠️ | `now - lastSweep < 24h` → skipped → file remains (consistent) |
| Second sweep after 25h | New stale file | `Set.has = true` → skipped forever → file remains ❌ | `now - lastSweep >= 24h` → sweep runs → file removed ✅ |
| pruneExpired I/O failure | Exception thrown | Set already added → future calls still skipped ❌ | `Map.delete` clears timestamp → next caller retries ✅ |

### Pre-fix RED (main source reverted, test kept)

With the pre-fix `Set` guard restored and the current test kept, the recurrence assertion fails: 25 simulated hours have passed and a fresh 8-day-old stale file is on disk, but the guard returns early, so `fs.access` resolves and the `.rejects` assertion reports:

```console
AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
  ❯ src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:368  await expect(fs.access(staleAfter)).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "ENOENT" })
```

This proves the bug: on the second call to `prepareCliPromptImagePayload`, 25 simulated wall-clock hours have passed, a fresh 8-day-old stale file exists on disk, and the test expects pruneExpired to have removed it. The Set guard skips the sweep and the file remains.

### Post-fix GREEN (fix source, same test)

Terminal output verbatim — the focused proof test now passes, and the full helpers suite still passes (no regression):

```console
$ git checkout HEAD -- src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts
$ npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts --reporter=dot

· · · · · · · · · · · · ·
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)   // 12 existing + 1 new proof case
   Duration  30.24s
```

### Real behavior proof — shipped gateway entry, one long-lived process

The vitest case above shows the regression, but it runs in-process. This is the same behavior
observed through the shipped entry point, with a single long-lived process serving both turns.

Setup (no repo changes; `git status` clean apart from the lockfile):

- Entry point: `openclaw gateway run` (repo bin entry, `src/entry.ts`). The gateway process is the
  process that executes the CLI backend and therefore owns the sweep guard.
- Turns are driven by the shipped client entry: `openclaw agent -m "<prompt>" --json --session-key …`,
  which routes to that same gateway process.
- CLI backend: shipped `google-gemini-cli` (imagePathScope=workspace). Its binary is replaced on
  `PATH` by a local stub that records argv and emits a minimal valid stream-json response, so no
  external model is called. The image pipeline, `writeCliImages`, `sweepCliImageRoot`, the
  filesystem and the file mtimes are all real; nothing in `src/**` is patched or mocked.
- Clock: libfaketime 0.9.7 via `LD_PRELOAD` with a dynamic timestamp file (`+0s` → `+25h` between
  turns), plus `FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC=1` so timers/heartbeats/leases stay on real time.
  `Date.now` / `Date` are **not** monkey-patched and there is no test-only clock hook — the code
  under test reads the virtualized clock without knowing about it.

```console
$ LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib64/faketime/libfaketime.so.1 \
  FAKETIME_TIMESTAMP_FILE=/tmp/bug317/clock.txt FAKETIME_NO_CACHE=1 \
  FAKETIME_DONT_FAKE_MONOTONIC=1 \
    node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts gateway run --port 19199 --token <redacted>

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agent \
    -m "Inspect the attached image: <workspace>/pic.png and say ok" \
    --json --session-key agent:main:bug317-turn1
```

Same process for all three turns:

```console
LISTEN 0 511 127.0.0.1:19199 0.0.0.0:* users:(("openclaw-gatewa",pid=964443,fd=158))
    PID                  STARTED     ELAPSED
 964443 Tue Nov 10 12:49:47 2026       08:55 4119808
clock file now: +25h
```

Turn 1 — first sweep runs, the 8-day-old file is pruned:

```console
=== CACHE ROOT BEFORE TURN 1 ===
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>  7 2026-11-02 12:53:12.000000000 +0800 stale-a.bin   # 8 days old
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>  5 2026-11-10 12:53:12.812404542 +0800 fresh.bin

=== CACHE ROOT AFTER TURN 1 ===
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>    5 2026-11-10 12:53:12.812404542 +0800 fresh.bin
-rw------- 1 <uid> <uid> 7831 2026-11-10 12:56:46.xxx +0800 89b906…0225.png      # new image
# stale-a.bin gone
```

Turn 2 — gateway clock advanced +25h, a **second** sweep runs and prunes the next stale file:

```console
=== CREATE SECOND STALE FILE (8 days old) FOR TURN 2 ===
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>    7 2026-11-02 12:56:54.000000000 +0800 stale-b.bin

=== CACHE ROOT AFTER TURN 2 ===
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>    5 2026-11-10 12:53:12.812404542 +0800 fresh.bin
-rw------- 1 <uid> <uid> 7831 2026-11-10 12:57:52.894539506 +0800 89b906…0225.png
# stale-b.bin gone — the pre-fix Set guard early-returns forever and cannot reach this point
```

The gateway's own log timestamps confirm the clock moved inside that one process:

```console
2026-11-10T12:56:46+08:00  [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: … turn 1
2026-11-11T13:57:53+08:00  [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: … turn 2   # +25h, same pid 964443
```

Negative control — a third turn **without** another clock jump must not re-sweep, which shows the
gate is the 24h recurrence and not "sweep on every turn":

```console
=== CACHE ROOT AFTER TURN 3 (stale-c.bin must survive: <24h since last sweep) ===
-rw-rw-r-- 1 <uid> <uid>    7 2026-11-02 12:57:55.000000000 +0800 stale-c.bin   # still present
```

Image delivery succeeded on both turns (the stub received a readable path each time):

```console
--- invocation 1 {"stubPid":996280,"readableImagePaths":["…/.openclaw-cli-images/89b906…0225.png"]}
--- invocation 2 {"stubPid":1002174,"readableImagePaths":["…/.openclaw-cli-images/89b906…0225.png"]}

turn1: status=ok text=["stub-backend-ok turn-1 images=1"]
turn2: status=ok text=["stub-backend-ok turn-2 images=1"]
turn3: status=ok text=["stub-backend-ok turn-3 images=1"]
```

| Turn | Gateway clock | Expected sweep | Observed | Image delivery |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | real | yes (first) | stale-a.bin pruned | ok, images=1 |
| 2 | +25h (same pid) | yes (recurrence elapsed) | stale-b.bin pruned | ok, images=1 |
| 3 | +25h, no further jump | no (<24h since last) | stale-c.bin kept | ok, images=1 |

### Static checks

```console
$ npx oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 2.9s on 2 files with 259 rules using 8 threads.

$ pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet
Test lines OK: 6622897; ceiling: 6623122; slack: 225.
```

### What was not tested

- No real external model call. The runtime proof above uses the shipped `google-gemini-cli` backend
  with its binary swapped for a local stub, so no provider is contacted. That stub only replaces the
  model process; the prompt/image payload, `writeCliImages`, `sweepCliImageRoot` and the filesystem
  are the production paths.
- No real 24-hour wall-clock wait. The gateway clock is virtualized with libfaketime instead, which
  is what makes the recurrence interval observable at all in a test session; `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` is
  deliberately left un-faked so leases/heartbeats behave normally.
- The map-growth unboundedness risk: in practice `imageRoot` values come from workspace dirs plus a single tmp dir, so the set of distinct roots is small and finite; no test specifically forces unbounded growth.
- The hard-coded 24h interval: no test parameterizes it. It lives next to the hard-coded 7d TTL constant at the same module top, matching the style of the existing codebase, and changing it would require consensus on a better value.

### Open PR collision check

Searched all open PR topics and scanned changed-file lists for `src/agents/cli-runner/helpers.ts` on the day of submission. No open PR touches this file. Related CLI-image PRs exist (#262 area) but all target different files under `src/agents/cli-runner/` (prompt serialization, reliability hooks), not `helpers.ts`, and do not overlap the sweepCliImageRoot guard.

prs.title: improve(ui): show message reactions as one quiet tab on the bubble corner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reactions on a chat message sat in a row of bordered chips inside the sender's footer row, where they pushed the sender name aside and grew into several rows on busy messages.

## User Impact

User impact: each message now shows its reactions as one small tab on the outer bottom corner of its bubble, so the sender name stays in place and no row is added.

- One reaction shows only its emoji. More show the three most-used emoji and a total.
- Hovering or focusing the tab names who reacted. Clicking it lists every reaction above the usual palette, and any of them toggles in place.
- The hover toolbar keeps its add-reaction button before and after the first reaction.

Things to know:

- Toggling one specific existing reaction is now two clicks (open the tab, press the reaction) instead of one.
- Flat assistant text has no bubble edge, so its tab shares the hover footer row under the end of the text. Under a short reply the tab starts up to 240px in, capped at half the message column so narrow panes keep it reachable. A footer wider than that meets the tab on hover; this is an accepted edge case.
- On touch, names stay hover/focus-only as before; tapping the tab opens the list with counts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bubble now owns the reactions anchor, so one placement replaces three (group footer, earlier-message action row, inline). That removes the picker hand-off between the action row and the chip row, and the `compact` picker variant that only the chip row used. A caption under images anchors the tab with CSS anchor positioning, so the tab hangs from the caption instead of the wider image box.

## Evidence

Screenshots are from the mocked Control UI with one synthetic stress conversation, in Chromium on Linux. "Before" is the merge base with the same fixture.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before, desktop: chip rows beside the sender name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13f7f8fd-030a-4053-a5ae-5eb1f3f0ae6a) | ![After, desktop: one tab on each bubble corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83a5e555-de11-44c9-8cb4-d1298ec039c8) |
| ![Before, 390px: twelve reactions wrap into six rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79e4a5b7-79ae-4e06-977a-0483a0368b26) | ![After, 390px: one tab with a total](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0451eed7-e00c-4d35-8155-131ebd4dbdf9) |

Dark theme, and odd content (image with a caption, image alone, right-to-left text, a long unbroken link):

| Dark | Odd content |
| --- | --- |
| ![After, dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe994526-6fd4-4f72-8b55-220dca8cf733) | ![After, images, right-to-left text and a long link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b676a38e-a83a-4fd1-b74d-0a514d6d43f6) |

Hovering names who reacted; clicking lists every reaction above the palette:

| Hover | Click |
| --- | --- |
| ![Hover: who reacted, capped at eight kinds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74c18a62-8354-419f-8160-91469d5b92bf) | ![Click: existing reactions above the palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7408b09f-af20-4b51-9c30-15b43ea26303) |

- Focused tests, all passing: `chat-message-reactions.test.ts`, `chat-pane-offline-metadata.test.ts`, `chat-transcript-controller.test.tsx`, `chat-message-group.solid.test.tsx` (78 tests), `chat-message-reactions.browser.test.tsx` (4, Chromium), and the E2E `chat-flow.reactions.e2e.test.ts` (4).
- `tsgo:ui`, stylelint on both stylesheets, `check:control-ui-controllers` and `ui:i18n:verify` pass.
- Visual QA covered light and dark, 1280px and 390px, bubble mode, RTL, counts from 1 to 1.25M, ZWJ, flag, skin-tone, keycap and text-presentation emoji, image with and without caption, code block, table, long unbroken text, a reply above the composer, hover, keyboard focus, and toggling from the opened tab.
- Local review: autoreview (`--mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`, base `bbed5e958a8d`, local head `42ae895c640e`; the published head `73d885b46877` has the same tree) reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. It did not execute the code.
- Delta against the merge base: production +386/−283, tests +140/−90, and one documentation sentence updated.

Gaps:

- WebKit and Firefox were not run locally; no cross-browser coverage is claimed for this change.
- Emoji alignment was measured with Noto Color Emoji only. The half-pixel lift on the tab's emoji is unverified with Apple Color Emoji.
- No real Gateway was exercised; reactions came from the mock gateway.

## Final validation

Read-only sessions can open the summary to inspect every emoji count, while mutation controls remain disabled and the add/search palette stays hidden. Removing write access while the popover is open also disables its existing controls. Flat assistant replies use their message column to size the footer clearance, preserving the tab on narrow and split panes.

- Extended two existing reaction tests for nine reaction kinds and write-access removal; no new permanent test cases.
- 78 focused reaction, group, transcript and offline-metadata tests passed. The final reaction file passed all 16 tests in 1.32 seconds.
- All four existing Chromium browser tests passed in 3.61 seconds. All four original mocked-Gateway reaction E2E cases passed, plus a temporary read-only scenario (five total, 15.64 seconds).
- Temporary production-build E2E proof also passed at 320px and 390px, and in a 320px message column on a 1280px desktop (three cases, 12.69 seconds). The pre-fix 320px tab extended to 354.23px; the repaired tab stays inside its column.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint and stylelint, controller guards, English catalog verification and formatting passed. Fresh independent P0–P2 review of the staged candidate reported no actionable findings; it did not execute the code.
- The rendered proof uses synthetic conversation data and a mocked Gateway. No real Gateway or external channel was exercised. CI run 43309084002 reports +1,183 B raw / +295 B gzip total CSS and +97 B gzip New-session boot JS versus its base. These budget overages are explicitly accepted for this design; they are not classified as inherited failures.

![Read-only counts in a 320px pane](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bc168b4-4def-4a13-837b-535bafcbef23)

## Worked on by

- @vyctorbrzezowski

## Work sessions
