prs.title: fix(onboard): let Enter skip the skills dependency step
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

At the optional "Install missing skill dependencies" step of onboarding, pressing Enter right away shows "Please select at least one option." and does not advance, because the highlighted "Skip for now" row is not ticked.

This PR starts that prompt with "Skip for now" ticked, so Enter continues without installing anything. Ticking dependencies still installs them, including when "Skip for now" stays ticked beside them. The validation rule and the installer are unchanged.

Fixes #195577.

## Evidence

Head `d4aeb9bf0ece126c77c9d400b0aacae78859c186`.

### Real onboarding in a clean macOS 26.6 VM

Package built from this branch with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (build stamp `4e840e4`; `d4aeb9b` changes only the test file), installed with `npm i -g`, and driven with real key presses in Terminal running `openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart --auth-choice skip --skip-channels --skip-search --skip-daemon --skip-health`.

1. **Fresh setup, immediate Enter skips.** The skills prompt opens with "Skip for now" ticked; a single Enter submits it and onboarding moves on to the next step. No validation error appears anywhere in the captured terminal transcript.

   ```
   ◇  Install missing skill dependencies
   │  Skip for now
   │
   ◇  Optional apps ──────
   ```

2. **Existing setup, saved settings kept.** With `skills.install.nodeManager` saved as `pnpm`, onboarding again detects the existing config, and an immediate Enter at the skills prompt skips. Comparing `openclaw.json` before and after: the only change is `wizard.lastRunAt`; `nodeManager: pnpm` and the gateway settings are kept.

3. **Choosing a dependency still installs it.** On the same existing setup, ticking `tmux` beside the preselected "Skip for now" and pressing Enter installs it through Homebrew (`tmux -V` → `tmux 3.7c` afterwards). The config again changes only in `wizard.lastRunAt`.

   ```
   ◇  Install missing skill dependencies
   │  Skip for now, 🧵 tmux
   │
   ◇  Installed tmux
   ```

### Regression test through onboarding's own prompt

`src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts` runs `setupSkills` inside `runWizardWithPromptNavigation(createClackPrompter(...))`, the same navigation-aware prompter onboarding uses, and sends keypresses on stdin: Enter alone must finish without installing, and Down/Space/Enter must install the chosen dependency. A trailing Ctrl-C cancels a prompt that stays open, so a failure ends at once instead of waiting on a timer.

- Without the `initialValues` line in `onboard-skills.ts`: 1 failed, 11 passed (`Enter skips` fails with `WizardCancelledError`).
- On this head: 12 passed (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`).
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt` on the changed files, the test-lines ratchet (the test file is 5 lines shorter than on `main`) and `git diff --check` passed. The full suite was not run locally.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice requests stall before the backing agent starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Talk can recognize and acknowledge a spoken request without ever starting the backing agent. A provider callback can register the request under a different Gateway scope; execution then misses that reservation and creates a second input blocked behind the original.

Related: #183597, reported and investigated by @bdjben. His retained-state analysis establishes the failure structure in native Control UI calls. @Suiah98 also supplied independent live recovery evidence for the registration-wrapper portion of this repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register each consultation under its captured Gateway and carry the exact registered source into the existing session-controller admission path. Reject stale or mismatched sources and consume each consultation's registration once.

Rebased onto main `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`, resolving the integration conflicts while preserving metadata-write authority, asynchronous PostgreSQL-compatible call validation, current retained-authority APIs, accepted-work cleanup, and terminal-write settlement.

## User Impact

Voice requests reach the selected agent and return their answers instead of remaining at an acknowledgement. No new configuration or migration is required by this PR.

## Evidence

Validated runtime head: `518f63b332a69bf1f71400706d3fdb88569605f5`. Current head `3ad8007b26ad87bb2d72ea63ee5c152aed06ba19` adds only the test-line allocation record; production and test source are identical to the built and live-tested runtime.

- The scope-mismatch regression fails on unpatched main because it creates two inputs instead of reusing one; the matching-scope control passes.
- All **130 tests across ten focused files** pass on the integrated candidate, including native-plugin handoff, source identity/FIFO/reuse, browser disconnect/close, permission parity, cancellation, relay adoption, and terminal writes.
- Production and Gateway-other test typechecks, six-file type-aware lint/format checks, and whitespace checks pass.
- Full source build passes, including runtime/plugin bundles, SDK declarations and export checks, CLI startup checks, and Control UI assets.
- Independent inspection of the resolved production diff found no concrete integration regression in the two-file scope.
- The documented test-line budget check passes with a 43-line allocation: the repair adds 443 net test lines against the 400-line allowance. The allocation retains distinct public native-handoff coverage and exact-source identity, cancellation, one-shot reuse, and FIFO regressions. It changes no executable code or tests.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43300181834) and the required CI gate passed for current head `3ad8007b26ad87bb2d72ea63ee5c152aed06ba19`, including the repaired test-line budget check.

### Real Behavior Proof

**Claim:** the complete repair lets an accepted voice consultation execute through the backing agent and deliver its answer as speech.

**Surface and fixture:** the installed Omarchy companion and native GStreamer/WebRTC worker, connected to a real VPS Gateway, GPT-Live, and the configured backing agent. Generated speech asks the agent to check the current date. Capture and playback are pinned to temporary private PulseAudio/PipeWire devices.

**Before:** installed revision `753f48d41b0c705661e7c6fdfafc2d547f58c006` transcribed and acknowledged the question but returned no substantive answer within 100 seconds. The correlated source claim waited at mailbox selection with four pending inputs, following an earlier failed request in the same conversation.

**After:** the VPS runs the complete validated main-plus-PR build. On 2026-11-12 UTC, the correlated source claim had **one input** and transitioned from waiting to selected in approximately **1 ms**. The backing agent executed its check and recorded a successful terminal answer. The voice layer returned the correct date after approximately **25 seconds**, with non-silent reply PCM captured at the companion output. Independent offline dictation recognized Thursday, November, and twelfth in that answer audio.

**Trace:** ready 20:12:26.725; source waiting 20:12:40.183; selected 20:12:40.184; agent terminal answer 20:12:51.731; final voice transcript 20:12:57.880. Temporary audio resources were released and desktop audio defaults were preserved.

**Follow-up validation:** a second live call asked for today's date and then tomorrow's date. Both consultations used one input and were immediately selected; both reached the backing agent and returned the correct voice transcripts. Offline dictation of the follow-up audio recognized Friday, November, and thirteenth. The call stayed active for approximately 78 seconds, including approximately 27 seconds after the final voice transcript, with no unexpected session end. Temporary devices were released and desktop audio defaults were unchanged.

**Limits:** these are three completed consultations across two live calls through the external Omarchy client, not an ordinary browser Control UI test. They use generated input and virtual audio devices, so they do not establish human microphone or physical speaker behavior. The live before and after use different main revisions; the separate red/green regression isolates the PR's admission repair on the pinned main baseline. Raw conversation records, credentials, endpoints, and identifying trace values remain private. This does not establish recovery for every provider failure or long-running session.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/gateway/talk/handlers/client.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/client-agent-runtime.scope.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-native-actions.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/client-permission-parity.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/relay/agent-consult.registration.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/relay/relay-consult-adoption.regression.test.ts \
  src/sessions/session-controller.rpc-sources.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/handlers/client-consult-authority.test.ts \
  src/gateway/talk/client-agent-consult.terminal-writes.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

Human contributor: @bdjben. Original implementation was published by @roboclaw-bot; the integrated repair preserves those commits and contributor credit.

prs.title: fix(onboard): ask for the agent's model after a utility-only provider
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Classic QuickStart can finish Apple utility-only setup without a primary model, causing the first ordinary chat to fail with an OpenAI authentication error (#195576).

## Solution

When utility setup leaves no primary model, preserve the utility selection, display “Choose your agent's model,” and reopen provider selection. Preserve an existing primary model.

Fixes #195576.

## Evidence

Recorded CLI capture from November 9:

```text
◇  Model/auth provider
│  Apple Foundation Models (detected)
◇  Choose your agent's model
│  Pick a provider for your agent's conversations, or Skip for now.
◇  Model/auth provider
│  Ollama
│  Default model set to ollama/qwen3:0.6b
│  AI access works. Replied in 2.7s.
```

Saved configuration retained `apple-fm/system` as utility and `ollama/qwen3:0.6b` as primary. First ordinary chat in the isolated setup returned the correct arithmetic answer. Selected result fields:

```json
{
  "exitCode": 0,
  "status": "ok",
  "provider": "ollama",
  "model": "qwen3:0.6b",
  "executionTrace": {"fallbackUsed": false}
}
```

**Upgrade/preservation, November 12:** Installed stable `2026.11.2` in isolated state, then updated through an integrity-checked package built from `b6eaf2d`. Update exited 0 with status `ok`. The candidate’s version field is `2026.11.1`; the command allowed that lower version field.

Classic QuickStart offered “OpenAI (currently configured)” and “Keep current config,” then completed with exit 0. After update and onboarding, full `agents.defaults`, persisted synthetic auth values, and the workspace sentinel were unchanged. Final model status loaded primary `openai/gpt-5.4`, utility `apple-fm/system`, and `openai:api-key`; database integrity was `ok`.

**Recorded regression:** 19/19 passed on this head; the handoff assertion failed with the pre-fix implementation. Tests were not rerun for this evidence task.

**Limits:** Two-provider secret persistence, real cloud authentication, stable `2026.11.3`, rollback, and browser/TUI chat were not validated. An interrupted optional AI check failed on plugin SDK export `HEARTBEAT_RESPONSE_TOOL_NAME`; the completed preservation run declined that check. Doctor/plugin advisories are recorded with the proof.

## Maintainer Decision

Should classic QuickStart immediately offer primary-provider selection after utility-only setup? The feature owner still needs to choose between this implementation and #195790.

prs.title: feat(chat): edit queued messages and get rejected sends back in the composer
prs.body:
Related: #197846

## What Problem This Solves

A message queued in native chat (iOS and macOS) can only be retried or deleted. To fix a typo you have to delete the message and retype it. When the Gateway rejects a send for good, the text sits in a red "Not sent" bubble instead of coming back to you.

## User Impact

- **Edit:** touch and hold a queued message, or a failed one, and choose Edit. The message leaves the queue and its text and attachments go back into the composer, below anything you were already typing.
- **Restore:** when the Gateway definitely rejected a send and chat history proves it never arrived, the message goes back into an empty composer by itself, with a note: "Not sent: <reason>. Your message is back in the composer."
- **Never loses or duplicates text:** a message that may already have been delivered is never moved.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #197846 gave each chat a saved draft. Edit is one store operation that, in a single transaction, removes the outbox row and appends its text and attachments to that draft. It uses the same canonical-proof lock as cancel, so a row that chat history shows as delivered is removed as confirmed and the draft is not touched. Rows whose delivery is unknown (`delivery_unconfirmed`, branch-parked) offer no Edit, and the store refuses them too.

Auto-restore is an automatic Edit with stricter gates:
- **Rejection kind:** the final attempt was rejected, or the row expired after a single attempt with no unacknowledged send.
- **Proof of absence:** a complete chat history page (or applied delta) for the same agent and session was requested after the failure was first seen and after the last connection change, and the turn never appeared in history this view has observed.
- **Safe moment:** the chat is on screen and active, the composer is empty, and the merge fits the draft limits without evicting other drafts' attachments. Edit, as a user action, may evict.

The gates are re-checked inside the draft write chain, right before the composer changes. A refusal (another view claimed the row, or the draft is full) is remembered for that failure, so it is not retried on every history load.

**Accepted edges** (named in code):
- A refused move that races a keystroke or session switch can leave the text in the draft next to its row.
- A second macOS window on the same draft keeps last-writer-wins.
- A rejected first message in an empty chat restores on the next full history load, not immediately.

## Evidence

**Simulator (iOS 27, isolated local Gateway):** pair, stop the Gateway, send a message (it queues), touch and hold it.

| Build | Menu on the queued message | After choosing Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `main` with #197846 | Copy, Select Text, Reply, Delete | (no Edit) |
| this PR | adds **Edit** | queued bubble gone, text in the composer with the cursor at the end |

Screenshots are in the PR comments, taken on this head (`a333ce50c09`).

**Tests:** every restore gate was disabled one at a time, and its test failed:
- history requested before the failure was seen
- history requested before a connection change
- a turn history already showed (cumulative, including across an empty delta)
- another agent's row (it neither restores here nor blocks a provable row)
- incomplete and lagging pages
- a branch-parked ambiguous live send
- a restore over the gateway draft budget (never evicts)
- `had_unacknowledged_send`
- the pinned failure version
- typing while a restore is on its way (the recheck inside the write chain)
- a restore proved before the draft binds lands when it binds

Edit cases: a queued row, a failed row, a proven-delivered row (removed as confirmed, draft untouched), unconfirmed and branch-parked rows (no Edit), a session switch during the move (no error shown in the new chat), and attachments that keep their stored positions.

**Suites:** the OpenClawKit store and outbox suites pass. Full-run failures are limited to audio and TLS timing tests that also fail on the base and pass in isolation. iOS chat suites pass, except one audio render case that also fails on the base. The macOS app builds. i18n verify reports no changes.

**Reviews:** three second-model review rounds. All findings applied, including the final round's low items, after a simplify pass that shares the attachment SQL with the draft insert path and makes restore use the same Edit rule.

**End to end, with an upgrade from v2026.11.3** (see the PR comment): messages queued on v2026.11.3, including one with a photo, survive the upgrade. Edit moves the text and the full photo into a draft that survives a kill and relaunch. A real Gateway rejection (archived session, three attempts) restores the first message into the empty composer. The second stays "Not sent" because the composer is no longer empty, and Edit then appends it below.

prs.title: fix: bundled runtime assets fail for arbitrary container users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unreadable generated runtime files and missing bundled dependency targets when containers run as arbitrary users, which can prevent the Control UI, plugin assets and runtime modules from loading.

## User Impact

Container users can read shipped application assets and execute declared launchers without widening access to private configuration or operator state. Local image builds accept ordinary group-writable or restrictive source modes, and the mandatory image check uses an unrelated identity within normal rootless UID/GID mappings.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one generated-artifact permission owner across builds, staging, and packaging; verify finished packages and images without repairing them during acceptance. Plugin assets precede staging, required workspace targets stay in the image, and partial development profiles and authenticated historical receipts retain their contracts.

The maintainer correction normalizes only the selected final public image payload, honors executable declarations, and safely separates mode-changing hardlinks only when every alias belongs to that payload. External aliases remain rejected. Already-correct modes are left untouched to avoid unnecessary Docker layer copies. The controlled high-UID release matrix is unchanged.

## Evidence

Current head: `2a00d5a2335e2ce0e6985cf34827e6a5ed3a7ba9`. Contributor history is preserved; main is integrated through `1e6a5af06e3df70b60417c55c2f4e641685b97aa`.

- Resolved current-main conflicts without dropping asynchronous UI/cache publication or plugin consumed-input tracking. Public permission normalization still follows the last metadata/cache writer. The worker-wire test now matches canonical main settlement/queued-turn handling; the superseded PR-local helper was removed.
- Extended the existing cold/warm partial-profile fixture to check late cache metadata permissions. Clarified that arbitrary-UID public reads do not grant access to private state.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 review completed with no actionable findings. Trusted targeted static lint: zero warnings/errors; changed-file formatting and diff checks passed. Contributor code was not executed on the credentialed host. Executable tests and typechecks are delegated to secretless PR CI; current-head CI and ClawSweeper results are pending.
- The previous integrated head's CI failures are not relabeled as flakes or all inherited. Fresh AMD64 image and historical-tag legacy-source proof remain pending. Earlier proof below remains explicitly bound to its original tree.

**Retained permission-repair proof at `2d8aa0aa` (not a rebuild of the new integrated head):**

- [Final isolated proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_110a239f1186e082855266a6b3ea6d87) completed successfully. Validated tree `5d7d59f3f23005d169eb3352a3f314947a6411a6` exactly matches the published `2d8aa0aa` candidate; the remote checkout retained the admitted contributor HEAD while the complete candidate tree was separately bound and checked.

Retained affected-owner/sibling proof: **451 passed** (76.01s); direct declaration-fixture consumer: **11 passed** (27.38s). These overlapping scopes are not summed.

A real bounded Linux user namespace passes using UID/GID `65532:65531` with zero effective capabilities, actual file reads, and unchanged private state.
- Final AMD64 Docker build passed (436.63s). Immutable acceptance read **84,134 files / 8,571 directories / 67 plugins**. Network-disabled, read-only CLI smoke passed; private runtime directories remain `0700`. Final image: `sha256:b35c1a714136e02ff214678dfb5b7d9533e031b36c016d28c33e56bf02689afe`.

ClawSweeper reviewed `a1a056d5` with no code or security findings and complete product-fix scope, but retains a CI-triage hold. These retained checks are not relabeled as current-head results.

**Limits:** this correction was validated with native Linux namespace proof and an AMD64 Docker build, not a fresh full rootless Podman-engine build or new arm64/browser-interaction matrix. The earlier 12-cell evidence below is historical, not current-head proof. No release or merge performed.

prs.title: improve(systems): tidy finished workers and show friendly run names
prs.body:
Related: #165865
Depends on: #163995 (unmerged; do not merge this follow-up first).

## What Problem This Solves

Finished worker rows clutter Systems, and generic names make individual runs difficult to identify.

## User Impact

Finished workers leave the sidebar and mobile picker after 15 minutes by default (10/15/30/60 selectable), with immediate manual clearing and a retained-history view. Task/start-time labels and editable names make runs recognizable across clients. These controls do not reclaim resources or delete diagnostic history; active workers and failed workers still requiring cleanup remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep lifecycle inventory authoritative while storing presentation choices through existing authenticated-user preferences and compare-and-swap updates. The shared Control UI owns this behavior; native clients displaying that UI consume the same implementation.

**Dependency:** The follow-up is commit `079f019294fb87175e6f7371f0d5facb0e0df6a8` over `5cfbf3932db1c714e1196cba404aedb186927ba2` from #163995. Because that prerequisite is not merged and its branch is in the contributor fork, this draft targets main and includes the prerequisite commits. Review the incremental commit separately. Retarget/rebase and rerun affected checks after the prerequisite lands; this is not currently a standalone merge candidate.

## Evidence

Prior exact-commit validation: 42 focused Systems UI tests; 9 browser scenarios covering expiry, rename, manual dismissal, retained history, and interval changes; 22 Gateway environment tests. Full UI/core TypeScript checks, targeted lint, CSS lint, formatting, localization, and diff checks passed. Browser suite wall time: 69.67 seconds including production UI build (19.35 seconds test file); UI focused batch 13.08 seconds; Gateway batch 173.8 seconds wall (163.18 seconds test runner including cold compiled-worker preparation). These are local wall times, not measured hosted CI seconds.

Fresh independent review of all 18 changed files found no actionable code defect. On the unchanged exact head, independently reran:

- `pnpm vitest run ui/src/pages/systems/systems-controller.test.ts ui/src/pages/systems/systems-page.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **27/27 passed**, exit 0; 6.79 seconds runner time, 17.9 seconds including startup.
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/environments.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **22/22 passed**, exit 0; 14.45 seconds runner time, 22.2 seconds including startup.
- Runtime: Node 26.8.2, pnpm 12.5.1. No source changes during the review; earlier browser/typecheck/lint evidence remains exact-head evidence.

### Real paired-client, concurrency, upgrade and restart proof (2026-10-05)

[Sanitized assertion outputs, methodology, and portable replay scripts](https://github.com/genaro23/openclaw/tree/7a516a1e14e96343c0a4e17c21b730b7fb5dbe5d) — all described runs passed at head `079f019294fb87175e6f7371f0d5facb0e0df6a8`.

| Boundary | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Two paired clients, same user | Separate Chromium contexts obtained fresh single-use Dashboard bootstrap links. Verified distinct device identities, issued device auth tokens on both, and the same durable canonical user profile. No authentication check was disabled. |
| New preference writer | Invoked the shipped Systems controller's rename, dismissal, and retention methods against real existing terminal inventory and the actual Gateway/storage owner. Other client received each change without reload. No preference or inventory RPC response was mocked in these live runs. |
| Client reconnect | Reloaded the second client; name, interval, and terminal-state dismissal remained present. |
| Concurrent edits | Held the first outgoing set request on each client until both had read the prior value, then released both unchanged requests. Observed a real server CAS conflict; the shipped writer retried and both different worker-name edits reached both clients and survived reload. No response was fabricated. |
| Unrelated existing data | Compared every unrelated preference entry before/after; unchanged. This profile had an unrelated existing setting, so the comparison was not empty. Original presentation settings were restored with CAS and read back. |
| Actual binary upgrade | In a separate disposable state/port, booted retained prerequisite build `5cfbf3932db1c714e1196cba404aedb186927ba2`, paired two devices, and stored unrelated preference data. Stopped that process and started `079f019` over the same state. Both device identities, canonical profile, and every saved preference value survived. |
| Existing-profile defaults | Before any new-feature preference existed, the upgraded profile received the 15-minute default; reading it did not rewrite existing preferences. |
| Gateway restart | Exercised candidate retention and name/dismissal writers, then stopped/restarted the disposable candidate Gateway against the same state. Names, dismissal timestamps, retention, and unrelated data survived. Both clients reconnected. |
| Fresh candidate profile | A separately created candidate profile had neither feature key, received the 15-minute default, and persisted an interval change through the real writer and reload. |
| Cleanup | Original live settings restored; owned isolated Gateways stopped and their temporary state removed. No production Gateway restart/config/plugin change, worker allocation, or resource reclaim. |

**Exact boundaries:** the actual upgrade baseline is the retained prerequisite build `5cfbf393`, not every published release. The isolated name/dismissal restart scenario supplies one synthetic UI inventory row to the unchanged Systems controller; its authenticated RPC and SQLite-backed preference storage are real. The separate live runs use actual finished-worker inventory. These are web-client proofs, not native-platform acceptance. The added broader source-tree UI fixture is not counted as a passing test; the independently executed replay scripts above supply the passing evidence.

This supersedes the earlier anonymous/unpaired CLI attempt, which was not counted as proof. The product/default decision and dependency integration remain outstanding; successful persistence evidence does not resolve those maintainer decisions.

Review noted non-blocking coverage opportunities for malformed/retention-boundary inputs, the 80-character rename rejection, and the 4000-byte presentation-payload overflow. No claim is made that every input or native platform has been tested.

**Proof boundaries:** Screenshots use synthetic Gateway inventory in desktop/phone-sized browser viewports, not fresh native Windows/Linux/macOS/iOS acceptance. Production deployment is deliberately excluded: earlier local cutover attempts encountered service/plugin recovery failures, so isolated feature validation must not be presented as successful rollout. No live Gateway restart is required to review this change.

### Before

![Before: generic worker labels and retained rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/genaro23/openclaw/0e3f40113bea145e644d6ee55baf6c600f25523e/before.png)

### After: desktop

prs.title: fix(text): gate delivery filters on real tag shape, not bare mentions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming a reply that mentions `relevant-memories` or `minimax:tool_call` without emitting a real tag currently makes the delivery sanitizer re-run the canonical memories/minimax transform over the whole accumulated reply on every delta — a 64 KB reply that only mentions these words pays ~4.1 s (memories) and ~49 s (minimax) of per-append work before it completes. This PR replaces bare-word activation with one bounded tag probe shared by both delivery stages, so ordinary prose stays off the hot path while every shape the canonical transforms strip is still stripped from streamed visible text.

- **Problem**: both filters used bare-word activation tokens. Any mention latched `createActivatedProjector` permanently; with no checkpoint, a latched stage runs `text = transform(input.text)` on the entire accumulated reply for every delta.
- **Solution**: one `createBoundedTagProjector` folds each delta's whitespace runs into a bounded tail and matches a canonical-shaped regex. `memoriesTextFilter` uses `<\s*\/?\s*relevant[-_]memories\b` directly. `minimaxToolCallTextFilter` requires an earlier `minimax:tool_call` (or encoded envelope) marker plus an invocation/tag shape, because the canonical transform also removes completed `<invoke>` blocks whenever that marker occurs — even without an exact `<minimax:tool_call>` token. A bare mention has no such shape and never latches.
- **What changed**: `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts` (the shared probe and both filter definitions), `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts` (whitespace-tag and batch/streaming parity cases), and the test-lines allocation. Net PR surface: ****182 changed lines including deletions** (172 added, 10 removed)**.
- **What did NOT change**: the `transform` bodies (`stripRelevantMemoriesTags`, `stripMinimaxToolCallXml`) are untouched, so batch parity, syntax ownership, code protection, and `recoverUnclosed` streaming semantics are preserved exactly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repo invariant at `model-special-tokens.ts:148-149` ("Delivery filter: batch parity through `transform`, bounded work through `create`") requires bounded work once a stage activates. These two delivery stages were the last that still latched on a bare word and re-scanned the whole reply per delta; every other stage already ships a `create`/`checkpoint`.

- **Best fix**: keep the canonical `transform` as the single source of truth and only replace activation gating. The carried tail and the incoming delta are normalized **together** before truncation, so a whitespace run delivered as many one-character deltas still collapses to one space instead of pushing the opening `<` out of the 32-character tail. Shape and marker are latched **independently and order-free**: the canonical MiniMax transform needs its marker anywhere in the accumulated text, so an `<invoke>` shape seen before the marker must still be remembered. One character after a shape match is required, which confirms a delta-split `\b` boundary instead of latching on a partial tag word.
- **Alternative considered**: literal tag-shaped activation tokens (the earlier revision of this PR). Rejected after review on two counts: literal tokens cannot express the parser's unbounded `\s*` or a tag word split across deltas, and they miss the invocation-cleanup path where a completed `<invoke>` block is stripped without an exact minimax envelope. A fixed-size raw tail probe was also rejected, since an unbounded whitespace run can push the `<` out of the window.
- **Original activation intent in both profiles is preserved**: `#153944` introduced selective activation to stop ordinary angle-bracket comparisons (`x < y`) from repeatedly rescanning a growing answer **while preserving canonical parsing and delivered text**; `a36d0483f` later reused that policy for the `internal-scaffolding` profile. The single shared `memoriesTextFilter` constant is still consumed by both profile orderings, so the two paths cannot drift. Activation remains selective — a bare mention or `x < y` never latches — and unlike literal tokens it restores the full parser grammar and the invocation-cleanup behavior, i.e. the "canonical parsing + delivered text" half of `#153944`'s intent.
- **Risk**: the probe holds only bounded state (a 32-character tail, one armed flag, one latch flag). Per-delta work is linear in the delta itself, not the accumulated reply. A tag word still incomplete at the end of a delta stays pending rather than latching; this is the same `recoverUnclosed` behavior the canonical transform already applies.

## User Impact

Long streamed replies that merely discuss `relevant-memories` or `minimax:tool_call` no longer stall on a whole-reply re-scan per token. Replies containing real memory tags — including whitespace-bearing or delta-split ones — and completed minimax invocations are stripped exactly as the batch parser would strip them, so users no longer briefly see internal scaffolding that later disappears. No configuration, migration, or change to which content is stripped is required.

## Compatibility

- **Preserved**: bare mentions and ordinary angle-bracket prose are delivered byte-identically; real memory tags, exact minimax envelopes, encoded transport envelopes, and completed `<invoke>` blocks keep their existing stripping behavior; batch output is unchanged.
- **Related**: selective activation origins in `#153944`; internal-scaffolding reuse in `a36d0483f`.
- **Not claimed**: no change to the parser itself, no new tag syntax, and no claim about clients that bypass the shared assistant-visible projection.

## Evidence

All runs below used an **isolated local Gateway** started from this checkout with a real configured provider, driven through the shipped `chat.send` RPC (so the agent turn and the assistant-visible text projection run inside the Gateway process). A `GatewayClient` subscribed to the broadcast `chat` frames. Credentials, the provider endpoint, host paths and non-public addresses are omitted; only loopback and aggregate numbers are shown.

### Before / after behavior matrix

`Before` = the code on `main` before this PR (bare-word tokens). `After` = this PR. `Reviewed head` = `8dc32ed5`, the RED arm for the two newly reported P2 findings; the earlier whitespace-tag and spaced-marker findings had already been fixed by that head, so their RED arms were the literal-token / `3f73a42` revisions (sections 3 and 4). Rows use the same captured Gateway delta frames (290 frames / 36,107 chars for `S1`, 4 frames / 299 chars for `S3`) or the reviewer's exact fixtures.

| Workload | Before (bare-word tokens) | Reviewed head `8dc32ed5` | After (this PR) | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S1` bare mention: sanitizer scan work (`regexWorkChars`) | 122,139,945 | 8,754,268 | **9,851,722** | bounded, ~12x less than Before |
| `S1` bare mention: delivered visible chars | 36,107 | 36,107 | **36,107** | unchanged |
| `S2` real `<relevant-memories>` tag: delivered visible chars | 48 | 48 | **48** | block stripped |
| `S3` whitespace tag: delivered visible chars | 165 | 165 | **165** | 165, block stripped (RED was the earlier literal-token revision: 299) |
| `P2` completed `<invoke>` with spaced minimax marker: batch/streaming parity | parity | parity | **parity (GREEN)** | parity (RED was `3f73a42`) |
| `P2` whitespace run delivered as 64 single-space deltas: batch/streaming parity | parity | **parity broken (RED)** | **parity (GREEN)** | parity |
| `P2` invocation shape before a later minimax marker: batch/streaming parity | parity | **parity broken (RED)** | **parity (GREEN)** | parity |
| `S2`/`S3` batch final text across variants | 82 / 198 | 82 / 198 | **82 / 198** | unchanged |

The `After` scan-work number is slightly above the intermediate `PR head` because the shared probe also covers the invocation-cleanup shape; it is still ~12x below `Before`, and the delivered text is identical in every workload.

### 1. Shipped-path streaming run, three source variants

```console
$ # isolated Gateway, one variant per run; chat.send + agent.wait over the Gateway RPC
$ node --import tsx p314-chatsend.mts S1-pre && node --import tsx p314-chatsend.mts S1-head && node --import tsx p314-chatsend.mts S1-fix
{"label":"S1-pre","sendStatus":"started","waitStatus":"ok","wall":38.2,"gatewayCpuSec":52.41,"eventCount":231,"finalTextChars":28559}
{"label":"S1-head","sendStatus":"started","waitStatus":"ok","wall":41.8,"gatewayCpuSec":47.64,"eventCount":256,"finalTextChars":31313}
{"label":"S1-fix","sendStatus":"started","waitStatus":"ok","wall":46.2,"gatewayCpuSec":48.79,"eventCount":295,"finalTextChars":36107}
```

The `chat` frames were captured to JSON. `replace:true` frames are the Gateway's delivered visible text:

```console
$ # S3 (whitespace-bearing memory tag), extracted from the captured chat frames
  seq 393 state delta                       ' ... < relevant-memories>\ninternal-only memory block for ops ... < / rele'   # raw provider delta
  seq 409 state delta replace=True len 198  'FIXTURE-START ... \n\n\n\nClosing paragraph ... FIXTURE-END'                  # delivered visible text (stripped)
  seq 414 state final                len 198 'FIXTURE-START ... \n\n\n\nClosing paragraph ... FIXTURE-END'
```

### 2. Reduced work on the real captured deltas

The exact delta frames broadcast by the Gateway in the `S1` run were replayed through the production `createAssistantVisibleStreamText("final_answer")` projector. `regexWorkChars` counts characters passed to `RegExp.prototype.test/exec` — a direct proxy for whole-reply re-scan cost. Same input for all three variants:

```console
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts pre  S1
{"arm":"pre","frames":290,"rawChars":36107,"visibleChars":36107,"regexWorkChars":122139945}
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts head S1   # reviewed head 8dc32ed5
{"arm":"head","frames":290,"rawChars":36107,"visibleChars":36107,"regexWorkChars":8754268}
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts fix  S1
{"arm":"fix","frames":290,"rawChars":36107,"visibleChars":36107,"regexWorkChars":9851722}
```

### 3. Whitespace-tag regression: failing on the literal-token revision, passing after repair

The same captured `S3` Gateway frames replayed through the production projector on the earlier literal-token revision and on the current source. Literal tokens never activate on a whitespace-bearing opener, so the internal memory block stays in the streamed visible text; the batch transform still removes it, which was the reviewed mismatch:

```console
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts pre  S3
{"arm":"pre","frames":4,"rawChars":299,"visibleChars":165,"visibleLeaksMemoryBlock":false,"visibleHasWhitespaceTag":false}
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts head S3      # earlier literal-token revision: RED
{"arm":"head","frames":4,"rawChars":299,"visibleChars":299,"visibleLeaksMemoryBlock":true,"visibleHasWhitespaceTag":true}
$ node --import tsx p314-replay.mts fix  S3      # after repair: GREEN
{"arm":"fix","frames":4,"rawChars":299,"visibleChars":165,"visibleLeaksMemoryBlock":false,"visibleHasWhitespaceTag":false}
```

Real tags (`S2`) strip identically on all three variants (`visibleChars: 48`, no leaked block).

### 4. P2 regression: invocation cleanup without an exact envelope

The reviewer's exact fixture — `Ready.\n<minimax:tool_call >\n<invoke name="exec">secret</invoke>\n</minimax:tool_call >\nDone.` — asserts batch/streaming parity (the payload must not be visible). Same assertion, same input, only the source variant changes:

```console
$ node --import tsx p314-p2-redgreen.mts pre
arm=pre batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true assertion=PASS
exit=0 for pre
$ node --import tsx p314-p2-redgreen.mts head      # earlier exact-envelope revision: RED
arm=head batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=true parity=false assertion=FAIL AssertionError: invocation payload stays visible in streamed delivery text
exit=1 for head
$ node --import tsx p314-p2-redgreen.mts fix       # after repair: GREEN
arm=fix batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true assertion=PASS
exit=0 for fix
```

The minimax stage's `requires` marker keeps a bare mention alone off the re-scan: `bareMentionPreserved=true`, `bareMentionRegexWorkChars=2841` for the same probe.

### 5. The two new P2 findings: RED on the reviewed head, GREEN after repair

Both findings were reproduced with the reviewer's exact append schedules. Same acceptance condition for every arm — batch/streaming parity, with the internal payload never visible. `head` here is `8dc32ed5`:

```console
$ node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts pre whitespace && node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts head whitespace && node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts fix whitespace
PASS arm=pre  scenario=whitespace batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true
FAIL arm=head scenario=whitespace batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=true  parity=false AssertionError: internal payload stays visible in streamed delivery text
exit=1 whitespace/head
PASS arm=fix  scenario=whitespace batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true

$ node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts pre markerLate && node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts head markerLate && node --import tsx p314-p2new-redgreen.mts fix markerLate
PASS arm=pre  scenario=markerLate batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true
FAIL arm=head scenario=markerLate batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=true  parity=false AssertionError: internal payload stays visible in streamed delivery text
exit=1 markerLate/head
PASS arm=fix  scenario=markerLate batchHasSecret=false streamingHasSecret=false parity=true
```

Both schedules are now pinned by added regression cases asserting `not.toContain("secret")` and equality with `sanitizeAssistantVisibleStreamText` (batch).

### 6. CDP CPU profiles of the Gateway process

`Profiler.start`/`stop` around each `S1` turn (the turn executes inside the Gateway process), measured on the earlier revision of this PR before the probe was consolidated:

```console
label=S1-pre-v4  profileTotal=42.20s sanitizerSelf=0.17s (0.4%)
label=S1-head-v4 profileTotal=45.50s sanitizerSelf=0.23s (0.5%)
label=S1-fix-v4  profileTotal=50.32s sanitizerSelf=0.31s (0.6%)
```

These columns are close across variants because a real provider emits coarse deltas (290 frames for this 36 KB reply), so the *number* of whole-reply re-scans is bounded by frame count even though each re-scan walks the entire accumulated reply. Process-wide self-time is too coarse to rank the variants; `regexWorkChars` in section 2 is the direct measure and was re-run on the final source for every row in the table above. On a client receiving one-character deltas (as in the original 64 KB measurement) the same ~12x ratio applies to every one of tens of thousands of appends, which is where the multi-second stalls come from.

### 7. Focused regression assertion and suites

```console
$ node --import tsx p314-redgreen.mts head       # earlier literal-token revision: RED
FAIL arm=head: frames=4 visibleChars=299 AssertionError: internal memory block is still visible in streamed delivery text
exit=1 for head
$ node --import tsx p314-redgreen.mts fix        # after repair: GREEN
PASS arm=fix: frames=4 visibleChars=165 internal memory block stripped from streamed delivery text
exit=0 for fix

$ CI=1 vitest run src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.streaming-work.test.ts src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.minimax.test.ts src/shared/text/tool-call-xml.streaming-work.test.ts
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  150 passed (150)
```

The `expectPrefixParity` case checks the spaced-marker P2 fixture at every delta split against `sanitizeAssistantVisibleStreamText` (batch), so the streaming path cannot drift from batch. Two further cases pin the newly reviewed schedules — a whitespace run delivered as 64 single-space deltas, and an `<invoke>` shape arriving before the minimax marker — each asserting both payload removal and equality with the batch transform. The original whitespace cases still cover a split opener/closer and an unbounded gap (4,096 then 2,048 spaces) in a single append. The low-value plain real-MiniMax-envelope case was removed on review feedback; `assistant-visible-text.minimax.test.ts` already streams complete envelopes in four-character chunks with surrounding prose assertions. `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` report 0 warnings and 0 errors on both changed source files.

### CI attribution

Two CI failures were attributed and fixed:

- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` / `test-lines`: the first run reported `over by: 7; net delta: +96` (the allocation under-funded the added test lines); the second run reported `Test line allocation credit 92 exceeds allowed ceiling growth 85` (the credit exceeded the new net delta). The allocation is now set to exactly the net test-line delta of this revision (109). Locally, in both `--staged` and working-tree modes, `check-test-lines-ratchet` reports `Test lines OK: 6613703; ceiling: 6613733; slack: 30` and `check-line-cap-ratchet` reports no new violations; the CI run on this head passed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`.
- `checks-ui-e2e (1/2)`: a `page.waitForFunction: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` in `ui/src/e2e/screen-requester-routing.e2e.test.ts` (mock-Gateway Control UI browser test, 80 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped), waiting on a `tools.github.status` request during GitHub-identity setup navigation. It is **not** caused by the shared-text changes here (this PR does not touch any `ui/` file, and the timeout is in a Control-UI routing flow unrelated to assistant text). The same test fails on unrelated PRs that also do not touch `ui/` — e.g. PR #196480 (`6b5c7e4396`) and PR #196937 (`56845faf22`) both report `checks-ui-e2e (1/2): failure` with the identical timeout. The repository's rerun endpoint requires admin rights, so this upstream-flaky job is left for a normal CI retry. `Scan changed paths (precise)`, the six `Security High` CodeQL shards and `Select Critical Quality shards` in earlier runs were GitHub installation API rate-limit errors, i.e. infrastructure.

`PR context and evidence` is `success` on the latest head, and `vitest` reports 150/150 passing across `assistant-visible-text.streaming-work`, `assistant-visible-text.minimax` and `tool-call-xml.streaming-work`; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` report 0 warnings and 0 errors.

### What was not tested

- The Gateway proof used one real provider and loopback transport; no remote or multi-node Gateway topology was exercised.
- CPU profiles are process-wide; `regexWorkChars` is the isolated measure of sanitizer scan cost, not end-user wall-clock time.
- No streaming replies larger than ~36 KB were measured on the shipped path; the 64 KB figures come from the isolated single-stage measurement.

### Open PR collision check

Searched open PRs by changed-file list for `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.ts` and `src/shared/text/assistant-text-transforms.ts`: apart from this PR (#196624), none of the matching open PRs (#192357, #181990, #196690, #143937, #191562) modifies either file. The related sibling PR #193871 (closed legacy-bracket checkpoint settlement) is a separate root cause in a different subsystem and remains its own open PR.

prs.title: fix(cli): restart probe fails to report several Gateway auth rejections as auth-rejected
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway restart` and update verification kept polling a Gateway that had *definitively refused* this CLI — instead of reporting `auth-rejected` — when the refusal carried a structured detail code whose close-reason text was not in the probe's hand-copied allowlist. `AUTH_SCOPE_MISMATCH` is one real case: the CLI waited out the whole restart budget instead of telling the operator the credentials were refused.

- Problem: `confirmGatewayReachable` classified auth rejections from a fixed text allowlist (`isGatewayAuthRejection`) plus one hard-coded `AUTH_VERIFIED_USER_REQUIRED` case; every other structured refusal stayed unclassified.
- Solution: `isGatewayAuthRejectionError` reads the structured `details.code` off the correlated protocol response and treats `AUTH_*` / `DEVICE_AUTH_*` as a rejection, mirroring the Gateway's canonical `authRejected` predicate (`packages/gateway-protocol/src/connect-error-details.ts`).
- Unchanged: the text allowlist, the `device identity required` close-reason contract, Gateway admission, and the HTTP identity / health gates.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text allowlist is a hand-copied mirror of Gateway rejection messages and drifts every time the Gateway adds a reason; the Gateway already publishes the machine-readable code with the refusal. Extending the existing structured predicate is smaller than widening text and reuses the documented terminal-rejection contract. Risk boundary: the probe runs against loopback and only decides restart liveness, not authorization, so this does not widen the trust boundary.

## User Impact

Structured refusals now settle as `auth-rejected` with the Gateway's own message instead of an unexplained timeout: pre-fix `Gateway restart timed out after 82s waiting for health checks.` → post-fix `Gateway restart failed: the Gateway rejected this CLI's credentials.` No new configuration, flag, or Gateway admission change.

## Evidence

### 1. Managed restart through the shipped CLI

Real Gateway under systemd (`proof315` unit, loopback `127.0.0.1:19977`) whose CLI holds an operator device token with scopes `[]`, so the probe is refused with `AUTH_SCOPE_MISMATCH`. Both runs share Gateway, state and credentials; only the CLI build differs.

![Annotated before/after: pre-fix polls until the budget expires, this PR settles as auth-rejected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/openclaw/proof-196426/196426-restart-auth-rejected.png)

```console
# pre-fix build (origin/main)
$ node dist/entry.js gateway restart
Gateway check failed: unauthorized: device token scope mismatch (re-pair or approve scope upgrade)
Gateway restart timed out after 82s waiting for health checks.        # exit 1, 92.8s

# post-fix build (this PR)
$ node dist/entry.js gateway restart
Gateway check failed: unauthorized: device token scope mismatch (re-pair or approve scope upgrade)
Gateway restart failed: the Gateway rejected this CLI's credentials.  # exit 1, 51.6s
```

| | pre-fix (`origin/main`) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| probe result | `reachable=false`, `authenticationError=null` | `reachable=false`, `authenticationError="unauthorized: device token scope mismatch (…)"` |
| `waitOutcome` | `timeout` | `auth-rejected` on the first probe |
| operator line | `Gateway restart timed out after 82s waiting for health checks.` | `Gateway restart failed: the Gateway rejected this CLI's credentials.` |
| wall clock | 92.8s | 51.6s |

The `Gateway check failed:` line is byte-identical in both runs — same refusal, same message; only the verdict changes (`timeout` → `auth-rejected`). Gateway side, same window:

```console
$ grep -E '\[ws\] unauthorized' gateway.log \
  | sed -E 's/.*client=([a-z]+).*auth=([a-z-]+).*reason=([a-z_]+).*/client=\1 auth=\2 reason=\3/' | uniq -c
     32 client=cli auth=device-token reason=scope_mismatch
```

Runs produced on `32698ce63c9b`; only the allocation file changed since.

### 2. Latest-stable upgrade keeps settings

Fresh state written by the published stable `openclaw@2026.11.2` (`b556fdf`, state schema 22), then upgraded in place to this build:

```console
$ openclaw doctor --fix          # this build, same state dir
Doctor: database migrations
$ # state schema 22 -> 39, tables 101 -> 98
schema=39 tables=98
```

`logging.level: debug` and `gateway.port: 19978` survived. Direction matters: published 2026.11.2 refuses schema 39 (`this build supports 22`), so it is stable → this build.

### 3. Regression matrix

`settles policy rejection through HTTP` keeps its five rows and adds two carrying a structured `details.code` — `AUTH_SCOPE_MISMATCH` (the real message above) and `DEVICE_AUTH_SIGNATURE_EXPIRED` (`device signature expired`), one per accepted prefix.

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts \
    src/cli/daemon-cli/restart-health-probe.test.ts src/cli/daemon-cli/restart-health.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  37 passed (37)

$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
Test lines OK: 6622037; ceiling: 6622037; slack: 0.
```

The +27 delta is the two rows plus an optional detail code on the shared `gatewayResponseError` fixture; the allocation declares exactly those 27 lines and nothing else (#196526 cleared the inherited credit).

Red on the base, green with the fix — same test file, only the probe source swapped:

```console
# this PR's tests against the base probe (cdd7ee5)
× settles policy rejection through HTTP (response, false, candidate-build) → expected 'timeout' to be 'auth-rejected'
Tests  2 failed | 26 passed (28)

# with this PR's probe
Tests  28 passed (28)
```

### What was not tested

No live model turn or channel traffic: the probe only decides restart liveness and the fixture Gateway has no agent. The fixture device token is synthetic (empty scopes).

## Open PR collision check

No other open PR touches `src/cli/daemon-cli/restart-health-probe.ts` or the `isGatewayAuthRejection*` predicates (#134665, #144056, #175537, #181395 touch other daemon-cli surfaces).

CI's infra planner includes tests that the selected infra config cannot execute, inflating its inventory and concealing a stale test membership entry.

- The regression fails on the original owner: 2,723 planned infra selectors versus 2,499 executable files. The correction removes exactly 224 inert or nonexistent selectors; the executable-inventory and database-consumer contracts pass.

Those three cases and the two inventory contracts pass after correction; the strengthened boundary admission case also passes. prs.title: fix(skills): keep remote bin probe suppression on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway suppresses repeated remote bin probes for a connected node, but both windows of that suppression are measured on the host wall clock (`Date.now()`), so a clock correction silently stretches or shortens them.

- Problem: `remoteNodeProbeStates` (`src/skills/runtime/remote.ts:51`) is a process-local `Map` holding `nextProbeAfterMs`, and all three places that touch it used `Date.now()`: the suppression gate (`remote.ts:491`), the failure backoff seed (`remote.ts:512`) and the success TTL seed (`remote.ts:608`). The success window is 30 minutes and the failure backoff is 15 s doubling to a 5 min cap (`remote.ts:65-67`). Because the deadline is compared against a clock that can be stepped by NTP, VM resume, suspend/resume or a manual change, the window is not a duration at all — it is a wall-clock instant.
- Observed with a real Gateway and a real `openclaw node run` host (details in Evidence): after a successful probe, stepping the Gateway clock forward by 31 minutes made the next node connection re-run `system.which` immediately, while the same reconnect without a step re-used the settled snapshot. After a failed probe, stepping the clock back by 10 minutes kept the refresh suppressed 42 s of real time later — the 15 s backoff had long expired, but the deadline was still 10 minutes in the future in wall-clock terms, so the node's bins stayed cleared and remote-only skills stayed unavailable.
- Solution: seed and compare the suppression deadline with the repository's canonical process-local clock, `monotonicNow()` from `src/shared/monotonic-time.ts`, whose header is literally "Process-local milliseconds: never persist or exchange these readings as epochs".
- What changed: `src/skills/runtime/remote.ts` imports `monotonicNow` and uses it at the gate, the failure seed and the success seed. `src/skills/runtime/remote.test.ts`: the three existing spies move from `Date.now` to `performance.now`, and the reconnect reuse test also steps `Date.now` forward 31 min (it fails on main with 2 probes).
- What did NOT change: the TTL and backoff values, the signature/pairing-generation gating, the in-flight coalescing, the disconnect rule that intentionally drops a failure backoff (`remote.ts:346-351`), the probing commands, and any persisted state. No new helper and no signature change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Because this state is exactly the shape the monotonic owner was written for, and the repository has already converged on that answer for the same class of private TTLs.

- `nextProbeAfterMs` is never persisted and never crosses a process boundary: the whole probe state lives in one in-memory `Map` and is dropped with the node (`removeRemoteNodeInfo`) or the registry. A monotonic reading is therefore always valid here — no epoch is exchanged, which is the only thing the owner forbids.
- The three touched sites are the only readers and writers of the field (`grep -rn nextProbeAfterMs src plugins` returns `remote.ts:491`, `:526`, `:608` plus the type at `:44`), so there is no second domain to reconcile.
- No rounding or flooring is needed: the deadline is only ever compared, never handed to `setTimeout` or `AbortSignal.timeout`, so the fractional milliseconds from `performance.now()` are harmless.
- This follows the precedent set by #191606 (`fix(cache): keep private cache TTLs on elapsed time`, merged 2026-11-03), which moved private cache windows to `monotonicNow()` for the same reason and left the public/epoch-facing values alone.

Risk is low and bounded: the only behavior change is that these two windows now measure elapsed time. Everything that decides *whether* to probe — pairing generation, command/platform/device-family/bins signature, live-owner checks — is untouched, and the surrounding suite passes unchanged.

## User Impact

Anyone running a Gateway with connected remote macOS nodes where a workspace skill requires bins, on a host whose clock is corrected while the node stays connected.

- After a probe failure, the node's bins stay cleared and the remote-only skills stay hidden until the wall-clock deadline is reached. A backward clock step (timezone-independent NTP correction, VM snapshot restore, a laptop waking in a different time zone) extends that outage by the size of the step — up to the 5 min backoff cap plus the jump. The failure is retried on schedule after this change.
- After a successful probe, a backward step keeps a stale bin snapshot in place for longer than the 30 min TTL (a 10 min step makes it 40 min), and a forward step expires a fresh snapshot early and re-probes the node (`system.which` over the node connection) sooner than needed.
- Steady clocks see no change at all: the same TTL and the same backoff, measured the same way in the common case.

## Evidence

Maintainer proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191908#issuecomment-6835891661

A real `openclaw node run` on a Mac is paired to a built Gateway in a Linux container, and only the Gateway's `Date.now` is stepped. After a successful probe, a +31 min step makes main re-probe 98 s later, while this branch holds off. With no step, both hold off. Failure backoff (15/30/60 s) is the same on both.

Focused suite: `src/skills/runtime/remote.test.ts` 25 passed on this head; the reconnect reuse test fails on main.

An earlier proof in this PR faked a macOS node identity on Linux and injected the probe failure. The maintainer proof above replaces it.

prs.title: fix(doctor): surface agent-dir read failures in OAuth shadow scan
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` folded every `fs.readdir` failure on the agent directory into `[]`. An unreadable `~/.openclaw/agents` therefore produced no stale-OAuth-shadow hits and no warning: Doctor reported clean, and `doctor --fix` did nothing while discovery was silently incomplete.

## User Impact

Doctor now prints a warning that names the agent directory and tells the operator to inspect permissions and rerun. A genuinely absent directory (ENOENT, the state before first boot) stays silent, and configured agents are collected before enumeration, so the warning says *additional* discovery was skipped rather than claiming repair failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`collectCandidateAgentDirs` swallowed the failure where it happens, one line from `loadRawAuthProfileStore`, which already pushes non-ENOENT store read failures into `warnings`. The catch now branches on `hasErrnoCode(error, "ENOENT")`; everything else pushes the sibling's warning contract. The return type becomes `{ dirs, warnings }` and the single call site merges them. No new exports, flags, runtime state, schema, or lockfile. Production +21/−7.

## Evidence

### Behavior, base `origin/main` vs this head

| Scenario | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agents root unlistable | silent, `warnings=[]` | warning surfaced |
| agents root absent (ENOENT) | `warnings=[]` | `warnings=[]` |
| agents root readable | dirs + configured agents | unchanged |
| auth store read failure | non-ENOENT surfaces | unchanged |

### Permission scene on an upgraded state

Real execute-only agents root (`chmod 111`: listing denied, known-path traversal kept) on the state upgraded below. No shim, no mock:

```
◇  Doctor warnings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Cannot list agent directories under                               │
│  /home/runner/work/_temp/proof/state/agents; additional directory  │
│  discovery was skipped. Inspect permissions and rerun doctor.      │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

`chmod 755` control on that same state: 0 matches. Silent branch: agents root absent → 0 warnings.

### Latest stable → this head

Published `openclaw@2026.11.2` (`b556fdf`, npm `latest`) wrote the settings (`config set gateway.mode`, `gateway.port 19123`, `logging.level`) and an auth profile (`models auth paste-token --agent main`), then the shipped updater moved that state onto a candidate built from this head:

```
$ openclaw update --tag file:openclaw-candidate.tgz --yes --timeout 900 --json
{"status":"ok","mode":"npm",
 "before":{"version":"2026.11.2","buildId":"2026.11.2-release-b556fdf457b0-2026-11-07T15-35-25.381Z"},
 "after":{"version":"2026.11.3","buildId":"2026.11.3-48859e13b2e7-2026-11-10T13-10-13.313Z"}}
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (48859e1)
```

Candidate Doctor completed the state upgrade on that state (`database migrations`, `state schema`), and it survived:

| Asset | driver 2026.11.2 | after this head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| settings `gateway`, `logging`, `plugins` | written by the driver | identical; candidate Doctor added `agents`, `skills`, `wizard` |
| `meta.lastTouchedVersion` | `2026.11.2` | `2026.11.3` |
| auth profile (`models auth list`) | `anthropic:proof (anthropic/token)` | same id, provider, type |
| stored secret | `sk-ant…(99 chars)` | same row, same shape |
| `state/openclaw.sqlite` schema | 22 | 39 |

`doctor --fix` afterwards left the settings and the profile unchanged. Raw transcript: [proof run 42821841713](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-196465-upgrade-proof/actions/runs/42821841713).

### Regression coverage

`stale-oauth-profile-shadows.test.ts` passes 15/15, with the added `it.each` driving ENOENT and EACCES through the same call path. Reverting the non-ENOENT branch fails the EACCES assertion (`expected warnings.length=1 got 0`).

```
 .../bug-360-stale-oauth-shadow-readdir.txt         |  2 ++
 .../shared/stale-oauth-profile-shadows.test.ts     | 37 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 .../doctor/shared/stale-oauth-profile-shadows.ts   | 28 ++++++++++++----
 3 files changed, 60 insertions(+), 7 deletions(-)
```

`scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` → `Test lines OK: 6617226; ceiling: 6617226; slack: 0.`

All proof runs used an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; no production state, Gateway, or lockfile was touched.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): give each agent its own realtime call voice
prs.body:
Related: #130054
Related: #78190
Related: #188732

## What Problem This Solves

Realtime phone calls handled by different agents all speak with the same voice, because Voice Call only reads the provider-wide `realtime.providers.<provider>.voice`.

## User Impact

Operators can map agent IDs to realtime voices with `plugins.entries.voice-call.config.realtime.voiceByAgent`. A call owned by a listed agent speaks with that agent's voice: an outbound call the agent placed, or an inbound call routed to it by `numbers.<E.164>.agentId` or the plugin `agentId`. Agents without an entry, and configs without the key, keep the provider voice exactly as today. No migration or required action.

Voice names go to the provider unchanged, so they must be valid for the selected realtime provider and model. Startup logs a warning for a key that matches no configured agent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Voice Call already resolves the realtime provider per call for the agent recorded on the call, and already builds per-agent realtime instructions. The voice now follows the same owner: call registration looks up the call's agent and passes its voice through the realtime-voice SDK's existing `providerConfigOverrides`, which applies before provider normalization and affects only that call. It sets both `voice` and `speakerVoice` because the bundled OpenAI, Google, and xAI realtime providers read `speakerVoice` first; Discord's per-session voice override does the same.

This is a new plugin config option, so it needs a maintainer product decision; the review on #130054 asked for an owner and a precedence. Proposed: Voice Call owns the setting, and the precedence is the call agent's `voiceByAgent` entry, then the provider's configured `speakerVoice`/`voice`, then the provider default.

Shape: a flat, optional `realtime.voiceByAgent: Record<agentId, voice>` beside the other realtime settings. It matches the provider-agnostic realtime voice keys sibling surfaces already use (FaceTime's `realtime.voice`, Discord's `channels.discord.voice.realtime.speakerVoice`) and keeps the new contract to the one value requested. A per-agent provider block such as `realtime.agents.<id>.providers.<provider>` would expose every provider setting per agent, which the review on #188732 cautioned against for route overrides. The setting stays plugin-owned rather than reading core `agents.entries.<id>.tts`, because realtime voice names are provider-specific and not interchangeable with TTS voices. Keys are normalized like the other Voice Call agent IDs.

Not included, proposed as a follow-up: a per-agent voice for classic (non-realtime) calls. That path has two voice consumers, TwiML `<Say>` voices mapped from `tts` and a Twilio media-stream TTS provider created once from the global `tts` config, so it needs per-call TTS preparation (likely from core `agents.entries.<id>.tts`) rather than a one-line override.

Budgets: the generated plugin config baseline grows by two entries (5018 → 5020: the map and its value schema); this is plugin-owned, optional, and adds no core config key. The test-line allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/voice-call-voice-by-agent.txt` (76) covers this change's +71 test lines plus the 5-line overage already present on the base commit; recompute it if the base moves before merge.

## Evidence

- Red before: with the new tests on base `4092d358a` and production files at base, each changed test fails for the intended reason while the other 82 tests in those files pass. `config.test.ts`: the runtime schema rejects the key (`Unrecognized key: "voiceByAgent"`). `runtime.test.ts`: the mapped agent's registration passes no override (`expected undefined to deeply equal { voice: 'marin', … }`). `runtime.realtime-routing.test.ts`: the inbound call routed to `support` reaches provider resolution without a voice override.
- Green after: the same three files pass (85 tests). They cover a mapped agent receiving `{ voice, speakerVoice }` (key `Support` normalized to `support`); an unmapped agent and an unset `voiceByAgent` passing no override; an inbound number route reaching its agent's voice through the real stream-start path while the other route keeps the provider voice; exactly one warning for an unknown key; and runtime and manifest schemas accepting and rejecting the same values (empty voice, non-string voice, empty agent key).
- Test cost, `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on a local Mac with a cold Vitest transform cache: `config.test.ts` 33.6 s, `runtime.test.ts` 35.7 s, `runtime.realtime-routing.test.ts` 34.7 s. Transform is 87–96% of each run; the new cases run in milliseconds, and the routing test's existing WebSocket flow (about 2.6 s) is unchanged. With a warm cache, all three files ran in 22.0 s (2 shards). CI seconds pending.
- `pnpm test:extension voice-call`: 65 files, 800 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed for lanes extensions, extensionTests, docs, tooling, and bundledChannelConfigMetadata, including extension and extension-test typecheck, extension and scripts lint, changed-file formatting, config docs baseline, bundled channel config metadata, plugin boundaries, dead-export scan, and the ratchets.
- Manifest consumers: `pnpm test src/plugins/bundled-plugin-metadata.test.ts src/plugins/manifest-config-groups.test.ts src/config/doc-baseline.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed (28 tests).
- Docs: `pnpm docs:check-config-examples` validates the new example against the plugin schema (a temporarily misspelled key fails it), and `pnpm docs:check-mdx`, `pnpm format:docs:check`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, and `git diff --check` pass. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports two broken anchors in pages this change does not touch (`/tools/acp-agents-setup`, `releases/2026.10.1.md`); the new `#per-agent-voices` links resolve.
- `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` pass with the regenerated baseline and the allocation record.
- Not exercised: no live Twilio call or realtime provider session, so the audible voice on a real call is not verified. Provider normalization reading `speakerVoice` before `voice` is from source (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-session-policy.ts`, `extensions/google/realtime-voice-provider.ts`, `extensions/xai/realtime-voice-config.ts`); the SDK applying `providerConfigOverrides` over configured values before normalization is covered by `src/talk/provider-resolver.test.ts`.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.title: fix: keep wide public conversation tables readable
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: public conversation tables split ordinary words into one-to-three-character lines when a comparison has many columns, making the conversation difficult to read on phones and desktops.

## User Impact

Readers can scroll wide tables horizontally without crushing their words. Ordinary short tables remain compact, and long cell text and URLs remain contained. A long two-column table can also scroll on a narrow phone instead of forcing its cells to fit. No configuration, public API, dependency, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public Markdown renderer now keeps native table layout separate from its bounded scroll viewport. One intrinsic sizing rule serves short, long, and many-column tables; there is no column-count cutoff. Long cells wrap at the existing chat sibling's 24rem cap. The native table is keyboard-focusable and its viewport has a visible focus indicator, preserving table/header semantics without adding named regions to every short table. Paragraph wrapping is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Red base → green repair:** real production renderPublicSessionDocument responses over isolated loopback HTTP, with the production CSP and self-hosted fonts, rendered in Chromium at 388×844 and 1280×900 in light/dark themes. The same synthetic 12-column, 3-row table was 2632.41px tall on the phone and 553.97px on desktop before the fix, with ordinary header words split across lines. It is now 182.47px tall in both viewports, with single-line headers.
- **Interaction and original proof:** ArrowRight keyboard scrolling and horizontal wheel input reach the final column without document overflow. The browser regressions also cover compact short tables, long notes/URLs, paragraph containment, and user bubbles. Original local proof passed: browser 2; renderer/refresh/locale/entry siblings 65; public-session HTTP 24; browser-lane ownership 1. Original browser wall time was 3.19s without captures, 8.84s with captures. A separate parent execution passed 2/2 on the reviewed source. The original production renderer-entry bundle passed; this was not a full package/release build. These are Chromium browser/HTTP results, not physical-app or live authenticated Gateway/model-flow qualification.
- **Base integration and patch custody:** the branch was mechanically integrated onto landed [#197873](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197873), commit f77a3600a3c811cca11f6e9ca3cd16369bf02b68, specifically to incorporate the named workflow-size gate repair, not merely because main advanced. Current head is 70f4eea2e7fd95a3c7ca33fb143aa1498e837642. The entire four-file authored patch remains byte-identical, SHA-256 86d131228afb499eaff652c3f4c1c3b8cc884a119b300b9ab7ad07a006976f13, and all four resulting blobs match the original published head. Both replayed commits preserve Vincent's co-author trailer and the publication credit/marker. Local backup branch `openclaw/ui-rhythm-public-table-readability-pre-f77-integration` preserves b845468a7527f00bb32393c528a57a386b064bef and its proof/history.
- **Current-head affected proof:** at 70f4eea2e7fd95a3c7ca33fb143aa1498e837642, the actual production-renderer HTTP/CSP/font browser regression passed 2/2 across phone/desktop and light/dark; native duration 3.70s, command wall time 5.138s. Renderer/refresh/locale/entry and public-session HTTP siblings passed 89/89 across five files. The actual workflow-size guard and E2E resource-ownership invariant passed 2/2; 216 unrelated cases were explicitly unselected. Targeted typecheck, lint and formatting of all four authored files, and git diff --check passed. No production UI build was needed for this standalone HTTP renderer proof; existing native owners prepared HTTP compiled artifacts and lint declarations. This is local affected-head proof, not broad CI or a full package/release build.
- **Current-head CI:** [run 43307427262, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43307427262) is attached to 70f4eea2e7fd95a3c7ca33fb143aa1498e837642 and was observed in progress. Current-head CI and remaining native landing gates are pending, not claimed green. No CI rerun or merge has been requested.
- **Prior-head failed CI:** [run 43259210471, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43259210471) finished **failed** at b845468a7527f00bb32393c528a57a386b064bef. It failed the then-unrepaired workflow-size guard and had a 20-minute step timeout in `checks-ui-e2e (3/7)`, not a reported Vitest assertion. The retained progress artifact identifies active fresh-Gateway and mocked-chat cases, but the timeout's cause remains unresolved. ## What Problem This Solves

The SQLite lifecycle verifier can race with its own agent run while deleting a session. Gateway correctly rejects the changed session, but the verifier fails before checking the final state.

## What changes?

Wait for that owned run to settle and retry deletion once, only for the exact, correlated `session-changed` response. Other errors and a second rejection still fail. The verifier still requires successful deletion, stable session absence, and empty history. Superseded-history handling lives in the shared proof helper.

This changes test support only. Following review, I removed the callback-only replay tests and the redundant CLI fixture rename.

## Evidence

On `fdbc70597`, the canonical runtime build, UI build, CLI transcript cases (9/9), SQLite helper cases (6/6), and the real Gateway built-CLI lifecycle proof (1/1) passed. The initial missing-UI setup timeout and successful same-head rerun are recorded in the [qualification report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197609#issuecomment-6823923953).

fix(cron): past schedule.at validation error says "1 minutes ago"

## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway rejected a `cron add --at` timestamp 60-120 seconds in the
past, the validation error said `(1 minutes ago)` instead of singular wording,
e.g.:

    schedule.at is in the past: ... (1 minutes ago). Current time: ...

## User Impact

The rejection now reads `(1 minute ago)` for exactly one minute and
`(N minutes ago)` otherwise. The CLI pair command already uses this singular
convention. The one-minute grace window, exit code and JSON shape are
unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`validateScheduleTimestamp` interpolated the raw count without pluralizing.
The fix mirrors the existing singular convention in `src/cli/pair-cli.ts`.

## Evidence

Reproduced through the built CLI against an isolated secretless local Gateway
at base e52cdb9, then re-checked against the rebuilt Gateway with the fix
(head 4043cd0):

new). The new test was verified red with the fix stashed and green with it
applied.
