prs.title: fix(voice-call): interrupting a reply leaves the agent working on the abandoned question
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A caller interrupts a reply, and the agent keeps working on the question they just abandoned.

Barge-in today is audio-side only: queued telephony audio is cleared and the active reply is
cancelled, so the caller is no longer talked over and no obsolete answer is spoken. But the agent
run behind that turn continues, so the caller waits out work they already interrupted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` that also aborts the in-flight run for the call.

**Cancellation is owned per response.** Each response creates its own `AbortController` and passes
it alongside the work-admission signal (`AbortSignal.any([...])`), then hands that abort to the
webhook. Barge-in fires that exact handle. This matters because a session-keyed abort resolves
whichever turn currently occupies the session: with `maxConcurrentCalls > 1` and
`sessionScope: "main"`, that can be another call's accepted work. The locally minted `runId` cannot
select a run either, since the harness never sees it. The controller is therefore the only authority
over this run, and it is retired when the response settles.

The abort is immediate rather than graceful: it does not wait for a tool-call boundary, and a
foreground exec child process is killed as soon as the signal fires.

History handling is delegated, not reimplemented. Tool calls that already completed stay persisted
by the embedded runner, so the next run resumes with that work intact. Tool calls killed mid-flight
are left without results, and the existing transcript repair layer synthesizes the placeholders on
the next run. The interrupted question is deliberately not carried forward: it is already in session
history, and the barged-in utterance becomes the next turn on its own.

Supporting changes, all needed for the abort to behave:

- **`command-queue`**: an `AbortError` is a deliberate cancellation, not a lane task failure.
  Without this, every interruption wrote two error lines for work cancelled on purpose. Added
  alongside the existing classifications rather than replacing them - `isExpectedRunCancellation`
  does not cover a bare `AbortError`.
- **`exec`**: log the killed child on abort so an operator can see which process died with the run.
  **Identifiers only** - session and pid, never command text and never a derived command label,
  because both retain arguments and arguments carry credentials.
- **One registry owner**: `registerRun` returns a cleanup closed over its own run id, so a
  late-settling turn cannot clear the run that replaced it.

## User Impact

- Opt-in and off by default: `bargeIn.abortAgentRun` defaults to `false`, so existing installs keep
  today's audio-only behaviour on upgrade. No stored data or config shape changes.
- With it enabled, interrupting stops both the speech and the work behind it.
- Explicitly backgrounded commands survive the abort; only foreground children are killed, and the
  documentation says so.

**Scope: the streaming path only.** The flag is read where the streaming trigger lives. The realtime
bridge does not consult it, and the documentation now states that explicitly instead of implying
both paths honour it. Streaming and realtime are mutually exclusive (`config.ts` rejects both), so
any one call is only ever on a single path. Realtime is a straightforward follow-up.

## Evidence

Two live outbound Twilio Programmable Voice + Media Streams calls on a build pinned to this PR's
code (`737a5060808`), verified before dialing by the `dist/index.js` build timestamp and its banner
reporting `2026.11.1 (737a506)`. Identifiers are redacted; structure and timings remain.

### Foreground child kill, and abort immediacy

```
11:11:39.396 Outbound call initiated: callId=<redacted> mode=conversation
11:12:06.144 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327125192
11:12:06.199 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
11:13:03.421 [exec] abort killed child session=<redacted> pid=81432
11:13:03.422 barge-in aborted agent run callId=<redacted> source=streaming runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327148253
11:13:03.428 Code Mode execution failed runId=voice:<redacted>:1794327148253 failureKind=aborted
11:13:03.490 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
11:13:29.742 Call finalized callId=<redacted> endReason=completed
```

The child dies at `.421`, **one millisecond before** the barge-in line at `.422`, and the whole
chain settles in 69 ms. That ordering is the immediacy claim: a cancellation waiting for a tool-call
boundary could not produce it. The diagnostic carries `session=` and `pid=` and no command payload.

### Completed results survive, and the next turn resumes

An earlier call on the same build:

```
09:51:47.039 Outbound call initiated: callId=<redacted> mode=conversation
09:52:28.321 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322335274
09:52:28.335 Code Mode execution failed runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322335274 failureKind=aborted
09:52:28.409 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:52:41.127 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322351728
09:52:41.184 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:53:02.243 barge-in aborted agent run runId=voice:<redacted>:1794322368701
09:53:02.310 Response generation aborted by barge-in <redacted>
09:53:25.826 Call finalized callId=<redacted> endReason=completed
```

Three interruptions, three **distinct** `runId` values, each settling within 60-90 ms, with an
in-flight tool call aborted 14 ms after the first barge-in. In session history the killed call's
result slot holds the repair layer's synthesized placeholder ("Tool call interrupted before a result
was recorded; its outcome is unknown"), while the preceding turn's **completed** tool result remains
intact - and the model reasoned over both on the next turn: "The first batch got interrupted before
anything was recorded, so I reran it and all five searches completed." The barged-in utterance
became the next turn on its own; the abandoned question was not carried forward.

No `barge-in agent run abort failed` line appeared in either call, so the guard never had to swallow
a throw.

### Cross-call isolation

Covered by test rather than capture, deliberately: proving it by phone means winning a race on
purpose, whereas the suite asserts it on every run. `webhook.barge-in-abort.test.ts` registers two
calls under one session id, barges in on A, and asserts only A's handle fires while B stays
abortable. That case and replacement-cleanup survival both fail against the previous session-keyed
implementation, so they are regressions rather than restatements.

## Local gates

```
oxlint                 0 warnings, 0 errors
tsgo:extensions        clean
tsgo:extensions:test   clean
tsgo:core              clean
vitest                 2 files, 13 tests passed
config:docs:check      OK
line-cap ratchet       webhook.ts no longer listed - back within baseline
```

### The earlier webhook line-cap failure is resolved

The previous revision pushed `webhook.ts` from 829 to 830 counted lines. Moving the turn's cleanup
ownership into the response generator - where the run lifecycle already lives - **removed** a line
from `webhook.ts` rather than adding one, so the file is back within baseline with no unrelated
decomposition of that file.

### Three remaining ratchet failures are inherited from `main`

```
src/secrets/egress-proxy/proxy-server.test.ts: 1000 -> 1021 counted lines (cap 1000)
src/state/agent-database-startup.ts:            700 ->  708 counted lines (cap 700)
test lines: 6590377; ceiling: 6590318; over by 59; net delta +10449
```

Neither file is touched by this PR, both are byte-identical to `main`, and
`config/max-lines-baseline.txt` and `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` are byte-identical to `main`'s.
The `+10449` test-line delta arrived with the merge from `main`. This PR's own contribution to the
test-line count is **negative**: the withdrawn exec suite and a leaner coordinator suite outweigh
the added webhook cases, and the allocation was recut 398 -> 272 to match the surviving suites.

## Review response

This revision addresses the ownership, logging, documentation, test-allocation and proof findings
from the Codex review. Command arguments no longer reach the abort diagnostic; cancellation binds to
the exact admitted response instead of the current session occupant; the duplicate run registry is
gone and cleanup carries its own identity; the realtime documentation claim is withdrawn; and the
exec abort-kill suite was withdrawn along with the command-label logging it existed to pin.

The product question - whether the preserved-accepted-work split from #133484 is a principle that
should always hold or a default a deployment may opt out of - remains open and is asked separately
in the thread.

## Provenance notes

This branch was ported fresh onto current `main`, not rebased: the source branch sat on a base
24,034 commits behind, on top of a local integration branch carrying unrelated work. Only the
barge-in scope is here. Deliberately excluded: the chunking work (#118727), deepgram changes from
closed PRs, a queued-message-marker removal that upstream has since extended rather than dropped,
and an `isOpenAIResponsesApi` parameter removal that fights the documented Codex-normalization
design.

`main` has since been merged in to clear a conflict; the only conflicted file was the generated
`docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`, resolved by regenerating it rather than taking either
side.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add creator-only and named-audience confidentiality
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People sharing an OpenClaw server need to control who can find and use each conversation.

## User Impact

A conversation can be personal to its creator and administrators, shared with selected people, or open to server users who already have the required permissions. This choice is separate from collaboration modes. Existing sessions without access metadata retain their previous behavior; existing roles and creation permissions still apply.

For attended Control UI conversations, the creator can be bound on creation or the first message when the creator-only default is enabled. No invitation UI is added, and “open to the server” does not mean anonymous access.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audience is enforced for discovery, history, updates and media. Restricted history can be forked only by the direct creator or a direct administrator. Native system input retains its provenance so it cannot be treated as an ordinary attended human message when applying the creator-only default; existing consent and privacy guards still apply.

## Evidence

The merge to pinned upstream `9ca793` passed focused local checks: 58 creator tests, 23 visibility tests, 7 restart tests, 5 replay and custody tests, and 9 owner tests. Core and gateway test types, typed lint, formatting, the test ledger and line caps passed. Independent P0–P2 reviews covered the merge and its subsequent test-only adjustment. Earlier native boundary evidence covered 21 tests; it is not a hosted CI result.

A merge simulation against upstream `07c8e141` found a conflict in the generated configuration baseline checksum. This PR still needs that conflict resolved; hosted CI and maintainer security review remain separate checks.

The following are real screenshots from an earlier isolated notebook run with synthetic admin, Alice and Bob accounts and additional local overlays. They illustrate the access behavior; they do not qualify this head or a real employee login. [Full screenshots and test context](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187836#issuecomment-6635034742).

Synthetic session visibility for admin, Alice and Bob:

![Synthetic admin, Alice and Bob session visibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/master/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-visibility.png)

Synthetic Alice opening an allowed history and being denied another:

![Synthetic Alice allowed and denied histories](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/master/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-alice-history.png)

[Earlier integrated-candidate and upgrade evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187836#issuecomment-6815411364) is separate from this public head. No real LDAP login is claimed.

prs.title: fix(sessions): reduce main-thread work when loading long transcripts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long transcript loads spend main-thread CPU constructing and discarding Zod validation results for every entry.

## User Impact

Transcript hydration does less allocation and validation machinery work while keeping recognized entries, opaque records, legacy migration, and corruption handling unchanged. No storage format or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared codec now uses direct structural predicates. Normal messages avoid parsed envelope/content copies, and unknown or malformed rows avoid constructing Zod errors. The reset-reason coercion retains its existing schema contract. Generic append and import can preserve opaque rows beneath a current-version header, so the header cannot authorize an unchecked type-tag bypass. Database admission certifies physical/schema integrity and canonical session metadata, not transcript message shapes; its separate owner remains unchanged.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, recorded before measured arms: exercise the actual `prepareSessionManagerEntries` hydration boundary at 1,000, 5,000, and 20,000 synthetic entries, with tool exchanges, compaction summaries, custom/plugin records, malformed rows, and both current and legacy headers. Run five counterbalanced A/A and A/B pairs. Require identical complete partition hashes, lower main-thread CPU and sampled allocation per load, and no material latency regression. Report median, p95, spread, and host load. Allocation sampling includes collected objects and runs separately from timing. SQL, worker transport, JSON decoding, and full Gateway latency are outside this owner measurement.

Reproduce with a baseline codec captured from the parent:

```sh
git show 8ef78ec2dc4e77058565bd1e68696848e49e4edd:src/config/sessions/session-entry-codec.ts > /path/to/base-codec.ts
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/session-entry-load-measure.ts --baseline-source /path/to/base-codec.ts --output /path/to/results.json
```


Controlled measurements completed: five counterbalanced pairs per experiment; all 120 partition digests match their size/version peers. Node v26.12.1 on macOS arm64. Timing uses main-thread CPU; sampled allocation includes collected JavaScript objects, excluding native allocations.

| Entries | Header | CPU ms before / after | Allocation bytes before / after | Mean wall ms before / after | Per-process p95 ms before / after |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | v4 | 0.474 / 0.115 | 2,572,964 / 235,586 | 0.479 / 0.116 | 0.739 / 0.164 |
| 1,000 | v2 | 0.464 / 0.093 | 2,238,847 / 224,136 | 0.467 / 0.093 | 0.849 / 0.103 |
| 5,000 | v4 | 2.849 / 0.400 | 13,236,540 / 1,173,458 | 2.863 / 0.401 | 3.999 / 0.514 |
| 5,000 | v2 | 2.080 / 0.412 | 11,192,214 / 1,167,542 | 2.095 / 0.415 | 2.615 / 0.464 |
| 20,000 | v4 | 11.961 / 1.817 | 51,315,302 / 4,609,986 | 12.079 / 1.821 | 18.711 / 2.160 |
| 20,000 | v2 | 9.356 / 1.836 | 45,103,792 / 4,469,202 | 9.408 / 1.843 | 11.977 / 2.039 |

Values are medians across five processes per arm. All six CPU medians fall 75.7–86.0%; allocation falls 89.6–91.1%. A/A median CPU differs at most 2.8%, allocation at most 0.8%. No measured wall/p95 regression.

The largest transcript is 169713025 serialized bytes. Fixtures are synthetic and predominantly tool exchanges, with compaction, plugin, opaque, corrupt, and legacy-hook rows. This measures the actual `prepareSessionManagerEntries` boundary after decoding. It excludes SQLite, worker transport, cold startup, and full Gateway load, and does not reproduce a 35 GiB database or filesystem workload. No live data was used.

Validation: 69 focused codec/persistence/replay/import tests and five local UI browser/E2E tests pass. Final independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2. A benchmark-only oversized-string defect found in review was fixed using incremental hashes before measured runs. Production +9 lines (+104/-95), tests +46, benchmark +173. The small production growth replaces schema machinery with explicit predicates without dropping malformed-input constraints. No cache, schema, configuration, session-row projection, or append-normalization change.

Final `pnpm check:changed` passes. Its initial patch-local proof-code lint findings were corrected, followed by the passing 25-case codec replay and fresh clean Codex review. CPU profiles corroborate reduced Zod work (389 package self samples before, 4 after, including startup); profiles are excluded from timing results. [ClawSweeper reviewed the final head with zero findings and no before-merge items](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197900#issuecomment-6835116534). [Exact-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43299917121) on `502b444f6f882698b43c61a358a63f341769b51c`, including all PostgreSQL conformance jobs. Native `scripts/pr` landed the reviewed head as `10285cd35ca7d696957430bbc6c8556f55af79fe`; no admin exception or CI rerun was needed.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): resume reclaim after Gateway startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: expired worktree scratch waits another full hour after each Gateway restart, so frequent restarts can prevent reclaim from running.

Related: #197772.

## User Impact

Reclaim starts after the existing post-ready startup barrier and grace period, then continues hourly. Completed scratch removals survive restarts without a checkpoint or schema change. Existing exclusive custody, identity, expiry, pressure brakes, and bounded budgets remain in force.

## Why This Change Was Made

The startup owner already waits for deferred recovery and admission to settle. The maintenance owner now schedules its first pass immediately when that barrier admits it, instead of adding another hourly delay. This changes one scheduling value; production executable LOC is unchanged, with two explanatory comment lines added.

The documentation also makes cleanup ownership explicit: clones directly under `.openclaw/<name>` and `loops/contributor-prs/worktrees/pr-*-native` remain owned by their creating task or maintainer workflow. Their names do not establish disposal authority, and the broader `.openclaw` directory can hold durable files. Native workflow cleanup owns registered landing worktrees; unregistered clones require their creator to verify closeout. Future disposable clones should use the existing `.openclaw/tmp/` roots. This deliberately avoids widening automatic deletion authority.

## Evidence

- Isolated shipped CLI proof on final head `69a4b4fbaf673db3574efcf7a8c413d5e03c823d`: two `pnpm openclaw gateway run` processes, separate synthetic state/workspace, real local Git clones, real timers and cleanup, no cleanup mocks. First startup removed three expired clones 2.223 seconds after `/readyz` returned 200 (18.494 seconds from launcher start). After a clean stop, restart removed a newly expired clone 1.468 seconds after ready (14.863 seconds from launch). The fresh file was byte-identical after both runs; earlier deletions remained absent. The first pass logged 3 entries / 86,247 bytes reclaimed with zero failures. On restart, filesystem assertions verified the new expired clone was gone; stopping immediately afterward canceled the remaining GC phase, so that pass has no completion-result line. Both Gateways reported clean shutdown; listener and owned process groups were verified absent. Channels/providers were disabled for this maintenance-only proof; no model or transport-load claim.
- The new startup regression fails on parent `0b04511ee505bd212f79172600f6228c2a9708cd` with “cleanup never started,” then passes with the scheduling fix. It reclaims real expired scratch before held GC, stops/restarts the owner, and verifies preserved progress and fresh contents.
- Restart replay discards the directory cursor after removing 256 of 258 expired entries. The next pass removes the remaining two; the following pass removes zero. Checkout scan counts fall to four then zero; coverage scans fall to six then two. Unrelated files survive.
- Focused owner, collector, maintenance consumer, runtime-service, real Gateway post-ready, telemetry drain, and all archive/delete/inbound worktree fixture consumers: 133 passed, one existing Linux-only skip. Real Gateway coverage verifies deferred startup and shutdown ownership. Existing maintenance test clocks were adjusted to settle the newly queued startup pass before asserting later idle recovery.
- Initial CI run 43297974897 exposed four assertions in two additional consumer fixtures that assumed delayed startup. These PR-caused failures reproduced locally. The fixture now completes startup cleanup before installing archive-ordering probes; telemetry setup completes startup before simulating a late wake that holds channel admission, then measures producers from drain. All 45 affected consumer tests pass; archive-response and shutdown assertions remain intact.
- `pnpm check:changed` for the original patch and the test-only repair; `pnpm docs:list`; `git diff --check`. Independent Codex autoreview: no actionable findings through P2.
- The cleanup algorithm and per-pass workload from #197772 are unchanged. Its production-shaped Linux/btrfs proof remains the throughput evidence: 0 to 256 entries per 60-second window, worst commit maximum 503 to 111 ms, worst loop p99 13.49 to 16.42 ms and maximum 59.9 to 83.3 ms. The maintainer accepted that measured background loop-tail cost. This follow-up adds deterministic scheduling and restart proof, not a new throughput/CPU claim.

Exact-head CI run [43302197524](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43302197524) passed. [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197898#issuecomment-6835073332) reviewed the final head with zero open items; both earlier findings are addressed in [the numbered response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197898#issuecomment-6835320793).

No runtime configuration options, runtime state-file format, database schema, or UI imports changed. No production deletion, restart, or deployment was performed; production count and commit-latency verification remain with the reliability session after deployment.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): link your OpenClaw ID so your owner devices connect as you
prs.body:
Related: #197559 (stacked on it; review that first)

## What Problem This Solves

When you connect to your claw from one of your OpenClaw ID owner devices, the Gateway shows you as "Shared owner" rather than as your own profile.

## User Impact

With OpenClaw ID Labs on, you can link your OpenClaw ID account to your own personal profile (Profile → Identity → Link). After that, your owner devices connect as you, while keeping full owner authority. Linking and unlinking affect only future connections. A linked owner device is never limited by the named role on the profile it's linked to.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One link step:** both sides are proven on one connection. The device sign-in from #197559 proves the account, and the personal sign-in proves the profile. So there is no profile picker.
- **One profile per account:** an account can be linked to at most one profile. A profile can hold several accounts, including after a profile merge, and unlink removes all of them.
- **Profile vs. certificate:** the linked profile decides who you appear as. Your owner certificate decides what you're allowed to do.
- **Role changes don't touch owner devices:** `users.setRole` publishes a role-only change. A linked owner device's runs, recovered runs, cron streams and socket are rechecked, not revoked, because its certificate is unchanged. A merge is still an identity change and still revokes them.
- **Owner-only bypass:** only a real owner tunnel connection whose certificate is currently valid skips the person's role. Synthetic clients, host ingress, members and nodes keep their existing limits. Once the owner certificate lapses, the person's role applies again.

<details><summary>Where owner authority is preserved</summary>

- connect and session attribution
- operator-run capture, tool dispatch and run recovery
- cron sandbox streams
- policy refresh
- access-grant resumption
- personal APIs (GitHub, model accounts, personal files, backgrounds)
- My Skills and session skill seeding

**Profile row states (Labs on):** the OpenClaw ID row is there from first paint. It shows Loading, then Link/Unlink on a personal sign-in. On other connections it says "Link over a personal sign-in, such as Tailscale", with no action. If loading fails, it shows an error with Retry. With Labs off the row is absent.

Link and unlink writes are fenced through to commit. They check the live personal connection, the profile and the Labs switch at commit time.
</details>

## Known limitations (fail closed: they deny, never grant)

- **OCF-513:** sessions a linked owner device creates are still sandboxed when the person's role requires a sandbox.
- **OCF-514:** GitHub publication can refuse a linked owner whose profile is restricted. The publication requester snapshot doesn't carry the owner-device principal, so the person's role applies.

Both are tracked as follow-ups blocked by this PR and are intentionally not fixed here.

## Evidence

- Focused tests pass, including a real-Gateway test with a linked owner whose role is `talker` (a role with no read access). It checks profile attribution, admin scope, personal APIs, backgrounds, My Skills, and a config refresh that does not drop the connection.
- Regression tests for each review finding fail without its fix:
  - role resolution in tool dispatch, policy refresh, access-grant resumption, skill-library limits;
  - stale-certificate personal APIs, and a link write fenced after authority changes;
  - **`be82b88`:** `users.setRole` keeps a linked owner's captured run (an identity change still revokes it), and keeps its real-Gateway socket and admin access;
  - **`be82b88`:** session skill seeding, checked by the actual seeded skills rather than mock arguments;
  - **`be82b88`:** the Profile row is present while loading, and a failed load recovers through Retry.
  - **`bc7c8ed`:** a *stored* role change (written through the profile writer, as `users.setRole` does) keeps a linked owner's run. Run capture, recovery and cron streams no longer compare the stored role for a current owner certificate; identity and certificate checks still apply. This test fails without the fix.
- Affected files rerun together after `be82b88` (role, merge, request context, run authority and recovery, cron streams, identity scopes, linked owner, Profile UI): 15 files pass.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:src`, `tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint, `ui:i18n:verify` and `check:control-ui-controllers` pass.

- **Test lines:** `config/test-lines-allocations/197628-openclaw-id-link-profile.txt` records 483 lines over the allowance. These are the regression tests for each review finding on linked-owner authority: dispatch, policy refresh, recovery, stored-role changes, personal APIs, skill seeding, fenced link writes and the Profile row.
- Restacked on #197559's boot-size change: the link option of the device sign-in now lives in the lazily loaded `device-sign-in.ts`.

- **Accepted CI failure — `control-ui-performance` (+68 B):** startup ("new"/"chat" boot) JS grows 68 B gzip against #197559's head; main is already over this cap, so only 64 B of build variance is allowed. None of this PR's code is in `control-ui-boot-shared.js`; the only change there is one extra preload-map entry (`claw-name`) for the Profile page's identity row. Two UI-only workarounds made it larger (+426 B, +228 B). Josh accepted the 68 B on 2026-11-12.

### Live proof against staging OpenClaw ID

Real Gateways built from this branch, with headless Chromium. The personal identity comes from a trusted proxy on the same host, and approvals happen on the staging issuer.

**Upgrade from stable `2026.11.3` → head `be82b88`** (fsn1, throwaway Gateway and state):
1. Stable created three personal profiles. It renamed two and added an email alias.
2. `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the standard migrations. Agent database schema 27 comes from main; this PR adds no schema.
3. This build started on the same state with Labs on.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Profiles, display names and email aliases load unchanged after upgrade | pass (`users.list` before = after) |
| Upgraded profile shows OpenClaw ID "Not linked" with Link | pass |
| Link: device code → approve on staging → the row shows the account with Unlink | pass |
| `link_status` returns the linked account without its account ID | pass |
| The same account linked from another profile | refused: "already linked to another profile"; nothing is linked there |
| Unlink | the row returns to "Not linked" |

**OpenClaw ID testnet, head `63ee6b00`.** The `gateway` lab host ran a throwaway Gateway; the claw's live service wasn't touched. It passed the same link → refuse → unlink checks. A testnet rerun at `be82b88` was stopped when an SSM port forward stalled, so `be82b88` was proven by the upgrade run above.

Not covered live: a real owner-device reconnect over the OpenClaw ID tunnel after linking. Enrolling an owner device needs Discovery enrollment and the tunnel, so the real-Gateway integration test covers that path.

| Before (`5f6001b`): no OpenClaw ID row | After, upgraded profile: not linked |
|---|---|
| ![Profile identity group without an OpenClaw ID row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f63dccc-a6fc-4cd3-a9ab-c69e4a1e8bf1) | ![Upgraded profile with OpenClaw ID Not linked and Link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6fe802af-7217-4221-bcf7-daab4e76f999) |

| Link sign-in | Issuer confirmation (staging) |
|---|---|
| ![Device sign-in dialog opened from Link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf948df0-0f8c-432f-9018-163834184e16) | ![Issuer asks to confirm the code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e8a3f22-f8b9-4ebe-8418-bbe979d8d8e2) |

| Linked | Same account on another profile | Unlinked |
|---|---|---|
| ![OpenClaw ID row shows the account and Unlink](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38ca5212-519b-4660-b0df-2e23d402ef21) | ![Bob's profile shows the already-linked message](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ceaf037-9b8f-4746-822f-48e132afd280) | ![Row back to Not linked](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddeaf266-41e2-4b5d-b67c-55e995957e56) |

prs.title: fix: Claude CLI turns hit the output limit after a few edits of large files
prs.body:
Closes #159929
Related: #150132, #153545, #159931, #119445

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Claude CLI (`claude-cli`) turns fail with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.` when the agent edits large files a handful of times in one turn.

## User Impact

User impact: agents on the Claude CLI backend can edit and rewrite large files (hundreds of KB) repeatedly in one turn without spending the per-turn stream-json output budget on copies of those files.

## Why This Change Was Made

For every Edit and Write, Claude Code's `user` record carries the model-facing `tool_result` message (a one-line "has been updated successfully" string) and a `tool_use_result` object meant for SDK consumers. For Edit and Write, that object holds:

- `originalFile`: the whole file as it was before the edit.
- `structuredPatch`: a diff that can span the whole file.
- For Write, `content`: the new file.

OpenClaw never reads `tool_use_result`; the only reference is the existing normalizer that strips echoed image and PDF bytes (#119486, #128699). The stream-json parser still charged these copies in full against the 8 MiB turn budget. Editing an 800 KB file three times used roughly 2.4 MiB of budget on text the model never sees.

This change drops those three fields in `normalizeClaudeCliStreamJsonRecord`, in the same way that function already omits echoed binary data. Details:

- **What is dropped.** `tool_use_result.originalFile`, `.structuredPatch` and `.content`.
- **When.** Only when `tool_use_result` has a string `filePath` and an `originalFile` key; Edit, Write-update and Write-create all carry both. Other `tool_use_result` shapes keep full accounting. That includes Read, whose `file.content` also duplicates the tool_result; it is left for a separate change.
- **What is kept.** `filePath`, `oldString`, `newString`, `type`, `userModified` and the model-facing `message.content` tool_result. The tool result OpenClaw emits is unchanged.
- **Per-line cap.** The raw per-line cap still applies unchanged. `frameBoundedCliJsonlChunk` checks each raw line against 8 MiB before any parsing, so a single echo over 8 MiB still fails with `CLI JSONL line exceeded …`. Only the per-turn total stops counting the echoes.
- **No new setting.** Configurability stays out, per #111382.

**Overlap with #153545:** none at the file level. #153545 changes partial-message delta accounting in `cli-output-stream.ts` and `cli-output-stream-limits.ts`. This PR touches only `cli-output-echoed-binary.ts` and adds tests in `cli-output-framing.test.ts`. The two fixes are complementary: #153545 makes streamed text cheaper, and this PR makes Edit and Write results cheaper. The residual `Math.max(normalized.line.length, rawLine.length - omittedRawChars)` accounting in the parser is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Real capture** from Claude Code 2.1.281 (`claude -p … --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits`, working on a 109,890-character file). The numbers are characters charged by the parser before and after this change:

| Record | Raw line | Charged before | Charged after | Model-facing tool_result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Edit | 113,870 | 113,870 | 617 | 147 bytes |
| Write (update, 6-byte content) | 232,433 | 232,433 | 565 | — |
| Whole 55-line session | 761,870 | 761,870 | 416,743 | — |

On a Write update, `structuredPatch` held one hunk covering all 3,001 old lines, so a Write costs about twice the file size. The rest of the post-fix session total is Read results and ordinary output.

**Production failures.** OpenClaw 2026.9.5, claude-cli backend, Opus, WSL2, overnight scheduled turns:

- **Sep 26:** made three edits each to an 831 KB and a 761 KB JavaScript file.
- **Sep 27:** made seven edits to a 599 KB test file.

By the per-record sizes above, those edits alone charged about 4.8 MB and 4.2 MB of the 8 MiB budget. The rest of the budget went to `--include-partial-messages` deltas, which #153545 addresses: about 6 MB and 11k lines by minute 130 in the Sep 27 turn.

Both turns then stopped showing progress, and stuck-session recovery ended them about 15 minutes later (after 45.8 and 147.8 minutes) as `CLI run aborted`, without logging the limit error. That silent stall is the failure mode in #143396, which #159931 addresses.

**Tests** (`src/agents/cli-output-framing.test.ts`, three new cases):

- 20 alternating Edit and Write results on a 560,000-character file (far over 8 MiB raw in total) parse without error and still emit the short tool results. This case **fails on main** with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters`.
- `tool_use_result` payloads that are not file echoes (a `filePath` with no `originalFile`) are still charged and still trip the budget.
- A single 8 MiB `originalFile` echo still trips the raw per-line cap.

Commands run:

- `pnpm test src/agents/cli-output-framing.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24/24 pass in about 2.3 s wall time. The new cases take 122, 7 and 13 ms, so CI cost is well under 1 s in the existing shard.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` (core and core-test lanes) passed: format, the ratchets, `tsgo:core`, the changed core-test typecheck shards, oxlint on the changed files, and the repo guards.
- The knip dead-export scan did not finish within the local 25-minute timeout. This change adds no exports.

Not captured: MultiEdit and NotebookEdit results. If their `tool_use_result` has no `originalFile`, it keeps full accounting, which is today's behavior, so there is no regression either way.

prs.title: fix(cron): cron show prints literal "\n" in multi-line run diagnostics
prs.body:
fix(cron): cron show prints literal "\n" in multi-line run diagnostics

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw cron show` rendered the stored run-diagnostics summary through the
terminal sanitizer, which escapes newlines, so a child command's multi-line
stderr printed as one line with literal `\n` sequences, like:

    diagnostic: boom-line-1\nboom-line-2

## User Impact

Operators running `cron show` can now read each output line instead of one
mangled line. Single-line values, exit codes, `--json` output and list output
are unchanged. This is the same newline-rendering class already fixed for
`sessions import` (#197255) and `approvals get`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostics fields carry Gateway/child output lines. Each line is now
sanitized separately and continuation lines are indented two spaces, keeping
the per-line control-character escaping intact while preserving layout.
`stream error`, `last error`, `last delivery error` and `diagnostic` share the
new helper; single-line values are unchanged.

## Evidence

Reproduced through the built CLI against an isolated secretless local Gateway
(secretless: no channels, no model auth, dedicated state dir) at base
e52cdb9, then re-checked after the fix (head 435ac8c). The multi-line state
came from a real flow: a command job whose run writes two stderr lines and
exits 3; `cron run` + `cron show`.

| Step | Output (excerpt) |
| --- | --- |
| Before | `diagnostic: boom-line-1\nboom-line-2` (one line, literal backslash-n) |
| After | `diagnostic: boom-line-1` + indented `boom-line-2` on the next line |

Exit code and every other line of `cron show` are identical on both runs.
Targeted test `src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`: 47 passed (46 existing + 1 new
regression). The new test was verified red with the fix stashed and green with
it applied.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local checks</summary>

Isolated Gateway (port 18801, loopback, dedicated state dir):

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=.../state node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port 18801
# job with multi-line stderr, then:
node scripts/run-node.mjs cron run <job-id>
node scripts/run-node.mjs cron show <job-id>
```

Before the fix the `diagnostic:` line contains literal `\n`; after it the
summary lines print separately with two-space indents. `node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/cli/cron-cli/shared.test.ts`
passes before (defect red on the new case only after stashing the fix) and
after (47 passed).
</details>

prs.title: fix: allow Gateway restart after late sidecar cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway in-process restarts exiting instead of returning ready when a sidecar takes more than five seconds to stop but successfully finishes during the mandatory final join.

## User Impact

A successfully cleaned-up Gateway can restart in the same process. Failed or still-pending sidecar cleanup continues to prevent resource release and restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

The early sidecar stop recorded a permanent timeout error, even though the later required sidecar owner had successfully joined that same operation. The restart loop treated this obsolete error as proof that resources were still retained.

Use the existing mandatory final sidecar join as the settlement decision for the two sidecar steps it owns. Preserve cleanup order, the five-second diagnostic grace, fatal failures, and other optional cleanup refusal contracts. Production growth is 12 lines to name this existing ownership explicitly; no new state, cache, configuration, timeout, or supervisor fallback.

## Evidence

- The scheduled Matrix restart/replay scenario recorded SIGUSR2, a five-second sidecar warning, successful sidecar and mandatory final settlement at 7.288 seconds, then an erroneous retained-resource restart refusal and exit 0: [run43258726252, QA job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43258726252/job/131324883400).
- Regression uses the actual sidecar stop owner and final join. Both successful late-stop variants fail on the original source; all nine shutdown tests pass with this change, including late rejection and genuine optional retained work. Talk prelude and actual run-loop siblings passed 177/177.
- Codex autoreview of the two-file local snapshot on d3ce53dde359c95f32d096a5a289eee17a1c47cc was scoped-clean through P2, with no findings. The reviewed source bytes and relevant lifecycle owners remain unchanged at 8fb0cf7a6d70a8bbb9ec583061cbe7943868e43a after integrating #197839.
- Ran `pnpm check:changed`: three compiler stages initially refused external dependency links, and the export scan reproduced the old-main unused exports. A private frozen install resolved all three compiler stages; after integrating #197839, production/full-tree/script export scans each report zero entries. All other selected changed-check stages passed in the original invocation.
- Actual unmodified Matrix restart/replay proof passed in [run 43299098210, QA profile 6/6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43299098210/job/131465840212) on inclusive head `7825ad2f2e3521fb095e14bfbbf3548b3723322d`. The two repair files and six inspected sidecar/lifecycle/QA files match this PR head byte for byte. Artifact `13981856526` contains one passing observation with no retry, matching launch/source and observation hashes, both accepted pre/post-restart replies, and no replay. The unchanged scenario sends SIGUSR2 to the existing child with `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`; the job records no replacement spawn during the scenario.
- Cleanup duration in that successful actual run is **unmeasured**: slim success artifacts and job output omit shutdown traces. There is no raw PID comparison or claim that the actual run crossed five seconds. The original real failure, exact-base controlled real-owner late-stop red/green, and actual same-process/replay/fresh-reply pass provide complementary evidence. No delay was injected into production.
- [Ordinary PR CI 43291949304](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43291949304) passed at exact `8fb0cf7a6d70a8bbb9ec583061cbe7943868e43a`; [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197883#issuecomment-6834095557) on the same head has zero findings/open items.
- Earlier local transport ancestry and remote native-preparation refusals happened before Gateway/payload startup (`commandMs: 0` remotely); they remain setup-only evidence. The task-owned remote lease was cleaned up and its resource absence verified.

The timeout-leftover behavior dates to #185730 (9344233e7a66fe36479d55b7f7ae8e10eb886586), before the last scheduled green. The initial slow sidecar’s cause remains unqualified; this change fixes the separately reproduced stale refusal after successful settlement. No flaky or infrastructure classification is inferred from a passing replay. Unit timings are not a controlled performance benchmark.

prs.title: fix: stop closed macOS dashboards reconnecting after native auth refusal
prs.body:
Related: #168743

## What Problem This Solves

Closing or replacing a natively authenticated macOS Dashboard can leave its committed page reconnecting after that window can no longer obtain native authorization, producing repeated pre-connect warnings.

## User Impact

Closing or replacing a native Dashboard now retires and unloads its document. A retained window reopens its trusted route using the same WebView storage; hiding or minimizing preserves its live document. Exact repeated native-refusal warnings retain the first diagnostic and periodic suppressed counts rather than one warning per attempt.

Real-WKWebView and Gateway evidence is available, with the revision and host limits below. The reporter subsequently supplied an exact-`4abd9e5` packaged-app-to-real-Gateway close/drop/reopen comparison on November 6, linked under Evidence. Historical negative results remain disclosed; no full native-suite green or native execution of a later integration is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Stopping WebKit navigation does not unload a committed page. The existing controller now retires that document and its identity at actual native close/replacement, retains its trusted reopen route, and keeps the inert retirement page non-deliverable. Browser identity, origin/account storage boundaries and transient native recovery remain intact; there is no refusal cap or retry-policy change.

The Gateway extends its existing bounded authentication-log limiter only for pre-connect code 4008 and the exact raw reason native authorization unavailable. Code 1006, near-matches and credential-mismatch warnings keep their previous behavior.

The supplied native run also exposed an obsolete notification-test oracle: after closing, it expected the outgoing page to remain at /. The follow-up test repair now requires about:blank while closed, explicitly reopens, then waits for the retained / route instead of the stale notification's completion route. Window identity, closed state and non-close navigation checks are preserved.

## Evidence

### Current integration qualification

The signed, ancestry-preserving integration is `6ca718a2884793bce8863d49eb7f916ab85b2cef` (tree `6fb3ad3c0b439843e9f009f46fde6717c2b11d9b`), integrating protected main `c00f78c93167086887753d75345d4803d4880ee2`. The sole conflict preserves both the native titlebar inset state and the retired-document route. All 12 files retain byte-for-byte identical ordered additions/removals to the original reviewed PR delta; a fresh independent integration review found no P0–P2 findings. Existing runtime proof remains labeled with its original executing revision.

[Exact published-head CI, run 43296884294](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43296884294), attempt 1, completed successfully for `6ca718a2884793bce8863d49eb7f916ab85b2cef`: 59 jobs, no pending or failed jobs. Separate dependency, security-sensitive-review and combined CI commit statuses were also observed successful. This is new-head CI, not a relabeling of the original-head runs below; no new native full-suite execution is claimed.

### Packaged-app proof received November 6

[The reporter's exact-head comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6678794210) used a packaged app identifying `4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4` and a real Gateway. The fixed app released its page socket on close, made zero reconnect attempts during the 10.1-minute observation window (and throughout 18.6 minutes closed), then connected a fresh page 0.6 seconds after reopening. The main control retained its socket and made 16 native-refusal attempts after the forced tunnel drop. This is contributor-reported evidence from one run per build on the same Mac/Gateway, with the forced-drop and attribution limits stated in that comment; it is not an independent rerun or proof for a later integration.

The earlier receipts and their negative results are retained separately below.

- The notification replay test is repaired without removing ownership checks. Supplied stock-host focused runs pass **9/9 only with that dirty test patch**; they are not executions of the new commit.
- Real WKWebView evidence denies stale credentials and permits a fresh document after close, replacement and immediate reopen. A selective base overlay actually fails the two immediate-reopen assertions.
- New supplied focused TypeScript proof is **65/65**, separate from the historical **67/5-file** run. The synthetic real-Gateway trace emits **2 native + 3 control** warnings versus **12 + 3** on the selective base overlay; it does not prove app reconnect cessation.
- **Lint is not green:** normal scope has one source-verified inherited file-length violation; a different explicit touched-test scope reports 60 serious diagnostics. Restricted sibling sweeps, crashes, timeouts and omissions are disclosed below—not counted passing.
- **Qualification limits:** the packaged-app proof above addresses the previously missing close/reconnect correlation at `4abd9e5`. Published-head CI and any later integration qualification remain separate. The historical hosted review rated overall readiness 3/6; ratings are advisory. No full native-suite green or native execution of a later integration is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Audited receipts, sanitized excerpts, source equivalence and all negative results</summary>

### Revision, source equivalence and hosts

The [reporter's public evidence comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6552265574) and independently audited supplied bundle concern head f56bd97a670203f386ff71e313f25e50d6562afc and admitted base 3a3246e7c1389c03e933e1f15805306945b1df1c. The audit inspected artifacts; it did not rerun supplied scripts or tests. All 70 declared bundle checksums matched; ZIP SHA-256: 3c684b5ed17f6304d842331974a271b140bfb86ee3a16b288d861b61d99b6bb2.

The [new repair commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4) changes only DashboardNotificationWindowTests.swift (+4/−1) from that recorded head. Its complete resulting file is byte-identical to the published f56 file plus the audited patch (patch SHA-256 3151270b79163551c9f5082ba0dc15a161bb855139191716f680dd6682235d64; resulting Git blob 7ab8659bf05356f99fddfef4e7a05b4db7236e31). All eleven earlier changed source files still match f56. This establishes tracked-source equivalence, not a new-commit test execution or complete generated/untracked/build-input attestation.

- Host A is reported as stock Xcode 27.1/Swift 6.4 on macOS 27.2 arm64 with a GUI. Library/platform/AppKit records partly corroborate that metadata; the bundle does not contain a complete pinned checkout/toolchain attestation.
- Host B directly records swift.org 6.3.3/SDK26.5 without GUI, substitute SwiftUI/Preview macro plugins, and two omitted XCTest files (SimpleTaskSupportTests.swift and MacNodeLocationServiceTests.swift). Its results are adapted, restricted coverage—not a stock/full native build. Supplied Studio scripts omit untracked files from dirty-state output.
- Head-plus-patch passes still record the old f56 HEAD and a modified test. Base-overlay runs retain the head checkout/tests and restore selected production files, not a clean full-base checkout. Exact overlaid bytes cannot be independently reconstructed from the bundle. No supplied scripts or macro stubs were executed during this audit/update.

### Real WKWebView outcomes — including the original red test

Unpatched f56 is not native-green: “older manager command replay does not cancel a newer notification click” fails refreshed-close and new-window-close, receiving an empty path where its old oracle expected /. The supplied base overlay and head-plus-patch each pass its four cases on both hosts. The source owner inspected the real retirement implementation and wait helper before applying the audited correction above.

| Supplied selection | Audited result and limit |
| --- | --- |
| A, recorded clean-state f56, focused 9 tests / 3 suites | 8 test functions pass; older-manager fails with 2 issues; EXIT=1. The WK ownership matrix (10 cases), forbidden frame/browser-identity cases (3), retained close/reopen (2), replacement unload, device-settings (9 cases) and 3 ControlUIDocument tests pass. |
| A, f56 plus dirty test patch, same selection | 9 tests / 3 suites pass in 31.181 seconds; EXIT=0. Separate older-manager rerun passes 4 cases. Not an exact-new-commit rerun. |
| B, adapted focused selections | Auth bridge 4 tests pass, including 3 + 10 + 2 parameter cases; device settings 1 test / 9 cases and isolated conversation factory pass. Socket-retirement and saved-profile selections crash with signal 5 on both head and base overlay; those are not passes. |
| B, adapted restricted sibling sweep | 252 test-pass records; 253 tests / 46 suites fail with 2 issues, EXIT=1. The completed sweep's failing test is older-manager. Other attempts abort or remain incomplete. No full-suite green. |

The important completed negative control uses the real WK reply boundary: A's selective native base overlay reaches immediate-reopen, delivers a grant to the retired document and fails two assertions. The recorded head denies that stale recipient and completes a fresh current recipient after close, replacement and immediate reopen. It also accepts current/current-password/current-device-only and rejects document/provider/socket/browser-identity stale replies.

Sanitized excerpts below are supplied-log evidence, not independent reruns. Anchors name bundle-relative files; they are not public download URLs. Credential payloads, local paths and endpoint/host values are omitted.

    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-base-native-WK_challenge_replies_are_owned_.log:20,23,41–48
      immediate-reopen: expected error != nil and result == nil; both fail
      transition=immediate-reopen result=true error=false
      ten cases failed with 2 issues; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-head-native-focused.log:26–32
      close and replacement: stale response denied; new current recipient completes
      transition=immediate-reopen result=false error=true
      current-recipient=new-document completed; ten cases passed
    EVIDENCE/laptop/laptop-patch-head-native-focused.log:45–49
      older-manager four cases passed
      Test run with 9 tests in 3 suites passed after 31.181 seconds. EXIT=0

Other negative results remain material: A's base unload/reopen and replacement attempts time out at planning with no test-start marker; these are noncompletion, not assertion-red. Its base forbidden-frame filter reports No matching test cases were run, not coverage. A's experience selection fails with Keychain -60006 (10 tests / 3 suites, EXIT=1). B sweep run2 aborts on an uncalled download completion handler (signal 6); run3 has a miniaturize wait failure and Keychain -61 failures without a completed summary. The saved sweep script has nine exclusion-regex alternatives; the completed log lacks exact argv and earlier filters evolved. Exclusions/crashes are not passes, and not every failure/exclusion is independently matched on base.

### Gateway and focused TypeScript proof

New supplied focused tests: 65/65 in 3 files pass, EXIT=0. The same head tests with selective base connection.ts and handshake-auth-log-limiter.ts yield 63 pass / 2 fail, EXIT=1; only the two native-refusal aggregation regressions fail. Both captures identify Vitest 5.0.5, test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts and:

    node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/server/ws-connection.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-helpers.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/handshake-auth-log-limiter.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

A real isolated loopback Gateway and synthetic WebSocket client receive connect.challenge and send 12 native-refusal closes (10, wait 31 s, then 2), plus 3 connect-failed controls. The selective base overlay emits 12 native +3 control lines; recorded head emits 2 native +3 control lines, with suppressed=9 on the second native warning. This proves transport logging suppression, not authentication success or app reconnect cessation. The final suppressed attempt has no later emitted summary; 2+9 must not be presented as accounting for all 12 attempts.

    EVIDENCE/head-ts-focused.log:127–135: 3 files passed; 65 tests passed; EXIT=0
    EVIDENCE/base-overlay-ts-focused.log:185–195: 63 passed; 2 failed; EXIT=1
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-head.log:3–15: 12 native closes +3 controls; 5 warning lines
    EVIDENCE/live-gateway-base-overlay.log:3–14: same plan; 15 warning lines

These captures do not establish complete dependency/configuration/source-state parity or a combined app-to-Gateway run.

### Formatting and lint — scopes are not interchangeable

Supplied SwiftFormat lint reports 0/416 files requiring formatting (6 skipped), then0/33, with one combined EXIT=0. It is not compilation or a blanket touched-test lint pass.

Both normal SwiftLint captures report 1 serious violation / 419 files, EXIT=2: DashboardManager.swift file_length 1505 >1500. Source comparison now independently establishes that DashboardManager.swift is byte-identical at admitted base 3a, recorded f56 and this candidate (SHA-256 896a2f6f9c430ab7cacde9f0345e43b26c809e4ce012e0965f713d0d51d5ec64). The PR does not introduce this failure. Current main has a separate provider addition, not identical bytes; it is not claimed lint-clean.

The additional explicit touched-file capture reports 60 serious violations / 5 files, EXIT=2, in the test-file inputs; DashboardWindowController.swift has no diagnostic there. This negative result is retained, not called green or silently attributed to base. Exact touched-command flags/effective config/version are absent from the bundle, so its 60 findings cannot be equated to the standard invocation.

The pinned standard owner is scripts/lint-swift.sh macos → run-swiftlint.mts --strict --config config/swiftlint.yml, plus the swabble config. Those wrappers/configs are unchanged across admitted base, f56, candidate and inspected current main. The standard config includes Sources roots, not the explicit test-file list. Its 1500 file-length warning becomes serious under local strict mode; the existing wrapper treats limit rules as advisory only in genuine GitHub Actions. This is source-policy inspection, not an executed CI/lint pass; no flags, baselines, exclusions or rules were weakened. The standard format wrapper also checks declared Sources roots, not every test file.

### Historical proof kept separate

Historical local October 27 validation leading to f69148d4cbef51ff1586c74a87637071b9ede57d: 67 tests /5 files passed (40.39s), targeted TypeScript lint/typecheck/format/diff checks passed. An isolated Gateway run observed 3 refused closes → 2 warnings including suppressed=1, another signed client remained connected, and a later signed reconnect received hello. Native-auth UI recovery 29 passed; draft-commit persistence 1 passed. The new 65-test bundle neither contains that historical terminal run nor independently reproduces it. Neither number is a new-head rerun.

The preconnect consolidation preserved 28 named tests and 38 transferred assertions; original/replacement overlap 36 passed and deliberate producer omissions failed the retained old/new guard families. Counted TypeScript test delta remains −24 with no baseline/counting-policy exception; these inputs are unchanged by the notification-test correction. [Recorded f56 ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537596408/job/122318487019), its test-line ratchet and [app/test-target compilation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40537596269/job/122307432139) passed. They are historical-head evidence, not current-head native execution.

### Original-head source review and qualification

Original-head Auto Review of the complete 12-file `4abd9e5` candidate against admitted base 3a: P0–P2 scoped-clean, no findings. Reviewed patch SHA-256 fb9a44316c87771416cdd5c746ba2c273e3f8d76b5bda6095f79a79be68e0452; expected tree 4d7f0fdfbe10ea8a93bdd46c0dd2ebba7a3a789d. This is independent static source review, not a hosted rating or native execution. Diff check passed. No configuration, protocol or persisted-data migration is introduced.

At original head `4abd9e5395cd30293cf5ffc625b97a114c6a2ec4`, [ordinary CI and its required gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485953/job/124731698532) (60 jobs, no failures), including the [unchanged test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485953/job/124730574678). [Current-head macOS Periphery app/test-target compilation passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41266485968/job/124730418174) (439.74s); this is not WKWebView test execution. The [durable hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185963#issuecomment-6444950457), reviewed November1 at02:54:58UTC for this exact head, reports high-confidence Ready for maintainer review, no findings and no Before-merge items. Its actual scores are overall3/6, proof3/6 and patch4/6. The optional rating improvement is a real built-app-to-Gateway close/reopen trace showing reconnect cessation; the requested overall Platinum threshold is not yet reached.

The supplied production extract is from unpatched OpenClaw 2026.10.9: 14 daily rows total 27,898 refusals (27,896 principal-group rows +2 timeout-bearing rows). October 31 has 746 inter-line gaps, 734 bucketed 12–16s. It supports occurrence/cadence, not a verified closed-window cause or a fixed-app result.

The November 6 packaged-app comparison above subsequently addresses the reporter-side close/reconnect gap at `4abd9e5`; it does not convert the earlier negative results into passes. A later integration still requires its own published-head CI and source qualification. No full native-suite green or native execution of a later integration is claimed.

</details>

prs.title: feat(sessions): keep useful names after context resets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resetting context should not turn a useful conversation title into `/model` or the text of a short “continue” message. This affects Telegram topics and Dashboard conversations.

## User Impact

The first real user message names the conversation without waiting for the agent to finish. Commands and bot or child-agent replies do not count as user tasks. After six follow-up user messages, the model compares the title with the opening message and those follow-ups, and keeps it when it still fits. After `/reset`, the first ordinary message compares the existing title with the new task rather than automatically replacing it. A fitting broad product, project, or person title keeps its exact wording, case, and language for related subtasks; replacement style instructions apply only if a new title is necessary. A manual edit that arrives during an older naming attempt wins.

Topics created by sending a message from Telegram’s **New Thread** screen also need a title. Telegram may give them an automatic name and mark it as implicit; this patch recognizes that marker instead of treating the name as a manual choice. Manual edits take precedence over an older naming attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

I normally reset a topic to continue the same work with a fresh context. Renaming it every time means repeatedly restoring the same title by hand. For example, after a reset, a broad title such as YouGile could become a narrow title about reviewing YouGile skills. The shared prompt now keeps a fitting umbrella title exactly for related work, and replaces it only when the subject has moved outside that title.

Naming starts after the incoming message is recorded, without waiting for the agent’s answer. A creation event with a real message still gets an answer; a title-only event stays silent. Buffered messages count individually, label collisions leave the existing names unchanged, and a failed Telegram rename preserves later manual edits.

Allowing a later reassessment of a manually chosen title changes the stable-title policy from #185337 and needs an explicit maintainer decision.

Related: #184821, #174317, #183368.

## Evidence

The screenshots below are from the installed integrated build `b2b6eb7`, not the public PR head alone. They do **not** prove the newly added implicit-topic case.

**First message: an automatic title.**

![Telegram topic title after the first ordinary message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-first-message-b2b6eb7-header.png)

**After reset and model selection: the title stays for the same subject.**

![The same Telegram topic title after reset and model selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-reset-same-b2b6eb7-header.png)

**After reset and a different subject: the title changes.**

![The changed Telegram topic title after a different subject](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-reset-different-b2b6eb7-header.png)

The [full report](https://github.com/dankarization/openclaw/blob/0f27d894bfa282460f9d5bdb1fbe7d4cdde95a59/docs/assets/qa/2026-11-12/telegram-naming-b2b6eb7.md) includes messages, commands, timings, and limits.

The public follow-up passed 118 focused tests, formatting, line-budget checks, type checks, and scoped lint. Independent local reviews covered the implementation and the final test-only adjustments. The integrated candidate also passed the native first-message-to-manual-edit regression; that test uses a mocked provider and is not a Telegram network or UI test. The native test was not rerun to completion on the exact public tree because its runner requires a separate runtime build.

[CI on head `573cad720`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43271819026) passed its selected type, lint, channel, naming and UI jobs. The build job still fails in the existing built-CLI proof with “Session … changed before deletion. Retry.” The separate repair is in open PR #197609. The overall CI gate is red; current Dashboard acceptance, existing-state upgrade proof, and the manual-title policy decision remain open.

The refinement lifecycle retains bounded excerpts of the opening input and up to six follow-ups in session or topic state so tool chatter cannot displace the task context. This retention proposal is broader than #174317 and needs maintainer review; it is not presented as accepted upstream behavior. For existing lifecycles without these excerpts, refinement reads up to four bounded opening pages; older inputs beyond that limit may be absent.

Authorized Telegram edited title events with an explicit private-topic thread are routed through the existing metadata owner without replaying the message body. The actual cause of a previously reported manual-rename mismatch is unknown because its event payload was not retained. Delayed title events follow the existing arrival-order behavior.

The screenshots and linked CI refer to earlier commits or integrated builds; they do not establish the status of CI for the new PR head. The actual cause of the previously reported live manual-rename mismatch remains unproven.

prs.title: fix(codex): retire idle shared app-server clients
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared Codex app-server clients can remain alive indefinitely after their final lease is released.

On multi-agent gateways, the keyed shared-client pool can therefore leave one Codex app-server process per runtime key resident even when no Codex work remains. This creates unnecessary process, task, and memory pressure on long-running gateways.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep warm shared clients for a short grace period so nearby turns can still reuse them, then retire and physically close the client once it has remained unleased and has no pending acquisitions for 5 minutes.

A new acquire cancels the pending retirement timer.

Explicit retirement and active native-subagent ownership continue to use the existing lifecycle rules.

## User Impact

Idle Codex app-server processes are reclaimed automatically instead of remaining resident for the lifetime of the Gateway.

Warm reuse during the grace period is preserved.

## Evidence

The problem is reproducible on long-running multi-agent gateways: after the final lease is released, shared Codex app-server clients can remain resident indefinitely. The most useful live evidence and focused validation are recorded below.

## Validation

The change adds focused fake-timer coverage for:

- reuse during the idle grace period
- cancellation of retirement when the client is reacquired
- no retirement while a lease is active
- retirement after the final lease remains idle
- creation of a fresh client after retirement

Live validation was performed on OpenClaw 2026.9.7 with the same patch applied to a multi-agent Gateway:

- Gateway startup created 41 Codex app-server clients
- after idle retirement: 41 -> 0 clients without restarting the Gateway
- TasksCurrent: 990 -> 41
- MemoryCurrent: ~4.54 GB -> ~2.76 GB
- a later OpenAI/Codex turn recreated clients on demand: 0 -> 2 -> 0 after the idle period

The Gateway remained running throughout the test.

The full 2026.9.7 source build also completed successfully with the patch applied.

Focused regression test measured wall time on the patched OpenClaw 2026.9.7 checkout: **33.45 seconds**.

Exact-current-main CI is left to this PR.

## Related

Related to #79495, whose keyed-pool discussion explicitly called out idle TTL / max-size cleanup as the follow-up needed to avoid leaking per-key clients.

Also relevant to #156674, which reports long-lived Codex app-server children causing sustained gateway resource pressure.

AI-assisted: yes. The fix was source-traced, covered by focused tests, built from source, and validated on a live multi-agent Gateway.

prs.title: fix(telegram): bound a rich draft's plain fallback to one chunk
prs.body:
Closes #135546

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Telegram live preview stops updating for the rest of the turn when a rich draft has to fall back to plain text and the draft is longer than 4,096 characters.

## User Impact

A long answer keeps arriving in the chat instead of freezing at the first preview update, so the user sees the reply stream in rather than a stale message while the log records a delivery failure. Only the rich-messages path is affected; nothing needs configuring.

## Why This Change Was Made

The preview path asked the plain fallback for one unbounded message (`fallbackLimit: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` in `draft-stream-message.ts`), but a draft page is planned at the rich transport limit of 32,768 characters while Telegram's plain `sendMessage`/`editMessageText` limit is 4,096. When the rich send or edit is rejected and the page degrades to plain text, the whole page is submitted as a single oversized message; Telegram refuses it, and the draft stream marks itself stopped, so no later update can revive it.

The fallback is now bounded to the shared `TELEGRAM_TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT` (4,000) and keeps only its first planned chunk, so "one preview replaces one visible message" is preserved by truncation instead of by paginating into extra messages. Final delivery still paginates and keeps its own unbounded plain fallback - the preview-only bound does not apply to it - but `stop()` now re-sends when the visible preview was truncated. Because a truncated preview now succeeds where it previously failed, three guards keep the tail from being lost: the visible-snapshot rule on `message is not modified` (that branch must not record the requested page as delivered), `lastDeliveredText` recording what is actually visible, and the render-dedupe key not masking the final answer's re-send. `editTelegramDraftMessage` / `sendTelegramDraftMessage` return a `truncated` flag for that, and each has exactly one caller.

## Evidence

CI on this head: `check-lint`, `check-test-types` and `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` all pass; the bundle ran the changed extension tests with `Tests 109 passed (109)`, including every case below. The two earlier revisions failed CI (`oxfmt` formatting, then two `TS2488` errors in this test) and both failures are fixed on the head under review.

The regression is parameterised over the two boundary cases of the `message is not modified` path - a 5,000-character preview (truncated from the first frame) and a 4,000-character one (fits until the append). Each case streams the preview, appends a character so the rich page crosses the bound, and answers the identical bounded plain fallback with `400: Bad Request: message is not modified`. It then asserts:

- the delivered snapshot stays bounded at 4,000, so the requested page is not recorded as delivered (this is the P1 from the first review - fail without the visible-snapshot rule);
- a later update still reaches the preview, so the stream was not stopped by the fallback;
- final delivery still attempts text beyond the preview, so the tail is not treated as already sent.

Discriminating assertions, stated honestly: the length bounds and the final re-delivery attempt would fail without the guards, while the call-count and id assertions would pass either way. I have not executed the suite against the base commit, so the red-on-base reading comes from those guards rather than from a recorded run.

Review gaps, stated rather than papered over: no local autoreview or ClawSweeper run was possible in this environment (a workspace install does not complete - pnpm fails with a store-operation lock), and no end-to-end Telegram run was performed, since that needs a live bot. CI on this head and the focused cases it executed are the whole of the executable evidence.

### Producing the evidence the review asks for

This environment cannot run a live bot, so the two minutes it takes with one are written out here. Anyone with a Telegram token can supply exactly what `Before merge` asks for:

1. Start the gateway with `channels.telegram.richMessages` enabled and a bot token, then ask the agent for an answer that renders as rich text with entities and runs past ~4,000 characters - e.g. a long markdown reply with many links, in one message.
2. The rich send is rejected with `RICH_MESSAGE_ENTITIES_INVALID`; the preview then falls back to one bounded plain chunk.
3. Keep streaming, let the answer finish, and capture: the gateway log lines for the rejected rich send and edit, the bounded plain send and edit, and the finished chat message.

On `main` the preview stops updating once the fallback is rejected and the final answer arrives missing its tail. On this branch the preview keeps updating and `stop()` re-sends the remainder. That log, with any IPs, tokens, phone numbers and private endpoints removed, is the evidence requested.

prs.title: fix: ClawRouter reference-image rejection
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `image_generate` rejects uploaded reference images before contacting ClawRouter, even when a qualified native Google image route supports editing.

## User Impact

Users can edit PNG, JPEG, or WebP references with an entitled `google/gemini-3.1-flash-image` or `google/gemini-3-pro-image` ClawRouter offer. OpenAI text-to-image behavior is unchanged; OpenAI reference editing and unqualified routes remain unsupported. No configuration migration or backend change is required.

The native slice accepts a prompt and up to five references, within the route’s 8 MiB JSON limit. Additional geometry/output controls are not enabled. Gemini has no native count parameter; all completed outputs, up to four, are retained without retrying a paid request. Availability still depends on the deployment, key grants, and budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin previously advertised no editing and implemented only OpenAI JSON generation. This adds the qualified native inline-reference contract, while keeping same-key live offer admission, guarded transport, response limits, cancellation, and the operation deadline. Model names alone do not grant access. No core production code changes.

Contributed with @hannesrudolph.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @hannesrudolph](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2ded57ed-2a92-4507-8666-0bdf27d05d06)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/29afb76a-911d-44e4-803a-650e03221334)

## Evidence

- Uploaded-reference regression: the actual `createImageGenerateTool.execute` path loads a PNG saved through the inbound media store, reaches the registered plugin and a real loopback HTTP fixture, and persists the returned image bytes. It fails on base `41ffd20207eaea4defbd54f2254e8864d6a6f93f` with the reference-image capability rejection and passes with this fix. The request’s native endpoint, inline bytes, and selected credential are checked.
- 131 final focused tests pass: 53 adapter, 64 image-tool/upload, and 14 prompt-prefix stability tests. An earlier focused run also passed 15 image-runtime tests. Strict source-resolved typecheck, scoped lint/format, whitespace, line-cap, and assertion-safety checks pass.
- Complete ClawRouter extension lane: **219 passed, 1 failed**. The unchanged audio-transcription explicit-proxy test resolves instead of rejecting. A focused run on the exact clean base reproduces the same failure; no audio code or tests were changed. This is not reported as a green extension lane.
- The wire contract and shared activation were inspected at [ClawRouter `17cb1a0`](https://github.com/openclaw/clawrouter/tree/17cb1a003efa00e572f2c88f227517c5bd9008f3), including the Google manifest and native image request/response owners.
- Full local ClawSweeper review completed using exact PR1756 build `7af0b3df82e30c661bd041fa09216724b3587658`, reviewing base `41ffd20207eaea4defbd54f2254e8864d6a6f93f` through head `e1917722cb57eb6a71fed49b5b9d37d75b28171b` (all four files, no truncation). No code findings or concrete security regressions. The reviewer judged the patch correct but live qualified-provider proof insufficient. This PR remains **draft pending live provider proof before merge**; a passing local review is not claimed to close that gap.

No live paid-provider proof or hosted CI was run before publication. The HTTP fixture proves the local tool/adapter contract, not production entitlement or provider image quality.

<details>
<summary>Validation and scope details</summary>

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-clawrouter.integration.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/audio-transcription.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "honors an explicit proxy" # exact-base failure reproduction
```

The initial package-boundary typecheck could not resolve SDK declarations in the fresh checkout. The subsequent strict source-resolved check passed; the initial setup failure is not counted as a pass.

Simplification retained two production files and two test files: +201 net production lines and +374 net test lines. The growth implements native encoding/decoding and exact route admission; no generic refactor, cache, dependency, or parallel auth owner was added.
