prs.title: feat(browser): allow operator-only access to chrome://settings in Control UI
prs.body:
Related: #197837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: navigating to `chrome://settings` (such as `chrome://settings/payments`) in the Control UI Browser panel fails with `Navigation blocked: unsupported protocol "chrome:"` because operator UI routes and agent tools share the same unprivileged navigation guard and CDP target filter.

## User Impact

User impact: human operators can now open, view, and interact with `chrome://settings` pages through the Control UI Browser panel to manage browser configurations and payment settings, while automated agent tools remain strictly blocked from opening, listing, capturing, snapshotting, or acting on those internal pages.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change establishes a bounded operator-only boundary for internal browser settings:
1. `navigation-guard.ts`: Adds `allowOperatorInternalUrls` to `BrowserNavigationPolicyOptions` and permits `chrome://settings` only when operator navigation is authorized. In `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed`, unprivileged agent access to internal URLs is explicitly rejected.
2. `cdp-target-filter.ts`: Permits `chrome://settings` in `isSelectableCdpBrowserTarget` only when `includeOperatorInternal` is enabled, keeping internal targets hidden from agent tab listings and default tab selection.
3. `server-context.tab-ops.ts` & `server-context.types.ts`: Plumbs `operatorMode` through `readTabs()` and `openTab()` so operator requests retain settings tabs and allow internal navigation, while raw CDP target creation enforces target selectability.
4. `routes/tabs.ts` & `routes/agent.snapshot.ts`: Distinguishes operator requests (`operatorMode` / `requester.isOperator`) from agent tool dispatches, allowing the Control UI to navigate and view settings while blocking agent snapshot, screenshot, and action routes from touching internal pages even if active.
5. `gateway/browser-request.ts`: Binds `isOperator: true` to the authenticated operator gateway session (`browser.request`), securely identifying operator requests without exposing spoofable client flags.

## Evidence

- Unit tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser/navigation-guard.test.ts`:
  - Verified `assertBrowserNavigationAllowed` rejects `chrome://settings/payments` by default with `InvalidBrowserNavigationUrlError`.
  - Verified `assertBrowserNavigationAllowed` permits `chrome://settings/payments` when `allowOperatorInternalUrls: true`.
  - Verified other internal schemes (e.g. `chrome://flags`) remain blocked even with `allowOperatorInternalUrls: true`.
  - Verified `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed` rejects unprivileged results on internal URLs.
- Unit tests in `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`:
  - Verified `openTab` and `assertBrowserNavigationAllowed` receive operator privilege when `requester.isOperator: true`.
  - Verified `listTabs` receives `operatorMode: true` when `requester.isOperator: true`.
- Regression test in `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.remote-profile-tab-ops.fallback.test.ts`:
  - Verified `remote.listTabs()` excludes `chrome://settings/payments` by default.
  - Verified `remote.listTabs({ operatorMode: true })` includes `chrome://settings/payments`.

prs.title: fix(cron): let configured fallbacks on other providers run for account-bound automations
prs.body:
Closes #192009
Related: #192463, #172590

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: since #172590, a scheduled automation records one inference account and refuses every model on any other provider. Configured cross-provider fallbacks never run, so a quota failure, outage or rate limit on the primary provider fails the job. The same refusal fires when a job with no model of its own follows a default that moved to another provider, and a replaced or signed-out account fails the run before any fallback is tried.

## User Impact

Cron jobs fail over to their configured fallback models on other providers again, with no Doctor step, edit or new command. That includes jobs already stored by 2026.10.10 and 2026.11.2.

- The job's recorded account still governs its own provider exactly as before. Changing interactive defaults, auth order or last-used account never moves the job to another account on that provider, so #172590's billing guarantee holds.
- Models on other providers select credentials live, the same way an interactive run does (auth order, last good, cooldowns).
- A replaced, signed-out or removed recorded account refuses only that provider's models; the rest of the fallback chain still runs.
- A job with no model of its own follows a default that moved to another provider, on live credentials.
- Refusals name the automation and its real id, and print a command that works as typed. `--model` help now mentions `@<profileId>`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#172590's goal was account and billing continuity on the provider a job already uses. Refusing every other provider protected nothing (the job had no account there to protect) and broke the documented fallback feature.

The recorded binding now applies per provider. `prepareCronRunInference` returns run parameters for a provider: the pinned recorded account for the binding's provider, or `scheduledLiveProviderAuth` for any other provider. The embedded runner's unrecorded-account guard (which exists for legacy unbound jobs) lets those live candidates through. A failed authorization of the recorded account is held and thrown only by that provider's candidate checks, so the chain continues.

No new state is stored and no schema, Doctor or standing-grant change is needed: stored bindings are read exactly as 10.10/11.2 wrote them, and older builds keep reading them the same way.

Accepted tradeoffs:
- A fallback provider uses whatever account its live config selects, including an API key if that's what its auth order picks. The user configured that fallback chain; interactive runs behave the same.
- Legacy jobs with no recorded account keep today's behavior (stored accounts need adoption). That rule is unchanged here.
- `@profile` on a fallback entry isn't applied to scheduled runs yet (same as interactive runs today).
- A healthy primary can still be skipped right after a quota failure while its billing cooldown lasts; that's existing fallback behavior, not specific to cron.

## Evidence
**Real-process matrix** (published npm builds and this branch on the same state, isolated `env -i` state, loopback providers; the primary fails with `insufficient_quota` unless noted).

Latest stable, 2026.11.2 → this branch, with no Doctor step or edit:
- **11.2:** a `--model …@profile` job refuses its configured fallback ("incompatible").
- **This branch, one or two backup accounts:** the same stored job fails over to the backup provider on its live account. The stored binding is unchanged.

2026.10.9 → 2026.10.10 → this branch (the #192463 path):
- **10.9:** fallback works. **10.10, after the documented `--model …@profile` repair:** refused as incompatible. **This branch:** fails over.

Fresh jobs on this branch:
- `insufficient_quota`, `rate_limit` and 503 on the primary all fail over to the backup provider.
- After `openclaw models auth logout` of the recorded account, the run still fails over (it sends nothing to the primary).
- A healthy primary runs on its recorded account.

Known limitation (unchanged by this PR): a branch-written state database is schema 39, which 2026.11.2 refuses to open, so rollback from this branch to 11.2 isn't possible. A stable hotfix needs a re-implementation on the release branch; this change is small enough for that.

**Integration tests** (real runner, SQLite, auth stores; only provider HTTP is faked, on loopback):
- `src/cron/isolated-agent.cross-provider-fallback.integration.test.ts`:
  - a job stored exactly as 10.10/11.2 write it fails over to the backup provider; the backup follows its live auth order across runs; no state is written;
  - recorded account replaced, removed, or signed out (store and config): backup still serves the run, nothing is sent to the primary;
  - a job with no model of its own follows a default that moved to another provider, on live credentials;
  - the recorded provider stays on its recorded account even when interactive auth order prefers another one.
- `src/cron/session-run.cross-provider-fallback.integration.test.ts`: the same failover through the `session:` target path, live and with the recorded account removed.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-continuity.integration.test.ts`: a replaced or revoked recorded account never reaches the primary provider with any key, and the configured fallback serves the run.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts`: a session-target job bound to `openai:primary` falls back to a Claude CLI candidate, which selects its own account instead of rejecting the recorded openai profile.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts`: CLI-runtime mismatches on the recorded provider still refuse, with the new message and real job id.

**Mutation checks:** restoring main's refusal of other providers, or failing the run when the recorded account can't be authorized, fails 4 of the 5 new isolated-path cases. Removing the per-provider scoping of the selected account fails the signed-out case; passing the recorded selection to a cross-provider CLI fallback fails the Claude CLI case.

**Suites (clean environment):** 131 related files (cron isolated/session/doctor, Gateway cron methods, plugin scheduled runs, reply-runner CLI/embedded/fallback candidates, embedded auth plan, exec cron grants, cron CLI): all pass, 1 skipped. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, format, line-cap and test-lines ratchets clean.

prs.title: fix(nostr): save profiles with blank optional fields
prs.body:
Closes #197871

## What Problem This Solves

Nostr users cannot save even a name-only profile edit when optional URL or identity fields are blank.

## User Impact

Users can leave optional fields blank and clear values they no longer want to publish. Partial API updates still preserve fields they omit.

## Why This Change Was Made

The form sends empty strings for unfilled fields. The plugin's PUT handler now records those explicit clears before validating the rest of the request, then removes the cleared fields from the merged profile before both publication and persistence. Nonempty values still undergo the same validation. The shared schema, authorization checks, and publish-before-persist policy are unchanged.

The existing handler tests continue to supply the same mocked Gateway request scope without loading the rest of the deprecated runtime barrel.

## Evidence

- On base `a3d5baaabd2ce88ace4b5d1c45a9577a61dbc08a`, both new HTTP cases failed with 400 instead of 200; the other 32 passed. The final patch passed all 34 handler tests and 14 profile UI tests using the repository runner (about 6 seconds total on Windows/Node 24.22.1).
- An offline run of the actual form factory, controller, and handler changed the name-only request from 400 to 200. The synthetic relay and config boundaries received the same profile, with no blank constrained fields. No live relay, packaged Gateway, or external account was used.
- Formatting, lint, and a targeted type-aware Oxlint check passed. The standard tsgo launcher rejected the borrowed dependency layout before compilation, so this does not claim full-project typecheck parity.
- Independent Codex autoreview (P0-P2) completed with no actionable findings on the exact two-file diff committed as 96a86123ca46a4667b3e79249fb1d63223d0f74a. Review used the supplied diff and context; the focused suite separately covered unchanged URL validation and failed-publish behavior.
- The existing relay connection-failure test reports one socket still present in teardown on this Windows runner; the same assertion fails with the exact unmodified base handler and publisher. The patch does not change the relay fixture or publisher.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve steering refusal reasons
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Steering accepted behind a long embedded tool can expire at the transcript-delivery deadline and become a follow-up, while the final warning says only `runtime_rejected`. That hides whether delivery timed out, the turn ended, or admission was unavailable.

## User Impact

Operators receive the owner's closed `runtimeReason`, the preserved rejection reason, and error detail bounded to 512 characters, correlated by session key. Codes distinguish tool-boundary versus other transcript timeouts, session end/handoff, closure/cancellation, compaction and unavailable compaction state, failed availability checks, non-steerable turns, and missing injection capability.

Steering retains the existing 120-second delivery deadline. Every ordinary tool batch, including a non-interruptible one, reaches a steering checkpoint after completion. Immediate follow-up conversion would prevent same-turn corrections at that checkpoint. Provider token-stream state does not determine local queue acceptance. No timing, configuration, schema, or custody policy changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded lifecycle lacked machine-readable withdrawal reasons, Gateway dispatch reduced rejection outcomes to a string disposition, and controller submission reconstructed the outcome from only two fields. This change attaches reasons at the runtime/probe owners and retains the complete rejection through the existing outcome chain. Shared outcome types live below both reply options and controller contracts, avoiding a type-import cycle. There is one authoritative definition and no added cache or retry mechanism.

## Evidence

Six lifecycle regressions fail against the exact parent owner and pass with the fix. Focused embedded, registry, Gateway, and reply tests cover all 11 sub-reasons, exact-message withdrawal, unavailable admission, bounded logging, and outcome preservation. The real-session withdrawal suite passes all 9 cases, backend availability all 5, and the final reply-log replay both selected cases. Codex autoreview is clean through P2 on the complete repaired candidate.

The first-head CI exposed a new static type-import cycle; it was reproduced locally and repaired by moving the shared types. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` now reports zero cycles. All four type-move modules emit byte-identical JavaScript before/after, preserving the focused runtime and measurement evidence. The first-head CI had no selected Vitest failures; all other executed CI jobs passed. Final-head CI [43284875056](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43284875056) passed, including the architecture check and aggregate gate. ClawSweeper revision 3 has zero open items on `eed58e9e3775f9a737b710b2cecaa205bf9a37fd`.

Synthetic measurement: real Agent/controller path, 4,096 resident sessions, 10 warm-ups then 30 measured iterations per process, five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs and unchanged A/A controls. Non-interruptible tools held for 500 ms; expiry accelerated to 1 ms. The regression cases exercise the default 120,000 ms using a fake clock. Median CPU per 30 turns: 172.60→164.29 ms; median per-run refusal p50: 1.941→1.930 ms, p95: 3.189→3.327 ms; continuation p50: 499.24→499.39 ms. Separately sampled allocation median: 29.20→29.76 MB (+1.9%). Every process consumed all 30 inputs exactly once. The next-boundary pair accepted all 30 steers into the current turn on each revision, with zero follow-up turns.

Acceptance rule was published before measurement: preserve delivery/counts, report CPU/allocation and timings, investigate any 20% regression, and claim no speedup. The initial 50 ms series had a +21.3% median CPU observation and a large baseline outlier; a subsequent unchanged-baseline allocation warm-up allowed the short tool to finish before expiry. That failed process was excluded as an invalid rejection fixture. The qualified longer-hold series did not reproduce the CPU increase; its CPU difference is within A/A variation (160.83 and 142.25 ms). Both series are retained in the lane report. Profiles show no new sampled hotspot in the changed refusal path. Instrumented timing is not the performance score.

A separate exact-head real-model Gateway run used synthetic state with a 35.19 GiB agent database, 5,000 seeded sessions, 15,000 participants, and 62,000 workspace files (1,142,784,000 bytes), on APFS. A signed Control UI protocol client sent a steer during a non-interruptible plugin tool: acknowledgment 38.46 ms, pending input visible 192.41 ms, and `tool_authority_mismatch` / `followup-queued` observed 195.34 ms. After tool release, the input and assistant follow-up each appeared exactly once. The policy reason survived the complete Gateway-to-reply-log flow. This existing authority guard prevented reaching the 120-second runtime timeout; no live `tool_boundary_timeout` claim is made. Default-timeout classification is covered by the owner regressions and controlled real-Agent workload. The owner CPU/allocation workload has no database/workspace I/O; the large-state run is behavioral evidence, not a btrfs or Gateway performance comparison. Related: #197415.

Production growth is 107 lines (+171/-64), excluding tests/docs/benchmark, for the closed reason contract and propagation through existing owners. The final changed-file check passes all gates except two inherited dead-export failures reproduced on exact parent `25887573ebfb5641ed0d53abe4f2f8985c50c576`: `bindSessionPendingInputMentionInvitation` and `readPendingInputSource`, introduced by `baca36ea403cf` (#184512). These are reported main regressions; no suppression changed. The separate baseline checkout also reported five Talk type exports absent from candidate failures; those extra findings are not used for a gate exception.

prs.title: fix(knowledge): drop the Granola scribe's stop-when-context-is-short rule
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Learn from Granola scribe stops before ingesting a meeting, leaving it `pending`, when it judges its context might be running short.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled Granola scribe runs finish the meeting they start instead of deferring it to a later run. No configuration or data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Step 5 of the scribe's run instructions said "If context runs short, stop after the current meeting and leave the rest." An agent can't measure its remaining context, and the runtime already compacts long turns, so the rule only gave the model a reason to stop early. This removes that sentence. Step 5 still ingests one meeting at a time, in full, and still writes each checkpoint line as soon as a meeting's outcome is known, so an interrupted run resumes instead of redoing work.

## Evidence

- Live observation (2026-11-12, maintainer's Gateway): a scheduled run acquired and digested a large meeting (83k-character transcript), then stopped without ingesting it and recorded it `pending`. The Gateway log for that run shows no context overflow, compaction or watchdog.
- `git grep` over `extensions/knowledge/skills` on main: this is the only instruction that stops work because context is running short. The rule dates to #187659 and was carried over unchanged in #197018.
- `node extensions/knowledge/scripts/sync-skill-references.mjs --check` passes (the file is not a generated shared reference).
- `git diff --check` passes.

prs.title: fix: improve scrolling in touch dashboard panels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Candidate fix for dashboard content that cannot stay in view when scrolling an iPad side panel.

## User Impact

**Approved experimental follow-up with recording-observed physical iPad grid improvement in split and expanded views; remaining checklist gaps are unverified.** Auto-height HTML widgets can grow taller on touch layouts so more content scrolls with the board, instead of inside an oversized iframe. The original singleton-page viewport fix is retained.

Existing fixed-height widgets keep their saved sizes. Switching a very tall Auto widget to Fixed can shrink it to the existing fixed-size limit; switching to a fine-pointer mouse layout can also restore compact sizing. The reporter explicitly accepted this tradeoff on November 12. Fixed widgets and documents beyond the larger bound can still scroll internally.

**The previous 6ddce47 iPad grid result remains FAIL / unchanged versus its baseline**, separately from its tall-page improvement. No merge or deployment is authorized; keep this PR draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

One existing board owner shares the effective content-fit policy across grid allocation and exact card height. Coarse-pointer layouts reuse the existing 240-row document bound; fine-pointer layouts retain the ordinary 20-row bound. There is no new touch relay, schema, configuration, permission, or dependency change.

## Evidence

- **Before this experiment:** `6ddce47fac561860377eaaea68b094db3986c211`. **After:** `c7decbdf1a06fef89346ec221f79bee44ec97453`. Original PR/merge base: `8569bd9edfadb9d08539083cae19b3680ef49b3c`.
- **Red/green at the real UI boundary:** the before implementation retains 3,825px of inner-document scroll and fails the touch-fit assertion. The experiment reaches the final marker with trusted Chromium touch gestures through the real Control UI and native nested sandbox frames. The fixed-height control remains 260px; a fresh fine-pointer context retains ordinary inner scrolling. This does not prove the WebKit root cause or physical Safari correctness.
- **Passed locally:** full dashboard E2E **11/11**, board browser **26/26**, board unit **27/27**, owning UI-component and UI-E2E typechecks, targeted lint, formatting/whitespace, and Control UI build. E2E invocation 22.59s / tests 10.862s; added touch/fine cases 2.153s/1.170s. Browser/unit invocations 5.20s/3.13s. New-head CI and CI seconds are not claimed.
- **Fresh independent Auto Review:** OpenClaw engine, complete local snapshot against the pinned base, helper-selected **P0 scope**, scoped-clean with no findings. This is not a full-priority or Safari certification. The exact 200 net regression lines have their own allocation.
- **Warnings retained:** the successful build reports advisory bundle-budget overruns; no budget baseline was raised. Existing suites emit development strict-read/pointer-capture notices. An unsupported mid-context pointer-emulation attempt was replaced by independently verified native coarse/fine contexts, not counted as pointer-transition coverage.
- **Physical update:** new-head grid final-marker reachability improves in the recorded split/expanded trials below. Feed, Auto→Fixed and separately marked candidate-grid restored split remain unverified; normal current-head CI/review is still separate from this evidence.

### November 12 physical iPad video — new-head grid improvement

[Qualified report, complete observed sequence, ten UTC mark labels and clip hashes](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/2f88f8a13ce9a2fa448628dbff21ab8a2882be63/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.physical-ipad-20261112.md), pinned at `2f88f8a13ce9a2fa448628dbff21ab8a2882be63`.

The report binds **two complete production Control UI builds**: BEFORE `6ddce47fac561860377eaaea68b094db3986c211` and AFTER `c7decbdf1a06fef89346ec221f79bee44ec97453`. This comparison did not substitute only the stylesheet. It uses identical synthetic mock Gateway content and native nested iframe isolation; test-only HTML injection supplies the mock, passive telemetry and proof toolbar, without editing the selected product source. Physical-device identity is reporter-supplied; the video is not a source-hash or device-configuration attestation.

**Observed in the supplied paired clips:** BEFORE ordinary-grid content stops above its final markers in split and expanded views. AFTER reaches the green marker in split and, expanded, shows **both Auto cards' final markers**. The Fixed control's own final marker is also visible. This is accepted as **recording-observed physical iPad improvement for the new head**, not an unknown test outcome and not a full-checklist pass. It is separate from—and does not erase—the prior patch's FAIL / unchanged result.

The full report also records BEFORE restored-split failure and tall-page markers in split/expanded on both builds. Those additional intervals are attributed to the report/reporter; the four supplied clips cover the grid ranges below. Exact unchanged Fixed-card geometry, all input paths and physical release timing are not established by seeing its footer.

**Before — physical iPad expanded grid, visible mark 2 (19:54:35 UTC)**

![Physical iPad before: both Auto grids stop above their final markers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4810065-ae6f-4229-9f2f-35a5725c25ee)

**After — physical iPad expanded grid, visible mark 3 (19:55:41 UTC)**

![Physical iPad after: both Auto final markers and Fixed control marker are visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e87f7a4a-4509-49c3-906f-843179157377)

<details>
<summary>Four sanitized physical comparison clips and visible mark labels</summary>

Each clip and still **stacks a dashboard crop above the proof toolbar from the same source frame**. This disclosed spatial composition is not a full-screen capture; it excludes unrelated browser chrome, bookmarks and chat. MP4s have no audio or identifying source metadata. Clip bytes match the report's SHA-256 values. The private 115.91-second original is not published.

BEFORE split, original 18–24 seconds:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ded6a70-8643-44c3-8864-c14c9da2512d

BEFORE expanded, original 26–33 seconds:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/327dcb9b-119e-46e4-8941-757e50683ed6

AFTER split, original 76–93 seconds:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/107947f8-95bf-49c6-8fa3-c7a200ca68e4

AFTER expanded, original 94–101 seconds:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5df2cc21-dbb7-43c6-9f7b-e580117b4b18

The report transcribes five visible confirmations per build. Selected supplied clips independently show BEFORE marks 1/2 and AFTER marks 1/2/3; the other mark intervals are in the full reported sequence, not all in these four excerpts. Labels below are report-transcribed UTC text, **not recovered JSON samples**.

| Mark | BEFORE | AFTER |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 19:54:26 | 19:55:28 |
| 2 | 19:54:35 | 19:55:35 |
| 3 | 19:54:40 | 19:55:41 |
| 4 | 19:54:51 | 19:55:51 |
| 5 | 19:54:56 | 19:55:56 |

</details>

**Export qualification:** the reporter says the export was not working but confirms marking. The report records a terminal Safari View/Download confirmation for the candidate JSON; no successful file save is shown and **no iPad JSON was received**. Do not reconstruct samples, infer numerical geometry, or substitute a desktop export. Visible marked video remains usable evidence; an additional export is not required to accept the observed improvement.

**Remaining gaps:** exact iPad model/OS and input accessories, numerical geometry and actual media-query state, independently visible finger-release instant, a complete nested-feed trial, Auto→Fixed behavior, and a separately marked candidate-grid restored-split result. Keep these unverified rather than marking the entire checklist passed. No merge or production deployment is authorized.

### Earlier inspected Chromium comparison (local proof)

Before: the inner document is positioned at its end for geometry diagnosis, while the final marker lies below the visible board. This positioning is not itself gesture proof.

![Before: ordinary grid stops above its final marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37323ec1-b3fc-48ca-95bc-9fafeb9a7b3a)

After: the final marker is reached using trusted Chromium touch gestures; the next fixed-height card remains in the board. Both captures contain only synthetic dashboard content.

![After: touch auto-height grid exposes the final marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/091e2d16-0b81-4532-b423-58e3e313062b)

### Remaining iPad checklist after the recorded improvement

**Build the complete before and after revisions. Swapping only board.css will not test this follow-up: it also changes JavaScript sizing.** The live team server is unchanged.

The new full-build recording now establishes observed ordinary-grid improvement in split and expanded views. Remaining checks are a separately marked candidate-grid restored-split trial, complete nested-feed and Auto→Fixed behavior, and device/input configuration. Fixed-control footer visibility is not numerical proof of unchanged geometry. The original iPad tabs are closed; neither old-tab exports nor a new JSON export are required to accept the video improvement.

### Prior physical iPad results (6ddce47, not the new experiment)

[Qualified physical-device report](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/3efa515bb14297f6e514c3cec088fd9580c44a7c/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.physical-ipad-evidence.md), evidence head `3efa515bb14297f6e514c3cec088fd9580c44a7c`. Reporter clarification at 20:35 UTC: the multi-widget control is **FAIL, unchanged versus unpatched**; only the remaining bug/root cause is unresolved. Extra telemetry is diagnostic, not a prerequisite to accept that failure.

This is a **stylesheet-isolated physical-device comparison**: both fixtures use candidate runtime `6ddce47fac561860377eaaea68b094db3986c211`; baseline substitutes the exact `8569bd9edfadb9d08539083cae19b3680ef49b3c` stylesheet. It is not a full historical-baseline runtime build. Synthetic dashboards use the real Control UI, mock Gateway and native iframe isolation on the reporter's physical iPad Safari.

| Physical test | Baseline stylesheet | Prior candidate stylesheet (6ddce47) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tall page, split | FAIL: final marker not reached in recording | PASS / improved: green final marker reached |
| Tall page, expanded | Final marker reached | Final marker reached |
| Tall page, restored split | Final marker not shown | PASS / improved: final marker remains visible |
| Ordinary multi-widget grid | **FAIL** | **FAIL / unchanged versus baseline** |

Tall-page observations are supported by inspected paired clips and the reporter's outcome. The ordinary-grid failure is accepted from the reporter and paired videos, not held as an unknown test outcome. This does not establish a newly introduced regression. Clips have no touch indicators, so exact finger-release timing is not independently visible. Their fixed crop shows only the right dashboard portion when expanded; off-crop widget contents must not be inferred from those pixels.

**Before — baseline tall page in split, approximately 35.5 s of original recording**

![Physical iPad baseline split view stops above the final green marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d5eec26-d89c-4092-9958-f8845bd9d17f)

**After — candidate tall page in restored split, approximately 31.5 s of original recording**

![Physical iPad candidate restored split view shows the final green marker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee1dcd7e-bcf2-46fd-81a5-958887b5b557)

<details>
<summary>Four inspected dashboard-only recordings</summary>

Tall baseline, original 18–48 s; green appears expanded, not split/restored split:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f737bd38-524b-4769-bf4d-e00cdda71869

Tall candidate, original 15–33 s; green appears in split, expanded and restored split:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3199f91-5932-44d6-bbeb-de116c6c0efd

Ordinary-grid baseline, original 52–77 s — **FAIL**:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08178649-9441-4b49-ae69-f210bc5c044e

Ordinary-grid candidate, original 36–52 s — **FAIL / unchanged**:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05c5d07c-269c-4a84-97e9-0823f57efab7

All four uploaded files match the report's SHA-256 values. The inspected 440×736 dashboard-only crops have no browser tabs, bookmarks, unrelated chat, audio or source metadata. Private originals remain outside the repository.

</details>

**Telemetry qualification:** the first JSON was a Windows Chrome validation export, not iPad telemetry. The report describes the actual candidate Safari export only as a partial PDF screenshot, cut off mid-object during early tall scrolling around 20:18:53.830Z: 1376×867, DPR 2, board clientHeight/scrollHeight 756/756 with overflow hidden, iframe height 726. It is not a complete machine-readable export and contains no full grid trial. Exact iPad model/OS and independently visible release timing remain unverified. Silent Mark moment recording explains the absence of later tester marks; no missing marks or samples have been reconstructed.

**Separate grid diagnosis, not acceptance:** the original iPad tabs are now closed; no further export from them is assumed available. For a future reproduction, in the same identified grid widget, compare a swipe over ordinary widget content outside the nested feed with an outer-gutter swipe. Record before/after outer-board, intermediate-sandbox, inner-document and feed offsets/remaining ranges, plus the final marker's bounds. Inner-at-end + outer remaining + gutter progress distinguishes cross-frame handoff from an inner document that still has remaining distance; both-at-end + clipped marker points instead to bounds/clipping. Complete Safari exports would aid that diagnosis, but the observed control already failed. Do not broaden the page-only CSS rule or restore a touch relay on hypothesis alone.

### Historical November 11 checkpoint (superseded)

The touch-sizing experiment was held while its pinning tradeoff was discussed. The reporter approved that tradeoff on November 12; the latest candidate above implements it. The interrupted exploratory run was not counted as proof.

### External Chromium geometry evidence (not fix verification)

- [Collector report](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/8355ee1654c79e16641b43e579b33fa12f83611d/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.chromium-evidence.md) and [ordered readings](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/8355ee1654c79e16641b43e579b33fa12f83611d/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.chromium-readings.json), pinned to evidence head `8355ee1654c79e16641b43e579b33fa12f83611d`. The comparison against the original investigation head `023ef9b66c1e34a5be8d7e0b5f97908f4be4c1a9` contains exactly two evidence files and two commits; that evidence branch changed no product code or tests.
- The collector used live in-app Chromium on Windows at 1280×720. The live identity label was `git@ecbad2e`, not a verified full SHA; exact browser version, zoom, and per-action timestamps were unavailable. These are NOT runtime checks of the pinned checkout or native Safari proof.
- Sampled right-side layout: 1346px iframe inside a 634px board, with independent inner-document and outer-board scroll ranges. An outer-gutter action reached the outer end in a geometry sample. Expanded mode fitted the iframe to 634px and its screenshot showed the footer.
- The split screenshot instead shows the feed/People section, inconsistent with the adjacent footer projection. Changing content height, locator auto-scroll and an unexplained later offset change remain unresolved. Neither stable over-iframe gesture reachability nor product snap-back is established.
- **Windows automated comparison blocker — capture baseline did not qualify:** [timestamped no-input audit](https://github.com/PollyBot13/openclaw/blob/83d528bafbd0014ba68f915d65ab6b9b727bc8ea/ui/src/e2e/side-panel-scrolling.capture-audit.md), pinned to evidence head `83d528bafbd0014ba68f915d65ab6b9b727bc8ea`. After setup, the collector used only read-only probes and captures, including the intermediate sandbox. One bracket changed outer offset 22→369 and inner 1255→210. A later bracket preserved those offsets but changed board bounds from (800,86,480×634) to (0,456.32,1280×177.68); layout classes changed from desktop to mobile-host/narrow while the reported top viewport stayed 1280×720. Both captures are unmatched. The widget-versus-gutter comparison was correctly not run. Capture behavior, asynchronous layout/restoration, or another interaction remain possible; no cause or product snap-back is established. Reconcile capture/layout coordinates before repeating gesture tests. That Windows automated comparison remains unqualified; it is separate from the later physical iPad stylesheet-isolated results above.

### Reporter-provided physical iPad Safari recording (November 10)

The reporter supplied a fresh 13.72-second iPad screen recording and states that pulling the lower dashboard upward exposes more content only until the finger is lifted, when it reverts. Private frame inspection of the final seconds shows the lower card moving upward and returning, with the surrounding side-panel layout visually stable. The recording does not show touch indicators; release timing is supplied by the reporter. This documents the original-device symptom separately from the Windows automation/capture discrepancy. It is not a verified fix, an instrumented Safari regression, or proof of which scroll owner is responsible. Elastic overscroll at a boundary is a working hypothesis only; the footer is not reached in the excerpt.

Dashboard-only excerpt of the final 4.70 seconds, cropped to exclude unrelated browser tabs, bookmarks, chat, profile details and URLs; audio and source metadata removed. GitHub accepted the inspected 741,983-byte MP4; unauthenticated reviewer access was verified as HTTP 200 with video/mp4 after association with this PR.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0008f5f9-6920-476b-a890-6758f122f785

The linked session contains the original report, both candidate implementations, local verification and physical evidence qualifications. New-head physical grid improvement is recorded; the remaining iPad checklist gaps are explicitly unverified.

prs.title: feat(chat): keep composer drafts across app restarts
prs.body:
## Problem

Native chat (iOS and macOS) kept composer drafts only in memory (`draftsBySession`). If the app is killed, crashes, or iOS terminates it in the background, whatever you were typing is lost, and so are any picked attachments. On iOS a pending attachment also blocked switching sessions, because nothing else would keep it.

## Solution

Composer drafts are stored per session in `client-state.sqlite`, the client-owned store that already holds the chat outbox. The schema was approved by the iOS owner.

- **New tables** (migration `client-state-composer-drafts-v11`): `composer_drafts` (text, revision, updated time per gateway and session key) and `composer_draft_attachments` (same columns as `outbox_attachments`).
- **Forget:** the existing Forget deletes a gateway's drafts. A trigger on the irreversible forget phase (same pattern as `watch_message_forget`) does the same when an older build performs the Forget.
- **One owner:** when a store exists it owns the draft. The view model keeps only the visible session's text and attachments.
  - Text saves are debounced 300 ms through one chained write task. Switch, send, detach and app background wait for it.
  - Attachments are written and deleted one by one as they change.
  - Recall mode saves the draft underneath the recalled message, never the recalled message itself.
  - A draft is not loaded or saved until the session key's agent (and, for `main`/`global`, its routing) is known, so nothing is stored under a key that later changes. Text typed before the load arrives is appended to the loaded draft.
- **Clearing after send:** a queued send clears the draft in the same transaction as the outbox insert; a live send clears it right away. Only what was actually sent is cleared, so text typed after the send stays.
- **Limits:** a draft holds at most 40 MB of attachments, the same as the outbox per-message limit; going over shows the existing "Too large to send" notice. Drafts on one gateway share 50 MB. When a new attachment would pass that, attachments (never text) are dropped from the least recently used other drafts first.
- **Attachments and switching:** pending attachments no longer block session switches once they are stored. An attachment whose save failed keeps the chat pinned, shows "Could not save … with this draft. Send or remove it before switching chats." and is retried on every flush.
- **Failed saves:** a text save that SQLite rejects does not advance the saved revision, so the next flush, background or quit save retries it. Text switched away from before its save lands stays in memory and replaces the stored row on return.
- **Docs:** `docs/reference/database-schemas/personal-data.md` describes the new tables, retention (until sent, cleared, or the Gateway is forgotten), and Forget.

## Impact

What you type in a chat, including picked attachments, is still there after an app restart, a crash, or iOS ending the app in the background. Switching sessions with a pending attachment works. Older app versions ignore the new tables.

## Evidence

**Simulator (iOS 27, isolated local Gateway):** type a message into a chat, terminate the app, relaunch.

| Build | Composer after relaunch |
|---|---|
| `main` (`5d6a026`) | empty ("Message main…") |
| this PR | the typed text is back |

Screenshots are in the PR comments.

**Upgrade from v2026.11.3 (simulator, local Gateway):** queue a message offline on v2026.11.3 → install this PR over it → relaunch offline: no onboarding, message still "Queued" → Gateway back: reconnects and delivers it → type a draft, kill, relaunch: draft is back. Screenshots in the PR comments.

**Tests:** each new test fails with its fix removed and passes with it.
- Survives a rebuilt view model (text and attachment).
- Text typed before the draft loads is appended, and survives a switch away and back.
- Cold launch waits for the agent and routing before keying the draft.
- A draft bound through the agent catalog keeps saving after the catalog resets.
- A send captured before its draft loads clears the composer.
- A send clears its saved draft without waiting for the save pause: offline (enqueue clear) and online (live clear) each fail without their clear.
- A replacement view model reads the draft its predecessor was still writing.
- Recall mode saves the draft underneath, never the recalled message.
- Attachments stay with their session across switches.
- Failed writes (real SQLite failure via a temporary trigger): a failed text save is retried by the next flush; it survives a switch away and back; a failed attachment save keeps the attachment and blocks the switch.
- macOS: the web conversation's pending check waits for the draft load.
- Store: a v10 upgrade adds the draft tables and preserves the queue; Forget and the trigger path delete drafts; eviction drops only attachments of the oldest other drafts; an enqueue clears only the revision and attachments it carried.

**Suites:** OpenClawKit chat suites pass. Two `ChatMediaVideoPlayerTests` timing failures under parallel load pass when run alone, and that file is unrelated. iOS: 560 Swift Testing tests in 12 suites and 9 XCTest tests pass. macOS: `swift build --product OpenClaw` succeeds.

**Reviews:** a second-model design review and code review. All findings are applied: unbound text survives a switch, one draft key for revisions, a send captured before load, a test rewrite, macOS pending checks, a shared write chain across view-model rebuilds, and saving on macOS quit.

**Accepted edge cases, named in code:**
- Two macOS windows on the same session: the last writer wins.
- Text typed before the key resolves stays in memory until it does.
- Only image previews are rebuilt on reload.

**Size:** production +710/−31 (two new files), tests +391/−7, docs +39/−1.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): sign in with OpenClaw ID over a verified personal sign-in
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-509. Depends on openclaw/openclaw-id#30 (the issuer's device grant) and openclaw/openclaw-id#31 (lets real browsers approve a code). Both are merged and deployed to staging.

## What Problem This Solves

Sign in with OpenClaw ID works only in a Control UI opened on the claw's own computer. Over Tailscale or another verified proxy, the menu says "Sign in on the computer that runs this claw", so setting up a remote claw needs an SSH tunnel.

## User Impact

With the OpenClaw ID Labs switch on, a Control UI connection with a verified personal identity can sign in with OpenClaw ID and see the account in the identity menu. This covers Tailscale Serve, Cloudflare Access or another trusted proxy, and enterprise principals.
- The sign-in proves only which OpenClaw ID account the browser holds. It grants nothing: no owner device, no root ceremony, no membership, no claw-record write.
- **Turn on remote access** and its link code stay on the claw's computer (OCF-511).
- Shared token or password connections, members and owner devices over the OpenClaw ID tunnel, host-bound ingress grants, and connections without a personal profile still cannot sign in.

## Why This Change Was Made

The issuer only redirects to the loopback callbacks the Control UI client registers, so a remote origin can't receive a redirect. For those connections the Gateway uses the issuer's device grant (RFC 8628) instead of the popup:
- `openclawId.account` (`device_begin`) asks the issuer for a user code.
- The Control UI shows the code and an **Open OpenClaw ID** link.
- `device_poll` asks the Gateway to poll the token endpoint.
- The Gateway checks the ID token (iss, aud, exp, sub; the device grant has no nonce) and returns the account over the authenticated connection.

Design details:
- **Who can poll:** a pending device sign-in is bound to the profile that started it. Another connection can neither redeem nor cancel it.
- **Scope:** `openclawId.account` needs `operator.read`, because it changes no authority. `openclawId.authority` keeps `operator.admin`, and its `account_*` popup actions stay loopback-only.
- **No account record:** remote sign-ins never call `recordVerifiedAccount` (the owner-name overwrite is OCF-512).
- **Status:** `openclawId.status` reports `accountSignIn: "popup" | "device" | null`, and the menu uses it.
- **Sign-out:** signing out in another tab while a device sign-in is starting or polling retires that sign-in.
- **Token custody:** after the issuer returns the ID token, the Gateway checks again before handing it over: the Labs switch, a live personal connection, the device route, and the profile that started the sign-in. If any of these changed while it waited, the token is discarded.

## Evidence

- Gateway tests:
  - `account-sign-in.test.ts`: device flow pacing, slow_down, single redemption, owner-bound polling, denial, and refusals for the wrong aud, an injected nonce, an expired token, or a device endpoint that is missing or off the issuer origin.
  - `server.openclaw-id-sign-in.test.ts`: the route for each connection kind; real dispatch admits `openclawId.account` with read scope while `openclawId.authority` needs admin; personal connections can't use the popup or link-code actions; Labs off.
  - `labs-off.test.ts`.
  - Token custody (`5f6001b`): six handler cases cover Labs switched off, the connection gone, the route changed, and the profile changed while the issuer answered. Four of them fail on the previous commit.
- UI tests (`account-menu.test.tsx`, `ui-error.test.ts`): device sign-in to the stored account and the identity menu, sign-out during start, cancelled polling stops, no owner actions after a device sign-in.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, the ui-components, gateway-root and gateway-other test typechecks, oxlint, `check:control-ui-controllers` and `ui:i18n:verify` pass.
- Autoreview (Astra): no P0 or P1 findings. Both P2s are fixed: the method scope is now read, and the sign-out generation is captured before the attempt begins.

- **Boot size (`a46b423`):** the device sign-in code and dialog strings load with the device sign-in dialog. New and chat boot JS are within build variance of main (+3 B; the first full CI run measured +460 B). `ui:check-performance:base` passes locally against main.
- **E2E (`a46b423`):** the account-menu and popup fixtures report `accountSignIn: "popup"`, as a loopback Gateway does. Both e2e files pass locally.
- **Test lines:** `config/test-lines-allocations/197559-openclaw-id-personal-sign-in.txt` records 188 lines over the allowance. Device sign-in over a personal connection is security-sensitive, so the tests cover:
  - issuer pacing and single redemption;
  - token checks (aud, nonce, expiry);
  - profile-bound polling and token custody;
  - read-scoped dispatch and Labs off;
  - UI sign-out races.

### Live proof against staging OpenClaw ID

Real Gateways built from this branch, with headless Chromium. The personal identity comes from a trusted proxy on the same host (`x-forwarded-user`), so the browser connects as a named person, not as the claw's own computer.

**OpenClaw ID testnet, head `5f6001b`.** The `gateway` lab host in us-west-2 ran a throwaway Gateway with its own port and state directory. It didn't touch the host's live claw, and everything was removed afterwards. The browser reached it through SSM port forwards.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| "Sign in with OpenClaw ID" is enabled over a personal sign-in | pass |
| Successful sign-in: device code → approve on staging → the browser holds the account | pass |
| Identity menu after sign-in shows the account and Sign out; owner actions stay unavailable | pass (Turn on remote access stays disabled until OCF-511) |
| Cancel while waiting stops polling | pass (2 polls before, 2 after) |
| Another profile tries to collect someone else's pending code | refused, `state_mismatch`; the owner's code stays pending |
| Sign out in another tab while waiting, then approve | stays signed out: "You signed out while sign-in was in progress" |
| Profile merged away while its approved code is pending | no token: both sockets close (4001), and a fresh connection gets `state_mismatch` |

**Mac Studio, base `082ed658` and head `5f6001b`.**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Base: "Sign in with OpenClaw ID" is disabled over a personal sign-in | pass |
| Shared token over the network can't sign in (`accountSignIn: null`, `device_begin` → `not_personal_connection`) | pass |
| Loopback (both builds) still opens the issuer's PKCE popup and gets no device code | pass |

The testnet Gateway installed only core runtime dependencies, because the host didn't have room for the agent SDK binaries. The ACP and Codex plugins therefore didn't load; neither is involved in sign-in. The redacted traces contain no tokens, codes or addresses.

| Before (`082ed658`, personal sign-in) | After (head) |
|---|---|
| ![Before: Sign in with OpenClaw ID is disabled and says to sign in on the claw's computer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1acc73ba-5d24-4e0f-a6ca-2c6e44c8d3d2) | ![After: Sign in with OpenClaw ID is enabled for alice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90b52817-d034-4fbf-a634-8825fb6bbb7c) |

| Device code in the Control UI | Issuer confirmation (staging) |
|---|---|
| ![Device sign-in dialog with a code and Open OpenClaw ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e544dd0-e3cf-4ff9-95e5-05759f45d233) | ![Issuer page asking to confirm the same code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/159d5d64-1b67-4ed7-b130-854b171b2db0) |

| Signed in | Signed out in another tab while waiting |
|---|---|
| ![Identity menu showing the OpenClaw ID account and Sign out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c580808-8c9b-4938-b5ab-587f78031401) | ![Dialog says sign-in did not finish](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff9d6e3d-f974-40f4-ab96-525e23dca00d) |

prs.title: fix: native Codex MCP config keeps plugin OAuth credentials
prs.body:
Closes #197763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-provided MCP servers that use OpenClaw-managed OAuth (for example `@openclaw/atlassian`) are projected into the native Codex thread config with the URL but no credential, so Codex fails to initialize them with `invalid_token` and no tools appear, even though Settings reports the connection as authorized.

## User Impact

Authorized plugin MCP connections now reach native Codex with a usable bearer, so Jira-style remote MCP tools become discoverable and callable right after the plugin is authorized. No configuration change or re-authorization is required, and servers without a saved credential are still omitted rather than sent unauthenticated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle projection path built Codex `mcp_servers` straight from the prepared bundle config, while only the owner-configured path ran `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig` first. The plugin server therefore kept `auth: "oauth"` into normalization, which has no credential to emit, leaving `http_headers` and `bearer_token_env_var` empty. The bundle path now resolves the same way the owner path does — literal token projection, `omitUnavailableOAuthServers` so a missing credential drops that one server instead of failing the thread, and a diagnostic naming the plugin whose credential could not be resolved. Unauthenticated and non-OAuth servers are projected exactly as before.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression test red→green: `projects the resolved OAuth bearer for a plugin-only server` in `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts`. With the previous projection line restored, the test fails because `http_headers` is absent (`1 failed | 7 skipped`); with this change it passes (`8 passed`, file-level run). Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts --reporter=verbose`.
- [x] Targeted suite: `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.test.ts` → `8 passed (8)`, including the pre-existing projection, grant, and requester-scope cases, so the added resolution step changes nothing for servers that carry no OAuth credential.
- [x] Lint/format on the touched files: `oxlint` reports `0 warnings and 0 errors`; `oxfmt` reports the files formatted.
- [x] Scope: `src/agents/codex-mcp-config.ts` only gains the bearer-resolution step plus its diagnostic; the owner-config projection path, `resolveMcpBearerBundleConfig`, and the Codex TOML/args paths are untouched.
- [x] Honest boundary: this proves the bundle projection now emits the Authorization header produced by the existing resolver, using a stubbed credential store. It does not perform a live OAuth refresh or a real Jira tool call against Atlassian; token acquisition itself is covered by the existing resolver path, which this change now reuses rather than reimplements.

prs.title: fix(gateway): restart after slow sidecar cleanup finishes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an in-process Gateway restart exits instead of restarting when a sidecar exceeds its diagnostic cleanup grace but finishes successfully before shutdown completes.

## User Impact

User impact: a successfully joined slow sidecar no longer prevents the Gateway from restarting. Pending cleanup, rejected operations, explicit retained-resource failures, and fatal shutdown errors retain their existing authority. No configuration, schema, migration, or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

An expired diagnostic grace was recorded permanently even after the existing required owner join completed the exact cleanup operation. Final shutdown disposition now omits only that operation's obsolete grace warning after successful settlement. It does not increase a timeout, add a retry, reorder shutdown steps, or clear unrelated failures.

In the failing main QA run, the GitHub OAuth sidecar finished after 7.288 seconds and shutdown reported a clean join, but the stale retained-resource classification still forced exit 0 instead of the requested restart.

## Evidence

- Regression proof on base `c097873adcf685540c2ff9dd737b52929b848285` with the new test cases: **2 failed, 5 passed**. `late-joined` incorrectly returned `GatewayShutdownCleanupRetainedError`; `late-joined-fatal` incorrectly retained that classification after a fatal close failure.
- The reviewed candidate `d5a515bea2db2841b389648b20410ce13e895e31`: **8/8 tests passed across 2 files** (`server-shutdown.test.ts` and `server-sidecar-retention.test.ts`), including the existing optional/fatal/required cases and the two late-join cases. Scoped typed lint and repository-config formatting both passed.
- The actual isolated Gateway, real Matrix channel adapter, and Crabline local transport completed `matrix-restart-replay-dedupe` on the **first scenario attempt, 1/1 passed, no retries**. The private QA runtime was built under Node 24.22.1. This uses a synthetic local provider/transport, **not a live Matrix homeserver or live model**.
- Fresh full-context independent Codex review of the shutdown owner, fixture, and sidecar owner found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Exact published-head PR CI and post-merge main qualification remain pending. These focused results do not establish full-main green or a permanently fixed flake.

<details>
<summary>Retained proof excerpts and source binding</summary>

The remote proof applied the reviewed patch to the exact base above. The QA applied patch differs from the reviewed patch only in Git index abbreviations; patch content was verified identical.

```text
BASE + regression cases:
FAIL joins required work and preserves fatal close status (late-joined)
FAIL joins required work and preserves fatal close status (late-joined-fatal)
Tests  2 failed | 5 passed (7)

CANDIDATE:
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       8 passed (8)
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
All matched files use the correct format.

ISOLATED QA:
[qa-suite] scenario start (1/1): matrix-restart-replay-dedupe
[qa-suite] scenario pass (1/1): matrix-restart-replay-dedupe
[qa-suite] run complete: passed=1 failed=0 skipped=0 total=1
```

The QA scenario verified a reply before restart, successful resume after restart, a fresh reply, and no replay. No production Gateway, external credentials, workflow rerun, or dispatch was used for this proof.

</details>

Requested by @obviyus and @steipete.

prs.title: fix: backup restore accepts a symlinked --target for PostgreSQL archives
prs.body:
Closes #197779

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw backup restore --target <dir>` refuses to restore a PostgreSQL archive with "PostgreSQL recovery configuration must be inside the restored archive." when any ancestor of the target directory is a symlink (for example `ln -s /Volumes/data/work ~/work`), even though the recovery configuration really is inside the freshly extracted archive.

## User Impact

Restoring a PostgreSQL backup into a directory reached through a symlink now works instead of aborting before any data is written. No configuration change, migration, or extra flag is required, and archives whose configuration genuinely escapes the restore target are still rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The containment guard compared two different spellings of the same location: `targetPath` kept the caller's spelling, which still contains the unresolved symlinked ancestor, while only the configuration path was run through `fs.realpath`. Once the ancestor resolved, the canonical configuration path was no longer lexically inside the unresolved target, so a legitimate archive was rejected. Both sides now go through the repo's containment canonicalizer (`canonicalizePathForContainment`) before `isPathInside`, so the comparison is between two canonical spellings while the existing escape rejection is preserved.

## Evidence

- [x] Regression test red→green: `accepts a recovery configuration below a symlinked restore target` (in `src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts`). With the previous guard restored, the test fails with `Error: PostgreSQL recovery configuration must be inside the restored archive.` (`1 failed | 19 skipped`); with this change it passes (`1 passed | 19 skipped`, 435ms). Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts -t "symlinked restore target" --reporter=verbose`.
- [x] Targeted suite: `src/commands/backup-restore.test.ts` → `18 passed | 2 skipped (20)`. The two skips are pre-existing `it.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")` cases, unrelated to this change.
- [x] Lint/format on the touched files: `oxlint` reports `0 warnings and 0 errors`; `oxfmt --check` reports `All matched files use the correct format.`
- [x] Scope: only `src/commands/backup-restore.ts` (the guard is now one exported helper, `assertRecoveryConfigInsideRestore`) and its test file changed. Extraction, manifest verification, and PostgreSQL restore orchestration are untouched.
- [x] Honest boundary: this proves the symlinked-ancestor false negative is gone and that a configuration outside the target still throws. It does not exercise a full PostgreSQL restore (no database engine is started); the guard runs before any engine work, so the test asserts the guard contract directly.

Claude CLI runs could discover the provider's `CronList` tool even though the adapter already excludes `CronCreate` and `ScheduleWakeup`. That exposes a separate scheduler inventory alongside OpenClaw's native cron owner.

Add the known `CronList` name to the existing `--disallowedTools` argument. Update the existing fresh, resumed, and managed-shell expectations; no new routing or tool-name guesses. On isolated Railway Linux with Node 24.20.0, pnpm 12.5.1, and the frozen selected native source:

- Updated existing expectations fail on the original fresh/resumed arguments exactly because `CronList` is missing.
- Corrected existing `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.test.ts`: 42/42 pass, one provider worker.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): reclaim scratch before the cleanup backlog
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Expired scratch can wait behind an entire worktree-GC backlog while normal shared-host IO repeatedly trips an absolute PSI-full threshold. This moves the existing bounded scratch slice ahead of GC and makes the pressure owner brake on observed latency and sustained severe stalls.

## Behavior and Safety

The pressure predicate retains the one-second fresh/in-progress btrfs commit brake, measures a one-second local asynchronous kernel-counter round trip, and uses PSI `some avg60 >=50%` for sustained host distress. Ordinary PSI-full and short spikes alone no longer veto cleanup. Scratch retains its 256-candidate, 4096-name and separate two-million-entry scan/removal budgets, depth 64, resumable cursor and batch pacing. Lease, identity, live-run, expiry and link protections remain. A pressure observation consumed by scratch carries into the existing five-minute idle/template removal clock; capacity GC remains reachable.

No config, schema, dependency or new cache. Runtime net +21 lines for scratch-first failure/cancellation handling and pressure handoff. Docs describe the thresholds and budget; release-note context is this starvation fix.

## Evidence

**Owner-accepted performance tradeoff (2026-11-12, 11:55 PST):** Peter explicitly accepted landing with the measured loop-tail cost: worst-arm p99 increased from 13.49 to 16.42 ms and maximum delay from 59.9 to 83.3 ms. These background-maintenance delays remain far below Team's production loop p99 of 250–450 ms. Fresh commit maxima improved from 503 to 111 ms and reclaim improved from 0 to 256 entries per window; without this fix, 806 nested clones pinning about 3.3 TB remain unreclaimed. The CPU/allocation table below records the cost of resuming real cleanup. The physical workload includes an uncontrolled stronger host episode: the fourth baseline's full median was 21.805%, maximum 45.39%; other arm medians were 0.83–2.56%. No sample is discarded.

All 102 focused runtime/consumer tests pass. Three original assertions fail on the exact main parent; two consumed-pressure assertions fail on the previous PR head. `pnpm check:changed`, targeted checks and Codex autoreview through P2 pass. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43280024466) passes on `c9ad63eaf05bf340b324c9cdb654b11a68538903`. ClawSweeper has zero open items on this head; its prior pressure-handoff finding is fixed and [answered by number](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197772#issuecomment-6830705924). Earlier PR-caused timer and lint failures were repaired. No inherited-red waiver.

The committed `scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts` runs the production maintenance owner under normal Gateway spawn-broker context. Final Linux/btrfs proof uses a closed 35.18 GiB DB with 5000 synthetic sessions, two 62000-file/1.143 GB workspaces, and 806 clone-shaped scratch entries distributing that fanout. No production data. Two A/A controls plus five interleaved pairs use equal 60-second windows. Preparation and the existing runtime import warmup are excluded and reported separately; no cleanup is pre-executed.

Background 4 KiB random writes/fdatasync have a fixed 100 ms duty and 2 ms bursts for two seconds every thirty. Exact probe inputs replay PSI-full 1–5% plus 30% spikes; actual kernel counters remain separate. Physical PSI-full arm medians span 0.83–21.80%, with spikes to 45.39%; 446/720 raw samples are in 1–5%.

**Reclaim: 0 -> 256 entries / 363.34 MB logical per 60-second observation**, leaving 806 -> 550. Candidate owner completion 36.63–59.38 s. All controls reach admission and remain blocked; all candidates finish the bounded slice without errors. One ordinary worktree is removed, and the other remains correctly protected by its remaining nested repositories.

| Metric: median / sample p95 (range) | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Process CPU, s | 14.778 / 21.255 (11.177–21.255) | 30.387 / 57.087 (24.754–57.087) |
| Main CPU, s | 0.423 / 0.724 (0.317–0.724) | 7.249 / 14.355 (5.229–14.355) |
| Main-V8 allocation, MiB | 22.467 / 25.781 (21.562–25.781) | 2655.690 / 2680.761 (2650.933–2680.761) |
| Loop p99, ms | 11.567 / 13.492 (11.272–13.492) | 11.633 / 16.425 (11.280–16.425) |
| Loop maximum, ms | 44.990 / 59.900 (26.231–59.900) | 52.658 / 83.296 (46.531–83.296) |
| Fresh sampled commit maximum, ms | 118.000 / 503.000 (108.000–503.000) | 100.000 / 111.000 (92.000–111.000) |

A/A loop p99 11.22–11.75 ms, maxima 33.52–47.55 ms. Sample p95 is nearest rank across five arms. CPU includes workers but excludes broker/Git children; allocation is main V8 only. Increased CPU/allocation is the cost of resumed cleanup versus blocked work, not an equal-work efficiency improvement.

Cold-source results remain separate: median loop p99 11.207 -> 11.223 ms, but maxima 36.44–51.61 -> 112.59–243.66 ms. Profiling found a 123 ms synchronous source-loader burst on the first existing runtime import. The benchmark now records that import warmup outside steady-state timing; no production workaround was added. The first warm series also reclaimed 256 consistently, but physical pressure often fell below 1%, so the stronger fixed-duty series above supplies the completed physical-pressure comparison, including the loop-tail limitation.

Limitations: the loop probe covers the maintenance owner in broker context, not full live transport/model traffic; btrfs is a 64 GiB loop image on ext4. Logical bytes are not physical freed space, and a bounded hourly pass is not continuous throughput. No production deployment, restart or manual deletion is included.

Reproduction command per arm (synthetic fixture paths):

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/worktree-cleanup-pacing-measure.ts \
  --source "$FIXTURE_SOURCE" --output "$ARM_OUTPUT" --worktrees 2 \
  --scratch-clones 806 --observe-ms 60000 --psi-trace \
  --agent-db-fixture "$CLOSED_AGENT_DB"
```

Baseline arms set `OPENCLAW_BENCH_BASELINE_DIR` to the extracted maintenance and pressure modules from `8864d2764ded33714df5334aa842e75582c55ef1`; candidate arms unset it.

prs.title: fix(android): realtime Talk hangs up when a navigation prompt or notification sound plays
prs.body:
Closes #181710

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk hangs up with "audio focus lost" as soon as another app plays a short sound, for example a navigation prompt or a notification.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk now keeps going while you drive with navigation on or when a notification sound plays. During the prompt Talk gets quieter and stops listening, then carries on. A ringing or active phone call still ends Talk, and now so do VoIP calls that ring or use the microphone in call mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

The focus listener in `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` treated every focus change except `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN` as fatal. Navigation apps grab transient focus for each prompt (on my phone it arrives as `AUDIOFOCUS_LOSS_TRANSIENT`, not just `..._CAN_DUCK`), so every "turn left" ended the session.

Now a transient loss keeps the session and marks Talk as interrupted until `AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN`:

- Microphone frames are dropped through the existing capture gate, so the prompt itself doesn't reach the provider as user speech.
- `RealtimePlayout` lowers its track volume to 20 %. Android never auto-ducks speech, so the app has to do it. The playout owner applies the gain on every write and on every periodic poll, which also covers audio that's already buffered.
- I chose ducking over `AudioTrack.pause()` on purpose. The playout's stall detection, write timeouts and mark timing all assume a playing track, and pausing would have meant reworking that.

Calls take transient focus too, and Talk shouldn't keep talking over a call. So while focus is lost, Talk still ends when a call shows up through any of these signals:

- a telephony mode (`MODE_RINGTONE`, `MODE_IN_CALL`, `MODE_CALL_SCREENING`) for regular phone calls,
- an active player with `USAGE_NOTIFICATION_RINGTONE`, which covers ringing in most VoIP apps,
- another app's `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` capture, which VoIP apps start once a call is answered. Talk's own recorder is excluded by its audio session ID; unprivileged apps get anonymized recording configs, but those keep the session ID and source ([`anonymizedCopy`](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/media/java/android/media/AudioRecordingConfiguration.java)).

These can arrive before or after the focus loss, so the focus, mode, playback and recording callbacks all check again. The loss is reported only once. No new permissions are needed.

Known limits:

- VoIP detection is best effort. An app that neither plays a ringtone nor captures with `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` only interrupts Talk instead of ending it, and a ringtone preview while Talk is interrupted would end it.
- Ducking still lets Talk's speech be heard quietly under the prompt.

## Evidence

- Real phone, navigation running ([screen recording, 29 s](https://github.com/mcdax/openclaw/releases/download/talk-focus-proof-181713/talk-focus-before-after.mp4)): with the current app, starting navigation during Talk immediately shows "Sprachfunktion fehlgeschlagen: audio focus lost" and the session ends. With a debug build of this branch, navigation starts while Talk is active and Talk keeps listening and answers normally. The Gateway only saw a normal `session.closed` in the failing case, no server error.
- Real phone, phone call during Talk ([screen recording, 18 s](https://github.com/mcdax/openclaw/releases/download/talk-focus-proof-181713/talk-call-ends-talk.mp4)): same debug build of this branch (`2026.8.2-debug`). Realtime Talk is listening, then a call to the carrier voicemail is placed from the same phone. As soon as the call connects, Talk ends with "Sprachfunktion fehlgeschlagen: audio focus lost", so a transient focus loss during a call still ends Talk. The VoIP path (ringtone or another app's `VOICE_COMMUNICATION` capture) is covered by the tests below, not by a device recording.
- A build that only tolerated `..._CAN_DUCK` still dropped at the prompt, which is why transient losses are handled too.
- New tests: transient loss interrupts without ending Talk; a call ends Talk once, whether the mode change comes before or after the focus loss; a VoIP ringtone or foreign voice capture ends Talk while Talk's own capture does not; buffered speech is ducked without new writes and restored afterwards; mic frames are held back while focus is lost.
- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.voice.*'`: 280 passed. `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:lintPlayDebug` are clean and `:app:assemblePlayDebug` builds.

prs.title: fix(models): disclose recorded provider failures behind refreshFailed
prs.body:
Fixes #194330

## What Problem This Solves

When a model catalog refresh fails for a provider, the published catalog carries the aggregate `refreshFailed: true` flag without any provider outcome explaining which discovery failed. Channel clients then show a generic "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." over a fully populated catalog with no actionable scope. In plain terms: the system says "something failed" but never says what, so users cannot tell whether their configured provider is broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recorded acquisition failures go through `createCatalogAttemptReporter.failed()`, which only books providers into the attempt's failure scope; no `ProviderCatalogOutcome` is written for them, so the models.list projection forwards a bare flag. The published catalog now discloses those providers as `status: "unavailable"` outcomes alongside any real discovery outcomes, live with the attempt: settling a provider (successful renewal) withdraws the synthesized disclosure, and a provider that already has its own determinate outcome is never shadowed. Model availability decisions are unchanged — the decision layer gates only on `auth-rejected` outcomes, and ready-only consumers ignore unavailable rows.

## User Impact

Clients reading `models.list` receive the failing provider scope behind `refreshFailed` (e.g. `providerOutcomes: [{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}]`) and can show which provider failed instead of an unexplained retry notice. No availability or eligibility change.

## Evidence

- Regression: `prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.test.ts > "discloses recorded acquisition failures as unavailable provider outcomes"` — a recorded failure surfaces `{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}` on the published catalog, the healthy provider's real `ready` outcome is untouched, and `published(["unreachable"])` withdraws the disclosure. Suite 4/4 green.
- Adjacent consumers unchanged: `models-list-result.provider-outcomes.test.ts`, `models-list-result.access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.account-access.test.ts` all green (37 tests).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxfmt clean.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194330, trace the missing outcome path in prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.ts, and implement the disclosure merge. The implementer understands the code: the synthesized outcomes are disclosure-only and the decision layer's availability gates consume only auth-rejected outcomes. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(cron): inherit authorized fallback policy for existing jobs
prs.body:
## Why
Scheduled jobs should recover from quota errors and outages through their configured fallback chain, without a manual migration or an unintended account or billing change.

## What changed
- Existing and new jobs automatically snapshot eligible, already-authorized model/account/runtime policy at admission. Explicit overrides, including an empty fallback list, stay in force.
- Preserve recorded account lifetimes and check revocation through execution and settlement. Loss of admitted authority stops the run.
- Remove the separate CLI, bulk, and editor review controls. Run-local conversion does not rewrite stored job definitions.

## Scope
Cron private inference bindings/grants and persistence; isolated and session-target admission; embedded/CLI execution; Doctor diagnostics; Gateway/protocol, CLI/editor, documentation, and focused regressions.

## Tradeoffs
Unavailable or ambiguous optional accounts can be skipped without blocking a healthy primary. Recorded authority loss remains terminal: the run cannot escape it by switching providers. This is broader than the provider-scoped reliability repair in #196539, which selects other providers' credentials live and lets their candidates continue after a recorded-provider refusal.

## Blast Radius
Existing and new scheduled jobs. Automatic conversion preserves IDs, schedules, enabled state, payloads, and delivery. Tool, session, and sandbox restrictions remain in force. No deployment or live-state migration is included.

## Verification
- Source-bound focused authorization/revocation, placement, CLI/Gateway, Doctor, and editor/browser evidence retained; browser keyboard coverage uses a mocked Gateway.
- Native core/UI typing and core lint accepted; the final targeted Doctor-test typecheck passed with no diagnostics. Earlier build evidence is historical, not a final-head build rerun.
- No full-suite, fresh combined-matrix, or CI-green claim. Earlier Doctor timeout and omitted-finding causes remain unresolved. Exact-head hosted review and CI remain landing gates.
