prs.title: fix(ci): respect fixture readiness and resource ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled and full CI exposed seven fixture assumptions about readiness, resource ownership, and process isolation. These tests could fail while their production owners correctly refused stale resources, completed asynchronous preparation, or enforced an existing deadline.

## User Impact

The fixtures verify their intended public behavior after their own setup is ready and with task-owned resources. Production behavior is unchanged. Existing page bounds, refusal outcomes, descriptor release, diagnostics sanitization, archive refusal, Git object retention, automatic skill discovery, and real browser crash/recovery assertions remain intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

| Fixture | Cause and correction |
| --- | --- |
| [Agent deletion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43261987532/job/131336350240) | A released descriptor number can be reused before the next asynchronous observation. Observe the actual final close while preserving prior admission custody and closed-auth-reader assertions. |
| [Transcript paging](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43258726252/job/131324892019) | Large synthetic seeds schedule background projection preparation. Join that existing preparation in the shared fixture before asserting pagination, without changing the history request’s three-second deadline. |
| [Diagnostics ZIP](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43247741400/job/131285665040) | Earlier export cases initialized the process logger before a later fixture selected a different synthetic log. Reset the existing logger at setup and cleanup. |
| [Browser lifetime](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43261987532/job/131336350471) | The deliberately crashed Linux renderer can remain in piped core collection. Limit only the nested fixture runner with the existing one-byte suppression convention, preserving inherited hard-zero limits, the real crash, diagnostics, privacy and sibling recovery. |
| [Backup ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43258726252/job/131324891517) | The loop fixture used shared temporary scratch that another real maintenance operation could retire before admission. Use the existing scratch-isolation helper. |
| [Git pack byte budget](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43261987532/job/131336350715) | A byte-budget test also depended on finishing retirement within a separate wall-clock budget. Freeze its monotonic fixture clock; retain the independent deadline/sidecar/object-retention coverage. |
| [Automatic skill refresh](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43258726252/job/131324891849) | The fake-clock helper joined started worker scans but could advance past the debounce before asynchronous directory reconciliation had scheduled one. Join the forwarded filesystem-access promises before advancing that clock. |

Production delta: **0**. Test delta: **+25 lines across seven files**. No new cases, configuration, caches, production seams, retries, dependencies, schemas, retention changes, or runtime deadlines. Native/macOS repairs and runtime restart changes are outside this PR.

The diagnostics owner transition is #197742 (`5d6a026e43757ea6302e4c1151d6ace28468ced0`); asynchronous skill reconciliation is #197445 (`36afa92b2370c23bfd64d3f4a6f1b3aab68fd300`); bounded Git retirement is #195968 (`280e1de139e77b1a62e33ec4362d74a42f7e8ae8`). The descriptor expectation dates to #167739 (`bb7d32e55d48a85c6a08b374064e7a45d1e52b9c`); the paging case dates to #188483 (`b195f61511f9310d9a4dd416e517fb9ec0755f4d`), with its existing read deadline from #161451 (`5c4041708d668c273ce7f96853279ed40e2ad017`). These predate the last known green full run. Backup refusal preserves the accepted pre-payload admission policy from #175983 (`5588de47ba5cbec1cbd5bd997b446b8f2b27014e`). Their exact recent exposure, the original descriptor reuser, and the original competing backup maintenance operation remain untraced; no passing replay is treated as proof of flakiness.

Browser fixture history is #183498 (`a3027303409267e2456f8621e8e8e2d2be970fdd`) and intentional-crash coverage #190823 (`aca02bcd82294778f99ea3651f3d9366f73030de`); these identify the fixture origins, not a proven historical failure-introduction commit.

The cache-handoff fixture was excluded after exact-base inspection found the canonical owner repair already landed in #197841 (`df93b4c8aab664ec43d0ac0eaf074a0415826431`). Its stronger normalized refusal contract and new missing-cache case remain intact.

## Evidence

- **Descriptor:** a real same-number/different-inode control fails the original assertion and passes the correction. The final deletion file passes 26 cases.
- **Transcript:** the original unchanged case reproduces the CI rebuilding error. The unchanged request deadline expires after exactly 3,000 ms while the actual reconcile callback is held; after release, real readiness and all page assertions succeed. Identical 3.5-second preparation delay fails the old fixture and passes this one. Final reader/title consumers pass all 25 cases, including separate unavailable/recovery coverage.
- **Diagnostics and backup:** the ordered diagnostics reproduction is red and the complete fixed file passes 22 cases. Real scratch retirement reproduces the backup failure; the same control with isolated scratch and the complete 14-case file pass.
- **Git and skills:** real delayed pack retirement reproduces completed/3→2, while the corrected byte-budget fixture reaches 3→1 with all objects readable; 18 applicable final cases pass. Held real filesystem reconciliation reproduces the missing skill; the corrected helper joins it and publishes the expected snapshot. Skill/observer consumers pass 20 cases. These controls establish ownership/completion defects, without claiming the original hosted interleavings were traced.
- **Browser:** the retained Linux diagnostic observes the intended renderer in CoreDumping while its siblings remain healthy. The unchanged macOS branch passes. The exact candidate also passes the actual Linux fixture in [prior-head proof run43279826643](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43279826643/job/131398697096), in 5.461 seconds. The combined PR’s exact-head [checks-ui (1/3) job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43289758264/job/131433574665) also executed this fixture successfully in 4.848 seconds: one pass, zero failures, zero skips. The retained Vitest module receipt confirms actual execution.
- Individual scoped Codex reviews and final-source hashes are retained. The candidate is assembled on the verified #197839 merge `76024435027d4ac4e51a58468bb1b5c4842d9fb0`. All seven final source hashes match their individual reviewed receipts; 420 retained owner/context inputs are unchanged. Fresh all-seven-file Codex P2 review is scoped-clean. The full required combined `pnpm check:changed` passed on that exact base, including all three unused-export scans, eight affected TypeScript graphs, UI catalog/controller checks, format, lint and ratchets. Earlier per-file checks that failed on pending-input exports remain recorded as failures on their old bases; the named repair and green combined check resolve that gate, including backup’s first required changed check. No inherited-red exemption is requested.
- Temporary gates, timing output and diagnostic instrumentation are absent. All fixtures use synthetic owned data. Final-head ClawSweeper completed at `cd83b33e371985d62d2a56efafb89042fedc48b7` with no findings or open items ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197879#issuecomment-6833808731)). Exact-head [CI43289758264](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43289758264) completed successfully: 34 jobs passed and 28 skipped. Native scripts/pr landing and the first scheduled full run containing all repairs remain separate required gates.

prs.title: fix(tasks): recompute terminal retention after lost-task recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a task loses its backing session, maintenance marks it `lost` and stamps the
short 24-hour lost-window retention (`cleanupAfter = lostAt + 24h`). When the
durable ledger later records a real terminal result, maintenance recovers the task
to `succeeded`/`failed` but never recomputes `cleanupAfter`, so the recovered
record keeps `lostAt + 24h` instead of the standard 7-day terminal retention from
its actual `endedAt`. If recovery happens more than 24h after the lost-mark
(Gateway down overnight, long-running job), the recovered terminal record is
pruned on the very next sweep — the user never sees the recovered outcome,
defeating the recovery feature's purpose of preserving finished work across
Gateway restarts (#145940). Even on quick recovery, the record gets only the
remainder of the short lost window instead of the documented 7-day terminal
retention (#126063, #126095).

## Why This Change Was Made

The defect is in `applyTaskRecordPatch` (`src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts`),
the lifecycle owner that stamps `cleanupAfter` for terminal records: it only
recomputed when `cleanupAfter` was missing, so the numeric lost-window value
survived a `lost` → terminal transition. Recovery paths (`markTaskRecovered` /
`projectTaskRecovered` in `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts`) also
preserved the numeric value.

The fix recomputes the terminal retention whenever a terminal status is reached
from `lost`, and makes the `projectTaskRecovered` projection always recompute.
The invariant: the short lost-window retention applies only while the record is
still `lost`; once recovered, the standard terminal retention from the recovered
`endedAt` applies. Files changed: `src/tasks/task-registry-records.ts` and
`src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.ts` (fix), `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`
and the `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` fixture (regression
tests). No new dependencies, configuration options, or schema changes.

## Review-followup fixes

- **Exclude unchanged `lost` status from the recovery predicate (P2).**
  `isTerminalTaskStatus("lost")` is true, so the recovery recompute also ran when
  a still-`lost` record received a metadata-only or cleanup-only update
  (e.g. `setTaskCleanupAfterById`), silently replacing the explicit deadline the
  retention owner honors with `endedAt + 24h`. The predicate now requires a
  *different* terminal status (`next.status !== "lost"`): only a real recovery
  recomputes, and a still-`lost` record keeps its existing deadline. A regression
  test ("preserves an explicit lost-task deadline on a cleanup-only update")
  covers this: it fails on the pre-fix predicate (deadline 45260000 replaced by
  88400000) and passes with the fix.
- **Prove persistence across real OS process restarts, not just reload (proof
  followup).** The previous proof reloaded the registry from SQLite inside one
  process, which is not independent proof of an operating-system process
  restart. The committed subprocess regression test now spawns the fixture as
  three genuinely separate OS processes (`node --import tsx`, distinct PIDs)
  sharing one SQLite state dir: seed → recover → verify, then the parent reloads
  and runs the next sweep. The corrected deadline demonstrably survives real
  process restarts, and the next sweep keeps the recovered record.

## User Impact

Recovered terminal cron tasks now keep the documented 7-day retention from their
recovered end time, so their outcome stays visible in task history instead of
being pruned shortly after recovery. Tasks that are never lost are unchanged;
`lost` records still use the 24-hour window (and still honor an earlier explicit
lost-task deadline).

## Evidence

- **OS-process-restart recovery proof (before/after).** The real task-registry
  module chain runs against one real SQLite state dir across three genuinely
  separate OS processes (each a distinct `node --import tsx` child), so
  persistence is proven across real process restarts — the same boundary a
  Gateway restart crosses — not just an in-process registry reload. A lost cron
  task whose 24h lost-window deadline has already expired is written by process
  1, recovered by process 2, and read + swept by process 3. Timestamps and PIDs
  are redacted below; each phase printed from a distinct process.

  **Before (pre-fix source):** recovery keeps the expired lost-window deadline,
  so the very next sweep prunes the recovered record (`pruned: 1`,
  `still-present: false`) — the recovered outcome is lost.

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:41:39.953Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... corrected-in-future=false corrected=false
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=false
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":1} still-present=false
  ```

  **After (fixed source):** recovery restores the standard 7-day terminal
  retention from the recovered `endedAt`; the corrected deadline survives all
  three process restarts and the next sweep keeps the record
  (`pruned: 0`, `still-present: true`).

  ```
  [seed]    seeded lost task: status=lost cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-17T05:42:28.485Z) expired=true
  [recover] reload saw: status=lost cleanupAfter=... stale-expired=true
  [recover] recovered: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... (2026-09-23T15:42:38.378Z) corrected-in-future=true corrected=true
  [sweep]   reload saw: status=succeeded cleanupAfter=... preserved-across-restart=true
  [sweep]   sweep: maintenance={"reconciled":0,"recovered":0,"cleanupStamped":0,"pruned":0} still-present=true
  ```

  `RESULT: PASS` — the corrected deadline survived 3 real process restarts and
  the recovered record is not pruned. The before/after traces are from the same
  script and state dir; the only difference is the two fixed source files.

- **Subprocess regression test (committed).** The same OS-process-restart flow is
  committed as a real persisted-SQLite regression test in
  `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts` ("persists the corrected deadline
  across real OS process restarts and survives the next sweep"). It spawns the
  fixture `test/fixtures/task-registry-recovery-restart.ts` three times via
  `node --import tsx` (seed → recover → verify) against one
  `withOpenClawTestState` state dir, then reloads and runs the next maintenance
  sweep in the parent. On the pre-fix source this test fails
  (`expected <expired lost-window deadline> to be greater than <now>`); with the
  fix it passes.

- **Regression tests** in `src/tasks/task-registry.store.test.ts`:
  - a `lost` record with the short lost-window `cleanupAfter` is recovered via
    `markTaskTerminalById({ status: "succeeded", ... })`; the recovered record's
    `cleanupAfter` equals the standard terminal retention from the recovered
    `endedAt` and is greater than the stale lost-window value (fails on the
    original code, passes with the fix);
  - a still-`lost` record keeps an explicit deadline on a cleanup-only update
    (P2 followup, fails on the pre-fix predicate);
  - the reload + next-sweep proof (fails on the PR base);
  - the OS-process-restart proof above (fails on the pre-fix source).
- Existing suites pass locally: `task-registry.store.test.ts` (59),
  `task-registry-records.test.ts`, `task-retention.test.ts`,
  `task-registry.maintenance-projection.test.ts`. `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`
  clean.
- Production LOC delta: net +4 — no new dependencies, config, protocol, or schema.
- AI-assisted: yes

prs.title: fix(test): reject malformed PID receipts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The test helper previously accepted PID receipt text with a valid numeric prefix, such as `42stale`, because `parseInt` stopped at the first non-decimal character.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the complete trimmed receipt as a positive safe decimal integer before returning it, while preserving the existing AbortSignal lifecycle. Rebased onto current `main`; commits carry the corrected author identity (`qingminglong`).

## User Impact

Test and CI cleanup helpers no longer treat contaminated PID receipts as real process identifiers.

## Evidence

### Real caller trace (red → green)

Direct `waitForPidFile` invocation from a cleanup-caller perspective, against a real temp-dir receipt file (unredacted terminal output, no credentials involved):

- **Base `main` helper** (bug reproduced):

  ```text
  BASE: receipt="42stale" -> resolved PID 42  (contaminated text accepted!)
  ```

- **This head** (fix applied):

  ```text
  receipt="42stale" -> rejected: aborted waiting for pid in ...\Temp\pid-probe-...
  receipt="42" -> resolved PID 42
  ```

### Regression suite (red → green)

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts`

- **Red** (base `test/helpers/process-wait.ts`, this PR's tests): `3 failed | 13 passed (16)` — exactly the malformed-receipt cases `42stale`, `42`, and `4.2` fail.
- **Green** (this head): `16 passed (16)`, including real process-death observation cases.

### Supporting checks

- Test-lines allocation record added: `config/test-lines-allocations/145959-pid-receipt-rejection.txt` (15 net test lines); `check-test-lines` passes locally (slack: 9).
- `oxfmt --check test/helpers/process-wait.ts test/helpers/process-wait.test.ts` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Proof boundary

This proves complete PID receipt parsing in the shared test helper and regression fixtures only; it makes no production runtime or platform-specific claim.

Exact head: `ebd701824afd630d3b933e25638eb8fc32ae1a5a`

prs.title: fix(telegram): cap rich message media at 20
prs.body: Closes #129004 ## What Problem This Solves Rich Telegram replies can appear successful while losing attachments and trailing content when a message contains more than 20 media items. Direct edits can bypass send pagination. ## User Impact Twenty media remain in one rich message; 21 are delivered in ordered pages of 20 and 1 with their trailing text intact. An over-limit edit becomes one complete plain replacement when it fits 4096 Unicode code points, or fails locally without overwriting the existing message. No new configuration, SDK surface, or migration is introduced. **Remaining merge-proof gap:** the Telegram Test Server userbot path (Convex-leased credentials) is still not exercised — this environment has no access to that QA broker. A final-revision **production Bot API recipient readback** is now recorded below (independent Telethon recipient, isolated Gateway built from this head); a maintainer with Test Server access can still run the userbot variant. ## Why This Change Was Made The existing rich-block owner now enforces the observed 20-media budget for ordinary blocks, media-heavy list items, and wrappers whose own summary/caption exceeds the local text target. List metadata, gallery captions, ordering, and trailing text remain intact. The edit owner checks the complete normalized plan and preserves current literal-text entities and request authorization. This refresh integrates main `44b6d7ca4a96074fef68870cc6f3a210b42856b8` with a regular merge, not a force-push. Edit regressions moved into the maintained HTTP suite rather than restoring the retired test file. The duplicate standalone 20/21 unit case was removed; distinct list/gallery contracts remain. ## Evidence Candidate: `cac84a8fe91e07fef1401bd2faf65bc585e3f62c` (tree `d9a249bc9317cafda8bfad343efc6e0b84df9c7c`). - **Baseline discrimination:** pinned main plus the same regression tests finished with **14 expected failures / 82 passes / 96 cases**. Failures include 21-media sends, long-summary/caption wrappers, complete Markdown/native edits, Unicode overflow rejection, and list/gallery boundaries. Setup failures are not counted as baseline-red. - **Candidate:** **96/96 passed** across `rich-blocks.test.ts` (35) and `send.telegram-http.test.ts` (61), including the long-wrapper case through the production HTTP send path. The final lint-repaired snapshot was rerun: Vitest 35.01 s; complete monitored wall time 41.767 s. These are combined-run timings, not individual-file wall times. - **Local static gates:** six-file format and syntax checks, focused syntax-only boundary lint (0 warnings/errors), and pinned-base whitespace checks passed. Full build, repository-wide typecheck/type-aware lint, and full test suites were not run locally. - **Independent review:** one completed local Codex autoreview campaign against the pinned base was `scoped-clean` through P2, with no material findings in an additional independent source review. Reviewed tree: `7108acc25f0139b68f246e205d5930cb714f05e8`; that review was followed by formatter-only changes plus the exact test-line allocation, verified mechanically before retesting. The later lint correction received the separate fresh delta review described below. This is not human approval or a new hosted ClawSweeper verdict. - **CI lint repair and fresh delta review:** the first refresh run [41936092465](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41936092465) failed on the newly introduced `oxc(no-map-spread)`. The correction uses ordinary loops with fresh continuation items, preserving immutable originals. The exact rule was reproduced red and then green locally; all 96 tests passed again. A fresh independent delta autoreview against `30a6cafae7b6d4c18cf7017890ae77f8e3357155` was `scoped-clean` through P2 on the candidate tree above. No suppressions or lint configuration changes were added. - **Hosted CI:** [41938814684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41938814684) **SUCCESS**, attached to `cac84a8fe91e07fef1401bd2faf65bc585e3f62c`. The repaired Telegram lint lane, 7 type jobs, 6 QA smoke jobs, all 5 selected test jobs, and the test budget passed (slack 15). The changed-extension bundle passed 394 cases across 20 test-file executions. All current required checks/statuses passed; pending/failed = 0. Full build was **SKIPPED**, not passed. Hosted jobs tested synthetic PR merge `65e7be5479aef46cdfe8e8c814e349df4b6706de` against then-current main, rather than a literal checkout of the author tree. The dedicated test-line allocation is **226 LF**, matching the exact net growth of the two maintained test files. It covers the distinct HTTP transport, whole-edit/Unicode, wrapper, and list/gallery contracts; the shared scalar budget is unchanged. Separate per-file measurements on the pre-lint-rewrite commit `30a6caf` were 7.707 s for 35 rich-block cases and 37.238 s for 61 HTTP cases (complete monitored wall). The test files are unchanged; these measurements are not relabeled as timings for the new commit. Hosted per-file wall time has not been reported. ### Final-revision recipient readback (production Bot API, dedicated stand bot) Isolated Gateway built from `cac84a8fe91e07fef1401bd2faf65bc585e3f62c` (`build-info.commit` = this sha) on a clean WSL2 Ubuntu host, dedicated throwaway bot and state dir, `richMessages: true`, DM allowlist of one numeric user. prs.title: fix(cron): give helpers spawned by linked automations their run's memory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a helper started by a scheduled automation gets an empty memory partition instead of the memory its run has, when the automation is linked to a conversation and runs as a child (`isolated`/`current` session target).

## User Impact

Helpers that an owner's linked automation starts (for example, Knowledge scribe runs that delegate) now get the same owner-private memory the run itself has. Non-owner automations' helpers are unchanged. There's nothing for users to do, and existing linked jobs pick up the fix on their next run.

## Why This Change Was Made

A child-placement scheduled run executes in its own hidden `:run:` row. The run resolves memory through the parent its occurrence was admitted against, but only for itself: a helper it spawns walks its lineage to the run row and stops there. Owner runs also carry no sender bit, so helpers recorded `spawnedBySenderIsOwner: false`.

- Cron run preparation stamps a private `scheduledMemoryParent` receipt on the run row: the parent key, `sessionId`, `lifecycleRevision` and the occurrence's admitted owner bit. It's written once per attempt by the run-continuation write, before the agent runs. Nothing else writes it.
- Spawns from a child-placement run record the occurrence's admitted owner bit, rechecked against a retained requester on every `sessions_spawn` and `sessions_create` call.
- Memory audience follows the receipt only from a spawned session's lineage, and only when both the spawn and the occurrence are owner-attributed. It then applies the same parent incarnation check as every other hop, so the helper gets the parent's audience (owner-private, or the parent's own conversation partition), bound to the parent's current incarnation.

The live execution-context registry was the first candidate owner, but it ends when the attempt settles or the Gateway restarts, and helpers outlive both (the E2E below shows a helper turn after a Gateway restart). The receipt therefore lives on the run row, the one durable fact helpers already reach.

### Threat model

- **Asset:** the owner-private memory partition. No new principal gains access. A helper inherits owner-private memory only when its own spawn receipt and the run's receipt both say owner, so a later non-owner turn in a run row can't pass the run's access on.
- **Forgery:** only the cron run-continuation write sets the receipt. `sessions.create` and `sessions.patch` are closed schemas without the field (tested). Spawn parameters never reach it. The plugin session-store API strips it from reads and rejects it in writes, and the slot key is reserved (tested against `applySessionEntryPatch`). Same-incarnation public patches preserve it, and rotating the session clears it.
- **Stale authority:** a parent reset or replacement (`sessionId` or `lifecycleRevision` mismatch) denies the helper with `stale-lineage` (unit-tested and shown live below), and existing grants go stale before provider I/O. The existing scheduled owner cap still applies. A requester who stops being an owner spawns as a non-owner, and a revocation mid-spawn refuses the commit (tested for both `sessions_spawn` and `sessions_create`).
- **Non-owner automations:** the owner bit comes from the occurrence's admission, never assumed. A receipt with `owner: false` leaves helpers resolving from the run row exactly as before (tested).
- **Cross-agent:** unchanged. The receipt hop stays within the run row's agent.
- **Lifetime:** the receipt lasts as long as the run row (cron removes it once the run and its descendants settle, otherwise after `cron.sessionRetention`, 24 hours by default) and is bounded by the incarnation check. Reset, rollover and carry-over never copy it.
- **Upgrade and downgrade:** no SQL table, column or schema-version change. Run rows and helpers from before the upgrade keep resolving from the run row; the next occurrence of an existing job records the receipt (shown live below). After a downgrade the older Gateway ignores the receipt. A helper spawned after this change already recorded the occurrence's owner bit, so until its run row expires it resolves from the run row's copied chat type: owner-private for a direct-chat parent, without the parent-reset check (observed live below; documented in `storage-changes.md`).

### Coverage and follow-ups

- **ACP children** (`sessions_spawn` with `runtime: "acp"`) record the same lineage receipt through `captureSpawnParentLineage` in `acp-spawn-creation.ts`, so they're covered.
- **Run rows copying `spawnedBy`:** can't happen for `isolated`/`current` jobs, which prepare with `forceNew` and drop ambient fields. Only non-detached `session:cron:*` targets carry ambient `spawnedBy`, and those aren't child placement.
- **In-session runs** execute on their parent's own row and record no receipt; their spawn bit is unchanged.
- **Follow-up: automation-removal revocation.** Removing a job doesn't revoke its run rows' receipts. The run's own memory grant doesn't check it either; it depends only on session incarnations. Enforcing it would make memory audience read the cron store.
- **Follow-up: fail closed for scheduled-run helpers in the conversation partition.** A helper that still lands in the run row's conversation partition (non-owner occurrence, unbound run after a parent reset) gets an empty, writable store whose writes are orphaned when the run row expires. A denial would be clearer; that's a separate change to the denial rules.
- **CODEOWNERS:** no entries cover `src/plugins/memory-audience.ts`, `src/cron/` or `src/config/sessions/`.

## Evidence

### Isolated-Gateway end-to-end (Mac Studio, real agent and model)

Two isolated Gateways on the Mac Studio, each with its own state directory, loopback port and synthetic data: the PR head (`b8c7acc46c6c`, runtime-identical to the current head) and its base `main` (`f817a8b3eb11`). Model: `clawrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. Memory slot: the bundled Knowledge plugin. No live Gateway was touched; both Gateways and their state were removed afterwards.

Flow, driven over the Gateway protocol with an owner (admin) operator:

1. `sessions.create` → owner direct chat (`chatType: direct`); one turn saves three synthetic claims with `knowledge_remember`. `knowledge_status` there: `records: 3`, no `scope` (owner-private).
2. A second turn asks the agent to create an automation with the automations tool: `sessionTarget: "current"`, payload "spawn one subagent with `sessions_spawn`; its task: call `knowledge_status` and reply with the result".
3. `cron.run {mode: "force"}`; the run spawns the helper; the helper's `knowledge_status` result is read from its transcript (`chat.history`).

| Step | `main` (`f817a8b3`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Helper of the owner run: `knowledge_status` | `scope: "conversation:<run session id>"`, `records: 0` | no `scope` (owner-private), `records: 3` |
| Helper row `spawnedBySenderIsOwner` | `0` | `1` |
| Run row `scheduledMemoryParent` | absent | `{sessionKey: <owner chat>, sessionId, lifecycleRevision, senderIsOwner: true}` |
| Helper follow-up turn, parent unchanged | — | owner-private, `records: 3` |
| Helper follow-up turn after `sessions.reset` of the owner chat | — | denied: `memory audience unavailable: session agent:main:subagent:… has stale lineage: ancestor agent:main:dashboard:… was reset or removed after its child was spawned … event=memory_audience_denied kind=stale-lineage`; the tool returned `Knowledge access unavailable` |
| New run after the parent reset (unbound occurrence, no receipt) | — | helper resolves from the run row: `scope: "conversation:<new run session id>"`, `records: 0` |

Upgrade, restart and downgrade on one shared state directory:

| Step | Helper `knowledge_status` |
|---|---|
| `main` creates the chat, the job and a run; helper A | `conversation:<run>`, `records: 0` |
| Upgrade to this PR; helper A follow-up turn (pre-upgrade run row, no receipt) | unchanged: `conversation:<run>`, `records: 0`; no load errors |
| PR runs the pre-existing job; helper B | owner-private, `records: 3`; run row carries the receipt |
| PR Gateway restart; helper B follow-up turn | still owner-private, `records: 3` (the receipt is durable) |
| Downgrade to `main`; helper B follow-up turn | owner-private via the run row's copied direct chat type (the downgrade case described in the threat model); no load errors |

Upgrade from the latest stable release, `v2026.11.3` (`847611dc`), to this PR (`e8bc8549`) on one isolated state directory. `v2026.11.3` doesn't bundle the Knowledge plugin, so it ran with its default memory, and the upgrade enabled the Knowledge memory slot:

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `v2026.11.3`: owner chat, linked `current` automation, forced run; helper A | run `ok`; helper A recorded `spawnedBySenderIsOwner: 0`; stable removed the settled run row |
| Upgrade: start the PR build | refused with "requires state migration", as for any `main` build after a stable release; `openclaw doctor --fix` migrated the agent database (schema 27 → 41) with pre-migration backups, then the Gateway started with no errors |
| Existing state after the upgrade | owner chat, job (`enabled: true`, `sessionTarget: current`, same parent) and all 3 jobs intact; the owner chat's next turn saved 3 Knowledge records |
| Helper A follow-up turn | denied with `stale-lineage`: its ancestor run row was removed by stable's cleanup before the upgrade (same as `main`; unchanged by this PR) |
| PR runs the pre-existing stable job; helper B | run row receipt records `senderIsOwner: false`; helper B gets `conversation:<run>`, `records: 0`. The stable job stored a parent link but no requester, so `main`'s existing admission rules already admit its occurrences as non-owner; this PR changes nothing for it |
| New job created after the upgrade from the same pre-existing chat; helper C | owner-private, `records: 3` |
| Gateway restart; helper C follow-up turn | still owner-private, `records: 3`; 4 jobs listed |

Not covered live: a **non-owner occurrence**. On a single-operator Gateway every operator turn is the Gateway owner: a parent-bound operator source is non-owner only for an OpenClaw ID member, and a reduced-scope token connection is still the owner profile. Producing one needs a team role, an OpenClaw ID member or a channel group member. The non-owner case is covered by `memory-audience.test.ts` (receipt `owner: false` and non-owner spawn both resolve from the run row), `run.bind-parent.test.ts` (a real scheduled occurrence whose requester is not the owner stores `senderIsOwner: false` on the run row) and `execution-context-admission.test.ts`.

Also observed on both `main` and this PR: every forced run that waited for its helper with `sessions_yield` ended with `accepted continuation children could not transfer terminal delivery`. It's inherited from `main` and unrelated to this change; the helper itself runs normally.

### Tests

- Regression tests that fail on `main`'s `memory-audience.ts` and pass with this change: a run's owner-spawned helper is granted owner-private memory, and is denied once the parent is reset or replaced.
- Unchanged-behavior tests: non-owner occurrence, non-owner spawn, owner spawn on a non-owner receipt, missing receipt.
- Writer and forgery: `run-session-state.lineage.test.ts` (cron writes, clears and seals the receipt; plugin patches can't set or replace it), and the `sessions.create`/`sessions.patch` schema tests.
- Production path: `run.bind-parent.test.ts` runs real occurrences through the scheduler and reads the run row before the agent starts; the stored receipt equals the occurrence's admitted parent for the owner, non-owner and unbound cases.
- Spawn bit: `openclaw-tools.scheduled-targets.test.ts` (scheduled targets reach the spawn and create tools with the occurrence's bit and its owner recheck), `execution-context-admission.test.ts` and `sessions-spawn-tool.owner-recheck.test.ts` (`sessions_spawn` and `sessions_create`).
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, the core test-type shards, oxlint and oxfmt pass on the touched files. The added test lines carry an allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/scheduled-run-child-memory.txt`.
- Independent review (Astra) found one P1: a captured owner bit wasn't rechecked when spawning. Fixed. No other P0–P2 findings.
- CI on `e8bc8549`: all green except an unrelated intermittent Bun-shard failure in `extensions/codex/src/native-thread-tool.test.ts` (`Session reader validation does not match its current physical owner`). The same error also fails #192623 and #195011; details in the PR comments.

prs.title: fix: make failed workspace preparation diagnosable
prs.body:
Related: #197849

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: managed workspace preparation failures discard unmatched Git diagnostics, leaving users and operators unable to identify the initiating clone or refresh failure.

## User Impact

Users receive a diagnostic ID that remains intact after reopening the session. Gateway operators can match it to the original Git process output and exit status. Raw transport output stays out of shared conversations.

The original production clone cause remains unknown. This does not change credentials, cancellation policy, or automatically retry failed workspaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing clone owner now records unmatched failures in its operator logger and returns a short correlation message. Keeping the message within the existing retained-summary bound prevents middle truncation from cutting through the ID. Existing preparation and cancellation owners remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Native Git regression: red on base, green with the fix; 23/23 clone-owner tests passed (39.19 s command wall time, including compiler preparation).
- Workspace preparation/recovery: full file 18/18 passed (57.04 s); final shared-fixture replay 7/7 passed. Covers initial failure, another failure through real preparation/source cancellation, then successful same-session recovery.
- Actual isolated Gateway: `sessions.create` → real Git failure → `chat.send` failed retry in the same session. Both restored complete, distinct IDs from history and matched the original causes in operator logs; clone I/O was not mocked.
- Core and affected-test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2): base `5dab86f716c9cc5cc8d4ac4ddfb48a400f3fca01` to the final working-tree snapshot committed as `5543bf00ec80bf927094b4abab8df8553ca6ccc7`; no actionable findings in the supplied diff and summary-owner context.
- Registry sibling coverage: 36 passed; two fixture cases were blocked at `git fetch --depth 1 origin` by this host's linked-worktree shallow-history safeguard, before reaching the changed classifier. The safeguard was not bypassed.
- Exact-head hosted checks: `openclaw/ci-gate`, `openclaw/dependency-review`, and `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` passed for `7d09274671fbb31caa551ab9126fda5a3fed2fe7` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43285589656)).

prs.title: fix(agents): treat embedded-run compaction as progress for stall recovery
prs.body:
Related to #191822

## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery aborted subagent runs that were compacting: the compaction window produced no semantic progress, so the attention classifier reached its stall deadline while the run was doing real work, and the controller watchdog cancelled it. Compaction — including automatic compaction after a context threshold — should hold the run's progress allowance for its own safety window, after which normal staleness handling resumes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compaction allowance now lives on the existing controller watchdog instead of an independent SessionActivity record, matching the recovery ownership consolidated by 36e277d (#175837). Compaction opens a bounded `compaction` wait (`beginWait({ kind: "compaction", deadlineAtMs })`) sized to the compaction safety ceiling: `decideSessionWatchdog` keeps observing while real compaction work runs, `projectControllerDiagnosticActivity` surfaces the wait as `activeCompactionDeadlineAtMs`, and the classifier treats an in-deadline compaction as `long_running("active_compaction")` before staleness. The allowance is wired into both compaction lifecycles: direct compaction (`compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirectOnce`) and the AgentSession automatic-compaction path (`runCompactionWork`, reached by `runAutoCompaction` on threshold and overflow).

## User Impact

Subagents and main sessions that trigger automatic compaction survive the stall threshold: the watchdog observes within the compaction safety ceiling instead of aborting, and the completed compaction still hands off normally. A hung compaction still expires — the wait deadline equals the compaction safety ceiling, after which staleness classification and recovery apply unchanged.

## Evidence

Controller-backed red/green regressions through the shipped watchdog and the real automatic lifecycle (`node scripts/test-projects.mts`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Watchdog: a `compaction` wait observes within its deadline and projects `activeCompactionDeadlineAtMs`; projection clears after close (`session-controller.watchdog.test.ts`) | green |
| Classifier: in-deadline compaction → `long_running("active_compaction")`; expired → `active_work_without_progress` (both cases) | green |
| Automatic lifecycle: real `AgentSession` threshold run inside a controller admission — the summary request observes the projected compaction deadline and the wait is closed after completion (`agent-session-compaction.test.ts`) | green |
| Red: bypassing the watchdog allowance in `runCompactionWork` fails exactly that regression (`expected undefined to be type of 'number'`); restored → green | red → green |

Suites: `session-controller.watchdog.test.ts` 56/56, `agent-session-compaction.test.ts` 20/20, plus `diagnostic-run-activity.test.ts`, `diagnostic-session-attention.test.ts`, `server.sessions.compaction-preemption.test.ts`, `diagnostic-controller-recovery.integration.test.ts` green.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep/file reads to work the review findings, moved the allowance onto the controller watchdog, and wired both compaction lifecycles. The implementer understands the code: the watchdog owns run recovery, so the bounded compaction wait is a watchdog wait projected into diagnostics, not an independent SessionActivity record. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(ui): default model save looks stuck while model discovery runs
prs.body:
Fixes #197857

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on the Models settings page, picking a default model looks stuck when provider discovery is still running after the save.

The save to `agents.defaults.model` completes right away. The Gateway then refreshes the provider catalog in the background, and that refresh can take several seconds. During that time the only feedback under the defaults is a spinner labelled "Discovering more models…", which reads as if the save is still running.

## User Impact

After a default model, utility model, fallback, thinking or fast-mode change is saved, the defaults section says **"Saved. Looking for more models in the background…"** while discovery runs. When discovery runs without a recent save (for example on page load or after Retry), it says "Looking for more models in the background…". Discovery itself is unchanged and still finishes in the background.

## Why This Change Was Made

The defaults section autosaves and deliberately shows no success banner; the picker showing the new value is the confirmation. The discovery status line was the only text left on screen, so it has to say that the save is done and that discovery is background work.

- The defaults save presentation (`config-mutation-presentation.ts`, which already tracks the saving field) records when the Gateway acknowledged the latest defaults write. The flag resets when the next defaults save starts.
- `default-models-view.tsx` uses that flag to choose between the two labels. Nothing else about discovery, its spinner, errors or Retry changes.

Accepted edge case: the "Saved." prefix stays until the next defaults change, so a later discovery on the same page (for example after Retry) also starts with "Saved.". That statement stays true, so it is not tracked further.

This does not overlap with #194939. That PR scopes the server-side catalog refresh to the published agents in `src/agents/*`; this one only changes Control UI copy and presentation in `ui/`.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway with a local Ollama model, in a VM.** Default model saved on the Models page, screenshot taken while the post-save discovery was still running. Local discovery normally finishes too fast to catch on screen, so for both runs catalog responses were delayed by 2 s through a transparent proxy, during a Retry after an Ollama outage. The delay only lengthens how long the status is visible; it does not change which label is shown.

Base: the status after the save is "Discovering more models…".

prs.title: fix(acp): relay exec approvals when Claude CLI and MCP tool call IDs differ
prs.body:
Closes #197829

## What Problem This Solves

An ACP client can wait indefinitely for an exec approval when Claude CLI and its MCP bridge assign different IDs to the same tool call.

## User Impact

The originating ACP turn can prompt the user for permission even when those IDs differ. Concurrent turns sharing a Gateway session remain isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already authenticates the agent runtime and knows which run requested approval. It now includes that verified run ID on the approval event. ACP matches both the session and the run. Requests without that provenance keep their existing matching behavior. An ordinary caller cannot select another turn by supplying a run ID in the request body.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing permission prompt and the missing runtime provenance on the base revision. On the branch, 38 tests passed across four ACP and Gateway test files. Coverage includes two concurrent turns, mismatched tool-call IDs, a stale run, a different session, and a caller-supplied run ID.
- Six additional Gateway MCP HTTP exec egress and completion tests passed using the Node Vitest runtime.
- The repository-wide production unused-export check flagged two exports outside the changed files, `bindSessionPendingInputMentionInvitation` and `readPendingInputSource`. Both exports and their consumers are unchanged from the base revision.
- Tested the Gateway and ACP code paths locally. A live authenticated Claude CLI session has not been exercised.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep dictated text when the window loses focus
prs.body:
Fixes #197843

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI composer dictation discards the whole transcript when the window loses focus or the page is hidden. Window `blur` and `visibilitychange` to `hidden` both routed to `cancel()`, which calls `stop({ commit: false })`, the same path as Escape. A screensaver, Alt+Tab or a tab switch during a long dictation silently threw away everything already transcribed. No notice was shown, and the text could not be recovered.

## User Impact

Losing window focus no longer destroys dictated text. The live capture stops, as before, but the transcript received so far, including the pending partial, is committed into the composer draft. The user can then edit or send it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`handleWindowBlur` in `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-dictation.ts` now handles three cases:

- **Capture is active** (connecting, recording or stopping): it clears click suppression and calls `stop({ commit: true })`, the same commit path as the Stop control.
- **A commit from an earlier interruption is still waiting for the final transcript:** it leaves that commit alone. A tab switch or minimize fires `blur` and then `visibilitychange`, and on the first revision the second event retired the draining commit.
- **No capture has started yet**, for example during the hold gesture before the threshold: it still cancels, as before.

Explicit discards are unchanged: Escape and draft replacement still discard. The visibility handler already delegates to `handleWindowBlur`, so both events share the new behavior.

No notice text was added, to avoid new locale strings. The kept text appears in the composer, so the outcome is visible to the user.

## Evidence

![test run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/197843/proof2.png)

**Setup:**

- The real `ComposerDictationOwner` is driven through its gateway-relay transcription session with the existing harness.
- A final transcript (`five minutes of speech`) and a partial (`and more`) arrive, then the window goes hidden or blurs.
- The only difference between the two runs is `composer-dictation.ts` (main `7b8ef42d8e91` vs this branch).

| event during live capture | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `visibilitychange` to `hidden` | transcript discarded; `onCommit` not called | committed: `five minutes of speech and more` |
| window `blur` | transcript discarded | committed |
| Escape / draft replacement | discarded | discarded (unchanged) |
| `blur` then `hidden` before the final transcript | discarded (also discarded on the first revision, `562e140`) | committed |
| blur during a hold, before capture starts | cancelled | cancelled (unchanged; the existing test passes) |

**Tests:**

- `composer-dictation.test.ts` has a new `keeps the dictated text when the window goes hidden / blur / blur then hidden` test. All three cases fail on main. `blur then hidden` also fails on the first revision, `562e140`. All pass here.
- The old `discards active capture on hidden` case was the behavior this issue reports as a bug, so it was removed from the discard table. The Escape and draft-replacement cases remain.
- `composer-dictation.test.ts` and `composer-direct-dictation.test.tsx`: 40 tests pass.

**Checks:** `oxlint`, `check:line-cap-ratchet` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` pass (net +4 test lines, within the allowance).

**Not run live:** a live browser run needs a microphone and a transcription provider, so it was not done here.

Fixes #145309.

## What Problem This Solves

Claude CLI can write valid transcripts outside the directory the Gateway checks when its child environment or working directory differs, causing lost resume continuity or missing imported/fallback history.

## User Impact

Resume checks and history consumers follow the effective child-selected location retained in the existing native binding. Changing the selected profile withholds its old native transcripts; committed canonical OpenClaw history remains readable. This access policy still needs maintainer acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The child-environment owner selects the transcript root once for execution and retains it through the existing binding lifecycle. Readers authorize it against the currently selected profile. Native lookup, file reads and publication retain their checks; node-placed sessions do not trigger Gateway-local discovery.

Fallback input carries caller-owned authority to the host effect: CLI argument spawn, stdin write, plugin dispatch, and embedded canonical capture/first request. Revocation before commitment fails with a typed local coordination error and retry guidance, without provider cooldown. A captured model-prompt projection is canonical history, including retries. Plugins own their asynchronous work after host dispatch; the private callback is removed from their SDK view.

The live probe also exposed overlapping authorization requests when scanning multiple project directories. One fresh grant now precedes each bounded batch of synchronously initiated filesystem probes; content reads and publication remain separately guarded. The latest repair checks again after discovery immediately before the fallback file read, retaining the post-read check.

## Evidence

Current head: `a57b433f46bb58656b9160c09d3a654f143bdc5b`; integrated main: `c53c53e749fbd0ec74eceb488f299ed25cd864b3`. Results below identify the revision and flow they cover.

### Installed Gateway fallback on the current candidate

The canonical package build passed in 5m59.2s and tarball/import-graph integrity in 94s. An isolated installation's build commit matched `a57b433f46b`. The server ran that installed package; the driver used public Gateway RPCs and a temporary public-SDK CLI backend, without invoking core attempt/assertion helpers.

A real official Claude Code turn created the retained native binding. After restart, an intentional retryable primary CLI fixture failure triggered the configured fallback through the Gateway's **`agent` RPC**. A synthetic native-only marker was absent from the current prompt and canonical transcript. The temporary backend used the normal host process runner; its allowed control then invoked official Claude Code 2.1.319 with the explicitly requested Opus 5.5 model through the existing subscription login, tools/hooks disabled and no API-key fallback.

Actual redacted terminal results:

```text
candidate=a57b433f46bb58656b9160c09d3a654f143bdc5b
no-model-preflight: primaryShim=true observer=true hold=true fallbackChild=true
reconciled-primary-not-resent: nativeIdStable=true localIdStable=true nativeOnlyMarker=true
natural-fallback-dry-control: primaryFailedRetryably=true nativeContextAtChild=true
profile-published: restart=false pidStable=true
revoked-final-transport: nativeContextPrepared=true revokedDuringDownstreamWait=true childStarted=false retryMessage=true nativeBindingStable=true
profile-published: restart=false pidStable=true
allowed-real-fallback: nativeContextAtChild=true realReplyMatched=true requestedModel=true apiFallback=false

```

The public `llm_input` observer recorded only marker-presence booleans. A public `beforeExecution` wait held downstream preparation while `config.patch` changed the skill-selected profile. The revoked run stopped with `NativeHistoryAuthorizationChangedError` / local runtime coordination before the argv child started. Restoring the profile let the real model return the exact native-only marker; its model identity was checked in the CLI result. Canonical-marker absence was rechecked immediately before that control. Test-owned Gateways, state, ports and process identities were used; profile junctions were removed without following them.

**Scope and setup limits:** this proves the documented `claude-cli/...` model reference with an explicit canonical SQLite session store and a relative child profile. The first driver attempt used `chat.send`, a sibling auto-reply path, and did not carry the marker; it was not counted as proof. The successful recovery reused the original binding instead of resending the first real turn. A no-model preflight with the default legacy store selector stopped at a transcript-store fence; the explicitly configured canonical store passed. Default-selector and `chat.send` fallback coverage are not claimed. Real embedded-provider fallback remains covered at its request-owner integration boundary, not by a new real-model Gateway run.

- New pre-read regression: revoke during the actual awaited discovery access and assert no native content read. It fails on `13744a3`; the snapshot/input suites pass 20/20 with the added pre-read assertion (10.19s wrapper). Targeted lint and diff checks pass.

Embedded tests cover typed rejection, zero requests/capture before revocation, and canonical capture/retry after commitment. Outer-run tests preserve coordination classification, one attempt, no auth-profile failure and safe retry text.
- Host-owned SQLite projection tests initially failed in the worker-thread CI lane. `13744a3` adds their single entry to the existing forked storage-state owner, beside projection/replay siblings; no assertions were changed or skipped. Thread-pool RED: 2 failed/2 passed, 76.56s. Correct owner: 4/4 pass, 91.83s. Registry suite: 12/12 pass, 2.47s.

Earlier focused repair128/128, prefix14/14 and multi-directory history/fallback-root35/35 results remain attributed to their pre-integration repairs.
- Canonical staged test-line check on the current repair: 6,608,663 lines / ceiling 6,608,663. The exact PR allocation is 2686; the shared scalar is unchanged. The redundant separate absolute-root worker case was consolidated into the existing profile table.

prs.title: fix(session): let replay admission cross mirrored command exchanges
prs.body:
Fixes #194303

## What Problem This Solves

A `/stop` sent while a queued follow-up turn was replaying could invalidate that turn: the stop's mirrored command exchange landed in the transcript between the follow-up's persisted user row and its replay admission, and admission refused the turn with "Persisted user turn changed before replay admission" — the queued message was persisted but never answered and nothing retried it. In plain terms: a stop command that arrived while a waiting message was starting should not make that waiting message fail; the stop is bookkeeping, not a new conversation turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replay admission walks the transcript back from the turn tail and only crosses entries that cannot start foreground work (context metadata, compaction, operational notices per #181473). Mirrored command exchanges (`command-input:` / `command-reply:` rows written by `recordDeliveredCommandExchange`) are operational history in the same sense — they never carry agent turn input — but the walk treated them as turn changes. This change lets the interrupted-turn walk cross them; the turn's identity is still pinned by the exact idempotency-key/user-row match, so a genuinely newer conversation user row still invalidates admission as before.

## User Impact

A queued follow-up survives a `/stop` that raced its admission and gets answered instead of failing with a generic error. The transcript still records the stop exchange; no cleanup or retry machinery changes.

## Evidence

- Regression (adapted from the issue's repro): `attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` (registered in `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` next to `attempt-session-replay.test.ts`). With the stop exchange appended after replay selection and before admission, the follow-up now makes 1 model call and answers ("FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED"); the persisted user turn is written once and the stop exchange once. Red check: reverting the walk change makes the same scenario fail with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission` and 0 model calls (6/6 pre-fix assertions green, post-fix 6/6 green).
- Controls unchanged: no interposed write and a Workshop notice interposed both still answer across both replay windows (selected reader on/off).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194303, adapt the issue's repro into a regression test, and extend the existing interrupted-turn walk predicate in pre-persisted-user-turn.ts. The implementer understands the code: command exchange rows are operational mirrors whose identity checks stay keyed to the exact idempotency match. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(agents): apply the authHeader override to simple completion models
prs.body:
fix(agents): apply the authHeader override to simple completion models

Closes #192866

## What Problem This Solves

Simple completions (utility-model helpers such as conversation labels) skipped the provider `authHeader: true` handling: helper calls went out with the SDK's default auth headers only, so a Bearer-only gateway rejected every helper call with 401 while agent turns on the same provider succeeded.

## User Impact

Utility-model helpers authenticate exactly like agent turns on `authHeader` providers. Conversation labels, session companions, and other helpers work against Bearer-only gateways instead of failing with repeated background 401s.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyAuthHeaderOverride` was only wired into the agent-turn dispatch and the compaction runtime; `prepareSimpleCompletionModel` stopped at the secret-ref sentinel pass. This change applies the same override (mirroring the compaction runtime's call shape) after the sentinel pass, so helper models carry the canonical `Authorization: Bearer` header on `authHeader` providers. Providers without the flag are untouched.

## Evidence

- Focused run on latest main content: src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts 20/20 passed, including the new case asserting the prepared helper model carries `Authorization: Bearer <key>` when the provider sets `authHeader: true` (mock for model-auth.js switched to a partial importOriginal passthrough so the real override runs).
- Red check: reverting only the production wrap fails exactly that case (1 failed | 19 passed); restoring passes.
- Adjacent simple-completion suites (selection, selected-model): 40/40 passed.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep and module tracing to analyze issue #192866, locate the missing override in src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.ts, and implement it mirroring the existing compaction-runtime call shape. The implementer understands the code: the sentinel pass alone leaves the SDK's default auth header in place, which Bearer-only gateways reject. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(worktrees): worktrees create prints only "The CLI command failed." when the source checkout path doesn't exist
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw worktrees create <repoRoot>` prints only "The CLI command failed. For help, run `openclaw doctor`." when `<repoRoot>` doesn't exist (for example a typo), and `--json` shows only the raw "ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath '<path>'".

## User Impact

User impact: the command now says "Source checkout not found: <path>. Pass the path to an existing git checkout." Exit code is unchanged, and nothing is created.

## Why This Change Was Made

`worktrees create` resolves the source path with `realpathSync.native` before admission, and the raw `ENOENT` reached the root failure renderer as an unexpected error. A missing path (`ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR`) is now reported with the existing `throwExpectedCliError` helper; other filesystem errors still propagate as before.

## Evidence

Current verification on `d8cbceafd1dd9fb8bc63712d739dc103795ce0bd` (2026-11-12): merged `main` at `9ca7932563ff3a8d2d3eca37e50d6ea7b031a527`, preserving its consolidated invalid-request cases and newer worktree diagnostics. The PR delta remains two files, +32/-1. Independent source review found no actionable issue in the resolution.

Original CLI before/after proof, unchanged production behavior: built from `main` at 67416fcc27 on Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath './my-repo'" } }
```

After:
```
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo
Source checkout not found: ./my-repo. Pass the path to an existing git checkout.
$ openclaw worktrees create ./my-repo --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "Source checkout not found: ./my-repo. Pass the path to an existing git checkout." } }
```
Both exit 1, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/worktrees-cli.test.ts src/cli/worktrees-cli.import-boundary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 passed on the resolved branch (20 CLI cases plus one import-boundary case). The CLI suite took 57.48 s, including 46.58 s of shared worker preparation; the boundary case took 102 ms.
- New test "names a missing source checkout instead of failing generically" runs the real `formatCliFailureLines` path and checks the service is never called. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- Current targeted type-aware lint, `oxfmt --check`, and PR-delta whitespace checks on both files: clean. Fresh CI applies to the pushed head; prior-head CI is not counted as current-head proof.

prs.title: fix(models): models scan prints only "fetch failed" when OpenRouter cannot be reached
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models scan` prints only `fetch failed` when the OpenRouter `/models` catalog request cannot connect (offline, DNS failure, refused proxy). The same bare text is the `--json` error message. Nothing says which request failed or why.

## User Impact

User impact: the command now prints, for example, `OpenRouter /models request failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9. Check your network connection and retry.` (or `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND openrouter.ai` offline). Exit code, `--json` envelope shape, timeouts, and HTTP-status errors (`OpenRouter /models failed: HTTP 503`) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node's `fetch` rejects network failures with a bare `TypeError("fetch failed")` and puts the real reason in `cause`. The CLI shows only `error.message` outside `--debug`, so the reason was lost. `fetchOpenRouterModels` now wraps a non-abort `fetch` rejection with the existing `formatErrorMessage` of its cause, keeping the original error as `cause`. Aborts from the scan timeout are rethrown unchanged.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at f24a3f03cd, Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory, with the network made unreachable by pointing `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` at a closed local port.

Before:
```
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe
fetch failed
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "fetch failed" } }
```

After:
```
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe
OpenRouter /models request failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9. Check your network connection and retry.
```
Exit 1 in both cases, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/agents/model-scan.test.ts src/agents/model-scan.probes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed.
- New test "names the network failure when the catalog request cannot connect" stubs `fetch` to reject like undici (`TypeError("fetch failed", { cause: ENOTFOUND })`). It fails on `main` (`got 'fetch failed'`) and passes with the fix.
- Test-line budget: 16 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/models-scan-network-failure.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged` passes.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

prs.title: fix(proxy): proxy run prints only "The CLI command failed." when the command cannot be started
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw proxy run -- COMMAND` prints only `The CLI command failed.` when the command cannot be started, for example a mistyped command name or a file that is not executable. The proxy starts and stops cleanly, but the user is not told that the child command never ran or why.

## User Impact

User impact: the CLI now says which command could not be started and why (`command not found` or `permission denied`) and still exits with status 1. A child that starts and then fails keeps its own exit code and output, and a successful run is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runDebugProxyRunCommand` already detects a child that failed during launch (no exit code and no signal) and throws the raw spawn error. The root renderer hides the reason of an unclassified error unless `--debug` is passed, so only the generic line was shown. Launch failures with `ENOENT` or `EACCES` are now raised as `ExpectedCliError` with a specific message, the same way #191295 handled `proxy run` without a command and `proxy blob` with an unknown id. The original spawn error is kept as the cause, other launch failures still throw as before, and the proxy server and capture session are still closed (the new test asserts the server stop).

## Evidence

From source on `main` at f5d0c194fc, Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw proxy run zz-nope --version
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
exit=1
$ openclaw proxy run /etc/hostname
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
exit=1
```

After:
```
$ openclaw proxy run zz-nope --version
proxy run could not start "zz-nope": command not found.
exit=1
$ openclaw proxy run /etc/hostname
proxy run could not start "/etc/hostname": permission denied.
exit=1
```

Unchanged controls with the fix:
```
$ openclaw proxy run -- sh -c "exit 3"
exit=3
$ openclaw proxy run -- echo ok
ok
exit=0
```

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/proxy-cli.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 27 passed.
- New cases "names the launch failure when the proxied command fails with ENOENT" and "... with EACCES" fail on `main` (the raw `Command failed with ENOENT` error is thrown) and pass with the fix.
- Test-line budget: 20 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/proxy-run-launch-failure.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged` passes.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean. `docs/cli/proxy.md` mentions the new reason next to the existing note from #191295.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw logs` prints the `Gateway target`, `Source` and `Config` lines twice when the Gateway cannot be reached, closes the connection, or times out.

## User Impact

User impact: the connection details are printed once, right under the reason. The `--json` error record, the exit code, the `Hint:` line, and errors that do not already carry the target (for example missing credentials) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway transport errors (unreachable, closed, timeout) already end with the connection details block, and the `logs` error path printed that block a second time after the error text. The text path now skips the extra block when the error text already contains it. Both strings go through the same URL redaction, and when they differ the block is still printed as before. `logs-cli.ts` is over the line cap, so the change replaces one line and the file does not grow.

prs.title: fix(gateway): credential remedy prints "--password ***" in place of a word when --url is used without credentials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the remedy line for a Gateway `--url` without credentials prints `***` where a word should be, for example `Fix: pass --token or --password *** --url`. It affects every Gateway-backed command (`cron list`, `logs`, `devices list`, `gateway call`), `gateway probe`, `sessions import` and `tui`.

## User Impact

User impact: the four remedy lines read as full sentences again. The exit codes, the JSON envelope shape and the rest of each message are unchanged. No secret handling changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Error and console output goes through the shared secret redaction, which treats the word after `--token` or `--password` as a secret value. Four remedies put an ordinary word there (`with`, `once`), so that word was masked. The remedies are reworded so the flag is followed by punctuation, and the redaction rules are not touched. This is the same approach as #191233. The process test for `devices list` already carried a note that redaction masks the word after `--password` and asserted around it; it now asserts the whole line. `call.ts` and `gateway-chat.ts` are over the line cap, so each call site changes in place.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at a764305e69, Linux, Node 24.22.2. `$STATE_DIR` is a fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw cron list --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: pass --token or --password *** --url (or gatewayToken in tools).
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
Config: $STATE_DIR/openclaw.json
exit=1
$ openclaw gateway probe --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: pass --token or --password *** --url.
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
exit=1
$ openclaw sessions import codex thread-1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
Failed codex/thread-1: No stored device auth for ws://127.0.0.1:9. Pass --token or --password ***, approve the pairing request in that gateway's Control UI (Settings > Devices), then retry.
0 imported; 0 updated; 0 unchanged; 1 failed.
exit=1
$ openclaw tui --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: pass --token or --password *** to request pairing, approve it in that gateway's Control UI (Settings -> Devices), then retry with the same credential so OpenClaw can store the device token.
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
exit=1
```

After:
```
$ openclaw cron list --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: pass --url together with --token or --password, or gatewayToken in tools.
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
Config: $STATE_DIR/openclaw.json
exit=1
$ openclaw gateway probe --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: pass --url together with --token or --password.
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
exit=1
$ openclaw sessions import codex thread-1 --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
Failed codex/thread-1: No stored device auth for ws://127.0.0.1:9. Run once with --token or --password, approve the pairing request in that gateway's Control UI (Settings > Devices), then retry.
0 imported; 0 updated; 0 unchanged; 1 failed.
exit=1
$ openclaw tui --url ws://127.0.0.1:9
gateway url override requires explicit credentials
Fix: to request pairing, run once with --token or --password, approve it in that gateway's Control UI (Settings -> Devices), then retry with the same credential so OpenClaw can store the device token.
For the default local or SSH-tunneled Gateway, remove --url to use the configured target.
exit=1
```

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/cli/session-ref.test.ts src/tui/gateway-chat.connection.test.ts src/commands/gateway-status.test.ts --maxWorkers=2`: 79 passed across the three files.
- Each remedy now has an assertion on the text after `formatErrorMessage`, which is where the masking happened. Those assertions fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `src/cli/gateway-backed-exit.process.test.ts`: the `devices list` URL-override case asserts the full remedy line from the real process stderr. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix. Three other cases in that file need a non-loopback private IPv4 address and could not run on my host, on `main` or on this branch.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the 8 files: clean.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the warning about passing a Gateway secret inline prints `Warning: --token *** be exposed via process listings.` The word `can` is replaced by `***`. It happens on `openclaw acp`, `openclaw mcp serve` and `openclaw gateway run` when `--token` or `--password` is given on the command line.

## User Impact

User impact: the warning reads `Warning: process listings can expose --token.` and keeps the same advice (`--token-file`, `--password-file`, or the environment). Nothing else about the commands changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Console output goes through the shared secret redaction, which treats the word after `--token` or `--password` as a secret value, so `can` was masked. The sentence now ends on the flag, and the redaction rules are not touched. The shared helper in `gateway-secret-options.ts` covers `acp` and `mcp serve`, and `gateway run` has its own copy of the sentence. The standalone `src/acp/server.ts` entry writes straight to stderr without redaction and already prints correctly, so it is left alone.

## Evidence

Current verification on `7e9a7fd0c92f8e8b81d3202a6a29bcf731dcd546` (2026-11-12):

- Repaired the diagnostic-export test fixture's logger lifecycle without changing production logging or sanitization. Earlier exports cache the log target; the namespaced-path fixture now resets the logger after installing its synthetic config, then resets it again in `finally`. There is no reset between the two exports, and all content/idempotence assertions remain intact.
- The failed CI shard was reproduced on untouched upstream base `5cef30a310125838abdbd3400a4db3dd334e8220`: 166 passed, one failed, 130.01 s. The sole failure was `gateway diagnostics export redacts namespaced paths in the ZIP across repeated exports`. Upstream #197742 (`5d6a026e43757ea6302e4c1151d6ace28468ced0`) introduced cached log-target resolution; this fixture did not invalidate its previous configuration. The warning patch did not cause it.
- That same baseline plus the fixture repair passes all 22 coverage tests (10.22 s). The PR head plus repair passes the coverage, ACP/Gateway option-collision and MCP suites: 155 passed, one existing skip, 109.20 s.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 issue and confirmed repeated-export coverage is preserved. The fixture file is identical on the old PR head and failing CI base, so no unrelated main refresh was needed.
- Fresh CI applies to this pushed head; the old failed run is retained as failure evidence, not relabeled passing.

Original CLI before/after evidence:

From source on `main` at a764305e69, Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory.

Before:
