prs.title: fix(ui): remember the session Details rail collapse preference
prs.body:
Closes #194649

## What Problem This Solves

The right-hand session Details rail re-opens itself on every page load and window refocus: its mount state starts at an "auto" intent that re-docks whenever the window is wide enough, and any presentation reset (gateway reconnect scope identity changes on refocus) resets a manually collapsed rail back to that auto state. A collapsed rail cannot be kept collapsed, and it overlaps the chat column on every focus return.

Plain language: you close the side panel, switch to another window and come back, and the panel has popped open again by itself. Now the panel remembers being closed and stays closed until you open it again.

## Why This Change Was Made

A manual open/close is a durable preference; presentation-driven resets are not. The rail now persists a device-local `chatDetailsCollapsed` preference (same UI settings store as other browser-local preferences) on manual open/close, and both re-open paths — the mount initializer and the presentation-reset clause — restore that preference instead of forcing "auto". When no preference exists yet, behavior is exactly as before (auto-dock). Programmatic closes (outside click, Escape handling unchanged) do not write the preference.

## User Impact

Collapsing the Details rail survives page reloads, tab switches, and gateway reconnects; opening it manually likewise persists. Fresh profiles keep the current auto-dock behavior, so the discovery path is unchanged.

## Evidence

Real runtime runs on the latest main tree this change is based on (files byte-compared as `main` + exactly this delta; dependencies installed fresh because main added `@solidjs/vite-plugin`):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `chat-details.browser.test.ts` new test (real browser, 1700×900 viewport where auto-dock would open): saved `chatDetailsCollapsed: true` → rail stays closed on mount AND after a gateway-scope presentation reset; manual open persists `false`; manual close persists `true` | green |
| Existing `chat-details.browser.test.ts` suite (auto-dock, revisions, mobile, Escape focus) | 20/20 green |
| `settings.chat-details.test.ts` new jsdom test: preference round-trips through `saveSettings`/`loadSettings` including unset | green |
| `chat-pane-header-details.test.tsx` (jsdom) | green |
| Red check: reverting the component wiring (initializer restore + manual persistence) makes exactly the new browser test fail | confirmed |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.ui.json`: zero errors in changed files | verified |

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used grep to trace the Details rail state machine (`chat-details.tsx` choice/intent signal), identify the two force-open paths, and implement the preference wiring. The implementer understands the code: the "auto" intent plus presentation resets are the only re-open sources, so restoring a saved preference in both spots is sufficient. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(browser): stop sending credentialed CDP wsUrl to the model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #158966.

With a loopback CDP profile whose `cdpUrl` carries HTTP Basic credentials or a query token (as used by Browserless/Browserbase-style endpoints), `browser action=tabs` and `browser action=open` hand the model a fully usable, credentialed `wsUrl`. Every tool action addresses tabs by `targetId`, so the model never needs the connectable socket URL, and its credentials leak into model-facing (and page-adjacent untrusted-content-wrapped) output.

This carries forward the unresolved problem from #137756, whose implementation PR was retired at the author's request without the underlying defect being fixed. Independent code reading against current `main` confirms the same root cause the retired PR identified, at the same two call sites (line numbers shifted slightly since that PR's base commit, behavior identical).

## Root cause

- `formatAgentTab` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts`) explicitly copies `source.wsUrl` onto the agent-visible tab it builds for `action=tabs`.
- `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` (`extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts`) is documented as removing internal metadata before model output for `action=open`, but only stripped `ownership`/`resolvedProfile`, leaving `wsUrl` and its paired `wsLookup` intact.
- `normalizeCdpWsUrl` (`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.ts`) deliberately propagates the configured endpoint's credentials onto the per-tab socket URL — that part is correct, it's needed for the runtime's own connection. The defect is only that the derived value then reaches the two model-facing formatting paths above.
- The declared output contract (`BrowserToolOutputSchema` in `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.ts`) does not include `wsUrl` at all, and `client.types.ts` already documents `wsLookup` as "omitted from model-facing summaries" — `wsUrl` was never supposed to survive to model output either.

## Fix

Stop copying `wsUrl` in `formatAgentTab`, and strip both `wsUrl` and `wsLookup` in `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`, matching the class of internal CDP connection metadata that already gets removed for other fields (`ownership`, `resolvedProfile`) and already gets redacted elsewhere in the codebase (`chrome.diagnostics.ts` calls `redactCdpUrl` before diagnostics output).

No other call site reads `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` back off a tool result — every consumer (screenshot capture, snapshot, page sessions) reads `tab.wsUrl` internally before the tool formats its result — so removing it from the two output paths changes nothing else.

## Evidence

New regression test `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts` drives the real, unmocked `executeTabsAction` and `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata` production functions with a synthetic credentialed CDP URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`, then asserts the credential and the `wsUrl`/`wsLookup` keys are absent from the serialized model-facing result.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix — reverted the two source files to `HEAD~1` (pre-fix) and reran:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
   → expected '{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"\n…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: ...\"wsUrl\": \"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=22>\"...

 × browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
   → expected '{"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox",…' not to contain 's3cr3t-pass'
   Received: {"targetId":"AAA111","title":"Inbox","url":"https://mail.example.com","type":"page","wsUrl":"wss://admin:s3cr3t-pass@chrome.example.net/devtools/page/AAA111?token=<redacted len=24>...

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed (2)
```

Restored the fix and reran — both pass, plus the full existing browser-tool suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=tabs model output
 ✓ browser tool tab output redaction > omits the CDP wsUrl from action=open model output
 ...
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  277 passed (277)
```

Lint, typecheck and format on the changed files:

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions.tsbuildinfo
(clean)

$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
(clean)

$ npx oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.actions.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool-session-tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.wsurl.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.
```

## What was not tested

No real Chrome/CDP proxy end-to-end run — this fix and its test operate at the same production-function boundary (`executeTabsAction`, `stripBrowserOpenInternalMetadata`) as the issue's own real-behavior proof, using a synthetic credentialed URL built through the real `normalizeCdpWsUrl`. The retired PR #137756 previously ran a full real-Chrome/authenticating-proxy round trip proving the same before/after behavior; that evidence is preserved in its history for reference.

prs.title: fix(codex): shed abandoned cleared bindings at namespace capacity
prs.body:
Related: #125910.

## What Problem This Solves

The Codex app-server thread-binding namespace rejects new bindings after 50,000 rows accumulate, leaving later requests unavailable until the state database is cleaned manually.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier revisions of this PR moved the namespace to evict-oldest, which let the SQLite store delete binding rows it cannot read: retirement fences, legacy-clear provenance, live leases, and active sessions all ranked the same as garbage. This revision keeps reject-new everywhere and puts capacity recovery at the binding domain boundary.

`session-binding-overflow.ts` wraps the composed binding store's `mutate` and `withLease`, the insert and lease-admission paths. When an insert fails with a row-count limit error, the wrapper pages the worker-backed handle on the same namespace with `entriesInKeyRange` (512-row pages, storage-side ordering, decode in the storage worker) and sheds up to a few strictly validated disposable rows per failure through `observe` + `compareAndApply`, then retries. A lexical cursor persists across calls and wraps at the end of the namespace, so spaced failures keep advancing instead of re-reading the same protected prefix, and rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered. Destructive eligibility is decided on the raw record, not the tolerant codec: a lease in any malformed shape, a retirement marker in any shape at all, and any non-object row are preserved as ambiguous. Everything else (active bindings, retirement fences, live leases, `conversation:legacy-` provenance) fails closed with the original limit error. Recovery is gated on the current host's required capabilities; a host that lacks them cannot run the sweep and keeps reject-new behavior.

The sync store stays exactly where it was: hot reads. Listing and deletion during recovery run on the worker side of the store broker, so a full namespace never turns into a whole-table decode on the Gateway thread.

Sidecar migration keeps its main-branch reject-new store: at capacity the existing failure path retains the source, and no live row can be displaced by an import.

## User Impact

A namespace clogged with abandoned cleared rows recovers on its own instead of hard-failing every new session. Fences, leases, legacy-clear provenance, live bindings, and every ambiguous existing record are never shed; when nothing strictly disposable exists the limit error surfaces unchanged.

## Evidence

- `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` (16 tests; runs in the database-workers shard on the forks pool for the broker): recovery sheds an abandoned cleared row while an older live binding survives; fail-closed when the namespace holds only a retirement fence plus a live binding; a live lease is never shed; legacy-clear provenance survives recovery while an abandoned row next to it is shed; a cleared row with a non-object lease is preserved while a strictly valid abandoned row next to it is shed; a namespace of only ambiguous rows rejects with both rows intact; a host without ranged listing propagates the limit error with no inline scan; recovery through `createLazyCodexAppServerBindingStore(state, undefined, recoveryState)`, the exact production composition; a scan stalls mid-prefix under a one-page budget and the next insert resumes from the persisted cursor and succeeds (goes red when cursor persistence is broken); rows whose leases lapse after a fully protected pass are reconsidered.
- `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` (new): the real extension entry boots and builds the binding store plus the lazy recovery adapter from `api.runtime.state` itself; the openers delegate to the plugin-state test factories (same worker-backed SQLite stores, fixture module resolution; production additionally needs the Gateway host broker no in-process test has), with the binding namespace cap clamped 50,000 -> 3 as the only knob. Through that registered assembly: a fresh session's lease admission overflows, recovers, starts exactly once, and sheds exactly the disposable cleared row while the live binding and a held row survive; a caller whose authority is revoked at admission gets zero deletes with the disposable row intact; and a real `resolveCodexSessionBinding` authority whose `previousSessionId` changes between observe and `compareAndApply(delete)` is rejected at final worker admission with one delete attempt and the disposable row preserved.
- Real run, isolated state dir, production plugin-state store plus the production lazy composition over real SQLite at capacity (3/3: retired fence, live-leased cleared row, abandoned cleared row): the insert recovers, only the abandoned row is shed, both protected rows survive, and a fresh store handle on the same database still shows fence + lease + the new binding afterwards. Verbatim output is in the review reply below.
- `doctor-contract-api.overflow.test.ts`: at capacity the sidecar source is retained, nothing is imported, and the pre-existing row is intact (limit error injected through the production registration path); a revisited legacy sidecar cannot resurrect its cleared thread because the canonical cleared marker wins and the source archives without its row.
- Sibling Codex checkout inspection (`../codex`, origin/main 286d4ecf44): threads persist durably as rollout files plus the state db with paged listing and no retention eviction (`codex-rs/rollout/src/state_db.rs:352`, `codex-rs/rollout/src/maintenance.rs`), so shedding an abandoned OpenClaw binding row can never delete native Codex data.
- Before the final test-lint and format-only follow-ups, the full `extensions/codex` suite, `check-changed` lanes, and fresh `$autoreview` were clean with no actionable findings.
- At prior head `e721d349d2b6c9dca567e240c681829378c8fc45`, the registered-path test lint findings and the two overflow files' formatting were addressed without changing recovery behavior. PR CI at that head was green, including `check-test-types`. The xAI type failure seen at `f8d62fcb212d7adb73e5a51f89a3be618be7623f` was fixed upstream by #177830, and this PR does not change xAI.
- At current head `58efcd3c65f944499b2ff7454f05787e4ecadccc`, the final-delete negative control now starts revocation only after the unbound observation completes, limits rejection to caller-bound stores, and asserts exactly one `compareAndApply(delete)` attempt before rejection while preserving the disposable row. The strengthened assertion failed with zero attempts before the timing correction and passes with one after it. The low-value source-snippet inventory was removed; the registered production-path behavior test remains.
- Current head `acd84820f892ff2517adc6853e19cf6a9bb192e7`: `session-binding-overflow.test.ts` passed 16/16 and `session-binding-overflow.registered-path.test.ts` passed 2/2 through `node scripts/test-projects.mts`; oxlint passed on the changed test file. `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passes after merging current `upstream/main`, and `test/scripts/pr-dependency-cache.test.ts` passes 41/41 locally, resolving the darwin workflow/source mismatch seen before that merge. Full extension-test typecheck passed with the already-landed #177830 xAI baseline fix temporarily overlaid and then restored. Without that overlay, the local branch reports only the known xAI baseline error, not an error in this PR's changed files.

Remaining evidence gaps: this head strengthens the final-delete negative control but does not supply a shipped Gateway fresh-session recovery trace with real session reset/reassignment lineage, a latest-stable upgrade run, or the maintainer's retention-policy decision. Those gates remain open and are not represented as complete here.

## What this PR is not

This is a partial fix with one open policy decision and no claim to close the underlying issue's storage architecture. Shedding strictly validated abandoned cleared rows is a durable-retention change, and it needs an explicit maintainer decision before merge; the review thread carries the full inventory. The store-level eviction primitive (storage-side disposal by policy rather than a domain-side sweep) remains the owner's call, as does any broader migration of the sync binding reads onto the async handle.

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- Current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, including upstream main `3f2e7078de23`: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.usage.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.transcript-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 4 files and 50 tests. oxfmt and direct type-aware oxlint pass on the consolidated test; the net PR diff passes `git diff --check`.
- Shipped diagnostic builder proof on `591ef68b2e9`: the real settled Gateway compaction events drive the production `buildReplyDiagnosticsPayload` raw diagnostic path through `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptAsync`, not just a direct reader call. With usage fields removed, the boundary-terminal artifact emits `total=139` and the full artifact emits `total=176`. The measured control emits `input=105`, `output=25`, `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=0`, `total=120`. The probe prints only the session usage block, with no transcript text, credentials or endpoints. This builder-level evidence does not satisfy Revision 17's separate shipped CLI/Gateway diagnostic request gate; that proof requirement remains open.
- Test budget: the four repeated retained-window fixtures now share one table helper, preserving all 10 scenarios while reducing the new test file from 157 to 145 lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-usage-active-window.txt` grants exactly those 145 added lines. The full-index ratchet on current head `dcfc49a70dfb`, using hosted CI's current main `3f2e7078de23` with `--no-merge-base`, reports `Test lines OK: 6561328; ceiling: 6561328; slack: 0.` An earlier sparse local run omitted 566 tracked test lines and produced a false slack result; materializing those files reproduced hosted CI's over-10 failure before this consolidation.

prs.title: fix(agents): omit message when no supported route exists
prs.body:
Related: #169091

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents are offered `message` when their session/runtime has neither a supported source route nor configured outbound messaging capability.

## User Impact

Agents without routes stop receiving an unusable tool. Supported source replies/reactions and configured outbound-only or offline channels remain available. Source-only target/action restrictions still apply at execution. Configuring a channel restores availability through the existing refresh lifecycle. No new public configuration, permission rule, or database schema is introduced; existing WebChat sessions record prompt support on their next operator declaration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery uses existing session metadata and channel configuration owners, not transport health or default schema actions. Omission follows final policy/schema filtering and child/cron capture, so presentation does not become an inherited permission denial. All registered configured senders participate in the absence check; binding-based schema pruning is not an outbound allowlist. Modern text senders and pending synchronous configuration remain supported; payload-only adapters rejected by delivery are not advertised.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `0f4973e22dc005d67c0b860d26c3bafae54d8ada`, tree `03cde946b665d63f56ce2734c670073c381cb34f`, exactly matches tested/reviewed local `4889a7ce90f0b23664bc312c3993f08198b41174`. Original published history and pinned main `b48d16bf6e98f0b9c1e110548fc46b3b35f2becd` are preserved. The PR is open and **unmerged**. No merge or deployment is authorized.

### Codex regression check requested by Vincent

**Passed with real pinned Codex 0.164.0 and an isolated built Gateway**, after the normal private-QA prerequisite build on exact local `4889a7ce…`. Build, runtime-postbuild and build-info stamps all match that commit; the published tree is identical.

- Three actual native turns: `automatic`, `message_tool_only`, then omitted/default. Each turn's **first provider request** includes flat, direct, nondeferred `message`.
- The same native session/cache identity, static instructions/tool definitions, prior history and per-turn source-delivery policy assertions pass. Each turn produces **exactly one actual synthetic channel-bus outbound receipt**.
- This uses the real app-server binary and Gateway against a deterministic loopback provider—not a fake app-server, paid inference or real external send. Provider-body assertions are parsed structural wire evidence, not raw HTTP byte-count or cache-efficiency measurements.
- Consumer qualification found 11 route-less positive-fixture failures on the previous candidate versus 81/81 on main. Eleven positives now declare a real supported WebChat source through awaited existing public SDK metadata writers, with matching session ID/store path; no availability/authority mock was added. Two new direct/searchable route-less cases are red on main and green on the fix.
- Final integration: **148 tests across five selected files passed**, covering Codex construction/Gateway policy, real-adapter availability, registration and prefix stability. Three unchanged bridge/source-reply/availability siblings previously passed 48/48; core message tests passed 98/98. Core types, scoped typed lint, format, six-file snapshot check and diff check passed.

The real main conflict affected two generated Codex prompt snapshots. Both were regenerated canonically; main's newer schemas and this PR's message contract coexist. A real line-cap refusal was repaired by moving the unchanged embedded-message inclusion gate/allowlist into the **existing registration owner**, not by packing formatting or raising a cap. Final line-cap check passes across 35 changed source files. Exact regression allocation is **523 LF**, covering the task's +523 LF against pinned main; the current test-line ratchet **passes** (allowance 400, allocation credit 523). Shared baseline is unchanged. The earlier 27-line deficit belongs to historical main `3b13df…`; it is not relabeled green or waived by this PR.

### Retained paired built-product qualification

These are **historical matched measurements**, BASE `3b13df5767c256222e8cd4ed8fea17c6b836b2aa` versus FIX `5eef5c184ff36339a551c2b48abd7c447cc66bcb`, not fresh whole-body measurements for the newer main integration. All **19 strict paired rows** passed using original raw UTF-8 provider HTTP bodies, complete inventories, authority negatives and synthetic adapter receipts:

| First request | Raw bytes BASE → FIX | System bytes | Tools bytes | Direct/catalog/deferred BASE → FIX |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| No route | 34,991 → 30,556 | 24,644 → 23,945 | 9,848 → 6,112 | 5/57/56 → 4/56/56 |
| Internal WebChat | 37,364 → unchanged | 26,724 → unchanged | 10,141 → unchanged | 5/57/56 unchanged |
| External delivery + WebChat | 35,518 → unchanged | 25,194 → unchanged | 9,825 → unchanged | 5/57/56 unchanged |
| Configured outbound, no inbound | 34,184 → 33,243 | 23,837 → 23,844 | 9,848 → 8,900 | 5/43/42 unchanged |

No-route removes exactly `message` from direct/catalog and 4,435 bytes from this fixture's initial request. Deferred names are unchanged. Supported-source definitions/logical system prefixes stay identical through normal → source-only → normal, internal wake and process reentry. Configured sending retains one synthetic adapter receipt per edition; phantom local reaction advertising disappears. Wrong-target send/reaction remain execution-policy denials; broadcast remains a schema denial. Later-stage accumulated transcript differences are not fresh-turn savings. No timing, token, billing or cache-efficiency claim.

Other retained proof: full earlier integration build, 112 focused tests/seven files, two selected wrapper-closure checks (21 unrelated cases skipped), and scoped released-state upgrade. Actual `2026.11.3` / `847611d` created the isolated session/receipt; Doctor migrated schema 27 → 41. Integrated CLI and public SDK reentry retained released history, external delivery, `inline-widgets` and declared `webchat-prompt-reactions`. Doctor's fixture-plugin warning remains a limitation: **targeted core-state compatibility, not full plugin/service/native/live-Gateway upgrade certification**. The repaired source-delivery fixture's six cases passed prior-head CI; that is retained evidence, not new-head CI.

### Review and current CI

Fresh independent **P0–P3 clean** reviews cover the seven-file Codex follow-up and final main integration/registration-owner transfer. The completed [hosted Codex review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197553#issuecomment-6815833811) covers production at `8dbb4a17…`: patch correct, no blocking code defect; its one P3 reproduction-documentation finding is fixed. Earlier full-candidate autoreview and independent repair reviews are retained, not relabeled as a hosted review of this new head. No duplicate hosted run requested. Final discussion/review reads found no new comments since 12:40 UTC and no submitted formal reviews.

**Exact-head CI assessment is terminal: build passed; CI failed.** [Build-artifact run 43220034371](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034371) completed successfully (one successful build, one skipped admission job). [CI run 43220034539](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539) completed with **116/116 jobs terminal: 86 successful, 24 skipped, six failed**. Those failures are the five leaf jobs below plus the [aggregate CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131204807394), not a sixth independent defect. No jobs remain pending. Both runs cover `0f4973e22dc005d67c0b860d26c3bafae54d8ada`, attempt 1. This is **not green CI or a cleared-to-land claim**.

| Current-head failure | Bounded investigation | Attribution / remaining uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex whole-skill delivery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131189870251): oversized skill read returns success | Same file under official Node 24.22.1 fails 1/3 on the candidate and 1/3 on an isolated exact pinned-main `b48d16bf…` source installation, at the same assertion | Reproduced on pinned main; not introduced by this PR. Distinct from the passing native message-delivery proof |
| [Native hook approval relay](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131189870033): replacement pending approval test times out at 120 seconds | Candidate full file: 96 pass, same one timeout. Exact pinned main named-case replay: same 120-second timeout; 96 deliberately unselected | Reproduced on pinned main; not introduced by this PR. No timeout increase or approval-policy change |
| [Local-checkout publication fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131189870197): expected published, received push_rejected | Candidate full file passes 23/23 under Node 24.22.1 | Unattributed CI-only failure; passing replay is not a repair or main attribution |
| [Plugin lifecycle](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131189870206): expected applied, received deferred pending retained work | Candidate full file passes 3/3 under Node 24.22.1 | Unattributed CI-only failure; original shard/concurrency profile not reproduced |
| [Docker seed preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43220034539/job/131189866878): packing acorn@8.19.0 fails during Codex package preparation | Full completed job log inspected; failure precedes Docker scenarios. Packing owner and dependency manifests are unchanged from pinned main | Unattributed; npm diagnostic is only referenced in the runner-local debug log. Classifier's job-name-only pre-existing label is insufficient evidence |

The repository's exact-run classifier reports the four test jobs unknown because it has no matching main job. The two explicit paired reproductions above provide narrower main attribution; unchanged files alone do not. Main comparison setup failures were corrected only in the disposable installation before tests ran and are not counted as product results. No source changes were made during this CI investigation. The complete run artifact inventory contains only startup-memory and SDK declarations, not the failing worker/npm diagnostics. **Remaining qualification blocker:** failure-time shard/runtime evidence for publication and plugin lifecycle, and the npm debug log for Docker preparation, are needed to identify a safe causal repair or establish main attribution. No green-CI, repaired-failure or full qualification claim is made. The polling continuation ends with this terminal assessment; unfinished source and recovery proof are retained.

Two failed groups on **prior head `5e67cd43…`** remain explicitly unattributed, not silently dismissed or fixed by passing replays:

| Prior-head failure | Bounded investigation | Remaining uncertainty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Deep Research recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43177319618/job/131045382169): provider reload abort / portable-documents stack overflow | Four-file selection passed 81/81 on FIX and 81/81 on exact main, pinned Bun; named Node 24.22.1 parity cases passed | No proven owning repair or main attribution for the original CI shard |
| [Updater split-root fixture](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43177319618/job/131045381812): missing installed version / invalid dist inventory | File 12/12, observed twenty-file selection 360/360; additional official Node 24.22.1 + pinned CI Bun with `CI=true` and `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` passed the named case | Passing replay is not a fix; another PR's main reproduction is only a lead until applicable source/profile equivalence is verified |

No rerun-for-green, weaker assertion, timeout increase, CI exception, speculative production repair or live service change was used.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, provenance and retained artifact identities</summary>

The maintained workload self-spawns from its entry. Run it **inside the disposable staged installation** so bundled-plugin discovery cannot borrow the source checkout's package root. Earlier external-entry nonconfigured captures were rejected after an unrelated Google Meet mismatch; causal controls established ambient root contamination, not a production bug. They were superseded, never normalized or counted as savings. Both editions use identical physical installation/state paths and fresh state/output. Correctly rooted configured CLI evidence was retained.

```bash
cp scripts/perf/message-tool-availability.mjs "$INSTALL/message-tool-availability.mjs"
sha256sum scripts/perf/message-tool-availability.mjs "$INSTALL/message-tool-availability.mjs"
node "$INSTALL/message-tool-availability.mjs" --build "$INSTALL" --state "$FRESH_STATE" --out "$FRESH_OUTPUT" --route none
```

Repeat with `internal`, `external-webchat`, `configured`; never overlay editions or reuse populated state/output. Script SHA256: `d75b30dd4c59edf1292c9a31b4d0b6e7aba9e19fb67682185ea492f3d6c71255`. Configured `--unbound-sender` separately proves disabled bound Telegram plus configured unbound Signal through an actual synthetic receipt.

Artifacts retained in the implementation session:
- Corrected paired report SHA256 `261e9448aab2909ed53de199aa953cdf6d0b15263d6be116b6f1f0ee10cc79fb`; strict comparison `750a51c6528379946700d1d2b3d1dfc9373ef689bab0537bd9e43d3df231eab6`. Parent independently reran the strict raw-buffer comparator with exact equality; 76 original bodies and complete inventories/actions/hashes are retained.
- Seven-file Codex follow-up patch `90d682f37c76e57b0bc13679ce82e8175dc56ee0b49bb8f27a665f08361bbcc1`; clean review report `0ebdf01d18e22410729fa339abbfe6adaa272d789233a4ab41d7d8ced03fe92d`.
- Final integration clean review report `9c95156bac2e3b338ed1fcf7fd72fa3595a3ef515969a70ac7f652f693665850`.
- Exact integration native Gateway/Codex proof log `3c084c4e60df4a2dcf5d0517dac5931ca78a95ff97acf7e63231ae445b390474`; all three build stamps match `4889a7ce…`. The earlier pre-integration native proof also passed and is retained separately.

Historical raw-body runner/CLI proof and current native Gateway proof use deterministic loopback providers/synthetic adapters. Neither certifies real-model compliance or real external channel delivery. State recovery is isolated process reentry, not an operator Gateway restart. No paid inference, credentials or private conversation contents are published.

</details>

prs.title: fix(sessions): restore dependency checks for pending-input reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Main's dependency gate still rejects `readPendingInputSource`, which became an unused export in #184512 (`baca36ea403cf681b9ec531c5f27837d0586dcad`). Exact parent `74999886c2f98ecaa9c205b220f79bcd5e862371` fails the production scan on that one export. Its production caller is already in the same module; only tests import the raw reader.

## User Impact

Restore dependency checks without changing submitted-input reads, replay decisions, or invitation authority. The reader implementation and maintained `readSessionSubmittedInput` API remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make the raw reader private and migrate every test consumer. Four Gateway consumers retain their exact stored-row comparisons through a shared test helper that uses existing store reads and releases the store in `finally`. Memory tests use the maintained submitted-input API and retain explicit current-window checks.

#184513 merged a real invitation-binder consumer while the earlier revision's CI ran. The final premerge source check caught that change, and the earlier revision was held as a draft. This revision integrates that named owner change and preserves all invitation machinery and retention tests exactly as they appear on the pinned parent. No invitation deletion or new invitation test remains in this PR.

Open #184515 still imports the raw reader in a test; that branch should migrate its test to the maintained reader or the shared test snapshot helper when integrated. Its production invitation feature remains outside this repair.

The final seven-file change has production LOC delta 0 and test/support delta +20. The 23-line test helper serves four existing consumers. No schema, configuration, protocol, or permission change is intended.

## Evidence

- Literal pristine parent `74999886c2f98ecaa9c205b220f79bcd5e862371`: production Knip fails with exactly one unused export, `readPendingInputSource` (59.18 seconds wall; 54.52 seconds user; 32.29 seconds system; 2.95 GB peak RSS). Scanner cost is not a runtime performance benchmark.
- Fresh independent Codex review of the final seven-file delta: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Fresh current-base UI proof: eight pending-composer browser cases pass in 3.22 seconds; both selected pending-send handoff E2E variants pass in 27.24 seconds.
- Fresh current-base consumer proof: 36 Gateway custody/read-scope/retry cases and 10 memory/source cases pass (360.29 seconds including worker compilation); all seven collected-input replay variants pass (30.95 seconds). No assertions or deadlines are loosened.
- Canonical `pnpm check:changed --base 74999886c2f98ecaa9c205b220f79bcd5e862371` passes on the reviewed merge head, including all core/test type graphs and production/full-tree/script export scans with zero entries. The earlier staged-merge attempt resolved the old parent and was stopped; this completed run records the correct parent and seven-file scope.
- Fresh exact-head CI and hosted review are required for this revision. The earlier `fc3ff91a` CI/review results are historical and do not qualify this head.

prs.title: fix(session-events): retry exec completion wakes refused by an unavailable session lease
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a background `exec` completion wake that is refused with `SESSION_DELIVERY_GENERATION_UNAVAILABLE` before it starts is cancelled for good. Its producer never retries, so the agent never hears that the command finished. #177063 closed the turn-end settings window. Any other moment where the wake's session lease turns unavailable still loses it. One live trigger: the command finishes while the agent is still mid-turn, so its wake waits in the queue, and meanwhile something publishes a sessions-wide change, such as renaming a sidebar session group. That change invalidates every prepared lease, so the wake is refused once the turn ends (live run in Evidence).

Related: #185085 (this fixes `main`; the issue also asks for a stable backport)

## User Impact

User impact: completion wakes survive a transient session-storage refusal. The agent resumes after a background command finishes instead of going silent until the user sends another message. Revoked or rotated sessions, Stop and abandonment still end the wake as before. The Control UI also stops showing the misleading "source execution authority is no longer active" failure, which came from a fallback model that could never succeed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-event handoff already re-admits an unstarted occurrence once a config publication rejects it (bounded at two attempts, with a fresh lease). This PR gives a lease refusal of the "unavailable" kind the same treatment. A refusal of the "revoked" kind (the session was replaced) stays terminal. Model fallback now stops on both session delivery generation errors, because switching models cannot restore session storage authority. This is the design the issue's automated review endorsed: bounded pre-execution readmission plus a fallback stop.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

**Cause** (at `7ef5469ac3c`, current `main`):

- `enqueueSessionEventAttempt` (`src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-handoff.ts`) re-admits only when `configPolicy.changed`. Any other pre-start failure ends in `ownership.cancel()`, and the exec producer (`maybeNotifyOnExit`) only logs a warning.
- The wake's generation lease refuses with `SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError` on many branches (`session-delivery-generation.ts`; #196724 added diagnostics to find which ones fire in the field). One reproducible branch: a runtime-wide `sessionChanges` publication sets `invalidated` on every prepared lease, so the wake's next `assertCurrent` refuses even though the session row never changed.
- When the refusal surfaces during primary model preparation, `prepareAgentRunAdmission` latches it as "source execution authority is no longer active". `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES` (`src/agents/failover-error.ts`) does not list the generation errors, so `runWithModelFallback` runs the next candidate, which fails on the latched error. That is the message users see.

**Change:**

- `classifySessionDeliveryGenerationRefusal` walks an error's cause chain and returns `"unavailable"`, `"revoked"` (which wins) or nothing.
- New sibling `session-event-readmission.ts` holds the readmission policy. The attempt bound (`MAX_READMISSION_ATTEMPTS`, still 2) and the 100/200 ms backoff move there unchanged, which keeps the handoff within its line-cap ratchet.
- Only an error that ended this attempt counts: the terminal failure, the failed operation's cause, or the rejection of `onAdopted` itself.
  - `onAdopted` runs through `readmission.adopt()`. A rejected adoption otherwise surfaces only as abandonment, which keeps no error. That covers lease refusals from `prepareRead`, a compaction rebind or the final `assertCurrent` during adoption. The body is unchanged, only re-indented (the diff reads best with whitespace hidden).
  - The lease's current state is deliberately not consulted. Stop clears queued work through the same abandonment, and a waiting wake's lease may already be invalidated by unrelated writes. Inferring the cause from the lease would revive a stopped wake.
- An unstarted, undelivered, non-aborted, non-abandoned occurrence whose ending error is an `"unavailable"` refusal reuses the existing bounded readmission. `onAbandoned` treats that rejection like a stale-policy one. Revocation is never retried, and the re-admitted attempt still checks the original captured target.
- `SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError` and `SessionDeliveryGenerationRevokedError` join `RUNTIME_COORDINATION_ERROR_NAMES`.

**Regression tests:**

- `session-event-config-readmission.test.ts` runs a real exec-source wake against a real session row, with only the model decision mocked, as the rest of that file does. A real runtime-wide session change retires the wake's prepared lease at two points:
  - `queued`: the command finished while the agent was mid-turn, so the wake waits behind that turn. The base fails it with `SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError`.
  - `adopting`: the change lands at adoption, just before model start. The base cancels the wake ("Session event was abandoned before execution").
  - With the fix, both are re-admitted once and complete their real tool write.
  - Control, `stopped`: as `queued`, but Stop clears the queue (`clearSessionQueues`) after the lease is invalidated. The wake never runs, before and after the fix.
  - Control, `rotated`: the session's lifecycle is replaced at adoption. The wake fails closed and never reaches the model, before and after the fix.
- `model-fallback.terminal-boundary.test.ts` adds the latched wrapper around an unavailable refusal and a bare revoked refusal to the "does not replay" table.
- `session-event-readmission.test.ts` unit-tests the policy: errorless abandonment stays terminal, a refusal wrapped by latched source authority counts, `adopt()` records its rejection's cause, and revocation wins over a later unavailable refusal.

**Review:** local autoreview and a second review by Gemini 4 Carbon (details in Evidence).

</details>

## Evidence

- **Live, before and after:** a throwaway Gateway with the claude-cli runtime and a real model (`claude-haiku-5-5`), no fallback models. The same script ran on each build. One agent turn starts a background `exec` (`sleep 5; echo BG-DONE`), then holds the turn with a 45 s foreground `exec`, so the completion wake waits in the session queue. 35 s in, the script renames a session group created before the turn (`openclaw gateway call sessions.groups.rename`, the Control UI's rename). The control run skips the rename. Verdict: `openclaw sessions tail` shows a second `prompt.submitted` when the wake ran.
  - **Base `7ef5469ac3c`** (packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts`): the wake is lost. The session has only the one turn. When the turn ends, the lease refuses on #196724's `active-invalidated` branch, and the exec producer gives up:
    ```
    18:43:41Z prompt.submitted agent:main:wake-trigger-124334   (the turn)
    18:44:33Z session.ended    agent:main:wake-trigger-124334 success
    {"event":"lease-unavailable-first-refusal","branch":"active-invalidated","state":{"active":true,"invalidated":true,"revoked":false},"flip":{"kind":"row-invalidated","captured":true,"frames":["dist/listeners-B2PFtJVV.mjs:5:3","dist/session-row-changes-D3sFetzF.mjs:120:23","dist/session-row-changes-D3sFetzF.mjs:126:4","dist/sqlite-post-commit-byt81Oml.mjs:22:7"],"async":false},…}
    [session-events] session event execution failed source=exec agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:wake-trigger-124334 eventId=c01f40e0-… error="SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError: Session delivery generation is unavailable; retry after session storage is ready."
    [exec] completion delivery failed (SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError: …); inspect the process result.
    ```
  - **2026.11.5-beta.2** (newest prerelease, includes #177063): the same two failure lines; it predates the diagnostic.
  - **This PR at `dc48c07e7c2`**, packed the same way: the same refusal fires on the same branch, and the wake is re-admitted. The session gets its second turn 3 s after the first ends, that turn completes, and no failure lines appear:
    ```
    18:12:39Z prompt.submitted agent:main:wake-trigger-121229   (the turn)
    18:13:32Z session.ended    agent:main:wake-trigger-121229 success
    {"event":"lease-unavailable-first-refusal","branch":"active-invalidated","state":{"active":true,"invalidated":true,"revoked":false},"flip":{"kind":"row-invalidated","captured":true,"frames":["dist/listeners-B2PFtJVV.mjs:5:3","dist/session-row-changes-D3sFetzF.mjs:120:23","dist/session-row-changes-D3sFetzF.mjs:126:4","dist/sqlite-post-commit-byt81Oml.mjs:22:7"],"async":false},…}
    18:13:35Z prompt.submitted agent:main:wake-trigger-121229   (the re-admitted wake)
    18:13:38Z session.ended    agent:main:wake-trigger-121229 success
    ```
  - **Control, no rename:** the wake runs on every build (second `prompt.submitted` 0 s after the turn ends), with no refusal or diagnostic.
  - Not exercised live: the model fallback stop. This trigger refuses at adoption, before model selection; the fallback rows below cover that half.
- **Regression, red then green** (at `b5468c6b8c5`, before rebasing; `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-config-readmission.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.terminal-boundary.test.ts`, the new cases):
  - With the production files reset to `5203424051f`: `queued` fails with `SessionDeliveryGenerationUnavailableError`, `adopting` with `Session event was abandoned before execution`, and both fallback rows with `unexpected provider policy consult…` (the fallback candidate ran). The `stopped` and `rotated` controls pass.
  - With the fix: all 4 scenarios and both fallback rows pass.
- **Stop guard.** An earlier revision of this branch (`3516a6e7c30`) inferred the cause of an errorless abandonment from the lease state. The `stopped` case fails there (`expected true to be false`: the stopped wake ran) and passes at head.
- **Related suites pass:** 41 files, 531 tests. They cover the session-event handoff, policy, permissions, context and automation-result suites, `agent-runner-execution-session-events`, the abort and Stop suites (`abort*.test.ts`, `abort-cutoff.runtime`), the exec notify producers (`bash-tools.exec-notify.*`), all `model-fallback*` suites, `failover-error` and the session delivery generation suites.

prs.title: fix(update): old updater runtimes pile up while the Gateway is running
prs.body:
Related: #197445

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: old updater runtimes (about 640 MiB and 44,500 files each) pile up on Linux and Windows because neither `openclaw update` nor `openclaw doctor --fix` can reclaim them while the Gateway is running.

## User Impact

User impact: each update again removes the previous update's retained runtime, and `openclaw doctor --fix` reclaims leftover runtimes while the Gateway keeps running, so disk usage no longer grows by one runtime per update.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #197445 the Gateway's directory watch helper runs as its own process on every platform (it used to exist only on macOS). Before deleting a retained runtime, the reclaim step checks that no other OpenClaw process could still be using it. That check already treats the Gateway, its spawn broker and the Windows job anchor as safe unless they reference the runtime, because none of them runs updater code. The watch helper was missing from that list, so a running Gateway's watch helper always looked like a holder: every reclaim stopped with "other OpenClaw processes are still running".

The watch helper only watches directories and monitors its caller. It now joins the same list. A watch helper launched from inside a retained runtime still references that runtime through its own script path, so it still counts as a holder, and the test covers that case.

## Evidence

- `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.test.ts`: the extended "releases runtimes from Gateway processes without artifact evidence" case fails on `origin/main` (the watch helper PID is reported as a holder) and passes with the fix; both census suites pass (87 tests).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (+3 net test lines) clean.
- Daily update matrix on main `46350dafd29` (Crabbox AWS), before the fix:
  - Linux: every published-updater lane left the previous runtime in place with `Runtime retained at …: other OpenClaw processes are still running`; the second hop kept both the first hop's runtime and its own.
  - Windows: after 2026.11.3 → main → second hop, two runtimes remained and `openclaw doctor --fix` with the Gateway running reclaimed none (2 → 2). The previous day's matrix on `d3942b51328`, before #197445, removed the first hop's runtime during the second hop and reclaimed the last one with `doctor --fix` (1 → 0).
- Native after-fix proof (Crabbox AWS, this head relabelled 2026.11.31/32):
  - Linux: published 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.31 → 2026.11.32. The second hop, now run by the fixed updater, removed the first hop's runtime and kept only its own (deferred until its workers settle); before the fix the second hop kept both. `openclaw doctor --fix` with the Gateway and its two watch helpers running then printed `Removed abandoned updater runtime` and left 0 runtimes; the Gateway stayed ready.
  - Windows: from the regressed state above (2 retained runtimes), updating to 2026.11.32 and running `openclaw doctor --fix` with the Gateway running reclaimed all 3 runtimes (3 → 0); the Gateway stayed ready. That update was driven by the unfixed 2026.11.31 updater, whose own census still refused, as expected.
- Autoreview (P2): scoped-clean. Independent read-only Codex review: no findings.

prs.title: improve: reduce memory churn during Responses continuation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long Responses conversations allocate generic object-comparison bookkeeping when deciding whether to continue a prior response.

## User Impact

Continuation and request bytes remain unchanged; the intended benefit is lower per-request allocation and CPU. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Responses continuation compares JSON projections with Node's generic deep comparator on every mutable-history fallback. The projection owner has already normalized JSON values and rejected cycles, so generic property-descriptor arrays and cycle bookkeeping repeat work whose contract is already established. Compare the prepared JSON directly, preserving mutable payload checks, replay-ID ownership, projection order and the immutable-prefix shortcut.

This removes generic comparison allocation; it does not claim to repair a production retained-heap leak. A synthetic post-GC allocation-tracked snapshot found no surviving comparison key arrays, memo or descriptor records. Existing frozen JSON projections and retained request state remain intentionally owned upstream.

The specialized traversal adds 41 production lines. There is no new cache, configuration, schema or dependency. A request/response ID cannot establish compatibility after mutable provider hooks, so deleting the check or trusting the ID would change continuation semantics.

## Evidence

### Performance acceptance rule (recorded before measurements)

Use `scripts/perf/responses-continuation.ts --flow resolve --initial-turns 120 --frozen --reuse-input --conversations 10`, with `--image-every 25` (mixed history with rebuilt images) and `--image-every 0` (immutable fast-path control). Each process measures 2,000 decisions over 200-turn conversations, starting with more than 600 history items, including tool calls/results, reasoning and response deltas.

Five counterbalanced A/B pairs plus five A/A pairs per workload, timing and sampled-allocation processes separate, Node 26.12.1. Report median, process-mean p95 and range for main-thread CPU, wall time and bytes/request; record host load. Full request, wire request and decision hashes must be identical in every arm. Keep only an allocation/CPU gain beyond A/A noise with no material regression; a 20% regression in any metric stops landing. Run a separate 20-session, 2,000-item/session retained-only/forced-GC diagnostic. Owner timing excludes request preparation/encoding, Gateway/network latency and production database/workspace costs.

Baseline: `4c04a9e952646a506b0d0cda4c197746ebfcca43`, substituted through the committed benchmark's owner replacement loader. Production data is not used.

### Validation

- The extended existing mutable-history work-count test fails on the base (3 generic deep comparisons; expected 0).
- Candidate: 117 focused continuation, steering, HTTP integration, retention, agent-loop and tool-prefix tests passed.
- After moving the unchanged comparator beside its projection owner, all 72 directly affected continuation/HTTP integration tests passed again.
- Production-build chat E2E: 10 passed; Chromium chat rendering: 11 passed.
- Independent Codex review: scoped clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings on the final candidate.
- Source-size ratchet passes after placing the traversal at the projection owner. `pnpm check:changed` passed completely; all paired measurements are complete and meet the acceptance rule.
- Candidate allocation-tracked post-GC snapshot: only 104 bytes of enum-cache metadata tied to projected object shapes, no comparison containers. Both arms released all 40 watched history references after state release. This is a diagnostic, not a retained-heap improvement claim.

The patch was rebased unchanged onto main `e52cdb9b3f88de333b8c6ad7d791d5f72d5ac722` at the maintainer's request; candidate head is `2a40464734281864b8f0c0113fd11aa6c3b8c6ab`. All 117 focused tests passed again, and a fresh isolated Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm check:changed` completed: all checks passed except the production unused-export scan for `readPendingInputSource`. The same pinned scan reproduces exactly on parent `e52cdb9b3f88de333b8c6ad7d791d5f72d5ac722`. #184512 (`baca36ea403cf681b9ec531c5f27837d0586dcad`) moved the last external production caller into the helper owner and left its export behind; tests still import it, explaining the passing full-tree scan. This is an inherited main regression, not a change in this PR. Exact-head [CI run 43280358328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43280358328) completed all 72 jobs without failure; `node scripts/watch-pr-ci.mjs 197579 2a40464734281864b8f0c0113fd11aa6c3b8c6ab` returned **GREEN**, excluding superseded older runs. ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head with zero findings/open items. Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 prepare-run` passed, and `scripts/pr merge-run` merged the exact prepared head as `41ffd20207eaea4defbd54f2254e8864d6a6f93f`. No admin merge or CI exception was used.

The prior full runtime build passed at the original patch head in [run 43166310096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43166310096), job 131009670353. Earlier broad-run failures and exact-parent reproductions remain recorded in the lane report; main has since incorporated the separately owned runtime repairs. They are historical evidence, not a claim that the rebased head passed CI. The new exact-head run is green and supersedes the earlier CI evidence for landing. No CI rerun is requested merely for green.

The paired performance results below are from the unchanged patch before the rebase; the continuation owners have not changed on main. They remain owner-level measurements rather than a claim about end-to-end Gateway latency or retained production heap.

### Paired results

Mixed history reduces allocation by **18.25%** and main-thread CPU by **13.61%**, beyond A/A median drift of **0.10%** and **1.55%** respectively. The immutable fast-path CPU result is effectively unchanged (-0.39%, within A/A noise). No measured candidate metric regressed. Each cell below is the median of five process means, followed by its range; with five samples, the reported empirical p95 equals the range maximum. These are owner costs per request, not per-request tail latency or Gateway/network latency.

| Workload / metric | Baseline median [min–p95] | Candidate median [min–p95] | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed history: main CPU µs/request | 970.476 [969.908–982.654] | 838.423 [821.788–867.755] | -13.61% |
| Mixed history: wall µs/request | 973.028 [971.468–983.670] | 839.601 [822.578–905.233] | -13.71% |
| Mixed history: sampled bytes/request | 1,767,626.976 [1,758,576.640–1,768,970.368] | 1,444,958.740 [1,442,242.972–1,449,834.096] | -18.25% |
| Immutable control: main CPU µs/request | 30.390 [29.933–37.083] | 30.271 [29.581–30.486] | -0.39% |
| Immutable control: wall µs/request | 29.852 [29.377–100.139] | 29.762 [29.033–29.957] | -0.30% |
| Immutable control: sampled bytes/request | 7,557.708 [7,287.564–8,171.128] | 6,308.928 [5,822.572–6,366.896] | -16.52% |

A/A controls (both arms use the baseline owner):

| Workload / metric | A1 median [min–p95] | A2 median [min–p95] | Drift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed history: main CPU µs/request | 1,040.518 [966.134–1,426.329] | 1,056.695 [973.643–1,092.877] | +1.55% |
| Mixed history: wall µs/request | 1,337.373 [968.206–3,000.084] | 1,445.163 [976.305–2,556.646] | +8.06% |
| Mixed history: sampled bytes/request | 1,765,193.688 [1,761,689.612–1,776,374.708] | 1,767,040.352 [1,753,835.596–1,776,478.280] | +0.10% |
| Immutable control: main CPU µs/request | 33.500 [30.221–38.092] | 31.145 [29.904–44.411] | -7.03% |
| Immutable control: wall µs/request | 34.252 [29.689–180.336] | 38.922 [29.311–79.384] | +13.63% |
| Immutable control: sampled bytes/request | 7,373.484 [6,858.820–8,056.160] | 8,157.440 [7,335.436–8,334.996] | +10.63% |

All **80 fresh processes** completed on Node 26.12.1. Host one-minute load ranged from 18.66 to 69.22; sampling and timing ran separately, and heavy local checks had exited before timing. The benchmark asserts hashes before and after the measured region; cross-arm comparison also matched all full-request, wire-request and continuation-decision hashes.

Mixed full-request SHA-256: `160c8d32f653f4918eab14e52898c176cef46b3599c413e0efeaabd9d9f123f2`.
Immutable full-request SHA-256: `20ceeeb40f3ae138d4c2712c1ede1298b4329b3c21127a074302cbe93a497950`.

Both workloads' wire SHA-256: `dcdf73f2b82070fc4a6784a5506bf7ea66ad77236192d0a34b7bf9ec281498e2`; decision SHA-256: `4d54683027705a410276013fcc162b18363661a4bd1bf63e21a29a772850fd76`.

The generic comparator work-count falls from 3 to 0 in the regression fixture. Separate CPU profiles confirm its removal from the continuation stack. The single retained-heap diagnostics are not a performance claim: both release all 40 watched history references; the candidate leaves only 104 bytes of V8 enum-cache metadata associated with projected object shapes, not per-request comparison containers.

prs.title: feat: isolate node workers with OpenShell filesystem enforcement
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw node workers on OpenShell need writable PVC ancestry without allowing model-controlled processes to replace private directories. The exception in [fs-safe#1073](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1073) requires external isolation; enabling the flag alone is insufficient.

**Draft for design review, not ready to merge.** The isolated worker flow passes locally, but the global dependency upgrade and OpenShell companion remain blocked below.

## User Impact

Opt-in `nodeHost.workerRuns.isolation: "filesystem"` confines the worker and descendants before runtime startup. Writes are limited to the workspace, model HOME and private scratch. Existing `none` and `container` behavior is unchanged; missing enforcement fails closed.

This requires Linux Landlock ABI 3+, a trusted `/usr/local/bin/openshell-sandbox` providing `restrict-exec`, and no other unconfined writers, including old workers. It is a filesystem boundary, not full same-UID isolation: inherited descriptors are not revoked, and signals/network/all metadata operations are outside this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenShell owns enforcement through its existing Landlock implementation and binary distribution. OpenClaw retains existing process supervision, extinction confirmation and cleanup. No PVC migration or second proc-safe enforcement implementation is introduced; proc-safe stays at 0.4.2.

The node captures operator ancestry policy for admission/transfers/publication and strips it from workers. Worker scratch is admitted without that exception before launch: select a strict fallback or reject early. The device-placement fix resolves an eligible named device before requiring its identifier.

Descriptor-relative I/O could protect host operations against hostile directory writers, but completing it across Git, publication, cleanup and recovery is separate work and does not restrict arbitrary subprocess writes. This proposal instead establishes the external filesystem boundary required by the existing exception.

### Companion contract for design review

The trusted native process owner launches the fixed OpenShell helper before worker code:

```text
native process owner
  -> /usr/local/bin/openshell-sandbox restrict-exec
       --read-only <runtime/system/CA path> ...
       --read-write <workspace> --read-write <model HOME>
       --read-write <private scratch> --read-write /dev/null
       --cwd <workspace> --env HOME=... --env TMPDIR=... ...
       -- <absolute Node executable> <worker arguments>
```

The companion must apply explicit grants through OpenShell's existing Landlock path before starting the target, with no implicit cwd grant or unrestricted fallback. Missing paths, unsupported enforcement or failed setup reject execution. Target HOME/temp overrides apply only after confinement. The helper then replaces itself, preserving PID and admitted IPC descriptors; OC's existing process owner remains responsible for descendants, extinction and cleanup. Descriptor admission and excluding other unconfined writers remain deployment/caller responsibilities.

The local companion has 112 production lines, 336 test lines and 42 documentation lines. It adds an entrypoint to the existing binary; no new PVC layout, supervisor or release pipeline. Its implementation is not yet publicly reviewable. This contract and the OC call site support design review now; complete cross-repository implementation/security approval still needs the companion PR diff and owner review. Issue acceptance does not substitute for that review.

### Merge prerequisites

- **Fixed published fs-safe and upgrade qualification.** This draft aligns the root and 12 plugin pins at 0.28.0 because it contains the required API. However, [#194589](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194589) previously rolled it back for integration failures. Runtime repairs [fs-safe#1079](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1079) and [#1081](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1081) are merged but absent from the latest published 0.28.0. The open alternative [fs-safe#1078](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/1078) proposes reverting the separate lock-publication changes; upstream must confirm release contents and timing. Adopt a published version that retains the ancestor API and resolves these regressions, reuse the fixture work in [#194909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194909), and run the required full upgrade matrix. No overrides, vendoring or duplicate fixture migration are proposed here.
- **Accepted and released OpenShell companion.** [NVIDIA/OpenShell#5482](https://github.com/NVIDIA/OpenShell/issues/5482) awaits contributor feature acceptance. Its local `restrict-exec` implementation is tested, but no companion PR or release exists yet.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh `0954ce8f743` incorporates main `2f95bd3c3a5`. Both captured-state fallback and worker-strict scratch admission are preserved. Affected validation: 85 host tests pass (one existing skip), 82 Linux/Node tests pass as UID 10001 including the real OpenShell/native-owner lifecycle cases, plus core/infra/services type graphs, touched lint/format and an independent resolution review. This refresh does not claim a new full composed E2E or global dependency-upgrade matrix.
- Protected-registry frozen install, canonical Docker packaging, full runtime build and three affected TypeScript graphs pass. The main integration at `91e4ac5bef9` passes 157 Linux/Node tests with one existing skip. These targeted checks do not qualify the global dependency upgrade.
- The subsequent scratch repair has two real-filesystem regressions: both fail before repair; all 28 tests pass afterward. Final repair `b98c61d82a7` passes **34 Linux tests as UID 10001**. Qualification includes the real OpenShell binary and native process owner, IPC startup, extinction, cleanup failure and early exit.
- The OpenShell companion passes five real-binary tests, Clippy with warnings denied and the existing Linux arm64 musl release build.
- Real OpenShell integration of feature `83b72f2b5e4` in the retained bridge fixture passes initial execution, Gateway/node restart and new-workspace restoration: model-driven Git commits, hashed transfer, publication readback and cleanup. A same-UID unconfined control can replace the test directory; the worker is denied replacement and outside writes in all three phases. The resolved Gateway policy has no private-ancestry write grant. This is a retained OC/OCE bridge fixture with the feature and published dependencies, **not current OCE-main exact-head qualification**.
- Three independent reviewers find no required scratch/design correction and agree the dependency blocker remains. Hosted ClawSweeper identified the scratch and upgrade issues; the former is repaired, the latter is explicitly outstanding. Ordinary broad PR CI skips drafts; no passing full matrix is claimed.

A macOS `sessions.create` timeout also reproduces on exact official main `945efbb662f` with its own frozen dependencies; the candidate passes that file on Linux. No assertion or timeout was weakened. Early source-built experiments labeled 0.27.2 are not proof for published 0.27.2, which lacks this API.

Alternative drafts retained for comparison: [OpenClaw#193823](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193823), [proc-safe#39](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/39).

prs.title: fix(codex): cold web-search support verdicts no longer rotate bound threads
prs.body:
Closes #174676

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: a Codex conversation's native thread is replaced — re-sending its full selected history — on the second turn after a Gateway cold start, because turn 1 recorded the web-search policy from a cold capability probe.

## User Impact
Conversations that start right after a Gateway start keep their native thread and prompt context. A cold "unsupported" capability read no longer forces a full history re-send once the provider's web-search support resolves (the issue measured ~1.2M characters re-injected on a lossless session).

## Why This Change Was Made
A cold app-server can answer `modelProvider/capabilities/read` before its model metadata hydrates, producing a definitive-looking "unsupported" verdict. The lifecycle persisted that verdict's disabled thread config as the binding's authoritative web-search fingerprint, so the first informed turn counted the change as a persistent policy change and rotated the thread.

The preflight now also computes the fingerprint an uninformed ("unknown") plan produces under the same config. When a binding's stored fingerprint equals that uninformed shape and the current plan is informed, the lifecycle adopts the informed fingerprint on the existing thread instead of replacing it. Genuine policy edits (allowed domains, provider opt-outs, persistent denial) move the plan away from the uninformed shape and still rotate as before; a first turn under an "unknown" verdict already keeps a provisional binding and is untouched.

The stored fingerprint alone cannot prove the plan was uninformed: an explicit `tools.web.search.enabled=false` turn writes the same disabled shape. The binding now also records whether the durable policy requested search (`webSearchRequested`, taken from `persistentWebSearchAllowed` with the effective value as fallback, so capability filtering such as domain-restricted management does not look like a denial). Cold-support settlement requires `webSearchRequested: true`, so re-enabling an explicitly disabled search remains a policy transition that rotates; bindings written before this field keep rotating exactly as before.

## Evidence
- Regression in `thread-lifecycle-web-search.test-support.ts` (registered from the binding suite): turn 1 under `nativeProviderWebSearchSupport: "unsupported"` persists the disabled fingerprint; turn 2 under `"supported"` keeps `thread-1` with exactly one `thread/start`. Fails on base — the thread is replaced via the "web search config changed" rotation named in the issue — and passes with this change.
- Policy-transition regression: turn 1 persists an explicit denial (`webSearchRequested: false`, disabled fingerprint); turn 2 enables search with a supported verdict and rotates to `thread-2` with two `thread/start` calls. This is the case the earlier revision misclassified as cold settlement.
- The branch is rebased on current `main`; both regressions and the 4 neighboring search cases pass (6/6 `-t search`, plus the cold-verdict case), and the new test-line allocation `174676-codex-web-search.txt` (63 lines) is the exact net growth.
- Neighbors stay green: 5/5 `search`-filtered cases in `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` (including the existing unknown-support preservation case) and 8/8 in `thread-lifecycle.assignment-rotation.test.ts`, run with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on Node 24.19.
- Not run locally: full extension suite and project typecheck (CI covers).
