prs.title: fix(cron): agent-less automations cannot be added or edited on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on a Gateway with several agents and `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` set, `openclaw automations add` without `--agent` and `openclaw automations edit <job-id> --model ...` on an agent-less job fail with `invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. Select an agent explicitly; CLI callers can pass --agent <id>, ...` (`cron.add` likewise). The scheduler itself runs that same job on the configured system agent, so the job works but cannot be created or have its model changed without repeating `--agent` on every call.

## User Impact

User impact: agent-less automations now add and edit on the agent the scheduler runs them on. The inference-account capture for `cron.add` and `cron.update` resolves the owner the documented way (`docs/cli/cron.md`: explicit `--agent`, then an agent-qualified session key, then `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` or the legacy/sole-agent fallback). When no owner is resolvable at all, the request now fails with the cron-specific hint (`Agent-less cron job has no resolvable owner. Pass --agent <id> when creating or editing the job, or set agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.`) instead of the generic selection error. Jobs with an explicit `agentId` are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.ts` resolved the account owner with `resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg)` in three places (create capture, scheduled operator source, update capture). That helper is marked `@deprecated` in `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts` because it only honors a raw legacy default marker or a sole agent and throws `AgentSelectionRequiredError` otherwise; it ignores `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`. The run path (`src/gateway/server-cron-targets.ts`, `src/cron/local-service.ts`) uses `resolveCronJobEffectiveAgentId(job, tryResolveAmbientOwnerAgentId(cfg))`. The three sites now share one small helper that applies that same resolution, so validation and execution agree on the owner.

## Evidence

- New `src/gateway/server-methods/cron-input-validation.owner.test.ts` (two cases: an agent-less edit on an explicit two-agent fleet with `systemAgent.agentId: "main"` resolves; the same fleet without a system agent rejects with the cron ownership hint): without the change `2 failed (2)` (both reject with `AgentSelectionRequiredError: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`, `agentIds: ['main', 'worker']`), with it `2 passed (2)`.
- Consumers unchanged: `cron.validation.test.ts`, `server-cron.test.ts`, `server-cron.session-target.test.ts`, `cron.list-scoped.test.ts`, `server-cron-completion.test.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent.auth-profile-propagation.test.ts` (the existing test of the update capture): 160 + 120 + 40 = 320 passed across their three shards, 0 failed.
- `oxlint --type-aware` on the two TypeScript files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `oxfmt` clean, `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` clean (exit 0), line-cap ratchet OK (2 changed source files, no over-cap growth) and max-lines ratchet OK.
- Field data from one Gateway on 2026.11.1 (`agents.ownership: "explicit"`, two agents, `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId: "main"`): `2026-11-07T16:15:08 [ws] res ✗ cron.update 1ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.update params: Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner. ...` for `automations edit <id> --model ...` on an agent-less job, and `2026-11-07T18:52:36 [ws] res ✗ cron.add 2ms errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=invalid cron.add params: Multiple agents are configured, ...` for `automations add` without `--agent`; the same job runs on `main` from the scheduler, and the same edit succeeds with `--agent main`.


### Runtime proof (isolated Gateway)

Full trace in the proof comment: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194890#issuecomment-6717691469. Summary: an isolated Gateway (own state directory, loopback port, loopback OpenAI-compatible stub provider that logs the model and the sha256 prefix of the bearer key per request, synthetic keys) ran from the released `openclaw@2026.11.1` package and then from the same package with this PR's change transplanted into its `dist` cron chunk, on the same state directory.

- 2026.11.1, single agent: agent-less job j1 created and run (`succeeded`, request with main's key).
- 2026.11.1, agents `main` + `worker`, `agents.ownership: "explicit"`, `systemAgent.agentId: "main"`: `cron add` without `--agent` and `cron edit <j1> --model ...` fail with `Multiple agents are configured, but this operation has no explicit owner`.
- 2026.11.1 + this change, same state: j1 loads with its stored binding unchanged; `cron edit <j1> --model stub/stub-b` and `cron add` without `--agent` succeed; j1 and j2 run `succeeded`, both requests carry main's key, never worker's.
- Replaced key (same profile id) → later run `failed` with `Automation inference account was replaced ...`, 0 provider requests. Profile removed with `models auth logout` and Gateway restarted → later run `failed` with `MCP_AUTHORIZATION_RETIRED` (rendered as `... was removed or signed out ...` on current main), 0 provider requests.
- Another principal's personal account: not reproducible in our CLI-only setup; verified by @daniel-lxs on built head `18d86606a13` through real Gateway WebSocket RPCs (see the next section).

### Personal-account case (verified by @daniel-lxs)

Full report: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194890#issuecomment-6828837295. Built head `18d86606a1379fd7fd32eadae61c159fee04509b`, agents `main` and `worker`, explicit ownership, `systemAgent.agentId: main`, automation requests without `agentId`, two synthetic users connected through the trusted-proxy handshake, each with their own stored personal account:

- Each user could create an automation that selects their own account.
- From Alice's authenticated connection, selecting Bob's account was refused by both `cron.add` and `cron.update` with `INVALID_REQUEST` ("This account action requires a current authorized connection; reconnect and try again."). The provider recorder received 0 requests during the refused captures, no foreign-account job was created, and the rejected edit kept Alice's model selection.
- A forced run of Alice's unchanged job then completed `succeeded` with exactly 1 provider request carrying Alice's synthetic credential.
- Limits stated in the report: compiled PR source, isolated state directory, synthetic credentials seeded through the state owner APIs; real OAuth enrollment and external providers were not tested.

prs.title: fix(discord): Activity hangs on npm installs because the SDK asset returns 404
prs.body:
Related: #127421

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Discord Activity iframe spins forever when the Discord plugin is installed from npm or ClawHub, because the Activity shell's Embedded App SDK request returns 404.

## User Impact

User impact: Discord Activities load their SDK again on standalone plugin installs. Source checkouts and bundled dist builds keep working as before. This PR covers only the asset half of #127421. The Entry Point command deletion in `reconcileGlobalCommands` is left alone, because ClawSweeper routes that half to coordination with the open Activities work first, so the issue stays open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The published `@openclaw/discord` package copies the generated SDK to `dist/assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` (`openclaw.build.staticAssets`), but `registerDiscordActivities` resolved `assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` against the plugin root. That path exists in a source checkout and in the bundled dist layout (`dist/extensions/discord/assets/`), and not in the standalone package. Registration now resolves both candidates and uses the one that exists, the same two-layout lookup `extensions/diffs/src/plugin.ts` uses for its viewer runtime. When neither exists, it keeps the old path, so the vendor route still answers 404 and retries the read on the next request.

## Evidence

- Red first. Test commit 013848773c2 adds a case to `extensions/discord/src/activities/interaction.test.ts` for each layout. Each registers the plugin against a temp root holding the SDK in that layout, then fetches `/discord/activity/vendor/embedded-app-sdk.mjs` through the registered route handler. With only the test commit applied, the standalone-package case fails with `expected 404 to be 200` (1 failed, 18 passed). With the fix (d086ab61e08), 19/19 pass.
- Published artifact. With the unpacked `@openclaw/discord@2026.9.8` tarball from `npm pack` as the plugin root, the same route returned `404` (9 bytes) with main's `register.ts` and `200` (159348 bytes, contains `DiscordSDK`) with this branch. The tarball has `dist/assets/embedded-app-sdk.mjs`, and its `assets/` holds only `icon.png` and `activity.svg`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/discord/src/activities`: 6 files, 54 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean and `oxlint` 0 warnings and 0 errors on the 2 changed files. `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` (through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`) exit 0. `check-line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` OK on the 2 changed files.
- Test cost. `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities/register.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on 4bee5b11580 (before the rebase): 13 passed, 8.2s wall on a warm run (vitest reports 6.46s, 77% of it transform), 15.9s on a cold run. The 13 tests take 50ms in total; the two new layout tests take 18ms and 5ms. In CI the file ran in `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` (job 111259868399), inside the `vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` shard of 7 files and 72 tests, which took 31.85s (86% transform); the file's own tests add about 0.05s of CI time.
- Not verified: a real Discord client opening the Activity. Even with the SDK served, the client handshake still depends on the Entry Point half of #127421.

AI disclosure: an AI agent (Claude Code) reproduced the 404 against the published package, wrote the test and the fix, and ran the gates above: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities/register.test.ts`, `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/activities`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt --check`, and `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main`.

Rebased 2026-10-27 onto main 183f52b9cd7 (head d086ab61e08). Main's #184882 deleted `activities/register.test.ts` and moved its route registration test into `interaction.test.ts` on the shared `createRegisteredActivityFixture` helper. The two layout tests moved there too, and the helper's `vendorAssetPath` argument now also accepts a resolver function so a test can map each relative path into its temp root. No change to the fix in `register.ts`. On d086ab61e08: `interaction.test.ts` 19/19 with the fix and 1 failed, 18 passed without it; the activities directory 4 files, 52 passed; oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files; `tsc --noEmit -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` reports no errors in `activities/` (2 errors elsewhere, in `outbound-payload.ts` and `voice/audio-worker-thread.ts`, which this PR does not touch). Not rerun on this head: the packed-tarball HTTP proof, the test-cost timings, tsgo, and autoreview.

## Maintainer verification

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes. Additional packed-artifact HTTP proof, source/bundled Gateway controls, live-call outcome, and the offline standalone-install trust limitation are recorded in [this handoff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/164439#issuecomment-5973429815). A maintainer must confirm via a real ClawHub install or accept the handler-boundary evidence; standalone Gateway acceptance is not claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the session system prompt stable across completion wakes
prs.body:
## Problem

The system prompt of one session changes between turns, depending on what started the turn. Anthropic prompt caching keys on an exact prefix, so each change discards the cache for the whole conversation. Long sessions (several hundred thousand tokens) then re-write the full prefix at cache-write price.

On a production gateway over 3 days (`anthropic-messages`, `cacheRetention: short`), the existing `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped` detector attributed most breaks to `systemPrompt`/`systemPromptSuffix` digest changes. The largest group was `trigger=event provenance=internal_system:exec` (background exec completion wakes): the stable prefix and almost every suffix section changed at once.

## Root cause

1. **Completion wakes switch the prompt to minimal mode.** A session event (exec or child completion wake) carries its producer's tool ceiling in `toolsAllow` (`session-event-target.ts`, `session-event-handoff.ts`). `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSystemPrompt` treats any restrictive `toolsAllow` as a narrowly scoped run and forces `promptMode: "minimal"`. A wake therefore renders a different prompt for the same session: no Execution Bias, Bootstrap/Project Context changes, no Memory Recall, Documentation, Session routing, Output Directives, UI Presentation or messaging guidance. The tool definitions were already kept stable for these turns (`resolveTurnToolSurface`); only the prompt mode was not.
2. **Run-granted tools in the cached deferred-tool directory.** `skill_library` is a run-granted core tool: it exists only on turns whose requester granted it. A system-started wake of the same session does not have it, so the "Available deferred-schema tools" list inside the Tooling section differed by one row between user turns and wakes.

## Fix

- A host system turn (`trigger=event` with `internal_system` provenance, the existing `isHostSystemTurn`) keeps the session's prompt mode. Its tool ceiling still gates calls exactly as before. Narrowly scoped runs that are not host wakes (cron `toolsAllow`, plugin commands, etc.) keep the minimal prompt.
- The cached deferred-tool directory omits run-granted core tools. The turn that holds the grant lists them in its own runtime context, beside the turn's input, so its discoverability does not change.
- Remote worker turns render that per-turn listing in the worker tool projection, before the projection disposes its catalog, and carry it into prompt preparation (including refresh).
- When another catalog source shares a run-granted tool's name, or the entry requires an exact id, the listing names the exact catalog id (for example `openclaw:core:skill_library`), so `tool_describe` / `dispatch_action` resolve it.

## Proof

**Real route, before vs after.** Isolated throwaway Gateway (scratch state, no channels), real Anthropic-compatible provider route, `cacheRetention: short`, the same configured scratch workspace for both arms. A logging proxy recorded the provider's own `cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens` and the request system-prompt digest. One session per arm: user turn that starts a 10 s background exec → exec completion wake → user turn → wake → final user turn.

| call | kind | before: read / write | after: read / write |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | user | 11,640 / 17,955 | 11,640 / 18,156 |
| 2 | tool result | 29,595 / 392 | 29,796 / 396 |
| 3 | **exec wake** | **12,157 / 16,379** | **30,192 / 987** |
| 4 | user | 29,987 / 1,331 | 31,179 / 441 |
| 5 | tool result | 31,318 / 419 | 31,620 / 440 |
| 6 | **exec wake** | 28,536 / 1,727 | 32,060 / 988 |
| 7 | user | 31,737 / 1,292 | 33,048 / 400 |
| **total** | | **174,970 / 39,495** | **199,535 / 21,808** |

- Before: 2 distinct system prompts in one session; the detector logged `cache read dropped 29595 -> 12157 … trigger=event provenance=internal_system:exec` with the same section signature seen in production.
- After: 1 system prompt for all 7 calls; no `[prompt-cache]` drop warnings.
- Cache writes in this short session fell 45% (39.5k → 21.8k). The first wake re-wrote 16.4k tokens before and 1k after. In the before arm, the second wake still hit, because both prompt variants were warm inside the 5-minute window. In production, each wake that arrives after the wake variant has expired re-writes the whole conversation. With 400–750k-token sessions, that is one full re-write per such wake.

The cost saving at production scale is an extrapolation from this mechanism. I measured it only on this short probe session, not on a production deployment.

**Focused tests:**
- `attempt-system-prompt.test.ts`: a completion wake with an inherited tool ceiling renders the user-turn prompt byte for byte. A non-wake restricted run still renders the minimal prompt.
- `tool-search-directory.test.ts`: the cached directory is identical with or without the run grant, and the grant is listed separately. With a colliding client tool, the listing gives an exact id that `ToolSearchRuntime.describe` resolves.
- `worker-gateway-tool-runtime.test.ts`: the worker projection leaves `skill_library` out of the cached directory and returns it in the per-turn listing.
- Each test fails without its fix.

The real-route numbers above were measured before the worker and collision fixes. Those fixes change no prompt bytes on the measured embedded path.

## Not covered (separate follow-ups)

- **User-turn `systemPromptSuffix` changes** (Tooling / Session routing / Skills) on `inter_session` user turns (`sessions_send`, subagent settle). The Tooling part matches the run-granted directory row fixed here. The Session routing and Skills differences were not reproduced or measured in this PR.
- **History rewrites** (`historyRewrite: message N (assistant) differs … content.length, content[k].type/id/name/arguments`). An earlier assistant message gains or changes tool-call blocks after it was already sent. This is often together with `replayed thinking dropped … prefix_binding_mismatch`, and sometimes with changed `envelope.api/provider/model` (a fallback route). This change does not address it.

prs.title: feat(macos): sign in with OpenClaw ID and approve this Mac as your device
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Mac can join an OpenClaw ID claw only as a node with a separate invite, and nobody signs in. That isn't how a person uses their own Mac. Josh approved sign-in-first enrollment on 2026-11-11: the person signs in and the Mac becomes their own device.

## User Impact

- **Sign in with OpenClaw ID** in onboarding (and Settings for an existing Tailscale/token/SSH Mac) now does this:
  1. Signs in natively.
  2. Lists the person's claws.
  3. Makes this Mac an **owner device** of the chosen claw, either by comparing six digits with a device that already has access or by entering the recovery kit.
- The Mac then reaches chat and the dashboard over OpenClaw ID with its own key and runs tools through its bound node. There's no VPN and no Gateway token.
- Settings → Connection gets an OpenClaw ID section with these actions:
  - Stop using this Mac for tools, or use it again.
  - Remove this Mac.
  - Sign in again, shown when a tools-off Mac's Discovery session has ended.
  - Switch to OpenClaw ID (migration from a Tailscale, token or SSH connection).
- Migration *replaces* the existing connection and clears its saved Gateway token and password. Tailscale itself is untouched, and going back means Change connection… with a new setup code.
- The headless node-invite path (#196759) is unchanged and is still offered as "Use a node invitation".

**Not live-testable yet:**
- The staging Mac OAuth client is registered (`DulSrXtaYtPaLEnzEyHGuAHpVNWmaNbf`), but Discovery staging only accepts its tokens after openclaw/discovery#14 is deployed.
- The node binding in `start` and `add_owner_device` needs openclaw/discovery#13 and this protocol stack (#197573) deployed.
- Until then, sign-in reaches the issuer, and every Discovery call is refused.

**Stacking:** stacked on #197585 (`feat/ocid-mac-ocid-connection`). The protocol side is #197573 (`node` on the SAS `start` and on `add_owner_device`, and the approver UI).

**Member invite join is not in this PR.** It goes in a second stacked PR to keep this one reviewable. A member account that picks a claw here gets "Ask for an invite" instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mac follows the protocol's "Owner device node" design (enrollment.md). It holds three keys, each in its own Keychain service, and none of them ever goes over the node bridge:
- D_mac signs.
- W_mac is its owner peer key, used for chat and the dashboard.
- W_node is the only key the node worker sees, and it never carries human authority.

Enrollment works like this:
- **SAS.** The Mac is the new-device side of the owner-browser SAS. `start` carries `node {peer_key: W_node, description}`, so the compared digits bind all three keys and the tool surface. Before the Mac opens the sealed handoff, the person must confirm the digits on the Mac too. The handoff's binding must then verify under its root for this claw and hostname, and its cert must name this D and W.
- **Recovery kit.** R is derived in-process from the typed code or a kit file. If fp(R) isn't the descriptor's root, nothing is signed. R signs `OwnerDeviceCert` and `add_owner_device {cert, node}` at snapshot seq + 1, and they're sent as a `root_statement`. A `seq_conflict` notice is answered by re-signing at the re-read verified snapshot's seq + 1 (up to 3 times).
  - R is dropped when the attempt ends: admitted, refused, cancelled or after 2 minutes. The deadline is checked again right before every signature.
  - R is never stored, logged or sent. CryptoKit-held key bytes can't be explicitly zeroed (the same limit as the browser's WebCrypto key); the seed and decoded secret are zeroed. The typed `String` can't be zeroed either.
- **Admission.** The Mac is admitted only when the claw's K_gw-signed snapshot lists W_mac as an owner peer key and W_node in `node_peer_keys`. The existing join-completion owner then switches the primary connection and opens the dashboard.

The Swift ports (JCS statements, kit decode, R derivation, SAS commitment, transcript, code, AES-GCM handoff and peer-key proof) are checked byte for byte against vectors generated from the TypeScript protocol at #197573.

## Evidence

All build and test runs were on the Mac Studio in a separate checkout, built with `OPENCLAW_IROH_NATIVE=1`.
- Builds: `swift build --build-tests` for `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` and for `apps/macos` (both green).
- Shared tests: `OpenClawID` filter, 45 tests in 6 suites, 8 consecutive green runs at `3d4dabcb9221`.
  - `OpenClawIDOwnerEnrollmentTests` checks the kit, root, SAS and statement vectors.
  - It also covers: the handoff must name this claw and device; kit seq_conflict re-sign; wrong kit or invalid code signs nothing; SAS opens the handoff only after the code is confirmed on the Mac (a mismatch aborts and pins nothing); a declined request.
- App tests: 45 tests in 9 suites green, run in the sandbox (`sandbox-exec`: no network or Keychain).
  - Includes the new `OnboardingOpenClawIDSignInTests`: build config, the callback's state and issuer checks, claw routing by relationship, no claws, cancelled sign-in, invalid kit installs nothing, the automatic approval wait, and switching to the kit cancels the wait.
- `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` are clean. The native i18n baseline was regenerated.
- Inherited from the base: `OnboardingPageTests` "verified node setup…" hangs in the sandbox inside `DashboardManager.shared` init. It hangs the same way on #197585's head.
- Review:
  - **pr-simplify:** no architecture removed. One owner per responsibility: crypto port, Discovery account calls, enrollment client, route refresh, owner actions, sign-in, device store, Settings model.
  - **Astra autoreview:** 5 findings, all verified and fixed. P0: confirm the SAS code on the Mac before opening the handoff. P1: reconcile a self-removal whose answer is lost. P1: Sign in again for a tools-off Mac. P2: the route re-reads the node key and session on every verification. P2: kit deadline across awaits.

Renders are real views with fixture data from the sandboxed render harness; screenshots: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197630#issuecomment-6818359924 (local copies: `~/.openclaw/workspace/reports/ocid-mac-sign-in-first-mockups/impl/`). Recovery-kit entry can't be rendered there: `NSSecureTextField` blocks on the window-server lookup the sandbox denies. Its render is the mockup of the same view.

### Live-proof checklist (blocked on discovery#13 + #14 deploy)
- [ ] Sign in on staging; the claw picker lists the owned claw.
- [ ] SAS approve from the original local Control UI. The approval dialog shows "will also be able to run tools", the codes match on both screens, and the Mac pins and connects.
- [ ] Expected chat attribution: on main every OpenClaw ID owner device maps to the **shared Owner profile** (`gateway-owner-profile.ts`, `openclawIdOwner`). The Mac's chat should land there with owner/admin scopes, not as an accountless person. Personal-profile mapping is OCF-510, out of scope.
- [ ] The node connects with W_node, and Access shows it as this device's node.
- [ ] Recovery-kit enrollment works. Owners see "Recovery kit used". A wrong kit shows "That recovery code didn't work".
- [ ] Settings: stop tools, then use tools again; remove the Mac (connection ends, keys and primary cleared).
- [ ] Migration from a Tailscale connection: the token is cleared and Tailscale is still running.

### Known gaps
- Member invite join comes in the stacked follow-up PR.
- A Mac with tools off reads the claw with the person's 12-hour Discovery session. After it ends, Settings offers Sign in again; chat reconnects fail until then.
- Self-removal whose answer is lost is reconciled from Discovery's snapshot. If that also can't be read, Settings shows an error rather than guessing.
- The token is kept only as a Discovery session in the Keychain. The ID token itself is never stored.

prs.title: refactor(agents): isolate CLI model capabilities
prs.body:
Related: #192609 ([cleanup tracker](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192609))

## What Problem This Solves

CLI preparation mixes model context-window and thinking-level policy into prompt and authority preparation, making those rules harder to review independently.

## User Impact

This is an internal extraction. Existing model aliases, context limits, selectable windows and backend thinking-level behavior are preserved; no configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing policy into `resolveCliModelCapabilities`. Preparation retains native-model identity selection and its authority/hook flow. The helper preserves the minimum owned alias limit, defaults, selectable-window caps, logical/native catalog fallback, backend-owned thinking resolution, synchronous errors and undefined values.

Agents reviewing long conversations cannot request visible message text beyond the fixed 4,000-character `sessions_history` preview, even when the complete message fits within the existing response budget.

This is not an unbounded export: oversized source rows remain explicitly incomplete, and historical/pre-reset discovery is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool requests a bounded read through its existing authorized `chat.history` owner and applies the requested limit to visible text locally. Reads retain at least the existing upstream preview size so smaller text requests do not shorten reasoning/tool previews. The existing Control UI full-message/export path serves interactive readers; it does not supply this model-facing reader option. prs.title: fix(channels): cancel pending status read in channels list on Ctrl+C
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw channels list` issues the same `channels.status` RPC that `channels status` uses, but never passes an AbortSignal. When the user presses Ctrl+C while the gateway status read is pending, the RPC keeps running until its 5s timeout, delaying process exit and then printing a late command-local fallback account list on top of the cancelled output.

## Why

`channels status` was already hardened for this in #196976 (thread `getAsyncWorkSignal()` through the RPC and re-raise cancellation). `channels list` calls the same RPC but was missed — a same-source call-site neighbor. Without a signal, `callGateway` has no abort handler, so the pending request is not cancelled and the CLI waits out the full timeout on Ctrl+C.

## Solution

Thread the work-scope signal through the read, and re-raise the cancellation when the RPC settles after abort, instead of falling back to the command-local account list:

- `channelsListCommand` captures `getAsyncWorkSignal()` and re-checks `signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the entry and after the gateway read.
- `readGatewayChannelStatus(signal)` passes `signal` to `callGateway`, and on a caught error calls `signal?.throwIfAborted()` so a Ctrl+C surfaces as the canonical abort instead of an "unreachable gateway" fallback.

## Evidence

**Shipped CLI proof** — real `openclaw channels list` executed from source trees (`/ws-base` vs `/ws-head-channels-list`) inside an isolated container, driven against a synthetic loopback WebSocket gateway peer speaking the real OpenClaw wire protocol. SIGINT is delivered to the PTY while the `channels.status` request is held pending (peer delays its response past the interrupt). Capture below is the machine-readable peer transcript produced by the harness (`ws-peer-harness/drive.mjs`), redacted (token shown as `***`).

### base (before) — late fallback printed after Ctrl+C

```
exitCode: 130, sigintToExitMs: 765
targetRequestSeen: true, method: channels.status
lateResponseSent: true, lateResponsePrinted: true

stdout:
Chat channels:
- Discord default (L8E_MARKER_7f3a91): installed, configured, enabled, token=***

stderr:
... Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.

peerEvents:
  listening -> connect(role=operator, scopes=[operator.read]) -> req channels.status {probe:false, timeoutMs:5000}
  -> held -> released {socketOpen:true}
```

### head (fix) — no late output; cancelled promptly

```
exitCode: 130, sigintToExitMs: 461
targetRequestSeen: true, method: channels.status
lateResponseSent: true, lateResponsePrinted: false

stdout:
<empty>

stderr:
... Command interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.

peerEvents:
  listening -> connect(role=operator, scopes=[operator.read]) -> req channels.status {probe:false, timeoutMs:5000}
  -> held            (request never released; process exits without printing the fallback)
```

The decisive difference: base shows `held -> released {socketOpen:true}` and prints the marker list after SIGINT; head stops at `held` and prints nothing — the pending read is cancelled and the cancellation propagates instead of the late fallback.

Discriminative unit test added (`propagates cancellation during a pending gateway status read`): red on base (promise resolves instead of rejecting with the cancel reason), green on head.

Precedent: #196976



Maintainer proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197815#issuecomment-6831316033

prs.title: perf(gateway): follow publication facts for passive PR subscriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI PR subscriptions revalidate every watched session during metadata-only transcript updates, although no receipt, identity, lineage, or access fact changed. Each sweep rereads publication rows. The minute GitHub poll also rechecks passive receipt-only subscriptions.

## User Impact

Streaming sessions spend less Gateway CPU and allocate less memory maintaining sidebar PR indicators. Receipt commits and relevant session changes still refresh subscribers; active views retain GitHub polling and explicit refresh. No configuration or schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The subscription owner already observes committed GitHub receipt facts and session facts/invalidation. Skip metadata-only notifications before they schedule the all-key `setImmediate` sweep, and remove passive currency checks from the minute poll. Authorization, physical-source, session-incarnation, lineage, and per-recipient delivery guards remain at actual reads and delivery. Production LOC: +8/-8, net zero. Benchmark and browser-fixture growth supplies the requested work-count, allocation, and real-Gateway proof; no production instrumentation or new cache.

## Evidence

- Baseline fails both regression cases; candidate: 109 passed, one existing skip across subscription, lifetime, receipt-owner, and access suites.
- Isolated Gateway plus Chromium: a committed third receipt arrives in an already subscribed sidebar; an explicit GitHub refresh changes all three PRs to merged. Existing access-revocation and reader-lifetime browser cases pass. GitHub HTTP is synthetic. The fixture advances the clock past the existing ten-second metadata quota window before its second refresh.
- 10,000 synthetic persisted sessions, 40 agents, 64 subscribed roots, four descendants/root, 320 initial receipts. Five alternating A/B pairs; separate main-thread CPU and sampled V8 allocation runs, with identical-source A/A controls.

| Workload | Before → after |
| --- | --- |
| 400 metadata-only notifications | 25,600 → 0 currency assertions; 755.43 → 84.66 ms CPU; 720.20 → 79.46 MB allocated |
| Idle, one minute poll (100 accelerated samples) | 0.0885 → 0.0260 ms CPU; 119.89 → 42.14 KB allocated; zero candidate currency assertions |
| 20 actual receipt commits, all subscription work settled | 964.15 → 1021.06 ms CPU; 273.31 → 272.60 MB allocated; 57.56 → 58.50 ms median delivery |
| Large-state confirmation, 400 metadata-only notifications | 1129.51 → 208.74 ms CPU; 698.86 → 80.35 MB allocated; 25,600 → 0 currency assertions |

Large fixture: 37.69 GB allocated canonical SQLite pages, 62,000 workspace files totaling 1.116 GB. Synthetic only, local APFS rather than btrfs; workspace files are present but the passive path does not read Git/workspace contents. Residual CPU/allocation includes notification/projection/harness work. Sampled allocations exclude native/worker allocations. No claim about production notification frequency or whole-Gateway CPU.

A/A medians: metadata CPU 729.01/719.00 ms, allocation 716.83/716.82 MB; receipt CPU 1144.73/1184.46 ms, allocation 284.24/275.60 MB. Actual receipt work is unchanged within this noise; no material change-delivery regression.

Codex autoreview: complete, no actionable P0–P2 findings. `pnpm check:changed --staged` passed its format, type, boundary, schema, and changed-core lint checks. Its benchmark wait-loop lint finding is fixed and the exact script lint passes. The production dead-export scan reports two unchanged pending-input exports introduced/left unused by `baca36ea403cf` (#184512): `bindSessionPendingInputMentionInvitation` and `readPendingInputSource`. Both exports reproduce on exact main parent `d3ce53dde359c95f32d096a5a289eee17a1c47cc` with the production Knip scan. This is a reported main regression, not a passing full gate.

First exact-head CI found the benchmark receiver-preserving suppression missing from the explicit inventory. The follow-up records this exact exception: the setup Proxy forwards the original receiver with `Reflect.apply` and restores the method in `finally` before measurement. The focused suppression inventory now passes all 14 tests, benchmark lint passes, and Codex review of the two-line repair is clean. Production code and measured behavior are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: only label scheduled heartbeat alerts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving an event-driven completion through the heartbeat dispatcher could see it mislabeled as their “First heartbeat alert.” The same event delivery could also consume the state marker, preventing the next genuine scheduled heartbeat alert from receiving the onboarding context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first-alert preamble and its persisted delivery markers now apply only to scheduled heartbeat runs: explicit `interval` wakes and the existing source-less scheduled compatibility path. Explicit event, manual, hook, and other non-scheduled wakes keep their original text and do not advance scheduled-heartbeat onboarding or dedupe state.

A regression test covers the user-visible sequence: an exec completion is delivered unchanged and leaves heartbeat state unset; the following scheduled heartbeat receives the first-alert preamble and persists its state.

## User Impact

Background task and event completion messages are no longer presented as heartbeat onboarding alerts. Users still receive the onboarding explanation on their first genuine scheduled heartbeat alert.

## Evidence

- Regression demonstrated red on unmodified main: the event-driven delivery included the first-heartbeat preamble.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.structured-delivery.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.isolated-session-mirror.test.ts` — 83 passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/heartbeat-dispatch.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent P0/P1 targeted review — clean after two identified state-ownership edge cases were fixed.

Full local core/test typecheck did not produce a terminal result: one attempt encountered a stale artifact lock left by an interrupted check, and a subsequent run exceeded the local tool timeout. Exact-head CI remains the source of truth for the complete typecheck lanes.


## Production reproduction (2026-09-10)

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed publication no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. An existing Corefile keeps its mode, its uid/gid, and its parent directory's mode across the rewrite instead of silently taking the invoker's group or the helper's restrictive defaults. CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile`, a symlinked `conf.d`, or a chain like `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing file` publish to the final file and keep working; the previous revision of this PR aborted setup on the dangling-chain shape.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

Two review findings against the earlier revision are fixed at the same owner rather than at call sites:

- `resolvePublicationTarget` walks the whole symlink chain (bounded at 40 hops, reporting `ELOOP`) before publishing. The earlier revision handed a dangling chain's link itself to fs-safe, which rejects a symlink destination and aborted setup where `writeFileSync` used to create the final target. A missing parent still fails like `writeFileSync` instead of creating the directory tree.
- `preservePublicationOwnership` runs in fs-safe's `beforeRename` hook and restores the destination's uid/gid on the staged file, because a rename publishes a new inode and `preserveExistingMode` carries only rwx bits. If the invoking user cannot restore them (`EPERM`), the pre-existing privileged fallback takes over — it edits the existing inode, so the owner is not lost.

The branch was rebuilt as one commit on current `main` because the earlier head merged against a newer main whose test harness had been refactored; the regression tests now use that harness.

## Evidence
Level B (registered `dns setup --apply` CLI entry driven in-process against a real temporary filesystem, with `darwin` platform and `brew`/`sudo` subprocesses mocked):
- Atomic publication: with a rename of the Corefile forced to fail, setup rejects and the previous bytes are byte-identical. Red on `main` (`promise resolved instead of rejecting`), green with this change.
- Operator metadata: an existing Corefile at mode `0640` in a `0755` directory whose gid differs from the publisher's is published with the same gid, mode, and directory mode. Red on the earlier revision of this PR (`expected [ 1000, 416 ] to deeply equal [ 10, 416 ]`), green with this change.
- Symlinked/dangling publication: a `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing` chain and a symlinked `conf.d` both publish to the final file. Red on the earlier revision (`Serialized Error: { code: 'symlink', category: 'policy' }`), green with this change.
- All 11 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts`.
- Local lanes for this head: core oxlint on both changed files (0 errors), `node scripts/run-format.mts --check`, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety ratchets, and `git diff --check`.
- Test-line budget: the three regressions add 57 test lines, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/184888-dns-atomic-corefile.txt` (the ratchet's allocation mechanism), so this PR adds no unaccounted test lines. The branch is rebased on current `main`; the local ratchet now reports `Test lines OK ... slack: 1`, which clears the earlier `over by 16` inherited from the older merge snapshot.
Real shipped-CLI run on this head (`node openclaw.mjs dns setup --domain proof.test --apply`, `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (a15387c)`), Linux host with an isolated loopback netns carrying a `100.64.0.1` tailnet address, a documented `process.platform` preload selecting the macOS-gated path, and `brew`/`sudo` shims (no real Homebrew, sudo, or CoreDNS service):

| fixture | observed |
|---|---|
| `Corefile -> Corefile.link -> missing.conf` (dangling chain) | exit 0; `missing.conf` created with `import .../conf.d/*.server`; both links intact |
| existing Corefile mode `0640` in a `0755` directory | exit 0; mode, uid, gid, and directory mode unchanged, import block appended |
| publication forced to fail by `RLIMIT_FSIZE` (1.5 MB Corefile, 2 MB write limit) | CLI rejects; Corefile byte-identical (same sha256), no temp files left |
| control: the previous `writeFileSync` writer under the same limit | file truncated to exactly 1,048,576 bytes |

Evidence files: `~/openclaw-evidence/pr185017-cli-atomic/{scenario-a2,scenario-b,scenario-c}.log` and `SUMMARY.txt`.

- Known boundaries disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the group assertion is guarded and only runs when the test process has an assignable foreign group; the `mode: 0o666 & ~umask` path for a newly created Corefile is implemented but not asserted by the trimmed regression set; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not obtained: an installed-macOS trace against a real CoreDNS install, including an upgrade from the latest stable. The host is Linux, so the macOS path ran behind a disclosed platform preload and `brew`/`sudo` shims; the gid-preservation case was not exercised because no second group is assignable without root.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes (the local checkout uses a shared dependency install that tsgo rejects); CI runs the type lanes for this head.
- Review status for this head: no autoreview helper verdict was produced — the helper's reviewer route failed as unavailable on the authoring host. The ClawSweeper verdict still describes `4154ed2`, the earlier revision; the two P2 findings it lists (ownership, dangling chains) are implemented and regression-covered on this head and need the fresh review to confirm.

prs.title: chore(update): record 2026.11.5-beta.2 in the update compat inventory
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a 2026.11.5-beta.2 install updating to a build from current main has no post-swap compatibility bridges, so its recovery imports can fail with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

## User Impact

User impact: beta.2 users get the same post-swap recovery coverage as 11.3 and beta.1 users when they update to the next build from main.

## Why This Change Was Made

2026.11.5-beta.2 was published to npm on 2026-11-11, but main's update compatibility inventory still stopped at 2026.11.5-beta.1. I regenerated the published window with `pnpm update:compat:gen` from integrity-verified npm tarballs. Every existing entry regenerated byte-identical, and the only change is the new beta.2 entry (77 chunks, commit `c0f42f64814`).

2026.9.37 (extended-stable) is still reported as missing by `pnpm update:compat:check`. Adding it fails the build with `Cannot bridge ... isRetiredPnpmGenerationOfInstall: no equivalent current export`, the same as 2026.9.36. Per the release guide it stays uncovered.

## Evidence

On a Crabbox AWS box (main `ec789a4124d`):

- **Base `pnpm update:compat:check`:** fails with "missing current npm release versions: 2026.11.5-beta.2, 2026.9.37".
- **With this change:** the build passes, and the check reports only 2026.9.37.
- **Packaged tarballs:** of beta.2's 77 inventory chunks, the base package ships 19 and the fixed package ships all 77.
- **Reviews:** autoreview is scoped-clean at P2, and an independent read-only Codex review found nothing.

prs.title: fix(discord): replies show an empty or broken code block when it starts at a message split
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord reply shows an empty code block, or loses its code formatting, when a fenced code block starts right at the point where the reply has to be split into a second message.

With the default limits (2000 chars, 17 lines), a reply with a 14-item list followed by a fenced block is split so the first message ends with the opener and a synthetic closer and nothing between them (`buildDiscordTextChunks`, the send path, on `main`):

```
"...14. Step number 14\n```bash\n```"   <- empty code block in Discord
"```bash\nnpm install\nnpm test\n```\nDone."
```

When the opener lands one to three characters short of the 2000-char cap instead, the opener line itself is cut in half:

```
"aaaa...a\n``"
"`ts\nconst x = 1;\n```\nafter"   <- `ts is prose, and the closing ``` opens an unclosed block
```

## User Impact

User impact: Discord replies with a code block near a message boundary no longer show an empty code block or render the code as text and the rest of the message as code. The opener now starts the next message together with its code.

## Why This Change Was Made

The range helper already keeps a fence opener with its body (`cutBoundary`), but `flush` only used it when the chunk overlapped an inline code span. A plain-text chunk ending on or inside an opener line went through `boundary`, which doesn't know about fences. `flush` now always uses `cutBoundary`.

## Evidence

Current verification on `01e53f1bda1a3cb6ff0f395caa667b65b6c80e6e` (2026-11-12):

- Added a production send-path regression using `sendMessageDiscord`, the real `RequestClient`, and an isolated loopback HTTP server. It checks the default 17-line boundary (15 prose lines followed by an opener/body) and the 2,000-character boundary (1,993 prose characters before the opener), without overriding either limit.
- Both cases fail against the original production chunker: one emits an empty fenced block; the other splits the opening marker. Both pass with the fix. Assertions check the two actual message POST paths, ordered payloads, and delivery receipt IDs.
- The complete chunk and basic-message send suites pass: 83 tests, 7.72 s Vitest duration / 9.85 s wrapper wall time after worker preparation.
- Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and staged test-line budget checks pass. Total regression allocation is now 39 lines (12 chunker + 27 HTTP-boundary).
- Autoreview of the complete change against `826999cd5f76f4867a69869489a4fc51cd5e4a35`, with full surrounding chunk/send/REST/harness source, found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Execution evidence above is separate from that source review.
- This proves outgoing HTTP payloads through the production sender. A live Discord bot/client render and native client screenshots remain unverified. The read-only Discord QA readiness probe failed during Convex lease acquisition before any Discord checks or fixture messages; the QA broker must be available to complete that evidence.

Original implementation evidence:

- New `it.each` case in `extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` (opener after 1990-1994 chars of text). On `main` all five fail; for 1993 the received chunks are `"aaa…\n``"` and `` "`ts\nconst x = 1;\n```\nafter" ``, for 1990 the first chunk ends with `` "\n```ts\n```" ``. They pass with the fix.
- Before/after on 6,000 generated replies (prose, lists, quotes, inline code, emoji, well-formed `` ``` `` / `~~~` blocks) at 2000 and 500 chars: 466 outputs differ, and every difference removes a chunk ending in an empty fenced block (466 before, 0 after). No chunk goes over the limit and no chunk has an unbalanced fence, before or after.
- `pnpm test:extension discord`: 258 files, 2,683 tests pass. The touched test file runs in under 0.1 s of test time. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): rate-limit replies say "try again in a few minutes" when the harness reported a reset time hours away
prs.body:
Closes #195184

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a native harness such as Muse reports a usage limit with a reset time, the user still reads "Please try again in a few minutes", even when the provider says the limit resets hours or days later. Plugins had no way to hand the host a reset time, so the host's reply copy could not use it.

## User Impact

User impact: a rate-limit failure whose provider reported a reset time now says how long to wait, for example `⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in ~3 h.` (seconds, minutes, hours or days). Replies without a reset time are unchanged, provider text never reaches the user (the raw diagnostic stays in the operator log), and the host still owns the wording. The Muse harness passes its typed `quota.resetsAtMs` through as `retryAfterMs`.

## Why This Change Was Made

A thrown harness error can now carry a numeric `retryAfterMs` (milliseconds until the limit lifts), the name the failover signal and the Gateway's 503 envelope already use. `resolveRateLimitResetAt` reads it from a `FailoverError` or from a raw error's cause chain, and the shared reply facts (`resolveReplyFailoverFacts`) expose it as `rateLimitResetAt`, separate from saved-login cooldowns (`soonestCooldownExpiry`) and retry exhaustion.

The copy owners then render the wait from it instead of the generic notice: `renderRateLimitReplyCopy` in its direct branch (which returned before reaching the cooldown copy), `renderRateLimitOrOverloadedCopy` after the existing provider-hint check, the embedded runner's incomplete-turn and terminal-preparation copy (the path `agent --local` and Gateway turns actually take), and the auto-reply error handler, where a known reset time now outranks the generic quota-429 facet the same way recorded retry exhaustion already does. One wait formatter serves all of them. Muse sets `retryAfterMs` from `TurnError.quota.resetsAtMs`, the follow-up left open in #195148.

## Evidence

Current verification on `931964c463a5342ed2ce1846a152dc12e10518fc` (2026-11-12): merged `main` at `9ca7932563ff3a8d2d3eca37e50d6ea7b031a527`. The only conflict was the request-error-facts import block: both the rate-limit reset helper and main's `AgentHarnessModelRequestPolicyError` handling are preserved. The original PR's added/removed lines remain unchanged (14 files, +177/-23). Independent source review found no actionable issue in the resolution.

- Current focused verification: 142 core tests plus four Muse `surfaces` cases pass. The other 49 Muse cases were not rerun; the existing limitation below remains.
- The resolved file passes targeted type-aware lint and formatting; the PR delta passes whitespace checks.
- Original CLI before/after proof below remains applicable to the unchanged production patch. Fresh CI is required for the pushed head; prior-head CI is not current-head proof.

From source on `main` at 54b059c478 (merged into this branch), macOS, Node 26.7.0. Shipped `openclaw.mjs agent --local` entry point, the real `@muse-code/sdk` MSP transport, and the repository's `extensions/muse/src/test-support/fake-muse.mjs` as the Muse binary (its `quota` prompt reports `limitKind: tierLimit`, `resetsAtMs` = 2030-01-02T03:04Z). Fresh state directory, `meta/muse-spark-1.3` routed through the `muse` runtime, first turn `hello`, second turn `quota`.

Before (`main`):
```
$ openclaw agent --local --json --message quota
      "text": "⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in a few minutes.",
```

After (same setup plus this change):
```
$ openclaw agent --local --json --message quota
      "text": "⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in ~1151 days.",
$ openclaw agent --local --message quota
⚠️ The AI service needs a short break. Please try again in ~1151 days.
```
Operator stderr keeps the diagnostic in both cases (`[plugins] Muse Code: Muse usage limit reached (tierLimit); resets at 2030-01-02T03:04:00.000Z. fixture quota exhausted`); none of it appears in the reply. The `hello` control turn still answers `started: hello`.

An earlier revision of this branch changed only the copy renderer and the coercion site; the same CLI run still printed "a few minutes", which is how the incomplete-turn and facet paths above were found. The final revision was rerun end to end as shown.

Tests:
- `pnpm test` on `src/agents/failover/user-copy.test.ts`, `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn-resolution.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-preparation.test.ts`: 142 passed. `extensions/muse/harness.test.ts -t surfaces`: 4 passed (the quota row now asserts `retryAfterMs`).
- New cases: reset-time copy for 45 s / 90 min / 3 h / 10 days plus a past reset falling back to the generic notice, for both `renderRateLimitReplyCopy` and `renderRateLimitOrOverloadedCopy`; `coerceToFailoverError` keeps `retryAfterMs` as `rateLimitResetAt` and `resolveRateLimitResetAt` reads it through a wrapper's `cause`; the terminal reply for a `FailoverError`, the raw harness error and a wrapper around it, through both `buildKnownAgentRunFailureReplyPayload` and `buildExternalRunFailureReply`. With the production files reverted to `main`, the copy, coercion and reply cases fail and the Muse quota row fails; all pass with the change.
- Test-line budget: 70 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/harness-rate-limit-reset-copy.txt`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files: clean.

Not covered: the three `cancels only its own catalog check on a shared host` cases in `harness.test.ts` time out after 120 s on this macOS host both with and without this change; the rest of that file passes. The red `check-test-types-core-5` job on the earlier heads is `test/chat-history-legacy-refusal-notice.e2e.test.ts(46,45)` from main's 86cb0bde5b, which also fails on `main` at 75c2c49cec. Local autoreview / local ClawSweeper were not run.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selected mentions can grant session access, but the composer says only that it will notify; later notification failures also need a visible outcome.

## User Impact

The composer and queued message show Notify or invite, explain the creator/admin access effect, and display scoped mention-delivery failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep existing mention selection and toast presentation; update their disclosure and bounded failure event handler.

Stack step **16/17**, based on [fix/guest-access-11-runtime-adapters-20261026](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/tree/fix%2Fguest-access-11-runtime-adapters-20261026). Review and merge in order; each upper PR contains only its own slice against its predecessor.

Previous: [preserve invitation authority through runtime writes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184513).

Next: [enable invited roles; add full-stack behavior tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515).

Stack order: [complete stack](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#stack-order).

## Evidence

Slice head: `bb2aa8653b242d3074c98cd9ba199d8c08a23ea7`, on fixed main `5bf0c41a03f1dba03d625460607ed5b959710458`. The complete 13-file integration matrix passed 46/46 on pinned Bun at `ddc49fd63d3b82e41eb6c74af4ad935a56aebc8f` before this main rebase. Main's canonical fixture repairs are preserved and duplicate prerequisite changes removed. Prefixes are not separately built locally; this prefix's hosted CI and review are recorded below.

UI mention/composer/queue coverage passed 67 cases before the export-preserving mock repair; the touched 28-test mention file passed again afterward. UI production/test types passed. The real toast exports remain in the partial mock, satisfying the mock-export guard.

The optional connected-UI toast recording is not added: existing mention-handler tests cover the failure toast, and Gateway event tests cover recipient isolation. The captures below establish actual component wording/layout only. This restack changes no UI source.

The [stack evidence ledger](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184515#evidence) records runtime results, prior build/upgrade proof and limits. Integration tests are owned by the final activation PR. Current-head hosted CI and review remain required before landing.

### Current-head qualification

[Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40526307443) passed at `bb2aa8653b242d3074c98cd9ba199d8c08a23ea7`. The [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184514#issuecomment-6414264871) covers the same head and reports no actionable findings or required rank-up moves. Merge in the recorded stack order.

## Change size

Production **+23/-6**; tests **+60/-9**.

prs.title: fix(cli): stop the ID rebind publication wait when the command is cancelled
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw id rebind` commits the key rotation first, then waits up to 30 s for Discovery to publish the new binding. Ctrl+C during that wait did not stop it: the loop kept reading `openclawId.people` every second and only reported when the wait ended.

So on a slow publication an interrupted command:

- held the terminal for the rest of the 30 s window,
- kept issuing Gateway RPCs after the user asked it to stop,
- and then printed a result as if the command had finished normally (`Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect by themselves.` / `Discovery doesn't have the new keys yet`), which reads as "the move may still be pending" even though the move was already committed and the keys already rotated.

The read side of the same flow was fixed in #197747 (merged): interrupted `openclaw id status` reads exit promptly. The publication wait in `rebind` was left out, so an interrupted *mutation* still behaved like an uninterruptible one.

## Why This Change Was Made

`waitForPublication` is the only place that keeps working after a committed move, so this is a targeted change to that loop, its sleep, and the receipt printed when the wait is cancelled:

- `waitForPublication` reads the ambient cancellation signal once, checks it before each Discovery read, and hands it to the sleep. The in-flight `openclawId.people` read now also carries the signal (the read helper gained that parameter in #197747).
- `runRebind`'s publication `catch` distinguishes "the wait was cancelled" from "the wait failed". A cancelled wait reports the committed move once and returns; a genuine failure keeps the existing `Publication check failed` warning and exit code 2.
- `docs/cli/id.md` documents the interrupted-wait receipt next to the existing committed-but-unreadable receipt, so the `cancelled: true` field is not an undocumented output change.
- The new receipt says the move is committed, that Discovery checking stopped because the command was cancelled, and to run `openclaw id status` instead of repeating `rebind` — repeating it would rotate keys again. It does not set an exit code: the SIGINT handler already owns the exit status, and the mutation itself succeeded.

This follows the repo's existing rule for committed mutations under Ctrl+C (see the suspend CLI): a committed mutation still prints its receipt exactly once, it just stops waiting for the follow-up work.

## User Impact

- Ctrl+C during `openclaw id rebind`'s publication wait returns immediately instead of after up to 30 s, and stops reading Discovery.
- The user still learns that the move committed and what to run next, so an interrupt cannot be mistaken for "nothing happened" (which would tempt a second `rebind` and another key rotation).
- No behaviour change when the wait completes normally or fails for a real reason.
- Exit status stays owned by the signal handler; no new exit codes, options, or output fields for successful runs.

## Evidence

### Real CLI against an isolated Gateway

The shipped CLI (`src/entry.ts id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …`) against the shipped
Gateway (`src/entry.ts gateway`, real loopback WebSocket, real state directory, real key files
and recovery kit). A local Discovery stand-in answers descriptor reads and then refuses the
post-commit descriptor write with `503`, so the Gateway's own publisher cannot finish and the
stored `published_binding_seq` stays behind: the delayed-publication condition this wait exists
for. No Gateway or CLI code is replaced. The harness watches the Gateway log for
`moved to new keys` and sends one SIGINT 1.5 s later.

| Run | SIGINT to settle | Exit | Printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| current `main` (`src/cli/id-cli.ts` from `origin/main`), `--json` | 30.8 s | 0 | the late wait result, `published: false` |
| current `main`, text | 29.9 s | 0 | the normal "moved" result |
| this branch, `--json` | **0.65 s** | **130** | the committed receipt, `cancelled: true` |
| this branch, text | **0.63 s** | **130** | the committed receipt, three lines |

Before (`origin/main` `src/cli/id-cli.ts`), the interrupt is ignored — 30 s more of Discovery
reads, then a result that says nothing about the move that already committed:

```console
$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code … --json   # SIGINT after the commit
{"moved": true, "bindingSeq": 2, "published": false}      # +30.8 s, exit 0

$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …           # SIGINT after the commit
Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect by themselves.       # +29.9 s, exit 0
Discovery doesn't have the new keys yet; the Gateway keeps publishing them (openclaw id status).
If you did this because you think a key leaked, also check Your devices and People.
```

With this branch the receipt is printed once and the command stops reading Discovery:

```console
$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code … --json   # SIGINT after the commit
{
  "moved": true,
  "bindingSeq": 2,
  "published": null,
  "cancelled": true,
  "nextStep": "openclaw id status"
}                                                          # +0.65 s, exit 130

$ openclaw id rebind --kit-stdin --yes --code …           # SIGINT after the commit
Moved to new keys (committed).
Stopped checking Discovery: the command was cancelled.
Run openclaw id status to check publication. Do not repeat rebind: it rotates keys again.
                                                           # +0.63 s, exit 130
```

### Regression tests at the CLI boundary

In the existing `id-cli.commands.test.ts` suite (production scope gate, ambient `AsyncWorkScope`,
same RPC fixture as its sibling cases). Base = `origin/main` with only `src/cli/id-cli.ts` reverted.

| Check | Base (`origin/main`) | With this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reports the committed move once when the publication wait is cancelled (json=true)` | FAIL — `expected { moved: true, bindingSeq: 2, published: false } to deeply equal { moved: true, bindingSeq: 2, published: null, cancelled: true, nextStep: "openclaw id status" }` (it kept polling, then reported the wait result) | PASS |
| `reports the committed move once when the publication wait is cancelled (json=false)` | FAIL — `expected 'Moved to new keys. Devices reconnect …' to contain 'Moved to new keys (committed)'` | PASS |
| `id-cli` suite (`src/cli/id-cli.commands.test.ts`, `src/cli/id-cli-rebind.test.ts`) | 2 failed \| 10 passed | 12 passed |
| `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` on both code files, `oxfmt --check docs/cli/id.md` | clean | clean |

Both new cases assert that no further Discovery read happens after the cancel and that no
failure text or exit code is produced.

Remaining gap, stated plainly: the real Discovery service and the iroh tunnel are not exercised
here — this host has no Rust toolchain, so the bundled iroh binding is unavailable and the
repository's own `src/gateway/server.openclaw-id-rebind.test.ts` skips for the same reason
(`describe.skipIf(!hasBinding)`). The tunnel/key-switch side of a re-bind therefore still rests
on CI and on a machine with `pnpm build:iroh`. `tsgo` also cannot run here (its native binary
needs GLIBC ≥ 2.34), so typechecking is left to CI; the change uses existing typed helpers
(`setTimeout(..., { signal })`, `AbortSignal.throwIfAborted`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Profile confusing personal GitHub publishing with shared agent access and displaying issuer-qualified proxy subjects as names and linked emails.

## User Impact

Users can see how to publish a PR as themselves without changing the shared default. The GitHub section is now **GitHub connections**, with the personal publishing choice explained directly in its row and shared-owner guidance in help. prs.title: fix(ci): right-size serial central type checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary PRs reserve a 4-vCPU runner for serial extension/script type checks whose compiler policy uses at most two Go threads.

## User Impact

Reduces the requested runner to 2 vCPUs for this measured workload. Type-check coverage and execution order stay the same. Full, frozen, release, compatibility, root-test and non-hosted plans retain their current allocation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing ordinary-PR capability and selected graph names identify the narrow workload. Only its admission label changes; the planner's legacy runner identity remains intact.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith's 24-hour sample: 939 central type jobs, maximum memory 29.015% on the current 4-vCPU machine; the sampled workload runs `extensions-test` then `scripts`. [Maximum-memory job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43158875747/job/130986258062).
- Planner regression: the two new positive cases fail on the base with the expected 4-vCPU versus 2-vCPU mismatch. All 44 planner tests pass with the change (52.19s file duration, including existing subprocess integration cases).
- Independent source review and local ClawSweeper found no blockers on `baca36ea403c..0e9ff11ca30e`.
- Targeted script lint, script typecheck, test-tooling typecheck, formatting and whitespace checks pass. [Exact-head CI and its final gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43242358803).

### Linux results

All samples use the same source tree. Compiler build-info files were removed before each sample; OS page cache was uncontrolled.

| Workload | Samples | Median | p95 | Peak compiler RSS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4-CPU affinity on the 4-vCPU VM | 5 | 43.064s | 44.386s | 4.071 GiB |
| 2-CPU affinity on the same VM | 5 | 42.037s | 44.981s | 4.067 GiB |
| Physical 2-vCPU VM, 7.65 GiB RAM | 5 | 51.207s | 55.028s | 4.066 GiB |

The paired comparison passed the predeclared rule: median -2.4%, p95 +1.3%, requested CPUs -50%. [CPU comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43243121409).

The separate small VM was slower than the affinity samples; those cross-machine times are not a causal performance comparison. It passed all five workloads. Blacksmith measured **4,792,717,312 / 8,218,361,856 bytes (58.3%)** peak job memory across 182 samples, including setup, and **zero OOM events**. [Physical capacity qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43244543739/job/131273699624).

Both successful Testbox leases were stopped. Their backing Actions jobs can show cancellation because the delegated lifecycle owns teardown. An earlier setup-only attempt stopped before any sample because the harness compared the original commit ID with the transport's carrier commit; the corrected harness verifies the exact source tree instead.

No invoice savings are claimed. The measured result supports using the smaller allocation for these graphs; full and other graph shapes retain their original capacity. The change adds 7 production lines and 44 test lines without a new configuration surface.

### Acceptance rule recorded before benchmarking

Use the unchanged committed workload `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --ci-graphs-json '["extensions-test","scripts"]'` with `CI=1`. Run five serial A/B pairs on one Linux Blacksmith Testbox, alternating 4-CPU and 2-CPU affinity. Remove only these two graphs' generated build-info files before each sample; OS page cache remains uncontrolled. Record actual CPU/RAM, wall time, peak RSS, exit status, median and p95. Reject any failed sample or a candidate median/p95 wall-time regression of 20% or more. This isolates CPU allocation; it does not simulate lower physical RAM.

Require an actual 2-vCPU runner to complete both graphs with no OOM and less than 80% peak memory, including setup. The PR's own change selects root-test tooling and correctly retains the 4-vCPU job, so the physical 2-vCPU proof uses the existing focused Testbox workflow instead; the criteria are unchanged. Compare complete-job duration and billed allocation with the baseline where workloads match, distinguishing runner qualification from a causal billing claim. The expected gain is half the requested CPU allocation, not a measured invoice reduction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Perplexity decision model id `pplx-decider-v1.2` (added in #195641) is printed as `***.2` in human CLI output, for example by `openclaw capability model list`, `capability model providers` and `capability model inspect`. The id cannot be read or copied from the listing.

## User Impact

User impact: the model id is shown in full. `--json` output was already correct and is unchanged. Perplexity API keys are still masked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The vendor token rule for Perplexity API keys matches `pplx-` followed by 10 or more key characters. The published model id has the same prefix and fits that shape up to the dot, so console redaction masked it. The rule now skips text that starts with `pplx-decider-v`. Every other `pplx-` string is still masked, including one that starts with `pplx-decider` without the version marker. A real key would have to begin with the nine characters `decider-v` to be missed. A stricter lookahead that pins the whole version shape is rejected by the safe-regex guard on the default pattern table, so the exemption uses the plain prefix.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at f471c34c1e, Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory.

Before:
```
$ openclaw capability model list | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*","name":"Decider v1.2"'
"id":"***.2","name":"Decider v1.2"
$ openclaw capability model providers | grep perplexity-decisions
{"provider":"perplexity-decisions","count":1,"defaults":["***.2"],"available":true,"configured":false,"selected":false}
$ openclaw capability model inspect --model perplexity-decisions/pplx-decider-v1.2 | grep '"id"'
  "id": "***.2",
$ openclaw capability model list --json | grep pplx
    "id": "pplx-decider-v1.2",
```

After:
```
$ openclaw capability model list | grep -o '"id":"[^"]*","name":"Decider v1.2"'
"id":"pplx-decider-v1.2","name":"Decider v1.2"
$ openclaw capability model providers | grep perplexity-decisions
{"provider":"perplexity-decisions","count":1,"defaults":["pplx-decider-v1.2"],"available":true,"configured":false,"selected":false}
$ openclaw capability model inspect --model perplexity-decisions/pplx-decider-v1.2 | grep '"id"'
  "id": "pplx-decider-v1.2",
$ openclaw capability model list --json | grep pplx
    "id": "pplx-decider-v1.2",
```

Unchanged control with the fix (a key-shaped value is still masked):
```
$ openclaw capability model inspect --model pplx-abcdefghij12345
Model not found: pplx-a…2345
```

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/logging --maxWorkers=3`: 57 files, 751 passed, 5 skipped, including the safe-regex guard, the prefilter fixtures and the byte-identity fixtures.
- `redact.test.ts`: the "preserves ..." case now includes the model id and fails on `main` (`***.2`); the vendor token case now also requires `pplx-abcdefghij12345` and `pplx-deciderabcdefghij` to be masked.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged`, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

prs.title: fix(goals): require a note to resume a blocked goal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resuming a blocked goal with an empty note made it active again and queued another pursuit turn. The operator had not said what changed, so the same blocker came back. A blocked goal now stays blocked until the resume includes a note. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without one.

The command table and the blocked-status paragraph still told people that a bare `/goal resume` makes a blocked goal active. Those two lines now say the note is required, and that an empty resume leaves the goal blocked.

## Evidence

Head `834bd8c1ed7` on macOS. An isolated loopback Gateway served the Control UI. Session `agent:main:main` held a blocked goal whose objective was `Read the operator inbox.`

In the browser, Resume with an empty note showed `Enter what changed before resuming.` The Gateway did not receive `sessions.goal.update`.

Typing `The mail grant is still missing, so stop this goal.` and choosing Resume called the Gateway. The card changed from `Goal blocked` to `Pursuing goal`, and the same run started a model turn.

```console
[ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
[ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 agent=main session=main stream=lifecycle phase=start
[openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A blocked goal cannot resume from the Control UI until the operator enters what changed. That noted Resume is admitted by `sessions.goal.update` and starts the model continuation. An empty note stays on the card and does not call the Gateway.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node v26.12.1, worktree `/tmp/oc-192883`, head `834bd8c1ed7`. Loopback Gateway and its Control UI in Chromium. Model `xai/grok-4.7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Open the chat for `agent:main:main` with a blocked goal. Choose Resume with an empty note. Enter a note and choose Resume again. Read the Gateway log for `sessions.goal.update` and the following model turn.
- **Evidence after fix:** Control UI text and Gateway log:

  ```console
  empty note: Enter what changed before resuming.
  after note: Pursuing goal
  [ws] res ok sessions.goal.update 65ms runId=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49
  [ws] event agent run=aa506ced-2261-46a0-b6a5-c3948291ae49 stream=lifecycle phase=start
  [openai-transport] responses start provider=xai model=grok-4.7 sessionKey=agent:main:main
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The empty Resume stays on `Goal blocked` and does not call the Gateway. The noted Resume returns `sessions.goal.update`, switches the card to `Pursuing goal`, and starts the `grok-4.7` turn.
- **What was not tested:** A goal database written by the latest stable package, then opened by this build. The blocked goal in this run was created on this head.

## Summary

A blocked goal stays blocked until `/goal resume` or the Control UI Resume includes a note. The command table and the blocked-status paragraph say that. Paused, limited, and completed goals can still resume without a note.
