prs.title: fix: sessions keep using an old fallback model after the default model is changed
prs.body:
Part of #88372 (the stale-catalog and Google 401 symptoms in that issue are not addressed here)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat that was moved to an automatic fallback model by v2026.4.26 through v2026.6.0 keeps sending every turn to that fallback, and keeps announcing the old model as the one selected, after the configured primary is switched to a different model. This happens both on channel and Control UI replies and in `openclaw agent`, the gateway `agent` method and the embedded TUI (`openclaw chat`, `openclaw terminal`, `openclaw tui --local`).

## User Impact

After changing `agents.defaults.model.primary`, those sessions go back to the configured primary on their next message, without deleting session state or running `/model default`. Explicit `/model` pins, locked sessions and self-origin subagent selections keep their model.

## Why This Change Was Made

Those builds stored the fallback as `modelOverrideSource: "auto"` together with the primary it fell back from. Recovery only ever probes that recorded origin, so once the origin is no longer the configured primary there is no probe to run and nothing clears the pin. Heartbeats already treated that case as stale; ordinary turns skipped the check entirely. The stale-origin check in `stored-model-override.ts` now applies to ordinary turns too, as ClawSweeper's review of the issue suggested, and both owners of stored-override selection use it: the reply path resets through the existing reset in `createModelSelectionState`, and agent command selection (`src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`) resets through its existing session repair, next to the no-origin legacy repair. Both keep the auth profile pin. For that, agent command selection resolves the primary (default or channel model override) before the repair instead of after it; the block moved unchanged. Ordinary turns only reset a real fallback: an entry whose override equals its origin is a self-origin subagent selection (`hasSessionActiveAutoModelFallback`) and stays. The heartbeat branch and the no-origin legacy path are unchanged, so the function is renamed from `isStaleHeartbeatAutoFallbackOverride` to `isStaleAutoFallbackOverride`. `docs/concepts/model-failover.md` gets one sentence for the new rule. Nothing in the closed cross-references tried this path; #115808 (open) handles auto pins that have no origin metadata, and this handles the ones that do.

## Evidence

**Real turns on Windows 11:** `getReplyFromConfig` (reply path) and `agentCommandFromIngress` with the embedded TUI's arguments (agent command path), no mocks, plugins disabled, a real on-disk session store, and two local OpenAI-compatible providers that log each request. Config primary is `newprov/new-model`; the session was seeded the way those builds left it, on `oldprov/fallback-model` with source `auto`, then sent two turns.

| Seeded origin | Path | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `firstprov/first-model` (primary since changed) | reply | both turns sent to `oldprov/fallback-model`, turn 1 says "Model Fallback: oldprov/fallback-model (selected firstprov/first-model; selected model unavailable)", pin still stored | both turns sent to `newprov/new-model`, no fallback notice, override cleared from the store after turn 1 |
| `firstprov/first-model` (primary since changed) | agent command | both turns sent to `oldprov/fallback-model`, pin still stored | both turns sent to `newprov/new-model`, override cleared after turn 1 |
| `newprov/new-model` (still the primary) | reply | turn 1 probes `newprov/new-model`, turn 2 on `oldprov/fallback-model` | same |
| `newprov/new-model` (still the primary) | agent command | turn 1 probes `newprov/new-model` and clears the pin, turn 2 on `newprov/new-model` | same |
| `oldprov/fallback-model` (self-origin) | both | both turns on `oldprov/fallback-model` | same |

- `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` adds an ordinary-turn case that resets a fallback whose origin is no longer the primary (asserting reason `stale`) and one that keeps a self-origin selection; `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` checks that an ordinary turn with a replaced origin reaches directives on the primary; `model-selection.configured.test.ts` checks that agent command selection picks the primary and clears the stored override. With main's four source files the reset, get-reply and agent command cases fail (2 failed, 40 passed for the two reply files; 1 failed, 21 passed for the agent command file); the self-origin case passes on both.
- `--maxWorkers=1`: those three files plus `model-selection.test.ts` and `agent-runner-auto-fallback.test.ts`, 150 passed. `model-selection.turn-model-differential.test.ts`, 9 passed. `src/commands/agent.test.ts`, 70 passed and 1 timed out at 120 s ("rejects a missing harness-owned session before local CLI dispatch"); that test has no session entry, and it times out the same way run alone with main's source files.
- Test cost, `--maxWorkers=1` wall per file on a busy laptop: `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` 97 s, `model-selection.configured.test.ts` 74 s, `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` 148 s, mostly transform; the new tests take 82 ms, 10 ms, 11 ms and 413 ms. No timers, sleeps or gateway boots. In CI (Ubuntu, Node 24.21.0), after the 09-28 merge from main, each file passed in full in its own shard: `model-selection.resolved-pin.test.ts` 21 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-3-4, the new ones in 21 and 8 ms; `model-selection.configured.test.ts` 27 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-31, the new one in 10 ms; `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` 14 tests in job checks-node-changed-compact-large-16, the new one in 53 ms.
- oxfmt (including the docs file), oxlint, `tsgo:core`, the messaging and commands core-test tsgo graphs, `git diff --check`, and the assertion, line-cap and max-lines ratchets pass. The whole-tree `format-docs.mts --check` cannot start on Windows (it passes every docs file to oxfmt on one command line).

On Windows every test in `get-reply.auto-fallback.test.ts` fails in `afterEach` on unmodified main (13 of 13, `EPERM` removing the temp store dir while SQLite still has it open; there are no assertion failures), and passes on Linux CI. The get-reply runs above used a local-only change that skips that `EPERM` on win32 in `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts`; it is not part of this PR.

Not covered: on the reply path, when the origin is still the primary, a successful turn-1 probe did not clear the pin in the local run (row 3, same on main): the clear in `agent-runner-auto-fallback.ts` was rejected by its `updatedAt` guard because the stored entry had been updated during the turn. The agent command path clears it (row 4). This was observed by calling `getReplyFromConfig` directly and is not confirmed through a built gateway; it is separate from this change. Agent command runs with hidden session effects (`suppressVisibleSessionEffects`) do not write the reset, so they still use the old pin until the next visible turn. The live runs use local stub providers rather than Groq, Google or LiteLLM. The issue's other symptoms, stale ids left in `models.providers.*.models` and the partial-onboarding Google 401, are outside this fix, as the review noted.

prs.title: fix(memory): keep backfilled snippets tied to their sources
prs.body:
Closes #157827

## Current Status - October 31

**Draft; blocked on reinforced legacy evidence handling.** Fresh-store staging proof does not qualify an existing reinforced store. No maintainer decision has been posted in response to the October 4 migration concerns, and the proposed migration remains unapplied.

Proposed decision for the memory owner: retain ambiguous legacy rows and their original support without redistribution, but exclude them from new promotion until their provenance is resolved. This is a proposal, not an implemented retention or promotion change. Previously promoted `MEMORY.md` content requires separate validation; this PR does not repair it or claim verified corruption.

Before ready: accept the legacy policy, implement it in the existing store/promotion owner, resolve conflicts, and exercise pre-fix reinforced state through backfill and actual promotion, including edited text at the same location, multiple legacy rows, and already-promoted state. No new code or tests are claimed on October 31; head remains `1c91be19e628e548f1b1e8ecc16aeeefeeec09fe`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes misleading source citations when `memory rem-backfill --stage-short-term` stages a REM summary drawn from several nonadjacent lines but attaches only the first line's location.

## User Impact

Freshly staged short-term memories retain each contributing source location together with the text it supports. Coalesced atomic claims stay compact instead of absorbing transient details from the surrounding source line.

There is no configuration or persisted-format change, but per-source snippets change persisted claim hashes and entry keys. Rerunning backfill regenerates grounded-only entries, not all previously staged entries. It does not rewrite existing `MEMORY.md` content. The reported final wrong-citation outcome in `MEMORY.md` remains unverified, as clarified on the issue.

## Open Upgrade Blocker

The September 27 review identified a valid gap: `removeGroundedShortTermCandidates` retains an old merged entry if it has any recall or daily support. The new per-source keys do not replace that reinforced entry. The real CLI proof below covers fresh and repeated grounded-only staging, not this upgrade case. This PR is not merge-ready until existing-store handling is resolved and proved.

Deleting reinforced entries or copying their aggregate counts into each new source would lose or misattribute valid evidence. No such migration or retention change has been made. The next scoped proof must seed a pre-fix SQLite row with recall/daily support, run backfill, and verify preserved evidence without a promotable misleading citation; final promotion also needs examination because it rehydrates candidates from live source ranges.

October 4: source-reviewed the proposed upgrade patch and [reported two concrete risks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/157912#issuecomment-5979542710): transferring old support to unrelated text edited at the same location, and losing accumulated counts when multiple legacy entries reuse a stale replacement snapshot. The proposal has not been applied or executed. Existing evidence retention/promotion policy and a real final-promotion regression remain unresolved; the branch also needs conflict resolution before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Staging now resolves every reference against the same scratch copy used for the preview. Joined summaries use the corresponding source snippet; recognized atomic claims retain the existing extraction rules. Source resolution finishes before replacing the prior grounded candidates.

The unchanged Markdown parser is shared with staging through a sibling module, keeping normalization and line numbering consistent without growing the already over-cap evidence file. Preview rendering, promotion policy, scores and day buckets are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Red on the base: the registered backfill CLI persisted one merged entry for two nonadjacent short preferences. A second regression caught display-time colon trimming retaining merged text at the first location.
- After rebasing onto `b9dc1ac9b366`: 96 evidence/promotion tests passed, then all 3 CLI regressions passed after adapting their mocks to the current host SDK imports. The earlier head also passed 268 focused tests and its full changed-file gate.
- The three new CLI cases use real temporary Markdown and SQLite state, covering per-source text/locations, repeated backfill, coalesced atomic claims and live-source rehydration. Deleting a source rejects its candidate. Configuration and manager acquisition are mocked; this is not a full Gateway E2E claim.
- Real CLI proof: `pnpm openclaw memory rem-backfill --path <isolated-workspace>/memory/2025-01-01.md --stage-short-term --json`, using isolated home/state/config and `memory.search.provider: none`, exited 0. The supported wrapper rebuilt the current source. No command, manager, or persistence mocks were used. Direct read-only inspection of the resulting SQLite store verified the rows below. Running the same CLI again reported 2 staged and 2 replaced entries.
- Fresh new-file cost: all 3 cases passed in 33.11s wrapper wall (29.79s Vitest, 21.39s compiler preparation; 799ms case execution).
- Fresh checks passed: production extension typecheck, formatting, line/maximum-line/assertion ratchets, plugin boundaries, doctor contract tests, dependency checks, and `git diff --check`. The all-extension test typecheck was stopped after 8m47s under local memory pressure; the remaining changed-file checks and refreshed full CI are not claimed green.
- Independent review found only the obsolete staged test imports; the reviewed working-tree correction has been staged. No other actionable P0-P2 finding. This proves CLI staging, not a Gateway/model run or the unverified final `MEMORY.md` corruption claim.

Sanitized rows read from the actual CLI-created `plugin_state_entries` store:

```json
[
  {"path":"memory/2025-01-01.md","startLine":2,"endLine":2,"snippet":"Always use UTC.","groundedCount":2},
  {"path":"memory/2025-01-01.md","startLine":4,"endLine":4,"snippet":"Prefer tea.","groundedCount":2}
]
```

prs.title: fix(retry): honor nested channel hints behind invalid metadata
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: empty or invalid `parameters.retry_after` metadata on an outer error prevents the shared channel retry runner from honoring a valid hint in its response or nested error. For example, it can retry after the 400 ms backoff despite a nested response requesting one second.

## User Impact

Channel requests using the default hint reader wait for the available provider-requested delay even when an earlier wrapper contains incomplete metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the first finite hint in the existing root, response, nested-error order. Missing or invalid hints fall through; finite hints, including zero, retain their precedence. The existing runner continues to own retry admission, injected readers, backoff, jitter, and delay caps. No public signatures, configuration, or exports change.

## Evidence

The earlier baseline reproduction had six fake-clock timing failures on the original production code. The repair retains ten distinct cases for invalid outer metadata, nested fallback, finite and zero precedence, and default backoff alongside main's newer coverage.

- Follow-up review removed two duplicate cap tests. The existing table still covers a 45-second hint capped at 30 seconds by default and allowed at 45 seconds with an explicit 60-second retry-after cap.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/retry-policy.test.ts src/infra/retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 38 tests passed across both owning files, 4.79 seconds wrapper wall time.
- Type-aware test lint, formatting, whitespace, and the documented test-line budget passed after the cleanup. Source-backed core lint from the unchanged production repair also passed. The unique allocation now matches the remaining 76 added test lines; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Fresh independent reviews found no actionable code findings. Main `3115c80e8` was integrated without rewriting existing PR commits; its current tests and the distinct PR regressions remain.

Validation gaps: no live channel/provider/Gateway trace with real transport, full build/test, or broader production/test type graphs were run. Fake-clock proof does not claim a live provider result. Exact-head CI is pending on the follow-up cleanup.

prs.title: fix(exec): preserve empty quoted values during shell preflight
prs.body:
Related: #154513

## What Problem This Solves

Shell preflight drops intentionally empty quoted option values. `env --argv0 "" python3 bad.py` then loses its interpreter position and bypasses the Python source check; Node target extraction similarly misses a preload following empty inline code. This repair also addresses the reported POSIX backslash-newline discrepancy in the same permissive shell tokenizer.

## User Impact

Shell analysis keeps empty words and their comment boundaries. Outside single quotes, permissive shell parsing removes backslash-LF without creating an argument or starting a word. The public process-command parser retains its existing empty-entry/backslash behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict is reconciled using main's existing word-start state rather than adding a second tracker. Strict raw-syntax rejection remains intact: both strict tokenization and the actual `planShellAuthorization` entry point continue refusing line continuations. Permissive preflight normalization does not establish execution approval.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main, the empty-word/continuation regressions and both original script-target cases failed. Through the actual ExecTool preflight flow, the empty `env` value caused the malformed Python command to start and return a completed exit-1 result on this host, instead of rejecting with a `not_started` receipt. The repair rejects before launch with the expected Python shell-injection error.
- The Node `--eval "" --require ./preload.js` case executes its real preload and returns `preload`; this is a compatibility control, not a claimed baseline failure.
- Four owning files pass: 67 tests and 3 Windows-only skips, 99.74s total wrapper wall, including utility behavior, script metadata, full ExecTool preflight, and actual approval-plan refusal. Cold transformation dominates the preflight file's 93.27s duration; test execution accounts for 3%.
- Targeted owning-file TypeScript graph, production and test type-aware lint, formatting, diff checks, and the documented test-line budget passed. The unique 68-line allocation accounts for the distinct tokenizer, execution-boundary, metadata, and approval regressions against current main.
- Existing control-command and approval-binding consumer files: 43 tests passed, 4.46s total wrapper wall. CI timing is pending.
- This is a real ExecTool/preflight/subprocess component chain with the fixture's existing approval stub. No live Gateway/model/user-approval transport or native Windows execution proof is claimed; the full repository suite was not run.

prs.title: fix(meeting): own a fresh root admission for agent consults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #142610.

Every spoken question in a Google Meet agent-mode session fails with a misleading
`Gateway is draining; new tasks are not accepted` error, even though the gateway is
healthy. `consultMeetingAgent()` in `src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts` calls
`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent()` directly, without acquiring its own root-work
admission. Because the consult runs inside the same async chain that handled the
`googlemeet.create` request, it inherits that request's AsyncLocalStorage
root-work context — a context that is already `released` by the time a
participant actually asks a question minutes later. `enqueueCommandInLane()`
then rejects the consult via `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()`,
which returns `true` for a released inherited root.

The browser Talk path (`src/gateway/talk-client-agent-consult.ts`) already
handles this correctly by acquiring an independent root admission with
`runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission(tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission)` before
running the consult, and releasing it in a `finally`. The meeting path omitted
this step.

## Fix

`consultMeetingAgent()` now acquires its own root-work admission outside the
inherited (possibly-released) context before calling
`consultRealtimeVoiceAgent()`, mirroring the Talk path exactly, and releases it
once the consult settles. If admission is refused (a genuine drain/suspension),
it now throws `GatewayDrainingError` from an accurate state instead of from a
stale one.

## Evidence

Added a regression test that reproduces the real bug shape: it opens a root
admission (simulating the `googlemeet.create` request), schedules the consult
call as an async descendant of that root's callback (so it inherits the store
via Node's AsyncLocalStorage propagation, exactly like a transcript-triggered
callback registered during meeting creation), releases the root (simulating the
finished creation request), and only then lets the consult proceed. It asserts
that `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()` is `false` at the point the
consult actually runs — i.e. a fresh, open admission was acquired instead of the
stale released one.

Confirmed the test fails without the fix, for the intended reason:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts

 × |unit| ... > consults successfully under a fresh admission after the meeting's creation-request root released
   → expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 Tests  1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

And passes with the fix restored:

```
$ git checkout HEAD -- src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts

 ✓ |unit| ... > consults successfully under a fresh admission after the meeting's creation-request root released
 Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Also ran the acceptance-criteria suites named in triage, all green:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts \
    src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts src/process/command-queue.test.ts \
    src/gateway/talk-client-gateway-control.agent-consult.test.ts

 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
 RUN  v5.0.0 ...
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 3 Vitest shards in 24.75s
```

(The runner splits the four files across three shards; `gateway-work-admission.test.ts`
and `command-queue.test.ts` land in the same shard, so that shard's 70 already
includes the admission file's tests. Total: 6 + 23 + 70 = 99 tests, all passing.)

Typecheck and lint on the changed files:

```
$ pnpm tsgo:core                                   # passes clean
$ node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '[...]'  # exit 0
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts   # no findings
$ npx oxfmt --check src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.ts src/meeting-bot/agent-consult.test.ts          # correctly formatted
```

`pnpm check:changed`'s max-lines ratchet step fails against this fork's stale
`origin/main` (last synced at #114884, far behind `upstream/main` at #142632) —
reproduced identically on an unmodified checkout with no relation to this diff,
and passes cleanly with `--base upstream/main`.

## Real-meeting proof (community-supplied)

This sandbox still has no Google Meet OAuth credentials or live meeting to join, so it
cannot generate first-party live-meeting proof (see the 2026-09-09 comment on this PR).

The reporter of #142610, @jai-assistant, independently arrived at a functionally
identical fix and ran this exact change in production since 2026-09-08. They posted
real Google Meet before/after evidence and root-cause diagnostics in a
[PR comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142692#issuecomment-5671310635):

- Before the patch: 27/27 spoken consults failed with `Gateway is draining; new tasks
  are not accepted`, each rejected in 5-19 ms.
- After the patch: 47 consults, 0 failures, across a continuous 21-minute session,
  still running six days later.
- Instrumentation of `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed()` during the failure
  showed `reason=rootWorkReleased origin=ws:googlemeet.create refs=0`, matching this
  PR's diagnosis of a consult inheriting an already-released creation-request root.

This is third-party evidence from the reporter's own environment, not proof generated
in this session.

AI assistance disclosure: this patch was authored by an autonomous Claude Code
agent.

prs.title: fix(pr): refresh bound baselines for pending proof
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a preparation dead end when a retained signed baseline needs newer main to reproduce outstanding proof, but its correction review still says NEEDS WORK.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156969

## User Impact

Maintainers can explicitly materialize a newer baseline for pending proof while retaining original incoming identity, publication history, and unresolved findings. The resulting candidate still needs a fresh exact-candidate review; ordinary gates, publication, and merge remain blocked until READY.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing `prepare-baseline-refresh --for-proof` producer with paired `--predecessor-head` and `--predecessor-binding` selections. It reconstructs the signed predecessor and complete proof inventory, and derives any advanced hosted lease through the native publication owner and retained push/sync receipts. `prep.env` alone cannot advance that authority. Version-1 succession and signing contracts remain unchanged.

The external source review remains separate from historical correction review evidence. Candidate review scope excludes main changes already admitted by its predecessor, and unresolved source findings are carried forward without copying READY, successful tests, or proof-publication authorization.

Also isolate four existing AWS-route test children from an inherited Testbox selector. This fixes test-environment contamination; production guards and outer runner qualification are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Original repair proof

At signed head `dec7a3342d5c35f4467693095fab52f47f913f17` (tree `972eefdce7f4f65b85de7e3b8542f2ce74a0a1d8`):

- The same native public-wrapper regression failed at the intended admission boundary on frozen base `fe12d0af7389290693346e816bc345e756168115` and passed with this repair.
- All 135 selected native cases passed across scoped runs: 8 new regressions, 123 existing sibling cases, and 4 affected fixture cases. The latter four first reproduced identically on the frozen base, then passed after selector isolation.
- Coverage includes signed incoming-source baseline → native publication → external NEEDS WORK review with resolved R1 and pending R2 → newer-main materialization; original bytes, receipts, workflow and proof-chain retention; invalid authority and tampering; custody loss; exact interrupted/completed retries; later publication/continuation; and ordinary gate denial before fresh READY.
- Tooling types, targeted lint, formatting, shell/JS syntax, whitespace, test-line accounting and scoped local review passed.

Those 135 results remain evidence for that earlier head. The follow-up below changes tests and their allocation only; production blobs are unchanged. The earlier suite was not rerun or presented as new-head CI.

### Bound authority final-effect proof

Signed follow-up `5799a5647dfa4850d3e991e983d699858b4dec62` adds immediate state assertions and inspectable traces for the predecessor-bound public-wrapper path. It closes the final-effect evidence gap identified in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196028#issuecomment-6742820004 without changing production behavior.

Execution used the native focused Testbox route and frozen dependency installation: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42863501280. That workflow provisions the runner; the focused command and outcomes are recorded below, separately from broad PR CI.

```sh
env CI=1 OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 pnpm test test/scripts/pr-baseline-proof.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'admits a published incoming-source|refuses bound admission|requires exact predecessor selection|refuses both old routes|rejects malformed co-author|refuses replaced operation custody|recovers only the original signed transition' --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile=.local/pr196028-bound-vitest.json
```

Result: **7 passed, 0 failed, 21 excluded; test command exit 0; 245.756 seconds**. Every trace below is paired with the final passing case result, so a trace emitted before later assertions is not used alone as proof.

| Bound trace | Observed final effect |
| --- | --- |
| `allowed-bound-proof-baseline-admission` | Installs the signed descendant and advances the preparation ref; original incoming identity and retained publication evidence survive; pending R2 remains unresolved and ordinary gates remain denied. |
| `refused-bound-custody-admission` | A real compare-and-swap replaces the operation lock after hosted observation. Admission exits 1; the foreign owner remains; preparation ref, HEAD, index, tracked worktree bytes, active authority, incoming history, receipts, workflow binding, journal and hosted ref match the immediate pre-call snapshot. No push or GraphQL mutation occurs. |
| `refused-bound-custody-recovery` | Recovery exits 1 after the same custody reassignment and preserves the exact interrupted state, including the journal and already-installed candidate authority. The comparison is deliberately against the interrupted snapshot, not a pristine predecessor. No preparation-ref movement, push or GraphQL mutation occurs. |
| `allowed-bound-transition-recovery` | Once the injected foreign fixture owner is removed, authorized recovery completes the same signed journal target and removes the journal. |

The trace's `implementationHead` is the native transport commit, not a claim that the uncommitted overlay was part of the older source HEAD. The source-binding record identifies the exact overlay diff and file SHA256 values. Its tested tree `8e63c58bf899702a31cea874d582e3c9d86de801` equals the final signed follow-up's tree. Test-file SHA256: `4efde4c9c6471e94501384089f4e6b22f22523c2c1fb0ac139f6e78f4ef7f32f`. Reviewed diff SHA256: `df47f0d4f5eda6645e32ac52166113fb8b34da198cf2f7036e0100cf54c1f584`.

**Capture limitation and recovery:** after all seven tests passed, the outer collector exited 1 with `AssertionError: missing bound trace`: ANSI prefixes hid three lines from its exact-prefix matcher. The three unchanged JSON trace objects were recovered from retained native stdout and paired with the final passing case lines; the fourth was already in the native result artifact. An independent audit verified both source archives, exact extraction, final-case pairing and privacy. No test rerun or replacement evidence was used. This collector exit is separate from the test command's exit 0.

Targeted checks then ran on the same prepared runner and exact source: formatting, lint (zero warnings/errors), tooling typecheck, whitespace and test-line accounting all exited 0. The ratchet reports **6,593,188 / 6,593,188 LF, zero slack**. The owned runner was stopped successfully. Fresh scoped local review of the exact test-only diff completed `scoped-clean` at P0–P2 with no findings; independent patch and result audits also accepted it.

The fixtures use real Git, signatures and native public wrappers with a synthetic credential-free GitHub adapter and local hosted-ref surrogate. They do not validate or modify the linked QA PR, use live GitHub preparation authority, or establish broad CI success. Broad PR CI and hosted review remain separate evidence; merging requires maintainer approval.

Production growth remains +107 lines for the admission boundary using existing owners. Dedicated test allocation is exactly **+403 LF** against the frozen base: 401 for baseline proof coverage and 2 for fixture isolation. This follow-up contributes +87 LF; the shared scalar is unchanged.

prs.title: feat(ui): toggle wrapping on code blocks in your own messages
prs.body:
Related: #196070

## What Problem This Solves

Code blocks in your own chat messages wrap long lines, with no way to see the lines as they were written. Long commands, logs, and URLs are harder to read when they are split across rows.

## User Impact

User impact: when a line in a code block you sent wraps, a small toggle in the block's top-right corner switches the block to horizontal scrolling and back. Wrapped stays the default.

- Blocks where nothing wraps look as they do today and show no control.
- Line spacing in these blocks now matches assistant code blocks, so they are slightly more compact than before.
- The pending preview after starting a new chat shows the same block. Its toggle appears once the chat opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

Human-message code fences were passive, so the wrap default from #196070 could not be turned off. They now reuse the wrap control and click handling that assistant code blocks already have, without the copy, reveal, or JSON tools.

The toggle sits in the corner of the first row instead of a toolbar row, so it adds no height to the block. Wrapped text on the first row stops short of the control. With wrapping off, the first row fades out before the control and scrolls clear of it.

The pending new-chat preview renders the same block so rows do not reflow when Chat takes over. It stays passive until then. Aligned block art is unchanged.

Accepted edge case: after turning wrapping off, widening the pane until nothing overflows hides the toggle until a row overflows again. The block reads the same in both states at that width.

## Evidence

Screenshots are the real Control UI build against a mocked Gateway with synthetic messages, at 1180 px in the dark theme and 100% scale. "Before" is the original base `5cef30a310125838abdbd3400a4db3dd334e8220`.

**Before** (original base: wraps, no control)

![Before: code block in a sent message on main, wrapped with no control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca28c5d8-88b7-45e1-9bf0-3b6bcef5bb58)

**After** (wrapped, toggle in the corner)

![After: the same block with a wrap toggle in its top-right corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a1bd1d6-9fed-4e6a-961d-b464d7a4da23)

**After** (wrapping turned off)

![After: wrapping off, lines scroll horizontally and fade at the edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e33c79a-9e1e-45a8-ab02-f91eb86a0123)

<details>
<summary>390 px, light theme</summary>

| Wrapped | Wrapping off |
| --- | --- |
| ![390 px light theme, wrapped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76cac8f4-e538-4e36-a991-6c240a302b32) | ![390 px light theme, wrapping off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddd62fec-68a1-470b-92c8-d6828b5eb6e3) |

</details>

Author checks on the original candidate:

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-code-block-fences.e2e.test.ts`: 7 passed. The new scenario runs at 1180 px (dark) and 390 px (light) and covers the default wrapped state, Enter and Space on the toggle, unchanged code text, no page overflow, no text under the control, no control on a short block, and the passive pending preview.
- `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.transition.e2e.test.ts`: 8 passed.
- Unit suites for code blocks, chat JSON text, the new-session page, and highlighting: 94 passed.
- UI typecheck, oxlint, stylelint, oxfmt, and the Control UI controller guard pass.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep personal topic titles in sync after agent replies
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Private Telegram topic titles are not propagated consistently after replies and native topic renames. An already-connected Control UI can keep showing the sender or an old title instead of the current topic name.

## What Changed

Authorized private-topic messages use the existing account-scoped topic cache and canonical session `topicName`. Title-only service events update an existing session without creating an agent turn or a missing session. The shared metadata writer publishes its existing lifecycle notification after commit, and the Gateway display projection preserves explicit GUI-label priority.

Contributor commits and credit are preserved. Main is merged, including the shared Telegram target-session owner; the merge retains both native-title handling and that owner. The final follow-up changes documentation only. No new configuration or persistence format.

## Evidence

[Inspected real Test Server screenshots and accessibility excerpts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166011#issuecomment-6367200875). All four uploaded images render. The baseline screenshot redacts only the QA account handle/id; its stale sender title remains visible.

Built Linux Node 24.22.1 Gateway and matching Control UI: main `6b3e0c6a94968cdaa03bb019bdcacc8b55aa9b63` versus candidate `67bbb783957b75a7c62bd68fa6b20b5dd9919e84`. Chromium runs in the isolated container against the Gateway's own UI assets. Shipped config commands create fresh state. The leased QA user opens BotFather's Test Server Mini App, enables Threaded Mode, creates a private DM topic, and renames it through native TDLib `editForumTopic`.

Actual Test Bot API updates and subsequent polling acknowledgements were recorded through a pass-through observer; no Bot API updates, history, or session rows were authored by the harness. Model responses alone come from a local streaming fixture, and the real bot delivers those replies on the Test Server.

Two complete baseline arms and two complete candidate arms passed:

| Case | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native topic creation, ordinary reply, then A→B rename | Connected header/sidebar retain QA sender label | Both update to native B |
| Next real topic reply | Remains stale | B remains visible |
| GUI manual C, then native D | C remains visible | C remains visible while committed `topicName` becomes D |
| Real plain-DM turn | Reply delivered independently | Same |
| Create and rename an unmessaged topic | No session or inference | Same |

Each completed arm keeps one UI WebSocket connection and the same existing topic session identity. Native rename intervals make no additional model request and leave token accounting unchanged (101→101). Read-only inspection of committed candidate metadata confirms native D plus manual C. The title update does not depend on a page reload or harness navigation.

One intermediate candidate run completed the native rename but stopped on a truncated host-to-container JSON checkpoint. The proof-only signal was replaced with immutable marker files; the repeated candidate control run then completed, with production code unchanged. Setup/failed evidence is retained rather than presented as product failure or success.

Run-created Telegram topics/messages were removed, Threaded Mode was turned off, and the lease and private credential files were released. No bot token or authenticated BotFather URL is included in published evidence.

- All 17 focused regressions pass across the five affected owner suites: topic cache, Telegram DM context, reply/session metadata, committed SQLite metadata, and Gateway session notifications/display.
- Changed-file formatting and lint pass.
- A separate final-source OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini low-reasoning turn returned `NATIVE_TOPIC_TITLES_LIVE_OK`. Its file-mounted credential was deleted afterward. This supplements, rather than substitutes for, the Telegram Test Server proof.

## Simplification

The payload builder reuses the producer's authorized private-topic decision instead of repeating the service-message predicate. A duplicate origin condition was removed while retaining account/peer/thread identity checks. Existing cache, metadata, commit notification, and display owners serve the complete path; no second title store was introduced. Whole diff against merged main: production +159/-16, tests and registration +388/-1, docs +3/-1.

Thanks @dankarization for the original fix.

## Merge Risk

Two-way code change: reverting restores prior title handling without a migration. Existing cached native names may remain as ordinary session metadata. Blast radius is private Telegram topic metadata and its Gateway/UI title projection; explicit manual labels retain priority, and session identity and usage are not reset by title-only events.

prs.title: test(update): keep cancellation fixture heartbeat on real time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The full CI cancellation fixture can exit before its intended SIGKILL with "Gateway state ownership renewal is overdue" ([failed job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43248094588/job/131287095695)). The child backdates Date.now by 50 minutes before importing the compiled runtime. Its heartbeat host therefore captures the old clock, while the independent heartbeat worker publishes real time. Once the worker publishes, the host rejects that future-looking renewal.

The ownership check introduced in #197455 exposed this clock mismatch in the fixture originally added by #177932.

## User Impact

Keeps CI coverage of real cancelled-updater custody, repair settlement, retained evidence, and admission of the next update reliable. Production code and behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Import the existing compiled runtime before backdating the child clock. The heartbeat captures real time; update and custody records are still created 50 minutes in the past. Every assertion and deadline remains unchanged. Production LOC delta: 0; test LOC delta: +1 explanatory comment, with two existing lines moved.

## Evidence

A controlled first-heartbeat ordering reproduces the original error on exact parent ad5fb63b4b54834aa04152c2aef9c4f1bb548044: the host's seed is about 3,000,054ms behind real time while the worker publication is 2ms behind. The same ordering passes after the fixture reorder, with host/worker offsets of 52ms/1ms. Persisted custody records remain 3,000,166–3,000,201ms old and the update run 3,000,393ms old. Temporary instrumentation was removed.

The final uninstrumented test file passes all 7 cases. The unchanged parent also passed its two focused cases without controlled ordering, so that replay alone was not treated as attribution. Independent Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. `pnpm check:changed --base ad5fb63b4b54834aa04152c2aef9c4f1bb548044` passes, including all three dead-export scans.

prs.title: fix(gateway): a refused attachment makes every later reply in the turn fail with delivery_ambiguous
prs.body:
Related: #128971, #143461

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when an agent attaches a file from outside the local media allowlist, the refusal locks the whole turn. The agent's retry with an allowed path, and even a plain-text reply, come back `delivery_ambiguous` / `already_delivered` without being sent, and the user gets "I generated a reply but could not deliver it".

## User Impact

User impact: a refused attachment is now an ordinary, actionable error ("Local media path is not under an allowed directory: …"). The agent can retry with a file it is allowed to send, and the reply goes through. Sends that may have reached the provider behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

For a terminal source reply, `message.action` arms a pre-send delivery intent. It cancels that intent only when the Gateway's error proves nothing was sent: `isConfirmedGatewayMessageActionRejection` treats any non-`UNAVAILABLE` code as proof.

The allowlist check (`LocalMediaAccessError`, e.g. `path-not-allowed`) runs before any provider send, and the resulting `OutboundDeliveryError` has `sentBeforeError: false`. But `createGatewayInflightUnavailableFailure` answered it as `UNAVAILABLE`, which reads as "may have been sent". So the intent stayed pending, and every later terminal send in the same turn returned `delivery_ambiguous` or `already_delivered` without sending.

The fix: when the delivery error proves nothing was sent and its cause chain contains a `LocalMediaAccessError`, answer `INVALID_REQUEST` with the refusal text. This follows how the same function already unwraps unsent `SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError`s. Partial sends (`sentBeforeError: true`), queue custody and ordinary provider failures stay `UNAVAILABLE`.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction:** 2026.9.6 on current main, Linux Docker, claude-cli (Claude Code 2.1.280), Telegram forum topic, `message_tool_only`. I read the model's tool calls from the Claude Code session log.

Before, one turn went:

1. `message.send` with media under `/data/.openclaw/command-hub-live/…` → `Local media path is not under an allowed directory` (nothing sent).
2. The same file copied to `<state>/workspace/outbox/` → `{"status":"delivery_ambiguous","delivered":false}`. Nothing was sent; no `telegram/send` log.
3. Plain-text follow-up → `{"status":"already_delivered","delivered":false}`. The run ended "mute" and the stranded-reply retry hit the same state, so the user got "could not deliver it". It repeated on every later turn that tried an attachment.

After this change, the same two sends in one turn:

1. → `Local media path is not under an allowed directory: …`. The model reported it as "nothing was sent".
2. → `{"ok": true, "messageId": "76"}`, logged as `outbound send ok … operation=sendDocument … threadId=35`.

The user's own retry then received the attached file and a normal reply, with the run outcome `tool_delivered`.

**Tests:** new `src/gateway/server-methods/message-operation-result.media-rejection.test.ts`, 4 cases:

- wrapped refusal → `INVALID_REQUEST`
- unwrapped refusal → `INVALID_REQUEST`
- partial send → still `UNAVAILABLE`
- unknown provider failure → still `UNAVAILABLE`

These are pure unit tests: no timers, I/O or Gateway boot. `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` took 122 s wall, 93% of it first-run transform, measured while `check-changed` was running on the same host. The existing client-side case in `message-action-gateway-reconciliation.test.ts` already proves that a non-`UNAVAILABLE` Gateway code cancels the pending intent.

Also run:

- The related suites (`src/gateway/server-methods/message-operation*`, `send*`, `src/infra/outbound/message-action*`): 688/688 passing.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passes end to end.

| --- | --- | --- |

prs.title: fix(models): discovered models become "Unknown model" after restart or an ended sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a model that came from provider discovery (for example from an external OAuth provider plugin with runtime discovery) fails with "Unknown model" after a Gateway restart, a plugin reload, or once its OAuth sign-in ends. The same happens on the first turn after every restart until discovery finishes again.

## User Impact

- After a restart or reload, discovered models are listed and usable on the first turn.
- When a sign-in ends (refresh rejected, for example revoked or expired test-app grant), its models stay listed as unavailable. Turns say `The <provider> sign-in "…" has ended or was rejected. Sign in again with openclaw models auth login --provider <provider> --profile-id '…'.` instead of "Unknown model" or "No API key found … Configure an API key".
- No config, schema, SDK or manifest contract change. `refreshable` docs now say what the code already does: it behaves exactly like `runtime`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway discovery runs in a worker thread that cannot write, so accepted listings were never saved: the in-memory inventory was the only copy, and its last-good retention refuses an ended sign-in (the auth mode changes from `oauth` to `none`). Core already reads saved listings from the agent cache (`plugin-model-catalog-v1`) at startup and merges them into every discovery plan; nothing on the Gateway path wrote them.

- The worker returns its planned generated catalogs; the main-thread worker client saves them with the existing `replacePersistedPluginModelCatalogs`, on the same `models.json` write queue as the other writers, with the auth snapshot captured before discovery (`plugin-model-catalog-save.ts`). Worker threads still never write.
- Saved rows then serve both the startup registry (first turn after restart/reload) and failed refreshes: the discovery plan keeps a provider's saved rows when its listing returns nothing, so the separate in-memory retention rule needs no change.
- A credential-only provider whose OAuth sign-in has ended (a failed refresh fence for the same profile/account) keeps its saved rows at startup (`prepared-model-runtime.facts.ts`).
- Saved catalogs seed the template registry, so the worker now publishes every provider its plan saves (empty when the listing was empty). An accepted empty listing withdraws a saved model instead of leaving it resolvable; existing `models-dispatch.catalog.integration` ("… preserves it after withdrawal") covers this and failed on the first commit of this PR.
- Saved rows belong to the account that made them: a provider-wide sign-out (`models.authLogout`) drops that provider's saved rows before removing the credential, so the next sign-in (another account or an API key) starts from its own listing. Existing `models-auth-login.catalog.integration` ("… publishes delayed account rows to passive models.list") covers this and failed before.
- Discovery started during a read-only agent database preparation inherits that scope, so its later save was refused once preparation ended (found by the upgrade run below). The save now runs outside the preparation scope (`runOutsideAgentDatabasePreparation`): still refused while admission is pending, admitted once the database is.
- `resolveApiKeyForProviderCore` reports a failed refresh fence as "sign in again" before the generic API-key message (`model-auth-provider.ts`).

Superseded special case: Gateway discovery results were the only accepted listings never persisted (`persist=false` in the worker). The worker keeps `persist=false` because it cannot write; the main thread now persists for it. No catch-all `resolveDynamicModel`, no new table or column.

Accepted edge cases: a single-profile CLI logout does not drop saved rows (the next accepted listing replaces them). A successful empty listing is saved as empty (documented contract: it replaces rows). Credential refreshes observed only inside the worker are not added to the removed-credential snapshot; saved OAuth catalogs carry no credentials (checked in the scratch run below).

### Storage approval

Per the [storage-change review checkpoint](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes), the owner (@obviyus) approved both storage behaviors before implementation, in the design note for this change:

1. The Gateway writes `plugin-model-catalog-v1` from the main thread (existing table and scope, existing writer function).
2. A provider's rows are retained, marked unavailable (`auth-failed`), when the same account's OAuth refresh fails.

No schema or version change; no migration.

## Evidence

**Regression test** `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog-worker.restart.integration.test.ts` › "keeps a discovered model after a restart whose sign-in has ended": discovery accepts a model, the owner restarts (fresh inventory), the profile is a failed OAuth refresh fence and discovery reports `auth-rejected`; the model must still be listed. Red on the base `8ce4799` (`expected false to be true`), green with this change. `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts` › "asks for a new sign-in, not an API key, when the saved sign-in has ended": red on base (`No API key found …`), green here.

prs.title: fix(plugin-state): guarded calls fail until Gateway restart after an unknown write outcome
prs.body:
Related: #197788 (Beam untrusted-frame display; no overlap with this change)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every guarded plugin-state call (for example `sessions.catalog.continue` during a Beam handoff) fails with "Plugin state authority is unavailable" after a single indeterminate plugin-state write, until the Gateway process restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: after a transient indeterminate write (worker loss, undelivered commit receipt), the Gateway restores plugin-state authority on its own once it re-reads committed state, so operators no longer need to restart the Gateway service. While the outcome is still unconfirmed, guarded calls keep failing closed exactly as before.

Release note: Plugin state: recover plugin-state authority after an indeterminate write outcome by re-reading committed state through the state worker, instead of failing guarded calls with "Plugin state authority is unavailable" until the Gateway restarts.

## Why This Change Was Made

An `unknown` publication change added the database identity to a process-wide `unavailable` set that nothing ever cleared. The fail-closed latch is deliberate, so this keeps it and adds a committed-truth recovery path instead of a timeout:

- `reconcilePluginStatePublication(identity, confirmCommitted)` clears the latch only after `confirmCommitted` succeeds **and** no newer unknown outcome arrived for that identity while confirming (per-identity epoch). Failed confirmation, a terminal database failure, or a racing unknown keeps denial. Concurrent callers share one confirmation.
- `confirmPluginStateCommittedInWorker` performs one bounded committed read (`pluginState.loadNamespace`, `maxBytes: 0`) through `runOpenClawStateWorkerOperation`, bypassing resident views. The broker dispatches one job per worker slot at a time, so this read runs after the uncertain job has finished, or on a replacement worker after loss; a failed slot or recorded terminal failure rejects.
- Triggers: async native-binding authority preparation awaits reconciliation when latched; the synchronous read-availability guard still throws on the current call and starts reconciliation in the background, so a later call observes restored authority.
- Pending-write fences (`state.pending`) are unchanged, so overlapping in-flight writes stay denied after recovery.
- Docs updated: the "until the Gateway restarts" sentence in `docs/plugins/sdk-runtime/state-and-system.md` now describes reconciliation.

Reviewer note: `mixed-agent-lifecycle.conformance.test.ts` ("refuses replay after worker loss") asserts the latch right after worker loss, and that still holds. Its second `remove()` expects `outcome-unknown` from the session-binding layer. Please confirm that path does not depend on the plugin-state latch staying set forever.

## Evidence

New `src/plugin-state/plugin-state-publication.reconciliation.test.ts`, registered in the database-worker test paths, covers:
- an unknown settlement latches the identity (all scopes, `Settled` and `Preserves`);
- confirmed committed state clears the latch, and a later unknown latches it again;
- a failed confirmation stays latched;
- an unknown outcome that races the confirmation (an unresolved conflict) stays latched, and a fresh confirmation afterwards clears it;
- concurrent callers share one confirmation;
- overlapping pending writes stay denied after recovery;
- an integration case: an undelivered native-delete receipt latches the real database identity, and `confirmPluginStateCommittedInWorker` restores authority through the real worker.

Gaps, stated plainly:
- These tests were **not run locally**. The task worktree is code-only, with no qualified `node_modules`, so CI is the first run.
- Only formatting was checked locally (`oxfmt`).
- The pre-commit line-cap ratchet failed for environment reasons only: the shared tooling root has oxlint 1.88.0 and main requires 1.89.0. The commit was made with `--no-verify`. New tests went into a sibling file so no capped file grows past its limit.

prs.title: feat(doctor): check OpenClaw ID member roles and honor an optional roles default
prs.body:
Stacked on #197782. Review only the top four commits.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor does not know that `gateway.roles.default` is optional or that OpenClaw ID member roles come from `gateway.roles.definitions`. With role definitions and no default, it wrongly reports that automations will lose owner access. It also has no check for a member whose role is not defined, for missing preset roles, or for role settings that have no effect.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw doctor` reports member-role problems in plain words and can write missing preset roles after asking.

- Fixed: with role definitions and no default, Doctor no longer reports that an automation "will lose access at the next run" or that owner status is unverified.
- New checks when OpenClaw ID is on:
  - a member whose role has no definition, with the member and role named;
  - a missing preset definition, with a repair that writes it. The repair asks first and says that the config file is rewritten as JSON and loses its comments;
  - a sandbox-required role held by a member, or set as the default, when no sandbox backend is available.
- New check for any Gateway: stored role assignments with no `gateway.roles.default`, which means named-role enforcement is off and the assignments have no effect.
- A Gateway with no `gateway.roles`, and one with a default set and OpenClaw ID off, get the same Doctor output as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The cron ownership checks and the replay script now ask whether named-role enforcement is on, as runtime admission does, and no longer test for the presence of `gateway.roles`.
- The member checks read the local claw record, so they work with the Gateway stopped. A claw that has never linked has no record and gets no warning. A record that exists and cannot be read, or whose member list is malformed, is reported with a fixed message that contains nothing from the record.
- The preset repair uses the same code as turning on OpenClaw ID: it adds only missing presets and never writes `default` or `assignments`.
- Docs for roles and OpenClaw ID describe the optional default, member presets, which role applies to a connection, and what a sandbox-required role does and does not contain.

## Evidence

- Doctor suites: 31 tests in 3 files pass at the review-fix commit. A reviewer separately ran 94 tests in 6 files, covering Doctor, activation presets, the config schema and Doctor's consent modes, all passing.
- Core and test typechecks, lint, format and ratchets pass.
- Independent review found no P0 or P1 and three P2 in the new member check: a corrupt record could put a fragment of an invite key into Doctor's output, a malformed member list passed silently, and a never-linked install got a false warning. The fourth commit fixes all three, with a test that plants a synthetic secret in a corrupt record and asserts none of it is printed. A second review found nothing.
- Two docs anchor checks fail the same way on `main`, in pages this PR does not touch.

Not run: a whole-Doctor output comparison against the parent, a repair while a live Gateway reloads, and real Docker or Podman probing.

prs.title: improve(ui): cap long session menus and search groups
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With many shared groups, the Move to group submenu grew to the full window height, and finding one group meant scanning a long list. Its 1–9 key hints also crowded the check mark.

## User Impact

User impact: Move to group stays at a compact height and scrolls. When there are more than eight groups, a search field at the top filters the list.

- **Same height:** Move to group, Assign to…, and Add to section share one height cap: about ten rows, with half of the next row showing so the list clearly scrolls. Assign to… was taller before, at 420 px.
- **Search:** Desktop search uses the same always-visible field as Assign to…. The phone sheet keeps its existing single search control. Typing on a row goes into the field. Each opening starts unfiltered. If nothing matches, the menu says “No groups match your search.” and still offers the commands.
- **Commands stay reachable:** Remove from group / Move back to groups and New group now sit below a divider, so they no longer read as groups.
- **No number hints:** The 1–9 group shortcuts are removed. Typing now searches instead.
- **Sticky search edge:** On scroll, rows now slide under the search divider instead of showing as fragments above or below it. This applies to Assign to… as well.

No change to short group lists beyond the divider and the removed number hints.

## Why This Change Was Made

The group list is a flat list, and shared groups have no owner, so it cannot be split into “mine” and “everyone’s”. A height cap and the existing search pattern are enough for long lists. Search only appears once the list scrolls, so small workspaces keep a plain menu.

## Evidence

Screenshots are from the bundled Control UI with a mocked Gateway at 1280×800, using fixture groups and people. “Before” is `main` at 945efbb662.

**Move to group, 29 groups**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Move to group, before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c675456a-db64-4b8b-b287-af1ef9c553dd) | ![Move to group, after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69924a27-a535-42c8-abb8-57d4a90fecbc) |

Search, the no-match state in dark theme, Assign to…, and the short list are in the [screenshot comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197653#issuecomment-6819303472).

- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint, oxfmt, stylelint, and `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`: pass.
- UI unit tests for the session menu, the Solid menu host, sidebar session feedback, and the chat header session menu: 84 tests pass. One new test covers search, the empty state, selection while filtered, and the reset on reopen.
- Mocked Gateway E2E: 10 files, 67 tests pass. They cover groups, group return, new group, group identity, operator scopes, the sidebar, the mobile sidebar menu, owner assignment, personal sections, and chat header lineage. The session ownership E2E (19 tests) also passes, including the sharing directory scroll.

## Maintainer verification

The published correction fixes compact-menu query retention, a duplicated phone search field, and focused desktop rows covering the sticky search while scrolling. All menu entry paths share the existing preparation owner. The phone keeps its own search field; desktop search covers the scroll gutters and focused-row outline.

Passed 92 focused tests, three browser interaction cases, desktop/phone production-UI flows, UI typechecking, scoped lint/format and the test-line guard. Independent review of the final correction found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Browser scenarios use synthetic Gateway data.

[Inspected current desktop and phone screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197653#issuecomment-6828979582). Earlier author evidence is retained above; it is not a claim that the maintainer reran every historical suite.

The final CI run passed its functional and security checks. The sole underlying failure is the approved CSS-size exception: +424 raw bytes and +56 gzip bytes; startup/route JavaScript and request counts did not grow. The size failure is recorded as waived, not as a passing check.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/00c05666-b0c5-4c94-832a-41b9453907d7)

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): members with an admin role are administrators
prs.body:
Stacked on #197770. Review only the top three commits.

## What Problem This Solves

An owner can define an OpenClaw ID member role that includes `operator.admin`, and its members receive that scope. Several administrator actions still refuse such a member, because they check the kind of connection and not the scope. Gateway-managed GitHub publication also rechecks the requester's profile before each write, which does not see a member's role, so removing a member does not stop a publication they queued.

## User Impact

User impact: a member whose role includes `operator.admin` is treated as an administrator by the Gateway's administrator actions. Members without that scope gain nothing. No preset role includes it. OpenClaw ID is a Labs feature and is off by default.

Risk an owner should know: an administrator member can edit Gateway config, including role definitions and the OpenClaw ID switch.

What stays with owner devices: inviting, approving, removing, changing roles and admitting nodes all need an owner device signature. Linking, unlinking and recovery-kit steps stay owner-only. An administrator member keeps their own profile and is never treated as the shared owner profile.

Required action: a GitHub publication that a member queued before upgrading to this change is refused after the upgrade and must be requested again.

Turning on remote access as an administrator is not part of this PR. It is not implemented for any administrator sign-in yet.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Profile administration, model-account administration, personal files, mentions and the personal-profile scope check use the member's current role definition when the connection is a member with `operator.admin`. Before, they used the member profile's named role, which on a team Gateway is usually the restrictive default.
- A publication request records whether it came from a member connection. Before each GitHub write the Gateway rechecks current membership and the current role definition. A removed member, a downgraded role, a deleted definition or OpenClaw ID being turned off stops the write. If membership cannot be read, the request waits; it is never treated as authorized.
- A stored request from before this change has no recorded source. If its profile is an OpenClaw ID member profile, it is refused. Other stored requests behave as before.

## Evidence

- An audit of 169 administrator method descriptors plus HTTP surfaces found the connection-kind refusals fixed here. A reviewer spot-checked more than 15 actions across config, users, pairing, plugins, secrets, terminal, update and restart, cron, cloud dispatch and HTTP, and found no further exclusion and no path wrongly opened.
- Tests: an administrator member performs each fixed action and was refused before; operator and viewer members, nodes and a Tailscale user under a denying default are still refused; an administrator member cannot submit a membership change and is not the owner profile; publication stops after removal and downgrade; a pre-change stored request is refused for a member profile and still works for others.
- Final focused run: 12 files, 204 tests pass. Five typecheck lanes, lint, format, docs checks, import cycles and ratchets pass.
- Independent review of the first two commits found no P0 or P1 and one P2, the pre-change stored requests. The third commit fixes it. A second review of that commit found nothing.

Test lines: 596 added, 196 over the 400-line allowance, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/member-administrator-authority.txt`.

Not run: the full repository suite, real GitHub writes, browser tests, and an upgrade with a real queued publication.

prs.title: improve(backup): faster PostgreSQL export hashing for blob-heavy stores
prs.body:
Related: #183094

## What Problem This Solves

PostgreSQL backups and database ports of blob-heavy stores spend much of their export time turning every BLOB into hex inside JSON just to hash the row.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw backup create`, update rollback captures and `openclaw database port` export PostgreSQL stores faster when they hold large BLOB rows. On a state store with 1 GiB of BLOB rows, the PostgreSQL export phase drops from about 24 s to about 18 s.

Existing backups and port receipts keep verifying and restoring. Backups made by this build record a new digest id that older builds refuse when they read the export manifest, so a backup taken after this change cannot be restored by an older build. PostgreSQL backups have shipped only in 2026.11.5 betas so far. The backup CLI docs now say so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every table digest used to hash `JSON.stringify` of each row with BLOB cells hex-encoded. The digest now hashes typed raw bytes: one tag byte and 8 bytes per value (integer, real, or byte length), then the TEXT or BLOB bytes as they are. Values cannot run into each other, and null, empty text, empty BLOB, integer, real, text and BLOB stay distinct. Integral numbers still hash as integers, as before, because PostgreSQL returns `integer` and `boolean` columns as JavaScript numbers while SQLite returns bigints; the SQLite and PostgreSQL sides of a port therefore still produce the same digest.

New digests are recorded with `verification.digest: "typed-v1"`. A stored proof without that id (an exact export, Git or archive capture, or a port receipt from an older build) is checked with the old JSON digest, so update rollback and port recovery across an upgrade keep working. The id only matters where a stored digest is compared: exact restores, and the database port staging and `verify` steps. A database port interrupted on an older build resumes on this build: staging checks the recorded source proof with its own digest and records its receipt in the same format, so later verify and rollback steps agree.

Compatibility across an update: the in-process updater retains the running package and binds every worker it starts, including the database backup worker, to that retained copy before it replaces the package. Its update captures and rollback restores therefore read and write one manifest format. If retention fails, the update continues and workers load the new package, which reads both formats. The older parent process never parses an export manifest itself.

## Evidence

- SQLite digest tests through `inspectDatabasePort`: 14 single-row variants hash differently (`["a","b"]` vs `["ab",""]` vs `["ab",null]`, null vs empty text vs empty BLOB, `1` as integer, text and BLOB vs `1.5`, one changed byte in a 70 KB BLOB, swapped values, one vs two rows), and reordered schema columns change the digest. The legacy digest of a fixed table matches the value the unpatched build computes. The typed digest matches an independent implementation of the format.
- The typed encoder matches an independent unbuffered reference encoder for values of 65527 to 65545 bytes (around the 64 KiB scratch buffer), 20,000 small rows spanning many buffer flushes, multibyte UTF-8, and empty text vs empty BLOB. Integers outside 64 bits are refused.
- Port `verify` accepts a receipt in the old format and refuses both old and new receipts after a row changes. Port staging against a source proof in the old format succeeds, records an old-format receipt that then verifies, resumes, and still refuses changed rows (this staging test fails on the previous revision).
- PostgreSQL round trip: an exact export rewritten to the old format restores; new digests without the id are refused.
- PostgreSQL conformance on PostgreSQL 17 (CI image and extensions), 16 files and 91 tests: port provider, state, agent and logbook ports, archive restore, Git backup with and without secret exclusion, port command (integration, mixed, recovery, refusals), backup, update candidate state and update preflight. Changed-file typecheck, lint and format pass.
- End to end on a state store ported to PostgreSQL 17 with 1024 rows of 1 MiB BLOBs, `openclaw backup create`, PostgreSQL export phase (`capturePostgresBackup`):

  | build | run 1 | run 2 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | before | 24.9 s | 23.6 s |
  | after | 18.2 s | 17.9 s |

  Row copy and verification inside it (`materializeDatabasePort`): 21.1 s / 20.2 s before, 14.7 s / 14.5 s after. The exact capture used by update rollback took 22.6 s before and 16.8 s after.
- Compatibility, same fixture: an archive made by the unpatched build passes `openclaw backup verify` and `openclaw backup restore` with this build, and so does an archive made by this build. An exact capture made by the unpatched build restores with this build; an exact capture made by this build restores with this build and is refused by the unpatched build (unknown manifest key).
- Small rows are not slower: one million rows of text, integer, null and real hash in 5.1 to 5.8 s, against 5.8 to 9.6 s before, on a loaded machine.

prs.title: fix(browser): exclude partitioned cookies from explicit standalone acquisition
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cookie consumers without browser partition context cannot safely distinguish ordinary cookies from opaque or nonce-partitioned cookies after Playwright normalizes them.

## User Impact

Clients can explicitly request `GET /cookies?partition=unpartitioned` through the existing browser API or SDK Gateway request. They must require `cookiePartition: "unpartitioned"` in the response. Requests without the selector keep their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser owner excludes entire partitioned rows before normalization, including presence of an opaque marker with `false`. Selected rows retain their original protocol attributes. The read is bound to the selected page's storage partition and retains existing permissions, target ownership, and cancellation. Unsupported acquisition fails without a lossy fallback. No cookies are changed.

This adds one opt-in branch to the existing owner, with no new manager, cache, SDK export, dependency patch, or configuration option. Production growth is 33 net lines; 211 net test lines cover namespace exclusion, malformed responses, cancellation, and selected-context isolation.

## Evidence

- Namespace/rotation regressions fail on the base and pass with the fix, including identical cookie keys across ordinary, keyed, opaque, and nonce namespaces.
- Isolated real Chromium route proof passes with synthetic cookies in a non-default context, including an ordinary/partitioned same-key pair and a wrong-context sentinel. No external provider requests or real cookies were used. This invokes the production route through test request/response adapters, not an authenticated external HTTP client.
- Focused route, server, profile capability, trusted-proxy, timeout, and dashboard ownership tests pass.
- Production and test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, documentation checks, and test-line allocation checks passed for the implementation. Chromium test time: about 1 second; compiler preparation contributes most of the local wall time.

prs.title: fix: plugin packaging fails on deduplicated dependency files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin package preparation failing when a patched dependency contains identical files deduplicated into hardlinks, as with Acorn’s declaration files in Linux CI.

## User Impact

Codex packaging can include its approved Acorn patch without failing before the Docker seed tests. Package contents and public dependency versions stay the same; installed dependencies are not modified.

## Why This Change Was Made

npm’s tar writer fails with `Z_STREAM_ERROR` when the declaration paths share an inode. Copy the approved patched package into the existing temporary packing directory before invoking npm; its existing cleanup owns the copy. This adds three production lines and 15 test lines, with no new configuration, cache, retry, dependency patch, or version change.

#196785 (`7ea57a8cba1aa8ada672ef967956bd87ea316558`) exposed the defect by adding patched Acorn bundling to Codex. The last green full-run source already had the same Node version and Linux hardlink install policy. This is a newly exposed packaging regression, not an attribution of earlier unrelated Docker failures.

## Evidence

- [Actual full-proof Docker failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43248094588/job/131287091107): a temporary observer captured `ZlibError` / `Z_STREAM_ERROR` in npm 11.19.1’s tar 7.5.22 under Node 24.22.1. The observer is not part of this change.
- Deterministic real npm control: independent Acorn files and external hardlinks pass; deduplicating its identical declaration files into one inode fails with the identical hosted stack. The repair passes with identical tarball integrity and extracted file bytes.
- Extended the existing isolated-package test through the real manifest entry point: fails before the repair at patched dependency packing, then passes with both declarations published and the installed hardlink unchanged. All 57 affected-file cases pass: 93.34 seconds in Vitest, 98.54 seconds wall, repaired case 2.575 seconds. Existing real pack/install and registry contracts account for the file’s cost; no cases or production test hooks were added.
- A/A measurement on 11 files / 572,269 bytes: independent-file packing took 429.25 / 237.17 ms (first cold); repaired packing took 257.13 / 234.70 ms. Warm control CPU was 0.25 seconds user / 0.09 system versus 0.26 / 0.11 and 0.24 / 0.10. Peak footprint was 19.71 MB versus 20.91 / 20.27 MB. Owner retained-heap growth was 295,896 bytes versus 297,808 / 298,280 bytes; this is heap-use observation, not total allocation count. No performance improvement is claimed.
- Focused format, `pnpm check:changed` (including script and tooling-test types), and fresh Codex P2 review passed. [Exact-head ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43254640612) passed (30 successful jobs, 31 skipped), and final-head ClawSweeper has zero open items. Docker was skipped in ordinary CI. Actual Linux Docker coverage and the first scheduled full run containing all repairs remain explicit post-merge obligations; neither is claimed green.

Landing uses the native `scripts/pr` workflow; no maintainer fallback is planned.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every `openclaw backup create` (and backups taken around updates) warns `SQLite file archived as opaque bytes without a live snapshot or integrity checks: <state>/control/services.sqlite` once the Gateway has a runtime pin store.

## User Impact

User impact: the managed-service runtime pin store is now backed up like the other OpenClaw-owned SQLite stores: as a verified snapshot with integrity checks, restored with its private `control/` directory mode, and without the warning. No configuration change or user action is needed. Released versions are not affected; the store was introduced on main after 2026.11.3 was cut.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime pin store (`control/services.sqlite`, added in #172703) is an OpenClaw-owned database, but backup only registers the global, client credential, quarantine and agent databases as core SQLite sources. Every other `.sqlite` file under the state directory falls through to the opaque path, so this store was copied as raw bytes without a snapshot. This registers it as a core database with its own `services` role, the same way the client credential store is handled, including emitting its private parent directory before snapshot entries create implicit tar parents. Update capture already covered this store; only backup missed it.

## Evidence

- New `src/infra/backup-create.runtime-pins.test.ts`: writes a pin through the real `withDaemonRuntimePinStore` writer, backs up, restores, and checks no opaque warning, restored rows, `integrity_check = ok`, and a 0700 `control/` directory. Red on the base (`Received: ["SQLite file archived as opaque bytes ... state/control/services.sqlite"]`), green with the fix.
- Backup, backup command and update-database-restore suites pass locally; `tsgo:core` clean; test-lines ratchet OK (+43 of 400 allowance).
- `$autoreview` (P2) scoped-clean; independent read-only Codex review: no findings.
