prs.title: feat(mattermost): message actions and multi-file sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost's message tool only supports send, react and read, and rejects sends with several attachments. This adds the channel-local actions available on other chat integrations and sends multiple files together.

## User Impact

Adds edit, delete, pin/unpin/list-pins, channel-scoped search, member/channel information, custom emoji listing, and file upload/download. A send groups up to ten files in one post; overflow continues in the same thread. If a later post fails, the shared partial-delivery error retains receipts for posts that landed.

| Gate | Default | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reactions` | `true` | `react`, `emoji-list` |
| `messages` | `false` | `read` |
| `messageWrites` | `false` | `edit`, `delete`, `upload-file` |
| `fileDownloads` | `false` | `download-file` |
| `pins` | `false` | `pin`, `unpin`, `list-pins` |
| `search` | `false` | `search` |
| `memberInfo` | `false` | `member-info`, `channel-info` |

The optional gates live under `channels.mattermost.actions` and account overrides. Existing `messages: true` remains read-only. Unchanged configurations gain no writes, file transfers, pins, search or member lookup; the read-only `emoji-list` action is the one addition where reactions are already enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin reuses native message dispatch, media, conversation authorization and partial-delivery owners. Delegated post writes stay within the authorized conversation. Reads honor the existing channel-read policy; account-bound discovery refuses a different account, member lookup requires conversation membership, and delegated search rejects caller `in:` operators and filters results to the authorized channel. The host's live caller-authority check runs before provider requests, including the download's file-body request.

Action discovery remains lightweight and execution loads lazily. The CLI-compatible result envelopes, action documentation and generated channel metadata are updated together.

## Evidence

Current head `715f1d7d477333f4407dd43d313a78978489f48a` adds only the 531-line test allocation for the measured regression coverage. The local test-line ratchet passes. The runtime and tests are byte-identical to the build and live proof head below. Hosted CI has restarted.

Runtime proof head `90ab39b9183d7d2410208fefe0ca4d032685e255` integrates OpenClaw main `8ae6b3852f97`. Native Markdown and long media captions share the same provider-post loop with attachment overflow and per-post delivery receipts. Delegated file download scope is derived from the current conversation. The focused tests also cover equivalent DM target spelling, missing authority, and current-caller revalidation.

- Channel metadata, config-doc generation, focused lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass. The send and outbound delivery suites passed with the merge repair. All 23 action tests passed after the DM target fix.
- The broad local Mattermost run stalled after a slash HTTP boundary timeout and was stopped. The exact clean head completed a Node 24.22.2 / pnpm 12.15.0 runtime build. A disposable Gateway and Mattermost Team Edition 11.1 accepted a single CLI send with 11 files and a long fenced caption. REST readback found six posts in one reply thread, 10 files on the initial post and one on overflow, and all 14 caption segments with balanced fences. A real pin followed by the shipped `message read`, `message pins` and `message search --channel-id` commands returned the seeded human post. Each command’s rendered output contained the synthetic marker `octogeeverification`. The build reported nonfatal Control UI CSS size warnings. Hosted CI on this head remains separate.

prs.title: feat(agents): preserve stores during controlled Gateway handoff
prs.body:
Related: #178748

## What Problem This Solves

Removing an agent from a Gateway currently requests session-store purging even with `deleteFiles: false`. An operator moving an agent to another Gateway needs an explicit way to release the source while retaining the agent's database identity, history and files.

## User Impact

Adds administrator-only `agents.detach({ agentId })` and offline `openclaw agents detach <id> --force --json`. Detach removes local roster/routing references and execution approvals, drains work through the existing deletion lifecycle, closes database owners, and retains the agent store, workspace and scheduler jobs. Source writes and retained jobs remain refused after restart. Existing `agents.create` can reattach the retained store; ordinary deletion keeps its destructive behavior.

The controller still owns exclusive placement, routing, credentials and file transfer. Detach is sequential per-agent handoff, not a whole-installation migration. Recreate required schedules on the destination and remove source jobs after cutover. Restrictions on the sole configured agent and shared/inherited credential owners remain.

## Implementation and Compatibility

The existing journal records durable retention intent. Recovery and deletion retries cannot turn a pending detach into destructive deletion. There is no database schema-version change, adoption RPC or distributed ownership manager. The method uses native core descriptor options.

The journal phases are a compatibility commitment: older binaries reject retained detach records at journal read sites while still serving other agents. A compatible runtime must remain in use while those records remain. Explicit source recreation or duplicate adoption is outside the source tombstone's protection.

## Evidence

Current head `9ab2bb65835aeacf9075c0c787f00deb84b7660d` integrates OpenClaw main `8ae6b3852f97`. The CLI uses the native expected-error owner. The detach schema shares the existing agent schema module, the descriptor uses the current protocol train, and the PostgreSQL suite follows the native shard inventory. Generated validators and protocol registry, Swift/Kotlin contract and method metadata checks pass.

- Fresh focused checks passed for the journal fence, pending destructive-deletion refusal, and database-conformance inventory. The disposable Gateway RPC and offline CLI SQLite cases both pass.
- **PostgreSQL reattachment is blocked on this head.** With the documented search extensions installed, the exact-source Gateway retained the PostgreSQL store identity, seeded session, transcript and cron job; refused CLI detach while the Gateway owned state; detached offline; restarted; and kept the source write and scheduler fences. Subsequent `agents.create` for that retained agent failed with `UNAVAILABLE` / agent database unavailable while the agent is deleted. The namespace was cleaned. Extending the creation claim through preflight alone did not fix the failure and was left out.
- The maintainer decision on the public API and retained journal compatibility, enforced security approval, packaged stable upgrade and a live deletion-lease replacement control remain open.

The following historical evidence was collected before this integration. The older PostgreSQL success does not qualify the current reattachment path.

The refresh removes downstream-only `cron.migration` hold/export/resume references from tests and docs. Both upstream-supported RPC and offline CLI preservation paths remain, including retained history/jobs, source refusal across restart, reattachment, and a destructive-delete control. Protocol outputs were regenerated; the native descriptor owner replaces the old extracted constants file. No test-line budget increase is needed.

- Warm isolated integration run: **2 passed, 1 PostgreSQL case skipped**, 125.29 seconds (wrapper 133.63 seconds). RPC and offline CLI both pass. The first concurrent run timed out; the isolated retry passed without timeout or behavior changes.
- Journal/command unit checks: **17 passed**; conformance-routing tests: **7 passed**; pending destructive-deletion refusal: **1 passed**.
- Core production and Gateway test types, focused native lint/format, protocol checks and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Test-line ratchet: **6,381,349 lines**, effective ceiling **6,394,553**, unchanged native baseline and allocations.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings in the refresh. Hosted CI for the refreshed commit is running; no aggregate success is claimed.

The transcript below is **prior-head live proof at `fcc6e8302b8`**, not a new PostgreSQL run for this refresh. It demonstrates two real Gateways retaining the same PostgreSQL store/session/history, administrator authorization, source refusal before and after restart, offline recovery/refusal, and existing data created by a no-PR upstream build. PostgreSQL conformance was not rerun during this refresh; neither was a packaged stable-release upgrade or a live two-process lease-replacement race.

issues.title: Tool parameter validation silently skips $ref / anyOf / oneOf schemas and crashes on tuple-form items
issues.body:
`Tool.validate_params` / `Schema.validate_json_schema_value` (nanobot/agent/tools/base.py) never resolve local `$ref` fragments and never evaluate `anyOf`/`oneOf` branches. Those are exactly the shapes MCP servers emit for model-typed and union parameters (e.g. a FastMCP tool built from `def book(addr: Address, count: int | str)`), so for such parameters local validation is a no-op:

- `addr` given as `{"zip": "98101"}` (missing required `city`, `zip` not an integer) → `validate_params` returns `[]`
- `addr` given as the string `"Seattle"` instead of an object → `[]`
- `count` given as a dict matching neither the integer nor the string branch → `[]`

The invalid arguments are forwarded to the MCP server unchecked, instead of producing the recoverable "invalid parameters" error other parameter shapes get.

Separately, an array parameter whose `items` is a list (draft-07 tuple form; `prefixItems` positions have the same problem) crashes both `cast_params` and `validate_params` with `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. That happens inside `ToolRegistry.prepare_call`, outside the tool-execution error handling, so one such tool schema turns every call into an unhandled exception rather than a tool error the model can react to.

Root cause: the validator reads `schema.get("type")`, which is absent for `$ref`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` fragments, and returns without checking anything; the array branch passes `schema["items"]` into the recursion assuming it is always a dict. The existing validation tests only use flat, native-type schemas, so none of these shapes are covered.

I have a fix with regression tests ready (validation resolves `$defs`/`definitions` refs and evaluates the composition branches; tuple/`prefixItems` elements are validated and cast positionally) and would like to open a PR.

issues.title: feat(discord): backfill recent thread history + optional startup presence
issues.body:
## Problem

The Discord channel starts a fresh session per thread and never reads prior messages. If the thread predates the bot (or the gateway restarted), the agent answers blind: it cannot see earlier decisions, replied-to messages, or its own prior replies in that thread.

There is also no way to set a presence (no statusText equivalent).

## Repro

1. Enable the discord channel, open a thread with 5+ messages.
2. Mention the bot with a question that requires thread context (e.g. "summarize what we decided above" or "list the last messages from X").
3. The reply ignores thread history.

## Proposed fix (ready, 2 commits on hodr-bot/nanobot@discord-history-backfill)

- `historyLimit` (int, default 20, `0` disables): on the first inbound message per session key per gateway run, fetch `channel.history` plus the replied-to message when outside the window, prepend as a delimited `<recent thread context>` block. Best-effort (never blocks delivery), once per thread so ongoing conversations are untouched.
- `statusText` (string, default `""`): when set, `Playing <text>` on connect, best-effort.

## Verification

- 7 new tests (5 backfill: first-message context, once-per-session, disabled at 0, reply-to resolution, failure best-effort; 2 presence), full discord suite 85/85 green, `ruff check` clean.
- Proven live on a self-hosted gateway: after the fix the bot summarized 5 older thread messages it had never seen in-session, and shows presence.

Happy to open a PR from the fork if you want it, or adapt defaults.

issues.title: Suppressed message-tool sends during internal turns return a success-phrased ack instead of an error
issues.body:
## Summary

During internal turns (heartbeat), message-tool delivery is intentionally suppressed so all output funnels through the post-run evaluator. However, a suppressed `message` call returns a success-phrased acknowledgement to the calling agent:

    Message acknowledged for {channel}:{chat_id} (not delivered)

The non-delivery is only a parenthetical; there is no error and no unambiguous signal. The agent treats the send as (at least partially) successful — in practice we saw a run believe it had posted a report to a designated room, record the send in its notes as made "with uncertainty", and continue. Nothing was delivered anywhere (later verified: no delivery row for the target room).

## Expected

While delivery is suppressed, the tool should make non-delivery explicit and machine-actionable — e.g., `ToolResult.error("delivery suppressed during internal turn: output is gated by the post-run evaluator, nothing was sent")` or an equivalent clearly-non-success result. The current "Message acknowledged" phrasing actively misleads the calling model.

## Observed

- nanobot-ai 0.4.1 (community docker image), Matrix channel.
- A heartbeat turn called `message` targeting a specific room; the tool logged "delivery suppressed during internal check" and returned the acknowledgement string. No message arrived in the target room; the delivery queue has no record for it.

## Code (v0.4.1)

- `agent/tools/message.py`, suppressed branch:

    if self._suppress_delivery_var.get():
        logger.debug("MessageTool: delivery suppressed during internal check")
        return f"Message acknowledged for {channel}:{chat_id} (not delivered)"

- Suppression is set around heartbeat turns in `cli/gateway_runtime.py` (`set_suppress_delivery(True)`), so output funnels through the post-run gate — that gate design is sound; the return shape is the problem.

## Suggested fix

Return an explicit error/structured non-success result while suppressed so the agent can react (fall back to a quiet final response, write content to disk for later delivery, etc.). Small change, no impact on normal sends.

prs.title: fix(tools): validate arguments with jsonschema without coercion
prs.body:
## Why

Fixes #6485. This is an alternative implementation to #6486, building on the bug report and reproductions from @xiong-wei1.

The hand-written tool validator silently skips references and composition keywords, and positional array schemas can crash call preparation. Use the established `jsonschema` library instead of extending our own JSON Schema implementation. Incorrect arguments should produce actionable tool errors so the model can correct them, not be silently converted into different values.

## What changed

- Replace the hand-written validator with cached `jsonschema` validators and actionable errors, including instance paths and union-branch failure details.
- Validate MCP arguments against the server's original `inputSchema`, independently of provider-facing adaptations. This preserves nullable referenced models and handles Notion-style `oneOf` / `const` discriminators.
- Remove automatic argument casting and nested JSON-string decoding. Invalid arguments return errors; corrected calls execute without rewriting model/session history.
- Stop cron's action-specific checks when schema validation fails. Adapt already-valid JSON integers such as `2.0` to Python integers at built-in indexing/pagination boundaries, including file reading/editing, search, cron history and shell output limits.
- Return recoverable tool errors for unsupported or malformed explicit `$schema` declarations. Use draft 2020-12 only when the declaration is absent.
- Extend decimal `multipleOf` validation with exact rational arithmetic over decimal spellings, without an epsilon tolerance. Use the mature `regex` engine for Unicode string `pattern` constraints such as FastMCP's `^\p{L}+$`.
- Update the architecture documentation and avoid assertions tied to a dependency's exact error wording.

## Scope

This intentionally changes argument handling for built-in tools, MCP tools, and entry-point plugins: strings such as `"123"` are no longer converted to numbers, numbers are no longer converted to strings, and serialized nested objects/arrays are not unpacked. The removed `cast_params` hook is no longer part of tool call preparation. Parsing the outer provider JSON arguments envelope is unchanged. Built-in Python index adaptation does not change the original tool-call arguments or MCP submissions.

Validation defaults to draft 2020-12 and honors supported explicit dialects, including draft-07 tuple-form `items`. Legacy tuple schemas must declare their dialect; invalid schemas return a tool error. Provider-facing nullable/ref adaptations remain unchanged and are not the validation contract.

## Tradeoffs

Declare `jsonschema>=4.21.0`, `referencing`, and `regex` directly; all were already transitive dependencies. Testing 4.20.0 exposed its incorrect nested enum equality for booleans versus 0/1, fixed upstream in 4.21.0, so the lower bound now requires that fix rather than duplicating equality logic.

Error wording comes from `jsonschema` with small compatibility extensions for decimal multiples and Unicode string patterns. Other keyword handling remains library-owned. Unicode regex compatibility here is scoped to string `pattern`; object-key regex keywords retain the library's default implementation. Nanobot retains rejection of non-finite JSON numbers and disables external HTTP/file reference retrieval.

## Blast Radius

Callers that relied on argument coercion must supply the declared JSON types. Error results identify the offending field and reason so the model can retry. Existing agent retry/history behavior is retained, with real in-memory MCP coverage for correction and unchanged call history.

## Verification

- `python -m pytest tests/tools tests/agent tests/cron tests/providers --ignore=tests/tools/test_exec_platform.py -n 4 --dist loadfile -q --tb=short`: **5251 passed, 109 skipped**. Windows native process compatibility remains for CI.
- Focused regressions across schema/MCP, built-in file/search/web/shell and cron paths: **305 passed**.
- Minimum supported `jsonschema==4.21.0`, covering MCP, schema/registry/plugin validation and cron contracts: **423 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Real FastMCP in-memory tests and stdio acceptance: `4.02` with `multipleOf: 0.01` and `北京` with a Unicode letter pattern succeed; `4.021` and `123` are rejected locally. Earlier argument-correction/history integration remains covered by the broader suite.
- Repository Ruff checks, import boundaries and `git diff --check`: passed. Strict BasedPyright on all changed production modules: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- Full BasedPyright still **fails with the same four previously reproduced Windows FileLock return-type errors** in `mcp_oauth.py`, `gateway/runtime.py`, `process_runtime.py`, and `providers/xai_oauth.py`. Those files and their dependencies are unchanged by this follow-up; the errors remain unresolved.
- Full-project platform/build checks are left to this PR's CI for the updated head.

prs.title: fix(webui): prevent single-dollar math from crossing code spans
prs.body:
## Problem

The WebUI's single-dollar math scanner can start at prose such as `$ref` and consume the `$` inside a later inline code span such as `` `$defs` ``. This sends prose to KaTeX and destroys the intervening bold/code formatting. The reported full message, spaced code such as `` `$defs / definitions` ``, and preceding Windows paths are covered by regressions.

## Parsing rule

A tentative single-dollar formula must not end inside a complete CommonMark code span. Reuse micromark's `codeText` tokenizer to find the span boundary, then let the existing math scanner find its unescaped closing dollar. If that closer lies inside the code span, reject the math candidate and let Markdown parse the code normally.

This replaces the earlier identifier-tail regular expression and TeX-command guessing with a boundary check. Spaces, punctuation, and Windows paths no longer change code precedence. Ordinary formulas such as `$n$th` and `$x$2`, and backticks wholly contained within a formula such as ``$\text{`value`}$``, remain supported. The streaming fixture covers the reported reply's partial code span and completion.

When math and code delimiters cross, code wins. For example, `$th` is code in:

```text
A $x`$th`
```

An author intending a backtick inside math followed by Markdown code can use explicit TeX delimiters:

```text
A \(f(`x')\)th`code`.
```

This is a deliberate precedence choice, not an attempt to infer every author's intent. In particular, two bare dollar-prefixed identifiers without code spans remain outside this fix. Existing currency and explicit/display-math parsing rules are unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused renderer/streaming tests: 199 passed. The three added common-code regressions failed before the implementation change and passed afterward.
- Full WebUI unit suite: 205 files / 3,755 tests passed.
- Typecheck, lint, and production build passed.
- Full Chromium suite: in progress on this revision.

Earlier intermediate revisions had un-attributed full-suite failures (two `app-layout` unit cases, and `apps-connection-layout` / `history-hydration` browser cases). Their results are not reused as current-revision verification.

prs.title: feat(agent): integrate mst-python as a metasearch provider
prs.body:
This PR adds the Meta-Search Tool (mst) as a new web search provider for nanobot.

## What it is

MST aggregates results from multiple search engines (DuckDuckGo, Google, Brave, Bing, etc.) simultaneously and merges them using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). This gives richer coverage than any single provider alone.

Inspired by [SearXNG](https://github.com/searxng/searxng) — MST brings the same metasearch concept to Python code directly, without needing a separate web server or Docker container. Package at https://github.com/openmtx/meta-search-tool.

## Changes

- **`nanobot/agent/tools/web.py`** — added `mst` as a new search provider with `_search_mst()` method. Supports:
  - `mst_engines` config / `MST_ENGINES` env var to select which engines to query (defaults to all ready engines)
  - `mst_weights` config / `MST_WEIGHTS` env var for per-engine ranking weight overrides
  - Graceful fallback when `mst-python` is not installed
- **`nanobot/webui/settings_api.py`** — added JSON parsing and validation for `mst_engines` and `mst_weights` in the WebUI settings API
- **`pyproject.toml`** — moved `mst-python` to `[project.optional-dependencies] mst` (optional, not installed by default)
- **`tests/tools/test_search_tools.py`** — 6 new tests covering success, missing package, env vars, config priority, and timeout
- **`tests/webui/test_settings_api.py`** — 4 new tests for MST engine/weight validation in the settings API

## Usage

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "web": {
      "search": {
        "provider": "mst",
        "mst_engines": ["ddg", "google", "brave"],
        "mst_weights": {"google": 2.0, "ddg": 1.0}
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Or via env vars:
```bash
export MST_ENGINES="ddg,google,bing"
export MST_WEIGHTS="{\"google\": 2.0}"
```

Install with: `nanobot plugins enable mst` (or `uv pip install 'nanobot-ai[mst]'`)

## Testing

- All existing web search tests pass
- 10 new unit tests cover MST-specific functionality

## Problem

Stable PyPI uploads require a maintainer credential and manual artifact selection. Start PyPI Trusted Publishing when a maintainer publishes an approved GitHub Release. Keep a manual workflow for testing and recovery.

- Start the protected main-branch publisher after a stable GitHub Release. Preserve the original release actor and require an independent PyPI approval.

prs.title: perf(subagent): read saved task history by loaded turns
prs.body:
## Problem

Opening a long conversation loaded **every saved subagent task** for the session. `GET /api/sessions/{key}/subagents` had no scope, so a 500-turn session with 5000 finished tasks shipped **7.3 MB** of JSON on open — while the thread only renders a handful of messages — and the cost grew without bound as history accumulated.

## Change

Saved tasks are now read for the **turns the thread actually displays**.

- The WebUI sends the loaded user-turn ids (`?scope=window&turn_id=…&track=…`) and skips ids it already read, so growing the window reads only the new part.
- Hosts answer with tasks whose `subagent_task.origin_turn_id` falls in that window, plus every live task and any task the client still tracks. `origin_turn_id` is already persisted for every delegation, so no schema data change is needed.
- That JSON path is indexed by a **schema v6 partial index** (`sessions_subagent_origin_turn_id`), scoped to subagent child rows; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows an index SEARCH instead of a table scan.
- The WebUI always uses the turn-window read, without an additional capability negotiation or a full-history fallback for older gateways. The backend's unscoped interface remains available to callers that need the complete task list.
- The window read reuses the existing session read — `read_statuses_for_session(session_key, turns=…, tracked=…)` — instead of a parallel method: stored window, one query for tracked tasks outside it, live-work reconciliation, all on one store connection. A test fails if a request opens more than one connection.
- The window is keyed by turn alone. The first version of this branch also filtered on `origin_message_id`, but the WebUI never sets that field: message frames carry only a turn id, and the message ids the thread renders are projection ids (`history-…`), not channel message ids. The dimension matched nothing while costing a second partial index, a UNION branch and up to 400 ids per request. It is gone, together with the `active=0` chunking flag — live tasks are always included and the client merges by task id.

Python: `list_subagent_session_metadata` / `read_child_session_metadata` in `SqliteSessionStore` / `SessionManager`, `SubagentSessions.load_turns` / `load_tracked`, `SubagentManager.read_statuses_for_session`, query parsing in `ws_http.py`.
WebUI: `SubagentTasks` reads per visible turn window with in-flight coalescing and an epoch/invalidate path for events, `ThreadViewport` reports the rendered turns, `api.ts` chunks long windows (≤400 ids / 5000 encoded chars per request) by tracking the encoded length instead of re-serializing the target per id.

## Measurements

These measurements were collected at `3ff53358f`, before removing the client negotiation. The backend query/index and the supported same-version request path are unchanged.

Synthetic, task-owned runtime (500 turns, 5000 finished tasks, 1024-byte results; latest 20 turns requested; no production data):

| | full read (before) | window read (after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| response bytes | 7,283,659 | 291,358 |
| median latency | 180.7 ms | 10.7 ms |
| tasks returned | 5000 | 200 |

A second identical run measured 160.4 ms / 30.1 ms on the same commit and store, so treat the median as single-machine timing noise; the byte and row counts are exact.

Index cost, 200 subagent metadata updates per transaction, `synchronous=FULL`, 6 samples per path: **5.1–5.4 ms** with the index against **4.3–4.5 ms** without — about +4 µs per updated child row. A parent-session metadata write, the common path, never touches it because the partial predicate does not match. Building the index on a populated 5000-row store takes **26.5 ms**, a one-time startup cost on the first run after the upgrade. The write path pays that small per-row cost; the read path is where the win is.

Read-path scaling on a throwaway copy: at **50,000** stored tasks the same 20-turn read returns 200 rows in **0.3 ms**, against **283.9 ms** for the full read of the same parent.

## Verification

### Uniform-read follow-up

- `pytest tests/webui/test_client_contract.py tests/webui/test_remote_proxy_bootstrap.py tests/webui/test_subagent_persistence.py tests/session/test_subagent_metadata_query.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` → 44 passed.
- Full `bun run test --pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=2 --poolOptions.forks.minForks=1` with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2560` → 202 files, 3688 tests passed. An App fixture still matching the old query-free URL was corrected before this final full run.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.browser.json`, and `ruff check nanobot tests scripts` → passed.
- `history-boundary.spec.ts --workers=1` → 24 passed, 1 failed: `cross-path older errors never float after latest or a loaded rail jump, but boundary retry remains available` showed a blank page on its second navigation and timed out waiting for the thread. One focused diagnostic run with tracing passed on the same source; the suite failure remains unclassified. No timeout, retry, or assertion was relaxed. The task-pagination browser case passed and verified that loading older messages requests only the newly displayed turns.

### Earlier snapshot (`3ff53358f`)

The broader Python run, performance measurements, and real-gateway acceptance below were performed before this follow-up; they are retained with that snapshot identity.

- `pytest tests/session tests/webui tests/agent/test_subagent.py tests/agent/test_subagent_lifecycle.py tests/agent/test_session_manager_history.py tests/triggers/test_local_triggers.py` → 1289 passed, 22 skipped.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build` → clean; full `bun run test` → 202 files, 3687 tests passed.
- `ruff check nanobot tests scripts` → clean. `basedpyright` 1.40.2 → 4 errors, the same pre-existing `BaseFileLock` `reportReturnType` errors; the five touched Python files report none.
- Browser acceptance on a real gateway with the synthetic 500-turn session: opening the conversation issued **one** scoped request (`content-length: 203959`, 14 turns) instead of loading 5000 tasks, each user message showed its own 10 finished tasks, scrolling into older history issued a second request covering only the newly loaded turns (0446–0485), and the console stayed clean.

CI note: on an earlier commit of this branch, `tests/webui/test_gateway_webui_smoke.py::test_real_gateway_goal_single_run_and_stop[True]` failed twice with its 30 s shutdown budget (35.5 s), then passed on a rerun of the same commit. The shutdown dump puts the wait at `nanobot/agent/loop.py:1767` — `_aclose_unlocked` draining `_background_tasks` — and no case in that file requests the subagent endpoint. It reads as a nondeterministic shutdown race in that smoke test, not a regression from this change; I recorded it instead of widening the timeout.

## Scope

Correctness work that this read depends on is *not* in this PR: the persisted `origin_turn_id` field is already on `main`, and the deeper attribution/consumption cleanup stays in a separate branch. This PR covers the window read, its index, and the WebUI integration.

Contributes to [NAN-438](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-438/按已加载消息按需读取-webui-子任务历史).

prs.title: refactor(telegram): derive command regexes from the alias map
prs.body:
## Why

Telegram cannot render `-` in a tappable command, so `/dream-log` needs the underscore spelling `/dream_log`. The channel therefore keeps the same alias list in four places: the alias map, the display-name regex, the inline-code regex, and two routing regexes. Adding or removing a command means editing each one, and a missed edit shows up as a command that renders but does not route. Derive the spellings from the existing map instead.

## What changed

- Build the display, inline-code, and routing alternations from `_TELEGRAM_COMMAND_ALIASES`, so one map entry now feeds every spelling.
- Keep the routing split explicit: `_TELEGRAM_BUS_CANONICAL_COMMANDS` names the canonical spelling the shared handler also accepts, and `TELEGRAM_DEDICATED_COMMAND_RE` covers the rest.
- Hoist the display-name map out of `_telegram_command_text`, which rebuilt it on every call.

## Scope

Only how the patterns are assembled. The command list, handler order, matching boundaries, `@bot` suffix handling, code-fence skipping, inline-code exemption, and the text sent to the core router are unchanged. `BOT_COMMANDS` descriptions stay where they are; no command registry or dispatch framework.

## Tradeoffs

Keeping the four regexes spelled out is more readable in isolation. The cost is the silent divergence between them, which is the failure this change removes. Routing rules that differ on purpose, such as `evaluator-prompt` sharing the bus handler, remain explicit constants rather than being inferred.

## Blast Radius

Telegram command display in control replies and `/help`, and command routing through `_forward_command`. Other channels and the core command router are unaffected.

## Verification

- `nanobot/channels/telegram/tests/test_telegram_channel.py`: 178 passed, matching the pre-change result on the same base.
- `tests/channels/test_channel_plugins.py` and `tests/command` (excluding `test_compact_command.py`, which fails to import `agent.session_helpers` on this base before and after the change): 241 passed.
- `ruff check` and `basedpyright` on the changed file: clean, same as the baseline.
- The generated patterns differ from the previous literals only by `re.escape` output (`-` becomes `\-`, which matches identically); the inline-code pattern is byte-identical.
- No new tests: existing coverage already pins the observable routing and rendering behavior, and the change adds no new contract. Full CI not run locally.

prs.title: refactor(agent): clarify run-local input and checkpoint ownership
prs.body:
## Why

Changing injected-input preparation currently requires understanding queue snapshots, rollback, authorization, terminal waiting and checkpoint closures inside `_run_agent_loop`. Give the run-local queue state one owner and make the Loop–Runner adapters explicit, without replacing the existing execution or persistence model.

Resolves [NAN-188](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-188/评估并改进-agent-执行生命周期与隔离边界)

## What changed

- Extract `PendingInputs` to own each batch's FIFO boundary, rollback and shared terminal-wait deadline; keep channel/workspace/runtime-context preparation in `AgentLoop`.
- Type Runner checkpoint payloads and move persistence adaptation to a named method; retain private provider-state handling and `SessionState` commits.
- Scope existing context bindings with `ExitStack`, and cover cancellation during input conversion while another run is making its model request.

## Scope

Behavior-preserving execution-boundary refactor. FIFO barriers, input authority, follow-up acknowledgement, generation checks, recovery and background-task lifetime stay with their current owners. No new scheduler, task UI, replay behavior, persistent format or tool-reload policy.

The accompanying [design record](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/document/nanobot-执行生命周期与隔离边界评估-1cc3dbb675bc) records the existing MCP live-reload interleaving separately; this PR does not silently choose between immediate revocation, idle-only changes and retained in-flight connections.

## Tradeoffs

Moving every closure to a Loop method would leave the queue/deadline lifecycle threaded through the adapter. A small run-local buffer gives that state a coherent lifetime without receiving the entire Loop or Session. This improves ownership and readability, not net line count or measured performance.

## Blast Radius

Agent execution through both the Loop and child-task Runner checkpoint callback. The main regression risks are input order after cancellation, cross-run context leakage, terminal-wait budgeting and recovery-state persistence. Storage and client protocols are unchanged.

## Verification

- Focused execution, input, cancellation, Goal permission, recovery and follow-up commit suites: **416 passed** on Windows/Python 3.14.
- Full configured Ruff check, `uv run --no-sync basedpyright`, `uv run --no-sync python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Existing terminal-wait tests now patch the new owner while retaining the same timeout-budget assertions. The added concurrency case uses controlled events and synthetic model responses, not timing sleeps.
- [Remote CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43206051733): passed, including Linux Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python 3.14, Windows 3.12 process compatibility, Docker build/startup/upgrade acceptance, and the required gate. Checkout logs confirm the tested merge contains this PR head.
- Standalone WebUI/TUI/native-package lanes were not selected by the unchanged CI scope. Native update/installer tests were not run on the local interactive desktop.

prs.title: feat(webui): show the full token-usage picture in settings
prs.body:
## What

This improves the existing 30-day usage charts and model drill-down using content-free call data already recorded in SQLite. No database schema changes are needed.

**Usage card**
- states the 30-day window explicitly
- splits input into cached / written / missed / unknown using per-call partitions calculated before aggregation, so independently reported cache reads and writes cannot overlap (the hatch stays on cached input)
- keeps the previous cached / missed / unknown breakdown for older backends that cannot provide those partitions, without guessing a separate write segment
- labels the daily axis with peak / average / zero, prints the peak date on its own column, and keeps compact `zh` values from wrapping
- names the segment rows in the tooltip and adds request / failure counts

**Model trends**
- `model_days_30d` also sums measured output tokens, generation time, first-token time, and cache coverage, reusing the shared aggregate SQL
- the daily tooltip lists speed, first-token time, cache hit rate, and tokens as aligned columns; `—` keeps unmeasured values distinct from zero
- speed is the decode rate (`generation_ms` starts at the first streamed delta), with the first-token wait reported beside it

**Shared and detail dialog**
- `usage-chart.tsx`, `usage-number.ts`, and `usage-model.ts` share axis geometry, cached locale formatters, and model-id normalisation
- the dialog focuses on model trends, with a visible title, 30-day range, and estimated share when applicable
- the axis uses `Intl`, and the residual model series is named "other models"

**On-demand requests**
- the settings page owns its initial settings read; overlapping reads share a pending promise only within the same client
- ordinary `/api/settings` reads do not aggregate or embed usage history
- overview refreshes request only the visible 30-day daily totals; opening details requests model aggregates with `?details=true`
- per-view backend caches prevent overview and detail readers from evicting one another
- usage responses support gzip and content-derived ETags; unchanged polls return 304 without JSON re-encoding or a response body
- telemetry refreshes stay inside the usage card instead of updating the whole settings controller; the 5-second refresh and focus checks stop when hidden or outside Overview, with pending requests aborted
- standalone overview previews remain presentation-only

## Performance

An isolated development browser used the same 39-day synthetic database before and after this follow-up. Direct Overview startup changed from two full settings reads plus a usage read to one settings read plus a thin usage read. The root settings response fell from 163,092 to 48,935 bytes; the initial usage response fell from 114,146 uncompressed bytes to 6,859 gzip bytes. Subsequent unchanged overview polls returned 304 with zero body bytes (requests and headers still exist). Model details were requested only on opening the dialog, and leaving Overview produced no usage requests during a 5.5-second observation.

Local aggregate measurements compared published `607b18530` with this change on identical synthetic SQLite data: 100,000 calls, 30 provider/model pairs, fixed timezone and timestamp, 9 shuffled/interleaved payload-cache misses with warm SQLite/filesystem, and 40 cache hits. Assertions checked identical visible 30-day daily rows and model aggregates. The old response contains extra history that the current UI does not display; projections intentionally remove that work.

| Call distribution | Old full response: miss median / max | New overview: miss median / max | Cache-hit median, old → overview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Concentrated in 30 days | 2448.29 / 3109.54 ms | 860.62 / 1242.21 ms | 0.65 → 0.39 ms |
| Spread over 371 days | 470.00 / 547.37 ms | 28.62 / 55.83 ms | 10.44 → 0.69 ms |

These are local aggregation/deepcopy timings, not end-to-end HTTP latency. Model details still cost work: in the concentrated fixture their miss median / max was 2434.64 / 3173.71 ms, so no zero-regression tail-latency claim is made. The fixtures retain provider/date correlation (30 and 900 model-day rows respectively), rather than modelling every provider on every date.

## Verification

Performance follow-up (`3febcd343`):
- `.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/llm_usage tests/webui/test_settings_routes.py tests/webui/test_settings_api.py -q` — 194 passed; the final conditional-response header adjustment was also checked by all 54 route tests
- `bun run test --maxWorkers=4 --minWorkers=4` — all 205 files / 3695 tests passed, with all cases and assertions retained
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, and `bun run build` — passed
- `bun run check:imports` — passed; `bun run test:imports` — 42 passed
- Python import-boundary checks, Ruff on touched Python files, and BasedPyright on the five changed Python modules — passed
- the restarted isolated backend returned the expected thin projection, reconciled cache partitions with input tokens, gzip responses, and 304 / zero-body responses for both overview and model views
- full Python and automated browser suites were not run locally at that snapshot; subsequent CI and browser repair results are recorded below

The first full local frontend attempt exposed a presentation/provider coupling and an unstable client fixture, which were corrected. It also lost four Node workers to explicit out-of-memory errors. The replacement full run bounded workers to four without changing production configuration, skipping cases, weakening assertions, or increasing timeouts. An import-helper run concurrent with the failing full run hit four existing CLI child deadlines; the isolated follow-up passed all 42 cases. Both earlier failures remain recorded rather than being described as baseline defects.

CI repair (`41f16a789`):
- [Run 43188038655](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43188038655) tested merge `2d4ce322` (target `0ce10533d`, PR head `3febcd343`). Its browser job failed 14 cases and passed 503; the other checks passed. The same 17 affected cases passed on that exact target locally, while the failed merge reproduced 16 failures / 1 pass on Windows.
- the skeleton fixture now returns a typed usage payload instead of an invalid `{ usage: null }` wrapper; the 30-day subtitle uses its own line height so it does not move the loaded rows by 1px
- the shared tooltip restores its previous close lifecycle by removing this PR's global exit-animation classes; immediate chart tooltips and configurable opening delay remain intact
- all 17 affected browser regressions passed; all 205 frontend files / 3695 tests passed; full lint, typecheck, browser TypeScript check, and build passed

It recorded a Chromium target crash, a worker exit with code 3221226505, and six other assertion/timeouts in history, queued drafts, and skeleton cases. Their causes remain unresolved; this run is retained as a failure and was not rerun to obtain a pass. No assertions, timeouts, retries, or production settings were weakened.
- [Final-head CI run 43193380297](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43193380297) is still running its browser job at the last bounded check. Python, WebUI checks/build, Terminal UI, and Docker passed; installer/native-package acceptance were skipped. The remote merge run is separate from these Windows PR-head results.

prs.body:
## Why

A persisted empty answer-stream ending can become a streaming assistant row even when the model produced no reasoning. Treating that generic streaming flag as reasoning displays a misleading “thought process” alongside tool calls.

## What changed

- Distinguish real reasoning from empty transport rows while retaining their stream identity and replay bookkeeping.
- Preserve activity grouping, history-window and fork-boundary accounting, and generic progress for active turns, including assistant-only runs.
- Exercise tool-only history, live continuation, real reasoning, session switching, and WebSocket reconnection in controlled WebUI fixtures.

## Scope

WebUI presentation and regression coverage only; no gateway protocol or persisted history changes.

## Tradeoffs

Empty stream rows remain in the event projection for ordering and late-frame fencing, but are absorbed rather than rendered as activity. Explicit reasoning events continue to drive the reasoning UI.

## Blast Radius

The change affects thread activity rendering, history windows, fork dividers, and the running indicator. It does not alter the underlying tool execution or stream delivery.

- `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2`: 202 files, 3,698 tests passed.

The `history-hydration.spec.ts` touch case timed out waiting for `scrollTop <= 1` (received 114). On the unmodified base, the same test failed at the same assertion with the same value. prs.title: fix(webui): preserve session caches during history revalidation
prs.body:
## Summary

Contributes to [NAN-439](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-439/统一-webui-session-缓存所有权并恢复切换前的阅读位置).

Keep the existing cache and transcript architecture. The final diff is **7 files, +67/-42, with no new test files or test cases**:

- Reject oversized LRU entries before evicting unrelated sessions; exclude pinned temporary working state from the reusable budget.
- Raise both the message-snapshot and history-response cache budgets from 16 MiB to 32 MiB each; retain the 12-entry limit and the existing fixed-budget LRU policy.
- Estimate shared objects once per snapshot and re-estimate mutable collections instead of reusing stale size memoization.
- Start the network read after installing a cached seed, and classify restored history as `latest`, allowing a safe disjoint page to replace its durable baseline without relaxing live-input reconciliation.
- Update the existing cache assertions and the ThreadShell test that previously expected stale history until another refresh.

The earlier broad draft's SessionStore, reading-position persistence, navigation and list/deletion changes have been withdrawn through follow-up commits, without rewriting published history. A history GET when returning to a session remains normal conditional revalidation; this change does not suppress it or introduce a new cache lifecycle.

## Validation

- Latest 32 MiB follow-up: all 7 existing cache tests, typecheck and ESLint passed. A separate synthetic probe against both default constructors accepted a snapshot above 16 MiB, rejected one above 32 MiB, and retained the admitted neighbor.
- Complete CI for the updated 32 MiB head is pending; the full-suite and real-data results below were obtained before this two-constant follow-up.
- Updated regression cases against the original production code: 5 failures reproduced.
- Local focused checks: 9 files / 387 tests passed; after the final read-binding cleanup, the 244 affected stream/shell tests passed again.
- Typecheck, ESLint, client import boundaries and their 42 tests, and production build passed.
- Current-instance real-data black-box acceptance passed on the production build: three idle histories rendered, the larger history paginated, and returning to the ordinary session restored cached rows while its HTTP response was held; release returned a real conditional 304. Larger histories and pagination did not evict that unrelated cache.
- A separately marked synthetic same-generation disjoint response replaced the restored history immediately; a subsequent real GET restored the original server data. No production history was modified.
- [Pre-budget-change CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43169520497) passed: all 3,679 WebUI unit tests (202 files), all 517 browser tests, import checks, lint, typecheck, production build, Docker acceptance and the required gates. Both WebUI jobs checked out the same PR merge snapshot; its tree was identical to the then-published head.
- NAN-439 retains the broader design record; reading-state/persistence and ownership refactors are not delivered by this narrowed PR.

No protocol change or shared-instance restart. Real-data acceptance used a GET-only adapter with a synthetic local WS: it could not write to production, and private history/credentials stayed local. The synthetic history-update case is reported separately from real HTTP-data checks; this is not full live-WS acceptance. Earlier local all-suite attempts exhausted host memory and were not passes; their complete WebUI suite replacement is the pre-budget-change CI above, not a claim of complete validation for the newer 32 MiB head.

prs.title: fix(webui): correlate chat requests and cancel stale reconnects
prs.body:
## Why

Creating or forking a topic during reconnect could open an existing topic instead, and a timed-out queued request could still create a chat later. Closing the client during reconnect token refresh could also reopen it or apply stale authentication. Give chat requests and reconnect work explicit ownership so late events cannot complete a different operation.

## What changed

- Match new-topic, temporary-chat, and fork successes and expected errors by `request_id`. The gateway echoes the ID; unrelated attachments and errors cannot complete a creation request.
- Keep creation requests in one `queued / sent` owner, separate from the reconnect replay queue. Timeouts release the pending request, expired unsent work is removed, sent work is never automatically replayed, and late temporary creations are discarded.
- Abort in-flight reauthentication before applying bootstrap state, settle connection-owned requests synchronously on close, and ignore callbacks from replaced sockets. Update protocol and user-facing timeout documentation.
- Focus the added regression coverage on distinct failures: 18 added cases instead of 44. Shared request handling is tested with representative lifecycle flows; all three creation commands retain ID-correlation coverage and temporary-chat disposal remains covered. Existing UUID-shim and untagged WebSocket/TUI coverage is reused instead of adding duplicate combinations.

## Scope

Support and test coverage are limited to same-version WebUI/gateway combinations, including remote gateways. Cross-version combinations may work but have no compatibility guarantee, even when protocol checks pass; align versions first when troubleshooting. This is a support policy, not a package-version equality gate: connections are not rejected solely because package versions differ.

This PR does not add chat-request capability negotiation or untagged response matching for older gateways. It fixes the confirmed WebUI lifecycle defects without rewriting application state machines or changing cron policy, tool-result durability, process startup, ordinary-message replay, or TUI behavior.

The shared WebSocket API still accepts requests without IDs for current callers such as the TUI; this is not a WebUI fallback to an older gateway. Existing unrelated capabilities are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

A timeout does not prove that creation failed. The user can initiate another request with a different ID, but the client does not automatically retry the old operation. Correlation IDs are not an exactly-once or deduplication promise. WebUI protocol remains 1.

## Blast Radius

WebUI connection/bootstrap handling and the gateway's chat-creation envelopes. Existing session data, execution ownership, authentication checks, workspace permissions, and message payload semantics are unchanged. No new `ready` capability field is introduced. The support-policy and test-consolidation follow-up does not change runtime code.

## Verification

- Follow-up: `cd webui && bun run test src/tests/nanobot-client.test.ts src/tests/app-layout.test.tsx src/tests/temporary-chat-navigation.test.tsx src/tests/main-randomuuid.test.tsx`: **4 files / 261 tests passed**.
- Follow-up: WebUI lint and typecheck, Ruff on both changed Python test files, Python syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local Python regression execution is unavailable in the current environment because `pytest` is not installed. Full Python, browser, and TUI verification for the follow-up is delegated to the latest-head CI checks.
- Before the follow-up, [Test Suite](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43004728027) passed for `d18fe83cff9ba8bf7addd11d9f030b857065ede7`: 12 checks succeeded; native package acceptance and Windows installer compatibility were skipped. See the PR checks for the follow-up head's results.

Resolves [NAN-432](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-432/修复-webui-会话创建与连接生命周期竞态)

issues.title: [Bug]: Android Webapp voice conversation ignores speech during an active assistant response
issues.body:
## Bug Description
During a continuous voice conversation in the Android browser-hosted Webapp, speech made while the assistant is still generating its reply is ignored. The reporter sees no responding audio waveform during that period and cannot give a spoken mid-turn correction; voice input becomes usable only after the reply has fully finished.

This is about capturing speech during an active response, not merely queuing a recognized transcript or choosing how to interrupt a running tool.

## Steps to Reproduce (reported on the user's phone)
1. Open Hermes Webapp in Chrome on Android and start a continuous voice conversation.
2. Speak a request that produces a sufficiently long assistant reply.
3. While the assistant is still responding, speak an additional instruction or correction.
4. Observe that the speech is ignored and there is no visible waveform response; wait until the assistant's reply finishes before attempting speech again.

## Expected Behavior
When voice barge-in is enabled, the voice conversation should detect speech during model generation and support interruption/steering rather than requiring the whole reply to finish. If listening is intentionally disabled, the UI should make that state and the controlling preference clear. This report does not request hard-cancelling side-effecting tools on any detected sound.

## Actual Behavior
The reporter says the input is ignored, not transcribed and queued, and no waveform appears. Lack of a waveform by itself is not proof of no active microphone stream: the barge-in monitor may not use the normal recording meter. Exact failure stage (capture, VAD, gating, transcription or presentation) remains unconfirmed.

## Verification / Environment
- User-reported on Android Chrome Webapp; exact Android/Chrome versions, selected voice engine and effective client barge-in state were not recorded.
- Observed deployed client `v0.23.1+4394`, backend `0.23.1`, Windows 11 host; installed commit `c9b20d7bc08dec1e10779a06d7d9073bc6e7e418`.
- Latest upstream fetched during reporting: `71b676524e1e26f69a4ddcc9945a89e59a38d650`; installed checkout remains unchanged, so no claim of a latest-build phone reproduction.
- No independent phone capture/network trace or automated microphone reproduction has been performed. No live settings were changed.

## Source Inspection (not a proven root cause)
`use-voice-conversation.ts` explicitly intends to arm a barge-in monitor while thinking/busy, before reply audio exists. `ensureBargeMonitor()` exits when `$bargeInEnabled` is false. The actual phone preference and whether this path ran still need verification.

- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/c9b20d7bc08dec1e10779a06d7d9073bc6e7e418/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts#L1057-L1063
- https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/c9b20d7bc08dec1e10779a06d7d9073bc6e7e418/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts#L612-L625

## Related Reports / Duplicate Search
- #93583 concerns CLI voice interruption being unreachable during thinking/tool execution, rather than Android Webapp capture.
- #133561 concerns detected speech hard-interrupting tools instead of steering; this report's symptom occurs before any recognized transcript is delivered.
- #108301 concerns becoming deaf after stopping read-aloud, not the general reported wait-until-reply-finishes pattern.
- #154819 is the separate mobile fan-menu tap/dictation collision.
- #154820 requests independent call-speech versus chat read-aloud preferences.

The same user has separately reported Chrome showing microphone activity after ending voice use. That cleanup symptom has not been verified as sharing this cause and is not presented as an established root cause here.

## Debug Report
Not uploaded because full dumps contain private conversation/configuration data. Targeted sanitized diagnostics can be gathered if requested. This report was prepared with assistant help and distinguishes user observations from source inspection; no source patch or PR is being submitted.

issues.body:
# [Bug]: Desktop boot loop on Windows: repair rewrites the unsigned `hermes.exe` launcher, Smart App Control blocks the new copy, probe fails forever

**Labels (if selectable):** comp/desktop, area/install-update, os/windows, type/bug

## Summary

On Windows 11 with **Smart App Control On**, a routine Hermes self-update can turn into an
unrecoverable desktop boot loop:

1. Desktop's runtime probe (`bin\hermes.exe --version`, exit-code gate in
   `apps/desktop/electron/backend-probes.ts` / `source-backend.ts`) fails during/after an update
   while the install is being rebuilt (shim temporarily points at a replaced hash-named PM
   environment → fast non-zero exit; non-timeout probe failures get no retry).
2. Probe failure → desktop declares the install "not usable" → prompts local/gateway setup and/or
   hands off to `hermes-setup.exe --repair --branch main`.
3. The repair "succeeds" — but it **rewrites `bin\hermes.exe` with a freshly built unsigned copy**.
4. Smart App Control judges files by identity: the long-lived launcher was accepted, but the new
   unsigned copy has no reputation → **Code Integrity blocks it** (events 3033/3077,
   "did not meet the Enterprise signing level requirements").
5. Next boot: probe cannot even spawn the launcher → "not usable" again → repair rewrites the
   launcher again → blocked again. **The loop is self-sustaining and never clears.**

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro, x64, `SmartAppControlState: On` (`(Get-MpComputerStatus).SmartAppControlState`)
- Hermes Agent v0.23.1 (commit `3b421578588243f920886e6fe79a6faa87ea026e`), install method: git bootstrap
- Desktop: `apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/Hermes.exe` (also NotSigned, but allowed by SAC reputation)
- CLI launcher: `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\bin\hermes.exe` — `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` → **NotSigned**

## Timeline from logs (one incident, Nov 12 2026, UTC+5:30)

- 20:15–20:26 — desktop boots during/just after self-update rebuild; probe fails fast each boot,
  logged as `[bootstrap] Hermes install at ... (from ...bin\hermes.exe) is not usable`.
  (Same transient pattern occurred after the Oct 15 update and recovered — no OS block involved then.)
- 20:26:22 — desktop hands off: `hermes-setup.exe --repair --branch main`.
- 20:44:52 — repair completes, **rewrites `bin\hermes.exe`** (new unsigned file).
- 20:27 onward — `Microsoft-Windows-CodeIntegrity/Operational` logs events **3033 + 3077 at every
  desktop boot**, blocking `bin\hermes.exe`: "did not meet the Enterprise signing level requirements".
- Direct confirmation: `& bin\hermes.exe --version` from PowerShell →
  *"An Application Control policy has blocked this file"*; CLI runs fine through the venv
  (`python -m hermes_cli.main --version` → exit 0), so the runtime is healthy — only the
  rewritten launcher is OS-blocked.
- Result: desktop forever shows first-run "local or gateway setup" prompt; every repair re-poisons
  the launcher. User had to wipe the install to recover.

## Why it recurs (root cause)

- `bin\hermes.exe` is shipped/self-built **unsigned**. SAC accepts a file once (reputation), but
  any rewrite creates a new identity and re-triggers evaluation.
- The repair flow re-publishes the launcher instead of preserving file identity.
- The desktop probe treats one failed spawn as "install not usable" (non-timeout failures fail
  immediately with no retry), funneling into repair instead of a bounded, explained recovery.

## Suggested fixes (any one breaks the loop)

1. **Sign the launcher** (`bin\hermes.exe`) with a certificate that satisfies SAC/Enterprise
   signing level — cleanest.
2. **Preserve file identity across repair/update**: if the existing `hermes.exe` is a valid
   launcher for the new install, keep the existing bytes and only rewrite when content actually
   changes; when it must change, write to a new name and swap.
3. Surface the real probe error (exit code / spawn error) in `desktop.log` next to
   "is not usable", and distinguish "OS blocked the launcher" (Code Integrity 3033/3077) from
   "CLI crashed", with distinct recovery copy instead of the generic first-run setup prompt.
4. On timeout-only retry exists today; consider one retry on **non-zero exit** when a
   `git`/PM operation was recently in flight (update window).

## Repro

1. Windows 11 with Smart App Control **On**.
2. Install Hermes (bootstrap). Works.
3. Trigger `hermes update` / repair that rewrites `bin\hermes.exe`.
4. Launch desktop → local/gateway setup prompt forever; Code Integrity events 3033/3077 each boot.
5. Only escape: disable SAC (permanent) or wipe + reinstall (which then gets blocked again on the
   next rewrite).

## Workaround used

Disabled Smart App Control (permanent) and reinstalled clean. Note the On→Off switch is one-way on
Windows, so affected users lose SAC entirely to keep using Hermes — worth fixing upstream.
