prs.title: fix(desktop): keep framed portrait markdown images inside their frame
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Keeps a framed portrait image in the desktop chat inside its reserved frame, so it no longer paints over the text below it.

A cold markdown image frame reserves a 4:3 box, and the image is capped with `max-h-full`. That percentage resolves against the click-target `<button>`, whose height is `auto`, so CSS drops the cap. A 1080x1920 image then draws at 640x1138 over a 640x480 frame.

This PR gives the click target the frame's height (`h-full`) when the image is framed, through a new optional `buttonClassName` prop on `ZoomableImage`. The image's `max-h-full` now has a definite height to resolve against.

Thanks to @lokeshvara123 for the precise root-cause write-up in the issue. The issue suggests a full-width container with a centred, flex button. That also stops the overflow, but in Chromium it moves the download button off portrait and small images, which the code comment in `MarkdownImageContent` wants to avoid ("the w-fit container hugs it so the download button and shadow sit on the image"). Keeping the `w-fit` container and only giving the button a height fixes the overflow and keeps the button on the image. I also left out `overflow-hidden` on the frame, so the image shadow is not clipped at the frame edges.

## Related Issue

Fixes #154409

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/components/chat/zoomable-image.tsx`: optional `buttonClassName` prop, merged into the click target's classes.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx`: `MarkdownImageContent` passes `buttonClassName="h-full"` when the image is framed, with a comment that explains why.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/chat/image-geometry.test.tsx`: two tests. A framed 1080x1920 markdown image keeps the height chain (frame aspect ratio, container `h-full`, button `h-full`, image `max-h-full`). An unframed image (a source that failed before) keeps its natural-height button.

## How to Test

1. In the desktop chat, show a portrait image taller than 4:3 (for example 1080x1920) as a markdown image or `MEDIA:` path.
2. Before: the image draws at 640x1138 and covers the next paragraph. After: it draws at 270x480 inside the 640x480 frame, and the next paragraph is readable and clickable.
3. Landscape (1920x1080) and small (300x300) images do not change, and the download button stays on the image.

prs.title: perf(desktop): reduce streaming and terminal hot-path work
prs.body:
**Stack 4/6:** Depends on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153067. Targets that branch; review the incremental diff.

- Preserve settled transcript identity through reconciliation and runtime normalization; deduplicate tool calls only on cache misses.
- Patch the live tail, use reference comparisons on live publishes, and retain the full preservation path for view-only assistant errors.
- Avoid unchanged metadata writes and activity notifications; keep one deadline timer per watchdog, with silence deadlines and event timestamps on the same monotonic clock.
- Move microphone levels into a recorder-owned nanostore, batch preview-console updates per frame, and isolate splitter-height subscriptions.
- Keep terminal backlog in capped chunks; read the composer prefix without cloning DOM and take conversion undo snapshots only on Space.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  D[Gateway delta] --> F[Flush scheduler]
  F --> T[Patch live tail]
  T --> V[Identity-preserving view sync]
  V --> R[Reuse settled runtime rows]
  R --> A[assistant-ui / Streamdown]
  F -. hidden, no voice consumer .-> H[250 ms floor]
  F -. visible or voice consumer .-> C[40 ms base floor]
```

- Visible base floor: 33 → 40 ms. Hidden streams use a 250 ms floor; voice consumers retain responsive updates.
- `session.info running=false` drains queued text before settling a live turn; superseded-turn orphan handling is preserved.
- Identity caches require immutable published rows and arrays. Reconciliation uses weak references so earlier streamed snapshots remain collectible.

- No blanket renderer-speedup claim: final whole-stack measurements show a strong terminal-backlog improvement, near-parity prose CPU, and worse dense-fence frame p95 despite lower script work. These are not incremental measurements against this PR’s parent.
- [Whole-stack measurements and remaining limits](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153070#issuecomment-6844735970).

**Next in stack:** https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/153069

prs.title: fix(prompt-caching): enable prompt caching and session affinity on Vercel AI Gateway
prs.body:
## Summary

When `model.provider` is `ai-gateway` / `vercel` (`https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1` on `chat_completions`), `anthropic_prompt_cache_policy()` previously only matched `openrouter.ai`, `nousresearch.com`, LiteLLM, and Alibaba/OpenCode — causing Claude, Kimi, and Qwen sessions on Vercel AI Gateway to return `(False, False)` with **0% prompt cache writes/reads** (e.g. 21M input tokens billed at full uncached input rates).

### Changes
1. **`agent/prompt_caching.py` & `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`:** Add `is_vercel_ai_gateway_route(provider, base_url)` (`vercel` / `ai-gateway` aliases and `ai-gateway.vercel.sh`) and opt Claude, Kimi, and Qwen on `chat_completions` into OpenAI-wire envelope `cache_control` (`(True, False)`).
   - Keeps `anthropic_messages` falling through to `(True, True)` (native inner-block layout) and `codex_responses` / `bedrock_converse` / implicit-cached models (`gpt-*`, `gemini-*`, `deepseek-*`) at `(False, False)`.
   - Uses Hermes's explicit `system_and_3` `cache_control` breakpoints rather than `providerOptions.gateway.caching: "auto"` because (a) AI Gateway ignores `cache_ttl` (`"1h"` / `"auto"`) when caching is configured only via `providerOptions.gateway.caching`, (b) Hermes's system+tools breakpoint survives mid-conversation context compression and tool-result pruning whereas `caching: "auto"`'s two tail markers miss after middle-of-prompt compaction, and (c) combining 4 explicit breakpoints with 2 automatic breakpoints would exceed Anthropic's 4-block limit.
   - Preserves part-level `cache_control` on `role: "tool"` content blocks (AI Gateway relocates tool-part `cacheControl` onto `tool_result.cache_control`) and `"ttl": "1h"` for Claude/Kimi (while Qwen still clamps to `"5m"` via `effective_cache_ttl`).
2. **`plugins/model-providers/ai-gateway/__init__.py`:** Send `x-session-affinity` derived from the conversation's cache scope so AI Gateway keeps multi-turn conversations pinned to the upstream provider (e.g. Direct Anthropic vs Bedrock vs Vertex) holding the warm prompt cache.
3. **CLI & Docs:** Update startup / `/model` switch prompt-caching labels, golden wire snapshots, unit tests, and user/developer docs.

## Test Plan
- `scripts/check` — 17/17 checks passed (`0 blocking, 0 advisory`)
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_anthropic_prompt_cache_policy.py tests/agent/test_prompt_caching.py tests/agent/test_litellm_tool_part_cache_markers.py tests/agent/test_provider_parity.py tests/agent/test_provider_attribution_headers.py tests/agent/transports/test_provider_wire_snapshot.py` — 267 passed, 0 failed

prs.title: fix(pm): survive a host that resets the TLS handshake
prs.body:
## What was wrong

A host can accept the TCP handshake and then reset the TLS ClientHello. To the caller
that looks like "the network blocks this client": every local-model download died with
`WinError 10054`, while the same URL downloaded fine in a browser.

Measured on one Windows host against `huggingface.co`, 20 interleaved rounds so network
drift cancels out:

| Variant | Handshakes |
|---|---|
| default `getaddrinfo` order (IPv6 first) | **3/20** |
| **IPv4 only** | **20/20** |
| classic Groups via `OPENSSL_CONF` | 6/20 |
| TLS 1.2 max | 4/20 |
| curl (prefers IPv4) | 20/20 |

Two independent causes, two fixes.

## 1. The address loop could not see the failure

`socket.create_connection` moves to the next address only when the **TCP connect**
itself fails. A reset during the TLS handshake happens *after* `connect()` returns, so
the failure is invisible to that loop — the working address is never tried and the
caller just sees a reset from a perfectly good network.

`_address_families` and `_AddressRacingHTTPSConnection` now race every resolved address
with the TLS handshake inside the loop, IPv4 first. IPv6 is still tried, so an IPv6-only
host works; a broken IPv6 path becomes a fallback rather than a failure.

## 2. No transport alternative

`pm/curl_transport.py` adds a curl fallback for connection-level failures, wired into
`Download._probe` and `Download._transfer`. curl's own retry budget rides out resets that
a 4-attempt urllib budget cannot.

The fallback is deliberately narrow — it fires only when the transport never got an
answer:

- **never on an HTTP status** — a 503 curl gets past would publish bytes the other client
  reports as an error
- **never on a truncated body** — the ranged path already resumes that byte by byte
- **never on a certificate failure** — trust is not transport, and a second trust store
  would launder an untrusted cert into a successful download

Disable with `download.allow_curl_fallback: false`. That is config, not an env var —
`.env` is secrets only. A missing or unreadable config leaves it on, so a broken config
file cannot take downloads down with it.

## Repro

```python
import socket, ssl
ok = 0
for _ in range(20):
    try:
        ip = socket.getaddrinfo("huggingface.co", 443, socket.AF_INET,
                                socket.SOCK_STREAM)[0][4][0]   # force IPv4
        with socket.create_connection((ip, 443), timeout=10) as s:
            with ssl.create_default_context().wrap_socket(s, server_hostname="huggingface.co"):
                ok += 1
    except Exception:
        pass
print(ok, "/20")   # 20/20 with AF_INET; ~3/20 with the default AF_UNSPEC
```

## Tests

- `tests/pm/test_address_racing.py` — pins the racing loop, including the
  `create_connection` behaviour it replaces (asserting the stock path *cannot* see a TLS
  failure, so the extra loop is justified rather than stylistic)
- `tests/pm/test_curl_fallback.py` — pins the fallback's gate: it fires on a dead
  transport and does not fire on a 404, a 403, or a certificate failure

**89 downloader tests pass.** Two suites fail in this sandbox and fail identically on
`main` — both assume the canonical repo layout.

## Note for reviewers

The `OPENSSL_CONF` ClientHello workaround documented for Codex device login does **not**
apply to this failure mode. Forcing classic Groups measured 6/20 against the same 3/20
baseline, so measure before reaching for it.

prs.title: fix(gateway): make FooteredReply survive copy, deepcopy and pickle
prs.body:
## What & why

`gateway.session_events.publish` `deepcopy()`s every frame it publishes. When `display.runtime_footer.enabled` is on, the `message.complete` payload carries a `FooteredReply` (a `str` subclass whose `__new__` takes `text, footer`). The default reduction for a `str` subclass reconstructs with `cls.__new__(cls)` and no arguments, so the deepcopy raised:

```
TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
```

That exception aborted the publication. `gateway.session_settlement_recovery` then logged `Settlement or publication of admission <id> failed`, the turn's admission never settled, and the viewer stayed on a stuck "working" indicator after **every** reply. The reply text itself still arrived (delivery is a separate path), so the visible symptom was a hang, not a lost answer.

Confirmed in `logs/agent.log` (`Settlement or publication ... failed` at 23:11:36, 23:18:00, 23:18:03) on a git install at `5c3421082d`.

## The fix

`FooteredReply` is immutable, so:

- `__copy__` / `__deepcopy__` return `self` (cheap, no state to duplicate);
- `__reduce__` rebuilds it from the original `(text, footer)` pair, so a pickle roundtrip yields the same subtype with the footer **once** instead of doubling it.

No behavior change for any other consumer: the object is still a plain `str` whose value is `text + "\n\n" + footer`, and any rewrite still degrades to a plain `str`.

## How to test

Reproduce before the fix:

```python
from copy import deepcopy
from gateway.runtime_footer import FooteredReply
deepcopy({"text": FooteredReply("hi", "model · 68% · ~")})
# TypeError: FooteredReply.__new__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'footer'
```

After the fix the same call returns the payload with `runtime_footer` intact.

New regression tests in `tests/gateway/test_runtime_footer_copy.py`:

```
python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_runtime_footer_copy.py -q   # 3 passed
```

- `deepcopy` of a payload holding the reply keeps the footer and the subtype,
- `copy`/`deepcopy` return the same object,
- pickle roundtrip keeps the footer exactly once.

Also verified end to end on a real install: with the patched module loaded after a gateway restart, replies publish `message.complete` normally — no `FooteredReply` tracebacks and no `Settlement or publication` failures in `agent.log` across several turns, and the indicator no longer sticks.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11 (git install, Python 3.14, desktop + CLI surfaces). The change is pure Python copy/pickle protocol — no platform-specific code.

## Related issues

No existing issue found for this (searched `FooteredReply`, `deepcopy`, stuck `working` indicator).

Post-deadline update, no features changed. Submitted pin: b3a3916 (still in
this pull request's history). New pin: 4d6f0cc, with two small fixes: a leftover
template file renamed, and the approval prompt moved to Hermes's public

Adds **Handle It** (`hermes-handle-it`), pinned to `4d6f0cce639c8f8c69919bf3678cfe8d752f410d` of https://github.com/casualsav/hermes-handle-it. Submitted by the repository's owner.

Handle It: a Hermes plugin that deals with customer support for you, by chat or by phone. Hermes holds a company's live support chat in its own browser, or phones its support line through bland.ai, waits on the human agent for as long as it takes, negotiates toward your goal, and asks you before it agrees to an offer, pays, cancels or shares a detail you did not allow. Ends with the outcome and a saved transcript.

Provides tools `support_chat_start`, `support_chat_send`, `support_chat_wait`, `support_chat_end`, `support_call_start`, `support_call_wait`, `support_call_end` and hooks `pre_tool_call` (routes risky messages through Hermes's approval gate) and `on_session_finalize`. `hermes plugins validate` passes at the pinned commit.

On a call, bland.ai's voice agent says at once that it is an AI assistant calling for a customer, knows only the details you allow, and cannot agree to anything: an offer is noted and comes back to you after the call. Approval while support holds works only if you expose the plugin's approval bridge at a public HTTPS address (`SUPPORT_CALL_BRIDGE_URL`). Afterwards the plugin checks the transcript against your allowed details and approvals and notes anything outside them.

**Disclosure**
- Opens the support pages you name in a local Chromium (Playwright), with its own profile.
- Types messages into those sites on your behalf.
- For phone calls: talks to bland.ai's API with your own key (`BLAND_API_KEY`) and places calls to the numbers you name. bland.ai records the call when you ask it to (`record: true`), and the agent then says the call is being recorded. Call costs are yours, billed by bland.ai.
- Reads a password from Hermes's vault only for a login handle it is given, and types it only on that login's own origin.
- Saves transcripts, screenshots, call records and the browser profile under `$HERMES_HOME/hermes-handle-it/`.
- No other network calls, no telemetry, no stored credentials.

**Tried:** a stand-in demo shop (included in the repo), end to end in Hermes Agent 0.21.5 on Linux arm64 in the CLI, including the vault sign-in; in tests, a chat in the page, a chat in an iframe behind a launcher, and a sign-in with a one-time code. One real call to a retailer's automated support line, asking its return window for online orders: answered in 1.6 minutes for $0.22.

**Not tried yet:**
- a human support agent on a call;
- an offer coming back for approval during a call;
- a real company's live chat (real widgets add cookie banners, pre-chat forms, canvas and closed shadow DOM);
- the approval card on a messaging gateway such as Telegram;
- macOS;
- chats that need a pre-chat form first.

prs.title: fix(desktop-plugins): reconcile installed halves by content, not mtime
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

An installed (non-linked) desktop half re-copied only when its source `plugin.js` carried a newer mtime than the marker's `sourceMtimeMs`. That misses the cases timestamps cannot see:

- changed bytes with the same mtime (`cp -p`, restores, timestamp-preserving checkouts) or an older one (`git stash pop`) left the published copy stale;
- a touch (same bytes, newer mtime) re-copied needlessly;
- a missing installed `plugin.js` under a current marker was never repaired.

Both writers now judge the copy current only when its entry point already holds the source's bytes — the rule linked dev checkouts already used. The marker keeps `sourceMtimeMs` untouched for older writers (no format change, no migration); only a corrupt stamp is repaired in place, best-effort, without a re-copy.

## Related Issue

No upstream issue filed; found as R2 during SpendSense release-acceptance review of desktop-half reconciliation.

## Type of Change

- `tests/hermes_cli/test_desktop_plugin_halves_content.py` (new): same/older-mtime content change installs; touch skips without marker churn; legacy marker judged by content; missing entry repaired; corrupt stamp repaired without re-copy; fresh install still stamps `sourceMtimeMs`; unwritable repair fails open.

prs.title: MCP servers whose reply cuts an emoji in half answer at once instead of hanging to the timeout (Copilot CLI 1.0.110 port)
prs.body:
When an MCP server sent a reply containing half of an emoji (a description or result cut in the middle of one), Hermes threw that reply away and kept waiting for it: `hermes mcp test` and startup discovery hung until the connect timeout, and a tool call hung for its full 5-minute budget. Now the broken character is read as a `�` and the reply arrives at once.

**Outcome:** an MCP server reply that carries a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape (or invalid UTF-8) answers its request immediately with U+FFFD in place of the bad character, on stdio, SSE and streamable HTTP.

Inspired by Copilot CLI [1.0.110](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/releases/tag/v1.0.110): *"A local MCP server whose reply contains a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape (such as a tool description cut inside an emoji) no longer fails after 60 seconds or hangs a tool call for 3 minutes; the reply is read with a replacement character."* Their CLI is closed source, so only the changelog line is available. The mechanism here comes from our own repro.

## What changes

| Server reply | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/list` description `"cut emoji \ud83d"` (`hermes mcp test sur`) | `✗ Connection failed (20.1s): ... timed out after 20s` | `✓ Connected (1845ms)` / `✓ Tools discovered: 1` / `t  cut emoji �` |
| `tools/call` text `"hi \ud83d"` (raw SDK session) | `TimeoutError` after the caller's wait (300 s default in Hermes) | `hi �` in 0.0 s |
| `hermes -z "call tool t on sur"` (OpenRouter gemini-3.7-flash, real gateway) | 157 s. The server never registered, so the model spent 40+ turns probing the SDK through `execute_code` before it reached the tool by hand | 10 s. `tool_describe` → `tool_call` → `hi �`, 3 model calls |
| Valid reply | unchanged | unchanged (the strict parser answers first, so the fallback never runs) |
| Reply that is not JSON at all | parse error | the same parse error (the original exception is re-raised) |

## Root cause
The MCP SDK (`mcp==2.3.0`, our pin and the latest on PyPI) parses every inbound JSON-RPC message with one pydantic `TypeAdapter` (`mcp_types.jsonrpc_message_adapter`). pydantic's JSON parser rejects a lone surrogate escape (`unexpected end of hex escape`). The transport logs the error and drops the message, so nothing ever answers the request id.

## Changes
- `tools/mcp_tool_wire_repair.py` (new, 60 lines): `install()` wraps the shared adapter's `validate_json` once. When the strict parse fails, it re-parses with stdlib `json` (which accepts lone surrogates; bytes are decoded with `errors="replace"`), replaces each lone surrogate with U+FFFD, and runs `validate_python`. If both parsers fail, the original error is raised. The install is idempotent.
- `tools/mcp_tool.py::_ensure_mcp_sdk`: calls `install()` while it binds the SDK. Every client transport (stdio `_parse_line`, SSE, streamable-HTTP SSE and JSON bodies) goes through that one adapter, so this single seam covers all of them.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_lone_surrogate_reply.py`: two invariants against a real stdio subprocess server: (1) `list_tools` and `call_tool` answer with `�`; (2) malformed JSON still raises. Test 1 fails on base (`TimeoutError`) and passes on head.

## Verification
- **Live repro:** `hermes mcp test sur` against a real stdio server whose `tools/list` description ends in `\ud83d`. main: `✗ Connection failed (20.1s)`; head: `✓ Connected (1845ms)`, 1 tool. A real `hermes -z` run on OpenRouter `google/gemini-3.7-flash` through the auto-spawned gateway: main 157 s with a degraded path, head 10 s with a direct `mcp__sur__t` call. Read back from each run's `state.db` (about 45 flash calls in total; cost not metered).
- Control: the same server with the surrogate removed answers on main in 0.0 s, so the surrogate is the only cause.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp*.py`: 105 files, 987 passed, 1 skipped.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking; ruff clean.

Not covered: no live HTTP/SSE server was run. Both transports call the same `jsonrpc_message_adapter.validate_json` (read from `mcp/client/sse.py` and `mcp/client/streamable_http.py` in 2.3.0).

## Infographic

![mcp-lone-surrogate](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab241c6/nvWOr86w1aEYAbM529bcg_rXpRRZmh.png)

prs.title: Stopping a command on macOS no longer lets the next step of the line run (port pi#11252)
prs.body:
On a Mac, pressing stop on a command like `build; rm -rf dist` could still run the `rm`: the stop killed `build`, and the shell woke up and started the next step before the stop reached it. Now the whole command line stops, and nothing after the step that was running gets to start.

Ported from earendil-works/pi 27cc6bfc0 ([pi#11252](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11252)). Deferred by the weekly Pi scout since 10-23 ("needs a macOS proof"); this run measured it on real macOS runners.

## Root cause

When a command is stopped (`/stop`, Ctrl+C, timeout), the local backend kills the shell's process group with `killpg(SIGTERM)`. Linux signals every member of the group under one kernel lock. macOS signals them one at a time, so the foreground `sleep` can die and wake its waiting shell first, and the shell then runs the next command of `a; b` before its own TERM arrives.

## Change

`tools/environments/local.py::_signal_group_frozen`: on darwin it SIGSTOPs the group, sends the signal, then SIGCONTs it. While stopped, each member holds the signal pending and takes it on SIGCONT before it runs another instruction, so no member can act in between. The stop is best-effort (a failed SIGSTOP never blocks the TERM). The TERM → wait → KILL escalation, the PID-reuse guard and the escaped-descendant sweep are unchanged. Linux and Windows are unchanged.

## Live A/B (GitHub `macos-latest`, real `LocalEnvironment.execute` + `tools.interrupt`)

`sleep 30 &` ×30 then `sleep 30; echo leaked > marker`, interrupted after 200 ms, 6 interrupts in parallel, every core loaded, 200 trials per leg:

| leg | rep 1 | rep 2 | rep 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | **22** leaked | **62** leaked | **70** leaked |
| this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The same probe with a single background member leaked 2/180 on main (0/180 on a second main leg). The race is real but rare in that shape, so the test uses the 30-member shape. Linux legs leaked 0 on both trees, as the kernel lock predicts. Proof run: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/43361359814 (temporary `proof/cancel-race-macos` branch, deleted after this PR).

## Test

`tests/tools/test_local_interrupt_next_command.py` is the same scenario (80 interrupts) marked `platforms("macos")`, so it runs in the tests-os macOS lane where the race exists and skips on Linux. With main's code, the leak rates above make 80 clean interrupts essentially impossible. Two `# health: allow HX013` sleeps are part of the scenario: the 200 ms before the stop, and the bounded window that proves the next command never wrote its file.

Also run: `tests/tools/test_local_interrupt_cleanup.py`, `test_local_setsid_descendant_sweep.py`, `test_local_env_session_leak.py` (20 passed). `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking.

Related open PR: #102518 changes how macOS children are spawned (no fork) and guards `killpg` on groups the child does not lead. It does not touch this signal-ordering race, and the two compose.

prs.title: Cron run transcripts and session previews show the job's prompt, not the scheduler's frame (port kimi-code#4780, salvage #137379)
prs.body:
When a scheduled job ran, its session opened with a wall of Hermes' own instructions to the model ("[IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job. DELIVERY: …"), and a skill-backed job opened with the entire skill file. Now the TUI and Desktop transcripts, and the session list, show the prompt you wrote for the job.

Cron run sessions now show the job's own prompt as their first message and as their sidebar/picker preview, on every surface that reads stored history.

Salvages #137379 by @ds-002 (5 commits cherry-picked, authorship kept) and ports MoonshotAI/kimi-code#4780 ("show only the scheduled prompt in cron-fired user messages").

## What changes

Real rows from a live `state.db` (one plain cron job, one skill-backed cron job), read through each surface's projection on `origin/main` vs this head:

| Surface | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar / session picker preview (plain job) | `[IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job. DELIVER...` | `Daily Scout Digest — compile the last 24 hours of cron job o...` |
| Sidebar / session picker preview (skill job) | `/hermes-agent-dev` | `Weekly Kimi Code PR Scout — scan merged PRs from MoonshotAI/...` |
| TUI + Desktop transcript, first bubble (plain job) | `[IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job. DELIVERY: Your final response will be…` | `Daily Scout Digest — compile the last 24 hours of cron job output…` |
| TUI + Desktop transcript, first bubble (skill job) | `/hermes-agent-dev [IMPORTANT: You are running as a scheduled cron job. DELIVERY: Your fina…` | `/hermes-agent-dev Weekly Kimi Code PR Scout — scan merged PRs…` |
| Desktop REST transcript (`/api/sessions/{id}/messages`, `display_content`) | raw frame | `Daily Scout Digest — …` |
| Bot Chat mirror (control) | `[Cronjob "x" output — …]` banner | unchanged in transcripts (the banner is the attribution a Bot Chat reader needs); preview shows the payload, per #137379 |

Nothing stored changes: the model still receives the identical prompt bytes, so prompt caching and the cron hint's injection-defence framing are untouched. Old sessions are fixed on read.

## Changes

- **#137379 (@ds-002):** `agent/system_wrappers.py` recognizers (cron hint, Bot Chat banner, previous-run block) + preview SQL/shaper cuts in `hermes_state_common.py`, `/rewind` and roster previews.
- **Hardening on top:**
  - The scheduler added a `[CURRENT RUN TIME: …]` line right after the hint after #137379 was written. On the contributor head every cron preview read `[CURRENT RUN TIME: Thursday, 2026-11-12 19:24 PST…`; the preview SQL and Python shaper now skip it.
  - Transcript bubbles (kimi #4780's actual fix): `cron_prompt_display_text` feeds the TUI/Desktop resume projection (`tui_gateway/session_history.py`), the Desktop REST projection (`display_content` in `hermes_cli/web_routers/sessions.py`), and the skill-invocation describer, so a skill-backed job reads `/skill <job prompt>`.
  - Preview SQL size: the contributor's chained cuts re-copied each input into every `CASE` arm (19.1 KB per-row expression, 150 KB once the run-time cut is added). Each cut now binds its input once via a correlated derived table: 4.9 KB (main: 2.4 KB).
  - Contract test reads the banner from `cron.scheduler_delivery.bot_chat_message`; the `_run_bot_chat_turn` seam it patched no longer exists on main.

**Root cause:** the cron scheduler stores its full model-facing frame as the run's user row, and no display projection knew that frame's shape.

## Verification

- **Live repro:** real cron rows from `~/.hermes/state.db` (read-only) inserted into a scratch `SessionDB`, read through `list_sessions_rich`, `tui_gateway.server._history_to_messages` and `web_routers.sessions._project_for_display` on an `origin/main` worktree vs this head. Output is the table above.
- Tests: `tests/agent/test_system_wrapper_preview_strip.py` + `tests/cron/test_system_wrapper_contract.py` 17 passed. New/updated assertions are red on the contributor head (3 failures: run-time line, transcript projection). Neighbour suites (hermes_state, skill_commands, skill_invocation_description, web sessions, tui history, cron prompt injection): 1692 passed. `tests/hermes_state/test_hermes_state.py` hits the runner's local 300 s cap on this host for origin/main too; CI decides it.
- `scripts/check --only health`: 0 blocking. `audit_pr_attribution.py`: all mapped.

**Not covered:** no Desktop screenshot pass. The Desktop renderer is unchanged: it already prefers `display_content` and the gateway `text`. The evidence is the projection output above.

## Infographic

![cron transcripts show the job prompt](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab2416d/L0_RiIOTwJ3cnUdf76beL_Pj3neYVG.png)

prs.title: fix(tui): keep a detached session alive while a subscribed Kanban card is in flight
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A Desktop/TUI agent that creates a Kanban card is auto-subscribed to it (`platform="tui"`, `chat_id=session_key`) and typically ends its turn with "I'll report back when it finishes". The only delivery path for that notice is the session's own notification poller. When the window closes, the WS-orphan reaper can pop the detached session before the poller claims the card's `completed` event, losing the notice until the user reopens the chat.

The poller continues running while the session is detached (`tui_gateway/session_registry.py:145`, `tui_gateway/session_notifications.py:824-850`). The keepalive therefore covers both moving subscribed cards and recent, unclaimed notification events. Unclaimed events expire from the guard after 60 seconds; the bound prevents a stuck event from pinning the session forever. `blocked`, `triage` and `scheduled` cards do not pin the session.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tui_gateway/session_notifications.py`: keeps a detached session alive while its subscribed card is moving, its completed event is still unclaimed within the 60-second TTL, or a claimed notice is buffered for the next turn.
- `hermes_cli/kanban_db_notify.py`: adds a read-only count of recent unclaimed subscribed events, filtered by session and event kind.
- `tests/tui_gateway/test_detached_kanban_notify_keepalive.py`: replaces the settled-card release expectation with contract coverage for keeping the session until claim and releasing it after the TTL.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tui_gateway/test_detached_kanban_notify_keepalive.py` — 5 tests passed on this branch. The replacement contract asserts an unclaimed completion keeps the detached session alive and that claiming the event allows reaping; the same scenario is unprotected on baseline `c6a7fcd6a1`.
2. `python scripts/check` — attempted, but the tool call timed out after 420 seconds; result unverified.

prs.title: fix(agent): recover Azure cross-resource Responses replay rejection
prs.body:
## What changed

Recognize the Azure rejection:

> The requested item was created under a different Azure OpenAI resource. Use the same resource that created the item to access it.

Map it to the existing `invalid_encrypted_content` recovery rather than an unrecoverable request-format error. The classifier keeps its bounded, single-sentence rejection frame and negative controls; unrelated resource, authentication and rate-limit errors do not match it.

**The initial classifier-only commit was insufficient.** Follow-up investigation found that recovery removed `codex_reasoning_items` but retained `codex_message_items[].id`. The Responses adapter suppresses a linked message ID while encrypted reasoning is present; removing that reasoning can therefore reintroduce the saved ID into the next request.

This follow-up:

- Removes cached assistant message item IDs from canonical history and the independent request copy before either the unverified-replay or full-reasoning-strip rung returns.
- Handles message-ID-only histories, including when encrypted reasoning replay is already disabled, with the existing per-route retry guard.
- Preserves message text, status, phase, tool-call IDs and their result associations. Normal successful serialization is unchanged.
- Preserves the existing reasoning replay policy. A message-ID-only repair does not mark fresh reasoning unusable. A `token_expired` 401 still requires cached reasoning before bypassing credential recovery.

No relay-specific configuration, credential changes, broader classifier matching or history reset is introduced. This extends the recovery mechanism used by #106718, for a different rejection and an additional retained replay carrier.

## Reproduction and verification

Follow-up baseline: `90f7560c1de312c46a7bc61edf0f6cda843fe9bd`, the original head of this PR. The original classifier change was tested against upstream base `392f551498d0832ec99be520fcbfd398e3f9b7aa`.

The final regression file on the unchanged follow-up baseline: **19 passed, 4 failed**. The four failures cover unverified reasoning, current-route reasoning, ID-only history and replay-disabled history. The identical test file passes on the candidate: **23 passed, 0 failed**.

Selected regression run on Windows with the prepared Python 3.14 test environment: **307 passed, 0 failed**:

```bash
bash scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/agent/test_error_classifier.py \
  tests/agent/test_codex_token_expired_replay_recovery.py \
  tests/agent/test_azure_cross_resource_replay_recovery.py \
  tests/agent/test_stale_replay_prune.py \
  tests/agent/test_reasoning_replay_routes.py \
  tests/agent/test_replay_cleanup.py \
  tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py \
  -j 2 --file-retries 0 --file-timeout 180 -q --tb=short
```

```bash
python scripts/check --base 90f7560c1de312c46a7bc61edf0f6cda843fe9bd --staged
# 15 checks, ok
```

Tests use real SDK exception types, the recovery chain and `ResponsesApiTransport.convert_messages`. They inspect the rebuilt wire input, not just deletion of the reasoning field, and check that ordinary errors, non-Responses requests, ID-free histories, exhausted repair guards and credential refresh remain unaffected. Raw logs, failure IDs and source hashes are retained outside the repository.

## Live diagnosis and limits

A separate, bounded three-request diagnostic probe used neutral text: a clean request succeeded (200); a request carrying a saved historical message ID received the same Azure rejection (400); the identical request with only that ID removed succeeded (200). No real conversation text was sent. This demonstrates one reproducible failure path, not that every relay error has this cause.

That probe predates the candidate and is **not** an end-to-end live validation of the patched agent. The full repository suite and a controlled switch between two owned Azure resources were not run. This is client-side recovery, not a fix for relay routing affinity or general availability.

The masked `*** OpenAI resource` variant remains a synthetic classifier test based on local logs; whether that wording originated upstream or in local redaction is unverified. No credentials, private transcripts, historical item IDs, ciphertext or local bot configuration are included. Implementation and evidence review are AI-assisted.

issues.title: Model identifier validation suggests lowercasing unknown provider prefixes, breaking case-sensitive upstream model IDs
issues.body:
## Summary

In the model edit sheet, entering a model identifier whose prefix is **not** a picoclaw provider but is an upstream model namespace (for example `ACME/gpt-4o-mini`, where the upstream API is case-sensitive) shows a warning:

> "ACME" should use "acme" — Fix

Clicking **Fix** rewrites the model to `acme/gpt-4o-mini`. With case-sensitive upstream routing this breaks a previously working configuration (401 / provider not found).

## Steps to reproduce

1. WebUI → Models → Edit (or Add) a model.
2. Provider = OpenAI, API Base = an OpenAI-compatible gateway, Model identifier = `ACME/gpt-4o-mini` (the prefix is an upstream namespace, not a picoclaw provider key).
3. The form shows the warning `"ACME" should use "acme"` with a Fix button.
4. Click Fix → the field becomes `acme/gpt-4o-mini`; saving it makes the upstream reject the request because its provider namespace is case-sensitive.

## Expected

- No "should use" suggestion unless the prefix actually maps to a known provider/alias in the provider catalog.
- When a Provider is selected and the field is documented as a full model ID (the field hint says a slash-containing value is kept as a full ID and not re-split), provider-prefix validation should be skipped.
- At minimum, do not offer a destructive one-click "fix" that lowercases an unknown prefix.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:26-28` — `normalizeProvider()` lowercases the input.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts:76-82` — `getCanonicalProviderKey()` returns `aliasMap[normalized] ?? normalized`; for an **unknown** prefix it falls back to the lowercased input instead of returning empty.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts:85-91` — the validator treats that fallback as a real alias and emits `models.validation.shouldUse` with `fix: ${alias}/${model}`.
- `web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:268-269` — the Fix button applies `modelValidation.fix` to the input.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/provider-registry.ts
@@ -79,7 +79,7 @@ export function getCanonicalProviderKey(
   const normalized = normalizeProvider(provider)
   if (!normalized) return ""
-  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? normalized
+  return getProviderAliasMap(backendOptions)[normalized] ?? ""
 }

--- a/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
+++ b/web/frontend/src/components/models/model-validation.ts
@@ -64,6 +64,17 @@ export function validateModelField(
   const provider = trimmed.slice(0, slashIdx)
   const model = trimmed.slice(slashIdx + 1)
   if (!model) {
     return { level: "error", messageKey: "models.validation.emptyModel" }
   }
 
+  // When a provider is explicitly selected, a slash-containing identifier is
+  // documented as a full model ID for that provider (see modelIdHint) — do not
+  // re-interpret its first segment as a provider prefix.
+  if (selectedProvider) {
+    return {
+      level: "success",
+      messageKey: "models.validation.parsed",
+      messageParams: { provider: selectedProvider, model: trimmed },
+    }
+  }
+
   if (!knownProviderKeys.has(provider)) {
```

Add a regression test with an uppercase upstream namespace (e.g. `ACME/model`) and a lowercase provider alias in the catalog, asserting that no `shouldUse` warning is produced.

## Impact

One click can silently change a working model ID to a different, invalid one; the UI appears to be helping but breaks the configuration. This is more than a cosmetic warning.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI

issues.title: WebUI falsely reports "restart required" after gateway hot-reload has already applied the config
issues.body:
## Summary

With `gateway.hot_reload: true`, changing the default model in the WebUI is applied by the gateway within ~2 seconds (confirmed in the gateway log), but the WebUI still shows the "restart required" toast, and `gateway_restart_required` in the gateway status stays `true` until the launcher/gateway is restarted.

This makes operators think the change did not take effect and repeatedly restart the service, interrupting active chats.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"gateway": {"hot_reload": true}` in `~/.picoclaw/config.json` (default is `false`) and restart `picoclaw-launcher.service` once so the watcher is enabled.
2. In the WebUI, change the default model (or edit a model setting) and save.
3. With `gateway.log_level: info`, `~/.picoclaw/logs/gateway.log` shows:
   ```
   🔄 Config file changed, reloading...
    New model is '<new-alias>', recreating provider...
   Provider and config reloaded successfully
     ✓ Provider, configuration, and services reloaded successfully (thread-safe)
   ```
   The gateway PID does not change, and the new model is actually used.
4. The save toast still says "restart required", and `GET /api/gateway/status` returns `gateway_restart_required: true`.

## Expected

- When hot reload has successfully applied the change, the WebUI should not ask for a restart.
- If a change genuinely requires a process restart, the prompt should only appear in that case.

## Actual

The flag stays `true` after every config save, even though `handleConfigReload` already applied the new provider/config in-process.

## Root cause (v0.3.1, git 2cf030d2)

- The flag is computed by the launcher backend, not the gateway:
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:807-814` — `gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus)`.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:864-868` — `attachToGatewayProcessLocked()` records `gateway.bootConfigSignature` when the launcher attaches.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1086` — the launcher records it when it starts the gateway.
  - `web/backend/api/gateway.go:1471-1477` — status compares the recorded signature with the current config signature.
- Hot reload happens inside the gateway process (`pkg/gateway/gateway.go:257` starts the polling watcher; `pkg/gateway/gateway.go:586-660` `handleConfigReload` recreates the provider and restarts services). There is no callback to the launcher, so `bootConfigSignature` is never refreshed.
- The WebUI consumes `gateway.restartRequired` directly (`web/frontend/src/components/models/edit-model-sheet.tsx:395-399`, `web/frontend/src/lib/restart-required.ts`).
- `computeConfigSignature()` only covers model/default/streaming, tool enablement and channel settings — all of which `handleConfigReload` applies. It does not include process-level fields such as `gateway.host`/`gateway.port`, so the current flag is effectively only ever about hot-reloadable config.

## Proposed patch

```diff
--- a/web/backend/api/gateway.go
+++ b/web/backend/api/gateway.go
@@ -804,14 +804,20 @@
-func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string) bool {
+func gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(bootSignature, currentSignature, gatewayStatus string, hotReload bool) bool {
 	if gatewayStatus != "running" {
 		return false
 	}
 	if bootSignature == "" || currentSignature == "" {
 		return false
 	}
+	// With hot reload enabled, the gateway watcher applies every field covered
+	// by computeConfigSignature (model/tools/channels) in-process. A launcher-
+	// side restart is not required for these changes.
+	// Process-level settings (host/port) are not part of this signature.
+	if hotReload {
+		return false
+	}
 	return bootSignature != currentSignature
 }
@@ -1468,9 +1474,12 @@
 	gatewayStatus, _ := data["gateway_status"].(string)
 	currentConfigSignature := computeConfigSignature(cfg)
+	hotReload := cfg != nil && cfg.Gateway.HotReload
 	gateway.mu.Lock()
 	bootConfigSignature := gateway.bootConfigSignature
 	gateway.mu.Unlock()
 	data["gateway_restart_required"] = gatewayRestartRequiredBySignature(
 		bootConfigSignature,
 		currentConfigSignature,
 		gatewayStatus,
+		hotReload,
 	)
```

Alternative (more robust long-term): have the gateway publish an "applied config signature" (pid file field or health endpoint), update it on every successful `handleConfigReload`, and have the launcher compare the current config against that value instead of its boot-time value.

## Verification after patch

1. Enable `hot_reload`, restart once.
2. Change the default model in the WebUI and save.
3. The toast should be the normal "saved" success message; `gateway_restart_required` should be `false`.
4. Switch back and repeat.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git 2cf030d2), Linux, WebUI
- `gateway.hot_reload: true`

issues.title: Add Android API 19 support for x86_32 and x86_64 architectures
issues.body:
## 🎯 The Goal / Use Case

Expand PicoClaw's Android compatibility to cover legacy devices and emulators running **Android 4.4 (API 19)** on **x86_32 (32-bit)** and **x86_64 (64-bit)** architectures. 

Many older TV boxes, tablets, and single-board computers (SBCs) still in use today rely on x86-based Android builds (e.g., Intel Atom or AMD APUs) with API 19. Furthermore, x86 Android emulators are widely used for testing and development. Providing pre-built binaries or APKs for these targets would fulfill the project's goal of being a truly lightweight AI assistant that runs on almost any hardware. 

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Provide dedicated release artifacts (standalone binaries or APK builds) for the following targets:
- `android/386` (x86_32)
- `android/amd64` (x86_64)

These builds should be compiled with a minimum API level of 19.

## 🔧 Potential Implementation (Optional)

- **Go Cross-Compilation**: Since PicoClaw is written in Go, adding these targets to the build matrix (e.g., in `.goreleaser.yaml` or the Makefile) is straightforward:
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=386 GOARM=` (for x86_32)
  - `GOOS=android GOARCH=amd64 GOARM=` (for x86_64)
- **CGO/NDK**: Ensure any C dependencies (if present) are compiled using the Android NDK with `APP_PLATFORM=android-19`.
- **Binary Size**: The current build is already very small (~10MB); x86 builds should remain similarly lightweight.

## 🚦 Impact & Roadmap Alignment

- [x] This is a Nice-to-Have / Enhancement
- [ ] This is a Core Feature
- [ ] This aligns with the current Roadmap

**Justification**: While modern Android devices are predominantly ARM64, the x86 Android ecosystem (especially for old TV boxes and emulators) is still active. This feature would significantly expand the user base and align with the project's "runs anywhere" philosophy. 

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Running via Termux**: The current Termux guide only supports ARM64 devices. Termux on old x86 Android builds is often unstable and not officially supported.
- **Using the current APK**: The current APK requires a minimum of Android 7 (API 24) and is built for ARM64, making it incompatible with API 19 x86 devices.

## 💬 Additional Context

- **Existing 32-bit limitation**: A related issue (#2954) already reports that 32-bit Android is not supported. This request extends that to the x86 architecture.
- **Low resource footprint**: PicoClaw is known for using less than 10MB of RAM. It is an ideal candidate for reviving extremely old x86 Android hardware (e.g., first-generation Intel TV sticks).
- **Testing**: I am willing to test the binaries on an x86_32 Android 4.4 emulator and an old x86_64 TV box if the builds are provided.

prs.title: build(deps): bump modernc.org/sqlite from 1.53.0 to 1.61.1
prs.body:
Bumps [modernc.org/sqlite](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite) from 1.53.0 to 1.61.1.
Release notes

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's releases.

v1.61.1

Signed provenance for this release: the two files below. VERIFYING.md in the repository says how to check them.

Changelog

Sourced from modernc.org/sqlite's changelog.

Changelog

Entries for v1.38.1 through v1.44.1 and for v1.49.1 were added on 2026-09-05, reconstructed from the git history and the merge requests they cite; they were missing at release time.

  • 2026-11-02 v1.61.2:

    • Limit now works on a connection handed out by a driver.Connector that wraps the ones NewConnector opens, provided the wrapper has an Unwrap() driver.Conn method; it used to fail with unexpected driverConn type. NewConnector now also says which optional interfaces such a wrapper must forward. Resolves [GitHub issue #11](modernc-org/sqlite#11), thanks Andres Morey (@​amorey)!

  • 2026-10-31 v1.61.1:

    • Prepared statements are no longer parsed and planned again on every execution. Since v1.61.0, SQLite 3.54 expired a cached statement that has a col = ? term in a join or an ORDER BY query whenever the driver cleared its bindings after a run, so a statement prepared with db.Prepare or tx.Prepare cost about twice what it did in v1.60.1. Integer bindings now stay in place between executions, so a parameter bound to 0 or 1 does not re-prepare it either. Resolves [GitLab issue #264](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/264). See [GitLab merge request #147](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/147), thanks Roman Khafizianov (@​requilence)!
    • Fix a panic reachable from SQL through a VFS made by vfs.New. It reported its files as writable, so with PRAGMA journal_mode=OFF a write reached a write method the VFS does not have and the process panicked, as did closing a WAL database shipped with its -wal file; with the journal on, the write failed with a misleading SQLITE_NOMEM. Such files are now read-only to SQLite, and every write fails with SQLITE_READONLY. See [GitLab merge request #145](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/145), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Fix a process abort reachable through a VFS made by vfs.New. SQLite's request to delete a journal, made when PRAGMA journal_mode leaves PERSIST or TRUNCATE and on the first read of a 0-byte database that has a -journal file next to it in the served file system, reached the transpiled xDelete, an unimplemented stub that aborted the process. It now fails with SQLITE_IOERR_DELETE, which SQLite tolerates, and nothing is deleted; the write methods the VFS lacked answer SQLITE_READONLY instead of being nil.
    • Tx.Commit now stops waiting for a lock once the context given to BeginTx is done, and Rows.Next and Rows.Close once the query's context is done, each returning the context's error; they used to wait the full busy_timeout when a reader's lock in rollback-journal mode blocked the COMMIT, or the commit of an autocommit INSERT ... RETURNING finished or closed after its first row. Only the wait watches the context; Rollback is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #263](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/263), thanks SirLouen!
    • The attest CI job now copies vendor.json into the provenance document from the tagged commit, not from the working tree make vendor-check has just stamped with its own Go release; the v1.61.0 job failed its own verification over that field, so v1.61.0 has no provenance document, see VERIFYING.md. Tooling only.
    • Add THREAT-MODEL.md, the threat model behind the scope in SECURITY.md: the connection string, the connection lifecycle, the page cache binding and the VFS bridge, one row per concern with its status and the commit that settled it. TestVFSReadEOF now also checks the short read on vfsRead itself. Documentation and tests only. See [GitLab merge request #146](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/146), thanks Ian Chechin!

  • 2026-10-21 v1.61.0:

    • Upgrade to SQLite 3.54.1, re-vendoring lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.2 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.7.0; sqlite-vec stays v0.1.9. The pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.79.0; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Add _time_format=string_no_monotonic, opt-in: times are written in the default layout but without Go's monotonic clock reading, the m=+... suffix, so a scanned time matches its row again when bound in WHERE col = ?. The default is unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #259](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/259). See [GitLab merge request #142](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/142), thanks 不插电 (@​r27153733)!
    • Each release tag now gets a signed provenance document, linked from its GitLab release; VERIFYING.md says what it proves and how to check one. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #141](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/141).
    • Add an opt-in SQLite authorizer per connection: AuthorizerRegisterer, reached through sql.Conn.Raw or installed on every pooled connection from RegisterConnectionHook; existing connections are unchanged. Resolves [GitLab issue #256](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/256). See [GitLab merge request #139](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/139), thanks Tedla Brandsema (@​TedlaBrandsema)!
    • Closing a connection now forgets the pre-update, commit and rollback hooks registered on it; their entries used to linger after Close.
    • With a shared cache, BeginTx now waits for a lock another connection holds instead of failing at once with SQLITE_LOCKED_SHAREDCACHE (262), as executing BEGIN IMMEDIATE did; Commit and Rollback wait likewise while another connection changes the schema. busy_timeout does not bound the wait; the call's context does. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • PrepareContext and BeginTx with a context that is already done now return the context's error, as ExecContext and QueryContext do. See [GitLab merge request #143](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/143), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • A context that is done before a statement starts running, for example while its arguments are being bound, now stops the statement within 1000 VM steps. SQLite discarded that interrupt, so a long statement ran to completion and only then returned the context's error. See [GitHub pull request #9](modernc-org/sqlite#9), thanks Chris Gianelloni (@​wolf31o2)!
    • A statement waiting for a lock under busy_timeout now stops waiting once its context is done, with the context's error, instead of sleeping on until the timeout; the wait's retry schedule and its bound are otherwise unchanged, and so is a call without a deadline. PrepareContext ended this way returns the context's error too, where it returned SQLITE_BUSY. Resolves [GitLab issue #262](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/262), thanks SirLouen!

  • 2026-09-29 v1.60.1:

    • Binding arguments to a statement is no longer quadratic in the number of its parameters, which made multi-row INSERTs with thousands of ? parameters slow. Resolves [GitHub issue #8](modernc-org/sqlite#8), thanks wencycool!

  • 2026-09-28 v1.60.0:

    • A fault while reading the memory-mapped -shm file of a WAL database no longer crashes the process. The statement fails with a disk I/O error, extended code SQLITE_IOERR_IN_PAGE (8714), and the connection stays usable, as in MSVC builds of SQLite. On by default on every platform and not switchable; lib.SehInject and lib.SehPending inject such a fault for tests. Resolves [GitLab issue #221](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/221), thanks Roman (@​requilence) for the report, and supersedes libsqlite3!4 and [GitHub pull request #7](modernc-org/sqlite#7), thanks hazyhaar for the two rounds, the ccgo finding and the Windows Server runs!
    • Re-vendor lib/ from modernc.org/libsqlite3 v1.15.0 and vec/ from modernc.org/libsqlite_vec v0.6.0; SQLite stays 3.53.4 and sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Go 1.26 is now required, and the pinned modernc.org/libc becomes v1.77.1; as always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does, see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Nine exported lib constants that never had a meaningful value are gone: INFINITY, MB_CUR_MAX, NAN, RESERVED_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST, SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT, SQLITE_CORRUPT_BKPT, SQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE and SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT. The transpiler now evaluates object-like macros as C expressions, so other constants take their C value (lib.WALINDEX_PGSZ is 32768, not 0) and some appear; the full list is in libsqlite3's CHANGELOG under 2026-09-19.
    • make vendor now writes vendor.json, the modernc.org/libsqlite3 and modernc.org/libsqlite_vec commits and the Go toolchain lib/ and vec/ were vendored with, so git show vX.Y.Z:vendor.json says which revisions a release carries; the test suite fails when they no longer match. Tooling only. See [GitLab merge request #140](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/140).
    • vfs.FS.Close now refuses while a database opened through it is still open, returning an error that wraps the new vfs.ErrInUse and leaving the VFS registered. It used to free the VFS the open connection still called through, so the next query crashed the process or read through freed memory. Close the databases first, then the FS.
    • Fix handle reuse in modernc.org/sqlite/vfs on 32-bit targets: after 2^32 file opens in one process the handle counter wrapped and could overwrite a live entry, such as a file system registered at start-up, and crash. 64-bit targets were not affected.
    • The pluggable page cache now panics when a Cache breaks its contract by returning nil, or a different Page, from Fetch for a page SQLite still holds pinned. It used to free memory SQLite was still using, corrupting the database without an error. Only a Cache implementation with that bug is affected; modernc.org/sqlite/pcache is not.
    • Document three limits of the pluggable page cache on RegisterPageCache and Cache: it cannot be combined with modernc.org/sqlite/vec, PageCache.Create may be called concurrently, and under cache=shared a Cache is called from several goroutines. Documentation only.
    • Document in the package documentation that state set on a pooled connection is inherited by the next caller to borrow it, and that a connection reached through sql.Conn.Raw is not safe for concurrent use. Documentation only.
    • Add StrictPragmas, opt-in and off by default: once enabled, a connection whose _pragma DSN value holds more than one SQL statement fails to open with ErrMultiStatementPragma, before any DSN parameter is applied. A _pragma value runs as SQL text, so anything after a ; runs too. Recommended for any application whose DSN is not a compile-time constant.
    • Document SQLite's own URI query parameters on Driver.Open: mode, cache, immutable, nolock, psow and modeof, which have always worked in a DSN starting with file:, and the trap that a plain file name has its query stripped before SQLite sees it, so /path/to.db?mode=ro opens read-write. Resolves [GitLab issue #257](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/257). Documentation only.
    • Add SECURITY.md, the vulnerability reporting policy: three private channels, what is in scope, that only the latest release is supported, and how a confirmed report is disclosed, including an entry in the Go vulnerability database so govulncheck reports it. IRP.md, linked from it, is the maintainers' incident response plan. Documentation only.
    • Add CONTRIBUTING.md: where to send a merge request, which files are generated and must not be edited by hand, how to build and test across the 20 supported targets, and the AUTHORS/CONTRIBUTORS convention. Documentation only.
    • Ship LICENSE-3RD-PARTY.md, a transitively flattened inventory of every third-party component this module carries with all seventeen license texts in full, and a Software Bill of Materials, sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.6) and sbom.spdx.json (SPDX 2.3), explained in SBOM.md. Both cover what a module-graph tool cannot see: the transpiled SQLite and sqlite-vec C, and the upstreams modernc.org/libc carries, musl among them. Documentation only.

  • 2026-09-15 v1.59.0:

    • Bump the pinned modernc.org/libc to v1.75.7 and re-vendor lib/ and vec/. The transpiled SQLite is unchanged, still 3.53.4. On the Linux targets the new libc replaces transpiled musl memcpy, memmove, memset, memcmp and strlen with native Go, cutting CPU time on query-heavy workloads by up to a third; see the new Performance section below. As always, downstream go.mod files must pin the same modernc.org/libc version this repository's go.mod does; see [GitLab issue #177](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/177).
    • Hand user-defined function and aggregate callbacks a pooled *FunctionContext instead of allocating a fresh one per call, removing the last driver-side allocation per invocation. Like the argument slice, it is valid only for the duration of the callback and must not be retained past its return. Updates [GitLab issue #226](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/issues/226). See [GitLab merge request #137](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/137).
    • Add regression tests pinning the identity and the pooling of that context. See [GitLab merge request #138](https://gitlab.com/cznic/sqlite/-/merge_requests/138), thanks Ian Chechin!
    • Add a Performance section to the package documentation: measured CPU-time ratios of this driver against the same SQLite compiled from C, where the gap comes from, and the two consequences for applications — index the columns that ORDER BY, GROUP BY and WHERE use, and bound the database/sql pool with SetMaxOpenConns.

... (truncated)

Commits

  • e699042 conn.go, stmt.go, rows.go: unbind only the parameters that point into the dri...
  • 519e1d2 Merge branch 'clear-bindings-reprepare' into 'master'

prs.title: fix(discord): bump discordgo fork past the gateway handshake deadlock
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

The Discord channel can go permanently deaf: the bot stays "connected", but nothing comes in or goes out, no heartbeat is sent, and nothing is logged. The cause is a deadlock in the pinned `discordgo` fork commit (`yeongaori/discordgo-fork@e8e546f`, 2026-03-19). The fork fixed it a week later. This PR moves the pin forward and adds a regression test.

**The deadlock.** `Session.Open` holds `s.Lock()` (deferred unlock) for the whole handshake. If Discord's first packet after IDENTIFY/RESUME is Op 9 (Invalid Session) or Op 7 (Reconnect), `onEvent` handles it by calling `CloseWithCode`, which calls `s.Lock()` again. `sync.RWMutex` isn't reentrant, so `Open` never returns. The heartbeat goroutine waits behind it, and the reconnect loop never runs. Op 9 is Discord's normal reply to a failed resume, so a network blip followed by a resume is enough to trigger it.

Goroutine dumps from two real wedges on one bot, same stack both times (`wsapi.go:186 → 631 → 931`):

```
sync.(*RWMutex).Lock
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).CloseWithCode(0xc0002d4708, 0x3f4)   // 1012, wsapi.go:931
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).onEvent(...)                           // Op 9 branch, wsapi.go:631
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).Open(...)                              // holds s.Lock(), wsapi.go:186
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).reconnect(...)
github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo.(*Session).heartbeat(...)   // second dump: (*Session).listen
```

**The fix** was upstreamed to the fork as `16ef341` ("Fix deadlock (#5)", 2026-03-26). `onEvent` now returns `errReconnect` for Op 7 and Op 9, and the caller reconnects once `Open` has released the lock. This PR moves the `replace` to the fork's current head, `a10ba9c`, which also includes the fork's later fixes for the gateway resume loop (`6f7dfa3`) and silent gateway stalls (`a10ba9c`). The only change on our side is `go.mod`/`go.sum` plus a test.

**Regression test.** `pkg/channels/discord/discord_gateway_test.go` runs a fake gateway that answers IDENTIFY with Op 9 or Op 7, and checks that `Open` returns and the session lock is released afterwards. It uses its own `websocket.Dialer`, because the default dialer's `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` caches the environment on first use and would break `TestApplyDiscordProxy_*`.

| pin | result |
|---|---|
| `e8e546f` (current `main`) | both cases FAIL: `session.Open() never returned: deadlocked on the session lock` |
| `a10ba9c` (this PR) | both cases PASS in under 1 ms |

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [x] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [ ] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

Written with Claude Code. The analysis comes from the goroutine dumps above, and the fix and test were verified red then green and on a real bot (below). Opened as a draft so a human reviews it first.

## 🔗 Related Issue

None filed. The description above covers it. I can open an issue if you'd like to track it separately.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://github.com/yeongaori/discordgo-fork/commit/16ef34198ced6c051880166ecbcda6fc9cc7f011 (fork fix), https://discord.com/developers/docs/events/gateway#resuming (Op 9 after a failed resume). The same deadlock is still open in upstream `bwmarrin/discordgo`: https://github.com/bwmarrin/discordgo/pull/1694 (unreviewed since 2026-02-09), so dropping the fork for upstream wouldn't fix this either.
- **Reasoning:** The bug and its fix are in the dependency, and picoclaw already pins that fork with a `replace`, so moving the pin is the smallest correct change. The test guards that pin from regressing, because a future fork bump could bring the deadlock back without anyone noticing. Release branches may want this cherry-picked: `v0.3.1` has the bug.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (Intel Xeon W-3265, x86_64)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, picoclaw in a rootless Podman container (v0.3.1 + this pin)
- **Model/Provider:** N/A (gateway-level change)
- **Channels:** Discord (also running Slack, unaffected)

Checks, run in `golang:1.25` to mirror `.github/workflows/pr.yml`:
- `go test -tags goolm,stdjson ./...`: pass as a non-root user. As root, `pkg/evolution`'s `TestRuntime_RunColdPathOnce_DraftSaveFailureRollsBackAppliedSkill` fails, because it needs an unwritable path. That's the same on `main` and unrelated.
- `golangci-lint run --build-tags=goolm,stdjson` (v2.10.1): 0 issues.
- `golangci-lint fmt --diff`: no diff in changed files. It flags `pkg/providers/bedrock/provider_bedrock.go`, which is already on `main`.
- `govulncheck`: results identical to `main`'s.
- `go vet`, `go mod verify`, `scripts/lint-docs.sh`, `web/backend` tests: pass.

## 📸 Evidence (Optional)
<details>
<summary>Real bot: gateway outage, failed resume answered with Op 9, clean recovery</summary>

Outbound 443 was blocked in the container's network namespace for 150 s, then restored. On reconnect, Discord rejected the resume with Op 9, the sequence that wedged the old pin. The new pin re-identified and recovered without a restart:

```
22:17:39 [test] blocked 443
22:18:02 WRN error reading from gateway wss://gateway.discord.gg/ websocket, websocket: close 1000 (normal)
22:18:03 INF calling reconnect() now
22:18:48 ERR error connecting to gateway wss://gateway.discord.gg/, dial tcp 162.159.130.234:443: i/o timeout
22:19:34 ERR error connecting to gateway , dial tcp 162.159.136.234:443: i/o timeout
22:20:09 [test] unblocked
22:20:10 INF Op 10 Hello Packet received from Discord
22:20:10 INF sending resume packet to gateway
22:20:10 INF Received Op 9 (Invalid Session) from gateway
22:20:10 INF Gateway session is not resumable, discarding its information
22:20:10 ERR error reconnecting to gateway, reconnect required by gateway
22:20:14 INF trying to reconnect to gateway
22:20:15 INF Op 10 Hello Packet received from Discord
22:20:15 INF We are now connected to Discord, emitting connect event
22:20:15 INF successfully reconnected to gateway
[test] container restarts: 0
```
</details>

prs.title: fix(anthropic): make claude-haiku-5-5 (thinking-always models) work with token credentials
prs.body:
## Problem

Every token-based Anthropic call to a thinking-always model (e.g. `claude-haiku-5-5`) fails with:

```
status=400 invalid_request_error: "temperature" is deprecated for this model
```

Repro: model entry with `provider: anthropic`, `auth_method: token` (API key stored in `auth.json`), any Claude 5 model. Reproduced on picoclaw 0.3.1 / Termux armv7; current `main` has the same code path.

## Root cause

Two separate bugs on the token path (`oauth.ClaudeProvider`):

1. The wrapper does not implement `ThinkingCapable`, so `applyTurnThinkingOptions` treats the provider as not thinking-capable, **never injects `thinking_level`**, and the inner SDK provider then always sends an explicit `temperature`. Claude 5 family models reject an explicit `temperature` with 400.
2. `buildParams` sends `temperature` unconditionally, so even when thinking injection is fixed or absent, thinking-always models still get a `temperature` they reject.

## Fix

- `pkg/providers/oauth/claude_provider.go`: delegate `SupportsThinking()` to the inner SDK provider so `thinking_level` is honored for token/OAuth credentials as well.
- `pkg/providers/anthropic/provider.go`: omit `temperature` for models that have thinking enabled by default and reject an explicit one (`haiku-5`, `sonnet-5`, `opus-5`, `opus-4-5`, `sonnet-4-5`).

## Verification

- On-device (Termux armv7, picoclaw 0.3.1 + these patches): `picoclaw agent -m ...` against `claude-haiku-5-5` with `thinking_level: adaptive` now succeeds (verified with a real API round-trip).
- `go test ./pkg/providers/... ./pkg/agent/...` passes with tags `goolm,stdjson,whatsapp_native`.

Note: Claude 5 models only accept `thinking.type: "adaptive"` (not `enabled` + `budget_tokens`); that is a config-side concern and unaffected by this change — with the wrapper fix in place, `thinking_level: adaptive` now actually reaches the API.

## AI assistance disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING.md ("Disclosure Is Required"): this change is AI-assisted. The patches were written by an AI coding agent (Hermes Agent) on the contributor's machine, tested on-device (Termux armv7) and with the project test suite, and reviewed, submitted and taken responsibility for by the human contributor (sebbY82).

prs.title: Optimize memory and cache performance
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR optimizes memory and cache performance in PicoClaw by:

1. **Adding in-memory cache to MemoryStore** - Reduces file I/O operations by caching long-term memory and daily notes
2. **Improving LRU implementation in SearchCache** - Replaces slice-based LRU with doubly-linked list for O(1) operations
3. **Enhancing cache expiration** - More aggressive removal of expired entries
4. **Reducing memory overhead** - Optimized data structures and better memory management

## Changes Made

### 1. MemoryStore Optimization (`pkg/agent/memory.go`)
- Added `longTermCache` string for caching MEMORY.md content
- Added `todayCache` and `todayCacheKey` for caching daily notes
- Updated `ReadLongTerm()`, `WriteLongTerm()`, `ReadToday()`, and `AppendToday()` to use cache
- Added `getCacheKey()` method to generate cache keys based on date

### 2. SearchCache Optimization (`pkg/skills/search_cache.go`)
- Replaced `order []string` with doubly-linked list (head/tail pointers)
- Added `prev` and `next` pointers to `cacheEntry` struct
- Implemented O(1) LRU operations with `addToTailLocked()`, `removeEntryLocked()`, and `moveToTailLocked()`
- Enhanced cache expiration to remove expired entries during Get operations
- Improved memory usage by avoiding slice reallocations

## Benefits

- **Reduced file I/O** - Memory operations are now faster with cached content
- **Improved performance** - O(1) LRU operations instead of O(n) slice manipulation
- **Lower memory usage** - More efficient data structures and aggressive cleanup
- **Better concurrency** - Optimized lock usage and reduced contention
- **Faster response times** - Cache operations are now more efficient

These changes make PicoClaw even more lightweight and responsive, especially on resource-constrained devices like the $10 hardware it's designed to run on.
