issues.title: [Feature]: Auto-retry once in RetryChatModel when HTTP 200 stream completes with no answer content (empty / thinking-only EOF)
issues.body:
> **AI Disclosure:** This issue was drafted and submitted with AI assistance on behalf of `@djj532` after inspecting QwenPaw `v2.3.0` runtime behavior and source code. All referenced file paths, line behaviors, and observations have been verified directly against the codebase and runtime logs.

## Summary

Add an opt-in (or default 1-time) empty-turn recovery retry in `RetryChatModel` when an upstream model returns HTTP `200 OK` and completes normally without producing any visible answer content or tool calls (either completely empty or thinking-only EOF).

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

In QwenPaw `v2.3.0`, some upstream models and compatible gateways intermittently finish a streaming response with HTTP `200 OK` and a normal EOF (`is_last=True`), while emitting **no `TextBlock` (non-whitespace) and no `ToolCallBlock`** — for example, returning only a reasoning/signature block or `text: ""` with `finish_reason: STOP` (observed repeatedly during long multi-step tool-calling sessions across both Anthropic- and OpenAI-Responses-compatible upstreams).

Inspecting the current retry and stream-progress implementation:

1. **`qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py` (`_stream_with_retry`, around lines 1117–1124)**:
   ```python
   async for chunk in active_stream:
       emitted = emitted or (
           has_meaningful_stream_content(chunk.content)
       )
       yield chunk
   return  # stream completed without error
   ```
   `emitted` is currently only used to decide whether an **exception** can be safely replayed. When the stream closes cleanly without raising an error (`is_last=True`), it returns unconditionally even when `emitted` remained `False`.

2. **`qwenpaw/providers/stream_progress.py` (`_block_has_meaningful_content`, lines 36–43)**:
   `has_meaningful_stream_content` treats a non-empty `ThinkingBlock` (`bool(block.thinking)`) as meaningful content. As a result, a turn that emits only reasoning/thinking and then terminates with empty answer text and no tool calls is treated as having produced meaningful output.

3. **Relationship to #8521 and open PR #8676**:
   PR #8676 nicely addresses the UI silent-completion bug by adding `has_answer_content()` (excluding thoughts) and raising `RuntimeError("The model returned an empty answer. Please retry or switch models.")` so users know the turn failed.
   However, because #8676 checks this at the `QwenPawAgent._reasoning` boundary and does **not** retry inside `RetryChatModel`, every transient empty-EOF turn still aborts the ongoing ReAct tool loop and forces manual user intervention — even when an immediate single retry succeeds reliably.

## Proposed Solution

1. **Separate "visible answer / tool-call progress" from "thinking-only progress"** (consistent with `has_answer_content` in PR #8676):
   - Keep `has_meaningful_stream_content` for idle-timeout / liveness tracking if needed (so long thinking does not trip TTFT), **or** track a dedicated flag `answer_emitted` (`non-whitespace TextBlock`, `DataBlock`, or `ToolCallBlock`).
2. **Optional single auto-retry in `RetryChatModel` on empty normal EOF** (for both streaming and non-streaming):
   - When a stream finishes cleanly (`is_last=True`, no exception) with `answer_emitted == False` (and non-interrupted, non-`max_tokens` truncation), allow a configurable `empty_response_retries` (e.g., default `1`) before surfacing the final empty state / error to `QwenPawAgent`.
   - **Trade-off on thinking chunks**: Because `RetryChatModel` yields chunks immediately, if `ThinkingBlock` chunks were already streamed to the caller before EOF, replaying could duplicate thinking in the UI unless either:
     - (a) a small bounded pre-answer buffer (e.g., up to N bytes before the first `TextBlock`/`ToolCallBlock`) holds pre-answer chunks until the first answer/tool token arrives or buffer threshold overflows, or
     - (b) auto-retry triggers only when no chunks (`not emitted`) or no UI-visible blocks were yielded yet, while thinking-only turns with already-yielded thoughts fall back to PR #8676's explicit retry prompt (or a clear notice).
   - **Strict safety invariant**: Once any non-whitespace `TextBlock` or `ToolCallBlock` has been emitted (`answer_emitted == True`), **never retry**, preventing duplicate side effects / duplicate tool calls.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Plugin `on_model_call` middleware**: We implemented a scoped middleware plugin using a bounded pre-answer buffer (`BUFFER_FLUSH_BYTES`) and 1-time retry on empty/thinking-only EOF. Verified in real `v2.3.0` sessions: when an upstream returned a `0`-output-token turn (`371k` input tokens), the middleware caught the empty EOF and retried once, recovering normal tool-calling output immediately.
- Putting this directly into `RetryChatModel` (and unifying with #8676's `has_answer_content`) avoids duplicating provider-specific middleware plugins and ensures consistent behavior across all channels (Console, Feishu, DingTalk, etc.).

## Additional Context

- Tested on QwenPaw `2.3.0` (macOS arm64 Desktop).
- Related issue & PR: #8521, #8676.

issues.title: [Feature]: Per-conversation session binding for messaging channels (/chats, /switch, and a /new that actually rotates the session)
issues.body:
## Summary

In every messaging channel, one transport identity maps to exactly one conversation, permanently. On WeChat a user's `session_id` is always `wechat:<sender_id>`, so there is no way to open a second conversation, return to an older one, or have `/new` actually start from a clean session. The Console already has this capability (`POST /chats` with an explicit `session_id`); channels have no equivalent. I'd like the channel→conversation binding to become a pointer, with a small command set (`/chats`, `/switch <n>`, `/new`) handled before the message reaches the agent.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Problem / Motivation

### Current behavior (verified against the installed 2.3.0 package)

`ChannelBase.resolve_session_id()` derives session identity from transport identity alone:

```python
# qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:1293-1303
def resolve_session_id(self, sender_id: str, channel_meta=None) -> str:
    return f"{self.channel}:{sender_id}"
```

The WeChat channel plugin (0.1.0.dev0) does not override it, so a given WeChat contact is permanently bound to `wechat:<sender_id>`.

That one string is the key for five subsystems simultaneously:

| Subsystem | Keyed by `session_id` | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Chat registry (Console list) | `get_or_create_chat()` looks up `(session_id, user_id, channel)` and returns the existing row | `app/chats/manager.py:144-210`, `app/chats/repo/base.py:48` |
| Durable session state | one file per session under `sessions/<channel>/` | `app/chats/session.py` |
| Queue / per-session lock | `QueueKey = (channel_id, session_id, priority_level)` | `app/channels/unified_queue_manager.py:31` |
| Debounce key | WeChat sets `debounce_key = session` | wechat plugin `driver.py:161` |
| Scroll history | `conversation_history(session_id, …)` in `history.db` | `history.db` schema |

Consequences:

1. **One contact = one conversation, forever.** The Console chat list shows a single WeChat row regardless of how many unrelated topics the user discussed.
2. **`/new` cannot rotate the session.** It is dispatched inside the agent's command handler and only resets modes/summary/memory:

   ```python
   # qwenpaw/agents/command_handler.py:689  (_process_new)
   await self._reset_modes()
   ...
   ```

   Dispatch happens at `command_handler.py:1592` (`getattr(self, f"_process_{command}")`), i.e. after the channel has already decided which session this run belongs to. The durable session never changes, and Scroll keeps evicting into the same `history.db` partition. This is the same root cause reported in #6966 for Telegram (`/new` does not create a new session id, context window fills indefinitely); that issue is the *symptom* of a channel session that cannot rotate. This request asks for the underlying capability.
3. **Mobile-only users have no alternative.** The Console is the only surface where multiple conversations exist, and it has a sidebar. A user whose primary surface is WeChat / Feishu / Telegram cannot reach the feature at all.

### Why it matters

- Separating contexts by project / client / topic without leaking one into another, which is the practical reason people reach for `/new` in the first place.
- Keeping a long-running companion thread while also opening a short task thread, then coming back.
- Avoiding unbounded Scroll growth on a single partition: memory, `history.db` rows and the eviction index all accumulate for the lifetime of the contact.

## Proposed Solution

The Console already demonstrates that the Conversation layer is transport-agnostic: `POST /chats` accepts a caller-supplied `session_id` and mints a chat row (`app/chats/api.py:349-379`), and `ConsoleChannel.resolve_session_id()` honours an explicit `channel_meta["session_id"]` (`app/channels/console/channel.py:194-204`). Channels need the same indirection plus a persisted pointer.

### 1. Persist a channel↔conversation pointer

Per `(agent, channel, sender)`, record the active conversation, either as `channel_bindings.json` next to `chats.json` or as `meta.bound_transport` + `active` flag on the chat row:

```json
{
  "wechat": {
    "<sender_id>": {
      "active_conversation": "c3",
      "conversations": [
        {"slug": "main", "title": "…", "created_at": "…", "last_active_at": "…"},
        {"slug": "c3",   "title": "…", "created_at": "…", "last_active_at": "…"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### 2. Derive session ids with a conversation suffix

```
wechat:<sender_id>:main     # default, back-compatible binding
wechat:<sender_id>:c3       # second conversation
```

Keeping the `<channel>:` prefix and the sender inside the id matters: the `sessions/` layout, `QueueKey`, `debounce_key` and `history.db` partitioning all keep working untouched, and `get_or_create_chat()` auto-registers one chat row per conversation because its dedupe key is `(session_id, user_id, channel)`.

### 3. Fix outbound routing (this is what breaks if you only change the id)

The WeChat driver currently recovers the recipient by stripping the channel prefix:

```python
# wechat plugin driver.py:94-105
sender = meta.get("wechat_from_user_id") or (
    session.removeprefix("wechat:group:") if session.startswith("wechat:group:")
    else session.removeprefix("wechat:") if session.startswith("wechat:")
    else user
)
```

With a `:c3` suffix this yields `<sender_id>:c3`, which is not a valid recipient. The code already prefers `meta["wechat_from_user_id"]` when present, so the fix is to always populate it (or use `AgentRequest.user_id`, which stays the transport sender). This is worth doing regardless of the feature: inferring the recipient from the session string is fragile by construction.

### 4. Handle three commands in the channel layer, before the agent run

`/new` is currently consumed inside the agent (`command_handler.py:1592`), which is too late to change which session the run belongs to. These three need to be intercepted where `session_id` is resolved:

| Command | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `/chats` | list this sender's conversations: index, title, last activity, marker for the active one |
| `/switch <n\|title>` | repoint `active_conversation`, confirm with the title |
| `/new [title]` | create a conversation with a fresh slug, repoint, confirm |

Keep the existing summarize-then-clear semantics reachable (`/new --clear`, or the old handler while the feature is off), since some users treat `/new` as "compact now".

### 5. Gate it behind config, default off

`channels.<id>.session_mode: "fixed" | "multi"`. Default `fixed` preserves today's behavior exactly. On the first switch to `multi`, bind the existing `wechat:<sender_id>` session as the first conversation and point at it, so no history is lost.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Override `resolve_session_id()` per channel plugin.** Cheapest, but duplicates the logic in every plugin, still cannot list or switch, and leaves `/new` unable to rotate.
- **Reuse the chat UUID as `session_id` (Console style).** Cleaner conceptually, but breaks three things at once: the `sessions/` layout and `QueueKey` are channel-namespaced by convention, `history.db` partitions would be re-keyed, and every channel's outbound routing that infers the recipient from the session string would need rewriting. The suffix scheme reaches the same result with a fraction of the blast radius.
- **Leave it to the Console (status quo).** Rules out mobile-only users and leaves #6966 unfixed.
- **Patch `site-packages` locally.** Not a real solution: pip upgrades overwrite it, and it forks Scroll/queue behavior with no upstream review.

## Additional Context

- Environment: QwenPaw 2.3.0 (pip install, Python 3.13), macOS; WeChat channel plugin 0.1.0.dev0.
- The analysis comes from reading the installed 2.3.0 package rather than a source checkout, so line numbers may drift on `main`. The call paths are the substance: base resolver → chat auto-registration → queue key → debounce key → history partition → driver recipient inference.
- Not verified, flagged as open questions rather than solved: how cron deliveries (a `target` that references a `session_id`) and subagent sessions should behave when the pointer moves; and archiving a conversation would also need to close its per-session browser session (`ChatManager._close_browser_session`, `app/chats/manager.py:628`).
- Related: #6966 (Telegram `/new` does not rotate session id), #7534 (Feishu queue consumer stays alive and stalls a session).

issues.title: [Bug]:  [2.3.0] WeChat channel cannot start (`ACCOUNT_IN_USE`) and successful sends are reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## Environment

| item          | value                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| QwenPaw       | 2.3.0 (PyPI latest at time of report; no 2.3.1 available)    |
| agentscope    | 2.0.10                                                       |
| openai SDK    | 2.33.0                                                       |
| Python        | 3.12.13                                                      |
| OS            | Linux (Manjaro, x86_64), systemd system service              |
| wechat plugin | `wechat` 0.1.0.dev0 (bundled with 2.3.0, `publish: false`)   |
| Channel setup | single agent `default`, wechat enabled with an existing iLink bot token (`bot_token`, no `bot_token_file`) |

## Bug 1 — WeChat channel never starts: `ACCOUNT_IN_USE` (critical)

### Symptom

On every boot (6+ restarts, always identical — unrelated to restart count):

```
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/app/multi_agent_manager.py:1076 | Failed to start new workspace instance for default: Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
ERROR qwenpaw/plugins/loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@...:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
```

The plugin then gets unregistered (`Unregistered channel 'wechat'`), so the workspace no longer has a wechat channel at all and the bot is silently offline.

`GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `404 {"detail": "Channel 'wechat' is not running."}`

### Traceback

```
manager.py:1602  start_one
manager.py:1671  _start_one_unlocked
manager.py:1342  _reserve_channel_auth
wechat_auth_custody.py:117  _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence
    raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

Line 117 is the loop that treats **another agent profile** as a competing owner of the same WeChat credential:

```python
scopes, others = evidence
for runtime_key, configured, other_scopes in others:
    if (
        configured or any(lease.key == runtime_key for lease in leases)
    ) and (scopes.intersection(other_scopes)):
        raise ManagementError("ACCOUNT_IN_USE")
```

### Root cause

`_read_wechat_auth_evidence()` skips "myself" with a case-sensitive id comparison:

```python
for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
    if agent_id == workspace_id:
        continue
```

but the workspace id that `manager._reserve_channel_auth()` resolves and passes in is **`Default`** (capital D), while the profile key in `config.json` is **`default`**. The guard therefore never skips itself and evaluates `default` as "another profile". Instrumenting the guard shows the conflict is with the very same workspace, with identical scope hashes:

```
BLOCK workspace_id=Default other=<WORKING_DIR>/.copaw/workspaces/default
      configured=True lease_hit=True overlap=True
      own=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
      other_scopes=['260b8fc0ee','c52f3d47c7','d7162d88f8']
```

Note also that with `bot_token_file` left empty, `wechat_auth_scopes()` derives the token paths from `WORKING_DIR`, so **any** profile is guaranteed to hash to the same scopes — meaning a second (even dormant, non-wechat) agent profile is enough to trip this check once the id comparison fails.

### Suggested fix

Normalize identity instead of comparing raw strings; e.g. casefold both sides and/or compare resolved workspace directories. A `workspace_dir` parameter is already available at both call sites.

```python
if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
    continue
if own_dir is not None and Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve() == own_dir:
    continue
```

## Bug 2 — Plugin recovery deadlocks on a leaked custody-only lease (critical)

### Symptom

After the plugin has been probed once in a process, it can never be (re)enabled:

```
ERROR loader.py:5703 | Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: ...
POST /api/plugins/wechat/enabled {"enabled": true}
→ 500 {"detail": "Failed to update plugin enabled state: Plugin 'wechat' recovery failed; needs_restart: Recovery has runtime resources; unload first"}
```

`POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` returns `clean: true, quiescent: true`, yet the next enable still fails, and the `_recovery_blocked` entry is never cleared for the lifetime of the process.

### Root cause

`loader._has_runtime_custody()` is just `bool(registry.runtime_owners.leases(plugin_id))`. Probe reservations are made with `custody_only=True` and **no stop adapter**, and `RuntimeOwners._invoke()` refuses to attest a stop for them:

```python
async def _invoke(entry):
    if entry.stop is None:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

`release()` then returns `False` for that lease, so the entry stays in `_entries` forever → recovery sees "runtime resources", blocks, and caches the error.

### Suggested fix

A custody-only reservation owns no process, so it can always be released:

```python
if entry.stop is None:
    if entry.custody_only:
        return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
    return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")
```

## Bug 3 — Successful sends reported as `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`; replies dropped (critical)

### Symptom

Inbound works and the agent produces a reply, but the user never receives it:

```
INFO  channel _consume_with_tracker: chat_id=... session=wechat:...        (message received)
INFO  builder: built agent for session=wechat:... model=...
INFO  Usage for session wechat:...: {'input_tokens': 142422, 'output_tokens': 102}
ERROR base.py:1040 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
WARNING isolated_proxy.py:637 | Channel diagnostic: RESPONSE_FINISH_FAILED
qwenpaw.app.channels.isolated_proxy.ChannelDeliveryError: PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN
```

`qwenpaw channels send --channel wechat ...` fails the same way (`500` on `/api/messages/send`).

### Reproduction of the platform side

Calling the iLink API directly with the same bot token and the stored `context_token`:

```
POST https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com/ilink/bot/sendmessage
{"msg": {"to_user_id": "...@im.wechat", "message_type": 2, "message_state": 2,
         "context_token": "<token>", "item_list": [{"type": 1, "text_item": {"text": "test"}}]},
 "base_info": {"channel_version": "0.1.0"}}

→ HTTP 200  {"message_id": <MESSAGE_ID>}
```

**A successful send returns only `message_id` — no `ret`, no `errcode`.**

### Root cause

`plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py:406`:

```python
@staticmethod
def _check_result(response, sent):
    if not isinstance(response, dict) or not (
        {"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()
    ):
        raise WeChatDeliveryError(
            "PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN",
            side_effect_possible=True,
        )
```

Every successful send is therefore classified as an unknown result and the reply is discarded (the proxy also marks `_reply_unknown`, so there is no retry).

### Suggested fix

Accept `message_id` as success (and/or fall back to the HTTP status):

```python
if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
    return
```

## Bug 4 — `top_k` / `repetition_penalty` from per-model `generate_kwargs` crash the model call (major)

With an OpenRouter model whose stored `generate_kwargs` contain `top_k` and `repetition_penalty`:

```
TypeError: AsyncCompletions.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'top_k'
  File ".../openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.py", line 2714, in create
```

OpenAI-compatible endpoints generally expect these in `extra_body`; the SDK signature does not accept them as top-level kwargs. Removing them from the model's `generate_kwargs` (`PUT /api/models/{provider}/models/{model}/config`) fixed it. Suggestion: filter known-unsupported keys into `extra_body` in the OpenAI-compatible wrapper instead of passing them through.

## Observation (not necessarily a QwenPaw bug)

While testing, `openrouter/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` repeatedly returned an empty stream while its connection test reported `status=available, verification=live`:

```
WARNING retry_chat_model.py:1201 | LLM stream failed (attempt 1/4):
        LLM stream for openrouter:nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free produced no content
```

Switching the agent's chat model to `deepseek-custom/deepseek-flash` produced normal replies, so this looks model/provider-specific, but the retry loop silently consumed 4 attempts without surfacing a user-visible error.

## Minimal patch set that made the channel usable (for reference)

```diff
--- a/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/app/channels/wechat_auth_custody.py
 def _read_wechat_auth_evidence(config, workspace_id, working_dir,
+                               workspace_dir=None):
     for agent_id, profile in root.agents.profiles.items():
         if agent_id == workspace_id:
             continue
+        # NEW: the resolved workspace id may differ in case from the profile key
+        if str(agent_id).strip().casefold() == str(workspace_id).strip().casefold():
+            continue
+        # NEW: or point at the very same workspace directory
+        if workspace_dir is not None and (
+            Path(profile.workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+            == Path(workspace_dir).expanduser().resolve()
+        ):
+            continue

--- a/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
+++ b/qwenpaw/plugins/ownership.py
     async def _invoke(entry):
         if entry.stop is None:
+            if entry.custody_only:
+                return RuntimeStopReceipt(True, "CUSTODY_ONLY_NO_PROCESS")
             return RuntimeStopReceipt(False, "RUNTIME_STOP_UNATTACHED")

--- a/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
+++ b/plugins/wechat/qwenpaw_channel_wechat/platform.py
     def _check_result(response, sent):
         if not isinstance(response, dict) or not ({"ret", "errcode"} & response.keys()):
+            if isinstance(response, dict) and response.get("message_id"):
+                return
             raise WeChatDeliveryError("PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN", side_effect_possible=True)
```

After these three changes (plus removing `top_k`/`repetition_penalty` from the model's `generate_kwargs`):

- `GET /api/config/channels/wechat/health` → `{"channel":"wechat","status":"healthy"}`
- plugin → `status: active, diagnostics: ["channel_validation_passed"]`
- inbound messages are consumed, replies are delivered, no `PLATFORM_RESULT_UNKNOWN`

## Additional notes

- A zero-downtime agent reload (triggered by any config change) can leave the previous wechat channel handle undelivered: subsequent `POST /api/config/channels/wechat/restart` returns `CHANNEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` indefinitely, and a stale `shared_worker.py` keeps polling (reported `platform_state: connected`) while its messages no longer reach the app. Killing the stale worker unblocks the drain.
- Plugin source edits require `POST /api/plugins/wechat/unload` + `enabled=true` to take effect; `channel restart` fails with `SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH`.
- With a large wechat session (142k input tokens per turn) replies take 60–90 s end-to-end, which may be close to the iLink reply window.

issues.title: [Bug]: [creator] Creation Assistant input lags on every keystroke — full AgentDock re-render re-parses all conversation markdown (no memoization)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

QwenPaw 2.3.0 (pip venv install), PawApp plugin `qwenpaw-creator` 2.0.5.

## Description

In a project workspace, typing into the left-side "Creation Assistant" (创作助手) input box lags noticeably: characters appear with a per-key delay that grows with conversation length. Chinese IME composition makes it worse, since every composition update travels the same path.

I recovered the plugin's own `ui/src` from the shipped sourcemaps (`ui/dist/app/assets/*.js.map`) and traced this to a render-path defect in `AgentDock.tsx`: **every keystroke re-renders the entire dock, which re-parses the markdown of every message in the conversation through ReactMarkdown**.

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none (pure front-end render performance).

## Component(s) Affected

Not covered by the checklist — PawApp plugin frontend: `qwenpaw-creator` (`ui/` React bundle), specifically `ui/src/components/agent/AgentDock.tsx` and `ui/src/components/agent/MentionInput.tsx`.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0, plugin qwenpaw-creator 2.0.5
- **OS:** Windows Server 2022 (x64)
- **Install method:** pip (managed venv)
- **Python version:** 3.12
- **Browser:** Chromium-based; the console serves the plugin UI inside an iframe

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Creator app and enter a project whose Creation Assistant conversation already has a substantial history (dozens of messages, including long assistant markdown replies with tables/code blocks).
2. Click the assistant input box (the contentEditable `MentionInput`) and type a sentence at normal speed, optionally via an IME.
3. Observe typed characters appearing with a per-key delay; the longer the conversation history, the worse it gets.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the main thread blocks on every keystroke (per-key delay scales with conversation size and markdown complexity); typed text lags behind the keystrokes.
- **Expected:** keystrokes appear immediately regardless of conversation length.

## Root cause analysis

Line numbers refer to the sourcemap-recovered `ui/src` of plugin 2.0.5.

1. `MentionInput.tsx` (~L443): the contentEditable's `onInput` → `sync()` → serializes the DOM → calls `onChange(text)` **on every keystroke** (and on every IME composition update).

2. `AgentDock.tsx` `handleInputChange` (~L1909) performs three re-render-triggering writes per keystroke:

   ```ts
   const handleInputChange = (text: string) => {
     const content = inputRef.current?.getContent();             // 2nd DOM serialization
     setCanSend(Boolean(content?.text.trim()));                  // local state
     setInlineRefs(content?.refs.map((item) => item.ref) ?? []); // new array identity every time
     setDraft(text);                                             // zustand agentDockUiStore
   };
   ```

   - `setInlineRefs(... ?? [])` creates a **new array identity on every keystroke**, so this state always counts as changed even when the ref list is identical.
   - `setDraft` writes `agentDockUiStore.draft`, and **AgentDock subscribes to that same slice itself** (~L1156: `const draft = useAgentDockUiStore((state) => state.draft)`), so the dock re-renders from its own write.
   - A `useEffect` keyed on `[draft, open]` (~L1748) runs after each keystroke and calls `getContent()` again (3rd DOM serialization per key).

3. `AgentDock.tsx` is ~2,900 lines and contains **zero `memo()` / `React.memo` in the entire file** (verified: no occurrence of `memo`). Every re-render redraws the whole conversation (~L2407–2455): each `ConversationMessage` → `MessageParts` → `MarkdownContent` (~L304) → `ReactMarkdown` with `remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}` (an inline array, new identity per render). ReactMarkdown re-parses **every historical message** through the unified/remark pipeline on **every keystroke**; `ToolCallCard` (~L760), `AgentProgressOverview`, and `DecisionTray` re-render in full as well.

Net effect: per-key main-thread cost grows with conversation size × markdown complexity. A fresh conversation feels fine; a long one becomes painful — matching the reported symptom.

## Verified local hotfix (workaround)

Wrapped five typing-stable-prop components with `React.memo` in the shipped bundle: `MarkdownContent`, `ConversationMessage`, `ToolCallCard`, `AgentProgressOverview`, `DecisionTray` (a one-line append to the built chunk, `X = react.memo(X)` per component; minified names are build-specific). Their zustand subscriptions live inside the components, so streaming updates and tool-progress re-renders are unchanged; memo only skips the keystroke-driven redraws. After applying it (and clearing site data, since `ui/dist/app/assets/*` is served `immutable`), typing is immediately responsive even in long conversations — confirmed by the reporter on the same projects that previously lagged.

## Suggested proper fix (in impact order)

1. `memo()` the per-message components (`ConversationMessage`, `ToolCallCard`, `MarkdownContent`) and hoist the `remarkPlugins` array to a module constant.
2. Isolate composer state (`canSend`, `inlineRefs`, draft writes) into a small composer child component so keystrokes never re-render the dock and the conversation list.
3. Let AgentDock not subscribe to the same `draft` slice it writes on every keystroke — read it via `getState()` inside the restore effect, or debounce draft persistence.
4. Skip the `setInlineRefs` update when the ref list is unchanged (compare with the previous value).
5. Reuse the single serialization result from `MentionInput`'s `onChange` instead of serializing the contentEditable DOM three times per keystroke.

## Differentiation from existing perf issues (searched; not duplicates)

- #8288 — main-console chat full re-render on conversation **switching**; different surface and trigger (this one is per-keystroke, inside the creator plugin).
- #8668, #8135, #3915, #7176 — main-console perf (compositor/CSS, streaming render cost, virtual scrolling); this issue lives in the creator PawApp bundle and is driven by React re-render + markdown re-parse on each keystroke.
- #6889 — console IME event-target correctness; IME here only amplifies the same re-render chain.

## Logs / Screenshots

No server logs — this is purely front-end render performance, and no profiler trace is attached. The fix direction is validated by the memo hotfix above: with the same long conversations, the typing lag disappears.

issues.title: cron 任务执行的 token usage 未写入 turns.jsonl，与对话 channel 路径不一致
issues.body:
## 现象

QwenPaw 控制台「用量」面板展示的 token 账单来自 `turns.jsonl`。该文件由通道层在每个轮次结束后通过 `_commit_turn_usage` 持久化。

实测发现：cron 任务（`crons/executor.py`）执行期间产生的 token 用量**没有进入 `turns.jsonl`**，导致用量面板统计缺失 cron 任务的消耗，归因口径不完整。

## 根因

对比两条路径的实现：

- **对话路径**：`app/channels/base.py` 的 `consume_one` / `_stream_with_tracker` 在成功完成或异常时均显式调用 `_commit_turn_usage(session_id, ...)`，把当轮的 prompt/completion/token 等信息写入 `turns.jsonl`（见 `app/channels/base.py:2034-2100`）。
- **cron 路径**：`app/crons/executor.py` 的 `execute()` / `_run()` 通过 `self._workspace.stream_query(req)` 拉取事件并直接向 channel 投递，**全程未调用** `_commit_turn_usage`，也未有等效的 usage 持久化逻辑。

也就是说：
- cron 任务会建立 session、发起 model request、返回 token 计数
- 但这段计量数据没有落盘到 `turns.jsonl`

差异在两条路径的处理不对称，且没有任何注释说明为何要跳过。

## 影响面

1. **账单口径有缺口**：`turns.jsonl` 的累计 token 仅含对话轮次，cron 任务的模型调用全部被排除在外。cron 任务（每日早报、定时拉取、自动化提醒等）在实际使用中往往占相当比重，缺口不可忽略。
2. **归因不完整**：现有 `turn_usage.resolve_turn_usage` 能按 session 区分用户聊天 vs cron session，说明数据模型本就具备区分能力——只要 cron 路径补齐 `_commit_turn_usage` 调用，即可让账单自然覆盖 cron 任务。
3. **可观测性偏差**：依赖 `turns.jsonl` 做用量分析/告警/计费的下游都会少算 cron 部分。

## 复现

1. 配置一条 `task_type=agent` 的 cron 任务（使用任意 model slot，开启用量记录）；
2. 触发执行；
3. 观察 `{workspace}/sessions/<session_id>/turns.jsonl`：正常对话 session 每次轮次结束后都有新行，但该 cron session 在请求完成后无任何新增行；
4. 对照 `console` 日志中已打印的 `Usage for session <id>` 条目（说明 model 已返回用量），确认是持久化路径缺失而非模型不返回。

## 修复建议

在 `app/crons/executor.py` 的 `_run()` 内，于 `stream_query` 收敛后（成功或异常分支均需覆盖）补一次 usage 持久化。推荐复用 `base.py` 已有的 `_commit_turn_usage` 机制，例如：

- 选项 A：把 `_commit_turn_usage` 提取为 workspace/channel 的公共方法，供 executor 调用；
- 选项 B：在 executor 内 import 并重用 `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage.resolve_turn_usage` + `qwenpaw.token_usage.persist_turn_usage`，传入本次 cron 的 `session_id` / `user_id` / `channel`。

两种方案任选其一即可；关键是 **cron 路径与 channel 路径保持用量落盘的一致**。若出于设计考量认为 cron session 本就不应写 `turns.jsonl`，建议在 `executor.py` 补一行注释说明原因，避免后续维护者误以为遗漏。

## 补充说明

- 此 issue 仅针对框架行为本身，不涉及任何第三方插件（如 `ledger_ingest` 等消费模块）；插件只是暴露了此缺口，非问题来源。
- 当前框架版本为 v0.3.17。

issues.title: Channel plugin startup race: _wait_connected treats the initial platform_state="disconnected" as fatal -> CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED on every start (feishu deterministic)
issues.body:
### What happens

In a packaged desktop build (2.3.0b4, Windows), the bundled `feishu` channel plugin fails on **every** start with:

```text
Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED; channel 'feishu' failed: <agent>@<tenant>:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
```

The plugin ends up `status=failed`, `loaded=true`, `enabled=true`, with only those two generic diagnostics. The **Repair** button (`POST /api/plugins/{id}/repair-dependencies`) changes nothing, because `PluginLoader.repair_dependencies()` only re-runs *gate + install + load* — it re-enters the exact same failing activation path.

Other channel plugins (`wechat`, `yuanbao`) stay `active` in the same build, so this is not a general plugin/dependency failure.

### Evidence that the plugin itself is fine

Running the plugin's own driver with the **same** interpreter and support root that the worker uses:

- interpreter: `binaries\python-runtime\python\python.exe`
- `sys.path`: `binaries\channel-runtime\site` + `~/.qwenpaw/plugins/feishu`

```text
PREPARE OK  0.69s
[Lark] connected to wss://msg-frontier.feishu.cn/ws/v2...
CONNECT OK  0.55s
[Lark] disconnected
```

Credentials, network, `lark_oapi` and the WebSocket handshake all work. The failure is in the **host ↔ worker startup contract**, not in the plugin.

### Host log timeline (one of four identical attempts)

```text
02:04:37 INFO  registry.py:538  Registered startup hook 'channel_feishu_feishu' from plugin 'feishu'
02:04:39 WARN  worker_logs.py:107 [worker stderr plugin_id=feishu ... mode=run] Dependency warning: idna: DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_AMBIGUOUS; attempting load
        ... (only these dependency warnings — no plugin-side traceback)
02:04:39 ERROR api.py:688      Plugin 'feishu' Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
02:04:39 ERROR loader.py:5703  Plugin 'feishu' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'feishu' failed: ...:CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
```

The worker never reported a platform error; it was aborted ~2 s after spawn.

### Root cause (suspected): the initial `disconnected` is treated as fatal

`src/qwenpaw/app/channels/isolated_proxy.py` (`_wait_connected`, v2.3.0-beta.4, lines 466-487):

```python
async def _wait_connected(self):
    timeout = (
        self._launch_spec.startup_timeout
        if self._connection_timeout is None
        else self._connection_timeout
    )
    async with asyncio.timeout(timeout):
        while True:
            snapshot = self.channel_process.health_snapshot()
            if (
                snapshot["state"] == "ready"
                and snapshot["platform_state"] == "connected"
            ):
                return
            if snapshot["state"] != "ready" or snapshot[
                "platform_state"
            ] in {
                "failed",
                "disconnected",
            }:
                raise RuntimeError("CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED")
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
```

`ChannelProcess` starts life with the *sentinel* value `disconnected`:

```python
# src/qwenpaw/app/channels/process_supervisor.py
state_key = "platform_state"
initial_state = "disconnected"

# src/qwenpaw/plugins/execution/process.py
self._platform = self.initial_state                       # ~line 172
def health_snapshot(self):
    return {..., self.state_key: self._platform}           # ~line 316
# _launch(): self._state, self._platform = "starting", self.initial_state   # ~line 551
```

But the channel driver only publishes `connecting` **after** its own bootstrap work:

```python
# qwenpaw_channel_feishu/driver.py
await self._platform.prepare(...)   # imports lark_oapi + tenant-token probe (>=0.7 s here)
await self._connect()               # -> set_platform_state("connecting"), ~line 105
```

So between "host marks the process ready" and "worker publishes `connecting`" there is a window in which `health_snapshot()["platform_state"] == "disconnected"` — the very value `_wait_connected` treats as fatal. With a 0.01 s poll interval the host aborts on the **first** poll.

Channels with a trivial pre-connect path (`wechat`, `yuanbao`) usually publish `connecting` before the first poll and survive; `feishu` needs a network auth round-trip first, so it loses the race deterministically.

This also explains why the failure always arrives after ~2 s rather than at the 10 s `startup_timeout`: the abort comes from the `disconnected` branch, not from `asyncio.timeout`.

### Suggested fixes (any one should do)

1. Distinguish "never reported" from "reported `disconnected`": remember whether the worker has published a platform state at least once, and only treat `disconnected` as fatal after `connecting` has been observed.
2. Use a non-fatal sentinel for the pre-connect phase, e.g. `initial_state = "connecting"` for `ChannelProcess`, or a separate `"pending"` value that `_wait_connected` ignores.
3. Have the worker publish `connecting` as soon as it receives the run request, before the driver's `prepare()` runs.

### Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop 2.3.0b4 (frozen build), Windows 10 19045, no proxy environment variables
- channel-runtime site: `qwenpaw-2.3.0b4.dist-info`, `lark_oapi 1.7.5`
- one feishu channel in the workspace; `wechat` and `yuanbao` in the same workspace are `active`
- `#8653` (dependency-gate `supported_tags` fix) is already in this build; this failure is a different, later stage and survives that fix

### Note

I have not patched the frozen host locally (host modules live inside `qwenpaw-backend.exe`), so this report is diagnosis-only. Happy to test a patch against the `site` copy or a dev checkout if that helps.

---

**中文摘要**：打包版 2.3.0b4 里飞书插件每次启动都报 `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`，UI 的 repair 无效（它只做「过依赖门 + 装依赖 + 重新加载」）。用同一解释器与 `channel-runtime\site` 手工跑飞书 driver 可正常连上（prepare 0.69 s、WS 连接 0.55 s），故凭据/网络/依赖都正常。根因判断：`isolated_proxy._wait_connected` 把 `platform_state in {"failed","disconnected"}` 当致命，而 `ChannelProcess.initial_state` 就是 `"disconnected"`，飞书 driver 要先跑 `prepare()`（导入 lark_oapi + 租户 token 探活）才在 `_connect()` 里置 `connecting`，宿主 0.01 s 轮询首轮即判死；`wechat`/`yuanbao` prepare 快、赶在首轮前进入 `connecting`，因此只有飞书稳定复现。

issues.title: [Bug]: Matrix channel plugin fails to activate when multiple workspaces enable it (10s shared startup window only covers the first)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2

## Description

In 2.3.0b2 the Matrix channel has been converted to the official channel plugin `matrix-0.1.0.dev0`. On this machine three workspaces (A, B, C) all have Matrix enabled. After the upgrade the plugin fails to activate and none of the three accounts come online.

Authentication is not the problem: the Matrix authentication service returned `200 OK` for all three `/login` requests, and the channel worker produced no error output at all. The failure happens later, in workspace projection, with `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`.

Startup timeline (service started at 00:44:05):

| Account | Login succeeded | Time since start |
|:---|:---|:---|
| @alpha (workspace A) | 00:44:11.3 | 6.3s |
| @beta (workspace B) | 00:44:14.95 | 9.95s |
| @gamma (workspace C) | 00:44:17.3 | 12.3s |

Workspace A connected inside the window. Workspaces B and C were reported as timed out around the 10 second mark.

In `qwenpaw/plugins/channel_adapter.py:62`, `ChannelRuntimeSettings.startup_timeout` is a fixed `10.0`, and the comment states `never read from channel configuration`, so it cannot be adjusted via configuration. The three channels log in sequentially inside the same runner process, taking about 13 seconds in total, so only the first channel can fit inside the window.

Additionally, a projection failure in a single workspace marks the whole plugin as FAILED and unregisters it, which also tears down the channel in workspace A that had already connected.

**Related PR(s):** None

**Security considerations:** None

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b2
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (x86_64)
- **Install method:** uv environment created by the official install.sh, later upgraded with `uv pip install --upgrade-package qwenpaw`
- **Python version:** 3.12

Matrix server is deployed separately: Synapse v1.158.0 + matrix-authentication-service 1.23.0, exposed as `matrix.example.org`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable Matrix in the `agent.json` of three workspaces, with the same homeserver, `device_name`, and password-based login.
2. Restart the QwenPaw service.
3. Inspect the startup logs and `~/.qwenpaw/workspaces/<workspace>/channel_state/matrix/`.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** All three accounts log in successfully, but only the first workspace establishes a connection within 10 seconds. The other two report `CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED` during projection, the plugin is marked FAILED, and the already-connected channel is unregistered as well. The Matrix channel is entirely unavailable.
- **Expected:** All three workspaces come online; or a failure in one workspace does not affect the others or the plugin's overall state.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
00:44:03  Registered startup hook 'channel_matrix_matrix' from plugin 'matrix' (priority=80)
00:44:15  ERROR plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'matrix' Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/api.py:688 | Plugin 'matrix' Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/loader.py:5287 | Plugin 'matrix' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'matrix' failed: workspace-b@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED; workspace-c@...:Projection channel failed: CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED
00:44:17  ERROR plugins/loader.py:5002 | Failed to activate plugin 'matrix': ...
```

Authentication service logs for the same period (all three succeeded):

```
00:44:11  POST /login  200 OK  @alpha
00:44:14  POST /login  200 OK  @beta
00:44:17  POST /login  200 OK  @gamma
```

The channel worker's stderr was empty; no `MatrixChannel:` log lines were produced.

## Additional Notes

On the first start after the upgrade, `DEPENDENCY_PLAN_UNVERIFIED` was reported (hosts qwenpaw-hub / clawhub-hub). Running `qwenpaw plugins prepare-upgrade` cleared that error; the current problem is unrelated to the dependency gate.

Suggestions:

1. `startup_timeout` is currently a single shared window for all workspaces, while channel initialization is serialized. As the number of workspaces grows, the window will always be insufficient. Consider measuring the timeout per channel, or making it configurable.
2. A projection failure in one workspace should not fail the entire plugin, and channels that already connected should not be unregistered.

issues.title: [Bug] Doom-loop gate kills legitimate task-authorized polling; cron records false success after termination
issues.body:
## Description

The doom-loop gate terminated a **legitimate, task-authorized polling pattern** while the awaited background task was genuinely progressing. The gate cannot distinguish "agent stuck repeating itself" from "agent waiting for a long-running background task exactly as its task instructions require".

Additionally, the cron scheduler recorded `last_status: "success"` for the killed run — the termination is invisible to operators.

## Reproduction (real production case, 2026-10-12 08:00 Asia/Shanghai)

A daily cron job (`6e7d12f7`, 08:00, agent-type) runs a ~12-minute report script in the background (`nohup ... &`), then polls for a completion marker (`---CHARTS---` in an output file) every 30 seconds, exactly as the job's task text instructs.

Observed sequence (from `history.db` of session `5ff775cf`, seq 33987–33994):

1. Agent issues, four times in a row, the **identical** tool call:
   `sleep 30 && (ps -p 18280 > /dev/null && echo "PID 18280 存活" || echo "PID 18280 已退出") && tail -c 300 /tmp/morning_output.txt`
2. Each result was byte-identical and showed **real external progress**: the background script advanced from "连接数据库..." to "腾讯新闻 AI 详摘 42 条" between polls.
3. After the 4th identical call the gate fired: `Doom loop: agent stuck after 4 consecutive repetitions` and killed the session at 08:02:38.
4. The background script (PID 18280) was completely healthy and finished on its own at ~08:12. Nothing was stuck — only the *waiting pattern* matched the repetition heuristic.
5. `qwenpaw cron state 6e7d12f7` afterwards: `{"last_run_at": "2026-10-12T08:02:38+08:00", "last_status": "success", "last_error": null}` — a killed run reported as success. The failure only became visible by manually inspecting session files.

## Root cause discussion

The repetition gate compares tool calls for similarity (and after PRs #7919/#7906, requires new evidence to escalate — good). What it still ignores:

1. **Intent context**: the repeated call is explicitly instructed by the task text ("poll every 30 seconds until marker X appears"). Within a cron/agent task, periodic `sleep + check` is a *waiting* idiom, not a stuck loop.
2. **External progress**: the awaited world state (log file content, process liveness) *was* changing between calls. A stuck loop has static observed state; a poll has evolving observed state.
3. **Inter-call spacing**: 30s between identical calls is not the tight-fire behavior the gate was designed for (sub-second or back-to-back regeneration).

The combined effect: any task instruction that says "wait for a background job by polling" is a guaranteed gate trip after N polls, and the operator gets a false success.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Recognize wait/poll morphology** (e.g. `sleep N && check-same-target`, or same tool+args with N-second spacing): exclude from repetition accounting, or place in a separate slower-escalation track, while the awaited condition (marker file / process) can still change.
2. **State-change awareness**: if the observed environment between identical calls changed (file grew, process still alive, log advanced), treat as polling-with-progress, not repetition.
3. **First-class wait primitive**: a `wait_for`-style tool (wait for file marker / process exit / condition, with timeout) removes the need for agents to hand-roll polling loops entirely.
4. **Cron truthfulness**: when a run is terminated by the doom-loop gate (or any loop gate), record it distinctly — e.g. `last_status: "terminated"` with `last_error` naming the gate — instead of `success`.

Longer term, a `script`-type cron task (see our feature request #4963 — direct shell execution without agent inference) would structurally eliminate this class: no agent in the loop means no polling loop to misclassify.

## Related

- #6116 — original doom-loop report (closed as wontfix; today's case is a *different* failure mode: authorized polling, not model repetition)
- #4963 — feature request: script-type cron tasks (structural avoidance)
- #7919 / #7906 — doom-loop gate accounting fixes (merged; today's case survives them)
- #7420 — different mechanism (runtime re-dispatch after `write_file`)

## Environment

- QwenPaw: 2.2.1 (Docker, Linux x86_64)
- Channel: Feishu; session `5ff775cf`; cron job `6e7d12f7` (daily 08:00 Asia/Shanghai, agent type, runtime timeout 1800s)
- Models routed via self-hosted gateway (free-pool small models on this job)
- We mitigated on our side by rewriting the task text to use a single blocking wait command instead of repeated polling; the gate/cron behaviors above remain unfixed framework-side.

---
*Tooling disclosure (per #4333): this report was prepared with AI assistance under human direction. All timestamps, commands, and state outputs come from a real live deployment.*

issues.title: DoomLoopGate never triggers when agentscope accumulates a reply into one assistant message
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0 (Docker image `agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0`). Also reproducible on `main` at `fc1db1a`.

## Description

With the default loop configuration (`window_size=3`, `similarity_threshold=1.0`, stages `after=3 / modify_prompt` and `after=4 / stop`), a turn that repeatedly calls the same tool with identical arguments never triggers either stage.

In a real 9-iteration console session on the default mode (the same failing SQL through `execute_readonly_sql` every round), `--log-level debug` showed `DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)` and `LoopGate 'doom-loop' activated` on every iteration, but never `Doom loop: sim=`; the turn only ended via `IterationGate`. The persisted `agent.state.context` contained just two messages: the user message and one assistant message with 8 accumulated `tool_call`/`tool_result` block pairs.

**Root cause**

- agentscope 2.0.10 keeps **one assistant message per reply**. `Agent._save_to_context` uses `state.reply_id` as the message id and appends every iteration's blocks (reasoning, tool calls, tool results) to that same message.
- `DoomLoopGate._auto_record_from_ctx` (`src/qwenpaw/loop/gates/doom_loop.py`, around L205) returns as soon as the latest message id matches the last recorded one:

  ```python
  last_msg = context[-1]
  if last_msg.id == state.last_recorded_msg_id:
      return
  ```

  Within a reply the id never changes, so after the first check no further tool calls are recorded, `history_dirty` stays `False`, and `check()` returns `BYPASS` for the rest of the turn.
- Consequence: only a model response whose **first** snapshot already contains at least `window_size` identical tool calls (parallel calls in one response) can trip the window. Even then `consecutive_hits` is seeded to `window_size` and only increments on a later dirty check, so the `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable in the default mode.

**Related PR(s):** coming in a follow-up PR.

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0 (`main` at `fc1db1a` also affected)
- **OS:** Debian 12, aarch64
- **Install method:** Docker
- **Python version:** 3.12 (agentscope 2.0.10)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the default mode (console chat) with the default `agents.running.loop.doom_loop` stages.
2. Ask something that makes the agent call the same tool with exactly the same arguments at least 4 times (for example, the same failing SQL).
3. Observe that no doom-loop warning is injected and the loop is never stopped by the doom gate.

Minimal reproduction without an LLM:

```python
import asyncio
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.config.config import DoomLoopStageConfig
from qwenpaw.loop.gates.doom_loop import DoomLoopGate


async def main():
    msg = SimpleNamespace(id="reply-1", role="assistant", content=[])
    agent = SimpleNamespace(state=SimpleNamespace(context=[msg]))
    ctx = {
        "agent": agent,
        "final_msg": None,
        "iteration": 0,
        "has_tool_calls": True,
    }
    gate = DoomLoopGate(
        window_size=3,
        similarity_threshold=1.0,
        stages=[
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=3, action="modify_prompt", prompt="warn"),
            DoomLoopStageConfig(after=4, action="stop", prompt="stop"),
        ],
    )
    for i in range(1, 7):
        # Same message id, one more identical tool call per formatting round,
        # exactly like agentscope accumulates blocks into one reply.
        msg.content.append(
            {
                "type": "tool_call",
                "name": "execute_readonly_sql",
                "input": {"sql": "SELECT 1"},
            },
        )
        result = await gate.check(ctx)
        state = gate._ensure_state()
        print(i, len(state.history), state.consecutive_hits, result.action.value)


asyncio.run(main())
```

Actual output on 2.3.0 / `main`:

```
1 1 0 bypass
2 1 0 bypass
3 1 0 bypass
4 1 0 bypass
5 1 0 bypass
6 1 0 bypass
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `history` stays at 1 for the whole reply; both the warning and the stop stage never fire. The `after=4 / stop` stage is unreachable.
- **Expected:** the third identical call produces `INTERRUPT_AND_CONTINUE` with the configured warning prompt, the fourth produces `TERMINATE` with the stop prompt.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
[DEBUG] DefaultMode configured 2 gate(s)
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 1/100
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 2/100
...
[DEBUG] IterationGate: 9/100
(no "Doom loop: sim=" line anywhere)
```

## Additional Notes

The current unit tests only call `gate.record()` directly (`tests/unit/loop/test_doom_loop_gate.py`), so the `_auto_record_from_ctx` path has no coverage and this regression shipped unnoticed. A fix that consumes the tail of the accumulated message (count of already-recorded `tool_call` blocks) restores the intended 3-warning / 4-stop behaviour and keeps the 2.3.0 improvements (recording every tool call in the message, the `has_tool_calls` guard, and warning injection).

issues.title: [Bug]: 升级2.3.0失败：uv venv --seed 未使用 PyPI 镜像导致安装中断

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## 环境

| 项目     | 版本                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| OS       | Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS                                      |
| uv       | 0.13.6                                                  |
| Python   | 3.12.11                                                 |
| 网络环境 | 官方 PyPI（pypi.org）不可达，安装脚本自动选择阿里云镜像 |

## 现象

执行升级（`curl -fsSL https://qwenpaw.agentscope.io/install.sh | bash`）时输出：

```text
[qwenpaw] Using Aliyun PyPI mirror (official source is unreachable)
[qwenpaw] Installing QwenPaw into /home/xxx/.qwenpaw
[qwenpaw] uv found: /home/xxx/.local/bin/uv
[qwenpaw] Existing environment found, upgrading...
error: Failed to install seed packages into virtual environment
  cause: No solution found when resolving: `pip`
  cause: Request failed after 3 retries in 48.8s
  cause: Failed to fetch: https://pypi.org/simple/pip/
  cause: error sending request for url (https://pypi.org/simple/pip/)
  cause: client error (Connect)
  cause: operation timed out
```

## 升级后环境状态（已损坏）

失败后 `~/.qwenpaw` 下的虚拟环境处于残缺状态，**QwenPaw 不可用**：

```text
$ ls ~/.qwenpaw/venv/bin
python  python3  python3.12        # 没有 qwenpaw、没有 pip

$ ~/.qwenpaw/bin/qwenpaw --version
Error: QwenPaw environment not found at /home/xxx/.qwenpaw/venv
```

`~/.qwenpaw/logs/nm-host.log` 中出现 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'websockets'`。

损坏原因：install.sh 设置了 `UV_VENV_CLEAR=1`，升级时会**先清空旧环境**再重建，而重建在 seed 阶段就失败，旧环境无法恢复。

## 根因分析

install.sh 开头有镜像探测逻辑（`choose_pypi_mirror`）：用 `curl --connect-timeout 3` 探测 `https://pypi.org/simple/`，不可达时自动选择阿里云镜像 `https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/`。

**但探测结果没有被一致使用：**

| 步骤                            | 命令                                                                  | 是否使用镜像 |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| 创建虚拟环境（含 pip 等种子包） | `uv venv "$QWENPAW_VENV" --python "$PYTHON_VERSION" --quiet --seed` | 否           |
| 安装 qwenpaw 及依赖             | `uv pip install ... --index-url "$PYPI_MIRROR"`                     | 是           |

`uv venv --seed` 需要联网下载 pip 等种子包，由于没有传 `--index-url`（也没有设置 `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX` / `UV_INDEX_URL` 环境变量），uv 回退到默认的官方源 `pypi.org`。在官方源不可达的网络环境下，该步骤必然超时失败。

即：探测逻辑已经知道官方源不通，但种子包安装这一步仍然直连官方源——镜像选择只覆盖了一半的安装流程。

## 引入版本

该问题为当前版本新引入的缺陷。对比 GitHub 仓库 `agentscope-ai/QwenPaw` 中 `scripts/install.sh` 的全部历史版本：

| 提交                             | 日期       | `uv venv` 命令           | 是否受影响   |
| -------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------- | ------------ |
| `17a6ea2b` 初始版本            | 2026-02-27 | `uv venv --quiet`        | 否           |
| `48cee232` 加入镜像探测        | 2026-03-11 | `uv venv --quiet`        | 否           |
| `ca82e1a6`                     | 2026-06-17 | `uv venv --quiet`        | 否           |
| `d905bf24`（v2.2.2post1 合入） | 2026-10-23 | `uv venv --quiet`        | 否           |
| `0a62d632`（当前版本）         | 2026-10-29 | `uv venv --quiet --seed` | **是** |

`--seed` 参数由 2026-10-29 的 PR #8187（"extract channels into plugins with subprocess isolation"）引入——channels 改为插件化运行后，venv 中需要预置 pip，因此给 `uv venv` 加上了 `--seed`。但该提交没有同步处理镜像参数，导致官方源不可达时必然失败。上一个版本 v2.2.2post1 的 install.sh 不创建种子包环境，不受影响。

## 规避方法

执行升级前通过环境变量覆盖 uv 的默认索引，让 `--seed` 也走镜像：

```bash
export UV_DEFAULT_INDEX=https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/
curl -fsSL https://qwenpaw.agentscope.io/install.sh | bash
```

`UV_VENV_CLEAR=1` 会清掉残缺的旧环境并重建，重跑不会受残留影响。

issues.title: [Bug]: Attachments cannot be resolved when the workspace path contains #
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Reproduced on `main` (`fc1db1a4568b44c74094aa2a748ee0eba70d1990`) and with the same source-level probe on `v2.2.2`.

## Description

On Windows, an attachment saved under a workspace directory containing `#` cannot be resolved after QwenPaw converts its local path into a message. The converter copies the raw `#` into the file URI, where the reader interprets the remainder as a fragment. This affects both image and file blocks.

Related investigation: #8655 and [the reproduction comparison](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8655#issuecomment-6819991930). This report covers the reproducible fragment case. It was also present in `v2.2.2`, before the beta release discussed in #8655.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows
- **Install method:** source-level offline probe
- **Python:** 3.12.14
- **AgentScope:** 2.0.10

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In an installed source checkout, run the snippet below. It creates a synthetic attachment under a temporary workspace.
2. Compare the raw Windows path used by the converter with the encoded URI control. The two inputs point to the same file.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from types import SimpleNamespace

from qwenpaw.app.channels.utils import file_url_to_local_path
from qwenpaw.runtime.message_convert import _request_input_to_msgs

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory, "workspace#draft", "media", "sample.png")
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    path.write_bytes(b"synthetic attachment")
    for value in (str(path), path.as_uri()):
        part = SimpleNamespace(type="image", image_url=value)
        [message] = _request_input_to_msgs(
            [SimpleNamespace(role="user", content=[part])]
        )
        resolved = Path(file_url_to_local_path(str(message.content[0].source.url)))
        print(resolved == path, resolved.is_file())
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The raw path resolves only as far as `workspace`. The encoded URI control resolves to the full file.
- **Expected:** Both inputs resolve to the same existing attachment. A literal `#` in the local path is encoded as `%23` when forming the URI.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
workspace with spaces | raw path | image + file: same_file=True, exists=True
workspace#draft       | raw path | image + file: same_file=False, exists=False
workspace#draft       | encoded  | image + file: same_file=True, exists=True
```

## Additional Notes

I would like to work on a focused fix in the shared local-path converter. The reproduction uses no channel connection or model credentials. AI assistance was used for investigation.

issues.title: [Bug]: Attachment path truncated to drive root ("C:\") passed to the model since 2.3.0-beta.1 - file saved fine but images fail to load

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0-beta.1 (introduced) / beta.2 / **beta.3** - still reproduces on beta.3, tested 2026-11-10 12:13 (`qwenpaw --version` = 2.3.0b3)

## Description

Since 2.3.0-beta.1, the local path of a user-uploaded attachment is truncated to the **drive root** before it reaches the model. The file itself is downloaded and saved correctly into `media\`, but the model only receives the root, so images can never load and the agent cannot see attachments.

Actual message content received by the model:

- Console / WeChat: `已经下载到 C:\` - the real path `C:\Users\<user>\...\.copaw\workspaces\<agent>\media\<uuid>_<name>` is cut to `C:\`
- QQ channel: `已经下载到 \` (backslash only)
- Console tool side also shows `saved into file:///C:/.`
- Images render as: `[Image unavailable: Error:  is not a valid image: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'C:\']`

**Related PR(s):** none found (searched; unrelated to #8585 which was about recall SQLite URIs)

**Security considerations:** none (local path only, no credentials involved)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0-beta.1 (introduced) / 2.3.0-beta.3 (still present)
- **OS:** Windows 10 & Windows 11
- **Install method:** Desktop installer
- **Python version (if applicable):** bundled

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Windows, upgrade QwenPaw Desktop to 2.3.0-beta.1 or later
2. Send any image/attachment to the agent (console, WeChat, or QQ channel)
3. Observe the model-side message: the saved path is truncated to the drive root (`C:\`), and images fail with `[Image unavailable: ... No such file or directory: 'C:\']`

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** model receives `已经下载到 C:\` (drive root only) plus `[Image unavailable: ... 'C:\']`. Clean time boundary at the beta.1 upgrade moment (2026-10-29 15:05): 258 attachment messages before the upgrade -> **0** truncations; 12 messages after -> **12/12** truncated (last OK 14:12:27, first failure 15:43:08). The file body is **always saved correctly**: 14/14 attachments found on disk as `media\<uuid32>_<original name>`, cross-checked against history.db records. Re-verified on beta.3 (2026-11-10 12:13, console): PNG uploaded -> `C:\` truncation again, file on disk intact (19,397 bytes).
- **Expected:** the model receives the full absolute path (`...\media\<uuid>_<name>`), and no `[Image unavailable]` for files that exist on disk.

## Logs / Screenshots

Model-side rendering of a console upload (beta.3, 2026-11-10):

```
测试看看 [Image unavailable: Error:  is not a valid image: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'C:\']
用户上传文件，已经下载到 C:\
```

The same file on disk: `media\33514bf61c5242e9bcfa40cdf8bce0c3_image.png` (19,397 bytes, saved 12:13:53) - download/save layer is fine; the path value is already truncated when passed back into the message pipeline. Message rendering and image freezing consume the same bad value; the `file_url_to_local_path()` helper in `channels/utils.py` behaves correctly on known-good inputs, so the corruption happens upstream, at the "return URL/path" stage.

## Additional Notes

- Workaround in use: a read-only helper re-finds the real path in `media\` by (filename fragment + time window), then the agent calls view_image/read_file with the reconstructed path. Works 100% so far, but without it every attachment is effectively invisible to the agent.
- Truncation artifact differs by channel: console/WeChat keep `C:\`, QQ keeps `\` - consistent with a string cut at a fixed offset rather than a per-channel bug.

issues.title: 微信渠道报错
issues.body:
[Bug]: Official WeChat channel plugin fails to activate on startup with ACCOUNT_IN_USE — channel startup path and workspace projection both reserve the same runtime key
Summary
After upgrading to QwenPaw 2.3.0, the official WeChat channel plugin fails to activate on every startup with:

ProjectionError: channel 'wechat' failed: default@<id>:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE
The channel never connects. This happens with a single QwenPaw instance, a single enabled agent, and no other process holding the WeChat account — so it is not the "account logged in elsewhere" case, and it is not the same bug as #8682 (that one crashes the worker at import with Could not determine home directory; here the worker starts fine and the failure is on the host side during projection).

The failure is deterministic and reproduces on every restart.

Environment
QwenPaw 2.3.0 (fnOS NAS app-center deployment, com.dustinky.qwenpaw, port 19091)
Linux x86_64, kernel 6.18.18.c1126-trim
Official WeChat channel plugin wechat 0.1.0.dev0 (qwenpaw_channel_wechat.driver.WeChatDriver)
Agents configured: 4 (default, QwenPaw_QA_Agent_0.2, Mikasa, Eren1) — only default has channels.wechat.enabled = true
Symptom (host log, every startup)
Plugin 'wechat' registered startup hook 'channel_wechat_wechat' (priority=80) Plugin 'wechat' registered workspace_created hook 'channel_ws_wechat_wechat' (priority=80) ... ERROR Plugin 'wechat' Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE ERROR Plugin 'wechat' marked FAILED after startup: channel 'wechat' failed: default@<id>:Projection channel failed: ACCOUNT_IN_USE ERROR Failed to activate plugin 'wechat': channel 'wechat' failed: ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE qwenpaw.plugins.workspace_projector.ProjectionError: channel 'wechat' failed: ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE
The worker's startup_diagnostic trace shows it reaches control / process_ready normally with platform_state: "disconnected" — i.e. the worker process itself does not crash. The failure is raised by the host while projecting the channel into the workspace.

What I ruled out
Not a second QwenPaw instance / not "logged in elsewhere". Confirmed only one qwenpaw process running and no other listener on the WeChat token. The worker never reaches the WeChat server (platform_state stays disconnected), so the account is not being contested remotely.
Not a cross-agent token conflict. Only default has wechat enabled. I computed wechat_auth_scopes for default vs every other agent — the scope intersection is empty, so the "cross-agent credential intersection" branch of _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence is not what fires.
Not stale custody / leftover worker. No leftover worker.py / channel_wechat process after a clean stop; no lease/lock files on disk (plugin_provisions/wechat.json is empty, no persistent owner rows).
Suspected root cause
In 2.3.0 the WeChat channel moved from the built-in in-process implementation to the plugin + workspace-projection architecture. During startup two code paths both try to reserve the same channel/wechat runtime key for the default workspace:

the channel startup hook (channel_wechat_wechat) → start_channel → manager._reserve_channel_auth → reserve_wechat_auth_async, which reserves RuntimeKey("channel", "wechat", workspace_dir) plus the wechat_auth claims; and
the workspace projection path (workspace_projector._apply / channel_ws_wechat_wechat), which reserves the same key again.
Whichever path runs second finds the key already owned by a different owner and raises ACCOUNT_IN_USE (via _reserve_wechat_auth_evidence, the resource.owner != owner branch). With the old built-in implementation there was only one path, so this never collided.

The plugin is then torn down and marked FAILED, so the channel never recovers without a restart (and a restart hits the same race).

Suggested direction (for maintainers to confirm)
Make the two paths idempotent for the same workspace — e.g. have the projection path reuse an existing channel/wechat lease owned by the same plugin/instance instead of treating it as ACCOUNT_IN_USE, or ensure only one of the two startup paths performs the reservation. (I'll leave the exact fix to you — happy to test a candidate build.)

Reproduction
QwenPaw 2.3.0 on Linux, official WeChat plugin installed and enabled for a single agent.
Start / restart the app.
Observe Plugin 'wechat' ... ACCOUNT_IN_USE and the channel stuck failed.
Deterministic — reproduces on every restart.

Notes
Separately, #8682 / PR #8692 address a different failure mode (worker crashes for lack of HOME / QWENPAW_WORKING_DIR). Applying #8692 does not fix this ACCOUNT_IN_USE issue — the worker here starts fine; the failure is in the host projection/lease path.
Happy to provide more logs or test a fix.

prs.title: feat(channels): add plugin updates, version guards, and official marketplace releases
prs.body:
## Description

This PR improves channel plugin updates and distribution:

1. **Channel plugin updates**
   - Add an update action when the bundled plugin version is newer than the installed version.
   - Read static metadata through the existing background I/O path without importing drivers, starting workers, or enabling channels.
   - Reuse the existing installation, dependency confirmation, and rollback flow while preserving configuration and enabled state.

2. **Plugin version checks in PRs and releases**
   - Compare actual published files against the PR target branch and require a version increase when content changes.
   - Calculate deterministic content digests from sorted relative paths and file contents, excluding ZIP metadata differences.
   - Reject different content under the same plugin/version while allowing identical release retries.
   - Apply the shared guard across release entry points.

3. **Official marketplace distribution for channel plugins**
   - Enable publication of 17 additional official channel plugins.
   - Add a unified channel release workflow so compatible plugin versions can ship independently of QwenPaw releases.
   - Reuse official catalog installation/update flows and add channel card uninstall actions.
   - Preserve bundled distribution and existing channel-page repair, install, and update behavior.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8684

**Security Considerations:** Version discovery remains passive and does not modify channel credentials or activation settings. Explicit updates reuse existing lifecycle safeguards. Publication uses the existing non-overwriting OSS mechanism, with credentials supplied through CI secrets.

prs.title: fix(media): downscale oversized images and mark stripped media as omitted
prs.body:
## Scope

Type: A (single-point fix) — media handling on the freezing, request-normalization
and agent-recovery paths. No public API or configuration changes.

## What Problem This Solves

An oversized image is sent verbatim and rejected by the provider; the recovery
then strips every image from the request while the tool text still says
`Image loaded: x.png`, so the model answers as if it had seen an image it
never received.

## Description

Two defects on the media path share one real-world trigger: an agent loaded a
9000px-wide PNG through `view_image`, the provider rejected the payload
("You have uploaded an unsupported image"), and QwenPaw's recovery stripped
**every** image from the request. The model then answered from a tool result
that still read `Image loaded: timeline_states_48h.png` — it was told it had
seen an image it never received.

**1. Oversized images are downscaled on the request copy only**

`freeze_image_bytes` enforced the byte cap but never checked dimensions, so a
wide-but-lightweight PNG (line art, timeline charts) passed straight through
and was rejected downstream. Freezing now keeps the original bytes, and
`downscale_oversized_images` (`agents/utils/image_resize.py`) shrinks the
cloned request inside `normalize_messages_for_model_request`. History, memory
and any later explicit request for the same media keep full resolution.

The helper:

- keeps the source format when it can carry alpha, so a transparent WebP no
  longer becomes a multi-megabyte PNG;
- if the re-encoded payload still exceeds the byte limit, steps quality down
  and then halves the dimensions; if every attempt fails it returns the
  original bytes, never a larger payload;
- detects animation with `n_frames > 1` **before** resampling and passes it
  through untouched (GIF, animated WebP, APNG) instead of keeping only the
  first frame;
- applies `ImageOps.exif_transpose()` before `thumbnail()`, so a rotated JPEG
  is scaled along its displayed axes.

**2. Stripping media now leaves an explicit marker**

When only some blocks of a `tool_result` were stripped, the surviving text was
kept as-is — that is how the model ended up holding an "Image loaded" claim
with no image behind it. The blanket "this model supports no media" strip now
appends `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` to the surviving output, in the same
shape as its siblings (dict for 1.x blocks, block object for 2.0).

Targeted strips (audio / video / document / empty) are deliberate per-modality
decisions, so they keep their current output shape. This is a deliberate
behaviour change and is covered by an updated assertion in
`test_react_agent_media_strip.py::test_nested_media_in_tool_result_stripped`.

## Evidence

Before / after, same input (9000x60 PNG):

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stored message | 9000x60 | 9000x60 (unchanged) |
| request copy | 9000x60, sent verbatim | 8192x55 |
| provider payload | rejected as unsupported | accepted |
| tool result text after strip | `Image loaded: x.png` | `Image loaded: x.png` + `[Media content removed - model does not support this media type]` |

Regression tests, grouped by the module they cover:

- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_freezing.py` — an oversized image stays
  byte-identical after freezing; an in-limit image is not re-encoded.
- `tests/unit/agents/utils/test_image_resize.py` — oversized side is
  downscaled with the aspect ratio preserved; transparent WebP stays WebP with
  alpha; animated WebP and APNG keep every frame; EXIF orientation is applied
  before resizing; the normalizer shrinks the request copy while the stored
  message keeps its bytes.
- `tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py` — a partial strip
  yields the full output list `["Image loaded: a.png", placeholder]`; an
  all-media strip collapses to the placeholder string.

Checked the tests are not vacuous: with the `src/` changes stashed the same
files report 2 failed (freezing still downscales, normalizer does not
rescale), and pass again once restored.

## Follow-up direction

The other two halves of the same bug. They are deliberately left out because
both need an interface decision first, and neither is required for this fix:

- **Per-provider media capability table** (max side / max bytes / accepted
  formats). Today the limit is inferred from a 400 response; with a declared
  table the request could be shaped correctly instead of being repaired after
  a rejection. It touches provider registration and the formatters.
- **Rejection-site attribution.** If each image carried an id, a rejection
  could name the offending one, and the recovery could transcode and retry
  *that* image instead of stripping every image in the request.

Happy to open an issue with the exact failure shapes and take either item once
the owning layer is agreed.

## Test scope

- Target: `test_image_freezing.py`, `test_image_resize.py`,
  `test_message_request_normalizer.py` — 81 passed.
- Adjacent: `tests/unit/agents -k "image or media or normalizer"` — 488
  passed, 3 skipped.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files <changed>` — all hooks passed (black 23.3.0,
  mypy, pylint, flake8, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, AST,
  private-key, encoding-pragma, trailing-whitespace).
