prs.title: fix(desktop): persist early startup errors and show native error dialogs
prs.body: ## Description QwenPaw Desktop can fail before the main window exists. Some of these early startup failures currently leave no visible window, no actionable message, and no log entry. The regular desktop logger is only initialized during Tauri setup, while earlier startup errors were only written to `stderr`, which Windows release builds do not show. This PR adds startup diagnostics that start at the very beginning of the desktop shell's startup path: - Write an independent startup log before Tauri builds the app. - Primary location: the app's local data directory, under `logs/startup/`. - Fallback: the system temporary directory. - Each process gets its own log file, so concurrent launches do not overwrite each other. - Record startup stages, the failing operation, relevant paths, OS errors, the error source chain, and a diagnostic backtrace. - Flush and sync fatal errors to disk before showing a dialog. - Show a native error dialog for desktop startup failures, with the failed stage, the reason, and the saved log location. - Windows uses `MessageBoxW`. In our Windows testing, the task-dialog path shortened long log paths in the middle (e.g. `C:\Use...\startup-xxx.log`), so users could not see where the log was; `MessageBoxW` displayed the full path. - macOS and Linux use `rfd`. - Report errors returned from Tauri setup. Tauri runs setup inside the event loop and panics on setup errors, so these failures previously bypassed the normal `build()` error path. They are now logged, shown, and followed by exit code `1`. - Record `Desktop ready` only after setup completes successfully. - Add path and operation context to early errors in installation coordination, shared-runtime directory setup, and installer process inspection. - Never show a dialog for `--agent-host` failures; they are logged only. The update admission and installer waiting rules are unchanged. While an installer is still running, a newly launched desktop process still waits quietly, as before. The only addition is that the wait start, the end, and the elapsed time are now recorded in the startup log. **Related Issue:** Relates to #8616 **Security Considerations:** - The startup log does not dump environment variables, `runtime.json`, runtime tokens, user configuration, or command lines. - Logs are written under the current user's local app data directory, or the system temporary directory as a fallback. On Unix-like systems, new log files are created with `0600` permissions. - Old startup logs are cleaned up only when they match this feature's log naming pattern and are no longer in use. Symlinked log entries are not followed. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [ ] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy Affected area not listed above: desktop shell (`console/src-tauri`). ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [ ] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ## Testing Commands run on Windows: ```powershell pre-commit run --files ` console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml ` console/src-tauri/Cargo.lock ` console/src-tauri/src/lib.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/backend/runtime.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/updates/coordination.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/updates/windows.rs ` console/src-tauri/src/startup_diagnostics.rs cargo test --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets ``` I also built a Windows release desktop shell from this change and ran it in Windows Sandbox. To match the packaged build, I used `STATIC_VCRUNTIME=true` and `tauri/custom-protocol`. The backend and other bundled resources were copied from an existing beta.4 installation. Scenarios checked: 1. **Failure before any window is created.** I made the working directory path an existing file. 2. **Background supervisor failure** (`--agent-host`). 3. **Default startup log directory not writable.** 4. **Tauri setup failure.** I made the regular desktop log directory path a file. 5. **Normal startup.** 6. **Launch while an installer handoff is still active**, then let the installer exit. ## Evidence ```text pre-commit run --files check toml...............................................................Passed detect private key.......................................................Passed trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed (other hooks skipped: no matching files) ``` ```text cargo test --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib running 66 tests test result: ok. 66 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out ``` ```text cargo clippy --locked --manifest-path console/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets exit code: 0 No warnings in the changed files. ``` Windows Sandbox results: | Scenario | Result | | --- | --- | | Failure before window creation | Native error dialog shown. It includes the stage, the full path with Chinese characters and spaces, `os error 183`, and the full log path. The log was saved before the dialog closed. Exit code `1`. | | Background supervisor failure | No window shown. The failure is written to the startup log. Exit code `1`. | | Default log directory unavailable | The log is written to the temporary directory, together with the reason the primary directory failed. | | Tauri setup failure | Native error dialog shown with stage `Initialize desktop logging and backend attachment`. The log is saved to the fallback directory. Exit code `1`. `Desktop ready` is not recorded. | | Normal startup | Main UI rendered. Backend ready. No error dialog shown. `Desktop ready` is recorded after setup completes. | | Active installer handoff | No extra prompt or window while waiting. The wait is recorded in the startup log. The main window appears after the installer exits, and the stale handoff record is removed. | Screenshots: - Tauri setup failure dialog - Early startup failure dialog ## Additional Notes - This PR improves startup observability and gives users actionable failure information. It does not claim to fix the unconfirmed root cause reported in #8616. - For the setup-failure case, the stage is reported, but the regular log plugin's own error does not include the target directory path.

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)

## Testing


prs.title: fix(console): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in chat Markdown
prs.body:
## Description

### What Problem This Solves

The chat message body renders Markdown through the vendor `Markdown` component, whose parser follows CommonMark's emphasis "flanking" rules. Those rules classify CJK sentence punctuation as Unicode punctuation, and CJK text is written without inter-word spaces. A closing `**` that sits immediately after CJK punctuation and immediately before CJK text is therefore judged "not a valid closer", and the raw markers leak into the bubble:

```
**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

The reader literally sees `**没有改动任何设置。**` instead of bold text. This is a common pattern in Chinese/Japanese/Korean replies, so it shows up frequently.

### Fix

Add `normalizeCjkEmphasis` in `console/src/utils/markdownCjk.ts`, which moves the trailing CJK punctuation run outside the delimiter (`**中文。**后` becomes `**中文**。后`), and apply it to the deferred content inside `AssistantMarkdown` — the shared deferred Markdown renderer used by host bubbles — before the text reaches `<Markdown>`.

`AssistantMarkdown` has two render paths (plain, and plugin-backed stable code blocks); the normalization is applied once to `displayContent` and both paths consume it, while the streaming comparison keeps using the raw deferred value.

The repair is deliberately conservative and display-oriented:

- only `*`, `_`, `**`, `__`, `***`, `___` are considered;
- only `。！？；：，、…` plus full-width trailing closers (`”’」』】》〉）〕］`) are moved;
- only when the delimiter is immediately followed by Han / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul;
- fenced, indented and inline code, escaped delimiters, CRLF endings and unrelated unfinished Markdown are preserved verbatim.

The helper is a pure, idempotent string transform, so applying it to a streaming (partial) value is safe — the result converges to the same text once the message completes.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `main` (`27d22cd1`); the deferred-rendering block this originally patched was moved into `AssistantMarkdown` by the host-bubble refactor, so the patch now lives there.

- `npx vitest run src/utils/markdownCjk.test.ts src/pages/Chat/AssistantMarkdown.test.tsx src/pages/Chat/HostBubbles.render.test.tsx` -> **37 passed** (3 files; 15 of them new in `markdownCjk.test.ts`).
- `tsc -b --noEmit` -> exit 0, no diagnostics.
- `npx eslint` on the three changed files -> exit 0.
- `npx prettier --check` on the three changed files -> "All matched files use Prettier code style!".
- Direct checks:
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。")` -> `"**没有改动任何设置**。所有内容保持不变。"`
  - `normalizeCjkEmphasis("**重点**后接中文")` -> unchanged
  - fenced code block containing `**代码。**后` -> unchanged
  - `**内容。**latin` -> unchanged (follower must be CJK)

## Notes

- Targeted, display-oriented repair rather than a general Markdown parser; ASCII punctuation and non-CJK followers are out of scope by design.
- Related: CommonMark discussion `commonmark/commonmark-spec#650` on CJK-friendly emphasis.

---

> **Note:** this supersedes #8068, which the PR Spam Gate auto-closed on 2026-10-01 (author had >10 open PRs at the time). Same branch, same diff; GitHub refused to reopen the original, so this is a fresh PR.

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]
23 passed in 0.49s
```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

prs.title: fix(providers): keep boolean additionalProperties in tool schemas
prs.body:
## Description

`_sanitize_boolean_schemas` expands every boolean schema value into a nested `not` schema, including keyword values such as `additionalProperties`. A tool schema that declares

```json
"additionalProperties": false
```

was therefore sent as

```json
"additionalProperties": {"not": {}}
```

`false` is the native JSON Schema keyword spelling and the form OpenAI strict-mode tool definitions use. `{"not": {}}` is semantically equivalent, but several OpenAI-compatible servers do not implement `not`: they either reject the schema or silently drop the surrounding `properties` map. When the parameter map is lost the model sees a zero-parameter function and returns `{}`, so a tool whose schema has required properties fails validation before it runs (see #8603, where `run_code` fails on custom OpenAI-compatible providers while the same model works through a built-in provider that only applies the nullable pass).

This change keeps the native spelling for `false` on the `additional*` / `unevaluated*` keywords and still converts standalone boolean schemas at positions where an object schema is expected. `true` is deliberately out of scope: it keeps its previous treatment, so the wire format does not change further than the compatibility bug requires.

## Evidence

Sanitizing the `run_code` tool schema (`{"properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["code"], "additionalProperties": false}`):

| | `additionalProperties` | `properties` | `required` |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `{"not": {}}` | `{"code": {"type": "string"}}` | `["code"]` |
| after | `false` | `{"code": {"type": "string"}}` | `["code"]` |

The parameter map is identical in both cases; only the keyword spelling changes. The new tests fail on the previous implementation (`assert {'not': {}} is False`) and pass after the change.

## Self-review

- The new branch only matches `value is False` for those four keywords; `true` and object values walk exactly as before.
- `additionalProperties: true` is still removed before the walk (unchanged), so only `false` reaches the new branch.
- Standalone boolean schemas at schema positions (`{"properties": {"payload": false}}`) still become `{"not": {}}` — covered by a test so the rewrite is not over-broadened.

## Test scope

- Target: `tests/unit/providers/test_openai_tool_schema_compat.py` — 19 passed (5 new tests: `additionalProperties: false` kept, tuple-form `additionalItems: false` kept, `unevaluated*: false` kept, `true` unchanged, standalone boolean schema still converted). Red/green on the `true` guard: stashing the source change makes it `1 failed, 18 passed`.
- Neighbouring module: `tests/unit/providers` — 1156 passed, 1 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are pre-existing environment gaps in this check-out (`reme 0.4.1.11` does not provide `reme.components.as_decision_model`), unrelated to the changed code.
- Lint: `pre-commit run --files <both files>` — 10 hooks passed (black, flake8, pylint, mypy, add-trailing-comma, docstring-first, …).

Refs #8603

prs.title: fix(crons): persist cron and heartbeat token usage to turn records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

Fixes #8705

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:
  - `commit_turn_usage` resolves and persists one finished turn's usage, never raises
  - `discard_turn_usage` drops staged usage when a run does not finish normally
- `Channel._commit_turn_usage` and `_clear_session_turn_usage` now reuse the shared helpers (no behavior change)
- Cron executor: commit usage after a successful run; discard on timeout / cancel / error
- Heartbeat: same treatment for all three `stream_query` sites

prs.title: fix(channels): hide injected context blocks at the display boundary
prs.body:
## Description

**Problem.** Two framework sources store control markers inside ordinary assistant text, and `MessageRenderer.message_to_parts()` forwards every `ContentType.TEXT` block unchanged, so channel users see them as the assistant's own words:

- `src/qwenpaw/tool_calls/_hint.py::make_offload_hint_msg()` builds `Msg(role="assistant", content=[TextBlock("<system-notification>…"), *result_blocks])` with no metadata marker. Its docstring says this flattening is deliberate, “so that provider formatters treat it as an ordinary assistant message”.
- Scroll context-compression / continuation notes carry `<system-info>…</system-info>` blocks.

The existing display flags cannot suppress either one: `show_thinking` / `show_tool_calls` / `show_tool_results` only gate structured block types.

**Fix.** Add `strip_injected_context()` next to `strip_headline()` and call it from the same `TEXT` branch. It follows the contract that `strip_headline()` already documents: display-only — the live context and the persisted row keep the original bytes.

Risk is kept minimal by four guards:

1. **Start only** — a block is removed only when it opens the text; mid-text mentions are untouched.
2. **Balanced only** — opening and closing tags must both be present; a dangling `<system-info>` is left alone.
3. **Quoted is safe** — a leading backtick means the marker is being quoted (`` `<system-info>` is … ``), so the text is returned unchanged.
4. **Fail-open** — if nothing can be removed, or stripping would empty the message, the original text is returned.

A trailing reasoning fragment is **not** addressed here; that is a separate boundary problem.

Fixes #8293.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/unit/agents/context/test_serialize.py tests/unit/app/channels/test_renderer.py -q` → **96 passed** (6 new sanitizer tests + 1 renderer test).
- `pre-commit run --files <the four changed files>` → **all hooks Passed** (black, flake8, pylint, mypy, add-trailing-comma, check-docstring-first, trailing whitespace).
- Before/after on a real installation: a text block that starts with `<system-notification>…</system-notification>\nDone.` renders as `['Done.']`; a normal reply and the quoted-mention case render unchanged.
- Not covered by #7835: that PR guards a message carrying `AUTO_MEMORY_SEARCH_BLOCK_HIDDEN_KEY`. The offload hint and the context note carry no metadata, so a message-level guard cannot see them — this is a text-level guard for a different source.

prs.title: fix(console): stop Open in browser from failing silently outside the workspace
prs.body:
## Description

Clicking **Open in browser** on an HTML file that lives outside the workspace did nothing at all: no window opened, no message appeared, nothing. The button looked broken.

Two things combined:

1. `openHtmlFile()` only attached `.catch()` to the native opener and **never inspected the value it resolved with**:

```ts
void pywebviewApi
  .open_workspace_html(resolverUrl, headers)
  .catch((error) => console.warn("[html-preview] Native open failed", error));
```

2. `open_workspace_html` **answers `false` — not an error —** for anything that does not resolve inside the workspace (`resolve_workspace_path()` refuses paths outside the selected root). So the refusal was reported as an ordinary negative result that nobody read.

Worth separating two surfaces that are easy to confuse: the *preview* keeps working for such files because it fetches the bytes through a different route; only *open in browser* was a silent no-op.

### What this changes

- All three branches (pywebview, Tauri, blob) now inspect the result instead of only catching rejections.
- When the native shell declines **or** rejects, the in-memory copy of the HTML is rendered in a preview window, so the click always shows something.
- `openHtmlFile()` returns an `OpenHtmlFileResult` (`{ opened, mode }`) so callers can tell the user what happened. `FilePreview` shows a toast when the fallback path was taken.

### Scope

This is deliberately the **first half**: it removes the silent no-op. A follow-up can add explicit user confirmation (show the resolved path, ask, then open in the real browser) and/or a reveal-in-folder action for files that stay outside the workspace. That needs its own change because the backend does not currently return an absolute path to the client.

**Related Issue:** none found. I searched the tracker first: `"open_workspace_html"` returns 0 hits and `"html-file-uri"` only appears in passing in #6976.

**Security Considerations:** none. No new file access is added: the fallback renders content the client already holds, and the workspace restriction on the native opener is untouched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Checklist

- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

> Note on the first two boxes: `pre-commit run` cannot initialize its hook environments on this machine (github.com fetches abort with `Recv failure: Connection was reset/aborted`, direct and via proxy). I ran the equivalent console commands instead — `tsc -b --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, `eslint` — and they pass; see Evidence.

## Testing

```bash
cd console
npx vitest run src/utils/openHtmlFile.test.ts
npx vitest run src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.test.tsx
npx vitest run src/utils src/pages/Coding
npx tsc -b --noEmit
npx prettier --check <changed files>
npx eslint src/utils/openHtmlFile.ts src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.tsx
```

The three new cases cover the exact regression: the opener resolving `false`, resolving `true`, and rejecting.

## Evidence

Targeted unit tests — 10 cases, including the three added here:

```
$ npx vitest run src/utils/openHtmlFile.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10 D:/QwenPawContrib/qwenpaw/console

 ✓ src/utils/openHtmlFile.test.ts (10 tests) 7ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The component test that exercises the changed file, plus the surrounding suite:

```
$ npx vitest run src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.test.tsx
 ✓ src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.test.tsx (17 tests) 130ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  17 passed (17)

$ npx vitest run src/utils src/pages/Coding
 Test Files  39 passed (39)
      Tests  362 passed (362)
```

Type-check, formatting and lint all clean for the touched files:

```
$ npx tsc -b --noEmit
(no output - clean)

$ npx prettier --check src/utils/openHtmlFile.ts src/utils/openHtmlFile.test.ts \
    src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.tsx src/locales/en.json src/locales/zh.json

All matched files use Prettier code style!

$ npx eslint src/utils/openHtmlFile.ts src/pages/Coding/FilePreview.tsx

                                      # on getPreviewType/isPreviewable, not touched here
```

How it was reproduced before the fix: opening a chat, previewing an HTML file that lives outside the workspace, and pressing the button produced no window and no message. The same button on an in-workspace HTML opens normally. Backend-side, `GET /api/workspace/html-file-uri?path=<outside>` answers `400 Path contains an invalid segment`, which is what the old code silently discarded.

## Additional Notes

- The regression test for the rejection path already existed; it still passes, which is why the new tests only add the `resolve(false)` and `resolve(true)` cases.
- I kept the fallback silent-free on purpose: rendering the in-memory copy is a *degraded but working* outcome, so the toast is informational rather than an error.
- Only `en` and `zh` carry the new string. The other locales do not define `files.openHtmlInBrowser` today, so nothing becomes inconsistent; they fall back to `en` as they already do for that section.

prs.title: fix(install): use the selected PyPI mirror when seeding the venv
prs.body:
## Description

`scripts/install.sh` probes `pypi.org` and falls back to the Aliyun mirror when it is unreachable, but only the `uv pip install` calls receive `--index-url "$PYPI_MIRROR"`. Since #8187, the environment is created with `uv venv ... --seed`, and seeding pip downloads it from the default index, which is `pypi.org`. On networks where the official index is unreachable, upgrading to 2.3.0 fails at that step, and because `UV_VENV_CLEAR=1` has already wiped the old environment, the existing install is left broken (only `python` left in `venv/bin`, no `qwenpaw`, no `pip`).

This passes the same `--index-url "$PYPI_MIRROR"` to `uv venv --seed`, so the whole install uses the source chosen by the probe. When `pypi.org` is reachable, `PYPI_MIRROR` is `https://pypi.org/simple/` and behaviour is unchanged.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8698

**Security Considerations:** None. The seed packages now come from the same index the script already uses for every other package.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change

- [ ] Refactoring

- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)

`pre-commit run --all-files`: every hook passes except `pylint`, which reports the same existing findings in untouched Python files on `main` (fc1db1a4) without this change. `pytest`: passes with 33 tests deselected that also fail on unchanged `main` in my environment (real-browser Playwright tests, plugin install/upgrade and process-isolation tests). No test or Python file is touched by this PR. Details under Evidence.

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes
- [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_<channel>.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery)
- [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py`
- [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/`

## Testing

Reproduced on Ubuntu 24.04 with uv 0.13.5 by routing HTTPS through a small local CONNECT proxy that refuses `pypi.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org` (`HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:18698`), using an empty `UV_CACHE_DIR` and an existing `$QWENPAW_HOME/venv`, then running `bash scripts/install.sh`:

- Before: the probe picks the Aliyun mirror, then `uv venv --seed` fails on `https://pypi.org/simple/pip/`; `venv/bin` contains only `python python3 python3.12`.
- After: the environment is seeded from the mirror, `qwenpaw` is installed from it, and the script exits 0; `venv/bin` contains `pip`, `qwenpaw` and `qwenpawmail-mcp`. The only `pypi.org` requests in the proxy log are the reachability probes.

Also checked:
- fresh install (no existing venv) with `pypi.org` blocked: `uv venv --seed --index-url <aliyun>` succeeds and pip is seeded;
- normal network: `uv venv --seed --index-url https://pypi.org/simple/` succeeds as before;
- uv 0.13.4 (the minimum the script accepts) supports `-i/--index-url` on `uv venv`.

## Evidence

Upgrade with `pypi.org` unreachable:

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/QwenPaw/eb8d3d584af16e08ff9af24d7fce827c583568d4/draft_bdf13f/ev_a148f6.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shu-chen-dot-ca/QwenPaw/eb8d3d584af16e08ff9af24d7fce827c583568d4/draft_bdf13f/ev_dd6c33.jpg) |

```bash
SKIP=pylint pre-commit run --all-files
# all other hooks Passed (pylint fails identically on main fc1db1a4)

pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --deselect <33 tests that also fail on main here>
# 18862 passed, 57 skipped, 33 deselected, 2 xpassed in 5064.81s
```

## Additional Notes

`scripts/install.ps1` and `scripts/install.bat` also call `uv venv --seed`, but they have no mirror detection, so they are left unchanged here.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): probe Landlock without requiring securityfs
prs.body:
## Description

`_probe_linux_landlock()` 在无法读取 `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` 时直接返回
`supported=False`。容器不挂载 securityfs，该文件因此通常不存在——即便宿主内核的
Landlock LSM 完全可用。

后果不只是能力报告错误。当 `security.sandbox_enabled=true` 时，
`ResourceGovernor.execution_sandbox_config()` 走 fail-closed，于是每次 Code Mode
的 `run_code` 都以如下错误失败：

```
Script failed: Sandbox is enabled but unavailable
```

在官方 `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest` 镜像（2.3.0）、WSL2 宿主内核 6.18 上复现，
此时内核通过 `landlock_create_ruleset` 系统调用报告 Landlock ABI v7：

| 步骤 | 容器内结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 第 1 步 — 内核 >= 5.13 | 通过（6.18） |
| 第 2 步 — 读取 `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` | `FileNotFoundError`，securityfs 未挂载 |
| 探测结论 | `supported=False`，`reason='Cannot read /sys/kernel/security/lsm'` |
| 系统调用探测（根本没执行到） | 本应返回 ABI v7 |

根因是第 2 步和第 3 步对"支持"的定义存在冲突。第 2 步只是读一个文件；第 3 步
才是真正决定能否创建 ruleset 的系统调用。第 2 步被当成了权威判据，导致权威检查
永远没有机会执行。

**修复方式：** 把 LSM 列表降级为尽力而为的旁证。

- 文件不可读 → 结论未定（securityfs 未挂载）。记 debug 日志，继续走系统调用探测。
- 文件可读但不含 `landlock` → 仍然是真正的"否"，仍返回 `supported=False`。不放松安全边界。
- 系统调用失败（如 `ENOSYS`）→ 仍返回 `supported=False`。

未知架构分支（没有硬编码系统调用号，例如 `riscv64`）此前仅凭"内核版本 + LSM 检查"
就假定支持。LSM 检查变成可选后该假定失去依据，因此现在只有 LSM 列表确实确认过
`landlock` 时才报告支持，否则返回 unsupported 并给出明确原因。这是有意的收紧，
在 `x86_64` / `aarch64` 上行为不变。

`_probe_linux_landlock()` returns `supported=False` whenever
`/sys/kernel/security/lsm` cannot be read. Containers do not mount
securityfs, so that file is routinely absent there even though the host
kernel exposes a fully working Landlock LSM.

The consequence is not just a wrong capability report. With
`security.sandbox_enabled=true`, `ResourceGovernor.execution_sandbox_config()`
fails closed, so every Code Mode `run_code` call dies with:

```
Script failed: Sandbox is enabled but unavailable
```

Reproduced on the official `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest` image (2.3.0) on a
WSL2 host kernel 6.18, where the kernel reports Landlock ABI v7 via the
`landlock_create_ruleset` syscall:

| Step | Result in the container |
| --- | --- |
| Step 1 — kernel >= 5.13 | passes (6.18) |
| Step 2 — read `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` | `FileNotFoundError` — securityfs not mounted |
| Probe outcome | `supported=False`, `reason='Cannot read /sys/kernel/security/lsm'` |
| Syscall probe (never reached) | would have returned ABI v7 |

The root cause is that steps 2 and 3 disagree about what "supported"
means. Step 2 reads a file; step 3 performs the syscall that actually
determines whether a ruleset can be created. Step 2 was treated as
authoritative, so the authoritative check never ran.

**Fix:** demote the LSM list to best-effort corroboration.

- Unreadable file → inconclusive (securityfs not mounted). Log at debug
  and fall through to the syscall probe.
- Readable file that omits `landlock` → still a genuine "no", still
  `supported=False`. No security regression.
- Syscall fails (e.g. `ENOSYS`) → still `supported=False`.

The unknown-architecture branch (no hardcoded syscall number, e.g.
`riscv64`) previously assumed support from "kernel version + LSM check"
alone. With the LSM check now optional that assumption would become
unfounded, so it only reports supported when the LSM list actually
confirmed `landlock`; otherwise it returns unsupported with a clear
reason. This is a deliberate tightening, not a behavior change on
`x86_64` / `aarch64`.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #5982, #6023

**Security Considerations:** 本改动让一条此前被阻断的执行路径变得可达，因此隔离性
是经过实际验证的而非假定（见 Evidence）。探测在未知架构上收紧，此前那里会高报支持。
不改任何配置默认值，`security.sandbox_enabled=false` 的关闭路径不受影响。

This change makes a previously-blocked execution path reachable, so the
isolation itself was verified rather than assumed — see Evidence. The
probe tightens on unknown architectures, which previously over-reported
support. No configuration defaults change, and the switch-off path
(`security.sandbox_enabled=false`) is untouched.

## Type of Change

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)

- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass

Not applicable — 本 PR 不涉及任何频道。

## Testing

针对探测函数的每个分支编写单元测试，并跑既有沙箱套件确认无回归：

```bash
pytest tests/unit/sandbox/ tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
```

新增文件 `tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py` 覆盖：

1. LSM 文件不可读 + 系统调用可用 → `supported=True`（本次容器回归场景）。
2. LSM 文件不可读 + `ENOSYS` → 仍为 `supported=False`。
3. 可读列表包含 `landlock` → 支持。
4. 可读列表不含 `landlock` → 仍为 `supported=False`（防止过度放行）。
5. 内核低于 5.13，以及 `os.uname()` 不可用/无法解析。
6. 未知架构，分别在有无 LSM 确认的情况下。

关于可移植性：测试整体替换 `os` 模块而非 patch `os.uname`，因为非 POSIX 宿主上
`os.uname` 不存在，`patch()` 会抛 `AttributeError`。因此该套件在 Windows 开发机
上也能运行。

Targeted unit tests for every branch of the probe, plus the existing
sandbox suites for regression:

```bash
pytest tests/unit/sandbox/ tests/integration/test_sandbox_module.py -q
```

The new file `tests/unit/sandbox/test_landlock_probe.py` covers:

1. Unreadable LSM list + working syscall → `supported=True` (the
   container regression).
2. Unreadable LSM list + `ENOSYS` → still `supported=False`.
3. Readable list containing `landlock` → supported.
4. Readable list without `landlock` → still `supported=False`
   (guards against over-permitting).
5. Kernel below 5.13, and unparsable/unavailable `os.uname()`.
6. Unknown architecture with and without LSM confirmation.

Note on portability: the tests swap the whole `os` module for a small
fake instead of patching `os.uname`, because `os.uname` does not exist on
non-POSIX hosts and `patch()` would raise `AttributeError` there. The
suite therefore also runs on a Windows development host.

## Evidence

> 说明：以下记录均在本地产生，镜像与宿主内核版本已在各块中注明。
> Note: the transcripts below were produced locally; the container image
> and host kernel are named in each block.

```text

........................................................ssssssssssssssss [ 20%]
sssss................................................................... [ 41%]
.............s.........................s................................ [ 62%]
........................................................................ [ 83%]
...................................................s....                 [100%]
320 passed, 24 skipped in 0.83s
```

因此本修复并没有把"探测失败"变成"无沙箱裸跑"，而是变成"在一个可用的
Landlock 沙箱内运行"。
So the fix does not turn "probe fails" into "runs unsandboxed" — it
turns it into "runs inside a working Landlock sandbox".

## Additional Notes

- 这实际上是一个容器场景的回归，但探测改动与平台无关，同时消除了未知架构上
  一处潜在的高报。
- #5982 被以 "Fixed in #6054" 关闭，但那个 PR 只是新增了
  `security.sandbox_enabled` 开关并调整了 fallback 动作，并未改动 LSM 探测。
  开关默认关闭恰好掩盖了探测缺陷，直到用户打开沙箱。之后的 Code Mode
  （#8224）让探测结果变成 fail-closed 路径上的硬依赖，两者这才叠加成硬故障。
- 后续可选工作（不在本 PR 范围）：把 securityfs 挂进容器仍是有效的运维规避手段，
  且不受本改动影响。

- This is a container-only regression in practice, but the probe change
  is platform-independent and also removes a latent over-report on
  unknown architectures.
- #5982 was closed as "Fixed in #6054", but that PR added the
  `security.sandbox_enabled` switch and changed the fallback action; it
  did not touch the LSM probe. The default-off switch masked the probe
  bug until a user enabled the sandbox. Code Mode (`#8224`) later made
  the probe result load-bearing on a fail-closed path, which is how the
  two combined into a hard failure.
- Possible follow-up (not in this PR): mounting securityfs into the
  container remains a valid operator workaround and is unaffected.

prs.title: fix(cron): record a gate-terminated run as an error
prs.body:
## Description

A cron job that the doom-loop gate stops is still recorded as a success.

When a loop gate terminates a turn, the agent returns an ordinary assistant message, so the cron executor sees `delivery_status: "success"`, and the cron manager maps everything that is not `failed` to `last_status: "success"`. In the report on #8184 the job killed at 08:02:38 still showed `last_status: "success"` and `last_error: null` a day later, so `cron state` and the inbox both hide the failure from the operator.

This PR does not change the gate decision. Repeated polling tripping the gate is expected behaviour, as explained in the issue, and PR #8192 explores the spaced-polling side of it. What changes here is only how the outcome is recorded: the stop reason now travels from the gate, through the agent and the runtime executor, onto the finalized message metadata, and a cron run that carries a reason is recorded as an error.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8184

**Security Considerations:** None. No new input surface, no credential, config or channel handling.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

The pre-commit hooks are not installed in this environment, so the box is left unticked; the equivalent hooks were run directly at the versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (black 23.3.0, add-trailing-comma 3.1.0, flake8 with the file's arguments enable/ignore list). Details under Additional Notes.

## Testing

Targeted suite:

```text
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/crons tests/unit/runtime tests/unit/loop -q
735 passed, 1 skipped, 15 warnings in 119.38s (0:01:59)
```

The five new cases in `tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py` cover the hand-off chain, and the cron tests cover both outcomes:

- `test_executor_hands_the_stop_reason_to_the_envelope`, `test_executor_skips_a_turn_that_was_not_stopped`, `test_executor_tolerates_an_envelope_without_the_hook`
- `test_finalized_message_carries_the_stop_reason`, `test_finalized_message_has_no_reason_without_a_gate_stop`
- `test_gate_stop_reason_is_reported_in_the_result` (cron executor result and trace status)
- `test_execute_once_records_a_gate_stop_as_an_error` (state, error text, inbox status/severity/body)

Regression comparison over `tests/unit/{loop,runtime,agents,app}` on the same machine: 43 failed / 7656 passed before the change, 38 failed / 7661 passed after it. The five-case delta is the new suite; no existing case turns red. The remaining failures are environmental and predate this branch (worktree/branch tests that need a real git repository, console static assets, symlink privileges).

Formatting: `black --line-length 79 --check` and `add-trailing-comma` report no changes for the nine files, and flake8 reports only the three findings that already exist on `main`.

## Evidence

Unit tests for the new behaviour:

```text
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py \
    tests/unit/app/crons/test_executor.py::test_gate_stop_reason_is_reported_in_the_result \
    tests/unit/app/crons/test_manager.py::test_execute_once_records_a_gate_stop_as_an_error -v
tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py::test_executor_hands_the_stop_reason_to_the_envelope PASSED [ 14%]
tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py::test_executor_skips_a_turn_that_was_not_stopped PASSED [ 28%]
tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py::test_executor_tolerates_an_envelope_without_the_hook PASSED [ 42%]
tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py::test_finalized_message_carries_the_stop_reason PASSED [ 57%]
tests/unit/runtime/test_stop_reason.py::test_finalized_message_has_no_reason_without_a_gate_stop PASSED [ 71%]
tests/unit/app/crons/test_executor.py::test_gate_stop_reason_is_reported_in_the_result PASSED [ 85%]
tests/unit/app/crons/test_manager.py::test_execute_once_records_a_gate_stop_as_an_error PASSED [100%]
============================== 7 passed in 0.31s ==============================
```

End-to-end demo with the real `Envelope`, `AgentExecutor` and `CronExecutor` (a stub agent emits a final message carrying a `StopResult` with the doom-loop reason, then the cron executor runs it):

```text
finalized message metadata: {'qwenpaw_stop_reason': 'Doom loop: agent stuck after 4 consecutive repetitions'}
carries the stop reason: True
cron executor stop_reason: Doom loop: agent stuck after 4 consecutive repetitions
delivery_status: success
```

The cron manager turns that `stop_reason` into `last_status: "error"` with the reason as `last_error`, and into an inbox event with `status: "error"` and `severity: "warning"`; `test_execute_once_records_a_gate_stop_as_an_error` asserts exactly that.

## Additional Notes

Two design decisions worth a look:

1. **Metadata key instead of a new status value.** `CronJobState.last_status` is a `Literal` that the console and the HTTP API read, so adding `stopped` would be a public schema change for a state the UI has no branch for. The reason is carried as `qwenpaw_stop_reason` in the finalized message metadata (next to the existing `qwenpaw_*` keys), and cron reuses `error` plus `last_error` to say what happened.
2. **A gate stop without a reason is a normal completion.** `loop/gates/runner.py` can return a bare `TERMINATE` when no handler matched, which is how a regular turn ends. Only `TERMINATE` with a reason is recorded, so ordinary turns are never marked as stopped.

Also worth knowing:

- `delivery_status` is untouched. Whether the final message reached the channel is a different question from whether the agent finished its work, and the issue only asks about the latter.
- The reason is cleared at the start of every reply, so a later turn cannot inherit a stale one.
- The trace (`finalize_trace`) for a gate-terminated run is now written as `error` as well, matching the state; it used to be unconditional `success`.
- Out of scope and left alone: `heartbeat.py` records its own task type with a separate `success` path, and `no_content` runs are still counted as success because there is no machine-checkable signal for them. Happy to take that as a follow-up if you want it.
- AI assistance: the patch was drafted with an AI coding agent (DeepSeek Harness) and reviewed line by line before submission. The test runs, the demo and the formatting output above were produced locally on Windows with Python 3.13.

prs.title: fix(loop): record tool calls appended to one reply message
prs.body:
## Description

`DoomLoopGate` never fired on 2.3.0. agentscope 2.0.10 keeps **one assistant message per reply**: `_save_to_context` uses `state.reply_id` as the message id and appends every iteration's blocks to that same message. `_auto_record_from_ctx` treated the message id as a per-iteration cursor and returned as soon as it matched, so only the first snapshot of a reply was ever recorded. With the default `window_size=3`, the warning could fire only when the first snapshot already held 3 identical calls, and the `after=4 / stop` stage was unreachable.

This PR tracks how many tool-call blocks have already been consumed from the latest message and records only the newly appended tail. Each iteration contributes its own calls again, while re-checking the same snapshot stays a no-op.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8700

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native `POST /api/show`. Discovery does **not** call `/api/ps`. After the training-context clamp, a served `context_length` cannot change the window, so the `/api/ps` tier is gone.

The window is the explicit Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `/api/show`, **clamped to the model's training context**. Ollama clamps `NumCtx` to that maximum (`llm/server.go`, v0.19.0). The cap is exactly `model_info[general.architecture + ".context_length"]` (`fs/ggml/ggml.go`, v0.19.0):

- `model_info` must be a dict.
- `general.architecture` must be a non-empty string (whitespace is stripped; empty or non-string → no cap).
- That one key is parsed as a strict positive integer: real `int` or digit string, at least 1. Bools, floats, `0`, negatives, and non-digit strings are rejected.
- A bare `context_length` key and other architectures' `*.context_length` keys are ignored. The cap is not the minimum of every `*.context_length` key.

When the cap is missing or not positive, the raw Modelfile value is kept. Example: Modelfile `num_ctx 65536` with `{"general.architecture": "qwen3", "qwen3.context_length": 32768}` is persisted as **32768**.

If the show has **no explicit Modelfile `num_ctx`**, the value stays unset and the **128K default remains**. GGUF training context is **not** a window by itself. A show that has only `model_info` and no `num_ctx` leaves the window unset. That field is used only as the cap on an explicit Modelfile `num_ctx`.

Chat `generate_kwargs` / `options.num_ctx` is **not** used, and it does not skip the native probe. QwenPaw chats through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which cannot set Ollama's context size (`options` / `num_ctx` passed to `AsyncCompletions.create()` raises `TypeError`).

Failed `/api/show` probes (`show_payload is None`: timeout, 401/403, or an invalid body) leave the model **unchanged**, so merge keeps any previous auto-detected window. A present non-string `parameters` value, including explicit JSON `null`, is malformed and is treated the same way (retain the old value), not as “successful but unknown”. An omitted `parameters` field, or a successful `/api/show` whose Modelfile string has no `num_ctx`, sets `max_input_length_auto_detected=None` (the field is in `model_fields_set`) and **clears** a stale auto-detected value. That clear is not gated on `/api/ps`.

`/api/show` runs for every listed model under one shared wall-clock `timeout`. HTTPX's per-call timeout does not cap total response time, so a slow show is cancelled at that deadline. Completed `/api/show` results are kept; only unfinished probes stay unset. Cancelled probes are drained with `run_async_to_completion` before the client is closed. `httpx.AsyncClient` is built off the event loop via `run_sync_io`.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show`.

Native `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py \
  tests/unit/cli/test_ollama_model_selection.py -q
# 113 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes the architecture-key training clamp (`num_ctx 65536` + `general.architecture=qwen3` + `qwen3.context_length` 32768 persists 32768; a bare `context_length` or another architecture's key does not replace that cap; 0 / missing / bool / float / invalid training length still persists 65536; `model_info` alone stays unset), chat `options.num_ctx` neither skipping `/api/show` nor being persisted, GGUF training context ignored as a window, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, a successful show without `num_ctx` clearing a stale auto-detected value, malformed `parameters` (including explicit `null`) retaining a prior window, an omitted `parameters` field clearing a stale value, the shared `/api/show` deadline keeping completed probes, discovery not requesting `/api/ps`, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, `AsyncClient` constructed off the loop, repeated cancellation draining probes before `aclose`, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

prs.title: fix(memory): OpenViking follow-up cleanup, compatibility, and shutdown fixes
prs.body: ## Description Follow-up to #7613. This PR applies the plugin-local cleanups suggested during review, adapts automatic-recall budgeting to the host's current `HintBlock` format, and addresses the shutdown edge case accepted as a non-blocking follow-up in #7613. All changes are confined to `plugins/memory/openviking/`. **Related Issue:** Relates to #7613 **Security Considerations:** [If applicable, e.g. channel auth, env/config handling] ### Automatic-recall budgeting - Account for the actual `HintBlock.hint` content when reserving space for the host-generated recall wrapper. - Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and bound the full injected recall text, rather than only the retrieved body. - Update budget tests to measure the actual hint content instead of fields from the previous message format. - Remove the hard-coded request-budget expectation derived from the old host prompt. Existing boundary tests verify the complete-message budget. - Update the toolkit-builder test's mock configuration to include `coding_mode.enabled`. ### Shutdown lifecycle - Store and reuse a single HTTP cleanup task across repeated and concurrent `close()` calls, rather than treating a cleared client reference as proof that cleanup completed. - Use `asyncio.shield()` so cancelling a caller's wait does not cancel the underlying cleanup. Cancellation still propagates to the caller. - Preserve the actual cleanup result. If HTTP cleanup fails, subsequent `close()` calls continue to return `False` instead of incorrectly reporting success. - Add regression coverage for repeated close after failure, caller cancellation followed by successful or failed cleanup, concurrent close calls, and repeated close after success. Preserve credential redaction in failure logs. ### Review follow-up **Item 1 — Reuse the base automatic-recall flow** The session-aware `auto_memory_search()` override is retained in this PR. I agree that the base flow could serve the current default configuration with query expansion disabled. The retained override passes the current QwenPaw session ID to OpenViking, allowing session-based query expansion when `query_expansion="auto"` is enabled through the documented source change. The READMEs now clarify that query expansion remains disabled by default, requires editing source and redeploying, and depends on available session history or an archive overview. No Console or Agent configuration switch is introduced. **Item 3 — Use one UTF-8 clipping implementation** Reuse `_clip_utf8()` for both automatic recall and explicit search. When truncation cannot retain meaningful text, return an empty string rather than a marker-only result. Preserve the complete untrusted-history notice and multibyte character boundaries. **Item 4 — Flatten persistence filtering** Combine role, persisted-ID, and pending-ID filtering into one pass, and calculate the `every_turn` condition once. Preserve the existing separation between successful append and successful commit progress. **Item 5 — Reduce test coupling** Move shared fixtures into `conftest.py` and centralize manager cleanup. Budget tests measure the complete injected message and check the intact notice and nonempty recalled body, rather than relying on hard-coded values derived from host prompt wording. ### Additional small cleanups - Use a direct relative import in `plugin.py`. - Return `await self._request(...)` directly in the two forwarding client methods. - Catch `httpx.RequestError` alone, since it already includes `TimeoutException`. The explicit-search small-budget guard is retained as a defensive useful-body check if the fixed source limits are reduced, with boundary-test coverage. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Breaking change - [x] Documentation - [x] Refactoring ## Component(s) Affected - [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models) - [ ] Console (frontend web UI) - [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.) - [ ] Skills - [ ] CLI - [x] Documentation (website) - [x] Tests - [ ] CI/CD - [ ] Scripts / Deploy ## Checklist - [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally and it passes - [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks - [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass - [x] Documentation updated (if needed) - [x] Ready for review ### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.) - [ ] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes - [ ] Official channel changes are covered in `tests/unit/channels/test_.py` (startup, shutdown and message delivery) - [ ] Shared host/process changes are covered in `test_channel_host.py` / `tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_process.py` - [ ] Console changes retain the built-in contract checks in `tests/contract/channels/` ## Testing The tests cover complete-message recall budgets, oversized and multibyte results, intact safety notices, empty-result handling, persistence retries and deduplication, bounded caches, and shutdown lifecycle behavior. Shutdown regression tests verify that repeated or concurrent calls cannot report success before cleanup completes, caller cancellation does not cancel the shared cleanup task, and genuine cleanup failures remain reported as failures. ## Evidence ```bash PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src:$PWD" \ PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \ PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED=1 \ .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \ -p no:cacheprovider \ plugins/memory/openviking/tests ``` ```text 146 passed in 1.21s ``` ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --all-files git diff --check ``` All applicable hooks passed. ### OpenViking v0.5.2.1 — session-based query expansion For this verification, the request was changed in source to `query_expansion="auto"` and the commit policy was set to `auto`. The user first established the current project, then asked a follow-up using only “它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？” After switching from R3 to R4, the server’s expansion followed the new project. Selected response fields from the OpenViking v0.5.2.1 query-expansion verification: ```json { "query_expansion": "used", "planned_queries": [ "它的设备编号和维护窗口是什么？请直接回答，不要主动调用工具，也不要读取本地文件。", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 设备编号", "升级验收-R4-b610e899 维护窗口" ] } ``` The corresponding answer returned `OV-UP-B610E899` and Sunday at 20:45. Additional checks confirmed that recall remained functional after a message-count-triggered commit retained recent messages, and a fresh session did not borrow the previous session’s history for query expansion. Long-term memory remains shared across those conversations. The `used` status alone is not treated as proof of query rewriting; the expanded `planned_queries` above provide that evidence. ## Additional Notes 1. The plugin keeps its own automatic-recall method to pass the current session ID to OpenViking. prs.title: fix(sandbox): never write a sandbox ACE on a volume root
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, sandbox ACLs are **inheritable** and are written on the
workspace, on every mount (including the session project directory, which
is mounted writable) and on every deny path. A volume root has no parent,
so writing one there re-propagates it to every existing child of the
volume. When the root DACL is missing (a NULL DACL) it gets replaced with
a sandbox-only DACL, and SYSTEM / Administrators / the user vanish from
the subtree — the drive becomes inaccessible even to an elevated
Administrator, and the sandbox-only ACE has to be removed by hand.

This closes every path that could create that state:

1. **A volume root is never a sandbox grant root** — `SandboxConfig`
   collects them (`volume_root_paths`) across `workspace_dir`, any mount
   (read-only mounts get an inheritable ACE too) and any `deny_paths`
   entry, and warns. `create_sandbox` then downgrades such a config to
   `SandboxMode.NONE` and logs a warning, so **the command still runs**
   while the volume stays usable. One check covers the AppContainer,
   elevated and unelevated backends.
2. **Never fill a NULL DACL** — `_set_path_ace` and `_add_traverse_ace`
   refuse instead of letting `SetEntriesInAclW` produce a DACL that holds
   only the sandbox SID.
3. **Never rewrite a volume root's DACL** — both DACL-reset fallbacks
   (`icacls /reset` in the elevated backend and
   `_reset_dacl_to_inherited` in the unelevated one) skip volume roots.
4. **A second guard in `_set_path_ace`** — it is the single point where
   sandbox ACEs are written (the AppContainer and elevated backends both
   delegate to it), so no caller can reintroduce the write.

The console warns before the user picks such a directory
(`ProjectSelectModal`), so the loss of the sandbox is not silent.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7943

**Security Considerations:** This tightens, rather than loosens, the
sandbox — no auth or config surface is added. Two judgement calls worth
flagging:

- **Fail-open on the volume root.** The sandbox is *skipped* rather than
  the session failing, because the reporter's expected behaviour is
  "command runs in the host / volume stays usable". That means a
  volume-root workspace runs **unsandboxed**; the backend logs a warning
  and the console asks the user first. If you would rather refuse
  outright (fail-closed), it is a two-line change — happy to switch.
- **The volume-root check is platform-independent**, so a POSIX
  `workspace_dir` of `/` also falls back. The ACL hazard is Windows-only,
  but "a volume root is not a usable workspace" holds everywhere. Happy
  to scope it to Windows if you prefer.

prs.title: fix(security): guard inline Office COM automation before unsandboxed fallback
prs.body:
## Description

On Windows, with approval level `auto` and the security sandbox off, an
agent-authored inline Office COM command is executed instead of denied. The
Office COM servers (`PowerPoint.Application`, `Excel.Application`,
`Word.Application`, `Outlook.Application`) are single-instance, so `Quit()`
on an inline-constructed object terminates the user's already-open app.

The command matched no signature in `dangerous_shell_commands.yaml`, was
classified `SANDBOX_FALLBACK` by `GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, and — with the
sandbox off — was rewritten to `ALLOW` by `ResourceGovernor`
("running unsandboxed"), so it ran silently.

This PR adds a CRITICAL detection rule (`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION`)
covering the inline-construction verbs against the four Office ProgIDs:

- `New-Object -ComObject <App>.Application` (PowerShell)
- `GetActiveObject(...)` / `[Marshal]::GetActiveObject(...)`
- `CreateObject(...)`
- `win32com.client.Dispatch` / `DispatchEx(...)`
- `[Type]::GetTypeFromProgID(...)` (used by `[activator]::CreateInstance`)
- `Activator` + `CreateInstance`

The CRITICAL finding surfaces in Phase 1, so the call is held for approval
*before* the unsandboxed fallback, instead of running silently.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8002

**Security Considerations:** Local impact only — a shell command the agent is
already allowed to run can no longer silently close the user's Office
process. Ordinary shell commands are unaffected.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Tests

## Checklist

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` locally and it passes
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest`) and they pass
- [x] Ready for review

## Testing

The new rule is matched through the real loader
(`load_rules_from_yaml` → `RuleBasedToolGuardian`) and through
`GovernancePolicy.evaluate`, not by re-declaring the patterns in the test.

Verified behaviour with a default policy (`execution_level` = smart / auto):

| command | decision | finding |
|---|---|---|
| `New-Object -ComObject PowerPoint.Application` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `win32com.client.Dispatch('Word.Application').Quit()` | ASK | `TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` |
| `echo hello` | SANDBOX_FALLBACK (unchanged) | — |

`ASK` maps to the approval card, so in `auto` + sandbox-off the command is
now held for the user instead of closing their PowerPoint.

## Evidence

```bash
$ pre-commit run --files \
    src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules/dangerous_shell_commands.yaml \
    tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py
check python ast.........................................................Passed
check yaml...............................................................Passed
check docstring is first.................................................Passed
detect private key.......................................................Passed
trim trailing whitespace.................................................Passed
Add trailing commas......................................................Passed
mypy.....................................................................Passed
black....................................................................Passed
flake8...................................................................Passed
pylint...................................................................Passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py -q
41 passed

$ pytest tests/unit/security/tool_guard/guardians/test_office_com_rule.py \
         tests/unit/governance/test_policy.py -q
141 passed
```

## Additional Notes

Approval (`ASK`) rather than a hard `DENY` is deliberate. Per
`policy.py`, severity alone does not hard-deny — only rule IDs listed in
`resolve_auto_denied_rules()` do (default:
`SAFETY_CHECKS_DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND`). `ASK` is the right outcome here
because legitimate COM automation that drives a *private* instance should
remain approvable, while an accidental `Quit()` on the user's open app can
no longer slip through. If a hard deny is preferred, adding
`TOOL_CMD_OFFICE_COM_AUTOMATION` to the default auto-denied set is a
one-line follow-up — happy to do it if that's the intended policy.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support CLI commands and extension points
prs.body:
## Description

Adds plugin CLI commands to the existing Click command tree and connects them to the plugin registry, dependency checks, and resource lifecycle.

### 1) Key CLI features

- Register root commands, nested commands, or complete Click groups through `ctx.register_cli(CliSpec(...))`. Native commands retain priority.
- Installed, enabled plugins expose their commands. Disable/uninstall removes them. Core commands remain available without plugins.
- Plugin commands run without starting the App. Root help uses static declarations; selecting a command checks dependencies and loads its implementation.
- Invocation cleanup completes before resources and source leases are released, including after Ctrl-C. No dedicated session thread or process is added.
- Core `models`, `channels`, and `doctor` commands discover plugin contributions. Unavailable implementations retain their saved configuration without becoming executable.

### 2) Supporting plugin-core changes — review requested

The design separates application declarations, capability registration, driver execution, and resource ownership, following OS concepts.

#### 2.1 Shared registration, independent receiver execution

Previously, `entry.descriptor` and `entry.backend` were mutually exclusive. They can now coexist under one plugin instance and rollback ledger.

Simplified flow:

    App loading:
        register static channel metadata
        register lightweight public contributions

    Plugin CLI:
        load the public entry and selected command

    Enabled workspace receiver:
        start the existing channel worker

This lets a channel plugin also provide CLI or client Tools without requiring its receiver to run. Global plugin disablement still blocks execution. Public registration failure rolls back the combined registration; per-capability failure isolation is not implemented.

#### 2.2 Capability dependencies and invocation side effects

Package-wide dependencies remain supported. Named `optional_dependencies` and per-contribution `requires` distinguish lightweight operations from SDK-dependent operations:

    status.requires = []
    send.requires = ["transport"]

    install/update/repair:
        prepare packages referenced by declared capabilities

    selected command:
        check requires -> build implementation -> execute -> clean up

This prevents an unrelated SDK prerequisite from gating a lightweight command. Authors must keep the public entry lightweight and defer SDK imports themselves.

CLI execution also skips installation callbacks and backend provision commits. It reuses registration and runtime cleanup without rewriting existing Tool/Skill configuration.

#### 2.3 Update: reduce plugin CLI startup and cleanup overhead

Cleanup previously imported memory/model implementations just to inspect resource ownership. The existing memory registry now lives in a lightweight module, preserving public imports and the shared registry instance.

    Before: cleanup -> public memory API -> memory/model imports
    After:  cleanup -> lightweight ownership registry

Dependency observation now retains only file paths matching imported modules while still validating every RECORD row. Existing dependency checks, cache invalidation, and ownership protection remain in place.

For the same local Hello command, median peak RSS fell **214.77 → 193.69 MiB (-21.08 MiB)** and runtime fell **2.656 → 2.385 s (-10.2%)**.

The fixed plugin still uses **17.86 MiB / 0.591 s more** than the native reference. This includes shared-environment inspection and loader/SDK setup. Runtime environment inspection remains a current design tradeoff; reducing it further requires the environment-management work described below.

### 3) Reviewer decisions and TODOs

- [ ] Approve version choices: proposed SDK `1.1.0`, new API `since` values, and channel versioning/schema changes.
  - Channel descriptor schema v3 adds named `requires`; schema v2 remains supported.
  - Review compatibility and migration policy. The worker IPC protocol version is unchanged.
- [ ] Review test necessity and cost: 32 added runtime scenarios took approximately 70.4 seconds locally, primarily real installation and worker rollback.
- [ ] Complete installed-SDK author type validation and cross-platform CI.

Follow-up TODO comments cover installation/runtime lifecycle separation, Tool/Skill dependency declarations, live cross-plugin services, broader extension consumers, per-capability failure/reclamation scopes, and shared runtime/source ownership infrastructure.

Current boundaries: SDK modules may remain cached in the App process; synchronous checks cannot be forcibly interrupted; source locks provide cooperative replacement protection rather than sandboxing.

Additional TODO comments in `loader.py` and `python_backend.py` describe a future environment-management change:

    install dependency updates into a new directory
    new processes use the new packages
    running processes keep their existing packages
    delete the old directory after its last process exits

The package/file lookup could then be prepared during installation and reused at runtime. This belongs in a separate PR covering installation, process startup, recovery, and cleanup. It must define when an existing App restarts to activate new dependencies and preserve desktop/user-managed Python environments.

Until those guarantees exist, retain runtime observation of the mutable shared environment. Its cost depends on installed packages and loaded modules; the measured residual memory difference is not a fixed per-plugin charge.

The performance follow-up also adds two focused regression tests and adapts one existing memory test fixture. These should be included in the test-cost review.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

- [ ] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
  - Targeted suites pass; one additional failure also reproduces on main. Details below.
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)

### For Channel Changes (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Console, etc.)

- [x] I ran `./scripts/check-channels.sh` (or `./scripts/check-channels.sh --changed`) and it passes

The final `pre-commit run --all-files` passed after the performance fix. The new registry file also passed a separate file-scoped run before staging. Neither final run modified files.

Same Hello Click business implementation on macOS/Python 3.11: one warm-up, then five fresh processes per variant, with alternating execution order.

| Invocation | Median runtime | Median peak RSS | Peak threads |

prs.body:
Fixes #8521

Addressed an issue where models returning empty responses were incorrectly treated as successful completions, and ensured that a notification appears when an output limit is reached—allowing users to identify whether a response is incomplete.

Changes:
- If the final response is empty or contains only whitespace, the system now triggers an existing error flow, prompting the user to retry or switch to a different model.
