prs.title: fix(chats): resolve the process timezone per timestamp so naive Msg timestamps keep their instant across DST
prs.body:
## Description

`_process_local_tz()` resolved the process timezone with

```python
return datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo or timezone.utc
```

`.tzinfo` there is a **fixed offset frozen at the current UTC offset**. `Msg.created_at`
is a naive process-local wall clock (`datetime.now().isoformat()` in
`agentscope/message/_base.py:80`), so attaching that offset reads every past message
with *today's* offset. On a US-East host, a message recorded in January is displayed
an hour early for the whole summer — no exception, just a silently wrong timestamp.

The object is now a `tzinfo` that delegates to the platform, which applies the offset
in force at each timestamp's own date. It deliberately does **not** resolve an IANA
name: `$TZ` is usually unset and Windows reports `tzname` values such as
`China Standard Time`, so a `ZoneInfo` lookup would fail there and fall back to UTC —
strictly worse than the original behaviour.

This is the residual surface of #6855. #6871 (a +8h double offset) was fixed there;
what #6855 did not address is that the `tzinfo` it resolves carries no DST rule.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8046

**Security Considerations:** None. No credential, network or config handling is touched.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Testing

```bash
export TZ=America/New_York && pytest tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py -q
```

The new tests run the **real** `_process_local_tz()`; only the process clock is moved.
No mocks of the code under test.

- `test_process_local_tz_resolves_offset_per_date` — the two halves of the year must
  report different offsets, and both must match `ZoneInfo("America/New_York")`.
- `test_normalize_msg_timestamp_across_dst_boundary` — picks a month in the half-year
  the host is *not* currently in and asserts the exact normalized string.
- `test_process_local_tz_matches_zoneinfo_without_dst` — a DST-free host is unchanged.
- `test_system_local_zone_fromutc_round_trip` — `fromutc` places a UTC instant and
  survives the round trip.
- `test_normalize_msg_timestamp_near_representable_limit` — `9999-12-31T23:59:59` sits
  at the top of the range; conversion overflows in a zone east of UTC, so the zone falls
  back to the current fixed offset rather than raising. (Previously this value fell
  through as an unannotated passthrough.)

The five pre-existing timestamp tests are unchanged and still pass — they patch
`_process_local_tz` with `ZoneInfo("UTC")` / `ZoneInfo("Asia/Shanghai")`, both DST-free.

## Evidence

```console
$ pytest tests/unit/app/chats/test_utils.py -q
46 passed, 2 warnings in 1.38s
```

Full `tests/unit/app/chats/` before and after, same environment, to show no regression:

```console
$ pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q          # baseline, at b944e1d5
91 failed, 242 passed, 53 warnings in 2.48s

$ pytest tests/unit/app/chats/ -q          # with this change
91 failed, 247 passed, 53 warnings in 2.89s
```

The 91 failures are identical in both runs and are environmental: this sandbox has no
`pytest-asyncio`, so the `async def` tests in that directory are collected but never
executed. The +5 is the new tests above.

The defect and the fix, on a host in EDT replaying a January conversation:

```console
# before
carries DST rule : False
true instant           : 2026-01-15T09:00:00-05:00
expected transcript ts : 2026-01-15T22:00:00+08:00
actual   transcript ts : 2026-01-15T21:00:00+08:00     <- one hour early

# after
carries DST rule : True
drift : 0:00:00
```

`mypy` and `pylint` were not available locally. Please let CI be the authority on the
formatting hooks.

## Additional Notes

The pre-existing `0001-01-01T00:00:00` case still raises `OverflowError` inside
`_normalize_msg_timestamp`; it did so before this change as well (an east-of-UTC
offset underflows into year 0). It is out of scope here and left untouched, but

arithmetic can raise, if someone wants to follow up.

The wider fix raised in #7399 — making `Msg.created_at` an aware value — would remove

prs.title: fix(tests): let a full pytest run collect both test_backup modules
prs.body:
## Description

CONTRIBUTING.md lists the required local gate as:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
pytest
```

On a clean checkout of `main` the last command aborts during collection and exits 2:

```
import file mismatch:
imported module 'test_backup' has this __file__ attribute:
  .../tests/integration/test_backup.py
which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:
  .../tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py
...
ERROR tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
20810 tests collected, 1 error in 61.97s
```

`tests/unit/routers/` has no `__init__.py`, so with pytest's default `prepend` import mode the module
name of a test file is derived from its basename whenever the containing directory is not a package.
`tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py` and `tests/integration/test_backup.py` are therefore both
imported as the module `test_backup`, and the second import fails the file-mismatch check.

This PR adds the missing empty `tests/unit/routers/__init__.py`, which gives the files in that
directory the package-qualified module name `tests.unit.routers.*` and removes the collision.

`tests/integration/` has no `__init__.py` either, but all of its helper imports are already
package-qualified (`from tests.integration.helpers import ...`), so it needs no change and is left
untouched. Renaming a test file instead would break the path for anyone referencing it, and would
collide with the existing `tests/integration/test_backup_router.py`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8377

**Security Considerations:** Not applicable. The change only affects pytest module naming; no runtime
code, dependency, configuration or public API is touched.

prs.title: fix(plugins): report an unusable dependency state root at startup
prs.body:
## Description

On restricted POSIX deployments, an unusable passwd home can make QwenPaw fail during import with a bare filesystem exception. This change reports `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` during state-root selection, naming the source, reason and `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` remedy.

The startup probe must not reject a working configuration. An existing coordination root can be read-only while its prepared per-environment subdirectories remain writable: lease files and maintenance markers are written inside those subdirectories, so creating a missing directory needs write permission on its parent, but using an existing one does not. The probe now requires `W_OK` only where a directory will actually be created; an existing root is left to be validated by the real filesystem operation, whose failure keeps its original `OSError` type so `install_lock.py`'s `InstallLockError` handling still applies.

POSIX selection remains: explicit override → absolute passwd home → absolute `HOME` fallback. The deployment guide documents the override and requires every process sharing a dependency environment to resolve the same root.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8515 (diagnostics and documentation).

**Security Considerations:** The existing `HOME` fallback can still select different roots when no absolute passwd home is available. Restricted deployments should configure one shared absolute override.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Documentation

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend
- [x] Tests
- [x] Scripts / Deploy

## Changes

- Probe the proposed POSIX home-derived coordination directory before canonicalization and report unusable paths with actionable context.
- Accept an already prepared, writable coordination directory under a read-only home.
- Require `W_OK` only where a directory will actually be created; do not reject an existing read-only coordination root whose prepared per-environment subdirectories are writable.
- Add seven regressions: unusable passwd home, dangling coordination link, read-only home, prepared root under a read-only home, one root shared by processes with different `HOME` values, read-only root with prepared per-environment subdirectories, and a read-only root with no prepared subdirectories deferring to the actual operation.
- Document the override in `deploy/DEPENDENCY_MAINTENANCE.md`.

The probe is best effort; later writes can still fail because of filesystem changes, capacity limits or races. Explicit overrides and Windows are not probed. When a root is accepted but a needed subdirectory cannot be created, the failure surfaces from the filesystem operation itself rather than from selection.

## Checklist

- [ ] Full-repository `pre-commit run --all-files` passes
- [x] Relevant tests pass
- [x] Documentation updated

## Testing

Run `pytest tests/unit/plugins/test_install_lock.py -v -rs`, including a non-root run for permission-bit cases (root ignores directory permission bits). Both columns below use the same Python 3.12 virtualenv.

## Evidence

Linux, current PR head `dd71ddd8`:

| Scope | root | uid 65534 |
|---|---|---|
| `state_root` tests (`-k state_root`) | 7 passed / 4 skipped | 11 passed |
| Complete `test_install_lock.py` | 33 passed / 7 skipped | 38 passed / 2 skipped |

The two new permission-bit regressions fail against the previous head `4943c14c` (2 failed) and pass on this head; they are not tautological.

Real filesystem comparison with uid 65534 and a home owned by that uid with mode `0500`: baseline raises `PermissionError`; patched selection raises `DEPENDENCY_STATE_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` with "not writable" and the override remedy. This is the missing-directory case, where the probe still applies.

With the coordination root itself at mode `0555` and its prepared per-environment subdirectories writable, base `c26d31c0` and this head both admit lease acquisition and maintenance, while the previous head `4943c14c` rejected the root at selection with "not writable". With no prepared subdirectory, selection no longer guesses: the failure comes from the actual operation with its original `OSError` type.

Two-process comparison with different `HOME` values and a valid absolute passwd home: base and PR head select the same root, see the peer reader, and reject maintenance with `DEPENDENCY_ENVIRONMENT_BUSY`. After the reader releases, maintenance succeeds on both.

Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed when the PR was first published. The full-repository gate remains unchecked; the broader process-isolation/plugin-process run has failures reproduced on both base and patched source. These are source checks, not fnOS or wheel acceptance.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep a failing import-cache refresh from taking out the plugin system
prs.body:
## Description

Every backend plugin failed to load on hosts whose interpreter is CPython 3.11.9+ but whose `importlib.metadata` is older (Debian 12 ships 3.11.2): `importlib.invalidate_caches()` raises `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`, and the call was unguarded in `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()`, which runs once per backend plugin during startup. One raising stdlib call took out the whole plugin system instead of one plugin.

This change makes the import-cache refresh best effort: the failure is logged at debug level and the caller continues.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8473

**Security Considerations:** None. The refresh is a cache invalidation; failing to refresh it can only make an import resolve to a stale entry for the rest of the process, which is what the call was already trying to avoid.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the call can fail

Since CPython 3.11.9 the frozen `PathFinder.invalidate_caches()` ends with:

```python
from importlib.metadata import MetadataPathFinder
MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches()
```

`MetadataPathFinder` is resolved through `sys.path`. When an older distro stdlib sits ahead of the bundled one, that name resolves to a plain function without `@classmethod`, so the call raises `TypeError`.

Reproduced on CPython 3.12.15 by replacing `MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches` with a plain function, which is the shape the pre-3.11.9 stdlib has:

```
bundled MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches: classmethod
importlib.invalidate_caches() -> TypeError: plain_invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## The change

`src/qwenpaw/plugins/module_isolation.py` gains `_invalidate_import_caches()`, which calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` inside a `try`/`except` and logs the failure at debug level. Both call sites in the module — `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()` and `clear_plugin_bytecode()` — go through it.

This covers the startup path of #8473. The install path of #8265 is a different call site; #8345 and #8107 are open against it, and this change does not touch `loader.py`.

prs.title: fix(channels): carry Telegram quoted reply context into the agent
prs.body:
## Description

The Telegram adapter never reads `message.reply_to_message`, so a quoted message is dropped before it reaches the agent. A user replying "what about this?" leaves the agent with no idea what "this" referred to.

This is the odd one out rather than a missing feature: Feishu (`parent_id`), DingTalk (`repliedMsg`), WeChat (`ref_msg`) and OneBot (quoted segments) all surface the quoted parent already.

**What's broken and how it works.** Telegram delivers the quoted parent on `message.reply_to_message`. Nothing read it, so the handler built a content list containing only the user's own text. `_extract_query_from_payload` and `_extract_chat_name` both read the *first* text part, so the quoted context never existed as far as the agent was concerned. A `/stop` sent as a reply to a quoted message is therefore not recognised as a control command either — it arrives as ordinary chat text, and `is_control` is False.

**What this changes.** Read the quoted message and append it as a `[Quoted message]` text part, falling back to its caption when it carries media rather than text, and cap the quoted text so a long quote cannot flood the context window. +323 lines, no existing line modified.

**One deliberate ordering choice.** The quoted part is appended *after* the user's own text. `_extract_query_from_payload` and `_extract_chat_name` read the first text part, so a leading quoted block would hide control commands such as `/stop` and mis-name the chat. An adversarial review pass caught this: prepending it made a `/stop` sent as a reply stop being recognised, which is the same class of bug this PR fixes.

Two points I raised on the issue and did not decide unilaterally: the ordering above, and whether the attacker-controllable author prefix should be rendered at all (`[Quoted message] alice_h: hi from alice` — the name comes from the quoted message, so it is untrusted text landing in the agent's context). Happy to change either.

**Related Issue:** Refs #8329

**Security Considerations:** The quoted text and the quoted author's display name are attacker-controllable and reach the agent's context. The text is length-capped. I have not stripped the author name in this patch — that is the second question above.

## Description

Ali-compatible gateways can return `data_inspection_failed` or `inappropriate content` when a request is rejected by content inspection. prs.title: fix(xiaoyi): emit working frames so long turns stop looking dead in the client
prs.body:
## Description
Issue #8394: the XiaoYi channel writes nothing user-visible during a long turn — the only traffic is the invisible 30s protocol heartbeat, so a multi-minute turn shows a blank client and users reasonably conclude the bot hung (report: 7m36s of silence, then cancelled).

Minimal plugin-side fix (host contract untouched):

- **codec**: `build_working_msg()` — the A2A `status-update` envelope with `state=working` (same shape as the existing `build_completed_msg`, empty text parts, `final=False`).
- **platform**: `send_working(route)` — best-effort effect-wrapped send, returns False on delivery errors instead of raising, so a keepalive tick can never take down a turn.
- **driver**: after the first outbound send of a response route (`_perform_send`), spawn a per-route keepalive loop from `_platform._spawn` (reusing platform task accounting — cancelled on `stop()` via `_tasks` and explicitly via the new `_working_tasks` map). The loop sends an immediate first working frame (the "received" cue the issue asks for), then one frame every `working_frame_interval` (default 12s). It self-cancels when a later send replaces it, when `_before_cleanup_complete` starts (completed/final frames are about to land), and is hard-bounded by `WORKING_FRAME_MAX_WAIT=1800s` so an abandoned session cannot tick forever.
- **channel.json**: new `working_frame_interval` integer property registered in `config_fields` (set 0 to disable), read `config.get()`-style like `task_timeout_ms`.

The frames ride the existing `agent_response` envelope and keepalive loop never touches the shared driver's delivery journal, mirroring `send_finish_step` best-effort semantics (`continue_on_delivery_error=True`).

## Evidence
- `tests/unit/channels/test_xiaoyi.py` — 9 passed, including 2 new cases:
  - `test_working_frames_tick_between_sends_and_stop_at_cleanup`: a send triggers the keepalive (a `status-update.state=working` frame lands on the wire after the artifact), the loop is alive after `send`, and `channel.response.finish` cancels it (task done).
  - `test_working_frame_interval_zero_disables_keepalive`: config interval 0 → `_working_frame_interval()==0.0` and `_resume_working_frames` registers no task.
- The 4 pre-existing count-based assertions were updated to filter by frame kind/`state` instead of exact totals (working frames now appear between sends by design); frame sequences asserted (artifact → completed → final) are unchanged.
- Environment note: dingtalk/matrix/telegram/discord/twilio channel tests don't collect on this machine (deps `dingtalk_stream`/`nio`/`telegram`/`twilio` not installed) — those failures exist on a clean checkout and are unrelated.
- Local validation: same-turn silence eliminated (immediate working frame + periodic refresh), `py_compile` clean for all four touched plugin modules.

prs.title: fix(governance): preserve unresolved tilde paths during deep scans
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes #8688. A harmless Python heredoc containing `values = ['x', '~', 'y']` yields the path candidate `~,` after shell tokenization. `Path.expanduser()` treats the comma as a username and raises `RuntimeError`, aborting the remaining deep detectors for that invocation.

Use `os.path.expanduser()` before constructing `Path`, preserving unresolved tilde spellings as literal paths while retaining normal home expansion and canonicalization. Do not strip punctuation, skip heredocs, disable detection, or change policy/approval behavior.

This is a robustness fix; no authorization or sandbox boundary bypass is demonstrated. Reproductions are synthetic and contain no production commands or user data.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix

Six regression cases cover unresolved tilde names, regular home expansion, a harmless heredoc, a literal comma filename that is itself sensitive, and a mixed command where both sensitive-path and shell-evasion findings must survive.

prs.title: feat(memory): allow a separate model for ReMeLight memory writing
prs.body:
## Description

`ReMeLightMemoryManager` currently injects the agent's main model into ReMe's `as_llm` component before every memory-writing job (`auto_memory` / `auto_dream` / `daily_paper` / `auto_fin`), so memory writing always consumes the same (often expensive) model used for chatting.

This PR adds an optional `memory_model` slot to `reme_light_memory_config`, so memory writing can run on an independent, lighter model:

- Uses `{"provider_id": "...", "model": "..."}` as the canonical format; a string is treated as a bare model name that inherits the main model's provider, including version-tagged names such as `qwen2.5:7b`.
- When unset, behavior is unchanged (main model is used).
- If dedicated-model construction fails (including non-`ProviderError` SDK exceptions), the manager logs a warning and injects the usable main model. Runtime failures before output can also fall back to that model. Main-model failures still propagate. Image jobs exclude the main-model fallback unless it has confirmed image support.
- The injected model is refreshed before every LLM job, so config changes take effect without a restart.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7664

**Security Considerations:** `memory_model` stores only a provider/model reference; no credentials are written to `agent.json` (API keys stay in the provider store).

issues.title: [Feature]: Write-only WebUI credential management and scoped secret references
issues.body:
### Summary

Provide an operator-only credential catalog under Storage → Secrets: metadata-only listing, write-only creation/replacement, disable/delete actions, and controlled credential references for approved tasks. Draft PR #12402 covers write-only management for existing plugin TLS bindings. This issue tracks the broader catalog and scoped runtime references.

### Problem statement

Operators need to provision service credentials without pasting them into agent conversations, model prompts, session history, or skills. Existing encrypted configuration and masked secret fields provide useful building blocks, but configuring a credential is different from authorizing an agent/tool to use it.

An operator should be able to say “query the service using credential `monitoring-api`”; the model should handle a reference, while an authorized backend component supplies authentication.

### Proposed solution

**1. Administrative UI**

- List only identifier, type, configured/disabled state, permitted consumers/destinations, and appropriate lifecycle metadata.
- Create or replace a secret through a password/multiline draft field over the authenticated administrative API.
- Once saved, return only set/not-set state or a fixed mask. No reveal, copy, export, plaintext read endpoint, or value-length disclosure.
- Support explicit disable and delete, with dependency warnings and clear confirmation. Explain that deletion from ZeroClaw does not revoke a credential at its upstream service or erase existing backups.
- Keep the submitted draft transient; clear it after success, cancellation, and navigation. Do not persist it in browser storage, conversation state, analytics, or error reports.

**2. Controlled use by reference**

- Expose an identifier to the model, never a generic tool that returns the stored value.
- Resolve the reference within the existing trusted tool/connector execution boundary. Reuse applicable plugin secret-binding mechanisms rather than creating a second source of policy.
- Bind use to explicitly authorized agents/components and, where applicable, trusted destinations and operations. Possession of a reference must not grant permission.
- Preserve tool approvals, sandboxing, destination policy, and normal operation authorization. A chat instruction may request use but cannot create a credential grant.
- Re-evaluate current authorization and credential enabled/version state at use time; do not retain stale grants after disable, replacement, or permission revocation.
- Ensure authentication is not forwarded on cross-origin redirects or to model-selected arbitrary endpoints. Do not interpolate secret values into arbitrary shell text, URLs, or process command lines.

**3. Storage and API protections**

- Reuse the established SecretStore/key-source abstraction and an appropriate canonical storage owner; do not introduce custom cryptography or a parallel plaintext store.
- This feature must refuse secret writes if encrypted storage is unavailable/disabled; it must not silently inherit plaintext storage.
- List metadata without decrypting values. Credential value writes and lifecycle mutations remain operator-only, including authorization revalidation at commit time.
- Apply the established session/origin/CSRF protections, no-store responses, input bounds, and safe error handling.
- Audit actor, credential identifier, consumer, operation and outcome, never the value. Secret values must not enter prompts, memory, tool results, receipts, logs, telemetry, or traces.

### Example operator workflow

1. Open **Config → Storage → Secrets**, choose **Add credential**, and enter a reference name such as `MEU_GMAIL`. Choose the credential type and supply its value in the write-only form. For OAuth, complete the provider's consent flow with the requested scopes.
2. Bind that reference to an approved agent and connector, with explicit destinations and operations where applicable. For `MEU_GMAIL`, grant a Gmail connector read-only access to the authorized mailbox.
3. In chat, ask “Read my unread Gmail messages using `MEU_GMAIL`.” The model sends the reference and operation to the connector. The backend checks the current grant, uses OAuth to read the mailbox and returns the authorized results. Chat and tool output contain no OAuth tokens.
4. Return to Secrets to replace, disable, re-enable, or delete the credential. The list shows metadata and state. A disabled reference denies subsequent use.

| Credential type | What the operator provisions | Example request by reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TLS certificates and keys | PEM CA certificate, client certificate and private key, or a supported certificate file format such as CER/DER | “Check the inventory API using `INVENTORY_MTLS`.” The connector uses the configured TLS profile for the approved destination. |
| API token or key | A token in a write-only field | “List open findings using `SCANNER_API`.” The scanner connector authenticates to its configured origin. |
| Username and password | A credential record containing a username and write-only password | “Check the account status using `PORTAL_LOGIN`.” An approved connector performs authentication for the configured service. |
| TOTP | A write-only enrollment seed bound to an approved authentication flow | “Run the approved status check using `OPS_MFA`.” The connector generates the one-time code in the backend and supplies it only to that service's authentication flow. |
| OAuth | Consent for an approved connector and its requested scopes | “Read my unread Gmail messages using `MEU_GMAIL`.” The Gmail connector uses the mailbox's read-only grant. |
| Other connector-specific secrets | For example, an SSH private key bound to an approved SSH connector | “Check uptime on the approved host using `FLEET_SSH`.” The SSH connector authenticates within its existing host and operation policy. |

These examples describe the target behavior. Each credential type needs a compatible consumer with explicit policy. The identifier alone grants no access. Secrets, derived TOTP codes and authentication headers stay inside the trusted execution boundary.

### External secret providers

Under **Config → Storage → Secrets**, show each registered credential's source alongside its alias and configured/disabled state. Example sources are **Local encrypted storage**, **1Password**, and **OpenBao**. An operator can bind an existing external reference to an alias such as `SCANNER_API` without copying the secret into local storage. In chat, “List open findings using `SCANNER_API`” works through the same consumer and destination grants regardless of the source.

- **1Password.** Reuse ZeroClaw's existing `op://` reference integration. Show the provider and binding state, and let authenticated operators configure references such as `op://Operations/Scanner/token`. Use the existing backend integration and a least-privilege service identity.
- **OpenBao.** Propose a KV v2 backend with an operator-configured server profile and an explicit mount, path, and field, for example mount `kv`, path `integrations/scanner`, field `token`. Keep authentication server-side, verify TLS, and restrict the service identity to the required paths.
- **Additional providers.** The same backend interface could support Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Google Cloud Secret Manager, and other secret managers. Each adapter would use native provider authentication and least-privilege policies, with the same alias, binding state, and consumer authorization in ZeroClaw.
- List only references registered in ZeroClaw and their metadata. Keep external locators operator-only. Resolve values within the approved backend consumer and fail closed on denied or unavailable references. List operations must not fetch secret values.
- Start with binding and unbinding existing external secrets. Disabling or deleting a ZeroClaw binding affects local use. Rotation and deletion in the external vault remain under that provider's policies. Evaluate external write support separately.

References: [1Password secret references](https://www.1password.dev/cli/secret-references) and [OpenBao KV v2](https://openbao.org/docs/secrets/kv/kv-v2/).

### Non-goals / out of scope

- A general password manager with stored-value retrieval or export.
- A new master-key algorithm, universal vault replacement, automatic import of existing secrets, or a new MITM proxy.
- An unrestricted shell secret-injection tool.
- Claiming that encryption at rest or a write-only UI isolates secrets from a compromised daemon or unrestricted same-user shell. That requires a separately assessed execution/security boundary.
- Automatically migrating, revoking upstream credentials, or changing existing installations' behavior.

### Alternatives considered

- Continue provisioning through CLI/configuration: useful, but lacks the requested administrative workflow.
- Supply secrets through chat/skills: creates avoidable exposure and should not be the intended provisioning path.
- External secret managers: retain them as a possible backend direction rather than requiring every installation to run an additional service.

Related: #12001 (broader egress proxy and secret substitution), #8398 (plugin permissions/config/secrets model), #8556 (set/not-set secret UI), and #12142 (existing public discussion of daemon-state access). This proposal should complement their ownership and threat-model decisions, not duplicate or bypass them.

### Acceptance criteria

- Network responses and metadata listing never disclose saved values or lengths.
- Unauthorized, revoked, cross-agent and wrong-destination use is denied, including authorization changes between request admission and commit/use.
- Create/replace/disable/delete are covered through the real API and UI boundaries; duplicate identifiers, concurrent changes, missing key material and storage failure have explicit behavior.
- Regression tests verify no secret appears in model input, output, history, audit payloads or error responses.
- Existing consumers/configuration remain compatible. Stored ciphertext and metadata have one canonical owner; no new long-lived policy snapshot becomes authoritative.

### Architecture impact

Gateway administration, dashboard Storage UI, encrypted secret storage, and narrowly scoped tool/connector credential resolution. Reuse existing ownership, authentication and permission contracts. The administrative UI and runtime reference consumption can be separate PRs after the design is agreed.

Please advise which existing subsystem should own the catalog, whether reference consumption should be planned under #12001/#8398, and whether the eventual design crosses the RFC trigger for a material security-model change or a new subsystem. This issue does not assume that approval.

### Risk and rollback

Principal risks are credential disclosure, confused-deputy use, stale authorization, and a misleading isolation promise. Keep the capability opt-in and default closed, enforce grants server-side, document limits, and preserve encrypted-state backups. Disabling the new surface should leave existing credential consumers unchanged; any migration needs a separately reviewed rollback plan.

### Expected routing

Needs maintainer design assessment.

### Next decision surface

Discussion on this issue and the related security/plugin design trackers. Seek maintainer feedback on ownership and authorization for the remaining scope. Promote to an RFC if the substantive design requires it.

### Breaking change?

No intended breaking change.

### Data hygiene checks

- [x] Removed personal/sensitive data and deployment-specific details.
- [x] Used neutral, project-focused identifiers and examples.

issues.title: [Bug]: Tool-context collapse (`keep_tool_context_turns`) breaks Claude Opus 5.5 chats with a thinking-signature 400 after a few tool-using turns
issues.body:
### Affected component

runtime/daemon

### Severity

S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior

Since v0.9.0, a chat on the native `anthropic` provider with `claude-opus-5-5` fails for good once an older tool-using turn leaves the `keep_tool_context_turns` window. Every request from then on is rejected:

```text
400 invalid_request_error
messages.13.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block". That setting requires the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` value in the `anthropic-beta` header. Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.4.content.0`.
```

The dashboard shows only "The selected model provider rejected the request". Reopening the chat recovers it, because the reopened socket reseeds from the stored transcript, which has no tool rows or thinking blocks.

Cause, from the code at v0.9.0:

- #11297 made the tool loop build each provider request from a collapsed copy of the history (`crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/agent/turn/mod.rs` L2180–2189, `collapse_tool_context_older_than` in `history_trim.rs` L518). Turns older than the newest `keep_tool_context_turns + 1` are sent as their prompt and closing reply only; their tool-call and tool-result rows are left out. The default is 2 (`schema.rs` L6845).
- The Anthropic adapter replays the signed thinking blocks of the turns that are still sent whole, unchanged.
- Opus 5.5 binds each thinking block to the conversation that preceded it. A block from a retained turn was created while the older turn's tool rows were still in the request. Once those rows are collapsed away, the block no longer verifies, and the API rejects the request. Anthropic enforces this check by default for accounts created on or after 2026-08-31.
- Nothing strips or adjusts thinking blocks when the collapse changes the history, the adapter doesn't send `thinking.block_binding`, and the error is classed as non-retryable.

This is separate from #11696 / #11698 (the system prompt changing mid-session). It happens with #11698 applied and with no file edits; the API's diagnosis names missing message content, not the system prompt.

### Expected behavior

Collapsing older tool context should not end the session. The request should stay valid for models that bind thinking to the conversation.

### Steps to reproduce

```text
1. Native `anthropic` provider, `claude-opus-5-5`, on an account where Anthropic enforces the
   thinking-block conversation check. Set `keep_tool_context_turns = 1` in the agent's runtime
   profile (the default of 2 needs one more turn) and reload.
2. Open a new dashboard chat.
3. Send three messages that each make the agent use a tool, for example
   "search the web for <topic> and tell me the 3rd result".
4. The third message fails with the 400 above, and so does every later message in that chat.
   (It needs the previous turn's tool call to carry a thinking block, which Opus usually but
   not always produces; if it doesn't fail, the next tool-using message usually does.)
```

With `keep_tool_context_turns = 0` it does not fail: only the running turn is sent whole, so no retained block predates a collapse. With a large value (1000) it does not fail either, because nothing is collapsed.

### Impact

Any long enough tool-using chat on Opus 5.5 breaks on an affected account, with default settings from about the fourth tool-using turn. Anthropic's documentation says the same check applies to Claude Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1, which I have not tested. The collapse also rewrites the middle of the cached prefix each time the window moves.

Workaround: set `keep_tool_context_turns` high enough that nothing is collapsed (I use 1000), at the cost of sending all older tool output.

Possible fixes:
- When a collapse removes rows, also leave out the thinking blocks that were created before it (text and tool calls can stay).
- Skip the collapse for models that bind thinking to the conversation, or use Anthropic's server-side context editing to clear old tool results there, which does not count as a history edit.
- As a stopgap, catch this 400 and retry with the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta and `prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"`, keeping that for the rest of the session.

### Logs / stack traces

```text
One occurrence with a profile that keeps 8 prior turns (times UTC):
16:07:47.732  Tool context collapsed for this request: 1 older turn(s) sent without 6 tool row(s); the newest 9 turn(s) sent whole
16:07:48.042  HTTP 400 invalid_request_error: messages.13.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. […] Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.4.content.0`.
16:07:48.219  Non-retryable error, moving on (error_kind=client_error)

Two earlier occurrences the same day had the same diagnosis (`messages.3` / missing from `messages.0`, and `messages.31` / missing from `messages.24`); I did not capture the collapse line for those.

With keep_tool_context_turns = 0 (no failure), every request logs e.g.:
16:59:14.860  Tool context collapsed for this request: 11 older turn(s) sent without 30 tool row(s); the newest 1 turn(s) sent whole
```

### ZeroClaw version

v0.9.0 (with open PRs #11698, #11660, #11875, #11918, #12250, #12374 and #12375 merged locally; none changes the collapse or the Anthropic adapter). #11297 is in v0.9.0 and not in v0.8.7. Before it, per its description, `keep_tool_context_turns` only acted as a boolean and no request-time collapse existed, so v0.8.7 could not fail this way; I did not test that on v0.8.7 itself.

### Rust version

_No response_

### Operating system

Linux server (amd64)

### Regression?

Yes, it worked before

### Pre-flight checks

- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

issues.body:
### Current status — 2026-10-15

**The foundation and initial principal-owned storage have landed; the program is incomplete.** #10248 established canonical identity/grants; #10259, #10263 and #10265 plus #11082 delivered the core enforcement, session and private-memory slices. It is no longer necessary to wait for Stage 2 or to extract the first storage slice from #8672.

The open implementation queue remains #9646/#9746, #9647/#9745 and #5982/#11068, together with the later principal/revocation follow-ups #11126, #11127 and #11198. #11197 is closed after forwarded-environment fix #11222 merged. Draft #11737 addresses durable Chat-owner recovery after restart; integration and full acceptance remain open. #11068 is only the sender-role slice, not proof of complete principal-aware RBAC or memory isolation. Keep the close criteria below unchecked until their full boundaries are verified.

---

### Tracker kind

roadmap / implementation tracker

### Purpose

This tracker coordinates the detailed multi-user authorization program: principal-owned session and memory storage, per-sender authorization across users and agents, and the scope-hardening work that builds on those boundaries.

It depends on Stage 2 of #8289: canonical identity and the shared grant resolver defined by #7141. Authentication providers verify credentials into authenticated identities; the shared resolver produces a canonical `PrincipalId` and effective ZeroClaw grants. This tracker consumes that principal and those grants. It does not ask providers or raw IdP roles to make authorization decisions.

The principal-owned storage work may begin once the canonical identity/resolver contract lands. It does not need to wait for the later OIDC provider and gateway stages in #8289.

### Scope and non-goals

In scope:

- [ ] **Principal-owned sessions.** Every session lookup, approval, attachment, resume, mutation, and deletion agrees on one canonical owner. Unknown, conflicting, and legacy-unowned records fail closed for scoped principals.
- [ ] **Principal-owned private memory.** Principal ownership is enforced in atomic storage predicates alongside applicable agent, session, namespace, and tenant dimensions. Session checks or post-filtered reads alone are not sufficient.
- [ ] **Explicit shared memory.** Shared agent memory is visible only when the deployment enables it and the principal has the corresponding grant.
- [ ] **Per-sender authorization.** Authorization decisions use the resolved principal rather than a client-asserted sender, username, session, or agent identity.
- [ ] **Per-sender RBAC.** Multi-user deployments map authenticated identities through the shared ZeroClaw permission-profile vocabulary.
- [ ] **Scope hardening.** High-risk cross-agent and per-agent operations, including model selection and session/channel tools, enforce the same principal and ownership boundaries.
- [ ] **Migration and auditability.** Existing single-operator records have an explicit migration policy, and administrative cross-principal access remains owned and auditable.

Out of scope:

- Credential verification, provider selection, OIDC enrollment, native pairing, peer credentials, and gateway login flows. #8289 tracks those authentication stages.
- Provider-specific authorization vocabularies or direct IdP-role grants. #7141 requires the shared resolver and permission profiles.
- The runtime tool and command security-decision pipeline in #7142 and operating-system sandbox policy in #6996.
- Completing every future provider, channel identity, agent-to-agent identity, or policy-administration interface.

### Linked work

Dependencies and governing contracts:

- [x] #7141: accepted and closed governing contract; implementation acceptance remains here
- [ ] #8289: Stage 2 canonical identity/shared resolver and Stage 4 dependency tracking

Current implementation queue:

- [ ] #9646 / #9746: scope session/channel tools and Discord archive search to trusted agent ownership
- [ ] #9647 / #9745: add per-agent attribution and migration policy to the knowledge graph
- [ ] #5982: per-sender RBAC for multi-tenant agent deployments
- [x] #8672: closed prototype; canonical identity and core session/private-memory slices landed individually and through #11082

Completed groundwork:

- [x] #8044 / #8690: harden `/model --agent` scope with per-sender authorization

### Routing evidence and next decision

- Reason to stay open: this issue is the active detailed queue for principal-owned storage, per-sender authorization, and later scope-hardening work.
- Next decision: land #9646 and #9647 as independent agent-boundary prerequisites. The canonical identity/resolver and initial principal-owned session/private-memory slices are already merged. Complete the remaining issue-level ownership and revocation acceptance against that landed foundation.
- Dependency boundary: #5982 and broader principal-aware RBAC depend on canonical principal and grant resolution, but #9646 and #9647 address current agent-ownership gaps and can proceed independently.
- Visible owner and cadence: implementation ownership belongs on each child issue or PR. Refresh this body whenever a child opens, merges, is replaced, or is deferred.

### Close criteria

Close when:

- sessions and private memory enforce canonical principal ownership at their storage boundaries;
- private and shared memory have distinct, tested visibility rules;
- session, approval, attachment, resume, deletion, and cross-agent operations fail closed for foreign or unresolved ownership;
- per-sender authorization and RBAC consume the shared resolver's principal and effective grants rather than provider-specific or client-asserted identity;
- the current agent and knowledge-graph ownership gaps are closed or explicitly deferred;
- administrative cross-principal access is explicit and audited; and
- the required work has landed as independently reviewable and reversible storage and authorization changes.

Later provider implementations, channel or agent-to-agent identity, broader policy administration, and unrelated sandbox work do not block closure unless a later decision explicitly promotes them into this tracker.

### Stale-exemption requested?

Yes - this tracker is the active detailed queue for the multi-user authorization program. Revisit the exemption when the program closes, is superseded, or stops representing live implementation state.

issues.body:
### Current status — 2026-10-15

**The core OIDC stack is merged; this remains a close-out tracker.** #10248, #10255, #10259, #10263 and #10265 landed individually. #11082 merged the consolidated enrollment, gateway, private-memory and migration slices; the corresponding older slice PRs are no longer pending merges.

Recent follow-ups #11121, #11133, #11151, #11177, #11202 and #11206 also merged. The documentation close-out PR #11190 and incremental Nevis cleanup PR #11191 have merged. Enrollment #10592 has merged. Forwarded-environment fix #11222 has merged, and #11197 is closed. Remaining work includes the unresolved issue-level hardening linked below, UI/token lifecycle acceptance, and the required two-provider migration/rollback evidence. #11082's functional evidence explicitly uses a local mock IdP; it is not by itself proof of the full two-provider criterion. Keep the tracker open.

The open supplemental drafts are #11408, #11409, #11410, #11411, #11422, #11423 and #11737. The SOP workshop repair on #11410 passed [focused tests and negative controls](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38633025640) at `754cbb2a859efff35371300899e019c789703cc6`. These drafts still need current-master integration and independent review. Keep provider, lifecycle, migration and rollback acceptance open.

---

### Tracker kind

roadmap / implementation tracker

### Purpose

This tracker coordinates the staged implementation of #7141 for the `Identity & Access: Authentication, Isolation & Authorization` milestone.

The governing contract has three separate stages: an `AuthProvider` verifies one credential into an authenticated identity; one shared resolver maps that identity to a canonical `PrincipalId` and the current ZeroClaw permission profile; dispatch, gateway, session, memory, tool, and configuration boundaries enforce that principal and its effective grants. Providers do not emit a parallel authorization vocabulary, and raw IdP roles do not become grants directly.

OIDC is the headline external provider. Native pairing and local peer credentials are required compatibility paths so inbound enforcement can ship without requiring an IdP.

Current governance state: #7141 Rev 8 is accepted and the RFC issue is closed; implementation close-out continues here. #8672 is implementation evidence and a source of reusable slices, not the architecture authority or an approved single landing unit.

### Scope and non-goals

| Stage | Status | Required result | Evidence / next boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Foundation seam | Landed | Behavior-neutral `Principal`, `AuthProvider`, registry, and contract-test groundwork | #8063 and #8272 merged. The Rev 8 seam amendment (identity/grant separation, issuer+sub keying, explicit provider selection) is the first commit of #10248. |
| 2. Canonical identity and grant resolution | Core landed | Canonical principals and current ZeroClaw grants | #10248 merged; later integration is in #11082. |
| 3. Native/local compatibility and RPC enforcement | Core landed; follow-ups open | Shared native/peercred authority and authenticated dispatch | #10259 and #10263 merged; #11082 consolidated the rollout. Remaining scoped follow-ups include #11123 and #11126. |
| 4. Principal-owned sessions and private memory | Core landed; hardening open | Principal-owned storage and private-memory isolation | #10265 merged; #10268 was incorporated through #11082. #11127 and #11198 remain open. #11197 is closed after #11222 merged; #8290 owns wider isolation work. |
| 5. OIDC and gateway integration | Core landed; UI/lifecycle close-out open | Verification, user/service enrollment and principal-aware gateway routes | #10255 merged; #10270, #10274 and #10321 were incorporated through #11082. #6250 original route-layer scope is complete. Dashboard sign-in and token-expiry/re-enrollment acceptance still need close-out. |
| 6. Migration, recovery and end-to-end proof | Partial; close-out open | Truthful migration, recovery, reconnect, two-provider and rollback evidence | #11082 landed the core migration path. #11190 and #11191 merged. Draft #11218 covers load-time schema retirement. Preserve #11191’s incremental-save cleanup, live Notion routing references, and private pre-upgrade backups. Draft #11737 adds durable Chat-owner recovery; its full provider acceptance remains incomplete. Mock-IdP evidence must not be represented as the two-standards-compliant-provider close criterion. |

Non-goals for this tracker:

- Completing the local password provider in #8076, SSH-key authentication, mTLS, SCIM, or later provider extensions. They may reuse the architecture but do not block this OIDC milestone unless separately promoted.
- Completing channel or agent-to-agent principal resolution. Those surfaces require separately reviewed boundaries.
- Defining the runtime tool and command security-decision pipeline in #7142 or operating-system sandbox policy in #6996.
- Landing #8672 as one combined provider, dispatcher, gateway, storage, migration, and documentation change.

### Linked work

Governing contract:

- [x] #7141: accepted and closed governance record; implementation close-out remains tracked here

Landed foundation:

- [x] #8063: `Principal` and `AuthProvider` seam
- [x] #8272: `Principal` and `AuthOutcome` contract tests

Active implementation and delivery boundaries:

- [x] #9587 / #9744: authenticated webhook ingress delivered; #9744 merged and #9587 is closed, including the #8586 dispatch-centralization prerequisite
- [x] #8672: closed integration prototype; its core slices were delivered individually and through #11082, with attribution retained: #10248 (stage 2), #10255 (OIDC verification), #10259 + #10263 (stage 3), #10265 + #10268 (stage 4), #10270 (stage 5 enrollment), #10274 (stage 5 gateway consumption), #10275 (stage 6 close-out), #10321 (stage 5 browser PKCE + cross-surface enrollment API). The old slice PR states in this historical breakdown are superseded by the current stage table above.
- [x] #6250: original config/quickstart route-layer authentication acceptance delivered through #11082
- [ ] #8290: detailed principal-isolation and per-sender-authorization rollout

Linked extensions and adjacent security work:

- [ ] #8076: local username/password provider; accepted child extension, not a closure requirement here
- [ ] #7142: runtime-owned tool and command security-decision pipeline
- [ ] #6996: operating-system sandbox policy

This tracker remains part of the v0.9.0 security program in #7432 and shares the identity-and-access milestone with #8290.

### OIDC production-integration prerequisites — implementation landed

The encoding implementation is present: [OAuth Basic credentials are form-encoded before base64](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/blob/72209d9967b24cdd768135ae181e4f96f1278d53/crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/security/auth_provider/oidc.rs#L238-L251), with reserved-character unit coverage. Accepted inbound-auth configuration is validated before the production registry is published. Provider activation is no longer a future library-only step. Preserve the original proof requirement: link the reserved-character HTTP wire assertion and activation-boundary evidence during final close-out; the unit assertion alone should not be described as wire evidence. The rollout close criteria below still apply.

### Routing evidence and next decision

- Reason to stay open: this issue is the active sequencing and progress surface for the multi-PR #7141 rollout.
- Next decision: finish the open close-out and hardening items linked in the current stage table; reconcile dashboard sign-in, token-expiry/re-enrollment and two-provider migration/rollback evidence against the shipped code. Broader gateway route sweeps are separate from the completed original #6250 scope.
- Revisit boundary: after each stage lands, verify that the next stage still matches the ratified contract and that no combined branch has crossed more than one independently reversible security boundary.
- Visible owner and cadence: Audacity88 is the current RFC sponsor; implementation ownership belongs on each child issue or PR. Refresh this table whenever a stage opens, merges, is replaced, or is deferred.

### Close criteria

Close this tracker only when all six stages above are complete or explicitly deferred through a recorded decision, including:

- providers verify credentials into authenticated identities without assigning runtime grants directly;
- the shared resolver produces globally unambiguous principals and current permission-profile grants;
- native pairing, peer credentials, RPC dispatch, and gateway routes enforce authentication by construction without unauthenticated remote fallback;
- expiry, introspection revalidation, pairing revocation, roster changes, permission-profile changes, and reconnect continuity affect established authorization at the documented boundary;
- sessions and private memory enforce principal ownership at their storage boundaries;
- OIDC browser, browserless-user, and service-principal flows work end to end against at least two standards-compliant providers;
- existing remote WSS and Nevis users have tested migration paths, and local-only recovery cannot create a remote bypass; and
- the required implementation landed as independently reviewable and reversible security changes with truthful documentation and rollback evidence.

Password, SSH-key, mTLS, SCIM, channel identity, A2A identity, broader per-sender RBAC, and policy-administration expansion do not block closure unless a later decision explicitly promotes them into this tracker.

### Stale-exemption requested?

Yes - this tracker is the active sequencing and progress surface for the #7141 rollout. Revisit the exemption when the rollout closes, is superseded, or stops representing live implementation state.

prs.title: feat(providers): support multiple models per provider profile
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Separate schema-v4 connections, capability models, presets and fallback graphs. Complete TOML keys are opaque, including dots and case. Historical profile/section and embedding inputs are normalized only in `zeroclaw-config`; V3→V4 migration retires profile-local fallback with actionable notices. Loading and disk migration share route conversion, including older V4 input, and loading converts historical model lists and speech bindings before any consumer receives Config.
  - Centralize chat, embedding, TTS, ASR and native decision protocols in `zeroclaw-providers`, behind capability contracts in `zeroclaw-api`. Share wire implementations across vendor adapters; model-specific text reasoning/tool extraction runs before empty-response validation, independently of native structured calls.
  - Make runtime, channels, memory, delegation, SOP, Doctor, CLI, gateway and UI consume canonical models. Gemini OAuth selects connection-owned credentials through a connection or model key, preserving implicit historical OAuth clients at the input boundary. Quickstart locality and route validation/display use the same admitted canonical registry as construction; model-switch and factory guidance use canonical model/connection names. Model identity is the exact ref plus upstream ID; every route, fallback and switch rematerializes the target model's full policy while connection descriptors may be reused within construction.
  - Use one validated registry editor for exact-key changes, secret restoration/encryption and dangling-reference validation. Editors no longer migrate historical source tables. Provider CLI CRUD manages connections/models/presets/fallback; renames update config consumers and refuse environment-owned references. CLI writes hold exclusive offline ownership; live edits use the daemon's existing transaction. Config deserialization and schema migration share one provider-input normalizer, with generated transient fields from the Config declarations. Historical driver, nested-model, OAuth and memory environment names are adapted at the same input transaction; file migration and environment input share driver field mappings. Environment snapshots follow relocated fields; external op:// references use the same exact-key secret traversal as encryption and survive unchanged saves or connection renames, while edited/deleted references are pruned.
  - Keep model bindings, RPC session refresh and embedding refresh in the admitted config generation lifecycle. Canonical Quickstart/Web/Zerocode pickers and Doctor/pricing use exact keys; context-window discovery addresses `/api/config/models/{model_ref}/refresh-context-window` and rechecks the target after network I/O.
- **Scope boundary:** Provider/model configuration and its consumers; no unrelated dependency/security upgrade or tool-permission expansion.
- **Blast radius:** Config migration/loading, provider construction/protocols, model routing/rebuild, agent turns, gateway sessions, channels, voice, memory embedding, delegation, and summaries.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A connection owns one endpoint and credential. Several independently named models can reuse it, including models for different capabilities. Consumers select a complete model key; model names may contain dots without becoming a path.

```toml
[providers.connections."gateway.prod"]
kind = "openai-compatible"
uri = "https://gateway.example.com/v1"
auth = { mode = "api_key", api_key = "<API_KEY>" }

[providers.connections."gateway.prod".api.chat]
wire_api = "chat_completions"
preset = "chat.balanced"
request_timeout_secs = 120
read_timeout_secs = 300

[providers.model_presets."chat.balanced"]
capability = "chat"
options = { max_tokens = 4096, extract_text_reasoning = true, extract_text_tool_calls = true }

[providers.models."chat.fast.us"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o-mini"
options = { temperature = 0.2, extract_text_tool_calls = false }

[providers.models."chat.backup"]
capability = "chat"
provider = "gateway.prod"
model = "gpt-4o"

[providers.fallback]
"chat.fast.us" = ["chat.backup"]
```

An agent selects `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Its model options override inherited preset values. Each selected fallback or switched model applies its own extraction policy; disabling text tool extraction does not disable native structured tool calls. Existing channel delivery sanitization and permission checks still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` and `surface=web`; gateway/channel consumers use the same admitted model registry.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A synthetic test account or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint, a connection and two models as above, and an existing agent/risk profile with `model_provider = "chat.fast.us"`. Use a deterministic local fixture when checking textual extraction rather than relying on a model to repeat markup.
- **Steps to run:** Load the config, run `zeroclaw doctor`, then `zeroclaw agent -a assistant -m "hello"`. Repeat with each extraction option enabled/disabled, a native structured tool response, and a failed primary followed by the configured fallback. Switch the selected model and repeat.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Exact dotted model keys resolve, including in `llm_task`; model presets and invocation overrides apply. Route credentials override the primary only; backups use their own credentials. Fallback and switching use complete model settings. A tool-bearing request explicitly rejects a fallback chain mixing native and text protocols before dispatch; homogeneous chains and scalar calls remain supported. Registry Save all locks editing until its masked server baseline is refreshed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The canonical connection/model/preset arrangement and per-model extraction switches are unavailable; text tool parsing is controlled by a runtime-profile `strict_tool_parsing` setting and reasoning markup is stripped unconditionally.

### How I tested

- **Current follow-up (2026-11-12, `da09279218`):** Formatting, working/staged diff checks, migration-fixture TOML parsing and static call-site audits passed. Local compilation, Clippy and tests were intentionally deferred; no historical result below is claimed for this head.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Format`, `Lint`, the Rust `Check` lanes and `Test` are pending for this revision. `Test` runs workspace nextest, including config migration/editor, provider OAuth, projected model locality/routes and heartbeat request-body regressions. `Docs Style` covers the documentation edits.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Compilation, tests and lint for the new input-admission boundary and adapted fixtures are pending. Added regressions cover V3/V4 admission, disk migration idempotence, mixed canonical/historical fallback, encryption and exact-key external-reference retention. No new live-vendor, manual terminal or browser capture was performed for this follow-up; existing screenshots retain their recorded revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:** For follow-up commit `dd2116a081`, `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` completed successfully. Source checks cover moved API call sites and test-only fixture boundaries; standard TOML parsing checked the new admission fixtures. No Rust build, test or Clippy was run locally for this follow-up; those results remain pending in CI.
- Added CI regression cases for V3/older-V4 route migration equivalence and idempotency, legacy-only model lists, speech namespace normalization/promotion/rename, explicit capability rejection, selected-connection key inheritance, heartbeat preset/options/clear behavior, and Gemini OAuth connection/model references plus active-profile selection. Follow-up cases also cover projected local models in mixed configs, route validation without canonical fixture injection, implicit Gemini OAuth clients across V3 migration/editor save/reload, masked secrets, and explicit API-key priority. These cases have not been executed locally.
- Added regression coverage for exact dotted keys, complete temporary model policy/fallback inheritance, canonical/legacy environment override restoration and promotion, exact rename/delete atomicity, environment-owned consumer refusal and canonical provider CLI parsing. These tests have not been run locally for this follow-up.
- The preceding CI run identified an exact-model pricing test expectation; the fixture now expects independent entries for both configured models. An inherited dependency advisory and a Landlock tool-install timeout remain outside this PR's scope.
- **Historical evidence:** Earlier revisions passed the targeted provider/config/gateway/Zerocode and Web checks recorded in the PR history. They do not establish compilation or behavioral correctness of this consumer refactor. The existing Web screenshots below cover the earlier UI revision; this follow-up does not change Web layout.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Chrome rendered the production Web bundle against isolated synthetic API fixtures. Selecting `chat.fast.us`, clearing and selecting `main`, following an exact model key into the registry Models tab, and requiring Azure `extra.resource` before staging all passed, with zero page script errors. This is interface evidence rather than real-backend/vendor evidence.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Six existing screenshots and the browser record are in [`.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110`](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/tree/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110). The older registry-save captures in the parent evidence directory are historical.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `surface=web`, production bundle routes `/quickstart` and `/config/providers.registry?model=chat.fast.us`, Chrome `en-US`, desktop 1280×900 and mobile 390×844. The [browser record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/observations.json) records the tested Web tree and bundle digest.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Quickstart desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-desktop.png), [selected model](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-selected.png), [Azure required field](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-azure-required.png), [Quickstart mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/quickstart-mobile.png), [registry desktop](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-desktop.png), and [registry mobile](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/worktree-providers-multi-model/.pr-evidence/pr9809/canonical-ui-20261110/registry-mobile.png). All data is synthetic and credentials are masked.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** HTTP and RPC configuration navigation expose one registry editor. UI and catalog consumers keep complete opaque model keys. Cost accounting reads canonical model metadata, response-cache identity includes connections/presets, and channel/voice consumers construct canonical ASR/TTS managers without legacy enable flags. Quickstart, factory dispatch, embedding construction and semantic-search diagnostics consume normalized definitions; the production family factory no longer accepts an optional Config for historical profile lookup. Doctor enumerates canonical chat models, retains single-part cache keys, and recognizes Codex authentication on connections. Quickstart writes typed connections plus models and validates required connection fields before publishing. CLI flag prefills, authentication prompts, and subscription login use the same canonical field names; Anthropic setup tokens update the exact connection and use the existing encrypted persistence lifecycle. Existing model selection no longer derives a provider kind from name segments.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local compilation, Rust tests and Clippy were intentionally deferred to CI at the requested validation scope. No unrelated dependency/security upgrades were added. Live-vendor and manual terminal checks require their configured environments.


## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, provider capability support and authenticated registry editing.** The whole-registry editor requires Config read/create/update/delete grants and root `providers` write scope; narrower scopes cannot use replacement to bypass existing restrictions. Native decision and shared audio protocols are available on supported provider adapters; this does not grant new tool permissions or filesystem access. Model capability admission and configured connection restrictions remain enforced.
- New external network calls? **Yes, supported native protocol endpoints.** Requests use the selected configured connection, authentication, transport policy, and timeouts; native decision calls are not synthesized through chat.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Typed connection authentication and all `extra_headers` values follow the existing credential encryption policy. Both editors receive masked snapshots and restore unchanged masks under the config commit lock. Models reference connections rather than duplicating credentials.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Examples use synthetic credentials and endpoints.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Text tool instructions/extraction now follow the selected model's boolean policy. Only admitted tools can execute, and existing approval, permission, and channel delivery sanitization boundaries remain in place.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Selecting the wrong connection or protocol can send a request to an unintended configured provider or expose incompatible model output. Exact-key resolution, capability/type validation, admitted generations, explicit factory errors, encryption, and unchanged execution authorization constrain those changes.

## Compatibility (required)

- Provider CLI CRUD now addresses canonical registry sections and complete keys; legacy category/family/alias arguments are removed. `models set` edits the selected model's upstream ID. These writes require offline ownership; use the running daemon's configuration editor for live updates.
- `ModelIdentity` exposes exact `model_ref` and effective `model_id`; ASR manager construction accepts full `Config`. Context-window discovery uses the exact-model HTTP route documented above; the family/alias route is removed.
- Registry rename updates in-config model/connection/preset bindings and fallback edges, and refuses environment-owned changes. External SOP files must be updated separately. Config loading retires historical source tables before internal consumers run; registry writes edit only those admitted definitions, so deletion cannot regenerate removed models. Historical fixture adapters live in the config migration module and are gated to tests/test-helpers.

- Backward compatible? **No for removed config fields; historical provider input is normalized at the config boundary, including legacy route input in already-versioned V4 files.** Canonical exact keys take precedence when both forms are admitted.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Canonical provider tables and boolean extraction options are available; `strict_tool_parsing` is removed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: This PR is part of schema v4, not a v5 change. Run `zeroclaw config migrate` for v3 input, review retirement notices, define shared connections and capability models, and update consumers to exact model keys. Replace an old `strict_tool_parsing = true` intent with `options.extract_text_tool_calls = false` on the corresponding chat model/preset. Omit a boolean to inherit; use `true`/`false` to override. The two extraction booleans do not accept the `"null"` clear sentinel used by nullable request options.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the PR commits through a reviewed branch. Keep a pre-migration config backup when evaluating the new layout.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. Textual extraction can be adjusted per model/preset through the two boolean options.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Config admission/capability mismatch errors, unresolved exact model keys, provider construction or model-switch failures, exhausted fallback chains, and voice/embedding initialization failures. Text extraction regressions appear as unexpected markup in replies or missing textual tool calls.

prs.title: fix(channels): hand replied-to documents to the agent as files
prs.body:
## Summary

Quoting (replying to) a Telegram message that contains a document previously produced only a bare `[Document]` marker in the reply context. The agent could not read the referenced file - e.g. a user replies "summarize this" to a posted PDF and the model has nothing to summarize.

This change pre-downloads the replied-to document into the agent workspace before parsing and quotes it as `[Document: name] path` followed by the media caption:

- New `reply_file_paths` cache keyed by `{chat_id}:{message_id}`. The pre-download runs before the mention-only gate can drop the original message, so quoting works even for messages the bot never acknowledged.
- `extract_reply_context` resolves the cache for the document branch; with no cached path it keeps the previous `[Document]` marker, so nothing regresses when downloads are unavailable.
- Media `caption` on the replied-to message is now included after the file reference.

Scope is documents only; voice/audio reply context is covered separately.

## Test evidence

- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib repl` - 112 passed, 0 failed (includes a new wiremock end-to-end test: getFile + download + cache + quoted path with caption, and a no-cache marker regression test).
- Battle-tested in production on our fork (Windows service, live group): quoting a document hands the agent a readable path.

## Risk

Medium - `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs` behavior change, no boundary/security impact. Rollback: revert; cached files are best-effort workspace artifacts.

## Side effects

Replied-to documents are downloaded once per `{chat_id}:{message_id}` into `{workspace}/telegram_files/` (same directory the existing attachment pipeline uses).
