prs.title: fix(anthropic): classify incomplete terminal responses
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Treat incomplete Anthropic responses and semantic-empty terminals as typed failures, not successful blank or partial answers. Validate buffered envelopes and SSE framing, terminal reasons, content-block lifecycles, and execution-bearing tool input.
  - Preserve the first incomplete cause, observed usage, and opaque reasoning state through provider parsing and downstream consumers. Valid signed/redacted reasoning remains available for later provider reuse without becoming final display text.
  - Carry typed recovery and chargeability policy through Reliable and the runtime. The changed typed-terminal paths reject replay after immutable output, client-tool activity, provider-executed work, or cancellation; retain the documented pre-send connection, exact image-replacement, and sole-candidate exceptions.
  - Bind final failure and serving-provider identity to the same physical attempt. Reconcile terminal usage field by field, account rejected work once, and attribute successful fallback to its actual serving route. Preserve combined usage for direct unscoped structured calls, while scoped runtime calls retain accepted and rejected usage separately. Derive missing accepted-summary input estimates from the finalized sanitized request, floored at known cached input; estimates remain display-only.
  - Deliver localized terminal failures through CLI, ordinary turn/RPC, SOP, and delegation. Settle completed rejected-attempt usage when provider-backed work is cancelled, times out, or its future is dropped; controlled summary exits flush the existing usage-event projection before returning. Isolate the real peer-execution cost regression in an exact subprocess and wait for its durable terminal task before asserting accounting.
- **Scope boundary:** No OAuth/authentication, credentials, provider-default, gateway/config-schema, deployment, Matrix-adapter, telemetry-schema, or generic response-metadata changes. No paid/live provider calls. OpenAI-compatible output-limit classification remains a separate slice. The SOP accounting change is a narrow fix for usage lost at cancellation/timeout; broader SOP lifecycle architecture is deferred rather than folded into this PR. The peer-test correction does not change production cost-tracker policy.
- **Blast radius:** Provider API/parsers; Reliable/Router recovery and attribution; ordinary runtime turn, history, accounting, RPC, SOP and delegate delivery; direct CLI error output; external Rust consumers of changed public error types.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9421. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9421

### What this does, simply

A provider can finish an HTTP request without finishing the answer: it may exhaust its output/context budget, pause, refuse, return malformed tool data, or return no usable answer. Those outcomes should not be reported as success. This PR preserves their cause and usage all the way to the caller and restricts recovery of these typed outcomes so an already visible answer or tool operation is not silently repeated. Any text already streamed remains visible as partial output; the turn still ends as incomplete, not as an accepted final answer. An unchanged generic outer context-overflow recovery path can still restart after visible output when it recognizes an overflow diagnostic; that pre-existing limitation needs a separately scoped follow-up and is not claimed fixed here.

Merged #11625 records the original bounded runtime holding-crate exception. The additional production accounting changes in `src/agent/turn/mod.rs` still require the separate Core-approved scope record proposed in #11816 to land before #9447 merges. A pending proposal, green CI, or earlier approval does not grant that additional scope or establish merge readiness.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11625
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11816
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9447

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A - deterministic buffered/SSE, recovery, accounting, and production-CLI fixtures cover the contract without credentials or paid/live requests.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Hosted checks for `ed53b1521f04c4a7737fba8237f076ee9dd5a94d` are pending. The earlier green checks on `a5f45f52da4c514399956f4834803c8bf976c048` do not validate this merge.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head hosted results are pending. No live Anthropic or Matrix/ZeroCode smoke, external downstream-crate build, local Windows execution, or full-workspace local test run. The provider library suite was run serially; ignored cases were not executed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Rust 1.98.1 with isolated build output, incremental compilation and debug information disabled. The tested tree is `ed53b1521f04c4a7737fba8237f076ee9dd5a94d`, integrating official `master` at `2c0a8c26354b7fbd52fc8ff52cb1ba81c6fcaf0c`.

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib -- --test-threads=1
test result: ok. 2099 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 66.43s

bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh
# Three runtime and three channel repetitions completed successfully.
# Two captured runtime result tails:
test result: ok. 6254 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 52.78s
```

This integration preserves upstream's version-based Anthropic thinking-style selection and its native and compatible request tests alongside the terminal-response changes. The macOS compact-unwind linker warning also occurs when building the runtime test executable on clean `master` at `2c0a8c26` with the same toolchain and profile. The docs gate reports a duplicate heading already present on that base, outside changed lines.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live manual session. Local automated fixtures cover buffered/SSE terminals, opaque continuation reuse, replay restrictions, usage settlement, serving identity, summary interruption with open/full/closed event sinks, and the real peer execute-to-durable-terminal boundary. Generic outer context-overflow recovery remains outside this PR.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final-interface output for the semantic-only CLI change; no presentation-sensitive redesign is claimed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ed53b1521f04c4a7737fba8237f076ee9dd5a94d`; `surface=cli`; production `zeroclaw agent`, one-shot and piped interactive modes, `locale=en`, logging disabled; `tests/component/direct_cli_terminal_completion.rs`. No terminal-width claim is made.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The one-shot output-limit fixture observes empty stdout, exit status 1 and stderr `Error: The provider reached its output token limit before completing the response.\n`. Interactive mode retains streamed partial text and emits the localized error with one provider request. The production component suite checks all five terminal reasons and the image-recovery control.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Submit a prompt to deterministic incomplete buffered/SSE responses. One-shot fails; interactive mode reports failure and remains usable. Incomplete output is not accepted or replayed. Image recovery and the subsequent text-only turn retain request image counts `[1, 0, 0]`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Live/provider credentials and local Windows execution were outside validation. Authenticated Grok CLI and the other ignored cases remain unexecuted. There were no added HTTP(S) links to check. Full-workspace local validation was not run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Recovery uses existing configured provider calls and is more constrained by typed terminal state.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Provider-controlled signed/redacted reasoning continuation data is newly retained and reconstructed for later Anthropic requests; this does not add human-authored prompt text or a credential/permission surface.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Opaque provider continuation data crosses the later-request boundary and must not become displayed text or executable client-tool input. Structural validation, typed block reconstruction, opaque retention outside final display, and preservation/rejection fixtures constrain its reuse to provider continuation state; raw diagnostics remain separate from localized user delivery.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for Rust consumers of the changed Experimental APIs and for callers that previously accepted incomplete output as success.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes for CLI terminal-error semantics; no public flags, configuration keys, environment variables, or defaults are added or changed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Add exhaustive match arms for the new `StreamError::TerminalCompletion` and `StreamError::SemanticEmpty` variants. Include `provider_executed_tool_activity` when constructing `ModelRefusalError`: set it from actual provider-executed work, using `true` when replay could duplicate that work and `false` when none occurred. Use the new typed terminal/semantic-empty error helpers rather than diagnostic-string matching, and handle incomplete turns as failures. Accounted/scoped calls keep rejected usage separate from accepted context; direct unscoped structured Reliable calls retain legacy combined totals, including billable typed failures and cache-write counters. `ThinkingDelta`, `ReasoningFinalized`, and `ModelRefusal` already exist in the base and are not additions made by this PR. Provider implementations should return typed terminal/semantic-empty errors with known usage rather than emit `Final` for incomplete output. Direct string consumers must account for stripped trailing `<eom>`/`<|eom|>` markers and hidden `<think>` content; marker/think-only output is now a semantic-empty failure. Use the canonical normalizer in `zeroclaw-api` (re-exported by `zeroclaw-tool-call-parser`) instead of maintaining a separate vocabulary. Existing users need no config migration; CLI callers must honor error status/output rather than treating HTTP completion as answer success.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, revert the merge/squash commit that GitHub records for #9447: `git revert <squash-sha>` or `git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>`, as appropriate to the actual merge method. Before merge, abandon the unmerged proposal or revert its owned functional commits on the feature branch while preserving upstream integration; do not revert one historical repair as if it represented the complete change.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Unexpected localized incomplete-terminal errors, lost/duplicated rejected usage, wrong serving-provider attribution, or repeated work after visible/tool output. A summary context estimate smaller than its cached subset or describing stale history indicates an estimate-projection regression; estimates must remain labelled and non-billable. Typed diagnostics distinguish output/context limits, paused turns, refusals, invalid terminal state, and semantic-empty output without relying on payload logging.

## Summary

This lets you pick Parallel for ZeroClaw’s built-in web search. It uses [Parallel’s Unified MCP server](https://docs.parallel.ai/integrations/mcp/quickstart) and works without an account or API key.

```toml
[web_search]
search_provider = "parallel"
```

I work at Parallel. I’d like to see it become the default because agents get links and excerpts they can cite on their first search, with no setup. This PR keeps DuckDuckGo as the default so people can try it first.

## Testing

The tools crate passed locally (1,793 tests). That includes searching through a proxy and surfacing a rate limit when Parallel returns HTTP 429.

## Security & privacy

Selecting Parallel sends the query to Parallel. Anonymous searches are rate limited. The provider honors ZeroClaw’s search proxy settings.

## Compatibility and rollback

Existing configs keep working. To switch back, set `search_provider = "duckduckgo"`.

prs.body:
## Summary

Goal V1 proposal 2/12: configuration and command grammar only; this slice does
not execute Goals.

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Define the Goal command grammar, including multiline resume responses and
    immediate-pause syntax, without advertising an unwired command.
  - Add default-disabled Goal configuration and verifier-alias validation.
    Preserve absent budget defaults separately from explicit zero through
    full, incremental and gateway saves.
  - Reject invalid edits to Goal inputs with field-specific errors while
    allowing unrelated edits with a pre-existing warning.
  - Fix the shared dashboard numeric parser so clearing an optional number
    sends `null` through both Save and Save all; an explicit zero remains zero.
- **Scope boundary:** This builds on the durable task/control-plane foundation
  in #11878. It activates no Goal executor, provider call, transport admission,
  scheduler or Goal usage-ledger integration. The general first-error policy
  for unrelated non-Goal settings is not repaired here.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task, config and command APIs; schema
  introspection, alias references, configuration persistence and gateway
  validation; and the shared Web configuration form.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10341 and #8303; Depends on #11878. The broader
  editor repair is in #11881. The separate runtime-policy proposal is #12407.
  This slice closes neither the tracker nor the RFC.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12407

### What this does, simply

This describes and validates Goal commands and settings, but does not run them.
Omitted budget defaults stay unconfigured; positive defaults provide a finite
limit, and both explicitly zero defaults select unlimited. Later admission must
still check opt-in, verifier validity, authorization and the effective budget.

In the dashboard, clearing an optional numeric field now unsets it rather than
silently saving zero. Invalid edits to Goal inputs are rejected rather than
being saved as an unrelated warning.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for the dashboard save paths.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, ordinary dashboard over a paired
  gateway. No messaging channel or Goal execution is required.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use a disposable config and loopback-only gateway
  with pairing enabled. No paid provider, installed daemon, operator config
  or live room is needed. Do not invoke Reload daemon or a Goal command.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config → Goal. Set Default Token Limit to `500` and
  use section Save; clear it and Save again. Inspect the request and disposable
  TOML, then open a fresh document. Save explicit `0`. Set the cost to `2.5`,
  clear it, navigate away and back, and use Save all. Finally save token `750`
  through Save all.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Clearing sends JSON `null` and removes
  the corresponding key. The fresh document shows an empty optional field.
  Explicit zero and the untouched sibling survive, and later edits remain
  possible.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Frozen base `535f0844` has no Goal
  section. With a disposable config, clearing an existing optional numeric
  field exercises the same shared parser, which sends zero rather than `null`.
  The earlier pre-repair proposal head `6e74d5a8` reproduced the bad zero write
  for the optional Goal schema. These are distinct comparisons.

### How I tested

Tested revision: `e3ac16d8d712d621535f96ab35ee7cf4b3343725`, based on frozen
upstream `535f0844d7e54f636b2fd1e7dea8b1110cbb4c68`.

  later execution. It constructs no model prompt or authority in this slice.

    `/goal` entry in this prefix. The existing enum variants remain available.
  - The cumulative diff inherits #11878's task and storage changes:
    `TaskRecord` literals need `session_id` and `execution_epoch`; Goal
    registry consumers must adapt to guarded APIs; non-Goal `list_running` and
    `list_by_agent` callers must handle propagated SQLite iteration errors.
    Back up task storage; reverting a binary does not downgrade schema 13.

    zero. Type `0` to retain zero. For optional fields with non-None defaults,
    the existing reset path may publish `None` before reload and restore the
    schema default after reload; that behavior is not changed by this PR.

The predecessor is unmerged. Applicable human/CODEOWNERS reviews, a separately
recorded Core-approved runtime exception
or authoritative ownership change (proposed in #12407), and an accepted
accounting-bridge receiving use case remain open before merge. The two normalized budget value

distinction between finite selection and explicitly unlimited defaults.
Later Goal producers must mint fresh IDs and never reuse them after disposal;
the dormant registry does not retain permanent tombstones.
Full-stack and rollout validation remain later obligations. Nothing has been
merged, deployed or tested in live rooms.

prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch `master`. This is a stacked draft. Depends on #12402.
- Related #12373. Adds separate Secrets tabs for HTTP Basic credentials and API tokens alongside plugin TLS.
- Authenticated operators can create, replace, and delete encrypted credentials. The catalog returns alias, type, and origin.
- The HTTP request tool accepts an alias for Bearer, X-API-Key, or HTTP Basic authentication. The alias is scoped to one HTTPS origin and the existing HTTP policy still applies. Browser form sign-in and TOTP are outside this change.

### What this does, simply

An operator can register an API token as INVENTORY_API and ask the agent to use that alias with the inventory endpoint. The HTTP tool adds the token during the request.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested after the draft is ready. Surface is web.
- With secret encryption initialized, open Settings → Secrets and register a disposable credential against an allowed HTTPS test endpoint. Use its alias in an HTTP request. Try another origin and then delete the credential and retry.
- This branch should show metadata in the editor, authenticate only at the configured origin, and refuse use after deletion. The corresponding tabs and scoped argument are absent on master.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked --release -p zeroclaw-gateway -j2` completed successfully.
- `npm ci` and `npm run build` completed successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a targeted test for refusing HTTP, another host, and another port. Execution of the focused Rust test and authenticated browser evidence are pending. This draft is for early review of the credential boundary.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. The HTTP tool can use an operator-created reference within the existing tool and network policies.
- New external network calls? No. The existing HTTP tool sends the operator-scoped request.
- Secrets handling changed? Yes. Values are encrypted at rest, omitted from the catalog, and sent only to the registered HTTPS origin. Redirects remain disabled.
- PII in fixtures or documentation? No.
- New untrusted model-visible content? No. HTTP responses continue to be untrusted. Common reflected credential strings are redacted.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible with existing config and requests. The optional credential map defaults to empty.
- Config surface changed. Existing installations require no migration. The editor requires an initialized encryption key.
- Toolchain floor unchanged.

## Rollback

Delete the new aliases to disable their use. Before reverting to a binary without the new config field, remove its entries and retain an encrypted backup as needed. Existing HTTP auth references continue to use their established config.

prs.title: fix(web): return focus to the chat message box when a turn ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `handleSend` focuses the message box, but the textarea is `disabled={!connected || typing || !hydrated}` for the whole turn. Disabling it drops that focus, and nothing focused it again when `typing` went back to false. `AgentChatInner` now arms a refocus when a turn starts. When the turn ends and the box is enabled again, it focuses the box.
  - It only does that when nothing else has focus (`document.activeElement` is the body, missing, or the box itself, which covers Firefox leaving focus on the disabled control) and when the pane is rendered (`getClientRects().length > 0`). That way a turn ending in a hidden chat tab, or after the user moved to another tab, the model picker or a dialog, doesn't steal focus. If the turn ends while the box is still disabled (disconnected or not hydrated), the refocus stays armed until the box is enabled.
  - Pressing Stop leaves focus on the composer's own Stop button, which turns into Send when the turn ends. `chatInputFocusOwner` treats that button as part of the composer, so a stopped turn also gives focus back to the box (found in the browser run below, fixed in 03b7786).
  - The decision is a small pure function in `web/src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.ts`, with node tests. A component-level regression test in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` runs a real `AgentChatInner` turn: send, `done` from the socket, then check the composer's focus calls.
- **Scope boundary:** The input lock during a turn from #6220 stays in place. No other focus behavior changes (the image upload and slash-command focus calls are untouched), and there's no new UI.
- **Blast radius:** The web dashboard agent chat only. The worst case is focus moving to the message box at the end of a turn when nothing else had focus.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11658

### What this does, simply

In the dashboard chat, the message box used to lose the cursor while the agent replied and didn't get it back, so every follow-up needed a click. Now the cursor goes back into the box when the reply finishes, unless you clicked somewhere else in the meantime or the chat is in a background tab.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. I ran the cases below in headless Chromium; a check in another browser (Firefox/Safari) would still be useful.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A running gateway with a working provider; open an agent chat in the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Type a message and press Enter. Wait for the reply to finish, then start typing without clicking. Also try clicking the model picker (or another chat tab) during a reply.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The text goes into the message box. If you moved focus during the reply, it stays where you put it.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Nothing is typed until you click the message box.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The web dashboard checks (`tsc -b` and the `test:contexts` suite) run the new logic tests and the `AgentChatInner` regression test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None of the CI suites runs a real browser, so CI checks focus against a mocked textarea node (react-test-renderer `createNodeMock`). The browser run below covers real DOM focus.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Node 24.21.0, in `web/`):
  - `JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` → `ℹ pass 20` / `ℹ fail 0`. With `AgentChat.tsx` reverted to `master`, the new test fails:
    ```
    ✖ the composer takes focus back when a turn ends, unless hidden or focus moved
      AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: focus returns to the composer
        actual: 0,
        expected: 1,
    ```
  - `node --experimental-strip-types --test src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.test.ts` → `ℹ tests 8` / `ℹ pass 8` / `ℹ fail 0` (with `chatInputRefocus.logic.ts` from ae47552 the new Stop test fails: `actual: 'other'`, `expected: 'nothing'`)
  - `npm test` → all suites `fail 0`
  - `npm run test:contexts` (run by web CI; the new logic test lives here since ae47552) → all suites `fail 0`, including the node suite `ℹ tests 40` / `ℹ pass 40` (at 03b7786)
  - `cargo web check` (generates the API files, then `npx tsc -b`) → passed
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A Playwright 1.64.0 run in headless Chromium (Playwright's chromium-1248 build) on Debian 13, 1280×800, English locale, against the dashboard from this branch at 03b7786 (`npm run dev` in `web/`, proxying to a local `zeroclaw` gateway built from the same tree, one agent `local` on a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that answers after ~3 s). Script, full log and screenshots: [proof/11661-chat-focus](https://github.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/tree/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092).
- **Visual interface evidence:** [normal completion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-A-normal-completion.png), [focus moved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-B-focus-moved.png), [Stop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-C-stop.png), [hidden pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-D-hidden-pane.png), [offline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-offline.png), [reconnected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-reconnected.png).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 03b7786, web dashboard agent chat (Vite dev server, not the gateway-embedded production bundle), screenshots and log linked above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see the screenshots above and the results in the next item.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**
  - Normal completion: after the reply, `document.activeElement` is the visible textarea; typing with no click puts `typed without clicking` in it.
  - Focus moved to the conversation picker during the turn: after the turn, focus stays on the picker button.
  - Stop: right after clicking Stop focus is on the Stop button; after the turn ends it is on the textarea and `after stop` types into it. (At ae47552 it stayed on the button; fixed in 03b7786.)
  - Hidden pane: during the turn I opened a second chat tab; when the hidden tab's turn ended, its composer did not take focus (`hiddenComposerFocused: false`, active element is the body).
  - Disconnected: browser context set offline mid-turn; the composer stayed disabled (`Running…`) and unfocused while offline, including after the mock turn would have finished. After going back online and the composer being re-enabled, focus was on the textarea and `after reconnect` typed into it.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No Rust code changed, so I didn't run `cargo test` / `cargo clippy`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(channels): include media captions and voice paths in telegram reply context
prs.body:
## Problem

When a user replies to a media message, `extract_reply_context` reduces the quoted reply to a bare `[Photo]`/`[Document]`/`[Video]` placeholder, dropping the media caption that often carries the actual content of the replied-to message. Replies to voice/audio are thinner still: without a cached built-in transcription the context is a content-free `[Voice message]`, even when the audio was already downloaded — and when the original voice message was dropped by the `mention_only` gate, its transcription is never cached at all, so every later reply to it quotes nothing.

## Change

- Include the trimmed, non-empty `caption` of photo/document/video/voice replies in the quoted reply context.
- For voice/audio replies, quote the transcript from `voice_transcriptions` when available; otherwise fall back to the local file path from a new `voice_file_paths` cache formatted as `[Document: <file_name>] <path>` (consumable by the `transcriber__transcribe_audio` tool); only then `[Voice message]`.
- New `prepopulate_voice_reply_context` runs before update parsing: for a reply targeting a voice/audio message it pre-downloads the file (into `<workspace>/telegram_files`) and, when built-in transcription is configured, transcribes and caches it — so reply context stays complete even when the original message was dropped by the mention-only gate. Allowlist is still enforced; caches keep the existing 100-entry clear-on-full bound.

## Tests

- `extract_reply_context_photo_includes_caption` — captioned photo reply quotes `[Photo] <caption>`.
- `extract_reply_context_voice_with_cached_file_path` — voice reply with cached path quotes `[Document: voice_<chat>_<msg>.ogg] <path>`.
- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib extract_reply_context` — 9 passed, 0 failed; `cargo check -p zeroclaw-channels` clean.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose scoped Goal integration exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Propose one bounded runtime exception for the Goal task-lifecycle/storage
    and provider-accounting integration in the first four Goal Mode slices.
    This is the separate exception record Core requested when approving the
    ownership direction; that decision did not approve the exception or
    implementation.
  - Name the destination owners, the accounting factory's receiving contract,
    the proposed callers, and the extraction or scope-change review condition.
    The factory must not merge unused ahead of an accepted receiving use case.
    Neither proposed caller has yet been established as accepted for this
    condition.
- **Scope boundary:** This changes only the runtime exception table. It does
  not approve or implement the Goal stack, authorize the receiving callers'
  own runtime changes, or permit a new Goal scheduler, policy subsystem,
  storage owner, or usage ledger.
- **Blast radius:** If separately approved, the record affects the placement
  review of the covered runtime changes in #11878–#11881. Their implementation
  reviews and the receiving-use-case condition remain separate.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related [#10341](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341)
  and [#8303](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303).
  Related proposals: [#11878](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878),
  [#11879](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11879),
  [#11880](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11880),
  [#11881](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11881),
  [#11883](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11883), and
  [#11884](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11884).

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw is moving work out of its transitional runtime crate. Goal Mode needs
limited changes to the existing task store and accounting path while that
extraction is pending. This proposal records the exact intended boundaries for
Core to review. It does not itself make those changes mergeable: the separate
policy record still needs Core review, approval, and merge, and the accounting
factory needs an accepted receiving use case.

## Testing

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. This is a policy-only Markdown change;
  the useful review is of the scope and its cited ownership decision.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** None. No remote CI
  result was available for the proposed head when this evidence was prepared.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Remote CI was not available when this
  evidence was prepared. The local link
  gate collected the added link, but skipped its optional HTTP validator
  because `lychee` is not installed.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Tested revision: `fd1a5d60a09d9a57f421d7918c94d516186c51a9`.

  ```text
  git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
  (no output)

  BASE_SHA=not-a-commit DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  BASE_SHA=2c0a8c26354b7fbd52fc8ff52cb1ba81c6fcaf0c \
    DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
  Ran 6 tests in 0.487s
  OK
  Collected 1 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).
  Added HTTP(S) links detected, but lychee is not installed; skipping optional HTTP(S) validation.
  ```

  The invalid `BASE_SHA` forces full-file Markdown lint. The quality gate also
  reported an npm warning about an unknown local `python` configuration key.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Checked the [Core ownership
  decision](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11878#issuecomment-6673833227)
  through the GitHub API and inspected the named accounting contract and
  proposed caller paths. This does not verify the Goal implementation's
  correctness or approve the receiving callers' placement. Core approval of
  this record and an accepted receiving use case remain outstanding.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No user-visible interface changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** The revision above;
  no interface output is affected.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A; no live behavior
  was changed or exercised.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Cargo, runtime tests,
  and live-room tests were not run for this policy-only change. Optional
  `lychee` validation was unavailable; the added URL was checked separately
  through the GitHub API.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- **New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope?** Yes, if the
  record is approved and merged: it would permit the named bounded runtime
  integration. Core review, the explicit scope, and the receiver condition
  remain gates.
- **Risk and mitigation:** The exception could permit misplaced runtime work
  if interpreted too broadly. The named paths and responsibilities bound its
  scope, and widening them requires renewed review.
- **New external network calls?** No.
- **Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed?** No.
- **PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?**
  Yes. The row cites a public GitHub handle solely to trace the existing
  ownership-direction decision.
- **Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed?** No.

## Compatibility

- **Backward compatible?** Yes. This proposal changes no runtime interface.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** If merged, revert the resulting squash commit

prs.title: feat(web): manage write-only plugin TLS credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch is `master`.
- Add a write-only operator panel under Config → Storage → Secrets for credentials already referenced by a plugin TLS profile.
- Reuse the canonical encrypted plugin configuration and existing host-mediated TLS authorization. The catalog returns instance, property, destinations and configured state.
- This is the first implementation slice of Related #12373. The broader catalog, reversible disable, and references usable by other consumers are open design work. This PR leaves the issue open.

### What this does, simply

An authenticated operator can provision a PEM value for a configured plugin TLS profile without putting the value in a chat. Rotation and deletion use the existing configuration commit path. New connections continue to use the existing instance and destination checks.

## Testing

### How you can test

- Reviewer testing requested. Surface is web.
- Pair the dashboard, enable encryption with an initialized key, and configure a plugin TLS profile referencing a schema-declared secret.
- Open Storage → Secrets → Plugin TLS credentials. Set, replace, refresh and delete a synthetic PEM value. Inspect the responses and verify they contain only metadata or configured state.
- On master, the dedicated panel is absent.

### How I tested

- `cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --tests -j2` completed successfully.
- Web TypeScript type checking passed. The four existing read-only configuration UI regression tests passed.
- Rust formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Added a real config-router test for scoped-principal rejection, missing key, encrypted persistence, duplicate creation, replacement and deletion. The gateway test exposed a deletion failure. The follow-up persists only the selected credential and tests that neighboring ciphertext and the TLS profile survive. The current-head gateway test is pending CI. A Chrome walkthrough of the real WebUI with a synthetic API passed create, replace, refresh, delete, and draft clearing on cancel. This browser test did not use a live gateway.

## Security & Privacy Impact

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new route requires a current authenticated administrator. It accepts only existing TLS binding slots.
- New external network calls? No.
- Credential handling changed? Yes. Bounded request bodies carry write-only values. The route requires encryption and an existing key, returns metadata with no-store, and emits mutation metadata without the submitted value.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in the diff or fixtures? No.
- Model-visible inputs or prompt injection surface changed? No.

## Compatibility

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config, env or CLI surface changed? No. The API and dashboard gain a panel for existing bindings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback

Revert this change to remove the panel and route. Values already saved remain standard plugin configuration. Restore a known-good encrypted configuration backup to undo a credential rotation or deletion, and retain the corresponding encryption key. Watch for unexpected 403, 409 or 412 responses on the new route and for connection failures after credential edits.

prs.title: feat(security): canonical sandbox_policy schema with application-layer enforcement
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds `SandboxPolicyConfig` as the canonical filesystem-policy model (refs #6996): an additive, serde-defaulted field on `RiskProfileConfig`, with `SandboxPolicy::from_effective()` as the single resolver both the OS-sandbox construction and the application-layer path guard derive from. Legacy `workspace_only`/`forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` are compatibility inputs mapped into it. `EffectiveSandboxInputs` owns canonical-vs-legacy precedence with presence-preserving fields, so an explicit value (including an empty list, or one shaped like a schema default) is never confused with an omitted field. A `deny_read_is_canonical` flag records whether the deny list came from the canonical field or the legacy fallback; provenance, not spelling, decides whether a `/tmp`-shaped entry is a built-in default root or an operator denial.
  - **Application-layer enforcement is live in this PR, not deferred.** `SecurityPolicy::from_profiles()` consumes the same resolver, so `deny_read`/`allow_read`/`allow_write`/`deny_write` are enforced by the existing path guard even on `NoopSandbox` setups with no OS backend active. This is a behavior change for every profile's file tools, not a schema-only addition; see Compatibility.
  - Enforcement applies at each boundary that claims it: `file_write`/`file_edit` check the **exact write target** (with admission before any `create_dir_all`); `file_upload`/`file_upload_bundle` check **read** admission before reading bytes; `content_search` re-checks every result file and falls back to the per-file-checked backend when a nested denial exists; `git_operations` lists the exact working-tree files each operation reads or changes (`diff`, `add`, `checkout`, `stash` push/pop including the untracked half, `worktree` add/remove) with NUL-delimited strict-UTF-8 decoding and repository-root-relative names, failing closed when the set cannot be listed exactly.
  - **Git builds on master's #10337 design; this PR adds the per-file checks.** #10337 already binds repository discovery and `.git` metadata to approved roots, runs read-classified commands with repository-configured helpers disabled (filter drivers from the effective config, `core.fsmonitor`, external diff/textconv, signature display, mailmap, transport), and keeps Git's normal behavior for write-classified commands (hooks, filters and other helpers can run) behind the runtime sandbox adapter, which rejects them under the Docker runtime. This PR keeps that design unchanged and adds the canonical checks on the working-tree files each operation touches. Git's own metadata is checked against the operator's `deny_write` but not the built-in guardrails (new `SecurityPolicy::is_resolved_managed_store_writable`); see **Deviation from RFC #6996 needing sign-off** below. Per RFC #6996's acceptance record, helper I/O is **not** constrained by the canonical policy: any confinement comes from the selected backend's own baseline, and a no-op backend confines nothing.
  - **Default write-deny guardrails, per-entry exceptions only.** A default list (shell configs, `.git/config`, `.git/hooks/`, `.gitmodules`, `.env`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/agents/`, `.vscode/`, `.idea/`, ZeroClaw control surfaces) is always enforced for writes. There is deliberately **no switch that disables the whole list**; relaxation is per-entry via `sandbox_policy.guardrail_exceptions`, which re-permits only the named file or subtree (same matching rules as guardrail entries), leaves every other default enforced, never relaxes operator `deny_write`, and emits a visible WARN when non-empty. The guardrails apply to every tool write except the two tool-managed stores in the next bullet.
  - **Deviation from RFC #6996 needing sign-off.** The RFC's "Default write guardrails" section says the default list (including the Git control surfaces `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/`, and, per the acceptance record, the install `config.toml`) is always enforced, with matching pinned so implementations cannot diverge, and relaxable only per entry through operator-listed `guardrail_exceptions` (which WARN). This PR adds two built-in, non-configurable exemptions that check only the operator's `deny_write`:
    1. **Git's own metadata during an authorized `git_operations` write.** #10337 checks every entry under the repository's Git directories for write before any write-classified command. With the guardrails applied there, every Git write (`add`, `commit`, `stash`, `worktree`) is refused, because every repository has a `.git/config`. Git can write `.git/config` itself during some operations (branch tracking, `worktree add`), so this does let `git_operations` modify a guardrailed surface; direct tool writes (`file_write`, `file_edit`, path-guarded tools) to `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` stay denied.
    2. **`backup` archive copies under its own `backups/` directory** (create and rotation). The bare `config.toml` guardrail otherwise refused backing up any tree containing one. Restoring into the workspace keeps the full guardrails.

    Operator `deny_write` still applies to both (`deny_write = ["<repo>/.git"]` refuses all agent Git writes). Alternatives considered: requiring operators to list `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` in `guardrail_exceptions` (breaks every Git write under the default profile); keeping `.git/config` and `.git/hooks/` guarded inside Git's own writes (not possible without changing #10337's whole-tree metadata check to a narrower per-path one). Reviewers: please confirm this exemption is acceptable under the accepted contract, or say which alternative you prefer.
  - **Network-shaped fields are rejected at parse time**, not accepted-and-inert: `allowed_domains`, `denied_domains`, `allow_unix_sockets`, and raw Bubblewrap argument keys fail with an unknown-field error (RFC #6996 removed them for this filesystem slice; they return only with the separately reviewed network-policy RFC and its enforcing consumer). Unknown keys anywhere in the table fail parsing, so typos cannot silently drop a restriction.
  - `ensure_no_escalation_beyond()` (SubAgent spawn admission) includes `deny_write` in the parent-subset contract and verifies the child `workspace_dir` stays inside the parent's writable envelope. `SecurityPolicy::rebase_workspace()` re-resolves every path-derived field from raw inputs.
  - **Latest round (round 7):** the branch now merges current `master` (`72d4f9d7d`, `4e344a43e`), taking #10337's `git_operations.rs` as the base; this branch's own hook-override and filter-refusal code is gone, per the reviewer's narrowing (issuecomment-5858146384). Changes on top: (1) the per-file Git checks re-added onto #10337's runner (`3baff4e67`), fixing two issues in the old version: Git's root-relative output is now joined onto the repository root rather than the caller's subdirectory, and user-supplied refs go after `--end-of-options`; (2) Git metadata writes and `backup` archive writes check the operator's `deny_write` without the built-in guardrails (every Git write, and backing up a `config.toml`, were otherwise refused); (3) legacy `allowed_roots` stay read+write under `workspace_only` (they had silently become read-only, contradicting the documented compat mapping).
- **Scope boundary:** No OS sandbox backend (Landlock, Bubblewrap, Seatbelt, Docker, Firejail) enforces the canonical deny lists. Landlock and Seatbelt receive the resolver-derived allow tiers as extra roots; canonical deny-list enforcement is RFC #6996 Phase 2, one PR per backend. Arbitrary user-supplied shell/script child-process I/O remains unconfined by these lists on any backend today; the runtime logs a WARN saying exactly that whenever denials are configured. The same is explicitly uncovered for helper programs Git runs during write-classified `git_operations` commands (repository hooks, filter and merge drivers, other configured helpers): the canonical policy does not constrain their I/O, any confinement is the selected backend's own baseline, and a no-op backend confines nothing.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config` (schema, resolver, path guard), `zeroclaw-runtime` (workspace reassignment call sites, delegate admission, enforcement-gap WARN predicate), `zeroclaw-tools` (`file_write`, `file_edit`, `git_operations`, `backup`, path-guarded wrappers), and `docs/book/src/security/sandboxing.md` / `docs/book/src/developing/tool-inventory.md`. Any crate that struct-initializes `RiskProfileConfig`/`SecurityPolicy` without `..Default::default()` gets a compile error, caught by CI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6996

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. The round-7 deltas are observable without any OS backend.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: cli` (tool execution through the agent loop); no messaging channel involved.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Git repo as the workspace, default profile, no sandbox backend required (`NoopSandbox` is the interesting case).
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Set `[risk_profiles.default.sandbox_policy] deny_read = ["/tmp"]` with the agent workspace at `/tmp`, then ask the agent to `file_read` a file inside the workspace. **Expected:** refused, naming the deny. On `master`-era heads of this branch the default-spelling carve-out admitted it.
  2. With the default profile, ask the agent for `git_operations` `operation: add` + `operation: commit` on an ordinary file. **Expected:** both succeed (the built-in `.git/config`/`.git/hooks/` guardrails do not block Git's own metadata). Then set `sandbox_policy.deny_write = ["<repo>/.git"]` and repeat. **Expected:** refused.
  3. Commit a `.env` on a second branch, switch back, then ask for `git_operations` `operation: checkout` of that branch. **Expected:** refused, naming `.env`. Also ask for `operation: diff` of a file listed in `deny_read`, from a subdirectory of the repository. **Expected:** refused without printing its content.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** All three above behave as stated; each is pinned by an automated regression in this PR.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** No application-layer policy consumes these fields at all on `master`.

### How I tested

Full local sweep run fresh against `ea2148893` (branch contains current `master` via merge `4e344a43e`, so this is the exact PR diff):

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0, no output

cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings
# exit 0, zero warnings

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config
# 1933 passed; 0 failed (all binaries)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools
# 2102 passed; 1 failed: web_search_tool::tests::test_serply_connection_refused_error_is_query_free
# (network-dependent; fails identically on master here)

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime
# 5038 passed; 1 failed: rpc::dispatch::tests::forwarded_environment_demotion_while_queued_refuses_prompt_and_resume
# (macOS-only, fails identically on clean master df941bca5: the held /var/... workspace is
#  compared with its canonical /private/var/... form; not touched by this PR)

cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features sandbox-landlock,sandbox-bubblewrap
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-config --features schema-export
cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --features schema-export
# Finished, no errors

cargo test --locked --test architecture
# 51 passed; 0 failed

bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
# No blocking markdown issues on changed lines

bash scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
# local link targets OK; HTTP(S) validation skipped (lychee not installed)

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
# passed
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Check (default features, all targets)`, `Lint`, `Test`, `Test (Landlock)`, `Parallel Runtime Test`, `Check (plugins cranelift backend)`. Fresh branch checks are requested on the push of the round-7 head; `gh pr checks 7821 --required` is the authoritative record.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** No CI job exercises an OS sandbox backend consuming the resolved policy, because no backend consumes it yet.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Round-7 items: every failing test after the master merge was rerun against a clean `master` worktree built in its own target directory to separate merge breakage from pre-existing failures; the six merge breakages (all Git writes refused, `backup create` refused on a `config.toml`, five session-workspace tests on legacy `allowed_roots`) were traced and fixed; the ported per-file checks were exercised from a repository subdirectory and with an option-like ref. Round-6 items: the canonical `/tmp` collision was reproduced against the pre-fix behavior, then denied after the provenance flag. Round-5 items were each verified with revert-to-fail probes in that round and are pinned by regressions (read specificity, NUL pathset identity, once-per-upgrade compat-narrowing marker, operator workspace-root denial with non-default spelling, write tie semantics).
- **What I did NOT verify:** any OS sandbox backend consuming the policy (nothing does yet), dashboard sub-form rendering of the nested config, and the full-workspace `--all-features` check (`alsa-sys` needs a system `alsa.pc` this machine lacks; CI covers it). Windows default-root collision regressions are compiled under `cfg(windows)` and exercised by CI's Windows leg, not locally on macOS.
- **Visual interface changed?** `N/A` — no rendered text, layout, or other visible state changes; the diff is config schema, policy resolution, path-guard enforcement, Git per-file checks, and docs.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes, and both directions are intentional.** Enforcement narrows in most directions (exact-target checks, guardrails, Git per-file checks, canonical deny provenance closing the default-spelling carve-out). The canonical resolver also *widens* one case: an explicit `sandbox_policy.allow_write` is authoritative regardless of `workspace_only`, per the RFC #6996 mapping table, so `workspace_only = true` + `allow_write = ["/granted"]` can write outside the workspace. `deny_read`/`deny_write` still win over every workspace-scoped grant, including the workspace itself, in any spelling. **Mitigation for the widening:** it requires an explicit `allow_write`; profiles that never set it are unaffected.
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes, strengthened.** `.env`, `.mcp.json`, `.git/config`, and git hooks are write-denied by default at the application layer, including through `git checkout`, `git stash push/pop` (tracked and untracked halves), and `git worktree add/remove`. Git's own metadata writes and `backup` archive copies are checked against operator `deny_write` only, so Git keeps working and backups can contain a `config.toml`; direct tool writes to those paths stay guardrailed (see the RFC deviation bullet in Summary). Risk is over-blocking a legitimate write rather than exposure; the mitigation is the per-entry `guardrail_exceptions` list, which WARNs when used.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No new untrusted text.** The relevant change is defensive: a model following injected instructions can no longer reach `.env`/`.git/config` through `file_write`, `file_edit`, or the enumerated `git_operations` paths. Shell/`python`/`node` child processes, and helper programs Git runs during write-classified commands, remain unconfined by these lists, which the docs, `security status`, and the runtime WARN state explicitly.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Partially; the breaking changes are intentional RFC #6996 behavior and are called out here.** `sandbox_policy` is `#[serde(default)]`; legacy `workspace_only`/`forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` configs resolve through the compatibility mapping with round-trip coverage. The behavior changes:
  1. **Default write guardrails are always on.** There is no all-or-nothing disable switch (the old `mandatory_deny_write_enabled` field is gone). Relaxation is per-entry via `guardrail_exceptions`; writes that previously succeeded may now be refused. Exception: Git's own metadata during `git_operations` writes and `backup` archive copies check operator `deny_write` only (see the deviation bullet in Summary).
  2. **Network-shaped keys are rejected at parse time.** Configs carrying `allowed_domains`/`denied_domains`/`allow_unix_sockets`/Bubblewrap argument keys inside `sandbox_policy` now fail to load with an unknown-field error instead of being silently carried.
  3. **Application-layer enforcement is immediate** for every profile's file and repository tools, including `NoopSandbox` setups.
  4. **Legacy `allowed_roots` under `workspace_only = false`/`Full` is a real write allowlist** (historically additive-only); effective writable set is the workspace, `/tmp`, and the listed roots.
  5. **`git_operations` refuses an operation whose working-tree files include a denied path** (for example a `checkout` that would overwrite `.env`). Hook and filter behavior is unchanged from master (#10337). Legacy `allowed_roots` under `workspace_only = true` stay readable and writable.
  6. **A canonical `deny_read` entry spelled like a default root is authoritative**; only the legacy fallback (where the default list ships) keeps coexisting with a workspace rooted at that default.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** New `[risk_profiles.<alias>.sandbox_policy]` keys (deny_read, allow_read, allow_write, deny_write, guardrail_exceptions), reachable through `config get/set` and env overrides via `#[nested]`. `forbidden_paths`/`allowed_roots` remain valid compatibility aliases indefinitely.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** No new dependencies, no edition or toolchain change. Stash enumeration relies on `git stash show --include-untracked` (Git 2.32, June 2021); older Git fails closed rather than checking a partial set.
- Upgrade steps: review any profile that populated `sandbox_policy.*` expecting inertness (it is enforced now) and any config that carried the removed network-shaped keys (it will fail to load until those keys are deleted). Otherwise none required.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`. Downstream crates that struct-initialize `RiskProfileConfig` or `SecurityPolicy` without `..Default::default()` need review on revert; CI catches missing-field errors.
- **Guardrail-only rollback (blocked legitimate write):** add the specific path to `[risk_profiles.<alias>.sandbox_policy] guardrail_exceptions = ["<path>"]`. This re-permits only that file/subtree, keeps every other default denial and all operator `deny_write` entries active, and emits a WARN. There is intentionally no switch that disables the whole default list; full rollback is the revert path.
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - `file_write`/`file_edit`/`git_operations` returning `success: false` with a resolved-path violation naming a specific denied path.
  - `git_operations` refusing a whole operation with "cannot determine which files it would..." — the fail-closed enumeration path, expected when a ref or stash entry cannot be read.
  - `git_operations` refusing with "repository metadata … is not authorized" when an operator `deny_write` covers the repository's `.git` directory — intended; remove that entry to allow agent Git writes.
  - Delegate/SubAgent spawn failures: `EscalationViolation::DenyWriteDroppedByChild { path }` or `EscalationViolation::WorkspaceEscalation { .. }`.
  - Log line `sandbox_policy denials are enforced for file tools only; shell child processes are not confined` — expected on every backend whenever denials are configured; it names the open Phase 2 gap, it is not a fault.

prs.title: fix(channels): hand replied-to photos and videos to the agent as files
prs.body:
Depends on #12404

## Summary

Extends the replied-to document handling from #12404 to photos and videos. Quoting a message that contains a photo or video previously left a bare `[Photo]`/`[Video]` marker in the reply context, so the agent could not see the content - e.g. a user quotes a screenshot of a comparison table asking "what does this say?" and the model has nothing to look at.

- The reply-attachment prepopulation now also covers photos (highest-resolution size from the `photo` array) and videos, downloaded into the same `{chat_id}:{message_id}` workspace cache.
- `extract_reply_context` quotes the cached path as `[Document: name] path` followed by the caption; without a cached path the previous `[Photo]`/`[Video]` markers are kept, so nothing regresses when downloads are unavailable.

## Test evidence

- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib repl` - 116 passed, 0 failed, including new wiremock end-to-end tests for a replied-to photo (with caption) and a replied-to video, plus no-cache marker regressions.
- Battle-tested in production on our fork (Windows service, live group): quoting a photo hands the agent a readable path.

## Risk

Medium - `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/telegram.rs` behavior change, no boundary/security impact. Rollback: revert.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): open local file paths from the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - ZeroCode only recognised HTTP(S) links. Terminal link detection splits paths at spaces and wrapped rows, so a continuation-row click can target the wrong path. Existing absolute and `~/` paths now use ZeroCode's wrapped link hit map.
  - Plain click opens a document. Right-click offers Open, Reveal in Finder or Show in folder, Copy path, and Add path to chat. The optional `:line[:col]` suffix stays highlighted but is not passed to the opener.
  - Existence checks run on background threads, with five-second cached answers and at most 32 checks in flight. Completed checks request a redraw, including when another path was skipped at the limit.
  - Open and Reveal canonicalize the target first. The launch gate checks that canonical path for script and installer extensions, executable bits, and bundle metadata, then uses the same path in the opener arguments. Recognised launching targets are revealed instead of opened, with a notice.
  - Path links are enabled only for local sessions and disabled on Windows. Known host-keyed automount roots `/net`, `/Network`, and `/automount` stay plain text without existence probes.
- **Scope boundary:** No relative-path links, Cmd-click handling, OSC 8 hyperlinks, editor line navigation, remote-path transfer, daemon or wire changes, or new configuration. Paths are not limited to the workspace: this launch gate is not a filesystem sandbox. Finder aliases and file replacement between validation and launch remain limitations.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode transcript styling, wrapped hit regions, context menus, local filesystem probes, and platform opener invocation. HTTP(S) links retain their existing behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A - no linked issue or Supersedes relationship.

### What this does, simply

File paths in a local ZeroCode chat become clickable, including paths with spaces and paths that wrap onto several rows. A click on a continuation row targets the whole path. You can also copy the path or add it to your next message. Files recognised as scripts, applications, or installers are shown in the file manager instead of opened. This is a launch precaution, not a sandbox or a guarantee that an arbitrary file association cannot run code.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real macOS Open and Reveal interaction evidence is still needed.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat and Code panes over the local daemon transport. Also check a remote WSS session for unchanged URL links and plain file paths. No messaging channel applies.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this branch and `master` separately. On macOS, use a local session and a narrow pane that wraps a long file path. Create a harmless document in a temporary directory containing a space, a non-executable `.command` fixture, and a `notes.md` symlink to that fixture. Use synthetic paths and no private data.
- **Steps to run:** On each revision, send the same document path, a `~/` path with `:12`, and a missing path. Left-click the document's continuation row. Right-click it and exercise Open, Reveal in Finder, Copy path, and Add path to chat. Click the `.command` fixture and its `notes.md` symlink. Capture the actions, default-app or Finder result, and the reveal-instead notice. In a WSS session, send a path that also exists locally and an HTTPS URL. Inspect both. Use automated tests for automount exclusion rather than probing an actual host.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Existing local paths are underlined across wrapped rows. The continuation-row click opens the whole document path. Copy and Add path to chat preserve the full path. The `.command` and symlink clicks reveal the canonical target in Finder and show `zc-chat-path-revealed-instead`. Missing paths remain plain. WSS paths remain plain while HTTPS URLs remain actionable. Windows path links are disabled.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** File paths have no ZeroCode link hit regions or path-specific menu. A plain click does not invoke the file opener. Terminal-managed Cmd-click may stop at a space or interpret a wrapped continuation row as a relative path. HTTPS links already work.

### How I tested

The published head e0ca66ae08a129f29b5081ab45796436da9cc15d has green GitHub CI. The master merge at 95808cfbe490a403675da11671c100015af39395 leaves `apps/zerocode` unchanged from that published head. The current head 40b7cca5227 adds the Greptile follow-up (path checks off the chat event loop, link restyle keeps the selection, localized path refusals) and was validated locally (results below).

The previous validation report at e0ca66ae08 records formatting and all-target ZeroCode Clippy passing, and `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p zerocode` with 1,647 passed and one failure in `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`. The author reported that failure on clean master f2b432db on the same host. Those are historical results, not a test run of the local merge.

Focused coverage already present includes `path_open::tests::symlink_launch_checks_and_opener_use_the_canonical_target`, which tests a `notes.md` symlink to non-executable `.command`, `.terminal`, `.fileloc`, `.webloc`, and `.inetloc` targets and asserts `OpenOutcome::Revealed` and canonical opener arguments. Other tests cover automount exclusion before the existence callback, background-probe scheduling, busy-slot retries, exact punctuation, Markdown backticks, installer extensions, wrapped continuation-row hit regions, and remote-session path rejection.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate and its jobs](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40996128554) passed on `95808cfbe`; CI for the current head `40b7cca52` is pending. Format, Lint, workspace Test, default-feature all-target Check, and Zerocode RPC Boundary cover formatting, compilation, regressions, and the client dependency boundary. They do not exercise real Finder interaction.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Unit tests assert launcher arguments without launching the default app or Finder. The real macOS Open and Reveal gestures, including the symlink case, were checked live instead (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11633#issuecomment-6514494165).
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `40b7cca52` (master merge `95808cfbe` + Greptile follow-up), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  ok
  cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings        ok
  cargo test -p zerocode
    zerocode (lib)   54 passed; 0 failed
    zerocode (bin)   1587 passed; 2 failed; 2 ignored
    terminal_disconnect  3 passed
  ```

  Both failures, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events`, also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine (1561 passed; same 2 failed) and are not touched by this PR.

  New regression tests in that run (all pass): `path_open::tests::open_and_reveal_report_missing_paths_from_the_blocking_pool`, `path_open::tests::path_refusals_use_the_fluent_catalogue`, `chat::tests::path_open_failures_arrive_off_the_event_loop`, `chat::tests::path_link_restyle_keeps_the_transcript_selection`.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** This recheck inspected the full local diff, every review and inline reply, the master changes affecting the integration, and all five locale catalogues. No live opener was run. The earlier interface smoke used a scratch configuration, a dead provider URI, and a 110×32 tmux pane with a demo home directory. It showed wrapped absolute and home-relative links, a missing path remaining plain, the continuation-row context menu, and Add path to chat inserting a code span. That earlier smoke did not launch Finder or a default app.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real macOS window captures of the current code: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11633#issuecomment-6514494165.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Debug build of `e0ca66ae08` (`95808cfbe4` only merges master; the current head `40b7cca52` moves the path checks off the event loop, keeps the selection on link restyle and localizes the refusal text, all covered by unit tests, without changing the Open/Reveal results shown), ZeroCode Chat pane in Terminal.app at 80×30, with TextEdit and Finder windows captured by `screencapture -l`. The two images below are earlier tmux renders from `b1c0571f9211`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:**

  ![Wrapped paths underlined across rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-00-wrapped-path.png)

  ![Path context menu opened from the continuation row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/b1c0571f9211e1d4093c8c7029a7209c9565cd35/.pr-evidence/pr-path-links-01-wrapped-path-menu.png)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** In the live run, left-click on the wrapped continuation row opened the `.txt` file in TextEdit. Clicking a `.command` path showed "This file could run code when opened, so it was revealed instead." and Finder selected the script without running it. A `notes.md` symlink to that script showed the same notice and revealed the resolved target. Right-click on the continuation row opened the path menu, and Add path to chat inserted the whole path in backticks.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Workspace-wide tests were skipped: the change is confined to `apps/zerocode`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes. Rendering path-shaped transcript text schedules background `metadata` probes without a click, and an explicit click can hand a local path to the platform opener. Any existing absolute or home-relative path can qualify, including paths outside the workspace.
- New external network calls? Yes, indirectly possible through filesystem lookup. There is no new network client, but metadata probes can contact mounted filesystems, custom automount maps, or symlinks into them. Known host-keyed roots `/net`, `/Network`, and `/automount` are excluded before probing, including lexical dot-component variants. This reduces that risk without eliminating all filesystem-triggered network I/O; the automount concern was assessed in code and was not reproduced live.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Tests use temporary synthetic fixtures and the existing captures use demo paths.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Model or quoted text can nominate local paths for probes and user-triggered opening.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Background checks are capped at 32, cached, and kept off the draw thread. Remote sessions and Windows do not enable path links. Open and Reveal revalidate and canonicalize at action time, reject relative and control-character paths, and pass separate arguments without a shell. Recognised launching extensions, executable bits, and bundle metadata cause a reveal with a notice. This is not a workspace sandbox or a complete code-execution barrier: Finder aliases are not resolved by canonicalization and remain a follow-up, file associations can have side effects, and replacement between validation and launch remains possible.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing URL links, transcript data, and daemon protocol remain compatible.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. This adds TUI link and menu behavior without new configuration, environment variables, or command-line flags.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A - no migration or new configuration is required. Windows and remote sessions retain URL-only transcript links.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

This is a high-risk launch interaction confined to ZeroCode. No wire, configuration, or persisted-data migration is involved.

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, run `git revert <actual-squash-commit-sha>` through the normal reviewed rollback process. This restores URL-only transcript links. The squash SHA does not exist yet; do not revert the master-refresh merge as a feature rollback.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. Roll back the feature commit and rebuild ZeroCode.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A continuation-row click opens the wrong file, paths remain unlinked after checks complete, a remote path links locally, clicks appear to do nothing, or a launching target opens instead of revealing. Look for the localized `zc-chat-open-path-failed` and `zc-chat-path-revealed-instead` notices. No new log metric or alert is added. Opener subprocess completion is not reported, so confirm the actual app or Finder result.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A - no Supersedes

- Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line): N/A - no Supersedes.
- Scope materially carried forward: N/A - no superseded work.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why (inspiration-only, no direct code/design carry-over): N/A - no incorporated superseded contributions.

---

**Labels** live in the GitHub label UI, not in the body. The PR path labeler owns path/scope labels from `.github/labeler.yml`, and the PR size labeler owns canonical `size:*` labels. Maintainers and reviewers with label permissions still set `risk:*` and any missing manual labels via the sidebar. Contributors without label permission can note obvious label mismatches in a comment. Canonical colon-scoped labels use no-space spelling; during migration, copy exact live label spelling from the GitHub UI.

**Do not add bot/AI attribution footers** such as `Co-authored-by: Claude ...`
or `Created with Claude Code` to the PR body or commit-message tail. Human
co-author trailers are appropriate only for incorporated contributor work under
the supersede-attribution section and privacy contract.

**Privacy contract** (`docs/book/src/contributing/privacy.md`) is a merge gate. Never commit real identities, secrets, personal emails, or PII in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs.
