prs.title: fix(delegate): keep a bounded delegate's workspace, tool ceiling and command policy bound beyond the turn (#9872)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. The head under review is `aa2b45b56`; `master@0f8fb9d37` was merged in by `ba665d125`, `master@be354a7ac` by `abf3896e4` and `master@4e82ce46e` by `a3f7fe257`, so all three are ancestors of the head. `master` has moved on since (`cdefa0d0a` is 2 commits after `4e82ce46e`); `git merge-tree` of the head against it reports no textual conflict, which does not show that the result compiles (the previous head merged cleanly and did not, see *CI*). I have not built that merge. Re-read the head before relying on this line: it names the revision the numbers below were taken on.
- **Problem:** the bounded-delegation contract says the caller bounds what a bounded target can do: its filesystem tools work in the target's own workspace, the caller's tool registry is a ceiling, and the caller's command policy stays authoritative. That bound was applied while the target's turn was assembled and then lost by anything that runs *after* that point, because such work rebuilt its tools or its policy without it. Each escape below is repaired where the bound has to survive, not at the reported symptom.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **Workspace (original scope, #9872).** A bounded delegate's filesystem tools are rebuilt against the target's own policy and workspace. Follow-ups in the same spirit: `git_operations` gets a real command boundary built from the target's sandbox (`DelegateTool::rebuild_target_git_operations_tool`), and `backup`/`data_management` keep the target's policy over `master`'s shared data directory.
  - **Tool ceiling carried into work that outlives the turn.** `SopStepReassembly` carries `caller_allowed`; `all_tools_with_runtime` forwards the ceiling to the scheduler tools and to `spawn_subagent`, which closes the replay of a stored job; `send_message_to_peer` takes a `caller_ceiling` and the entry point it relays through, `process_message_shared_with_live_config_and_admission_and_principal`, an `allowed_tools`, so a relayed peer's turn is capped by the sender's ceiling (including the SOP step that peer starts).
  - **Ceiling derivation.** The sealed ceiling is a set of names, so two stand-ins that report the name of a real capability are excluded at the one place it is sealed: `BoundedSopApproveDenied` (`sop_approve`) and `sub_delegate_tool` (`delegate`). It is sealed after the headless SOP step-scope exclusions.
  - **Deferred shell.** A shell job stores a command, not a tool list, and the scheduler runs it under the owning agent's policy. `require_shell_within_ceiling` refuses `cron_add`'s shell branch, `cron_update`, `schedule` and `cron_run` unless the caller held `shell`; `cron_run` now branches on `job_type`.
  - **Persistence windows.** `cron_update`/`schedule` resume check the ceiling as a `JobGuard` inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that commits the write (`cron/store.rs::update_job_inner`), so a concurrent write from another turn of the owning agent cannot land in between. `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run they would leave parked (`WaitApproval`, `CheckpointWait`, `Pending`), and so does the live SOP driver at a park it reaches after running a queued step (`QueuedSopAction::bounded_caller`); a cancellation that cannot be persisted is reported, never claimed. The bounded rebind of `sop_execute` records no initiating agent.
  - **Command policy across hops and deferred work (`fe804dd56`).** The maintainer's review of `5758af5b2` asked for this in the PR. The mechanism: *any command a bounded target runs, or leaves behind to run later, under a policy rebuilt one hop below the caller, was judged only by the target's command policy.* The callers' command fields (`autonomy`, `allowed_commands`, `block_high_risk_commands`, `require_approval_for_medium_risk`) now travel inside `SecurityPolicy` as `caller_command_bounds`, root first (`policy.rs:514`, anchor `pub caller_command_bounds: Vec<CallerCommandBound>`), and `validate_command_execution_for_shell` requires a command to clear the policy's own rules and each caller's (`policy.rs:3491`, anchor `for bound in &self.caller_command_bounds`). ### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw lets one agent hand a task to another. In the "bounded" mode the second agent is supposed to stay inside three limits set by the first: it works in its own workspace, it may only use tools the first agent had, and it may only run commands the first agent could run. Those limits held while the second agent's turn was running. They were lost by anything that kept going afterwards: a scheduled job it created, a procedure (SOP) run that was waiting for approval, a message relayed to a peer, a sub-agent it started, or a further hop of delegation. In those cases the work ran later with the full authority of whichever agent owned it.

This PR carries the limits along with that work. A job or run created under a limit is capped by it, a procedure run that would wait for an approval nobody in the turn can follow is cancelled instead, and a command has to satisfy the rules of every agent above it. It adds no capability; it only removes authority that leaked.

What stays the same: agents that are not under a limit behave as before, and jobs already stored are not retroactively capped. The limits listed under "Known boundary", "Second declared gap" and "Third and fourth declared gaps" are not closed here. The first has a follow-up issue (#11667); the second, third and fourth are tracked in #12394. What operators will notice: a job or run restricted by `allowed_tools` can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval, and can no longer write SOP definitions through `sop_workshop`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: every escape needs a bounded delegation to line up, plus, depending on the case, a peer relay, a concurrent second writer, an externally triggered resume or a further hop. The regressions drive exactly that through real `agent::run` / `process_message`, provider, scheduler and SOP-engine boundaries.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (one-shot `agent::run`); the other boundaries are driven in-process by the regressions: the cron scheduler executing a stored job, a peer turn via `process_message`, a second SQLite connection racing a guarded write, and the live `SopEngine` through `sop_execute`/`sop_advance`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**: this only removes capability from bounded targets and their relayed peers.
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes**
- **Risk and mitigation:** the refusal strings are model-visible. Most are static authored text; `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published, so the recipient's turn cannot be bounded` fires only on an internal wiring failure, the same fail-closed contract as `spawn_subagent`'s. The two SOP refusals interpolate values the caller supplied in the same tool call (`sop_execute`'s `name`, `sop_advance`'s `run_id`), each validated against a real SOP definition or run before being echoed, the same class as the existing `require_within_ceiling` echo of stored tool names. Their failure branch also echoes the backend `StoreError`, and the live SOP driver's error echoes an engine-generated run id and the same `StoreError`: backend-internal values, so no new injection surface, with the leak risk (a storage path or driver message in a tool result) of the class already accepted for `require_within_ceiling`. `fe804dd56` adds two strings in `caller_ceiling.rs`: the `refuse_deferred_shell` refusal (static text plus the tool's own name and the literal `shell`) and the stored-command refusal `{tool}: refused — {reason}`, where `reason` is the command policy's message and can echo the stored command text (`Command not allowed by security policy: <command>`). That command was supplied when the job was written and is echoed into a tool result, again the same class. `sop_workshop`'s refusal is static text plus the action's wire name, which comes from a fixed enum (`sop_workshop.rs:208`, anchor `bounded-ceiling-sop-workshop-action`; text in `locales/en/cli.ftl`). The 15 refusals this PR adds render from `bounded-ceiling-*` Fluent keys with their previous English wording, pinned by a test, so that change introduces no new model-visible text.
- **Declared gaps:** see the Known boundary, the Second declared gap and the Third and fourth declared gaps under *Declared gaps*: the command chain does not reach a peer relay or a cross-agent SOP step, a principal-narrowed `Agent` session's scheduler tools carry no sealed ceiling, a SOP step's ceiling is the caller's raw list, and the seal's inputs at its two call sites are not pinned by a test. They are limits of what this PR closes; the code before this branch had neither bound.

  - a bounded delegation made inside a headless SOP step seals a ceiling that excludes what the step's scope denies;
  - `backup`/`data_management` follow `master`'s shared data directory under the target's policy;
  - every command a bounded target runs, or stores to run later, must also clear the command policy of each caller above it, at every bounded hop and for a `spawn_subagent` child; a command the caller's policy refuses is refused even if the target's profile allows it;
  - a bounded registration cannot store, launch or re-arm an agent job whose `allowed_tools` keeps `shell`, and `schedule` resume reads the request's `approved` like the create routes. A job already stored with `shell` stays stored, but a bounded turn cannot launch or re-arm it;
  - a command denied by both the target's and a caller's policy reports the target's message;
  - any `agent::run` given a per-run `allowed_tools` (a stored cron agent job with its own list, for example) now builds its scheduler tools with a ceiling sealed to the tools that run actually holds (the list intersected with its assembled registry), so a job it stores or launches is capped by it and an agent job that keeps `shell` is refused (`agent/loop_.rs:1735`, anchor `crate::tools::caller_ceiling::seal_to_registry(`, and `cron/scheduler.rs:1180`, anchor `job.allowed_tools.clone()`). Read from the code.
  - `sop_workshop` keeps only `list` and `inspect` under a caller ceiling, and `sop_execute`/`sop_advance` cancel a run that would park in every registry built with one: a bounded target, a restricted `agent::run` (so a `spawn_subagent` child and a cron-fired job) and a peer relay; a SOP step turn never holds these two tools, because the step scope excludes them by name. Under a ceiling `sop_execute` also records no initiating agent. This includes a job whose `allowed_tools` an operator wrote: such a job can no longer leave a SOP waiting for approval or write SOP definitions, so a job that has to do either must not be restricted by `allowed_tools`. An RPC principal session restricted by tool names builds its registry with no ceiling and is not covered (see the Second declared gap).

  - a turn given a per-run `allowed_tools` seals its ceiling to the tools it actually holds (plus the deferred MCP tools it may activate, and, when its set does not name `tool_search`, the ones a `mode = "always"` group already activated), not to the names it was handed: a name its own policy removed no longer counts as held, for example `shell` for a peer whose profile has none;
  - a bounded delegate's rebuilt tools read the config the delegation was admitted against, so a feature switched on or off in that config is seen by the target;
  - a nested bounded hop is handed only the MCP tools its own bundles grant;
  - the 15 refusals added by this PR render from Fluent keys; in a locale without a translation they stay English.

  Jobs already stored under the old, wider ceiling are **not** retro-capped, and a SOP run already left parked before this is deployed is not retroactively cancelled.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the commits on this branch, or revert the PR merge commit. No migration or state cleanup: nothing persisted changed shape.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The bound is active whenever a ceiling is in force.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a legitimate scheduled job stops being created, re-armed or launched; a legitimate `sop_approve`/`delegate` capability stops surviving into a stored job; a legitimate peer relay stops receiving a tool the peer's own profile grants; a legitimate concurrent job update starts losing to a rival write; a SOP run started by a bounded caller is cancelled instead of resumable; a bounded target's command is refused that its own profile allows. Grep tool results for:
  - `refused — this stores or re-arms a shell job` (`cron_add`, `cron_update`, `schedule`, `cron_run`)
  - `refused — this job's stored allowed_tools reach beyond` and `refused — this job stores no allowed_tools`
  - `refused — this agent job would keep 'shell'`: a bounded registration tried to defer an agent with `shell`; the job has to list its tools without it
  - `<tool>: refused — ... Command not allowed by security policy` from `cron_update` or `schedule` resume: a caller's policy refuses the job's stored command; check the caller's `allowed_commands` before treating it as a regression
  - `refused — this tool was registered under bounded delegation but the caller's tool ceiling was never sealed`, and `send_message_to_peer: refused — a delegated caller ceiling was declared but never published`: fail-closed paths that indicate a sealing bug, not a policy decision
  - `refused — SOP` / `refused — run ... left outside this turn ... has been cancelled` (`sop_execute`, `sop_advance`): the parked-run cancellation path
  - ``sop_workshop `<action>` is not available under a caller tool ceiling``: the `sop_workshop` write refusal (`propose`, `capture_run`, `apply`, `reject`, `quarantine`); `list` and `inspect` are unaffected
  - `could NOT be cancelled ... may still be active - treat it as unresolved, not closed`: the cancellation failed to persist, the run is still parked and resumable; investigate the persistence backend
  - log line `bounded live SOP driver: cancelled a run that would have parked outside the turn`; its unpersisted counterpart `bounded live SOP driver: parked run could not be cancelled` comes with a turn error containing `reached a park that a bounded caller's tool ceiling cannot follow past this turn`
  - a cron job update or resume that fails with no obvious cause: check for a concurrent write from another turn of the same agent; it now surfaces as lock contention or a guard refusal instead of silently winning or losing
  - From `1a328ea53` the refusal strings above come from the `bounded-ceiling-*` keys in `locales/en/cli.ftl`; in a locale without a translation they stay the English text quoted here.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose the composition-seam row for bounded-delegation ceiling carriage (#9872, #10391)
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #10391 (the #9872 fix) carries a bounded delegate's tool-name ceiling into the scheduler tools, `sop_execute`, `sop_advance`, `sop_workshop`, `spawn_subagent` and `send_message_to_peer`. To do that through the native registry factory it adds a crate-private `caller_ceiling` input on `NativeRecipeInputs`, forwards it in `src/composition/config_backed.rs` (two added lines), adds one `None` in the owned SOP step assembly call in `src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`, adds 15 `bounded-ceiling-*` refusal messages in `locales/en/cli.ftl`, and adds tests.
  - Review on #10391 pointed out that the ceiling-carriage row (#11652) does not list `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, and that threading the ceiling through that factory needs its own Core-approved row before #10391 merges.
  - This adds one row, directly under the #11652 row, for that extension. The approval cell says "Pending Core Team approval on this pull request", the wording the table already uses for a row awaiting its decision.
  - The #11652 row and every other row are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** The table in `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` only. No code. The row does not add a construction, a public API, a capability kind or a tool grant, and does not change approval, admission or budget authority. It does not build a ceiling for sessions narrowed by an RPC principal's tool selector (`src/agent/agent.rs` still passes `None` there; #12232 withholds the tools that need an unrestricted principal from such sessions, see #12394), and it does not cover a recipe or factory that builds those tools itself.
- **Blast radius:** Merge eligibility of #10391's runtime changes under ADR-016.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9872, Related #10391, Related #11652, Related #12394

### What this does, simply

The runtime crate is a holding crate: new work there needs a recorded Core decision. The row from #11652 records the decision for carrying the bounded-delegation ceiling through the tools, the loop and SOP code. #10391 also needs a new input on the composition seam, a forwarding line in the config-backed registry source, new refusal messages and tests, which that row does not list. This row lists them, so Core can approve or narrow them explicitly. It also records what stays outside: recipes that only forward their inputs carry the ceiling without reading it, and a recipe or factory that builds those tools itself needs its own row.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for scope only.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** None. This changes a governance table, not a `surface` or `channel`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A checkout of this branch and of #10391's head.
- **Steps to run:** Compare the row's path list with `git diff --name-only master...<#10391 head> -- crates/zeroclaw-runtime`, and check that every runtime path in that diff is listed either in the #11652 row or in the new one.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** One added row with four cells; every existing table line unchanged; every runtime path of #10391 named by one of the two rows.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `src/composition.rs`, `src/composition/config_backed.rs`, `src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`, `locales/en/cli.ftl`, `src/sop/test_support.rs` and the new test files are not named by the #11652 row.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The docs checks on the changed file (Docs Style runs on `.md` changes).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` only selects `docs/book/src/*.md`, so on this diff it is expected to skip; I ran it with the file forced.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `git diff --numstat origin/master HEAD`: `1	0	crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`.
  - `DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh`:

    ```text
    No prose em-dashes in changed docs files.
    markdownlint-cli2 v0.20.0 (markdownlint v0.40.0)
    Linting: 1 file(s)
    Summary: 0 error(s)
    ```

  - `python3 scripts/ci/collect_changed_links.py --base <merge-base> --docs-files crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md --check-local-targets`: `Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Each path and symbol the row names, against #10391 at `02e647d3a` and against `master` at `2c0a8c263`: the field and `#[non_exhaustive]` (`src/composition.rs`), the two forwarding lines (`src/composition/config_backed.rs`), the `caller_allowed` parameter (`src/agent/turn/mod.rs`) and its one `None` (`src/composition/supplied_only_traps.rs`), the 15 locale keys, the added test files, and which SOP tools receive the ceiling (`src/tools/mod.rs`). Also which build paths pass `None` (independent delegation in `src/tools/delegate.rs`, the RPC-principal session path in `src/agent/agent.rs`). Not verified: I did not run the docs gates through CI, and I did not read the #11652 head.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** N/A for interface; the row was checked against #10391 at `02e647d3a`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No build or tests: no code changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes, if Core approves: the row permits the named additions in the holding crate. It grants no runtime authority, and it keeps the existing ceiling (no new tool grants, no change to approval, admission or budget authority).
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: The only `Yes` is conditional on approval. The risk is that approving the row is read as approving more than the code does; the row names each file and states what it does not cover.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the commit. If #10391 has merged by then, the code it covers stays; reverting withdraws the permission for further additions under this row.

### Question for Core, not changed here

The #11652 row lists "the matching call in `src/rpc/dispatch.rs`". Searching `assemble_owned_execution`, `all_tools_with_runtime` and `caller_allowed` in that file, on `master` at `2c0a8c263` and on #10391 at `02e647d3a`, finds no match, and #10391 does not change the file. I did not read the #11652 head to see whether the call existed then. This PR leaves that mention as it is.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add durable task lifecycle foundation for Goal Mode [Goal V1 proposal 1/12]
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Put the canonical task types in `zeroclaw-api` and retain the existing
    runtime import paths. Add a durable session binding and execution epoch to
    task records so later Goal execution can fence stale work.
  - Add guarded session-Goal transitions, one pending-operation slot and
    accounting-state contracts to the existing SQLite control plane. Ordinary
    task mutations cannot bypass the session-Goal guards.
  - Converge existing task databases transactionally to schema version 13,
    rechecking the version after acquiring the migration write lock. Reconcile
    dead-owner Goals before ordinary startup recovery.
  - Use WAL with `synchronous=FULL` and request `fullfsync` for the
    control-plane database. Preserve terminal Goal history on agent deletion;
    refuse the control-plane cleanup step while a bound Goal is nonterminal.
  - Cover the migration, fencing, recovery, settlement and compatibility
    behavior with file-backed and ordinary-task regression tests.
- **Scope boundary:** This is the first foundation slice of the Goal Mode V1
  proposal. It does not implement a complete Goal controller, verifier,
  commands, Matrix or ZeroCode integration, or enable a deployable Goal feature.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust task/Goal interfaces, the shared control-plane
  database and its recovery and agent-deletion paths, and ordinary
  delegate/peer/subagent task producers.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related RFC #8303 and tracker #10341; neither is closed
  by this slice.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/8303
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341

### What this does, simply

Goal work needs a durable record tied to the session and the specific execution
that owns it. This slice adds that foundation and guards its state changes; the
remaining proposal slices supply the actual Goal workflow and user surfaces.

**Placement gate:** Before this PR can merge, the runtime control-plane
placement needs a separate Core-reviewed exception record or an authoritative
ownership change. This proposal requests review of that placement; it does not
grant itself an exception. Required CI, CODEOWNERS review and the rest of the
stack remain separate requirements.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — this slice has no user-reachable Goal
  entrypoint; the file-backed control-plane tests exercise its storage and
  recovery boundaries.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The exact-head
  [Quality Gate run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/43291656408)
  passed at `859833f5a43320ca9ddd911135ea44e2dfbf61ac` against base
  `535f0844d7e54f636b2fd1e7dea8b1110cbb4c68`. Its required aggregate gate,
  Test, repeated parallel runtime/channel tests, Security, lint, and required
  Windows selection/recovery/service/build checks passed. These and the local
  API/runtime tests exercise the changed storage and lifecycle boundaries.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** User-boundary Goal execution is not
  available in this foundation slice. The config/provider test
  command below failed locally and remains failed. The FULL/`fullfsync` write
  latency and a database downgrade have not been measured or executed. Earlier
  stack-wide security and validation failures remain tracked in #10341; they
  do not establish the result of this candidate's security checks.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10341
- The terminal GitHub snapshot reports 48 successful checks and 10 skipped;
  skipped checks are not counted as passes. The skips are the path-, event-,
  version- or opt-in-gated docs, Nix, relay, package preflight, targeted
  Windows Clippy, benchmark, master-push debounce and advisory Windows jobs.
  Required Windows jobs ran and passed. The hosted Test job reported 20,533
  passed, 44 skipped, one slow and two leaky annotations. The hosted parallel
  gate ran three runtime repetitions (6,194 passed, 10 ignored each) and three
  channel repetitions (2,059 passed, 2 ignored each).
- **Commands run and tail output:** Local macOS checks on candidate
  `859833f5a43320ca9ddd911135ea44e2dfbf61ac`, frozen upstream base
  `535f0844d7e54f636b2fd1e7dea8b1110cbb4c68`:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | PASS |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-fail-fast` | PASS: API 326; runtime 6,198 passed, 10 ignored; 27 Goal contract tests passed |
| `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-providers --no-fail-fast` | **FAIL**, exit 101; five tests detailed below |
| `bash scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh` | PASS: three runtime and three channel repetitions |
| `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings` | PASS |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh` | PASS: 58 passed, 0 failed |
| `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` | PASS |

Relevant output from the failed command:

```text
test result: FAILED. 1986 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 10.11s
test result: FAILED. 1987 passed; 3 failed; 4 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 15.70s
error: 2 targets failed:
    `-p zeroclaw-config --lib`
    `-p zeroclaw-providers --lib`
```

The five failures are:

1. `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception`:
   a case-variant fixture collides on a case-insensitive filesystem. macOS
   filesystems can also be case-sensitive. See #11959.
2. `platform::tests::native_build_rejects_bare_name_not_on_path`: a local
   PATH entry returned permission denied; the focused test passed with that
   entry omitted. This signature was not rerun on the exact frozen base.
3. `openai::tests::responses_model_listing_carries_header_only_profile_and_surfaces_auth_failure`:
   response decoding reported missing `data`.
4. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults`:
   response decoding reported missing `choices`.
5. `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config`: the proxy
   saw four calls rather than two.

The case-variant and three OpenAI signatures were reproduced on an earlier
upstream comparison revision whose relevant source and dependency inputs match
the frozen base. The PATH failure is supported as environment-specific by the
focused diagnostic, not by an exact-base reproduction. Shared proxy state is
a plausible cause of the OpenAI failures, but the precise interleaving was not
reproduced. No failure is reclassified as a passing test.
https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11959

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Reviewed the migration,
  guarded-transition and recovery paths, public compatibility and the
  existing review requests. No live-room, deployment, rollback, power-loss or
  manual end-to-end Goal test was performed.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — this slice changes no rendered user
  interface.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Candidate `859833f5…`;
  Rust test and control-plane boundaries, as listed above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A — no visual interface change.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The automated contract tests
  exercise stale-epoch rejection, recovery and operation settlement; the
  counts and failures are recorded above.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The conditional hosted
  jobs listed above were skipped under their workflow conditions. No live-room
  or deployment test was requested.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** The
  existing control-plane database is migrated and used for the new records.
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs?
  **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any **Yes**, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- **Backward compatible?** No for downstream Rust source that constructs the
  changed public records or implements/calls `GoalTaskRegistry`. Runtime task
  import paths and existing enum variants remain available; legacy serialized
  task records use defaults for the added fields.
- **Config / env / CLI surface changed?** No.
- **Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed?** No declared change in this slice.
- **Exact upgrade steps for existing users:**
  1. Add `session_id` and `execution_epoch` to direct `TaskRecord` literals;
     ordinary tasks use `None` and `0`. Update Goal record literals for the
     pending-operation and accounting fields.
  2. Migrate Goal registry implementations and callers to the guarded
     session/epoch create, pause, resume, finish, limits, disposal and
     operation-settlement interfaces. Handle `Applied`, `Stale` and `Missing`;
     supply an objective on creation and preserve any continuation context
     through its existing setter. Generic task creation now rejects Goals.
  3. Handle errors from task and settlement enumeration rather than assuming a
     partial list is complete. Ordinary non-Goal task producers continue to use
     the generic registry.
  4. Before opening an existing control-plane database with the new binary,
     take a consistent backup and validate a disposable copy. Migration is
     forward-only: invalid nonterminal legacy Goals may be marked failed and no
     down-migration is supplied. Rebuilding an older binary does not undo it.
  5. Later Goal producers must use fresh task and operation IDs and a valid,
     matching process owner identity. The storage interface does not reject a
     zero PID or malformed owner identity, and restart recovery cannot fence
     such a record. This slice adds no in-tree Goal producer, so that
     producer-contract concern remains for later slices.

Same-boot executor loss can leave an unsettled operation fenced until the
owning later lifecycle integration classifies it or the daemon restarts. A
terminal Goal can also retain an unsettled slot until settlement or recovery,
preventing replacement. Later slices must order accounting settlement, handle
reload and dispose bound Goals before agent/session removal. Agent deletion in
this slice reports a refused control-plane cleanup as a warning after earlier
cascade steps; it is not a transaction-wide rollback.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable later Goal admission and fence or
  drain active work, preserve the current database and usage ledger, then
  revert dependent slices in reverse order before reverting this slice. A
  binary revert does not reverse schema version 13; assess recovery using the
  retained consistent backup without discarding later durable usage or state.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None introduced by this slice; later
  Goal admission controls own operational disablement.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Task registration, recovery or terminal
  transitions fail or leave tasks unexpectedly stuck; inspect task lifecycle
  errors and the durable task records.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A — this PR does not claim to supersede another PR.

prs.title: fix(canvas): drop empty unused canvases so clear frees slots
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #12205.

Empty canvases (viewer `subscribe` without content, or `clear` that left the HashMap entry) stayed in the store forever, appeared in `list()`, and counted toward `MAX_CANVAS_COUNT` (100). Clearing never freed a slot until process restart.

- `list()` returns only canvases with a current frame (matches its doc comment).
- `clear()` removes the entry when there are no live subscribers after the clear signal.
- `render` / `subscribe` prune empty entries with zero receivers before enforcing the count limit, so dropped viewers free slots without another clear.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- canvas_store` — **10 passed** (includes new `canvas_store_list_omits_empty_canvases_and_clear_frees_slots`)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check -p zeroclaw-tools`

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse
prs.body:
## Summary





Base branch: `master`.





Add opt-in task-owned SSH transport reuse. Related #11867.





### What this does, simply





One logical task owns its transport pool. Healthy idle connections can be recreated; failed or unexpectedly dead transports remain unavailable until the task ends.





## Testing (required)





### How you can test (when useful)

prs.body:
<!-- replay-cache-fix-20261110 -->
## TLS replay cache follow-up

Revision `f5b5735eb` classifies new TLS-only message IDs at insertion and evicts only that class. Older and encrypted markers remain in the shared replay table, preserving cross-mode deduplication and reviewed inbox release. The private store recognizes the exact legacy and classified schemas.

The old query reproduces a missing encrypted replay marker after exceeding the TLS retention limit. The new regression drives the real private store and offline review/release command through TLS eviction; fresh TLS-to-OMEMO initialization and earlier socket deadline regressions also pass. Integrated XMPP, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI remains authoritative.

<!-- control-write-fix-20261110 -->
## Control-write deadline follow-up

Revision `5e1f62ae7` includes `adbc57d18` and master `a4beef9a6`. Control stanzas now have a 60-second write deadline. A stalled or failed control write returns an error from the connection writer, which releases queued replies and lets the existing listener supervisor reconnect. The writer does not replay uncertain sends.

A regression driving the real writer with a stalled sink fails before the fix and passes after it. Healthy and broken control writes are also covered. Integrated XMPP, HTTP-cache and runtime tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed locally. Fresh hosted CI on this revision remains authoritative.

<!-- review-fix-20261110:start -->
## Review follow-up (2026-11-10)

Published head: 1d062fc50eb74070a6267b4d838875edf763e892. Updated with master 6877da56d.

Atomic peer-device index cleanup for reviewed offline OMEMO session reset, with index-bound review tokens and an actual encrypted send to the surviving device.

Local integration regression tests, formatting and all-target Clippy passed. Hosted CI for this exact head is pending; earlier CI/approval does not validate the new revision. Detailed boundary evidence is in the reply to the corresponding review thread.
<!-- review-fix-20261110:end -->

## Summary



Base branch: `master`.



Implement feature-gated native Rust XMPP with optional Linux legacy OMEMO. Related #9814. Depends on #12015.



### What this does, simply



The native channel owns encrypted receipts independently of the socket. Reconnect reuses the exclusive store; completed runtime and control receipts can be recorded while offline. First-contact key publication explicitly requests readable public nodes.



<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at f120f8722. Retained scoped-chat authorization and XMPP policy coverage. Canonical API generation, npm run test:auth (including xmppPolicy.test.ts), and the production build passed. Native XMPP/OMEMO validation remains covered by the published commit's CI. The dependency on #12015 remains.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)



### How you can test (when useful)



Run the `xmpp` and `native_ingress_` channel-library filters with `--no-default-features --features channel-xmpp`; then run `crates/zeroclaw-channels/tests/xmpp_native/managed_server.py` using the documented disposable loopback-only fixture.



### Earlier validation (historical)



Current-head CI Required Gate and all executed checks pass at 47f16954424bcc3787379e5e1d2c21df52daf100, including every source-image build. The inherited master root-fixture packaging fix is confirmed across the current Dockerfile/Containerfile source matrix. Integrated validation passed 69 XMPP tests (4 separately marked ignored), 5 shared-ingress tests, all four real encrypted interoperability scenarios and strict channel/test and root binary Clippy. Fresh-account scenarios remove pre-created bot nodes and verify public key discovery without roster subscription. Offline receipt completion, explicit publication policy/refusal, live admission filtering, queue overflow and deferred authorized ping ordering are covered. Human changes-requested review has not been dismissed; re-review is requested.



Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.



## Security & Privacy Impact (required)



OMEMO identity keys, signed prekeys and ratchet state are stored as JSON in the private omemo.sqlite3 database with mode 0600 and exclusive ownership; they are not encrypted at rest by the vault. The vault is required for new identity creation and encrypts queued ingress payloads. The account password uses the existing secret configuration field. Uncertain admitted work remains unreleasable. Public device lists and bundles request open access; these contain public keys, while live peer allowlists and fingerprint pins still gate message admission. Server publication refusal fails explicitly. No private deployment information, real identities, credentials, or messages are included.



- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: Yes â€” the optional channel owns a private mode-0600 OMEMO database and existing-vault access for identity creation and ingress sealing.

- New external network calls: Yes â€” configured XMPP service and bounded protocol exchanges.

- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes â€” the account password is a secret field; queued ingress uses vault ciphertext, while long-term OMEMO keys and ratchet state use the private database described above. Fingerprint pins authorize peer devices; they do not encrypt the local key store.

- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.

- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No â€” protocol content remains inside the existing shared dispatch/policy boundary.



## Compatibility (required)



Feature-gated XMPP; encrypted operation is Linux-only. Legacy OMEMO remains distinct from OMEMO v2. The existing migration and replay-protection boundaries remain documented. Offline administration requires stopping the channel owner, including while its socket is disconnected. Existing nodes with incompatible publication policy require owner reconciliation. No toolchain-floor change.



## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)



Disable the XMPP feature/configuration or revert the code subject to documented state compatibility. Preserve newer ratchets, replay markers and uncertain admitted records. Stop the channel owner before supported offline inspection/release. Observe explicit publication errors, refused admission and unreleasable completed receipts.



## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)



None. Incorporated maintainer commits retain their original authorship.


SQLite scope correction: #12322 remains draft pending a published Matrix storage dependency (matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk#7456). Its workspace-only bridge was removed from this PR; registry compatibility is preserved and #12320 remains the shared advisory tracker. No SQLite waiver is added here.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
The discovery exchange now waits for outbound queue capacity inside its existing 10-second budget; queue admission and response share one deadline. Peer timeout remains a typed inbound rejection. Added regressions cover full queue admission, the shared deadline, and cancellation without a late IQ. Integrated validation: 76 XMPP tests pass (4 lab-only ignored).

Local evidence above is from the integrated candidate. Fresh hosted CI will run on the published branch commit; maintainer architecture/merge decisions remain unchanged.
<!-- followup-20261110-b:end -->

prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Labels:** docs, gateway, security:pairing, web, size:XL
- **Base branch:** master.
- Add opt-in browser dictation and narration in agent chat, with paired-device voice preferences and a localized guide under Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio.
- Save microphone, recognition mode, language, voice, speed and automatic narration on the authenticated paired-device record, not browser storage. Operators can select another paired device's record without changing the current browser's identity.
- Add one global `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs` setting in that same voice screen: default 15 seconds, accepted range 0â€“300, with 0 disabling automatic submission. It applies to every device/conversation and uses the existing authenticated configuration property API.
- Speak rendered Markdown text rather than hidden delimiters; omit only a trailing crab signature. Preserve meaningful literal code punctuation. Formatting-only replies do not block the continuous reading queue.
- **Scope boundary:** browser speech APIs, paired-device preferences, one gateway configuration field and normal chat submission. No server STT/TTS backend, microphone-audio upload endpoint, new identity or external service is added.
- **Blast radius:** web Config/chat, existing device-registry migration, gateway configuration and same-origin microphone Permissions Policy.
- **Linked issues:** none.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable microphone and speaker controls next to the composer. Recognition starts only when the user clicks the microphone and grants browser permission. Local recognition is the default and never falls back online automatically; browser-service recognition is an explicit choice.

Dictation appends final recognized text to the draft. After the global silence interval, capture stops and final results are accepted before the normal send path is invoked once. Empty captures, hidden/cancelled chats, disconnected/busy sessions and stale conversation requests do not auto-send. A browser ending recognition early still honors the remaining silence interval. Local slash commands remain for manual submission. Set the global value to 0 for manual sending only.

The speaker reads a reply once, stops it, or enables continuous reading through a hold/Shift+Enter gesture. Automatic reading skips restored history and consumes unreadable formatting/signature-only replies so later responses can play. Changing the speech text never changes the displayed/stored response.

<!-- jarvis-validation-update:start -->
## Validation update (2026-11-10)

Updated to master a11a5ce5b at 9a9f6a1be. Combined voice controls with scoped chat while retaining operator-only image uploads. Voice submission honors the existing canSend/first-conversation path. A regression drives the actual voice callback through a restricted account's first WebSocket conversation, verifies exactly one message after session_start, and verifies that file uploads remain unavailable. Canonical API generation, the auth suite, all 31 voice tests, and the production build passed. Five gateway voice authorization tests also passed, including revocation during a write. This update was validated locally; earlier installed-browser evidence below describes its recorded revisions.

CI results and maintainer decisions on the published revision remain authoritative.
<!-- jarvis-validation-update:end -->

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interfaces:** web Config and agent chat; authenticated gateway configuration/device APIs.
- **Preconditions:** HTTPS or localhost, a paired browser, browser/OS speech support; select a locally available voice to test playback.
- **Steps:**
  1. Open Config â†’ Other â†’ Browser Voice and Audio. Enable dictation/narration, select language/voice and try the sample.
  2. Change global silence to 15, dictate and pause: verify exactly one send after the interval. Test 0 (manual only), another value, empty capture, manual stop, conversation switch and hidden chat. Confirm the same value appears on another paired device.
  3. Read a response with headings, emphasis, lists, a link and a horizontal rule. Formatting must not be spoken; code such as `apt-get --yes` must retain literal punctuation. A final crab signature is silent, but a crab in the body remains content.
  4. Enable continuous reading; place `---` or a signature-only reply before another readable answer. The latter must play. Restored history and trim notices remain silent.
  5. Reload settings and switch the device selector: per-device choices remain isolated, while the silence timeout stays global. Revoke a technical device and confirm its voice API refuses access. No voice preference storage key is added to browser storage.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: no online fallback. Browser-service mode and online voices remain explicit choices.
- **Expected after:** documented opt-in controls, durable per-device voice choices, one adjustable global silence deadline and readable narration.
- **Before on master:** these browser speech controls and preference APIs are absent.

### Earlier validation (historical)

- **Latest functional/layout revision:** 61aeff4bb (global silence, narration fixes and responsive settings/toolbar spacing); the corresponding integrated candidate uses the same feature changes.
- **Latest checks actually run:** 24 voice tests passed; configuration default/range test passed; canonical `cargo run -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` passed; integrated TypeScript check and production WebUI build passed. The checks exercise the actual component speech-submission callback, global property save, zero-disable, final-results ordering, activity resets, empty/hidden/cancelled capture, early recognition end, signature filtering and continuous queue progress.
- **Historical baseline checks:** gateway paired-device tests (14), security-header tests (5), auth/session/UI tests and format/diff checks passed at earlier documented revisions. These are not reattributed to the new head.
- **CI status:** current head includes master755bc9a4e. Its SQLite exception was approved and merged by maintainers in#12321; this PR does not introduce its own exception. The functional/layout source and installed bundle remain unchanged by that policy-only merge. Current-head CI is authoritative. The independent PR's shared SQLite advisory remains tracked by #12320; the checkout-only #12322 bridge was removed here after its registry-publication limitation was found. No advisory ignore was added. The preceding head's 32-bit check failed during runner `apt install` timeouts, before checking this code.
- **Coverage limits:** component tests simulate speech APIs. Actual microphone hardware, audible OS voice output, language pack downloads and browser-provider network behavior require device testing. New browser validation/deployment results will be reported separately, not inferred from unit tests.
- **Installed-browser validation:** synthetic microphone transcript, actual WebSocket/model completion, exactly one automatic send after **15,131 ms**, technical conversation deleted, global field verified at15 in Browser Voice and Audio; a nondefault16-second value was saved, verified on disk/after reload, then restored to15. Actual microphone hardware/audio playback are not claimed.
- **Responsive layout follow-up at61aeff4bb:** label above the numeric input (8px gap), separate help and save row (16px gap), and nonshrinking40px microphone/speaker buttons. Verified the installed UI at1280px and390px wide; both controls remain visible. The layout-only static update preserved configuration and binary and did not restart the daemon.

![Current desktop voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-desktop.png)

![Current mobile voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/0cc369ed976c610335df3a05e7fc6db4bfc0b6c1/.pr-evidence/web-voice-layout-mobile.png)

- **Earlier functional-field evidence (before the spacing follow-up):** cropped from the installed UI matching the feature changes at3f70b1efc; the evidence branch adds only this image, without changing the reviewed feature head.

![Global browser voice silence setting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6423d16e3db0b77a369c815b7839f81bbe79d357/.pr-evidence/web-voice-global-silence-live.png)

- **Visual evidence provenance:** the following captures were originally recorded at 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae and retained at the evidence revision below. They show the prior device selector, guide and controls; they do not show the newly added global field.

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

![Settings and usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

[Mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png) Â· [Portuguese guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/183d5eaed671ebc6d8e8621ea71a46cc1bc22c02/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- **Permissions:** same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is permitted; microphone and narration default disabled per device. Browser consent and user initiation are still required. Global silence defaults to 15 only after dictation is explicitly started.
- **External calls:** optional browser language-pack downloads, explicitly selected online recognition/voices; no microphone audio reaches the gateway.
- **Credentials:** own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer under the live pairing guard; other-device management uses existing operator authorization. Global timeout reads/writes use the existing config property API and its authorization/validation. No credential is returned or logged by this feature.
- **Personal data in fixtures/docs:** none; synthetic content only.
- **Model-visible text:** recognized text follows the existing user draft/send path; no approval bypass or additional execution capability.

## Compatibility (required)

- **HTTP/config:** existing paired records receive disabled voice defaults; the new global field defaults to 15 when absent. Its range is validated on configuration writes/load. Rust struct-literal callers may need the new field or `..Default::default()`.
- **Config surface:** `gateway.voice_silence_timeout_secs`; existing device preference routes remain per-device. No new environment variable or transport endpoint.
- **Toolchain floor:** unchanged.
- **Upgrade:** build matching gateway/WebUI, enable desired device controls and adjust the global interval in Browser Voice and Audio. Cookie-only sessions without a paired-device identity cannot edit device preferences.

## Rollback

- Disable automatic sending by setting global silence to 0; microphone/narration/continuous reading can be disabled independently in the voice screen.
- For binary rollback, restore a verified prior binary; remove the new configuration key if rolling back to a version rejecting unknown fields. The nullable device-preference column can remain. Preserve state and credentials rather than blindly restoring an old database after accepted work.
- Observable failures: Config save/load errors, browser capture/playback errors or preference-API refusals. Global-setting load failure disables automatic submission rather than guessing a deadline.

### Localization

The existing voice guide/device strings retain their ten-language translations and English fallback. The six new global-setting strings are provided in English and Portuguese; other locales use the existing English fallback.


<!-- followup-20261110-b:start -->
## Additional review follow-up
Continuous reading now checks readiness, listening and speaking before parsing a queued Markdown answer. - **Blast radius:** Shared runtime proxy HTTP client builders, including provider calls.

### What this does, simply



A cached client could outlive the runtime that owned its connection tasks. A later request then failed with “dispatch task is gone”. Cache lookup now checks the current runtime identity, and clients built without a current runtime are not cached. Ordinary calls on one runtime still reuse their client.

prs.title: fix(runtime): keep personality files stable per session so edits don't bust the prompt cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. After its session lookups, the handler re-resolves the caller's current grants and holds it to ownership of the admitted record right before the reload, as `session/append` and `session/abort` do. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the changed prompt may reduce cache reuse on the next request.
  - A turn now makes sure the history starts with a system prompt. A resumed session whose snapshot failed (for example a broken `identity.json`) used to keep its history with no system message, and later turns never added one. Now each turn inserts it once the snapshot succeeds; until then the turn fails with the load error.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** every `zeroclaw-runtime` file this PR changes (`src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`) is inside the merged personality-snapshot row from #11697 (ADR-016). Since `eb4822217`, `src/agent/personality.rs` is unchanged from `master`: the snapshot path calls the existing `load_personality_files` and rereads only the files it reported missing. If a reread finds text that the first read missed (a file saved mid-read), it captures again, up to 3 times, and then fails rather than pin a partial snapshot. Any read error other than not-found also fails. So no amendment to that row is needed.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`. Its prompt then changes, so the next request may get less use out of the provider's cache; you choose when that happens.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request reads less from the cache. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **AIEOS failure path (head `51e26a3c3564`):** a configured `identity.json` that can't be read or parsed now fails the snapshot capture with `Could not load AIEOS identity: …` instead of silently falling back to the Markdown files. A failed `/reload-context` keeps the previous snapshot and system prompt, and a failed first capture isn't pinned, so the next build after the file is fixed captures the full identity. The non-snapshot renderer stays lenient. New tests: `mixed_aieos_markdown_reload_failure_keeps_previous_snapshot` and `mixed_aieos_markdown_failed_first_capture_is_not_pinned` (each covers malformed JSON, a directory in place of the file, and a missing file, with `AGENTS.md` still present, then recovery after repair), plus `legacy_identity_renderer_tolerates_aieos_load_failure`. With only the test commit applied to `19c478e3b0`, both mixed tests fail (`0 passed; 2 failed`: the old renderer accepts the degraded render). On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5889 passed; 2 failed`, the two being `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `19c478e3b0`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Current head `650ab4b2a761`** (`de9462e2f` plus the fixes for Greptile 4429288963 and 4429288973), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast` → `5914 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, including the new `resumed_history_gets_its_system_prompt_once_the_identity_loads`, `personality_capture_rereads_a_file_that_gained_text_during_the_read`, `personality_capture_fails_when_a_file_keeps_changing` and `personality_capture_accepts_files_that_are_really_missing_or_empty`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.
  - CI for this head is pending. The Security job fails on every current PR run because of new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands. This PR doesn't touch wasmtime.
- **Earlier head `de9462e2f8ec`** (`eb4822217` plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`): `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc:: tools::delegate` → `2547 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored`. Clippy and fmt clean.
- **Earlier head `51e26a3c3564`:** CI Required Gate green.
- **Commands run and tail output** at `3794bcf4a254` (rebased onto `ee2f5f58f7d7`), through the remote cargo wrapper:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- reload_context a_reload_` → `4 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5811 passed; 2 failed`. The two failures are `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `ee2f5f58f7d7` in a clean detached worktree. This PR doesn't touch `relay`.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode` → `1550 passed; 2 failed`. `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` also fail on `ee2f5f58f7d7` (the second is timing-sensitive; it passed once and failed three times there).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → clean.
- **Earlier runs** at `f0fd4f895a78`, before the rebase:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Authority regression guard:** `a_reload_is_refused_when_its_grant_is_revoked_while_it_waits` and `a_reload_by_a_demoted_administrator_is_held_to_ownership` pause the reload after its gate, republish the policy, then release it. Both expect `FORBIDDEN` and an agent that still holds its first snapshot. `a_reload_of_an_own_session_survives_an_unrelated_policy_change` is the permitted control. With the recheck removed, the first two fail and the control still passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live provider cache check on this head. Real screenshots of the `/reload-context` outcomes, built from `725dcbbf69`, are linked under Screenshots below.
### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11698#issuecomment-6514495140 (macOS Terminal.app captures of `725dcbbf69`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. It's the same text as before; only the time it's read changes.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes on the wire: the new method is additive, and an old daemon returns method-not-found to `/reload-context`, which ZeroCode shows as an error line. The behavior change is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No config. The RPC method `session/reload_context` and the ZeroCode command `/reload-context` are new.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an agent ignoring a personality-file edit in an already-open session (expected until `/reload-context`). Report it if a new session doesn't see the edit.

prs.title: feat(channels): notify owner chat about unauthorized inbound messages
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Unauthorized Telegram senders currently get the public "requires operator approval" stub, but the operator learns about the attempt only from logs — in a group, the stub is all bystanders see and the owner of the bot hears nothing. This adds an opt-in `owner_chat_id` field to `[channels.telegram.<alias>]`; when set, the channel also delivers a short heads-up to that chat (typically the operator's DM with the bot) naming the sender identity, the source chat, and a bounded preview of the turned-away message, plus the same authorization hint the sender received.
  - The heads-up reuses the existing text-only unauthorized-notice delivery path and resolves `owner_chat_id` live from the published config, exactly like the existing `unauthorized_message` override, so `/bind` persists and control-plane writes are visible to the next notice without a restart.
  - A configured owner chat equal to the sender's own chat is ignored: the public notice already reached it, and echoing it back would double every attempt (and loop an owner who tests their own bot from the DM).
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the public stub text, the authorization decision, peer resolution, or any other channel. No new Bot API method — delivery is plain `sendMessage` through the existing flood-gated path. The message preview is capped at 160 chars, whitespace-collapsed, single-line, and caption-aware; non-text payloads preview empty.
- **Blast radius:** Telegram channel only, and only on the unauthorized-inbound path. Default `owner_chat_id = None` preserves current behavior exactly (no extra network calls).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12228-adjacent operator-visibility ergonomics (no tracking issue; happy to open one if preferred).

### What this does, simply

A bot owner running a Telegram channel today has no in-chat signal when someone unauthorized writes to the bot: the sender sees the approval stub, the group sees it too, but the owner only finds out by reading logs. This PR adds one optional config key, `owner_chat_id`, per Telegram alias. With it set, every turned-away sender produces a second, operator-facing notice in the owner's chat: who wrote, from which chat, a bounded preview of what they said, and how to authorize them. Without the key, nothing changes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — user-visible channel behavior with a named CI coverage gap (mock-server tests cover delivery; a live Bot API pass is cheap to eyeball).
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (telegram)
- **Setup / preconditions:** any Telegram bot alias; one unauthorized sender (not in `peer_groups.telegram_<alias>.external_peers`); a second chat (the reviewer's DM with the bot).
- **Steps to run:** set `owner_chat_id = "<your numeric chat id>"` under `[channels.telegram.<alias>]`, reload, then send a message to the bot from the unauthorized account.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the unauthorized account receives the usual stub; the reviewer DM additionally receives the heads-up (sender, chat, preview, authorize hint). Repeating with `owner_chat_id` unset sends only the stub; setting it to the unauthorized account's own chat sends only the stub.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** only the stub is ever sent; the owner chat receives nothing.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust required CI (fmt/clippy/test) — changed surfaces are `zeroclaw-config` (schema field), `zeroclaw-channels` (behavior + tests), one `zeroclaw-runtime` locale string.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None known; wiremock-based tests cover the delivery path.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo +1.98.0 fmt -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-runtime` — clean
  - `cargo check -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-channels` — `Finished dev profile` with no errors
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib owner_notice` — `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib unauthorized_preview` — `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib telegram` — `test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --lib --tests` — `Finished` with no warnings in the changed crate (three pre-existing Windows-only warnings in `zeroclaw-config` platform files and three in `zeroclaw-runtime` service files are untouched by this diff)
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Preview truncation/collapse/caption semantics via the unit test; that the owner notice is skipped for sender-chat echo and for unset config via the two behavioral tests. Not manually verified against the live Bot API.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — plain-text Telegram messages, no presentation-sensitive change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch HEAD; wiremock-captured `sendMessage` bodies.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full `cargo test` workspace run — targeted filters cover the changed surface; channels lib test binary is the slow path and is exercised for the new tests.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (No)
- New external network calls? (No — the heads-up is a `sendMessage` to a configured chat on an already-authorized Bot API token; zero calls when `owner_chat_id` is unset)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (No)
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (No — tests use synthetic ids/usernames: 100050, 3030, 9001)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (No — the preview is operator-facing copy, never enters any model prompt; the sender cannot influence formatting beyond the 160-char collapsed cap)

prs.title: fix(runtime): surface exit status and stderr on failed shell runs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Failed `shell` tool results now put `exit status N` plus stderr into the `error` field, so the model and run logs can see why a command failed.
  - If stderr is empty, the error falls back to stdout; if both are empty, it still reports `exit status N` instead of `"error":""`.
  - Successful commands are unchanged: stderr still goes only to `error`, with no exit-status prefix.
- **Scope boundary:** This does not change command validation, sandboxing, output size caps, credential scrubbing in the tool dispatcher, or how success-path stdout/stderr are captured.
- **Blast radius:** Only the failed-`shell` `ToolResult.error` / `output` shape. Downstream, `tool_execution` already folds `error` and `output` into the model-visible tool result and scrubs credentials there.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12390

### What this does, simply

When the shell tool ran a command that exited non-zero, it treated `error` as “whatever landed on stderr.” A command that printed its failure on stdout, or that failed silently, produced an empty `error`. Run logs then showed `tool failed: shell` with `"error":""`, and the model often could not see the exit status or the diagnostic text.

This change always records the exit status on failure, appends stderr when present, and uses stdout only when stderr is empty. If stdout is used as the failure detail, `output` is cleared so the dispatcher does not show the same text twice. Successful commands that write to stderr still behave as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the behavior is covered by focused unit tests on `ShellTool::execute`; there is no new UI or manual click-through.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** N/A
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

Focused checks on Linux with the CI toolchain (`1.98.0`), in crate `zeroclaw-runtime` only. I did not run the full workspace `cargo test --locked`, `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh`, `cargo doc`, `./dev/ci.sh all`, or Windows jobs.

```text
$ cargo +1.98.0 fmt -- --check crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/tools/shell.rs
# exit 0

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib -- -D clippy::correctness
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 50s
# exit 0 (no clippy findings)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --locked --lib tools::shell::tests:: -- --test-threads=1
    Finished `test` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.37s
     Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/deps/zeroclaw_runtime-27c940ef742be463)

running 68 tests
...
test tools::shell::tests::shell_captures_exit_code_and_stderr_on_failure ... ok
test tools::shell::tests::shell_captures_stderr_output ... ok
...
test tools::shell::tests::shell_reports_exit_status_when_failure_has_no_output ... ok
...
test tools::shell::tests::shell_uses_stdout_in_error_when_stderr_is_empty_on_failure ... ok
test tools::shell::tests::shell_warns_on_ephemeral_success_with_stderr ... ok
test tools::shell::tests::shell_warns_on_ephemeral_workspace ... ok
test tools::shell::tests::shell_warns_on_ephemeral_workspace_failure_path ... ok
...
test result: ok. 68 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 6142 filtered out; finished in 1.47s
```

The new tests use unrestricted `allowed_commands = ["*"]` so `exit` is not rejected by the default command policy. They check: non-zero exit + stderr (`exit status 2: fail_msg`), stdout-only failure (`exit status 3: fail_out` with empty `output`), and silent failure (`exit status 4`). Existing success-with-stderr and ephemeral-workspace failure tests still pass.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** After this PR is opened, the required `zeroclaw-runtime` unit-test jobs on `master` will compile and run `tools::shell` tests, including the new regressions.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Windows shell dialect is covered by `cfg(windows)` command helpers in the new tests, but those jobs were not run locally. Full-workspace lint (`rust_quality_gate.sh --strict` / `-D warnings` on `ci-all`) was not run locally.
- **Commands run and tail output:** See the block above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** I did not manually drive a live agent turn or `gh pr merge` the way the issue described. The unit tests reproduce empty-`error` vs populated-`error` on `ShellTool::execute` directly. I did not verify Android or sandboxed production wrappers beyond the existing unit tests in this module.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible GUI/TUI/layout change. The model-visible text is unstyled tool-result content covered by the unit assertions.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Head `3f5bee2` (full: `3f5bee269550938f32dc498944456c4a2fff6efe`), Linux x86_64, toolchain 1.98.0, `cargo test` of `tools::shell::tests`.
